title: feat(security): self-installing authority derivations for static DDL
description:
Split 6 of wamn-0h0g.22.6, DISCOVERED WHILE MEASURING SPLIT 3.

THE OBSTACLE. wamn_authority.tenant_key bakes the database name in as a LITERAL at CREATE time. That is ratified on wamn-0h0g.22.6.1 and cannot be relaxed: current_database() is STABLE, not IMMUTABLE, so reading it at call time makes the function non-indexable and destroys the sargability option (c) depends on.

But catalog-schema.sql and app-schema.sql are STATIC files applied to project-environment databases whose names are unknown when the file is authored. A static file cannot carry the literal, and split 3 cannot re-key a single static-file policy until this is solved.

THE SHAPE. A second RENDERING of the SAME template, not a second definition. The builder in crates/control/provision/src/tenant_key.rs grows an internal template taking the database literal and its octet length as pre-rendered fragments, and two public renderings over it:
  authority_derivations_sql(database)          - the literal form, for callers that know the database
  authority_derivations_bootstrap_sql()        - a DO block that substitutes current_database() and its length at APPLY time and EXECUTEs the result

The bootstrap form is what the static files carry.

WHY THIS IS NOT A SECOND DEFINITION. Both renderings come from one template, and the proof is not the shared code: a live test applies BOTH forms to the same database and asserts the md5 of pg_get_functiondef is IDENTICAL. That is the same digest probe wamn-0h0g.22.6.1 established, doing exactly the job it was created for - one pin, two appliers, zero drift tolerance.

Also verify the bootstrapped function is genuinely IMMUTABLE from pg_proc and that an expression index on it is creatable, because a bootstrap that quietly produced a STABLE function would apply cleanly and break every index.
acceptance_criteria: A DO-block rendering installs the authority derivations into a database whose name is not known at authoring time, and the installed function is byte-identical to what authority_derivations_sql produces for that same database name - proven LIVE by comparing pg_get_functiondef digests, not by reading the builders. The bootstrapped function reads IMMUTABLE and PARALLEL SAFE from pg_proc and an expression index on it is creatable. A second apply is a no-op by post-state. Named mutants that drift the database length from the literal, drop the quoting of the substituted name, or let the bootstrap emit STABLE each fail a named test.
close_reason:
Split 6 landed, LIVE-GATED AND ARMED, six live tests green with zero skips.

WHY IT EXISTS. Measuring split 3 hit a constraint no bead named: tenant_key bakes the database name in as a LITERAL because current_database() is STABLE and would make the function non-indexable, but catalog-schema.sql and app-schema.sql are STATIC files applied to project-environment databases whose names are unknown when the file is authored. Neither can carry a literal, and split 3 could not re-key a single static-file policy without this.

WHAT LANDED. ONE TEMPLATE, TWO RENDERINGS. derivations_template takes the database literal and its octet length as pre-rendered fragments; authority_derivations_sql substitutes a real name, authority_derivations_bootstrap_sql substitutes placeholders and wraps the whole thing in a DO block that fills them from current_database() at APPLY time and EXECUTEs the result. The installed function is IMMUTABLE either way, because the name is baked in as a literal rather than read at call time. quote_literal runs on the SERVER, so a database name containing a quote cannot break out of the body.

SHARING A TEMPLATE IS NOT THE PROOF. the_bootstrap_and_literal_renderings_install_the_same_object applies BOTH renderings into one database and asserts md5(pg_get_functiondef) is identical for both functions. That is the digest probe wamn-0h0g.22.6.1 created doing exactly the job it was created for: one pin, two appliers, zero drift tolerance. It also reads IMMUTABLE from pg_proc, builds the expression index, and checks the bootstrapped value against Rust across all seven boundary tenants.

*** THE GATE USES A MULTI-BYTE DATABASE NAME ON PURPOSE. *** The bootstrap counts the name's length on the server, and length() counts CHARACTERS while octet_length(convert_to(...)) counts BYTES. For an ASCII name the two agree exactly, so an ASCII-only gate cannot tell a correct implementation from a broken one - and the disagreement it would miss is every guest read refusing. The scope's database name now carries two 2-byte characters, and the connection URI percent-encodes them.

FOUR MUTANTS, ALL KILLED, ALL COMPILING:
  P1 octet_length replaced by length -> killed by the multi-byte gate. On the ASCII name it had been EQUIVALENT, which is what prompted the multi-byte scope.
  P2 quote_literal dropped from the substitution -> killed.
  P3 IMMUTABLE downgraded to STABLE in the shared template -> killed the flags arm and the pin. NOT bootstrap-specific: one template makes a bootstrap-only volatility drift structurally impossible, which is a stronger answer than a mutant.
  P5 the replace argument misspelled so the placeholder survives -> killed.

AND A COVERAGE HOLE THE MUTANTS FOUND. P1, P2 and P5 initially died ONLY in the live gate, and the ordinary sweep arms no live gate - so all three would have shipped green. The unit test now asserts the PAIRING (each placeholder against the exact expression that substitutes it), and all three now die in the pure arm as well.

ONE PIECE OF MY OWN RESIDUE, cleaned rather than worked around: an earlier run of this test under its ASCII database name left objects owned by the scope role, and DROP OWNED BY only reaches the current database, so the reset could not drop the role. The stale database was removed by name.

wamn-control-provision and wamn-schema-compiler both fully green with both live gates armed, zero skips.

title: feat(security): wamn_authority.current_tenant_key, the session side of the guest predicate
description:
Split 5 of wamn-0h0g.22.6, DISCOVERED WHILE MEASURING SPLIT 2 and filed under rule 7 rather than absorbed into it.

THE GAP. Split 1 shipped wamn_authority.tenant_key(tenant), which derives a 40-hex key FROM A ROW. The predicate also needs the OTHER side: the key of the CONNECTED ROLE. Nothing in the tree produces it.

WHY A SCALAR FUNCTION IS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. The owner ruling fixes the expression index as CREATE INDEX ... ((tenant_key(tenant_id))) - the indexed expression is the BARE call. PostgreSQL only uses an expression index when the predicate side matches that expression exactly, so the predicate must be tenant_key(tenant_id) = <scalar>. Every alternative that wraps the indexed expression (comparing a concatenated role name, or pg_has_role over a derived name) is unsargable and therefore refuted by the same ruling that demands the index.

THE ROLE NAME IS NOT THE KEY. workload_generation_role mints prefix + underscore + 40-hex + underscore + a-or-b, so current_user is never equal to tenant_key output. The scalar must EXTRACT the digest from current_user.

SHAPE. wamn_authority.current_tenant_key() RETURNS text, LANGUAGE sql, STABLE (current_user is stable, which is all an index scan needs on the comparison side), PARALLEL SAFE, SET search_path = pg_catalog, owned by the platform role, REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, EXECUTE to the guest ACL role. Body is a single anchored regex capture over current_user cast to text. A role that does not match returns NULL, so the predicate is NULL, so no row passes - FAIL CLOSED, the same posture session_author_tenant() takes for an unmapped login.

NO SECOND NAMING CONVENTION. The prefix, the 40-hex length and the a-or-b suffix are all read from the SAME Rust constants workload_generation_role uses, so wamn-0h0g.22.6.4 cannot change the role name without changing this function. That coupling is asserted by a test that feeds a REAL minted role name through the emitted regex.

APPLY SITE. Rides the same builder and the same two appliers as split 1 (catalog-schema.sql for fresh installs, wamn-0h0g.11.49 for existing project-env databases), so there is ONE place to remember rather than two.
acceptance_criteria: wamn_authority.current_tenant_key() exists, is STABLE and PARALLEL SAFE read from pg_proc, is not SECURITY DEFINER, is owned by the platform role, grants EXECUTE to the guest ACL role and nothing to PUBLIC. Connected as a role minted by workload_generation_role for family App, it returns exactly tenant_key(tenant) for that tenant, proven LIVE. Connected as any other role it returns NULL. The emitted SQL is pinned. Named mutants that drift the prefix, the digest length, the generation suffix set, or drop the anchors so a crafted role name matches, each fail a named test.
close_reason:
Split 5 landed, LIVE-GATED AND ARMED, five tests green with zero skips.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS. Split 1 shipped the ROW side (tenant_key). Measuring split 2 found the SESSION side missing entirely: nothing derived the connected role's key, so the predicate the ruling requires could not be written. Filed under rule 7 rather than absorbed into split 2, because it is a separate database object with its own grants, its own pin and its own live proof.

WHY A SCALAR FUNCTION WAS FORCED, NOT CHOSEN. The owner ruling fixes the expression index as the BARE call tenant_key(tenant_id). PostgreSQL matches an expression index only against that exact expression, so the predicate must be tenant_key(tenant_id) = scalar. Every alternative that wraps the indexed expression - comparing a concatenated role name, or pg_has_role over a derived name - is unsargable and therefore refuted by the same ruling that demands the index. Precedent for the shape is wamn_authority.session_author_tenant() in control-portable-store.sql, minus its mapping table.

WHAT LANDED. wamn_authority.current_tenant_key() RETURNS text, LANGUAGE sql, STABLE PARALLEL SAFE SECURITY INVOKER, SET search_path = pg_catalog, owned by wamn_db_owner, REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, EXECUTE to the guest ACL role. Body is one anchored regex capture over current_user cast to text; anything that is not a guest generation returns NULL, so the predicate is NULL and no row passes - FAIL CLOSED.

ONE BUILDER, NOT TWO. tenant_key_function_sql is renamed authority_derivations_sql and now emits BOTH functions. Both must reach both appliers (catalog-schema.sql for fresh installs, wamn-0h0g.11.49 for existing project-env databases); two builders would have been two places to remember and one place to forget.

NO SECOND NAMING CONVENTION. The pattern is composed from the SAME constants workload_generation_role mints from - the family generation prefix, SCOPE_HASH_HEX_LEN, and CredentialGeneration - so wamn-0h0g.22.6.4 cannot move the role name without moving the pattern with it. A named test asserts the shape against a role the mint ACTUALLY produced, and a second refuses a prefix carrying a regex metacharacter, because a metacharacter there turns the anchored pattern into a wildcard and a wildcard is a cross-tenant read.

THE LIVE ARM IS THE ONLY PLACE THE TWO LANGUAGES MEET. the_session_derivation_returns_the_key_of_the_connected_guest_login mints the login, connects AS IT, and asserts both current_tenant_key() and the full governed equality. It also creates two near-miss logins - x plus the login, and the login plus x - and asserts both derive NULL. Those two prove the ANCHORS, which are the difference between a derivation and a cross-tenant read.

FIVE MUTANTS, ALL KILLED, ALL COMPILING, each failing a NAMED test and each killing at least one LIVE test:
  M1 anchors dropped -> killed the session test via the near-miss logins.
  M2 STABLE downgraded to VOLATILE -> killed the flags test.
  M3 the prefix hardcoded instead of read from the family -> killed the session test AND the mint-shape test.
  M4 SECURITY DEFINER added -> killed the flags test AND the session test, confirming that current_user inside a DEFINER function reports the DEFINER.
  M5 the PUBLIC revoke removed -> killed the grants test.
Baseline sha256 verified identical before and after every mutant.

ONE DEFECT IN MY OWN TEST, FOUND BY ARMING IT: boolean concatenated with boolean renders one side as true/false and the other as t/f, so the first grants assertion compared truefalse against tf.

wamn-control-provision fully green: 98 + 11 + 6 + 5 + 2 + 1 passed, 0 failed. The workspace sweep runs at the split-2 close.

title: feat(provision): per-tenant guest LOGIN generations
description:
Split 4 of wamn-0h0g.22.6. The identity half: the roles whose current_user the predicates from splits 2 and 3 read.

Extend the A/B generation machinery owned by wamn-0h0g.13.59 to mint per-project-environment and per-TENANT guest LOGIN generations, selecting exactly one active Secret while permitting bounded overlap.

NAMING - RULED, and the bead premise it replaces was REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. The design used to say the opaque bounded tenant-key convention; no such convention existed. The measured reality is the scope-digest pattern (workload_role_scope_hash, effect_writer_scope_hash, SCOPE_HASH_HEX_LEN = 40), extended here: wamn_guest_ + 40-hex digest + generation suffix = 53 bytes, inside the 63-byte cap.
*** THE TENANT ID MUST NEVER BE EMBEDDED VERBATIM. *** valid_tenant admits 64 bytes, PostgreSQL caps identifiers at 63 and TRUNCATES SILENTLY with a NOTICE, so two long tenants would collapse onto ONE role - a cross-tenant breach wearing a naming bug. The mint must REFUSE at 64 bytes rather than trust the server to reject. Recorded as a standing hazard class in docs/operations/build-and-test.md.

The digest MUST equal what wamn.tenant_key returns, or the predicate and the role name disagree and every guest read refuses.

Each generation is LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE, NOREPLICATION, NOBYPASSRLS, owns nothing, and inherits ONLY the stable NOLOGIN guest ACL role with SET false and ADMIN false.

Inherits the connection-multiplication ledger item: per-tenant credentials imply per-credential pools, and the recorded pooler tripwire fires as tenant count grows. The pool key from wamn-0h0g.22.8.2 already carries the generation role, so a new tenant generation is a new pool by construction.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning deterministically issues per-project-environment and per-tenant A/B guest LOGIN generations and selects exactly one active Secret while permitting bounded overlap. Each generation is LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE, NOREPLICATION, NOBYPASSRLS, owns nothing, and can inherit only the stable NOLOGIN guest ACL role with SET false and ADMIN false. The role name carries a bounded digest equal to what wamn.tenant_key returns, never the tenant id verbatim, and the mint REFUSES rather than truncates at 64 bytes. Named mutants restoring a shared wamn_app LOGIN, granting SET membership, embedding the tenant id verbatim, and drifting the digest from wamn.tenant_key each fail a named test.
notes:
INHERITED FROM wamn-0h0g.22.6.3, which landed the DDL half.

*** THIS BEAD IS WHAT UN-REDS THE GUEST-PATH LIVE GATES. *** The 43 guest-reachable relations now derive tenant authority from current_user. Until per-tenant guest LOGIN generations exist AND the runtime connects as them, every live gate that reads as wamn_app under a SET LOCAL app.tenant claim sees ZERO ROWS on those relations. That is the intended half-state of one construction proven once at wamn-0h0g.22.15, not a regression to chase.

*** THESE REDS ARE INVISIBLE TO THE ORDINARY SWEEP. *** Every one of those gates is env-gated and self-skips, and a self-skipping test reports PASS. The workspace sweep stayed at its standing failing NAME SET across the whole sweep. Do not read that as the guest path being healthy.

THE INVENTORY IS BY INSPECTION, NOT BY ARMING - stated plainly because the difference matters. The class is: any live gate that (a) applies one of catalog-schema.sql, app-schema.sql, run-state.sql or postgres-init.sql, and (b) reads rows as wamn_app under an app.tenant claim. Clearest members, verified by reading them: crates/identity/project-state/tests/schema.rs (app_schema_applies_and_enforces_isolation_and_claims_on_postgres, WAMN_SYSSCHEMA_PG_URL), services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs, tests/integration/src/causation_e2e.rs, crates/platform/runtime/tests/common/mod.rs and the runtime's s2 claim gates, services/dispatcher/tests/read_authority.rs.

THE PATTERN THAT FIXES THEM is already proven twice in the tree: mint the role with workload_generation_role for family App and the gate's tenant and database, create it, GRANT the stable wamn_app ACL role to it, and SET LOCAL ROLE to it instead of setting a claim. See crates/schema/compiler/tests/ddl.rs (the_generated_tenant_floor_admits_only_the_connected_guest_on_postgres) and crates/control/provision/tests/deploy_sql_authority.rs.

ALSO INHERITED: the RUNTIME still injects SET LOCAL app.tenant (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/claims.rs). That injection is now inert on every swept relation, so it is dead authority that must be replaced by per-tenant connections here, not left as belt and braces.

title: feat(security): sweep the hand-written tenant predicates onto current_user
description:
Split 3 of wamn-0h0g.22.6. The hand-written half of what split 2 does by generator.

MEASURED FOOTPRINT at 2e22da39 - 94 current_setting(app.tenant) predicates:
  catalog-schema.sql   49   (26 grants to wamn_app)
  app-schema.sql       15   ( 8 grants)
  postgres-init.sql    15   (11 grants)
  run-state.sql        12   ( 6 grants)
  run-queue.sql         3   ( 0 grants - the ONLY file the guest ACL role cannot reach)
91 of the 94 sit on relations the guest ACL role holds grants on.

Re-key each GOVERNED TENANT predicate onto the schema-qualified wamn.tenant_key(tenant_id) derived from current_user, and give each re-keyed relation ITS EXPRESSION INDEX IN THE SAME SWEEP - the owner ruling puts the index alongside the predicate everywhere, not only in the generator.

*** SCOPE IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY ALL 94. *** Determine per relation whether the guest family can actually reach it. run-queue.sql has no wamn_app grant at all and is the clear negative case. A relation the guest cannot reach carries a HOST-INJECTED claim, which is a different security posture, and re-keying it would be change without a threat. Record the per-relation determination; do not sweep by grep count.

DO NOT TOUCH the RESTRICTIVE per-role and per-user policies from crates/schema/compiler/src/rls/, which key on app.role and app.user_id and layer INSIDE the tenant floor. Those are a different claim class and are out of this bead scope.

Two drift guards move with any retained-relation change to control-portable-store.sql: a runtime pg_catalog fingerprint (READ ITS VALUE FROM THE FILE, never from memory) and a seven-name literal inventory. If this sweep touches a retained relation, they move in the same change or the file refuses to apply.
acceptance_criteria: Every governed tenant predicate on a guest-reachable relation derives from current_user through the schema-qualified wamn.tenant_key, and each such relation carries its expression index. The per-relation reachability determination is recorded rather than inferred from a grep count, including the relations deliberately left alone because the guest cannot reach them. The app.role and app.user_id restrictive policies are untouched. control-portable-store.sql drift guards move with any retained-relation change. Named mutants restoring a GUC predicate on a guest-reachable relation and dropping one expression index each fail a named test.
notes:
RIDERS ADDED 2026-08-26 while implementing split 2. Three of them, each measured.

1. THE SCHEMA NAME IS wamn_authority, NOT wamn. Every wamn.tenant_key in this bead means wamn_authority.tenant_key. The two qualified names now live in wamn-pg-core (AUTHORITY_SCHEMA, TENANT_KEY_FUNCTION, CURRENT_TENANT_KEY_FUNCTION) because both the provisioner that CREATES the functions and the schema compiler that EMITS CALLS to them must name one object; take them from there rather than writing the string again.

2. THE PREDICATE HAS TWO HALVES. tenant_key derives a key from a row and wamn_authority.current_tenant_key() derives the connected role's key (wamn-0h0g.22.6.5). The governed form, verbatim, is
  wamn_authority.tenant_key(tenant_id) = wamn_authority.current_tenant_key()
and the left side must stay a BARE call, because that is the only expression PostgreSQL will match the expression index against.

3. THE FRESH-INSTALL APPLY SITE IS THIS BEAD. Split 1's ruling put catalog-schema.sql on the fresh-install path and wamn-0h0g.11.49 on the converge path, but neither has landed: the derivations builder still has no production caller. This bead already owns catalog-schema.sql, so carrying authority_derivations_sql output into it belongs here. Without it a fresh project-environment database cannot apply ANY generated catalog DDL at all, because the emitted policies and the tenant-key index reference a function that does not exist.
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-26 at 97efffb3, from the SERVER, not from grep. Fresh postgres:18, the five files applied in dependency order (postgres-init, then catalog-schema, run-state, run-queue, app-schema - run-state needs the catalog schema, run-queue needs wamn_run), all clean.

THE 94 IS AN OCCURRENCE COUNT, NOT A WORK COUNT. The distinct population is 45 POLICIES on 45 relations. The arithmetic closes exactly: 45 policies x 2 clauses (USING and WITH CHECK) = 90, plus 4 occurrences in file header COMMENTS = 94.

AND THE POPULATION IS POLICIES ONLY. Measured zero app.tenant occurrences in column defaults (pg_attrdef), zero in function bodies (pg_proc), zero in CHECK constraints (pg_constraint). There is no second population hiding behind the policy count.

PER-SCHEMA: catalog 24, app_system 7, wamn_run 7, s2 4, s3 3.

REACHABILITY, from has_table_privilege on the live catalog: 43 of 45 relations are reachable by wamn_app; 2 are NOT, and the bead named only one of them.
  wamn_run.run_queue           ---- (predicted: run-queue.sql has no wamn_app grant)
  wamn_run.operator_run_actions ---- (NOT predicted: it lives in run-state.sql, which the bead counted as fully reachable)
Both carry a HOST-INJECTED claim and are out of scope by this bead's own criterion. Determination recorded; they are deliberately left alone.

s2 and s3 are the S2-S6 GATE FIXTURES built by postgres-init.sql and mounted as the kind cluster's init ConfigMap. wamn_app holds SIUD on all seven, so they ARE guest-reachable and in scope by the criterion. Re-keying them will red the runtime gates that set app.tenant against s2 until wamn-0h0g.22.6.4 lands the per-tenant logins - the intended half-state of one construction proven once at wamn-0h0g.22.15.

app_system is in scope and not a fixture: its own header calls it PER-PROJECT TENANT DATA, tenant-scoped, wamn_app-readable, under the same RLS floor as the catalog and the generated data tables.

*** A STRUCTURAL OBSTACLE THE BEAD DOES NOT NAME. *** tenant_key bakes the database name in as a LITERAL at CREATE time, because current_database() is STABLE and would make the function non-indexable - ratified on wamn-0h0g.22.6.1. catalog-schema.sql and app-schema.sql are STATIC files applied to project-environment databases whose names are not known when the file is authored, so neither can carry a literal. The install must therefore compute it at apply time. Filed as wamn-0h0g.22.6.6 and made a hard dependency; this bead cannot re-key a single static-file policy until it exists.
SHAPE MEASURED 2026-08-26 - THE SWEEP IS UNIFORM, which is the single most useful thing measurement found here.

ONE DISTINCT PREDICATE across all 45 policies, read back from pg_policy:
  (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant'::text, true), ''::text))
WITH CHECK is either that same expression or absent (the read-only policies, polcmd r). Every policy is PERMISSIVE and applies TO PUBLIC. There is no per-relation variation to discover.

In the FILES that is 89 byte-identical occurrences of
  tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant', true), '')
plus 5 more in prose. 89 = 45 policies x 2 clauses minus the read-only policies' missing WITH CHECK.

RE-KEY COUNT, closing exactly against the reachability determination:
  catalog-schema.sql  24 policies  -> all 24
  app-schema.sql       7 policies  -> all 7
  postgres-init.sql    7 policies  -> all 7 (s2 4, s3 3)
  run-state.sql        6 policies  -> 5, SKIPPING operator_run_actions
  run-queue.sql        1 policy    -> 0, the whole file is skipped
  total re-keyed 43, matching the 43 guest-reachable relations exactly.

THE STATIC-FILE BOOTSTRAP IS OWNED BY CURRENT_USER, not by wamn_db_owner. These files already carry AUTHORIZATION postgres (three of them) or AUTHORIZATION CURRENT_USER (run-state.sql), so naming a role that may not exist would add a new precondition to EIGHT appliers - seven tests plus the production path in services/ctl/src/author_wiring.rs. CURRENT_USER is the applier, which in every real deployment IS the platform role, and it introduces no new required role. wamn_app is already required by these files (26 grant lines in catalog-schema.sql alone), so the bootstrap's grants add nothing new either.

THE CHECKED-IN BOOTSTRAP TEXT NEEDS A DRIFT GUARD, and it is the exempt kind: byte-equality against a named artifact, which is the sole exemption wamn-hopk R5 leaves for a test reading a file as text.
close_reason:
Split 3 landed, LIVE-GATED AND ARMED, and the sweep is complete rather than partial: 43 of 45 permissive tenant policies re-keyed, with the other 2 determined out of scope from the SERVER.

MEASURED, NOT GREPPED. The bead's 94 is an occurrence count; the population is 45 POLICIES, and the arithmetic closes exactly (45 x 2 clauses minus the read-only policies' missing WITH CHECK = 89 in-file occurrences, plus 5 in prose). Column defaults, function bodies and CHECK constraints carry ZERO app.tenant occurrences, so there was no second population hiding behind the policy count. Every one of the 45 carries the SAME predicate - one distinct expression across the whole set - so the sweep is a single uniform substitution, not 45 judgements.

REACHABILITY FROM has_table_privilege, on a live cluster with all five files applied in dependency order: 43 reachable, 2 not. The bead predicted one negative case (run-queue.sql). The second, wamn_run.operator_run_actions, lives in run-state.sql - a file the bead counted as fully reachable - and would have been swept on the bead's own numbers. Both keep their HOST-INJECTED claim, and the determination is now written into both files rather than left in a report.

A POPULATION THE FIRST MEASUREMENT MISSED, found and closed: control-portable-store.sql creates EIGHT more permissive app.tenant policies through format() with doubled quotes, so no grep for the plain spelling finds them. They are CONTROL-plane, and that file contains ZERO occurrences of wamn_app - the guest ACL role holds nothing there - so they are out of scope by the same criterion, and its comments about the permissive policy above remain TRUE because they describe its own policies. It needs no change, and neither of its two drift guards moves.

WHAT LANDED. 43 policies onto wamn_authority.tenant_key(tenant_id) = wamn_authority.current_tenant_key(), each with its <table>_tkey expression index, plus the wamn-0h0g.22.6.6 bootstrap at the head of all four files. Verified from the server: 43 policies keyed on current_user, 43 of 43 with index coverage from pg_index, zero uncovered, and exactly the ruled pair still on the claim.

SEVEN HAND-MAINTAINED INVENTORIES MOVED WITH IT, six of which the tests found rather than I did:
  run_plane.rs ENVIRONMENT_POLICY_TENANT_QUAL and the reconciler's own CREATE POLICY - the important one. Left alone, reconcile-run-plane would REVERT the sweep on every existing run-plane database, silently re-opening the settable-claim boundary rather than failing.
  run_plane.rs index inventory (5 new names), and the catalog tail pin.
  project-state's tenant_floor guard - retired subject, kept CHECK half, now pinned in BOTH directions.
  run-state's drift guard and the wiring-relation guard, both caught by the failing NAME SET diff after the first full sweep, not by inspection.

THE INDEX FORM IS PLAIN CREATE INDEX, not IF NOT EXISTS, and that is load-bearing: run_plane.rs parses index statements by taking the word after INDEX, so IF NOT EXISTS would have produced an index named IF - in the PRODUCTION reconciler, not just in a test.

FOUR MUTANTS, ALL KILLED, EACH ON A FRESH CLUSTER, each killing at least two named tests including the live one:
  Q1 one policy reverted to the claim -> killed the both-directions pure test and the live settable check.
  Q2 one expression index removed -> killed the index-count test and the live pg_index coverage arm.
  Q3 ONE CHARACTER changed in a checked-in bootstrap block (scope domain v0.1 -> v0.2) -> killed the identity pin AND the live cross-tenant assertion, because the drifted function replaced the good one and the guest's key stopped matching. That is precisely the attack the identity pin exists for.
  Q4 the out-of-scope run_queue re-keyed -> killed the exception-set assertion.

ONE DEFECT IN MY OWN GATE, FOUND BY THE SWEEP AND NOT BY ME: it applied postgres-init.sql, which carries a bare CREATE DATABASE and bare CREATE ROLEs, so it passed alone and FAILED on a surviving cluster. It now drops the database and all three roles first and passes twice in a row - and the recipe says plainly that it owns its server.

title: feat(security): re-key the generated tenant floor onto current_user
description:
Split 2 of wamn-0h0g.22.6. THE LEVERAGE POINT - one site moves the entire generated developer surface.

crates/schema/compiler/src/emit.rs carries a single function that emits, for every generated entity table: ENABLE and FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE POLICY {t}_tenant USING (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting(app.tenant, true), )) WITH CHECK (same), and GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE TO wamn_app.

CHANGE IT TO DERIVE FROM current_user via the schema-qualified wamn.tenant_key from split 1, AND EMIT THE EXPRESSION INDEX IN THE SAME OPERATION: CREATE INDEX ... ((wamn.tenant_key(tenant_id))). The owner ruling is explicit that the index rides the generator, so sargability moves with the predicate and cannot be forgotten per-table.

The NULLIF empty-claim guard exists because an empty GUC claim would otherwise match a hypothetical empty-tenant row. current_user cannot be empty, so that specific guard dissolves - but the CHECK (tenant_id <> ) in create_table_op stays, and the predicate must still refuse a row whose tenant_id does not derive to the connected role key.

The GRANT stays TO wamn_app: the bead keeps wamn_app as the stable NOLOGIN ACL grant owner, and retiring its runtime LOGIN class is wamn-0h0g.12.140, not this.

Pin the emitted SQL string. This is GENERATED SQL from a Rust builder, which is the form this repo pins - it is the only thing that catches the builder moving.
acceptance_criteria: The generator emits a current_user-derived tenant predicate through the schema-qualified wamn.tenant_key, and emits the matching expression index in the same operation, for every generated entity table. No emitted policy contains app.tenant or a current_setting tenant predicate. The emitted SQL string is pinned. The grant to the stable wamn_app ACL role is unchanged. Named mutants restoring the GUC predicate, dropping the expression index, or unqualifying the function call each fail a named test.
notes:
PREMISE CORRECTIONS, measured 2026-08-26 at 705943d2 before implementing.

1. THE SCHEMA NAME IN THIS BEAD IS WRONG. Split 1 landed the function as wamn_authority.tenant_key, not wamn.tenant_key. Every occurrence of wamn.tenant_key in this bead and its parent means wamn_authority.tenant_key.

2. THE PREDICATE NEEDS A SESSION SIDE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. tenant_key derives a key from a ROW; nothing derives the CONNECTED ROLE's key. Filed as wamn-0h0g.22.6.5 and made a hard dependency rather than absorbed here, because it is a separate database object with its own grants, its own pin and its own live proof. The emitted predicate is therefore:
  wamn_authority.tenant_key(tenant_id) = wamn_authority.current_tenant_key()

3. THE INDEX NAME ENTERS A SHARED NAMESPACE AND MUST BE BUDGETED. ENTITY_NAME_BUDGET is MAX_IDENTIFIER_BYTES minus the length of _pkey, so an entity name may be 58 bytes. A suffix longer than 5 bytes overflows 63 and PostgreSQL TRUNCATES SILENTLY - the standing hazard class. The suffix is therefore _tkey, exactly the width of _pkey, so the existing catalog budget covers it by construction with no validation change; the R22 truncate-plus-hash branch stays as defense in depth for migrate_plan, which is the unvalidated entry.

4. A SYNTHESIZED RELATION NAME IS NOT JUST AN EMIT. The tenant-key index shares pg_class with tables, secondary indexes and unique backing indexes, so it must also be registered in derive_identifiers (wamn-schema-model), in migrate_plan's all_relnames collision scan, in the index_asides set when a dropped table's name is reclaimed, and it must FOLLOW a table rename the way <table>_pkey does. Omitting any of those is the deletion-collateral defect class inverted.

title: feat(security): wamn.tenant_key and its frozen-definition probe
description:
Split 1 of the rule-7 decomposition of wamn-0h0g.22.6 (94 tenant predicates across five DDL files plus a generator - not one commit). FOUNDATION: splits 2, 3 and 4 all depend on this.

THE FUNCTION. wamn.tenant_key(tenant_id) is the pure derivation RLS uses to reach the tenant from current_user. Owner ruling 2026-08-26, option (c): the ban on mapping tables and caller-settable indirection targets MUTABLE SETTABLE STATE between identity and authority. A fixed derivation with no writer and no state is computation, not indirection.

REQUIRED SHAPE, all four binding:
  - IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE. Immutability is what makes it indexable; without it the expression index in split 2 is not even creatable.
  - SCHEMA-QUALIFIED at every use site. An unqualified call is search_path-resolvable, which would reintroduce exactly the caller-settable hijack the design forbids.
  - Owned by the platform role, EXECUTE granted to the guest family. The guest may CALL it and may not REPLACE it.
  - Its digest must equal the 40-hex scope-digest convention already in the tree (workload_role_scope_hash, effect_writer_scope_hash, SCOPE_HASH_HEX_LEN), so the value it returns is the same key the role name carries in split 4.

*** THE FROZEN-DEFINITION PROBE IS THE ONE NEW DENIAL THE DESIGN NEEDS. *** An attacker who can redefine wamn.tenant_key owns EVERY governed predicate at once - a single write that silently unlocks every tenant. Pin a digest of pg_get_functiondef and assert it. Assert the SERVER answer, never the static DDL text: the point is what the server will actually execute.

Also prove the ownership and grant posture from the catalog: the function is owned by the platform role, the guest family holds EXECUTE and does NOT hold ownership or any privilege permitting CREATE OR REPLACE.
acceptance_criteria: wamn.tenant_key exists, is IMMUTABLE and PARALLEL SAFE, is owned by the platform role and grants EXECUTE to the guest family. Its return value matches the 40-hex scope-digest convention already used for workload roles, so split 4 role names and split 2/3 predicates agree by construction. A live probe pins a digest of pg_get_functiondef and fails if the definition changes. A live probe proves the guest family cannot redefine or replace it. Named mutants that alter the body, drop IMMUTABLE, drop PARALLEL SAFE, or grant the guest family ownership each fail a named test.
notes:
DESIGN MEASURED AND SETTLED 2026-08-26, implementation NOT STARTED. Everything below is measured, not assumed.

THE DIGEST IS ALREADY DETERMINED - DO NOT INVENT A SECOND ONE. wamn.tenant_key(tenant) in database D must equal exactly:
  workload_role_scope_hash(WorkloadRoleFamily::App, WorkloadRoleScope::Tenant { tenant, database: D })
because WorkloadRoleFamily::App has scope_kind Tenant and scope_domain wamn.app.scope.v0.1. The Rust side is therefore a THIN WRAPPER over the existing function; a second Rust implementation of the digest would be the drift this construction cannot afford.

THE PREIMAGE, measured from workload_role.rs and effect_writer_credential.rs:
  frame(domain) || frame(tenant) || frame(<tenant value>) || frame(database) || frame(<db value>)
where frame(v) = 8-byte BIG-ENDIAN length prefix followed by the bytes. In SQL that is exactly
  int8send(octet_length(convert_to(v,UTF8))::bigint) || convert_to(v,UTF8)
and the result is substr(encode(sha256(preimage),hex), 1, 40) - SCOPE_HASH_HEX_LEN is 40.

*** THE DATABASE NAME MUST BE BAKED IN AS A LITERAL AT CREATE TIME, NOT READ AT CALL TIME. *** current_database() is STABLE, not IMMUTABLE, so using it would make the function non-indexable and destroy the whole point of option (c). The function is created per project-env database, so a literal is correct and available. It also cannot be dropped from the preimage: without the database, the same tenant in two project-env databases would collide on one role name.

PRECEDENT FOR THE SHAPE: wamn_authority.session_author_tenant() in control-portable-store.sql already does the schema-qualified-authority-function-in-RLS pattern, with SET search_path = pg_catalog plus its own schema, REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, and GRANT EXECUTE to exactly one role. Copy that posture.

*** OPEN QUESTION, RAISED TO THE OWNER: WHERE THE FUNCTION IS CREATED FOR EXISTING PROJECT-ENV DATABASES. *** catalog-schema.sql is what publish_catalog.rs applies into a project database, and its own comment says it applies WHOLE ON A FRESH INSTALL AND NEVER AGAIN. So adding the function there reaches new installs only. Existing databases need a converge path, and R55 applies to whichever is chosen: the mechanical test is whether a SECOND RUN IS A NO-OP, not merely whether it exits zero. wamn-0h0g.11.49 owns insert-or-verify-identical typed-refusal convergence for both migration paths and is the likely home for the pattern.
CONVERGE PATH RULED 2026-08-26: wamn-0h0g.11.49 IS THE HOME, and the open question on this bead is CLOSED.

catalog-schema.sql carries the function for fresh installs; .11.49's path carries existing project-env databases; THE DEFINITION-DIGEST PROBE THIS BEAD OWNS IS WHAT MAKES THE TWO APPLIERS PROVABLY IDENTICAL - one pin, two appliers, zero drift tolerance.

R55 applies and its real test is POST-STATE, not exit status. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is naturally convergent, but the converge arm asserts: the function exists, its definition digest matches the pin, IMMUTABLE and PARALLEL SAFE are present read from pg_proc rather than from DDL text, and the EXECUTE grants are exact. A function that silently lost IMMUTABLE still creates fine and breaks every expression index depending on it, which is why the flags are asserted from the catalog and not assumed from the statement that created them.
close_reason:
Split 1 landed, LIVE-GATED AND ARMED. crates/control/provision/src/tenant_key.rs emits wamn_authority.tenant_key(text) as IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE STRICT with SET search_path = pg_catalog, owned by wamn_db_owner, REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC, USAGE and EXECUTE to the guest ACL role.

NO SECOND DIGEST EXISTS IN RUST. tenant_key() is a thin wrapper over workload_role_scope_hash(App, Tenant{tenant, database}), asserted by a named test, so the role name provisioning mints and the key the predicate computes cannot drift.

THE DATABASE IS A BAKED-IN LITERAL. current_database() is STABLE, not IMMUTABLE, and would have made the function unusable in an expression index - destroying the sargability option (c) depends on. It also cannot be dropped: a named test proves the same tenant derives a DIFFERENT key per database, which is what stops two project-env databases colliding on one role name.

THE LIVE GATE IS ARMED AND EXECUTES - zero skips, verified. Throwaway postgres:18 (18.6), four tests, all green in PARALLEL as well as serially:
  - the_sql_tenant_key_equals_the_rust_tenant_key - the sharpest failure mode in this construction, proven across seven tenants spanning the valid_tenant charset INCLUDING the 64-byte boundary. One of the two implementations only exists inside PostgreSQL, so no pure test could have caught a disagreement.
  - the_function_carries_the_flags_the_expression_index_requires - reads provolatile and proparallel FROM pg_proc, not from DDL text, and then actually CREATES the expression index.
  - the_guest_may_execute_the_derivation_and_may_not_replace_it - EXECUTE held, ownership on the platform role, PUBLIC holds nothing.
  - a_second_apply_leaves_the_definition_identical - R55 as post-state: md5(pg_get_functiondef) unchanged across two applies, which is what makes catalog-schema.sql and the wamn-0h0g.11.49 path provably the same object.

THREE MUTANTS, ALL KILLED, ALL COMPILING, each on a hermetic preamble and the GRANT mutant on a FRESH CLUSTER because roles are cluster-wide:
  M1 SQL domain drifted one version from Rust -> killed the agreement test.
  M2 IMMUTABLE downgraded to STABLE in the builder -> killed the flags test.

title: spec(authoring): demolition spec for the stateless-gate collapse
description:
OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-25. ONE DAY, ROUGHLY 300 LINES. COMES TO THE OWNER FOR RATIFICATION; ON APPROVAL IT IS A PHASE-A-STYLE DELETION WAVE, NOT A REFACTOR.

PREMISE: wirings are documents with content-hash identity. A draft is a CLIENT-SIDE FILE (studio buffer, git), not server state. The load-bearing surface is TWO VERBS PLUS READS.
  gate(document) -> report        STATELESS. Report immutable, KEYED BY WIRING-HASH. Idempotent BY CONSTRUCTION: same hash, same report. NO run-row, NO retry-resumption protocol, NO Pending convergence semantics, NO draft tables.
  publish(document, report-id)    catalog row plus activation, AS LANDED.

THE SPEC MUST:
  1. Map the seven authoring ops onto the two-verb reading.
     EXPECTED SURVIVORS: publish, get-report, gate.
     EXPECTED COLLAPSES: save-draft, read-draft, validate, draft-run - client-side, or absorbed into gate.
     These are EXPECTATIONS TO TEST, NOT CONCLUSIONS. Measure and report refutations.
  2. Enumerate the draft-persistence TABLES that delete.
  3. Enumerate the COMPOSITION MACHINERY that deletes.
  4. Enumerate the CONTRACT SURFACE that deletes.
  5. State what wamn-0h0g.8.5.4's landed work REDUCES TO under hash-keyed stateless reports.

OPEN QUESTION TO ANSWER IN THE SPEC, NOT BEFORE: does case execution need ANY server-side state at all beyond the report row?

CONSTRAINT IN FORCE NOW: no new fields, grants or gates on any surface the spec would delete.
notes:
SPEC WRITTEN AND PUSHED at 0c7e7543: docs/PLAN/authoring-stateless-gate-demolition.md, 253 lines. DRAFT, AWAITING OWNER RATIFICATION. Lands in docs/PLAN because that is the non-normative tier - it is NOT design authority and must not be read as such.

FOUR THINGS RATIFICATION MUST DECIDE, in order of consequence:
  1. *** ARE GATE CASES EFFECT-FREE BY CONTRACT? EVERYTHING ELSE FOLLOWS FROM THIS. *** Producing a report needs no stored state and idempotency needs only a uniqueness constraint - but PARTIAL EXECUTION does. Cases invoke components that perform effects, so a gate that dies at case 7 of 10 and retries with no stored state RE-FIRES SEVEN CASES' EFFECTS. Position 1, cases are effect-free and truly stateless, is the only one that delivers the directive's goal - but it is a REAL CONSTRAINT that must be STATED AND ENFORCED, not assumed, and neither the statement nor the enforcement point exists today. Position 2, cases may have effects, KEEPS the machinery the directive exists to delete and merely re-keys it.
  2. Is gate the renamed test-set-run? The directive names gate as a survivor and DOES NOT MENTION test-set-run in either list. Nothing else in the contract produces a report, so the spec treats them as one verb - FLAGGED AS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A MEASUREMENT.
  3. Does gate_report_id collapse into wiring_hash? Recommended yes. catalog.wirings carries BOTH, and gate_report_id is bare text WITH NO FOREIGN KEY TO ANYTHING, on the same immutable row as a real content hash. Two identifiers for one fact.
  4. Is catalog.draft_safe_connection_grants deleted by this wave or a separate one.

HALF THE PREMISE IS ALREADY LAW: catalog.validated_flow_drafts is gone and the control store's own comment states the wiring document IS the validated artifact and its hash IS the identity (wamn-pm7k). This finishes a direction the tree started.

WHAT 8.5.4 REDUCES TO: roughly 350-400 of store/admission.rs's 528 lines SURVIVE - candidate resolution by wiring hash is exactly the stateless lookup, built early. The ~900 lines of composition and retry machinery DO NOT. Its most valuable output was never the loop; it was the measurement that wiring_hash is a sufficient key, which is this spec's premise.

ONE CLAIM WAS ASSERTED AND MEASURED FALSE BEFORE COMMIT: draft_safe_connection_grants does not grant anything to gate runs. ZERO production DML; it exists only to be named in the authoring role's privilege probe.

NOT STARTED, AND NOTHING IS DISPATCHED. The transitional-hardening ban is in force.

SPEC RATIFIED, AMENDED, AND ITS SUBJECT SHIPPED. Closed by owner ruling 2026-08-25.

Written and ratified at 858169d3, then AMENDED at 2a54c32f when the owner struck two survivor-clauses the wave-65 lane had correctly refused - section 3.2's test_set.rs mostly deletes became deletes, section 3.3's authoring_test_reports survives re-keyed was struck, and a new section 3.3.1 records the ruling, the measurement that refuted the old text, the re-derivation from the effect-free premise, and the standing rule it produced.

THE SUBJECT SHIPPED: wamn-0h0g.8.5.5 is CLOSED, all four subjects, across five commits ending at dc1fb111. title: [SR-MVP] feat(components): component admission records effects and typed connection requirements
description:
PHASE B ITEM 1. Owner ruled 2026-08-25 option (a): file and build now. Component publishing today mints the digest, enforces the closed import allowlist, and persists ports and parameters. It records NOTHING about effects, and connection requirements sit in an untyped JSON object that admission never writes. This bead closes both gaps at the shape ratified by wamn-0h0g.21.8.

MEASURED AT c935b88f, do not re-derive:
- crates/platform/runtime/src/component_admission.rs is 226 lines and contains ZERO occurrences of effect.
- catalog.component_library columns are tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, component, interface_version, operation, component_digest, imports, imports_fingerprint, input_ports, output_ports, parameters, admitted_at. THERE IS NO EFFECTS COLUMN.
- catalog.connection_requirements carries requirement_json jsonb plus requirement_hash, already re-grained onto (component_digest, store_alias), but the payload is a free-form object and validate_component_admission NEVER WRITES IT.

WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS: wamn-0h0g.21.8 closed as RATIFIED - NOT IMPLEMENTED, naming downstream beads as the delivery owners. Its only two downstream edges, wamn-0h0g.18.3 and wamn-0h0g.21.1, are BOTH CLOSED and delivered the ports-and-allowlist half only. Every other wamn-0h0g.21 child is closed. The remaining child wamn-0h0g.13.7 is parked hold:post-mvp behind a promotion guard. Phase B item 1 therefore had NO CLAIMABLE OWNER until this bead.
design:
Extend the pure validator to derive effect facts from admitted imports, persist them as a normalized column on catalog.component_library, and give connection requirements a typed schema whose writer is admission itself rather than a free-form object minted elsewhere.

CONSTRAINTS CARRIED FROM THE RATIFIED RULING - do not relitigate: the validator stays PURE over bytes with exactly ONE production publishing caller; the import allowlist stays CLOSED with no wasi wildcard; wiring compatibility stays EXACT schema-digest equality; ONE logical operation per digest preserves the uniform ABI; environment stays WIRING-owned and never becomes admission state.
acceptance_criteria: Admitted component facts carry effects derived from the component imports, and connection requirements carry a typed schema rather than a free-form object. Admission is the writer for both. The validator remains pure over bytes with one production caller. The closed import allowlist, exact schema-digest equality, one-operation-per-digest, and wiring-owned environment all still hold.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED. Filed 2026-08-25 on the owner ruling. Effects and typed connection requirements are the DELTA on top of what wamn-0h0g.21.1 landed - this is not a re-do of the library relation.
WAVE 62 LANDED IT: commits edf85c72 (effect facts) and 4ad9894d (typed connection requirements).

REFUTATION WORTH KEEPING: *** THE FREE-FORM PROBLEM WAS AT THE PERSISTED BOUNDARY, NOT IN THE TYPE. *** ComponentConnectionRequirement over ConnectionTypeDescriptor was ALREADY a typed deny_unknown_fields record. What was actually broken: no production writer, and TWO READERS THAT DISAGREED ABOUT THE SHAPE - promote.rs:711 deserialized the whole wrapped record while connection_http.rs:469 pointer-read /requirement-type at the TOP level. A row satisfying either REFUSED the other. A live correctness bug, latent only because nothing minted rows. Reconciled toward the wrapped record, which is what requirement_hash hashes.
ALSO REFUTED: effect is NOT the same as admitted platform package. components/no-std/publish.sh:71 passes --admit-platform-package wamn:node for a PURE transform component, so that classification would have labelled every component effectful. Hence an explicit non-effect list, complement of two closed lists, no wildcard, FAILING SAFE - an unlisted new wamn: package counts as an effect.
ALSO: admission CANNOT derive store aliases from bytes - the alias is the requirement string the guest passes at call time, nowhere in the component type. So it is DECLARED and admission CROSS-CHECKS it.

- Ordinal drift between fresh and converged installs (effects lands at position 10 fresh, at the end converged): the identical hazard ALREADY SHIPPED for connection_requirements.component_digest, so precedent was matched rather than a fix invented.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: wamn-0h0g.21.10 (effects backfill), wamn-kf2k (state-owners writers).

title: decide(publish): register_release_flow_test_evidence is SECURITY INVOKER, so EXECUTE alone cannot write the evidence
description:
wamn-0jsr's ruling - GRANT EXECUTE on catalog.register_release_flow_test_evidence to the control
author - is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, and implementing it as written would remove an
authority-boundary check WITHOUT delivering the capability. Measured in the main loop during wave
60's lane-5 attempt; implementation STOPPED rather than half-built, per rule 7.

*** THE FUNCTION IS SECURITY INVOKER. *** deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql:473 declares it
RETURNS timestamptz, LANGUAGE plpgsql, AS - with NO SECURITY DEFINER clause. The only SECURITY
DEFINER in that entire file is at :1012, on a DIFFERENT function (LANGUAGE sql STABLE). Verified by
reading the header, not by grep count alone.

*** ITS BODY TOUCHES THE TABLE BOTH WAYS. *** It INSERTs INTO catalog.release_flow_test_evidence,
and on the conflict path it SELECTs FROM the same table to compare the stored row. Under SECURITY
INVOKER the body runs with the CALLER's privileges, so a control author holding EXECUTE and nothing
else would enter the function and fail inside it with permission denied for that table. There is NO
grant of table privileges on catalog.release_flow_test_evidence to wamn_control_author anywhere in
deploy/sql - measured, zero hits.

*** THERE ARE THEREFORE TWO DENIALS IN THE WAY, NOT ONE. The bead names only the first. ***
1. FUNCTION denial, deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql around :1167 - a has_function_privilege
   test inside the boundary check that RAISEs 42501 control-author-authority-boundary-violated.
   Granting EXECUTE while it stands is a boot failure.
2. TABLE denial, services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs around :133-135 - the startup probe
   asserts NOT has_table_privilege SELECT and NOT has_table_privilege INSERT on
   catalog.release_flow_test_evidence, and refuses at startup if either is gained. Granting the
   table privileges the INVOKER body needs is ALSO a boot failure unless that probe moves.
   The bead treats the authoring.rs probe as possibly not needing to move because it targets the
   TABLE while the grant targets the FUNCTION. That reasoning is right about the mechanism and
   WRONG about the conclusion: SECURITY INVOKER is exactly what makes the table privilege necessary.

THE OPTIONS:
(a) GRANT EXECUTE plus GRANT SELECT, INSERT on the table. Both denials move in the same commit.
    WIDEST SURFACE: the control author gains DIRECT table read and write, so the function stops
    being the only path to evidence and anything running as that principal can write rows straight
    into the table, bypassing the conflict-detection the function exists to enforce.
(b) MAKE THE FUNCTION SECURITY DEFINER and grant EXECUTE only. NARROWEST SURFACE: the table stays
    denied, the authoring.rs probe stays exactly as written, and only the :1167 function clause
    moves. The function becomes the SOLE path to the table, which is presumably why it exists.
    *** BLOCKED ON A STANDING RULE: SECURITY DEFINER re-proposals MUST CITE THE PRIOR REJECTION,
    ratified as wamn-0h0g.7.5. This bead is that citation request, not an end run around it. ***
    Whoever rules it should also settle search_path pinning on the function.
(c) A DIFFERENT PRINCIPAL owns the evidence write. The ruling already rejected the admitter for it
    on plane grounds - evidence registration is step-A gate territory, control-plane - so this
    means naming a new one, which is machinery the ruling was trying to avoid.

WHAT IS NOT IN DOUBT: register_deployment_attestation at the neighbouring clause around :1172 is a
DIFFERENT function and STAYS DENIED under every option. Anchor on the signature, never the line.

BLOCKS wamn-0jsr, and through it wamn-0h0g.8.5.4, which cannot mount the publish leg without an
evidence write that actually executes.
close_reason: RULED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-24: OPTION (b), SECURITY DEFINER. 7.5 is satisfied by the plane distinction, not bypassed - its holding was no second run-creation path into the PROJECT plane, whereas this is the sole EXISTING writer on the CONTROL plane keeping its insert-or-verify invariant enforced rather than advisory, and session_author_tenant at :1009 is the same pattern already blessed in-tree. Option (a) was rejected on its own text: direct table INSERT retires the conflict check, R55's class, minted deliberately. Riders all implemented at f700a0cc - pinned search_path of pg_catalog and catalog, GRANT EXECUTE to wamn_control_author alone, the boundary clause moved in the same commit, authoring.rs left exactly as written so its table denial is now the proof of narrowness, a new probe arm asserting a non-author caller is refused, and the commit body citing 7.5 with the plane distinction.

title: fix(publish): no role can execute register_release_flow_test_evidence
description:
The control author CANNOT WRITE RELEASE TEST EVIDENCE, so the authoring surface cannot mount Publish.
Measured 2026-08-24 by wave 58 lane S while scoping wamn-0h0g.7.4's publish leg.

deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql:526 REVOKEs ALL on catalog.register_release_flow_test_evidence FROM
PUBLIC. Verified independently: ZERO GRANT EXECUTE for that function anywhere in deploy/, crates/ or
services/, and the function is NOT SECURITY DEFINER. So no role can call it.

Separately, services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs's startup probe asserts the control author has NO
SELECT and NO INSERT on catalog.release_flow_test_evidence, and the process REFUSES AT STARTUP if it ever
gains them. The denial is therefore actively defended, not an oversight.

The credential structurally cannot perform the evidence half. Per rule 7 there is no partial mount, so
lane S did not take .7.4.

probe's denial assertion moves with it. Note the probe's refusal is a deliberate guard - changing the grant
without changing the probe turns a running process into a startup failure.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24 - THE CONTROL-AUTHOR PRINCIPAL EXECUTES IT. Implementation NOT STARTED.

RULED: evidence registration is STEP-A GATE TERRITORY - control-plane, inside the publish transaction -
NOT the admitter's project-plane job. Grant EXECUTE on catalog.register_release_flow_test_evidence to the
control author.

*** BINDING AND EASY TO GET WRONG: THE STARTUP PROBE'S DENIAL ASSERTION MOVES WITH THE GRANT, IN THE SAME
COMMIT. *** services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs currently asserts the control author has NO SELECT
and NO INSERT on catalog.release_flow_test_evidence and REFUSES AT STARTUP if it ever gains them. Granting
without moving that assertion is a MINTED BOOT FAILURE - the process would start, check, and kill itself.

THE OWNER'S OWN SENTENCE GOES IN THE COMMIT BODY: grant-without-probe-move is a minted boot failure.

This unblocks wamn-0h0g.7.4's publish leg.

*** IMPLEMENTATION STOPPED, NOT STARTED. THE RULING IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT AND IMPLEMENTING IT AS WRITTEN WOULD REMOVE AN AUTHORITY-BOUNDARY CHECK WITHOUT DELIVERING THE CAPABILITY. *** Measured in the main loop during wave 60. catalog.register_release_flow_test_evidence is SECURITY INVOKER - control-portable-store.sql:473 has no SECURITY DEFINER clause, and the file's only one is at :1012 on a different function. This bead's own text guessed the probe might not need to move because it targets the table while the grant targets the function; that reads the mechanism right and the conclusion wrong, because SECURITY INVOKER is precisely what makes the table privilege necessary. THE FORK IS FILED AS wamn-ey3j (P0) and this bead is blocked on it. Nothing was edited in deploy/sql or authoring.rs.

title: fix(provision): the management-admitter cannot select runs.status or runs.result_json
description:
The management-admitter credential CANNOT OBSERVE A RUN'S OUTCOME, so the scenario-worker cannot poll a
project run to terminal. Measured 2026-08-24 by wave 58 lane S while attempting wamn-0h0g.8.5.4.

crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs:211 MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_RUN_SELECT_COLUMNS grants SELECT on exactly 17
named runs columns. NEITHER status NOR result_json is among them. status appears in the INSERT list only.
grant_management_admitter_surface_sql REVOKEs all table and per-column privileges first, so the surface is
closed, not merely unmentioned. There is no compensating function grant, no view, and nothing replicates
run status into the control database.

WHY IT BLOCKS .8.5.4: that bead's middle third - observe the immutable terminal result, copy asserted facts
plus the frozen binding world into the control case summary, then admit the next ordinal - has no
credential that can execute it. The bead cites MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_QUEUE_INSERT_COLUMNS as confirmation
that scenario-worker admits and polls; the queue INSERT columns are real, but the run SELECT columns refute
the polling half.

Lane S deliberately did NOT half-build it. Mounting AuthoringCommand::TestSetRun without the observation
leg would create durable admissions that can never converge - strictly worse than the current 501.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS: widen the admitter run-select grant to include status and result_json, or give
the observation leg a different mechanism. Widening is a grant change in crates/control/provision and must
carry its own probe arm per R12.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24 - WIDEN THE GRANT. Implementation NOT STARTED.

RULED: add status and result_json to MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_RUN_SELECT_COLUMNS. Those two columns are exactly
what the observation leg exists to read, and the admitter is ALREADY THE RUN'S PRODUCER PRINCIPAL. A second
mechanism for two columns - a view, or a separate reader role - is machinery.

REJECTED by that reasoning: a view, a separate role, or replicating run status into the control database.

BINDING RIDER: THE DENIAL-SET PROBE UPDATES IN THE SAME COMMIT. The grant and the assertion about what the
principal may not read move together, or the next process start disagrees with the tree.

R12 applies: this LANDS rather than being filed, because it is a grant the principal legitimately needs to
do the job it already owns - but it carries its own probe arm in the same commit.

This unblocks wamn-0h0g.8.5.4's observation leg, which was the reason .8.5.4 could not be built.
close_reason: DONE at dabc47cc (wave 60, main loop). MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_RUN_SELECT_COLUMNS widened 17 to 19 with status and result_json, exactly as ruled. The alternatives the ruling rejected were not built: no view, no separate reader role, no replication of run status into the control database. Carries its own probe arm per R12, and the arm was NEEDED - every existing consumer derives its expectations from this same constant, so a widening flows through them silently and proves nothing; the new assertion names both columns in the emitted GRANT text. Mutation-checked: removing status from the array fails management_admitter_surface_is_current_column_exact_and_convergent, file restored sha-for-sha. The stale-column-ACL revoke is a generic pg_attribute loop and needed no change. Measured: wamn-control-provision 109 passed 0 failed, wamn-ctl 107 passed 0 failed. NOT VALIDATED AGAINST A LIVE DATABASE - WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL was not armed and this is a builder-text change; the DDL itself has not been executed.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(management): sequential case composition against the candidate wiring
description:
SPLIT OUT OF wamn-0h0g.8.5.3 by the owner ruling of 2026-08-24. .8.5.3 kept the
connection leg (the arg, the manifest env, the Secret key); this bead owns the
composition, which .8.5.3's acceptance described but its ruled scope could not
deliver. Parents track, children own: .8.5 must not carry this as residual prose.

SCOPE — the composition, one ordinal at a time:
- Mount AuthoringCommand::TestSetRun. It exists in the model
  (crates/authoring/model/src/lib.rs: AuthoringCommand::TestSetRun, TestSetRunReceipt,
  TestSetRunRefusal) and in the ledger literal test, but has no handler.
- Compose control report reservation with the retained project management admission,
  one ordinal at a time: admit the deterministic project run, recover exact retries
  after either database commit, observe its immutable terminal result, copy asserted
  facts plus the frozen binding world into the control case summary, and only then
  admit the next ordinal.
- Sequential admission, at-most-once per ordinal, crash-after-commit convergence.

CARRIED VERBATIM FROM THE .8.5.3 RULING, because it is easy to miss:
"STILL IN SCOPE AND EASY TO MISS: AuthoringCommand::TestSetRun exists in the model but
the authoring dispatch returns 501 for it. Without that, the composition is unreachable
from the wire."

THE ASSERTION THAT MUST FLIP WITH IT — this bead owns rewriting it, so the bare-501
audit note does not strand:
services/scenario-worker/tests/management_live.rs currently PINS the 501. It asserts
the bare 501 audits nothing and mutates nothing. The dispatch site is the let-else at
the top of dispatch_command in services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs:
    let AuthoringCommand::SaveFlowDraft(input) = and command.command else {
        return Ok(empty(StatusCode::NOT_IMPLEMENTED));
    };
SaveFlowDraft is the only mounted command. The 501 is empty-bodied by design (a 501 is
the absence of a route, not a product refusal, so it carries no document) and fires
AFTER authorization so the surface is not a route-existence oracle. Preserve both
properties for the still-unmounted kinds.

MEASURED, 2026-08-24 (wave 56 measurement pass):
- Adds a workspace dependency: services/scenario-worker/Cargo.toml does NOT depend on
  wamn-run-state, which owns management_admission_transaction,
  ManagementProducerKey::TestCase{report_id, ordinal}, AdmissionResult (11 variants),
  and AdmissionProducer::TestCase.
- Correctly does NOT need wamn-execution-host. Execution is the executor's, via
  RouterDriver::execute_candidate reached from services/executor/src/lib.rs off
  QueueDriverRequest::Candidate. Scenario-worker admits runs plus run_queue rows and
  polls. The admitter grants confirm this: MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_QUEUE_INSERT_COLUMNS is
  tenant_id, run_id, available_at, stream_seq.
- Do not weaken the in-module statement in services/scenario-worker/src/store/
  test_orchestration.rs that a transaction cannot span the two databases.
- Size: roughly 700-1100 lines, possibly low. TestSetRun handler plus wire decode/
  receipt/refusal ~150; the sequential loop reserve_test_report to management admission
  txn to poll terminal to finalize_test_case to reconcile_test_report ~250-400; second
  connection lifecycle on Surface ~50; live-test extension ~250-400.
- This is the largest remaining .8.5 child. Size it honestly when scheduling; it is not
  a wave filler.

DEPENDS ON: wamn-0h0g.8.5.3 (the connection leg lands the arg this composition uses).
acceptance_criteria: AuthoringCommand::TestSetRun is mounted and reachable from the wire. A report's cases execute sequentially, one ordinal at a time, at most once per ordinal. An exact retry after a commit on either database converges rather than double-admitting. Each case's asserted facts and frozen binding world are copied into the immutable control case summary before the next ordinal is admitted. The management_live.rs assertion that pinned the bare 501 for TestSetRun is rewritten, and the bare-501 audits-nothing property is preserved for the kinds that remain unmounted.
notes:
WAVE 58 LANE S: ATTEMPTED, REFUTED, NOT STARTED IN CODE. No partial mount was committed. Every refutation
below was RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE INTEGRATOR against 616b94bf, not taken on the lane's word.

BLOCKER ONE, now filed as wamn-oici and added as a dependency. The management-admitter credential CANNOT
OBSERVE A RUN'S OUTCOME. crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs:211
MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_RUN_SELECT_COLUMNS is exactly 17 columns and contains NEITHER status NOR result_json;
status is in the INSERT list only. grant_management_admitter_surface_sql REVOKEs all table and per-column
privileges first, so the surface is closed rather than merely unmentioned. No function grant, no view,
nothing replicating run status into the control database.

THIS BEAD'S OWN CITATION IS THE TRAP. It cites MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_QUEUE_INSERT_COLUMNS as confirmation
that scenario-worker admits and polls. The queue INSERT columns are real and correct; they say nothing
about the run SELECT surface, which refutes the polling half. Do not re-derive from the queue columns.

WHY NOTHING WAS BUILT: mounting AuthoringCommand::TestSetRun without the observation leg would create
durable admissions that can never converge - strictly worse than the current 501. That judgement is
endorsed.

BLOCKER TWO, an unruled CONTRACT decision, not a grant. TestSetRun carries only validated_draft_id, but
management admission requires wiring_id, wiring_version, wiring_hash and gate_report_id. Those live in
DIFFERENT DATABASES: catalog.wirings is defined in deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql (project plane),
catalog.validated_flow_drafts in deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql (control plane). Nothing in tree
resolves one to the other.

WORSE, AND VERIFIED: catalog.validated_flow_drafts HAS NO PRODUCTION WRITER AT ALL. Every occurrence in
Rust is a test insert, a schema/DDL manipulation in crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs, or a guard

OWNER DECISION NEEDED before this bead is workable.

cannot span the two databases. It was not touched.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-24 - REINTERPRET validated_draft_id AS THE WIRING HASH. Implementation NOT STARTED.

RULED: do NOT build a cross-database mapping. The DRAFT CONCEPT DIED WITH THE PIVOT - the wiring document
IS the validated artifact and its hash IS the identity, one document lineage, per the test-contract ruling.

CONSEQUENCE, and it removes the blocker: the wiring identity admission needs no longer has to be joined

RULED SEPARATELY, SAME PASS: catalog.validated_flow_drafts HAS NO PRODUCTION WRITER and is DEAD. It is

WAVE 60: BOTH STRUCTURAL BLOCKERS ARE NOW CLOSED IN CODE. THIS BEAD IS UNBLOCKED AND BANKED, NOT
STARTED. No partial mount exists; nothing was edited in services/scenario-worker for it.

  wamn-oici  CLOSED at dabc47cc. MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_RUN_SELECT_COLUMNS is now 19 and carries status
             and result_json, so the observation leg has a credential that can execute it.
  wamn-0jsr  CLOSED at f700a0cc under the wamn-ey3j ruling. The control author holds EXECUTE on
             catalog.register_release_flow_test_evidence, which is now SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned

  wamn-0h0g.8.5.3 verified CLOSED and landed at ca62445b, so the connection arg this composition uses

MEASURED AT THE WAVE-60 TIP, because this bead's description predates .8.5.3 landing:
  services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs:882  dispatch_command
  :887-889  the let-else is INTACT and unchanged in shape - SaveFlowDraft is still the only mounted
            command and everything else returns an empty NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
  :802      a SECOND 501, AuthoringQuery::ReadDraft, on the query side. Not this bead's, but it
            shares the empty-bodied property and must not be collaterally changed.
  services/scenario-worker/Cargo.toml does NOT yet depend on wamn-run-state. Still true; this bead
            adds it.

*** A GUARD THIS BEAD MUST MOVE THAT NO NOTE HAS NAMED, AND IT IS THE BRITTLE CLASS THE OWNER
FLAGGED ON 2026-08-24. *** management.rs:1494-1501 is a SELF-SCANNING SOURCE SCAN over its own file:
it slices at the dispatch_command signature and asserts
matches("save_flow_draft(&mut backend").count() == 1 with the message that save is the sole mounted
audited command. Mounting TestSetRun makes that assertion false by construction. DO NOT simply bump
the count to 2 - that preserves a guard whose subject is a substring of its own source. Replace it
with a behavioural assertion over dispatch_command's actual responses: each unmounted kind returns
an EMPTY-BODIED 501, each mounted kind does not, and the 501 still fires AFTER authorization so the
surface is not a route-existence oracle. Those are the two properties the bead already requires be
preserved, and they are decidable by calling the function rather than by reading its text.

ACCEPTANCE UNCHANGED. Size still honest at roughly 700-1100 lines; the owner explicitly banked it
rather than run it as a wave tail-end. Do not start it as filler.

WAVE 62: NOT STARTED IN CODE, AND CORRECTLY SO. BLOCKED ON wamn-0h0g.8.25 (dependency wired) - the management admitter is DENIED the four caller-outcome columns that case evaluation consumes, so mounting TestSetRun would create durable admissions whose cases can never be evaluated.

MEASURED THIS WAVE SO THE NEXT ATTEMPT IS CHEAP - do not re-derive:
- THE CATALOG-COORDINATE QUESTION RESOLVES WITHOUT NEW GRANTS. TestSetRun carries no catalog coordinate and the admitter is denied catalog.catalog_heads, BUT it HAS GRANT SELECT on catalog.wirings, which carries catalog_id, wiring_id, version, gated_catalog_version, gate_report_id and graph_json. Keying on wiring_hash (the owner ruled validated_draft_id IS the wiring hash) yields every admission parameter. expected_catalog_version MUST equal gated_catalog_version because the candidate CTE joins on that equality. NOT A BLOCKER.
- Cases are reachable: WiringDocument.cases rides catalog.wirings.graph_json (crates/catalog/model/src/wiring.rs:189-198).
- This bead would be the FIRST production caller of management_admission_transaction. The only existing caller is crates/execution/run-state/tests/admission_live.rs:71, whose test_case_admission helper at :83-102 is the exact 17-param call shape to copy.
- The self-scanning guard that must be replaced is now at services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs:1493-1498, re-anchored by the wave-62 rename, still FALSE BY CONSTRUCTION once a second command mounts.

REMAINING PIECES, sized by the lane, for splitting if the owner wants them separate: (a) the grant widening - NOW wamn-0h0g.8.25; (b) project-admission connection on Surface plus candidate resolution by wiring hash, ~120 lines; (c) the sequential per-ordinal loop reserve-admit-poll-evaluate-finalize-reconcile, ~350 lines; (d) the TestSetRun handler, receipt/refusal and ledger row, ~150 lines; (e) replace the self-scanning guard with a behavioural assertion over dispatch_command; (f) rewrite the management_live.rs bare-501 assertions while PRESERVING the empty-bodied-501 property for kinds that stay unmounted, ~300 lines and env-gated.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-25 - THE PENDING-REPORT CONVERGENCE QUESTION. NO DRIVER. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED.

RULED: REPORTS ARE CALLER-CONVERGED BY DESIGN. The design premise is same-key-retry-as-resumption. A background sweeper would be a SECOND CONVERGENCE AUTHORITY RACING THE CALLER - the split-brain shape the single-claim model exists to prevent - and building a driver for reports nobody is polling is machinery ahead of demand.
Deadline exhaustion TERMINALIZES INLINE.
A deadline-exhausted or effect-uncertain composition that a caller never retries STAYS HONESTLY NON-TERMINAL. That is correct behaviour, not a defect.
VISIBILITY, NOT CONVERGENCE, IS THE OPERATOR'S TOOL.

*** THE ACTUAL DEFECT IS THAT THIS CONTRACT IS UNSTATED. Landing it means WRITING IT DOWN, not building machinery. ***

RIDER, the cheapest honest hardening: the report's Pending payload carries last_attempt_at so staleness is observable without a sweeper.

*** PREMISE CORRECTION, MEASURED AT 10bbe597 - THE RULING SAYS THE EXISTING REPORT-READ SURFACE SHOWS AGE. IT DOES NOT. ***
  ReportProjection::Pending (crates/authoring/model/src/lib.rs:588) carries EXACTLY report_id and
  validated_draft. NO TIMESTAMP OF ANY KIND reaches the wire for a pending report.
  The DATABASE has the facts and the PROJECTION DROPS THEM: wamn_run.authoring_test_run_reservations
  (:352-373) carries created_at NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp() and whole_deadline_at NOT NULL with a
  CHECK that it exceeds created_at. So age and the exhaustion point both exist and neither is exposed.
  wamn_run.authoring_test_reports holds FINALIZED reports ONLY - passed, summary and finalized_at are all
  NOT NULL - so a pending report HAS NO ROW THERE. Anything about pending state reads the reservation.
  NOTHING TRACKS RETRY ATTEMPTS TODAY. last_attempt_at is a NEW COLUMN on the reservation, not a
  projection of an existing one.
SO THE RIDER IS TWO THINGS, NOT ONE: expose pending age at all, and add the attempt stamp.

WIRE IMPACT, measured: ReportProjection is deny_unknown_fields with JsonSchema. The frozen-literal
contract test at crates/authoring/model/tests/contract.rs:192 covers the Finalized variant ONLY - Pending
is NOT frozen there, so adding a field to Pending breaks no existing frozen literal. It is still a wire
change and should be frozen as a whole-value literal when it lands, per the wire-contract rule.
The only producer is services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs:856.

NAMED RE-OPEN TRIGGER FOR A DRIVER BEAD - FILE IT THEN, NOT NOW: a real operational need for UNATTENDED
convergence, specifically scheduled publishes or CI-driven gates with no waiting caller. Its design must
ANSWER THE SINGLE-AUTHORITY QUESTION - how a sweeper does not race the caller - before it is built.
*** SUPERSEDED BY OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-25 - THE PENDING/last_attempt_at RIDER IS CANCELLED. DO NOT BUILD IT. ***
Authoring collapses to a STATELESS-GATE model. Wirings are documents with CONTENT-HASH IDENTITY; a draft is a CLIENT-SIDE FILE (studio buffer, git), NOT server state. Two verbs plus reads:
  gate(document) -> report   STATELESS. Report immutable, KEYED BY WIRING-HASH. Idempotent BY CONSTRUCTION: same hash, same report. NO run-row, NO retry-resumption protocol, NO Pending convergence semantics, NO draft tables.
  publish(document, report-id)   catalog row plus activation, as landed.
Under that model the entire convergence question this bead's last note answers CEASES TO EXIST - there is no Pending state to observe, so there is nothing to stamp. The measurement in that note stands as evidence for the demolition spec; the RIDER does not.
NO FURTHER 8.5.x COMPOSITION HARDENING. Spec owner: see the demolition spec bead.

LANDED at 523750fc. 2171 insertions across 10 files. AuthoringCommand::TestSetRun is mounted and reachable from the wire; cases execute sequentially, one ordinal at a time, at most once per ordinal.

*** THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING, WHICH NO BEAD NOTE CARRIED: report_id IS NOT FREE. *** crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs:405-407 classifies a test case whose report_id IS DISTINCT FROM gate_report_id as gate-report-mismatch, and :432 requires gate_report_id to equal catalog.wirings.gate_report_id. The report identity is DERIVED FROM THE CANDIDATE, NEVER MINTED BY THE COMMAND, and the reservation is per-candidate. Everything downstream - command_hash, retry convergence, the receipt - follows from that. admission_live.rs states it in a comment; no bead carried it.
