title: feat(exec): wire the OCI release reader into host and executor startup
description: *** wamn-0h0g.15.98 LANDED THE READER BUT NOTHING CALLS IT. *** Commit c2f6ce2e added ReleaseManifestSource::pull_verified and ReleaseManifestWeld::load_canonical_bytes in crates/platform/runtime, but the two production call sites still read a FILE: services/executor/src/lib.rs and services/host/src/host.rs both call ReleaseManifestWeld::load_from on a ConfigMap mount. The hunks for those two files were handed to the wave-53 host-config lane and NEVER ARRIVED, so the OCI path is dead code today. This is the half that makes the OCI artifact actually the desired-state source. Exact hunks are recorded in the .15.98 lane report: executor arg block replaces the release-manifest-root arg with an artifact-base plus digest pair, and load becomes async pull_verified then load_canonical_bytes; host.rs is the mirror, and its load_release becomes async.
design: CONFORMANCE CONSTRAINT: tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs:29 counts the raw text ReleaseManifestWeld::load. load_canonical_bytes CONTAINS that substring, so the one-per-process count is preserved by construction - do not rename it to something that does not.
acceptance_criteria: services/executor and services/host construct ReleaseManifestSource from an artifact base plus digest, pull and verify the manifest from OCI, and no longer read a ConfigMap file mount; the runtime_inventory weld-site count still passes.
notes: MEASURED 2026-08-23 at b8b474b6. IMPLEMENTABLE_NOW but TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS ENLARGE IT. (1) *** THE DRAFTED HUNKS ARE INSUFFICIENT: ReleaseManifestSource::new builds its OWN OciClient with NO extra_root_certificates. *** The sibling type says why in its own doc comment at crates/platform/runtime/component_artifact_source.rs:58-75 - a source that builds its own oci-client does NOT receive the process-wide trust roots a host installs through wash_runtime::oci::set_extra_ca_certificates. The reader landed at c2f6ce2e BEFORE .15.155 moved both host manifests onto --oci-ca-path, so ON THE CURRENT POSTURE THE RELEASE PULL FAILS TLS. release_manifest_source.rs must gain a CA-bundle path mirroring component_artifact_source.rs:260-267. (2) The host has NO release at all today - values-host-default.yaml never sets WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_ROOT and mounts no volume, so load_release(None) is the live path. The host YAML is an ADDITION, not a swap. CONFORMANCE CONSTRAINT CONFIRMED HOLDING: RELEASE_WELD_CONSTRUCTION at runtime_inventory.rs:29 is a raw-substring count of ReleaseManifestWeld::load and load_canonical_bytes contains it, so one-per-process survives BY CONSTRUCTION - do not rename to anything not prefixed ReleaseManifestWeld::load. ASYNC RIPPLE: NONE, both run() are already async and each load has one call site; casualties are two sync tests in host.rs and one clap-parse test in executor. DESIGN POINT TO SETTLE IN LANE: host's arg is Option and a base-plus-digest PAIR creates a third state that does not exist today - base present digest absent - so it needs an explicit exactly-one-of-two refusal. MANIFEST LAG: executor.yaml MUST change in the same commit because release_manifest_root is a REQUIRED clap arg, so both skew directions crashloop; mitigating fact, executor.yaml already says NOT APPLIABLE AS CHECKED IN with a 64-zero placeholder, so nothing live breaks. values-host-default.yaml CAN lag. KEEP load_from - tests/integration/src/release_fixture.rs:81 and plugins/flow_http_routing.rs:690 still use the file carrier. SIZE medium, 250-350 lines.
close_reason: Landed at adf26eac (runtime + host + executor) and 72bbc8b5 (both serving manifests). Host and executor now pull the release manifest over OCI at startup, with a mutually-requires-d Option pair so half a release pair refuses to parse. PREMISE CORRECTION: ReleaseManifestSource::new's signature COULD NOT change - crates/platform/runtime/tests/release_manifest_source.rs has four three-argument call sites and is outside the lane's domain - so CA support landed as a with_ca_paths builder with client construction factored into registry_client, rather than a fourth parameter. The bead's own note that the CA gap means TLS failure on the current .15.155 posture was confirmed correct. *** THE END-TO-END LEG IS UNPROVEN AND THE LANE SAID SO RATHER THAN CLAIMING IT. Only the refusal paths are proven, hermetically. *** At the time the lane ran, no release could be minted in any environment, so no real artifact existed to pull. THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE - wamn-cdky and wamn-04m1 landed in the same wave and the mint-to-OCI path is now proven with the registry tag equal to the Postgres manifest_digest. The end-to-end proof is therefore constructible today and is filed as wamn-8yao P1. Three mutants killed by named tests, including removing both requires on the release pair (a_host_given_half_a_release_pair_refuses_to_parse) and reading the executor's release_version from std::env::var instead of the weld (every_production_release_identity_is_read_off_the_weld, whose refusal names the field and the ruling).

title: [SR-MVP] decide(identity): freeze trusted caller-to-AuthorityClass mapping
description: wamn-0h0g.22.8 freezes four exact AuthorityClass values and says class selection belongs only to trusted host composition/operator binding, never a guest. Source-check at df4d12b9 finds one WamnPostgres instance serving materially different production call sites: tenant wamn:postgres imports, executor claim/reap and wiring-resolution queries, callable-HTTP effect authorization/snapshots, and the built-in event materializer. The issue does not freeze the caller-to-class projection or the trusted discriminator that distinguishes the materializer's SQL from an ordinary tenant guest import. Choosing that mapping in implementation would mint authority policy silently. Freeze the exact production mapping and the host-owned discriminator carried into every checkout; guest configuration, component-returned data, and caller-supplied strings must not select or override it.
design: Recommended mapping: tenant component wamn:postgres imports -> guest-sql; executor run-state/catalog operations and wiring doorbell/listener -> executor-platform; connection HTTP authorization/effect snapshot operations -> callable-http; materializer-owned event consumption/admission SQL -> event-materializer. The owner must also choose where the materializer distinction is minted: an explicit trusted construction/binding parameter is preferred over component name or guest configuration. Every provider lookup, pool/cache key, direct connect, and listener identity then carries (project, authority_class, generation) unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: The exact trusted production call-site projection onto guest-sql, executor-platform, callable-http, and event-materializer is frozen; the materializer discriminator is host-owned and unforgeable by tenant code; fallback/default-class behavior is forbidden; wamn-0h0g.22.8 depends on this ruling before modifying provider and pool keys.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-23 — APPROVED ON SHAPE; PROPOSED ROWS VERIFIED; RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. Invariant 1: every AuthorityClass maps to exactly one stable role family; no class fans across families. Invariant 2: the mapping is closed and total over the exact enum; every variant is matched explicitly, no wildcard or default arm exists, and an added or unmapped class is a compile error rather than a runtime fallback. The proposed rows satisfy that shape: guest-sql -> wamn_app; executor-platform -> wamn_executor_platform; callable-http -> wamn_http_admitter; event-materializer -> wamn_event_materializer. The trusted call-site projection remains tenant wamn:postgres -> guest-sql, executor run-state/catalog and wiring listener -> executor-platform, connection-HTTP authority/effect snapshot -> callable-http, and materializer-owned event work -> event-materializer. The materializer discriminator is minted only by an explicit host-owned construction or binding parameter. If implementation discovers any row needs two families, that row returns as its own owner question. IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — NOT STARTED: wamn-0h0g.22.8 encodes the exhaustive match and carries project, class, and generation unchanged through provider, pool, direct-connect, and listener identity.
BINDING RULE ADDED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-24, arising from wamn-0h0g.22.8's question two. This bead is
closed; the rule is recorded here because .22.8 asked whether .22.14's host-owned unforgeable requirement
can be met by localResources.config, and the answer constrains .22.14's own contract.

THE RULE: localResources.config is host-WRITTEN at deploy - operator and template owned, guest-readable
and not guest-writable. It satisfies host-owned and unforgeable IF AND ONLY IF THE HOST BINDS THE CLASS
DISCRIMINATOR AT WORKLOAD-BIND TIME AND REFUSES RUNTIME MUTATION. The guest never supplies the
discriminator; it arrives with pod identity.

TRIPWIRE: if the config path turns out to be guest-writable, the discriminator MOVES HOST-SIDE and this
rule is void. Verify writability against the actual on_workload_item_bind path before relying on it.

No scope, priority or acceptance change to this bead. Recorded so a later reader does not re-derive the
contradiction .22.8 surfaced.

title: [SR-MVP] decide(provision): freeze bounded management-admitter generation prefix
description: Implementation of wamn-0h0g.12.118 measured a PostgreSQL identifier-cap contradiction after the approved seventh-family ruling. The generic generation identity is <family-prefix>_<40-hex-scope-hash>_<a|b>. Reusing the stable ACL role name wamn_management_admitter as the family prefix produces a 67-byte identifier, but PostgreSQL identifiers are capped at 63 bytes. Truncation is inadmissible because it makes the persisted login identity implicit and can collapse future names. The owner must freeze an explicit generation prefix of at most 19 bytes while leaving the stable ACL role exactly wamn_management_admitter and retaining the 160-bit scope hash. The recommended prefix is wamn_mgmt_admitter, producing a 61-byte generation name. The six pre-existing family identities must remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
design: Recommended ruling: add a closed generation_prefix() projection on WorkloadRoleFamily. It equals acl_role() for the six existing families and is exactly wamn_mgmt_admitter for ManagementAdmitter. acl_role() remains wamn_management_admitter. workload_generation_role and generation-member validation consume generation_prefix(); scope hashing, A/B suffixes, grants, and memberships remain unchanged. Record the <=19-byte prefix bound and freeze a known project-environment generation literal.
acceptance_criteria: Owner freezes the exact ManagementAdmitter generation prefix at 19 bytes or fewer; stable ACL role remains exactly wamn_management_admitter; the 40-hex (160-bit) scope digest and _a/_b suffix remain unchanged; all six prior generation identities remain byte-for-byte unchanged; wamn-0h0g.12.118 depends on this decision before its derived-name proof can complete.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-23 — APPROVED; RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. ManagementAdmitter generation_prefix is exactly wamn_mgmt_admitter. The stable ACL role remains exactly wamn_management_admitter. The full generation form wamn_mgmt_admitter_<40-hex-scope-hash>_<a|b> is 61 bytes, below PostgreSQL 63; project-environment scope is inside the fixed 40-hex digest, so no unbounded environment text is appended. The six prior family identities remain byte-for-byte frozen. IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — NOT STARTED: wamn-0h0g.12.118 consumes this prefix through the existing generic lifecycle and adds the exact derived-name bound proof.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23 in commit 2616150b as part of wamn-0h0g.12.118, exactly as this ruling designated. MANAGEMENT_ADMITTER_GENERATION_PREFIX is wamn_mgmt_admitter, consumed by workload_generation_role and by ctl is_workload_generation_role. Frozen derived-name proof asserts wamn_mgmt_admitter_c1e0f3849ce98895f9593009bc5f60e870150758_a at exactly 61 bytes. RULING CORRECTION MEASURED AT IMPLEMENTATION: the acceptance criteria state a universal 19-byte-or-fewer prefix bound, and that is WRONG - wamn_dispatch_reader is 20 bytes and yields exactly 63, which fits. title: [SR-MVP] feat(auth): DB-enforce the closed run-queue authority matrix
description: Database-enforce the closed run-queue operation matrix for executor-platform claim and reap, private management admission, ordinary callable HTTP admission, and event-materializer admission. design: Use ordinary role-specific SQL statements plus database guards keyed only to current_user, so producer kind is a non-settable grant fact rather than caller input. SECURITY DEFINER remains rejected. Cross-class attempts fail with SQLSTATE 42501 and stable class-specific messages. The matrix is closed: adding a class or operation requires code and schema change plus a new refusal arm. Test-local restrictive roles prove the complete matrix now without creating production role lifecycle; provisioning fragments later mint the same shaped principals. wamn_app loses queue authority immediately. Any breakage identifies a mis-homed caller and is repaired at that caller, not preserved through compatibility grants.
acceptance_criteria: The matrix names exactly executor-platform, management-admission, callable-http, and event-materializer. Executor-platform receives only the measured queue claim and reap SELECT, row-lock, UPDATE, and DELETE operations; each producer receives only its own guarded admission INSERT statement. Every database guard derives authority from current_user and no caller-supplied producer kind can confer it. A direct SQL attempt by any role to execute any other class operation fails with SQLSTATE 42501 and the frozen class-specific message. Pairwise PostgreSQL tests use restrictive test-local principals to cover every ordered cross-role denial plus positive controls for each exact production statement. Forging producer kind, supplying another class fields, calling another statement, or bypassing the Rust API cannot cross the matrix. wamn_app has no run-queue grant or statement authority after this cutover; exposed callers are treated as mis-homed defects. Named mutants that collapse two statements, trust a producer parameter, remove one current_user guard or pairwise denial, restore a shared or wamn_app grant, change a refusal code or message, or widen one role fail named static and PostgreSQL gates. title: [SR-MVP] feat(security): dedicated guest-SQL generations and current_user RLS
description: Replace the guest-visible shared wamn_app LOGIN and caller-settable app.tenant boundary with opaque, bounded per-project-environment and tenant LOGIN generations. PostgreSQL current_user supplies the tenant identity used by RLS. A mapping table or caller-settable session indirection is forbidden. Per-credential pools are the consequence of per-tenant roles, not a competing mechanism. The stable wamn_app role remains only as a NOLOGIN ACL grant owner; wamn-0h0g.12.140 owns retiring its runtime LOGIN class.
design:
Extend the shared A/B generation machinery owned by wamn-0h0g.13.59. Each tenant generation inherits the narrowed guest ACL role without SET or ADMIN authority.

ROLE NAMING - CORRECTED 2026-08-26. The earlier text said role naming uses the opaque bounded tenant-key convention. THAT PREMISE IS REFUTED: no such convention existed anywhere in crates/control/provision. The measured reality is the workload SCOPE-DIGEST pattern (workload_role_scope_hash, effect_writer_scope_hash, SCOPE_HASH_HEX_LEN = 40), and the ruling extends it: wamn_guest_ plus a 40-hex digest plus the generation suffix, 53 bytes, inside the 63-byte identifier cap.
Embedding the tenant id verbatim is FORBIDDEN, not merely unchosen: valid_tenant admits 64 bytes, PostgreSQL caps identifiers at 63 and TRUNCATES SILENTLY with a NOTICE, so two long tenants would collapse onto ONE role - a cross-tenant breach wearing a naming bug.

TENANT AUTHORITY - RULED 2026-08-26, option (c). RLS derives the tenant from current_user through wamn.tenant_key(tenant_id), a PURE IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE function: computation, not the forbidden indirection, because the ban targets mutable settable state between identity and authority. Schema-qualified in the predicate, owned by the platform role, EXECUTE to the guest family, and ITS DEFINITION FROZEN BY A pg_get_functiondef DIGEST PROBE.
The expression index rides the same generator that emits the predicate, so sargability moves with the developer surface in one site; hand-written DDL relations get theirs in the same sweep. Index coverage is machine-checked from pg_index on wamn-0h0g.22.15.

The existing SQL blocklist remains defense in depth. This issue inherits the connection-multiplication ledger item: per-tenant credentials imply per-credential pools, and the recorded pooler tripwire fires as tenant count grows.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning deterministically issues per-project-environment and tenant A/B guest LOGIN generations and selects exactly one active Secret while permitting bounded overlap. Each generation is LOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE, NOREPLICATION, NOBYPASSRLS, owns nothing, and can inherit only the stable NOLOGIN guest ACL role with SET false and ADMIN false. Every governed tenant RLS predicate derives authority from current_user and contains no app.tenant, current_setting tenant predicate, mapping-table indirection, or caller-writable equivalent. The guest pool refuses wrong session_user, current_user, database, tenant binding, membership, or ACL. Positive live controls prove only documented entity CRUD and required row-event behavior; cross-tenant access, platform bookkeeping, admission, retention, dynamic SET or RESET, set_config, SET ROLE, search-path, and qualified-name attacks refuse. Named mutants restoring a GUC predicate, shared wamn_app LOGIN, SET membership, missing tenant identity, or an excess bookkeeping grant fail. No component receives a database URL, no raw-SQL enablement lands, and wamn_app retirement remains owned by wamn-0h0g.12.140.
notes:
SPLIT ORIGIN: wamn-0h0g.22.4. OPEN, UNCLAIMED, POST-MERGE; implementation not started. Do not claim or implement until wamn-0h0g.12.68 and wamn-0h0g.15.173 are complete, the wamn-0h0g.15.25 RC is green, and that RC is merged into mvp. This is the sole successor for the guest-SQL and non-rewritable-RLS scope formerly duplicated by wamn-1nd; reciprocal transfer and supersession must leave only this owner.
SEQUENCING SUPERSESSION 2026-08-21 — Earlier POST-MERGE / wait-for-wamn-0h0g.15.25 text is superseded by the owner's active rule: all scope-reduction and authority work lands before the single final RC and merge. This issue no longer waits on .15.25; .15.25 waits on it. Scope, priority, acceptance, and product semantics are unchanged.
MEASURED 2026-08-26 at 2e22da39, BEFORE any implementation. Two findings: the scope is larger than the bead implies, and the bead's naming premise does not exist.

SCOPE, MEASURED. 94 current_setting('app.tenant') predicates across five DDL files, PLUS one generator:
  catalog-schema.sql   49 predicates, 26 grants to wamn_app
  app-schema.sql       15 predicates,  8 grants
  postgres-init.sql    15 predicates, 11 grants
  run-state.sql        12 predicates,  6 grants
  run-queue.sql         3 predicates,  0 grants  <- the only file the guest ACL role cannot reach
  crates/schema/compiler/src/emit.rs - THE LEVERAGE POINT. One function emits the permissive tenant floor for EVERY generated entity table: CREATE POLICY {t}_tenant USING (tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant', true), '')) plus GRANT SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE TO wamn_app. Re-keying this one site moves every generated developer table at once.
So 91 of the 94 sit on relations the guest ACL role holds grants on. This is not a narrow change.

DISTINCT POPULATION, NOT IN SCOPE: crates/schema/compiler/src/rls/ emits RESTRICTIVE per-role and per-user policies keyed on app.role and app.user_id, layered INSIDE the tenant floor. Those are a different claim class; this bead's acceptance names the TENANT predicate.

*** THE BEAD'S NAMING PREMISE DOES NOT EXIST. *** The design says role naming uses the opaque bounded tenant-key convention. There IS NO SUCH CONVENTION: no tenant_key anywhere in crates/control/provision, and name.rs carries no tenant-key function. What DOES exist is the workload scope-digest convention - workload_role_scope_hash and effect_writer_scope_hash produce a 160-bit digest at SCOPE_HASH_HEX_LEN = 40 hex characters. That is the pattern to extend, but extending it is a decision, not a lookup.

*** AND THE OBVIOUS OPTION IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. *** Putting the tenant id verbatim into the role name CANNOT WORK: valid_tenant admits up to 64 BYTES (identifiers.rs), PostgreSQL caps identifiers at 63, and it TRUNCATES an over-long identifier with a NOTICE rather than refusing - so two long tenants would silently collapse onto ONE role, which is a cross-tenant breach rather than an error. A bounded digest is therefore forced. With a 40-hex digest: wamn_guest_ (11) + 40 + _a (2) = 53 bytes, which fits.

WHAT REMAINS AN OWNER DECISION: how the RLS predicate recovers the tenant from current_user, given that a mapping table and caller-settable indirection are both forbidden. Options are on the report to the owner; both live ones apply to all 91 predicates and the generator, so the choice is load-bearing across the whole construction and the rule-7 split shape depends on it. NOT STARTED.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-26: OPTION (c) - A PURE IMMUTABLE FUNCTION.

THE BAN IS ON MUTABLE SETTABLE STATE BETWEEN IDENTITY AND AUTHORITY - mapping tables anyone can write, GUCs anyone can set. wamn.tenant_key(tenant_id) is a fixed derivation with no writer, no state and nothing to hijack: computation, not the forbidden indirection. Refusing it would ban sha256 as a lookup.
(b) IS REFUTED BY ITS OWN COST LINE: a derived-duplicate column on 91 relations that could drift if anything writes it directly mints a NEW INTEGRITY INVARIANT, plus backfill, plus a generator change, purely to avoid an expression index. Buying state to avoid computation is backwards.
(a) REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT (silent identifier truncation). (d) contradicts the ruled design and the topology ruling both.

THE SARGABILITY CLIFF IS SOLVED BY THE SAME LEVERAGE THE MEASUREMENT FOUND: the expression index RIDES THE GENERATOR. emit.rs emits the predicate AND CREATE INDEX ... ((wamn.tenant_key(tenant_id))) per governed entity table, so one site moves the whole developer surface. The hand-written DDL relations get theirs in the SAME SWEEP.

NEW DENIAL-GATE ARM, on wamn-0h0g.22.15: EVERY RELATION CARRYING THE GUEST PREDICATE HAS ITS EXPRESSION INDEX, machine-checked from pg_index. The cliff becomes structurally unreachable rather than remembered.

RIDERS, BINDING:
  - The function is IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE, SCHEMA-QUALIFIED in the predicate, owned by the platform role, EXECUTE granted to the guest family.
  - *** ITS DEFINITION IS FROZEN BY PROBE: a digest of pg_get_functiondef is pinned. *** An attacker who can redefine the function owns every predicate. This is the ONE NEW DENIAL the design needs.
  - ROLE NAMING adopts the measured reality: the scope-digest pattern extended - wamn_guest_ plus a 40-hex digest plus the generation suffix, 53 bytes. The bead's phantom opaque bounded tenant-key convention is corrected in the body with the naming premise cited as refuted.
  - The truncation finding becomes a STANDING HAZARD CLASS in the item-2 build notes: PostgreSQL identifier truncation is silent, so any future name embedding tenant-controlled length refuses at mint if >= 64 bytes. This stops (a)'s breach-wearing-a-naming-bug being reinvented by a later convenience.
RULE-7 SPLIT EXECUTED 2026-08-26, shape determined by the option (c) ruling:
  .22.6.1  wamn.tenant_key plus its frozen-definition probe - FOUNDATION, the other three depend on it
  .22.6.2  the generator: emit.rs emits the current_user predicate AND the expression index per generated entity table
  .22.6.3  the hand-written sweep: the guest-reachable subset of the 94 predicates, each with its expression index
  .22.6.4  per-tenant guest LOGIN generations, digest equal to what tenant_key returns
Plus the index-coverage arm on wamn-0h0g.22.15.

THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN AS THE CONSTRUCTION CONTAINER, exactly as wamn-0h0g.22.8 did. It blocks seven beads including the RC; closing it would force repointing all of those onto a terminal child, which is churn that buys nothing and reads as four doors. It closes when its children do.
ONE LANE, four commits, one proof pass - proven once governs the EVENT, not the internal shape of the proof.

*** THE TWO HALVES MUST AGREE OR EVERY GUEST READ REFUSES: *** .22.6.1's function and .22.6.4's role name must produce THE SAME 40-hex digest. That is the single sharpest failure mode in this construction, and it is why the function lands first.
OBSERVATION FOR THE OWNER, found while designing .22.6.1 - NOT acted on, and not this bead's scope.

THE CONTROL-AUTHOR PATH ALREADY USES THE SHAPE THIS BEAD'S RULING REJECTS. control-portable-store.sql creates wamn_authority.author_login_tenants, a MAPPING TABLE, and wamn_authority.session_author_tenant() reads it. Control-author RLS policies then read tenant_id = wamn_authority.session_author_tenant().

The owner ruling of 2026-08-26 rejects mapping tables for the guest path on the principle that the ban targets MUTABLE SETTABLE STATE BETWEEN IDENTITY AND AUTHORITY - a table anyone with write access can alter. That argument is about the shape, not about who is using it, so on its face it applies to the author path too.

TWO DIFFERENCES THAT MAY OR MAY NOT MATTER, for the owner to weigh rather than for a lane to assume:
  - The author path is control-plane and its principals are authors, not tenant guest code, so the threat model is different in degree.
  - session_author_tenant() READS A TABLE, so it cannot be IMMUTABLE and cannot be indexed the way wamn.tenant_key can. Converting it would be a real change, not a rename.

Raised because the same principle produced a strong ruling here, and leaving the contradiction unrecorded would let it read as settled when nobody has looked at it. Not filed as a bead: it is one question, and the owner may rule it out of scope for the MVP in one line.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): retire the shared wamn_app runtime login and prove it dead

OWNER RULING 2026-08-19 -- RE-SCOPED. DO NOT ROTATE NOW. Rotate THROUGH the generation-family extension when that lands.

*** DELIBERATE ACCEPTANCE, DATED, WITH A TRIPWIRE: measured exposure on frozen non-production infrastructure, accepted for the extension's duration by owner ruling 2026-08-19. REVISIT TRIGGER: any promotion of these clusters toward real tenant data, or any unfreeze. ***

The ruling directs a HARD DEPENDENCY on the bead for extending the A/B generation family to APP_ROLE, described as already filed as multitenancy Finding 1 with scope per-env generations, CONNECT confinement and probe flips. I could not locate it. Searched bd for: generation family, multitenancy, per-env generation, CONNECT confinement, extend the generation, app role generation, Finding 1 -- all returned nothing. That bead, once identified, gains ROTATION OF THE MEASURED-EXPOSED VALUE AS A NAMED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION -- the extension is not done until the known credential is dead through it, downtime-free, with probes asserting the new generation.

CURRENT EDGE: this bead depends on wamn-0h0g.12.129 (the required-arg fix that kills the minting path). The generation-extension edge is still owed.
THE VERIFIER INSTRUMENT, BANKED AS A RECIPE. The 2026-08-19 script lived in a SESSION-SCOPED scratchpad and is GONE; a note in the now-closed wamn-0h0g.12.139 points at that path and is therefore a dead reference -- recorded here so the same false-reference class I flagged twice this session does not bite this bead. Everything needed to rebuild it in ~20 lines:

WHAT IT DOES. Tests whether a candidate password matches a role's STORED verifier WITHOUT authenticating. No login attempt, no auth-log entry, no write, no DDL. Safe against a frozen cluster.

VERIFIER FORMAT in pg_authid.rolpassword:
  SCRAM-SHA-256$<iters>:<salt_b64>$<StoredKey_b64>:<ServerKey_b64>
ARITHMETIC:
  SaltedPassword = PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(password, salt, iters, dklen=32)
  ClientKey      = HMAC-SHA256(SaltedPassword, 'Client Key')
  StoredKey      = SHA256(ClientKey)
  match iff StoredKey == the stored StoredKey
In Python: hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', pw.encode(), salt, iters, 32), then hmac.new(salted, b'Client Key', hashlib.sha256).digest(), then hashlib.sha256(client_key).digest().

*** ALWAYS RUN THE POSITIVE CONTROL FIRST, BEFORE TOUCHING ANY LIVE VERIFIER. *** Without it a no-match is indistinguishable from broken arithmetic. RFC 7677 test vector:
  password    pencil
  salt_b64    W22ZaJ0SNY7soEsUEjb6gQ==
  iterations  4096
  StoredKey   WG5d8oPm3OtcPnkdi4Uo7BkeZkBFzpcXkuLmtbsT4qY=
If that does not reproduce, STOP -- every result after it is meaningless.

HARVEST (read-only, per cluster, via kubectl exec):
  psql -U postgres -tAF'\t' -c "SELECT rolname, rolpassword FROM pg_authid WHERE rolcanlogin AND rolpassword IS NOT NULL ORDER BY rolname"
Clusters as of 2026-08-19: wamn-pg (pod wamn-pg-1), wamn-sysdb (pod wamn-sysdb-2), and the fixture Deployment pod postgres-* -- all in namespace wamn-system. 11 login roles carried verifiers.

DISCIPLINE THAT MADE THE 2026-08-19 RUN CLEAN: extract the candidate PROGRAMMATICALLY from source rather than typing it, never echo it, and print only per-role match / no-match. Report per-cluster, because a mixed result is live information -- one cluster provisioned by hand and two by tree is a different remediation than three of three.

CLOSING CRITERION FOR THIS BEAD: re-run this instrument after the rotation and get no-match on every role for the OLD value, plus probes asserting the new generation.
DEPENDENCY EDGE CREATED 2026-08-19: this bead now DEPENDS ON wamn-0h0g.13.59, the APP_ROLE generation-family extension, filed the same day at owner direction as the 'multitenancy Finding 1' record that could not be found. The edge the owner asked for on 2026-08-19 is now real; the blocker is no longer prose-only and this bead will correctly stay out of bd ready until the machinery exists.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER, SURFACED NOT RESOLVED: .13.59 was filed P1 while this bead is P0. The owner's acceptance ruling ties them -- the exposure is accepted 'for the extension's duration' -- so the extension's priority is what actually governs how long the accepted window runs. If the window should be short, .13.59 is the bead whose priority needs to say so, not this one.
=====================================================================
OWNER RULING, 2026-08-19 (dkk) -- THE ACCEPTED-EXPOSURE WINDOW GAINS A
TIME TRIGGER. RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.
Companion ruling on wamn-0h0g.13.59; read both together.
=====================================================================

CONTEXT. R4's acceptance for this exposure runs "through the extension", i.e.
through wamn-0h0g.13.59, which BLOCKS this bead. It was put to the owner that
.13.59 should therefore inherit P0. THAT WAS OVERRULED.

THE PRINCIPLE: "priority prices risk; it does not inherit through dependency
edges." Inheriting would make every P0's transitive closure P0, "which is how P0
queues inflate until the label prices nothing." wamn-0h0g.13.59 STAYS P1.

THE HAZARD THE OWNER CONCEDED, AND WHAT CLOSES IT:
"an accepted window with no clock quietly becomes indefinite through inattention
-- THE FADE-NOT-DECISION FAILURE. The tripwires we set are EVENT-triggered
(promotion toward tenant data, unfreeze); WHAT'S MISSING IS THE TIME TRIGGER."

THEREFORE, IN FORCE ON THIS BEAD:
 1. The EVENT tripwires already recorded stay exactly as they are -- any
    promotion toward real tenant data, or any unfreeze of the cluster.
 2. A DATED REVIEW is added. At that date, one of two things happens and both
    are decisions, not drift:
      - RE-AFFIRM the acceptance against THEN-CURRENT facts, or
      - ESCALATE wamn-0h0g.13.59 ON EVIDENCE.
 3. ESCALATION TRIGGER, RULED: "If the review date arrives and the extension
    hasn't moved, THAT -- a lapsed window, not an edge -- is the legitimate
    escalation trigger."

Owner on what this buys: "That converts 'accepted through the extension' from an
open-ended clause into a bounded one ... NOT A BIGGER LABEL, A SHORTER LEASH."

=====================================================================
*** OPEN: THE REVIEW DATE IS NOT YET NAMED. ***
Asked of the owner 2026-08-19. Until a date is recorded here, item 2 is NOT
SATISFIED and this window is still uncloked -- which is precisely the failure
mode the ruling exists to prevent. DO NOT LET THIS SIT.
=====================================================================

STANDING CONSTRAINT, UNCHANGED AND RESTATED BECAUSE IT IS EASY TO BREACH WHILE
WRITING ABOUT THIS BEAD: the candidate credential string MUST NEVER land in bead
text or logs. Cite it as "the documented default at provisioning.md:79".

=====================================================================
*** CORRECTION TO THE RULING RECORDED ABOVE, SAME DAY, 2026-08-19. ***
ITEM 2 (THE DATED REVIEW) IS WITHDRAWN BY THE OWNER.
=====================================================================

Owner, asked to name the review date: "i dont want a dated review".

THEREFORE THE NOTE ABOVE IS SUPERSEDED IN EXACTLY ONE RESPECT. Read it with this
correction applied:

 - ITEM 2 (a dated review at which the acceptance is re-affirmed or .13.59 is
   escalated) DOES NOT EXIST. Do not add one. Do not treat its absence as an
   oversight to be tidied up later -- it was proposed, considered, and declined.

 - ITEM 3, the escalation trigger, LOSES ITS TRIGGER. It read: "if the review
   date arrives and the extension hasn't moved, that -- a lapsed window, not an
   edge -- is the legitimate escalation trigger." With no date, nothing can lapse,
   so this clause is inert. It stands only as a description of what WOULD have
   escalated.

WHAT REMAINS IN FORCE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE CONTROL:
 - The EVENT tripwires, unchanged and undiminished: any promotion toward real
   tenant data, and any unfreeze of the cluster.
 - wamn-0h0g.13.59 stays P1, on the ruled principle that priority prices risk and
   does not inherit through dependency edges.

STATED PLAINLY FOR THE RECORD, BECAUSE AN HONEST LEDGER IS THE POINT: this window
is now EVENT-TRIGGERED ONLY. The fade-not-decision hazard the owner named in the
same ruling -- "an accepted window with no clock quietly becomes indefinite
through inattention" -- is therefore ACCEPTED, not closed. That is the owner's
call to make and it is made. It is recorded here so that a future reader finds a
decision rather than an omission.

The exposure's underlying facts are unchanged and continue to justify it: frozen
NON-PRODUCTION infra, the minting path already dead (.12.139 landed), threat
population = whoever already owns the local cluster.

It removes wamn_app run-queue mutation and banks the converged evidence into the single wave-end regeneration; no finalizer bead duplicates that ownership. title: remediate(auth): --app-password defaults to a known static string on the LOGIN app role, and the docs teach the default
description:
SIBLING OF wamn-0h0g.12.134, FOUND WHILE VERIFYING WAVE-6 STATE 2026-08-19. Same mechanism, different role, and a materially WORSE blast radius.

THREE call sites carry a static default credential; .12.134 filed only the first:
  services/ctl/src/enable_cdc_project_env.rs:82  --replication-password default wamn_cdc  -> .12.134
  services/ctl/src/provision.rs:49               --app-password default wamn_app          -> UNFILED until now
  services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs:126  --app-password default wamn_app          -> UNFILED until now

Both app-password sites flow to crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs:28 ensure_app_role_sql, which emits CREATE ROLE wamn_app LOGIN PASSWORD <literal> NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOBYPASSRLS. So the default mints a LOGIN role whose password is the role name.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN .12.134, not equal to it:
 (1) .12.134's live blast radius was MEASURED EMPTY on 2026-08-19 — no login role on any of the three clusters carries the password wamn_cdc. No such measurement exists for wamn_app, and wamn_app is the shared application role the entire K-epic confinement program is about narrowing.
 (2) NOTHING IN deploy/ EVER SETS IT. Repo-wide, --app-password / WAMN_APP_PASSWORD appears in exactly two places outside the arg definitions: deploy/mvp/tests/bootstrap.sh:472 (a test sentinel) and docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79. So no production manifest overrides the default.
 (3) THE DOCUMENTATION TEACHES THE DEFAULT AS CORRECT. provisioning.md:79 reads: Password for the shared wamn_app role (default wamn_app, matching the hand-written schemas). The default is not an oversight — it is documented, and the checked-in SQL schemas are built around it. That makes this the doc-comment-as-mechanism class again, except here the doc is accurate and the DESIGN is the defect.

THE REMEDY TEMPLATE IS ALREADY IN THE SAME STRUCT. provision_project_env.rs:137 declares --dispatch-reader-password with NO default_value at all (the wamn-0h0g.12.122 required-arg shape), eleven lines below the --app-password on line 126 that does have one. One file, two credentials, two opposite policies.

OPEN: whether this rides .12.134's remedy ruling (required-arg vs generate-when-absent) or takes its own; and whether the live wamn_app role actually carries the literal password, which is answerable read-only by the same SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier arithmetic used for wamn_cdc — PBKDF2 the candidate against each role's stored verifier, no login attempt. NOT YET AUTHORIZED, NOT YET RUN.
notes:
FILED DURING WAVE-6 STEP-0 VERIFICATION, NOT DURING IMPLEMENTATION. Nothing has been edited. Priority set P0 provisionally BECAUSE the live value is unmeasured and the role is the shared app role; if the cluster read shows the live password is not the literal wamn_app, this drops to P1 and becomes a hardening bead rather than an exposure. If it IS the literal, the rotation question is live and belongs to its own bead.

DO NOT ASSUME THE .12.134 EVIDENCE TRANSFERS. The empty-blast-radius finding there was specific to the candidate string wamn_cdc.
VERIFIER READ EXECUTED 2026-08-19, OWNER-AUTHORIZED, READ-ONLY. *** RESULT: LIVE EXPOSURE CONFIRMED. R4 FIRES. ***

METHOD. SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier arithmetic against pg_authid, NOT authentication: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(candidate, salt, iters) -> ClientKey -> StoredKey, compared to the stored verifier. No login attempt, no auth-log entry, no write, no DDL. The frozen cluster was not modified. The candidate was extracted programmatically from services/ctl/src/provision.rs:49 and never typed or echoed; it is cited here only as THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT AT docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79.

POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED FIRST. The RFC 7677 SCRAM-SHA-256 test vector was computed before any live verifier was touched and reproduced its published StoredKey exactly. A no-match in this run therefore means no-match, not a broken instrument. Script retained at scratchpad/scram_check.py.

PER-CLUSTER FACTS, 11 LOGIN roles with verifiers across 3 clusters:
  wamn-pg    wamn_app                        *** MATCH ***
  wamn-pg    app / postgres / wamn_system    no-match
  fixture    wamn_app                        *** MATCH ***
  fixture    postgres / wamn_author_acme_receiving_dev / wamn_cdc_rie__app__dev   no-match
  wamn-sysdb postgres / wamn_scenario_worker_identity / wamn_system               no-match
             (wamn-sysdb has NO wamn_app role at all)

*** THE RATIO THAT MATTERS IS NOT 2 OF 3 CLUSTERS. IT IS 2 OF 2 -- EVERY CLUSTER ON WHICH THE ROLE EXISTS CARRIES THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT. Nothing, anywhere, in any environment, ever overrode it. That is the predicted consequence of the tree-side finding that no manifest in deploy/ sets the flag or the env var, and it is now measured rather than inferred. ***

CONFIRMED AS A SIDE FACT: wamn_cdc_rie__app__dev does NOT carry the CDC default -- independently reproducing wamn-0h0g.12.134's empty-blast-radius finding with a controlled instrument. The two roles genuinely differ; the evidence did not transfer, exactly as ruled.

SEVERITY STAYS P0. This is an active exposure, not a hardening item: a LOGIN role whose password is its own name, on the shared application role the entire K-epic confinement program exists to narrow.

ROTATION IS OWED AND IS **NOT** DONE. See the blocker recorded separately -- the owner's ruling routed rotation through the wamn-0h0g.13.31 generation machinery, and whether that machinery covers wamn_app today is a premise that must be checked before any credential is changed on a FROZEN cluster. NO CREDENTIAL HAS BEEN CHANGED.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-19 — REMEDY IS A REQUIRED ARG, NO DEFAULT. RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. Lane 3 has NOT started.

THE RULING. Delete default_value from all three call sites; the env var stays so deployment supplies it. The evidence is eleven lines of one struct: services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs:126 declares --app-password WITH a default (the defect) and :137 declares --dispatch-reader-password with NO default at all (the cure, the wamn-0h0g.12.122 shape the plan pre-ruled as the remedy template). This is not choosing a policy; it is FINISHING one already chosen, at the two call sites that predate it plus the one that copied the old line.
FAILURE-MODE ASYMMETRY, stated as the security argument: a required arg fails loudly at provision time, in the operator terminal, once. A default fails silently, in every environment nobody overrode, forever. The verifier read has now MEASURED what forever looks like — see wamn-0h0g.12.139 and .12.140.

OPTION 2 REFUSED BY NAME. Mint-when-absent looks friendlier and is the trap: it converts a loud misconfiguration into a silent credential-custody problem — the generated secret must then be captured, stored and threaded to every consumer, or the environment provisions green and fails later, elsewhere, as an auth error nobody connects to the provisioning run. That invents a secrets-management obligation at the CLI layer when the platform already has exactly one blessed shape for machine-minted credentials: the wamn-0h0g.13.31 A/B generation family (provisioner mints, Secret carries, wrapper rotates, probes assert). If auto-generation is ever wanted for the app role it arrives as EXTEND THE GENERATION FAMILY, already filed as multitenancy Finding 1 — not as ring SystemRandom sprayed at a flag default. THE ring IMPORT AT provision_project_env.rs:66 BEING RIGHT THERE IS TEMPTATION, NOT PRECEDENT.
OPTION 3 REFUSED: a fixture carve-out solves a problem the test infrastructure does not have — fixtures pass explicit throwaway strings and the live suites construct their own roles, so the genuinely-needs-a-default set is EMPTY, and a mixed policy with an empty exception class is the uniform policy wearing a loophole for the next copy-paste to find.

RIDERS ON THE LANDING, all owner-specified:
 - ALL THREE SITES IN ONE COMMIT. The defect is one pattern; this is the R12 singular-defect reading from .20.9 applied verbatim.
 - docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79 REWRITES IN THE SAME COMMIT, from defaults-to-X to required, supplied via the env var. That doc line was the exposure's own citation, so it dies WITH the exposure rather than surviving as a stale instruction. NOTE: provisioning.md is under docs/archive but is NOT one of the integrator-reserved files, so the lane may edit it — confirm at integration.
 - THE ERROR PATH GETS ONE HONEST TOUCH: the missing-arg failure names the ENV VAR, not just the flag, because deployment supplies it that way.
 - bootstrap scripts and any runbook invocation gain the explicit args in the same sweep — grep the three flag names.
 - SEQUENCING UNCHANGED: this remedy lands under the clause transferred from R28; rotation of the measured-exposed value rides wamn-0h0g.12.140 per the verifier read; R28's narrowed posture half is untouched.

RECIPROCAL CITE, per the transfer ruling: THIS BEAD'S ORIGIN IS FINDING R28 / wamn-2jkm.46, ARC8 EVIDENCE 2026-07-23, whose static-default-credential clause was transferred here on 2026-08-19 under the two-owners rule. Severity archaeology continues there.
CREDENTIAL-HYGIENE CORRECTION 2026-08-19. This bead was filed BEFORE the owner instruction that the candidate string must never land in bead text or logs, and it stated the value outright. The title has been amended and all subsequent notes cite it only as THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT AT docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79.

THE TENSION IS WORTH STATING RATHER THAN HIDING, because it is load-bearing for how this bead reads: THE DEFAULT PASSWORD IS THE ROLE NAME. So the value cannot be fully scrubbed without making the defect undescribable — naming the role at all discloses it. That identity is not incidental, it IS the finding. Anyone reading this bead should understand the hygiene rule here can only be honored in form, and treat the remaining role references accordingly. The original description text may still carry the older phrasing.

Practical consequence: the value is already public in the source tree (services/ctl/src/provision.rs:49, provision_project_env.rs:126) and in committed documentation (provisioning.md:79), so the tracker is not the disclosing surface. It is still worth not adding another copy on a separately-synced remote.
close_reason:
DUPLICATE of wamn-0h0g.12.129, which was filed 2026-08-18 and is open. My error: I filed this on 2026-08-19 during wave-6 step-0 verification WITHOUT SEARCHING THE TRACKER FIRST, having found the defect independently by grepping default_value across the tree. wamn-0h0g.12.122's close reason names .12.129 explicitly ('The adjacent --app-password default defect was filed separately as wamn-0h0g.12.129, not folded in') -- a single bd search would have found it.

ALL UNIQUE CONTENT HAS BEEN MIGRATED to .12.129 before closing: (a) the third call site services/ctl/src/provision.rs:49, which .12.129 does not name; (b) the owner-authorized verifier read of 2026-08-19 proving 2-of-2 live exposure with an RFC 7677 positive control; (c) the owner's required-arg remedy ruling with all riders; (d) the credential-hygiene note. NOTHING WAS LOST.

title: decision(security): the wiring resolution cache is not tenant-scoped — key it before any production driver is wired
description:
## The hazard

crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs keys its Pointer as (environment, wiring_id) ONLY -- verified at :61-65. WiringCache never receives a tenant on ANY entry point: new(max_entries) at :151, get(environment, wiring_id) at :180, insert(...) at :223, invalidate(environment, wiring_id) at :284, invalidate_all() at :315. The only three occurrences of the word tenant in the whole file are prose in comments.

That key is safe if and only if a serving process is fixed to one tenant. IT IS NOT.

## The in-process counterexample

The sibling plugin in the SAME process is keyed per workload bind, not per process: crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_flow_invocation.rs takes tenant, catalog and environment from wamn.tenant / wamn.catalog / wamn.environment workload config (:34-36, :44-45, :106) and holds a RwLock HashMap of registrations by component_id (:179, :197). One wash host process demonstrably serves MANY (tenant, catalog, environment) triples.

So a single shared WiringCache in that process, keyed only by (environment, wiring_id), would serve tenant A's wiring to tenant B whenever two tenants share an environment name and a wiring id. That is a cross-tenant serve, not the benign extra store read the current comments describe.

## Why this is filed separately rather than as a rider

The hazard outlives wamn-0h0g.16.18 and survives its re-sequencing. .16.18 is blocked on two beads that do not exist yet (the catalog-to-router lowering, and host-tier release-root plumbing), so welding this decision to that feature's schedule would hide a tenancy-boundary question inside a deferred feature bead where the security sweep cannot see it.

## What was already done, and what was not

LANDED (doc amendment, this session): the false assertions were replaced with a hazard notice at the three consumer sites -- resolution.rs Pointer, resolution.rs WiringCache, and wiring_doorbell.rs DoorbellScope -- each naming this bead. Those comments previously asserted the OPPOSITE (that a serving process already fixes tenant and catalog), which is how a settled hazard gets re-derived as a surprise.

NOT DONE, and deliberately: no structural guard. The owner's rider asked for a cheap single-tenancy assertion at the construction site if one was available. IT IS NOT AVAILABLE: the cache never receives a tenant at any entry point, so there is no value to assert against, and adding one IS the keying decision this bead owns. Reported rather than forced.

## The decision owed

Key the cache so a cross-tenant serve is structurally unrepresentable. PRESUMPTIVE DIRECTION, not a ruling: key it by the same tuple the sibling plugin already uses, (tenant, catalog, environment), since that is the process's demonstrated unit of isolation. Alternatives include one cache and doorbell per (tenant, catalog) held plugin-style, or adding tenant to Pointer -- note the latter reopens two include_str! pins on resolution.rs (crates/execution/run-state/tests/shelving_contract.rs ROUTER_SOURCES and crates/execution/router/tests/resolution.rs:353) plus the metric-name substring pins.

## Blocking condition

THIS BLOCKS WIRING ANY PRODUCTION DRIVER AGAINST THE RESOLUTION CACHE -- wamn-0h0g.16.18 or any successor. Stated structurally: no production process may construct a WiringCache until the keying is ruled. Today nothing does, which is the only reason this is a latent hazard rather than a live incident.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling is recorded naming the cache's key and the isolation unit it enforces. The hazard notices at the three consumer sites are replaced by a description of the ruled behaviour. Any production construction of WiringCache is gated on this bead being closed.
notes:
DOC HALF LANDED at commit 733ea4ce on deploy-simplification (docs(wamn-0h0g.12.138)), per the owner's split of this finding into a today-defect and a decision.

Three blocks now state the hazard and name this bead as the owner of the keying decision: crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs Pointer, resolution.rs WiringCache, and crates/platform/runtime/src/wiring_doorbell.rs DoorbellScope. Each says plainly that no production driver may be wired against the path until this bead is ruled. Zero design commitment -- which key is correct is THIS bead's to decide.

THE RIDER'S GUARD WAS NOT LANDED, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, NOT RELUCTANCE. The ruling asked for a cheap single-tenancy assertion at the construction site IF one was available. It is not: WiringCache receives no tenant at any entry point -- new(max_entries) :151, get(environment, wiring_id) :180, insert(...) :223, invalidate(environment, wiring_id) :284, invalidate_all() :315 -- so there is no value to assert against. Adding one IS the keying decision this bead owns. Reported rather than forced.

VERIFICATION of the doc commit: rustfmt clean; run-state shelving_contract 4/4 (it include_str!s all seven router sources); wamn-router --all-targets 58/58 including the resolution pin; wamn-runtime --lib 159/159 including wiring_doorbell's include_str! self-pin and the_listen_is_established_before_the_pointers_are_dropped; wamn-proof-conformance --all-targets green except the known .15.173 baseline red.

DEPENDENCY EDGE ADDED: wamn-0h0g.16.18 now depends on this bead (blocks).
=====================================================================
OWNER RULING, 2026-08-19 (dkk). RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.
=====================================================================

THE KEY IS RULED: (tenant, catalog, environment).

Owner's reasoning, recorded as given:
"The key: (tenant, catalog, environment) on the sibling-plugin evidence is the
decisive shape -- wamn_flow_invocation already receives exactly that triple from
workload config, so it's the PROCESS'S DEMONSTRATED UNIT OF ISOLATION, and two
caches in one process disagreeing about what a boundary is would be the .16.18
hazard reborn one layer up."

ALTERNATIVES REJECTED, with the reason each fell:
 - One cache+doorbell per (tenant, catalog), plugin-style: "buys isolation-by-
   construction at the cost of a doorbell per bind and a DoorbellScope lifecycle
   change -- machinery answering a question the key already answers."
 - Add tenant to Pointer: "option 3's own warning disqualifies it as written (a
   'minimal edit' whose blast radius includes two source pins and metric
   substring pins is not minimal, it's option 1 done timidly)."

=====================================================================
THE TIMING IS ALSO RULED, AND IT COMPOSES WITH THE KEY RATHER THAN
COMPETING WITH IT.
=====================================================================
Owner, recorded as given:
"nothing constructs this in production -- that latency is the standing structural
block from the .16.18 ruling, and it's WHY implementing now would mint code with
no consumer to prove it against."

THEREFORE, IN FORCE AS OF THIS RULING:
 - The ruled key is recorded on this bead. No code lands from this ruling alone.
 - The hazard comments at the three consumer sites STAY IN FORCE, and so does the
   single-tenancy assertion.
 - HARD EDGE: implementation lands WITH the production driver wiring (.16.18 or
   its .19.x successor), where the triple arrives from real workload config.
 - The conformance test has something real to bite only at that point: TWO
   TENANTS, ONE ENVIRONMENT NAME, INTERLEAVED RESOLUTIONS, NO CROSS-SERVE --
   the .17.7 adversarial shape.

=====================================================================
RIDER 1 -- THE PIN INVENTORY, CARRIED VERBATIM SO THE IMPLEMENTER PRICES
IT ON DAY ONE INSTEAD OF DISCOVERING IT.
=====================================================================
Adding a tenant to the key reopens, per this bead's own description:
 - crates/execution/run-state/tests/shelving_contract.rs ROUTER_SOURCES
   (it include_str!s all seven router sources)
 - crates/execution/router/tests/resolution.rs:353
 - the metric-name substring pins
These are NOT optional collateral. They are the measured cost of the ruled shape
and belong in the implementing bead's estimate from the start.

=====================================================================
RIDER 2 -- THE DOC COMMENTS CHANGE MEANING, NOT JUST WORDING.
=====================================================================
The three hazard notices (resolution.rs Pointer, resolution.rs WiringCache,
crates/platform/runtime/src/wiring_doorbell.rs DoorbellScope) currently say the
keying decision is OWED. They update to say:
  keyed (tenant, catalog, environment) by ruling; implementation rides the driver.
Owner: "the hazard notice becomes a pointer to settled law."
NOT STARTED. This edit is part of the implementing bead, not of this recording.

=====================================================================
STATUS
=====================================================================
The acceptance criterion "a ruling is recorded naming the cache's key and the
isolation unit it enforces" IS NOW MET by this note. The remaining two criteria
(hazard notices replaced by ruled behaviour; production construction gated) are
satisfied at implementation, which rides the driver.
This bead does NOT close on this ruling alone.
close_reason: RATIFIED — decision complete: cache isolation scope is tenant+catalog+environment; full pointer adds wiring_id and entries add version. Implementation/comments/adversarial proofs transferred to .16.24, which now depends directly on this receipt.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(sql): control-portable-store.sql cannot be applied to a fresh PostgreSQL 18
description:
## Why -- MEASURED ON A THROWAWAY postgres:18, NOT INFERRED

Applying deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql to a fresh PostgreSQL 18.6 database FAILS with ERRCODE 55000 and MESSAGE control-portable-retained-shape-drift, raised by the retained-shape DO block near the end of the file. A fresh control-plane bootstrap is therefore broken at HEAD.

## Root cause, pinned to a commit

The block recomputes a sha256 over every retained relation column fact (attnum, name, formatted type, notnull, default) and every constraint definition, and compares it to a literal. 99a84c46 (wamn-0h0g.15.170, delete the inert resolution-map columns and the project authoring-tests copy) DELIBERATELY dropped the resolution_map and resolution_map_hash columns and four CHECK constraints from retained relations in this file, and did not regenerate the literal. Because the fingerprint hashes exactly those facts, the pin went stale in the same commit that made it wrong.

  pinned:  749c6904e8f8506b5bbc3fd6a7a45e80d177ae9546f89bbd78cfb7f2478ada37 (set by cd9462f9, wamn-0h0g.15.159)
  actual:  6666b100885d0c8c9e94a6c1cdaceb1997ad884db6e2d654b38806ebf6aaaf9a

Measured by applying the file to postgres:18.6 with ONLY the comparison replaced by a RAISE NOTICE. The repository file was not modified to obtain this. With that one check neutralised the whole file applies cleanly, so the fingerprint is the sole blocker.

## LOCALE HAZARD -- read before pasting the value

The fingerprint aggregates with ORDER BY relation, fact and there is NO COLLATE "C" on that ORDER BY, so the constant is locale-sensitive BY CONSTRUCTION. The value above was computed with datcollate and datctype both en_US.utf8 on PostgreSQL 18.6 Debian. If the gate database uses a different collation the correct value differs. That is why this was not committed as part of wamn-0h0g.15.22 -- baking a locale-dependent constant measured in an unverified locale is the hazard wamn-0h0g.15.32 exists to address, and it deserves an explicit decision rather than a silent re-pin.

## Blocks

services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs cannot install its control database (it panics at :278, install canonical control-plane schema), so WAMN_UPDATE_PROTECTED_RELATIONS cannot regenerate architecture/protected-writes.json. That regeneration is the last piece of wamn-0h0g.15.22 and the only remaining cause of protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership.

## Scope

Decide whether to re-pin the literal (accepting the .15.170 shape, which its title says was deliberate) or to add COLLATE "C" to the ORDER BY first so the constant stops depending on the gate host locale. Doing the second before the first means the value is computed once and stays valid everywhere.
acceptance_criteria: deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql applies cleanly to a fresh PostgreSQL 18; the fingerprint is either locale-independent or its computing locale is recorded beside it.
notes: OWNER RATIFICATION (dkk, 2026-08-19): KEEP. The fix at 0e360cbc and its gate-fixture prereq at 12b8d2b0 were implemented and pushed after the owner had merely RULED the decision, which under the standing rule (memory workflow-rule-decisions-are-recorded-not-implemented) means record-only. The owner was asked explicitly whether to keep or revert them and answered KEEP. They stand as landed; no revert, no amend, no history rewrite. This note exists so the sequencing irregularity is on the record rather than in session memory.
close_reason: Landed at 0e360cbc. COLLATE C added to the retained-shape fingerprint's ORDER BY (per key, preserving the existing two-key sort), then the constant re-pinned to 6666b100885d0c8c9e94a6c1cdaceb1997ad884db6e2d654b38806ebf6aaaf9a. Collation first, re-pin second, because adding the collation changes the sort. Treatment completion, not new policy: wamn-0h0g.15.32 applied the same fix to the evidence and attestation fingerprints in the same file and missed this one. CLASS CLOSED -- swept every string_agg in deploy/sql; the only other occurrence builds a diagnostic string and is hashed against nothing; the rule is now written into docs/archive/build-and-test.md. LOCALE INDEPENDENCE MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: identical fingerprint on throwaway postgres:18.6 under datcollate en_US.utf8 AND under C. The value is unchanged by the collation edit, so the two changes are independent. Verified end to end -- the live gate now installs the canonical control database cleanly, which it could not do at all before. The population statement is in the commit body: the artifact now accepts post-.15.170 shapes and pre-.15.170 control databases refuse by name, which is the fingerprint's documented attnum-hashed design and must not be reverted.

title: feat(exec): Verdict::Emit has no consumer — the middle of the emit boundary does not exist
description: Found by the EXE wave-3 lane 4 while landing wamn-0h0g.19.7, and it is why that bead could not be completed end to end. wamn-0h0g.16.3 landed the router's typed Verdict::Emit. wamn-0h0g.19.7 landed the admission half: admit_sql composes the event identity ONCE in its input CTE as event_idempotency_key, with two disjoint identities — evt:<reg>:dedup:<id> when the body carries the author's dedup-id, evt:<reg>:<stream-seq> otherwise. BUT NOTHING JOINS THEM. Verdict::Emit has no consumer anywhere outside crates/execution/router: there is no publisher and no emit-to-boundary wiring. The router half exists, the admission half exists, THE MIDDLE DOES NOT. Until it lands, 'at-least-once in-stream becomes exactly-once-admitted at the boundary' — the single sentence R2's default is sold on — is true of the two ends and unproven across the path.
design: Publish router Emit through the host JetStream boundary using the wamn-0h0g.19.16 DerivedEvent contract. Derive tenant, project, and environment only from bound claims; derive entity and insert/update/delete only from the admitted terminal wiring; accept only the component-authored dedup id as the logical dedup operand. Use the existing event subject grammar and a host-owned Nats-Msg-Id scope. The materializer decodes DerivedEvent separately from CDC Envelope 0.1 and applies the existing registration event-or-batch gate. Publish and server ACK must precede queue completion; retries converge through JetStream dedup.
acceptance_criteria: A terminal Verdict::Emit reaches the host-owned JetStream publisher with the exact admitted entity and operation, host-bound tenant/project/environment, arbitrary payload, author dedup id, and host-derived causation. The serialized DerivedEvent is versioned and cannot be decoded as CDC Envelope 0.1; it carries no lsn, txid, commit_ts, or table. Subject and Nats-Msg-Id are derived without guest authority; publish ACK precedes queue completion; replayed emits dedupe and reach matching registrations exactly once without SQL flow/run admission. Focused golden, subject, dedup, causation-depth, retry, and end-to-end registration proofs pass.
close_reason: Implemented exact admitted Emit selector through router, host-owned versioned DerivedEvent publication, server-ACK-before-completion for direct and queued delivery, stream-wide selector-scoped dedup, truthful causation propagation, and separate materializer registration decoding. Green: runtime/execution-host/executor/host production check; wiring-lowering 7/7; router terminal 11/11; event-wire 14/14 plus exact digest 1/1; catalog 31/31; materializer 22/22; flow-http 11/11; materializer component 8/8. JetStream live replay proof is present and skips when WAMN_EVT_NATS_URL is absent. Runtime lib-test gate remains baseline-broken on nested-worktree include_str and unrelated wiring_doorbell test-only symbols; execution-host lib-test was capped during cold link, with production graph green.

title: feat(router): wire the pointer-flip doorbell to WiringCache::invalidate — the seam is open on both sides
description: THE JOINING BEAD for the seam EXE wave 2 deliberately left open across two concurrent lanes. wamn-0h0g.16.5 landed WiringCache::invalidate(environment, wiring_id) -> bool in crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs; NOTHING IN THE TREE CALLS IT outside its own unit test, and that is documented on the method. wamn-0h0g.18.2 owns the pointer-flip notification emitter. Neither lane was permitted to reach into the other, so the two halves exist and are untied: a pointer flip does NOT currently invalidate the routers cache, which means the env-hot read path can serve a stale active version indefinitely after an activation or a rollback. Sub-decision already taken and worth preserving: invalidate drops the POINTER ONLY, not the cached graphs — a version is immutable so only the pointer can go stale, and keeping the entries is what makes a rollback flip an in-memory hit. If a purge variant is wanted it is a one-line addition.
acceptance_criteria: A pointer flip performed through wamn-0h0g.18.2s activation verb causes the routers cache to serve the new active version on the next delivery, proven end to end; invalidate is no longer reachable only from its own test.
notes:
ADDENDUM (integrator, 2026-08-18) — THE EMITTER HALF HAS LANDED, AND IT CARRIES A MANDATORY
OBLIGATION FOR THE SUBSCRIBER. wamn-0h0g.18.2 is integrated; both halves of this seam now exist.

TRANSPORT AS BUILT: PostgreSQL pg_notify on channel `wamn_wiring_activation`, fired by
catalog.notify_wiring_activation() from trigger wiring_activation_doorbell,
AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON catalog.wiring_activation (deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:1872-1913).

WHY pg_notify AND NOT THE CONTROL-PLANE NATS: a NATS publish CANNOT BE INSIDE THE FLIP'S TRANSACTION.
Published before commit it can announce a flip that then rolls back; published after commit it can be
lost — and the waker's tolerance of loss is bought by the dispatcher re-hinting every due queue row
each sweep, which pointer flips have NO analogue for. pg_notify is delivered IF AND ONLY IF the
transaction commits, on a connection the router already holds to the same project database, scoped
per-database exactly like the catalog schema. In-tree precedent:
crates/platform/runtime/src/flow_invocation.rs:72 (LISTEN wamn_run_outcome).

*** THE OBLIGATION — THIS IS NOT OPTIONAL CORRECTNESS, IT IS THE TRANSPORT'S ONLY LOSS MODE. ***
PostgreSQL delivers a notification ONLY to sessions that are LISTENing at commit time, and queues
NOTHING for an absent one. A LISTENER THAT RECONNECTS HAS MISSED AN UNKNOWN SET OF FLIPS AND MUST DROP
ITS WHOLE CACHE, NOT RESUME. Anything less serves a stale active version indefinitely with no signal
that it is doing so. This is written into the DDL comment at catalog-schema.sql:1888-1891.
SECONDARY: the shared 8GB async notify queue can stall committing writers if a listener never drains
— bounded here by tiny payloads and rare flips, but it is why the subscriber must drain promptly.

THE PAYLOAD CONTRACT IS OWNED BY THE EMITTER AND IS ALREADY PINNED: WIRING_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL and
WiringActivationNotice (crates/catalog/model/src/wiring_activation.rs:52 and :67), a
deny_unknown_fields kebab-case struct pinned against the DDL's json_build_object keys by
the_notice_shape_is_exactly_the_payload_the_ddl_builds. THE SUBSCRIBER IS THEREFORE:
  serde_json::from_str::<WiringActivationNotice>(payload) -> cache.invalidate(..)

PREMISE REFINEMENT TO CARRY: wamn-0h0g.16.5's bead said "one read per (wiring, VERSION)". The pointer
stores only the HASH, so a join-free trigger can only carry the hash — and the hash is the FINER
identity (byte identity of the exact document the version names). THE REAL INVARIANT IS ONE READ PER
(wiring, definition-hash); version comes back for logs.
close_reason: Integrated 234414ca + 58d3e0dd. THE SEAM IS CLOSED: crates/platform/runtime/src/wiring_doorbell.rs LISTENs on wamn_wiring_activation, parses WiringActivationNotice and calls WiringCache::invalidate. Home chosen deliberately — the router crate declares no DB, no runtime and no clock, and a LISTEN is all three; crates/platform/runtime already owns the tree's only other LISTEN (flow_invocation.rs, wamn_run_outcome) and already has tokio-postgres. THE RECONNECT OBLIGATION IS MET AND IS ORDER-SENSITIVE: new WiringCache::invalidate_all() clears every pointer and keeps every graph, and the connector executes LISTEN FIRST, then drops — dropping first would leave a window where a flip is neither delivered nor covered. Pinned by the_listen_is_established_before_the_pointers_are_dropped. Reading committed to: drop every POINTER, keep every GRAPH — a version is immutable, so a missed flip can only have moved a pointer, and every graph entry is still the correct answer to its own key. PROVEN END TO END AGAINST A REAL POSTGRESQL 18 (throwaway container, removed): the real catalog-schema.sql DDL with its wiring_activation_doorbell trigger, flip_activation() and resolve_active_wiring(), and the production listener — activation, flip, rollback-is-an-in-memory-hit, and take-dark all verified, with the only path between writer and cache being pg_notify. 11 mutants, 11 killed, 11 byte-identical restores; three of them kill the LIVE gate, so it is demonstrably not passing vacuously. Integrator independently re-derived the channel-name mutant: left "LISTEN wamn_wiring_activated" / right "LISTEN wamn_wiring_activation", restore byte-identical (29302ad4). THREE FINDINGS FILED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: wamn-0h0g.16.16 (WiringCache::insert re-installs a pointer read before the flip — this bead's correctness is real but not complete while it stands), wamn-0h0g.16.18 (nothing in production constructs a WiringCache or starts the listener), wamn-0h0g.16.20 (AbortOnDrop duplicated). Two subscriber decisions beyond the addendum's one-liner: the cache pointer key has no tenant or catalog while pg_notify is per-DATABASE and tenants share one under RLS, so the subscriber filters on a DoorbellScope; and an unreadable payload (deny_unknown_fields vs a grown DDL) hides WHICH pointer moved, so it is treated as a missed flip and drops the whole cache rather than guessing. COST, RECORDED: +3 red from the unavoidable wamn-runtime -> wamn-router package edge, all against baselines FROZEN until wamn-0h0g.15.22, all banked on that bead with their exact regeneration commands. Branch baseline moves 30 -> 33.
