title: [SR-MVP] fix(security): per-digest pools have no checkout-time identity seam — cross-tenant leak once the router shares a pool
description:
## Why -- BLOCKS wamn-0h0g.17.1 SIGN-OFF AND ALL ROUTER WIRING. Cross-tenant leak by construction.

The .17.1 lane was required to produce a written tenant-isolation statement before dropping
`entitlement` from the pool key. It produced one, and the finding is that THE BEAD'S OWN PREMISE IS
FALSE AT HEAD.

.17.1 says isolation "now rests on host-injected identity per checkout, not per instance."
**THERE IS NO PER-CHECKOUT IDENTITY INJECTION ANYWHERE IN THE TREE.**

Identity is injected ONCE PER `ExecutionHost::instantiate`, and it is store-resident:
- `Ctx::builder(owner, owner)` -- crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:757
- `Store::new(raw, SharedCtx::new(ctx))` -- lib.rs:776, where `component_id` is a field of the
  Store's `Ctx` (fork engine/ctx.rs:364)
- process-resident: `plugin.set_tenant/set_schema/set_runner(owner, ...)` -- lib.rs:662/664/666 into
  `RwLock<HashMap<component_id, ...>>` (claims.rs:563/617/643)

`checkout(&self, key: &ExecutionPoolKey)` takes NO identity and has no hook that could. There is a
per-TRANSACTION re-read (`begin_with_claims`), but it looks up by the STORE-RESIDENT `component_id`
(resources.rs:270) -- it re-injects whatever identity the store was BUILT with, not the identity of
the run being served.

## The leak, precisely

One digest's pool filled from more than one identity. A checkout then hands tenant B a store whose
`Ctx.component_id` is A's. `begin_with_claims` injects `app.tenant = A`, and Postgres RLS admits A's
rows to B's run. Nothing in the pool can detect it: `insert(key, instance)` sees no identity.

**THIS DOES NOT REQUIRE INSTANCE REUSE TO BE ON.** `max_invocations_per_instance = 1` protects
residual GUEST state; it does nothing about misattributed IDENTITY. The reuse-off posture is not a
mitigation for this.

Host-side state also survives an instance and is tenant-bound: the store's `Ctx.plugins` map
(lib.rs:735-757) holds a `ConnectionHttp` constructed with a specific `tenant` and `project`
(lib.rs:722-729). A prewarmed instance is NOT tenant-neutral.

## Why it is latent today and live tomorrow

It holds VACUOUSLY today (the pool has zero non-test consumers) and STRUCTURALLY for the current
single-tenant process shape (lib.rs:632 -- "one process = one project = one owner").

exe-model rev 4 makes pools "keyed per component digest, SHARED ACROSS EVERY WIRING AND TENANT flow
using that component" -- fifty wirings sharing csv-parse share one warm pool. That cross-tenant
sharing is the decisive argument for the router. **The moment the router fills one digest's pool
across tenants -- the entire point of the rekey -- the safety condition is violated and the leak is
live.**

## The safety condition the pool ships under (written into pool.rs module docs)

> Every instance inserted under one `ExecutionPoolKey` must have been constructed for the same
> host-injected identity, until a checkout-time identity-injection seam exists.

## Scope -- what must exist before any router wiring

EITHER (a) `checkout(&key, identity)` that rebinds `Ctx.component_id` and the `wamn:postgres` claim
registration per checkout -- the real fix, and the one that makes the spec's cross-tenant pool
sharing safe; OR (b) a router-side invariant that one digest pool is filled from exactly one
identity -- which forfeits the cross-tenant amortization that justified the rekey, and should be
recorded as such if chosen.

Related but NOT the same defect: wamn-0h0g.23.1 (app.role/app.user_id never injected) and
wamn-0h0g.23.4 (no production identity source for them). The .17.1 lane verified independently that
its argument rests only on `app.tenant`, which IS injected. Also related: wamn-1nd -- the structural
close for claim mutation (per-tenant role + current_user); `reject_claim_mutation` remains a
defense-in-depth blocklist that `DO`/`EXECUTE` can still escape (claims.rs:277-284).

## Acceptance

A checkout-time identity-injection seam exists and is proven by a test in which two DIFFERENT
tenants check out from ONE digest pool and each sees only its own rows; or option (b) is ruled, the
cross-tenant sharing loss is recorded against the spec's pooling paragraph, and the router enforces
one-identity-per-digest-pool with a test that fails if a second identity inserts.
acceptance_criteria: A checkout-time identity-injection seam exists and is proven by a test in which two different tenants check out from ONE digest pool and each sees only its own rows; OR the one-identity-per-digest-pool alternative is ruled, its loss of cross-tenant pool amortization is recorded against the spec's pooling paragraph, and the router enforces the invariant with a test that fails when a second identity inserts into a populated pool.
notes:
RULING (owner, 2026-08-18): OPTION (a), THE CHECKOUT-TIME IDENTITY SEAM. RATIFIED.

WHY (b) IS REJECTED: it is not a cheaper option, it is a SILENT RETRACTION of the pooling
paragraph's own justification. Cross-wiring amortization IS the argument that beat WAC composition
("fifty wirings using csv-parse share one warm pool ... the decisive argument for the router over
compile-time composition"). One-identity-per-digest-pool forfeits exactly that, and the spec would
then owe a rewrite, not a footnote.

(a) is also the honest expression of what a pool IS: instances are FUNGIBLE COMPUTE; identity is
PER-ACQUISITION STATE. Conflating the two is how this leak came to exist.

RIDER 1 -- THE REBIND MUST COVER THE FULL IDENTITY TUPLE. A PARTIAL REBIND IS THE SAME LEAK WEARING
A FIX. Enumerate each element and its rebind point in the implementation; at minimum:
  - the tenant claim (app.tenant);
  - the workload/component claim registration keyed by component_id -- wamn:postgres
    set_tenant / set_schema / set_runner, AND the app.role / app.user_id registries added by
    wamn-0h0g.23.1;
  - trace context (the span parent for THIS acquisition, or spans cross-attribute silently);
  - connection-generation resolution scope (which bound generation this checkout resolves against).
Anything in the store's Ctx that is identity-derived and not rebound is a leak channel. Name them
all; do not rebind "the obvious ones".

RIDER 2 -- THE CONFORMANCE TEST IS ADVERSARIAL BY CONSTRUCTION. Two tenants, ONE digest pool,
INTERLEAVED checkouts, asserting no cross-bleed on claims OR spans. A sequential two-tenant test
would pass against a broken implementation and prove nothing.

BLOCKING RELATIONSHIPS: unblocks wamn-0h0g.19.1 and .19.6 on landing. wamn-0h0g.17.1's deferred
sign-off is released BY THIS BEAD LANDING, not before -- the rekey stays merged-but-unwired until
then.
close_reason: [f7e96856] THE CHECKOUT-TIME IDENTITY SEAM EXISTS. Option (a) as ruled. ExecutionInstancePool::checkout now takes an identity and rebinds through ExecutionHost::bind_identity (lib.rs:845-869), cleared at revoke_identity (:874-878); the tuple is documented as a TABLE on ExecutionAcquisition (lib.rs:695-772) in the code, not merely in a report. *** RIDER 1 DISCHARGED — THE FULL TUPLE IS REBOUND: app.tenant, project, search_path schema, app.runner, app.role and app.user_id (the .23.1 registries), release identity, and causation run context, all via WamnPostgres::bind_session_claims (claims.rs:864-950); wasi:logging (tenant, project) at lib.rs:859-863; the private effect-writer scope at :864; the trace parent at :865, consumed by call_run(..).instrument(span) at :1000. Connection-generation resolution scope needs no element of its own — a generation is resolved per effect by connection_effect_snapshot whose scope is exactly (tenant, project, schema) from the claims above. *** DELIBERATELY NOT REBOUND, WITH REASONS RECORDED IN CODE (lib.rs:743-760): the claim scope (Ctx.component_id) names the STORE not the tenant and is fixed per instance — the fork captures the workload id into a PRIVATE CtxHttpHooks field at CtxBuilder::build, so rebinding it per acquisition would DESYNCHRONIZE the egress declaration (set_allowed_hosts writes under Ctx.component_id, RunnerEgress::outgoing_request reads under the frozen hook id); keeping it per-instance also bounds every registry by max_instances rather than by acquisition count. Also the store memory limiter (label is the claim scope, counters cannot span acquisitions since reset_invocation_state always fails and the pool destroys the instance every checkout) and guest linear memory (the separate INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE argument). *** THE ONE ELEMENT THAT CANNOT BE REBOUND, AND THE BEAD UNDERSTATED IT: ConnectionHttp freezes (tenant, project) into Box<str> fields (connection_http.rs:77-78) and Ctx.plugins is a PRIVATE FORK FIELD, so the plugin is UNREBINDABLE FROM WAMN CODE AT ALL — no amount of host-side rebinding covers it. Covered by FAILING CLOSED instead: connection_effect_snapshot refuses a caller-supplied tenant that DISAGREES with the bound claim (claims.rs:1231-1252), so a stale ConnectionHttp yields a denial, never another tenant's rows. *** RIDER 2 DISCHARGED — THE TEST IS ADVERSARIAL BY CONSTRUCTION: interleaved_two_tenant_checkouts_on_one_digest_pool_never_cross_attribute (tests/conformance/tests/execution_pool_checkout_identity.rs:186) builds two ExecutionHosts from ONE component's bytes via the real ExecutionHost::instantiate so they share ONE digest key, then orders A-checkout, B-checkout, A-acts, B-acts, A-returns, B-returns, asserting A's claims WHILE B'S LEASE IS LIVE and again after B binds. Plus live_interleaved_bound_scopes_each_see_only_their_own_rows (claims.rs:2565), the acceptance criterion's 'each sees only its own rows', interleaved A/B/A against real Postgres 18 RLS with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS probe role. *** BOTH MUTANTS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY IN THE MAIN TREE: (a) pool.rs baseline sha256 dc51ba6b391a94787a178ed3539ac8206fdae74e8a0b3bfb8086a1300528b442, the bind_identity block in checkout replaced by 'let _ = (&mut lease, identity);' — the adversarial conformance test failed with left "prewarm-placeholder" right "tenant-a", i.e. THE INSTANCE RESOLVING ITS CONSTRUCTION-TIME IDENTITY, which is literally the leak this bead describes; it also killed exactly the three named pool unit tests (interleaved_checkouts_under_one_key_never_share_an_identity, every_ending_revokes_the_identity_it_served, a_refused_identity_destroys_the_instance). (b) claims.rs baseline sha256 ea751fdd4581f9491a5417fb2d62037402112e452651a9bb46c36e0aaa364c9c, the self.tenants..remove(component_id) statement deleted from revoke_session_claims — the live proof failed at claims.rs:2606 with left Some(SessionClaims{tenant:"seam-live-a",..}) right None, against a throwaway PostgreSQL 18 the integrator started and destroyed. NOTABLE: the lane reported that this second mutant SURVIVED its first version of that assertion (passing for the wrong reason, since a schema-only revoke also breaks the query) and that it strengthened the assertion to match the WAMN0 no-tenant code exactly; the integrator's re-derivation confirms the strengthened form catches it specifically. Restored byte-identical after each, shas match, wamn-execution-host 34/34 and wamn-runtime 143/143 green. *** BASELINE HONESTY: the lane built a detached worktree at 11488f03 with its own target dir and ran the full conformance suite --no-fail-fast on BOTH sides: 25 unique failing tests at base, 25 at its HEAD, comm diff empty in both directions. Nothing broken, nothing accidentally fixed. *** THREE FINDINGS FILED, NOT FIXED: wamn-0h0g.17.9 (instantiate never calls set_project, so guest DB calls and ConnectionHttp can resolve DIFFERENT DATABASES in one process — pre-existing split-brain, independent of pooling), .17.10 (revoke_identity is not exact: WamnLogging has no clear_claim and RunnerEgressPolicy no clear_declared, so an idle instance still carries a resolvable logging claim and egress declaration — bounded by instance count, not a growth leak, but blocks the router wiring), .17.11 (tighten the effect-tenant guard from disagreement-only to requiring a bound claim; needs one line in connection_http.rs, outside the lane's domain). THE ROUTER IS STILL NOT WIRED TO THE POOL, per instruction — checkout has zero non-test consumers.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(wit): uniform node-operation seam vs per-component typed operations
description:
## Why -- BLOCKING for the developer surface, surfaced by wamn-0h0g.16.2 at implementation

Two ratified sentences in exe-model rev 4 point at different WIT shapes, and .16.2 had to pick one
to author the package at all. It picked the UNIFORM seam and flagged the choice rather than burying
it. The router (.16.1) independently assumed the same shape -- `NodeInvoker::invoke(&call) ->
NodeOutcome`, one method for every component -- so both landed lanes now rest on an unratified
reading.

THE UNIFORM READING (what .16.2 built, wamn:node@0.2.0):
One `handler.run(ctx, input) -> result<emission, node-error>` exported by EVERY component;
per-component parameters travel as `config: json` inside the context. Grounded in "Execution
mechanics": the router will "acquire a pooled instance of that node's component and invoke THE
OPERATION over the existing typed WIT seam" -- singular, one seam the router can bind once.

THE TYPED READING (what R1 and .13.7 say):
R1 -- "Developers author components -- typed WIT operations with declared ports, parameters, effect
posture, and connection requirements". .13.7 (developer component SDK) -- "WIT ops, ports, effect
posture, data access". "Developer surface" describes the entity component as taking "relation and
filter spec as DECLARED PARAMETERS". Read literally, each component declares its own typed
operations and the wiring binds typed ports to typed params -- which `config: json` does not
express, because a JSON blob is exactly the untyped escape hatch the ruling's "typed" is contrasted
against.

## The options

(a) UNIFORM SEAM (as built). Router binds one world at compile time; pools stay per digest; wiring
    validation is shape-checking a JSON config against a component-declared schema, not WIT types.
    Cheapest, already implemented, but "typed WIT operations with declared parameters" becomes
    marketing rather than mechanism, and gate-time type-compat validation (.18.3) has no WIT types
    to compare -- it degrades to JSON-schema compat.

(b) PER-COMPONENT TYPED OPERATIONS, DYNAMICALLY INVOKED. Each component exports its own typed WIT
    operations; the router does not bind them statically but dispatches dynamically against the
    component's own exported type information (wasmtime's component API supports calling an export
    with runtime-typed values). Delivers the ratified sentence literally, keeps one shared pool per
    digest, and gives .18.3 real WIT types to check. Costs: a dynamic-invocation path in the router
    (value marshalling, per-call type resolution) and a harder story for the SDK's ergonomics.
    NOT YET INVESTIGATED against the pinned fork -- feasibility is the first question.

(c) TYPED-BY-CODEGEN. Per-component generated bindings, statically linked. Explicitly rejected in
    "Developer surface" for the entity case -- "N regenerating components and pool fragmentation" --
    so it is almost certainly wrong here for the same reason, recorded for completeness.

## Who is affected

- .16.1 router dispatch shape (LANDED on the uniform assumption -- `NodeInvoker` is one method).
- .16.2 the WIT world itself (LANDED as uniform, wamn:node@0.2.0).
- .18.3 type-compat shape validation of wirings -- under (a) it validates JSON schemas, under (b)
  WIT types. Materially different bead.
- .13.7 developer component SDK -- its whole surface is "declare typed WIT operations".
- .23.2 the entity component -- "relation and filter spec as declared parameters".
- .21.1 per-catalog component library admission -- what a library entry's interface signature IS.

## The question

Does a palette component export ONE uniform operation with JSON-carried parameters, or its OWN
typed WIT operations that the router dispatches dynamically? If (b), how does the router invoke an
operation whose type it learns at runtime, and is that supported on the pinned wamn/2.7.0 fork?

Rule before .13.7 claims. If the answer is (b), .16.1's NodeInvoker trait and .16.2's world are both
wrong in the same direction and should be revised together, before anything binds to them.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded ruling on whether palette components export one uniform operation with JSON-carried parameters or their own typed WIT operations dispatched dynamically by the router, with the consequence propagated to wamn-0h0g.16.1 (NodeInvoker), .16.2 (the wamn:node world), .18.3 (type-compat validation), .13.7 (SDK), .23.2 (entity component) and .21.1 (library admission).
notes:
RULING FRAMING + SPIKE AUTHORIZATION (owner, 2026-08-18). Bead stays OPEN; rule after the spike.

THE CONTRADICTION IS OWNED, NOT A LANE ERROR. R1's "typed WIT operations with declared ports,
parameters" and Execution-mechanics' singular "the operation over the existing typed WIT seam" were
written in different revs and never reconciled. The lanes surfaced it correctly.

WHAT THIS BEAD OMITTED: THE STUDIO'S DISPATCH PROBLEM -- the same problem one layer up. The costs
are not only wasmtime feasibility.

TYPED-PER-COMPONENT buys compile-time port shapes, and pays with THREE things, not one:
  1. dynamic invocation against arbitrary author-declared signatures on the pinned fork -- IF
     wasmtime's dynamic component APIs carry it;
  2. a wiring validator that must diff ARBITRARY WIT TYPES;
  3. a studio that must RENDER arbitrary type shapes to non-technical wirers.

UNIFORM (handler.run(ctx, input) + JSON-schema-declared ports) buys one frozen world, static
dispatch, and the schema-diff validation lanes 1-2 already built; it pays with runtime shape-checking
at edges and the loss of WIT-native port typing.

THE TIEBREAKER THE BEAD DID NOT STATE: THE WIRER'S TYPE SYSTEM WAS NEVER GOING TO BE WIT. Plant
engineers wire against PORT SCHEMAS THE STUDIO CAN RENDER, and JSON schema is that layer regardless
of which seam sits underneath. Typed WIT would exist for DEVELOPER ergonomics only -- and developers
already get their type safety from sqlx and from their own component's internal types.

OWNER'S RECOMMENDATION ON THE MERITS: **UNIFORM, ratified as the seam, with typed WIT recorded as
the demand-gated evolution.** It keeps the two merged lanes valid, keeps .18.3 as schema-compat
rather than WIT-type-compat, and the spec's two sentences amend to match rather than one of them
being quietly ignored.

THE SPIKE IS MANDATORY, AND IT IS A FALSIFIER -- NOT AN EXPLORATION. TIMEBOX: HALF A DAY.
One question: can wasmtime's dynamic component invocation carry per-component typed operations on
the pinned wamn/2.7.0 fork?
  - If NO -> the decision makes itself; uniform is forced and the merits argument is moot.
  - If YES -> the merits recommendation above STILL STANDS and must be ruled EXPLICITLY rather than
    adopted by default because it turned out to be possible.

SEQUENCING: rule after the spike lands and BEFORE wamn-0h0g.13.7 claims. This spike is the ONLY work
authorized against this bead; no implementation proceeds until the ruling is recorded.

CONSEQUENCE IF RULED UNIFORM: .16.1's NodeInvoker and .16.2's wamn:node world are both CORRECT as
merged, and the spec's R1 sentence amends. If ruled typed, both are wrong together and must be
revised together before anything else binds to them.

SPIKE RESULT (EXE wave 2 lane 3, 2026-08-18). *** THE ANSWER IS YES. *** Dynamic invocation against
arbitrary author-declared WIT signatures works on the pin, end to end, with NO FORK CHANGE. Proved by
RUNNING, not by reading documentation.

*** THEREFORE, PER THIS BEAD'S OWN RULING FRAMING, THE MERITS RECOMMENDATION MUST NOW BE RULED
EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN ADOPTED BY DEFAULT BECAUSE IT TURNED OUT TO BE POSSIBLE. THE DECISION DID NOT
MAKE ITSELF. *** This bead stays OPEN pending that explicit ruling.

PREMISE CORRECTION TO THE BEAD'S FRAMING (integrator-verified independently): the wamn/2.7.0 fork
does NOT vendor its own wasmtime. It consumes crates.io wasmtime 47.0.3
(source = "registry+https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index" in Cargo.lock) — the SAME one the
repo pins at Cargo.toml:41 and asserts in tests/conformance/tests/wasmtime_source_identity.rs. So
"feasible on the pinned fork" and "feasible on wasmtime 47.0.3" are the same question, and the spike
reached every API through wash_runtime::wasmtime rather than a private copy.

FEASIBILITY, MEASURED (debug builds — read the ratios, not the absolutes):
  full type resolution of one component ....  5.1 us   AMORTIZABLE PER DIGEST
  marshal 3 args JSON -> Val ..............  10.7 us   per call, unavoidable
  get_func by cached index ................    62 ns   per call, trivial
  instantiate one pooled instance .........   425 us   PER CALL ALREADY TODAY
  static  TypedFunc::call_async ...........  48.1 us/call
  dynamic Func::call + JSON marshal .......  59.8 us/call
  dynamic overhead ........................  11.6 us/call
With INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE = 1 every invocation already pays ~425 us to instantiate, so dynamic
dispatch adds ~2.7%. *** PER-CALL COST IS NOT AN ARGUMENT AGAINST (b). ***

THE FIVE SUB-QUESTIONS:
1. TYPE DISCOVERY — YES, and STORE-FREE. All 9 exports of two guests read off Component alone,
   including nested interface exports and resource constructors/methods.
2. MARSHALLING BOTH WAYS — YES for every non-handle type (record, nested record, list, option, tuple,
   enum, flags, payload and payload-free variants, result, f64, char, u64 all round-tripped).
   HARD WALLS: own<T>/borrow<T>, future/stream/error-context, non-string-key map. LOSSY: JSON has no
   char; NaN/+-Inf are legal f64 and illegal JSON so they become null and the type is destroyed;
   option<option<T>> is inexpressible under null-means-none; u64 > 2^53 does not survive a non-Rust
   JSON producer. *** THE VARIANT/RESULT/FLAGS ENCODINGS ARE HOST INVENTIONS — WIT HAS NO CANONICAL
   JSON PROJECTION. *** All five type errors were caught with a path ("at spec.window: tuple arity
   1 != 2"), which is the point worth flagging: DYNAMIC DISPATCH DOES NOT REMOVE RUNTIME SHAPE-CHECKING
   AT THE EDGES; IT RELOCATES IT.
3. A REAL INVOCATION — YES. `select` (record param, variant return) driven on all four outcome paths,
   plus `count` with a different signature on the same component; nothing statically bound. Resources
   are reachable dynamically (open(42) -> live Val::Resource passed into drain and dropped) but NOT
   from JSON; the router would own handle lifetime.
4. POOLING — YES, IT AMORTIZES PER DIGEST. types::Type holds Arc<ComponentTypes>, not a borrow, so a
   cached descriptor is Send + Sync + 'static (compile-time asserted) and works against instances from
   other stores. *** CAVEAT, VERIFIED NOT ASSUMED: Component::component_type() builds with
   resources: None, so own<T>/borrow<T> resolve to ResourceType::uninstantiated(..) — cached results
   compared UNEQUAL to live for a resource signature and EQUAL for a non-resource one. RESOURCE-
   CARRYING SIGNATURES MUST RE-RESOLVE PER INSTANCE. *** Separately, wasmtime itself calls
   self.ty(&store) inside every Func::call, a per-call resolution no host cache removes.
5. ASYNC / EFFECT POSTURE — YES. Ran on an async store via call_async with the guest's wasi:logging
   import served by a real wash_runtime::plugin::HostPlugin on a Ctx (4 records captured through the
   fork's plugin machinery). add_to_linker_async and linker.instantiate_pre are unchanged from the
   production path at crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:712-782. Func::post_return_async is DEPRECATED
   in 47.0.3, so the dynamic path carries no extra bookkeeping step.

*** THE FINDING THAT MOVES THE DECISION — COST #2 IS SMALLER THAN THE RULING ASSUMED. *** The ruling
listed "a wiring validator that must diff ARBITRARY WIT TYPES" as one of three costs. types::Type is
PartialEq + Eq and THE COMPARISON IS STRUCTURAL ACROSS SEPARATELY COMPILED COMPONENTS: Handle::equivalent
falls through to a TypeChecker holding a_types/b_types from two different Arc<ComponentTypes>. Proved:
alpha's spec/mode/opts/result compare EQUAL to beta's despite different packages (spike:alpha vs
spike:beta) and different type names (filter vs criterion, row vs record-out); one extra record field
makes them UNEQUAL; cross-port assignability (list<row> vs request) correctly returns FALSE. So the
validator is `a == b` plus a renderer, NOT a hand-written subtyping engine.
WHAT IS MISSING IS SUBTYPING: PartialEq is EQUIVALENCE ONLY, so "callee accepts a superset" and WIT
@since/@unstable compatibility remain hand-written. Filed as its own bead.

BONUS SAFETY FINDING, LOAD-BEARING FOR ANY DIGEST-KEYED CACHE: ComponentExportIndex::lookup compares
component.inner.id == self.id, so a cached descriptor used against the WRONG DIGEST returns None —
verified. INDEX-BASED LOOKUP IS SELF-FENCING; NAME-BASED LOOKUP IS NOT, and would happily find beta's
identically-named `select`. Filed separately; it matters regardless of how this bead is ruled.

WHAT THE SPIKE DID NOT TEST, stated so an unqualified YES is not read as broader than it is:
  - async-lifted (async_() == true) WIT exports — no guest declared one; component-model-async is on
    and Func::call_async has the concurrency_support() branch, but it was NOT exercised.
  - future/stream/error-context values at all.
  - THE 256 MiB POOLING CEILING AND EPOCH-DEADLINE TRAP UNDER A DYNAMIC CALL — the engine carried both
    but no deadline was made to fire. *** RESIDUAL RISK: TRAP/CANCELLATION CLASSIFICATION INTO
    node-error THROUGH THE DYNAMIC PATH IS UNPROVEN. ***
  - concurrency (single-threaded driver, no contended digest-keyed cache); release builds (the
    marshaller ran at opt-level 0, so 10.7 us is a pessimistic bound); SDK ergonomics entirely.

WHERE THIS LEAVES THE RULING: cost (1) dynamic invocation is SMALL and proven; cost (2) the validator
is SMALLER THAN ASSUMED; so the weight falls almost entirely on cost (3) — a studio that must render
arbitrary type shapes to non-technical wirers — and on the tiebreaker this bead already records, that
THE WIRER'S TYPE SYSTEM WAS NEVER GOING TO BE WIT. The spike's own artifact is evidence for cost (3):
a rendered `select` signature is one 400-character line of nested records and variants, and that is
what a plant engineer would be shown.

Spike code lives at spike-16-9/ on lane/exe2-3 (commits eea238a1, 63773b39, 27414d41). THROWAWAY, NOT
FOR INTEGRATION — both cargo projects declare their own [workspace], so no production file, WIT
package, root lockfile or feature resolution was touched.

DRIVER SUCCESSOR RULING 2026-08-21 (wamn-0h0g.16.21): both HTTP and queued execution invoke the uniform wamn:node seam through one wamn-execution-host router driver and the existing digest-keyed pool. No per-component typed WIT driver is introduced.
close_reason:
*** OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-18): OPTION (a) — UNQUALIFIED, NOT RELUCTANT. *** The wave-2 falsifier spike closed the escape hatch (dynamic invocation against arbitrary author-declared WIT signatures WORKS on the pin, no fork change), which is what makes this a real choice rather than a decision that made itself. The measurements then settled each cost ON ITS MERITS: 11.6 us of dynamic-dispatch overhead against a 425 us instantiation is 2.7% — NOISE against any effect, so cost 1 is not an argument either way; and the structural-PartialEq finding (wasmtime types::Type compares structurally ACROSS separately compiled components) kills the validator-cost argument FOR TYPED, not for uniform. With costs 1 and 2 neutralized the decision falls exactly where the recorded tiebreaker always pointed: THE WIRER'S CONTRACT LAYER WAS NEVER GOING TO BE WIT. The spike's own artifact is the studio-UX case closed by demonstration — a rendered  signature is one 400-character line of nested records and variants, and that is what a plant engineer would have been shown.

*** THE REFRAME, WHICH IS THE RULING'S ACTUAL CONTENT — 'UNIFORM' UNDERSELLS WHAT WAS CHOSEN. THIS IS TYPES MOVED TO THE LAYER THAT RENDERS. *** Port schemas are JSON Schema BECAUSE JSON Schema is what a wiring studio, a validation diff, and an agent-emitted document can ALL consume. WIT stays the PLATFORM's contract — the frozen wamn:node@0.1.0 world, ctx, and the import set. Developer-facing types live in the SDK's LANGUAGE layer: wamn-0h0g.13.7 generates typed Rust wrappers over the uniform seam, so AUTHORS STILL WRITE TYPED CODE and only the seam underneath is uniform. Nothing is being given up; the typing is relocated to where it is legible.

RIDERS, ALL BINDING:
1. R1's sentence AMENDS to 'typed PORTS (JSON Schema), declared parameters'. The spec catches up to the tree in rev 4.1 — this is a spec correction, not a tree concession.
2. wamn-0h0g.18.3 is SCHEMA-COMPAT BY RULING, not by drift. It is not a degradation to be apologized for in a later doc.
3. TYPED-WIT-PER-COMPONENT IS RECORDED AS THE DEMAND-GATED EVOLUTION, WITH ITS REOPEN TRIGGER NAMED: a consumer that needs WIT-LEVEL COMPOSITION — e.g. WAC fusion arriving. Absent that consumer this does not reopen. The spike proved it is buildable when wanted, which is exactly what makes deferring it safe.
4. wamn-0h0g.16.11 / .16.12 / .16.13 CLOSE AS DISSOLVED — all three are consequences of the typed reading only.
5. The spike worktree deletes only AFTER its measurement artifact is banked on this bead. VERIFIED BANKED before deletion: the per-call figures, the structural-equality finding and the ComponentExportIndex self-fencing result are all in this bead's notes. THE NUMBERS ARE THE RULING'S EVIDENCE AND OUTLIVE THE CODE.

RULED BEFORE wamn-0h0g.13.7 CLAIMS, deliberately: the SDK is where this becomes expensive to reverse. Both already-landed lanes (.16.1's NodeInvoker::invoke and .16.2's wamn:node world) rested on this reading and are now ratified rather than provisional.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(catalog): revise the frozen serving-manifest schema onto components + digests + wirings
description: crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs is a FROZEN document schema (.15.61) whose identity is the sha256 of its RFC 8785 canonical bytes — and it is flow-shaped: ServingFlow carries plan_hash (:165), source_artifact (:179), binding_base_artifact (:208); reachable_flows (:416) walks flows; the calls adjacency is a plans+call-flow artifact. Under the closure the manifest projects the component set a pod must warm (component, interface-version, digest), the wiring set, route attachments, and registrations (the one input that unambiguously survives — rule .15.164 with this revision in view). Revise once, re-pin the golden vector once (sha256:9eccdfb2... invalidates — .15.106's producer-side assertion re-pins with it), and keep the digest-named immutable ConfigMap + weld discipline unchanged. Coordinates .15.105 (newtypes), .15.112 (readiness walks the new projection), .15.164/.165 (registration projection + digest stability).
design: Replace ServingManifest with canonical format_version 2. Model deterministically sorted component, wiring, attachment, and registration collections. Components carry component identity, interface version, and digest; wirings carry wiring_id, wiring_version, and graph hash; attachments and registrations target exact wiring identity-version pairs. Remove plan_hash, call adjacency, callable contracts, and all flow_id fields. Mint only from authoritative current records supplied by the component/wiring/attachment/registration owners; never convert legacy plans. from_canonical_bytes accepts and validates only v2 and refuses v1 using a typed frozen literal. Preserve RFC 8785 canonical digest and released-if-and-only-if-attested enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: The public and persisted manifest model has format_version 2 and contains only the four ruled collections with canonical sorting and exact identity fields. No plan, call, adjacency, callable-contract, or flow identity remains in the schema or direct consumers. Attachment and registration targets include both wiring_id and wiring_version. The loader rejects v1 with the exact typed literal and rejects malformed or noncanonical v2 facts. Minting has no legacy-plan conversion or guessed provenance. Existing digest attestation remains exact.
notes: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22 in 71f9bf99. ServingManifest format 2 now canonically closes over sorted component/digest and wiring/version/graph facts; attachments and registrations target exact wiring versions; legacy flow/plan/call identities are absent; format-1 bytes refuse with unsupported-serving-manifest-version. Catalog tests: 58 passed, 2 ignored. Expected transitional compile reds remain in .25.2 legacy mint and .16.8 plan-closure effect reader; no compatibility arm added.
close_reason: Closed

title: [SR-MVP] feat(obs): a span per component invocation at the router seam, and a queue-path trace root
description: There is NO per-component-invocation span wamn-side (the whole tree has two host span sites: wamn_postgres db_span at resources.rs:247, scenario-worker authoring_query). Add the per-invocation span at the router's node-invoke seam carrying wiring id, wiring version, component digest, node id, port — parented to the ingress traceparent. Re-root the queue path: the wamn.trigger root span was removed with the cron path (25129131, stale reference at resources.rs:244), so queue-backed automations currently have no trace root at all. Copy db_span's non-spoofable host-side claim-map enrichment pattern.
close_reason: Implemented at 7167ce0f: RouterDriver emits one host-derived wamn.component.invoke span per node invocation, adopts valid ingress W3C context once per delivery, ignores malformed context, and queued execution runs under an explicit host-scoped wamn.queue.delivery root. Named in-memory exporter proofs cover remote parenting, queue child inheritance/rooting, malformed-context fallback, and exact identity attributes. rustfmt, diff-check, and locked offline metadata passed; the focused test build was hard-capped during cold Wasmtime compilation before affected crates per integrator direction.

comments.author: dkk
comments.text: Integrated on deploy-simplification as 2d3578f7. Root source-reviewed the remote-parent/queue-root spans and ran cargo check --locked --offline -p wamn-schema-control -p wamn-execution-host -p wamn-executor --lib successfully. The focused test-profile build was capped during duplicate cold dependency compilation; named in-memory exporter proofs remain in-tree.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): the observability proofs are unreachable from the orchestrator
description: metricbench::run (tests/integration/src/metricbench.rs:578), dashproof::run, and traceproof::run (tests/system/src/traceproof.rs:146) are library entry points that tests/orchestrator/src/main.rs:31-51 never registers as commands — ~2,160 lines of proof code with no way to run it, guarding the signal the spec makes load-bearing (OTel as THE RECORD). tracebench.rs was deleted (3554f140) and the traceproof/tracebench Job manifests plus the trace-relay fixture are gone from deploy/gates/ and components/fixtures/. title: [SR-MVP] decision(data-access): size the sqlx-over-wamn:postgres seam before committing
description: The ~200-line estimate is unsupported against the tree (grounded): sqlx is not a workspace dependency anywhere; frozen wamn:postgres 0.1 cannot carry sqlx's type system (11-case sql-value, no OIDs/arrays/int16/float32/date-time-interval, type-name string without OID, deliberately no prepare/describe, pg-error drops sqlstate on specific variants; :22-27 freeze rule makes fixing it a 0.2 break); and sqlx's compile-time query_as! macros dispatch on the BUILT-IN postgres/mysql/sqlite backends, so a third-party Database impl plausibly gets NO macro support — which would defeat the compile-time-checked premise of the whole ruling. Prototype and measure, then choose: (a) custom Database backend over the WIT — cheap only if the macros cooperate; (b) keep sqlx::Postgres and swap the TRANSPORT under it (sqlx-core's Socket seam) so the wire protocol, not the type system, crosses the WIT; (c) widen wamn:postgres to 0.2 with OIDs and raw binary encodings and accept the re-freeze. Record which one the ~200-line figure describes. Note docs/archive/results/p0-results.md records the opposite prior ruling (tokio-postgres over sqlx) — the spec supersedes it, but the reasons recorded there are inputs. Blocks the 0.2 contract and the prepare flow.
notes:
RULING (2026-08-18; ratified on the merits. BEAD STAYS OPEN -- closing is D's ratifying act.)

OPTION (b) IS FORECLOSED -- not a cost tradeoff, a contract breach. Prototype (a) under timeboxed
exit discipline. The ~200-line figure describes no branch that survives contact with the tree.

WHY (b) DIES. Grounded in the frozen contract's own security invariants, wamn:postgres@0.1.0 header,
crates/platform/runtime/wit/deps/wamn-postgres/package.wit:4-11:
- "The guest NEVER holds a socket; only resource handles. Connections live in the plugin's pool."
  Handing the guest a byte duplex over sqlx-core's Socket seam IS handing it a socket.
- "RLS claims (tenant/user/role) are derived from the executing workload's identity and injected by
  the plugin via SET LOCAL inside the plugin-managed transaction. There is deliberately NO way for
  a guest to set or override its own claims through this interface." A guest speaking wire protocol
  owns its own session, which is exactly where SET overrides live.
- It further implies the guest performs the Postgres auth handshake, defeating the host-injected
  credential-generation model that the spec's divergence paragraph exists to protect.
STRIKE (b).

WHY (a) AND (c) ARE BOTH GATED ON ONE UNKNOWN: both mean a third-party Database impl, and
sqlx's query_as! dispatches on the BUILT-IN backends. If the macros do not cooperate, the spec's own
premise -- "compile-time checked against the dev environment's applied catalog" -- collapses, and
with it the teeth of the release-closure "catalog >=" rule.
The 11-case sql-value variant is confirmed type-lossy exactly as filed: null, boolean, int32, int64,
float64, text, bytes, numeric, timestamptz, json, uuid -- no OIDs, no arrays, no int16/float32, no
date/time/interval.

EXIT DISCIPLINE (owner addition, binding). TIMEBOX the prototype. It answers ONE question: can a
third-party Database impl participate in query_as!, directly or through a thin wrapper? THREE NAMED
EXITS, and the chosen exit CLOSES this bead:
  E1  Macros cooperate            -> proceed as spec'd.
  E2  Our own compile-time checker over sqlx's offline-cache format. The .sqlx cache is structured
      query->type metadata; verifying it against the applied catalog is real but bounded work.
  E3  Runtime-checked queries, and the "compile-time fact" clause is STRUCK from the release-closure
      rule.
WIT 0.2 WIDENING STAYS FROZEN until the answer exists -- it is the expensive branch and it does not
buy back the macros.

SPEC DEBT (owner-owned, rev 4.1): rev 4's Developer-surface paragraph asserts "a thin sqlx driver
backend over wamn:postgres (~200 lines; sqlx's multi-backend traits exist for exactly this)". The
traits exist; the MACROS do not follow them. Owner is patching that paragraph to prototype-gated
language and striking the figure.

Note for the record: docs/archive/results/p0-results.md records the opposite prior ruling
(tokio-postgres over sqlx). The spec supersedes it, but its recorded reasons are inputs to the
prototype.

SUCCESSOR MEASUREMENT (2026-08-21, wamn-0h0g.22.13): the time-boxed prototype selected the runtime-checking exit. query_as! is built-in-driver-only; a Postgres alias is blocked by private PgArguments/PgRow representation; generic query_as::<DB, T> supports an arbitrary Database. MVP therefore removes the compile-time/offline-cache claim and implements only the runtime-checked custom wamn:postgres Database seam.
close_reason: RATIFIED (owner, 2026-08-18, batched ratification). The ruling, its grounding at HEAD e1d95806, and the owner's additions are recorded verbatim in this bead's notes; this close is the ratifying act, not a summary. Option (b) is FORECLOSED — a contract breach, not a cheaper tradeoff: the frozen wamn:postgres 0.1.0 header states the guest NEVER holds a socket and has deliberately NO way to set its own claims, and a transport swap violates both. Prototype (a) under binding exit discipline: timeboxed, one question (can a third-party Database impl participate in query_as!), three named exits — macros cooperate / our own checker over the sqlx offline-cache format / runtime-checked with the compile-time-fact clause struck from the closure rule — and the chosen exit closes the prototype. WIT 0.2 widening stays frozen until the answer exists. Owner owns the rev-4.1 patch striking the unsupported ~200-line figure.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(run-state): the durability-class fact shape
description: The class gate needs a runtime fact; a Cargo feature is not a candidate (both tiers ship in one image). Three shapes, grounded: (1) per-run runs.durability_class column mirroring the landed capture_mode recipe line for line — derived from the typed admission producer, never a caller parameter (admission.rs:90-99 with its stated authority rationale), CHECK-constrained, immutable under the BEFORE UPDATE trigger, INSERT column privilege withheld from wamn_app (run-state.sql:219-220,285-286,335 is the template); per-run granularity, costs one non-additive migration. (2) admission-class enum with no column, derived from AdmissionProducer — zero schema change but can only vary by trigger source, never by tenant plan ("this customer bought durability" is unrepresentable). (3) env-level tier on registry.env_policies (types.rs:132-157 already carries recovery_domain/backup_cadence/wal_retention — the natural sibling, org-scoped so it maps to billing) — but cannot express per-wiring premium and adds a claim-path lookup. Whichever is chosen, enforcement lands at the four narrow points named on the epic. Blocks the class-gate implementation.
notes:
RULING (2026-08-18; ratified on the merits. BEAD STAYS OPEN -- closing is D's ratifying act.)

COMPOSE OPTIONS (1) AND (3). The PER-RUN COLUMN is the carrier; the ENV/ORG POLICY is the source.

runs.durability_class is written at admission, its value DERIVED from registry.env_policies
(types.rs:132-157 -- the natural sibling of recovery_domain / backup_cadence / wal_retention), never
a caller parameter.

WHY THE COMPOSITION RATHER THAN EITHER/OR:
- Option (1) alone inherits capture_mode's limitation: a producer-derived value cannot vary by
  tenant plan -- the same defect that sinks option (2). "This customer bought durability" stays
  unrepresentable.
- Option (3) alone cannot express per-wiring premium and adds a claim-path lookup.
- Composed: billing maps to the policy, the claim path reads ONE column with no extra lookup, the
  run's class is FROZEN AT ADMISSION even if the plan changes mid-flight, and per-wiring premium
  later becomes a change to the DERIVATION, not to the schema.
- Coherent with exe-model "The boundary": the gate sits at path 3's claim, and path 3 is the only
  path carrying a run row -- paths 1-2 need no column at all.

THE PROVEN MOLD (grounded; this is the landed capture_mode recipe, line for line):
- capture_mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'off' + CHECK constraint -- deploy/sql/run-state.sql:219-220
- immutable via the column-scoped trigger runs_admission_pins_immutable -- :335
- INSERT column privilege withheld from wamn_app
- crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs:90-99 derives it from the typed producer with the
  stated authority rationale: "Capture is derived from the typed producer and is never an admission
  parameter: a caller able to choose it would hold management-only authority over an admitted run's

title: [SR-MVP] feat(ingress): hot HTTP routes run inline on the router — no Postgres in the path
description: The landed routing plugin already resolves attachments DB-free over the weld (flow_http_routing.rs:133-198, reader 3). notes:
MEASUREMENT VERDICT (integrator lane, 2026-08-19, read-only, no code changed): *** BLOCKED ON ABSENT MACHINERY, AND FOUR OWNER RULINGS ARE REQUIRED. NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN. ***

THE CENTRAL FINDING: THE ROUTER HAS ZERO PRODUCTION DRIVERS. wamn_router::route exists at crates/execution/router/src/lib.rs:102, but the ONLY implementor of NodeInvoker in the whole tree is the test fixture Scripted at crates/execution/router/tests/route.rs:53, and the ONLY call to route is crates/execution/router/tests/route.rs:70. The only production crate depending on wamn-router is crates/platform/runtime, and it uses ONLY WiringCache, for invalidation, never resolution. WiringCache::get (resolution.rs:116) and WiringCache::insert (:144) have NO production callers. THERE IS NO CODE ANYWHERE THAT READS A WIRING OUT OF THE STORE AND INSERTS IT INTO THE CACHE -- .18.2 landed only the SQL text, and resolve_active_wiring() at crates/catalog/model/src/wiring_activation.rs:163 is a static str with no Rust caller outside its own live test. So 'walk the resolved wiring inline' presupposes a NodeInvoker bound to a typed node-operation seam AND a store-to-cache resolution path, and NEITHER EXISTS. This bead builds the first driver; it does not retarget an existing one.

SECOND BLOCKER -- 'ON POOLED INSTANCES' IS UNREACHABLE AND WOULD CREATE A DEPENDENCY CYCLE. The .17.7 checkout seam does exist (ExecutionInstancePool::checkout at crates/execution/host/src/pool.rs:324-340; ReusableExecutionInstance :122-155; ExecutionHost impl at crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:769). But NOTHING IN PRODUCTION CONSTRUCTS AN ExecutionInstancePool -- every construction site is under tests/conformance/. And the direction is wrong: flow_http_routing.rs lives in wamn-runtime, loaded by services/host, whose only wamn dep is wamn-runtime; the pool lives in wamn-execution-host, WHICH DEPENDS ON wamn-runtime (crates/execution/host/Cargo.toml:10). Making the routing plugin reach the pool as written yields the cycle wamn-runtime -> wamn-execution-host -> wamn-runtime. Also INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE = 1 (pool.rs:59), so 'pooled' today means prewarmed single-use, not warm reuse.

PREMISE CORRECTION -- THE WELD ARITHMETIC IN THE BEAD IS WRONG. The bead says the weld is identity authority for TWO paths and says do not grow a THIRD reader. crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs:1 says 'one load, one verification, FOUR readers', enumerated at :52-65: plan supply (runner_plan_supply.rs:176), effect authority (connection_http.rs:80), flow-http routing (flow_http_routing.rs:3), jetstream delivery (wamn_jetstream.rs:24,135,166,387). The 'two' that is real is the PROCESS split (:66). A new reader would be a FIFTH. The underlying rule (:53-55, consult by reference, never load/parse/digest-verify your own) is real and correct; only the count is wrong.

ANCHORS VERIFIED: flow_http_routing.rs:133-198 CORRECT (734 lines; reader 3 verbatim at :3). guest.rs:85-118 CORRECT, real path components/ingress/flow-http/src/guest.rs (Backend::begin :85-117, wait :119-140). flow_invocation.rs:362 CORRECT but admit_sql IS NOT IN THAT FILE -- it is crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs:378, reached via InvocationBackend::admit (decl :325, Postgres impl :648).

A WIT CHANGE IS REQUIRED AND IT IS TWICE-VENDORED AND FROZEN BY A LITERAL. record route-definition has no disposition field. The two package.wit copies (components/ingress/flow-http/wit/deps/... and crates/platform/runtime/wit/deps/...) are byte-identical by test and pinned by crates/platform/runtime/tests/flow_http_routing_wit_coherence.rs, which freezes the record body as a string literal at :126-142 (const ROUTE_DEFINITION) plus the routes signature at :157. Any disposition field means THREE mandatory edits.

THE FOUR OWNER RULINGS: (1) Where does the router driver run, and how does the wash-host ingress process reach pooled instances -- extract the pool to a third crate both can depend on, move the driver into wamn-runtime, or invoke without a pool for MVP and defer pooling? This has a dependency-cycle consequence. (2) *** WHAT ACTUALLY INVOKES A NODE? NodeCall names component plus operation (walk.rs:203-210), but there is NO WIT INTERFACE IN THE TREE for 'invoke operation X on component Y', and no component-per-node catalog since components/nodes was deleted by .12.2. THIS IS THE MISSING KEYSTONE FOR THIS BEAD AND FOR .19.6. *** (3) What shape does route disposition take on the wire -- a field on route-definition, a separate dispatch func, or an out-of-band host decision? (4) Given INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE = 1, is 'pooled instances' prewarm-and-destroy (works today) or warm reuse (explicitly forbidden at pool.rs:53-58 until windowed state ships)?

SEQUENCING RECOMMENDATION: the router driver plus the node-operation seam is ONE shared prerequisite for .19.1 and .19.6. Land it once as a new crate (zero file collisions), after which the two beads are independent, small, and commit separately.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(authoring): where the in-draft cases contract attaches
description: exe-model.md keeps the "same in-draft test contract" but never says whether cases attach to a WIRING, a COMPONENT, or both. notes:
RULING (2026-08-18; ratified on the merits. BEAD STAYS OPEN -- closing is D's ratifying act.)

CASES ATTACH TO THE WIRING. Components are not carriers of the in-draft contract.

GROUNDED AT HEAD e1d95806:
- crates/execution/flow-model/src/test_set.rs:1 states today's carrier outright: "Bounded validation
  for the `cases` array carried by a flow document". TestSetCase is { case_id, input, expect }
  (:17-21) with MAX_TEST_SET_CASES = 256 (:12). A golden input plus a required observable is an
  END-TO-END shape, not a unit-of-logic shape.
- exe-model.md's compare table maps "Flow doc: 9-node language + expressions + in-draft tests" onto
  "Developer components (WIT ops) + user wirings; SAME in-draft test contract". The flow doc's
  successor as the COMPOSITION artifact is the wiring, so the test contract's lineage lands there.
- The sentence that reads component-shaped resolves the same way once read whole. "Promotion and
  the release closure": "component-vs-schema correctness is the gate's jurisdiction (cases run
  against the real applied catalog at authoring and at promote-time re-gate), never a packaging
  precondition." That says you CATCH a component's schema mismatch BY running the WIRING's cases

  http-entry -> entity.<op> -> respond.

under epic T (.21.x). Not MVP, and not a second contract competing with this one.

document, which .18.1's description already anticipates ("in-draft cases array rides the doc").

design: Validate wiring compatibility from the admitted typed component facts produced by wamn-0h0g.21.1. No subtyping or compatibility fallback exists, and admitted component facts project onto the lowering input without semantic loss.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(router): version-keyed wiring resolution cache
description: Resolution reads the active wiring version from the env-hot store once and serves every subsequent delivery from memory — the hot HTTP path touches no Postgres (spec path-1 rule). Model on ResolutionPlanCache's deterministic entry-bounded eviction (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs:75-160) but key (env, wiring id, active version) and invalidate on pointer flip rather than never. Include a cache-hit metric beside the existing wamn.run.* instruments. Blocked by the wiring store (epic P).
close_reason: [3ae75699] Version-keyed wiring resolution cache landed in the new crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs, modelled on ResolutionPlanCache's shape verbatim (Mutex<CacheState>, HashMap + VecDeque recency, touch() on hit, evict from the front) with the one structural difference the bead demanded: it INVALIDATES rather than never. *** DESIGN CALL WORTH RATIFYING — THE CACHE IS TWO LEVELS, AND IT HAS TO BE. The bead asked for a key of (env, wiring id, active version) AND invalidation on pointer flip; those only cohere if the cache also holds the pointer, because otherwise you must already know the active version to look anything up, i.e. you have already read Postgres. So: entries: HashMap<EntryKey, Arc<Wiring>> on the full triple (a version is IMMUTABLE — catalog.wirings.version monotonic, content pinned by confirmed_definition_hash — so a resident entry can never be the wrong answer to its own key), plus active: HashMap<Pointer, u32> mirroring catalog.wiring_activation as the ONLY mutable half and the only half invalidate touches. It pays off on ROLLBACK: a flip back to a still-resident version is an in-memory hit. One addition the model does not need — an evicted entry drops the pointer that named it, so a pointer can never read as a hit and find nothing (pinned by an_evicted_entry_leaves_behind_no_pointer). *** METRIC: one counter wamn.run.wiring.cache.lookups split by a two-valued result=hit|miss attribute, so the hit rate — the number that says whether the hot path is actually staying out of Postgres — is a single query; no wiring/tenant attribute (unbounded). Registered via the same global-meter pattern as memory_metrics.rs:56. DEPENDENCY ACCEPTED, FLAGGED: opentelemetry with the metrics feature added to a crate that previously had exactly one dependency. Integrator verified the Cargo.lock delta is a SINGLE LINE (+ opentelemetry under wamn-router), no version churn, no new crate; the bead explicitly scopes a cache-hit metric, so this is proportionate. Reversible by moving the counter to the host. BOTH MUTANTS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY IN THE MAIN TREE against baseline sha256 43382978f4f7a9d84a9e72a752dbf82f5f01c94c9c9ccf80025f1d1614a0acf1: (a) invalidate's .remove(&pointer).is_some() -> .contains_key(&pointer) (reports truthfully, forgets nothing) failed EXACTLY ONE named test, invalidate_sends_the_next_lookup_back_to_the_store at tests/resolution.rs:93; (b) eviction's .pop_front() -> .pop_back() (evict most-recent) failed EXACTLY ONE named test, eviction_is_bounded_and_least_recently_used at tests/resolution.rs:148. Restored byte-identical after each; sha matches baseline; wamn-router 49 passed / 0 failed. *** CARVE-OUT, FILED AS wamn-0h0g.16.15 (P0, dep on .18.2): invalidate has NO PRODUCTION CALLER — its caller is .18.2's doorbell subscriber, which a concurrent lane owns, so the two halves exist untied and a pointer flip does not yet invalidate the cache. title: [SR-MVP] W — Observability: OTel end-to-end and the live view
description:
exe-model.md §Observability: OTel end-to-end — traceparent from ingress, one span per component invocation and per effect, per-wiring/registration metrics (throughput, error, ack lag, DLQ depth). The studio live view taps at router edges — ephemeral payload previews on a bounded subject, possible precisely because the router owns every edge. No durable node facts, no get-run for the default tier. R2 makes OTel THE RECORD — this epic must land with or before the durability cut.

GROUNDED FACTS: today there are exactly TWO host-created span sites in the whole tree (wamn_postgres db_span at resources.rs:247; scenario-worker authoring_query) — no per-invocation span, no span on the HTTP effect (connection_http.rs, 1203 lines, warn-only), no queue-path trace root (wamn.trigger was removed with the cron path, 25129131). title: [SR-MVP] Q — Ingress: three paths onto the router
description:
exe-model.md §Ingress paths: (1) hot HTTP — landed routing plugin resolves the attachment -> router runs the wiring inline on pooled instances -> respond; no run row, no queue row, no Postgres; backpressure = bounded in-flight per route (chart value) then 429. (2) streams — per-registration durable pull consumers ({max_batch,max_wait}); registrations declare input: event | batch; batch delivers as one router run with the ordered array; ack-after-completion; nack under the consumer retry budget; poison to a capped per-registration DLQ subject; MQTT via NATS native bridging; the .15.95 manifest registration-identity gate unchanged. (3) automations — the SQL queue survives; a worker claims (SKIP LOCKED, lease) and hands to the ROUTER; begin/wait + same-key-same-outcome survive. §The boundary: emit publishes a derived event with an author-supplied dedup id; Class-D admission dedups on it — exactly-once-admitted.

GROUNDED FACTS: today the three paths are ONE path — HTTP and events both converge on admit_sql (crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs) and the same claim; the spec extracts two new paths out of the one that exists. flow_http_routing.rs is already DB-free over the weld (reader 3); the .15.95 gate is landed at consumer bind (wamn_jetstream.rs:437-495, reader 4) and generalizes for free. The materializer acks after ADMISSION today, not completion; input: event|batch does not exist; NO DLQ path exists anywhere (run_dead_letters was retired outright). The only bounded in-flight code in tree is flow-engine's throttle.rs:90-127. The classifier is welded into the claim predicate itself (EXISTS(effect_attempts) in select_production_claim_sql) — lifting it is epic R's seam.

title: [SR-MVP] P — Wirings as gated tenant data
description:
exe-model.md R3: wirings are data — versioned, gated, hot-activated by pointer flip, relocated from lattice state into our gated tenant store; tenant rows, not CRDs. §Tradeoffs owns the walk-back: hot wiring is bounded by the gate, types, versioning, and instant rollback.

Type-compat validation is shape-safety over component WIT ports; the seconds-fast gate carries semantic safety (its latency is a product requirement).

title: [SR-MVP] O — Pooled execution platform-wide

exe-model.md §Pooling, restored in full: pools keyed per component digest, shared across every wiring and tenant flow using that component; instance REUSE (linear memory across inputs) stays off until windowed state ships with explicit affinity; per-host pool sizing is a chart value; audit B's fresh-instance conformance re-runs under the allocator; the g2br.16 kill-switch narrows per-host -> per-capability, mechanism kept.

title: [SR-MVP] N — Host router: rehost the graph walk
description:
exe-model.md rev 4 §Execution mechanics: a host-native router replaces the flowrunner guest. Per delivery: resolve the wiring (active version from the env-hot store, cached by version) -> walk the graph in frontier order -> per node, acquire a pooled instance of that node's component and invoke the operation over a typed WIT seam -> route outputs by port -> terminal respond/emit/discard, bounded by a per-delivery hop limit.

The router MUST be a shared library crate (crates/execution/router) linked by BOTH services/host (ingress path 1 needs in-process execution) and services/executor (path 3), mirroring how crates/execution/host is linked today. title: [SR-MVP] decision(publish): where does the serving manifest's registration projection come from
description:
## Why -- BLOCKING. Found by wamn-0h0g.15.14 while implementing the mint, and measured on live PG 18.6.

*** catalog.event_registrations IS NOT IN THE CONTROL DATABASE. *** It appears 8x in
deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql and ZERO times in deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql; a freshly
bootstrapped control database has 16 catalog.* relations and event_registrations is not among them.
Every other manifest input IS in the control store: release_flows, flow_artifacts,
execution_bundles, validated_flow_drafts, release_attachments, release_sources.

control-portable-store.sql:6-9 states the design -- "both databases can therefore carry catalog.*;
database RESIDENCY, not a renamed schema, distinguishes them." Registrations were simply not carried
over. Meanwhile ServingManifest's own documentation names jetstream delivery as reader 4, gating on
`registrations`, so they must travel in the manifest. And publish step A holds NO project connection
by its own explicit contract, so it cannot read them.

The mint therefore ships today with the registration set as a REQUIRED ARGUMENT, forcing every call
site to decide rather than defaulting to empty. That was deliberate: left as a read that silently
returned nothing, a manifest with an empty registration set is a VALID manifest with a REAL DIGEST --
which is precisely the dual-representation under-report wamn-0h0g.15.159 was spent deleting.

## The options, with their evidence

(a) MOVE catalog.event_registrations INTO THE CONTROL PORTABLE STORE. The whole exposure plane
    (release_exposure_manifests, release_sources, release_attachments) is already there, which makes
    the absence look like an omission rather than a decision. Cost: a deploy/sql change plus a
    recomputed control-portable-retained-shape-drift fingerprint. NOTE the attnum hazard --
    control-portable-store.sql hashes a.attnum, so an already-provisioned control database needs a
    retirement arm that refuses by name, exactly as .15.159 needed.
(b) THE COMPOSING PUBLISHER SUPPLIES THEM, holding both connections. This is what wamn-0h0g.8.22
    described before rulings .13.43/.13.44 superseded it and re-anchored the publish path on .15.14.
    There is no composer in the tree today. The shipped mint signature is shaped for this option.
(c) REGISTRATIONS DO NOT TRAVEL IN THE MANIFEST FOR MVP, and reader 4 keeps a database read. This
    contradicts crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs:4, which calls the manifest "the SOLE
    carrier of release identity".

## Why it blocks

wamn-0h0g.15.97 pushes these bytes as an OCI artifact and .15.98 writes them into GitOps
desired state. Shipping a manifest whose registration set is structurally absent, and then
discovering it must travel, means re-minting every digest already published.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded ruling naming one of (a), (b), (c) with its rationale; wamn-0h0g.15.14's mint call sites
updated to match; the ServingManifest documentation and release_manifest.rs:4's "sole carrier" claim
reconciled with the ruling.
notes:
EXE-MODEL TRIAGE 2026-08-18: the spec FORECLOSES option (c) — exe-model.md §Ingress paths 2 keeps the .15.95 manifest registration-identity gate ('the host checks identity ∈ active manifest before the router sees the event'), so registrations must travel in the manifest. Premise re-verified at HEAD: catalog.event_registrations appears 9x in catalog-schema.sql, 0x in control-portable-store.sql. Live choice narrows to (a) move the relation into the control portable store (SQL move + retained-shape refingerprint, mind the attnum hazard) vs (b) a composing publisher holding both connections (no composer exists; the shipped mint signature is already shaped for it). Rule this WITH the serving-manifest schema revision (wamn-0h0g.25.1) in view — registrations are the one manifest input that unambiguously survives the flows->wirings re-projection.
RULING (2026-08-18; ratified on the merits. BEAD STAYS OPEN -- closing is D's ratifying act.)

OPTION (a): MOVE catalog.event_registrations INTO THE CONTROL PORTABLE STORE.

GROUNDED AT HEAD e1d95806:
- Confirmed absent from deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql (zero hits); present 8x in
  deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql, table at :1704, PK (tenant_id, catalog_id, registration_id).
- (c) is foreclosed twice over: exe-model.md rev 4 section "Ingress paths" case 2 keeps the .15.95
  identity gate ("the host checks identity IN active manifest before the router sees the event");
  and crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs:1-8 calls the mounted ConfigMap "the *sole*
  carrier of release identity".
- (b) rejected: no composer exists in the tree; publish step A holds no project connection by its
  own explicit contract; and it re-opens .8.22, which .13.43/.13.44 already superseded.
- (a) matches the store's own stated design, control-portable-store.sql:6-9 -- "both databases can
  therefore carry catalog.*; database RESIDENCY, not a renamed schema, distinguishes them." The
  whole exposure plane (release_exposure_manifests, release_sources, release_attachments) is
  already there, which makes the absence an omission rather than a decision.

FACT CORRECTION (grounded finding, not an owner call): THE STATED COST IS ALREADY BUDGETED.
control-portable-store.sql:11-13 requires the control-portable-retained-shape-drift fingerprint be
regenerated "whenever a retained relation's shape moves (wamn-0h0g.15.22)". .15.22 is the wave-13
registries/baseline regeneration -- already planned, already paying exactly this cost. Land .15.164
inside wave 13 and the fingerprint work is free.

RIDER (accepted): the attnum hazard is real. control-portable-store.sql hashes a.attnum, so an
already-provisioned control database needs a retirement arm that refuses BY NAME, exactly as
.15.159 needed.

SUPERSESSION -- NAMED, NOT BURIED:
This ruling and .15.165 together supersede the ENV-HOT CONDITION CLAUSE of wamn-0h0g.13.53 (CLOSED
2026-08-16, "PRESERVE HOT-EDITABILITY BY THE SAME SPLIT": registration IDENTITY is release content
carried in the manifest; the CONDITION stays an environment-hot column read by the materializer at
evaluation). Under exe-model rev 4 the materializer reads the MOUNTED MANIFEST rather than a
per-event project-database column -- simpler and plane-clean -- so the split's hot half no longer
holds.

CONSEQUENCE TO TRACK (found while citing): .13.53's own recorded CONSEQUENCE was "ServingManifest.
registrations changes from the stored document verbatim to IDENTITY-ONLY, as frozen in
wamn-0h0g.15.61" (closed, commit e38dd2a1). Superseding the env-hot clause REVERSES that
consequence, so the identity-only shape frozen in .15.61 must be re-opened deliberately rather than
allowed to drift. Rule .15.164 / .15.165 / the .15.61 shape together.
close_reason: RATIFIED (owner, 2026-08-18, batched ratification). The ruling, its grounding at HEAD e1d95806, and the owner's additions are recorded verbatim in this bead's notes; this close is the ratifying act, not a summary. Option (a): move catalog.event_registrations into the control portable store. Rides wamn-0h0g.15.22 (its fingerprint regeneration is already budgeted there); attnum retirement-arm rider accepted. SUPERSEDES the env-hot condition clause of wamn-0h0g.13.53, named not buried — and reverses .13.53's own consequence, the identity-only ServingManifest shape frozen in .15.61, which must therefore be re-opened deliberately.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): move project-env database ownership off wamn_app
description:
## Why -- OWNER RULING R9, 2026-08-17. Also filed as finding R45 (docs/archive/findings.md).

crates/control/provision/src/database.rs renders the CNPG Database CR with owner = APP_ROLE, and
APP_ROLE is wamn_app. THE ROLE THAT GUEST-AUTHORED SQL EXECUTES AS OWNS EVERY PRODUCTION
PROJECT-ENV DATABASE. The doc comment's own rationale -- 'so no tenant database is
superuser-owned' -- optimised superuser away and landed on the guest-reachable role.

Ownership confers implicit rights no grant matrix expresses: ALTER DATABASE, DROP DATABASE,
CREATE SCHEMA, GRANT ON DATABASE, TEMPORARY. NOCREATEDB restrains none of them on an
already-owned database. Five in-tree probes ALREADY treat owning the current database as
DISQUALIFYING for a runtime role (run_plane.rs:3537/:3576/:5069/:5096, authoring.rs:196), so
accepting this would overrule the platform's own written adjudication.

The owner rejected postgres-as-owner as the one-token trap: it swaps escalation-from-below for
maximal-blast-radius-from-above and makes the five probes false in the opposite direction.

## Scope -- the ruling's four riders, all binding

1. OWNER-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION: wamn_db_owner is NOLOGIN with ZERO grants, ZERO memberships and
   NO generation pair. It holds title; nothing connects as it. That keeps it out of the
   credential-rotation machinery -- a role nobody logs in as has nothing to rotate.
2. THE PROBES FLIP FROM DISQUALIFYING TO ASSERTING, so the migration's completeness is proven
   rather than assumed.
3. THE MIGRATION IS THE CR RECONCILER'S JOB, idempotently -- no bespoke one-shot script.
4. The naming survives the greenfield rule.

## *** OPERATOR HAZARD MEASURED DURING IMPLEMENTATION -- READ BEFORE ROLLOUT ***

ALTER DATABASE ... OWNER TO DESTROYS wamn_app's CONNECT GRANT. With wamn_app as owner, datacl is
{wamn_app=CTc/wamn_app} -- the explicit GRANT CONNECT MERGES INTO THE OWNER'S ACLITEM. Changing
the owner rewrites that aclitem and wamn_app loses CONNECT outright. Correct end state is
{wamn_db_owner=CTc/wamn_db_owner,wamn_app=c/wamn_db_owner}. An operator who applies the new CR
and stops leaves the runtime UNABLE TO REACH ITS OWN DATABASE. The privilege SQL is therefore
mandatory on existing environments, and the owner change must precede the CONNECT grant.
acceptance_criteria: No project-env database is owned by wamn_app; wamn_db_owner is NOLOGIN with zero grants, zero memberships and no password; wamn_app holds neither CREATE nor TEMPORARY on the database and owns zero objects; the ownership probes assert the positive state; convergence is idempotent on re-run; the CONNECT-grant ordering hazard is documented at the emission site.
close_reason: [47b404cf] wamn_db_owner NOLOGIN now owns every project-env database; wamn_app holds CONNECT only. Zero grants, zero memberships, no password, no generation pair -- it holds title and nothing connects as it, so nothing rotates. *** OPERATOR HAZARD MEASURED AND NOT IN ANY BRIEF: ALTER DATABASE ... OWNER TO DESTROYS wamn_app's CONNECT GRANT. With wamn_app as owner, datacl is {wamn_app=CTc/wamn_app} -- the explicit GRANT CONNECT MERGES INTO THE OWNER'S ACLITEM -- so changing the owner rewrites it and wamn_app loses CONNECT outright. Correct end state {wamn_db_owner=CTc/wamn_db_owner,wamn_app=c/wamn_db_owner}. An operator who applies the new CR and stops leaves the runtime UNABLE TO REACH ITS OWN DATABASE. The owner change is emitted FIRST and the privilege SQL is MANDATORY on existing environments; documented at both emission sites. *** Convergence is the reconciler's job: re-setting an existing owner is a no-op (verified by applying the batch twice) and CNPG maps spec.owner to both CREATE DATABASE OWNER and ALTER DATABASE OWNER TO, so existing CRs converge. No one-shot script. MUTATION-VERIFIED: owner set back to APP_ROLE turns the ownership probe red; restored. pg_shdepend zero-owned-objects carries a non-vacuity counter-assert of 2. PREMISE CORRECTION: ensure_effect_writer_acl_role_sql has NO advisory lock -- the advisory-locked create-or-harden house shape is ensure_control_author_acl_role_sql, which was followed (it also re-hardens on attribute drift, and avoids duplicating a gate-mutant NEEDLE literal). Closes finding R45. DEFERRED, filed separately: provision-project (legacy 2.3) creates postgres-owned databases -- create_database_sql has no OWNER clause -- the other failure mode the ruling names.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(publish): drop members_json and re-derive release membership from release_flows
description:
## Why -- OWNER RULING 2026-08-17, cut-3(a) single representation

wamn-0h0g.8.7 surfaced this: catalog.release_manifests.members_json and
catalog.release_flows are TWO REPRESENTATIONS OF ONE FACT, and the immutability
trigger has now proven why dual representations rot -- one is SEALED while the
other must GROW under the tested-publish model, so they cannot stay equal.

Publish step A appends a release_flows member to the catalog version the
validated draft was validated against (catalog_heads.applied_catalog_version).
release_manifests carries a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE immutability trigger, so
members_json can never be corrected. It permanently under-reports.

THE OWNER REJECTED BOTH ALTERNATIVES, WITH REASONS TO PRESERVE:
- Leaving it as built "ships a permanent lie into two live verbs."
- Minting applied+1 per tested publish is "the trap-shaped correct answer":
  bumping the catalog version per tested publish REDEFINES THE OPERATIONAL
  MEANING OF THE VERSIONING UNIT -- every publish becomes a catalog event, which
  collides with head-pointer semantics and the no-pinning model's "the release is
  the unit of change." A semantics change smuggled in as bookkeeping.

## Scope -- the ruling's three riders, all binding

1. RE-DERIVE THE TWO CONSUMERS FROM release_flows, KEEPING THE SAME REFUSAL
   LITERALS. services/ctl/src/copy_project_env.rs:763,772 (source-vs-destination
   membership comparison) and services/ctl/src/migrate_catalog.rs:599 (applied
   release manifest driving migration). `catalog-release-manifest-missing` KEEPS
   ITS NAME; its trigger condition becomes "no members for the applied version".
   Also re-point services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs:872,1706 and
   services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs:1088.

2. *** members_json DROPS IN THIS BEAD. It does not linger deprecated. A
   sealed-but-stale column that two verbs USED to read is exactly what a future
   lane resurrects. *** Both definitions go: deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:207 and
   deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql:78. The many test fixtures that INSERT
   members_json must move with it.

3. THIS TAKES THE HARD EDGE BEFORE wamn-0h0g.15.14 WIRES A CALLER. The gap being
   unreachable today (mint_tested_release has no caller) is THE DEADLINE
   ARGUMENT, NOT A DEFERRAL ARGUMENT.

## Implementation note measured 2026-08-17

deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql:869-918 self-asserts a
`control-portable-retained-shape-drift` fingerprint -- sha256 over
column:attnum:attname:type:notnull:default plus constraint defs for 17 retained
relations, catalog.release_manifests among them -- against the STORED LITERAL
b08e42cb2130ae46ebdcbb7c030f566ce37c29a287a5fdcae2ad6fb30cc82d29. Dropping a
column changes that digest, and the new value can only be obtained by applying
the modified DDL to a live PostgreSQL and reading it back. That literal is NOT
covered by the wamn-0h0g.15.22 freeze (which is architecture/*.json and
tools/gate-mutants EXPECTED_SHA), so this bead updates it itself.

Check the catalog inventory assertion at :776-786 and the wamn_run inventory at
:790-796 for the same reason.
acceptance_criteria: members_json no longer exists in either schema file; copy_project_env, migrate_catalog and the publish paths derive membership from catalog.release_flows; catalog-release-manifest-missing keeps its literal and fires when the applied version has no members; the retained-shape fingerprint literal is recomputed against a live PostgreSQL; and no caller of mint_tested_release exists until this has landed.
close_reason: [cd9462f9] members_json DROPPED, membership derived from catalog.release_flows. THE BEAD UNDERSTATED THE DEFECT AND THE CORRECTION IS MEASURED: there are TWO deferred constraint triggers (release_manifest_members_complete on release_manifests, release_flows_match_manifest on release_flows), release_flows FKs to release_manifests so the guard always runs, and appending a member to a sealed manifest in a later transaction was HARD-REFUSED at COMMIT with catalog-release-membership-mismatch -- not 'under-reporting'. Proven on live PG 18.6, and proven to commit after the drop. Exactly THREE production consumers (a prior list of six counted test-module sites); NO production Rust ever INSERTed the column. RIDER 2: register_release_manifest is insert-or-verify-identical, not DO NOTHING -- the conflict arm verifies every column the INSERT supplies, the fourth being verified_publisher_principal (IS NULL is the identity check); refusal proven live. RIDER 1: tier-move doc comment sits above the surviving RAISE. *** RIDER 3'S PREMISE IS FALSE: no gate-mutant ever pinned the SQL-side membership raise -- all 37 scripts searched, none even reads catalog-schema.sql -- so there is nothing to retire and no coverage to move. The enforcement arrives at the Rust tier with no mutant, as it had none at the SQL tier.
