title: [SR-MVP] fix(deploy): admit the plan registry in the runner egress policy
description:
## Why

Found while taking wamn-0h0g.15.49 (2026-08-17). Every plan pull the executor makes
is denied at the network, and nothing in the tree admits it.

## Measured

deploy/platform/runner-netpol.yaml declares runner-egress-platform selecting
wamn.io/egress-profile: runner with policyTypes: [Egress], which the runner pod
template carries. It admits exactly four peers: kube-dns 53, postgres 5432, NATS
4222, otel-collector 4317.

The plan pull added by wamn-0h0g.15.12 is HOST-process egress — oci-client running
inside wamn-run-worker, not guest wasi:http — so the --allowed-hosts guest
allowlist is irrelevant to it and the netpol is the only gate. Checked every policy
in the repo: runner-netpol.yaml, runner-connection-egress.example.yaml, and
deploy/gates/runner-connection-egress.yaml (which admits only app: serve-echo
8091). NONE admits app: registry or TCP 5000.

## WHY IT FAILS LATE, WHICH IS THE DANGEROUS PART

OciPlanSource::new never connects — it only builds a client
(crates/platform/runtime/src/plan_artifact.rs). So host construction SUCCEEDS, the
pod welds to its release and goes ready, and the denial surfaces per-run at the
first pull rather than at startup. A welded pod that cannot supply a single plan is
exactly the silently-degraded state the fail-closed posture exists to forbid.

## Scope

Add the plan registry as an egress peer in deploy/platform/runner-netpol.yaml:
namespaceSelector wamn-system plus podSelector app: registry on TCP 5000,
following that file's stated sibling-selectors-under-one-to-item rule. Check
whether deploy/gates/runner-connection-egress.yaml needs the same peer for the
in-cluster gates.

## Boundary

Network policy only. Does not change the pull, the posture, or runner.yaml — which
already records this gap in a comment pointing here.
acceptance_criteria:
The runner egress policy admits the plan registry on TCP 5000, and a run whose plan
must be pulled succeeds in-cluster instead of failing at the network.
close_reason: Commit 2e851ddf. runner-netpol.yaml admits the plan registry (namespaceSelector wamn-system + podSelector app: registry as SIBLINGS under one to-item, TCP 5000); all 6 peer entries now carry both selectors so no rule widens to a namespace. Selector/port verified against the manifests that define them and against DEFAULT_PLAN_ARTIFACT_BASE. PREMISE CORRECTION: 'every pull is denied at the network' is NOT live -- kind runs kindnetd, which does not enforce NetworkPolicy (already recorded in docs/archive/platform/builder.md and findings.md; no Calico/Cilium anywhere in the tree). So the defect was a manifest lying about its own posture plus a hard failure the moment a policy-enforcing CNI arrives, and the acceptance clause about a pulled run succeeding in-cluster is satisfied by construction, not measurement. runner.yaml's STILL-BLOCKED comment updated. Also recorded, not fixed: --plan-artifact-base defaults to the bare name registry:5000, which a pod outside wamn-system resolves locally first.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): add the executor readiness gate once its policy exists
description: Split out of wamn-0h0g.15.49 under the granularity rule. VERIFIED AND UNCHANGED: the run worker exposes no listener of any kind (grep for readiness/readyz/healthz/bind_addr/WAMN_.*BIND over services/executor/ and crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs returns zero; runner.yaml has no ports: block and no Service), so this needs a listener, a port and a readiness state machine, not a manifest edit. Under docs/exe-model.md the gate asserts three things: (1) the release manifest is loaded and verified — already structural, and the probe must NOT re-check it, since passing the root makes host construction fail on an unusable manifest; (2) every connection requirement of the release is bound in this environment, keyed on ServingFlow::binding_base_artifact against catalog.connection_bindings.artifact_hash and explicitly never source_artifact; (3) the release's component digests are resident in their per-digest instance pools. The active-synchronous-plan-set prefetch leg drops — execution plans, OciPlanSource and ResolutionPlanCache retire with the compiler. No runtime-revision check ships (wamn-0h0g.5.16 DESIGN, ruling 4). Also rewrites deploy/platform/runner.yaml's STARTUP + ROLLOUTS paragraph, whose whole justification is that there is no readiness endpoint and which is what makes maxUnavailable: 0 + minReadySeconds: 30 the rollout guard today; the probe TRANSPORT is an open decision belonging with .5.16's policy.
acceptance_criteria:
The executor exposes a readiness signal that is false until the manifest is
verified, the active synchronous plan set is resident and hash-verified, and every
connection requirement of the release is bound; runner.yaml carries the probe and
its STARTUP + ROLLOUTS paragraph no longer claims there is no readiness endpoint.
close_reason: Shipped in 601149ff: router-only executor image/deployment and bounded /readyz transport over RouterReadinessProbe

title: [SR-MVP] chore(exec): delete the dead artifact-reader plane
description:
## Why

Split from wamn-0h0g.15.12 (OWNER RULING 2026-08-17: "Split: deletion first"). That bead bundled a pure deletion with a design rewrite; this is the deletion half, and it carries no design decision at all.

VERIFIED 2026-08-17 at e87133fa: `ControlArtifactReader` HAS ZERO PRODUCTION CONSUMERS. Tree-wide it appears only in its own module, its own live test, and the `pub use` at crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/mod.rs:12. No host, service, gate or bench ever constructs it. The .9.10/.5.14 artifact-reader plane is therefore DEAD CODE: removing it is not a cutover, changes no behaviour, and needs no replacement to exist first.

## Scope

Delete the plane shipped by commits 7ac999b4 + 11aa572b (19 files, verified as their exact union) except the two files that survive it, plus the two guards whose subject dies with them.

  services/ctl/tests/artifact_reader_generation_live.rs (1424)
  crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/control_artifact_reader.rs (877)
  crates/platform/runtime/tests/control_artifact_reader_live.rs (480)

GUARD DELETES — they die with their subjects:
  tools/gate-mutants/artifact-reader-credential.sh (485 lines, 24 EXPECTED_SHA assignments — the single largest block in the 162-assignment guard surface)
  tools/gate-mutants/control-artifact-reader.sh (282 lines)

EDITS:
  crates/control/provision/src/lib.rs — mod at :53, the pub use blocks at :73/:74, and the reader names inside the :109 (name) and :121 (secret) re-export blocks
  crates/control/provision/src/{name,secret,sql}.rs — 51 / 26 / 55 hits
  crates/control/provision/Cargo.toml — the orphan cascade below
  services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs — 375 hits: ~25 reader-only fns from :1304 to :2811, the five args fields at :196/:210/:224/:237/:242, validate_artifact_reader_flag_closure at :309, and their dispatch inside run()
  services/ctl/tests/effect_writer_generation_live.rs:89-93 — the out-of-domain break: five reader fields in a ProvisionProjectEnvArgs literal, belonging to the effect-writer plane
  crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/mod.rs — :2 and :12
  crates/platform/runtime/Cargo.toml — :12 wamn-control-provision, orphaned by this deletion and only by it
  docs/archive/build-and-test.md:5998-6042 — the recipe section "SR-MVP — control artifact-reader credential (wamn-0h0g.9.10)", whose guard this commit deletes

NOT TOUCHED: tools/gate-mutants/plan-supply.sh (survives; its subject is mostly runner_plan_supply.rs, and only its moving-head-query mutant dies — with .15.12) and crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs beyond the two deletion-caused obligations recorded in DESIGN.

NOTHING TO DELETE ELSEWHERE, verified zero hits: architecture/, deploy/, every .sql / .json / .yaml, tests/, test-support/, components/, tools/ outside the two named guards, and services/ctl/src/*.rs outside provision_project_env.rs (the clap args are derived on ProvisionProjectEnvArgs itself, so no main.rs edit; there is no [[test]] entry for the deleted live test either). The reader DB role and Secret existed only as ctl-generated output, never as a checked-in manifest, so .15.22 has no reader rows to sweep.

## Boundary

NO REWRITE. The compile baseline stays at exactly 4 errors in plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs (:14, :206 x2, :388); this bead does not fix them and must not try. OCI pull-by-digest, the weld construction site, the manifest-derived plan supply, plan-supply.sh's repair, the executor registry knob, and the deletion of WamnPostgres::resolution_plan_bytes all remain on wamn-0h0g.15.12.
design:
THE ORPHAN CASCADE IN crates/control/provision/Cargo.toml — RECORDED NOWHERE BEFORE, measured 2026-08-17.

Commit 7ac999b4 added four normal dependencies for the reader and moved chrono up out of dev-dependencies. Which of them the deletion orphans, verified by grep over src/ and tests/:
  serde (:34)          — used ONLY by artifact_reader.rs. ORPHANED, remove.
  sha2 (:35)           — used ONLY by name.rs:12 and :351, and :351 is inside artifact_reader_scope_digest. ORPHANED, remove.
  tokio-postgres (:38) — the only REAL code use is artifact_reader.rs; the hits in name.rs:489 and sql.rs:1565 are COMMENTS. ORPHANED, remove.
  chrono (:36)         — also used by secret.rs. KEEP (and it must not go back to dev-dependencies: secret.rs is a normal module).
  url (:37)            — used by secret.rs, dump.rs and six tests. KEEP.
And the feature it gates:
  postgres-config = ["dep:tokio-postgres"] (:11) — gates exactly three sites: lib.rs:72, artifact_reader.rs:236, artifact_reader.rs:716. Its ONLY consumer in the workspace is crates/platform/runtime/Cargo.toml:12, which this bead deletes. DEAD, remove the feature too.
Other dependents of wamn-control-provision are unaffected: services/cdc-reader (no features), tests/integration (ops), services/ctl (ops).

TWO OBLIGATIONS INSIDE runner_plan_supply.rs THAT BELONG HERE. Both were created by .15.41's cache re-homing and are discharged by this deletion, not by the rewrite:
  1. ResolutionPlanCache::from_non_zero was private and is now pub(crate) SOLELY because ControlArtifactReader::from_credential is its only outside caller. Narrow it back to private. IT WILL NOT ANNOUNCE ITSELF — new() also calls it, so no dead-code warning fires; this line is the only reminder.
  2. The doc comment on ResolutionPlanCache::insert_verified still opens "The control-reader path hash-checks and parses before reaching this seam…". Prune that first clause.
Also discharged: control_artifact_reader.rs:21-22 imports ResolutionPlanCache and (under cfg(test)) InvalidPlanCacheLimit from runner_plan_supply — the temporarily INVERTED dependency .15.41 recorded. It evaporates here.

VERIFICATION IS BY INSPECTION AND BY THE TWO CRATES OUTSIDE THE FAILING CLOSURE. wamn-runtime has not compiled since .15.10 and will not until .15.12, so nothing in its 8-of-38 reverse-dep closure can be built or tested. What CAN be run, both confirmed outside that closure (wamn-ctl does NOT depend on wamn-runtime):
  cargo check -p wamn-control-provision --all-targets   +  cargo test -p wamn-control-provision
  cargo check -p wamn-ctl --all-targets                 +  cargo test -p wamn-ctl (the live tests are #[ignore]d)
  cargo check -p wamn-cdc-reader --all-targets          (the other provision dependent)
  clippy --all-targets -D warnings on each
And by inspection:
  the compile baseline is UNCHANGED at exactly 4 errors, all in plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs, none in any file this bead touches
  zero orphaned references tree-wide for artifact_reader / ArtifactReader / artifact-reader / ARTIFACT_READER, with exactly two deliberate exceptions: docs/plane-amendment.md:322/:333/:484 (inside .15.9's quoted amendment block, written to RECORD this deletion) and docs/deployment-simplification-spec.md's prose
  the remaining 40 gate-mutant scripts unchanged; bash -n clean on any script edited (none expected)

MUTANTS. The reader's own guards are being deleted, so there is nothing to mutate on the reader side. The load-bearing risk here is OVER-deletion, not under-deletion, and the two crates' own test suites are the instrument: a mutant that deletes a SURVIVING provision leg (e.g. an effect-writer or CDC name) must fail a named test in wamn-control-provision. One such mutant is enough; this bead adds no new asserts to protect.

TESTS INSIDE THE EDITED FILES THAT DIE WITH THEIR SUBJECT: name.rs:1117 artifact_reader_scope_identities_and_names_are_frozen, secret.rs:506 artifact_reader_secret_and_document_are_fixed_mount_exact (plus its :344 fixture and :289-293 imports), and the reader cases inside sql.rs's test module. Delete them with the code they pin — they are frozen-literal guards over names that no longer exist.
PREMISE CORRECTION, MEASURED DURING IMPLEMENTATION (2026-08-17).

THE ORPHAN CASCADE ABOVE WAS WRONG ABOUT `url`, AND THE TRUTH IS CLEANER. The design said "url — used by secret.rs, dump.rs and six tests. KEEP." That reading came from grepping the WORD "url", which matches parameter names, JSON keys and doc prose all over this crate. There is ZERO use of the `url` CRATE anywhere in src/ or tests/ (no `use url`, no `url::`, no `Url`) once artifact_reader.rs is gone. It is orphaned.

`chrono` was also mis-scoped: after the deletion its only remaining use is inside secret.rs's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (DateTime/Utc in the `instant` helper), so it belongs in [dev-dependencies] — exactly where commit 7ac999b4 took it FROM.

SO THE MANIFEST DELTA IS EXACTLY 7ac999b4's DELTA, REVERSED: serde, sha2, url and tokio-postgres leave [dependencies]; the postgres-config feature goes with its only consumer; chrono returns to [dev-dependencies]. That exact correspondence is the strongest available evidence the removal is complete — the commit that introduced the plane is the commit whose manifest footprint disappears.

ALSO FOUND: `use wamn_run_state::CredentialGeneration;` at name.rs:10 was orphaned too (its only non-test use was artifact_reader_generation_role); the test module imports it separately. And my function-removal pass initially left one dangling MULTI-LINE `#[expect(clippy::too_many_arguments, …)]` attribute above `const PAT_TTL` in provision_project_env.rs — a walk-back over preceding `///`/`#[` lines does not catch an attribute whose last line is `)]`. Both fixed; both are the kind of orphan the compiler catches only for imports, never for attributes.
acceptance_criteria: No artifact-reader role, Secret, plugin, provisioning leg, live test, guard or build-and-test recipe remains anywhere in the tree; wamn-control-provision is gone from crates/platform/runtime/Cargo.toml, and serde, sha2, tokio-postgres and the postgres-config feature are gone from crates/control/provision/Cargo.toml while chrono and url stay; ResolutionPlanCache::from_non_zero is private again and insert_verified's doc no longer names the control-reader path; wamn-control-provision, wamn-ctl and wamn-cdc-reader check, test and clippy clean; the compile baseline is unchanged at exactly 4 errors in plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs; the only surviving textual references are the two deliberate doc records.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(runtime): the weld derives both identity halves from verified content
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.102's ruling (2026-08-17) applies one level down, to code wamn-0h0g.15.100 already committed (e5c52aab).

The weld as built reads TWO mounted carriers: the manifest ConfigMap, and a SEPARATE release-identity ConfigMap supplying the expected digest and the release version (crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs, read_carried_release / read_identity_value). Two ConfigMaps that must agree is the same skew surface the ruling closes, one level down — the ruling's 'one deployment-varying line, one thing to roll, nothing to keep in agreement' forbids it just as it forbids the env keys.

## Scope

The weld derives BOTH halves from VERIFIED CONTENT:
  · release version <- ServingManifest.release.catalog_version, a header field inside the canonical preimage (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:111 under :284). The ruling's version-in-preimage edge is already priced and satisfied: it lives in the bytes, so deleting the asserted carrier does not orphan it. Expose it from content, NEVER from the object name.
  · manifest digest <- the manifest's own canonical bytes.

DELETE the release-identity mount read: read_carried_release, read_identity_value, WeldErrorKind::IdentityUnreadable and IdentityMalformed, and the identity half of CarriedRelease. Also delete the ReleaseVersionMismatch check and its kind — that check compared the identity mount's version against the manifest's own, so it loses its subject exactly as the half-a-pair bind refusal does in wamn-0h0g.15.103. Its test (an_identity_version_the_manifest_disagrees_with_refuses) and its mutant go with it.
If the release-identity ConfigMap has no surviving reader, delete RELEASE_IDENTITY_CONFIGMAP_NAME, RELEASE_IDENTITY_MOUNT_PATH, RELEASE_IDENTITY_VERSION_KEY and RELEASE_IDENTITY_DIGEST_KEY (serving_manifest.rs:66-79) rather than leaving dead scaffolding — the ruling is explicit that a carrier ruled redundant has its constants and read path deleted.

## THE ONE OPEN MECHANISM QUESTION — RULE IT BEFORE IMPLEMENTING

The ruling states the manifest is 'byte-verified at load (sha256(bytes) = <name>)'. That check needs the ConfigMap NAME inside the container, and today nothing supplies it: the volume projects to RELEASE_MANIFEST_MOUNT_PATH (serving_manifest.rs:58) with the file named RELEASE_MANIFEST_FILE_NAME (:64), so the digest-bearing name is not visible to the process. Options, all deployment-shaped and therefore coupled to wamn-0h0g.15.98:
  (a) Make the name discoverable — mount so the digest appears in the path, or name the file by digest.
  (b) Drop the name comparison and self-derive: parse, validate, and require canonical bytes, then take digest() from the verified content. ServingManifest::canonical_bytes() != bytes already catches corruption and truncation, so the name adds no integrity guarantee once the digest is derived rather than asserted; what binds pod to release is the pod template, a deployment fact the pod cannot and should not second-guess.
Note (b) needs a load path that does not take an expected digest — ServingManifest::read (:332) requires one — so it implies either a sibling constructor in wamn-catalog or making the expected digest optional there.

## Boundary

Keeps everything else wamn-0h0g.15.100 landed: one load, process-lifetime immutability, hand out by reference, fail closed, and the naming rule (it is a WELD, NOT A CACHE — no invalidation, TTL, refresh or eviction, ever). Host construction is wamn-0h0g.15.101; striking the env keys is wamn-0h0g.15.103, which depends on this.
design:
OWNER RULING, 2026-08-17: DROP THE NAME COMPARISON; THE WELD SELF-DERIVES. The projection change (digest-in-path) is REJECTED, not deferred.

WHY THE NAME CHECK WAS NEVER A VERIFICATION. Trace what the name inside the container would be: a string placed by THE SAME POD TEMPLATE that mounts the bytes. Template says name-X, template mounts bytes-Y; comparing X to sha256(Y) checks the template's internal consistency AGAINST ITSELF — one authority wearing two hats. A pod cannot second-guess its own birth certificate, and machinery that pretends otherwise is the wamn-0h0g.15.102 asserted-carrier bug re-entering through the mount path. The digest-in-path projection is rejected for the same reason: it would thread the digest through a filename purely to feed a self-comparison, adding a template knob that can itself skew — the very channel class .15.102 deleted.

WHAT THE WELD ACTUALLY DOES. Read /etc/wamn/release-manifest/manifest.json, parse, re-serialize through THE SAME RFC 8785 PRODUCER THAT MINTED IT, and let digest = sha256(canonical bytes) — self-derived. That digest is then handed to all four readers AND to the claim-time recording.

WHAT SURVIVES OF VERIFICATION IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, AND IT IS STRONGER THAN THE NAME CHECK. The canonical round-trip proves the mounted bytes are well-formed manifest content whose identity is COMPUTABLE. Corruption, truncation, or hand-editing either fails the parse or shifts the digest — and a shifted digest is NOT a masquerade, it is a CORRECT NAME FOR DIFFERENT CONTENT, carried honestly into every run record and authority decision downstream. Malformed means the pod never goes Ready (the existing readiness gate), which is the only refusal that means anything here.

THE TRUST STATEMENT — RECORD IT AT THE LOAD SITE SO NOBODY RE-ADDS THE CHECK. Pod-to-release binding rests WHOLLY on the pod template, and that is not a gap, it is the ratified design. The template is GitOps-converged, revision-controlled, rollout-controlled; 'which release does this pod serve' is exactly the class of fact assigned to the cluster when the wasmCloud-v2 model was taken. In-container name-matching is rebuilding, inside the pod, an attestation THE DEPLOYMENT PLANE ALREADY OWNS — the same instinct the readiness-revision check died for in ratification ruling 4, and it dies the same way. What the platform attests is downstream and already ruled: the digest the weld derives is the digest runs record, authority enforces, and wamn-0h0g.8.21 attests. That chain binds BYTES-THAT-SERVED to FACTS-THAT-RESULTED, which is the audit property. Binding bytes-to-intent is Git's job, and Git already does it.

THE PRODUCER-COUPLING RIDER. The canonical round-trip makes the weld's digest producer-coupled: it MUST import the wamn-0h0g.15.14 mint's serializer, never reimplement 8785, so a producer revision cannot silently fork weld-side identity. Lands as a shared function.

ALREADY STRUCTURALLY SATISFIED — VERIFIED 2026-08-17. ServingManifest::digest() (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:321) already calls wamn_flow::canonical_json_sha256 (crates/execution/flow-model/src/lib.rs:62), and canonical_bytes() (:316) calls wamn_flow::canonical_json_bytes (:76). The mint is independently required to use the same function (recorded on .15.14: using the other canonicalizer would produce bytes the reader rejects). So the weld calling digest() reimplements NOTHING and the shared function already exists. The golden-vector test is what proves it STAYS that way.

CONCRETE GAP THIS BEAD MUST CLOSE. There is NO load path that omits an expected digest: ServingManifest::read (:332) requires one, and new() (:297) builds from parts rather than bytes. This bead needs a sibling constructor in wamn-catalog that parses, validates, REQUIRES canonical bytes, and derives the digest — same refusals as read() minus the digest comparison. Do not make read()'s parameter optional; a distinct constructor keeps the self-derived path and the (now unused) compare-against-expected path from being confused later.

FORKING HAZARD ESCALATED: wamn-0h0g.15.63 records that TWO RFC 8785 canonicalizers live in this workspace — the shared wamn_flow one and a private ryu-js implementation at crates/catalog/model/src/lib.rs:1376-1386 used for identity-frame hashing. Under producer-coupling that duplication is exactly the silent-fork channel this rider forbids.
================================================================
OWNER RULING, 2026-08-17 (second pass): ONE HONEST CONSTRUCTOR, NOT TWO ENTRY POINTS.

An Option<expected> on read() is rejected outright: it would let every future call site quietly choose its trust model at the argument list, which is how the deleted name-comparison re-enters wearing a Some.

But the sharper question, which this bead must answer rather than assume: DOES THE COMPARE-AGAINST-EXPECTED PATH HAVE ANY SURVIVING CALLER AT ALL? If not, read(bytes, expected) is not the sibling of the new constructor — it is the corpse, and the shape inverts.

TARGET SHAPE IF THE SURVEY HOLDS:
  · from_canonical_bytes(bytes) -> Result<(ServingManifest, Digest)> becomes THE ONLY constructor from bytes: parse -> validate -> require-canonical via the shared 8785 round-trip -> derive.
  · new()-from-parts confines to the mint's internals (pub(crate) if it can).
  · Any caller holding an expectation writes: let m = from_canonical_bytes(b)?; ensure m.digest == expected. Comparison as a CALLER-SIDE ASSERTION against the one honest constructor, never a second trust path baked into the type's API.
  · The principle: two entry points with different verification semantics on one type is a FORK IN THE TRUST MODEL; one entry point plus external assertions is a TRUST MODEL WITH CALL SITES.

SURVEY VERIFIED IN-TREE 2026-08-17 (the ruling said not to trust the enumeration). IT HOLDS.
  ServingManifest::read — exactly ONE production caller tree-wide: crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs:152, which is the weld, and THIS BEAD removes its expected-digest argument. Every other caller is a test inside wamn-catalog: serving_manifest.rs:579, :584, :668, :673 and tests/serving_manifest_digest.rs:303. After this bead, read() has ZERO production callers.
  ServingManifest::new — ZERO production callers. All eight sites are tests: serving_manifest.rs:542/:557/:617/:635/:652, tests/serving_manifest_digest.rs:50/:71, and release_manifest.rs:270 (this bead's own fixture). Confirms the .15.14 mint does not exist yet, so 'confine to the mint's internals' is prospective.
  The prospective consumers check out too: the OCI pull path needs no manifest-side expected digest (content-addressed fetch verifies at transfer, and for plan bytes the authority check is membership (flow, plan-hash) in the manifest — keyed by what the manifest says, not by a caller expectation); the mint produces and never reads; the golden-vector test is an assertion on the derived digest, not a construction parameter.

TWO TEST CONVERSIONS THIS IMPLIES, and both get BETTER:
  serving_manifest.rs:673 read(PLAN_A, canonical_bytes) asserts a foreign digest is refused; tests/serving_manifest_digest.rs:303 asserts a candidate's bytes fail against a RELEASED digest. Both become: construct via from_canonical_bytes, then assert the derived digest differs from the expectation. That names the actual fact — different content, different name — instead of testing a comparison parameter. Keep the candidate-vs-released case; it is the republish-safety property, not incidental coverage.

FINDING 1 — pub(crate) ON new() CANNOT WORK YET, and the reason is a crate boundary, not reluctance. Two current callers are in DIFFERENT crates from the definition: release_manifest.rs:270 (wamn-runtime) and tests/serving_manifest_digest.rs:50/:71 (wamn-catalog's tests/ dir compiles as a SEPARATE crate, so pub(crate) is invisible to it). So narrowing to pub(crate) breaks both. The house rule that fits is M-TEST-UTIL, 'test utilities are feature gated': keep from-parts construction behind a feature-gated export rather than pub, so production cannot reach it while both test crates can. Decide that explicitly; do not leave new() pub with only a doc comment asking callers to behave.

FINDING 2 — THERE IS NO Digest TYPE TO RETURN. Manifest and flow digests are bare String throughout (plan_hash :133, source_artifact :147, binding_base_artifact :176, definition_hash :226). The crate does have a hash-newtype family — DefinitionHash (lib.rs:199), ArtifactHash (:224), DraftContentHash (:542) — so Result<(ServingManifest, Digest)> either introduces a ManifestDigest newtype in that family or returns String. A newtype makes the derived digest impossible to confuse with the flow-level hashes that are all bare String, which matters because the whole point is that this ONE value is the derived identity. It is also scope growth on a bead that is otherwise a deletion. Rule it; note wamn-0h0g.15.65 (catalog_version has four widths) is the sibling typing-discipline bead.

RIDER A — REFUSAL TAXONOMY IS SHARED, MINUS EXACTLY ONE. The new path must emit the IDENTICAL typed refusals as today's read() — malformed, non-canonical, schema-invalid — same literals, same tests, so that deleting or demoting read() later changes NO observable refusal behaviour. The only semantic difference between the paths is the absence of the comparison. State that in acceptance AS A DIFF; do not re-enumerate the taxonomy.

RIDER B — NON-CANONICAL IS A REFUSAL, NEVER A REPAIR. The constructor requires canonical bytes and refuses otherwise. It must NOT helpfully re-canonicalize and proceed: a manifest arriving non-canonical is EVIDENCE OF A PRODUCER OR TRANSPORT FAULT, and the digest of repaired bytes would name content nobody actually shipped. Parse-then-re-serialize is THE CHECK. The stored identity is always sha256(INPUT bytes), which under the canonical requirement equals the round-trip — assert that equality, refuse on mismatch, done. Today's read() already has this shape (canonical_bytes() != bytes -> NonCanonicalJson at :340-342); preserve it exactly.
================================================================
OWNER RULINGS, 2026-08-17 (third pass): BOTH OPEN QUESTIONS SETTLED.

RULING 1 — M-TEST-UTIL, AND IT IS THE STRONGER FENCE, NOT A FALLBACK.
#[cfg(feature = "test-util")] is not chosen because pub(crate) failed. pub(crate) would leave from-parts construction reachable to every future IN-CRATE production module — the mint's own neighbours — on nothing but discipline. The feature gate makes misuse A COMPILE ERROR IN PRODUCTION BUILDS. That is the M-TEST-UTIL rationale verbatim: visibility keyed to BUILD CONFIGURATION, not module geography.

  RIDER 1a — THE GATE MUST BE LOAD-BEARING, AND PROVEN SO. Acceptance includes the NEGATIVE PROOF: a production-configuration check of wamn-catalog fails to resolve from-parts construction. 'A fence nobody has ever watched fail is a doc comment with extra steps.'
  IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL VERIFIED IN-TREE: wamn-catalog has NO [features] section at all today (crates/catalog/model/Cargo.toml is 16 lines, dependencies only). This bead introduces the crate's FIRST feature. Consequence: there is no `default` list to subtract from, so --no-default-features and the default set are identical, and `cargo check -p wamn-catalog` IS the production configuration. Write the negative proof against that plain invocation and assert it FAILS; do not write it against --no-default-features and think you have proven something the default build does not already prove.

  RIDER 1b — THE DEV-DEPENDENCY, AND IT MUST BE ADDED, NOT AMENDED. wamn-runtime depends on wamn-catalog as a NORMAL dependency (crates/platform/runtime/Cargo.toml:11) and does not list it under dev-dependencies at all — [dev-dependencies] currently holds only wamn-run-state. So this bead ADDS:
        [dev-dependencies]
        wamn-catalog = { workspace = true, features = ["test-util"] }
  alongside the existing normal dependency. Dev-dependency features do NOT leak into the production graph, so wamn-runtime's own production build still cannot reach from-parts. SAY THIS AT THE CALL SITE: nobody may 'fix' a missing-feature compile error by promoting the feature onto the normal dependency. That promotion silently deletes the fence for the entire crate.
  SECOND CALL SITE THE RIDER DOES NOT COVER, and it needs the same treatment: wamn-catalog's OWN tests/serving_manifest_digest.rs is a separate compilation unit, so it cannot see the feature either unless the crate self-enables it. The idiomatic fix is a SELF dev-dependency —
        [dev-dependencies]
        wamn-catalog = { path = ".", features = ["test-util"] }
  — which keeps plain `cargo test -p wamn-catalog` working with no special flags and still leaves the production graph clean. The alternative (requiring --features test-util on every test invocation) breaks every existing sweep command and the gate-of-record recipes; do not take it.

RULING 2 — ManifestDigest: TAKE THE SCOPE GROWTH, MINIMALLY.
The String alternative was weighed and rejected on this specific value's traffic: this digest becomes the most-travelled identity in the system — claim-time recording, effect-authority equality, wamn-0h0g.8.21 attestation, the golden-vector weld — moving between TWO host processes and FOUR readers, in a codebase where every flow-level hash it could be confused with is a bare String. That is not a hypothetical mix-up class; it is the exact environment M-STRONG-TYPES exists for. The crate already made this call three times (DefinitionHash lib.rs:199, ArtifactHash :224, DraftContentHash :542), so returning String would not be avoiding a decision — it would be deciding that THE ONE DERIVED IDENTITY is the family's only untyped member.

  SHAPE — CLONE THE FAMILY EXACTLY. Verified pattern at lib.rs:195-235: tuple newtype over String; #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize)] with #[serde(transparent)]; a parse() constructor validating via validate_digest (DefinitionHash:201 has one, ArtifactHash does not — follow DefinitionHash, since this value is parsed from bytes); as_str(); Display. NOTE THE FAMILY DERIVES Serialize BUT NOT Deserialize, deliberately — the same reasoning ServingRelease documents at serving_manifest.rs:94-97, that a derived Deserialize bypasses validation exactly at the boundary where it matters. Follow that. The family exposes as_str() rather than AsRef<str>; match the house style even though AsRef would also be defensible.

  CONVERSION BOUNDARY AT THE CRATE EDGE. The constructor returns it. Weld, claim-time recording, and effect authority TAKE the newtype. Anything downstream already typed String — SQL bind params, WIT strings, log fields — converts at the call site. NO landed schema, wire field, or stored row changes; this is a one-file addition plus a signature ripple through code this wave already touches.

  A SHAPE CHECK DISAPPEARS AS A CONSEQUENCE, and that is the point of M-STRONG-TYPES-GUARD: crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/claims.rs:88 valid_manifest_digest() hand-checks the sha256:<64 lowercase hex> form because ReleaseIdentity.manifest_digest is a bare String (claims.rs:83). Once the recording takes ManifestDigest the invariant is carried by the type and that function loses its subject. Retire it with its subject rather than leaving a redundant guard.

  THE ONE SCOPE TRAP TO REFUSE: DO NOT retrofit the flow-level hashes (plan_hash :133, source_artifact :147, binding_base_artifact :176, definition_hash :226) to the family in this bead. That is the rename-sweep's territory, and dragging it here is how a deletion bead becomes a migration. File it if it is not already filed; do not do it.
acceptance_criteria:
THE CONSTRUCTOR: from_canonical_bytes is the ONLY bytes-to-manifest constructor, takes no expected digest, and returns ManifestDigest alongside the manifest; read(bytes, expected) is deleted or demoted with zero production callers remaining. title: [SR-MVP] chore(runtime): strike the asserted release-identity config keys
description:
## Why

Ruled by wamn-0h0g.15.102 (2026-08-17): the mount is the sole carrier of the (release version, manifest digest) pair; the config keys delete. Not a reconciliation — a dual-representation bug. An asserted carrier cannot correct a welded one, so a comparator would carry no information, and leaving the keys alive keeps the misdescription channel open for every future reader that grabs the env var because it is easier than taking the manifest handle.

## A FOLLOW-UP COMMIT, NOT A REVERT

wamn-0h0g.15.11's workload-config MECHANISM survives and is correct for genuinely per-workload knobs (wamn.tenant, wamn.project, wamn.schema, wamn.runner all stay). What deletes is RELEASE IDENTITY IMPERSONATING A PER-WORKLOAD KNOB. Release identity is a property of the pod's release, not of a component's configuration.

## Scope

DELETE the two asserted keys and their read path:
  · crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/mod.rs:143 RELEASE_VERSION_CONFIG_KEY and :147 MANIFEST_DIGEST_CONFIG_KEY, both consts.
  · The on_workload_item_bind read block at mod.rs:222-256, including its half-a-pair refusal — that refusal exists only because two asserted strings could disagree with each other, and it has no subject once the pair comes from one verified object.
  · The keys from every template that sets them (sweep deploy/ and any test/gate fixture).

REPOINT every consumer at the loaded weld instance. The claim-time recording above all: crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/claims.rs:633 set_release_identity and :660 release_identity_for, consumed at production_claim.rs:190 and :341. The pair now comes from verified manifest content — the digest from the manifest's own canonical bytes and the version from ServingManifest.release.catalog_version — never from an env string and never from an object name.

Keep the ReleaseIdentity type and the write-once claim behaviour that wamn-0h0g.15.11 landed (commit 618a5800); only the SOURCE of the pair changes. crates/platform/runtime/tests/production_claim_live.rs:701 and :705 call set_release_identity directly and will need their fixtures repointed, not deleted.

## Boundary

Does not touch the run-plane DDL, the paired CHECK, or the immutability guard — .15.11's database half is correct and stays. Does not change the claim write itself. The weld revision that makes both halves derivable from verified content is wamn-0h0g.15.104, and this bead depends on it.
acceptance_criteria: Neither release-identity config key exists in the tree or in any template; the claim-time pair is sourced from the loaded weld's verified content; the half-a-pair bind refusal is gone along with its subject; production_claim_live fixtures pass against the new source; grep for RELEASE_VERSION_CONFIG_KEY and MANIFEST_DIGEST_CONFIG_KEY returns nothing.
close_reason: Commit 3432ea52. Both config keys and the on_workload_item_bind read block deleted with the half-a-pair refusal, which had no subject once the pair comes from one verified object. Repointed at the weld in ExecutionHost::instantiate beside the tenant/schema/runner injections, reading the SAME PlanRelease plan supply resolves against via a new PlanRelease::weld(). PREMISE CORRECTIONS: the scope item 'the keys from every template that sets them (sweep deploy/ and any test/gate fixture)' is an EMPTY SET -- a tree-wide grep finds the two literals only at their const definitions, nothing in deploy/ or any gate/fixture ever set them, and no WorkloadDeployment sets wamn.runner either; and production_claim_live.rs needed NO repointing, because it calls set_release_identity directly, which the method's contract blesses. Guard added in runtime_inventory.rs (the drift guard IS the test -- injecting the pair needs a whole host): exactly one production injection, positioned after the weld, and zero occurrences of either struck key in three files, with 4 negative fixtures. Mutants 3/3 dead against named tests, sha256-restored.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(runtime): construct the release-manifest weld once in each host process
description:
## Why

Split from wamn-0h0g.15.100, which delivered the weld itself (ReleaseManifestWeld: load, digest-verify, hold, hand out — crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs, 11 tests, 6 mutants). The remaining half of that bead's scope — 'wire it into both host constructors and hand it to the four readers' — was NOT done, for two blocking reasons, and is carried here.

## WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN .15.100

1. UNVERIFIABLE AT THAT BASELINE. Both host crates are in the reverse-dependency closure of wamn-runtime, which does not compile until wamn-0h0g.15.12 lands (4 errors in plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs). Wiring could be written but not compiled or run, and this program's standard is verification by running.

2. IT WOULD BRICK EVERY HOST. The weld is fail-closed by design: an absent, unreadable, unparseable, non-canonical, digest-mismatched, or version-disagreeing mount is a construction error. NOTHING MOUNTS THE MANIFEST TODAY — grep for /etc/wamn/release across deploy/, services/ and crates/ returns only the two const definitions, and the mounts are wamn-0h0g.15.98. Making construction mandatory before .15.98 lands stops every host, gate and bench from starting.

3. THERE ARE NO READERS YET to hand it to: they are .15.12, .15.66, .15.95 and .15.96.

## Scope

Construct exactly ONE ReleaseManifestWeld per host process and hand it to that process's readers by reference:
  · crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs — the flowrunner in-process host (plugin map :564-585, linker :524-541). Serves readers 1 (plan supply) and 2 (effect authority).
  · services/host/src/host.rs — the wash host (.with_plugin chain :140-164). Serves readers 3 (flow-http routing) and 4 (jetstream delivery gating).
Two processes, one instance each, never two in one process.

## THE SEQUENCING DECISION THIS BEAD MUST MAKE

Decide what a pod with NO release-identity mount does. Two defensible positions:
  (a) STRICTLY FAIL CLOSED, matching .15.100's acceptance wording ('a pod with an absent manifest fails closed at construction'). Requires .15.98 to land first, and every gate, bench and non-serving path to gain the mounts.
  (b) ABSENT-IS-BYTE-UNCHANGED, matching the posture wamn-0h0g.15.11 already landed and ratified for the same identity pair: 'Optional: absent leaves a production claim recording nothing, so every path that carries no release identity is byte-unchanged' (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/mod.rs:140-142). A pod with no identity mount is a pre-release-model path (S2..S6, the gateway, benches); a pod WITH one must have a valid matching manifest or refuse.
Option (b) still forbids serving a WRONG manifest, which is the property that matters, and it is the precedent already in the tree. The weld's WeldErrorKind::IdentityUnreadable already distinguishes 'no identity mount' from every other fault, so either posture is implementable without changing .15.100.

## Boundary

Construction and handing out only. What each reader does with the manifest is that reader's bead. Do not add invalidation, refresh or eviction — see the naming rule on .15.100.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one weld construction site exists per host process, proven by a drift guard over both host files; each process's readers receive it by reference; the absent-mount posture is decided, documented at the construction site, and covered by a test.
notes:
CIRCULARITY CORRECTION, caught while wiring the dependency edges (2026-08-16).

As first written this bead claimed BOTH host constructors. That cannot hold: wamn-0h0g.15.12 fixes the compile break by replacing the deleted run_resolution_metadata() call in RunnerPlanSupply with a manifest-derived supply, and to do that it MUST construct the weld in the flowrunner in-process host itself. If this bead owned that wiring, .15.101 would depend on .15.12 for compilation while .15.12 depended on .15.101 for its construction site.

SPLIT AS BUILT:
  · FLOWRUNNER IN-PROCESS HOST (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs) — construction rides wamn-0h0g.15.12, unavoidably, because that is the bead whose call site forces it. Readers 1 and 2 take it from there.
  · WASH HOST (services/host/src/host.rs) — construction is THIS bead. Readers 3 (.15.96 routing) and 4 (.15.95 jetstream gating) take it from there.
  · THE ONE-SITE-PER-PROCESS DRIFT GUARD spans both files and is THIS bead's, since it can only be written once both construction sites exist.

The sequencing decision in the description (strict fail-closed vs absent-is-byte-unchanged) still belongs here and must be settled ONCE, for both processes, not per host — .15.12 should follow whatever this bead rules rather than inventing its own posture. If .15.12 lands first it must record which posture it assumed so this bead can confirm or correct it.

RELATED DECISION: wamn-0h0g.15.102 rules which carrier of the (release version, manifest digest) pair is authoritative — the mounted ConfigMap the weld reads, or the per-workload config keys .15.11 already landed. That ruling may change what the construction site feeds into set_release_identity, so read it before wiring.

NARROWED BY OWNER RULING wamn-0h0g.15.102 (2026-08-17). Two changes to this bead:

1. THE ABSENT-MOUNT POSTURE DECISION IS SETTLED AGAINST OPTION (b). The description offered a choice between strict fail-closed and 'absent-is-byte-unchanged', arguing (b) had precedent in wamn-0h0g.15.11's optional config keys. THAT PRECEDENT IS GONE — the ruling deletes those keys as an asserted carrier (wamn-0h0g.15.103), so it can no longer be cited as the ratified posture for release identity. What remains true is narrower and still needs an answer: a pod with NO manifest mount at all is a pre-release-model path (gates, benches, the S2..S6 and gateway paths), and mandatory construction stops them starting until wamn-0h0g.15.98 mounts everything. Decide that on its own merits, not by analogy to the struck keys.

2. THE CONSTRUCTION SITE NOW FEEDS THE CLAIM. Because every consumer takes the pair from the loaded weld, the construction site is what supplies set_release_identity (claims.rs:633) rather than on_workload_item_bind. That makes the hand-out ordering load-bearing in a way it was not when this bead was written: the weld must be constructed BEFORE any component binds, or the claim path has no pair. Verify that ordering explicitly in both hosts.

3. THE WELD SHAPE SETTLES FIRST. wamn-0h0g.15.104 removes the release-identity mount read and derives both halves from verified content, so what this bead hands out changes shape. It is now a hard dependency.
PREMISE CORRECTION AFTER .15.104 SHIPPED (verified 2026-08-17 at e87133fa).

THE ERROR VARIANT THIS BEAD RELIES ON IS GONE. Both the description and the .15.102 narrowing above argue that "the weld's WeldErrorKind::IdentityUnreadable already distinguishes 'no identity mount' from every other fault, so either posture is implementable without changing .15.100". .15.104 reduced WeldErrorKind from five variants to TWO — ManifestUnreadable and ManifestRejected. IdentityUnreadable, IdentityMalformed and ReleaseVersionMismatch are all deleted, because the release-identity mount they described is deleted.

An absent manifest mount now surfaces as ManifestUnreadable, the same kind as a permission error or a truncated read. So the absent-vs-unreadable distinction this bead's posture reasoning assumed is NOT available for free: it must either be made at the construction site (probe the path before calling the weld) or be restored as a variant. That is a real design consequence of ruling .15.102, not an oversight in .15.104.

CURRENT WELD SURFACE this bead hands out: load() -> Result<Self, WeldError>; load_from(manifest_root: &Path); release() -> &CarriedRelease { release_version: i32, manifest_digest: ManifestDigest }; manifest() -> &ServingManifest.

THE FLOWRUNNER CONSTRUCTION SITE IS BUILT AND ITS POSTURE IS RECORDED (wamn-0h0g.15.12, commit 0b8bc7f3, 2026-08-17). This bead's remaining half is the wash host plus the one-site-per-process drift guard.

WHAT TO MIRROR. crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs::load_plan_release, called from ExecutionHost::instantiate. Under owner ruling R2 the two absent-mount cases are told apart by the ARGUMENT, never by inspecting a failure:
  - Option<ReleaseSupply> is None => this process was never given a release. No weld, nothing to refuse; RunnerPlanSupply::new takes release: Option<PlanRelease> and load_run_snapshot reports Unavailable for every run. Gates, benches and every non-serving caller are byte-unchanged — verified: ExecutionHost::instantiate has exactly ONE real call site, services/executor/src/lib.rs, the other two greps being source-text assertions in tests/conformance.
  - Some(ReleaseSupply) whose mount is absent, unreadable or non-canonical => host construction FAILS and the pod never goes ready.

WHY IT CANNOT BE DONE ANY OTHER WAY, confirming this bead's own 12h correction: .15.104 collapsed WeldErrorKind to ManifestUnreadable | ManifestRejected, so "no mount" and "corrupt mount" are the SAME kind. There is no way to recover the distinction downstream of ReleaseManifestWeld::load_from. Either mirror the argument-shaped choice at the wash host's own construction site, or restore a variant on .15.100 — this bead's older claim that either posture is implementable without touching .15.100 is FALSE as written.

THE EXECUTOR KNOBS, for the wash host to match or deliberately differ from: --release-manifest-root (env WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_ROOT, Option<PathBuf>, absent = non-serving), --plan-artifact-base (env WAMN_PLAN_ARTIFACT_BASE, default registry:5000/wamn/execution-plans), --insecure-plan-registry (env WAMN_INSECURE_PLAN_REGISTRY), --plan-fetch-timeout-ms (default 10000).

DRIFT-GUARD SUBJECT, now concrete: there must be exactly one ReleaseManifestWeld::load / load_from call per process. Today the whole tree has exactly one production call site (load_plan_release) plus test call sites in release_manifest.rs and runner_plan_supply.rs; the wash host adds the second production one, in a different process.

FOR .15.98, which supplies the mount: the executor refuses to start if the path is passed and unusable, so a manifest ConfigMap that is mounted wrong is a CrashLoopBackOff, not a silently degraded pod.
close_reason: Landed at 09498e17. Wash host (services/host/src/host.rs) now constructs the weld via --release-manifest-root / WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_ROOT and load_release, mirroring load_plan_release's argument-shaped R2 posture exactly so both processes share ONE rule: no root passed = never given a release (byte-unchanged for gateway, S2..S6, gates, benches); root passed but mount absent/unreadable/non-canonical = startup fails. Forced into the argument because .15.104 collapsed WeldErrorKind to two variants. ONE knob here vs the executor's four, deliberately: readers 3 and 4 serve attachments and registrations from inside the verified manifest and pull nothing, so registry knobs would configure a fetch that never happens. Construction is the FIRST statement of run(), ahead of NATS, the engine and every plugin — the ordering is load-bearing under .15.102 (every consumer takes the pair from this object) and also makes an unverifiable host refuse before opening a socket. DRIFT GUARD in tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs spans BOTH host files and pins two facts per process: exactly one production construction site, and the weld reached before the first bind-capable call (ClusterHostBuilder::default() in the wash host, WasmtimeComponent::new( in the execution host, whose real position is the load_plan_release CALL not the fn definition). cfg(test) sites excluded and proven excluded. THREE SCOPE CORRECTIONS: (1) 'each process's readers receive it by reference' is VACUOUS in the wash host — there are ZERO readers today (.15.96 routing and .15.95 gating are unwritten), and nothing was pre-built for them because a receiver for a nonexistent reader is speculative; each will add its own hand-out line. What this bead delivers there is the construction site, posture, ordering and guard. (2) The .15.102 narrowing's 'the construction site supplies set_release_identity' is NOT this bead's: .15.103 owns that repoint in terms ('REPOINT every consumer at the loaded weld instance', naming set_release_identity and release_identity_for), and the call is keyed by component id which a construction site does not have. This bead's obligation from that narrowing was the ORDERING, now guard-pinned in both hosts. (3) MY OWN doc comment claimed a digest-mismatched mount was a construction failure — FALSE, caught by the .15.49 lane: load_from takes no expected digest and derives both halves from verified bytes, so name and content cannot disagree; the only digest comparison is at run time on the claim path. Corrected in-commit. VERIFIED: 2 posture tests green (cargo test -p wamn-host); runtime_inventory 11/11; whole conformance lib suite 63/63; cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean; clippy -D warnings clean on wamn-host and wamn-proof-conformance; rustfmt clean. FIVE MUTANTS DEAD with sha256 restore: weld-site-removed, weld-site-duplicated, weld-after-bind, exec-weld-unreached, and the decisive unusable-mount-degrades (returning Ok(None) instead of the weld's error fails a_host_given_an_unusable_root_refuses) — so the fail-closed posture is enforced, not merely documented. UNBLOCKS .15.95, .15.96, .15.103.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(runtime): one loaded release-manifest instance, four enumerated readers
description:
## Why — OWNER RIDER, 2026-08-16

'The plugin consults the same loaded, digest-verified manifest instance as effect authority, plan-supply, and routing — one object, one weld, four enumerated readers; nobody loads a second copy.'

This bead IS the weld. It exists so the constraint is a structural fact with an owner, not a convention four separate lanes are each trusted to honour. Every reader bead depends on it and none of them may load, parse, or digest-verify a manifest itself.

## THE FOUR ENUMERATED READERS — and they span TWO PROCESSES

  1. plan-supply         wamn-0h0g.15.12  — RunnerPlanSupply: reachable_flows(root) then OCI pull by digest
  2. effect authority    wamn-0h0g.15.66  — WamnPostgres/claims: run-to-plan binding, the restored link 1
  3. flow-http routing   wamn-0h0g.15.96  — new plugin: RouteDefinition from the attachment projection
  4. jetstream delivery  wamn-0h0g.15.95  — WamnJetstream: gate delivery on registration identity

Readers 1 and 2 run in the FLOWRUNNER IN-PROCESS HOST (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs; plugin map :564-585, linker :524-541). Readers 3 and 4 run in the WASH HOST (services/host/src/host.rs; .with_plugin chain :140-164). These are separate OS processes and cannot share one object instance.

So 'one object, one weld' is to be built as: ONE holder type, ONE loader, ONE digest-verification path, instantiated ONCE PER PROCESS and handed to that process's readers by reference. Not one global. The prohibition that actually bites is 'nobody loads a second copy': no reader re-reads the file, re-parses the bytes, or re-runs the digest check on its own, and no process holds two instances.

## Scope

Add the holder to crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/ (all four readers' code lives in that module tree). It must:
  · read the digest-named ConfigMap at RELEASE_MANIFEST_MOUNT_PATH (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:58) with RELEASE_MANIFEST_FILE_NAME (:60-63);
  · read the expected digest from the release-identity mount (RELEASE_IDENTITY_MOUNT_PATH :71, keys :75/:79);
  · call ServingManifest::read(expected_digest, bytes) (:333), which re-canonicalizes through wamn_flow::canonical_json_bytes and REFUSES on mismatch — that call is the single verification point;
  · expose the parsed ServingManifest to readers by shared reference, immutable for process lifetime (ruling 3: process-lifetime immutability, not durability);
  · fail closed and loudly at construction. A pod whose manifest is absent, unparseable, or digest-mismatched must not serve.

Wire it into both host constructors and hand it to the four readers.

## VERIFIED CONTEXT

  · ServingManifest is a frozen, fully-tested schema with a reader (read :332) and ZERO non-test producers. reachable_flows (:359-378) is already written and cycle-safe; validation already proves every calls edge names a member flow (:407-413).
  · NOTHING loads it today. Repo-wide, ServingManifest appears only in its own module, the lib.rs re-export, and tests. Grep for /etc/wamn/release across deploy/, services/ and crates/ returns ONLY the two const definitions — no mount exists in any deploy manifest.
  · Guests cannot read it and are not meant to: neither components/execution/flowrunner/wit/world.wit nor components/execution/materializer/wit/world.wit imports wasi:filesystem, and the production ctx is built with no preopens (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:596-602). Per the delivery ruling the host loads and the guests and their WITs are UNCHANGED.
  · The mounts themselves are wamn-0h0g.15.98. Build and unit-prove this against a fixture path; nothing runs in-cluster until that bead lands.
  · crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/mod.rs (20 lines: 9 pub mod + 9 pub use) is edited by this bead, .15.12 and .15.96. It is owned by the integrator, not by any lane.

## Boundary

Loading, verification and handing out the instance only. What each reader DOES with the manifest belongs to that reader's bead. No OCI pull here (.15.12). No mounts here (.15.98).
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one construction site per host process loads, digest-verifies and parses the release manifest; all four readers consume it by shared reference; no reader re-reads, re-parses or re-verifies; a pod with an absent, unparseable or digest-mismatched manifest fails closed at construction with a named refusal, proven by a focused test.
notes:
NAMING RULE — OWNER RIDER, 2026-08-16. BINDING ON THE IMPLEMENTATION.

THIS IS THE MANIFEST WELD. IT IS NOT A CACHE. Do not name the type, the module, the field, or any doc comment 'cache'.

The reason is not stylistic. A cache invites someone to add invalidation, and the entire point of a digest-named object is that INVALIDATION CANNOT EXIST. The digest IS the identity: different content is a different digest, is a different ConfigMap, is a different pod template, is a different pod. There is no state in which the loaded manifest is stale relative to its digest, so there is nothing to invalidate, no TTL, no refresh, no eviction, no revalidation. Any API surface offering one of those is wrong by construction and should fail review.

Name it for what it is — the weld: one load, one verification, held for process lifetime, handed out by reference. Prefer names in that register (release manifest weld / holder / the loaded manifest). Ruling 3's 'cache forever' means exactly process-lifetime immutability, never durability, and must not be implemented as a caching layer.

DO NOT CONFLATE IT WITH THE ONE REAL CACHE NEARBY. wamn-0h0g.15.12 keeps ResolutionPlanCache (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs, with InvalidPlanCacheLimit), which IS a genuine bounded cache over PLAN BYTES: it is entry-bounded, tenant-scoped, and has eviction, and its behaviour is pinned by named tests (cache_is_entry_bounded_and_tenant_scoped :408, hash_mismatch_never_enters_the_cache :425) and by tools/gate-mutants/plan-supply.sh. Plan bytes are fetched by digest from OCI and may be evicted and re-fetched. The manifest is not: it is read once from a mounted file and never re-read. Two different objects, two different lifecycles, adjacent in the same module tree — keep the names far apart so a later reader cannot mistake one for the other.
close_reason:
Commit e5c52aab. crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs (new) + lib.rs module declaration; 2 files, no other file touched.

DELIVERED: ReleaseManifestWeld — load once from the two mounts, verify the manifest against the digest the release identity names via ServingManifest::read, hold the parsed document for process lifetime, hand it out by reference through release() and manifest(). WeldError follows the house canonical-struct style (kind + detail, Display, Error) with five kinds: IdentityUnreadable, IdentityMalformed, ManifestUnreadable, ManifestRejected, ReleaseVersionMismatch.

PLACEMENT CORRECTED AGAINST MY OWN BEAD TEXT. The bead said to put the holder in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/. It is a top-level module beside connection_authority.rs instead: it exports no WIT interface and implements no HostPlugin, it is shared state plugins consume. Consequence worth carrying forward — plugins/mod.rs is UNTOUCHED by this bead, so the three-way collision on that file I flagged when scoping the wave is really only two-way (.15.12 and .15.96).

ONE CHECK ADDED BEYOND THE BEAD: the identity's release version must equal the manifest's own release.catalog_version. A pod whose halves disagree is mis-templated and would record one release onto a run while resolving against another. Its own kind, its own test, and a mutant proves it load-bearing.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING, WITH A STATED LIMIT. wamn-runtime does not compile at this baseline (the four known runner_plan_supply.rs errors owned by .15.12), so cargo test -p wamn-runtime CANNOT RUN and did not. Two substitutes: (1) workspace baseline re-measured, still exactly 4 errors, ZERO in the new file, so it type-checks in place; (2) the module compiled and executed VERBATIM in a throwaway crate against wamn-catalog — 11 tests green. Six mutants, ALL killed by named tests: manifest-bytes-trimmed -> a_trailing_newline_on_the_manifest_refuses; release-version-check-disabled -> an_identity_version_the_manifest_disagrees_with_refuses; empty-identity-value-accepted -> an_empty_identity_digest_refuses_as_an_identity_fault; identity-scalars-not-trimmed -> surrounding_whitespace_on_identity_scalars_is_tolerated (+1); manifest-parsed-without-verification -> three tests; digest-sourced-from-bytes-not-identity -> a_digest_the_bytes_do_not_match_refuses. The last two are the security kills: the weld verifies, and it verifies against the IDENTITY's digest rather than the bytes' own. Source file sha256-verified identical before and after the campaign. rustfmt no-op, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, components workspace unaffected.

FIRST MUTATION PASS FOUND TWO REAL SURVIVORS and both were fixed rather than explained away: the empty-value check was untested for the digest half (the version half fails its own parse either way), which is why an_empty_identity_digest_refuses_as_an_identity_fault exists; and my first bypass mutant was self-defeating, replaced with one that skips verification outright.

HOST WIRING DELIBERATELY NOT DONE -> wamn-0h0g.15.101. Two blockers: both host crates sit in wamn-runtime's broken reverse-dependency closure so wiring could not be compiled or run, and NOTHING mounts /etc/wamn/release today (.15.98), so mandatory construction would stop every host, gate and bench from starting. .15.101 also carries a circularity correction I caught wiring the edges: the flowrunner-host construction must ride .15.12, because .15.12 fixes the compile break by replacing run_resolution_metadata() with manifest-derived supply and therefore needs the construction site itself. .15.101 owns the wash-host half plus the one-site-per-process drift guard, and owns the absent-mount posture decision for BOTH processes.

ALSO FILED: wamn-0h0g.15.102 (P1 decision) — the (release version, manifest digest) pair now has TWO carriers, the mount this weld reads and the per-workload config keys .15.11 landed at wamn_postgres/mod.rs:143,:147, and nothing reconciles them. A pod could serve the manifest for digest D1 while the claim stamps D2 onto the run, silently, which is exactly what the .2.3/.2.7 successor rule exists to prevent. .15.66 now depends on it, because its equality check is only meaningful once the authoritative carrier is named.

The naming rule is enforced in code: the module documents at length that this is a weld and not a cache, why invalidation cannot exist, and how it differs from ResolutionPlanCache next door.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): invent the GitOps desired-state source and write releases into it
description:
## Why

Split from wamn-0h0g.15.14 (owner ruling 2026-08-16: mint-only scope, per-leg beads). wamn-0h0g.15.16 stands up CONVERGENCE 'over the GitOps source the publish bead writes' — this bead is that source and its writer. It must exist before .15.16 has anything to converge.

## VERIFIED: THE GITOPS SOURCE DOES NOT EXIST IN ANY FORM

This bead INVENTS it. It is not 'write to an existing source'.
  - Zero argo / flux / kustomize / gitops hits across all .yaml, .yml, .md, .rs, .toml, .sh outside docs/ spec prose. (helm hits are only the third-party runtime-operator chart.)
  - No directory named gitops, argocd, flux, clusters, overlays or base anywhere.
  - deploy/README.md:1-24 defines exactly four tiers — infra/, platform/, gates/, sql/ — ALL hand-applied by kubectl apply -f, and states 'A new file goes in exactly one tier; nothing lands at the top level.' There is no fifth desired-state tier.
  - deploy/platform/*.yaml are HAND-WRITTEN; every file carries a kubectl apply -f runbook header (e.g. runner.yaml:9-16). No generator, no DO-NOT-EDIT marker.
  - ZERO kind: ConfigMap renderers exist. The only K8s-object renderers are Secret/CR renderers in crates/control/provision/ (secret.rs:44, database.rs:64, org.rs:246, backup.rs:71/:116, dump.rs:268/:291) plus services/ctl/src/provision_org.rs:310 — all return serde_json::Value and emit to stdout or a file. The K8s write path is DELIBERATELY excluded: crates/control/provision/src/secret.rs:41-43 says so in terms.
  - Nothing mounts /etc/wamn/release-manifest or /etc/wamn/release-identity. The constants exist (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:58, :71) with no mount anywhere in deploy/.

## Scope

(1) Decide and document the GitOps source layout — a fifth deploy/ tier or a separate synced repo — and who syncs it. This is a DESIGN RULING and should be settled before implementation. (2) Write the environment desired state into it: the release manifest as an IMMUTABLE ConfigMap named by digest (release_manifest_configmap_name, serving_manifest.rs:82) referenced BY NAME in pod templates so manifest/image atomicity holds by construction (ratification ruling 4); the release-identity ConfigMap (release version, manifest digest — keys at serving_manifest.rs:75, :79); and any changed CRDs. (3) Add the missing ConfigMap renderer following the existing provision renderer idiom.

## DEPENDENCY NOTE

The mounts this bead creates are what wamn-0h0g.15.12 reads at runtime under the manifest-delivery ruling (host loads /etc/wamn/release-manifest, walks reachable_flows, supplies over the existing plan-supply WIT). .15.12 can be built and unit-proven against a fixture path first, but nothing runs in-cluster until this bead lands.

## Boundary

Convergence tooling (Argo/Flux, wrong-target protection, rollback-by-revert runbook) is wamn-0h0g.15.16. Minting is .15.14. OCI push is the sibling push bead.
acceptance_criteria: A GitOps desired-state source exists with a documented layout and sync owner; one publish writes the digest-named immutable manifest ConfigMap, the release-identity ConfigMap, and any changed CRDs into it; pod templates reference the manifest ConfigMap by name; a repeated publish is a no-op.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-23 - OCI-NATIVE. The OCI release artifact IS the desired-state source. Do NOT invent a fifth deploy/ tier and do NOT stand up a separate synced GitOps repo; that scope is deleted. Build on the already-landed OCI path: .15.97 (7e42cdfc publish release manifest OCI artifact), .15.111 (0632a5c2 pin OCI artifact layout), .15.17 (3781c220 OCI registry credentials).

PREMISE CORRECTIONS, measured 2026-08-23:
- Bead claim that nothing mounts /etc/wamn/release-manifest is REFUTED. deploy/platform/executor.yaml:98-99 mounts it, :108-110 declares the configMap volume with a 64-zero placeholder name, :76 sets WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_ROOT. Landed by .15.112 (601149ff). Only the ConfigMap OBJECT is missing.
- Bead note 3 cites deploy/platform/runner.yaml. That file was DELETED by ea71c1c4 (.26.7.2). Its successor is deploy/platform/executor.yaml, whose header at :11-14 names this bead as what makes it appliable.
- TWO pod templates are in scope, not one: services/host/src/host.rs:114-127 documents --release-manifest-root as set on the host template, which is the Helm host-tier values file deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml.
- Canonical bytes are minted into Postgres (services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs:80-81, catalog.release_manifest_v2_snapshots) but publish_release has no CLI verb, and push_release_manifest.rs:138-140 takes a FILE. Nothing bridges them; the lane must.

NOT CLAIMED.
close_reason: SPLIT AND CLOSED FOR THE PART THAT IS DONE. Landed as c2f6ce2e, pushed. Owner ruling held: the OCI release artifact IS the desired-state source, no fifth deploy tier, no synced GitOps repo. THE MEASUREMENT OVERTURNED THE BEAD'S SHAPE ENTIRELY. What a release artifact is today: canonical format-2 ServingManifest bytes, RFC 8785 JSON with the digest a plain SHA-256 over those exact bytes, published as a single-layer OCI data artifact by wamn-ctl push-release-manifest. *** WHAT READS IT: NOTHING. *** The media type and reference helper appeared only in the pusher and its own unit tests - the artifact was WRITE-ONLY. Serving processes read a FILE from a ConfigMap mount. So the gap was never a missing writer; it was a MISSING READER, and the bead's scope item to add a ConfigMap renderer is OVERTAKEN - on the OCI path the ConfigMap is a redundant second carrier of bytes the registry already holds. Shipped: ReleaseManifestSource::pull_verified deriving the immutable reference from base plus digest, refusing an oversized layer BEFORE download, and refusing unless sha256 of the body equals the digest; plus ReleaseManifestWeld::load_canonical_bytes so both carriers share one admission path. The OCI layout build and verify were hoisted out of ctl into the shared wire module so publisher and puller cannot drift, netting minus 90 lines in ctl. Property worth recording: the OCI carrier RESTORES the name-to-bytes check the ConfigMap path explicitly gave up - the digest travels in the pod template, the bytes come from a third party, and they must agree. Also measured: the bead cited serving_manifest.rs:75 and :79 for release-identity ConfigMap keys and NO SUCH CONSTANTS EXIST. *** REMAINDER SPLIT OUT AS wamn-3ceu, P0: the two production call sites still read the file mount, because those hunks were handed to the wave-53 host-config lane and never arrived, so the OCI path is DEAD CODE until they land. *** Further follow-ups filed: wamn-cdky bridge the minted snapshot to its push, wamn-04m1 expose publish-release as a verb, wamn-nguw retire the stale load_plan_release weld site.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(publish): push the release manifest as an OCI artifact
description:
## Why

Split from wamn-0h0g.15.14 (mint-only scope). Ruling .13.45 holds both copies: this bead delivers the OCI push as the audit/distribution copy; the digest-named ConfigMap is the serving copy and belongs to the GitOps-source-write bead. The plan-bytes leg is dropped — execution plans and the compiler retire under exe-model.md.

## VERIFIED GREENFIELD

No OCI push code exists in this repository: zero oci_client / oci_wasm / `use oci` hits outside target/, and services/builder does not exist. oci-client 0.17.0 is in Cargo.lock only transitively via wash-runtime.

## Scope

Push the minted release manifest as a content-addressed OCI artifact — a distribution projection, idempotently re-derivable, retries converging to identical digests with no re-push side effects. Use plain oci-client blob/manifest APIs, NOT oci-wasm and NOT wash_runtime::oci::pull_component (both wasm-layer-specific; wrong for canonical-JSON manifest data).

## HARD SERIALIZATION POINT

A direct oci-client dependency edits root Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies]; wamn-0h0g.15.12 and .15.20 edit the same file. Sequence, do not parallelise.

## Boundary

Registry surface and push/pull credentials are wamn-0h0g.15.17 — its dependency edge points at .15.14, which is backwards if a push needs credentials first; re-rule that edge. Minting is .15.14. GitOps writing is .15.98. Component-image push is the supply-chain floor, not this bead.
acceptance_criteria: One publish yields digest-stable manifest and plan artifacts in the registry; a repeated publish converges without re-minting or duplicate artifacts; the push is provably re-derivable from catalog.execution_bundles.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(ingress): first host-side implementation of wamn:flow-http-routing
description:
## Why

Split from wamn-0h0g.15.13 (owner ruling 2026-08-16: per-leg beads). VERIFIED TRUE: no host implementation of wamn:flow-http-routing exists anywhere in the tree. Full-tree grep returns 5 hits, all WIT/docs/deploy: docs/deployment-simplification-spec.md:221, deploy/platform/flow-http-workload.example.yaml:9 and :48, components/ingress/flow-http/wit/world.wit:4, and the package definition. Zero hits under crates/ or services/; no bindgen! on that world, no add_to_linker, no HostPlugin impl. flow-http therefore cannot serve a single route in-cluster today — components/ingress/flow-http/src/guest.rs:59-66 calls an import nothing implements.

## Scope

Implement the host side of package wamn:flow-http-routing@0.1.0, interface routing (components/ingress/flow-http/wit/deps/wamn-flow-http-routing/package.wit), serving RouteDefinition from the manifest attachment projection. Three functions: routes(method, authority), authenticate(policy, headers), caller-connected(). Per ruling .13.52 the manifest carries the attachment but NOT enabled — enablement is checked inside the EXISTING admission transaction and keeps the existing attachment-inactive refusal literal, so this plugin adds zero serving-path database reads.

## REGISTRATION SEAM — THE BEAD THIS WAS SPLIT FROM DID NOT DISTINGUISH THESE

There are two distinct host processes and wiring this into the wrong one silently fails:
  - crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:524-541 / :564-585 — the flowrunner-only IN-PROCESS host.
  - services/host/src/host.rs:140-164 — the WASH host that actually runs the flow-http and materializer workloads (.with_plugin chain: wasi_config, WamnLogging, WasiOtel, WamnPostgres, WamnJetstream, WamnFlowInvocation).
THIS PLUGIN REGISTERS IN services/host/src/host.rs, not crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs.

Plugin pattern to follow (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs): mod bindings { bindgen!({world, imports:{default: async|trappable|tracing}}) } -> pub const <ID> -> owning struct -> pub fn add_to_linker(linker) -> impl HostPlugin { id(); world() -> WitWorld{imports, exports} } -> fn plugin_of(ctx) via ctx.try_get_plugin::<T>(ID) -> impl <iface>::Host for ActiveCtx. Declaration and re-export both go in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/mod.rs (the pub mod block :1-9 and the pub use block :11-20).

## Boundary

HTTP exposure manifests belong to the operator-adoption bead. Attachment enablement stays a database read inside the existing admission transaction. Does not touch the flowrunner plan-supply path (wamn-0h0g.15.12) or the materializer (wamn-0h0g.15.95).
acceptance_criteria: flow-http serves routes from the manifest attachment projection through a host implementation of wamn:flow-http-routing registered in services/host/src/host.rs; enablement remains the existing admission-transaction check with its existing refusal literal; no route read hits the project database on the serving path.
notes:
MANDATORY RIDER — ONE MANIFEST INSTANCE (owner, 2026-08-16). This bead is READER 3 OF 4. It consults THE SAME loaded, digest-verified manifest instance as plan-supply (.15.12), effect authority (.15.66) and jetstream delivery gating (.15.95), supplied by wamn-0h0g.15.100, which now blocks this bead. It must NOT load, parse, or digest-verify a manifest itself — it reads the attachment projection off the shared instance. One object, one weld, four enumerated readers; nobody loads a second copy.

NAMING: the weld is not a cache. A digest-named object cannot go stale, so no TTL, refresh, eviction or revalidation may exist on it. Note this plugin serves routes on a hot request path, which is exactly where someone would reach for a cache — do not add one. The manifest is already in memory, parsed, for the life of the process; a second layer over it would be pure risk.

READERS 3 AND 4 SHARE A PROCESS. This plugin and the jetstream gate (.15.95) both run in the WASH HOST (services/host/src/host.rs, .with_plugin chain :140-164), so they take their reference from that process's single weld instance. Readers 1 and 2 run in the separate flowrunner in-process host (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs, plugin map :564-585). Per-process instantiation, one instance each, never two in one process.

FILE-DOMAIN NOTE FOR LANE DISPATCH: crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/mod.rs (20 lines: 9 pub mod + 9 pub use) is edited by this bead, .15.12 and .15.100. It is owned by the integrator and pre-edited before lanes start; do not touch it in a lane.
close_reason: Commit 9aba5a65. First host implementation of wamn:flow-http-routing anywhere, serving route-definition off the manifest's attachment projection with ZERO project-database reads on the serving path, and deliberately no route index -- that would be the cache the naming rule forbids, on the one hot path where someone would reach for one. PREMISE CORRECTION THAT WAS THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN LINKING AND NOT: the bead names runner_plan_supply.rs as the pattern, but that plugin is linked BY HAND by the flowrunner host; in the wash host HostPlugin::world() only gates whether on_workload_item_bind fires and the trait default links nothing, so following the named pattern would have produced a plugin that never links. Two prerequisites the bead omitted were applied by the integrator: a flow-http-routing-plugin world and a vendored dep package, since bindgen! resolves $CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/wit. Every field the manifest cannot source is deferred to its real authority and recorded at the field rather than guessed: enabled true (activation has no carrier under .13.52, and a constant false would invite a caller-side filter that 404s a live release), idempotency_required false (admission derives it from plan bytes and refuses with the identical literal), deadline_override None (passing the response deadline would invert the relation deadline-inversion validation protects), limits u32::MAX not u64::MAX (the guest narrows with usize::try_from and usize is 32 bits on wasm32), caller_connected true with the reason stated -- a host plugin cannot know, the socket is owned by the runtime's serve loop -- and its accepted consequence recorded. Release-less REFUSES rather than serving an empty set; a malformed attachment is skipped and warned so one broken document does not 503 the pod. There is NO auth-policy vocabulary in the tree (the resolver validates an auth source as only is_object(); four fixtures invent four shapes), so one policy is honoured and everything else typed-refused. 10 named tests each with its killing mutation. FILED: .15.117 (definition-hash prefix contradiction, dep .15.14 -- will bite the first end-to-end route), .15.118 (no entry input-schema guard for HTTP-admitted runs), .15.119 (authenticate trusts the echoed policy), .15.120 (no WIT-coherence test).

title: [SR-MVP] feat(events): gate jetstream delivery on manifest registration identity
description:
## Why

RE-SCOPED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-16. The original split-out leg ('deliver the manifest to the materializer, replace the registration sweep') was not dispatchable: the materializer guest world imports wamn:postgres and wamn:jetstream only — no plan-supply interface and no wasi:filesystem — so it can neither be handed a manifest nor read a mounted one.

The ruling moves the enforcement to where it already sits in the delivery path: GATE wamn:jetstream EVENT DELIVERY ON MANIFEST REGISTRATION IDENTITY, HOST-SIDE. THE GUEST IS UNCHANGED. Registration identity becomes a property of the release the pod is serving, enforced before an event is ever handed to a component, rather than something the materializer re-derives from a database sweep it must be trusted to run correctly.

## Scope
