In the WamnJetstream plugin (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_jetstream.rs, registered in the wash host at services/host/src/host.rs:140-164), gate delivery on the manifest's registration projection: ServingRegistration { flow_id, entity, ops } (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:255-273, held under ServingManifest::registrations :292). An event whose registration identity is not a member of the serving release is not delivered.

Ruling .13.53 stands as amended: IDENTITY (source, target flow, existence) is the manifest's and is what this gate enforces. The evaluation-time CONDITION is not identity and is not gated here.

## PREMISE CORRECTION — .13.53 IS WORDED WRONG AND IT MATTERS HERE

The ruling says the condition 'stays an environment-hot COLUMN'. It is not a column. catalog.event_registrations (deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:1742-1750) has exactly tenant_id, catalog_id, registration_id, flow_id, entity_id, registration jsonb. 'condition' is an optional KEY INSIDE the registration jsonb document (crates/events/registration/src/model.rs:70-79, compiled at crates/events/materializer/src/decide.rs:169-171). There is no condition column to read and none to leave behind — the jsonb document column stays because the condition rides inside it.

## MANDATORY RIDER — ONE MANIFEST INSTANCE

This plugin consults THE SAME loaded, digest-verified manifest instance as plan-supply, effect authority and routing, supplied by wamn-0h0g.15.100. It must NOT load, parse, or digest-verify a manifest itself. One object, one weld, four enumerated readers; nobody loads a second copy.

## Boundary

Guest unchanged: no edit to components/execution/materializer/ or its WIT. The existing per-event database transaction and the condition evaluation on it are untouched. The existing identity cross-check in the guest (components/execution/materializer/src/main.rs:311-320, mismatch => HELD) is superseded by this gate only insofar as the gate makes an unregistered event undeliverable; state explicitly whether it is retired or retained as defence in depth. Whether the crates/events/materializer/src/sql.rs:12 sweep can then narrow or drop is a consequence to be measured and recorded, not assumed.
acceptance_criteria: An event whose registration identity is absent from the serving release's manifest projection is refused delivery host-side, before reaching any component, with a named refusal proven by a focused test; the materializer guest and its WIT are byte-unchanged; condition evaluation still happens on the existing per-event transaction; the plugin holds no manifest of its own.
close_reason: Commit b405694e. Delivery gated host-side at consumer::bind on the manifest's registration projection; guest and WIT byte-unchanged; no new JsError variant. Gated at the SUBSCRIPTION not per message -- per-message filtering would force the host to take over an ack disposition the WIT gives the guest, and a bind refusal delivers ZERO events, satisfying 'before reaching any component' strictly while leaving events on the stream (the ratified HOLD posture). Release-less line drawn precisely: bind is gated, publish/ring/message methods are not (a message is only reachable through a bound consumer; publish and ring carry no registration identity, and gating them would break the doorbell on every release-less host). THE BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE IS WRONG: condition evaluation does NOT happen on the per-event transaction -- it is compiled once per sweep and evaluated per event in the PURE decide, before any transaction exists; the same error was in the serving-manifest doc and the spec and both are corrected. MEASURED per instruction: the registration sweep can neither narrow nor drop -- every value it selects has a consumer the manifest cannot supply -- and that measurement is now pinned by an assertion. flow_id is NOT enforceable at this seam (the host sees only entity.op from the filter subject); the guest's identity cross-check is RETAINED and is orthogonal, not defence in depth. REGRESSION REPAIRED IN THE SAME COMMIT: matbench, rie2ebench and causation_e2e drove the real guest release-lessly and would have fired zero runs; all three now load a real weld via one shared release_fixture helper, with each registration derived from the harness's actual filter subject. TRAP: ServingRegistration::ops is a BTreeSet and the canonicalizer preserves ARRAY order, so an unsorted ops array never round-trips and is refused as non-canonical. Pre-existing gap reported not filed: the gate checks only the entity.op tail, so a foreign org/project/env prefix with a colliding entity token would still bind.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(run-state): every claimability-reopening arm must clear the release record
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.55 redefines the record's contract as **the release of the claim currently executing this run** — the only definition coherent with no-pinning and with wamn-0h0g.15.55's per-claim-attempt scope.

wamn-0h0g.15.55 shipped the transition-constrained guard for ONE arm: the classifier's pre-effect reclaim. The ruling's premise that this covers every path is false in this repository, and .15.55's close records why: `park_sql` NULLs `lease_owner` and `lease_expires_at`, so `select_production_claim_sql` derives `had_prior_lease` false, `classify_production_claim` returns `Ordinary`, and the `Ordinary` arm resets nothing before falling through to the grant. A waking pod on a different release refuses.

wamn-0h0g.15.69 does not rescue it either: a park releases the lease, so the crash-evidence advance adds zero, and `select_exhausted_production_sql` requires a non-NULL `lease_expires_at`. A parked run that refuses on wake is BOTH UNREAPABLE AND PERMANENTLY THE FIFO HEAD.

## Scope

Make the rule uniform: **any arm that reopens claimability CLEARS the pair; any claim acquisition WRITES it.** Park's lease-null included. The Ordinary-classification hole closes and park stops being a latent head-of-line block.

Note that the landed guard's erasure arm currently requires no `node_runs` and no `effect_attempts` row for the run — a parked run has generally EXECUTED NODES, so extending the reset to park requires reconciling the arm with that predicate. Under the redefined contract that is coherent (the record names the current claim, not the run's history), but it is the load-bearing part of this bead and must be stated explicitly, not assumed.

## Boundary

LATENT TODAY, NOT LIVE: `park_sql` has no production caller — its only reference outside the builder and its export is a unit test. wamn-0h0g.15.55 left a proof leg pinning the current behaviour, and that leg must be inverted here.

The per-segment audit question — what nodes 1..k ran under — is explicitly NOT this bead's and is demand-gated by the ruling.

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16 (wave-3 decisions).
close_reason: SHIPPED d1973791. Ruling .13.55 applied uniformly: park_sql now clears (release_version, manifest_digest), closing the Ordinary-classification hole that made a parked run BOTH unreapable AND permanently FIFO head. GUARD RECONCILIATION: the node_runs leg is DROPPED (it encoded the old per-run contract; an executed node is history, not a current-claim fact -- the per-segment question is .15.85's, demand-gated). The effect_attempts leg is KEPT UNTOUCHED -- it is the mid-effect-rewrite defence, and a run with an attempt classifies ExpiredWithAttempt regardless of had_prior_lease, so it never re-executes under a second release. The status leg is kept. Because effect_attempts stays, park_sql carries AND NOT EXISTS(effect_attempts) so a post-effect park does not abort. The .15.55 leg pinning the WRONG behaviour is inverted and drives the shipped builder against real PostgreSQL. CORRECTION: not four byte-identical mirrors -- only two are; the DEF differs by escaping AND pg_get_functiondef header rendering, and the live-test copy is a hand reflow. All five normalized to one hash; the four non-reflowed bodies compared byte-for-byte.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(run-state): the audit story for a run that spans two releases
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13's .15.55 decision states that the classifier's pre-effect reset cures the park/doorbell collision because "every path that re-opens claimability flows through the classifier's reset". THAT PREMISE IS FALSE IN THIS REPOSITORY, confirmed twice independently at the wave-3 close.

`park_sql` (crates/execution/run-state/src/queue/sql.rs) NULLs `lease_owner` and `lease_expires_at`. `select_production_claim_sql` derives `had_prior_lease` as `lease_expires_at IS NOT NULL`, so after a park it is FALSE, and `classify_production_claim` returns `Ordinary`. The `Ordinary` arm of `claim_in_transaction` is empty — no projection check, no reset — and falls straight through to the grant. A waking pod on a different release therefore still hits `value -> value'` and refuses.

AND wamn-0h0g.15.69 DOES NOT RESCUE IT. A park releases the lease, so the crash-evidence advance adds 0 and `attempts` never moves; `select_exhausted_production_sql` additionally requires `lease_expires_at IS NOT NULL`, which a parked row fails. So a parked run that refuses on wake is BOTH UNREAPABLE AND PERMANENTLY THE FIFO HEAD — strictly worse than the expired-lease case the beads describe.

MITIGATING, AND THE REASON THIS IS NOT ALREADY BURNING: `park_sql` has NO PRODUCTION CALLER. Its only reference outside the builder and its export is a unit test. The collision is LATENT. It becomes a live head-of-line block the moment park is wired.

## The decision

The blocker is not mechanical, it is semantic: WHAT IS THE AUDIT STORY FOR A RUN WHOSE NODES 1..k EXECUTED UNDER RELEASE A AND k+1.. UNDER RELEASE B?

Only once that is answered can the arm be written. The options each presuppose a different answer:

(a) `park_sql` ALSO CLEARS THE PAIR. But a parked run has generally EXECUTED NODES, so the erasure is refused by the landed guard — and more importantly, erasing there destroys the record of the release the run's first half actually ran under. This answer says: a run has no single release, and the record names only its latest claim.

(b) THE `Ordinary` ARM GAINS A RESET. That is the always-clear-then-re-record shape — i.e. option (a) from the original .15.55 analysis wearing option (c)'s clothes. Same audit consequence as above, reached by a different path.

(c) ACCEPT THAT A RESUMED-ACROSS-ROLLOUT RUN HAS NO SINGLE RELEASE and change what the record MEANS — from "the release this run executed under" to "the release of the claim that is currently executing it". That is a documentation and contract change, not a code change, and it makes (a) or (b) honest rather than lossy.

## Boundary

Park/wake is left as-is by wamn-0h0g.15.55, now with a proof leg pinning the current behaviour so the gap cannot close silently. This must be settled before park is wired, and before the merge gate wamn-0h0g.15.25 if park is wired in this program.

Filed at the wave-3 close (2026-08-16).
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16, wave-3 decisions):

REDEFINE, AND UNIFY THE RESET.

The record's contract becomes "THE RELEASE OF THE CLAIM CURRENTLY EXECUTING THIS RUN". That is the only definition coherent with no-pinning ("runs execute under the claiming pod's release") and with wamn-0h0g.15.55's per-claim-attempt scope. The other two options are this same ruling done dishonestly.

MECHANICALLY: extend .15.55's transition rule to EVERY claimability-reopening arm — park's lease-null included. Any arm that reopens claimability CLEARS; any claim acquisition WRITES. The Ordinary-classification hole closes and park stops being a latent head-of-line block.

What nodes 1..k ran under is a PER-SEGMENT AUDIT QUESTION, and its honest home is per-claim, not per-run. DEMAND-GATED: if park ships to production and audit names the need, release joins the claim/lease event stream then. Nothing is built for it now.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. REDEFINE, AND UNIFY THE RESET.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(flow-model): carry test cases in the flow document
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.27 shipped parts 1 and 3 — the flat expect shape and the deletion of the test-set store on both planes. PART 2 DID NOT SHIP: it needs crates/execution/flow-model/**, which was outside that lane's file domain.

Until it lands there is NO PRODUCER for `TestSetCase` anywhere in the tree, and the acceptance clause "one draft hash covers flow and tests" is unmet.

## Scope

1. `cases: Vec<TestSetCase>` on `Flow` (crates/execution/flow-model/src/types.rs), `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`.
2. THE SAME FIELD IN `FlowPreimage` (src/preimage.rs, and `shared()`) — this is the load-bearing half. Without it the draft hash does not cover the tests, successor-draft copies do not carry them forward, and the publish weld stops meaning what it says.
3. A `validate_cases` call in src/validate.rs.

## Blocked on an owner decision

WHERE THE TYPE LIVES AND WHO OWNS ITS `JsonSchema` DERIVE. `Flow` derives `schemars::JsonSchema`; `wamn-scenario-model` has no schemars dependency today. Either (a) `wamn-flow` depends on `wamn-scenario-model` and that crate gains schemars — acyclic today, it depends only on serde/serde_json — or (b) `TestSetCase`/`Expect` move into `wamn-flow` and `wamn-scenario-model` shrinks to the evaluator. Do not guess; this sets a crate-graph direction.

Filed at the wave-3 close (2026-08-16).
design:
SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

RULED: THE TYPES MOVE INTO `wamn-flow`; `wamn-scenario-model` SHRINKS TO THE EVALUATOR.

The tests-in-draft ruling made the case PART OF THE FLOW DOCUMENT, and document types belong to the document's contract crate.

The alternative — `wamn-flow` depending on `wamn-scenario-model` — has the document crate depending on an EVALUATOR crate, and drags `schemars` into that crate for one type. It inverts the layering to save a move.

So: `TestSetCase` and `Expect` move into `wamn-flow`. `wamn-scenario-model` keeps `Captured`, `evaluate`, and the outcome record.

CONSEQUENCE NOTED FOR THE RENAME SWEEP: a crate that is now evaluator-only carries a name that says "model". Filed separately.
close_reason: SHIPPED eb1c3a88. Types moved into wamn-flow per the ruling; FlowFailureKind moved with them (reachable from Flow, and leaving it would drag schemars into the evaluator); validate_cases and its bounds moved with the type they bound. Edge is one-way and acyclic. cases on Flow AND FlowPreimage incl. shared(), so one draft hash now covers flow and tests. CASES ARE NOT SORTED -- test_orchestration.rs:194 derives ordinals by .enumerate() and test_case_run_id makes the ordinal durable run identity, so copying the nodes-sorted-by-id precedent would have let permuted documents share a draft hash. validate_cases REFUSES empty, so the flow-level call is guarded on non-empty; taken literally the scope would have marked every existing flow invalid. Expect::validate widened to pub -- deleting the cross-crate re-check would have let a contradictory Expect silently pass. CAUGHT A SILENT BREAK: a second Flow literal in components/execution/flowrunner/src/frames.rs, which root Cargo.toml EXCLUDES, so cargo check --workspace never compiles it; fixed and verified for wasm32-wasip2. Flow schema regenerated (+79 lines, no deletions).

title: [SR-MVP] feat(admission): check attachment enablement in the admission transaction
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.52. Enablement is environment-owned operational state and does not belong in a content-addressed document. The enforcement point is sharper than a readiness overlay: the admission transaction ALREADY EXISTS and ALREADY hits the database, so checking there costs zero added serving-path reads.

## Scope

Check attachment enablement inside the admission transaction, refusing with the EXISTING `attachment-inactive` literal. The manifest supplies the attachment; the database supplies whether it is on.

## Boundary

The property this preserves is operational: emergency-off stays ONE `UPDATE`, effective on the next admission — immediately — rather than a mint, a digest, a GitOps commit and a rollout. Pairs with the manifest amendment that removes `enabled`.

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16.
design:
EVIDENCE CORRECTION (2026-08-16, gathered at the wave-3 dispatch).

THE RULING NAMES A LITERAL THAT DOES NOT EXIST. Ruling .13.52 says to refuse "via the existing `attachment-inactive` literal". There is no `attachment-inactive` anywhere in the repository. The existing refusal is:
  - `attachment-disabled`, a 404 rejection at crates/platform/runtime/src/flow_invocation.rs:312 and :758
  - reached from `AdmissionResult::InactiveDefinition`
  - computed INSIDE the admission SQL at crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs:346, as `WHEN i.producer = 'http' AND d.attachment_id IS NULL THEN 'inactive-definition'`
The ruling's INTENT is satisfied by that path; only the name was wrong.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S SCOPE. Admission ALREADY checks enablement inside the admission transaction and already produces the refusal the ruling asks for. `catalog.attachment_activation.enabled` (deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:674, :756) is read there today, and crates/execution/run-state/src/invocation.rs:48 documents resolving an HTTP attachment from the applied release "even when disabled" so a released outcome stays retrievable — the §6.2 lookup order.

So this is NOT new machinery. It is a PIN: the invariant must survive wamn-0h0g.15.13 moving route resolution to the mounted manifest. When routes come from the manifest, enablement must still be an admission-transaction database read still yielding `attachment-disabled`, and the disabled-attachment-still-serves-a-released-outcome leg must still hold.

THE WORK IS THEREFORE: a test pinning that enablement is read from Postgres in the admission transaction and refuses with `attachment-disabled`, plus the disabled-but-released-outcome leg, standing before .15.13 lands so .15.13 cannot silently regress it. If .15.13's implementation preserves it by construction, this bead closes on that evidence rather than on new code.
close_reason: SHIPPED 549cfd19 as a PIN, not new machinery -- the ruling's intent was already satisfied by shipped code and nothing was missing except proof. THE LOAD-BEARING CORRECTION: the admit statement contains ZERO occurrences of 'enabled' and never names attachment_activation. It reads the catalog.active_attachments VIEW, and it is the VIEW -- in deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql, a different file -- that joins attachment_activation and filters WHERE activation.enabled. .15.13 could sever enablement without editing one byte of admission.rs, so the pin include_str!s the SQL artifact and asserts BOTH ends of the chain. The pre-existing admission_live assertion covered the WRONG HALF: its fixture uses an attachment id never inserted into release_attachments, exercising absence-from-the-release rather than activation; its one activation row is enabled=true and never flipped, so LIVE COVERAGE OF ENABLEMENT WAS ZERO. A real emergency-off block now proves off->refuse->on->admit with a byte-identical statement. flow_invocation.rs:312 is NOT in the admission transaction and is the gate .15.13 is likeliest to delete (.15.70 already removed enabled from ServingAttachment); deleting it AND :758 would silently remove emergency-off. An 8-item 'what .15.13 must not break' list is on the bead. attachment-inactive confirmed nonexistent for the fourth time.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(schema): amend the serving manifest to release shape only
description:
## Why

Rulings wamn-0h0g.13.52 and .13.53 set the governing principle: **the manifest carries release SHAPE; environment-operational state stays in Postgres.** The schema frozen by wamn-0h0g.15.61 (commit e38dd2a1) carries two pieces of environment-operational state that must come out.

## Scope

1. **Remove `enabled` from `ServingAttachment`.** Activation is environment-owned and wamn's own landed invariant says it 'never participates in hashes'. The attachment stays (routes are immutable per release); enablement moves to the admission transaction (separate bead).
2. **Reduce `registrations` to identity only** — source, target flow, existence. The condition stays an environment-hot column read by the materializer at evaluation. Today the field carries the stored `catalog.event_registrations` document verbatim.
3. Update the digest-stability and field-classification tests, which pin every key set by design.

## Boundary

Cheap now and expensive later: nothing consumes the schema yet. Must land before wamn-0h0g.15.13. Both removals change the canonical bytes and therefore every digest — that is correct and expected, since no manifest has been minted.

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16.
close_reason: Landed at 02172e28. ServingAttachment lost 'enabled'; registrations reduced to identity (flow-id, entity, ops) with the condition left as an environment-hot materializer read. New deny_unknown_fields guard refuses a document carrying either removed field, proven load-bearing by a restored mutant (sha256 1e77623d). cargo check -p wamn-catalog --all-targets clean, 39 tests pass. Unblocks .15.12 .15.13 .15.16 .15.29 .15.49. Two items raised for owner: the ruling's 'attachment-inactive' literal does not exist (real ones are inactive-definition and attachment-disabled), and ServingRelease.environment now scopes by label alone.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(run-state): a refused claim must not starve its own janitor
description:
## Why

Independent of any ruling, and the owner called it out as a fix to make regardless.

`attempts` is incremented inside the same statement that grants the lease. When that statement aborts — as it now can, since wamn-0h0g.15.11 made the release record refuse a differing write — the increment rolls back with it. The run therefore can NEVER reach `max_attempts`, so the production janitor can never reap it to `infrastructure-failure`.

Combined with the fact that nothing locks the run after rollback, it stays the FIFO head forever: **one run head-of-line-blocks a tenant indefinitely**, with a single per-turn WARN as the only operator signal and no run-level metric at all.

This is a defect in its own right. Any statement that can abort must not be the only thing that advances the crash-evidence counter, or a refusal becomes permanent by construction.

## Scope

Separate `attempts` advancement from the abortable grant statement so a refused or failed claim still counts as crash evidence and the janitor can eventually reap the run. Preserve the existing semantics: attempts counts crash evidence only — granting over a prior non-NULL lease increments it; first claim and park/wake reclaim do not.

## Boundary

Independent of wamn-0h0g.15.55's reset-per-attempt ruling — that ruling removes the most likely trigger, but the starvation shape must not survive it. Evidence gathered at the wamn-0h0g.15.11 close (commit 618a5800).

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16.
close_reason: Fixed at 30096599. The crash-evidence advance is now its own statement before the grant, and the grant runs in SAVEPOINT wamn_production_grant so a refusal rolls back to the savepoint while the outer transaction stays committable and retains the selector's FOR UPDATE locks. Counted semantics byte-identical (reads lease_expires_at before the grant overwrites it). Observability deferred to .15.81 (named in the bead's Why, not its Scope). Live proof leg rides e17b9b90, same fixture. cargo check -p wamn-runtime at baseline (4 known errors), 78 run-state tests pass.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(exec): restore the run-to-plan binding in effect authority
description:
## Why — this is a security regression, deliberately incurred and currently untracked in code

wamn-0h0g.15.10 deleted the `run_flow_resolutions` EXISTS predicate from the effect-authority CTE at crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/claims.rs:117-121. The deletion was FORCED — the predicate named the table the ruling deletes, and no narrower edit preserves it — but it removed link 1 of the five-link chain the spec states at docs/deployment-simplification-spec.md:63-66, and nothing replaces it.

THE CHAIN BECAME SELF-REFERENTIAL. All eight lookup parameters are guest-supplied; `validate_claims` (connection_http.rs:203-216) checks SHAPE ONLY, never authenticity. The deleted EXISTS was the only DATABASE-SIDE statement binding the guest-declared `current_plan_hash` ($3) and `source_artifact_hash` ($7) to the run: it matched an immutable claim-time row written before any guest code ran and protected by UPDATE/DELETE triggers, so effect authority held even against a fully compromised component.

Now `resolution_matches` is true whenever ANY bundle with hash $3 exists in the run's tenant. Every remaining constraint on $3 flows through `attempt_matches` — but `effect_attempts` is written by `begin_effect_attempt` (crates/execution/run-state/src/effect_writer.rs:1054-1071) from THE SAME guest-supplied context, gated only on the run being leased and running (:1038-1042), never on the plan hash belonging to the run. The guest asserts $3, the host writes $3, and authority then checks $3 against the row the guest just caused. The run-to-plan binding is no longer verified by the database at all.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCE — cross-flow effect-node borrowing within a tenant. A compromised or buggy component executing run R under flow A can present `current_plan_hash` = the bundle hash of ANY other flow B in the same tenant's catalog, paired with `source_artifact_hash` = any artifact bound in R's own (catalog_id, catalog_version, environment). If B's plan contains a node with the chosen local-node-id whose source-connection-requirement descriptor equals the descriptor recorded for that artifact/requirement, authority is granted and the host performs the HTTP effect under that node's connection generation and credential handle. A run executes an effect node its own flow does not contain, potentially under a superseded plan version.

WHAT STILL HOLDS (this is escalation WITHIN a tenant, not cross-tenant): tenant isolation is intact (catalog.execution_bundles has FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY with a tenant policy at deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:194-198, plus the outer LEFT JOIN on plan.tenant_id = r.tenant_id at claims.rs:142); the root plan is still server-pinned ($2, claims.rs:123); `binding` still joins on the run's catalog_id/catalog_version/environment, so only connections reachable by that run's release are in play; and the plan node's descriptor must match exactly.

## Scope

Restore a run-scoped predicate to `authorized_plan` once wamn-0h0g.15.11 lands `(release_version, manifest_digest)`, of the shape:

    WHERE bundle.execution_bundle_hash = $3
      AND EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM runs AS pin
                    WHERE pin.tenant_id = bundle.tenant_id
                      AND pin.run_id    = $1
                      AND <the recorded manifest_digest's manifest contains (flow, $3)> )

and re-add a mutant to tools/gate-mutants/current-plan-effect-authority.sh anchored on that predicate.

Also correct that campaign's OUTCOME line (currently "HTTP effects require the exact current plan, source artifact, and attempt"): after .15.10 no mutant in it can fail if the current plan is wrong for the run, so the stated outcome overstates what it proves.

## Boundary

MUST BLOCK THE MERGE GATE wamn-0h0g.15.25. The spec calls this change a "map lookup rewording" (line 190); link 1 was REMOVED, not reworded, and the spec text needs correcting too.

Filed from the independent verification of wamn-0h0g.15.10 (2026-08-16).
design:
OPTIONS FOR THE OWNER (2026-08-16, wave 3). THIS BEAD AS SCOPED IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE, and the reason is architectural rather than incidental.

THE SCOPE CLAUSE ASKS FOR SQL THE DATABASE CANNOT RUN. It proposes restoring a predicate of the shape "the recorded manifest_digest's manifest contains (flow, $3)". The manifest is a mounted ConfigMap file. Postgres cannot read it. Under the old model the equivalent fact lived in a table (run_flow_resolutions); the ruling moved that fact into a file, so no purely-SQL restoration of link 1 exists. Whoever implements this must first choose WHERE authority lives, and that is an owner call.

WHAT SURVIVES AND CAN BE BUILT ON: runs.execution_bundle_hash is retained as the server-pinned ROOT plan (deliberately kept at the .15.11 close, since the reconciler has no drop path for the FK); runs.(release_version, manifest_digest) is recorded at claim; the manifest carries call-edge adjacency; and claims.rs:200-205 still compares the plan node's source-connection-requirement descriptor against the stored requirement_json, so a drifted descriptor fails closed as node-not-permitted. That last check is why the residual hole is node-BORROWING rather than node-FORGING.

WHAT IS MISSING EVERYWHERE: the effect path carries no flow identity at all. Not in the WIT invocation-context (wamn-runner/package.wit:68-78 and the flowrunner mirror), not in HttpEffectPrincipal (invocation_context.rs:104-112), not in effect_attempts (run-state.sql:440-452). runs.flow_id is the ROOT flow only, so it cannot speak for a callee frame. Any option that wants to key authority on flow identity is a frozen-WIT wire change. (Established by the wamn-0h0g.15.62 probe.)

--- OPTION A: CLAIM-TIME MATERIALIZATION (restore link 1's exact shape) ---
At claim, after mounting, the worker derives the run's reachable plan-hash set from the manifest's adjacency starting at the root flow, and writes it to a run-scoped table protected by UPDATE/DELETE triggers. Effect authority joins it exactly as it joined run_flow_resolutions.
FOR: restores the original property verbatim — an immutable row written before any guest code runs, so authority holds against a fully compromised component; authority stays atomic with the grant, in one statement, in the database.
AGAINST: reintroduces a table that LOOKS like the one the ruling deleted, and will read as backsliding unless the difference is stated: it is derived from the manifest per claim attempt, not a resolution map pinned at admission — it carries no version pin and is re-taken on every reclaim, exactly like the release record. Adds a write to the claim path.

--- OPTION B: PUBLISH-TIME PROJECTION (digest-keyed adjacency table) ---
At publish, project (manifest_digest, flow_id, plan_hash) plus the call-edge adjacency into a control-plane table. Authority joins runs.manifest_digest to it.
FOR: no per-run write; one row set per release; authority stays in SQL and stays atomic.
AGAINST: duplicates release shape into Postgres, which is a THIRD category the ruled boundary does not name — the boundary says the manifest carries release shape and Postgres carries environment-operational state, and this is release shape in Postgres for authority purposes. Needs the owner to say whether that is permitted. Also couples publish to a projection that must never drift from the minted bytes.

--- OPTION C: HOST-SIDE PRE-CHECK (move link 1 out of SQL) ---
Before issuing the authority query, the host verifies $3 is adjacency-reachable from the run's root flow in ITS OWN mounted manifest, having first confirmed its mounted digest equals runs.manifest_digest.
FOR: cheapest by far, no schema at all, and the digest equality makes the check honest — if the mounted digest matches the run's recorded digest, the pod's manifest IS the run's manifest, so local adjacency is authoritative. The host is outside the guest trust boundary, so this still defends against a compromised component.
AGAINST: authority is no longer enforced by the database, so it no longer holds against a compromised HOST, and it is no longer atomic with the grant. The original design's stated strength — "effect authority held even against a fully compromised component" — becomes "against a compromised guest", a real narrowing that should be ruled on rather than absorbed.

--- OPTION D: ACCEPT THE NARROWING ---
Rule that the residual risk is acceptable for MVP and lift this bead's merge-gate block. The residual is cross-flow effect-node borrowing WITHIN one tenant and one release: tenant isolation holds (FORCE RLS on execution_bundles plus the outer join on tenant), the root plan is still server-pinned, binding still joins the run's (catalog_id, catalog_version, environment), and the node descriptor must match exactly. It is privilege escalation between flows of one tenant, not across tenants.
AGAINST: it is a real authority regression against a stated spec invariant, and it was incurred as demolition fallout rather than chosen.

RECOMMENDATION: A, with C as the fallback if the claim-path write is judged too expensive. A is the only option that restores the property as specified rather than redefining it, and the "it looks like the deleted table" objection is answerable in one sentence. B's cost is conceptual rather than technical and needs a boundary ruling first.

NOT STARTED. No lane was given this bead — choosing among these is an architecture decision, not implementation.

SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

RULED: OPTION (C), HOST-SIDE PRE-CHECK — AS THE RULING, NOT THE FALLBACK.

WHY THE OTHERS FAIL.
(A) claim-time materialization is `run_flow_resolutions` REBORN: per-claim writes proportional to closure size, a trigger-protected run-scoped table — the exact silhouette of the thing this demolition deletes. "Derived per attempt, not pinned" is a difference of CAPTION, not machinery. It fails the trap-check this program spent a week learning.
(B) puts release shape back in Postgres against the manifest boundary, and is a dual representation besides.
(D) MISCALIBRATES WHAT IS AT STAKE. The residual is NOT privilege escalation — tenant RLS, the server-recorded digest, and binding scoping all hold. It is PER-NODE ATTRIBUTION INTEGRITY AGAINST A BUGGY INTERPRETER, which is an audit property we SELL. It must be restored, not waived.

WHY (C) IS CORRECT RATHER THAN CHEAP. Link 1 existed when the database was the only trusted party at that point in the chain. Under the pod model the HOST is trusted there: it is already the ledger's writer and already the attestation minter, and it holds the run's release document as its own mounted config, WELDED TO THE RUN BY DIGEST EQUALITY — mounted digest equals the server-recorded run digest. A membership check in trusted native code against that mount is the SAME PROPERTY under the SAME THREAT MODEL: the guest is untrusted, exactly as before. Against a compromised HOST the database link never defended anything — the host writes the ledger.

TWO RIDERS, BOTH LOAD-BEARING:
1. The check runs BEFORE `begin_effect_attempt`, so no attempt row ever exists carrying an out-of-closure plan hash. THE LEDGER STAYS AUDIT-CLEAN — that is the point of the whole ruling.
2. Refusal is a TYPED TERMINAL `effect-authority-violation`.

THE MERGE-GATE BLOCK LIFTS WITH (C) IMPLEMENTED, NOT WITH (D).

IMPLEMENTATION FINDING (2026-08-16, gathered when the ruling was recorded) — THE TYPED REFUSAL IS CHEAPER THAN IT READS, WITH ONE CAVEAT.
The frozen WIT variant `effect-error` ALREADY CARRIES `authority-denied` (crates/platform/runtime/wit/deps/wamn-runner/package.wit:101, mirrored in the flowrunner copy), and it is already produced at ~10 sites in connection_http.rs. So the typed host-side refusal needs NO WIT CHANGE. It is also already terminal: flowrunner maps `AuthorityDenied` to `HttpCapError::Denied` (lib.rs:317) and standard-nodes maps that to `NodeError::Terminal` (http.rs:173).

THE CAVEAT: flowrunner collapses `AuthorityDenied` together with six sibling variants into ONE `HttpCapError::Denied`, which standard-nodes codes `egress-denied` with the message "the host refused the egress (allowedHosts policy)". So a guest would see an authority violation reported as an allowedHosts refusal, and the distinction the ruling names is LOST at the guest boundary.
Either the name `effect-authority-violation` lives HOST-SIDE only — in the log, the metric, and the ledger, which is where an audit property belongs anyway — or it needs a new guest-visible `HttpCapError` variant, which is an SDK change. RECOMMEND host-side only, and say so in the commit; flag if the owner wants otherwise.
notes:
MANDATORY RIDER — ONE MANIFEST INSTANCE (owner, 2026-08-16). This bead is READER 2 OF 4. It consults THE SAME loaded, digest-verified manifest instance as plan-supply (.15.12), flow-http routing (.15.96) and jetstream delivery gating (.15.95), supplied by wamn-0h0g.15.100, which now blocks this bead. It must NOT load, parse, or digest-verify a manifest itself. One object, one weld, four enumerated readers; nobody loads a second copy. Do not name the weld a cache — a digest-named object cannot go stale, so invalidation must not exist.

THE RIDER RESOLVES THIS BEAD'S OPEN ARCHITECTURE PROBLEM. The Scope section proposes restoring the predicate as SQL:

    AND EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM runs AS pin
                  WHERE pin.tenant_id = bundle.tenant_id
                    AND pin.run_id    = $1
                    AND <the recorded manifest_digest's manifest contains (flow, $3)> )

The angle-bracket clause could not be written as SQL. The release manifest is NOT IN THE DATABASE — it is a digest-named ConfigMap mounted into the pod (wamn-0h0g.15.98), and there is no table for a SQL predicate to join against. That is why the clause was left as prose.

Under the weld the check has a home: the host holds the parsed, digest-verified manifest and can answer 'does the manifest recorded on this run contain (flow, $3)' directly, in process, with no database round trip. The two halves then are:
  · DATABASE SIDE, and this half is already landed: wamn_run.runs carries write-once (release_version, manifest_digest), minted on the existing claim write from the claiming pod's own release identity, under a paired CHECK plus an extended immutability guard raising run-release-record-immutable (wamn-0h0g.15.11, commit 618a5800). That is the immutable, guest-unforgeable anchor the deleted EXISTS used to provide.
  · HOST SIDE, this bead: bind the guest-supplied current_plan_hash ($3) to the run by checking it against the manifest the run's recorded manifest_digest names. A guest cannot forge the recorded digest (write-once, trigger-protected, written before any guest code ran) and cannot forge the manifest (content-addressed, digest-verified at load by .15.100).

DECIDE AND STATE WHICH SIDE ENFORCES. The chain the spec states at docs/deployment-simplification-spec.md:63-66 must be unbroken, but the enforcement point moved; the acceptance criteria and the mutant should be written against the point that actually enforces, not against the SQL shape the bead currently proposes. Note the run's recorded manifest_digest must also be checked to EQUAL the digest of the weld's loaded manifest — otherwise a pod serving release A could authorise effects for a run pinned to release B. That equality check is the .2.3/.2.7 successor rule and is the thing that makes claim-time recording load-bearing rather than decorative.

ALSO STILL REQUIRED, unchanged: re-add a mutant to tools/gate-mutants/current-plan-effect-authority.sh anchored on whatever predicate actually enforces, and correct that campaign's OUTCOME line — after .15.10 no mutant in it can fail if the current plan is wrong for the run, so the stated outcome ('HTTP effects require the exact current plan, source artifact, and attempt') overstates what it proves. This bead HARD-BLOCKS the merge gate wamn-0h0g.15.25.

THE CROSS-CARRIER CHECK COLLAPSES INTO A TAUTOLOGY — owner ruling wamn-0h0g.15.102, 2026-08-17.

The note above required an equality check: the run's recorded manifest_digest must equal the digest of the manifest the serving pod actually loaded, or a pod serving release A could authorise effects for a run pinned to release B. That was written while TWO carriers of the pair existed — the mount the weld reads and the per-workload config keys .15.11 landed — so it was a genuine cross-carrier comparison defending against skew between them.

The ruling deletes the asserted carrier (wamn-0h0g.15.103). Every consumer, the claim-time recording above all, now takes its pair from the loaded weld instance. So THE RECORDER AND THE AUTHORITY ARE THE SAME OBJECT: the digest stamped onto the run at claim is by construction the digest of the manifest that pod loaded and verified. Equality is STRUCTURAL, not something a check establishes.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD, CONCRETELY:
  · The equality check is no longer load-bearing. Write it, if at all, as an assertion that DOCUMENTS the structural fact — not as a defence. Do NOT write a mutant against it: a mutant that disables a tautology cannot fail a test, and this program does not ship guards whose outcome is knowable in advance (that is the exact reasoning the ruling used to reject a comparator).
  · What REMAINS load-bearing is the original link-1 restoration: binding the GUEST-SUPPLIED current_plan_hash ($3) to the run through the manifest the run's recorded digest names. That is a guest-vs-host binding, not a carrier-vs-carrier one, and it is still entirely absent. The guest can forge neither the recorded digest (write-once, trigger-protected, written before any guest code ran — .15.11 commit 618a5800) nor the manifest (content-addressed, verified at load). THAT is where the mutant goes, anchored on whatever predicate actually enforces.
  · The '.2.3/.2.7 successor rule' framing in the note above is therefore satisfied by construction rather than by an enforcement point. Say so where the recording happens rather than adding machinery.

Net effect: this bead gets SIMPLER, and one of the two things the earlier note asked for turns out to need no code at all. The security regression itself is untouched and still hard-blocks the merge gate wamn-0h0g.15.25.
close_reason: RESTORED AT THE ORIGINAL GRANULARITY (9309addc), owner ruling option C. Host verifies the guest-supplied current_plan_hash is adjacency-reachable from the run's server-written runs.flow_id in the digest-verified manifest, before any effect attempt exists. run_flow_resolutions was by construction the transitive reachable set from the root under the run's release, so this computes the IDENTICAL set — same predicate, same granularity, different carrier, derived at check time instead of materialized at claim time. Not narrowed. Frame-to-plan binding is interpreter-attested per the attempt-attestation ruling; the database verifies closure membership, and flow identity is absent from the effect wire BY DECISION (that ruling withdrew the descends-from-root check and rejected run_frames), so .15.62's finding is the consequence, not a gap. No residual bead; .15.128 is the trigger-gated record should the interpreter trust model change. Reader 2 of 4 takes the weld by reference. No WIT change. No digest comparator and no mutant on one: equality is structural under .15.102, and the mechanism holding it across a re-claim is recorded at set_release_identity. UNBLOCKS THE MERGE GATE .15.25.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(proof): should a candidate manifest be distinguishable from a release manifest
description:
## Why

Ratification ruling 1 says a test-set run materializes a candidate manifest the same way a publish materializes a release manifest. The frozen schema (wamn-0h0g.15.61) implements that as literally the same document minted from draft inputs — the root flow's plan-hash and source-artifact simply point at the draft.

Consequence: the document carries no marker, so from a manifest digest alone the audit chain (run -> recorded release version + manifest digest -> manifest) cannot tell whether a run executed against a released manifest or a candidate one. A candidate manifest is never mounted or published, so this is not a serving hazard; it is an evidence hazard.

## Options

(a) No marker — a candidate is structurally identical and provenance is established by which pipeline minted it.
(b) Add a discriminator field, accepting that it changes the digest and therefore that a candidate and its eventual release never share a digest even when their content is otherwise identical.
(c) Keep the document identical and carry the distinction outside it, in the recorded pair or the attestation row.

## Raised by

Bead wamn-0h0g.15.61.

Filed at the wamn-0h0g.15.61 close (2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1).
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

(a) NO MARKER — with the audit rule stated: A DIGEST IS *RELEASED* IFF A DEPLOYMENT ATTESTATION REFERENCES IT. Candidates are distinguishable by attestation absence. Zero schema.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. (a) NO MARKER — with the audit rule stated: A DIGEST IS *RELEASED* IFF A DEPLOYMENT ATTESTATION REFERENCES IT. Candidates are distinguishable by attes

title: [SR-MVP] decision(events): freezing registrations ends their hot-editability
description:
## Why

The ruling says the materializer reads registrations from the mounted manifest. Event registrations are not built for that, in two independent ways.

1. THEY ARE NOT RELEASE-VERSIONED. `catalog.event_registrations` has primary key (tenant_id, catalog_id, registration_id) — there is NO catalog_version column — and the schema grants INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE (deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:1742-1756). A registration is a mutable per-catalog row, not an immutable per-release fact.
2. THEY ARE DELIBERATELY HOT-EDITABLE. crates/events/registration/src/model.rs:9-11 documents a condition as "hot-editable — filtered-out events stay on the stream, so a condition edit is replayable". That property is designed for, and it is the reason a mis-filtered condition can be corrected without replaying history.

Freezing registrations into an immutable per-release manifest ends both: a condition edit becomes a republish plus a rollout, and the replayability argument no longer applies because the stream position and the manifest generation move independently.

## Options

(a) Accept the loss — registrations become release-immutable like everything else, and a condition edit is a deploy.
(b) Keep registrations out of the manifest and let the materializer keep its database read for this one projection, narrowing the ruling's "no project-database read on the serving path" to routes only.
(c) Carry registrations in the manifest as the default with a live override path for conditions specifically.

## Raised by

Bead wamn-0h0g.15.61. Directly scopes wamn-0h0g.15.13, whose acceptance currently says "no route or registration read hits the project database".

Filed at the wamn-0h0g.15.61 close (2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1).
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

PRESERVE HOT-EDITABILITY BY THE SAME SPLIT.

Registration IDENTITY — source, target flow, existence — is release content and belongs in the manifest. The CONDITION STAYS AN ENVIRONMENT-HOT COLUMN, read by the materializer at evaluation, which is already a per-event database transaction: again zero new reads.

Killing seconds-scale filter repair to satisfy schema symmetry would be freezing away a designed-for operational capability. Don't.

Condition-edit audit history is demand-gated.

CONSEQUENCE: ServingManifest.registrations changes from the stored document verbatim to identity-only, as frozen in wamn-0h0g.15.61.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. PRESERVE HOT-EDITABILITY BY THE SAME SPLIT.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(deploy): attachment activation inside a content-addressed manifest
description:
## Why

Freezing the serving manifest forced a scoping choice with a real operational consequence, and it collides head-on with an invariant the code states in as many words.

The manifest must carry `enabled` — flow-http reads routes from the mounted manifest and `RouteDefinition::enabled` (components/ingress/flow-http/src/lib.rs:66) is part of that contract. But `enabled` lives in `catalog.attachment_activation`, which is keyed PER ENVIRONMENT. So the manifest is (release, environment)-scoped, not release-scoped.

Two consequences follow.

1. ENABLE/DISABLE STOPS BEING A LIVE TOGGLE. Today `catalog.set_attachment_activation` flips a row. Under the ruling, flipping a route means minting a new manifest, a new digest, a GitOps commit, and a pod rollout. Turning a broken endpoint off goes from one statement to a deploy.
2. IT CONTRADICTS A STATED INVARIANT. crates/catalog/model/src/lib.rs:1209 documents AttachmentActivation as "Current activation state for one attachment. It never participates in hashes." Putting `enabled` in a content-addressed document is precisely that.

## Options

(a) Accept it. The ruling wins, the invariant's doc comment and the set-attachment-activation verb are amended to describe the superseded model, and disabling a route is a deploy.
(b) Keep activation out of the manifest and have flow-http read `enabled` from somewhere else — which reintroduces a project-database read on the serving path, the thing the ruling deletes.
(c) Carry the attachment in the manifest but treat `enabled` as an overlay resolved at readiness rather than at mint, so activation stays live without a database read on the request path.

## Raised by

Bead wamn-0h0g.15.61. The schema currently implements (a); nothing consumes it yet, so a change is cheap right now and expensive after wamn-0h0g.15.13 lands.

Filed at the wamn-0h0g.15.61 close (2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1).
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

(c), WITH A SHARPER ENFORCEMENT POINT THAN 'READINESS OVERLAY'.

THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE, which also settles .13.53: THE MANIFEST CARRIES RELEASE *SHAPE*; ENVIRONMENT-OPERATIONAL STATE STAYS IN POSTGRES. This is the already-ratified bindings boundary applied again.

`enabled` is environment-owned operational state — wamn's own landed invariant says activation 'never participates in hashes'. So: the manifest carries the ATTACHMENT (routes are immutable per release); ENABLEMENT IS CHECKED INSIDE THE ADMISSION TRANSACTION, which already exists and already hits the database. Zero added serving-path reads. The refusal is the existing `attachment-inactive` literal. Emergency-off is one UPDATE, effective on the next admission — i.e. immediately.

CONSEQUENCE: the `enabled` field must come OUT of ServingAttachment as frozen in wamn-0h0g.15.61.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. (c), WITH A SHARPER ENFORCEMENT POINT THAN 'READINESS OVERLAY'.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(schema): freeze the release-manifest document schema
description:
## Why

The release manifest is the keystone of the whole ruling and it has no concrete schema. Six beads consume it and would each invent their own reading: wamn-0h0g.15.12 (mounted manifest arrival), .15.13 (adjacency, registration and route projections), .15.29 (the retained tested_resolution_map evidence source), .15.49 (the digest-named mount on runner.yaml), .15.11 (the recorded manifest digest), .15.16 (the ConfigMap that GitOps converges). The spec names the projections at clause level (lines 31-39) but stops short of a document: "RFC 8785 bytes, sha256:<digest>; flow to plan-hash / source-artifact / callable-contract, call-edge adjacency, attachment + registration projections".

Building consumers in parallel against an unspecified format is exactly the cross-lane contract gap that per-lane verification cannot catch. This bead freezes the primitive first.

## Scope

1. One manifest document type in a crate BOTH the publish side and the serving side can depend on, carrying: release identity (release version, catalog identity), the per-flow projection (flow -> plan-hash, source-artifact, callable-contract), the call-edge adjacency that gives the transitive callee set, the attachment projection, and the registration projection.
2. Canonical bytes and digest: RFC 8785 serialization and sha256. The canonicalizer already exists at crates/execution/flow-model/src/canonical.rs but is `pub(crate)` — expose or re-home it rather than writing a second one. Digest ordering has a precedent test at crates/execution/flow-model/tests/digest_ordering.rs.
3. The carriage convention the consumers share: ConfigMap named `release-manifest-<digest>`, its mount path, and the release-identity ConfigMap pair (release version, manifest digest).
4. Digest stability test: identical content mints identical bytes and digest irrespective of map iteration order.

## NAMING HAZARD — read before implementing

`catalog.release_manifests` ALREADY EXISTS and is a DIFFERENT THING: a catalog table whose `members_json` lists the member entities of a catalog release (services/ctl/src/migrate_catalog.rs:562-647, deploy/sql/run-state.sql:246 FK). It is not the deployment document this bead defines and it is not deleted by the ruling. Pick a type and ConfigMap name that cannot be confused with it, and say so in the code.

## Boundary

The mint pipeline, the OCI push, and the GitOps desired-state write are wamn-0h0g.15.14; consumption is .15.13. This bead is the type, its canonical bytes, and the carriage convention only. It does NOT resolve decision wamn-0h0g.13.45 (whether the manifest is ALSO pushed to OCI given ruling 4 makes it a ConfigMap) — the schema is identical either way, which is why it can land ahead of that decision.

Filed at the wave-2 open (2026-08-16) after reading all sixteen wave-2 beads: the schema is a prerequisite the recorded wave-2 partition did not name.
design:
FROZEN 2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1. crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs (587 lines) + tests/serving_manifest_digest.rs (251). cargo check -p wamn-catalog --all-targets clean; all 23 crate tests pass including 8 new serving-manifest tests and 4 digest-stability tests. wamn-catalog is a leaf (-> wamn-flow -> third-party only) so the run is uncontaminated by the concurrent claim-path demolition.

HOME. crates/catalog/model, no new crate, root Cargo.toml UNTOUCHED. All four consumers (services/ctl, services/scenario-worker, crates/platform/runtime, crates/events/materializer) already have a direct edge to wamn-catalog, so no other lane's manifest is touched. The crate already owns CallableContract, AttachmentKind, ReleaseId and validate_digest. No canonicalizer was written: flow-model's RFC 8785 is pub(crate) but already exposed as wamn_flow::canonical_json_bytes / canonical_json_sha256, which wamn-catalog already called, so flow-model is untouched.

THE DOCUMENT. ServingManifest { format-version, release, flows, attachments, registrations }, kebab-case, deny_unknown_fields, every collection a BTreeMap/BTreeSet.
- ServingRelease { tenant-id, catalog-id, catalog-version: u32, environment }
- ServingFlow (by flow-id) { flow-version: u32, plan-hash, source-artifact, callable-contract: Option<CallableContract> (key REQUIRED even when null), calls: BTreeSet<String> }
- ServingAttachment (by attachment-id) { kind: AttachmentKind, flow-id, definition-hash, enabled: bool, definition: Value, auth-policy: Value }
- registrations: BTreeMap<String, Value>, the stored catalog.event_registrations document verbatim
API: new() validating, canonical_bytes(), digest(), read(expected_digest, bytes), reachable_flows(root).
EXCLUDED for want of a consumer: RouteDefinition body/mapped limits (host config), input_schema and idempotency_required (derivable from the fetched plan), exact_bytes (excluded by the ruling itself).

CARRIAGE, stated once at serving_manifest.rs:47-89: format version "0.1"; ConfigMap prefix "release-manifest-"; mount /etc/wamn/release-manifest; file manifest.json; identity ConfigMap "release-identity" at /etc/wamn/release-identity with keys release-version and manifest-digest; release_manifest_configmap_name(digest).

ASSUMPTIONS FOR RATIFICATION — the spec is silent on each; a test pins each where testable.
1. (release, environment)-scoped, not release-scoped, because it carries `enabled`. -> DECISION wamn-0h0g.13.52.
2. The per-flow projection carries flow-version beyond the spec's three named fields, because every admission path writes (flow_id, flow_version) onto the run row. The spec's list is shorthand, not exhaustive. -> wamn-0h0g.15.64.
3. Projections carry the STORED DOCUMENTS (attachment definition, resolved source, registration) rather than typed copies, because their owners are wamn-schema-control and wamn-event-reg and a typed copy in wamn-catalog would be a second declaration of a frozen shape.
4. No separate top-level sources projection; the resolved source is folded into each attachment as auth-policy, matching what resolve_invocation_target_sql already returns.
5. release-manifest-<64 hex>, sha256: STRIPPED. A Kubernetes object name is a DNS-1123 subdomain and cannot contain a colon, so the ruling's literal spelling is unimplementable. Pinned by the_configmap_name_is_a_dns_1123_subdomain. -> wamn-0h0g.15.64.
6. Mount paths, file name and identity keys invented against the existing /etc/wamn/... convention (deploy/platform/runner.yaml:176); the spec says only "mounted config".
7. Mounted bytes must be EXACTLY canonical — read() re-canonicalizes before comparing digests, so the ConfigMap value must be byte-exact with NO TRAILING NEWLINE. Hard constraint on wamn-0h0g.15.16. Pinned by only_the_canonical_encoding_is_admitted_at_the_mount. -> wamn-0h0g.15.64.
8. No candidate variant: a candidate manifest is the same document minted from draft inputs. BUT CandidatePlanOverride carried both draft_artifact_hash AND source_artifact_hash, and the binding base has no home here. Judged acceptable only because the ruling moves the binding gate to readiness. -> wamn-0h0g.15.62.
9. No release-vs-candidate marker, so the audit chain cannot tell them apart by digest alone. -> DECISION wamn-0h0g.13.54.
10. Adjacency is caller -> sorted unique callee set with no call sites; the ExecutionNodeId is recoverable from plan bytes and has no manifest-level reader. Adjacency lives on the flow entry, not as a top-level map, so a dangling edge is structurally checkable.
11. Tombstoned attachments excluded at mint (matching resolve_invocation_target_sql); disabled-but-live ones ARE carried so released admissions stay recoverable.
12. internal and cron attachment kinds are carried even though only http/studio have a live consumer today.
13. A format-version key, following ExecutionPlanHeader and EventRegistration::schema_version; read() fails closed on a foreign version.
14. Names ServingManifest/ServingRelease/ServingFlow/ServingAttachment, verified to collide with nothing. The module header states why the Kubernetes object name cannot be confused with catalog.release_manifests.

CONTRADICTIONS WITH EXISTING CODE, all filed: activation never participates in hashes (13.52) · registrations are not release-versioned and are hot-editable by design (13.53) · manifest-as-OCI versus manifest-as-ConfigMap (13.45, already open) · catalog_version has four widths (15.65) · a second private RFC 8785 canonicalizer already exists in wamn-catalog (15.63).

FOR THE MINT BEAD wamn-0h0g.15.14: `calls` is built by walking each plan's call-flow nodes via CallFlowInstruction.flow_id (crates/catalog/model/src/execution_plan.rs:63). That walk existed ONLY in the deleted resolution.rs — recover it from git show b42c1310:crates/execution/run-state/src/resolution.rs.
acceptance_criteria: One frozen document type with RFC 8785 canonical bytes and a sha256 digest, depended on by both planes; identical content yields identical digests across iteration orders; the ConfigMap naming and mount convention is stated once and cited by every consumer bead; nothing in the type or its name collides with catalog.release_manifests.
close_reason: Commit e38dd2a1. ServingManifest frozen in crates/catalog/model with RFC 8785 canonical bytes and sha256 digest, reusing wamn-flow's existing canonicalizer rather than writing a second one (flow-model untouched, no visibility change needed) and requiring no new crate and no root Cargo.toml edit, because all four consumers already depend on wamn-catalog. Every field carries a named consumer with a file citation; fields without one were dropped. Verified by compiling and running: cargo check clean, all 23 crate tests pass including 8 new serving-manifest tests and 4 digest-stability tests, in isolation from the concurrent claim-path demolition. Unblocks .15.12/.15.13/.15.16/.15.29/.15.49. FOUR OWNER-LEVEL FINDINGS, all filed: the manifest must be (release, environment)-scoped because it carries per-environment activation, which makes enable/disable a deploy rather than a live toggle and contradicts AttachmentActivation's stated 'never participates in hashes' invariant (decision .13.52); event registrations are not release-versioned and are deliberately hot-editable, so freezing them ends that (decision .13.53); a candidate manifest is indistinguishable from a release manifest by digest alone (decision .13.54); and 'release-manifest-<digest>' is unimplementable as literally spelled because a Kubernetes object name cannot contain a colon, so the sha256: prefix is stripped and a test pins it. Fourteen assumptions recorded in the design field for ratification. Follow-ups filed: .15.62 binding-base artifact hash has no home, .15.63 a second RFC 8785 canonicalizer already exists in wamn-catalog, .15.64 spec amendment, .15.65 catalog_version has four widths.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(proof): what 'fresh namespace' means for the RC validation
description:
## Why

The wave's single RC validation (wamn-0h0g.15.25) is specified to prove on a fresh namespace, and the live kind cluster is frozen. The wamn-0h0g.15.3 verdict makes the two readings materially different:

(a) A fresh ENVIRONMENT namespace with the operator already installed in wamn-system — provable this wave, no cluster rebuild.
(b) A fresh everything, including the operator install and its cluster-scoped CRDs — needs a cluster rebuild, which the freeze forbids.

Reading (b) also means onboarding an environment is a chart upgrade rather than a pure GitOps apply, since a namespace absent from operator.watchNamespaces gets no reconciliation at all.

## Raised by

Spike wamn-0h0g.15.3 at the wave-1 close. Scopes the merge gate.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

(a) A FRESH ENVIRONMENT NAMESPACE on a cluster with the operator and CRDs PREINSTALLED. It is the only reading deliverable under the freeze.

The full cluster-rebuild proof (CRDs from nothing) is recorded as a NAMED POST-FREEZE INFRASTRUCTURE EXERCISE, explicitly NOT part of this merge gate.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. (a) A FRESH ENVIRONMENT NAMESPACE on a cluster with the operator and CRDs PREINSTALLED. It is the only reading deliverable under the freeze.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(deploy): namespace naming form and host tier shape
description:
## Why

Two coupled shape choices from the wamn-0h0g.15.3 verdict, both needed before wamn-0h0g.15.15 and .15.16 can be built.

1. NAMESPACE NAMING: `wamn-<org>--<project>--<env>` (matching the landed Secret convention at deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh:92 and Triple::host_label) or the flatter `wamn-<org>-<project>-<env>`? Either way the 63-character DNS-1123 cap needs a stated truncation rule — the hash-suffix pattern at crates/events/wire/src/lib.rs:132 is the existing precedent. Implementation is filed separately.

2. HOST TIER SHAPE: one Helm release with N runtime.hostGroups[] entries each carrying `namespace: <env ns>` (one upgrade, one image pin for all environments), or one Helm release per environment for the host tier alone (independent host image pins per environment, at the cost of N releases to keep in step).

## Raised by

Spike wamn-0h0g.15.3 at the wave-1 close.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

DERIVE, DON'T TRUNCATE — and one Helm release per environment.

NAMESPACES derive from the REGISTRY-MINTED ABBREVIATIONS, which are already bounded by construction: `wamn-<org<=12>--<proj<=12>--<env>`, well under the 63-character DNS-1123 cap. They are NEVER derived from raw names, so NO TRUNCATION RULE EXISTS. Provision REFUSES an environment name that would breach the bound.

HOST TIER: ONE HELM RELEASE PER ENVIRONMENT. Independent image pins are the environment-singular runtime-revision rule expressed in Helm. MVP's single environment makes it moot today, which is exactly why we take the principled shape while it is free.

CONSEQUENCE: wamn-0h0g.15.57 is rescoped — there is no truncation rule to write; the work is deriving from the registry abbreviations and refusing at provision.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. DERIVE, DON'T TRUNCATE — and one Helm release per environment.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(deploy): the CRD singleton versus per-environment operator version pinning
description:
## Why

Spec lines 117-120 accept 'chart + operator version pin per environment' as an alignment cost. The wamn-0h0g.15.3 spike established that v2.7.0 cannot deliver it: the five CRDs ship in charts/runtime-operator/crds/, which Helm installs once and never upgrades, and they are cluster-scoped objects. One CRD version therefore exists per cluster, and a second Helm release cannot carry a different one.

## Options

(a) Amend the spec clause to 'chart + operator version pin per CLUSTER', accepting that all environments in a cluster share an operator version.
(b) Cluster-per-environment, which delivers the clause literally at much higher cost.
(c) Take over CRD lifecycle management outside Helm.

Left unamended, a future environment is promised an independent operator version that the architecture cannot give it.

## Raised by

Spike wamn-0h0g.15.3 at the wave-1 close.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

(a) AMEND THE SPEC CLAUSE. The catch is correct: CRDs are cluster-scoped and Helm installs them once, so 'pin per environment' is unsatisfiable for CRDs.

AMENDED RULE: CRD + operator version pin PER CLUSTER, upgraded on the fork-sync cadence. Chart VALUES (host images, groups) vary per environment and per release.

REJECTED: cluster-per-environment — infrastructure multiplication to satisfy a constraint we can simply state correctly.
DEMAND-GATED: CRD lifecycle management outside Helm.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. (a) AMEND THE SPEC CLAUSE. The catch is correct: CRDs are cluster-scoped and Helm installs them once, so 'pin per environment' is unsatisfiable for CR

title: [SR-MVP] fix(deploy): NetworkPolicies use bare podSelectors that break on the namespace split
description:
## Why

deploy/platform/runner-netpol.yaml:35-58 uses bare podSelectors. Under Kubernetes semantics that restricts egress to SAME-NAMESPACE peers. Once environments move into their own namespaces (wamn-0h0g.15.3 verdict) while NATS, Postgres and the otel collector remain cluster singletons in wamn-system, the runner starts, passes its image pull, and then fails at connect time.

## Scope

Add namespaceSelector clauses (or equivalent) for the cross-namespace singletons, across every NetworkPolicy affected by the split.

## Boundary

A silent, deferred failure mode: nothing catches it until a pod tries to connect. Must land with, not after, the namespace mapping.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
close_reason: Fixed at 6ba57055. Every in-cluster egress peer now pairs a namespaceSelector with its podSelector as siblings of one to: item (AND), naming wamn-system via kubernetes.io/metadata.name. No widening: pre-split the paired selectors resolve to the identical peer set. Postgres kept as two items so the union of fixture+CNPG shapes is not hoisted into one permissive peer. Gate fixture deliberately unchanged (serve-echo travels with the policy; its failure mode is loud). Not cluster-verified: kindnetd does not enforce NetworkPolicy.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(run-state): write-once release record versus the expired pre-effect reclaim
description:
## Why

The claim-time record of `(release version, manifest digest)` is write-once under the existing immutability trigger (spec:61-64). docs/archive/execution/run-queue.md:97-99 restarts an expired pre-effect run from zero and re-claims it. During a rollout the reclaiming pod may carry a DIFFERENT release than the original claimant, so the write-once record and the reclaim path collide.

## Scope

Define and implement the behaviour: does the reclaim rewrite the record (breaking write-once), refuse (stranding the run), or is the record scoped per claim attempt? The answer shapes the claim-time recording implementation.

## Boundary

Surfaced by the wamn-0h0g.15.9 read-through amendment. Belongs to the claim-time recording bead wamn-0h0g.15.11.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
design:
WAVE-2 EVIDENCE AND RECOMMENDATION (2026-08-16). NOT RESOLVED — this is an owner ruling; wamn-0h0g.15.11 ships the write-once record WITHOUT the reclaim arm and this bead stays open and P0 against the merge gate.

THE COLLISION, exactly. docs/archive/execution/run-queue.md:90-99 (expired pre-effect) says: "Delete replaceable node_runs, clear runs.state_json, preserve all admission, input, context, catalog, event, deadline, idempotency, immutable evidence, AND RESOLUTION-MAP FACTS, then restart from zero." That preservation clause was correct under the OLD model, where the run was version-pinned at ADMISSION — one pin, one run, preserved across restarts by construction. The ruling moves the record to CLAIM: spec:61-64 says a worker "records (release version, manifest digest) FROM ITS OWN POD IDENTITY onto the run, write-once". A reclaiming pod during a rollout may carry a different release than the original claimant, so preserve-and-write-once and "a run executes under the release its claiming pod carries" (spec:19-20) cannot both hold.

THE THREE OPTIONS, and what each costs.
(a) RECLAIM REWRITES. Preserves "the release its claiming pod carries" for every attempt. Breaks row-level write-once, so the immutability trigger arm needs an explicit exception and wamn-0h0g.15.11's proof leg ("a second write refuses") stops being true unconditionally.
(b) RECLAIM REFUSES. Preserves write-once literally. Strands any run whose original release is gone from the cluster — during a rollout that is the normal case, not an edge case, so this converts a routine deploy into stuck runs.
(c) THE RECORD IS SCOPED PER CLAIM ATTEMPT. Write-once within an attempt; a reclaim opens a new attempt and records afresh. Both spec sentences hold.

RECOMMENDATION: (c), on three pieces of repo evidence.
1. The path is PRE-EFFECT by definition. The same doc deletes node_runs and clears state_json and restarts "from zero" — nothing executed under the old record, so nothing is being rewritten out from under a completed execution. Write-once exists to make the pair immutable FOR THE EXECUTION THAT USED IT, and no execution used it.
2. The run-queue model ALREADY treats a reclaim as a distinct attempt: "granting over a prior non-NULL lease increments [attempts]". Scoping the record the same way follows the existing grain rather than cutting across it.
3. (a) and (c) produce the same observable behaviour; (c) is the framing under which wamn-0h0g.15.11's acceptance stays literally true, so the trigger keeps one rule instead of one rule plus an exception.

CONSEQUENCE IF THE OWNER PICKS (c): the preservation clause in docs/archive/execution/run-queue.md:90-99 must drop "and resolution-map facts" and say the release record is re-taken on re-claim — a docs edit that belongs with whichever bead implements the arm.

OPEN QUESTION THE OWNER MAY WANT FOLDED IN: what the janitor does with an expired-at-budget row (same doc, :103-105) is untouched by all three readings, but it is the one path where a run dies still carrying a record for a release that may no longer exist.

SHARPENED BY THE wamn-0h0g.15.10 VERIFICATION (2026-08-16). The trigger mechanics change what each option costs, and they were not known when the options were first written.

wamn_run.guard_run_admission_pins_immutable (deploy/sql/run-state.sql:122-138) refuses ANY `IS DISTINCT FROM` change to its guarded columns — including NULL -> value — and its trigger (:265-268) is `BEFORE UPDATE OF <explicit column list>`, so it does not even fire for columns not named there. wamn-0h0g.15.11 must therefore extend both the body and the column list with a carve-out permitting exactly the first write.

Consequence for the three options:
(a) RECLAIM REWRITES now means a carve-out that is not merely NULL->value but value->value under a named condition — the widest exception, and the hardest to state safely in plpgsql.
(b) RECLAIM REFUSES needs no extra carve-out beyond NULL->value, so it is the cheapest to implement and the easiest to prove — but it strands runs during exactly the rollout it is meant to survive.
(c) SCOPED PER CLAIM ATTEMPT requires the reclaim to reset the pair to NULL before re-recording, which the guard must also permit. That is a two-way carve-out (value->NULL on the reclaim path, NULL->value on the claim path), which is implementable but means the "write-once" name describes a per-attempt property, not a per-row one — and the trigger, not prose, becomes the place that distinction is enforced.

The recommendation stays (c), but the owner should know it is no longer the cheapest option to implement — only the one that keeps both spec sentences true.

RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR AS IMPLEMENTED (wamn-0h0g.15.11, commit 618a5800) — this is the concrete input this decision needs, and it is WORSE than this bead's original description assumed.

WHAT NOW HAPPENS. The guard permits the first write and refuses any later DIFFERING one, so:
1. Reclaiming pod carries the SAME release -> IS DISTINCT FROM is false -> accepted no-op, claim proceeds. Ordinary non-rollout reclaims are unaffected.
2. Reclaiming pod carries a DIFFERENT release (the rollout case) -> RAISE 55000 / run-release-record-immutable.
3. Reclaiming pod carries NO release identity against a recorded run (partial rollout, misconfiguration) -> binds NULL -> NULL IS DISTINCT FROM 7 -> same refusal.

THE BLAST RADIUS OF CASE 2 AND 3. The raise aborts the grant statement; claim_in_transaction returns Err; claim_next_production rolls back and returns ProductionClaimError{ kind: Storage, operation: "grant production lease" }. Nothing rolls forward: the lease is still expired, status unchanged, state_json un-cleared, the recorded pair untouched. Critically ATTEMPTS IS NOT INCREMENTED — it lives in the same aborted statement. Consequences:
- The whole drain turn aborts, and the refusing run is still the FIFO head with nothing locking it after rollback, so THE TENANT'S QUEUE HEAD-OF-LINE BLOCKS. Runs behind it never drain.
- Because attempts never advances, the run can never reach max_attempts, so THE JANITOR CAN NEVER REAP IT to infrastructure-failure. It is stranded indefinitely rather than eventually retired.
- The only operator signal is one tracing::warn per drain turn from services/executor/src/lib.rs:239-247 ("run-worker: drain failed (retrying after backoff)"). No run-level metric, no observation — observe_drive is never reached and report.claimed stays 0.

NEW FACT THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION DOES NOT COVER. The collision is NOT limited to the expired pre-effect reclaim. park_sql NULLs lease_owner and lease_expires_at, so a queue-park followed by a doorbell wake classifies as ProductionClaimClass::Ordinary and goes straight to the grant — hitting the identical guard if the waking pod carries a different release. ANY OPTION CHOSEN HERE MUST COVER THE PARK/WAKE PATH TOO, not just the reclaim.

ERASURE IS ALSO REFUSED. OLD=(7,D1) -> NEW=(NULL,NULL) raises, because OLD IS NOT NULL and NULL IS DISTINCT FROM 7. So option (c), scoping the record per claim attempt, cannot reset the pair without a SECOND carve-out permitting value->NULL on the reclaim path. That is implementable but widens the exception surface.

REVISED COST OF EACH OPTION, given the guard as built:
(a) RECLAIM REWRITES — needs a value->value carve-out under a named condition. Widest exception, hardest to state safely in plpgsql.
(b) RECLAIM REFUSES — this is what is implemented TODAY. No extra carve-out. But the failure mode above (head-of-line block plus unreapable run) means it is not a safe resting state, only an honest one.
(c) SCOPED PER CLAIM ATTEMPT — needs a two-way carve-out (value->NULL on reclaim, NULL->value on claim). "Write-once" then names a per-attempt property enforced by the trigger rather than a per-row one.

The recommendation remains (c) on correctness grounds, but note it is no longer the cheapest to implement — only the one that keeps both spec sentences true. What is NOT tenable is leaving (b) as the resting state.

SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

RULED: (c) RESET-PER-CLAIM-ATTEMPT, AND IMPLEMENT IT INSIDE THE CLASSIFIER.

The two spec sentences reconcile once the record's scope is named: the pair is write-once PER CLAIM ATTEMPT, not per run-eternity.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS. The ratified classifier's pre-effect arm 'replaces the abandoned attempt's projection rows'. The (release, digest) pair IS projection of the dead attempt and joins that replacement set: the classifier reclaim clears it in the SAME TRANSACTION that re-enqueues, and the next claim writes it fresh.

NOTHING LOAD-BEARING IS LOST. Only PRE-EFFECT reclaims reach this path — post-effect is terminal effect-uncertain — so the dead attempt fired no effects and no attempt row references its release identity.

THE GUARD BECOMES TRANSITION-CONSTRAINED, NOT WRITE-ONCE:
  NULL  -> value   permitted, by the CLAIM only
  value -> NULL    permitted, by the CLASSIFIER ARM only
  value -> value'  REFUSED always

This also cures the park/doorbell collision reported at the .15.11 close, because every path that re-opens claimability flows through the classifier's reset.

SEPARATELY, AND REGARDLESS OF THIS RULING: fix the mechanical bug the .15.11 evidence exposed — `attempts` must NOT share the aborted statement. A refusal that starves its own janitor is how one run head-of-line-blocks a tenant forever. Filed as its own bead.
close_reason: Implemented at e17b9b90 per the owner's ruling (c). Guard is transition-constrained: NULL->value by the claim, value->NULL by the classifier's pre-effect arm, value->value' refused. Because a BEFORE UPDATE trigger cannot identify its caller and every way to fake it is forgeable, the erasure arm encodes the ruling's own safety argument as a checkable row predicate (runnable status, no node_runs, no effect_attempts). The status conjunct is an addition, flagged for the owner. Guard body byte-identical across all four mirrors. PARK/WAKE IS NOT COVERED and the ruling's premise that it is, is false here - park classifies as Ordinary, which resets nothing; .15.69 does not rescue it either, so a parked run refusing on wake is both unreapable and permanently the FIFO head. LATENT ONLY: park_sql has no production caller. Pinned by a proof leg; the fix needs decision .13.55.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(fork): DefaultOutgoingHandler quota-registry construction at the pin
description:
## Why

The wamn/2.7.0 pin requires crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:544 to become DefaultOutgoingHandler::default() (the fork type went from a unit struct to a fielded one). The fork's rustdoc (host/http.rs:520-531) notes that default() mints a PRIVATE quota registry per handler, whereas with_quotas(...) binds the handler to a shared registry.

RunnerEgress is built per ExecutionHost::instantiate, so default() gives each execution instance its own registry: a workload's HTTP connection pool and its raw-socket allowance end up bounded independently.

## Options

(a) default() — minimal, preserves upstream defaults, accepted as the pin fix by gate B.
(b) with_quotas(...) — one registry, coupling HTTP pool and socket allowances.

## Raised by
