Gate B (wamn-0h0g.15.6) at the wave-1 close. Note the pooled path is currently unreachable from production guests, so this is a posture choice, not a live bound.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.6 report.
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

DefaultOutgoingHandler::default(). Private per-instance quota registries — isolation-first posture. The pooled path is unreachable from production guests, and this is the pin fix gate B already accepted.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. DefaultOutgoingHandler::default(). Private per-instance quota registries — isolation-first posture. The pooled path is unreachable from production gue

title: [SR-MVP] decision(exec): is 'flow guests never perform raw wasi:http egress' a ruling
description:

Gate A (wamn-0h0g.15.5) proved the fork's pooled egress path is unreachable from every production guest — the flowrunner world imports no wasi:http interface at all (components/execution/flowrunner/wit/world.wit:9-14; flow egress is wamn:runner/http-effect). That unreachability is one of the two independent constructions that make the gate pass.

The audit specifies a conformance guard asserting the flowrunner world imports no wasi:http. Adding it turns today's fact into a RULING and will hard-fail anyone who later adds raw wasi:http egress to a flow guest.

## Options

(a) Ratify as a ruling and carry the guard (recommended by the audit — it pins a safety property).
(b) Leave the door ajar: no guard, and the pooled-path safety then rests solely on connection_http's per-request client.

## Raised by

Gate A at the wave-1 close.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(deploy): rewrite runner.yaml for release-manifest mount and readiness
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.18 plans to DELETE deploy/platform/runner.yaml once its Host CRD replacement stands, but per spike wamn-0h0g.15.4 no operator Host CRD can replace it — wamn-run-worker is not a wasmCloud host. Deleting it removes the executor with nothing standing in its place: a live-path regression.

## Scope

REWRITE runner.yaml instead: mount the digest-named release-manifest ConfigMap, add the readiness gate (manifest + plans fetched and hash-verified, every connection requirement bound), and drop the resolution-map and artifact-reader leftovers. deploy/platform/scenario-worker.yaml is in the same position.

## Boundary

Blocks wamn-0h0g.15.18, which must not delete these two manifests.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.4 report.
design:
BLOCKED IN FACT, NOT ONLY ON PAPER (verified 2026-08-16 at the wave-4 scoping).

All three scope items ride wamn-0h0g.15.12:
  1. 'mount the digest-named release-manifest ConfigMap' — the ConfigMap has no minter (wamn-0h0g.15.14) and no reader (.15.12).
  2. 'add the readiness gate (manifest + plans fetched and hash-verified, every connection requirement bound)' — readiness DOES NOT EXIST IN THE TREE. A manifest change here could only point a readinessProbe at an endpoint .15.12 has not yet defined, so the probe shape would be guessed and then rewritten.
  3. 'drop the resolution-map and artifact-reader leftovers' — the artifact-reader plane is still present; .15.12 is the bead that deletes it. Removing its YAML references first would break the running shape for no gain.

Taking only item 3 now was rejected under the granularity rule (a bead is not a container of separable sub-work). Dep edge to .15.12 added.

The bead's own reason for existing is UNCHANGED and still load-bearing: per spike wamn-0h0g.15.4, no operator Host CRD can replace runner.yaml, because wamn-run-worker is not a wasmCloud host. wamn-0h0g.15.18 must NOT delete deploy/platform/runner.yaml or deploy/platform/scenario-worker.yaml.
close_reason: Release-manifest mount landed in deploy/platform/runner.yaml at c88f9f1c as the fully-active target-state shape: digest-named ConfigMap volume (optional: false), whole-directory projection at /etc/wamn/release-manifest, WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_ROOT pointing at it, plus WAMN_INSECURE_PLAN_REGISTRY because an https-only client against the plain-HTTP dev registry would weld and then fail every pull. Per ruling .15.102 the ConfigMap name is the ONE per-release line; .15.98 rewrites exactly it, and the checked-in 64-zero name is a documented placeholder with a NOT APPLIABLE AS CHECKED IN header. Verified by YAML parse (2 docs), volume/mount coherence, 64-char DNS-legal placeholder, env-vs-mountPath agreement, and the four clap knob spellings read from services/executor/src/lib.rs. THREE PREMISE CORRECTIONS: (1) scope item 3 is an EMPTY SET — deploy/platform/ has zero artifact-reader or resolution-map references; the real residue is in deploy/sql/, owned by .15.29 and .9.11, and no edit was manufactured to satisfy the wording. (2) scenario-worker.yaml is NOT in the same position and is byte-unchanged — services/scenario-worker has no release-manifest knob and never calls ExecutionHost::instantiate. (3) the title said release-identity mount, a mount .15.104 deleted; corrected to release-manifest. CLOSED QUESTION, no bead: the authoring surface has no reader and no plausible need for release identity, so scenario-worker needs no follow-up implementation. SPLIT: .15.112 owns the readiness gate (the run-worker exposes NO listener — measured zero hits for readiness/readyz/healthz/bind across services/executor and the execution host — so a probe is new Rust, policy .5.16; runner.yaml's 'there is no readiness endpoint' paragraph is left true). FILED: .15.113 (P0 bug — no egress policy admits the plan registry on TCP 5000; the pull is host egress so --allowed-hosts is irrelevant, and it fails per-run rather than at startup because OciPlanSource::new never connects). Also appended four measured premise corrections to .15.98, whose scope item 2 still mints a struck release-identity ConfigMap and whose four serving_manifest.rs line cites are all stale.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(tracker): correct the Host-CRD premise in the operator-adoption beads
description:
## Why

Spike wamn-0h0g.15.4 established two premise corrections that make wamn-0h0g.15.15 and wamn-0h0g.15.18 unachievable as written:

1. The operator's Host CR is OBSERVED state written by the operator from host heartbeats (host_controller.go:223-270); the Host type has no image, replicas, or podTemplate (host_types.go:38-56). Images enter via the chart's runtime.hostGroups[].image, not by authoring Host CRDs.
2. wamn-run-worker is not a wasmCloud host at all — no ClusterHost, no heartbeat, its own entrypoint and CLI, plus DB/credential/effect-writer/egress volumes and a native claim loop — so it cannot become a chart host group this wave.

## Scope

Rescope wamn-0h0g.15.15 to pinning the operator chart per environment and setting runtime.hostGroups[].image for the wamn-host host groups, and rescope wamn-0h0g.15.18 per the runner.yaml rewrite bead.

## Boundary

Tracker correction only, no code.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.4 report.
close_reason: Tracker correction applied. wamn-0h0g.15.15 rescoped from authoring Host CRDs to pinning the operator chart and setting runtime.hostGroups[].image plus the four missing operator values (watchNamespaces, allowSharedHosts:false, hostNamespaces, per-environment hostGroups namespace); its acceptance now names the CrossEnvironmentSchedulingDenied refusal. wamn-0h0g.15.18 rescoped to record that on current evidence its delete set is EMPTY — the host tier is already chart-managed (deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml:17 sets runtime.hostGroups[].image.repository=wamn-host), there is no hand-rolled wasmCloud-host Deployment under deploy/, and runner.yaml/scenario-worker.yaml are not wasmCloud hosts so wamn-0h0g.15.49 rewrites them rather than .15.18 deleting them; final disposition left to decision wamn-0h0g.13.46, which already blocks it. Original wording preserved in Dolt history and the correction recorded in each bead's design field. No code changed.

title: [SR-MVP] test(egress): pin the connection_http per-request-client no-reuse construction
description:
## Why

Gate A (wamn-0h0g.15.5) proved wamn's credentialed egress is safe from pooled-connection reuse across credential generations TWICE OVER — connection_http builds a fresh reqwest::Client per invocation and drops it, and the fork's pooled path is unreachable from every production guest — but NOTHING in the repo pins either construction. The fork's pool is keyed by workload_id alone; if the credentialed path ever reached it, two generations WOULD share a connection, silently.

## Scope

Carry three guards, specified in full in the wamn-0h0g.15.5 audit:
1. Behavioral no-reuse test in the existing connection_http test module (no database): two generations, assert distinct connections.
2. Structural tripwire in tools/repo-lint over connection_http.rs: exactly one reqwest::Client::builder( occurrence, no client field, no static/OnceLock/lazy client, no wash-runtime pooled symbol reference.
3. Reachability guard in tests/conformance/tests/flowrunner_linker_imports.rs: the flowrunner world imports NO wasi:http interface.

## Boundary

Blocks the fork pin wamn-0h0g.15.20 — the pin commit must state that connection_http BYPASSES the upstream pool rather than keying into it, so the next fork sync does not re-derive it.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.5 report.
design:
SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

PROMOTED BY RULING .13.47 (2026-08-16): 'flow guests never perform raw wasi:http egress' is now a STANDING RULE, so the reachability guard this bead shipped graduates from description to ENFORCEMENT OF RECORD. Anyone adding raw wasi:http egress to a flow guest hard-fails, by design and by ruling.
close_reason: Commit 9ef83b54. All three guards from the gate-A audit landed: behavioral no-reuse test in the existing connection_http test module (two credential generations against an ephemeral keep-alive loopback probe, asserting connection indices 0 and 1 and exactly two accepts, and written so it cannot pass vacuously); structural tripwire in tools/repo-lint following that script's existing idiom (exactly one reqwest::Client::builder, no client struct field, no static/OnceLock/lazy client, no wash-runtime pooled symbol); and a reachability assertion that the flowrunner world imports no wasi:http interface. Production behaviour unchanged. Guard 2 was mutation-tested independently at integration with a stub cargo: a process-wide OnceLock client, a second Client::builder, and a wash-runtime DefaultOutgoingHandler import each exit 65 with a distinct message, clean tree passes, file restored byte-exact. Guard 1 could not be executed — this branch runs no gates by owner ruling — and is written for the RC validation wamn-0h0g.15.25. TWO AUDIT CORRECTIONS recorded on wamn-0h0g.15.20: the pooled path is unreachable from the egress interface but flow-http does import wasi:http/types@0.2.12, so a blanket 'no guest mentions wasi:http' is false; and response.bytes() is awaited before the client drops, so the connection briefly returns to that client's own idle pool and dies with it — safety comes from the client's lifetime, not from never pooling. The stale EXPECTED_SHA this introduces in current-plan-effect-authority.sh (four sites, fa581bea -> 26c4c626) is recorded on wamn-0h0g.15.22 for Tier D per the once-at-wave-end ruling.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(publish): re-source the retained tested_resolution_map evidence
description:

Landed 768dbeae on deploy-simplification (lane commit 71d7de32).

DESIGN READING (a), publish-side derivation, and the lane judged it not a close call.
tested_resolution_map is now derived from the minted release manifest, scoped to
ServingManifest::reachable_flows(request.flow_id), replacing the read of the report's

resolve_run_flow_resolutions' walk over plan bytes" -- and that deleted function (gone
in fcf0dd99, .15.10) emitted exactly flow_id/execution_bundle_hash pairs, so

evidence is immutable and an exact retry must recompute identical bytes. A whole-release

*** PREMISE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN "Why": the claim that the case-level maps are
gone is FALSE. 1dbfd097 (.15.7) deleted the report-level consistency CHECK and the map
WRITERS; the resolution_map / resolution_map_hash COLUMNS survive on all three tables
with their CHECKs (authoring-tests.sql:40-46, 98-104, 154-156), exactly as that commit
says ("Remove the check, keep the evidence"). Independently confirmed by the integrator.
The P0 is real, but the cause is a missing WRITER, not a missing column. ***

93a092f6f4b4d7f515c3c31d609c8dd85d28c26a609402537e7dd1193bdd0a69. An independently

## Why

Owner-ratified test-contract simplification (spec section + decision record wamn-0h0g.13.44): the gate stands, the contract flattens. Supersedes the landed shapes of closed .8.1 and .8.2 — this is landed-code demolition, correctly Tier C.

description:

title: [SR-MVP] chore(fork): pin wash-runtime to wamn/2.7.0 daba602, wasmtime 47.0.3
description:
## Why

Fork sync assessed 2026-08-14: wamn/2.7.0 (head daba602) is fit to pin — every load-bearing patch survived the port; the pin rides this wave green-up so one revalidate/republish/drain loop serves both changes.

## Scope

Move root Cargo.toml:39 workspace.dependencies.wash-runtime.rev from 09b1132f to daba602; lock moves to wasmtime 47.0.3 (wasmtime-wasi / wasmtime-wasi-http 47.0.1 at Cargo.toml:41-42); re-verify tests/conformance/tests/wasmtime_source_identity.rs; one ExecutionRuntimeRevision bump, one provider-manifest regeneration, one revalidate -> republish -> drain loop. Preconditions: audit gates A and B closed green.

## Boundary

wamn/2.6.1 stays frozen and reachable; never delete fork branches. Upstream PR filing is its own bead. Fork-sync gate subset (socketguard, egress-escape, trace, busyloop epoch) runs inside the RC validation bead.
design:
AUDIT CORRECTIONS FROM wamn-0h0g.15.35 (2026-08-16, commit 9ef83b54) — the pin commit must carry these so the NEXT fork sync does not re-derive them.

THE CLAIM THE PIN COMMIT MUST STATE: connection_http BYPASSES the upstream pooled egress path rather than keying into it. It builds a fresh reqwest::Client inside `execute` and drops it at function exit. Three guards now hold this (behavioral no-reuse test in the connection_http test module; structural tripwire in tools/repo-lint; reachability assertion in tests/conformance/tests/flowrunner_linker_imports.rs).

CORRECTION 1 to the gate-A wording. The audit says the pooled path is unreachable from EVERY production guest. That is true of the egress interface but NOT of the wasi:http namespace: components/ingress/flow-http/wit/world.wit:6 imports wasi:http/types@0.2.12 for its incoming-handler export. It does NOT import wasi:http/outgoing-handler, so the pooled egress is genuinely unreachable and the conclusion stands — but a blanket "no production guest mentions wasi:http" is FALSE and must not be written into the pin commit. The reachability guard is therefore scoped to the flowrunner world (six imports: wamn:postgres/{types,client}, wamn:runner/{plan-supply,causation,http-effect}, wasi:logging/logging@0.1.0-draft), where the stricter assertion is correct.

CORRECTION 2, a window the audit understates. `response.bytes()` is awaited BEFORE `client` drops, so the connection does briefly return to that client's own idle pool. It dies with the client, so there is no cross-generation reuse — but the safety comes from the client's lifetime, not from the connection never being pooled at all. That window is exactly what the behavioral guard pins.

POOL KEYING re-confirmed at the currently pinned rev 09b1132: crates/wash-runtime/src/host/http.rs defines OutgoingHandler::send_request(&self, workload_id: &str, ...) and send_request_p3 likewise; DefaultOutgoingHandler delegates to wasmtime_wasi_http::p2::default_send_request_handler, whose hyper client pool is process-global; wamn wraps that handler at crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:339 for the wasi:http path. workload_id is the only discriminator and nothing is credential-generation-aware. Re-verify this at daba602 — it is the premise the whole bypass argument rests on.

SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

SCOPED BY RULING .13.48: use DefaultOutgoingHandler::default() at crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:544. Private per-instance quota registries, isolation-first posture. The pooled path is unreachable from production guests, and this is the fix gate B already accepted.

ALSO: ruling .13.47 ratifies 'flow guests never perform raw wasi:http egress' as a STANDING RULE, so the .15.35 reachability guard is now enforcement of record rather than description. The pin commit states the bypass as a rule, not an observation.
acceptance_criteria: Lock resolves daba602 + wasmtime 47.0.3; wasmtime_source_identity green; exactly one revision bump and provider-manifest regeneration land with the pin commit.
notes:
RE-VERIFIED AT daba602 BY THE wamn-0h0g.15.36 LANE (2026-08-16). Three facts the pin commit can rely on rather than re-derive:

1. THE RULED ONE-LINE FIX STILL APPLIES AND IS STILL ONE SITE. At daba602 `DefaultOutgoingHandler` is a FIELDED STRUCT (crates/wash-runtime/src/host/http.rs:511-518), so crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:544 (`inner: DefaultOutgoingHandler,`) does need the ruled `DefaultOutgoingHandler::default()`. Exactly one site, as ruling .13.48 assumed.

2. THE p3 TRAIT SIGNATURE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL ACROSS THE BUMP. `outgoing_request_p3` and `send_request_p3` are unchanged between 09b1132 and daba602, so the `RunnerEgress::outgoing_request_p3` override that .15.36 just added survives the pin untouched.

3. AFTER THE BUMP, `self.inner.send_request_p3` ROUTES INTO THE FORK'S `WorkloadClients` POOL, KEYED BY `workload_id`. That is correct on this path and does NOT reopen the bypass finding: the raw egress path carries no credential generation. Credential-bearing egress is `connection_http`, which builds its own client and bypasses the pool — the property the three .15.35 guards pin.

ALSO CORRECTED AT THE SAME READING: the currently pinned rev is 09b1132f2bab36e6e71f4637bd0e4755e359dd43 (root Cargo.toml:39). The fork is NOT vendored in this tree — read it at ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/wasmcloud-8b42214d254eda9e/<rev>/. Earlier notes citing bare `crates/wash-runtime/...` paths mean that checkout, not a repo path.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-17 — RATIFIED AS A SOLO WAVE, SEQUENCED AFTER WAVE 9 AND BEFORE wamn-0h0g.15.22.

PRECONDITIONS CONFIRMED AGAINST THE RULING RECORD: gates A and B are exactly wamn-0h0g.15.5 (audit) + .15.35 (the three landed guards, commit 9ef83b54) and .15.6 -- all CLOSED. The DefaultOutgoingHandler::default() posture is ruling .13.48 verbatim. The pool-keying note reads the bypass finding correctly: credential-bearing egress (connection_http) never touches the workload pool.

WHY SOLO IS THROUGHPUT, NOT CAUTION: 44 files reference wash_runtime, so a rev bump invalidates that whole dependency closure and serializes every parallel lane onto one rustc pipeline.

WHY BEFORE .15.22: the churn doctrine applied to registries. One regeneration absorbs the pin's provider-manifest delta AND the 51 stale baseline pairs banked from wave 8; pinning after .15.22 pays the manifest twice for nothing.

RIDER ON THE PIN COMMIT (owner, binding): the commit body RECORDS THE THREE RE-VERIFIED FACTS BY BEAD REFERENCE rather than re-deriving them -- wamn-0h0g.15.36's findings that (1) DefaultOutgoingHandler is a FIELDED STRUCT at daba602 so exactly one site needs ::default(), (2) the p3 trait signature is BYTE-IDENTICAL across the bump so .15.87's outgoing_request_p3 clamp survives untouched, and (3) send_request_p3 routes into the fork's workload_id-keyed WorkloadClients pool, which does not reopen the bypass finding. That citation is the fork-sync record for 2.8's archaeology.

EXECUTABILITY CONFIRMED OFFLINE 2026-08-17: daba602 is already in ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/, and wasmtime + wasmtime-wasi 47.0.1/47.0.2/47.0.3 are all in the local registry. No network needed. No live contention on root Cargo.toml: .15.97 also edits it but is blocked on .15.14.

UNBLOCKS (hard dep edges added 2026-08-17): .15.52, .15.37, .15.39. Also a direct dep of .15.25, the RC.

merely logs-and-counts what it would refuse WHILE ALLOWING IT. wamn's
deny-without-opt-in therefore depends on BOTH halves of shape_socket_policy --
empty allowed_hosts AND egress_mode: Enforce. Pinning only the empty allowlist

## Why

The ruling's Deleted list names hand-rolled host Deployment manifests, on the premise that operator Host CRDs replace them.

## Scope (CORRECTED by wamn-0h0g.15.48 after spike wamn-0h0g.15.4 — ON CURRENT EVIDENCE NOTHING REMAINS TO DELETE)

The premise does not hold, and the inventory is empty:

1. No Host CRD can replace anything. Host CRs are observed heartbeat state with no image, replicas, or podTemplate; the wasmCloud host tier is ALREADY chart-managed through `runtime.hostGroups[].image` (deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml:17 = wamn-host). There is no hand-rolled wasmCloud-host Deployment anywhere under deploy/.
2. deploy/platform/runner.yaml and deploy/platform/scenario-worker.yaml are NOT wasmCloud hosts — wamn-run-worker has no ClusterHost, no heartbeat, its own entrypoint and CLI, and native DB/credential/effect-writer/egress volumes. Deleting them removes the executor and the scenario worker with nothing standing in their place. Both are REWRITTEN by wamn-0h0g.15.49 instead.
3. deploy/platform/dispatcher.yaml is retained by the ruling (queue reconciliation is ours). deploy/platform/waker.yaml rides the M2 trigger bead wamn-0h0g.15.26. Gate/Job manifests under deploy/gates keep theirs. flow-http/materializer example WorkloadDeployments are already CRD-shaped and are updated, not deleted, by wamn-0h0g.15.15.

That leaves this bead with an empty delete set. Its disposition — close as premise-failed, or retain a narrowed sweep of BoM references — is part of decision wamn-0h0g.13.46 (the operator adoption boundary and the Deleted-list scope), which already blocks it.

## Boundary

Do not delete runner.yaml or scenario-worker.yaml under any reading. If a BoM reference sweep survives the decision, it is a documentation sweep, not a manifest deletion.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): OCI registry and pull credentials for release-manifest and component artifacts
description:
## Why

Under R1/R3 the immutable things that ship as OCI artifacts are the per-catalog component library (digest-pinned, import-audited) and the minted release manifest. Plan bytes are gone with the compiler. Hosts and the publish pipeline still need a registry home plus pull/push credentials.

## Scope

Provide the registry surface for component images and release-manifest artifacts (build on the existing deploy/platform/registry.yaml ephemeral registry:2 for dev; name the production posture), plus pull-secret provisioning for executor hosts and push credentials for publish. Supersedes held wamn-d8i.

## Boundary

Fetch/verify logic is the executor OCI bead; push logic is the publish bead. The supply-chain floor (import audit, digest pinning, signing) is its own work.
acceptance_criteria: Publish can push and an executor host can pull by digest in a fresh namespace using only provisioned credentials.
close_reason: Implemented by 3781c220: exact redacting .dockerconfigjson credentials shared by component pull/push, host/executor/ctl wiring, authenticated dev registry, and explicit pull/push Secret posture. Focused production checks and credential tests green.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): GitOps convergence of desired state
description:
## Why

GitOps converges desired state: the release-identity ConfigMap and CRDs are written by publish and reconciled into the cluster; rollback is Git revert; wrong-target protection is namespace/context targeting.

## Scope

Stand up the convergence path — Argo or Flux for real environments, plain kubectl apply in dev — over the GitOps source the publish bead writes. Encode the namespace-per-environment mapping from the spike verdict as the wrong-target protection. Document the rollback-by-revert runbook. Supersedes held wamn-6s1.

## Boundary

What gets written to the source is the publish bead; operator internals are the adoption bead. No deployment saga, no reconciler of our own.
design:
SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

SCOPED BY RULING .13.50: the namespace is derived from the registry-minted abbreviations (`wamn-<org<=12>--<proj<=12>--<env>`), never from raw names, and provision refuses a name that would breach the DNS-1123 bound. There is no truncation rule to encode.
acceptance_criteria: A desired-state commit converges a fresh namespace without manual apply steps (dev path: one kubectl apply); a Git revert restores the prior release identity; a wrong-namespace apply is refused by targeting.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 at b8b474b6 against the .15.98 owner ruling. *** REFUTED AS WRITTEN. A small real residual survives under a different shape. *** Clause by clause. Scope 1 Argo or Flux for real environments - REFUTED, it names the reconciler the ruling deleted. Scope 1 plain kubectl apply in dev over the GitOps source the publish bead writes - VACUOUS, there is no such source and deploy/README.md:1-6 already establishes hand-applied kubectl apply as the convergence mechanism for all four tiers. Scope 2 encode the namespace-per-environment mapping as wrong-target protection - *** ALREADY DISCHARGED BY NATIVE CHART CAPABILITY: deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml:84,96,106 sets watchNamespaces, hostNamespaces and allowSharedHosts false, and values-host-default.yaml:93-104 documents that the host Pod's namespace BECOMES Host.Environment so a WorkloadDeployment can only schedule onto a host whose Environment equals its own namespace. *** The bead's own DESIGN block already conceded the other half per ruling .13.50. This is exactly the let-wasmCloud-do-it outcome - nothing to build. Scope 3 add the missing ConfigMap renderer - REFUTED by the .15.98 close, the ConfigMap is a redundant second carrier on the OCI path. Acceptance a desired-state commit converges a fresh namespace without manual apply steps - REFUTED, .15.3 recorded that onboarding an environment is a CHART UPGRADE, not a pure GitOps apply. Acceptance a Git revert restores the prior release identity - *** SURVIVES, AND IS THE ENTIRE RESIDUAL: under the OCI shape the release identity is the digest in two git-tracked pod templates, so git revert plus re-apply IS rollback. Real, cheap, and currently undocumented. *** Document the rollback-by-revert runbook - SURVIVES. RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION: close REFUTED-AND-SPLIT with this table as the close reason and file one small successor, docs(deploy) record the OCI release rollout and rollback-by-revert runbook, whose home is the two pod-template headers plus deploy/README.md - zero code. *** THAT SUCCESSOR CANNOT BE WRITTEN UNTIL THE OWNER ANSWERS WHO WRITES THE DIGEST INTO THE TWO POD TEMPLATES; a runbook that cannot say that is not a runbook. *** AWAITING OWNER RULING before closing a P0.
MEASURED 2026-08-23 (wave-55 read-only pass, agent verified at fa76974c). RECOMMENDATION ONLY - the close is the owner's ruling, not taken here.

PREMISE REFUTED. No GitOps controller exists anywhere in the tree: zero hits for flux/fluxcd/argo/argocd/argoproj/Kustomization/HelmRelease/GitRepository/OCIRepository/ApplicationSet across all manifests and CRDs. No kustomization file of any name. No CI applies anything - .github/workflows holds only client.yml with no kubectl or helm. The only kustomize strings are managed-by labels inside vendored upstream installs (cnpg-operator.yaml, barman-cloud-plugin.yaml).

The actual convergence mechanism is a human with kubectl, and deploy/README.md already documents that as the shipped design for all four tiers.

CLAUSE BY CLAUSE:
- Scope 1a (Argo or Flux for real environments): REFUTED - names the reconciler that .15.98 deleted.
- Scope 1b (plain kubectl apply over the GitOps source the publish bead writes): VACUOUS - no such source. .15.98 closed with "the OCI release artifact IS the desired-state source, no fifth deploy tier, no synced GitOps repo".
- Scope 2 (namespace-per-environment as wrong-target protection): ALREADY DISCHARGED by native chart capability. deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml watchNamespaces + hostNamespaces + allowSharedHosts false is annotated in-file as THE WRONG-TARGET LOCK, refusing cross-environment scheduling with CrossEnvironmentSchedulingDenied.
- Scope 3 (ConfigMap renderer): REFUTED by .15.98. The shape survives only as unused Rust constants in crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs; no deploy manifest carries it.
- Acceptance "fresh namespace converges with no manual steps": REFUTED - .15.3 recorded that onboarding an environment is a chart upgrade.
- Acceptance "git revert restores prior release identity": SURVIVES. This is the entire residual.

R55 APPLIED: there is no converge path for it to bite on, and that absence is the finding. kubectl diff appears zero times in the repository. No Makefile, justfile or Taskfile exists. tools/kubernetes-gate-run asserts exit status only. deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh applies only two generated Secrets and its writer-rotation branch is non-idempotent by construction. Idempotency claims in ops-schema.sql, dispatcher.yaml and run-plane-reconcile.example.yaml are unenforced prose. The one honest guard is chart_seam_governance.rs, which declares its own limit in-file ("Convergence itself needs a cluster, so what is guarded here is the agreement between the files") - that is a declared scope, not an invisible red.

THE OWNER QUESTION THAT WAS BLOCKING THE RESIDUAL IS NOW ANSWERED IN THE TREE. deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml carries the answer inline ("NOT ROLLABLE AS CHECKED IN ... Set both to the values the mint prints"), and wamn-duyl's description records the ruling: the operator reads the digest off publish-release stdout and hand-edits the template, with the pod-reads-its-own-digest option EXPLICITLY REJECTED because it reintroduces the dual carrier .15.102 and .15.103 deleted.

Both carriers hold a 64-zero placeholder today: deploy/platform/executor.yaml (env pair) and deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml (extraArgs flag pair). Also relevant to the runbook: NO image in deploy/ is digest-pinned - every one is a mutable tag - so the digest in those two git-tracked pod templates is the ONLY thing git revert actually rolls back.

PROPOSED DISPOSITION: close REFUTED-AND-SPLIT with the clause table above, and file one successor at P2, markdown only, zero code:
  docs(deploy): record the OCI release rollout and rollback-by-revert runbook
Home: deploy/README.md plus the two pod-template headers. Content: mint, push, read the digest off publish-release stdout, hand-edit both carriers, apply; git revert plus re-apply is rollback.
close_reason:
CLOSED REFUTED-AND-SPLIT by owner ruling 2026-08-23, on a wave-55 read-only measurement at fa76974c. Successor filed FIRST as wamn-o77w.

NO GITOPS CONTROLLER EXISTS ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. Zero hits for flux, fluxcd, argo, argocd, argoproj, Kustomization, HelmRelease, GitRepository, OCIRepository or ApplicationSet across every manifest and CRD; no kustomization file of any name; no CI that applies anything. The only kustomize strings are managed-by labels inside vendored upstream installs. A HUMAN WITH kubectl IS TODAY'S CONVERGENCE, and deploy/README.md already documents that as the shipped design for all four tiers.

CLAUSE BY CLAUSE, which is why this closes with a table rather than a sentence:
- Scope 1a, Argo or Flux for real environments: REFUTED. Names the reconciler that .15.98 deleted.
- Scope 1b, plain kubectl apply over the GitOps source the publish bead writes: VACUOUS. No such source; .15.98 closed with the OCI release artifact being the desired-state source, no fifth deploy tier, no synced GitOps repo.
- Scope 2, namespace-per-environment as wrong-target protection: ALREADY DISCHARGED by native chart capability - watchNamespaces plus hostNamespaces plus allowSharedHosts false, annotated in-file as the wrong-target lock and refusing cross-environment scheduling.
- Scope 3, ConfigMap renderer: REFUTED by .15.98. Survives only as unused Rust constants; no deploy manifest carries it.
- Acceptance, fresh namespace converges with no manual steps: REFUTED. .15.3 recorded that onboarding an environment is a chart upgrade.
- Acceptance, git revert restores prior release identity: SURVIVES. This is the entire residual and it is wamn-o77w.

R55 APPLIED, and its finding is an absence: there is no converge path for it to bite on. kubectl diff appears zero times in the repository; there is no Makefile, justfile or Taskfile; the gate runner asserts exit status only; bootstrap.sh applies two generated Secrets and its writer-rotation branch is non-idempotent by construction. Idempotency claims elsewhere are unenforced prose. The one honest guard declares its own limit in-file: convergence needs a cluster, so what is guarded is the agreement between the files.

OWNER REASONING OF RECORD: the spec's converges clause never landed, and the record must say so clause-by-clause or the spec keeps claiming machinery that does not exist. Rollback-by-revert is the load-bearing residue - it is the deployment model's stated rollback story, and with no controller THE RUNBOOK IS THE IMPLEMENTATION. Re-scoping in place was refused on the priority-mishoming it names itself: a P0 id holding P2 work stops the label pricing anything. Closing without a successor was refused because it drops the one clause clients actually feel, how do I undo a deploy, on board-hygiene grounds.

THE OWNER QUESTION THAT WAS BLOCKING THE RESIDUAL IS ANSWERED IN THE TREE, which is what made this closable: values-host-default.yaml carries the answer inline, and wamn-duyl's description records the ruling that the operator reads the digest off publish-release stdout and hand-edits the template, with the pod-reads-its-own-digest option explicitly rejected.

wamn-o77w carries both owner riders: its first line names the trigger that re-opens the controller question, and docs/exe-model.md's convergence sentence takes its one-line amendment in the same pass.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): runtime-operator adoption — Host CRDs for custom host images
description:
## Why

The runtime-operator manages hosts and component workloads as Kubernetes CRDs (state in etcd, reconciled over the NATS we already run). wamn's embedded wash-runtime custom host is the sanctioned v2 pattern — adoption is substitution: our host images enter the operator's host tier.

## Scope (CORRECTED by wamn-0h0g.15.48 after spike wamn-0h0g.15.4)

Host CRs are NOT authored. The operator writes them as OBSERVED state from host heartbeats (host_controller.go:223-270), and the Host type carries no image, no replicas, and no podTemplate (host_types.go:38-56). Images enter through the chart's `runtime.hostGroups[].image`, which deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml:17 already sets to `wamn-host` — the host tier is ALREADY chart-managed. This bead is therefore a chart PIN plus a values change, not CRD authoring:

1. Pin the runtime-operator chart and operator version (carriage verified at fork tag wamn/2.7.0; upgrades only on the fork-sync cadence; operator PRs reclassified from N/A to tracked). Per spike wamn-0h0g.15.3 the install is ONE OPERATOR PER CLUSTER in wamn-system, not one per environment — the five CRDs are a cluster-scoped Helm install-once singleton. Whether the spec's per-environment version pin (spec:117-120) is amended to per-cluster is decision wamn-0h0g.13.49.
2. Set the values that do not exist today: `operator.watchNamespaces`, `operator.allowSharedHosts: false` (the load-bearing wrong-target lock — it ships TRUE and the chart's own values file calls the default permissive across tenants), `operator.hostNamespaces`, and one `runtime.hostGroups[]` entry per environment carrying `namespace: <env ns>`.
3. Schedule the component workloads (flow-http, materializer WorkloadDeployments) onto the host groups. HTTP exposure rides operator-managed EndpointSlices on standard Services — the deprecated gateway is never adopted.

Supersedes held wamn-x09.

## Boundary

wamn-run-worker is NOT a wasmCloud host (no ClusterHost, no heartbeat, its own entrypoint and CLI, plus DB/credential/effect-writer/egress volumes and a native claim loop), so it cannot become a chart host group this wave; deploy/platform/runner.yaml is REWRITTEN by wamn-0h0g.15.49, never replaced by a Host CR. Host/workload replica scaling and the wake path are the M2-adoption train (wamn-0h0g.15.19). Live kind cluster stays frozen; proof is fresh-namespace only at RC. Host tier shape (one release with N hostGroups versus one release per environment) is decision wamn-0h0g.13.50.
design:
CORRECTED 2026-08-16 by wamn-0h0g.15.48 (wave 2), on the evidence of spikes wamn-0h0g.15.4 and wamn-0h0g.15.3. Prior scope text asserted that Host CRDs are authored to carry our custom host images and that they replace the hand-rolled host Deployments. Both halves are false at fork tag wamn/2.7.0: Host CRs are operator-written observed state with no image/replicas/podTemplate, images enter via the chart's runtime.hostGroups[].image (already set to wamn-host in deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml:17), and wamn-run-worker is not a wasmCloud host at all. The corrected scope is recorded in the description; the original wording is preserved in this bead's git-tracked Dolt history.

SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

SCOPED BY RULINGS .13.49 AND .13.50.

.13.49: CRD + operator version pin PER CLUSTER, upgraded on the fork-sync cadence. Chart VALUES (host images, groups) vary per environment and per release. Cluster-per-environment is REJECTED; CRD lifecycle outside Helm is demand-gated.

.13.50: HOST TIER IS ONE HELM RELEASE PER ENVIRONMENT — independent image pins are the environment-singular runtime-revision rule expressed in Helm. MVP's single environment makes it moot today, which is why the principled shape is taken now while it is free. This SUPERSEDES the 'one release with N hostGroups[] entries' alternative recorded at the .15.48 rescope.

.13.46: this bead's operator management covers the wamn-host host groups and the flow-http/materializer workloads ONLY. wamn-run-worker is out of scope and stays a plain Deployment.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh namespace converges from the pinned chart alone: the chart's host groups run our wamn-host images in that namespace, workloads schedule onto them, HTTP reaches flow-http through the operator-managed EndpointSlices, and a workload naming a host in another environment is refused with CrossEnvironmentSchedulingDenied.
notes:
CHART-CARRIAGE EVIDENCE, measured 2026-08-16 at the wave-4 docs lane. Two corrections this bead must not inherit.

1. *** THE FIGURE EVERY EARLIER BEAD REPEATED IS WRONG. *** wamn-0h0g.15.48 and wamn-0h0g.15.75 both say "images enter through the chart's runtime.hostGroups[].image, which deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml:17 already sets to wamn-host". Line 17 DOES read `repository: wamn-host`, but it sits under `runtime.image` (opened :15), NOT under `runtime.hostGroups[]` (opened :20). values-wamn.yaml sets NO per-host-group image at all; its hostGroups[0] carries only name, replicas, service, http, env, extraArgs, resources.
   `runtime.hostGroups[].image` IS real, but it is an OPTIONAL PER-GROUP OVERRIDE: charts/runtime-operator/values.yaml:358-363 at daba602 documents "any of registry, repository, tag set here take precedence over the chart-wide runtime.image; unset keys inherit it", and templates/runtime/deployment.yaml:7-10 implements that fallback.
   SO THE TRUE CARRIAGE IS `runtime.image`, with `runtime.hostGroups[]` as the host tier that consumes it. The conclusion the earlier beads drew — nothing is "replaced by Host CRDs", the host tier is chart-managed and always was — is UNAFFECTED and stands. Only the value path was misattributed.

2. THE INSTALLED CHART IS TWO MINORS BEHIND THE SYNC TARGET. deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml:1-7 documents the install as chart 2.5.2 at rev 8b53285. The fork sync (wamn-0h0g.15.20) targets chart 2.7.0 at daba602. Both revs carry the per-group override, so correction 1 holds across the bump — but this bead's chart/operator version pin must move the header too, or the file documents an install that is not the one running.

Host CR facts re-verified at daba602 (unchanged, they hold): host_types.go declares `type Host struct` at :39 with fields to :55 — HostID, Hostname, HTTPPort, Environment, Status, and NO image, replicas, or podTemplate. host_controller.go:223 handleHeartbeat builds the Host from the decoded heartbeat and Server-Side-Applies it, commenting "the heartbeat is the source of truth and is not validated against cluster state".
close_reason: [b605faad] Two pinned Helm releases: cluster-singleton operator (values-wamn.yaml, chart 2.5.2 -> 2.7.0, allowSharedHosts false, watchNamespaces, hostNamespaces, hostGroups []) and the environment's host tier (values-host-default.yaml, new), plus environment: on both component workloads and six derived conformance tests. *** CORRECTS RULING .13.50: the per-environment host release is NOT 'free'. certificates.yaml looks the CA up in .Release.Namespace only, so a second release mints a fresh CA and the host never registers; with generate:false the TLS Secrets are mounted BY NAME and the Pod never starts. Taken with the MVP namespace equal to the operator's, the one config where it IS free. Environment #2 is blocked on .15.152. *** NEW CHART FACTS: Host CRs always live in the operator's namespace (tenancy is Host.Environment); watchNamespaces is an RBAC MODE SWITCH that deletes the ClusterRole; hostNamespaces set to the release namespace renders no flag. The repeated values-wamn.yaml:17 figure is under runtime.image, not hostGroups[].image. Bead's spec:117-120 cite is wrong; .13.49 is already landed at spec:148-154. p0-results.md's 2.5.2 deliberately untouched (measured result). Nothing proven live -- cluster frozen; proof is .15.153. Filed .15.152-.15.158.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(publish): mint the release manifest
description:
## Why

Publish must produce the content-addressed release manifest. SCOPED TO THE MINT ALONE by owner ruling 2026-08-16: OCI push is wamn-0h0g.15.97, the GitOps desired-state write is wamn-0h0g.15.98, and the deployment attestation row is wamn-0h0g.8.21 (which already owns transaction C).

## Scope

Mint the release manifest as RFC 8785 canonical bytes with a sha256 digest: flow to plan-hash / source-artifact / callable-contract, call-edge adjacency, and the attachment + registration projections.

Populate binding_base_artifact per the ruling on wamn-0h0g.15.62: source_artifact for a released member, and the released base read from catalog.validated_flow_drafts.binding_base_artifact_hash for a candidate overlay. That is the whole reason the field exists — without it a candidate manifest's readiness and effect authority both miss every binding, because a draft artifact can never have a connection_bindings row by construction.

Ruling .13.54's audit rule applies where the attestation is written (.8.21): a digest is RELEASED iff a deployment attestation references it; candidates are distinguishable by attestation absence, with zero schema.

## VERIFIED PRECONDITIONS — the schema half is already done

  - ServingManifest (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:277-293) already has all five fields, and ServingFlow (:120-188) already has all six INCLUDING binding_base_artifact (:176, digest-validated :395). The .15.62 ruling text 'ServingFlow gains binding_base_artifact' is STALE — it landed. This bead POPULATES; it does not edit serving_manifest.rs.
  - All three projections already exist: calls (:187), attachments (:288), registrations (:292).
  - ServingManifest has ZERO non-test producers — verified tree-wide. The mint is greenfield against a frozen, fully-tested schema that has a reader (read, :332) and no writer.
  - CANONICALIZER: use wamn_flow::canonical_json_bytes (crates/execution/flow-model/src/lib.rs:76). Not a preference — ServingManifest::canonical_bytes (:316) and ::digest (:321) already call it, and read (:340) re-canonicalizes through it and REFUSES on mismatch. The second canonicalizer (private ryu-js one at crates/catalog/model/src/lib.rs:1376) would produce bytes the reader rejects. (wamn-0h0g.15.63 tracks the duplication.)

## PREMISE CORRECTION — THERE IS NO TRANSACTION A TO ATTACH TO

The prior text opened 'After the existing publish transaction A'. Transaction A (verify draft + green report -> mint release + evidence) IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. Its owner wamn-0h0g.8.7 is OPEN and was not even a dependency of this bead. What exists is services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs, which publishes a CATALOG SNAPSHOT DOCUMENT read from a file (:107-111) — never a validated draft, never a report — writes NO release_flow_test_evidence row (zero non-test Rust callers of register_release_flow_test_evidence), and hardcodes environment = "dev" at :314, so per-(release, environment) mint is impossible on that path. The dependency edge on .8.7 is now encoded.

Attach point if this bead ever rides the legacy path: publish_catalog.rs:365 is the single call to finish_publication_transaction (COMMIT at :393); note the connection is dropped at :143-144 BEFORE result? in run(), so post-transaction DB work must sequence before that drop or open its own connection.

## Boundary

No OCI push, no GitOps write, no attestation write, no root Cargo.toml edit, no serving_manifest.rs edit. Transaction A internals belong to .8.7.
design:
SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

SCOPED BY RULING .13.45: BOTH COPIES HOLD. The OCI push is the audit/distribution copy and the digest-named ConfigMap is the serving copy — this bead delivers push + ConfigMap, not one or the other.

ALSO CARRIES RULING .13.54's AUDIT RULE: a digest is RELEASED iff a deployment attestation references it. Candidates are distinguishable by attestation absence, with zero schema. The attestation write this bead already owns is therefore what makes a manifest a release, and that must be stated where the attestation is written.

SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

SCOPED BY RULING ON wamn-0h0g.15.62 (2026-08-16): THE MINT MUST SOURCE THE BINDING BASE.

`ServingFlow` gains `binding_base_artifact`. This bead's mint is what populates it: `source_artifact` for a released member, and the released base read from `catalog.validated_flow_drafts.binding_base_artifact_hash` for a candidate overlay.

That is not incidental — it is the whole reason the field exists. Without it a candidate manifest's readiness and effect authority both miss every binding, because a draft artifact can never have a `connection_bindings` row by construction (four independent DDL facts, recorded on .15.62).
acceptance_criteria: One publish mints a digest-stable release manifest whose canonical bytes round-trip through ServingManifest::read; binding_base_artifact is populated from source_artifact for released members and from catalog.validated_flow_drafts.binding_base_artifact_hash for candidate overlays; a repeated mint over identical content produces an identical digest.
close_reason: [911cc7de] mint_release_manifest projects one release coordinate into the frozen ServingManifest and derives its sha256 from the RFC 8785 canonical bytes it ships; step A runs it in its own transaction. Scoped to the mint alone per the 2026-08-16 ruling. UNBLOCKS .15.22 .15.29 .15.97 .15.98. title: [SR-MVP] refactor(serve): mounted-manifest resolution for flowrunner, flow-http, materializer
description:
## Why

Pods surface release identity as immutable mounted config; flow-http and the materializer read routes and registrations from the mounted manifest, and flowrunner resolves callees from its adjacency — resolution is a pure read of the pod manifest.

## Scope

(1) flowrunner: replace resolution-map consumption with mounted-manifest adjacency reads (transitive callee set from call-edge adjacency). (2) materializer: replace the registration sweep DB read (crates/events/materializer/src/sql.rs:12 select_registrations_sql over catalog.event_registrations) with the manifest registration projection. (3) flow-http: FIRST host-side implementation of the wamn:flow-http-routing import (components/ingress/flow-http/wit — currently no host impl exists anywhere) serving RouteDefinition from the manifest attachment projection.

## Boundary

Admission validation against the admitting pod manifest keeps its existing seam; the write-ahead row is untouched. Manifest FORMAT and mint are the publish-side bead; this bead consumes it. HTTP exposure manifests are the operator-adoption bead.
design:
SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

SCOPE CHANGED BY RULINGS .13.52 AND .13.53. THE GOVERNING PRINCIPLE: the manifest carries release SHAPE; environment-operational state stays in Postgres.

1. ATTACHMENTS: the manifest carries the attachment (routes are immutable per release) but NOT `enabled`. Enablement is checked INSIDE THE ADMISSION TRANSACTION, which already exists and already hits the database — zero added serving-path reads, and the refusal is the existing `attachment-inactive` literal.

2. REGISTRATIONS: the manifest carries registration IDENTITY ONLY — source, target flow, existence. THE CONDITION STAYS AN ENVIRONMENT-HOT COLUMN, read by the materializer at evaluation, which is already a per-event database transaction. This is a PARTIAL replacement of the registration sweep, not a full one.

THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS NOW WRONG AS WRITTEN. 'No route or registration read hits the project database' must be amended: routes come from the manifest, but enablement and registration conditions are DELIBERATELY database reads, on transactions that already exist. Amend it before implementing.
acceptance_criteria: No route or registration read hits the project database; flow-http serves routes from the mounted manifest via the host import; flowrunner callee resolution is adjacency-only; materializer decisions use manifest projections.
notes:
SPLIT PER OWNER RULING 2026-08-16 (granularity: a bead must not be a container of separable sub-work). This bead's three legs went three different ways, and all three of its premises were verified FALSE or wrong-seamed before the split.

LEG 1 (flowrunner adjacency) -> FOLDED INTO wamn-0h0g.15.12, no separate bead.
  The bead said 'replace resolution-map consumption with mounted-manifest adjacency reads'. FALSE. The flowrunner guest never consumed a resolution map and never walked adjacency: it receives a COMPLETE, PRE-RESOLVED plan set over wamn:runner/plan-supply (components/execution/flowrunner/wit/world.wit:11) and performs exactly three BTreeMap::get lookups (src/frames.rs:507, :844, :907). The adjacency walk lived HOST-side in the deleted resolve_run_flow_resolutions.
  Under the manifest-delivery ruling (host loads the ConfigMap, walks reachable_flows, OCI-pulls plan bytes, supplies over the EXISTING plan-supply WIT — guest and WIT unchanged), this leg IS the .15.12 host refactor. Same module (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs), same file domain. Nothing remains for a separate bead.
  Also already done: ServingManifest::reachable_flows (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:359-378) already implements the cycle-safe transitive callee set, and validation already proves every calls edge names a member flow (:407-413). Only the load and the wiring were ever missing.

LEG 2 (materializer registration sweep) -> wamn-0h0g.15.95.
  Carries the correction that ruling .13.53's 'condition stays a hot COLUMN' is false — condition is a key inside the registration jsonb document, not a column.

LEG 3 (flow-http routing) -> wamn-0h0g.15.96.
  The only leg whose premise held: no host impl of wamn:flow-http-routing exists anywhere (5 tree-wide hits, all WIT/docs/deploy). But the bead did not distinguish the two host processes; the plugin registers in services/host/src/host.rs:140-164 (the wash host that runs the flow-http workload), NOT crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs (the flowrunner in-process host).

ARCHITECTURE BLOCKER THAT FORCED THE DELIVERY RULING: guests cannot read a mounted manifest at all. Neither components/execution/flowrunner/wit/world.wit nor components/execution/materializer/wit/world.wit imports wasi:filesystem, and the production ctx is built with no preopens (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:596-602). Nothing in deploy/ mounts /etc/wamn/release-manifest or /etc/wamn/release-identity — the constants exist (serving_manifest.rs:58, :71) with no mount and no loader anywhere.

ALSO RECORDED: this bead's own acceptance criterion was already flagged wrong by its DESIGN section ('No route or registration read hits the project database' — enablement and registration conditions are DELIBERATELY database reads on transactions that already exist). The successor beads carry the corrected wording.

DEPENDENT RE-POINTED: wamn-0h0g.15.66 depended on this bead for the manifest to be authoritative for run-to-plan binding; that now lands in .15.12, and the edge was re-pointed there.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(exec): artifact reader becomes OCI pull-by-digest
description:
## Why

The artifact fetch API and the dedicated artifact-reader DB role are deleted; plan bytes and the release manifest are content-addressed OCI artifacts fetched by digest, verified at transfer, cached forever (process-lifetime).

## Scope

NARROWED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-17 ("Split: deletion first"). THE DELETION OF THE .9.10/.5.14 PLANE IS NOW wamn-0h0g.15.107 — the 19 files of commits 7ac999b4 + 11aa572b, the guards artifact-reader-credential.sh and control-artifact-reader.sh, the provision Cargo.toml orphan cascade, and the build-and-test recipe. It is a hard dependency of this bead and lands first. What remains here is the REWRITE.

Supply pre-resolved plans to the flowrunner from the loaded release manifest instead of the deleted run-resolution map, fetching plan bytes by digest-verified OCI pull per the wamn-0h0g.15.2 spike verdict (plain oci-client 0.17 blob/manifest APIs; NOT oci-wasm, NOT wash_runtime::oci::pull_component), preserving digest identity and the bounded in-process cache. Three parts:
  (1) CONSTRUCT THE WELD in the flowrunner in-process host (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs) — this bead's, unavoidably, per .15.101's circularity correction — and hand it to plan supply by reference.
  (2) REWRITE runner_plan_supply.rs off the manifest: read the run's root flow from wamn_run.runs, walk ServingManifest::reachable_flows(root), take each flow's plan_hash / source_artifact from the manifest, and fetch missing plan bytes by digest through the surviving ResolutionPlanCache.
  (3) ADD THE OCI PULL PRIMITIVE plus the executor's registry endpoint knob, and delete WamnPostgres::resolution_plan_bytes with RESOLUTION_PLAN_BYTES_SQL — the live DB plan-bytes path this bead orphans, per the acceptance criterion that plan bytes arrive ONLY by OCI pull.
Also repair tools/gate-mutants/plan-supply.sh: remove ONLY the moving-head-query mutant (its anchor dies with this bead's SQL change) and rename the gate plan_supply_reads_only_immutable_run_map_and_bundle_identity, which now overstates what it asserts. Carries superseded .5.15's pre-effect disposition table into acceptance: fetch timeout/unavailable before effects -> release and requeue; digest absent from the release -> deployment-invalid refusal; hash mismatch -> integrity refusal.

## Boundary

Claim transactions and lease semantics belong to wamn-0h0g.15.10; no project locks held across fetch; no disk cache (held deferral). READINESS POLICY stays owned by wamn-0h0g.5.16 (retained; re-scoped at freeze to consume this primitive and to add the every-connection-bound clause) — this bead provides fetch/verify, not the gate. Reader-role rows leave the registries at Tier D, not here. The WASH-HOST weld construction site and the one-site-per-process drift guard stay on wamn-0h0g.15.101. The effect-authority run-scoped predicate stays on wamn-0h0g.15.66. The OCI PUSH side is wamn-0h0g.15.97 and does not exist yet, so nothing here may assume a published artifact.

The cache re-homing is done: ResolutionPlanCache and InvalidPlanCacheLimit now live in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/runner_plan_supply.rs, which no longer names control_artifact_reader at all. The public path plugins::runner_plan_supply::InvalidPlanCacheLimit is unchanged. The dependency is temporarily INVERTED — control_artifact_reader.rs:21-22 now imports both symbols from runner_plan_supply — and that inversion evaporates when this bead deletes the reader.

FIVE OBLIGATIONS THIS BEAD MUST CLOSE, all verified present and deliberately left standing by .15.41 because they lay outside its file domain:

Once both are gone the dependency is orphaned and must be removed. NOTE: deadpool-postgres and tokio-postgres are shared with wamn_postgres and MUST STAY.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(run-state): admission pin becomes claim-time write-once recording
description:
## Why

The .2.4 admission-time bundle pin moves to claim-time recording: a worker records (release version, manifest digest) from its own pod identity onto the run, write-once under the existing immutability trigger.

## Scope

Rework the 24 execution_bundle_hash sites in deploy/sql/run-state.sql, the immutability trigger arm (:130 and the BEFORE UPDATE column list at :278), and the admission builders (crates/platform/runtime/src/flow_invocation.rs:614,625; crates/events/materializer/src/lib.rs:70,74,94,196). Add two write-once columns (release_version, manifest_digest) minted on the existing claim write. Carries the surviving proof legs of superseded .4.14: write-once enforcement under the immutability trigger, and mid-run republish invisibility of the recorded pair.

## Boundary

Which admission-time pins survive (catalog_id/catalog_version identity vs bundle-hash authority) follows the ratified spec text; runs.capture_mode and admission identity context are untouched. The claim SQL composition itself is the sibling claim bead — coordinate in one lane (shared files: run-state.sql, claims.rs, run_plane.rs).
design:
TRIGGER CORRECTION FROM THE wamn-0h0g.15.10 VERIFICATION (2026-08-16) — the spec is wrong here and this bead cannot be built as written.

docs/deployment-simplification-spec.md:60 says the claim-time pair is recorded "write-once UNDER THE EXISTING IMMUTABILITY TRIGGER". The existing trigger cannot do it, for TWO independent reasons:

1. NO NULL->VALUE CARVE-OUT. wamn_run.guard_run_admission_pins_immutable (deploy/sql/run-state.sql:122-138) raises 55000 / run-admission-pin-immutable on ANY `IS DISTINCT FROM` change to catalog_id, catalog_version, environment, execution_bundle_hash, capture_mode. `IS DISTINCT FROM` treats NULL as a distinct value, so the FIRST write (NULL -> value) is itself rejected. Simply adding the two new columns to the guarded list would refuse the claim.
2. THE TRIGGER IS COLUMN-SCOPED. deploy/sql/run-state.sql:265-268 is `BEFORE UPDATE OF <explicit column list>`. Two new columns would not even FIRE the guard unless added to that list.

So this bead must EXTEND BOTH the function body (with a NULL->value carve-out that permits exactly the first write) AND the trigger's column list. It cannot reuse them. Fold a correction of spec:60 into wamn-0h0g.15.64.

SEAM ALREADY PREPARED BY .15.10: select_production_claim_sql() still returns 14 columns while decode_selected_claim now reads only 1-6 and 13 — columns 0 and 7-12 are selected and discarded. That is the clean insertion point for the two write-once columns. Narrowing the selector itself lives in queue/sql.rs, which is a gate-mutant SHA target.
acceptance_criteria: Admission no longer requires a root bundle pin; claim records (release_version, manifest_digest) exactly once; a second write refuses via the existing trigger; redeploy between admission and claim is invisible to the recorded pair.
close_reason: Commit 618a5800 (plus 0d84f52f, a separate fix for a .15.10 regression found while testing this one). Two write-once columns (release_version int, manifest_digest text) on wamn_run.runs under one explicitly-named paired CHECK, minted on the EXISTING claim write — one UPDATE runs, not a second statement — from the claiming pod's own release identity, with new workload config keys and a per-component registry supplying it. THE SPEC IS WRONG AND THE CODE FOLLOWS THE CORRECTION: spec:60's 'write-once under the existing immutability trigger' is unachievable twice over (IS DISTINCT FROM rejects the NULL->value first write; the trigger is BEFORE UPDATE OF an explicit column list so new columns never fire it), so BOTH the guard body and the trigger column list were extended — a second arm short-circuiting on OLD IS NOT NULL, raising run-release-record-immutable on any later differing write. Guard body verified byte-identical across all three mirrors. Claim selector narrowed 14 columns to 7, consuming .15.10's seam. .4.14's two surviving proof legs carried against the real guard: republish-between-admission-and-claim invisibility, and write-once refusal from a differently-versioned pod. VERIFIED BY RUNNING, not just compiling: wamn-schema-control 111/111 and wamn-run-state 78/78 pass; cargo check --workspace --all-targets still errors in exactly one file, the known runner_plan_supply break owned by .15.12. Fixed three out-of-domain breaks this bead caused rather than leaving them: conformance and runnerbench stand-in DDLs (column parity) and one global-fifo mutant needle anchored on the removed projection tail. RECLAIM DELIBERATELY REFUSES per the HELD instruction — no carve-out added; the full runtime characterization is now on .15.55, which also gained a new fact (the park/wake path hits the same guard) and a hard edge to the merge gate, because option (b) as built head-of-line blocks the tenant queue AND leaves the run unreapable since attempts never increments. Deliberately retained with reasons: the execution-bundle FK/NOT NULL/CHECK/index as the server-pinned root plan, admission's missing-root-plan validation until .15.13, and no pod-identity producer until .15.49/.15.13.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(claim): delete release-bound resolution; lock/classify/lease claim
description:
## Why

Runs are never version-pinned: the five-step claim, resolution.rs, and run_flow_resolutions are deleted. A worker claims lock -> classify -> lease (the never-replay classifier, unchanged) and resolution becomes a pure read of the pod manifest.

## Scope

Also owns the reference sweep the spec list omits: crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs, tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs, tests/conformance/src/schema_drift.rs, tests/integration/src/runnerbench.rs, services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs, crates/platform/runtime/tests/production_claim_live.rs, services/scenario-worker store/test_orchestration references, deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql residue. Guards: one-line predicate update inside this bead for effect-writer-primitive.sh and current-plan-effect-authority.sh (they SURVIVE); global-fifo-claim.sh dies or narrows with its subject.

## Boundary

Effect authority verification set is otherwise untouched. The write-ahead run/queue row and the reclaim classifier are floor — unchanged. Claim-time recording columns are the sibling run-state bead. Red allowed until wave green-up; SHA baselines regenerate at Tier D.
acceptance_criteria: No run_flow_resolutions symbol remains outside docs; claim is lock/classify/lease; the two surviving effect-authority guards carry the reworded predicate; queue tests express the three-step claim.
close_reason: Commit fcf0dd99. 24 files, 2920 deletions / 77 insertions. resolution.rs deleted; run_flow_resolutions table, index, RLS policy, two immutability triggers, grants and map-builder function dropped; the five-step claim collapsed to lock/classify/lease in both postgres claim modules. No run_flow_resolutions symbol remains outside docs, the two Tier-D registries, and plan-supply.sh (which dies with its subject in .15.12). RETAIN CLAUSES INTACT, independently verified: the write-ahead run/queue row, the reclaim classifier (three arms byte-identical to b42c1310), the effect-intent fence position, runs.capture_mode, admission identity context; no claim-time columns added. global-fifo-claim.sh NARROWED not killed (4 of 18 mutants lost their subject or reachability; 14 floor mutants preserved); current-plan-effect-authority.sh survives with one mutant re-anchored and verified still killed; effect-writer-primitive.sh needed no change, contradicting the bead's premise. VERIFIED BY COMPILING: cargo check --workspace --all-targets errors in exactly ONE file, runner_plan_supply.rs, the known break recorded on .15.12. THIS COMMIT WEAKENS EFFECT AUTHORITY, deliberately and forcedly: deleting the run_flow_resolutions EXISTS removed the only database-side binding of the guest-supplied current plan hash to the run, so the chain is now self-referential (attempt_matches is written by begin_effect_attempt from the same guest context) and permits cross-flow effect-node borrowing within a tenant. Tenant isolation, the server-pinned root plan, and release-scoped bindings all still hold. Restoration is .15.66, P0, hard-blocking the merge gate .15.25; the hole is marked in code at three sites and the assertion that became false was restored inverted rather than deleted. An independent verification returned BOTH and all five required fixes were applied before commit. Filed: .15.66, .15.67 (hash-at-transfer has no producer), .15.68 (scenario-worker store lost all mutation coverage). Recorded on owners: .15.11 (the immutability trigger refuses NULL-to-value and is column-scoped, so it must be extended not reused — spec:60 is wrong), .15.27 (Captured::named_node_terminals has no producer), .15.12 (plan-supply.sh hollowed now), .15.33 (two pre-existing broken anchors this lane's blanket check wrongly reported healthy).

title: [SR-MVP] audit(fork): gate B — native plugins vs changed plugin API (#5452)
description:
## Why

Blocking gate before the wamn/2.7.0 pin: the plugin layer was adapted to upstream #5411/#5452; the five native plugins must recompile and the no-trap error-mapping discipline must survive.

## Scope

Recompile the five native plugins against the changed plugin API at daba602 and re-audit the no-trap error mapping (#5452): every host error path returns a mapped error, never a trap. Record findings per plugin.

## Boundary

Audit + compile proof only; the pin itself is the fork-pin bead.
design:
WAVE-1 VERDICT (2026-08-16, branch deploy-simplification, sub-epic wamn-0h0g.15): GATE B: PASS WITH CONDITIONS — and the gate's own premise needs correcting.

PREMISE CORRECTION. The native `HostPlugin` API is UNCHANGED at daba602: fork crates/wash-runtime/src/plugin/mod.rs has a 3-line diff (one rustdoc line plus `pub mod wasmcloud_secrets;`), the `HostPlugin` trait itself is byte-identical, engine/ctx.rs does not appear in the diffstat at all, and multiplex.rs's 21-line diff is pure rustdoc-link repair. #5452 ("avoid trapping the plugin") and #5411 both target the HOST COMPONENT plugin tier (plugin/component_host/, +2672 lines) — plugins that are themselves wasm components calling a workload's exports. wamn ships ZERO of those; its plugins are native in-store Rust HostPlugin impls. The "changed plugin API" the spec worries about is not the API wamn consumes.

PLUGIN COUNT CORRECTION. The spec's "five native plugins" is accurate only for the executor sandbox — crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:510-530 registers exactly five (WAMN_POSTGRES_ID, RUNNER_EGRESS_ID, RUNNER_PLAN_SUPPLY_ID, WAMN_LOGGING_ID, CONNECTION_HTTP_ID). Repo-wide there are SEVEN `impl HostPlugin` (adding WamnJetstream and WamnFlowInvocation) and nine modules under plugins/.

COMPILE PROOF. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`, debug, against the pin (wash-runtime rev daba602..., wasmtime-wasi/-http 47.0.3) in the isolated detached worktree: CLEAN — 0 errors, 0 warnings — after exactly two one-line fixes. Cargo.lock resolves to a SINGLE Wasmtime type universe (every wasmtime* crate at 47.0.3, no 47.0.1 residue), satisfying the one-family contract in substance. All six fork-source literals pinned by the conformance store-inventory guard (tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs:187-230, exactly-one matching) still match at daba602, including one inside plugin/component_host/mod.rs — the file that grew 1312 lines.

THE TWO FIXES THE PIN MUST CARRY, verbatim:
1. crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:544 — `inner: DefaultOutgoingHandler,` becomes `inner: DefaultOutgoingHandler::default(),`. The fork type went from a unit struct to one carrying per-workload keep-alive pools plus a quota registry. This is the ONLY value site repo-wide. Construction choice (default() private registry vs with_quotas() shared) is decision wamn-0h0g.13.48.
2. tests/conformance/src/egressbench.rs, in run_sockprobe's LocalResources literal, immediately after `allowed_ip_name_lookups: Default::default(),` — add `allowed_host_loopback_ports: Default::default(),`. Upstream added the field (fork crates/wash-runtime/src/types.rs:134); empty = deny is the fail-closed value. This is the only LocalResources literal in wamn.

THE LARGEST ACTUAL PIN RISK — and one a compile proof structurally cannot see. Roughly TEN conformance files hard-pin the OLD fork rev 09b1132f, the OLD branch name wamn/2.6.1, and Wasmtime 47.0.1. They all compile fine at the pin and then FAIL as tests. title: [SR-MVP] audit(fork): gate A — connection_http pool partitioning vs credential generations
description:
## Why

Blocking gate before the wamn/2.7.0 pin: upstream v2.7.0 introduced a pooled http_client.rs; a pooled connection reused across credential generations breaks exact-generation authority silently.

## Scope

Verify that connection_http per-generation credential injection KEYS or BYPASSES the upstream connection pool on fork branch wamn/2.7.0 (head daba602): read the pool keying, trace the injection path, and prove with a focused test that two generations never share a pooled connection.

## Boundary

Audit + focused proof only; the pin itself is the fork-pin bead.
design:
WAVE-1 VERDICT (2026-08-16, branch deploy-simplification, sub-epic wamn-0h0g.15): GATE A: PASS WITH CONDITIONS. Safe by construction, twice over — but unguarded.

PROVEN BY SOURCE at wamn b863a735 / fork daba6029, no compilation required.
1. wamn's credentialed egress BYPASSES the fork's new pool entirely. `connection_http::execute` builds a fresh `reqwest::Client` inside the call (crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/connection_http.rs:363-376), sends exactly one request, fully drains the body (:399-403), and drops the client at function exit. `ConnectionHttp` holds no client field (:52-59); the file has no static/OnceLock/lazy client. The object that would carry cross-generation reuse does not survive the request.
2. Every generation-scoped fact — authority, TLS policy, resolved address pin, credential handle and headers — derives from ONE per-request DB snapshot (:98-160) gated on `active_generation == generation` (:232-240). No connection can outlive the snapshot that authorized it.
3. Independently, the fork's pooled path is unreachable from every production guest: the flowrunner world imports no wasi:http interface at all (components/execution/flowrunner/wit/world.wit:9-14 — flow egress is `wamn:runner/http-effect@0.1.0`), and no non-vendored .wit in components/ imports wasi:http/outgoing-handler.

THE LATENT HAZARD. The fork's pool is keyed by `workload_id` ALONE (moka cache, fork crates/wash-runtime/src/host/http_client.rs:829, :901-928), with hyper keying scheme+authority inside each of the two protocol pools. Nothing about credentials, run, or generation enters the key. If the credentialed path ever reached it, two generations WOULD share a connection, silently. http_client.rs is entirely NEW between our pin 09b1132f and daba602 (+2,275 lines; the file did not exist before) and `DefaultOutgoingHandler` was rewritten from a stateless unit struct into a pool owner — that file plus the pooled rewrite of host/http.rs (+823) IS this gate's risk surface.

NOTHING IN THE REPO PINS EITHER CONSTRUCTION. The nearby guards target refusal precedence inside `authorize_snapshot`; none asserts that the HTTP client is per-request, that ConnectionHttp holds no client, or that the flowrunner world excludes wasi:http.

CONDITIONS FOR THE PIN (wamn-0h0g.15.20), guards filed as wamn-0h0g.15.35 which now blocks it:
- Behavioral no-reuse test (no database) in the existing connection_http test module: two credential generations never share a connection.
- Structural tripwire in tools/repo-lint over connection_http.rs: exactly one `reqwest::Client::builder(` occurrence, no client field, no static/OnceLock/lazy client, no reference to wash-runtime pooled symbols.
- Reachability guard in tests/conformance/tests/flowrunner_linker_imports.rs: the flowrunner world imports NO wasi:http interface — this turns today's fact into a ruling, so it is gated on decision wamn-0h0g.13.47.
- The pin commit message must state the relationship so the next fork sync does not re-derive it: connection_http BYPASSES the upstream pool, it does not key into it; the pool is keyed by workload_id alone and must never be asked to carry generation identity.
- Do NOT add pooling to connection_http as a performance fix in the same wave — the bypass IS the safety property (see wamn-0h0g.15.39).

BUILD BREAK FOUND AT THIS SEAM (shared with gate B): crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:544 constructs `DefaultOutgoingHandler` as a unit-struct value; the fork type is now fielded. Fix is `DefaultOutgoingHandler::default()` — construction choice is decision wamn-0h0g.13.48.

DEFERRALS FILED: wamn-0h0g.15.36 (outgoing_request_p3 skips the connection-derived narrowing), .15.37 (workload lifecycle callbacks not forwarded), .15.38 (credential material is a process-lifetime snapshot; rotation under an unchanged handle needs a pod restart), .15.39 (per-request TCP/TLS handshake per credentialed effect call). OWNER DECISIONS FILED: wamn-0h0g.13.47, .13.48.
close_reason: Gate A PASS WITH CONDITIONS. Source-level proof at wamn b863a735 / fork daba6029: wamn's credentialed egress bypasses the fork's new pool entirely (fresh reqwest::Client per invocation, dropped at function exit; no client field, no static/lazy client), every generation-scoped fact derives from one per-request snapshot gated on active_generation == generation, and independently the pooled path is unreachable from every production guest (flowrunner imports no wasi:http). Safe twice over — but the fork pool is keyed by workload_id ALONE, so nothing structural would stop cross-generation reuse if the path ever met it, and nothing in the repo pins either construction. Guards specified and filed as wamn-0h0g.15.35, which now blocks the pin .15.20. Also found the pin's build break at this seam (lib.rs:544 DefaultOutgoingHandler). Deferrals: .15.36 .15.37 .15.38 .15.39; decisions .13.47 .13.48.

title: fix(gates): ground Kind named-tag image identity without alias residue
description: A clean Kind image load exposes only a synthetic import repoDigest through CRI, so the M1 runner incorrectly requires leftover exact tag@digest alias metadata to pass preflight. Make the named-tag fence repeatable on a clean image store without weakening three-node manifest/runtime/config/provenance binding or final Pod imageID verification.
design: Use the exact named tag as lookup identity. Ground its target manifest and direct config child from the root-anchored containerd image tree plus completeness. Require CRI inspection by that tag to report the exact normalized singleton repoTag, the same config identity, pinned upstream provenance labels, and exactly one valid runtime digest across its repoDigests; the synthetic import repository name is diagnostic and never treated as named-tag authority. Cross-node identity is the pair of target manifest and CRI runtime digest plus config/provenance. Final Pod sidecar imageID must equal the preflight CRI runtime digest; it need not equal the containerd target manifest. No alias creation/deletion is part of the executable gate.
acceptance_criteria: On exactly three Ready amd64 nodes, a clean kind load of the commit-scoped sidecar tag passes without any tag@digest alias. Missing/ambiguous/wrong repoTag, target manifest, config child, completeness, CRI runtime digest, config, provenance, or cross-node tuple fails before server dry-run/Job creation. The preflight records target manifest and the distinct synthetic CRI runtime digest; final Pod sidecar imageID equals that runtime digest. Realistic fake tests use an arbitrary synthetic import repoDigest, prove its repository name is non-authoritative, and kill missing/ambiguous runtime identity or any manifest/runtime collapse. Focused runner/static/strict Clippy gates pass, then the blocked M1 Check 10 live gate passes from a clean exact-image setup.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(exec): fetch verified plans after lease acquisition
description:
## Why
After claim records the immutable project resolution map and grants a lease, execution must obtain exact plan bytes from the control artifact reader before any guest entry without holding project locks across the fetch.

## Scope
Compose the claimed map with the verified reader/cache. Fetch only cache misses under the lease, then enter execution only when every referenced plan is present and hash-valid. Implement the ratified pre-effect dispositions: store timeout or unavailability releases and freshly requeues; missing digest is deployment-invalid infrastructure failure; digest mismatch is integrity refusal.

## Boundary
This issue owns the post-lease transfer and disposition boundary. It does not change project claim resolution, artifact-reader credentials or pool internals, plan interpretation, effect activation, readiness prefetch, disk caching, or M2 orchestration.
acceptance_criteria: No plan fetch occurs before commit of the project claim transaction and no project lock survives into a fetch. A complete cache hit performs no store call. Successful misses verify all bytes before guest entry. Store timeout/unavailability produces no guest entry or effect and atomically releases/requeues under the existing pre-effect rule; missing and mismatched bytes terminalize with the ratified typed disposition and never execute. Focused runtime, throwaway two-database, concurrency, and mutation gates pass; image, cluster, readiness, M2, and full M0 gates remain with existing proof owners.

## Scope

Compute the finite transitive flow set from project adjacency, verify callable contracts, bindings, active-generation references, and the host-versus-manifest runtime revision, then materialize the complete immutable map and acquire in the existing project transaction.

## Boundary
This issue owns project-local resolution and claim atomicity only. It performs no control-database or network access, fetches no plan bytes, does not hold a project lock across fetch, and does not enter the guest or change effect execution.
acceptance_criteria: The sole production claim transaction reads only project-local run, manifest, adjacency, binding, and generation state. It produces the same complete immutable run_flow_resolutions map or an existing typed claim refusal, then grants the lease atomically. Exact retry and pre-effect reclaim preserve the map; republish or redeploy after claim is invisible. No execution_bundles read or external connection occurs in the transaction.
