title: [SR-MVP] feat(publish): compose convergent A then B then C
description:
## Why
Publish remains one client operation even though release minting, project deployment, and attestation are three database transactions. The composition must converge after interruption without introducing durable lifecycle machinery.

## Scope
Call control step A, project step B, and control step C in order. Preserve each immutable identity across retries, return the existing result from completed steps, and surface exact coordinate conflicts. Add deterministic failure injection after A and after B to prove a complete client retry converges.

## Boundary
This issue owns only orchestration and retry behavior. A, B, and C remain independently owned transactions. It introduces no lifecycle table, pending state, saga, publication reconciler, compensation delete, dual write, or cross-database transaction claim.
acceptance_criteria: One publish request executes A then B then C and returns the immutable release and deployed manifest identity. A crash after A or after B followed by the same request converges to exactly one release, one project manifest, and one attestation; it never remints or compensates. Conflicting retries refuse at the owning step and preserve prior facts. Focused orchestration tests use deterministic failpoints and one two-database live journey. No executor, guest, image, cluster, M0, M2, or broad workspace gate runs.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(admission): idempotent cross-plane management producers
description:
## Why
Draft runs and test cases cross a durable control reservation into a separate project admission transaction. A crash between those commits must never mint a second run.

## Scope
Extend ordinary project admission with stable private management producer identities: draft-run uses the authoring command id; a test case uses report id plus case ordinal. Enforce same-key same-content return-existing behavior and conflicting-content refusal. Use the private capture authority ratified by wamn-0h0g.7.5, and let the existing control reservation reconciler recover the resulting run id.

## Boundary
This issue owns producer identity, project admission idempotency, and crash recovery composition. It does not execute a test case, finalize a report, publish a release, add another reconciler, or expose management admission authority to wamn_app or any guest.
acceptance_criteria: A first private management admission atomically creates one ordinary run and queue row under the exact producer key. An exact retry returns the same run id without another row; same key with different content refuses atomically. Crash after project commit but before control recording converges through the existing reservation reconciler. Draft capture follows wamn-0h0g.7.5; every other management admission remains off-only. Focused admission, reservation, and PostgreSQL race tests plus narrow mutants pass; no case execution, runtime image, cluster, or broad proof-floor gate runs.
close_reason: [caeff98b] AdmissionProducer::{DraftRun,TestCase} with ManagementProducerKey (draft:<command-id>, case:<report-id>:<ordinal>) persisted under runs_idempotency; exact retry returns the same run id, divergence refuses atomically. A SEPARATE statement for two mechanical reasons: the callable statement has a SECOND positional binder in the materializer guest (a $25 breaks it at runtime), and wamn_app's grant on runs EXCLUDES capture_mode, so naming it in the shared statement would break every production admission. ZERO DDL CHANGE, so the derived model and protected-writes.json are untouched; the .7.5 authority wamn_management_admitter exists ONLY IN PROSE and the gate creates it. THE DRAFT MARKER IS A PAIR -- trigger_source and invocation_context producer must AGREE or every draft-safe connection grant silently refuses. A CONCURRENCY DEFECT was found and fixed in review: the first draft returned a run id no run carries on a key-only conflict. Two mutant anchor-count preconditions repaired without touching frozen baselines. admission_live.rs was already broken standalone (missing wamn_run_projection_writer); fixed. version_identity.rs count 2->3, required by CHECK (admission_context_version = '0.1'). OPEN: whether an exact retry should survive a catalog publish.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(auth): provision the control artifact-reader credential
description:
## Why
An execution-plan digest is an integrity identity, not authorization. Executors need a dedicated control-plane credential that cannot read drafts, reports, principals, evidence, or other control records.

## Scope
Define the artifact-reader database role and exact tenant-scoped SELECT authority on execution_bundles, then integrate its Secret with the existing issue, verify, rotate, and revoke wrapper discipline.

## Boundary
This issue owns credential and grant lifecycle only. It does not construct an executor connection pool, fetch or cache bytes, change claim behavior, or add readiness logic.
design:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-16 — CONTROL ARTIFACT READER, FINAL

Use one tenant-and-control-database scoped stable ACL role named wamn_artifact_reader_t_<40-lower-hex-scope-hash> and project-environment A/B LOGIN generations named wamn_artifact_reader_<40-lower-hex-scope-hash>_{a|b}. The stable role is NOLOGIN, NOSUPERUSER, NOCREATEDB, NOCREATEROLE, NOINHERIT, NOREPLICATION, and NOBYPASSRLS. A generation is restrictive LOGIN INHERIT, has exactly one direct membership in its tenant ACL role with ADMIN FALSE, INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE, CONNECT only to the exact control database, and no other parent, child, ownership, schema, relation, or routine authority.

Grant the tenant ACL role only catalog USAGE and column SELECT on catalog.execution_bundles for tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash, format_version, exact_bytes, and byte_length. Do not grant created_at, table-wide SELECT, writes, sequences, routines, or any other relation. Add a tenant-literal AS RESTRICTIVE FOR SELECT RLS policy targeted to that ACL role. The generation database setting app.tenant is a consistency input only; the literal restrictive policy is the structural boundary.

Use the fixed Secret name wamn-artifact-reader-<generation-scope-hash>, one credential.json key, and a whole-directory read-only mount. Never expose the credential through subPath, environment, logs, a registry row, or a guest. Credential lifecycle is scope-lock, drift refusal, inactive-slot prepare, authenticated own-tenant and cross-tenant probes, Secret replacement only after verification, rollback on any failure, replacement-use fence through an independent wamn-executor-artifact-reader session, then membership and CONNECT revoke, NOLOGIN, password removal, epoch expiry, old-session termination, and inactive verification. Emergency final revoke may omit a replacement and deletes the Secret only after database authority is removed.

This issue changes credential and grant lifecycle only. It does not construct an executor pool, fetch bytes, alter runtime behavior, build an image, touch a cluster, or change clients.
acceptance_criteria:
A fresh PostgreSQL 18 control database can provision and rotate exactly one tenant-scoped artifact-reader A/B credential whose effective authority is catalog schema USAGE plus SELECT of tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash, format_version, exact_bytes, and byte_length from only its own tenant rows in catalog.execution_bundles. A caller-set app.tenant change cannot expose another tenant because a tenant-literal restrictive policy remains load-bearing.

The stable role and generation attributes, exact one-parent membership options, exact control-database CONNECT, absence of ownership and child roles, five-column ACL, restrictive policy, role setting, and all effective authority are drift-observed and fail closed. The credential cannot read drafts, reports, evidence, principals, attestations, wamn_run, project databases, created_at, or any other relation or column; cannot mutate any relation; and cannot escalate through routines, DDL, role management, BYPASSRLS, or guest exposure.

Issue, verify, failed replacement, A/B rotation, replacement-use, emergency revoke, session termination, and rollback are exact and token-safe. A fixed wamn-artifact-reader-<generation-scope-hash> Secret contains only credential.json and is emitted only after the database probe passes. Focused provisioning tests, a disposable PostgreSQL 18 lifecycle gate, restored authority mutants, strict Clippy, rustfmt, Bash syntax, protected-inventory byte identity, and diff checks pass. No executor, runtime, image, cluster, client, or broad workspace gate runs.

Green evidence: wamn-control-provision + wamn-ctl all-targets; disposable PostgreSQL 18 artifact-reader lifecycle 1/1 including two-tenant RLS, failed publication rollback, published-Secret retirement fence, expired-old retirement, emergency revoke and session termination; protected_relations 1/1 and state_ownership 25/25 with canonical DDL/inventory hashes unchanged; strict affected Clippy -D warnings; fmt/bash/diff clean. Independent final audit GO; no executor pool/runtime/image/cluster/client activation.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): install project runtime manifest transaction B
description:
## Why
A project database needs one bounded runtime projection of an immutable control-plane release without importing portable draft, report, evidence, or plan bytes.

## Scope
Implement publish step B as one project transaction keyed by release identity. It installs the deployed release header and manifest hash, flow-to-plan/source/callable references, call-edge adjacency, request and event projections, bindings and active-generation references, attachment activation and tombstones, and release-to-generation retention. It verifies target-local bindings, active generations, and the ratified runtime revision.

## Boundary
This issue owns only the project transaction and its schema. It does not mint the control release, write control attestation C, orchestrate retries across planes, claim a run, fetch plan bytes, or retain any portable blob project-side.
design:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-16 — PROJECT DEPLOYMENT TRANSACTION B, FINAL; PROJECT-IDENTITY CORRECTION APPLIED

Project identity: the persisted release key is R = (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version). tenant_id remains on every project-plane row and in every PK as the established FORCE-RLS row convention; because one project database represents one provisioned target, it is not a cross-target discriminator. org_id, project_id, and environment are constants of the database and MUST NOT appear as columns in any of the seven deployed relations.

Target check: the control-plane 0.1 manifest carries intended (tenant_id, org_id, project_id, environment). The provisioner already writes the project's authoritative identity fact at database creation. B's first database statement compares all four intended coordinates to that fact. Any mismatch raises target-mismatch/55000 and ends before locks, reads that can lead to writes, or mutation. This is one session-level system-identifier check per install. The control-plane catalog.deployment_attestations key remains (release identity, org_id, project_id, environment) because control observes many targets; transaction B does not alter it.

Exact project record:
1. catalog.deployed_release_manifests: one immutable header per R, carrying format_version, manifest_hash, the provisioned runtime revision fields, and server-minted installed_at.
2. catalog.deployed_release_heads: one active pointer per (tenant_id, catalog_id), carrying catalog_version, manifest_hash, and activated_at, with a local FK to the header.
3. catalog.deployed_release_flows: one row per R + flow_id, carrying flow_version, execution_bundle_hash, source_artifact_hash, and the all-or-none callable contract fields.
4. catalog.deployed_release_call_edges: one row per R + caller_flow_id + call_site_id, carrying callee_flow_id, with local FKs to both projected flows.
5. catalog.deployed_request_attachments: bounded request projections keyed by R + attachment_id, carrying the allowlisted kind, flow, definition/source hashes, normalized route/input mapping, and run/response deadlines.
6. catalog.deployed_event_registrations: bounded 0.1 event projections keyed by R + registration_id, carrying flow/entity, operation booleans, optional condition, registration hash, and the ratified causation-depth bound.
7. catalog.deployed_connection_bindings: one row per R + flow_id + requirement_name, carrying source_artifact_hash, requirement type/contract, instance_id, generation, and validation_hash, with local flow and active-generation verification.

B reuses the existing attachment activation, attachment tombstone, and connection generation retention relations. It creates no parallel operational table and persists no portable draft, report, evidence, test, or plan bytes.

Manifest: input is a deny-unknown-fields format-version 0.1 envelope with canonical vector ordering. The exact received bytes use the landed RFC 8785 canonicalization. manifest_hash is lowercase sha256:<digest> over the canonical body with the hash field excluded. A computes it; B recomputes it from the transferred bytes before opening the mutation transaction; C attests the identical hash. The received manifest bytes are verified and projected, not retained project-side.

Runtime revision: after the first-statement target check, the manifest revision fields are validated against the environment's provisioned revision row. A foreign revision is foreign-revision and refuses before mutation.

Activation and retry: first install or a strictly higher catalog_version advances the (tenant_id, catalog_id) head. Gaps are legal. An exact retry of identical R + manifest_hash returns the original installed row and installed_at with zero writes, including after a newer release is head; it never reactivates history. Same R with different content is deployment-conflict. Any lower or equal non-retry is stale-release. Downgrade does not exist; rollback publishes a higher version.

Attachments and bindings: removed attachments are disabled and tombstoned by the existing tables; tombstoned IDs are not reusable. Literal cron attachments refuse under the allowlist. Every connection binding, source hash, contract, enabled instance, and active generation is verified before insertion.

Retention: install inserts one reference_kind = deployed-release, reference_id = manifest_hash, retained_until = NULL row for every distinct projected generation. retained_until is reserved and always NULL in MVP. Supersession deletes the prior release's deployed-release rows. release-evidence remains the control-plane kind; deployed-release is the project-plane kind. This ruling is the exact named-consumer amendment to the earlier .8.9 narrowing.

Authority: B runs through the owner-held ctl project deployment connection and adds no LOGIN or Secret. New relations use FORCE RLS. Mutation remains owner/deploy-adapter only. wamn_app receives SELECT only through active runtime views and no INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, or function path to B. Protected-write and state-owner inventories regenerate.

Frozen refusal literals and SQLSTATE: deployment-conflict uses 23505 only where natural R uniqueness enforces identity. stale-release, invalid-binding, invalid-generation, foreign-revision, and target-mismatch use 55000. Every refusal is raised before the first mutation.

Boundary: .8.19 owns only the project schema, pure manifest model/canonical verification, one project transaction, owner adapter, and focused proof. It does not mint A, modify control-plane deployment-attestation identity, write C, orchestrate A/B/C retries, claim runs, fetch plan bytes, or add executor/image/cluster behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
A closed format-version 0.1 ProjectRuntimeManifest input computes and verifies one RFC 8785 sha256 manifest hash shared by A, B, and C. Canonical-order, duplicate, unknown-field, malformed-hash, and foreign-revision failures occur before project mutation.

The install's first PostgreSQL statement compares manifest-intended (tenant_id, org_id, project_id, environment) to the provisioned database identity fact. Target mismatch returns target-mismatch/55000 before lock or mutation. The seven deployed relations contain tenant_id, catalog_id, and catalog_version but contain no org_id, project_id, or environment column. Control-plane catalog.deployment_attestations remains unchanged and continues to distinguish targets.

A fresh PostgreSQL 18 project database installs exactly the seven ratified deployed_release relations, their local PK/FK/CHECK constraints, active views, FORCE RLS, owner-only mutation path, and no portable plan/draft/report/evidence/test byte column. The provisioned identity and runtime revision facts are authoritative.

One project transaction atomically validates every binding and active generation, inserts the immutable R-keyed header and all bounded flow/edge/request/event/binding projections, applies attachment activation/tombstones, inserts deployed-release retention rows with reference_id = manifest_hash and retained_until NULL, and advances the (tenant_id, catalog_id) head only for first or strictly higher versions. Supersession removes the prior deployed-release retention rows.

Tests prove first install; exact current and historical retry returning original installed_at with zero writes and no reactivation; concurrent identical install; same-R different-content deployment-conflict/23505; stale-release/55000; and invalid-binding, invalid-generation, foreign-revision, and target-mismatch/55000 with byte-for-byte unchanged header, child, head, activation, tombstone, and retention sets. A structural test rejects org_id/project_id/environment columns from all seven relations. Cron refuses. Tombstoned attachment IDs do not revive.

wamn_app can read only active runtime views and cannot reach B mutation. Guests, scenario author, artifact reader, and effect writer have no mutation path. Generated protected-write/state-owner inventories match PostgreSQL. Focused pure tests, PG18 live tests, strict affected Clippy, rustfmt, diff checks, and restored hash/conflict/rollback/generation/target-identity mutants pass. No executor, image, cluster, A/C orchestration, or broad end-to-end gate runs.
notes: RATIFIED BY OWNER 2026-08-16; corrected by owner the same day. Execute .8.19 before .8.18. Project persisted identity is exactly (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version); org/project/environment never appear in the seven project relations. Target mismatch is a once-per-install first-statement comparison against the provisioned database identity fact. Control-plane deployment_attestations remains target-qualified. The project database owner/ctl deployment connection is the deploying principal for this bead; no new credential lifecycle is introduced. The release-evidence/deployed-release split supersedes any reading of .8.9 that would remove the control-plane release-evidence kind or leave deployed-release without transaction B as its named project consumer.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(management): use the control authoring and report store
description:
## Why
After the control portable-store record exists, management must stop treating a project database as the durable owner of drafts, authoring commands, test sets, reservations, case runs, and finalized reports.

## Scope
Retarget the scenario-worker management store, ctl copy/publish inputs, configuration, and owner-local tests to the control database while preserving the landed optimistic draft lifecycle, immutable test-set bytes, reservation state machine, case ordinal contract, and report bytes.

## Boundary
This issue changes storage residency only. It does not admit project runs, execute cases, publish a release, install a deployed manifest, fetch plan bytes, or delete the now-inert project relations.
design:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-16 — CONTROL MANAGEMENT RESIDENCY, FINAL

Principal and scope: create stable wamn_control_author as a NOLOGIN least-privilege ACL role. ctl provisions and the wrapper rotates project-environment A/B LOGIN generations named from the exact scoped identity under the .13.31/.13.34 generation model. wamn_scenario_author is never granted control-database CONNECT and is never reused across planes. One management instance serves exactly one (org_id, project_id, environment); its control login is that tenant's A/B generation pair. Multi-tenant management instances are out of scope.

Configuration: the sole authoring/report connection input is WAMN_CONTROL_AUTHORING_PG_URL. It connects only to the control database. Absence or invalid scope fails closed before I/O. There is no project URL fallback, dual read, or dual write. WAMN_SYSTEM_URL remains a separate identity-read connection.

Tenant security: an owner-maintained exact login identity to tenant mapping plus a fixed-search-path helper is the database-authoritative boundary. Every author-accessed portable relation has an applicable restrictive policy requiring row tenant_id to equal the tenant mapped from session_user. Caller-set app.tenant is retained only as a consistency assertion and cannot widen access.

Exact authority class: wamn_control_author receives only the reads needed for portable catalog/draft/test facts. flow_drafts is SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE. validated_flow_drafts, execution_bundles, authoring_command_audit, authoring_test_sets, and authoring_test_reports are SELECT/INSERT and remain immutable after append. Reservation and case-map relations receive only the SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE operations required by their landed state machines. A narrow owner helper provides catalog-head locking without table UPDATE authority. The role gets no evidence or deployment-attestation publication, no project run/binding authority, no artifact-reader authority, no effect-writer authority, and no UPDATE/DELETE over immutable facts. Author, publisher/deployer, artifact reader, and effect writer remain four separate principals.

Choreography: .8.18 performs control-database transactions only. Any project fact it consumes is an already-observed immutable input identified by the existing producer-idempotency coordinates. There is no claimed atomic transaction across control and project databases. Project admission and diagnostic run-id crash recovery remain .8.20; project run/node observation and case execution/finalization remain .8.5; release A, deployment B, attestation C, and publish orchestration remain .8.7/.8.19/.8.21/.8.22.

Cutover: until the replacement path lands, publish-catalog and copy-project-env --include definition or --include both refuse before any network/database/filesystem I/O with the exact literal control-definition-publish-requires-wamn-0h0g.8.19-and-wamn-0h0g.8.22. Data-only copy remains available.

Lifecycle and inventory: ctl owns stable/generation role provisioning and the wrapper owns A/B Secret rotation under the existing generation model. The P0 role battery gains the exact control-author allow/deny set, CONNECT scope, membership/options, session replacement, rollback, and revoke proofs. architecture/protected-writes.json regenerates under control scope; no project relation is reclassified as control authority.

Boundary: .8.18 moves management authoring/test/report residency and configuration only. It does not admit project runs, execute cases, publish A/B/C, fetch plans, mount artifact credentials, or delete inert project relations.

DEPLOYMENT-SIMPLIFICATION AMENDMENT (2026-08-16, rulings wamn-0h0g.13.43/.13.44; freeze wamn-0h0g.15.1): PARTIAL KEEP per ratification: the management->control authoring/report move proceeds (it is the retained gate). The temporary refusal literal re-anchors off superseded .8.19/.8.22 to the new publish path (wamn-0h0g.15.14); the B/C choreography paragraph is superseded. protected-writes.json regeneration moves to Tier D (wamn-0h0g.15.22). The test-set-bytes leg DELETES: authoring_test_sets is removed by wamn-0h0g.15.27; drafts, commands, case runs, and reports still move.
acceptance_criteria:
Every production read/write of the ratified authoring, draft, test-set, reservation, case-map, and report relations uses WAMN_CONTROL_AUTHORING_PG_URL and the control database. Missing configuration refuses before I/O. No project URL fallback, dual read, dual write, or cross-database transaction remains. WAMN_SYSTEM_URL stays separate.

Fresh and replay provisioning produce exact wamn_control_author NOLOGIN state and one scoped A/B LOGIN generation contract with control-database-only CONNECT, no wamn_scenario_author control membership, no ownership/escalation, and a strict Secret rotation/replacement/revoke lifecycle. One management process is bound to one org/project/environment.

PostgreSQL 18 live proof seeds two tenants and proves the login-to-tenant mapping plus restrictive RLS cannot be widened by changing app.tenant. The role's positive operations match the exact lifecycle class and the denial matrix covers evidence, attestations, project runs/bindings, artifact-reader/effect-writer relations, unrelated control relations, schema creation, routines, grant options, and cross-database CONNECT. Protected-write inventory regenerates under control scope.

Management store tests preserve optimistic draft behavior, immutable test-set/report bytes, reservation transitions, case ordinals, and producer-idempotency identities using already-observed immutable project facts as inputs. No code claims atomicity across the two databases.

Before any I/O, publish-catalog and copy-project-env definition/both paths return exactly control-definition-publish-requires-wamn-0h0g.8.19-and-wamn-0h0g.8.22. Data-only copy still works. Tests pin flag closure and prove zero connection/file calls on refusal.

Focused management/store tests, one control-DB PG18 lifecycle, role/protected inventory proofs, strict affected Clippy, rustfmt, diff checks, and restored tenant/RLS/authority/rotation/cutover mutants pass. Runtime execution, image, cluster, broad proof-floor, project admission, A/B/C publication, and project-residue deletion remain with their named owners.
notes: RATIFIED BY OWNER 2026-08-16. This design is final. Sequence after .8.19 as directed. The exact temporary refusal literal is control-definition-publish-requires-wamn-0h0g.8.19-and-wamn-0h0g.8.22. Do not reuse wamn_scenario_author, derive tenant authority from app.tenant, or introduce cross-database atomicity.
close_reason: Control authoring/report residency landed (4bee577a). Sole input WAMN_CONTROL_AUTHORING_PG_URL, fails closed pre-I/O; wamn_control_author NOLOGIN ACL role with scoped A/B generations under its own domain separator; database-authoritative tenant boundary via wamn_authority login-to-tenant mapping plus RESTRICTIVE policies on session_user, app.tenant demoted to a consistency assertion. Four retarget defects found by reading, not assuming: four probe relations absent control-side, a cross-database join in reconcile_test_report, lock_catalog_head missing control-side, and no --environment so one-instance-one-scope was unenforceable. Refusal literal re-anchored off superseded .8.19/.8.22. protected-writes/state-owners regeneration DEFERS to .15.22 with the full delta banked in prose; three state_ownership guards are red until then because wamn_authority is unregistered, which is expected. NOT DONE and named: the ctl rotation-lifecycle VERB is unwired (contract, DDL and mapping upsert all land and are unit-tested), and the retargeted live suites are compile-verified only. Unblocks .8.7 .8.20 .8.6 .9.11 .7.4 .15.123.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(schema): provision the control portable-store record
description:
## Why
The target control database must own the portable authoring, test, report, release, evidence, attestation, and execution-plan records before any consumer switches away from the project catalog.

## Scope
Define the exact control-plane relations ratified by wamn-0h0g.13.39, their local foreign keys and immutability constraints, canonical DDL, bootstrap/reconciliation ownership, and schema-model drift proofs. Cross-plane coordinates are plain identity fields, never foreign keys.

## Boundary
This issue creates the target storage record only. It does not switch management, publish, claim, or executor consumers; create the artifact-reader credential; delete project relations; or add compatibility reads or writes.
design:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-15 — CONTROL PORTABLE-STORE SHAPE, FINAL

The residency move relocates and never renames. Portable catalog relations retain catalog.* and authoring test-set, reservation, case-run, and report relations retain wamn_run.authoring_test_* inside the control database.

catalog.release_flow_test_evidence is one immutable row per release flow, keyed (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, flow_id) with a local FK to release_flows. Its self-describing snapshot fields are validated_draft_id with local FK, report_id with local FK, test_set_hash, source_artifact_hash, execution_bundle_hash, tested_resolution_map_bytes, tested_resolution_map_hash, and created_at.

tested_resolution_map_bytes is the exact RFC 8785 canonical byte sequence from the already-landed caller-outcome canonicalization implementation. JSONB is not authoritative because it cannot round-trip the original canonical bytes. A derived JSONB cast or generated column may exist solely for querying. The stored hash is checked against SHA-256 of the byte column. Exact publish retry compares every supplied coordinate and snapshot field and the map bytes byte-for-byte; mismatch refuses without mutation, while exact retry returns the existing row and server-minted created_at.

catalog.deployment_attestations is append-only at UNIQUE (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, org_id, project_id, environment), carries deployed_manifest_hash, deployed_resolution_map, and immutable attested_at, and uses the same exact-verify-or-conflict rule. attested_at is not key material.

Evidence and attestation records are self-describing snapshots. Denormalizing immutable hashes and coordinates already reachable by local FK is intentional for these two record families and is the sole evidence/attestation exception to the derived-state bias.

Both families install owner-only. Later consuming beads may add their ratified INSERT or SELECT authority, but no bead may grant UPDATE or DELETE. Cross-plane coordinates are identities, never foreign keys. Regenerated protected-write evidence records both relations under control scope. No owner-shape hold remains.
acceptance_criteria:
A fresh control database preserves the existing qualified catalog.* and wamn_run.authoring_test_* names and installs append-only catalog.release_flow_test_evidence plus append-only catalog.deployment_attestations.

catalog.release_flow_test_evidence has PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, flow_id) and a local foreign key to catalog.release_flows. It records validated_draft_id with a local foreign key, report_id with a local foreign key, test_set_hash, source_artifact_hash, execution_bundle_hash, tested_resolution_map as exact RFC 8785 canonical bytes produced by the landed caller-outcome canonicalizer, tested_resolution_map_hash, and immutable created_at. A CHECK proves SHA-256 of the stored bytes equals tested_resolution_map_hash. The byte column is authoritative; any JSONB cast or generated query projection is derived and cannot participate in identity, hashing, or retry comparison. Publish retry conflict-verifies every supplied identity and content field, including byte-for-byte equality of tested_resolution_map, and returns the existing immutable created_at only on an exact match.

Deployment attestations use UNIQUE (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, org_id, project_id, environment), carry deployed_manifest_hash, deployed_resolution_map, and immutable attested_at content, return the existing row only after exact-content verification, and refuse same-coordinate different content before mutation. attested_at is content, never key material.

Evidence and attestation rows are deliberately self-describing immutable snapshots. Hash and coordinate fields reachable through local foreign keys remain denormalized here; this is a narrow exception to the derived-state bias for evidence and attestation rows only.

The new relations install owner-only. No production role receives authority here; consuming beads add only their ratified grants. UPDATE and DELETE remain ungrantable now and in every future bead. Cross-plane identities are plain columns, never foreign keys. execution_bundles remains immutable and append-only. Bootstrap and reconciliation are idempotent and drift-detecting, and architecture/protected-writes.json regenerates with both relations under control scope. Focused PostgreSQL 18 tests prove byte identity, hash checks, local FKs, exact retry/conflict, append-only authority, and inventory shape.
notes:
BLOCKED FOR OWNER SHAPE 2026-08-14: residency/idempotency are ratified, but the DDL record does not mechanically fix (1) whether control authoring_test_* keeps wamn_run namespace, (2) exact relation/name/columns for tested release evidence, (3) exact relation/name/columns for deployment attestation C, or (4) whether dormant bootstrap grants project roles before .8.18/.9.10. Recommended minimum: preserve catalog.* and wamn_run.authoring_test_* names for the logical DB move; catalog.release_flow_test_evidence with landed charter fields plus tested_resolution_map; catalog.deployment_attestations keyed by tenant release identity + org/project/env; owner-only install until consumer/reader beads. No files edited pending owner ruling.
OWNER SHAPE RULING 2026-08-15: namespace preservation, deployment-attestation coordinate/content, append-only exact retry, owner-only installation, permanent UPDATE/DELETE denial, cross-plane no-FK rule, and protected-write control scope are ratified. The prior four-part owner hold is resolved except for the exact release_flow_test_evidence persisted record identified in design; do not edit that relation until its column/key/map shape is frozen.
FINAL OWNER LITERAL RULING 2026-08-15: the release-evidence hold is resolved with per-release-flow identity, exact RFC 8785 bytes plus SHA-256 check, local draft/report/release-flow FKs, byte-exact retry comparison, immutable timestamp, and the narrow self-describing evidence/attestation denormalization exception. .9.9 is mechanically executable; no owner-shape hold remains.
close_reason: Implemented the control portable-store record in be601c16: preserved catalog.* and wamn_run.authoring_test_* names, added append-only release evidence and deployment attestations with exact verify-or-conflict semantics, and made protected/state-owner inventories plane-aware. PostgreSQL 18 fresh/replay/drift/FK/hash/byte/ACL/RLS gates passed; 88 protected rows preserve the prior 68 plus 20 portable rows; portable 5/5 and protected 10/10 mutants killed/restored; independent audit GO.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(planes): ratify control/project residency and transfer seams
description:
## Decision
Ratify or reject one exact plane contract before any implementation bead becomes ready. The ruling must include a relation-by-relation residency table, identity fields replacing cross-database foreign keys, immutable keys and conflicts for publish A/B/C, management producer identities, artifact-reader authority, retention, and superseded contracts.

## Rationale
The draft moves portable authoring, gate, release, identity, and plan objects to control while projects retain deployed runtime projections, bindings, activation, run state, and application data. Existing publication and claim contracts assume one project-local catalog. An explicit owner ruling prevents implementation from inventing compatibility behavior and lets the work split into focused owner-local outcomes.

## Alternatives Considered
- One migration bead: rejected because it combines schema, management, publication, runtime, security, deployment, and proof work and repeats the long-wave failure mode.
- Dual-read or dual-write migration: rejected because only one pre-RC environment exists and compatibility machinery adds no product value.
- Deployment saga or publication reconciler: rejected by the amendment in favor of keyed retry convergence.
- Fetch plan bytes inside the project claim transaction: rejected because it holds project authority open across a remote store.

## Development Constraint
Treat this as one cutover train, not one implementation bead. Target primitives may land dormant, but no dual readers, dual writers, mixed-version rollout, saga, reconciler, or compatibility layer is authorized.
design: OWNER RULING 2026-08-14: Ratify docs/plane-amendment.md revision 2 for platform-hosted MVP. Control owns principals, drafts and authoring ledger, test bytes and reports, immutable flow and release definitions, tested evidence, deployment attestations, and append-only execution_bundles. Project owns applied schema, deployed manifest and runtime projections, call adjacency, bindings and activation, local generation retention, run state, and application data; cross-plane references are identity fields, never foreign keys. Publish is convergent A then B then C: A is tenant-scoped validated-draft plus finalized-report identity; B is project environment plus immutable release identity and projects the trusted runtime revision; C is UNIQUE on release identity plus project environment, with attested_at immutable content but not key material. Exact retries return existing facts and different content at the same coordinate refuses. Claim uses only project facts, verifies host revision, records resolutions and acquires, then fetches and hash-verifies plan bytes under the lease before guest entry. Store unavailability freshly requeues pre-effect, missing bytes are deployment-invalid, and mismatch is integrity refusal. Management producer keys are authoring command id for draft-run and report id plus case ordinal for test cases. Executors use a dedicated tenant-scoped read-only execution_bundles authority and separate pool. Project retention kinds are exactly active-attempt and deployed-release. Supersede project-local portable bytes, one-transaction publication, requires_green_suite, release-evidence/replay-seed/audit-seed retention, sagas, preflight, compatibility reads and writes, disk cache, OCI storage, and plan GC for MVP. Customer-hosted trust remains deferred to wamn-0h0g.13.42; OCI storage to .13.40, disk caching to .13.41, and plan GC to .13.22.
acceptance_criteria: The owner ratifies an exact relation residency map and all five requested amendment decisions. The tracked amendment and active PLAN decision map are updated as required. Exact A/B/C keys, retry behavior, coordinate-conflict refusals, claim versus post-lease verification, artifact-unavailable/missing/mismatch dispositions, stable management producer keys, dedicated reader authority, local retention, and explicit supersessions are named. No implementation, Cargo gate, or deployment action occurs. Every implementation and future deferral is represented by a granular dependent Bead.
notes:
Owner ratification is recorded in docs/plane-amendment.md revision 2, folded into docs/scope-reduction-mvp.md and docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md. Decision-gate validation: git diff --check and cached diff check passed; exact A/B/C coordinates, retry and conflict behavior, post-lease fetch and failure dispositions, stable management keys, dedicated reader boundary, exact local retention, supersessions, and all four held future decisions were audited; dependency graph has no cycles. No implementation, Cargo gate, or deployment action ran. Immediate dependents are wamn-0h0g.7.5, .8.8, .8.9, and .9.9; first parallel wave is .7.5, .8.8, and .8.9. Commit b1bd00d7186745434da8489627eb05e71e5c6643 is published to origin/mvp, and the closed issue state is published to the Dolt remote.
DETAIL RULING 2026-08-15: control release evidence is a self-describing immutable per-release-flow snapshot. tested_resolution_map authority is exact RFC 8785 canonical bytes plus checked SHA-256, not JSONB reserialization. Evidence and attestation rows alone may deliberately denormalize immutable hash/coordinate fields reachable through local FKs; exact retries conflict-verify every supplied field byte-for-byte.
close_reason: Owner-ratified plane residency amendment revision 2; exact control/project boundary, A/B/C convergence, post-lease artifact fetch, reader authority, retention, supersessions, and deferrals recorded.

description: Finding verification 2026-08-13: commits c12f1ea (wamn-0h0g.4.9) and 40de330 (wamn-0h0g.13.33) have empty commit bodies. c12f1ea also deleted tools/gate-mutants/single-shot-attempt-boundary.sh. title: [SR-MVP] decision(admission): private cross-plane management authority
description:
## Decision
Choose the one private database authority and connection/API used by management to admit draft runs and test cases into a project database after their durable control-plane reservation exists.

## Rationale
wamn_app cannot write capture_mode and must not gain management-only authority. wamn_scenario_author is read-only on project runs and wamn_effect_writer is ledger-only. The cross-plane design needs one narrowly provisioned caller that can bind stable producer identity and the contract-filled full or off capture value inside ordinary atomic admission.

## Alternatives Considered
- Expand wamn_app: rejected because it exposes management-only capture and producer authority to guests.
- Reuse wamn_effect_writer: rejected because it violates the effect-ledger-only boundary.
- Infer capture or producer identity from SQL text or mutable context: rejected because it is not a typed admitted fact.
- Add a second run creation path: rejected because every producer must converge through ordinary admission.
design: OWNER RULING 2026-08-14: The sole private management project-database admission authority is the stable ACL role wamn_management_admitter, with exactly NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS. Project-environment-scoped LOGIN generations are named wamn_management_admitter_<scope-hash>_{a|b}, belong only to that ACL role, connect only to the target project database, and use the existing issue, authenticate, Secret, verify, revoke A/B lifecycle. Management extends the existing sole native wamn-run-state admission API; there is no separate RPC or SECURITY DEFINER path. It atomically inserts ordinary run and queue facts with stable producer identity: authoring command id for draft-run and report id plus case ordinal for test cases, using capture_mode full for draft-run and off for test cases. Exact retry returns the existing run; the same coordinate with different admitted facts refuses before mutation. The authority cannot mutate admitted rows afterward or access unrelated surfaces. wamn_app, every guest, author SQL, wamn_scenario_author, and wamn_effect_writer remain denied.
acceptance_criteria: The owner ratifies exactly one private management admission authority. It may insert ordinary runs and queue facts through the sole admission transaction with stable producer identity and full or off capture as allowed; it cannot mutate admitted rows afterward or access unrelated protected surfaces. wamn_app, every guest, the authoring SQL role, and the effect writer remain denied. Provisioning, runtime construction, and positive/negative implementation proofs are owned by wamn-0h0g.8.20 rather than this decision.
notes: Decision-only documentation ruling recorded in docs/plane-amendment.md, folded into docs/scope-reduction-mvp.md, and added to docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md. Documentation/static checks and staged diff checks pass. No Rust, SQL, provisioning, runtime, Cargo, deployment, or implementation changes were made. wamn-0h0g.8.20 retains provisioning, runtime construction, and positive/negative implementation proofs.
close_reason: Owner ratified the private wamn_management_admitter ACL role, scoped A/B credential lifecycle, sole native admission API boundary, stable producer/capture facts, retry conflicts, and exact denials.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(cred): define overlap-safe effect-writer credential generations
description:
## Problem

The closed `.13.31` ruling requires exactly one cluster-global PostgreSQL LOGIN, `wamn_effect_writer`, while `provision-project-env` must rotate its validity-bearing per-environment Secret with an issue -> authenticate/verify -> publish/use -> revoke-old lifecycle.

PostgreSQL stores only one password and one `VALID UNTIL` value per LOGIN role. Installing a new password invalidates the old credential for new authentication before the replacement can be overlap-verified. Password changes, expiry, and `NOLOGIN` also do not revoke already-open pooled sessions. Because roles are cluster-global but provisioning is per project database, rotating the one role for one environment invalidates sibling environment Secrets in the same cluster.

The `.4.9` acceptance therefore cannot be implemented without changing either the one-LOGIN decision or the staged rotation contract. Secret-side validity metadata alone is not a server-enforced revocation boundary and cannot repair an exfiltrated URL.

## Decision required

Ratify one overlap-safe, server-enforced credential-generation model and its cluster/project scope. Material choices are:

1. a stable NOLOGIN ACL role plus per-project or per-generation LOGIN members;
2. two alternating generation LOGIN principals;
3. client-certificate authentication with overlapping certificates and server-enforced revocation; or
4. an explicitly weaker cluster-wide stop-the-world procedure that quiesces writers, drains and terminates sessions, changes the single password, replaces every environment Secret, and restarts consumers.

The first three amend the exact-one-LOGIN ruling. The fourth does not satisfy the currently ratified issue/verify/publish/revoke overlap lifecycle and is not safely owned by the present per-environment command.

This decision must also freeze how project/environment/database scope is enforced for a cluster-global credential and how old pooled sessions are revoked. It must not grant `wamn_app` ledger DML, introduce SQL statement inspection, expose the writer connection to guests, or move activation out of `.5.4`.

## Rationale

Credential replacement is part of the security boundary, not a Secret-rendering detail. Proceeding with the single-password role would either create an outage window, leave the old credential usable, or silently weaken the already ratified overlap lifecycle. A separate decision keeps `.4.9` implementable and makes the dependency graph report the real owner stop.

## Alternatives Considered

- Treat Secret metadata as revocation: rejected because it does not invalidate an exfiltrated PostgreSQL credential or existing sessions.
- Rotate the one password per environment without coordination: rejected because the role is cluster-global and sibling Secrets immediately become invalid.
- Let `.4.9` choose silently: rejected because every viable model changes the ratified principal count, authentication mechanism, or lifecycle guarantee.
- Grant `wamn_app` or add SQL inspection: rejected by the established grants/RLS trust boundary.
design:
FINAL OWNER RULING 2026-08-12

Credential topology:
- wamn_effect_writer is a stable cluster-global NOLOGIN ACL role. It owns no object, has no CONNECT, and in each project database holds only USAGE on wamn_run plus SELECT and INSERT on effect_attempts, effect_attempt_dispatches, and effect_attempt_outcomes.
- Each environment has exactly two credential-generation LOGIN principals named wamn_effect_writer_<scope-hash>_a and wamn_effect_writer_<scope-hash>_b. They are credential generations, never versions.
- A generation has membership solely in wamn_effect_writer and CONNECT solely to its project database. It has no direct schema/table/function privileges, no ownership, and no superuser, create-role, create-db, replication, or BYPASSRLS authority.
- Outside an active rotation window, at most one generation for an environment is LOGIN-capable. The inactive generation is NOLOGIN.

Rotation:
1. Make the inactive generation login-capable with replacement credentials and validity metadata, then authenticate and verify it.
2. Publish the fixed-mount Secret, reload/drain the private writer pools, and verify use of the replacement generation.
3. Revoke the old generation's membership and database CONNECT, set it NOLOGIN, then terminate all of its remaining sessions.
4. Only after server-enforced revocation may the old slot be prepared for a later rotation.

PUBLIC CONNECT is revoked on every project database. The P0 privilege battery asserts the steady-state generation invariant, ACL-role NOLOGIN, PUBLIC CONNECT revocation, wamn_app ledger denial, and that generation principals are denied every non-ledger object across wamn_system, catalog/wamn_catalog, application, and unrelated schemas.

Ownership follows the existing PAT split. wamn-ctl provision-project-env mints the ACL role, initial generation A, and the fixed-mount Secret. The bootstrap wrapper owns rotation sequencing and invokes ctl. ctl does not acquire a Kubernetes client; the wrapper performs no psql work except verification probes. Canonical run-state-owned SQL remains schema-control-carried installation content.

The executor's private native adapter is the sole consumer of the fixed-mount Secret. No guest, WIT, request, ordinary database URL, environment, CLI, SQL statement filter, SECURITY DEFINER bridge, or wamn_app grant exposes writer authority. .4.9 installs the inaccessible primitive and freezes the scope-hash, Secret document, name, key, and mount. .5.4 remains the first activation owner. All package, WIT, wire, schema, and contract identities remain 0.1 or 0.1.0.

SUPERSEDING NODE-PROJECTION MEMBERSHIP AMENDMENT — 2026-08-15

The same scoped A/B credential generations now inherit exactly two stable NOLOGIN ACL roles: wamn_effect_writer and wamn_run_projection_writer. The second role is limited to wamn_run schema usage and node_runs SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. The generation's effective authority is the union of that projection allowlist and the existing ledger allowlist; no other privilege is added.

The two-role membership is verified and revoked within the existing generation lifecycle. No third LOGIN, password, Secret, mount, pool, or alternate authority path is created. Stable wamn_effect_writer itself remains ledger-only. This block supersedes the earlier membership-solely and all-non-ledger-denied clauses for generation LOGINs only.
acceptance_criteria:
The decision is satisfied when the dependent implementation proves: (1) stable NOLOGIN wamn_effect_writer carries only wamn_run schema USAGE and effect-ledger SELECT/INSERT; (2) each environment has A/B scoped credential-generation LOGINs with membership solely in the ACL role and CONNECT solely to its project database; (3) outside an active rotation window at most one generation is LOGIN-capable; (4) replacement authentication/use is verified before old membership and CONNECT are revoked, old is set NOLOGIN, and old sessions are terminated; (5) PUBLIC database CONNECT and all non-ledger generation privileges are denied; (6) wamn_app and every other principal retain ledger DML denial; (7) ctl mints the ACL role, initial A generation, and Secret while the bootstrap wrapper sequences rotation by invoking ctl and uses psql only for verification probes; (8) the fixed mount has no override or guest surface; (9) no SECURITY DEFINER, SQL inspection, or activation before .5.4 exists; and (10) identities remain 0.1 or 0.1.0.

SUPERSEDING .12.43 AMENDMENT — 2026-08-15

11. Each environment's A/B generation LOGINs have membership in exactly the two stable NOLOGIN roles wamn_effect_writer and wamn_run_projection_writer. Their effective allowlist is exactly effect-ledger SELECT/INSERT plus node_runs SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, required schema USAGE, and CONNECT only to their project database.

12. No third LOGIN, Secret, mount, pool, or credential lifecycle exists. Both role memberships participate in the existing verify-before-publish, one-LOGIN steady-state, revocation, NOLOGIN, and old-session termination sequence.

13. The P0 battery proves the exact effective union and denies every other relation, operation, cross-tenant mutation, ownership, and escalation path. These clauses supersede the earlier membership-solely and all-non-ledger-denied wording for the scoped generation LOGINs only; stable wamn_effect_writer remains ledger-only.
notes:
Owner ratified the stable NOLOGIN ACL role plus per-environment A/B credential-generation LOGIN model on 2026-08-12, including the steady-state one-login invariant, PAT-style ctl/bootstrap ownership split, and generation-not-version vocabulary.
SUPERSEDING OWNER AMENDMENT 2026-08-15: .12.43 adds wamn_run_projection_writer membership to the existing scoped A/B generations. All rotation, scope, fixed-mount, one-LOGIN, and native-only rules remain unchanged; no third credential generation family exists.
close_reason: Owner ratified and the graph now records overlap-safe A/B credential generations: stable NOLOGIN ledger ACL role, per-environment scoped LOGINs, one-login steady state, PAT-style ctl/bootstrap rotation ownership, server-enforced revocation, and no authority or version downgrade.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(exec): split the effect writer primitive from activation
description:
## Problem

The effect-ledger primitive can be implemented and PostgreSQL-proven before the trusted frame-stack interpreter exists, but production activation cannot honestly be claimed until that interpreter supplies current-frame facts and drives the attempt-before-send sequence.

## Decision

Narrow wamn-0h0g.4.9 to stable-key deletion plus the inaccessible writer primitive ratified by .13.31. Move its first production caller, effect activation, and integrated crash proofs to wamn-0h0g.5.4. Preserve wamn-0h0g.4.1 as a consumer of the immutable classifier predicate before activation.

## Rationale

This keeps database/credential work independently testable, prevents fabricated frame facts or seeded attempts from masquerading as activation, and makes hard dependencies express the first point at which real wire I/O can occur.

## Alternatives Considered

Making .4.9 depend on .5.4 creates a semantic cycle because .5.4 needs the writer. Closing .4.9 while retaining activation acceptance is false completion. Adding a durable run_frames registry contradicts the memory-only frame-stack ruling. Hand-seeded proof rows do not demonstrate production attempt-before-send ordering.
design:
OWNER-RATIFIED DECISION 2026-08-12

wamn-0h0g.4.9 owns stable-key deletion, the inaccessible host-only effect writer primitive and dedicated wamn_effect_writer authority from .13.31, and its PostgreSQL/credential/ACL proofs. It has no production caller and claims no live dispatch activation.

wamn-0h0g.3.4 owns the trusted in-memory frame stack and authoritative current-frame facts. It creates no durable frame registry and does not fabricate history.

wamn-0h0g.5.4 depends on .4.9 and .3.4 and owns activation: durable attempt before wire I/O, one dispatch maximum, terminal outcome when known, pure and call-flow sites creating no attempt, and every attempt fact derived from the trusted in-memory stack.

wamn-0h0g.4.1 continues to depend on .4.9 because reclaim classification can land and be proven against inaccessible immutable facts while production execution remains hard-refused. Effect-exercising M0 proofs depend on .5.4.

No run_frames relation, fabricated attempt, guest writer surface, direct wamn_app ledger DML, SECURITY DEFINER bridge, or SQL statement filtering is introduced. All identities remain 0.1/0.1.0.
acceptance_criteria:
The decision is complete in Beads when:

1. .4.9 explicitly stops at stable-key deletion plus the inaccessible .13.31 writer principal, pool, private API, constraints, and PostgreSQL proofs; it has no production caller and makes no activation claim.
2. .3.4 owns trusted current-frame facts in memory and writes no effect ledger.
3. .5.4 owns the first production writer call and the integrated attempt-before-send, one-dispatch, outcome, pure-node, call-flow, nested-callee, and crash-window proofs.
4. .5.4 has hard dependencies on .4.9 and .3.4.
5. Effect-exercising M0 proofs depend directly or transitively on .5.4; .11.3, .11.4, and .11.7 have truthful direct edges.
6. .4.1 remains dependent on .4.9 but not activation, and its classifier proofs create facts only through the inaccessible writer API.
7. No run_frames registry, fabricated history, direct effect-ledger test DML, guest writer, or authority downgrade appears.
8. bd dep cycles reports no cycles and the wave label places .5.4 after its wave-4 and wave-5 prerequisites.
notes: Graph audit on 2026-08-12 found the ratified edges cycle-safe. Additional repairs .11.4 -> .5.4 and .11.7 -> .5.4 prevent those real-effect proofs from appearing ready before activation. .11.8 already reaches .5.4 transitively through .12.6. No dependency removal is required.
close_reason: Owner ratified and the graph now encodes the primitive/activation split: .4.9 owns the inaccessible reduced-principal writer and stable-key deletion; .3.4 owns memory-only frame facts; .5.4 owns first production use and integrated effect proofs; M0 effect checks depend on .5.4; graph is acyclic.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(run-state): isolate the effect-ledger writer credential
description:
## Problem

The immutable effect ledger must be writable before external send without granting the guest-visible wamn_app role, schema migration authority, or author SQL any ability to forge attempt, dispatch, or outcome facts.

## Decision

Use the reduced generation model ratified by .13.34: stable NOLOGIN ACL role wamn_effect_writer plus per-environment scoped A/B LOGIN credential generations and a private fixed-mount native adapter pool. Keep table-enforced ACL/RLS separation, immutable ledgers, database one-dispatch uniqueness, and exact-idempotent outcomes. Do not add SECURITY DEFINER functions or SQL statement inspection.

## Rationale

A dedicated database authority makes grants and forced RLS, rather than Rust visibility or SQL-text filtering, the persistence boundary. A/B scoped credential generations provide overlap verification and server-enforced revocation without sharing one cluster-global password across environments. Keeping activation in .5.4 allows the primitive and its PostgreSQL boundary to be proven before any wire effect is enabled.

## Alternatives Considered

- Grant wamn_app and rely on code confinement or statement filtering: rejected because author SQL shares that principal.
- One cluster-global LOGIN and password: rejected because PostgreSQL cannot overlap two password generations and rotation would break sibling environments.
- SECURITY DEFINER or execute-only bridge: rejected because author SQL could invoke any bridge granted to wamn_app.
- Separate function owner plus definer trio: rejected as unnecessary once scoped generation LOGINs inherit a ledger-only ACL role.
- Durable run_frames registry: rejected because frame ancestry remains memory-attested and activation belongs to .5.4.
design:
FINAL OWNER RULING 2026-08-12, amended by wamn-0h0g.13.34

Authority and grants:
- wamn_effect_writer is a stable NOLOGIN ACL role. It owns nothing, has no CONNECT, and receives only USAGE on wamn_run plus SELECT and INSERT on effect_attempts, effect_attempt_dispatches, and effect_attempt_outcomes.
- Each environment has A/B LOGIN credential generations named wamn_effect_writer_<scope-hash>_{a,b}. A generation has membership solely in the ACL role and CONNECT solely to its project database. PUBLIC database CONNECT is revoked.
- At steady state at most one generation is LOGIN-capable. During rotation the inactive generation is verified before Secret publication and pool reload; the old generation then loses membership and CONNECT, becomes NOLOGIN, and has all sessions terminated.
- Forced tenant RLS remains active. The private adapter derives app.tenant exclusively from host-held ExecutionIdentity for each transaction.
- wamn_app ledger INSERT revokes remain. PUBLIC, authoring, migration/schema-control, and unrelated principals cannot append or mutate ledger facts. Generation principals have no non-ledger authority.

Private connection and lifecycle:
- The production executor owns a second private pool for the active generation. The guest receives neither its connection nor a callable writer surface.
- One validity-bearing Secret is mounted at one fixed path with no request, WIT, guest, CLI, generic-environment, ordinary database URL, caller-GUC, or alternate-path override.
- wamn-ctl provision-project-env mints the ACL role, initial generation A, and Secret. The bootstrap wrapper sequences later A/B rotations by invoking ctl, performs psql only for verification probes, and never embeds a Kubernetes client in ctl.
- Schema-control carries and installs canonical run-state-owned SQL and ACLs only. It remains migration authority, never a lifecycle writer.
- No SECURITY DEFINER function, execute-only wamn_app bridge, or SQL statement filter exists.

Run-state API and database facts:
- Run-state owns private statement builders for begin_effect_attempt, acquire_effect_dispatch, and record_effect_outcome. The native adapter is their only runtime caller.
- effect_attempt_dispatches carries run_id, frame_id, local_node_id, and occurrence and has exact UNIQUE (tenant_id, run_id, frame_id, local_node_id, occurrence).
- acquire_effect_dispatch uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING. Only a newly returned dispatch row is a primitive wire-I/O permit.
- Attempt and outcome insertion are exact-idempotent: identical caller facts return the existing server-minted identity/timestamps; divergent facts refuse without rewrite.
- The immutable-fact trigger protects attempt, dispatch, and outcome UPDATE/DELETE.
- Attempt-before-send is a code invariant owned by .5.4 activation and its crash proofs; .4.9 installs no production caller.

Projection and ledger writes are intentionally non-atomic. Only immutable ledger facts classify reclaim. All identities remain 0.1 or 0.1.0.

SUPERSEDING NODE-PROJECTION CREDENTIAL AMENDMENT — 2026-08-15

The .12.43 owner ruling changes only the scoped generation LOGINs' membership and effective allowlist. Each wamn_effect_writer_<scope-hash>_{a,b} generation has membership in exactly the two stable NOLOGIN roles wamn_effect_writer and wamn_run_projection_writer. Generation principals have no authority outside the exact union of effect-ledger SELECT/INSERT and node_runs SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, required schema USAGE, and project-database CONNECT. wamn_effect_writer itself remains ledger-only.

No third LOGIN, Secret, mount, pool, guest surface, or CONNECT scope is added. Rotation verifies, grants, revokes, and proves both memberships as one generation lifecycle. .12.43 owns implementation and authority proofs; .5.4 remains the first production caller. This block supersedes the earlier membership-solely and no-non-ledger statements only.
acceptance_criteria:
The dependent implementation preserves all of these boundaries:

1. wamn_effect_writer is NOLOGIN, owns nothing, has no CONNECT, and holds only wamn_run USAGE plus ledger SELECT/INSERT.
2. Per-environment A/B LOGIN credential generations have membership solely in the ACL role and CONNECT solely to their project database. At steady state at most one is LOGIN-capable.
3. Rotation verifies the inactive generation before Secret publication and pool reload, then revokes old membership and CONNECT, sets old NOLOGIN, and terminates old sessions.
4. PUBLIC database CONNECT is revoked. wamn_app, PUBLIC, authoring, migration/schema-control, and unrelated principals cannot append or mutate ledger facts. Generations have no non-ledger privileges.
5. A private pool reads one validity-bearing Secret from one fixed mount. No guest, WIT, request, CLI, ordinary database URL, generic environment, caller GUC, or alternate path can supply writer authority.
6. ctl provision-project-env mints the ACL role, initial A generation, and Secret; the bootstrap wrapper owns later rotation sequencing by invoking ctl and uses psql only for verification probes.
7. No SECURITY DEFINER bridge, direct migration lifecycle DML, SQL statement inspection, or general public writer API exists.
8. Run-state private builders are the only code path for begin_effect_attempt, acquire_effect_dispatch, and record_effect_outcome.
9. Dispatch has exact UNIQUE (tenant_id, run_id, frame_id, local_node_id, occurrence); only first-insert-wins RETURNING grants the primitive permit.
10. Attempt, dispatch, and outcome rows are immutable. Attempt and outcome retry succeeds only for exactly identical caller facts.
11. PostgreSQL 18 and mutation proofs cover the role-generation steady-state invariant, exact ACLs, PUBLIC CONNECT denial, forced RLS, validity/scope, cross-tenant denial, dispatch concurrency, immutable rows, and exact retries.
12. Projection and ledger writes remain intentionally non-atomic; only the ledger classifies reclaim. .5.4 owns activation. All identities remain 0.1 or 0.1.0.

SUPERSEDING .12.43 AMENDMENT — 2026-08-15

13. Each scoped A/B generation is a member of exactly wamn_effect_writer and wamn_run_projection_writer, not solely the former. Its effective database allowlist is exactly effect-ledger SELECT/INSERT plus node_runs SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, required schema USAGE, and project-database CONNECT. It has no other object authority. Stable wamn_effect_writer remains ledger-only.

14. The existing Secret, fixed mount, private native pool, one-LOGIN steady state, validity, project scope, and revocation lifecycle are reused. No third LOGIN or credential path exists. Both role memberships and CONNECT are removed before an old generation is considered revoked.

15. PostgreSQL 18 and mutation proofs cover exact two-role membership, the effective-union allowlist, wamn_app node_runs mutation denial, forced-RLS cross-tenant denial, and absence of every non-allowlisted authority. These clauses supersede the prior sole-membership and no-non-ledger wording for generation LOGINs only.
notes:
Final owner ruling on 2026-08-12 resolves the re-audit condition with a reduced separate-principal model. The earlier NOLOGIN owner plus SECURITY DEFINER trio is rejected; the intervening shared-wamn_app/code-filter model is also rejected. .13.32 remains unchanged. The implementation must freeze the Secret name, key shape, and mount path in .4.9 and pin them as non-overridable contract facts.
SUPERSEDING CREDENTIAL TOPOLOGY: wamn-0h0g.13.34 replaces the prior exact-one-LOGIN wording with stable NOLOGIN ACL role wamn_effect_writer plus scoped A/B LOGIN credential generations. These are credential generations, not versions. All ledger/API/activation boundaries remain unchanged.
SUPERSEDING AUTHORITY AMENDMENT 2026-08-15: .12.43 reuses the existing scoped A/B LOGIN generations for node_runs by adding membership in stable NOLOGIN wamn_run_projection_writer. This replaces the prior sole-membership and no-non-ledger statements only for generation LOGINs. wamn_effect_writer remains ledger-only; ledger immutability, attempt-before-send ownership, credential scope/rotation, and native-only access are unchanged.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(run-state): break effect-intent writer/resolution bootstrap cycle
description: Readiness audit found wamn-0h0g.4.9 is false-ready. Its acceptance requires the current frame plan effect policy via the run resolution map owned by .4.12 and frame-keyed attempt identity owned by .4.13. Yet .4.12 depends on .4.1, while .4.1 depends on .4.9, producing the semantic cycle .4.9 -> .4.12 -> .4.1 -> .4.9. Adding .4.12 directly would make the Beads graph cyclic; omitting it would force .4.9 to infer effectfulness from mutable node_runs or catalog state, both explicitly forbidden. The stale .4.9 dependency inventory must be repaired before implementation.
design:
OWNER-RATIFIED CONTRACT (2026-08-11)

The false-ready semantic cycle is repaired by separating resolution substrate from production claim composition.

wamn-0h0g.4.12 owns run_flow_resolutions DDL, RLS and immutability; pinned-release reachable-name resolution; exact-byte/runtime/callable/binding verification; candidate override; complete-map validation/materialization; and a result of complete immutable map or typed refusal. It accepts an already selected/locked run identity and can execute inside a caller transaction. It does not classify reclaim, grant leases, delete queue rows, terminalize runs, or own the production transaction.

wamn-0h0g.4.13 owns only frame-keyed node_runs/effect_attempts schema and the six-field dispatched-effect payload contract. It does not populate or dispatch the payload. It depends on .2.4 because trusted root-plan-hash comes from the mandatory admission pin.

wamn-0h0g.4.9 consumes current-frame identity from .4.13 and policy/source authority only from a complete .4.12 resolution map; absent/incomplete map refuses. Pure and call-flow write no attempt. Effectful writes exactly one immutable intent before external send and at most one dispatch, with terminal outcome when known, populating the six trusted facts. Stable-key retry and compatibility deletion remain atomic with this writer; they are not split.

wamn-0h0g.4.1 is the sole production claim-transaction composer: select/lock/global-FIFO classify; invoke .4.12 resolve/verify/materialize or validate the preserved complete map; terminalize typed refusal or grant claim; preserve the map on pre-effect reclaim; classify effectful loss only from .4.9 immutable attempts. It retains the charter-atomic global-FIFO/partition-plane deletion and depends independently on .5.2.

Dependency repair: remove .4.12 -> .4.1; add .4.9 -> .4.12; add .4.1 -> .4.12; add .4.13 -> .2.4. Keep .4.9 direct .2.10/.2.4/.4.13/.13.30 edges. No artificial .4.12/.4.13 edge and no new issue split. Acyclic order: .13.28 -> .2.10 -> .2.4 -> .4.13 and .4.12 -> .4.9 -> .4.1, with independent .5.1 -> .5.2 -> .4.1.
acceptance_criteria: The owner ratifies one acyclic implementable split and order across .4.13 frame schema, .4.12 pinned-release/current-frame resolution, .4.9 immutable one-intent/one-dispatch writer, and .4.1 reclaim classifier. The contract preserves: current-frame plan policy as sole authority; no catalog inference or mutable node_runs authority; call-flow sites write no attempt; one immutable intent before external send; at most one dispatch; and claim retry/reclaim sees a complete preserved resolution map or refuses. Copy the result into all affected Beads and repair dependencies before any is claimed.
