Consumer contracts and exact dependency edges were repaired; no issue split was required and bd reports no cycles.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(build): freeze effect-provider manifest portability inputs
description: Readiness audit of wamn-0h0g.2.2 found four unresolved inputs in the otherwise owner-ratified digest recipe. Cargo normal dependency membership and enabled features vary by target, but the production target is not frozen. Local packages inherit edition, workspace dependencies, and other build-affecting fields from the root Cargo.toml, while the current closure hashes only member manifests and resolved package records. Git packages have no Cargo.lock checksum even though the manifest contract names a checksum for every external package. The trusted host-context plumbing for the compiled revision is also unspecified: there is no current revision field in ExecutionIdentity or WamnPostgres, and request/env/CLI override is forbidden. Freeze these choices before .2.2 is claimed so its v1 digest is portable and behavior-closed rather than machine-dependent.
design:
OWNER-RATIFIED CONTRACT (2026-08-11)

Resolution target: v1 is target-independent. Regeneration uses repository-pinned Cargo 1.97.0, locked/offline package-scoped resolution rooted at wamn-executor with --target all and normal edges only, projected to the wamn-execution-host descendant subgraph, plus the executor-selected feature union. For each full package identity, record the byte-sorted union of enabled features across all observed resolver units; never use last-one-wins or full-workspace feature unification. The framed manifest records cargo=1.97.0, target=all, edge-kinds=normal, root=wamn-executor, projection=wamn-execution-host. The current wash-runtime union remains exactly oci,washlet. This conservatively commits to target-conditioned provider code without inventing an unenforced x86-only deployment restriction.

Workspace inheritance: do not hash root Cargo.toml bytes. For each governed local package and executor composition package, record every package field inherited with workspace=true, keyed by normalized local package id and field name; baseline values are version=0.1.0, edition=2024, license=Apache-2.0. Record every normal dependency declaration in the projected graph using workspace=true, plus executor's direct wash-runtime edge, as its exact effective merged declaration: declaring package, dependency kind/target predicate/key, package rename, normalized repo-relative path or registry/git identity, version requirement, registry, git URL and rev/tag/branch, default-features, optionality, and byte-sorted declared features. Branch-valued git inputs are rejected. Future workspace-inherited lint/package fields used by governed manifests are included generically. Member Cargo.toml bytes remain governed. Root profiles, toolchain/codegen, linker/rustflags, and .cargo/config are excluded because v1 is a semantic source/dependency recipe, not a physical binary recipe.

Git checksums: every external record has a checksum key. Registry packages require Cargo.lock's exact lowercase 64-hex checksum. Git packages require JSON checksum:null; a string is noncanonical. In the framed preimage, git null is external/checksum plus a zero-length value, disambiguated by independently framed source-kind=git. Git identity is canonical URL with Cargo decorations removed plus the exact 40-lowercase-hex resolved commit. Branch/tag/abbreviated sources are rejected. The fork is https://github.com/dkkloimwieder/wasmCloud at 09b1132f2bab36e6e71f4637bd0e4755e359dd43, checksum null, features oci,washlet.

Trusted runtime context: wamn-execution-host exposes a read-only TrustedExecutionRuntimeRevision with private fields and no constructor accepting revision strings. Its sole constructor takes exact loaded flowrunner bytes and derives flowrunner_component_digest as SHA-256 of those bytes, effect_provider_revision from the compiled EFFECT_PROVIDER_REVISION constant, and host_effect_contract_version from the catalog 0.1 constant. ExecutionHost::instantiate constructs and retains it internally before guest entry; ExecutionIdentity remains owner/tenant/schema/project. No request, env, CLI, config, WIT, PostgreSQL GUC, public setter, or caller-supplied string may replace any member. A read-only accessor is allowed.

Scenario/management validation uses the same byte-derived constructor and deletes caller-supplied provider/host-contract revision fields. .2.2 owns generation, type/derivation/storage, scenario input removal, and equality proofs; it adds no WamnPostgres session state or refusal. .2.3 takes the retained context directly as bound host-side claim-preflight input within .4.1's transaction/.4.12 resolution substrate, compares all three members against every reachable plan before guest entry, and owns typed foreign-revision terminalization plus the zero-entry sentinel. .2.3 accepts no second context and depends on .4.1.
acceptance_criteria: The owner ratifies: one exact production target or target-independent resolution rule; the exact normalized workspace-inherited inputs or root-manifest record included in v1; canonical null/absence handling for git checksums while URL plus full commit remain identity; and the exact non-overridable executor-to-host context seam owned by .2.2 versus .2.3. The decision updates wamn-0h0g.2.2 acceptance before implementation, keeps every package and public contract at 0.1/0.1.0, and adds no code.
close_reason: Owner ratified target-independent Cargo 1.97 all-target provider resolution, normalized workspace inheritance, canonical git checksum null with URL/full-commit identity, and the immutable byte-derived TrustedExecutionRuntimeRevision seam; .2.2/.2.3 acceptance and the .2.3 -> .4.1 dependency were updated with every version retained at 0.1.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(plan): freeze exact own-flow ExecutionPlanV2 wire shape
description: Readiness audit of wamn-0h0g.2.10 found that the amendment freezes the semantic member list but not several exact durable wire choices. Before implementation, the owner must freeze: the plain node-id newtype name and scalar encoding; whether call-flow {site, flow_id} is an instruction collection or a specialized node representation; CallableContract presence/encoding plus the exact version literal and input_schema_hash construction; whether the single own-entry guard is mandatory or optional and its encoded representation; whether NonCanonicalJson is removed only from the plan reader while the unrelated CanonicalJson parser retains it; whether exact-byte hash verification is followed by structural and semantic validation; and ownership of the stable-normalization, golden-byte/hash, and cross-process rebuild proofs where .2.10 and .3.2 currently conflict. Do not claim .2.10 until the ratified contract is copied into its acceptance criteria.
design:
OWNER-RATIFIED CONTRACT (2026-08-11)

ExecutionPlanV2 remains a kebab-case, deny-unknown-fields JSON object with mandatory header and body fields.

Header: format-version "0.1"; plan-compiler-revision "0.1"; ExecutionRuntimeRevision; root-artifact-hash.

Node identity: introduce ExecutionNodeId, a transparent immutable JSON string scalar accepting exactly ^[a-z0-9-]+$. It replaces every ExecutionNodePath use in the plan: local-node-id, entry-instruction, edge endpoints, call site, responders, and source-map local-node-id. No segment/path API or array encoding survives. Respond termination encodes {"kind":"respond","responders":[...]}.

Call-flow: it is a specialized ordinary node, never a separate body-level instruction collection. A type "call-flow" node has exact config {site, flow-id}; site equals local-node-id; flow-id satisfies the lowercase slug rule; effect-policy is effectful; no connection requirement or callee artifact/plan hash, contract copy, enter/return instruction, or frame metadata is permitted.

Body: entry-instruction, nodes, edges, root-terminal-behavior, entry-input-schema-guard, callable-contract, and source-map are mandatory; empty collections are encoded. Optional node connection requirements and edge destination ports remain omitted when absent. The entry guard is a durable JSON Schema value: request entry stores the validator-accepted Draft 2020-12 schema, event/cron stores boolean true; remote references are forbidden. "Compiled" means validation successfully compiled this value, not persisted engine bytecode.

Callable contract: callable-contract is always present: null for non-callable, otherwise {version:"0.1", input-schema-hash:"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>", return-contract:"untyped-json-body", effect-ceiling:"effectful"}. input-schema-hash is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 bytes of the entry guard; readers recompute it. This semantic subvalue hash does not replace plan byte identity. Presence must agree with intrinsic callability.

Source map covers every node exactly once and carries local-node-id plus source-node-id only. The header root-artifact-hash is the sole plan artifact hash. Graph validation enforces unique node ids, valid endpoints/sites/responders/source-map coverage, unique fan-out identity, and complete nonempty responder sets where applicable.

Identity/reader order: execution_bundle_hash is lowercase sha256 over untouched exact stored bytes. A reader validates expected-hash syntax, hashes and compares raw bytes before parsing, refuses mismatch without parsing, then parses and performs structural/semantic validation. It never normalizes, reorders, reserializes, requires RFC 8785 plan bytes, or derives identity from parsed JSON. Matching-hash valid JSON with different whitespace/key order is accepted. Delete plan-specific canonical_bytes/into_canonical/from_canonical_bytes behavior. CatalogIdentityError::NonCanonicalJson remains for the unrelated CanonicalJson source contract; execution-plan readers never produce it.

Proof ownership: wamn-0h0g.2.10 owns wire/reader proofs only. wamn-0h0g.3.2 exclusively owns stable semantic-key normalization, exact emitted golden bytes plus hashes, and cross-process deterministic rebuild equality.
acceptance_criteria: One owner-ratified, implementable contract answers every listed wire/validation/proof choice; preserves textual plan_compiler_revision 0.1 and sha256 over exact emitted bytes; assigns each proof to exactly one issue; updates wamn-0h0g.2.10 and wamn-0h0g.3.2 acceptance/dependencies consistently; and introduces no implementation code.
close_reason: Owner ratified the exact ExecutionPlanV2 scalar-node wire, specialized call-flow node, mandatory guard and nullable 0.1 callable contract, exact-byte hash-before-parse reader, scoped NonCanonicalJson retention, and exclusive compiler-proof ownership in .3.2; consumer acceptance and the stale .3.2 -> .2.6 dependency were updated.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(run-state): freeze admission bundle-pin transition
description: wamn-0h0g.2.4 is false-ready: it requires every admitted run to pin non-null catalog_id, catalog_version, and execution_bundle_hash with durable referential integrity, but has no acceptance criteria. The authoritative release-member lookup, exact FK and non-null transition, handling of existing pre-plan rows/releases, complete admission-writer inventory, and removal timing for any duplicate JSON pin are not frozen. Multiple materially different migrations and refusal boundaries are possible. Keep implementation blocked until the owner ratifies one exact contract.
design:
RECOMMENDED OWNER CONTRACT (not yet ratified)

Authoritative root-plan source

- Published HTTP/event/release-scenario admission derives the root hash only from catalog.release_flows.execution_bundle_hash.
- Draft/test candidate admission derives it only from catalog.validated_flow_drafts.execution_bundle_hash.
- Callers, manifest JSON, invocation_context, and release_flow_test_evidence never supply or override runtime authority.

Exact catalog.release_flows addition

execution_bundle_hash text NOT NULL with lowercase sha256 check; tenant-scoped FK (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash) to catalog.execution_bundles; index (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash). Keep the existing release-flow primary key. insert_release_flow_sql gains the hash. Copying a conforming release copies the stored hash. A legacy publish path unable to provide a validated plan returns missing-root-plan without inserting a member; .8.7 still owns the successful gated publication transaction and release-flow test evidence.

Exact runs contract

- catalog_id text NOT NULL CHECK nonempty.
- catalog_version int NOT NULL CHECK > 0 (replace current bigint so it matches catalog keys).
- environment text NOT NULL CHECK nonempty.
- execution_bundle_hash text NOT NULL with exact lowercase sha256 check.
- Immediate NO ACTION FK (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version) to catalog.release_manifests.
- Immediate NO ACTION FK (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash) to catalog.execution_bundles.
- Indexes runs_release (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version) and runs_execution_bundle (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash).
- Remove the obsolete nullable-pair check.
- BEFORE UPDATE OF all four pins raises SQLSTATE 55000, run-admission-pin-immutable, when any changes.

Greenfield migration policy

Use one atomic schema-control/ctl cutover under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on release_flows and the selected runs table. If either target lacks the contract and either table contains rows, abort before DDL with SQLSTATE 55000 and execution-pin-cutover-requires-empty-run-and-release-membership. Never infer a plan from artifact identity, JSON, or a sole matching draft, and never rewrite history. Empty pre-plan databases receive columns, types/nullability, checks, FKs, indexes, and trigger atomically. Pre-plan installations must be re-provisioned. Schema-control observes types, nullability, FKs, indexes, and trigger, not only column names.

All admission writers/readback

Update shared HTTP/event admission, release-scenario admission, and draft/test candidate admission plus runtime/materializer/scenario-worker bindings. Release admission selects the release member hash and joins execution_bundles; draft admission joins execution_bundles. Every INSERT INTO runs writes the selected hash. Duplicate identity comparisons include it. Duplicate/recovery paths return the already-admitted row without rebinding to a newer head. Repoint the transitional flowrunner reader to runs.execution_bundle_hash. Do not expand dead open-run, child, replay, or raw write-ahead builders into alternate admission paths; the new constraints leave them fail-closed until their deletion owners remove them.

Missing-plan ownership

.2.4 owns the non-durable typed admission refusal missing-root-plan before any runs, run_queue, or invocation_admissions mutation. It proves presence and tenant-scoped FK identity only. .4.12 retains parsing/exact-byte verification, reachable-set resolution, runtime-revision checks, hash-invalid-bytes, and durable claim terminalization.

Remove the JSON duplicate atomically

Remove principal.execution-bundle-hash from draft invocation_context in the same commit after repointing the sole flowrunner reader. Do not add it to AdmittedPrincipal. Add a residue guard forbidding execution-bundle-hash in invocation-context construction/read paths.

Proof contract

Named pure tests: admission_derives_root_bundle_from_authoritative_member; draft_admission_persists_validated_bundle_without_json_duplicate; missing_root_plan_decodes_as_distinct_admission_refusal. PostgreSQL 18: all admission producers persist the exact immutable pin; missing/cross-tenant bundles refuse before any admission write; catalog-head movement cannot rebind an admitted run. Migration: empty schema converges; legacy rows/members refuse without partial DDL; reconcile is idempotent. Drift guards pin types/nullability/checks/FKs/indexes/trigger. Residue forbids invocation_context bundle pins.

Named mutants: release-member-hash-replaced-by-caller-json, missing-root-plan-admits-run, runs-execution-bundle-fk-removed, run-admission-pin-update-allowed, draft-json-bundle-pin-restored, and legacy-plan-pin-fabricated-from-artifact.

Alternatives rejected by the recommendation: release_flow_test_evidence couples runtime authority to proof lifecycle; members_json duplicates structural identity without FK; draft backfill fabricates an unrecorded selection; nullable or NOT VALID migration preserves structurally unpinned runs. Strict empty cutover is the only non-fabricating greenfield contract.
acceptance_criteria: Owner ratifies the authoritative release-member source for the root execution_bundle_hash; exact runs column types, nullability, FK/check/index shape and additive migration policy for existing rows; every admission writer and readback surface; exact missing-plan refusal ownership; duplicate invocation-context pin removal timing; and named pure, live-PostgreSQL, drift, and mutation proofs. Copy the approved contract into wamn-0h0g.2.4 acceptance before claim.
close_reason: Owner ratified the authoritative immutable bundle-pin and strict greenfield cutover contract; the exact contract is now the acceptance for wamn-0h0g.2.4.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(run-state): freeze recovery/lineage deletion boundary
description: wamn-0h0g.4.3 is false-ready: docs/scope-reduction-mvp.md F.2 requires deletion of the recovery-class triple, predecessor_attempt_id and legacy_imported exceptions, and cross-claim successor identity, but the implementation bead has no acceptance criteria. The exact Rust types, columns, transition branches, compatibility treatment for existing rows, and retained immutable write-ahead attempt facts are not frozen. Multiple materially different deletions are possible. Keep implementation blocked until the owner ratifies one exact boundary; do not infer survivors from current recovery code.
design:
RECOMMENDED OWNER CONTRACT (not yet ratified)

Boundary and sequencing

wamn-0h0g.4.3 is deletion-only and fail-closed. It deletes recovery policy, successor lineage, and duplicate mutable attempt authority, but does not activate the replacement writer. Existing execution remains hard-refused after .4.3 until .4.9 activates pure => no attempt and effectful => one immutable attempt. .4.13 later adds frame identity; .2.5 later adds plan/source/requirement authority.

Delete from Rust and execution transitions

- RecoveryClass, its SQL codec/re-export/docs/tests.
- AttemptStartResult and AttemptDispatchResult, including Redispatch and MissingAttemptKey.
- begin_attempt_sql and mark_attempt_dispatched_sql.
- Flowrunner RecoveryAdmission, recovery_admission, begin_attempt, mark_attempt_dispatched, and their imports.
- Every branch or literal for replay, idempotent-with-key, never-replay, redispatch, or missing-attempt-key. No compatibility enum or renamed taxonomy.

Delete from fresh node_runs

- current_effect_attempt_id, attempt, selected_recovery_class, recovery_class, generation_fact_kind, connection_generation, credential_generation, attempt_started_at, attempt_dispatched_at, attempt_deadline_at, attempt_input_ref, attempt_key.
- node_runs_current_effect_attempt_fk; selected/recovery/generation checks; and the attempt-shaped node_runs checks.

Delete from fresh effect_attempts

- attempt_index, predecessor_attempt_id, legacy_imported, selected_recovery_class, recovery_class.
- predecessor FK, attempt-index/lineage/recovery/key checks, UNIQUE identity containing attempt_index, and the old occurrence index containing attempt_index.
- Replace successor identity with exactly UNIQUE (tenant_id, run_id, node_id, occurrence). .4.13 later extends the identity with frame_id/local_node_id.

Delete from schema-control/ctl

- Current/predecessor effect-attempt FK specs; legacy effect-authority column inventory; legacy-row observation/count/backfill SQL and RunPlaneObservation field; BackfillEffectAttempts action and planner branch; CTL observation/backfill code and its live leg.

Exact surviving attempt ledger

effect_attempts retains tenant_id, attempt_id, run_id, node_id, occurrence, seq, generation_fact_kind, connection_name, connection_generation, credential_generation, verified_author_principal, verified_publisher_principal, attempt_started_at, attempt_deadline_at, attempt_input_ref, attempt_key, created_at. attempt_key is temporary .4.9-owned stable-key state and has no recovery-class check after .4.3.

Retain unchanged effect_attempt_dispatches (one row per attempt), effect_attempt_outcomes (one terminal success/error per dispatched attempt), temporal FKs, RLS, SELECT-only runtime ACLs, append guards, UPDATE/DELETE immutability, bulk-scope index, dispositions/history keyed by attempt_id, and attempt retention independent of run-history pruning. The future writer carries attempt_id directly; no mutable current-attempt pointer or successor identity returns.

Upgrade treatment

Fresh provisioning omits every deleted column. Existing immutable attempt/dispatch/outcome rows are never rewritten or deleted. On upgraded databases, retired columns may remain physically present as surfaced extra columns, but no record definition, reader, writer, constraint, index, or transition may use them. Reconciliation drops obsolete checks/FKs/indexes and drops NOT NULL/defaults from retired attempt columns; it performs no legacy backfill. Before adding one-occurrence uniqueness it refuses multiple historical attempts per occurrence with legacy-effect-attempt-successors-present. It refuses a nonterminal legacy node projection lacking an immutable intent with legacy-active-attempt-without-immutable-intent. Terminal legacy projections remain untouched. Reconcile is idempotent.

CDC lineage is outside this deletion

Do not touch runs.registration_id, trigger_source, event_source_run_id, event_root_run_id, event_depth, idempotency_key, input_json, invocation_context source evidence, catalog/version/environment/flow identity, CDC depth/root/immutability checks/indexes/triggers, or run_queue.stream_seq. replay_of/root_run_id belong to the separate rerun/reconstruction deletion owner, not this recovery-class cut.

Proof contract

Replace obsolete never-replay/recovery proofs with named tests recovery_and_successor_lineage_residue_is_absent, effect_attempt_schema_has_one_identity_and_no_successor_shape, upgraded_attempt_rows_are_preserved_but_retired, unsafe_legacy_attempt_upgrade_refuses, and trusted_cdc_lineage_is_unchanged_by_attempt_retirement. PostgreSQL 18 proves exact fresh shape, byte/count preservation, refusal of duplicate successors and mutable-only active attempts, obsolete constraint removal, idempotent reconcile, and unchanged CDC admission lineage.

Named mutation campaign single-shot-attempt-boundary kills: restore-recovery-literal, restore-predecessor-lineage, restore-current-attempt-pointer, allow-second-attempt-per-occurrence, rewrite-existing-attempt-history, accept-active-mutable-only-attempt, drop-effect-ledger-immutability, drop-cdc-source-lineage, and drop-cdc-root-depth-immutability.

Tradeoff requiring acknowledgement: the charter combines no live schema residue with non-destructive migration. This recommendation interprets that as clean fresh schemas plus inert surfaced extra columns on upgraded databases. If an upgraded database has multiple immutable successor attempts per occurrence, refuse and require reset/manual archival; never choose a winner.
acceptance_criteria: Owner ratifies the exact deleted Rust symbols, SQL columns/checks/indexes/transitions and obsolete proofs; the exact retained effect-attempt identity, generation, dispatch, outcome, and trusted CDC lineage facts; treatment of pre-existing rows during additive reconciliation; and named residue, live-PostgreSQL, and mutation proofs. Copy the approved contract into wamn-0h0g.4.3 acceptance before claim.
close_reason: Owner ratified the deletion-only, fail-closed recovery/lineage retirement contract; the exact contract is now the acceptance for wamn-0h0g.4.3.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(build): freeze effect-provider revision digest inputs
description: wamn-0h0g.2.2 is false-ready: its build-generated effect_provider_revision is a durable exact-executable identity, but the issue does not freeze the input manifest, deterministic framing and ordering, digest literal format, build-time generation and verification boundary, change policy, or named proofs. Multiple materially different implementations are possible. Keep implementation blocked until the owner ratifies one exact contract; do not infer it from the plan compiler or effect-provider code.
design:
RECOMMENDED OWNER CONTRACT (not yet ratified)

Choose a semantic native-provider recipe revision, not an ELF or OCI digest. The manifest must be closed over native effect behavior; a hand-picked three-root file list is insufficient.

Exact v1 input closure

Root the normal locked production dependency subgraph at wamn-execution-host, then add the exact executor production-composition inputs (services/executor/Cargo.toml and every regular file under services/executor/src) and the executor-selected wash-runtime feature union. Do not root the graph at the whole executor package because that would pull queue/NATS/CLI/telemetry/scheduler lifecycle into the provider revision.

At baseline 56173ef the first-party host closure is exactly: wamn-execution-host, wamn-runtime, wamn-catalog, wamn-component-policy, wamn-control-registry, wamn-event-wire, wamn-flow, wamn-flow-invocation, wamn-node-invoke, wamn-node-manifest, wamn-pg-core, wamn-run-state, and wamn-runner.

A checked-in canonical manifest records those local package IDs/roots and every normal transitive external package in the locked closure as name, version, source, checksum, and byte-sorted package-scoped enabled features. Git sources record canonical URL plus resolved commit, never a branch. The current wamn-executor package-scoped wash-runtime record is the repository fork URL, commit 09b1132f2bab36e6e71f4637bd0e4755e359dd43, and features oci, washlet; full-workspace feature unification must not add unrelated wasi-config/wasi-otel.

For each local package root, digest exact bytes of Cargo.toml, optional build.rs, and every regular file recursively under src/ and wit/. Every production include_bytes/include_str input outside those roots is an explicit asset record. Executor Cargo.toml/src are explicit composition records. Reject symlinks, non-UTF8/absolute/parent-traversing paths, missing roots/files, duplicates, unlisted include assets, and noncanonical git revisions.

Manifest ownership and generation

A conformance tool/test regenerates the closure from package-scoped locked/offline wamn-executor resolution (cargo tree or an equivalent temporary metadata root, never full-workspace unified metadata), projects it to the wamn-execution-host dependency subgraph, adds executor composition inputs, and byte-compares it with the checked-in manifest. Dependency, feature, source, checksum, local-root, or include-asset drift fails until intentionally updated. build.rs never launches nested Cargo.

One crates/execution/host/build.rs plus a pure helper reads the checked-in manifest and local files, emits cargo:rerun-if-changed for every input/root, computes the revision, and exposes one non-overridable wamn_execution_host::EFFECT_PROVIDER_REVISION constant. Executor and management/scenario-worker already depend on that crate and must use the same constant; request/env/CLI input is forbidden. Runtime never recomputes from source. Executor carries the constant through trusted host context; .2.3/run-state claim preflight compares every reachable plan to it before any component invocation.

Exact preimage and literal

Frame the domain wamn.effect-provider-revision.v1 followed by records byte-sorted by normalized UTF-8 tag/path. Frame every tag and value independently as u64 big-endian length followed by exact bytes, matching the existing catalog identity convention. Source bytes receive no newline/text normalization; external record fields are independently tagged/framed and feature names byte-sorted. Output is exactly lowercase sha256: plus 64 lowercase hex and reuses the catalog parser/type.

Change policy

Any local manifest/source/WIT/build/include-asset byte or path-set change, external locked package version/source/checksum/feature change, fork URL/revision/feature change, or executor composition change mints a new revision. Tests/examples/docs outside the governed roots, runtime config/data/credentials, and scheduler lifecycle changes do not. An allegedly non-semantic governed change still mints. Narrowing the closure requires a separately ratified v2 manifest, not an exception. Algorithm/framing/input-set changes increment the domain version and are runtime-revision changes. Per the charter, change requires revalidate/retest/republish of every active release and old-worker drain before removal; no side-by-side runtime revisions in MVP.

Named proofs

- effect_provider_revision_golden_preimage_and_literal
- effect_provider_revision_is_checkout_path_and_discovery_order_independent
- effect_provider_revision_rejects_noncanonical_manifest_entries
- locked_effect_provider_closure_matches_manifest
- each_local_closure_root_add_remove_rename_and_byte_mutant_changes_revision
- external_checksum_source_rev_and_feature_mutants_change_revision
- fork_rev_and_feature_mutants_change_revision
- out_of_scope_scheduler_test_doc_and_runtime_config_mutants_do_not_change_revision
- management_and_executor_embed_identical_revision
- foreign_effect_provider_revision_refuses_before_guest, with a zero-entry invocation sentinel, under .2.3

Alternatives

Hashing the final run-worker ELF gives physical identity but creates self-embedding/sidecar problems and churns on unrelated compiler/linker/lifecycle changes. OCI digest adds base-image/CA/publication churn, duplicates flowrunner identity, and creates publication bootstrap circularity. A hand-picked plugin-file list lowers churn but silently misses helper/dependency behavior and is rejected unless runtime is first split into a dedicated provider crate. Rooting at the whole executor dependency closure is exhaustive but unnecessarily includes scheduler/lifecycle. The recommended locked host closure plus explicit executor composition is the minimum defensible closed semantic set. If the owner interprets exact executable as physical bytes instead of the charter's semantic provider revision, choose ELF/OCI instead.
acceptance_criteria: Owner ratifies the exact digest input set, byte framing and ordering, output literal, generation and runtime verification owners, change and revalidation policy, and named deterministic and mutation proofs; the approved contract is copied into wamn-0h0g.2.2 acceptance before claim.
close_reason: Owner ratified the recommended semantic provider-revision contract; the exact contract is now the acceptance for wamn-0h0g.2.2.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(flow-engine): runtime call-depth + dispatch budgets
description:
Recursion and loops are supported; termination is runtime-enforced: a MAXIMUM CALL DEPTH per root run and a TOTAL-DISPATCHED-NODE budget; exhaustion is a typed failure (`depth-budget` / `dispatch-budget`) failing the run.

Re-scope the existing dispatch budget (flow-engine `Plan`, `DEFAULT_DISPATCH_BUDGET = 10_000`, today per-invocation → `runaway-budget`) to the ROOT RUN across all frames, and add the missing call-depth ceiling. Exhaustion surfaces through the NB3 `fail_kind` literals and `get-run`. The owner picks the two budget values as named literals in this bead.

No static termination analysis ships in MVP (claim performs static call-graph reachability only, NB4; the future analysis is held at NB14). The proofs — budget-exhaustion typed failures and a recursion case terminating by budget — ride 3.7.
design: OWNER RULING 2026-08-14: MAX_CALL_DEPTH is the platform constant 64. Root depth is 0; exactly 64 active callees are admitted; the 65th call refuses before frame-id allocation as typed depth-budget attributed to that call-site node occurrence in the caller frame. DEFAULT_ROOT_DISPATCH_BUDGET is the platform constant 10_000. One root-owned counter is debited exactly once for every emitted Step::Dispatch across every frame, including ordinary loop re-dispatches and call-flow steps; there are no effect retries under .13.2. Exactly 10_000 dispatches execute and attempted dispatch 10_001 fails typed dispatch-budget. Ordering is dispatch debit, call-enter input guard, depth check, then frame-id allocation/push. Budget failures are terminal run failures, visible in caller outcome and get-run, and never routable through a call-site error edge. Both constants remain non-configurable until a separate per-environment demand gate. This issue closes mechanism and typed mapping; production/get-run proof rides .5.4, with .3.7 after .5.4.
acceptance_criteria: MAX_CALL_DEPTH = 64 and DEFAULT_ROOT_DISPATCH_BUDGET = 10_000 are documented named platform constants. Root depth 0 admits 64 active callees; the 65th valid call refuses before frame-id allocation with typed depth-budget attributed to the caller call-site occurrence. One checked root counter debits every emitted Step::Dispatch across all frames, including ordinary loop re-dispatches and call-flow; exactly 10_000 execute and attempt 10_001 fails typed dispatch-budget. Debit precedes input guard, which precedes depth check. Both failures bypass call-site error routing, terminalize the root, preserve exact typed mapping to FailKind, and are visible in the caller outcome. Owner-local deterministic tests and restored mutants pin depth pre-allocation, dispatch off-by-one/globality, accounting order, and non-catchability. Guest activation and production/get-run proof remain exclusively .5.4; .3.7 runs after .5.4.

Implemented by e9225d79c0fdda33f57da74d822503e136aa6f97: MAX_CALL_DEPTH=64, DEFAULT_ROOT_DISPATCH_BUDGET=10_000, checked root-global Step::Dispatch accounting, debit then input guard then depth ordering, pre-allocation depth refusal, exact frame/node/occurrence attribution, non-catchable nested budget propagation, and exact FailKind mapping. title: [SR-MVP] feat(catalog): reduce ExecutionPlanV2 to own-flow structure + byte identity
description:
Successor to closed wamn-0h0g.2.1 and wamn-0h0g.2.6 for amendment-contradicted plan-model parts. catalog.execution_bundles remains immutable, append-only, and byte-for-byte unchanged.

Freeze the own-flow ExecutionPlanV2 wire ratified by wamn-0h0g.13.28. Header is format-version 0.1, plan-compiler-revision 0.1, ExecutionRuntimeRevision, and root-artifact-hash. Body has mandatory entry-instruction, nodes, edges, root-terminal-behavior, entry-input-schema-guard, callable-contract, and source-map. ExecutionNodeId is a transparent lowercase-slug JSON string scalar. A call-flow is a specialized ordinary node whose exact config is {site, flow-id}; it is effectful, has no connection requirement, and stores no callee identity.

Delete SyntheticInstruction/CallEnter/CallReturn, ExecutionPlanBody.synthetic_instructions, ReturnContinuation, CallFrameMetadata, per-node/source-map artifact hashes, multi-segment ExecutionNodePath and its schema/tests, and path-keyed input guard collections. Source map retains local-node-id plus source-node-id only.

Callable-contract is required as null or the fixed MVP 0.1 object; input-schema-hash is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 bytes of the mandatory own-entry guard. The plan identity is SHA-256 over exact stored bytes. Readers hash-compare untouched bytes before parse, then structurally and semantically validate without normalization or reserialization. Plan readers stop using NonCanonicalJson; the unrelated CanonicalJson parser retains that variant.

This issue owns the public plan types, validation, reader/hash boundary, old-shape deletion, and wire-focused proofs. It does not own semantic-flow compilation or deterministic compiler emission; wamn-0h0g.3.2 owns normalization, emitted golden bytes/hashes, and cross-process rebuild equality.
acceptance_criteria:
ExecutionPlanV2 carries exactly the ratified own-flow wire: header format-version "0.1", plan-compiler-revision "0.1", ExecutionRuntimeRevision and root-artifact-hash; mandatory body entry-instruction, nodes, edges, root-terminal-behavior, entry-input-schema-guard, callable-contract and source-map.

ExecutionNodeId is a transparent scalar string enforcing ^[a-z0-9-]+$ everywhere formerly using ExecutionNodePath. No path arrays, segments, aliases, callee hashes, synthetic instructions, continuations, frame metadata, per-node artifact hashes, or path-keyed guard collections remain. Respond termination uses responders. Source map bijectively covers nodes with local-node-id and source-node-id only.

Call-flow is an ordinary specialized node with exact {site, flow-id} config, site equal to local-node-id, effectful policy, no connection requirement, and no second instruction collection. The mandatory entry guard is the validated Draft 2020-12 JSON Schema or boolean true for unconstrained event/cron entry. callable-contract is always encoded as null or the fixed version "0.1", return "untyped-json-body", ceiling "effectful" object; its lowercase input-schema-hash equals SHA-256 of RFC 8785 guard bytes and callability is intrinsic.

Every reader validates and compares SHA-256 over untouched exact bytes before parse, then performs strict structural/semantic validation. It never normalizes, reserializes, or rejects matching-hash valid JSON merely for whitespace/key order. Plan code does not produce NonCanonicalJson; unrelated CanonicalJson behavior remains.

Named proofs here cover scalar node-id/old-path residue, hash-before-parse, matching-hash noncanonical JSON acceptance, semantic-invalid rejection after hash success, callable guard/hash consistency, removed-plan-shape absence, and unchanged catalog.execution_bundles DDL. Compiler normalization, exact emitted golden bytes/hashes, and cross-process deterministic rebuild are excluded and owned exclusively by wamn-0h0g.3.2.

It builds the ratified own-flow wire from the already validated flow, serializes once with serde_json::to_vec, and hashes those exact bytes. It performs no collection sorting, normalization, golden-byte pinning, or cross-process determinism proof; .3.2 replaces it with the permanent deterministic compiler. Transitional callable eligibility follows the existing flow semantics: fail paths are unsuccessful; cycles are allowed when they can reach respond/fail; only request flows whose successful paths reach respond and whose boundary responders have zero outgoing edges receive CallableContract, while other plans encode null.
IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE (2026-08-11): Own-flow wire, scalar node identity, exact-byte hash-before-parse reader, semantic validation, transitional scenario producer, flowrunner reader, and byte-pinned unchanged execution_bundles DDL are complete. Debug tests passed for wamn-catalog, wamn-schema-control, wamn-scenario-worker, and flowrunner; root strict all-target Clippy, wasm dead-code-exempt strict Clippy, rustfmt, and diff checks passed. Six focused mutants (hash comparison, canonical reserialization rejection, semantic-validation bypass, call-flow effect predicate, callable guard hash equality, and execution_bundles 0.1-to-0.2 drift) were each killed and restored with exact file-hash checks.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(plan): re-freeze ExecutionPlanV2 durable encoding under byte identity
description:
Supersedes the CODEC half of closed wamn-0h0g.2.8; its SQL/ACL half — the catalog.execution_bundles column set, hash/byte-length CHECKs, forced RLS, immutability trigger, grants, and the global recovery-representation deletion boundary — stays ratified and citable.

The amendment rules: "Identity is byte identity — hash the data — and the compiler is a function." The plan is the exact bytes the validator emitted; `execution_bundle_hash = sha256(exact bytes)`; no canonicalization layer, no preimage specification; readers verify by hash compare only (the landed `from_canonical_bytes()`/`NonCanonicalJson` re-canonicalization path deletes). Deterministic encoding becomes a contract of the plan compiler: same plan format version + same `plan_compiler_revision` + same semantic inputs = exactly the same bytes — sorted collections, no serializer-dependent ordering, golden byte vectors, one cross-process deterministic-rebuild test.

This decision must fix:
1. The `plan_compiler_revision` literal format and bump policy — a compiler or serializer change is a named revision requiring revalidation, never silent drift (a second named revalidation trigger beside 2.7's execution-runtime rule).
2. The exact statement of the deterministic-encoding compiler contract and where its three named proofs live (owner-local under epic A; NOT a 17th blocking check — the 16-check count stands).
3. Whether `exact_bytes` gains a `jsonb` projection for querying ("cast to jsonb where querying wants structure; the exact bytes remain the sole identity source").
4. Confirmation that RFC 8785-style emission may remain the compiler's internal serialization strategy, but is no longer a reader-enforced preimage.

Discipline per 2.8: approved literals copy into the implementing bead's (NB2) acceptance before it is claimed.
acceptance_criteria: Owner-ratified answers recorded for all four questions (plan_compiler_revision literal + bump policy; deterministic-encoding contract + proof homes; jsonb projection; RFC 8785 as internal strategy only); approved literals copied into the implementing bead's acceptance before it is claimed; 2.8's surviving SQL/ACL half explicitly re-cited.
notes: OWNER RULING (2026-08-11): ratified textual plan_compiler_revision 0.1 under the MVP version pin; output-affecting compiler or serializer changes rerun the three owner-local determinism proofs and, once the pin lifts, require a named revision change plus revalidation/retest/republication. No persisted jsonb projection. RFC 8785 may remain an internal emitter only; readers hash exact stored bytes without recanonicalization. Exact contract copied into wamn-0h0g.2.10 acceptance.
close_reason: Owner ratified the exact plan-compiler revision, deterministic proof homes, query-time-only jsonb projection, and internal-emitter-only RFC 8785 policy; copied into wamn-0h0g.2.10 acceptance.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(test-set): freeze four assertion wire shapes
description:
## Decision
Freeze the exact 0.1 TestSet assertion tags, JSON shapes, comparison rules, failure literals, and legacy-deletion ownership required before wamn-0h0g.8.2 can replace the current open assertion enum.

## Recommended contract
Use a deny-unknown externally tagged enum with these exact shapes: {"run-terminal-outcome":{"status":<terminal run status>}}; {"terminal-respond":{"status":<100..599>,"body":<JSON>}}; {"typed-flow-failure":{"kind":<FailKind>}}; and {"named-node-terminal":{"path":<ExecutionNodePath JSON array>,"status":"success"}} or {"named-node-terminal":{"path":<ExecutionNodePath JSON array>,"status":"error","failure-kind":<NodeErrorKind>}}. Run terminal status is completed, failed, infrastructure-failure, or effect-uncertain. Flow failure kind is terminal, retry-exhausted, invalid-input, runaway-budget, or effect-uncertain. Node failure kind is retryable, rate-limited, terminal, or invalid-input; cancelled is excluded from the MVP assertion contract. Terminal response requires both fields and compares parsed JSON bodies by exact deep equality; headers and output/subset/path matching remain absent. Missing facts fail. Named-node evaluation requires at least one matching path and every observed occurrence to match; success forbids failure-kind and error requires it. wamn-0h0g.8.2 owns the model/parser/pure evaluator plus deletion or adaptation of every direct legacy assertion consumer and assertion-only DB/egress capture code; wamn-0h0g.8.4 and .8.5 own durable fact acquisition/reporting, while .8.10 and .8.11 retain whole stored-suite/protocol deletion.

## Alternatives considered
Optional failure-kind on an error assertion weakens the typed claim. Reusing Equals/Subset for response bodies would retain the deleted output-matching surface. Deferring direct legacy consumers would leave two live assertion vocabularies.

The approved wire contract is copied into wamn-0h0g.8.2 acceptance before that issue is claimed; no implementation occurs in this decision issue.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(plan): freeze ExecutionPlanV2 durable encoding
description:
## Decision
Freeze the exact durable contract that wamn-0h0g.2.1 will hash and store: Rust/serde shape, collection ordering, canonical byte codec, format-version literal, hash spelling, SQL column/check/immutability/RLS contract, and the ownership boundary for deleting the recovery-shaped executable types.

## Recommended contract
Ship textual format version 0.1. Exact bytes are RFC 8785 canonical UTF-8 JSON of the single ExecutionPlanV2 object; object keys follow RFC 8785, semantically ordered sequences preserve their explicit order, and every otherwise unordered collection is normalized by a named stable key before serialization. The identity is sha256:<64 lowercase hex> over exact_bytes. catalog.execution_bundles uses tenant_id text, execution_bundle_hash text, format_version text, exact_bytes bytea, byte_length int, and created_at timestamptz; it pins format 0.1, byte_length = octet_length(exact_bytes), hash equality, composite tenant/hash identity, forced tenant RLS, and UPDATE/DELETE immutability, with author INSERT/SELECT and runtime SELECT only. wamn-0h0g.2.1 deletes ExecutableRecoveryContract, OccurrenceRecoverySelection, connection-recovery declarations, and their compatibility readers globally in the same atomic change; wamn-0h0g.4.3 is narrowed to any remaining run-state recovery residue.

## Alternatives considered
A tagged binary frame would also be deterministic but would add a second codec beside the repository RFC 8785 precedent. Leaving shared recovery types for wamn-0h0g.4.3 would preserve a second executable description after the new plan becomes authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: The owner either ratifies the recommended contract verbatim or supplies exact replacements for the codec/order/hash/storage/privilege and recovery-deletion choices. The approved literals and ownership boundary are copied into wamn-0h0g.2.1 acceptance before that issue is claimed; no implementation occurs in this decision issue.
notes: AMENDMENT NOTE (2026-08-11): the codec half of this ratification (RFC 8785 canonical bytes as the identity preimage) is superseded by the amendment's byte-identity ruling — successor decision 2.9 (plan_compiler_revision + deterministic-encoding compiler contract). The SQL/ACL half (execution_bundles contract, global recovery-representation deletion boundary) stands ratified and citable.
close_reason: Owner ratified the recommended ExecutionPlanV2 durable encoding, SQL/ACL contract, and global recovery-representation deletion boundary verbatim on 2026-08-11; exact contract copied into wamn-0h0g.2.1 acceptance.

title: [SR-MVP] decision: carry effective run capture mode
description:
## Decision
At the natural admission-integration point, choose the single canonical carrier for the effective full or off run capture setting after the authored Flow.capture field is deleted.

## Rationale
Asynchronous execution must receive the admitted setting exactly once without adding product configuration, duplicate state, compatibility readers, or more capture modes.

## Alternatives Considered
Persist full or off on the run row; carry it in an existing immutable admission envelope; or derive it from the admitted operation where that remains unambiguous. The owner will select the smallest boundary supported by the settled admission API.
design: RATIFIED 2026-08-12: The sole carrier is wamn_run.runs.capture_mode with exact DDL text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'off' CHECK (capture_mode IN ('full','off')). The existing wamn-run-state admission transaction writes it once and asynchronous execution reads it. A cross-column constraint permits full only for the canonical draft source; published HTTP/event and every test-set admission are off. Non-draft admission paths do not accept a mode. The draft-run operation schema fills an omitted value as full, while the storage default stays off so admission bugs fail closed. The runs admission-pin immutability trigger protects capture_mode and rejects post-admission mutation. There is no invocation_context field, derivation, contract change, duplicate carrier, compatibility path, or identity/version change. The generated protected-write evidence for wamn_run.runs must retain run-state ownership and show admission insertion plus the trigger guard that makes capture_mode non-writable by author SQL.
acceptance_criteria: The owner-ratified sole carrier is wamn_run.runs.capture_mode text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'off' with a full|off CHECK, written exactly once by the wamn-run-state admission transaction and read by asynchronous execution. A test-pinned cross-column constraint permits full only on the canonical draft source; published HTTP/event and all test-set paths are off and non-draft admission paths accept no mode. Draft-run omission is schema-filled to full at the operation boundary while the column defaults off. The existing runs admission-pin immutability trigger protects capture_mode. No invocation_context entry, derivation, authored per-flow field, duplicate carrier, compatibility reader, new contract, or new identity/version is introduced. wamn-0h0g.8.3 acceptance records this exact boundary before implementation.
close_reason: Owner ratified runs.capture_mode as the sole fail-closed admission-written carrier; decision and downstream acceptance updated, with authoritative PLAN fold-back.

DO NOT DISPATCH 12.6 WHOLE.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(management): sequential case execution against the candidate wiring
description: Execute a report's cases sequentially from the control-plane reservation through idempotent admission and ordinary execution against the candidate wiring version, using the report's pinned catalog version, the candidate override, and the stable report-id plus ordinal producer key. Cases come from the draft's cases array. The pinned world is the candidate wiring row plus the environment's bound requirements, not a scratch manifest ConfigMap or per-report Job — the gate's latency is a product requirement. Deadline, hop-limit and dispatch-budget terminal results finalize as failed cases and never enter operator machinery; effect-uncertain leaves this vocabulary with the shelved durable tier. Each ordinal is admitted at most once and reconciled back to the control report, including crash after commit; asserted result facts are copied into the immutable control report.
design: SUPERSEDING IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN: execute candidate cases through the single production router driver owned by wamn-0h0g.16.24 via one bounded internal candidate-wiring seam. Preserve sequential ordinal reservation and immutable control-report reconciliation, but delete the scratch candidate-manifest ConfigMap, per-report Job, execution_target placement shim, and old candidate-mount machinery. Success and every typed terminal outcome are copied into the immutable control report. Crash-after-project-commit remains reconcilable. No scratch ConfigMap, per-report Job, candidate mount, flowrunner path, or second driver remains.
notes:
2026-08-23 correction after focused review: the first direct in-process draft is rejected and will not integrate because it bypasses the ratified .8.20 project admission receipt and rereads mutable environment bindings. Split implementation into .8.5.1 candidate admission/binding-world freeze, .8.5.2 ordinary queue/RouterDriver candidate execution, and .8.5.3 sequential cross-plane observation/reconciliation. Existing .19.15 is the only decision blocker for queued Respond.
*** HALTED BY OWNER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-25. NO FURTHER COMPOSITION HARDENING ON ANY 8.5.x CHILD. ***
Authoring collapses to the stateless-gate model: gate(document) -> immutable report keyed by wiring-hash, plus publish(document, report-id). A draft is a client-side file, not server state.
PENDING A ONE-DAY DEMOLITION SPEC WHICH THE OWNER RATIFIES. On approval this is a PHASE-A-STYLE DELETION WAVE, NOT A REFACTOR.
*** THE TRANSITIONAL-HARDENING BAN APPLIES NOW, BEFORE RATIFICATION: NO NEW FIELDS, GRANTS OR GATES ON ANY SURFACE THE SPEC WOULD DELETE. ***

CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED, NOT DONE - AND THE DISTINCTION IS DELIBERATE. Owner ruling 2026-08-25: this closes once lane 68a lands wamn-0h0g.8.5.6, which it has (dac865db).

*** ITS SPECIFICATION WAS REFUTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED AS WRITTEN. *** Almost every mechanism this bead names was DELETED by the stateless-gate collapse under the owner's effect-free ruling:
- execute cases from the CONTROL-PLANE RESERVATION - wamn_run.authoring_test_run_reservations is dropped.
- the STABLE REPORT-ID PLUS ORDINAL PRODUCER KEY - the ordinal producer key is gone; the report id is now the wiring hash.
- CASES COME FROM THE DRAFT'S CASES ARRAY - draft persistence is dropped; catalog.flow_drafts and the SaveDraft, ReadDraft, ValidateDraft and DraftRun operations are all deleted.
- EACH ORDINAL ADMITTED AT MOST ONCE AND RECONCILED BACK, INCLUDING CRASH AFTER COMMIT, and the design note's PRESERVE SEQUENTIAL ORDINAL RESERVATION - that IS the resumption protocol, and section 5.1's ratified effect-free clause deleted the thing it was remembering. Effect-free cases make re-execution free, so per-case durable progress is not worth remembering.
Closing this DONE would record a protocol that does not exist as shipped.

WHAT THE CAPABILITY ACTUALLY BECAME, and it is delivered:
- the gate verb executes candidate cases through the surviving admission path - services/scenario-worker/src/store/admission.rs:367 run_gate, called from management.rs:873.
- cases are EFFECT-FREE BY CONTRACT, enforced at admission.rs:394 before any acceptance, with the refusal GateRefusal::EffectfulComponentReached. Verified live by the integrator: neutering it ADMITS an effectful candidate instead of refusing.
- the result is an IMMUTABLE REPORT KEYED BY wiring_hash at wamn_run.gate_reports, written inside the same transaction as the attribution ledger row and readable through get-report. That is this bead's surviving essence - immutable control-report reconciliation - re-derived on hash identity rather than on reservation-and-ordinal.
Delivered by wamn-0h0g.8.5.5 (five commits, ending dc1fb111) and wamn-0h0g.8.5.6 (dac865db). Both closed with full evidence.

TRACKER NOTE: this bead has NO tracker children - .8.5.5 and .8.5.6 are siblings by naming convention only, so no edge is orphaned by this close.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(wire): authoring contract 0.2
description: Atomic: SuiteRun -> TestSetRun; SuiteProjection removed; refusal literals renamed; public JSON schema regenerated; per-operation idempotency, read authorization, size limits, response types, and typed refusals enumerated; reads are query endpoints outside the command ledger; Grant/RevokeDraftSafeGeneration delete (bootstrap seeds the one draft-safe sandbox generation; validate/draft-run enforce it; publish never mutates it); 0.1 refused; the ftfc.14 reference CLI regenerates. design:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-15 — EIGHT-OPERATION AUTHORING SURFACE, FINAL

Five operations are commands: save-flow-draft, validate, draft-run, test-set-run, and publish. They carry command-id as correlation plus exact-retry ledger identity. Three operations are queries: read-draft, get-run, and get-report.

The query request envelope is exactly { schema-version, query-id, query }. Its response echoes both schema-version and query-id around an operation-specific success or typed refusal. query-id is length-bounded by a named public constant chosen and pinned by the implementation, is correlation-only, and never represents idempotency or retry identity. This is structural: query dispatch cannot call command-ledger storage, writes no durable row, and no query-log relation exists. Correlation appears only in traces.

Success and refusal types are operation-specific. Numeric count and size limits become named public constants with boundary proofs. GrantDraftSafeGeneration and RevokeDraftSafeGeneration delete through public models, handlers, dispatch, audit-command vocabulary, contracts, clients, and management mutation authority.

The bootstrap representation remains catalog.draft_safe_connection_grants. Provisioning seeds the sole sandbox generation; management receives read-only enforcement access; validate and draft-run require membership; publish never mutates it. The non-table representation is rejected. No public-wire hold remains.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(run-state): operator terminalize + operator_run_actions
description: One documented run-state transaction: lock run/node/attempt/queue -> verify effect-uncertain -> append one immutable operator_run_actions row (basis, non-empty evidence reference, correlation, prior state) -> mark node and run terminally failed -> fence queue eligibility -> commit. principal derives from session_user, labeled honestly as role attribution. No success assertion; no bulk selection. The F.2 effect-disposition breadth (writer-less requests/outcomes tables) deletes here. Outcome: crash floor.
design:
OWNER-RATIFIED OPERATOR TERMINALIZATION — 2026-08-15

The operation targets one (tenant, run) and never accepts or infers an attempt. Attempt and node identifiers are locked evidence only. Candidate node selection uses an exact framed-occurrence join to effect_attempts and never latest-row or ordering heuristics. The present sequential frontier permits zero or one linked started node; multiple is an invariant refusal. The transaction must be revisited before any parallel scheduler activates.

operator_run_actions is an append-only audit relation with server identity, tenant/run and tenant/correlation uniqueness, exact action/basis/principal/prior-state literals, non-empty opaque evidence/correlation, optional all-or-none prior node state, immutable timestamp, forced tenant RLS, and no cascading FK to prunable history. Identical retry is verified; divergent reuse refuses.

A present candidate becomes status error with error_kind terminal, ended_at set by the server, and fixed non-routable effect-uncertain/operator-terminalized detail. The run becomes failed while retaining the effect-uncertain failure classification and fixed terminal reason. Caller and effect-ledger columns are absent from UPDATE sets.

The public boundary is one contextual Rust adapter translated once at wamn-ctl terminalize-effect-uncertain. It derives principal from session_user and uses project-admin credentials. Internal storage errors do not create another product taxonomy.

The legacy pair is the actual project-run pair wamn_run.effect_disposition_requests and child wamn_run.effect_dispositions; no catalog relation belongs to this teardown. Empty-only removal is atomic. Populated history cannot truthfully map because the retired model allowed bulk and success assertions, so it refuses with SQLSTATE 55000 and requires ops archive plus reprovision.
acceptance_criteria:
wamn-ctl terminalize-effect-uncertain is the sole MVP operator mutation surface. It accepts exactly one tenant and run plus one basis, non-empty evidence reference, and non-empty correlation id under a project-admin database credential. It accepts no attempt id, node id, outcome, success assertion, continuation, or bulk selector. PostgreSQL session_user supplies principal and principal_kind is database-role; caller-supplied attribution is impossible.

In one tenant-scoped transaction, lock the run, node facts, immutable effect-attempt facts, and queue fact; classify an identical retry before attempting a second mutation; require runs.status = effect-uncertain, at least one immutable effect attempt, and no queue row. Never infer one uncertain attempt. Under the current sequential frontier, the eligible outstanding node is a node_runs.status = started row joined to an effect attempt by exact tenant/run/frame/local-node/occurrence. Zero or one is valid; more than one returns run-state-invariant. If present, terminalize that projection as non-routable error/terminal. If absent, terminalize the run without manufacturing a node fact. Any future parallel scheduler must reopen this cardinality contract before activation.

Append exactly one immutable operator_run_actions row, then set the run to failed while preserving fail_kind = effect-uncertain and using terminal reason operator-terminalized-effect-uncertain. Preserve caller outcome fields and hashes byte-for-byte, every effect attempt/dispatch/outcome fact, admitted input, execution state, result, and capture evidence. Never write an effect outcome, assert success, redispatch, continue, enqueue, create a successor, or leave a queue row.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(flowrunner): frame-keyed facts + source map
description: One author-visible fact for the call-flow node itself; callee node facts are ordinary facts keyed by frame — (run_id, frame_id, local_node_id, occurrence), schema owned by 4.13 — and each plan carries its own source map to original identifiers (2.10). The author-facing assertion selector is (flow_id, node_id): every observed frame and occurrence of the pair must match (8.16/8.17); call-site-specific selectors are a future addition (13.19). Outcome: flow composition.
design:
OWNER-RATIFIED FACT BOUNDARY — 2026-08-15

This issue owns the complete trusted in-memory frame-to-node-fact stream inside the frame interpreter. The fallible stream is the sole constructor of run_id, root_plan_hash, frame_id, parent_frame_id, call_site_id, current_plan_hash, local_node_id, occurrence, and one root-run-global monotonic sequence for each observed node occurrence. All frame, plan, and source facts derive from the immutable VerifiedResolutionSnapshot and active FrameStack; no guest or caller field is authoritative.

Each completed ordinary or reserved occurrence emits one terminal success or error observation. A call-flow occurrence emits exactly one author-visible fact in its caller frame after callee return or failure conversion; ordinary callee facts remain keyed to their callee frames. Routed and unhandled NodeError outcomes preserve the frozen taxonomy. The .3.8 depth and dispatch budget failures retain non-routable run-failure semantics.

Capture follows .8.3. Source identity resolves only through the active verified plan and its source map: durable identity remains current_plan_hash plus local_node_id, while the author selector is derived (flow_id, node_id). Sink refusal fails closed and is never treated as recorded success.

This issue adds no SQL, database credential, WIT writer, Guest::run activation, effect-writer call, external dispatch, run_frames relation, or durable ancestry. .5.4 owns production consumption and .12.43 owns node_runs persistence authority.
acceptance_criteria:
The frame interpreter exposes one fallible trusted fact stream covering every completed root and callee node occurrence. Each fact carries run identity, root plan hash, the exact .4.13 frame key and ancestry, current verified plan/local-node identity, occurrence, and one strictly monotonic root-global sequence; sibling, nested, self-recursive, and mutual-recursive executions cannot collide.

Exactly one caller-frame call-flow fact is observed per call occurrence after callee return or failure conversion. Callee node facts retain callee frame/current-plan identity. Call-enter invalid input and converted callee failure are attributed to the caller call site. Nested respond remains body-only and never becomes a root release. Success and NodeError terminal outcomes remain exact without widening the frozen error vocabulary. .3.8 depth and dispatch budget failures remain non-routable run failures.

Full/off capture matches .8.3, including scrub-before-write, ceiling, size/hash, and zero node input/output under off. Author-facing (flow_id, node_id) is derived from the verified resolution and the active plan source map; no caller-supplied source identity or reader-side normalization participates. Sink refusal fails closed.

Named deterministic tests and restored mutants prove root-global sequencing, exact call-site cardinality, callee attribution, routed and unhandled errors, nested response isolation, recursion, capture full/off, source-map derivation, sink-refusal fail-close, and zero Guest, SQL, writer, or effect activation. Guest::run remains hard-refused and no production database write occurs in this issue.
notes: OWNER RULING 2026-08-15: .3.5 is atomic at the trusted in-memory fact-stream boundary. .5.4 is its first production consumer and .12.43 exclusively owns node_runs persistence authority. Therefore .3.5 has no hard dependency on .12.43 and is executable while Guest::run remains fail-closed.

Verified 24/24 flowrunner tests, native and wasm32-wasip2 strict Clippy/checks, six killed/restored mutants, rustfmt/bash/diff gates.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(flowrunner): frame-stack call execution
description: The flowrunner keeps an in-memory frame stack (engine frame machinery per 13.17 — not a registry node). At a call-flow instruction: look up the callee plan in the run's snapshot (4.12/5.13) -> run the call-enter guard (3.3) -> push and execute -> the callee's terminal respond BODY becomes the site's main output on frame pop (landed child_outcome adapter semantics); a nested respond never releases the root HTTP caller; an unhandled callee failure is a normal node error following ERROR_PORT. Body-only return; the status hint does not propagate (deferral 13.5). Self- and mutual recursion are ordinary calls, bounded by the runtime budgets (3.8). Frame record: frame_id (root-run-local, monotonic) · parent_frame_id · call_site_id · current_plan_hash. Single-shot untouched: one root run, one claim; frames are memory; every write-ahead intent is a root-run intent; a call-flow site writes no effect attempt (13.15). Outcome: flow composition.
acceptance_criteria:
The flowrunner maintains the authoritative frame stack only in memory. Each frame has root-run-local monotonic frame_id, parent_frame_id, call_site_id, and current_plan_hash; the root and every callee derive from verified plans in the immutable run resolution snapshot.

Call-enter validates callee input, push/execute/pop returns only the response body, nested response never releases the root caller, and unhandled callee failure follows ERROR_PORT. Self and mutual recursion are ordinary calls bounded by root-run budgets.

The stack exposes exact trusted current-frame identity, plan, source, and immediate-parent facts consumed by .5.4. A call-flow site creates no effect attempt. This issue neither invokes the .4.9 writer nor dispatches an external effect.

No durable run_frames registry, caller-supplied frame authority, reconstructed frame history, or fabricated ancestry exists. Named push/pop, nesting, failure-conversion, and recursion proofs pin the boundary.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(run-state): pin execution_bundle_hash at admission
description: Every admitted run pins a non-null runs.execution_bundle_hash (the root plan hash — the run identity and anchor) AND a mandatory immutable catalog_id + catalog_version (nullable today — run-state.sql:179-180,227): claim-time resolution walks the run's pinned release, so activating a later catalog release affects later admissions, never an admitted or queued run. Admission refuses a missing root plan (presence/FK); byte verification for the root and every reachable callee runs at claim (4.12). Outcome: crash floor.
acceptance_criteria:
OWNER-RATIFIED CONTRACT (2026-08-11)

Authoritative root-plan source

- Published HTTP/event/release-scenario admission derives the root hash only from catalog.release_flows.execution_bundle_hash.
- Draft/test candidate admission derives it only from catalog.validated_flow_drafts.execution_bundle_hash.
- Callers, manifest JSON, invocation_context, and release_flow_test_evidence never supply or override runtime authority.

Exact catalog.release_flows addition

execution_bundle_hash text NOT NULL with lowercase sha256 check; tenant-scoped FK (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash) to catalog.execution_bundles; index (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash). Keep the existing release-flow primary key. insert_release_flow_sql gains the hash. Copying a conforming release copies the stored hash. A legacy publish path unable to provide a validated plan returns missing-root-plan without inserting a member; .8.7 still owns the successful gated publication transaction and release-flow test evidence.

Exact runs contract

- catalog_id text NOT NULL CHECK nonempty.
- catalog_version int NOT NULL CHECK > 0 (replace current bigint so it matches catalog keys).
- environment text NOT NULL CHECK nonempty.
- execution_bundle_hash text NOT NULL with exact lowercase sha256 check.
- Immediate NO ACTION FK (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version) to catalog.release_manifests.
- Immediate NO ACTION FK (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash) to catalog.execution_bundles.
- Indexes runs_release (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version) and runs_execution_bundle (tenant_id, execution_bundle_hash).
- Remove the obsolete nullable-pair check.
- BEFORE UPDATE OF all four pins raises SQLSTATE 55000, run-admission-pin-immutable, when any changes.

Greenfield migration policy

Use one atomic schema-control/ctl cutover under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on release_flows and the selected runs table. If either target lacks the contract and either table contains rows, abort before DDL with SQLSTATE 55000 and execution-pin-cutover-requires-empty-run-and-release-membership. Never infer a plan from artifact identity, JSON, or a sole matching draft, and never rewrite history. Empty pre-plan databases receive columns, types/nullability, checks, FKs, indexes, and trigger atomically. Pre-plan installations must be re-provisioned. Schema-control observes types, nullability, FKs, indexes, and trigger, not only column names.

All admission writers/readback

Update shared HTTP/event admission, release-scenario admission, and draft/test candidate admission plus runtime/materializer/scenario-worker bindings. Release admission selects the release member hash and joins execution_bundles; draft admission joins execution_bundles. Every INSERT INTO runs writes the selected hash. Duplicate identity comparisons include it. Duplicate/recovery paths return the already-admitted row without rebinding to a newer head. Repoint the transitional flowrunner reader to runs.execution_bundle_hash. Do not expand dead open-run, child, replay, or raw write-ahead builders into alternate admission paths; the new constraints leave them fail-closed until their deletion owners remove them.

Missing-plan ownership

.2.4 owns the non-durable typed admission refusal missing-root-plan before any runs, run_queue, or invocation_admissions mutation. It proves presence and tenant-scoped FK identity only. .4.12 retains parsing/exact-byte verification, reachable-set resolution, runtime-revision checks, hash-invalid-bytes, and durable claim terminalization.

Remove the JSON duplicate atomically

Remove principal.execution-bundle-hash from draft invocation_context in the same commit after repointing the sole flowrunner reader. Do not add it to AdmittedPrincipal. Add a residue guard forbidding execution-bundle-hash in invocation-context construction/read paths.

Proof contract

Named pure tests: admission_derives_root_bundle_from_authoritative_member; draft_admission_persists_validated_bundle_without_json_duplicate; missing_root_plan_decodes_as_distinct_admission_refusal. PostgreSQL 18: all admission producers persist the exact immutable pin; missing/cross-tenant bundles refuse before any admission write; catalog-head movement cannot rebind an admitted run. Migration: empty schema converges; legacy rows/members refuse without partial DDL; reconcile is idempotent. Drift guards pin types/nullability/checks/FKs/indexes/trigger. Residue forbids invocation_context bundle pins.

Named mutants: release-member-hash-replaced-by-caller-json, missing-root-plan-admits-run, runs-execution-bundle-fk-removed, run-admission-pin-update-allowed, draft-json-bundle-pin-restored, and legacy-plan-pin-fabricated-from-artifact.

Alternatives rejected by the recommendation: release_flow_test_evidence couples runtime authority to proof lifecycle; members_json duplicates structural identity without FK; draft backfill fabricates an unrecorded selection; nullable or NOT VALID migration preserves structurally unpinned runs. Strict empty cutover is the only non-fabricating greenfield contract.
notes: Implemented authoritative release/draft execution-bundle pinning, mandatory immutable run pins, typed missing-root-plan refusal, strict empty-only schema cutover including partial-schema ordering, publisher/copy/carry-forward handling, invocation-context duplicate removal, PostgreSQL 18 proofs, conformance parity, and six killed named mutants. All package, live, Clippy, format, drift, and mutation gates passed; versions remain 0.1.
close_reason: Authoritative execution-bundle admission pins, strict greenfield cutover, typed refusal, complete writer/readback migration, live proofs, and six named mutants are implemented and validated.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(build): effect_provider_revision digest
description: Charter cut 4: build-generated immutable digest over the native effect providers, the runtime fork, and host policy, completing ExecutionRuntimeRevision — required because effects execute natively (the executor constructs WamnPostgres/WamnCredentials/WamnLogging itself). Outcome: M0 execution.
acceptance_criteria:
OWNER-RATIFIED CONTRACT (2026-08-11)

Choose a semantic native-provider recipe revision, not an ELF or OCI digest. The manifest must be closed over native effect behavior; a hand-picked three-root file list is insufficient.

Exact v1 input closure

Root the normal locked production dependency subgraph at wamn-execution-host, then add the exact executor production-composition inputs (services/executor/Cargo.toml and every regular file under services/executor/src) and the executor-selected wash-runtime feature union. Do not root the graph at the whole executor package because that would pull queue/NATS/CLI/telemetry/scheduler lifecycle into the provider revision.

At baseline 56173ef the first-party host closure is exactly: wamn-execution-host, wamn-runtime, wamn-catalog, wamn-component-policy, wamn-control-registry, wamn-event-wire, wamn-flow, wamn-flow-invocation, wamn-node-invoke, wamn-node-manifest, wamn-pg-core, wamn-run-state, and wamn-runner.

A checked-in canonical manifest records those local package IDs/roots and every normal transitive external package in the locked closure as name, version, source, checksum, and byte-sorted package-scoped enabled features. Git sources record canonical URL plus resolved commit, never a branch. The current wamn-executor package-scoped wash-runtime record is the repository fork URL, commit 09b1132f2bab36e6e71f4637bd0e4755e359dd43, and features oci, washlet; full-workspace feature unification must not add unrelated wasi-config/wasi-otel.

For each local package root, digest exact bytes of Cargo.toml, optional build.rs, and every regular file recursively under src/ and wit/. Every production include_bytes/include_str input outside those roots is an explicit asset record. Executor Cargo.toml/src are explicit composition records. Reject symlinks, non-UTF8/absolute/parent-traversing paths, missing roots/files, duplicates, unlisted include assets, and noncanonical git revisions.

Manifest ownership and generation

A conformance tool/test regenerates the closure from package-scoped locked/offline wamn-executor resolution (cargo tree or an equivalent temporary metadata root, never full-workspace unified metadata), projects it to the wamn-execution-host dependency subgraph, adds executor composition inputs, and byte-compares it with the checked-in manifest. Dependency, feature, source, checksum, local-root, or include-asset drift fails until intentionally updated. build.rs never launches nested Cargo.

One crates/execution/host/build.rs plus a pure helper reads the checked-in manifest and local files, emits cargo:rerun-if-changed for every input/root, computes the revision, and exposes one non-overridable wamn_execution_host::EFFECT_PROVIDER_REVISION constant. Executor and management/scenario-worker already depend on that crate and must use the same constant; request/env/CLI input is forbidden. Runtime never recomputes from source. Executor carries the constant through trusted host context; .2.3/run-state claim preflight compares every reachable plan to it before any component invocation.

Exact preimage and literal

Frame the domain wamn.effect-provider-revision.v1 followed by records byte-sorted by normalized UTF-8 tag/path. Frame every tag and value independently as u64 big-endian length followed by exact bytes, matching the existing catalog identity convention. Source bytes receive no newline/text normalization; external record fields are independently tagged/framed and feature names byte-sorted. Output is exactly lowercase sha256: plus 64 lowercase hex and reuses the catalog parser/type.

Change policy

Any local manifest/source/WIT/build/include-asset byte or path-set change, external locked package version/source/checksum/feature change, fork URL/revision/feature change, or executor composition change mints a new revision. Tests/examples/docs outside the governed roots, runtime config/data/credentials, and scheduler lifecycle changes do not. An allegedly non-semantic governed change still mints. Narrowing the closure requires a separately ratified v2 manifest, not an exception. Algorithm/framing/input-set changes increment the domain version and are runtime-revision changes. Per the charter, change requires revalidate/retest/republish of every active release and old-worker drain before removal; no side-by-side runtime revisions in MVP.

Named proofs

- effect_provider_revision_golden_preimage_and_literal
- effect_provider_revision_is_checkout_path_and_discovery_order_independent
- effect_provider_revision_rejects_noncanonical_manifest_entries
- locked_effect_provider_closure_matches_manifest
- each_local_closure_root_add_remove_rename_and_byte_mutant_changes_revision

No release, component, signing, gate, kind, benchmark, timing, or shipping build ran; Cargo.lock, components/Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, .cargo/config.toml, components, deploy, signing, and shipping commands are unchanged.
