title: [BUILD-OPT-3] Audit duplicate dependencies and rebuild-trigger feature edges
description: Run cargo tree -d and audit duplicate major versions, shifted feature sets, and dev-dependency edges that drag test-only features into normal builds. Consolidate only cheap, bounded duplicates. Adopt a cargo-hakari workspace-hack crate only if daily source edits demonstrably trigger shared dependency rebuilds from feature-set shifts; otherwise explicitly decline it.
design: This is a bounded audit and judgment stage, not a benchmarking or measurement program. Preserve dependency correctness and do not force consolidation where versions are semantically incompatible. If the audit uncovers non-cheap implementation work, file each distinct change as its own granular child blocker before closing this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The close record lists duplicate-major and feature-edge findings, identifies every cheap consolidation made, and records an evidence-backed adopt/decline decision for cargo-hakari; test-only features no longer leak through any cheaply correctable dev-dependency edge; every non-cheap adopted follow-up is represented by a separate blocking bead; no timing gate or baseline program is introduced.
close_reason: Completed the locked/offline root and wasm32-wasip2 component dependency audit at commit 189ca556e913325da5c6f752d4dc9cfc680fcb0f with no builds or timing program. Duplicate findings: root version families are upstream compatibility splits across wash-runtime/Wasmtime cap 3/4, digest and sha2 0.10/0.11, rand 0.8/0.9/0.10, thiserror 1/2, darling 0.20/0.23, itertools 0.13/0.14, TLS roots, and WIT/wasm 0.236/0.251/0.252/0.253; components has transitive hashbrown 0.15/0.17, syn 2/3, and wit-bindgen 0.44/0.57 boundaries. Same-version cargo-tree repeats are resolver-2 build/target feature units, not multiple lock identities. Direct workspace requirements do not diverge. Cheap consolidations made: none; forcing pre-1.0/API, pinned-runtime, target, or upstream boundaries is not cheap, and no non-cheap follow-up was adopted. Feature findings: tokio sync versus dev rt/macros, hyper client versus dev server, and wamn-run-state test-util in conformance/integration/system are intentionally dev-only; the no-dev graph exposes only default and components has no dev-feature edges, so no test-only feature leaks into normal resolution. Cargo-hakari decision: decline because repository history, docs, and Beads contain no evidence that daily source edits rebuild shared dependencies due to shifted feature sets; resolver 2 contains the audited test edges and the Stage 2 source-only root/component dependency layers are already cache-stable. Locked cargo tree and cargo metadata validations passed for both workspaces.

title: [BUILD-OPT-2] Cache Docker gate dependencies across source-only rebuilds
description: Restructure the multi-stage gate Docker build on the cargo-chef plan/cook/build pattern so dependency layers survive workspace source edits. Add BuildKit target cache mounts and a registry-backed layer-cache path for kind builds. Treat the root and components manifests/lockfiles as separate cache keys. Coordinate with callable-flow image teardown so caching does not reintroduce unbounded uniquely tagged images. Use sccache only as the documented fallback if cargo-chef cannot support the multi-target layout.
design: This stage lands after Stage 1 because both touch Docker build tooling. Preserve the existing two-stage shipping image semantics, pinned component/signing artifacts, debug-first local workflow, and LLVM-backed gates. Do not add timing infrastructure; build-log dependency reuse is the acceptance evidence.
acceptance_criteria: After a dependency-changing build primes the cache, a source-only workspace change rebuilds the gate image without recompiling unchanged dependencies, visibly in the build log; root and components lockfiles key independent dependency layers; cache mounts and registry cache work in the kind flow without defeating verified image cleanup; the ordinary in-cluster gate build and one representative gate run pass; any sccache fallback is used only with recorded cargo-chef incompatibility.
notes: Owner decision 2026-08-06: use the recommended registry-agnostic kind-build wrapper. The caller supplies one stable mutable OCI cache reference; do not couple build cache to the ephemeral in-cluster component registry and do not derive cache refs from unique gate-image tags. Validate with a temporary local registry; retain exact gate-image cleanup through tools/kind-gate-image-remove.
close_reason: Implemented separate root/component cargo-chef dependency stages and lock keys, named BuildKit target caches, and a registry-agnostic kind wrapper with one stable caller-owned OCI cache ref. A fresh builder imported the OCI manifest with both cook stages CACHED; source-only native and component edits compiled only WAMN workspace crates, not unchanged third-party dependencies. The cached gates build and fresh in-cluster bench passed. All exact temporary images, jobs, builders, registry, network, and orphaned proof container were removed. Focused tests, strict Clippy, rustfmt, shell syntax, metadata, and diff checks pass. No sccache was needed.

title: [BUILD-OPT-1] Add target-scoped mold linker and optimized dev dependency profiles
description: Add .cargo/config.toml with the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu clang+mold linker configuration; add the specified root dev/package/build-override profiles; and install clang plus mold in the developer image and Docker build stage. If mold is unavailable, lld is the only allowed fallback. Keep the configuration target-scoped so wasm32-wasip2 continues using rust-lld, and do not touch the separate components workspace or stable toolchain pin.
design: The target table is load-bearing and must not be flattened into build.rustflags. Workspace crates remain opt-level 0 with full debuginfo; dependencies use opt-level 1 and line-tables-only; build dependencies use opt-level 1. Preserve readable panics/backtraces. Include the per-package dependency flip-back recipe in the commit message.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary debug builds and one representative existing gate-of-record pass; the native build uses clang+mold (or explicitly justified lld fallback); workspace crates retain opt-0/full debugging; dependencies receive the specified dev optimization; a wasm32-wasip2 component build remains on its existing linker path; rust-toolchain.toml and component/signing outputs are unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented target-scoped clang+mold linking, optimized dev dependency/build profiles, and builder-image clang/mold provisioning. No baseline program or timing gate is added. Ordinary builds and existing gates are the proof. Global constraints: rust-toolchain.toml stays untouched; wasm32-wasip2 keeps rust-lld; components remain insulated by their separate workspace/lockfile; release and gates keep LLVM; no component/signing flags change.

close_reason: Epic completed. All five ordered children are closed and published on origin/main: wamn-9ler.1 at 1a352e8 (target-scoped clang+mold and optimized native dev profiles; native/component/gate validation), .2 at 2e065e0 (cargo-chef 0.1.77, separate root/component dependency recipes, BuildKit target caches, stable registry cache, cached in-cluster gate pass, no sccache), .3 at 189ca55 (locked dependency/feature audit; no cheap consolidations, no test-feature leak, no Hakari), .4 at cca3340 (isolated opt-in native-debug Cranelift image/helper with stable LLVM shipping boundaries), and .5 at 0ed0abf (canonical docs/build-and-test.md guidance and staged-plan retirement). title: [FORK-2.6.0-D] Restore metricbench run metrics through the executor-owned seam
description:
## Goal

This regression predates the fork upgrade and was exposed only after wamn-8zht.33 repaired catalog provisioning.

## Owned collision domain
The executor-owned run-metric proof seam and metricbench process orchestration needed to exercise it.

title: [FORK-2.6.0-D] allowIpNameLookup runtime-primitive gate
description:
## Goal

Gate upstream's new `allowIpNameLookup` as a **runtime primitive**: prove what it does and
prove the fork's TCP/UDP restrictions still dominate it when lookup is permitted.

This is the hook the `8b76869` ledger entry said proper allowlist matching would need — it
rejected name→IP allowlists because `TcpConnect` sees a post-DNS `SocketAddr`. Upstream has
now built it. That makes it the missing primitive for the retirement investigation, not
evidence that retirement is likely.

## Normative anchors

docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md section 5 step 4, the `allowIpNameLookup` bullet, and
section 2's five conditions any replacement policy must satisfy.

Planning alias: FU-LOOKUP-GATE.

## Owned collision domain

wamn repository: a gate exercising the runtime primitive, plus its recipe entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** Exact, wildcard and literal-IP cases behave as upstream documents, and the
  fork's TCP/UDP restrictions still dominate when lookup is permitted. Default remains `[]`.
- **Negative:** This gate proves **upstream behaviour only**. Exposing the field through wamn
  workload generation is E1, deliberately separate so the base gate and the adoption
  milestone are not circular. No socket patch is weakened here.
- **Fault:** A configuration in which an approved lookup permits a connection the fork policy
  should deny must fail a named test.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --lib
```

## Explicit exclusions

No workload-generation exposure (E1). No retirement of `8b76869` or `eef76cd` (E2).

## Hard dependencies

- C1
close_reason: Added six allowIpNameLookup conformance tests covering exact, wildcard, literal-IP, and default-empty behavior through the pinned wash-runtime 2.6.0 public matcher, plus exact fork-source guards proving P2/P3 TCP and UDP remain governed by the independent raw-socket policy. The exact H5-IP-NAME-LOOKUP recipe passed 6/6, the full conformance library passed 59/59, conformance clippy passed with warnings denied, the complete build-recipe selector sweep and five recipe-structure tests passed, and the socket-dominance mutant failed approved_lookup_must_not_authorize_fork_denied_tcp_or_udp before restoration. Workload-generation exposure and socket-patch retirement remained excluded, with no deferrals or out-of-epic work.

title: [FORK-2.6.0-D] Raw TCP/UDP denial gate including the P3 mirrors
description:
## Goal

Gate that raw TCP and UDP egress remain denied after the rebase, **including the P3 mirrors**,
so the two security seams (B4, B5) are proven on every compiled, guest-reachable surface.

Host-boundary policies cover every such surface even where wamn deploys no P3 service
workload, because a guest that imports a P3 interface reaches it regardless.

## Normative anchors

docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md section 5 step 4: *"raw TCP and UDP still denied,
including the P3 mirrors."* Existing related gates: `egressbench` (walks the shipped
components) and `socketguard` (proves the publish-time guard rejects an adversarial world) —
`docs/build-and-test.md` sections "[2.6]" and "[E13a]".

Planning alias: FU-SOCKET-GATE.

## Owned collision domain

wamn repository: `tests/conformance/src/egressbench.rs`, `tests/conformance/src/socketguard.rs`,
their recipes, and any runtime-side negative gate needed to reach the P3 arms.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** A socket-importing component cannot connect over TCP or send UDP to a
  non-loopback address on either surface; an opted-in workload can. `UdpBind` is
  service-loopback-only.
- **Negative:** Publish-time refusal (`socketguard`) is not a substitute for runtime denial,
  and runtime denial is not a substitute for publish-time refusal — both layers are asserted.
  A gate that only walks the shipped first-party components cannot prove the guard rejects an
  adversarial world.
- **Fault:** Restoring unconditional allow on any one of TcpConnect, UdpConnect,
  UdpOutgoingDatagram, or widening UdpBind, must fail a named test naming that arm.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --lib egressbench::tests::
cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --lib socketguard::tests::
cargo test -p wamn-component-policy --lib tests::
# in-cluster: deploy/gates/socketguard-job.yaml
```

## Explicit exclusions

Does not retire either socket patch — that investigation is E2 and is gated on E1.

## Hard dependencies

- B4
- B5
- C1

title: [FORK-2.6.0-D] ExecutionHost deadline re-arming and trap-disposal regression gate
description:
## Goal

Prove Wasmtime 47 preserves the per-call epoch-deadline behaviour wamn **already has** on
`ExecutionHost`: the store takes `deadline_ticks(ttl_ms)` at instantiation and is re-armed
before each entry point, and a trap disposes the live instance so no later call reuses it.

At the pinned revision this is live at `crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:112`, with re-arming
at `:463`, `:488` and `:521`. This gate is a **regression guard on existing behaviour across
a runtime major**, not new enforcement.

## Normative anchors

docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md section 5 step 4, the `ExecutionHost` deadline
regression bullet, and section 3: *"Deadline enforcement is not upgrade scope."*

Planning alias: FU-DEADLINE-REG.

## Owned collision domain

wamn repository: a gate covering `crates/execution/host`, its recipe in
`docs/build-and-test.md`, and the recipe drift-guard entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** Invocation A consumes part of an epoch window and invocation B receives a
  newly armed **full** window; a trapped or interrupted call disposes the live instance so no
  later call can reuse it.
- **Negative:** This is explicitly **not** an expansion into H9. `NodeRuntime` stays out of
  scope — it attaches no finite deadline at `crates/platform/node-runtime/src/lib.rs:352` and
  that gap belongs to H9 / PLAN item 4, together with its missing memory limiter.
- **Fault:** Removing the re-arm so B inherits A's remaining window, or retaining a trapped
  instance instead of disposing it, must each fail a named test.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test -p wamn-executor -p wamn-proof-integration
```

## Explicit exclusions

No `NodeRuntime` deadline work. No cancellation-programme work. No pooling.

## Hard dependencies

- C1
close_reason: Added a Wasmtime 47 regression gate proving each ExecutionHost entry point rearms its epoch deadline, invocation B receives a fresh window, and a trapped call disposes the instance. Main-tree validation passed 8 host, 6 executor, 74 integration, 5 recipe-drift tests, and the complete build-recipe helper sweep. Independent removed-rearm and retained-live mutants each failed their named behavioral test and were restored; NodeRuntime/H9, cancellation, and pooling remained excluded with no unfiled deferrals.

title: [FORK-2.6.0-B] Re-port the epoch-deadline policy (94bf77f)
description:
## Goal

Re-port the epoch-deadline policy carried as `94bf77f` onto v2.6.0: every store created by
the crate's production store-creation site receives a finite epoch deadline resolved from the
active component's `wamn.epoch-deadline-ticks` config, else `WAMN_EPOCH_DEADLINE_TICKS`, else
effectively unbounded (`u64::MAX / 2` — `u64::MAX` wraps in `current_epoch + delta`).

Without it stores keep wasmtime's default deadline of 0 and trap on the first tick, so epoch
interruption is unusable.

## Normative anchors

docs/wash-runtime-fork.md ledger row `94bf77f`; exit condition: *upstream ships native
epoch-deadline support*. docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md section 2 verdict: **re-port
as-is** for the base upgrade; per-checkout re-arming is a reusable-store adoption
prerequisite, not base scope.

Planning alias: FU-SEAM-EPOCH.

## Owned collision domain

Repository /home/kaalin/dev/wasmcloud, branch `wamn/2.6.0`: the store-creation site in
`crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/` and this seam's ledger row only.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** The policy is reimplemented against v2.6.0's store construction — one call
  site by design, to minimise rebase drift — and its exit condition is re-derived.
- **Negative:** If the seam materially changed, the ledger row is amended explicitly,
  preserving the original operational intent and recording why the prior wording no longer
  expresses it. A difficult re-port must not produce a more convenient exit condition. If
  upstream now ships native epoch-deadline support, the commit is **deleted**, not re-ported.
- **Fault:** Removing the deadline resolution must fail a named test — without it, stores
  trap on the first tick.

## Validation

```bash
cd /home/kaalin/dev/wasmcloud   # branch wamn/2.6.0
cargo test -p wash-runtime      # in-crate suite for this seam
cargo build -p wash-runtime
```

Mutation: apply/test/restore with sha256; the mutant must fail a **named** test for this
seam alone. Debug builds.

## Explicit exclusions

No other seam's policy. No pin bump (C1). No gate work (D*). No pooling, host-component
plugins, P3 migration, or deadline-enforcement work. `NodeRuntime` behaviour is preserved
unchanged.

## Hard dependencies

- A1 (the re-port brief)

title: [FORK-2.6.0-A] Enumerate upstream drift and produce the per-seam re-port brief
description:
## Goal

Before any seam is touched, enumerate what upstream changed between v2.5.2 (`ec012da`) and

92 commits landed between the two releases. The upgrade doc's central claim is that this is
a policy re-port and not a dependency bump; this issue is what makes that claim checkable
rather than asserted.

## Normative anchors

docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md sections 1, 2, 3 and the step-2 rule "re-port policies,
not diffs". docs/wash-runtime-fork.md — the ledger's per-commit exit conditions are the
comparison basis; check the disposition against **those**, not against a fresh judgment.

Planning alias: FU-PREREAD. Fork target branch `wamn/2.6.0` @ `9bf8e97b`.

## Owned collision domain

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** `git fetch origin` is run first, all six carried commits are reachable, and
  the brief names per seam: the upstream commits touching its files, whether the

- **Negative:** A seam whose exit condition upstream now satisfies is marked for deletion,
  not re-port. A seam whose seam has moved is marked as requiring an explicit ledger
  amendment. Neither outcome may be inferred from compile success.
- **Fault:** Branching from the stale local `wamn/2.5.2` (`d3d83f31`) silently drops

## Validation

```bash
git fetch origin
git rev-parse origin/wamn/2.5.2                 # must be 981fdc56…
git log --oneline ec012da0..origin/wamn/2.5.2   # must list all six carried commits

```

Also inspect the v2.6.0 workspace manifest for the Wasmtime and `async-nats` lines that C1
must match.

## Explicit exclusions

No seam implementation, no pin bump, no ledger edits beyond recording the findings. Does not

notes:
## v2.6.0 per-seam re-port brief

Evidence was collected read-only in `/home/kaalin/dev/wasmcloud` after a fresh
`git fetch origin`. Comparisons use upstream `ec012da0..9bf8e97b` and the exit
conditions recorded in `docs/wash-runtime-fork.md`, not compile success.

### Baseline and fault proof

- `origin/wamn/2.5.2` is
  `981fdc56ebc1840f08161aef5edec592538e5d4c`.
- The stale local `wamn/2.5.2` is
  `d3d83f3152abe103fa49a538861cbc826c256d5e`.
- The three commits that stale local branch would drop are exactly
  `8b768692` (TcpConnect deny), `eef76cd8` (raw UDP deny/UdpBind), and
  `981fdc56` (limiter accessors + request counter).
- `wamn/2.6.0` and peeled `v2.6.0^{commit}` are both
  `9bf8e97b28bfbc26d629aca1d5c4d8f14a8cfe6b`.
- The upstream release range contains 92 commits.
- All six carried commits are reachable from `origin/wamn/2.5.2`, in order:
  `94bf77f1`, `5b158ffc`, `d3d83f31`, `8b768692`, `eef76cd8`,
  `981fdc56`.

### Upstream file-touch inventories

These inventories are exhaustive for the files patched by the carried commits.
Socket enforcement files are included where their v2.6.0 movement changes the
meaning of the central `socket_addr_check` policy.

`L` — `crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/linked_call.rs`:

- `11e0b76c` cross-store relocation for ephemeral stream/future calls

`C` — `crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/ctx.rs`:

- `1a5111c7` host-component plugins, `resource_registry`, and caller identity

`H` — `crates/wash-runtime/src/host/http.rs`:

- `c65e918f` trigger-service HTTP ingress
- `11e13e9c` trigger-service messaging ingress
- `9b67732e` TCP_NODELAY on accepted HTTP connections
- `33a1520b` warning on NODELAY failure
- `675b5079` service-replica ingress routing
- `bd7f88e7` lock-free/random replica routing
- `6130b07a` warm P3 HTTP dispatch

Socket enforcement additions:

- `bc136274` ports Wasmtime 47 and adds the P3 implicit-bind policy checks in
  `host_tcp_p3.rs` and `host_udp_p3.rs`.
- `d9c92186` makes the P3 UDP implicit bind happen once and persist.
- `host_udp.rs` has no commits in the release range.

### 1. `94bf77f` — per-store epoch deadline

- Upstream touches: `L`.
- What moved: `new_store_from_templates` remains the insertion point
  (`linked_call.rs:286-342`, `Store::new` at 323), but v2.6.0 adds warm reuse,

  `set_epoch_deadline`, `epoch_deadline`, or native epoch configuration.
- Exit satisfied: **no**.
- Disposition: **re-port**, not delete.
- Material movement / ledger: **yes — amend the description, preserve the exit
  condition**. Describe the central workload-store constructor and the enabled
  base-upgrade scope. Record pooling/trigger/plugin stores as disabled and
  per-checkout re-arming as a reusable-store adoption prerequisite, not base

### 2. `5b158ff` — per-component memory limiter

- Upstream touches: `L` + `C`.
- What moved: `SharedCtx` now carries plugin resource-bridge state; the central

- Disposition: **re-port and scope-broaden to enabled workload-store paths**,
  not delete. Preserve the config precedence, hard over-ceiling refusal,
  per-linear-memory semantics, table cap, logging, and counters.
- Material movement / ledger: **yes — amend the description, preserve the exit
  condition**. State the v2.6.0 coverage, keep plugin stores out while the
  feature is disabled, and name aggregate `pool_size × budget` enforcement as a
  separate reusable-store prerequisite.

### 3. `d3d83f3` — outbound W3C trace injection

- Upstream touches: `H`; `6130b07a` and `64d69427` also touch the P3 response

  `DefaultOutgoingHandler::{send_request, send_request_p3}`, but the target

  default sends forward requests without W3C injection. Only inbound extraction
  remains (`host/http.rs:1247-1251`).
- Exit satisfied: **no**.
- Disposition: **re-port across P2 and P3**, not delete, with independently
  failing proof per generation.
- Material movement / ledger: **yes — amend the ledger coverage and re-derive

  both releases branch gRPC through `send_grpc_request{,_p3}` before
  `DefaultOutgoingHandler`. Either use a common pre-transport injection point or
  explicitly state the intended gRPC coverage; two default-handler patches
  alone do not prove the current phrase “every outbound call.”

### 4. `8b76869` — deny `TcpConnect` unless opted in

- Upstream touches: `L`; `bc136274` touches P3 TCP implicit `listen` bind, not
  `TcpConnect`.
- What moved: `build_ctx_from_template` still creates the shared
  `WasiSocketsCtx::socket_addr_check`, and the target callback still returns
  `true` for `TcpConnect`. `b60e4016`/`e4a3aa57` add a DNS-name lookup allowlist

- Disposition: **re-port**, not delete.

  `UdpConnect`/`UdpOutgoingDatagram` unconditionally and permits loopback or

  operations consult no egress policy. Name lookup does not bind a resolved
  name to the later address and does not constrain literal addresses.
- Exit satisfied: **no**.
- Disposition: **re-port**, not delete, including both P2/P3 enforcement paths.
- Material movement / ledger: **yes — amend the description, preserve the exit
  condition**. Record the P3 two-decision implicit-bind path and add an explicit
  regression for its opted-in behavior; `allowIpNameLookup` remains supporting

### 6. `981fdc5` seam 1 — limiter introspection accessors

- Upstream touches: `C`.

### 7. `981fdc5` seam 2 — `wamn.api.requests` inbound counter

- Upstream touches: `H`.
- What moved: trigger-service HTTP adds a long-lived service-response branch,

- Exit satisfied: **no**.
- Disposition: **re-port**, not delete.
- Material movement / ledger: **yes — split the combined `981fdc5` row and exit

The v2.6.0 workspace manifest records:

All seven seams have unsatisfied recorded exits. **Re-port all seven; delete
none.** Required ledger amendments are descriptive/scope corrections for epoch,

title: [EPIC] · [FORK-2.6.0] Rebase the wash-runtime fork onto wasmCloud v2.6.0
description:
## Goal

Rebase the `wash-runtime` fork from upstream v2.5.2 (`ec012da`) onto upstream v2.6.0
(`9bf8e97`), re-porting every carried policy seam against the new architecture, and land
the wamn-side pin, dependency realignment, and gates — so that items 1 and 2A of
docs/PLAN/PLAN.md are built against the runtime they will ship on.

Treat this as a **policy re-port, not a dependency bump**. Upstream changed the same files
the fork patches (linked calls, HTTP handlers, store construction, runtime context) across
92 commits. Replaying six diffs line-for-line would compile and mean nothing.

## Normative anchors

- docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md — the design of record for this epic.
- docs/wash-runtime-fork.md — the carried-commit ledger, per-commit exit conditions, sync
  runbook, and the upgrade-gate subset. The ledger is authoritative over any summary.
- docs/PLAN/PLAN.md 0.3 — this upgrade is a one-time prerequisite preceding items 1 and 2A.
- D23 (runtime-maintainer posture): owned forks are first-class; immutable rev pin, ledger
  with exit conditions, upgrade-gate subset run and logged on every sync. No carried-commit
  ceiling.
- Fork target: `dkkloimwieder/wasmcloud` branch `wamn/2.6.0` at `9bf8e97b28bfbc26d629aca1d5c4d8f14a8cfe6b`,
  the peeled commit of annotated tag `runtime-operator/v2.6.0`.
- wamn baseline: `9f67ceb`.

## Success criteria

- The fork is based on v2.6.0 with **all seven carried policy seams re-ported** — six
  commits, with `981fdc5` tracked as two seams because its exit condition is an AND.
- Each seam's exit condition is re-derived against v2.6.0, and the ledger is amended
  explicitly wherever the architectural seam materially changed.
- One resolved Wasmtime type universe and one resolved `async-nats` across every native
  workspace package that links the runtime or exchanges Wasmtime/WASI types — production
  services **and** proof packages.
- Every existing gate is green on the new fork, plus the new mutation and regression proofs.
- The feature and deployed-workload inventory is recorded, making "three active store paths"
  a verified statement rather than an assumption.
- Pooling, host-component plugins, and P3 service workloads remain disabled.
- The fork doc's header and ledger agree, and the sync log carries this rebase.

## Collision and sequencing rules

- A1 blocks every seam bead. The re-port brief exists before any seam is touched.
- Seam beads B1-B7 are fork-side and may run as parallel lanes; each owns its own seam and
  amends only its own ledger row.
- C1 is a single coordinated change by design — `wash-runtime`, the Wasmtime family, and
  `async-nats` move together because intermediate states do not build.
- All gate beads depend on C1. D6 is the serial closure sweep and depends on every other
  child except E1/E2.
- The fork clone at /home/kaalin/dev/wasmcloud is three commits stale on `wamn/2.5.2` and
  its remote-tracking ref is stale too. `git fetch origin` before any carry-forward.
- docs/findings.md is not edited by this epic.

## Explicit exclusions

Carried from docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md section 6:

- **No global warm pooling.** A 2A experiment, gated on proving no cross-invocation leakage
  and an instance-retirement policy.
- **No `host-component-plugins`.** Off by default upstream; keep it off. It is the most
  interesting thing in the release for 2B connection providers, but that is a prototype.
- **No P3 migration** of `flow-http`, `flowrunner`, or `node-host`.
- **No replacement of the durable run plane with upstream trigger services.**
- **No removal of the socket patches** on the strength of `allowIpNameLookup` alone.
- **No deadline-enforcement work.** `NodeRuntime` attaches neither a finite epoch deadline
  nor a memory limiter (`crates/platform/node-runtime/src/lib.rs:352` sets `u64::MAX / 2`).
  Both gaps are the same class on the same store and stay together under H9 / PLAN item 4.
  This epic **preserves** `NodeRuntime` behaviour and adds nothing to it. The upgrade
  neither causes nor fixes that gap; absorbing it here would let an unrelated security item
  ride an untracked dependency bump.

## Closure

This epic closes only when D6 passes — the full existing gate sweep green on the new fork
with the sync-log row appended. E1 and E2 are the deliberately separate first post-upgrade
adoption milestone, so that "features only after green" is not circular with the definition
of green.

## Owned collision domain

This epic owns sequencing and the closure sweep. It owns no product-code implementation.
Child issues own their declared domains across two repositories: A1 and B1-B7 in the fork
clone at /home/kaalin/dev/wasmcloud on branch `wamn/2.6.0`; C, D, and E children in the wamn
repository.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** D6 passes on the new fork after all seam re-ports, the coordinated
  dependency realignment, and the new gates have closed; the ledger and sync log record the
  rebase with commits carried and dropped.
- **Negative:** A seam whose exit condition upstream now satisfies is deleted rather than
  re-ported, and a difficult re-port never produces a more convenient exit condition. No
  excluded item above is implemented under this epic.
- **Fault:** Carrying forward from the stale local `wamn/2.5.2` would silently drop three
  seams including both raw-socket denials; the brief and the rebased branch must both show
  all six carried commits present.

description:

title: [CALLABLE-FLOWS-P4] Expose fenced inline execution for admitted HTTP runs
description:
## Goal

Expose the production runner boundary required for the invocation provider to execute a run already claimed inline by final HTTP admission. The provider must be able to drive exactly the admitted `(tenant, run_id, executor_id, lease_generation)` without releasing it to the generic available-work queue.

## Normative anchors

FLOW-SPEC rev18 §§6.1, 9.1–9.7, 10, 11 and Phase 4; POC-PLAN r6 T1.

Planning alias: `CF-INLINE-DRIVER`. The tracked source baseline is `84f0584`.

## Owned collision domain

Flowrunner/execution-host invocation export and the minimal production host/runtime handoff for executing one already-claimed run. This issue is the sole owner of that runner boundary while active; it does not own HTTP adaptation, admission SQL, wait/cancel policy, graph semantics, or generic `run-next` claiming.

## Acceptance criteria

- Positive: Given an HTTP run atomically admitted with a claimed queue row, invoke the runner for that exact run/owner/generation and reach the normal release-or-terminal transition; the provider never needs to make the row available.
- Negative: Refuse tenant/run mismatch, owner mismatch, stale generation, non-claimed rows, and a second concurrent driver; a lost fence permits no subsequent run-state access.
- Fault: Independently inject crash after admission commit/before runner dispatch, during runner instantiation, and after runner completion/before provider observation. title: [CALLABLE-FLOWS-P2A] Carry queue ordering through centralized admission
description:
## Goal
Extend the single centralized admit transition so every producer carries its already-resolved queue partition key and typed partition policy into the admitted queue row without producer-side run_queue SQL.

## Evidence
The production dispatcher and materializer resolve ordering and stamp run_queue.partition_key/partition_policy. wamn_run_state admission creates queue rows but its typed/SQL parameter shape cannot carry either value. Cutting either producer over to admit would discard strict/partitioned routing and leapfrog policy; patching the row afterward would violate transition ownership.

## Owned collision domain
wamn-run-state typed admission inputs/results and admission SQL only. One run-state transition SQL owner at a time. Dispatcher and materializer consumers remain owned by wamn-5wd1.49 and .50.

## Acceptance criteria
Positive: admit accepts the resolved optional partition key and typed partition policy for every producer and atomically stamps them with the run and queue row; unordered admissions retain null key plus blocking, while strict/partitioned admissions preserve their resolved key and blocking/leapfrog policy.
Negative: unknown policy, unkeyed leapfrog, swapped producer parameters, producer-side post-admit queue mutation, and any policy/key shape mismatch are refused; direct producer run/queue SQL remains forbidden.
Fault: crash or retry at the run/queue seam leaves zero partial rows or one coherently ordered admission; duplicates cannot mutate stored ordering, and concurrent admissions converge to one run plus one queue row.

## Validation
cargo test --locked -p wamn-run-state
Run the admission live PostgreSQL gate from docs/build-and-test.md against a throwaway database, including cron/event, ordering, duplicate, concurrency, and mutation cases.

## Explicit exclusions
No dispatcher attachment/schedule conversion, materializer envelope conversion, event activation/release membership, cron catch-up/generation refinement, ordering reconciler, or Phase 3 attempt protocol.

## Hard dependencies
Depends on wamn-5wd1.48. Blocks wamn-5wd1.49 and wamn-5wd1.50.

title: [CALLABLE-FLOWS-P2A] Persist resolved interface bundles for runtime replay classification
description:
## Goal
Persist each immutable flow artifact resolved interface bundle, including typed purity and recovery class, and expose an authoritative pinned-artifact graph-plus-interfaces lookup to the production flowrunner so attempt replay policy is derived from the published artifact rather than legacy graph data.

## Normative anchors
FLOW-SPEC rev18 §§8.2, 10.3 and Phase 2A/3; POC-PLAN r6 T-NR. Discovered while implementing CF-ATTEMPTS (`wamn-5wd1.54`): CF-MANIFEST and CF-RELEASE hash the resolved interface but do not persist runtime-readable bundle bytes.

## Evidence
`wamn_catalog::Artifact` owns `Vec<ResolvedNodeInterface>` and publish computes it in `services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs`, but `catalog.flow_artifacts` and `register_flow_artifact` store only `interface_bundle_hash`. Production `components/execution/flowrunner::{load_active_flow,load_flow_at}` reads legacy `flows.graph_json`; `wamn_flow::ResolvedInterfaces` carries ports only. Therefore runtime cannot distinguish a custom pure node from absent purity without trusting mutable or unpinned input.

## Owned collision domain
Catalog `flow_artifacts` DDL, registry/publish/copy paths for resolved interface bytes, immutable artifact identity verification, and production pinned artifact graph-plus-interfaces lookup. One catalog-DDL/publish-path owner at a time.

## Acceptance criteria
Positive: publication atomically stores canonical resolved interface bundle bytes whose recomputed hash equals `interface_bundle_hash`; flowrunner lookup returns graph and bundle from the same pinned artifact and exposes typed purity/recovery for every custom node.
Negative: missing, malformed, noncanonical, hash-mismatched, mutable, or artifact-mismatched bundles are refused; absent custom-node purity resolves to effectful plus never-replay.
Fault: inject failures at bundle persistence and pinned lookup seams; publication leaves no partial artifact, retry converges idempotently, and a concurrent head/promotion change cannot mix graph bytes from one artifact with interfaces from another.

## Validation
`cargo test --locked -p wamn-catalog -p wamn-control-registry -p wamn-ctl -p wamn-runner`
Run the canonical catalog from-zero/live publication and promotion race recipes in `docs/build-and-test.md` against throwaway PostgreSQL.

## Explicit exclusions
No attempt intent/success transition, deadline enforcement, cancellation, event activation, Phase 2B normalization, or child orchestration.

## Hard dependencies
Depends only on `wamn-5wd1.36`, `.46`, `.47`, and `.63`. Blocks `wamn-5wd1.54`.
acceptance_criteria: Persist and hash-verify canonical resolved interface bundles on immutable artifacts; production flowrunner reads graph and typed recovery metadata from one pinned artifact under positive, negative, and injected-fault/race proof.
close_reason: Completed in main commit 1446c80. Persisted exact canonical resolved-interface bundle bytes plus typed supplied-component pins; publish/copy verify graph, bundle, component mapping, full artifact hash, and release-manifest pin; production flowrunner reads graph plus typed purity/recovery from one immutable release-pinned query with no legacy fallback. ## Goal

Implement synthetic entry completion, reserved `respond`/`fail`, release-and-continue, zero-successor release-and-complete, and frontier-exhaustion completion including unwired completion ports.

## Normative anchors

FLOW-SPEC rev18 §§2, 9.8–9.9, §10 and Phase 3.

Planning alias: `CF-ENGINE`. The tracked source baseline is `9ddcd7d`.

## Owned collision domain

crates/execution/flow-engine and flowrunner graph-driving semantics; serial state-machine lane.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** Implement synthetic entry completion, reserved `respond`/`fail`, release-and-continue, zero-successor release-and-complete, and frontier-exhaustion completion including unwired completion ports.
- **Negative:** Reject user execution of reserved nodes, post-terminal graph writes, response from cron/event, and ambiguous exhausted-frontier outcomes.
- **Fault:** Crash/restart at each reserved-node boundary must preserve exactly one caller release and terminal result.

## Validation

```sh
cargo test --locked -p wamn-runner -p wamn-flow
cargo test --locked -p wamn-proof-integration --lib runnerbench::tests::
```

The implementation commit must also update `architecture/state-owners.json`, `architecture/package-roles.json`, workspace tiers, build recipes, and conformance tests when this issue adds or moves a table, package, or deployment role.

## Explicit exclusions

No context checkpointing, effect attempt protocol, admission, or cancellation.

## Hard dependencies

- `wamn-5wd1.34`
- `wamn-5wd1.45`

Only the dependencies above block this work. Legacy findings/proofs are related evidence only and close solely on fixing commits with their required evidence.

Exact gates passed: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/kaalin/dev/wamn/target/cf-engine-52 cargo test --locked -p wamn-runner -p wamn-flow (86 tests plus doctests); cargo test --locked -p wamn-proof-integration --lib runnerbench::tests:: (3/3). Additional run-state 30/30 and flowrunner cargo check passed. Includes strict synthetic-entry replay, reserved respond/fail, release-and-continue, natural completion, RFC8785 outcome hash replay equality, D20 dead-letter preservation, and generation-fenced entry checkpoint.

title: [CALLABLE-FLOWS-P2A] Publish immutable flow releases
description:

Replace mutable flows with immutable `flow_artifacts`, `release_flows`, and stable `catalog_heads`; make publish/copy atomic and idempotent and promotion refuse while an old-release run is nonterminal.

## Normative anchors

Planning alias: `CF-RELEASE`. The tracked source baseline is `9ddcd7d`.

- **Positive:** Replace mutable flows with immutable `flow_artifacts`, `release_flows`, and stable `catalog_heads`; make publish/copy atomic and idempotent and promotion refuse while an old-release run is nonterminal.
- **Negative:** Differing content under an existing identity conflicts; promotion with a nonterminal old-release run and publication with unresolved sources are refused.
- **Fault:** Injected faults at each publication boundary must leave no partial release/head state and a retry must converge byte-identically.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H3-CTL] Type the catalog schema rewrite boundary with canonical PostgreSQL identifiers
description:
## Goal

Prevent catalog publication and run-plane DDL rewriting from accepting a schema name that PostgreSQL will truncate or reinterpret, and make pg-core the canonical owner of the shared identifier invariant before any superuser effect.

## Questions

- Which narrow bare-schema type should wrap or compose wamn_pg_core::Identifier while retaining the lowercase unquoted syntax required by rewrite_schema?
- Should rewrite_schema itself accept the validated type so every ctl, planner, and test caller crosses the same typed boundary?
- Which existing ctl validators and raw-string helper signatures become redundant once the boundary is typed?

## Evidence Required

- services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs valid_ident, run, publish, ensure_runstate, ensure_flow_registry, and ensure_flow_tests call paths.
- crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs rewrite_schema API and every caller.
- crates/platform/pg-core Identifier invariants and PostgreSQL 63-byte identifier behavior under quoted and unquoted DDL.
- A real-PostgreSQL or discriminating builder proof showing that two distinct overlong inputs cannot alias one physical schema and invalid input causes no privileged database effect.

## Steps to Reproduce

Pass publish-catalog a lowercase schema name longer than 63 UTF-8 bytes. valid_ident accepts it. PostgreSQL truncates the quoted CREATE SCHEMA and unquoted rewritten DDL identifier, while table_exists and other metadata probes continue binding the original overlong text value. Distinct Rust names can therefore resolve to one physical schema and repeated setup can mis-detect existing objects or fail after partial privileged work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The publish-catalog schema value is converted to a fallible strong type before the admin connection or any database effect; 63-byte names are accepted and over-limit or invalid names are rejected.
- The strong type delegates PostgreSQL empty, NUL, byte-length, representation, and quoting rules to pg-core; ctl and schema-control do not reimplement those invariants.
- Raw strings cannot reach the privileged rewrite_schema interpolation boundary through publish-catalog or its reusable ensure helpers, and the API/comment no longer relies on an unchecked caller convention.
- Tests cover 63 versus 64 bytes, multibyte length, invalid syntax, two inputs differing only after byte 63, and unchanged normal publish/run-plane behavior.
- Invalid input returns before mutation and leaves no schema, table, catalog, entity-map, or replica-identity residue.
- This issue changes identifier validation and API ownership only; it does not redesign catalog publication atomicity or migration semantics.
close_reason: Completed in 3d19f71: introduced pg-core-backed BareSchemaName, typed publish/rewrite/run-plane/migrate/copy/helper boundaries, and made the remaining ctl compatibility validator delegate. Verified 26 ctl + 58 schema-control unit tests, affected all-target check/clippy, two named mutants, new disposable-Postgres alias/zero-residue proof, and existing run_plane_live matrix.

- Repeated shared versions and source identities are declared once in the appropriate workspace and consumed with workspace inheritance.
- The root and component workspaces remain independent build contracts; no root feature defaults leak into guests.
- Package-specific feature selections remain at package ownership boundaries and broad workspace features are narrowed where they are not universal.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H2] Build embedded component bytes inside the Docker graph
description:
## Goal

Make every Wasm component copied into executor, scenario-worker, and gates images a locked source-derived output of the same Docker build context, without requiring caller-built components/target files.

## Questions

- Which embedded components are required by each final image target?
- What is the smallest shared component-builder stage that preserves the separate wasm32 workspace and build cache?
- Which locked toolchain and Cargo inputs are already authoritative?

## Evidence Required

- Dockerfile component COPY paths, .dockerignore behavior, and components/Cargo.lock.
- A clean build with components/target absent and a poisoned local-target build.
- Extracted embedded Wasm digests from executor, scenario-worker, and gates images.

## Steps to Reproduce

Delete or replace components/target/wasm32-wasip2/release/flowrunner.wasm without changing repository source, then build an affected image. The current Dockerfile does not build the component workspace and either fails or packages the caller-provided bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Docker build stage compiles every Wasm component embedded in executor, scenario-worker, and gates images from repository source using the component lockfile and pinned toolchain inputs.
- Final stages copy component bytes only from that stage, never from caller-workspace components/target.
- A clean checkout with no component target directory builds each affected image.
- Deleting or poisoning local component outputs cannot break or alter the source-derived image result.
- A targeted digest check proves the expected built component is the byte sequence embedded in each affected image.
- This issue does not implement the broader immutable release receipt or attestation work retained by SR17 and SR26.
close_reason: Built every embedded Wasm inside a locked Docker component-builder stage; integrated gates/run-worker/scenario images build cleanly, all 18 final-image copies match builder SHA-256 values, and isolated clean/poisoned-context proofs passed.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-M5] Keep execution-host adapter-only and move executor lifecycle to the service
description:
## Goal

Make crates/execution/host a coherent shared runtime adapter for executor and scenario-worker composition, while services/executor owns production polling, NATS, supervision, backoff, metrics, and shutdown lifecycle.

## Questions

- Which functions are required by both compositions to instantiate flowrunner, inject capabilities, invoke run-next, and drain one execution?
- Which current modules change only with the long-lived production executor service?
- How can the move preserve binary identity, behavior, and the WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first runtime posture?

## Evidence Required

- Complete module and dependency inventory for crates/execution/host and services/executor.
- Caller map from executor, scenario-worker, tests, Docker targets, and deployment manifests.
- Existing unit, integration, and deployed runner gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- crates/execution/host owns only component instantiation, capability injection, single-execution invocation/drain, and shared adapter state required by both compositions.
- NATS doorbells, polling/backoff, long-lived serve loops, production egress policy selection, production telemetry/lifecycle, and shutdown supervision are owned by services/executor.
- scenario-worker does not inherit executor-only infrastructure, and services/executor remains a deployable leaf.
- No facade or broad re-export leaves two canonical paths to moved APIs.
- Executor binary/image/deployment identity and existing run semantics remain unchanged; this is not authorization to replace native services or move away from WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first execution.
close_reason: Implemented in 48a3478: execution-host is now the shared WASI/Wasm adapter; executor owns NATS doorbells, cadence/backoff, retry, shutdown, production egress selection, tracing, and OTel run metrics. Verified by 8 focused tests, 47 integration tests, all-target compilation, strict Clippy -D warnings, dependency-tree/format/drift guards, canonical run-worker image build, runner-only kind rollout, and a dispatcher-fired live cron proof (71/71 terminal; named final run completed with 2 successful node records in 31 ms; zero queue residue). Temporary proof state was removed and baseline demo counts restored.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-M4] Move reusable schema-drift support out of conformance
description:

Place reusable schema-drift and fixture-control helpers under the schema contract owner or an existing narrow test-support package so conformance is a consumer rather than an architectural dependency.

## Questions

- Which schema contract package can own structural comparison without acquiring runtime dependencies?
- If no contract owner fits, which existing test-support package is the narrowest home?

## Evidence Required

- tests/conformance exports and integration/system consumers.
- Dependency closures of candidate contract and test-support owners.
- Existing SQL, JSON Schema, WIT, and generated-artifact drift tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No integration or system package depends on tests/conformance for reusable support.
- Shared helpers have one narrow owner with no unnecessary database/runtime closure; conformance consumes that owner.
- Contract-specific comparison lives with its contract owner where feasible.
- Existing drift proofs retain byte-for-byte or structural semantics and named negative mutations still fail.
- No generic proof framework or new crate is introduced when an existing owner can hold the code.
close_reason: Completed in 7ecafac: moved the run-queue stand-in drift guard to feature-gated wamn-run-state test-util; integration/system no longer depend on conformance; conformance remains a consumer and orchestrator retains its genuine conformance edge. Main verification: run-state 74 tests + 2 doctests, conformance 24, integration 45, system 14, no-default-features check, strict owner clippy, dependency/single-owner guards, and named negative mutation evidence all passed.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-M2-CTL] Remove proof-package library dependencies on services/ctl

Remove direct Rust library dependencies from proof and test-support packages to the services/ctl deployable while preserving every existing control-plane proof.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H8B] Bound DbState assertion execution and materialization
description:
## Goal

Prevent a DbState assertion from consuming unbounded database time or scenario-worker memory while preserving the exploratory SQL observation capability.

## Questions

- Which fixed POC limits are needed for statement time, row count, and materialized bytes?
- At which query and materialization boundaries can each limit be enforced deterministically?
- Which result shape and cancellation failures must remain distinguishable?

## Evidence Required

- services/scenario-worker query and JSON materialization path.
- Current stored scenario fixtures and consumer-hardware measurements sufficient to choose non-disruptive bounds.
- Tests for timeout, excess rows, excess bytes, cancellation, and normal results.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a DbState assertion using a long-running query or a query that returns a very large generated result. The current query and collect path has no statement-time, row-count, or materialized-byte bound and can occupy the worker or exhaust memory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- DbState execution has explicit finite statement-time, row-count, and materialized-byte bounds selected and documented from current POC evidence.
- Exceeding each bound cancels or stops work promptly and returns a distinct typed scenario failure.
- Partial results are never treated as a successful assertion.
- Normal existing scenarios remain green and tests prove each bound without wall-clock sleeps or large persistent fixtures.
- This issue adds no general query language, pagination API, or production capacity promise.
close_reason: Implemented in 374e5fc: DbState assertions now enforce documented 5s/256-row/1MiB POC limits with typed timeout, row, byte, cancellation, dependency, and result-shape failures; stream with server-side oversized-value suppression; discard partial captures; preserve read-only/rollback containment; and pass unit, PostgreSQL 18 live, scenario-worker, integration, conformance, rustdoc, scoped strict-Clippy, and four mutation proofs.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H8A] Execute DbState assertions in a read-only transaction
description:
## Goal

Guarantee that a stored DbState assertion can observe scenario state but cannot mutate it, including through statements that return rows.

## Questions

- Which existing non-superuser scenario credential can perform the required observations?
- Where should the read-only transaction be established and rolled back?
- How should PostgreSQL read-only violations become stable scenario failures?

## Evidence Required

- crates/scenarios/model DbState contract.
- services/scenario-worker query execution and credentials.
- Tests for SELECT, data-modifying CTEs, UPDATE RETURNING, DDL, and transaction-control attempts.

## Steps to Reproduce

Store a DbState assertion whose query is UPDATE of a fixture row with RETURNING. The scenario-worker sends the arbitrary query directly through Client.query, materializes the returned row, and leaves the fixture mutation durable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every DbState assertion runs inside an explicitly read-only transaction using the least-privileged existing scenario identity that can satisfy the observation.
- Mutating SQL, including UPDATE RETURNING and data-modifying CTEs, fails before durable state changes.
- Transaction control cannot escape the read-only boundary and the executor always rolls back assertion work.
- A successful SELECT retains current result semantics and a typed failure reports prohibited mutation without exposing credentials.
- The integration gate no longer performs a duplicate superuser observation for the same assertion.
- This issue does not introduce a structured query DSL or a new production observer service.
close_reason: Implemented in 50dc95a: DbState observations now use a shared scenario-runtime helper with a fresh explicit read-only transaction and rollback per assertion, tenant-scoped app identity, typed rejection classification, unit tests, strict Clippy/fmt/diff checks, and an independent PostgreSQL 18 live mutation proof.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H7] Separate scenario egress authorization from observation assertions
description:
## Goal

Make scenario egress authorization an independent trusted input so an assertion can observe an allowed request but can never grant the capability it is asserting.

## Questions

- Which existing scenario configuration should own the allowed-host set?
- How should RecordingEgress apply authorization before recording or matching observations?
- What deterministic failure should an expected but unauthorized destination produce?

## Evidence Required

- services/scenario-worker derivation of expected authorities.
- crates/scenarios/runtime egress adapter and its ignored allowed_hosts input.
- Positive, default-deny, and assertion-cannot-authorize tests.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create an egress assertion naming a host that is absent from the externally supplied allowed-host set. The worker derives expected authorities from assertions and RecordingEgress ignores its allowed_hosts argument, so the assertion itself permits the request it is meant only to observe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Assertions describe expected observations only and are not used to construct the egress allowlist.
- A separately supplied trusted scenario configuration authorizes destinations; absence is default deny.
- RecordingEgress rejects an unauthorized request before treating it as a matching observation, even when an assertion names that authority.
- Tests distinguish authorized-and-expected, authorized-but-unexpected, expected-but-unauthorized, and unconfigured cases.
- This issue establishes the correctness boundary only and does not define the deferred production trust or security model.
close_reason: Completed in 857ed5f with clippy-order correction ace90f4. Trusted outer and flow-declared policies are independent of observation assertions; focused owner/integration tests, mutation kill, strict scoped clippy, and main-tree compile pass.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H6B] Use one explicit clock model for scenario scheduling
description:
## Goal

Remove the mixed virtual-epoch and PostgreSQL wall-clock semantics from scenario scheduling so park, wake, retry, and deadline behavior is deterministic.

## Questions

- Is the POC scenario clock an absolute virtual instant or a relative offset from one captured database instant?
- Which queue operations compare against PostgreSQL now() and which receive the virtual epoch?
- What clock value must be recorded to make failures reproducible?

## Evidence Required

- services/scenario-worker fixed epoch and execution arguments.
- crates/scenarios/runtime scheduler behavior and run-queue SQL using database time.
- Deterministic tests spanning park, wake, retry, and deadline boundaries.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run a case with the scenario-workers fixed virtual epoch while the queue park and due SQL compare timestamps with PostgreSQL now(). The same virtual inputs can be classified differently as wall-clock time advances or when the fixed epoch is far from database time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One documented scenario clock contract governs every scheduling comparison in a case.
- Virtual and database time are translated at one explicit boundary; no query compares unrelated epochs.
- Replaying the same case inputs produces the same due/not-due, park, wake, retry, and deadline results.
- Boundary tests cover equal, just-before, and just-after instants without sleeps.
- No new scheduler service or production time architecture is introduced.
close_reason: Shipped in f64fd80. One absolute ScenarioClock now governs inclusive due classification; queue available_at is an opaque stale token translated only through DatabaseClockBoundary; delay wakes and deterministic retry delay-ms drive scheduling; reports record scenario-epoch-secs with legacy compatibility. Verified on main: 94 scenario/catalog/runtime/worker tests, 4 flowrunner tests, 5 scenario-worker gate tests, proof-integration check, scoped format checks, scenario/worker and flowrunner Clippy (only pre-existing wamn-runtime type_complexity and flowrunner unfulfilled expectation warnings), git diff --check, and live PostgreSQL 18 execution-scoped shift proof (1 passed). Four named mutations were killed in the isolated lane and restored: inclusive comparison, retry delay key, queue state authority, and checked retry arithmetic. No scheduler service or production time architecture added.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H6A] Scope scenario schedule shifts to the selected execution
description:
## Goal

Ensure a scenario case changes scheduling state only for the selected execution and cannot move unrelated future queue rows in the same tenant schema.

## Questions

- Which durable run identity or explicit case-owned row set is available when time is shifted?
- Which scheduler SQL currently selects one earliest row but updates a broader tenant set?
- How should no-row and multiple-row cases fail deterministically?

## Evidence Required

- crates/scenarios/runtime scheduler SQL and services/scenario-worker call path.
- Queue schema, run identity, and case setup/cleanup behavior.
- A real-PostgreSQL reproduction with two unrelated future runs in one tenant schema.

## Steps to Reproduce

Seed two future queue rows for different runs in one tenant schema, select the earlier run as the scenario target, and invoke the current schedule nudge. The selection identifies one row, but the update changes all matching future rows in the tenant scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The schedule-shift operation requires an explicit selected run or case-owned row identity.
- Only the intended queue row or documented case-owned set changes; unrelated tenant rows remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Zero-match, stale-run, and ambiguous-match cases return typed failures without partial updates.
- Concurrent cases cannot shift each others runs.
- A targeted real-database test fails against the current broad update and passes after the correction.
close_reason: Implemented execution-scoped run_queue schedule shifting in a7f3a4e: exact run_id plus selected available_at stale token, cardinality-gated atomic update, and typed stale/ambiguous/incomplete failures. Verified package tests (22 passed/1 ignored runtime; 4 worker), scoped Clippy and rustfmt, plus the exact lane tree passed the ignored PostgreSQL 18 two-session isolation/stale/ambiguity proof.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H5] Repair reorganized build and test commands

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H3] Make ScenarioSchemaName delegate to pg-core Identifier
description:
## Goal

Finish the canonical schema-name boundary by making ScenarioSchemaName delegate PostgreSQL identifier validity, representation, and quoting to wamn_pg_core::Identifier while retaining only the narrower scenario-specific lowercase bare-name rule.

## Questions

- Should ScenarioSchemaName store Identifier directly and translate InvalidIdentifier into its domain error, or should pg-core expose an existing narrow construction seam?
- Which scenario-only syntax and reserved-name rules must remain outside the generic PostgreSQL identifier owner?
- Which callers or tests currently depend on the duplicated error text rather than the stable domain failure?

## Evidence Required

- crates/scenarios/runtime/src/schema.rs ScenarioSchemaName representation, constructor, DDL builders, and tests.
- crates/platform/pg-core Identifier invariants, representation, quoting, and tests.
- services/scenario-worker and integration/test-support callers proving construction remains before every scenario database effect.

## Steps to Reproduce

Compare ScenarioSchemaName::new with wamn_pg_core::Identifier::new. Both independently enforce PostgreSQL's 63-byte limit, while ScenarioSchemaName stores a raw String and never constructs Identifier. A change or correction to the canonical pg-core invariant therefore does not propagate to the scenario boundary, and the repository has two owners for the same PostgreSQL rule even though current scenario behavior is correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ScenarioSchemaName stores or composes wamn_pg_core::Identifier and delegates generic empty, NUL, 63-byte, representation, and quoting invariants to it.
- Scenario-specific lowercase bare-name syntax is enforced exactly once without duplicating pg-core's PostgreSQL rules.
- Raw strings still cannot reach scenario create, reset, set, or drop-schema effects, and scenario-worker constructs every schema type before staging catalog, fixtures, or other database writes.
- Tests prove 63-byte acceptance, over-limit rejection, multibyte behavior, invalid scenario syntax, NUL rejection through pg-core, and non-aliasing between rejected inputs.
- Existing scenario reports, CLI inputs, schema names, and DDL behavior remain unchanged for valid names.
- This issue adds no lease, generation, token, expiry, scheduler, or production topology machinery.
notes: EXTERNAL-REVIEW VALIDATION 2026-07-25: crates/scenarios/runtime/src/schema.rs defines ScenarioSchemaName(String) and repeats value.len() > 63 while crates/platform/pg-core/src/lib.rs::Identifier already owns empty/NUL/63-byte PostgreSQL identifier validation. Preserve the narrower lowercase bare-name domain rule, but store/wrap Identifier and delegate the shared PostgreSQL invariant and representation/quoting to pg-core. Current five scenario schema tests pass; this is canonical ownership/drift debt, not a claim that the shipped scenario behavior is presently unsafe.
close_reason: Completed in d676d7a: ScenarioSchemaName now composes pg-core Identifier, delegates PostgreSQL identifier invariants/quoting, retains only scenario lowercase syntax, and preserves typed pre-effect worker/provisioner paths. Verified 23 runtime tests + 4 worker tests, scoped clippy -D warnings, exact rustfmt/diff checks, and a named delegation mutant.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-H1] Make scenario-worker the authoritative stored-suite execution proof
description:
## Goal

Make the deployed scenario-worker process the single authoritative executor for stored scenario suites and remove the duplicate execution algorithm from the integration gate.

## Questions

- Which existing process or HTTP boundary lets the gate invoke scenario-worker without importing its service library?
- Which selector, case-result, cleanup, and failure semantics must remain compatible with the current suiteexec Job?
- Which lower-level scenario contracts may be shared without creating another composition root?

## Evidence Required

- deploy/gates/suiteexec-job.yaml, tests/integration/src/testkitbench.rs, and services/scenario-worker source and CLI behavior.
- A dependency graph proving tests do not import the scenario-worker deployable as a library.
- A black-box comparison of success, refusal, cleanup, and failed-case behavior.

## Steps to Reproduce

Apply deploy/gates/suiteexec-job.yaml and inspect the container command and resulting process. It runs wamn-gates testkitbench, whose integration module performs its own suite scheduling, execution, assertions, and cleanup instead of invoking services/scenario-worker.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The suiteexec gate invokes the scenario-worker binary or deployed image and does not execute a second stored-suite engine inside wamn-gates.
- Duplicate scheduling, fixture installation, execution, assertion, and cleanup logic is removed from tests/integration; shared code is limited to canonical scenario contracts or clients.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-AUDIT] Audit completed reorganization for structural consistency
description:
## Goal

Perform a read-only audit of the repository reorganization completed through RESTRUCTURE-ORG-3 against docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md, with correctness controlling all naming and structural judgments. No remediation is authorized until the owner reviews the findings.

## Questions

- Are package, crate, module, binary, component, directory, test, and deployment names coherent and consistently applied?
- Does physical code ownership match runtime and architectural responsibility?
- Are package, conformance, integration, system, and orchestration proofs placed at the correct boundary and free of white-box deployment coupling?
- Do all normal, build, and development dependency edges preserve the target-class, service-leaf, bounded-context, product-versus-test, and two-workspace invariants in the restructuring source?
- Which apparent deviations are intentional stable-identity or compatibility exceptions, and which are violations?

## Evidence Required

- Complete workspace package, target, path, and local dependency inventories for both Cargo workspaces.
- Explicit invariant matrix derived from docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md, with pass, violation, or intentional-exception verdicts and exact repository evidence.
- Naming and stale-path searches across source, manifests, build files, deployment assets, test trees, and current documentation.
- Test-tier and dependency-closure maps proving production artifacts exclude scenario/test support and system proofs exercise public deployed boundaries.
- Risk-ranked findings with exact paths, lines, commands, and scope; no speculative style findings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every reorganized deployable, bounded-context package family, component role, proof tier, and repository-only support area receives an explicit structural verdict.
- Every dependency invariant in the restructuring source is checked across normal, build, and development edges, including feature-sensitive or target-sensitive exceptions where present.
- Confirmed findings distinguish correctness or architecture defects from naming debt and deliberate compatibility seams.
- Findings are presented to the owner for review before any source, documentation, deployment, findings-ledger, or remediation-issue change is made.
- RESTRUCTURE-ORG-4 remains blocked pending owner disposition of this audit.
notes:
READ-ONLY AUDIT COMPLETE; OWNER DISPOSITION REQUIRED; NO REMEDIATION AUTHORIZED. Overall: physical reorganization and the shipping dependency graph are substantially coherent, but Wave 4 should remain blocked. HIGH: (H1) deploy/gates/suiteexec-job.yaml runs wamn-gates testkitbench, whose tests/integration/src/testkitbench.rs duplicates stored-suite execution instead of invoking services/scenario-worker; the product worker therefore lacks behavioral proof. (H2) Dockerfile builds only native packages and copies ignored prebuilt components/target WASM into executor, scenario-worker, and gates images; artifact-to-source provenance is not established and the current flowrunner artifact predates source commit ae355c0. This can alias case schemas after PostgreSQL truncation and defeats structural case isolation. (H4) zero of 65 workspace packages has required package.metadata.wamn classification and no repository architecture/state-owner checker exists, so target-class, service-leaf, bounded-context, deployable, and state-owner rules are convention-only. (H5) docs/build-and-test.md still sends runtime/plugin/policy tests to the now binary-only wamn-host package; filters can execute zero matching tests and --lib/old --test commands fail. HIGH INVARIANT GAP: workspace dependency centralization is incomplete, including 11 repeated Wasmtime Git declarations; components has no workspace.dependencies. Current lock resolves a single Wasmtime revision, so no present source-identity divergence was observed. MEDIUM: integration proof and test-infrastructure packages import deployable service libraries; wamn-api has native Postgres/Tokio dev dependencies despite guest classification; root default-members includes all 47 packages; broad Tokio/wash-runtime features are owned at workspace level; conformance has runtime/database closure and exports schema-drift support to other tiers; system guard scans text/direct manifest rather than resolved closure; execution-host naming/role and facade reexports obscure canonical ownership; active runbook/navigation docs retain moved paths. LOW: stale wamn_run_store comment/test and unused system manifest dependencies. PASS: shipping services are leaves; principal contracts do not depend on runtimes/services; shipped guest component closures contain no native dependencies; standard-nodes depends on entity-access and not data-api; executor excludes scenario/test support; scenario-worker includes scenario runtime; production artifacts exclude test support; system package has no current resolved service dependency; two Cargo workspaces and physical hierarchy are correct; no new root peer. INTENTIONAL: wamn-executor retains wamn-run-worker deployed identity; wamn-gates remains compatibility router; direct DB seeding in system proofs is temporary pending a canonical invocation surface. UNRESOLVED/FUTURE: flow-http/invoke boundary is absent; policy for owner-local live tests and broad runtime conformance is not explicit. Evidence was gathered with locked/offline cargo metadata/tree and static source/manifest/deploy/doc inspection only; no compilation, tests, images, or live infrastructure were run. Corrections accepted: the inventory is 47 root-workspace plus 18 component-workspace packages, not one 65-package workspace; package.metadata.wamn is an example mechanism rather than a requirement; Docker context is governed by .dockerignore/COPY rather than .gitignore; local Wasm age is local evidence only. title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-3] Separate product scenarios from repository test architecture
description:
## Goal

Reorganize persisted scenarios, deterministic execution, replay/capture capabilities, repository-only test support, and deployed proof orchestration so product APIs and test infrastructure are structurally distinct and ergonomically coherent.

## Questions

- Which current testkit, flow-tests, doubles, recorders, fixtures, and suite concepts are user-facing product capabilities?
- Which adapters may exist only in scenario execution and must be absent from production serving artifacts?
- Which current gates are package/conformance, integration, or deployed-system proofs, and what public boundary should each exercise?

## Evidence Required

- Current testkit, flow-tests, host doubles, run-worker switches, gates, harness, fixtures, stored suites, replay, pinning, capture, and impact call/dependency inventory.
- Existing proof-class records and all structured gates that protect execution, custom nodes, events, data access, and deployment behavior.
- Artifact-content evidence for production executor and scenario/test compositions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Scenario model, persistence/catalog, and deterministic runtime expose coherent product APIs with one canonical vocabulary shared with execution where appropriate.
- Repository-only fixtures, harnesses, spies, temporary infrastructure, and orchestration do not appear in production dependency closures.
- Production serving artifacts cannot enable scenario doubles or recording through a runtime switch; scenario composition is structurally separate.
- Package/conformance tests live with contract owners, integration tests compose real adapters, and system tests use public deployed surfaces.
- No gate is removed or downgraded until equivalent evidence exists at the correct proof tier.
- Obsolete test-flavored product facades and white-box service-library dependencies are removed, with all retained tests and proof classifications green.
notes:

No audit/backlog work.

Execute as one issue with at most three focused subagents in isolated worktrees and distinct on-disk CARGO_TARGET_DIRs; these are collision-domain lanes, not separately completable issue slices or a review fleet. Lane A owns product scenario contracts: rename test-flavored packages/APIs to scenario-model and scenario-catalog, keep serialized/persisted shapes stable, move run-record pinning/query coupling to the catalog/application side so the model stays a pure product contract, and preserve assertion/replay semantics. Lane B owns capability/artifact separation: move runtime doubles out of platform runtime into scenario-runtime, extract the smallest reusable execution-host core needed by both compositions, make the production executor a service leaf with no scenario dependency or --test-doubles/test-egress switches, and add a separate scenario-worker using the same flowrunner component with scenario adapters. Production credentials/clock/random/egress remain production-only; scenario credentials/virtual time/seeded randomness/recording remain scenario-worker-only. Lane C first produces an exhaustive module-to-proof-tier/path map and then implements only disjoint test-support/test-layout moves: package/white-box tests with owners, conformance under contract ownership or tests/conformance, real-adapter compositions under tests/integration, deployed public-surface journeys under tests/system, and fixtures/infrastructure under test-support. Main-loop integration order: A, B, then C against the composed APIs. Main loop alone resolves Cargo.lock/root Cargo.toml, Dockerfile, README, docs/build-and-test.md, deploy manifests/jobs, shared test CLI wiring, and stale-name/path cleanup. Preserve WIT, JSON, SQL, event-wire, persisted status, metric, OCI/component identities unless an internal package/binary rename is required and all callers are migrated together. Prefer services/executor + services/scenario-worker source/package ownership while avoiding gratuitous Kubernetes/state identity churn. Add dependency/image-content guards proving executor !-> scenario-runtime/test-support and scenario-worker -> scenario-runtime; remove the monolithic service-library dependencies from system tests.

At completion close .7 with exact evidence, commit refactor(wamn-5wd1.7), push origin/main, bd dolt push, report any deferrals as granular beads, and stop before .8.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-2C] Rebuild execution, invocation, scheduling, and event boundaries
description:
## Goal

Restructure flow execution so model, engine, invocation, durable run state, scheduling, standard nodes, event registration/materialization, and deployable shells have coherent ownership and ergonomic APIs. Preserve PostgreSQL as the sole durable orchestration authority and the current WAL to CDC reader to JetStream to materializer path.

## Questions

- Which types form the canonical flow, invocation, run lifecycle, queue/lease, scheduler, node, and event contracts?
- Which run, queue, lease, timer, checkpoint, replay, and flow-registry transitions must share one transactional API owner?
- Where do scheduler decisions end and durable state begin?
- Which WIT/HTTP/event translations belong only in component or native adapter leaves?

## Evidence Required

- Current flow, runner, run-store, run-queue, SQL, nodes, node-invoke, event-wire, event-reg, materializer, dispatcher, worker, flowrunner, and materializer call/dependency graphs.
- Persisted literals, WIT and wire fixtures, SQL builders, retry/resume/replay gates, and event materialization proofs.
- Both native and wasm32 feature closures, including dispatcher-only scheduling dependencies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One canonical vocabulary exists for invocation, run/node status, failure, retryability, and persisted execution identity; adapters translate rather than redefine it.
- Flow graph decisions remain separable from effects while transactionally coupled run/queue/lease/timer transitions are exposed through one coherent durable-state API.
- Scheduling APIs own cron/due/cadence decisions without contaminating guest execution dependencies or creating another durable authority.
- Standard nodes remain guest-safe execution behavior and consume lower shared kernels rather than data-API transport code.
- Event contracts, capture, and materialization retain their distinct privilege/failure boundaries and current delivery semantics.
- Dispatcher, executor/flowrunner, and materializer shells are thin component-first leaves; native CDC remains its narrow protocol adapter.
- Obsolete duplicate types, cross-package SQL composition leaks, and compatibility facades in this bounded context are removed, with existing execution/event structured tests green.
