Evidence: schema byte-drift guard PASS; native execution/event/control suite PASS; standard-node purity PASS; wamn-gates check PASS; flowrunner/materializer/webhook wasm32 checks PASS; node/Postgres/JetStream WIT coherence PASS; builder deployment goldens PASS; strict rustdoc (-D warnings) PASS; root/component locked metadata and invariant diff checks PASS. No live cluster mutation.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-2B] Rebuild data, schema, control, and identity boundaries
description:
## Goal

Restructure the data/schema/control/identity area around canonical models, safe shared data-access primitives, explicit state ownership, and thin effect adapters. Produce coherent guest-safe APIs instead of cross-context implementation reuse.

## Questions

- What canonical API owns catalog-derived entity operations shared by the data API and standard Postgres nodes?
- Which SQL identifier, parameter, and fragment primitives require one audited guest-safe owner?
- How should schema model, compilation, application/control, registry/provisioning, and app_system identity state be organized without mixing decisions with deployment effects?
- Which durable PostgreSQL lifecycle owns each schema, migration, writer, and query API?

## Evidence Required

- Current catalog, API planner, DDL, schema, RLS, seed, migration, impact, registry, provision, sysschema, and SQL dependency/call graphs.
- Existing JSON Schema, SQL, migration, RLS, entity-operation, and drift tests.
- All data-api and standard-node call sites plus current Postgres WIT and adapter boundaries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Data API and standard Postgres nodes consume one canonical catalog-derived entity-access API without either context depending on the other transport or dispatch implementation.
- Security-sensitive identifier and parameter-fragment behavior has one guest-safe owner with adversarial tests.
- Schema model, compilation, and control/application responsibilities have distinct coherent APIs; effect adapters do not leak into guest-safe contracts.
- Registry, provisioning, and project identity state retain separate semantic ownership where their lifecycles differ, and PostgreSQL does not duplicate Kubernetes operating state.
- Every moved durable write/query path has one API owner and preserves existing schema bytes, migrations, tenant semantics, and compatibility unless separately proven equivalent.
- Obsolete facades and duplicate APIs in this bounded-context group are removed, and relevant native/wasm32/database tests pass.
close_reason: Consolidated guest-safe Postgres primitives, transport-neutral entity access, HTTP API adaptation, schema model/compiler/control, and control/provision/identity ownership; removed obsolete facades while preserving deploy SQL, WIT, persisted and wire semantics. title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-2A] Rebuild platform, runtime, node, and builder boundaries
description:
## Goal

Restructure the platform/runtime/node/build area so reusable component policy and runtime capabilities have coherent APIs and every native service or Wasm component is a composition leaf. Remove service-as-library reuse while preserving the WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first target.

## Questions

- Which host code is reusable runtime capability, pure component policy, node execution, or deployable-only composition?
- What is the smallest caller-oriented API needed by the wasmCloud host, node workload, builder conformance path, and execution workload?
- Which concrete HTTP, credential, egress, Kubernetes, OCI, CLI, and Wasmtime types must remain behind adapters rather than leak through shared APIs?

## Evidence Required

- Complete call and dependency inventory for host, builder, node invocation, node guest/SDK/manifest, execution host, and custom-node serving paths.
- Current WIT/node contracts, capability-grant derivation, component import normalization, and artifact identity tests.
- Native and wasm32 dependency closures plus existing node/build/runtime structured gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Builder, executor, node-host workload, gates, and other deployables do not depend on another deployable service package.
- Pure component policy, reusable runtime capability, and node execution APIs have minimal typed inputs/outputs, explicit resource ownership, and no concrete transport, credential, CLI, or deployment types.
- The general wasmCloud host remains runtime infrastructure; eligible platform behavior remains component-first and every retained native exception is isolated to its actual protocol or toolchain responsibility.
- Builder conformance and production node execution use the same canonical policy and node contract without sharing production credentials or service shells.
- Obsolete host-owned public APIs and compatibility paths in this bounded context are removed after consumers migrate.
- Relevant native, wasm32, node, builder, capability, and runtime tests pass without changing product semantics.
close_reason: Implemented coherent component-policy, wasmCloud runtime, node-runtime, and node-host boundaries; removed service-as-library reuse and the host-owned serve-node compatibility path; preserved WIT/product semantics. Verified package checks/tests, builder goldens, metadata, and WIT coherence at commit c76485a.

title: [RESTRUCTURE-ORG-1C] Rehome components, test support, tests, and POCs by role

- Which gate and harness sources are repository test support versus deployed black-box system tests?
- Which component workspace, Docker, Kubernetes Job, fixture, OCI, and documentation paths depend on current locations?

## Evidence Required

- Exhaustive inventory of component-workspace members, non-Cargo component samples, wamn-gates, wamn-gate-harness, deploy/gates assets, and poc/ sources.
- Component cargo metadata and wasm32 build inventory before and after the move.
- Docker COPY, include_str, Kubernetes Job, OCI build/push, fixture, and runbook path-reference searches.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: [SR28] Durable PostgreSQL objects and writers lack an executable ownership manifest
description:
## Goal

Make semantic, migration, schema-source, writer, reader, and drift-gate ownership executable for every Wamn PostgreSQL table and generated tenant-table family, without turning PostgreSQL into a model of Kubernetes or other infrastructure state.

## Questions

- Which checked SQL file or generated schema description is authoritative for each table/family today and in the target?
- Which Rust/component/query paths are authorized writers and readers?
- How can CI discover a new table or write statement without relying on an incomplete source grep?

## Evidence Required

- The current and target state-authority matrices in docs/findings.md F, R, U, and V.
- Exhaustive inventory of deploy/sql, generated tenant DDL, Rust SQL builders, component SQL, migrations, administrative commands, and gate stand-ins.
- Negative mutations adding an unregistered table, second migration owner, and undeclared writer.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A repository-only architecture/state-owners.toml or equivalent has one entry per Wamn PostgreSQL table and generated table family, naming semantic owner, migration owner, schema source, authorized writers/readers, compatibility horizon, and drift gate.
- CI validates the manifest against checked/generated DDL and known query/write owners and fails on an unregistered object, conflicting migration owner, or undeclared writer.
- Temporary multi-owner compatibility paths name an expiry Bead and cannot gain new writes.
- Kubernetes desired/observed state, Secret bytes, OCI artifacts, JetStream state, backups, and telemetry remain in their native authorities; the manifest neither stores nor reimplements their operating model in PostgreSQL.
- SR13 remains the physical DDL/query/stand-in generation and comparison owner; this issue owns accountability metadata and writer enforcement rather than duplicating SR13.

title: [AUDIT-VERIFY-WORKSPACE-TIERS] Measure and select developer, CI, proof, and release package sets

## Goal

Select explicit root and component workspace membership tiers from measured cost and coverage, without making POCs, fixtures, or heavyweight gates part of every developer command or allowing them to disappear from full verification.

## Questions

- Which exact packages belong to the fast native developer loop, product-component build, contract/conformance, full CI, system-proof, and release sets?

- Should Cargo default-members encode the fast sets, or should named aliases/scripts remain clearer?

## Evidence Required

- Cargo metadata for all 38 root and 18 component packages and their target/dependency closures.
- Cold and warm timing, cache, and coverage results for candidate sets on the current development machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Exact machine-readable package lists exist for fast development, product components, contract/conformance, full CI, deployed-system proof, and release.

- Bare developer commands have documented semantics, and a full command still covers both workspaces, all targets, POCs, fixtures, samples, and gates where intended.

title: [SR27] Package roles and component/native dependency rules are not machine-enforced
description:
## Goal

Encode the accepted target package layers, component-first posture, and native-exception rule as executable repository policy rather than naming convention.

## Questions

- Which Cargo metadata fields identify role, target class, bounded context, deployable status, and native-exception rationale?
- Which existing dependency edges are allowed transition exceptions, and what removes each one?
- How should both Cargo workspaces and non-Cargo component samples participate in release-set classification?

## Evidence Required

- The complete root and component dependency graphs in docs/findings.md H and S.
- STR9 package/deployable disposition and the owner-selected D21 component-first rule.
- Negative graph mutations covering a peer composition-root import, guest-to-native contamination, production-to-test-support dependency, and undocumented native service.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every workspace package declares or is deterministically assigned one role, target class, bounded context, and deployable status.
- A cargo-metadata-based check rejects contracts or pure cores depending on effects/deployables, peer composition-root reuse, guest-native contamination, and production dependencies on repository-only test support.

title: [AUDIT-DEC-RUNTIME] Confirm WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first platform target
description:
## Goal

Record the owner-selected development compute target and long-term role of
wasmCloud after the first-principles audit.

## Questions

- Is WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud only a tenant-code sandbox, or the platform runtime
  for trusted platform behavior as well?
- Under what conditions may a platform responsibility remain or become a
  native service?
- Which D16, D17, D21, and D23 obligations survive?
- Which state, deployment, compatibility, provenance, readiness, and rollback
  boundaries constrain later structural work?

## Decision

- Wamn is WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first for eligible trusted and untrusted
  workloads.
- wasmCloud is the platform runtime and capability/placement model, not a
  transitional implementation detail.
- Native services are exceptions only where a responsibility proves that a
  required protocol, toolchain, or capability cannot credibly run as a WASI
  component. Every exception must record the concrete constraint and an exit
  condition. PostgreSQL logical replication is the clearest current candidate.
- Keep and amend D17, D21, and D23; keep D16's hard per-component enforcement
  without inventing product tier sizes.
- PostgreSQL remains the sole durable flow-orchestration authority. Kubernetes
  remains deployment authority. The retained WAL-to-JetStream event path is
  unchanged by this compute decision.
- `docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md` is the highest-priority structural input to
  STR9, but its exact tree and migrations still require evidence-based
  assessment rather than wholesale adoption.

## Evidence Required

- ARC5 and ARC11 alternative comparisons, corrected for the explicit
  WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first product goal.
- STR1 through STR8 deployment, dependency, contract, artifact-provenance, and
  operational evidence.
- `docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md` and its assessed RP-D1 through RP-D9 findings.
- For every proposed native exception: the unavailable component capability,
  required protocol or toolchain, affected responsibility, and exit condition.
- Behavioral parity for any later migration against the retained PostgreSQL
  and JetStream authority boundaries.

## Rationale

The original ARC5/ARC11 recommendation treated compute technology as a neutral
variable and optimized away the component platform. That contradicted the
product goal. Kubernetes deployment authority does not imply native workload
implementation, and PostgreSQL durability does not make wasmCloud incidental.
The component platform is retained while structural problems in composition,
privilege, provenance, readiness, failure containment, and release identity
are corrected.

## Alternatives Considered

- Retain the current hybrid unchanged: rejected because confirmed structural
  and correctness defects still require amendment.
- Kubernetes-native trusted services with Wasmtime only for custom nodes:
  rejected as the default because it contradicts the platform goal; retained
  only as the shape of a specifically evidenced native exception.
- Introduce a durable workflow engine as orchestration authority: rejected
  because PostgreSQL is the accepted sole durable orchestration authority.

## Acceptance Criteria

- D16, D17, D21, and D23 have explicit verdicts and wasmCloud's target role is
  unambiguous.
- Every current responsibility is treated as component-first or routed to an
  explicit native-exception assessment without claiming production topology or
  cardinality.
- PostgreSQL durability, Kubernetes deployment authority, the retained event
  path, and WASI capability isolation remain distinct and coherent.
- STR9 is unblocked with `docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md` identified as its
  highest-priority structural input.
- The decision is not represented as an implemented fix for any open finding.
notes: OWNER DECISION INTEGRATION 2026-07-24: docs/findings.md sections G, I, L, and corrected ARC11 section U now consistently select WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first, retain/amend D16/D17/D21/D23, preserve PostgreSQL durable orchestration and Kubernetes deployment authority, and require an evidenced constraint plus exit condition for every native exception. docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md remains unchanged and is STR9's highest-priority structural input. Validation: docs diff check; U inventory of 24 canonical decisions, 9 RP decisions, and 5 diagrams; targeted Beads lint; and dependency-cycle check all pass. No implementation or finding closure is claimed.
close_reason: Owner decision recorded and integrated: Wamn is WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first for eligible trusted and untrusted workloads; native services require a concrete protocol/toolchain/capability exception and exit condition. Corrected docs/findings.md sections G, I, L, and U; retained/amended D16/D17/D21/D23; preserved PostgreSQL durable orchestration, Kubernetes deployment authority, and the current event path. STR9 is unblocked with docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md as its highest-priority structural input. No implementation or finding closure.

title: [CALLABLE-FLOWS-P3] Enforce attempt deadlines and dispose poisoned instances
description:
## Goal

Enforce absolute attempt deadlines immediately before dispatch and dispose of interrupted instances.

## Normative anchors

FLOW-SPEC rev18 §§10.5–10.7 and Phase 3; POC-PLAN r6 T-NR.

## Owned collision domain

Production host Wasmtime/host-interface/outbound HTTP/DB dispatch bounds and instance pooling/disposal.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** Enforce the persisted absolute deadline immediately before every dispatch with finite Wasmtime, host, outbound HTTP, and DB bounds; interrupted instances are disposed rather than reused.
- **Negative:** Expired work performs no dispatch; no unbounded host call or interrupted-instance reuse is possible.
- **Fault:** Inject timeout/trap at each boundary and prove disposal, fenced attempt state, and no follow-on call through the poisoned instance.

## Validation

```sh
cargo test --locked -p wamn-runtime -p wamn-execution-host -p wamn-runner
cargo test --locked -p wamn-proof-system --lib deadlineproof::tests::
```

## Explicit exclusions

No cancellation request persistence, deadline sweep, child cancellation, or dispatcher edits.

## Hard dependencies

- `wamn-5wd1.54`
notes: Implemented final fenced pre-dispatch refusal for elapsed attempt/run deadlines; attempt windows clamp to run_deadline_at; Wasmtime drive epochs and outbound HTTP/DB waits are finitely bounded; Wasmtime call traps immediately drop the live store and cause executor exit for replacement. title: Epoch interruption support in wash-runtime (carried patch)
description: S1 found wash-runtime 2.5.1 wires NO epoch interruption: nothing calls set_epoch_deadline/increment_epoch, Config::epoch_interruption never set, and stores are created inside the crate so there is no injection point without a fork. The S2 chaos gate (epoch-kill a component mid-transaction, 100x) and the platform's hard-cancellation guarantee (wamn-node design note 3) depend on it. Decide upstream PR vs carried patch; implement before S2's chaos test can run. See docs/p0-results.md S1 'Upstream gaps' #1.
acceptance_criteria: A wamn-host build exists where a running component can be hard-killed via epoch interruption on demand (API or deadline), demonstrated by killing a busy-loop component; approach documented (upstream PR link or patch file).
notes:
RESUME PLAN (pre-compaction; start here after bd prime). DECISION (user): carried PATCH ONLY — no upstream PR.
CONTEXT: S1 (closed wamn-u1u) proved wash-runtime 2.5.1 (git wasmCloud/wasmCloud@8b53285f) wires no epoch interruption. Stores are created inside the crate: crate wash-runtime, src/engine/linked_call.rs fn new_store_from_templates (called from ResolvedWorkload::new_store / new_store_from_metadata in src/engine/workload.rs ~:1161-1180). See bd memory 'wamn-host-build-facts-s1-for-s2-wash' for all build facts (git dep pin, features, bindgen syntax, protoc).
KEY INSIGHT — the patch is SMALL because two of three pieces need no patch:
(1) NO PATCH: enable epoch via wamn-host: EngineBuilder::with_config(cfg) LAYERS (does not replace) — pass wasmtime::Config with .epoch_interruption(true) from crates/wamn-host/src/engine.rs.
(2) NO PATCH: epoch ticker in wamn-host: wasmtime::Engine::increment_epoch() is pub — spawn a tokio task calling engine.inner().increment_epoch() every ~10ms.
(3) PATCH NEEDED: per-store deadline — with epoch_interruption(true) a store with default deadline 0 traps on first increment, so new_store_from_templates must call store.set_epoch_deadline(ticks) (default generous, e.g. u64-large; make configurable — simplest: read env WAMN_EPOCH_DEADLINE_TICKS or a LocalResources config key; keep patch minimal). Kill-on-demand = short deadline + ticker (acceptance allows 'API or deadline').
PATCH MECHANICS: patch file(s) live in OUR repo under patches/ (canonical artifact, committed). Local build: clone wasmCloud/wasmCloud at 8b53285f to ~/dev/wasmcloud (or scratch), git apply patches/*.patch, then in root Cargo.toml add: [patch.'https://github.com/wasmCloud/wasmCloud.git'] wash-runtime = { path = '<checkout>/crates/wash-runtime' } (path inside the real monorepo checkout keeps its workspace=true deps resolving). Dockerfile: add a stage that git clones the rev + applies patches/ + same [patch] (sed/append) so the image build is reproducible. Scratchpad clone from S1 session is gone after compaction — fresh clone needed.
STEPS: 1) add components/busyloop (infinite loop w/ occasional side-effect-free work; wasm32-wasip2 command) 2) write the wash-runtime patch (set_epoch_deadline in new_store_from_templates; plumb tick count) 3) wire epoch_interruption(true) + ticker + deadline config in wamn-host 4) demo: run busyloop as workload/service with small deadline -> killed (trap) while host stays alive; ALSO verify normal workloads (hello, http smoke) unaffected under ticker with generous deadline 5) record in docs/p0-results.md (S1 gaps section follow-up + note S2 chaos gate now unblocked) 6) quality gates (clippy/fmt) 7) bd close wamn-4p3 8) COMMIT (user rule: always commit after every issue — see bd memory workflow-rule-...always-commit).
ENV STATE: kind cluster 'wamn' running (3 nodes, operator+NATS+3 wamn-host pods, hello workload on NodePort 30950); image wamn-host:dev loaded; protoc at ~/.local/bin + PROTOC_INCLUDE in ~/.cargo/config.toml; toolchain 1.97.0 pinned. title: [CALLABLE-FLOWS-P3] Persist cancellation and sweep deadlines
description:
## Goal

Implement durable cancellation, deferred attempt seizure, propagation, and the dispatcher-owned deadline sweep.

## Normative anchors

FLOW-SPEC rev18 §§10.5–10.7 and Phase 3; POC-PLAN r6 T3/T4 cancellation cases.

## Owned collision domain

Serialized run-state cancellation transitions plus dispatcher deadline sweep; CF-CRON must land before dispatcher edits.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** Persist cancellation requests, defer seizure during a live attempt, apply cancellation at attempt completion, propagate cancellation, and sweep bounded expired work with fenced caller/run terminalization and waiter notification.
- **Negative:** Stale fences/generations, cancellation after an irreversible/released boundary, and mid-attempt seizure are refused.
- **Fault:** Race cancellation/deadline/attempt completion and prove first durable outcomes, no double effect, one waiter notification, and bounded sweep progress.

## Validation

```sh
cargo test --locked -p wamn-run-state -p wamn-runner -p wamn-dispatcher
WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5458/wamn cargo test --locked -p wamn-run-state --test cancellation_live -- --ignored --nocapture
```

## Explicit exclusions

No host timeout implementation, post-release child isolation, saga compensation, or unbounded cluster scanner.

## Hard dependencies

- `wamn-5wd1.54`
- `wamn-fqg.14`
- `wamn-5wd1.49`
notes:
cjv.4 (2026-07-17) DEFERRED the host epoch backstop HERE (user decision Q3a): the engine's per-invocation dispatch budget (wamn-runner Plan::set_dispatch_budget, default 10k, FailKind::RunawayBudget) closes the GRAPH-LOOP runaway (review C2-1) — but a single node that never RETURNS (infinite compute inside one node) is out of the engine's reach, and run_worker.rs still sets store.set_epoch_deadline(u64::MAX/2) (= C4-3). When 5.12 lands its epoch-interruption cancel layer, it should ALSO give run-next a finite epoch deadline (or tokio timeout) + handle the trap by RE-INSTANTIATING the flowrunner in RunWorker (a trapped store is poisoned) — the same machinery cancel needs. Until then a single hung node can still wedge a runner replica (lease ages out for failover only if the process dies; a live-but-hung replica renews nothing further, so its lease DOES expire and fqg.2 reclaim applies — but the wedged replica itself never recovers without restart).
Implemented on main in 5a02458 with ownership/docs in a3f3bac. Durable generation-fenced cancellation persists before seizure; live attempts defer seizure and apply it at attempt completion; descendant propagation, bounded dispatcher deadline sweep, fenced caller/run terminalization, and one transactional waiter notification are covered. Caller cancellation stores the exact rev18 HTTP 499 envelope and RFC8785-compatible outcome hash; elapsed post-release deadlines preserve the released caller response while terminalizing the run. title: [S5] Logging capture PoC (9.3)
description: wasi:logging (or stdout capture) in the host emitting OTel logs to Loki with tenant/project/flow/run/node enrichment. Fail branch: logging becomes a P1 workstream with a buffer/agent redesign; do not ship P1 without it — run history depends on the same enrichment. Design: docs/p0-exit-criteria.md S5
design:
S5 DECISIONS CONFIRMED (2026-07-10, user via AskUserQuestion) + LOCKED ARCHITECTURE.

DECISIONS: (a) enrichment = CUSTOM plugin crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_logging.rs (host-injects tenant/project, parses flow/run/node from wasi:logging `context`, owns drop counter). (b) sink = OTel Collector otlp/gRPC receiver -> otlphttp -> Loki 3.x native OTLP. (c) drop visibility = EXPLICIT bounded front queue + atomic drop counter (surfaced as OTel metric). (d) overhead = guest self-times log() via std::time::Instant. (e) gate of record = in-cluster Job (real Loki+collector); local docker for iteration.

KEY ARCH FACT: the vendored observability.rs logs pipeline has a FIXED 2048 BatchLogProcessor queue and ties its OTLP EnvFilter to --log-level -> both bottleneck/misfilter a 10k/s bench. THEREFORE the wamn_logging plugin OWNS ITS OWN OTel LoggerProvider (generous batch queue -> OTLP gRPC -> collector -> Loki), independent of observability.rs. OTel crates are v0.31 workspace-wide in vendor/wasmcloud (opentelemetry/_sdk/-otlp/-appender-tracing) + tracing-opentelemetry 0.32; wamn-host adds them as same-version direct deps (cargo unifies -> single type set, so opentelemetry::global meter for the drop metric matches observability's global provider).

PLUGIN (wamn_logging.rs): struct WamnLogging{ claims: RwLock<HashMap<component_id,{tenant,project}>>, tx: mpsc::Sender<Rec> (bounded=queue_capacity), dropped/accepted/emitted: AtomicU64, provider+logger, drain task }. log(level,context,message) on ActiveCtx: try_get_plugin -> claim by self.component_id (host tenant/project) -> parse flow/run/node/seq/run_label from context JSON -> build Rec -> try_send (NON-BLOCKING); Full/Closed -> dropped+=1 (also OTel observable counter wamn.logging.dropped). Drain task: recv -> optional pace (drain_rate_per_sec, 0=unbounded) -> logger.emit(LogRecord{severity, body=message, attrs tenant/project/flow/run/node/seq/run_label}) -> emitted+=1. set_claim(id,tenant,project) for the bench; on_workload_item_bind reads localResources.config[wamn.tenant]/[wamn.project] for prod. add_to_linker via extract_active_ctx. Knobs via WamnLoggingConfig::from_env: WAMN_LOG_QUEUE_CAP, WAMN_LOG_DRAIN_RATE, OTEL endpoint from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT.

GUEST (components/logspewer, Rust wit-bindgen): world log-bench { import wasi:logging/logging; export overhead: func(n:u32)->list<u64>; export emit-batch: func(count:u32, seq-base:u64, run-label:string, flow:string, run:string, node:string); }. overhead(n): self-time each log() (Instant), return per-call ns. emit-batch: loop log(Info, ctx=json{flow,run,node,seq,run_label}, msg="line <seq>"). Copy wasi-logging-0.1.0-draft wit dep into wit/deps.

SUBCOMMAND (crates/wamn-host/src/logbench.rs, Mode overhead|throughput|saturation|enrichment|all): build WamnLogging, set_claim(BENCH_ID,tenant,project), hand-built SharedCtx store w/ plugin in plugins map, link wasi p2 + wamn_logging, instantiate logspewer via get_typed_func. overhead: guest overhead(1000) -> p50/p99/max; gate p99<50us. throughput: large queue+unbounded drain; pace guest emit-batch to 10k/s x30s (300k); flush; query Loki count(run_label); assert dropped~0, unaccounted=(emitted-delivered-dropped)/emitted<0.1%. saturation: small queue OR slow drain; big burst; assert dropped>0 (visible) AND unaccounted<0.1%. enrichment: query Loki sample of run_label; assert tenant/project/flow/run/node present on every record. delivered=Loki count (primary); cross-check collector /8888 otelcol_exporter_sent_log_records. Env: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT->collector, LOKI_URL, COLLECTOR_METRICS_URL, RUST_LOG=error (fmt quiet), --log-level info.

DEPLOY: deploy/loki.yaml (loki 3.x single-binary, native OTLP /otlp, structured metadata on, generous ingestion limits, filesystem, Service :3100), deploy/otel-collector.yaml (contrib; otlp grpc :4317 -> otlphttp http://loki:3100/otlp; telemetry :8888; ConfigMap+Service), deploy/logbench-job.yaml (image wamn-host:dev, cmd logbench, no cpu limit, initContainer waits loki+collector, OTEL+LOKI env). Dockerfile +COPY logspewer.wasm /bench. Local docker equivalents for iteration.

RISK/NOTE: Loki query label semantics (service.name->service_name label; run_label as structured-metadata filter `| run_label="X"`) verified against LOCAL docker Loki FIRST, then in-cluster. Collector-sent metric is the authoritative cross-check if a LogQL selector mismatches. Downstream (plugin batch queue + collector + Loki limits) sized generously so the ONLY intentional drop point is the plugin front queue (counted) -> unaccounted ~0.
acceptance_criteria: PASS: 100% enrichment (tenant/project/flow/run/node on every record); < 0.1% loss at 10k lines/sec for 30s with rate-limit engaging visibly (surfaced as counter, not silent drops); < 50us per log call in-guest.
notes:
RESUME PLAN (S5 Logging capture PoC 9.3; start here after bd prime, then bd show wamn-7gc). GOAL: wasi:logging from a guest, enriched (tenant/project/flow/run/node) and shipped as OTel logs -> Loki, proving 100% enrichment, <0.1% unaccounted loss at 10k lines/s for 30s with drops surfaced as a COUNTER (not silent), and <50us per log call in-guest.

ACCEPTANCE / DECISION RULES (docs/p0-exit-criteria.md S5, and bd show wamn-7gc): (1) 100% enrichment = tenant/project/flow/run/node present on EVERY record (verify by querying Loki). (2) <0.1% loss at 10k lines/s for 30s (=300k lines) WITH rate-limit engaging visibly: drops must be COUNTED and surfaced as a counter/metric, NOT silent; unaccounted loss = emitted - delivered - counted_drops, gate unaccounted/emitted < 0.1%. (3) <50us per log call in-guest (guest-observed). FAIL BRANCH: logging becomes a P1 workstream with buffer/agent redesign; do NOT ship P1 without it (run history depends on the same enrichment). S5 blocks wamn-yf3 [9.3 production plugin] + feeds wamn-2rl [P0-EXIT].

CONTRACT: wasi:logging@0.1.0-draft (vendored at vendor/wasmcloud/crates/wash-runtime/wit/deps/wasi-logging-0.1.0-draft/package.wit). log: func(level: level, context: string, message: string); enum level {trace,debug,info,warn,error,critical}. Guest imports wasi:logging/logging; copy the wit dep into the guest wit tree (like pgprobe/flowrunner/node-rs did for their deps).

ARCHITECTURE — WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (do not rebuild): (a) wash-runtime plugin::wasi_logging::TracingLogger (vendor .../plugin/wasi_logging/mod.rs) routes wasi:logging log(level,context,message) -> tracing events, enriched with workload.component_id / workload.name / workload.namespace + the guest 'context' string; registered per component in on_workload_item_bind. (b) crates/wamn-host/src/host.rs registers TracingLogger + WasiOtel plugins (operator path). (c) main.rs calls wash_runtime::observability::initialize_observability for ALL subcommands: when ANY OTEL_* env var is present it wires an OTel LOGS pipeline = OpenTelemetryTracingBridge over a LoggerProvider with a BATCH OTLP LogExporter (gRPC/tonic, endpoint from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, default http://localhost:4317) + a traces pipeline + a metrics pipeline; without OTEL_* it is stderr-fmt only. So tracing::info! from the logging plugin ALREADY becomes an OTel log record over OTLP. WHAT'S MISSING for S5: (1) enrichment tenant/project/flow/run/node as STRUCTURED fields (built-in only has component/workload identity + opaque context); (2) a Loki sink + an OTel COLLECTOR (REQUIRED because the host exporter is gRPC/tonic and Loki's OTLP ingest is HTTP -> collector receives OTLP gRPC and exports to Loki); (3) a drop COUNTER surfaced when the pipeline saturates (the default BatchLogProcessor drops on queue-full ~silently); (4) a bench harness + guest fixture.

MEASUREMENT DESIGN (mirror pgbench/flowbench/nodebench Harness/Worker; manual SharedCtx store):
- OVERHEAD (<50us): guest fixture emits N wasi:logging log() calls, self-timing each with std::time::Instant (works on wasip2, proven S3/S4); return mean/p50/p99/max ns. Host log handler MUST be non-blocking (enqueue only) so the guest-observed cost is the boundary + enqueue, not the export.
- BURST/LOSS (<0.1% at 10k/s x30s, drops counted): harness paces emission to ~10k/s for 30s (e.g. call guest emit-batch(n) every ~10ms, n sized to hit rate; batches carry a unique run label + monotonic seq per line). After settle, account: emitted (harness-known) = delivered-to-Loki (Loki count query on the run label) + counted_drops (the plugin/collector drop counter) + unaccounted; GATE unaccounted/emitted < 0.1% AND counted_drops surfaced as a metric > 0 under saturation. Cross-check with OTel Collector internal metrics (otelcol_receiver_accepted_log_records / otelcol_exporter_sent_log_records / _send_failed_).
- ENRICHMENT (100%): query Loki for a sample (or all) records of the run label; assert EVERY record carries non-empty tenant, project, flow, run, node.

TOOLCHAIN/ENV STATE (probed 2026-07-10): cluster kind 'wamn' UP (3 nodes; wamn-system has in-cluster postgres[s2+s3], plus S4 leftovers deployment/serve-node + job/nodebench Complete — can delete). Image wamn-host:dev=a3771a601015 (S4, NO logbench yet). jco 1.25.2, wac 0.10.1 present (not needed for S5). HEAD 5cad811 (feat s4). NEEDED, not yet present: Loki (grafana/loki:3.x, has native OTLP HTTP ingest /otlp/v1/logs) + OTel Collector (otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib; otlp gRPC receiver -> loki/otlphttp exporter). Both pull from dockerhub in kind (network). No cargo/npm installs needed.

DECISIONS TO CONFIRM WITH USER FIRST (AskUserQuestion, recommendations):
(a) ENRICHMENT SOURCE = a CUSTOM wamn wasi:logging plugin crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_logging.rs (mirrors TracingLogger + wamn_postgres): host-injects tenant/project from a component->claim map (registered via a bench set method like WamnPostgres::set_tenant, and on_workload_item_bind from localResources.config in prod), merges guest-provided flow/run/node parsed from the `context` param (the runner legitimately knows these), attaches W3C trace context; emits enriched records + owns the drop counter. RECOMMEND. Alt: reuse built-in TracingLogger + carry tenant as an OTel Resource attr + flow/run/node in the opaque context string (weaker: tenant not host-trusted, flow/run/node not first-class).
(b) SINK TOPOLOGY = OTel Collector (otlp gRPC receiver) -> Loki. REQUIRED (host OTLP is gRPC/tonic; Loki OTLP is HTTP). Confirm exporter: otlphttp to Loki 3.x native OTLP endpoint (fidelity) vs the collector 'loki' exporter (simpler label mapping). RECOMMEND otlphttp -> Loki native OTLP; fall back to loki exporter if label mapping is fiddly.
(c) DROP-COUNTER MECHANISM = an EXPLICIT bounded queue + atomic drop counter in the custom plugin, surfaced as an OTel metric (satisfies 'rate-limit engaging visibly, not silent drops' cleanly + gives control), rather than relying on the OTel BatchLogProcessor's internal ~silent overflow. RECOMMEND. (Sizing the queue so it saturates at 10k/s to force visible drops is the point.)
(d) OVERHEAD MEASUREMENT = guest self-times wasi:logging log() via std::time::Instant, amortized mean + p50/p99/max; host handler non-blocking. RECOMMEND.
(e) GATE OF RECORD = in-cluster Job (real Loki + collector) for loss/enrichment (like pgbench p99); local docker Loki+collector for iteration. RECOMMEND.

BUILD ON: harness pattern crates/wamn-host/src/{pgbench,flowbench,nodebench}.rs (hand-built SharedCtx store: Ctx::builder(id,id).with_plugins(map).build() -> SharedCtx::new; wasmtime_wasi p2 add_to_linker_async + <plugin>::add_to_linker; get_typed_func for simple exports / bindgen! for records; call_async no post_return). Plugin pattern crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_postgres.rs (HostPlugin, impl Host for ActiveCtx, add_to_linker via extract_active_ctx, set_tenant-style registration, on_workload_item_bind from localResources.config). Built-in vendor .../plugin/wasi_logging/mod.rs as the reference to mirror/extend. OTel pipeline vendor .../observability.rs (LoggerProvider + OTLP LogExporter + OpenTelemetryTracingBridge). Deploy pattern deploy/postgres.yaml + deploy/pgbench-job.yaml + deploy/nodebench-job.yaml (no cpu limit = S2 CFS lesson; Job = gate of record). docs/p0-results.md S1/S2/S3/S4 sections for the results format.

STEPS: 1) confirm decisions (a-e) with the user. 2) deploy Loki + OTel Collector (deploy/loki.yaml + deploy/otel-collector.yaml; collector otlp:4317 gRPC receiver -> Loki; a Service for each) + a local docker equivalent for iteration. 3) guest components/logspewer: imports wasi:logging/logging; bench world exports overhead (emit N self-timed) + burst emit-batch(n, seq_base, run_label...) carrying flow/run/node in context. 4) custom plugin crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_logging.rs: enrich tenant/project (host)/flow/run/node (context)/trace; bounded queue + atomic drop counter surfaced as OTel metric; non-blocking log(); a register()/set method for the bench. Wire into host.rs (replace/augment TracingLogger) + mod.rs. 5) logbench subcommand crates/wamn-host/src/logbench.rs (Mode overhead|burst|enrichment|all): instantiate logspewer, link wasi + wamn_logging, drive; overhead gate (<50us guest), burst gate (pace 10k/s x30s, account emitted/delivered/dropped, unaccounted<0.1% + drop counter visible; query Loki HTTP API), enrichment gate (query Loki, 100% fields). Wire main.rs (mod + Command::Logbench). Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT + an OTEL_* enabler in the Job/env. 6) deploy/logbench-job.yaml (no cpu limit; OTEL endpoint -> collector; LOKI_URL -> loki svc). 7) run local (docker) then in-cluster (gate of record). 8) docs/p0-results.md S5 section (numbers + the D-nothing; feeds P0-EXIT). 9) clippy -p wamn-host --all-targets + fmt --check. 10) bd close wamn-7gc. 11) COMMIT (standing rule). Mirror any CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md Build&Test additions.

RISKS: (i) exact loss counting via Loki is imprecise -> use unique per-line seq + a run label + Loki count_over_time, cross-checked with collector internal metrics (accepted/sent/failed) and the plugin drop counter; the GATE is unaccounted loss, so end-to-end accounting matters more than Loki exactness. (ii) OTel Rust BatchLogProcessor drops ~silently -> hence the explicit plugin-owned counter (decision c). (iii) Loki/collector image pulls in kind need network. (iv) making log() non-blocking while still enriched: enqueue enriched record to a bg task that feeds the OTel logger, so guest-observed cost excludes export. (v) forcing visible drops requires saturating a bounded queue at 10k/s — size it so drops actually occur, else 'rate-limit engaging visibly' isn't demonstrated.

title: [S2] wamn:postgres plugin PoC — 2k qps + security gates (2.1–2.2)
description: Plugin implementing wamn-postgres.wit (query/execute/transaction/cursor) with claim injection via SET LOCAL. Measure sustained qps, p50/p99, pool behavior at saturation. Three mandatory security gates: chaos (epoch-kill mid-txn 100x), RLS isolation (10k randomized attempts), injection fuzzing. Fail branch: the platform thesis (safe in-process DB capability) is at risk — stop, redesign the plugin before anything else proceeds. Design: docs/p0-exit-criteria.md S2; docs/wamn-postgres.wit
acceptance_criteria: PASS: >= 2,000 qps sustained single host (single-statement, 8 params, 10-row results), p99 < 10ms in-cluster; graceful connection-unavailable (not hangs) at pool exhaustion. MANDATORY SECURITY GATES: (1) chaos — epoch-kill component mid-transaction 100x, every subsequent checkout transaction-free and claim-free, killed connection destroyed (pool churn observable) never reused; (2) RLS — two workload identities, same table: A gets zero rows of B's data across 10k randomized attempts; permission-denied carries no policy detail; (3) injection — no code path accepts interpolated SQL; fuzz params with SQL fragments, byte-identical treatment as data.
notes:

(a) driver = tokio-postgres + deadpool-postgres. User asked whether sqlx helps future "users write SQL in nodes" (D8): no — sqlx's edge is compile-time checked macros for statically-known SQL; runtime user SQL uses its dynamic path, equivalent to tokio-postgres parameterized queries, and D8 lives above the plugin layer (same WIT interface either way). tokio-postgres exposes sqlstate + constraint names (pg-error taxonomy); deadpool Object take/detach = destroy-never-repool for chaos gate.
(b) Postgres = postgres:18 (user corrected 17->18): in-cluster single-pod Deployment+Service in kind under deploy/ + throwaway docker on host for iteration, same fixture SQL both.

CONTRACT (docs/wamn-postgres.wit = vendored crates/wamn-host/wit/deps/wamn-postgres/package.wit; bindings ALREADY PROVEN by S1 stub): client.query/execute = single stmt in implicit txn, claims injected, committed on success, parameterized ONLY; begin -> transaction resource (drop without commit = ROLLBACK, host guarantee incl. guest crash); transaction.open-cursor -> cursor.fetch(max-rows), empty batch = exhausted. pg-error taxonomy: connection-unavailable (pool exhausted/backend down — MUST be returned gracefully at saturation, never hang), permission-denied (NO policy detail), serialization-failure, statement-timeout, row-limit-exceeded(u64), unique/fk/check-violation(constraint), query-error(sqlstate,msg). sql-value: numeric + timestamptz travel as canonical STRINGS (exact-decimal rule). HOST INVARIANTS: guest never holds socket; claims derived from workload identity, SET LOCAL inside plugin-managed txn, no guest override path; statement timeout + row limits host-side; abnormal instance death DESTROYS the connection (never repooled); no LISTEN/NOTIFY.
WHAT EXISTS: S1 stub crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_postgres.rs — replace canned internals, keep bindgen skeleton (with: keys StubTransaction/StubCursor -> real structs holding pooled conn + txn/portal state). title: [S6] Test host plugin-swap PoC (11.1)
description: Alternate host build: wamn:postgres -> ephemeral schema from template; wasi:http outgoing -> recorder/stub; wasi:clocks -> virtual. The same S3 flow binary must pass unmodified. Fail branch: mock-at-capability-boundary thesis weakened — identify which capability leaked ambient behavior and fix determinism rules (design-note 9) before Epic 11 is planned in earnest. Design: docs/p0-exit-criteria.md S6
acceptance_criteria: PASS: zero component/runner changes between prod and test hosts (same S3 flow binary); flow containing a 24h delay node completes in < 1s wall time under virtual clock; egress spy catches an intentionally added unexpected call.
notes:
RESUME PLAN (S6 Test host plugin-swap 11.1; start after bd prime, then bd show wamn-jy9). GOAL: prove the mock-at-capability-boundary thesis — the SAME flow binary runs unmodified under a PROD host and a TEST host; only the host capability wiring differs. Test host: wamn:postgres -> ephemeral schema from template; wasi:http outgoing -> recorder/stub (egress spy); wasi:clocks -> virtual. Validates design-note 9 (determinism contract). S6 is the LAST open P0 spike; closing it unblocks [P0-EXIT] wamn-2rl (S1-S5 already done).

ACCEPTANCE (docs/p0-exit-criteria.md S6): PASS = (1) ZERO component/runner changes between prod and test hosts (byte-identical flow .wasm runs under both); (2) a flow containing a 24h delay node completes in <1s wall under virtual time; (3) the egress spy catches an intentionally-added unexpected outbound call (recorded egress vs an expectation list). FAIL BRANCH: mock-at-capability-boundary thesis weakened -> identify which capability leaked ambient behavior and fix design-note 9 determinism rules before Epic 11 is planned in earnest.

DESIGN-NOTE 9 (docs/wamn-node-design-notes.md line 50, the contract S6 validates): "Time only via wasi:clocks, randomness only via wasi:random — so the test host can virtualize time (24h delay resolves instantly) and seed randomness. Streamed-payload reads are deterministic given the fixture store. Builder lints imports against the allowlist." Also line 33: "the test host swaps in a fixture-backed implementation with zero node changes."

KEY FINDING: the S3 flowrunner (components/flowrunner) imports ONLY wamn:postgres/{types,client} — NO wasi:clocks, NO wasi:http. So S6's 24h-delay (clocks) and egress-spy (http) gates cannot be exercised by the S3 binary as-is. S6 must EXTEND the runner with a delay node (wasi:clocks) + an http-call node (wasi:http/outgoing-handler), build it ONCE, and prove that one binary runs unmodified under both host wirings. "Same S3 flow binary" = same-across-hosts (prod vs test), not byte-identical to the S3 deliverable; the extension is additive and the S3 flowbench gates (dispatch/hot-reload/resume) must still pass as a regression check.

WHAT EXISTS — the swap seams are ALL already in wash-runtime's CtxBuilder (vendor/wasmcloud/crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/ctx.rs), so the plugin swap is a per-store wiring change, component unchanged:
  * CLOCK: CtxBuilder::with_wasi_ctx(WasiCtx) (line 478). Build the WasiCtx via WasiCtxBuilder with a VIRTUAL monotonic/wall clock (wasmtime_wasi exposes HostMonotonicClock/HostWallClock traits). Prod = default WasiCtx (real clock); test = virtual clock driven by a shared VirtualTime handle the harness advances.
  * HTTP EGRESS: CtxBuilder::with_http_handler(Arc<dyn host::http::HostHandler>) (line 490); the outbound path is CtxHttpHooks::send_request (ctx.rs line 346) which uses the ctx's http_handler. Prod = real outbound handler (to a loopback/echo target); test = a recorder/stub HostHandler that records (method,url,headers) to an egress log, returns a canned response, and flags any request not on the expectation list. SharedCtx already impls WasiHttpView; wasmtime-wasi-http is in the lock (transitive). Also with_allowed_hosts(Arc<[AllowedHost]>) for the outbound allowlist.
  * POSTGRES: CtxBuilder::with_plugins({wamn-postgres: <variant>}). Prod = the S2 WamnPostgres shared pool; test = an ephemeral-schema variant (CREATE SCHEMA from the s3 template DDL per run, set search_path, drop after) for isolation.
Bench harness pattern (pgbench/flowbench/nodebench): hand-built SharedCtx store, wasmtime_wasi::p2::add_to_linker_async + <cap>::add_to_linker + (S6 NEW) wasmtime_wasi_http add_to_linker; get_typed_func / call_async. S3 checkpoint/resume infra (s3.flow_runs, run-until-kill, ON CONFLICT idempotency) is reusable for the parked-wake delay.

DECISIONS TO CONFIRM WITH USER FIRST (AskUserQuestion; recommendations):
(a) DELAY-NODE MECHANISM = PARKED-WAKE (the delay node reads wasi:clocks wall-clock now(), computes wake=now+24h, checkpoints "parked until wake" via the S3 checkpoint mechanism, returns parked; the harness/scheduler advances virtual now >= wake and re-invokes run() -> node sees now>=wake -> proceeds; completes <1s wall). RECOMMEND. Only needs now() virtualized (clean via with_wasi_ctx), reuses S3 resume, matches durable-flow design + POC-F3 cron/parked-wake, and matches design-note 9 ("virtualize time -> 24h delay resolves instantly"). ALT: in-guest wasi:clocks monotonic subscribe-duration(24h) sleep — needs virtualizing the TIMER/poll subsystem (not just now()), much more infra for the same gate.
(b) CLOCK VIRTUALIZATION = custom HostMonotonicClock/HostWallClock in a WasiCtx built by WasiCtxBuilder, driven by a shared Arc<VirtualClock> the test host advances; injected via CtxBuilder::with_wasi_ctx. RECOMMEND (uses the existing seam). ALT: a custom wasi:clocks HostPlugin (more code, redundant with the WasiCtx seam).
(c) EGRESS SPY = a test HostHandler (with_http_handler) that records every outbound request + returns a canned stub response + flags requests not on an expectation list; prod uses a real outbound handler to a harness-spun loopback echo (the S4 serve-node pattern). RECOMMEND. The "unexpected call" gate: the flow's http-call node hits an EXPECTED url; a second intentionally-added call to an UNEXPECTED url must be flagged by the spy.
(d) EPHEMERAL POSTGRES = a WamnPostgres test variant/config that provisions a fresh schema per run from the s3 template DDL (CREATE SCHEMA + clone tables, set search_path), torn down after. RECOMMEND. ALT (simpler): reuse S2 RLS tenant isolation + TRUNCATE between runs (less "ephemeral schema", but proves isolation). Confirm which.
(e) HARNESS + GATE OF RECORD = a new `testhostbench` subcommand (crates/wamn-host/src/testhostbench.rs) that builds the extended flowrunner ONCE and runs the identical bytes under a PROD store and a TEST store; asserts the 3 gates. Needs postgres -> local docker for iteration + in-cluster Job (deploy/testhostbench-job.yaml, co-located, no cpu limit — S2 lesson) as gate of record. RECOMMEND. Confirm whether to also re-run S3 flowbench as a regression gate on the extended binary.

STEPS: 1) confirm decisions (a-e). 2) EXTEND components/flowrunner: add native std nodes `delay` (parked-wake via wasi:clocks now() + S3 checkpoint) and `http-call` (wasi:http/outgoing-handler outbound); add wasi:clocks + wasi:http imports to the world; keep it ONE binary. Re-run S3 flowbench (regression: dispatch/hot-reload/resume still PASS). 3) TEST-host wiring in the harness: VirtualClock (Host{Monotonic,Wall}Clock over a shared advanceable handle) -> WasiCtx -> with_wasi_ctx; EgressRecorder HostHandler (record+stub+expectation-list) -> with_http_handler; ephemeral-schema WamnPostgres variant -> with_plugins. 4) PROD-host wiring: real WasiCtx (real clock), real outbound handler to a loopback echo, S2 shared-pool WamnPostgres. 5) `testhostbench` subcommand (crates/wamn-host/src/testhostbench.rs, mirror flowbench): build flowrunner bytes ONCE (assert same bytes both stores); gate1 = same-binary runs under both; gate2 = 24h-delay flow <1s wall under test (advance virtual clock, assert parked-wake resume); gate3 = egress spy flags the injected unexpected call. Wire main.rs (mod + Command::Testhostbench). 6) deploy/testhostbench-job.yaml (co-located w/ postgres, no cpu limit). 7) run local (docker postgres) then in-cluster (gate of record). 8) docs/p0-results.md S6 section (numbers + the design-note-9 confirmation; feeds P0-EXIT). Consider whether S6 closes [P0-EXIT] wamn-2rl entirely (last spike) -> then wamn-2rl becomes actionable: record p0-results, close D5/D7/9b, sanity dispatch SLOs. 9) clippy -p wamn-host --all-targets + fmt --check. 10) bd close wamn-jy9. 11) COMMIT (standing rule). Mirror any CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md Build&Test additions.

RISKS: (i) extending flowrunner must NOT regress S3 gates — additive nodes only; re-run flowbench. (ii) virtual-clock only covers now(); if the delay is implemented as an in-guest wasi:clocks SLEEP (subscribe-duration) it needs timer virtualization (avoid via parked-wake, decision a). (iii) wasi:http linking is NEW to the host benches (add wasmtime_wasi_http::add_to_linker + ensure SharedCtx WasiHttpView is satisfied in the hand-built store — the bench store must populate Ctx.http/http_hooks; verify the CtxBuilder default provides a usable WasiHttpCtx). (iv) prod http-call needs a real reachable target (loopback echo / reuse serve-node) or the prod-run of the http node fails. (v) ephemeral schema teardown + template DDL must match the s3.* fixtures (deploy/postgres-init.sql). (vi) "same binary" proof = assert identical .wasm bytes loaded into both stores (hash both), not just "no source diff".

Design: docs/p0-exit-criteria.md S3 + docs/platform-plan.md 5.2 (+5.3/5.14/D1/D3/D15).
ARCHITECTURE (from platform-plan): flow JSON is a versioned IR (nodes/edges/per-node config/credential refs) stored in a CATALOG TABLE; "deploy" = flip active-version pointer + NATS doorbell. The FLOW-RUNNER IS A COMPONENT; STANDARD NODES ARE NOT — one long-lived wasm component embeds the standard node library as NATIVE Rust code compiled in; it walks the graph, dispatches node logic (standard node = same-binary call = the <50us dispatch being measured), holds the run state machine. Runner hostInterfaces = union of standard-lib grants (wasi:http, wamn:postgres, wasi:config, clocks); per-node isolation is logical/dispatch-time. Run state CHECKPOINTS TO POSTGRES so a rescheduled runner resumes in-flight runs. 5-node graph: webhook-in -> transform -> wamn:postgres write -> conditional -> respond. NOTE 5.14 proposed dispatch SLOs (sync write-ahead p99<15ms, fast-path<10ms, async warm p50<25ms/p99<100ms) feed P0-EXIT sanity-check vs S2+S3.

DECISIONS TO CONFIRM WITH USER FIRST (AskUserQuestion, recommendations): (a) runner=wasm component components/flowrunner + new wamn-host flowbench subcommand (recommend; mirrors S2, gives dispatch timing + epoch-kill resume) vs host-side runner; (b) dispatch measurement = runner exports walk(n) doing N standard-only walks (transform->conditional->respond, DB write stubbed to a counter) so per-node dispatch is isolated from I/O AND from the wasm boundary (harness times, divides) — recommend — vs per-call export (boundary noise dwarfs 50us); (c) catalog+run-state in Postgres via S2 plugin: tables flows(id,version,active,graph_json) + flow_runs(run_id,flow_version,step_seq,state_json,status) + a business sink table with UNIQUE idempotency key (run_id,step) — recommend (dogfoods S2, literal "loads from catalog table"); (d) hot-reload doorbell: PoC re-reads active version from catalog on a trigger/generation-poll (recommend; real NATS doorbell is 5.14/prod) vs wire actual NATS; (e) flow JSON = minimal ad-hoc schema for the spike (5.1/wamn-34t finalizes later) — recommend; (f) webhook-in/respond modeled as walk input payload / return value (no HTTP server needed for the dispatch/resume gates; HTTP hop is S4) — recommend.

title: test(auth): the per-family denial matrix, as Phase B item 2's single proof pass
description:
## Why this is separate from wamn-0h0g.22.8.4

Split D wired the credential-exactness probe onto every pooled connection, with a PER-CLASS MEMBERSHIP ARM: each authority probes for its own ACL role (AuthorityClass::acl_role, drift-guarded against WorkloadRoleFamily). That arm runs on every connection and is proven by unit tests and two mutants.

What D could NOT carry is the ACL half - the matrix proving each family is UNABLE to perform the other families operations. That is not a per-connection check; it is a property of the grants, and it only means anything against a live server.

The owner ruled 2026-08-26 that PROVEN ONCE GOVERNS THE EVENT - one regeneration, one proof pass, one green - and NOT the internal shape of the proof. The denial matrix is therefore item 2s proof pass, not a fifth split of .22.8. This bead is that event.

## Shape

PER-FAMILY ARMS, ONE GATE BINARY. The matrix is pairwise by construction, so the arms are per-family FOR ATTRIBUTION: a red must name WHICH family over-holds, never merely that the matrix failed. They compose into ONE gate invocation.

Assert the SERVERS OWN ANSWER - has_table_privilege, has_function_privilege, aclexplode, and real SQLSTATE carried back into the Rust classifier. Never the static DDL text; that form is near-tautological here and cannot tell a declaration from a comment.

## Hermetic requirements, non-negotiable

- A throwaway docker postgres:18 is the correct tool. THE KIND CLUSTER IS FROZEN.
- Roles are CLUSTER-WIDE, so ONE FRESH CLUSTER PER ROLE OR GRANT MUTANT.
- DROP OWNED BY before DROP ROLE, inside an existence check: a leftover healthy object satisfies IF NOT EXISTS and MASKS a mutated builder.
- Connect as a role asserted NOT (rolsuper OR rolbypassrls), or RLS is masked and the floor is not being proven.
- A stock container leaves PUBLIC connectable; REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE postgres FROM PUBLIC or a single-database-reach suite false-reds on the harness.
- pg_isready LIES during postgres:18 init-then-restart; loop on docker exec psql -c select 1.

## Already in place

The four role families exist and are provisioned (wamn-0h0g.13.59, wamn-0fqa). The class-to-family projection is exhaustive and pinned to the role strings. The probe infrastructure - ExpectedCredentialIdentity, MembershipExpectation, AclExpectation, AclTarget - already exists in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/credential_exactness.rs and takes ACL expectations today; nothing supplies them yet. This bead supplies them and runs them.
acceptance_criteria: One gate invocation proves, for every ordered pair of authority families, that a principal of one family is REFUSED the operations belonging to the others, asserted from the servers own answer rather than from DDL text. A red names which family over-holds. The gate is hermetic: one fresh cluster per role or grant mutant, DROP OWNED BY before DROP ROLE, and a connecting role asserted to be neither superuser nor bypassrls. Named mutants that widen one family onto another families object, and that drop a denial arm, each fail with the offending family named.
notes:
ARM ADDED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-26, arising from wamn-0h0g.22.6's option (c).

EVERY RELATION CARRYING THE GUEST TENANT PREDICATE MUST HAVE ITS EXPRESSION INDEX on wamn.tenant_key(tenant_id). Machine-checked from pg_index, not remembered: option (c) puts a function call in every governed RLS predicate, and without the matching expression index every guest read goes non-sargable. Checking it here makes the performance cliff STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE rather than a thing someone has to keep in mind.

Pairs with the second new arm the ruling requires: THE FUNCTION DEFINITION IS FROZEN BY PROBE - a digest of pg_get_functiondef pinned - because an attacker who can redefine wamn.tenant_key owns every predicate at once. That probe belongs with the function itself; this bead checks the index coverage.
RIDER to the index-coverage arm, from the converge ruling 2026-08-26: an index that EXISTS UNDER THE WRONG EXPRESSION satisfies CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS and leaves every guest read non-sargable. So this arm reads the EXPRESSION BACK FROM pg_index and compares it - presence alone is not coverage. Per-object converge post-state is asserted on wamn-0h0g.11.49; this bead asserts coverage ACROSS relations.

title: feat(auth): wire the credential-exactness probe on every checkout and the listener
description:

PER-FAMILY ARMS, ONE GATE BINARY (owner ruling 2026-08-26). The denial matrix is pairwise by construction - each family proven unable to perform the others operations - so the arms are PER-FAMILY FOR ATTRIBUTION: a red must name WHICH family over-holds, never merely that the matrix failed. They compose into ONE gate invocation, because proven once governs the EVENT (one regeneration, one proof pass, one green) and not the internal shape of the proof.

Live gates are hermetic: DROP OWNED BY then DROP ROLE inside an existence check, ONE FRESH CLUSTER PER ROLE OR GRANT MUTANT because roles are cluster-wide, and a role asserted NOT (rolsuper OR rolbypassrls) so RLS is not masked. close_reason:
Split D landed, terminal. The credential-exactness probe now runs on EVERY newly-created physical connection, wired as a deadpool post_create hook beside the R18 standard_conforming_strings assertion - verified against deadpool 0.12.3 that post_create PUSHES rather than replaces, so both run, and R18 stays first so its error still surfaces first. It closes the loop split B opened: B keys the pool on (project, class, generation) taken from the resolved url, which is a CLAIM about who will connect; the probe is the server's own answer to whether that claim is true, comparing session_user, current_user and database and asking the server whether the principal really holds the class's ACL role. The duplication is deliberate and DRIFT-GUARDED - the_runtime_role_vocabulary_matches_the_provisioning_families asserts it equals WorkloadRoleFamily::from(class).acl_role(), so the two copies cannot diverge silently.

The listener needs no separate arm, and that is measured rather than assumed: checkout_wiring_listener takes a POOLED connection - its own doc says no direct connection or second pool is created - so the pooled hook already covers it. probe_listener stays unused API.

Five tests. Two mutants, both compiling, both killed: removing the hook from build_pool fails building_a_pool_requires_a_probeable_credential (added specifically so that removal is not an inert change - every other test builds the hook directly and would not have noticed), and drifting one class's acl_role fails the drift guard. Files sha256-verified restored.

NOT DONE HERE, AND FILED: the per-family DENIAL MATRIX is wamn-0h0g.22.15. The membership arm is per-connection and lands here; the ACL half is a property of the grants and only means anything against a live server. The owner ruled that proven once governs the EVENT - one regeneration, one proof pass, one green - so the matrix is item 2's proof pass, not a fifth split of .22.8. title: feat(auth): mint the authority class at trusted composition
description:
Split C of the wamn-0h0g.22.8 four-way decomposition, ~200 lines. Depends on split B.

Class selection originates ONLY in trusted host composition or operator-owned workload binding. Guests never receive, enumerate, set or read credential URLs, and never select their own class.

Mint the class at the four trusted composition sites: services/host (host.rs), services/executor (lib.rs), connection_http.rs and wiring_doorbell.rs.

Plus the HOST-OWNED MATERIALIZER DISCRIMINATOR. Ruling wamn-0h0g.22.8: the localResources.config discriminator is host-owned ONLY IF bound at workload-bind time with runtime mutation refused. THAT PREMISE IS MEASURED AND CONFIRMED - see the 2026-08-26 measurement note on the parent. on_workload_item_bind reads it at bind time, the guest-facing WIT exposes no setter, and the only two production callers of bind_session_claims take host-derived values (the run request plus driver config, and the mounted release manifest plus operator CLI args). Build on the confirmed premise; if a guest write path is discovered while implementing, that is the reopen clause firing and it goes to the owner with the measurement attached.

A separate host group is REJECTED - the materializer already shares the trusted process boundary and the selector provides the isolation grain without inventing another deployment unit.

Mutants: accepting a guest-supplied class, and a default class at any composition site, must each fail a NAMED test.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the four trusted composition sites mints an explicit AuthorityClass. The event-materializer discriminator is host-owned and read at workload-bind time. No composition site accepts a guest-supplied or defaulted class. Named mutants for a guest-selected class and for a default class each fail a named test. No new deployment unit is introduced.
close_reason:
Split C landed, with one half moved to its real owner and said so.

DELIVERED. (1) A REGRESSION IN SPLIT B, FOUND AND FIXED HERE: removing the ambient read left WamnPostgres::from_env deriving its default project from the config field B had just forced to None, so services/host lost the credential deploy/platform injects via secretKeyRef. Nothing in the sweep exercised that path. from_env now takes the credential as a parameter and services/host names its own source at composition, which is the shape services/executor already had; the environment stays the transport, but it is read once at trusted composition as the explicit source rather than as a silent fallback in the config layer. Guarded by the_composed_credential_becomes_the_default_project, which also asserts composing WITHOUT a credential resolves nothing. (2) The guest-authority refusal on checkout_platform was a debug_assert, which compiles OUT of release - the one build where it matters. Now a hard fail-closed refusal, guarded by a_platform_checkout_refuses_the_guest_authority.

MOVED, NOT DROPPED: the host-owned event-materializer discriminator is on wamn-0h0g.22.12 with the measurement. The materializer has NO database checkout path anywhere - crates/events/materializer is pure logic and nothing requests AuthorityClass::EventMaterializer - so a discriminator here would be machinery ahead of demand. .22.12 is what gives the materializer its authority and its connection; the vocabulary, projection, cache routing and class-carrying checkout are already in place for it.

THE STRING-PARSED-CLASS MUTANT, inherited from .22.8.1, REMAINS UNPROVABLE and is not claimed as covered. The class is a compile-time literal at every site, there is no parser and no Deserialize, and no composition site reads one from configuration - but the ABSENCE of a parser is a source property, source scans are barred by wamn-hopk R5, and the workspace has no compile-fail harness. Also repaired a dangling-attribute break I introduced in this split's own working tree: an insertion anchored on a fn line stole the #[test] from guest_and_platform_pool_caches_remain_distinct_under_interleaving, silently making it a non-test.
