title: feat(auth): re-key CredentialProvider and both pool caches on project, class and generation
description:
Split B of the wamn-0h0g.22.8 four-way decomposition. Largest piece, ~400 lines. Depends on split A supplying AuthorityClass.

THE REAL SEAM IS CredentialProvider::resolve in pool.rs - not the believed three-file domain (wiring_resolution.rs, production_claim.rs, claims.rs), which is 3 of at least 12 sites.

TWO ACCEPTANCE-FORBIDDEN BEHAVIOURS LIVE IN StaticCredentialProvider TODAY and this commit removes both:
  1. the or_else DEFAULT FALLBACK - an unlisted project silently falls back to a default;
  2. an AMBIENT WAMN_PG_URL read.
Both are named as forbidden by the parent acceptance. An unknown project must FAIL, not fall back.

Re-key the provider and BOTH pool caches on the triple (project, class, generation). Rotation must not reuse a stale principal, so the selected generation is part of cache and listener identity.

Rewire the 10 in-crate checkout call sites and update the SIX guard literals. Sites beyond the believed set: resources.rs (a checkout_guest call site), credential_exactness.rs (whose module doc already names wamn-0h0g.22.8 as the intended production caller), mod.rs, connection_http.rs, wiring_doorbell.rs.

Mutants: dropping project, class or generation from a cache key, and restoring the ambient or default fallback, must each fail a NAMED test.
acceptance_criteria: CredentialProvider and both pool caches key on (project, class, generation). The or_else default fallback and the ambient WAMN_PG_URL read are gone from StaticCredentialProvider; an unlisted project fails rather than falling back. All 10 in-crate checkout call sites are rewired and the six guard literals updated. Named mutants dropping any of the three key components, or restoring either forbidden fallback, each fail a named test. Credentials remain redacted in every log and error path.
notes:
MEASURED AT 7459a4fc, before writing any code. Two premise checks and one structural finding that changes how the third key component is obtained.

PREMISE CONFIRMED - both acceptance-forbidden behaviours are exactly where the parent said:
  pool.rs, StaticCredentialProvider::resolve - Ok(self.projects.get(project).cloned().or_else(|| self.default.clone())) is the default fallback. An unlisted project silently resolves to the default.
  pool.rs, WamnPostgresConfig::from_env - database_url: std::env::var(WAMN_PG_URL).ok() is the ambient read.

FINDING - THE RUNTIME HAS NO CREDENTIAL GENERATION AND DOES NOT NEED A NEW FIELD.
Every occurrence of generation inside the wamn_postgres plugin today is LEASE_GENERATION, the run-queue lease fence. That is a DIFFERENT CONCEPT from CredentialGeneration, the A/B credential rotation slot, and the two must not be conflated in a cache key.
The credential generation is nevertheless already present in the runtime: crates/control/provision/src/secret.rs documents the WAMN_PG_PROJECTS_FILE entry as { url: <url> } and carries NO generation field, because the provisioner mints the generation AS THE LOGIN ROLE (wamn_app_<scope-hash>_a / _b) and the role travels inside the URL's user component.
So the third key component is DERIVED, NOT DECLARED: it is the user parsed out of the resolved credential source. credential_exactness.rs already parses exactly that via explicit_credential_source and keys ExpectedCredentialIdentity on session_user, which is why that module names this bead as its intended production caller.
This satisfies the parent requirement that rotation cannot reuse a stale principal, because a rotated credential is a DIFFERENT ROLE NAME (_a -> _b) and therefore a different key. Adding a generation field to ProjectConfig or to the projects file would be a second source of truth for something the URL already carries, and the two could disagree.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS SPLIT: the cache key is (project, AuthorityClass, credential-source user). No projects-file schema change, no provisioner change, and nothing to re-key again when split D wires the probe - D verifies the same identity this split keys on.

AmbientCredentialState in credential_exactness.rs already encodes the rule that an explicit source plus ANY ambient source is a CONFLICT, so removing the WAMN_PG_URL read aligns the provider with a contract the probe module already states.
MUTATION RESULTS. Unmutated arm first (165 pass, 0 fail), then apply / test / restore with sha256 at each step, mutating only the production occurrence. All four KILLED, all four compiled cleanly.

B1 SILENT DEFAULT FALLBACK restored (resolve falls back to the DEFAULT_PROJECT entry). Killed by TWO named tests: an_unlisted_project_does_not_borrow_another_projects_credential and the_default_config_is_registered_under_the_default_project.
B2 AMBIENT WAMN_PG_URL READ restored. Killed by from_env_ignores_an_ambient_database_url, and the re-exec CHILD failed too, which is the proof that the child really runs with the variable set rather than passing vacuously.
B3 CLASS DROPPED from the pool key. Killed by two_authorities_never_share_a_pool_key.
B4 GENERATION DROPPED from the pool key. Killed by a_rotated_credential_is_a_different_pool_key.

*** ONE VOID MUTANT, DISCARDED AND RE-DERIVED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT ALMOST READ AS A SURVIVOR. *** The first B2 attempt anchored on the literal database_url: None, which occurs TWICE - once in from_env and once in a test fixture. The guarded replace refused, the script continued, and the run reported 165 passed against an UNMUTATED file. That is not a surviving mutant, it is no mutant at all. Re-derived with a context anchor matching only the production occurrence, and it died.

PREDICTION REFUTED - THERE ARE NO SIX GUARD LITERALS. The parent bead predicted six would need updating. Measured: zero broke, and the reason is that the credential-selection seam has NO external guard literals. The only consumer outside crates/platform/runtime is tests/integration/src/provisionbench.rs, whose three resolve call sites this split patched. tests/conformance references wamn_postgres/mod.rs only as a path in an inventory list.
That is an ABSENCE OF COVERAGE, not a defect to file: split wamn-0h0g.22.8.4 is what puts a probe on this seam.

ONE BEHAVIOURAL NARROWING WORTH KNOWING: a database url naming NO USER is now refused, because it carries no credential identity and pooling it under an empty generation would defeat the key. Every provisioned credential names its generation role, so production is unaffected. One in-crate test fixture used postgres://localhost/... and was updated to name a role; it failed loudly rather than silently, which is the correct outcome.
close_reason: Split B landed. CredentialProvider::resolve now takes the AuthorityClass; both pool caches are keyed on PoolKey(project, class, generation_role) instead of a bare project string. The two acceptance-forbidden behaviours are gone: the or_else default fallback (an unlisted project now FAILS instead of borrowing another project's credential, with the configured default registered under DEFAULT_PROJECT so single-DB deployments and the S2 bench still resolve) and the ambient WAMN_PG_URL read in from_env. Resolution now happens BEFORE the cache lookup, which is what makes rotation correct by construction: the generation is only knowable from the resolved url, and a rotated credential computes a different key. PoolLifecycle::for_class makes the class subsume the lifecycle, so a guest-sql checkout against the platform cache is unrepresentable; checkout_platform now requires a class because the platform lifecycle serves three authorities, and every call site carries the wamn-0h0g.22.14 projection (wiring resolution and run-queue claim to executor-platform, the wiring listener to executor-platform, HTTP authorization inputs to callable-http). Seven new tests including a re-exec child process that actually runs with WAMN_PG_URL set. Four mutants, all killed, all compiling: default fallback, ambient read, class dropped from the key, generation dropped from the key; one void mutant was caught, discarded and re-derived rather than being read as a survivor. The bead's prediction of six guard literals is REFUTED - the seam has no external guard literals; provisionbench.rs is its only outside consumer and its three call sites were patched. Sweep: 1453 passed, 2 failed, 37 ignored, zero compile errors, failing NAME SET identical to the standing baseline pair. LOCAL CARGO GATES ONLY - the in-cluster gate of record has not run.

title: feat(auth): closed AuthorityClass and its exhaustive role-family projection
description:
Split A of the four-way rule-7 decomposition recorded on wamn-0h0g.22.8 (measured ~800-1200 lines across 12-14 files, which is not one commit). One lane, one commit each, A -> B -> C -> D.

NEW MODULE ONLY. NO CALLERS REWIRED - that is split B.

AuthorityClass is a closed Rust enum: guest-sql, executor-platform, callable-http, event-materializer. A new class is a CODE CHANGE, never a configuration string; no wildcard, no default, no From<&str> that can accept an unknown value.

The projection to role family is TOTAL AND EXHAUSTIVE, per the wamn-0h0g.22.14 decision consumer note: ONE role family per AuthorityClass, closed total mapping, no wildcard or default arm. WorkloadRoleFamily already exists in crates/control/provision/src/workload_role.rs and is the projection target.

MEASURED PRECONDITION: AuthorityClass is NOT implemented today - a grep over rs, sql and yaml returns one unrelated hit. Selection today is by bare project string over two lifecycle-split caches, and PoolLifecycle {Guest, Platform} is a POOL-ISOLATION distinction and NOT an authority one: both lifecycles connect with the SAME url from the SAME ProjectConfig.

Table tests over every variant. Mutants: adding a wildcard arm, mapping two classes to one family, or accepting a class parsed from a string must each fail a NAMED test.
acceptance_criteria: A closed AuthorityClass enum exists with exactly the four variants, deriving no Deserialize and offering no string-parsing constructor or inverse of as_str. Its projection to WorkloadRoleFamily is total and exhaustive with no wildcard or default arm, one family per class, pinned all the way to the stable ACL role name the wamn-0h0g.22.14 ruling actually named. Table tests cover every variant. No existing caller is rewired by this commit. Named mutants for a wildcard arm and for a two-classes-one-family collapse each fail a named test. THE STRING-PARSED-CLASS MUTANT MOVES TO wamn-0h0g.22.8.3: it is a source property at this grain, source scans are barred by wamn-hopk R5, and the workspace has no compile-fail harness; at the composition grain it is behavioural and testable, and .22.8.3 already carries it.
notes:
MUTATION RESULTS, re-derived at the call site against the current tree. Unmutated arm run FIRST (91 + 45 pass, zero compile errors), then apply / test / restore with sha256 verified at each step, mutating only the production occurrence. Debug builds.

M1 WILDCARD ARM - replaced the callable-http and event-materializer arms with _ => Self::App. Compiled cleanly, so it is a valid mutant. KILLED by TWO named tests: the_ruled_authority_class_rows_hold and no_two_authority_classes_share_a_family. 89 passed, 2 failed.

M2 TWO-CLASSES-ONE-FAMILY - repointed callable-http onto Self::App with no wildcard, a different shape from M1. Compiled cleanly. KILLED by the same two named tests. 89 passed, 2 failed. Both failed for the intended reason: the ruled row is violated, and two classes share a family.

Production file restored and sha256-verified identical to the pre-mutation original.

M3 STRING-PARSED CLASS - NOT PROVABLE AT THIS SPLIT'S GRAIN, and the acceptance is narrowed rather than a false claim being made. The property is that no parser exists, which is a SOURCE property. wamn-hopk R5 bars proving it with a source scan, and the workspace carries NO compile-fail harness (no trybuild, no compiletest anywhere in any Cargo.toml), so adding one for a single assertion would be machinery ahead of demand.

THE PROPERTY IS NOT DROPPED - IT HAS A HOME AT THE GRAIN WHERE IT IS BEHAVIOURAL. What actually matters is that no CALLER turns a string into a class, and wamn-0h0g.22.8.3 already carries exactly that mutant: accepting a guest-supplied class, and a default class at any composition site, must each fail a named test. A caller-level test can observe that; a type-level test cannot.

What this split DOES structurally guarantee: the enum derives only Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq and Hash - no Deserialize - and offers as_str with no inverse, so nothing in the type itself converts a string into a class. That is a real property; it is just not one a unit test can assert without scanning source.
close_reason: Split A landed. AuthorityClass is a closed four-variant enum in wamn-run-state (NOT beside WorkloadRoleFamily: wamn-control-provision is a dev-only dependency of the runtime, which deliberately links no provisioner, so placing it there would have linked the provisioner into the shipped runtime). It derives no Deserialize and offers no parser or inverse of as_str. The wamn-0h0g.22.14 projection lands as From<AuthorityClass> for WorkloadRoleFamily in provision, where the target type is defined: exhaustive, no wildcard or default arm, one family per class, pinned all the way to the stable ACL role string rather than only to the family. Six tests. Two mutants re-derived at the call site and each KILLED by two named tests for the intended reason: a wildcard arm, and a two-classes-one-family collapse; both compiled cleanly and the production file was sha256-verified restored. The third proposed mutant, a string-parsed class, moved to wamn-0h0g.22.8.3 where it is behavioural rather than a source property - recorded on the bead with the reasoning, not dropped. No caller rewired. Full workspace sweep: 1445 passed, 2 failed, 37 ignored, zero compile errors; the failing NAME SET is identical to the standing baseline pair and the passed delta is exactly the six new tests. LOCAL CARGO GATES ONLY - the in-cluster gate of record has not run.

title: test(runtime): prove behaviourally that a guest never sees the host environment
description:
## Why

Owner spec, 2026-08-26, following wamn-hopk. tests/conformance/src/wasi_ctx_environment.rs is the
last guard over OUR OWN runtime behaviour that works by reading source text - it walks the pinned
wash-runtime checkout and greps for inherit_env and for two pinned WasiCtxBuilder literals.
wamn-hopk left it standing because it reads an external artifact, but the property it guards is
BEHAVIOURAL and can be proven behaviourally, which is strictly better than any scan.

THE PROPERTY: a guest must never see the host process environment. It is load-bearing, not
hypothetical - deploy/platform/executor.yaml and values-host-default.yaml inject a credentialed
WAMN_PG_URL into the HOST PROCESS via secretKeyRef (wamn-mrfr). So the WasiCtx construction is a real
second control.

RIDER, and it is why this is a floor and not the whole story: tenant admission separately DENIES
wasi:cli/environment to tenant code (the closed allowlist in crates/platform/component-policy, via
push_component.rs -> validate_component_admission). This bead tests the RUNTIME FLOOR BENEATH that
allowlist - the guarantee that holds even for a guest that does import the interface.

## The design

Replace the scan with a real guest driven against the real pinned runtime:
  1. host sets a SENTINEL environment variable in its own process
  2. build the engine, construct the context through THE FORK'S OWN Ctx::builder with no
     with_wasi_ctx, which is the fallback path the deleted scan pinned as text
  3. instantiate a guest that imports wasi:cli/environment, calls get-environment, and reports what
     it sees through a host-owned marker function
  4. assert the guest sees an EMPTY environment, and specifically not the sentinel

## THE GUEST IS AUTHORED AS COMPONENT-MODEL WAT, NOT AS A components/fixtures CRATE

This is a deliberate departure from the word "fixture guest" in the spec, on a reason the tree
already recorded. crates/platform/runtime/tests/executor_plugin_no_trap_live.rs states it directly:
a guest compiled from components/fixtures/ makes the test depend on a wasm32-wasip2 build of a
SEPARATE WORKSPACE, and a test that silently skips when that artifact is missing is exactly the
vacuous pass such a bead exists to prevent. components/fixtures guests (busyloop, sockprobe,
connection-http-standard) are driven by IN-CLUSTER gates through mounted volumes, not in-process.
The hermetic precedent is WAT encoded in-process - deadline_gate in crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs
and every guest in executor_plugin_no_trap_live.rs. No cluster, no daemon, no prebuilt artifact, and
no possible skip.

## Delete

tests/conformance/src/wasi_ctx_environment.rs and its mod line in tests/conformance/src/lib.rs.
acceptance_criteria: The source scan over the fork checkout is deleted. A guest importing wasi:cli/environment, instantiated through the fork's own context builder against the real pinned runtime, reports an empty environment while the host process holds a sentinel variable. The test cannot skip. A mutant that hands the guest the host environment fails this test by name.
close_reason:
Landed at the commit following 64ca0aa8. The source scan is deleted; the property is now proven by
running a guest.

tests/conformance/src/wasi_ctx_environment.rs (374 lines, 10 tests) walked the pinned fork checkout
for inherit_env and two pinned WasiCtxBuilder literals. It is gone, with its mod line.

WHAT REPLACES IT. crates/platform/runtime/tests/guest_environment_isolation.rs drives a guest that
imports wasi:cli/environment, calls get-environment, and reports the entry count through a host
marker function. The context comes from THE FORK'S OWN Ctx::builder with no with_wasi_ctx - the
fallback path every executor guest takes, because the executor's context builder never calls it.
Building a WasiCtx in the test would have proven something about the test's builder and nothing about
the runtime.

TWO DEPARTURES FROM THE SPEC AS WRITTEN, both measured:

1. THE GUEST IS COMPONENT-MODEL WAT, NOT A components/fixtures CRATE. The tree already recorded the
reason in crates/platform/runtime/tests/executor_plugin_no_trap_live.rs: a guest compiled from
components/fixtures/ makes the test depend on a wasm32-wasip2 build of a SEPARATE WORKSPACE, and a
test that silently skips when that artifact is missing is exactly the vacuous pass such a test exists
to prevent. The fixtures guests (sockprobe, busyloop, connection-http-standard) are driven by
IN-CLUSTER gates through mounted volumes. The hermetic precedent is WAT encoded in-process.

2. THE SENTINEL IS HANDED TO THE GUEST EXPLICITLY, NOT SET IN THE HOST PROCESS. The first version
called std::env::set_var, which Rust 2024 marks unsafe precisely because it races every concurrent
reader; proving an ISOLATION guarantee with a data race is the wrong trade. The sentinel now rides an
explicit WasiCtx in a POSITIVE CONTROL - a_guest_reads_the_environment_its_context_carries asserts the
guest reports EXACTLY ONE entry when handed one. That is strictly stronger than a host sentinel: it
permanently prevents the negative from passing vacuously, which a one-off mutation would not. The host
process environment is still asserted non-empty in the negative test.

THE RIDER IS RECORDED IN THE MODULE DOC: tenant admission separately DENIES wasi:cli/environment to
tenant code via the closed allowlist in crates/platform/component-policy, reached from
push_component.rs through validate_component_admission. That is the first door; this test proves the
runtime floor that holds for a guest importing the interface anyway. It matters because
deploy/platform/executor.yaml and values-host-default.yaml inject a credentialed WAMN_PG_URL into the
HOST PROCESS via secretKeyRef.

WHY THE POSITIVE CONTROL EXISTS AT ALL: the negative passed on its first run, which is when a test
deserves least trust. The control is what makes the zero mean something.

Gate: full workspace sweep 1439 passed / 2 failed / 37 ignored, no compile errors. Both new tests
green. Failing NAME SET unchanged - connection_http_maps_an_invalid_context and version_identity, both
standing reds. LOCAL CARGO ONLY - the in-cluster gate of record has not run.

title: test(ctl): reconciliation and migration post-checks call the proper database record
description:
## Why

Split out of wamn-0h0g.12.1 under rule 7 on 2026-08-26. That bead's record and drift work landed at
f145fdca, but ONE ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE WAS NEVER TOUCHED: "reconciliation and migration post-checks call
the proper database record."

The lane was fenced to crates/schema/control, deploy/sql and crates/control/provision/tests. The
shells this clause needs are elsewhere and were verified PRESENT at cec008d6:

  services/ctl/src/reconcile_run_plane.rs
  services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs
  services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs

## What this bead owns

Make reconciliation and migration post-checks assert against THE PROPER DATABASE RECORD rather than
whatever they check today, and prove it. The two-plane residency split is what makes this non-trivial:
catalog.releases exists in BOTH planes as two separate relations, so a post-check that reaches the
wrong plane's record can pass while the plane it was meant to guard has drifted.

## Read this before starting - it is the reason the bead exists in this shape

wamn-0h0g.12.1's lane MEASURED and the integrator INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED that the pre-existing live
gate control_portable_store_applies_twice_and_enforces_contract_on_postgres NEVER EXECUTES A SINGLE
RETIREMENT ARM. It applies the current artifact twice to a freshly dropped schema, so every retirement
sits behind a presence probe that is false both times. Proof: neutering the execution-bundle
retirement entirely left that gate GREEN, while the new convergence gate failed.

*** ASSUME THE SAME SHAPE HERE UNTIL MEASURED OTHERWISE. *** A post-check that runs only against a
freshly provisioned database proves the fresh path, not the converge path. R55 is the mechanical test:
does it assert A SECOND RUN IS A NO-OP, or only its exit status?
acceptance_criteria: Reconciliation and migration post-checks assert against the correct plane's canonical record, and a mutant pointing one at the other plane's record fails a named test. The post-checks are exercised against a converged (upgraded) database, not only a freshly provisioned one, and a second run is proven to be a no-op rather than merely exiting zero.

title: fix(traceproof): re-aim the cross-process traceparent gate at wamn:connection/http
description:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-26, decision 1 on the v2.8.0 sync merge (d455ffa8). Two arms of traceproof went RED in the merge sweep: traceproof::tests::p2_host_surface_injects_traceparent_without_guest_help and its p3 sibling, both at tests/system/src/traceproof.rs:499. The in-cluster gate deploy/gates/traceproof-job.yaml fails the same way, because its run() loops the same two HttpSurface arms through prove_surface -> capture_host_traceparent, which now returns None.

NOT A FUNCTIONAL REGRESSION. The injection those arms assert WAS fork patch g2br.4, which the native-alignment ledger drops at this sync. Measured at d455ffa8: zero production call sites for Ingress::builder, outgoing_request or outgoing_handler outside tests, so the vanilla wasi:http egress surface is unreachable from WAMN production. The live outbound path is wamn:connection/http and its injection is proven green - connection_http::the_effect_span_is_injected_onto_the_outbound_request and a_guest_supplied_traceparent_is_not_overwritten both pass in the same sweep.

THE DEFECT IS AN UNTAKEN TEST TAIL (rule 9): the g2br.4 drop did not carry its coverage down with it, leaving a named gate of record asserting a property WAMN deliberately gave up - the stale-defect-report-in-the-gate hazard.

RULED DISPOSITION: delete the two arms and RE-AIM the gate rather than retire it. The live path unit proofs passing is exactly why the gate keeps a cross-process subject: the real-network traceparent witness moves to the surface that actually carries production egress. The gate registry stays at three (m1-gate, socketguard, traceproof) and gate_registry.rs needs no inventory change. The gate doc line records the re-aim and cites the ledger row that dropped g2br.4.
acceptance_criteria: The two host-surface arms are deleted. traceproof proves traceparent injection on wamn:connection/http instead, still crossing a real process boundary to serve-echo and validating the echoed header against a controlled parent. deploy/gates/traceproof-job.yaml still names the traceproof subcommand and the gate registry still counts three. The gate doc line records the re-aim and cites the native-alignment-ledger g2br.4 row. No production behaviour changes.
close_reason:
LANDED. The two host-surface arms are deleted and the gate is re-aimed at wamn:connection/http.

WHAT CHANGED
- tests/system/src/traceproof.rs: the P2/P3 CaptureOutgoing transport, the HttpSurface enum and both host-surface arms are gone. The driver now runs the shipped injector under a wamn.connection_http span carrying a controlled remote parent, takes only the header that injector wrote, and sends exactly that header to serve-echo. One new named arm replaces the two: the_effect_span_injects_a_child_of_the_controlled_parent, which asserts a CHILD - the controlled trace id survives onto the wire under a span id that is NOT the caller's.
- crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/connection_http.rs: inject_trace_context is now pub. The gate drives THAT function rather than a copy, which is the whole basis of its claim.
- deploy/gates/traceproof-job.yaml: the doc line records the re-aim and cites the native-alignment-ledger g2br.4 row. Job args, image and prereqs unchanged.
- tests/conformance/tests/wasmtime_source_identity.rs: DIRECT_CONSUMERS drops the tests/system row, 5 to 4. traceproof reached wasmtime-wasi-http only to drive the P2/P3 surfaces, so the dependency died with them. Removed for the reason wamn-0h0g.15.191 already records one row above: a row kept alive by re-declaring a dead dep asserts nothing. THIS WAS CAUGHT BY THE FAILING-NAME-SET DIFF AND BY NOTHING ELSE - the totals before and after the re-aim were identical at 1479/5, and the two new wasmtime-identity reds exactly replaced the two deleted traceproof reds.
- tests/system/Cargo.toml: bytes, http-body-util and wasmtime-wasi-http removed (orphaned by the deletion); reqwest and wamn-runtime added.

RIDE-ALONGS, both one-line owner-ruled fixes
- crates/platform/component-policy/src/lib.rs drops its citation of docs/archive/data-path/security-db-path.md, a path deleted at ff04842e.
- The MANUAL_STORE_EPOCH_TICK mirror gets its tripwire. Upstream EPOCH_TICK is pub(crate) in wash-runtime src/engine/mod.rs and cannot be imported, so router_driver.rs restates 10 ms; an upstream retune that is not mirrored rescales every node deadline silently. runtime_inventory.rs now pins BOTH literals in the_manual_store_epoch_tick_still_mirrors_the_runtime_ticker, and the constant carries a comment naming the upstream declaration and its file. A source pin was chosen over the timing-band test the ruling also allowed: a wall-clock cadence assertion under a 170-binary parallel sweep is flaky, and a flaky gate is worse than none.

MUTATION, RE-DERIVED AT THE CALL SITE, UNMUTATED ARM FIRST, sha256-verified apply and restore

- M2 inject_trace_context made a no-op (additive early return, no compile break): KILLED by the_effect_span_injects_a_child_of_the_controlled_parent. This is the load-bearing one - it proves the gate observes production behaviour, so an injector that stops injecting fails here exactly as the old gate failed when g2br.4 was dropped.
Both files verified byte-identical to baseline after restore.

GATE. Full workspace sweep, debug, --no-fail-fast: 170 binaries, 1481 passed, 3 failed, 37 ignored, zero compile errors. The failing NAME SET is the merge baseline minus the two deleted arms and nothing added: connection_http_maps_an_invalid_context_to_a_wit_error_not_a_trap, the_terminal_vocabulary_is_class_independent, version_identity. All three are pre-existing standing reds, down from six at ccdf78eb.

*** THE IN-CLUSTER GATE OF RECORD WAS NOT RUN. *** traceproof's gate of record is the Job in the frozen kind cluster, and this session did not and must not touch that cluster. title: feat(publish): call the deployment attestation write from the publish pipeline
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.8.21 landed the attestation write, its wrapper and its proofs under an owner ruling that explicitly excluded a pipeline caller. Nothing calls it, so no release is ever marked deployed. Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.54 makes that load-bearing: a digest is RELEASED iff a deployment attestation references it, and candidates are distinguishable by attestation absence. Without this the release/candidate distinction does not exist at runtime.

There is no A/B/C orchestrator to hang it on. Transaction A (wamn-0h0g.8.7) landed and was then deleted; B (wamn-0h0g.8.19) closed with no implementation; wamn-0h0g.8.22, which was to compose them, closed superseded rather than shipped.

## The blocker, measured 2026-08-26 at 2531c93a

THE FOREIGN KEY CROSSES A PLANE THAT NOTHING BRIDGES.

catalog.deployment_attestations is control-plane only (state-owners.json, schema_source deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql) and its FK on (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version) targets the CONTROL copy of catalog.releases at control-portable-store.sql:56. catalog.releases exists as two separate relations, one per plane; the publish pipeline mints into the PROJECT copy at catalog-schema.sql:131. The control copy lists writers as control-portable-store-installer only.

So a caller writing an attestation for a release the pipeline just minted would violate the control-plane FK. Nothing projects a release across the planes today. Answering that is the first question this bead has to settle, and it is a design question, not an implementation detail: either something projects release identity into the control plane, or the attestation is keyed differently, or the FK moves.

SECOND QUESTION, from the wamn-0h0g.8.21 doorframe note. services/ctl/src/promote.rs:796 calls mint_release_manifest directly and is NOT covered by the wamn-xkgp environment verify arm - deliberately, because promote takes its environment from --target-environment and its --schema is a data schema, so the check does not transpose. If the caller is reachable from promote, promote attests into an environment nothing verified. That is decidable now that a caller is on the table.

## What is already built

The six-part key has a source. wamn-xkgp (f5c3892c) made --org and --project required on both publish verbs and built DeploymentCoordinate at services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs:170. report_deployment_coordinate at :517 LOGS the complete key, and push_release_manifest::run calls it immediately after the OCI push - which is wamn-0h0g.8.21's own stated trigger. That call site is the caller-shaped hole; it does everything but the write.

The Rust binding is wamn_schema_control::attestation::register_attestation, and the single failure translation is translate_failure in the same module.

Note that neither publish verb currently opens a CONTROL connection - both connect to the project environment database - so the caller needs one, which is also where the plane question bites.

## Boundary

This bead owns the caller and the plane question it forces. It does not re-open the attestation write, its wrapper or its proofs.
acceptance_criteria: One publish path writes exactly one deployment attestation for the release it just published, against a control-plane FK that resolves. The cross-plane release-identity question is answered explicitly rather than worked around, and the promote path is either covered by the environment verify arm or documented as deliberately outside it with the reason.

title: feat(ctl): author-wiring refuses without a green gate report for the document's own hash
description:
THE LOOP-CLOSURE LEG CARVED OUT OF wamn-0h0g.7.4 WHEN IT CLOSED AS SPLIT. Owner ruling 2026-08-25: the end-to-end demonstration is ARTIFACT-shaped, not adapter-shaped - document in, gated, published, routed - and the wamn-ctl CLI drives it.

services/ctl/src/author_wiring.rs is ALREADY act 1. It takes the wiring document whole, validates it against the gate scope's admitted catalog.component_library facts, and inserts one immutable row into catalog.wirings keyed by wiring_hash. It runs under the installer principal, which legitimately holds that write - so no grant, no state-owners edit and no regeneration are needed, and the grant door stays shut.

*** THE ONE MISSING PROPERTY: the insert must REFUSE unless a GREEN gate report exists for EXACTLY the document's own hash. *** Today there is no report check at all. author_wiring.rs:17-20 documents that omission deliberately, on the reasoning that a report id in argv would be a second name for an identity the artifact already carries - true about ARGV, but it left the publication ungated. That comment moves with this change.

HASH-BINDING IS AS LOAD-BEARING AS EXISTENCE: a green report for a DIFFERENT document must not authorize this one.

*** THE GUARD IS VERB-ENFORCED, NOT STATEMENT-ENFORCED, AND THE RESIDENCY SPLIT IS WHY. *** The owner's ruling said enforced in the statement, not by caller discipline. That is not reachable: wamn_run.gate_reports exists ONLY in deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql (CONTROL plane) while catalog.wirings exists ONLY in deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql (PROJECT plane), and catalog-schema.sql:958 records that wamn-0h0g.8.5.6 DELIBERATELY removed gate_report_id from the wiring row. So NO project-plane fact exists for a single statement to check. The property is preserved one level out: the check lives INSIDE the verb, is not optional, and no caller path reaches the insert without it. Reaching two planes is idiomatic in this service - promote.rs:150,154 takes source and target URLs; push_component.rs:90 and reconcile_run_plane.rs:140,146 take system_database_url plus another.

report_id IS the wiring hash (wamn-0h0g.8.5.6, see services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs:386). The report row is keyed (tenant_id, wiring_hash) with a passed boolean.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED: only services/ctl/tests/release_manifest_mint_live.rs calls author_wiring or AuthorWiringRequest, at :314, :440 and :467. That test is ignore-gated and env-gated so it will not run in a sweep, but it MUST still compile.

NOT IN SCOPE, DELIBERATELY: no grant change, no state-owners edit, no protected-writes regeneration, no HTTP Publish mount (that is wamn-0h0g.7.7), no release-mint work, no attestation work.
close_reason:
Landed at 7d3b1e4a (lane commit b4313e51). THE WORKING LOOP IS NOW CLOSED END TO END, ARTIFACT-SHAPED: document in, gated, published, routed, driven by the wamn-ctl CLI.

THE PROPERTY: services/ctl/src/author_wiring.rs now REFUSES to insert into catalog.wirings unless a GREEN gate report exists for EXACTLY the document's own hash.

*** THE LANE CHOSE A STRONGER SHAPE THAN THE BRIEF OFFERED, AND IT WAS RIGHT. *** I offered a typed-proof newtype as one acceptable option. The lane refused it as strictly weaker: a proof VALUE still has to be carried to the verb, so it can be minted once and REPLAYED, and its constructor is reachable from the module's own tests. Instead THE VERB PERFORMS THE READ ITSELF - there is no value to mint, forge or replay, and every call queries.

INTEGRATOR-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, because unbypassable is the whole property:
- THE VERDICT IS READ INSIDE THE VERB. author_wiring takes control: &Client - the CONNECTION, not a
  verdict. :425 calls read_gate_verdict; :426 decides. NO CALLER SUPPLIES THE ANSWER, which is
  exactly what separates this from caller discipline.
- ONE INSERT PATH. execute(INSERT_WIRING_SQL) appears EXACTLY ONCE, at :450, in the same function,
  after the guard. There is no path around it.
- HASH-BINDING IS THE QUERY KEY, not a post-hoc comparison: the read is keyed on the hash
  gate_wiring_document just computed from those exact bytes, so another document's green report sits
  under a different key and returns None - indistinguishable from never-gated, which is truthful.
- MY OWN MUTANT, re-derived rather than trusting the lane's: discarding the guard's result makes
  a_wiring_is_authored_only_under_a_green_report_for_its_own_hash FAIL. I ran the UNMUTATED arm first
  against two real databases so the pass/fail pair is meaningful in both directions. Restored
  byte-identical, sha256 96f3cb8b. Throwaway container removed by explicit name, no prune.

FOUR LIVE ARMS over two real databases: never gated refuses; passed=false refuses; a green report at
ANOTHER document's hash refuses; green at its own hash authors, and catalog.wirings.wiring_hash
equals the gated hash. catalog.wirings stays EMPTY on all three refusals.

REFUSAL VOCABULARY: one variant, AuthorWiringErrorKind::Report, under the existing
WIRING_AUTHORSHIP_REFUSAL prefix, with two distinct details separating no-report from gated-and-
refused because operators act on those differently. No parallel taxonomy.

*** THE GUARD IS VERB-ENFORCED, NOT STATEMENT-ENFORCED, AND THE OWNER'S RESIDENCY SPLIT IS WHY. ***
wamn_run.gate_reports is CONTROL-plane and catalog.wirings is PROJECT-plane, and catalog-schema.sql
:958 records that wamn-0h0g.8.5.6 DELIBERATELY removed gate_report_id from the wiring row - so no
project-plane fact exists for one statement to check. Recorded as a deviation from the ruling's
wording rather than absorbed silently.

MY BLAST-RADIUS MEASUREMENT WAS SHORT BY ONE and the lane caught it: I measured author_wiring( and
AuthorWiringRequest and missed the CLI entry point run(AuthorWiringArgs) at
release_manifest_mint_live.rs:887. Four call sites, not three.

GATE: 1453 passed, 14 FAILED, 35 ignored, zero compile errors. Failing NAME SET BYTE-IDENTICAL to
the pre-change baseline - zero new, zero cleared. Passes rose 1451 to 1453 (the unit arms), ignored
34 to 35 (the new live test, env-gated).

FLAGGED, NOT WIDENED: RLS IS UNPROVEN by both live tests because the fixture connects as SUPERUSER,
so FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is bypassed - the known superuser-masks-RLS trap. The session tenant
claim is present for production correctness but untested here. Recorded as inventory on
wamn-0h0g.15.137.

title: feat(management): mount HTTP Publish under the Phase B item 2 grant build
description:
SUCCESSOR CARVED OUT OF wamn-0h0g.7.4 WHEN IT CLOSED AS SPLIT. The other two surviving operations, Gate and GetReport, were already mounted; this is the one leg that could not be.

*** THE DOORFRAME IS ALREADY MEASURED. ITEM 2 CLAIMS THIS WITH THE INVENTORY DONE. *** Mounting Publish in the authoring adapter is not one insert. It is THREE THINGS MOVING, each verified against the tree at 5e4b9c77:

title: fix(ingress): http-route asks wit-bindgen for a world its own WIT does not declare

SAME CLASS AS THE TWO REGRESSIONS c935b88f ALREADY FIXED IN-COMMIT (tools/contract-diff selecting the old package, and three order-sensitive arrays in workspace-tiers.json). This one was missed because no gate ran the components workspace.

title: refactor(catalog): collapse gate_report_id into wiring_hash
description:
RATIFIED at 858169d3, spec section 2.1. catalog.wirings carries BOTH wiring_hash (a real sha256 content hash, CHECK-constrained) AND gate_report_id (bare text NOT NULL, WITH NO FOREIGN KEY TO ANYTHING) on the same immutable row. Two identifiers for one fact. THE REPORT ROW KEYS ON wiring_hash; THE gate_report_id COLUMN DIES.

*** SEQUENCED AFTER wamn-0h0g.8.5.5, NOT PARALLEL WITH IT. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: *** this subject spans TWENTY-SEVEN files and overlaps .8.5.5 on services/scenario-worker/src/test_set.rs and src/store/admission.rs, which .8.5.5 DELETES or rewrites, and on services/scenario-worker/tests/management_live.rs and crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs. Renaming a column through files that are about to be deleted is wasted work, and a concurrent lane would lose to the deletion. LET THE COLLAPSE LAND FIRST, THEN RE-MEASURE - the file count will drop.

MEASURED EXTENT AT 858169d3, twenty-seven files, and it is MUCH WIDER THAN THE CATALOG: deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql, deploy/sql/run-state.sql, crates/catalog/model/src/wiring_activation.rs, crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs, crates/execution/host/src/router_driver.rs, crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs, crates/execution/run-state/src/queue/sql.rs, crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/production_claim.rs and wiring_resolution.rs, crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs, services/ctl/src/author_wiring.rs and promote.rs, services/executor/src/lib.rs, plus tests in run-state, catalog, schema-control, platform-runtime, ctl, conformance and integration.
gate_report_id is threaded through the ENTIRE RUN-ADMISSION PATH because a run records which gate report certified its wiring. THIS IS NOT A CATALOG-LOCAL RENAME.

EXPECT TO MOVE: the admission statement's parameter shape, pinned by crates/execution/run-state/tests/admission_live.rs. tests/conformance/src/schema_drift.rs also names the column.
architecture/protected-writes.json carries gate_report_id and IS MACHINE-GENERATED - DO NOT HAND-EDIT; regeneration is blocked on wamn-8qpy and owned by Phase B item 6.
notes:
*** RE-SCOPED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-25, OPTION (c). READ THIS BEFORE IMPLEMENTING - THE OLD
FRAMING NAMES A TABLE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. ***

WAS: re-key wamn_run.authoring_test_reports on wiring_hash, migrating the existing table.
IS:  THE GATE VERB WRITES THE REPORT ROW KEYED BY wiring_hash. Construction against the
     surviving row, NOT migration of a corpse.

WHY THE OLD FRAMING DIED. The ratified spec used to say authoring_test_reports survives,
re-keyed by wiring-hash. The wave-65 lane refused that and was right: the table's only
production writer was insert_finalized_test_report_sql in
services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs, which the same spec section deletes,
and its only production reader drove off authoring_test_run_reservations, which that section
also deletes. Preserving a table's identity while its writer, reader and keying all die is a
rename wearing a survival ruling.

*** IT WAS ALSO CIRCULAR, AND THAT CIRCULARITY IS NOW DISSOLVED. *** The re-key was THIS bead,
which is sequenced AFTER wamn-0h0g.8.5.5 - so .8.5.5 could not complete without .8.5.6, and
.8.5.6 could not start until .8.5.5 landed. The owner cut it by deleting the table: all three
run-plane authoring_test_ relations now drop in .8.5.5, so nothing waits on a migration here.

THE RE-DERIVATION, from the ratified effect-free premise: an effect-free gate's report is
REPRODUCIBLE FROM THE DOCUMENT - same hash, same verdict, byte-stable. So the table as durable
state protected nothing; it was the composition machinery's memory for per-ordinal resumption
across effectful cases, and the effect-free clause deleted the thing it remembered. Persisted
case-level detail is a CACHE, and a cache for a reproducible computation is not built ahead of
demand. The gate's ONE durable fact is the report row keyed by wiring_hash that publish
consumes, whose home is the report-on-the-wiring lineage.

UNCHANGED BY THIS RULING: the catalog.wirings half. That relation still carries BOTH a real
sha256 wiring_hash AND gate_report_id as bare text with NO foreign key, on one immutable row,
and the gate_report_id column still dies. Only the report-side framing moved.

RE-MEASURE THE FILE DOMAIN BEFORE DISPATCHING. The twenty-seven-file count on this bead was
measured at 858169d3 and is STALE: wamn-0h0g.8.5.5 has since deleted
services/scenario-worker/src/store/drafts.rs and rewritten store/admission.rs and
management.rs, and the completion lane deletes store/test_orchestration.rs and test_set.rs.

SPEC AUTHORITY: docs/PLAN/authoring-stateless-gate-demolition.md section 3.3.1, added at
2a54c32f, records this ruling and the reasoning. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED.

*** A FUNCTIONAL HOLE IS OPEN AND THIS BEAD CLOSES IT. VERIFIED BY THE INTEGRATOR AT dc1fb111, NOT TAKEN FROM THE LANE'S REPORT. ***

wamn-0h0g.8.5.5 deleted the gate-report store, so get-report NOW ALWAYS ANSWERS report-not-found.
services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs:379 unconditionally returns Ok(GetReportResult::NotFound).
The Finalized variant still exists at :356 and is still CONSUMED at management.rs:736, but NOTHING
IN THE TREE CONSTRUCTS IT. GetReportResult::Pending and report_result() died with the reservation
protocol.

So the gate verb hands back a report-id that no query can resolve. That is the deliberate
intermediate state the owner accepted when ruling the table dies, and it is truthful rather than
faked - but it is a real capability regression and it lives until this bead lands.

*** THIS BEAD'S DELIVERABLE IS THEREFORE BOTH HALVES, NOT JUST THE WRITE. *** The re-scope note
above says the gate verb WRITES the report row keyed by wiring_hash. Recording explicitly, because
a written row nobody can read is worthless: GET-REPORT MUST READ THAT ROW TOO, and
GetReportResult::Finalized must have a producer again. If only the write half lands, get-report
still answers report-not-found and the hole is unchanged.

The surviving control-plane home is ready for it: wamn-0h0g.8.5.5 KEPT the wamn_run schema in the
control database - empty, with GRANT USAGE to the author - precisely so this bead has somewhere to
put the row. Only its tables were dropped.
close_reason:
DONE, BOTH HALVES. Landed at dac865db, 33 files, 679 insertions and 444 deletions.
*** THE FUNCTIONAL HOLE .8.5.5 OPENED IS CLOSED. ***

(A) catalog.wirings LOSES gate_report_id. Verified at HEAD: the column is gone from

            Key (tenant_id, wiring_hash), plus passed, summary, gated_at. wiring_hash is

            insert_gate_report at :308, called from the gate verb at :962 - IN THE SAME TRANSACTION
            as the attribution ledger row.
  reader    SELECT_GATE_REPORT_SQL at services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs:380, in get_report
            at :392. GetReportResult::Finalized HAS A PRODUCER AGAIN.
  Only an ACCEPTED judgment writes, and the report id handed back IS the wiring hash, so get-report

*** BOTH MANDATORY MUTATIONS RE-DERIVED BY THE INTEGRATOR AGAINST A LIVE DATABASE, NOT ACCEPTED ON
REPORT. *** Throwaway postgres:18 on port 55451, ground truth by looping on docker exec psql select 1,
ready in 3s, REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE postgres FROM PUBLIC per the harness recipe, container

  1. READ PATH BROKEN (wiring_hash = $2 || 'x'), write path untouched. The named test
     management_surface_authenticates_and_attributes_authoring_commands FAILS at
     management_live.rs:1271 with THE GATE'S REPORT IS NOT RETRIEVABLE UNDER THE ID THE GATE

     *** THIS IS THE PROOF THE HOLE ACTUALLY CLOSED, AND THE TEST IS BUILT TO SHOW IT: ***

  2. EFFECT-FREE CLAUSE NEUTERED at store/admission.rs. Same named test FAILS at :1412 - the

ZERO REGRESSIONS, FULL WORKSPACE, PROVED BY NAME-SET DIFF: 1454 passed, 18 FAILED, 34 ignored, zero

*** THE RETAINED-SHAPE FINGERPRINT MOVED: c898578124... to
a805088d01071b7b68949adb747f6ac110d13a84d33a6515bb27e6f11e949788 ***, measured identical on two

seed catalog.component_library WITHOUT the NOT NULL effects column wamn-0h0g.21.9 added, so the seed

title: fix(runtime): the serving-plane wiring resolver reads component effects without verifying the projection
description:
Measured by wave 64 lane B while landing wamn-0h0g.21.10, and OUT OF THAT LANE'S FILE DOMAIN so it was reported rather than fixed.

wamn-0h0g.21.10 refuted its own premise: effects is NOT unread. There are THREE live readers. Two were guarded at 2d81e5f1 - services/ctl/src/promote.rs decode_component (the chokepoint both load_components and load_one_component use) and services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs load_component_facts. THE THIRD IS STILL UNGUARDED AND IT IS THE SERVING PATH.

crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/wiring_resolution.rs projects component.effects into a JSON wire record at :69, :144 and :282, and deserializes it back into Vec of AdmittedComponent at :773 via serde_json::from_str. Nothing between those points re-derives the projection, so a row whose effects its own audited imports do not derive is handed to the serving plane intact.

THE FIX, and it is small: call wamn_catalog::verify_stored_effect_projection after the serde_json::from_str at :773, before components_used_by_document consumes the vector. The function landed at 2d81e5f1 and needs no argument beyond the AdmittedComponent.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE HERE THAN AT THE CTL READERS: ctl refuses at publication time, which is a human-visible failure an operator can act on. The serving plane is the delivery path, so an unverified projection reaching it is the exact silent-trust case wamn-0h0g.21.10 exists to prevent.

CHECK BEFORE FIXING: confirm wamn-runtime can depend on wamn-catalog without a cycle. wamn-catalog gained a wamn-component-policy dependency at 2d81e5f1, and wamn-component-policy has an empty dependencies table, so no cycle exists through that edge - but verify the runtime-to-catalog direction directly.
close_reason:
LANDED at d7f36905, in process, the same day it was filed. The serving path now calls wamn_catalog::verify_stored_effect_projection over the components a document actually uses, before delivery consumes them.

The loop is extracted as verify_served_effect_projections so the call site is provable BY CALLING IT rather than by scanning for it - a source scan proves a call is written, not that it fires. Two tests cover both directions: a migration-defaulted row whose audited imports reach Postgres is refused, and one whose empty projection its own imports do derive keeps serving. Both confirmed executing by name.

Verification runs AFTER components_used_by_document, so an unrelated impure row elsewhere in the catalog cannot fail a delivery that never serves it.

No manifest change was needed: crates/platform/runtime/Cargo.toml:14 already carries wamn-catalog and wiring_resolution.rs:7 already imports it. No cycle - wamn-catalog depends on nothing in platform.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(catalog): pre-migration component rows default effects to empty, claiming pure without a validator deriving it
description:
Filed by wave 62 lane 3 alongside wamn-0h0g.21.9. The converge ALTER that adds catalog.component_library.effects defaults existing rows to an empty array. An empty array is the POSITIVE statement that a component is PURE - a claim no validator derived for those rows.

INERT TODAY because nothing reads the column yet. *** MUST BE FIXED BEFORE THE FIRST CONSUMER, or the first reader silently trusts a fabricated purity claim. ***

The immutability trigger on catalog.component_library BLOCKS an in-place UPDATE, so the fix is re-admission or a deliberately trigger-disabled backfill - decide which.
acceptance_criteria: No component_library row carries an effects value that no validator derived, before any consumer reads the column.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-25 - OPTION (a): RE-ADMIT THROUGH THE VALIDATOR. It is the ONLY path where the effects value is DERIVED rather than asserted.
*** OPTIONS (b) AND (c) ARE REJECTED WITH REASONS - DO NOT RE-PROPOSE: *** (b) a trigger-disabled backfill FABRICATES A VALIDATOR CLAIM BY HAND - provenance fiction, and the immutability trigger exists PRECISELY to prevent this. (c) leaves a false purity claim readable.
*** IF ANY OLD COMPONENT'S BYTES ARE UNAVAILABLE, THAT ROW'S COMPONENT IS UNPUBLISHABLE-UNTIL-READMITTED. STATE THAT PLAINLY; DO NOT BACKFILL IT. *** A component whose bytes cannot be re-validated does not get a fabricated effects value under any circumstance.
close_reason:
LANDED at 2d81e5f1 as a REFUSAL, not a backfill. Third reader split to wamn-0h0g.21.11.

*** THE BEAD'S CORE PREMISE WAS REFUTED. 'INERT TODAY because nothing reads the column yet' IS FALSE AT THE TIP. *** Three live readers, all independently re-derived by the integrator:
  services/ctl/src/promote.rs:59,67 select effects::text, decoded at :555
  services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs:61 select effects::text, decoded at :564
  crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/wiring_resolution.rs:69,144,282 project it into the serving wire record, deserialized at :773
No code BRANCHES on the value yet and ServingComponent does not carry effects, so the fabricated value is not baked into the release manifest digest - but the bead's safety margin did not exist.

WORSE, AND THE REASON THIS WAS NOT MERELY LATENT: PROMOTE LAUNDERS THE FABRICATED CLAIM FORWARD. promote.rs:747-756 clones each source AdmittedComponent, rewrites only scope, and :808 writes it into a NEW catalog version. pull_verified does not re-derive, because component_artifact_config_bytes binds component_digest, imports and imports_fingerprint ONLY - NOT effects. A defaulted empty array therefore propagated into fresh post-migration rows where nothing distinguishes it at all, which defeats the naive re-admit-at-a-new-catalog-version remedy.

THE RULING WAS SATISFIED WITHOUT A BACKFILL AND WITHOUT A SCHEMA CHANGE. The load-bearing measurement: effects is a TOTAL FUNCTION OF imports ALONE - derive_effects at crates/platform/runtime/src/component_admission.rs:133 takes only ComponentImports and needs no component bytes - and imports is cryptographically attested by the OCI artifact config digest. So a stored row can be RE-DERIVED AND JUDGED WITHOUT ITS BYTES.
  normalize_effects gained its MISSING REVERSE DIRECTION. It previously refused only over-claiming; an import whose package satisfies is_effect_package may now not be absent from the projection. New kind UnprojectedEffect.
  New wamn_catalog::verify_stored_effect_projection applies exactly those admission rules to a stored row - no second derivation, no duplicated policy list, no tautology.
  Both ctl readers refuse a failing row. The promote guard sits inside decode_component, the single chokepoint both load_components and load_one_component use, so the laundering path is closed at its narrowest point.
A pre-migration component importing nothing that leaves the host KEEPS its empty array, now DERIVED rather than asserted. One that imports authority is UNPUBLISHABLE UNTIL RE-ADMITTED, stated plainly and never backfilled - exactly as ruled.

MEASURED LIVE on a throwaway postgres:18, removed by explicit name, cluster untouched: catalog.reject_immutable_row_change fires on BOTH UPDATE AND DELETE as superuser (SQLSTATE 55000, row survives), so re-admission can never replace a row at its existing coordinate. THERE IS NO PROVENANCE MARKER - a fabricated empty array and a derived one are byte-identical and admitted_at is untouched by the ALTER, so imports is the ONLY available discriminator, which is why the fix re-derives from it.

TWO SCHEMA-LEVEL ALTERNATIVES MEASURED AND REJECTED - DO NOT RE-PROPOSE: making the converge refuse on a non-empty table BRICKS THE STORE, because the column never gets added, so re-admission is impossible and the trigger blocks deleting the blocking rows; making the column nullable to NULL-mark old rows diverges the fresh-install shape from the converged shape and breaks the retained-shape fingerprint for clean stores too.

SQL FILES: COMMENT-ONLY. Integrator verified ZERO non-comment changed lines across both planes in both directions. The control-portable-retained-shape-drift fingerprint is computed at RUNTIME FROM pg_catalog (pg_class, pg_attribute, format_type, pg_get_expr, pg_get_constraintdef at control-portable-store.sql:799-845), NOT from file text, so a comment cannot move it. Value unchanged at 1475daeb. The recompute recipe was correctly NOT run and the lane said so plainly rather than claiming two matching runs it did not perform. The 14-name inventory array is unchanged.

GATES: wamn-catalog 56 passed 0 failed 2 ignored; wamn-ctl 107 passed 0 failed 18 ignored; clippy clean on every touched file. Three new tests confirmed executed by name. *** NO LIVE END-TO-END PROOF OF THE CTL REFUSAL PATH RAN - every services/ctl/tests file is ignore-gated on a Postgres URL nothing sets. Local gates only, stated unprompted. ***

JUSTIFIED EXCEPTION RECORDED so a future sweep does not delete them: the static-DDL text pins at crates/catalog/model/tests/component_library_storage.rs:74-86 look like the do-not-pin-static-DDL class, but the BEGIN and END MIGRATION marker strings are LOAD-BEARING - services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs does find(marker).expect(...) and would panic at runtime if one were renamed. Left in place deliberately.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(retire): release_flows and its startup probe lookup die with the legacy flow-artifact tables
description:
MEASURED REFUTATION 2026-08-25, wave 62 lane 1, independently re-verified by the integrator. The owner ruled that catalog.release_flows be renamed to catalog.release_wirings as part 3 of wamn-0h0g.26.18. THAT PART IS WITHDRAWN - the new name would be LESS truthful, not more.

WHY, and this is the whole argument:
- catalog.release_flows FOREIGN KEYS to catalog.flow_artifacts (tenant_id, flow_id, flow_version) at deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:334-335. Its members ARE flow-artifact coordinates. It is not wiring membership wearing a flow name.
- catalog.release_components at catalog-schema.sql:1921 ALREADY IS the wiring-grain release membership: columns wiring_id, wiring_version, component_digest, foreign-keyed to catalog.wirings and catalog.component_library.
- catalog-schema.sql:1917 calls release_flows Legacy IN ITS OWN COMMENT, and says legacy release_flows and execution plans are NEVER converted into release_components rows.
Renaming would put a wiring-named relation pointing at flow artifacts directly beside the relation that actually holds wiring membership.

TWO FURTHER BLOCKERS the lane measured, which stand regardless of the naming argument:
- services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs:63-76 probes to_regclass on catalog.release_flows as part of a ten-relation baseline gate. Renaming without a probe-gated ALTER TABLE RENAME slice makes every EXISTING project database SILENTLY SKIP ALL CATALOG SUB-MIGRATIONS. There is no ALTER TABLE RENAME precedent anywhere in deploy/sql.
- It would edit architecture/protected-writes.json (23 rows, machine-generated, forbidden) and architecture/state-owners.json.

THE QUESTION: release_flows is legacy. Does it DIE with the legacy flow-artifact plane (and if so, under which epic), or does it stay until something else forces the issue? DO NOT RENAME IT.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling recorded on this bead naming release_flows disposition and its owning epic. No rename.
notes:
DECISION ONLY - IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED. Wave 62 landed the other three rename parts; only part 3 was withdrawn.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-25 - OPTION (a): release_flows DIES WITH THE LEGACY FLOW-ARTIFACT TABLES. THE RENAME IS REFUTED AND WILL NOT HAPPEN.
Owner's reasoning, recorded verbatim in substance: a release_wirings name sitting on flow data beside the REAL wiring table is THE NAME-LIE CLASS INVERTED - the rename would manufacture exactly the defect it was meant to cure - plus a silent migration break.

*** RIDER, LOAD-BEARING, DO NOT DROP IT: THE STARTUP PROBE'S BY-HAND LOOKUP DIES IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE TABLE, OR IT SILENTLY SKIPS MIGRATIONS FOREVER. *** The probe is the to_regclass ten-relation baseline gate at services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs:63-76. A table dropped out from under that probe leaves the gate permanently false, and every catalog sub-migration silently skipped - no error, no signal. This is deletion rule 9 applied to a PROBE rather than a test: the lookup is part of the subject's tail.

OWNER ASSIGNED THE SCOPE TO wamn-0h0g.26.16 (release membership and evidence deletion). *** THAT BEAD CLOSED IN WAVE 62. *** This bead therefore CARRIES the deletion under .26.16's subject unless the owner reopens it. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED.
WAVE 63: PREMISE REFUTED. NOTHING DELETED, ZERO FILES CHANGED. The lane measured, refused, and reported - correct behaviour. Integrator re-verified all four load-bearing claims directly against the tree.

*** THIS IS NOT A LEAF DELETION. TWO SURVIVING RETAINED RELATIONS SIT STRUCTURALLY ON TOP. ***
BLOCKER A - catalog.release_attachments (RETAINED) FOREIGN KEYS to catalog.release_flows at catalog-schema.sql:488-489 and control-portable-store.sql:212-213. The RESTRICT drop tripwire FIRES: cannot drop table catalog.release_flows because constraint release_attachments_tenant_id_catalog_id_catalog_version_f_fkey depends on it. CASCADE would AMPUTATE a surviving relation, and publish_release.rs:22-25 states outright that nothing projects a wiring-grain replacement.
BLOCKER B - catalog.require_binding_release_environment() at catalog-schema.sql:1374-1411 is a LIVE BEFORE INSERT trigger on catalog.connection_bindings. It reads release_flows JOIN flow_artifacts inside ONE PL/pgSQL IF expression, so the legacy arm IS PLANNED EVEN WHEN NEW.artifact_hash IS NULL. Proven: after a CASCADE drop, a component-grain insert fails with relation catalog.release_flows does not exist instead of the normal environment-mismatch refusal. connection_bindings is read live by wiring_resolution.rs:221 and :323, run-state admission.rs:296 and promote.rs:101.

WHAT HELD: the PRODUCER half. catalog.register_flow_artifact has NO production caller (only cfg(test) at migrate_catalog.rs:715 and catalog_live.rs); select_release_members_sql has ZERO callers anywhere; live authoring touches ONLY catalog.flow_drafts, so SAVE-DRAFT IS NOT AT RISK.

*** THE RIDER'S REMEDY IS RIGHT AND MANDATORY; ITS STATED MECHANISM WAS WRONG. *** publish_catalog.rs feeds a TRISTATE gate: all-present migrates and returns at :254; all-absent installs; ANY MIX hits the ensure! at :257-260 and HARD-ERRORS EVERY RUN with catalog release storage is partially installed. So dropping without stripping the probe entries does NOT silently skip - it fails LOUDLY AND TOTALLY on every existing project database. Strip them in the same commit regardless.
TWO THINGS THE RIDER DID NOT COVER, both integrator-verified:
  1. publish_catalog.rs:261-263 slices CATALOG_SCHEMA_SQL from the LITERAL string CREATE TABLE catalog.flow_artifacts with an .expect(). *** DELETING THAT LINE PANICS THE INSTALLER. *** Re-point the anchor (catalog.releases) in the same commit. Invisible to relation-level analysis.
  2. THERE IS A SECOND REFUSE-TO-APPLY GUARD: control-portable-catalog-inventory-drift at control-portable-store.sql:741-752 compares pg_tables against a FOURTEEN-NAME LITERAL ARRAY containing both flow_artifacts and release_flows. Any deletion must update BOTH that array AND the retained-shape SHA-256, or the store refuses to apply. The fingerprint recipe alone is insufficient.

(http-admitter), not the AuthorityClass name (callable-http), matching every existing family.

title: fix(security): a live UPDATE grant is justified by a FOR KEY SHARE lock that does not exist
description: Found by the wave-57 ctl-docs lane while correcting adjacent comments; it did not edit these files because they belong to another lane and a half-fix would be worse. GRANT UPDATE (tenant_id) ON catalog.event_registrations TO wamn_app is justified at deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql around 2022 and crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs around 5041 by the claim that callable-flow admission locks the live registration with FOR KEY SHARE. The only production-side FOR KEY SHARE is in wiring_activation.rs, inside a test asserting the wirings hot read takes NO row lock. services/ctl/tests/catalog_confinement_live.rs around 321 carries the same dead citation to admission.rs:384. This is the false-coverage shape the branch keeps hitting, in its most dangerous form: a justification living in a DDL comment, adjacent to a real grant. Its former owner wamn-0h0g.12.29 is CLOSED, so it has no owner. ADJUDICATE UNDER R4: if nothing legitimately holds this authority the REVOKE lands immediately; if the grant is right, the justification is wrong and must be rewritten to name what actually needs it.
acceptance_criteria: Either the grant is revoked, or its justification names a caller that exists. The three citations agree with measured code. No comment claims a lock that no production path takes.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: REVOKE. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED.

R4 exactly: an UPDATE grant whose only consumer is the test proving the grant exists is dormant
authority with circular evidence. Rejected keeping it with a corrected justification - that keeps
live write authority for unbuilt machinery, which is the sentence-not-yet-true class. Rejected
deferring for a live-cluster read - R4 says a revoke never queues.

EVIDENCE, measured 2026-08-24. Only two FOR KEY SHARE occurrences exist in the tree and BOTH ARE
TESTS: crates/catalog/model/src/wiring_activation.rs:247 is inside a cfg(test) module beginning at
line 181 and asserts the wirings hot read takes NO row lock; services/ctl/tests/catalog_confinement_live.rs:328
is the confinement gate replaying this very grant. crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs has
no FOR KEY SHARE and never names catalog.event_registrations.

SCOPE, all in one commit:
- REVOKE the grant at deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql around 2057 and its emitter at
  crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs around 5051, plus the publish_catalog.rs EXECUTE at 467
  and its three has_column_privilege assertions.

ANY row-locking clause, so a revoke on a relation something still locks is a production outage. That
hazard is why this is safe here and only here - nothing locks it.

title: fix(schema): catalog-schema.sql bare LOCK TABLE is illegal under any non-transactional applier
description:
Found by the wave-56 implementing lane while executing services/dispatcher/tests/
read_authority.rs against a real PostgreSQL 18 for the first time.

THE DEFECT: deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql contains a bare LOCK TABLE ... IN ACCESS
EXCLUSIVE MODE (around line 1217 - anchor on content, line numbers drift). PostgreSQL
refuses LOCK TABLE outside a transaction block:
    ERROR: LOCK TABLE can only be used in transaction blocks

TWO APPLY PATHS DISAGREE ABOUT ONE FILE:
- PRODUCTION applies it via tokio_postgres batch_execute (services/ctl/src/
  publish_catalog.rs, around line 57). batch_execute wraps a multi-statement simple query
  in an IMPLICIT TRANSACTION, so the bare LOCK TABLE is legal there. This is why the
  defect has never been seen in production.
- read_authority.rs applies the same file via psql -f - with AUTOCOMMIT, where it is
  illegal. The DDL apply fails before anything else runs.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE GATE: the file is the schema of record. Any consumer that
applies it with psql, or with any client that does not wrap it in a transaction, fails at
that statement. That includes an operator applying it by hand during incident recovery,
which is exactly when the failure is least welcome.

SCOPE:
1. Make the statement safe under both apply paths - wrap it in an explicit BEGIN/COMMIT,
   or establish that every applier must supply a transaction and state that requirement
   in the file itself. Prefer the former: the file should not depend on how it is applied.
2. SWEEP for other appliers. Find every path that feeds deploy/sql/*.sql to psql or to any
   non-transactional client, and every other statement in those files that is illegal
   outside a transaction block. A single-instance fix here would be the single-element-loop
   fingerprint this branch has been bitten by before.

DISCOVERY CONTEXT: this gate had almost certainly never executed. WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL is
set by nothing in the repository, and the test self-skips silently when it is unset, so an
ordinary sweep reports 1 passed. The lane set the variable by hand against a throwaway
container to find this.
acceptance_criteria: deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql applies cleanly under BOTH tokio_postgres batch_execute and psql with autocommit. Every other applier of deploy/sql/*.sql is swept for the same class of statement, and the sweep result is recorded on this bead - a single-instance fix without the sweep does not close it.
close_reason: LANDED as commit 200517a4 on deploy-simplification. Premise CONFIRMED, not refuted: reproduced as ERROR LOCK TABLE can only be used in transaction blocks at catalog-schema.sql:1218 under psql autocommit. FIX: wrapped the WHOLE FILE in BEGIN/COMMIT, not just the LOCK. Wrapping only the LOCK region would have BROKEN PRODUCTION - under batch_execute a mid-file BEGIN promotes the already-open implicit transaction to explicit, so the COMMIT would commit everything before it and split the file's atomicity into segments. Whole-file wrapping is today's production semantics made explicit. PROVEN BOTH WAYS against postgres:18.6: psql -f autocommit exit 0 (was 3); the batch_execute wire shape exit 0; and atomicity verified by replacing the closing COMMIT with SELECT 1/0, after which the catalog schema was absent, so it is still one transaction. THE SWEEP, which this bead required to close: FIVE appliers feed deploy/sql/*.sql to a non-transactional client, not one - read_authority.rs (the defect site), ops_storage.rs, control_storage.rs, project-state/tests/schema.rs and authority.rs; the last four were clean. Exactly ONE illegal statement exists: the bare LOCK. The two LOCKs in control-portable-store.sql sit inside DO blocks, which always run in a transaction, and were measured legal. THE INVERSE CLASS WAS ALSO SWEPT: only postgres-init.sql is illegal INSIDE a transaction (CREATE DATABASE plus the psql meta-command backslash-connect); it is psql-only by construction and must NOT be wrapped. Reconciler-generated SQL audited too - every LOCK TABLE in run_plane.rs reaches PostgreSQL via batch_execute, so a lone-LOCK action would fail, but every emitter always pairs the LOCK with at least one DO, ALTER or DROP, so no lone-LOCK action exists. Consequential edits in run_plane.rs: table_section now stops at COMMIT so a repair action does not carry transaction control into the caller's batch. TWO FURTHER DEFECTS EXPOSED IN THE DISCOVERY GATE, which had almost certainly never run because WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL is set by nothing in the repository: the run seed predated the environment-policy trigger and was fixed in scope; the non-vacuity arm lost its principal to the .12.20-.12.29 confinement and is FILED AS wamn-dsyn, not forced.

title: test(ctl): prove publish-release actually calls its wiring-compatibility gate
description:
THE SAME DEFECT AS wamn-vr1q, ON A DIFFERENT AND WORSE CALL SITE. Found by the wave-56
measurement pass and confirmed independently by the implementing lane, which was told
NOT to fix it so this could be filed and priced on its own.

THE SITE: services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs, fn resolve_current_closure, calls
validate_wiring_compatibility(and document, scope, component_facts) at line 613 (anchor
on content - line numbers drift). Same validator, same crate, same load_component_facts
as author_wiring.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN wamn-vr1q's SITE:
1. MintManifestErrorKind::Component has THREE construction sites (around 507, 615, 640)
   and ZERO assertion sites anywhere in the repository. Nothing anywhere asserts that
   this refusal can happen.
2. Deleting the gate does not merely admit a bad wiring - it turns what should be a
   typed refusal into the panic .expect("the semantic gate resolved every wiring node")
   about 25 lines below. So the failure mode is a crash on a user-supplied document,
   not a silent admission.
3. release_manifest_mint_live.rs asserts MintManifestErrorKind::Wiring and
   ClosureConflict, but never Component - so the gate looks covered from the outside.

THE FIX SHAPE, measured: one more arm in services/ctl/tests/release_manifest_mint_live.rs,
the file wamn-vr1q just opened, roughly 15 lines. Drive the publish path with a document
naming a component that has no admitted fact in scope; assert
MintManifestErrorKind::Component specifically.

*** ASSERT THE KIND, NOT is_err. *** The same vacuity hazard wamn-vr1q hit applies: a
neighbouring failure (an FK, a missing seed) can return a DIFFERENT error kind and an
is_err-only assertion passes against the bypass mutant while proving nothing.

*** MUTATE THE CALL SITE, NOT THE FUNCTION BODY. *** The validator is already proven
correct; the defect is that nothing pins its invocation. A mutant inside
validate_wiring_compatibility proves nothing here.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE RECURRING SHAPE on this branch (wamn-vr1q author_wiring,
wamn-qk15 build_engine_sized socket policy, and this): a function is proven correct and
nothing proves the production path calls it. Worth noting on any future review of the ctl
verbs.
acceptance_criteria: A live arm drives the publish path with a document naming a component that has no admitted fact in scope, and asserts MintManifestErrorKind::Component specifically - not is_err. Replacing the validate_wiring_compatibility call in resolve_current_closure with its success value fails that named test. The mutant is applied at the CALL SITE, not inside the validator.
notes: EVIDENCE. Commit 83ee6868, test a_wiring_node_with_no_admitted_component_fact_refuses_the_mint. THE DEFECT WAS REAL AND MEASURED: the pre-existing current_component_and_wiring_facts_freeze_one_v2_manifest PASSES with the gate deleted, so the call site was genuinely unpinned. MintManifestErrorKind::Component had 3 construction sites and ZERO assertion sites repo-wide before this. Mutant applied AT THE CALL SITE in resolve_current_closure, publish_release.rs sha256 0cae1478 before, 4d0bf90f mutated, 0cae1478 restored byte-identical and absent from the commit. THE MUTANT FAILED THE NAMED TEST in the predicted way - a panic at the semantic gate resolved every wiring node, a crash on a user-supplied document rather than a refusal. Assertion is assert_eq on kind, never is_err. REFUTED ALONG THE WAY: withdrawing the fact via DELETE FROM catalog.component_library is impossible - catalog.reject_immutable_row_change fires BEFORE UPDATE and DELETE, so an admitted fact can never be withdrawn from under a gated wiring and that drift scenario does not exist. The arm injects a catalog.wirings row instead. Shared fixture renamed corrupt_stored_wiring_hash to inject_stored_wiring because both call sites now write rows unreachable through author-wiring and only one is about a corrupt hash. FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE RECURRING SHAPE REPORTED, NOT FIXED: push_release_manifest.rs verify_manifest_layout is unit-proven in-file but its production invocation at line 390 inside probe_exact_artifact is driven only by an ignored test gated on a live OCI registry; all five ReleaseManifestPublishErrorKind variants have zero assertions in any tests directory.

title: test(ctl): prove author-wiring actually calls its gate, not just that the gate gates
description:
Filed 2026-08-23 by the wave-55 integrator. THE LANE DISCLOSED THIS GAP IN ITS OWN DEFERRAL LIST; THE INTEGRATOR'S INDEPENDENT MUTATION PASS THEN PROVED IT IS NOT THEORETICAL.

*** A SURVIVING MUTANT EXISTS ON deploy-simplification TODAY. *** In services/ctl/src/author_wiring.rs, replace the call-site line

    let wiring_hash = gate_wiring_document(request.document, &scope, &components)?;

with

    let wiring_hash = request.document.wiring_hash();

and validate_wiring_compatibility never runs, an ungated wiring is written to catalog.wirings, and CARGO TEST -P WAMN-CTL --LIB STILL REPORTS 68 PASSED / 0 FAILED. Verified by the integrator, applied and restored sha256-clean.

WHY THE EXISTING PROOF DOES NOT CATCH IT. the_gate_is_the_only_producer_of_the_stored_hash calls gate_wiring_document DIRECTLY. It proves the GATE FUNCTION gates - correctly, and the lane's own mutant of the function body is killed by it. It does not, and cannot, prove that author_wiring CALLS that function. The lane's design claim - that no row can reach catalog.wirings ungated BY CONSTRUCTION - is TRUE OF THE CODE AS WRITTEN AND UNGUARDED AGAINST THE NEXT EDIT. That is precisely the regression class wamn-1xb5 exists to prevent.

WHY IT WAS NOT CLOSED IN THE LANE: author_wiring takes a live Transaction, so no unit test can reach the call site. The two honest homes are a live PostgreSQL test naming author-wiring as its subject, or a restructure that makes the call site reachable from a unit test.

*** DO NOT CLOSE THIS WITH A SOURCE-SCANNING include_str GUARD. *** This repository already carries 29 self-scanning guard sites across 14 files (wamn-3o3a) and the lane was explicitly forbidden from adding a thirtieth. A guard that greps author_wiring.rs for the string gate_wiring_document would pass while proving nothing about execution order.

SCOPE also covers the rest of the lane's proposed live surface: author-wiring's Gate, Document and Conflict refusal paths are unit-proven, and its happy path is proven only incidentally by the mint gate. A live test should name author-wiring as its own subject.

OPERATIONAL NOTES for whoever takes it: use a THROWAWAY postgres:18, never the frozen cluster; check the port is free first; the ONLY readiness ground truth is looping on docker exec CONTAINER psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -c "select 1", because pg_isready reports ready during the socket-only phase. Write the test in the LOUD-FAIL shape - an ignore attribute gates selection and a missing env var inside a selected run is an Err with context - never the self-skip shape, which reports PASS in every default run.
acceptance_criteria: The named call-site mutant (replacing gate_wiring_document with a direct document.wiring_hash) FAILS a named test. The test names author-wiring as its own subject and is not a source-scanning include_str guard. author-wiring's Gate, Document and Conflict refusals each have a live arm.

description: The missing half of wamn-3ceu.
