Proves mint, push, pull-by-digest, verify and weld against a THROWAWAY registry.
*** NEVER the kind cluster and NEVER the in-cluster registry. ***

export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=...           # per-lane, never shared
SCR=/path/to/scratch

1. PORTS MUST BE FREE BEFORE BINDING. A failed bind gives a connection-refused that is
   INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A TEST FAILURE.
     for p in 5055 55432; do
       ss -ltn | awk '{print $4}' | grep -qE "[:.]${p}\$" && { echo "port $p busy"; exit 1; }
     done
     docker run -d --name w55e2e-registry -p 127.0.0.1:5055:5000 registry:2
     docker run -d --name w55e2e-postgres -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pw -e POSTGRES_DB=db \
       -p 127.0.0.1:55432:5432 postgres:18

2. POSTGRES READINESS. *** pg_isready REPORTS READY DURING THE SOCKET-ONLY INIT PHASE, and a TCP
   connect is ALSO insufficient because Docker's proxy accepts immediately. The only ground truth is
   a real query over TCP from inside the container: ***
     until docker exec w55e2e-postgres \
             psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -d db -c "select 1" >/dev/null 2>&1
     do sleep 1; done

3. *** THE CREDENTIAL TRAP - THIS HAS BURNED THREE SEPARATE RUNS OF THIS PROGRAM AND EVERY FAILURE
   LOOKED LIKE A PRODUCT BUG. The credential loader's struct has NO auth FIELD AT ALL: docker's
   base64 form is silently ignored and never decoded, and plain docker login output yields
   registry-credentials-incomplete. THERE IS ALSO NO ANONYMOUS PATH - ReleaseManifestSource::new
   reads the file UNCONDITIONALLY and always builds Basic auth - so even an UNAUTHENTICATED
   throwaway registry needs a dummy non-empty username and password. The auths key is the BARE
   host:port; a scheme prefix fails registry-credentials-not-found, proven by
   crates/platform/runtime/tests/registry_credentials.rs::
   missing_or_partial_registry_entry_refuses_without_fallback. ***
   NOTE THE TWO DISTINCT SCHEME-PREFIX REFUSALS, do not conflate them: a scheme in the auths KEY
   fails registry-credentials-not-found; a scheme in the ARTIFACT BASE fails InvalidReference during
   base parsing, BEFORE credentials are read at all.
     cat > "$SCR/registry-auth.json" <<'JSON'
     {"auths":{"127.0.0.1:5055":{"username":"w55e2e","password":"w55e2e"}}}
     JSON

4. MINT AND PUSH (this leg also re-proves the mint-to-OCI bridge):
     WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_MINT_PG_URL="postgres://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:55432/db" \
     WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_ARTIFACT_BASE="127.0.0.1:5055/wamn/releases" \
     WAMN_REGISTRY_AUTH_FILE="$SCR/registry-auth.json" \
     cargo test -p wamn-ctl -p wamn-runtime --test release_manifest_mint_live -- \
       --ignored --exact the_publish_verbs_carry_a_first_release_from_mint_to_oci --nocapture
   The digest it prints is also catalog.release_manifest_v2_snapshots.manifest_digest AND the
   registry tag. *** THE TAG IS THE DIGEST HEX WITH NO sha256: PREFIX - OCI tags cannot contain a
   colon. ***

5. PULL AND WELD. The release version is the catalog version the mint froze (3 in the ctl fixture):

title: fix(schema-control): wiring_identity_cutover_sql was unexecutable on exactly the legacy schemas it exists for
description: PRODUCTION DEFECT, found and fixed during wamn-mn57, landed at 6bde9343 / fa76974c. wiring_identity_cutover_sql in crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs issued ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS wiring_id and ALTER COLUMN wiring_id TYPE as subcommands of ONE ALTER TABLE. PostgreSQL analyses EVERY subcommand of a single ALTER TABLE against the PRE-EXISTING relation, so the ALTER COLUMN beside the ADD COLUMN that creates it raises 42703 column wiring_id does not exist. *** THE FAILURE OCCURS ONLY WHEN THE CARRIERS ARE ABSENT - THAT IS, ONLY ON THE LEGACY SCHEMAS THE CUTOVER EXISTS TO MIGRATE - AND NEVER WHEN THEY ALREADY EXIST. *** So every from-zero path passed and the one path that mattered was broken. WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: every unit test pins the SQL TEXT rather than executing it, and every from-zero fixture already has the columns. This is the pinned-string guard class working exactly as designed and still missing the defect, because a pinned string cannot observe that PostgreSQL will refuse to plan it. Reproduced in isolation in psql, both halves. FIX: split into two statements inside the same batch, so the driver's implicit transaction keeps the cutover atomic.
acceptance_criteria: The cutover executes against a schema whose wiring carriers are ABSENT. A gate that exercises the legacy shape, not only the from-zero shape.
notes: Mutant M13, merging the two ALTERs back into one, is killed by run_plane_reconcile_live with 42703 - so the repair has a watcher that reproduces the original defect exactly. GENERAL LESSON worth more than this bead: a SQL-text pin proves the string has not drifted; it cannot prove PostgreSQL will accept it. Where a builder targets a shape the test fixtures never construct, the pin is structurally blind.
close_reason: Fixed and landed at 6bde9343 / fa76974c, in the same lane that found it. Split into two ALTER TABLE statements inside one batch so the cutover stays atomic, with the PostgreSQL analysis rule recorded as a comment at the site so nobody merges them back. Verified in the integration tree: the two statements are present and the comment explains why. Mutant M13 merges them back and is killed by run_plane_reconcile_live with the original 42703, so the repair carries a watcher that reproduces the defect exactly. Filed and closed together because the finding and the fix were one act of measurement; the bead exists so the defect has an id in the ledger rather than living only inside wamn-mn57's close.

title: feat(ctl): author and gate a wiring version from the CLI
description: THE LAST PRODUCER-SIDE GAP ON THE OCI-NATIVE RELEASE PATH. Measured during wamn-cdky and wamn-04m1: NOTHING IN PRODUCTION RUST WRITES catalog.wirings EXCEPT promote.rs:78, which COPIES FROM A SOURCE ENVIRONMENT. crates/authoring/ contains only model. So a genuinely empty environment still cannot produce a first release without hand SQL for its wirings, even though the other three inputs are now covered - migrate-catalog calls catalog.register_release_manifest, push-component writes catalog.component_library, and publish-release now mints and pushes. THIS SUPERSEDES THE HEADLINE CONSEQUENCE RECORDED ON wamn-04m1: the blocker was believed to be the missing mint verb; the mint verb now exists and the blocker MOVED to wiring authorship. Anything that says a first release cannot be minted because publish-release is unexposed is stale - cite this bead instead.
acceptance_criteria: A first release can be produced in an empty environment with no hand-written SQL: author a wiring version, gate it, then mint and push through publish-release and push-release-manifest.
notes:
Discovered by lane w54-ctl. Sequence AFTER wamn-cdky and wamn-04m1, both landed. Do not model this on promote.rs - promote COPIES an existing wiring between environments, which is a different operation from authoring one.

DECISION TO BE MADE BEFORE THIS CAN BE LANED (wave-55 prep). The bead names the GAP correctly but not the SHAPE, and three shapes are materially different work:
(a) EXPLICIT JSON-FILE ARGS, mirroring the interim publish-release that just landed. Cheapest, consistent with the sibling verb, and equally interim - it inherits the same wamn-0h0g.15.164 debt.
(b) A TYPED CLI SURFACE that constructs the wiring from named arguments. No JSON authoring by hand, but it fixes a wiring vocabulary in argv, which is the thing .15.164 is trying to stop doing.
(c) THROUGH crates/authoring. The principled home, but crates/authoring contains only model today, so this is the largest option and effectively creates the authoring plane.
SECOND, SEPARABLE QUESTION: does an authored wiring pass through the PUBLISH GATE, or is gating a distinct verb? The bead title says author AND gate as one act; promote.rs copies already-gated wirings, so there is no in-tree precedent for authoring one from nothing.
CONTEXT THAT SHOULD INFORM THE RULING: this is the LAST producer-side gap on the OCI-native release path. Everything else - migrate-catalog, push-component, publish-release, push-release-manifest - now works, so whatever ships here determines whether a first release in an empty environment is a real operation or still needs hand SQL.
MEASURED 2026-08-23 (wave-55 read-only pass at fa76974c). ONE PREMISE IN THIS BEAD IS FALSE - CORRECTED BELOW.

*** PREMISE CORRECTION. This bead's objection to option (b) - that a typed CLI "fixes a wiring vocabulary in argv, the thing .15.164 is trying to stop" - IS FALSE. wamn-0h0g.15.164 is a CLOSED, RATIFIED ruling about moving catalog.event_registrations into the control portable store so a PROJECTION can replace publish-release's two hand-authored PathBuf document arguments. Its acceptance names the mint's registration argument. It says nothing about typed argv and nothing about wirings. Wirings already live in catalog.wirings; there is no missing projection to replace. (.15.164 is also still UNIMPLEMENTED at HEAD: event_registrations appears 9 times in catalog-schema.sql and 0 times in control-portable-store.sql.) OPTIONS (a) AND (b) MUST BE COMPARED ON SIZE AND SIBLING-CONSISTENCY, NOT ON DEBT AVOIDANCE. ***

THE GAP IS CONFIRMED EXACTLY: INSERT INTO catalog.wirings appears in production Rust at ONE site, services/ctl/src/promote.rs, and it copies an already-gated wiring BETWEEN environments. Everything else is a read. The only other writers are hand SQL in three test files.

PRICED OPTIONS (measured, not estimated):
(a) EXPLICIT JSON-FILE ARG, mirroring publish-release - ~420 to 450 lines, 4 files: a new services/ctl/src/author_wiring.rs, plus main.rs, lib.rs, and retiring seed_wiring from services/ctl/tests/release_manifest_mint_live.rs. Likely also widens load_component_facts in publish_release.rs from private to pub rather than duplicating it. No cross-lane collision.
(b) TYPED CLI - ~650 to 750 lines, same 4 files. THE REAL COST IS NOT THE FALSE .15.164 CONFLICT: it is that argv CANNOT EXPRESS THE DOCUMENT. WiringNode carries params as an arbitrary JSON map typed by the component's WIT declaration, and WiringDocument.cases carries arbitrary test-set cases. So (b) needs FromStr grammars for node, edge and terminal AND STILL EMBEDS JSON IN ARGV. It fixes a vocabulary without eliminating hand-written JSON. Commits the product to a versioned argv grammar that must track WiringDocument - every future field becomes a CLI change.
(c) THROUGH crates/authoring - ~900 to 1400 lines, 5 to 8 files, and WORSE THAN "model only". Two facts enlarge it beyond the bead's estimate: (i) the crate's vocabulary is FLOWS, NOT WIRINGS - AuthoringCommand is SaveFlowDraft/Validate/DraftRun/TestSetRun/Publish with no wiring concept, and it is a versioned contract with a 443-line contract test that is itself a gate of record; (ii) the ONLY handler plane is services/scenario-worker, not ctl, so this means landing it in that service or standing up a second plane - most likely a new crate, which needs a root Cargo.toml members entry and an architecture/package-roles.json record. *** THAT MAKES (c) THE ONLY OPTION THAT COLLIDES WITH THE COMPONENTS-WORKSPACE LANE. ***

SEPARABLE SECOND QUESTION - NARROWER THAN FILED, AND PARTLY SELF-ANSWERING.
catalog.wirings is INSERT-ONLY IMMUTABLE (BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE triggers both rejecting the change) and gate_report_id is NOT NULL CHECK (not empty). *** SO "AUTHOR NOW, GATE LATER" IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE AGAINST TODAY'S SCHEMA: the row cannot be written ungated and later updated with a report. A distinct gate verb would need new staging storage, or it would have to write the catalog.wirings row itself - at which point it IS the author verb. ***
Gating inside authoring costs about +60 lines: load the scope's AdmittedComponent facts via ComponentCatalogScope, then call validate_wiring_compatibility, which documents itself in-file as "a publish/gate function, not a delivery-time fallback" and already has three production call sites (the mint, and promote's source and target verifies). The mint re-runs it anyway, so the check is idempotent and free at release time.
THE RESIDUAL RULING IS THEREFORE: does the author verb MINT its own gate_report_id, or REQUIRE one on the command line? There is NO gate_reports table anywhere in the schema; gate_report_id is opaque free text, and promote takes it as operator input.

Shape: ctl author-wiring --wiring-document ./wiring.json, with the identity and gate coordinates as flags.

THE REASONING, recorded because it changes how the verb is built and not merely which option won:
This is the ALREADY-RULED ARCHITECTURE ARRIVING AT THE CLI, not a fresh choice. THE WIRING DOCUMENT IS THE ARTIFACT - hash-identified, cases inline, and the controller-story ruling was verbatim that developers author it in their repos and the studio is one client of the format. So THE CLI'S JOB IS TO SUBMIT THE ARTIFACT, NOT TO BE AN AUTHORING SURFACE.
(b) is refused because a typed CLI composing wirings flag by flag would mint a SECOND AUTHORING GRAMMAR - flags against document, the two-dialect drift class - for a document that agents and repositories already emit whole.
(c) is refused because crates/authoring is flow-draft machinery ON THE DELETION LIST: wiring a new CLI to a corpse.
The document path also means the CLI validates through THE SAME GATE PATH as every other producer - one validator, one refusal set, no CLI-special semantics.

RIDERS, all binding:
1. The command's refusals ARE THE DOCUMENT VALIDATOR'S TYPED REFUSALS SURFACED VERBATIM. No CLI-side pre-validation that can drift from the real one.
2. seed_wiring's retirement CITES THIS BEAD AS SUCCESSOR. Test fixtures become documents too - one grammar everywhere.
3. The --gate-report-id flag CONFIRMS THE SHAPE: authorship SUBMITS AGAINST AN EXISTING GREEN REPORT, it does not run the gate inline. author-wiring stays ONE IDEMPOTENT VERB, per the command-ledger pattern.

*** RIDER 3 SETTLES THE SEPARABLE SECOND QUESTION. The measurement had narrowed it to "does the verb MINT its own gate_report_id or REQUIRE one"; the ruling is REQUIRE. That is also the only answer consistent with catalog.wirings being insert-only immutable with gate_report_id NOT NULL. ***

title: test(runtime): measure whether the fork WasiCtx hands guests the host environment
description: OPEN QUESTION THE PLATFORM SHOULD HOLD A VERIFIED ANSWER TO, independent of any workspace or allowlist decision. deploy/platform/executor.yaml:67 injects WAMN_PG_URL into the executor pod environment from a secretKeyRef - a credentialed PostgreSQL URL in the environment of the very process that hosts tenant components. Whether a guest could read it if it held wasi:cli/environment depends on how wash-runtime builds the guest WasiCtx, and that construction is IN THE PINNED FORK, not in-tree: crates/execution/host/src/router_driver.rs:1218 calls wasmtime_wasi::p2::add_to_linker_async and the context itself comes from wash_runtime SharedCtx and WorkloadComponent. It was NOT measured during the wamn-1yj4 decision, and the refusal to assert a leak unmeasured is why this is a separate bead rather than a claim. THIS IS NOT A PATH TO ENABLING wasi:cli. That was ruled out structurally. The point is blast radius: if the answer is that the host environment IS exposed given the capability, that is a finding for the ledger even with wasi:cli denied, because it means the denial is the ONLY thing standing between a tenant component and a database credential - a single-point defence, which this project treats as a finding in its own right. If the answer is that the fork builds an empty or explicitly-populated env, that is equally worth recording, because it means the allowlist is defence in depth rather than the sole control.
acceptance_criteria: A measured answer, cited to the fork source at the pinned rev, recorded on this bead: does a guest holding wasi:cli/environment observe the host process environment, an explicitly-populated subset, or nothing. If the host environment is reachable, a finding row follows.
notes:
Do NOT bump the fork rev to investigate. THE REV IS PINNED IN ABOUT 8 PLACES and cargo CANNOT RESOLVE AN UNPUSHED REV - bumping it before publishing makes the WHOLE WORKSPACE UNRESOLVABLE, not merely red (see wamn-9inf). Read the fork at the pinned rev in the cargo git checkout. Context: the platform design point is a credential-hiding wamn:postgres interface, and wamn-0h0g.12.117 already refuses DATABASE_URL and star-PG_URL keys inside component localResources.environment - but that guard explicitly does NOT cover host env, which is exactly the gap this bead measures.
ANSWERED 2026-08-23 (wave-55 measurement, read at the pinned fork rev daba602 in the cargo git checkout, revision verified to match the pin before any fact was taken).

*** THE ANSWER IS NO. THE FORK NEVER HANDS GUESTS THE HOST PROCESS ENVIRONMENT. ***

inherit_env - the only wasmtime-wasi call that copies process env vars into a guest - appears ZERO times in the fork and ZERO times in this tree.
There are exactly TWO WasiCtxBuilder constructions in the fork's src: a fallback that builds args of main.wasm plus inherit_stderr and nothing else, and the workload path that populates envs SOLELY from the deployment template's localResources.environment. The fork documents the latter in-file as the wasi:cli env variables copied at instantiation.
Per platform path: the EXECUTOR reaches the fallback (its context builder never calls with_wasi_ctx), so its guests see an EMPTY environment; the HOST takes the workload path and sees only the manifest's declared map; the gate harness and one plugin live test declare their own pairs explicitly.
IN-TREE SIDE: the whole of crates, services, tests and test-support contains ONE WasiCtxBuilder, in a test harness. crates/platform/runtime builds none. There is nothing to fix in-tree either.

TWO ADJACENT SURFACES CHECKED AND ALSO CLEAN: the host enables a wasi-config copy-environment option, but that merges the MANIFEST map into wasi:config/store, not host env. The fork's single std::env::vars call is an OTEL prefix test in the host process and is never handed to a guest; the config-source helper that does read named host vars has callers only in the wash CLI crate, which wamn does not depend on.

*** WHY THIS MATTERS ENOUGH TO PIN: deploy/platform/executor.yaml and deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml DO put a credentialed WAMN_PG_URL into the host process environment via secretKeyRef. So the WasiCtx construction is a genuine SECOND control, and the tenant wasi:cli import denial is defence in depth rather than the only thing between a tenant and that credential. Even a guest that somehow held the capability reads an empty map on the executor path. ***

title: chore(wave): parallel lanes share one scratchpad directory and clobber each other cargo logs
description: Wave-machinery defect measured during wave 54. All nine concurrent lanes resolve the SAME scratchpad path, so a lane that redirects cargo output to a conventional filename there has it silently overwritten by another lane running at the same moment. This is not a cosmetic collision: it produces the exact false-red the wave protocol exists to prevent. Lane w54-claims spent roughly twenty minutes diagnosing a wamn-executor compile error whose paths pointed at /target/worktrees/w54-host sources - a failure that did not exist in its own tree at all, read out of another lane's log. The lane brief already mandates isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR per lane for the same class of reason, and the same isolation was never extended to the log destination. Note this is the LOG path, not the target dir; target isolation worked correctly all wave.
acceptance_criteria: A lane brief names a lane-unique log destination, or the dispatch protocol requires lane-unique filenames. Two lanes running concurrently cannot read each other's cargo output.
notes:
Cheapest fix is to fold the lane name into the path the brief hands out, the way CARGO_TARGET_DIR already carries it. Belongs in the standing wave machinery, not in any one wave plan - wamn-findings-program-standing is the memory that carries the partitioning rules.

SECOND AND MORE SERIOUS DIMENSION, measured 2026-08-23 after a lane self-reported it.
*** THE SHARED SCRATCHPAD PATH IS EMBEDDED IN EVERY LANE'S COMMAND LINES, SO IT IS A CROSS-LANE PROCESS-SIGNALLING NAMESPACE, NOT JUST A FILE COLLISION. ***
A lane tidying its own stale waiters ran pgrep -f on the scratchpad path and SIGTERMed 10 PIDs. It could attribute only 4 to itself. Proof the namespace is shared: a PID referencing only that lane's own task UUID was in fact running cargo test -p wamn-host inside the w54-host worktree with the host lane's CARGO_TARGET_DIR. A per-lane target dir does NOT isolate this, because the shared path still appears in the argv.
NO DAMAGE THIS TIME - verified independently by the integrator, not inherited from the lane's own report: both surviving lanes were still registered as running afterwards, and one had advanced its branch tip since the incident, which is positive evidence of liveness rather than mere absence of a corpse. SIGTERM only, no SIGKILL.
THE RULE: a lane must never pattern-match processes on a shared path. Scope process cleanup to task IDs it owns, or use the harness stop mechanism on specific task IDs. Better, remove the cause: give each lane its own scratchpad SUBDIRECTORY, which fixes the log clobbering and the pgrep blast radius in one change.
CREDIT WHERE DUE, and worth preserving as the behaviour to want: the lane caught its own error, stated plainly that it had asserted isolation confidently before verifying it, enumerated what it could and could not attribute, and then DECLINED to delete 7.6 GB of its own orphaned cache on the grounds that it had just been wrong once about blast radius. That is the correct response to discovering you were wrong about scope.
SECOND ISOLATION LEAK, MEASURED LIVE IN WAVE 55 ON 2026-08-23. Same bead subject - a lane escaping its own boundary - but a DIFFERENT and more dangerous channel than the shared scratchpad this bead was filed for.

WHAT HAPPENED: mid-wave, two lines appeared in the MAIN TREE's root Cargo.toml at /home/kaalin/dev/wamn/Cargo.toml, uncommitted:
    [profile.dev]
    debug = "lines-tables-only"
    codegen-units=16
A build-speed tweak. *** ONE OF THEM IS A TYPO - the valid cargo value is line-tables-only, not lines-tables-only - SO EVERY CARGO INVOCATION IN THE MAIN TREE FAILED INSTANTLY WITH A MANIFEST PARSE ERROR, before compiling anything. ***

EVIDENCE IT WAS A LANE AND NOT THE OWNER OR THE INTEGRATOR:
- git status at wave start listed exactly 8 dirty paths and Cargo.toml was NOT among them.
- The file mtime is 21:14:18, about one minute after the last two lane worktrees were created at 21:13:03 and 21:13:08.
- NONE of the five lane worktrees carries the edit in its own copy - so this was not a lane configuring its own tree, it was a write that landed on the MAIN tree specifically.
- The integrated lane commit did not contain it; the cherry-pick touched only tests/conformance.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE LOG CLOBBERING:
1. It is a SHARED BUILD MANIFEST, so the blast radius is every lane and the integrator at once, not one lane's log.
2. THE FAILURE IS DISGUISED. A manifest parse error surfaces as a cargo failure inside whatever command happens to run next, so the lane or integrator that hits it reads it as their own breakage. This wave it landed on the integrator mid-cherry-pick.
3. It is UNCOMMITTED, so it survives no git operation and leaves no history - it can only be caught by noticing the dirty path.
4. A build-profile change is exactly the class that can produce FALSE GREEN AND FALSE RED without any source change.

RESOLUTION: the two lines were removed by targeted edit, NOT by git checkout (restoring uncommitted work by checkout is forbidden here), with the exact removed content recorded above. Cargo.toml is byte-identical to its committed state and the dirt list is back to the 8 protected paths. All four still-running lanes were sent a binding correction: write nothing outside your own worktree, add no profile or codegen tweaks anywhere, and treat a manifest parse error as contamination to REPORT rather than a shared manifest to FIX.

SCOPE THIS BEAD SHOULD NOW COVER - it is no longer only about log paths:
- lane-unique log paths (the original subject)
- a lane must never write outside its worktree root, and the brief must say so explicitly
- no lane may edit a shared build manifest or profile, even inside its own worktree, since CARGO_TARGET_DIR is already isolated per lane and a profile tweak buys nothing
- the integrator should snapshot git status --porcelain at wave start and diff it before each cherry-pick, so contamination is caught at its source rather than inside an unrelated command

*** CORRECTION 2026-08-23, SAME DAY: THE PRECEDING NOTE IS WRONG AND ITS CONCLUSION IS RETRACTED. THE OWNER EDITED Cargo.toml. IT WAS NOT A LANE. ***

The owner made a deliberate [profile.dev] build-speed edit - debug = line-tables-only and codegen-units = 16 - and one word carried a typo (lines-tables-only, where cargo's valid value is line-tables-only). That typo is a MANIFEST PARSE ERROR, so it failed before compiling anything and broke every cargo invocation in the main tree. THE TYPO WAS THE ONLY DEFECT. codegen-units = 16 was always valid.

title: fix(gates): self-scanning source guards can match their own search literals - 29 sites in 14 files
description: wamn-22xc was not a one-off. Twenty-nine guard sites across fourteen files call include_str! on their OWN source file and then locate implementation spans with find() on signature text. Because the search literal is spelled in the same file it scans, a DELETED subject is still found - it matches the test own search string - so the expect never fires, and any span bounded by that position silently collapses onto the test source instead of reporting the absence. The guard then either passes vacuously or fails for a misleading reason. THESE PASS TODAY ONLY BY POSITIONAL LUCK: the real definition happens to precede the test module, so find() reaches it first. Any deletion, or any reordering that moves a definition below the test module, converts the guard into a silent no-op. Counted independently at 5fcb9a88: services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs 8 sites; crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/production_claim.rs 5; tests/integration/src/causation_e2e.rs 2; services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs 2; services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs 2; crates/execution/run-state/src/transitions.rs 2; and one each in services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs, services/ctl/src/prune_run_history.rs, crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/pool.rs, crates/execution/run-state/src/effect_writer.rs, crates/execution/host/src/router_delivery.rs, crates/control/provision/tests/control_portable_store.rs, crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs. claims.rs is the fourteenth and is already FIXED at 5fcb9a88. HIGHEST RISK: production_claim.rs, whose production_claim_and_reaper_use_only_the_platform_pool at line 1642 is the exact sibling shape of the one just repaired. This is the general form of wamn-0h0g.15.137: a verification artifact reporting success without evidence.
design: The repo already has the idiom - tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs:18 defines CFG_TEST_MODULE as the marker for exactly this purpose, and 5fcb9a88 applies it inline in claims.rs. The boundary literal is itself immune because in source it is written with an escaped newline, not a literal one, so it cannot match its own spelling. Prefer hoisting one shared constant over fourteen inline copies, but note that a shared helper in a test-support crate cannot be used by guards that live inside production modules behind cfg(test).
acceptance_criteria: Every self-scanning guard slices its source at the test-module boundary before any find(), so a search literal can never be its own match and an absent subject panics on its expect. A mutant that repoints any one guard search literal at an absent signature must FAIL LOUDLY on the expect, not pass and not collapse its span.

title: decide(components): dropping no_std makes both palette guests unpublishable - std pulls 10 denied wasi:cli imports
description: MEASURED REFUTATION of the owner ruling on wamn-0h0g.11.56. Dropping no_std from transform and http-request DOES compile: the workspace check for wasm32-wasip2 goes from exit 101 with 4 errors to 0 errors, and both guests still build and validate clean with an unchanged exported world. But std adds FOURTEEN imports the components never had - 4 in wasi:io and wasi:clocks, which are already allowed, and TEN in wasi:cli: stdout, stderr, stdin, environment, exit, terminal-input, terminal-output, terminal-stdin, terminal-stdout, terminal-stderr. crates/platform/component-policy/src/lib.rs:74 defines TENANT_WASI_PACKAGES as a CLOSED four-element allowlist of wasi:io, wasi:clocks, wasi:random and wasi:logging, and its own doc comment names CLI environment and process as denied until the list is changed deliberately. components/library/publish.sh pushes these two guests admitting only wamn:node and wamn:connection. The enforcement chain is real and unconditional: publish.sh to wamn-ctl push-component to services/ctl/src/push_component.rs:97 to component_admission.rs:95 analyze_tenant, which refuses with ImportPolicyRefused. Running the policy rule against the actually-built components gives 10 denied imports each. BOTH PALETTE COMPONENTS BECOME UNPUBLISHABLE. Runtime linking is NOT the problem - router_driver.rs:1218 uses wasmtime_wasi::p2::add_to_linker_async, which satisfies all 14. The break is entirely at publish-time admission. The ruling was made on the premise that binary size was the only soft cost; size is in fact not the interesting cost and the import policy was not part of the ruling. Size delta measured for the record, debug builds: transform 2845337 to 4749436 bytes, plus 66.9 percent; http_request 3953185 to 5885265 bytes, plus 48.9 percent - roughly 1.9 MB flat each, the fixed cost of std, and an upper bound since release strips.
design: THREE LIVE OPTIONS. (1) KEEP no_std and give the two palette guests their own workspace, so serde_json feature unification cannot reach them - preserves the closed import policy, costs a workspace split. (2) WIDEN the policy to admit wasi:cli in TENANT_WASI_PACKAGES and in publish.sh - this is a SECURITY POLICY DECISION granting every tenant component stdio, environment, process exit and terminal access, and it is not reversible once components ship against it. (3) Keep no_std and instead make the components workspace build member-by-member rather than as one invocation, treating the bead acceptance criterion as the thing that is wrong. The refuted patch is preserved and applies cleanly if option 2 is chosen.
acceptance_criteria: An owner ruling that resolves the conflict, recorded on this bead, and wamn-0h0g.11.56 re-pointed at whichever option is chosen.
notes:
Lane w54-comp applied the ruling exactly, measured the consequence, and stopped rather than choosing - correct behaviour. The patch is at scratchpad/drop-no_std.patch, 182 lines. ALSO REFUTED: there are THREE no_std guests, not two - components/fixtures/connection-http-standard/src/lib.rs:5 is the third, with its own inline global_allocator, cabi_realloc and panic_handler at line 107. AND the 10 errors have TWO unrelated causes, not one: 2 errors in 2 targets from serde_json pulling std, and 8 errors in 3 targets from the TEST HARNESS pulling std, which is present regardless of serde_json and which connection-http-standard hits despite having no serde_json dependency at all. No no_std guest has a single test; their lib-test targets are empty harnesses. The 10-error figure only appears under --all-targets, which the bead acceptance criterion does not use.

OPTION 3 TESTED AND REFUTED 2026-08-23, which NARROWS THE DECISION TO TWO.
Hypothesis: components/Cargo.toml:15 declares serde_json = 1 with DEFAULT FEATURES, i.e. std, and two members inherit it that way (execution/materializer:8, ingress/flow-http:9), so setting the workspace declaration to default-features = false, features = alloc might dissolve the unification with no policy change, no workspace split, no no_std drop and no size cost.
MEASURED: it does not. Gate A stays at EXIT 101 with 4 errors, identical to base, same two E0152 panic_impl failures with the same note that std comes from serde_json. The change DID work on the two members - cargo tree confirms both then sit under serde_json feature alloc - but SIX OTHER CRATES in the wasm32-wasip2 target graph request serde_json with default features and components/Cargo.toml cannot reach any of them. Three are EXTERNAL with no feature knob: boon 0.6.1 via flow-http directly, jmespath 0.3.0 via wamn-event-reg and wamn-materializer, schemars 0.8.22 via wamn-schema-model. Four are ROOT-workspace path crates - wamn-event-reg, wamn-event-wire, wamn-materializer, wamn-schema-model - each declaring serde_json = workspace true, which resolves against /Cargo.toml:75, serde_json = 1, default features. Verified independently in the integration tree.
*** THE STRUCTURAL REASON: CARGO FEATURE UNIFICATION IS ADDITIVE-ONLY. No downstream declaration can switch off a feature an upstream crate switches on. boon, jmespath and schemars are fatal on their own, so even editing the ROOT workspace serde_json line would not help. As long as flow-http and materializer are members of the same cargo invocation, serde_json/std is on unconditionally. ***
RED HERRING RULED OUT: wit-component and wit-parser also pull serde_json default, but only through the wit-bindgen-rust-macro PROC-MACRO path, which resolver 2 correctly decouples from the target graph. cargo check -p transform --target wasm32-wasip2 exits 0.
CONFIRMED WHILE TESTING, and it is the argument for the split: built alone, both guests are BYTE-IDENTICAL to base and validate clean - transform 2845337 bytes with only wamn:node/types, http-request 3953185 bytes with only wamn:connection/http and wamn:node/types. Zero size change, zero import change. The guests are provably self-sufficient and publishable; the ONLY thing breaking them is co-residency in one invocation with members that transitively require serde_json/std through three external crates nobody controls.
STILL OPEN, do not record as proven: whether flow-http and materializer genuinely work on alloc-only serde_json was NOT established - they compiled only because std was still on transitively. The API survey (from_slice, from_str, from_value, json!, to_string, to_value, to_vec; no from_reader, no to_writer) looks right but was never exercised.
close_reason: RULED BY OWNER 2026-08-23: OPTION A, the second workspace. The drop-no_std ruling on wamn-0h0g.11.56 is REVERSED by its author, who recorded that it was made on the wrong cost - wasm bytes were sized, the IMPORT DELTA against the closed allowlist was never checked. OPTION B IS DISQUALIFIED STRUCTURALLY, NOT BY THE UNKNOWN: widening TENANT_WASI_PACKAGES to admit wasi:cli would grant EVERY tenant component stdio, environment, exit and terminal in order to serve the build convenience of TWO FIRST-PARTY GUESTS. The allowlist doc says denied until changed deliberately, and changing it as fallout from cargo feature unification is the opposite of deliberate. It is effectively irreversible once components ship against it. The owner ruling in one line: you do not widen a security boundary to fix a lockfile. IMPLEMENTATION RIDERS, all binding: the new workspace is NAMED FOR ITS PROPERTY so the reason lives in the name, and carries a doc line explaining feature unification so nobody simplifies it back; the second build leg joins tools/build-components and tools/profile IN THE SAME COMMIT, per the cumulative shape wamn-0h0g.10.3 established; wamn-0h0g.11.56 acceptance criteria rewords to INTENT - every component builds, workspace membership per isolation need - with the premise correction cited. FACTUAL CORRECTION to the ruling text: there is NO drop-no_std commit to revert. Lane w54-comp refuted the ruling BEFORE committing and landed only the lockfile prune (09323ce4); both guests still carry no_std and are byte-identical to base, so the guests are already in the state the reversal restores. The refuted patch survives unapplied in scratchpad and should be discarded, not reverted. Loose end filed as its own bead: measure the fork WasiCtx env exposure - not to enable B, but because whether the runtime hands guests the host environment is a question the platform should hold a verified answer to regardless.

title: feat(ctl): bridge the minted release snapshot to its OCI push
description: Measured by wamn-0h0g.15.98. mint_release_manifest WRITES canonical bytes to catalog.release_manifest_v2_snapshots. push-release-manifest READS a file via --manifest. NOTHING READS THE SNAPSHOT OUT. So publishing a real release today requires hand-extracting bytes from PostgreSQL BYTE-EXACTLY, and a stray newline is refused because the digest is a plain SHA-256 over those exact RFC 8785 bytes. This is the one remaining producer-side gap on the OCI-native path.
acceptance_criteria: A ctl invocation can publish a minted release from its snapshot row to OCI without a human copying bytes out of the database.
notes: MEASURED 2026-08-23 at b8b474b6. IMPLEMENTABLE_NOW, small and mechanical. Confirmed nothing bridges mint to push: mint_release_manifest writes via INSERT_RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_SQL and returns MintedReleaseManifest canonical_bytes; push_release_manifest::run reads a FILE; the only reader of catalog.release_manifest_v2_snapshots is promote.rs SELECT_SOURCE_RELEASE_SQL, and promote NEVER CALLS publish_release_manifest (zero grep hits). PREMISE SOFTENED: byte-exactness is not actually at risk in code - canonical_bytes is BYTEA, tokio-postgres returns Vec u8 verbatim, and catalog-schema.sql:1933-1935 enforces manifest_digest equals sha256 of canonical_bytes AT REST. The newline hazard is purely in today's HUMAN copy-out path, which is the argument FOR the bridge, not a risk in it. RECOMMENDED SHAPE (b): a --from-snapshot mode on push-release-manifest, making --manifest mutually exclusive with a database-url plus tenant plus catalog-id plus catalog-version group, selecting canonical_bytes and handing it to the existing pub async publish_release_manifest. About 80 lines, no new verb, gives a re-publish path for ANY snapshot. REJECTED SHAPE (a): promote --release-artifact-base pushing inline at promote.rs:862-874, about 40 lines but it couples push to promote and drags in promote.rs, the most contended file in ctl. FILE DOMAIN under (b): services/ctl/src/push_release_manifest.rs args and run at :128-165; services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs to expose the already-existing private SELECT_RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_SQL at :74-78; services/ctl/tests/release_manifest_mint_live.rs.
close_reason: Landed at 1834bdfe. The minted release snapshot now bridges to its OCI push: push-release-manifest takes EITHER --manifest OR the database quad, mutually exclusive, and reads canonical_bytes straight from the snapshot row. *** THE BEAD'S RECOMMENDED MECHANISM WAS WRONG AND WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A PRODUCTION DEFECT. *** It said to expose the existing private SELECT_RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_SQL - but that literal ends in FOR SHARE, and PostgreSQL requires UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE for ANY row-locking clause. catalog-schema.sql:1946 grants wamn_app only SELECT, which I verified independently in the integration tree. Following the bead literally produces a bridge that works for superusers and owners and is DENIED for the least-privileged role a publisher should run as. This is the same load-bearing fact the plane already learned from the other direction, where a bare REVOKE UPDATE on a row-locked relation is a production outage. The publisher instead owns a lock-free READ_RELEASE_SNAPSHOT_SQL selecting canonical_bytes alone; the mint keeps its three FOR SHARE literals unchanged. SECOND CORRECTION, and it is about proof quality: mutant M9, deleting the tenant claim, SURVIVED while the live test ran as superuser - release_manifest_v2_snapshots has ENABLE plus FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, but SUPERUSERS BYPASS RLS REGARDLESS OF FORCE. The lane re-pointed the push at wamn_app and the mutant became lethal, so the live proof now runs on the production connection shape rather than the fixture's. A fixture that masks a load-bearing claim is the false-green shape. INTEGRATOR RE-VERIFICATION, not inherited: the live gate is 2 passed / 0 failed against a throwaway postgres:18 and a freshly recreated registry:2, both on verified-free ports and both removed afterwards; the frozen cluster was never touched. Out-of-band proof that the artifact really landed: the registry tag list is exactly the manifest_digest from the snapshot row, f168d5442618837ce016f27dc84d450f9551bff016afbb2c58eea5aa7870b111. THAT DIGEST WAS IDENTICAL ACROSS THE LANE'S RUN AND THREE INDEPENDENT RUNS OF MINE, which is incidental but real evidence that the RFC 8785 canonicalization is deterministic across environments. Ten mutants killed by named tests, including M8 appending one newline - refused as release-manifest-document-refused, exactly the failure a human copy-out produces, now impossible on the code path. Follow-ups filed before this close: wamn-duyl (the print-the-env-lines verb, sequenced after wamn-3ceu), wamn-1xb5 (wiring authorship, the real remaining gap), wamn-txmd (catalog-schema hard-codes AUTHORIZATION postgres).

title: chore(retire): delete the bespoke instance pool for wash-runtime InstancePolicy
description:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-23: DELETE THIS WAVE. The clearest native-capability win measured in the wave-53 preparation pass.

## THE FINDING - a pool that pools nothing
crates/execution/host/src/pool.rs is 1356 lines. It pins
  pub const INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE: u64 = 1   (pool.rs:60)
so every instance is destroyed at the end of the checkout it was handed to. That is exactly
wash-runtime's InstancePolicy::Ephemeral, which is already the DEFAULT for any component that does
not set pool_size > 0 (fork daba602, crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/instance_pool.rs:227-231).

Everything built around that constant is therefore dead semantics: identity bind/revoke,
RetirementReason variants, 60s idle-age reaping, max_idle_per_digest, capacity errors.

Underneath it sit TWO real implementations it duplicates:
  wash-runtime InstancePool / InstancePolicy (native pooling, WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING is the
    native clamp to Ephemeral)
  wasmtime's pooling allocator, which already bounds live instances via total_component_instances
    and already makes fresh instantiation microsecond-cost
    (crates/platform/runtime/src/engine.rs:61-66 sets those knobs DIRECTLY on the real wasmtime
     PoolingAllocationConfig - that part is correctly native and must not be unwound)

Production wiring to remove: crates/execution/host/src/router_driver.rs:424-430 constructs it with
a hardcoded max_instances: 512 and max_reserved_bytes = MEMORY_CAP_BYTES * a third 512 literal;
:571-573 insert_batch; :1115 checkout; :1154 retirement.

## COVERAGE THAT GOES WITH IT
Three conformance suites exist ONLY to prove the hand-rolled pool behaves like Ephemeral:
  tests/conformance/tests/execution_pool_fresh_instance.rs
  tests/conformance/tests/execution_pool_checkout_identity.rs
  tests/conformance/tests/execution_identity_exactness.rs
*** ALL THREE ARE ALREADY BROKEN at HEAD *** - they import ExecutionHost, ExecutionAcquisition and
TrustedExecutionRuntimeRevision, none of which wamn_execution_host exports any more. They are
listed in wamn-0h0g.11.55.4 as compile-repair targets. THIS BEAD SUPERSEDES THAT FOR THESE THREE
FILES: deleting them is the repair. .11.55.4 cedes them.

## BOUNDARY
Do NOT unwind engine.rs's direct wasmtime PoolingAllocationConfig calls - those are the native path.
Do NOT touch crates/execution/host/src/router_delivery.rs, which wamn-0h0g.24.4 owns.
Coordinate with wamn-0h0g.17.3: this deletion removes the router_driver.rs 512, leaving .17.3 to
parameterize ONE literal (engine.rs:20) instead of two.

## VALIDATION
Red branch is acceptable per owner direction 2026-08-23. Report the per-package result.
acceptance_criteria: crates/execution/host/src/pool.rs is deleted; instance lifetime comes from wash-runtime InstancePolicy and wasmtime's allocator counts; the three Ephemeral-proving conformance suites are deleted rather than repaired; engine.rs's direct PoolingAllocationConfig calls are unchanged; no behaviour change, because INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE was already 1.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-23 - ACCEPTED, THE FORECLOSURE IS INTENDED.
Raised as a flag before dispatch: deleting crates/execution/host/src/pool.rs is behaviour-neutral ONLY because INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE = 1 (pool.rs:60) already destroys every instance at the end of its checkout. The deletion therefore forecloses ever raising that constant in the bespoke pool.
OWNER ACCEPTS THAT. Instance reuse, if it is ever wanted, comes from wash-runtime pool_size / InstancePolicy - the native path - not from reviving a bespoke pool. Do not preserve the constant, the idle-age reaping, max_idle_per_digest, the RetirementReason variants or the identity bind/revoke machinery as a hedge. Delete them.
Note exe-model.md already states the product position: fresh instances remain the rule, and memory reuse waits for explicit affinity/windowed-state semantics.
close_reason: Landed as d1a5d17e, pushed. Deleted crates/execution/host/src/pool.rs (1356 lines), the router_driver pool wiring, and the three conformance suites whose subject it was: execution_pool_fresh_instance, execution_pool_checkout_identity, execution_identity_exactness. Net minus 2748 lines. BEHAVIOUR-NEUTRAL, evidenced three ways: INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE = 1 fed max_invocations_per_instance so ExecutionLease::finish always retired before reaching reset_invocation_state, making reuse STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE; the only producer of idle instances was a one-shot prewarm from prepare_synchronous_release, and prune_idle, invalidate_digest and insert had ZERO callers outside pool.rs while RouterDriverSnapshot.instances had no reader anywhere; and the deleted bounds max_instances 512 and MEMORY_CAP_BYTES times 512 merely restated engine.rs POOL_SLOTS and max_memory_size, which the wasmtime allocator still enforces at the same values. Only first-invocation-per-digest latency is actually lost. TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS THE BEAD DID NOT NAME. First, THE POOL WAS ALSO THE IDENTITY SEAM: checkout called bind_identity and finish, retire and Drop called revoke_identity across the wamn:postgres, wasi:logging and connection-http registries. That is production behaviour, not pool semantics, and it is preserved as inherent NodeInstance::bind_identity plus impl Drop for NodeInstance, which also keeps the lease's mid-run cancellation guarantee a plain post-run revoke would have lost. Second, INSTANCE LIFETIME DOES NOT COME FROM wash-runtime InstancePolicy: NodeInstance::instantiate creates its own Store and never enters wash-runtime's InstancePool, so the Ephemeral policy it passes is INERT on this path - filed as wamn-hlp2 for a ruling. Deletion-collateral sweep over all 13 removed symbols plus the suite names returns zero hits; two repairs were needed and are in the commit, notably component_export_index.rs which used the removed trait impl as a section terminator and would have gone silently vacuous rather than red. Gates re-verified on the integrated tip. Follow-ups filed: wamn-8m4j restore the pooling-allocator ceiling proof, wamn-hlp2 the InstancePool bypass decision, wamn-ahuw the exe-model correction, wamn-7nhh confirm the single ceiling literal.

title: fix(components): the components workspace does not build as a workspace - serde_json std reaches two no_std guests
description:
## Measured 2026-08-23 at 99f33d20

The components workspace does not build as a workspace. Per-package builds hide it, which is why
this has never appeared in a lane report.

  cd components && cargo check --workspace --keep-going --target wasm32-wasip2   EXIT 101
  cd components && cargo check -p transform      --target wasm32-wasip2          EXIT 0
  cd components && cargo check -p http-request   --target wasm32-wasip2          expected EXIT 0

FAILURE
  error[E0152]: found duplicate lang item panic_impl
    --> library/transform/src/../../guest_runtime.rs:43:1
    note: the lang item is first defined in crate std (which serde_json depends on)
  Same error for library/http-request. Two of seven members.

CAUSE - WORKSPACE FEATURE UNIFICATION, NOT A GUEST DEFECT
  library/transform and library/http-request are no_std cdylib guests that supply their own
  panic handler from the shared components/guest_runtime.rs, and they declare
  serde_json = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }.
  ingress/flow-http and execution/materializer declare serde_json = { workspace = true }, and the
  workspace entry carries default features, so serde_json/std is on.
  Cargo unifies features across members built in one invocation. resolver = "2" is already set at
  components/Cargo.toml:2 and does NOT isolate features between workspace members in a single
  build. std therefore reaches the two no_std guests and collides with their panic handler.

CANDIDATE FIXES, owner picks
  (a) declare the workspace serde_json with default-features = false and have flow-http and
      materializer opt into the std feature explicitly. Smallest change, keeps one workspace.
  (b) move the two no_std library guests out of the shared workspace.
  (c) adopt whatever per-member feature isolation the toolchain offers and pin it.

ALSO MEASURED, SEPARATE AND LOWER CONFIDENCE
  cargo check --workspace --all-targets on this workspace additionally fails
  connection-http-standard (lib test), http-request (lib test) and transform (lib test) with the
  same duplicate lang item. A no_std cdylib guest arguably has no meaningful lib-test target, so
  --all-targets may simply be the wrong invocation for this workspace. Decide and record which
  invocation IS the components gate, because right now there is none.

WHY IT MATTERS
  This is the components baseline that has been recorded as missing. It is not a missing
  invocation - the invocation fails. tools/repo-lint declares four components legs and has never
  reached any of them for an unrelated reason (.12.157, closed), so nothing has ever measured this.
acceptance_criteria: Every component builds; workspace membership follows ISOLATION NEED, not tidiness. Concretely: the two no_std palette guests build clean, keep their no_std and their minimal import surface, and remain publishable through analyze_tenant against an UNCHANGED four-element TENANT_WASI_PACKAGES; the std members build clean; and tools/build-components plus tools/profile carry the second leg so both are built by the recipe of record. PREMISE CORRECTION, cited: the original criterion assumed one workspace could build everything. It cannot. Cargo feature unification is ADDITIVE-ONLY and applies PER INVOCATION, so a no_std guest and a std sibling that transitively enables serde_json/std cannot share a cargo invocation - std supplies a panic_impl that collides with the guest's own (E0152). Six crates in that graph request serde_json with default features, three of them external with no feature knob (boon, jmespath, schemars), so no declaration anywhere can narrow it. Separation is the mechanism, not a workaround.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 at b8b474b6. NEEDS_RULING - mechanism CONFIRMED exactly, but ALL THREE OFFERED FIXES ARE WRONG. Confirmed: components/library/{transform,http-request}/src/lib.rs:3 are no_std, each path-includes ../../guest_runtime.rs which defines panic_handler, and both declare serde_json default-features false with alloc; components/ingress/flow-http and components/execution/materializer declare serde_json workspace, which is default features and therefore std. resolver 2 is set and does NOT isolate members in one invocation. 7 members, 2 no_std. *** FIX (a) IS NOT SMALLEST, IT IS IMPOSSIBLE: cargo builds ONE serde_json per target per invocation with the UNION of requested features, so the moment flow-http and materializer opt into std, std is back in transform's graph - (a) is self-defeating as written. Worse, the std request is not even local: wamn-materializer, wamn-event-reg, wamn-schema-model and wamn-event-wire ALL declare serde_json against the ROOT workspace, which components/Cargo.toml cannot reach. flow-http additionally uses boon, which is std-only. *** FIX (c) AS WORDED DOES NOT EXIST - cargo has no per-member feature isolation within one invocation. REFUTED. *** THE BEAD MISSES THE CHEAPEST OPTION ENTIRELY: both guests carry a DEAD [features] std = [] entry with zero cfg(feature = std) uses in either lib.rs. Dropping no_std and guest_runtime from the two guests makes the problem vanish for the cost of .wasm size only, and the workspace already sets opt-level s and strip true. *** INTERACTION QUESTION ANSWERED NO: wamn-0h0g.26.4 does NOT change the offending consumer set and the cheap fix is NOT a side effect of it - flowrunner was deleted by 29db8e42 and is not a components member at the tip; the offenders are flow-http, materializer and materializer's native subtree, none of which .26.4 or .26.5 touches. .11.56 must be fixed on its own merits. REAL OPTIONS: (b) split the two no_std guests into their own workspace; (e) drop no_std from both guests; (f) define the components gate as two-or-more invocations that never mix the sets - *** (f) CONTRADICTS THIS BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, which demand cargo check --workspace exits 0, so it needs an AC amendment. *** SEPARATE FINDING: components/Cargo.lock is STALE - it records wamn-flow, wamn-catalog, wamn-run-state and wamn-pg-core as reachable, but at the tip wamn-materializer depends only on wamn-event-wire, wamn-event-reg, serde, serde_json and jmespath. wamn-flow is NOT actually reachable from the components workspace. Regenerate the lock independently.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-23 - DROP no_std FROM BOTH GUESTS. transform and http-request stop being no_std; guest_runtime.rs and its panic_handler go with them. Their [features] std = [] entries are ALREADY DEAD CODE with zero cfg(feature = std) uses, so nothing real is being given up. Cost is .wasm SIZE ONLY, and the workspace already sets opt-level s and strip true. The whole feature-unification problem vanishes and *** THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS MET AS WRITTEN - cargo check --workspace exits 0 - with no AC amendment. *** REJECTED: splitting the two guests into a second workspace preserves a size budget that is not a hard requirement, at the cost of a second Cargo.lock, a second gate leg and build tooling that must know both. ALSO REJECTED: defining the gate as two invocations that never mix the sets - it contradicts this bead's own AC and, worse, it is the shape where a gate passes because we stopped running the failing command, which is the recurring defect on this branch. SEPARATE, IN SCOPE: regenerate components/Cargo.lock, which is stale - it records wamn-flow, wamn-catalog, wamn-run-state and wamn-pg-core as reachable when wamn-flow is not actually reachable from the components workspace at all.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): enforce insert-or-verify conflict contracts for release copies
description:
## Why

The shared release-source and release-attachment builders currently end in ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. A same-identity request carrying different content therefore reports success while the requested state is absent. This is the R55 false-convergence class at row grain, not a target contract for migration.

The surviving migrate_catalog raw INSERT SELECT path is wrong in the opposite direction: it raises native PostgreSQL 23505 on a duplicate target identity, but does not provide the shared typed content-conflict contract. Loud-and-untyped is safer than quiet-and-wrong, so that raw behavior remains unchanged until this bead lands.

Owner ruling C on wamn-0h0g.11.47 narrows the release-candidate guard to conflict-free row-shape equivalence. This P1 bug owns conflict parity and the correct end state for both the shared publication builder surface and migration.

## Template

Follow wamn-0h0g.15.159 / cd9462f9 and catalog.register_release_manifest: insert, verify every supplied persisted value on identity conflict, make an exact retry a no-op, and raise a frozen typed content-conflict refusal on divergence. A bare DO NOTHING is forbidden because it silently blesses drift.

## Scope

Create one shared insert-or-verify-identical construction for catalog.release_sources and one for catalog.release_attachments, and route both the existing builders and migrate_catalog through them. Source verification covers source_kind, definition_json, and source_hash. Attachment verification covers attachment_kind, flow_id, source_id, definition_hash, definition_json, and every nullable route field with null-safe comparison. Preserve tenant, catalog, and version scoping plus CHECK and FK enforcement. Split row-shape construction from publish-only context when necessary; fabricate no draft, evidence, or other publish context. Keep the wamn-0h0g.11.47 conflict-free equivalence guard as the permanent two-sites-one-guard regression fence.
acceptance_criteria: catalog.release_sources and catalog.release_attachments each have one shared insert-or-verify-identical construction used by the publication builder surface and migrate_catalog. No production raw INSERT SELECT or direct ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING remains for either relation. An exact same-key retry succeeds with byte-identical persisted rows; a same-key divergent retry raises PostgreSQL 23505 with frozen typed source or attachment content-conflict literals after comparing every persisted non-key field, including hashes, JSON, and nullable routes. Tenant, catalog, and version scope plus table CHECK and FK enforcement remain intact. The wamn-0h0g.11.47 conflict-free guard remains. Live exact-retry and divergence probes plus named mutants for bare DO NOTHING, omitted field comparison, tenant-scope loss, hash drift, and nullable-route drift fail. Focused tests and strict Clippy pass.
notes:
*** OWNER RULING C, 2026-08-20: FIX BOTH CONFLICT DIALECTS HERE. ***

- Priority upgraded from P2 task to P1 bug because the shared builders are themselves an R55 instance: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING silently accepts same-key differing content.
- Aligning migration to those builders is explicitly disallowed. The target is insert-or-verify-identical on both surfaces, following wamn-0h0g.15.159 / cd9462f9.
- The current raw migrate INSERT SELECT remains unchanged and continues to raise native 23505 until this bead lands.
- wamn-0h0g.11.47 proves only conflict-free row-shape equivalence and must name this exclusion.
- There is currently no living production source or attachment publisher; this bead owns the shared publication builder surface and the living migrate writer without claiming two current production writers.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN - NOT STARTED
- Define shared insert-or-verify-identical source and attachment row operations with frozen typed refusal literals.
- Compare every persisted non-key field using JSON and null-safe semantics where required.
- Route the builders and migrate path through those operations without fake publish context.
- Preserve the wamn-0h0g.11.47 guard and add live exact-retry, divergent-retry, and mutation proof.
*** OWNER RIDER, 2026-08-20: THE TEMPORARY EXCLUSION EXPIRES IN THIS COMMIT. *** When insert-or-verify-identical conflict parity lands, the wamn-0h0g.11.47 equivalence guard and its documentation must stop saying conflicts are excluded or deferred. Extend the surviving guard to assert the full exact-retry and divergent-content contract in the same commit. A narrowed guard that outlives its narrowing reason is a false coverage claim at guard grain. IMPLEMENTATION PLAN remains NOT STARTED until the authorized Wave 12 lane begins.
SCOPE ADDED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-26, arising from wamn-0h0g.22.6.1.

THE wamn.tenant_key FUNCTION AND ITS EXPRESSION INDEXES RIDE THIS BEAD as one more CONVERGED OBJECT CLASS. This bead already owns insert-or-verify-identical typed-refusal convergence for both migration paths; these are the same shape at DDL grain.

TWO APPLIERS, ONE DEFINITION:
  - catalog-schema.sql carries the function for FRESH INSTALLS (it applies whole on a fresh install and never again).
  - THIS bead's path carries EXISTING project-env databases.
  - The definition-digest probe from the wamn-0h0g.22.6.1 ruling is what makes both paths PROVABLY IDENTICAL: one pin, two appliers, ZERO DRIFT TOLERANCE. Without it, two appliers is two chances to diverge.

*** R55: EXITS ZERO IS NOT THE BAR. *** CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is naturally convergent - a second run no-ops in effect - but that is not what the converge arm asserts. IT ASSERTS POST-STATE, all four:
  1. the function EXISTS;
  2. its DEFINITION DIGEST MATCHES THE PIN;
  3. the IMMUTABLE and PARALLEL SAFE flags are PRESENT (read from pg_proc.provolatile and proparallel, not from the DDL text - a function that lost IMMUTABLE still creates fine and silently breaks every expression index that depends on it);
  4. the EXECUTE grants are EXACT - the guest family holds EXECUTE and nothing holds more.

EXPRESSION INDEXES converge the same way: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plus THE SAME VERIFY-DO-NOT-TRUST ARM. IF NOT EXISTS is the idempotence; the verify arm is the proof, because an index that exists under the WRONG EXPRESSION satisfies IF NOT EXISTS and leaves every guest read non-sargable. Read the expression back from pg_index. Coverage across relations is checked on wamn-0h0g.22.15; the per-object post-state is checked here.
CONVERGE DEPENDENCY ADDED 2026-08-26 by wamn-0h0g.22.6.3.

deploy/sql/run-state.sql now carries the authority-derivations bootstrap and five tenant-key expression indexes, and crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs converges run-plane INDEXES object by object against that file. On an EXISTING run-plane database the reconciler will therefore try to create CREATE INDEX ... ((wamn_authority.tenant_key(tenant_id))) before anything has installed wamn_authority.tenant_key there, and the index creation fails.

The fix is this bead's subject: the converge path must apply authority_derivations_bootstrap_sql() before it converges indexes or policies. The builder exists and is idempotent by construction; R55 still applies, so the arm asserts POST-STATE - the function exists, its pg_get_functiondef digest matches, IMMUTABLE and PARALLEL SAFE read from pg_proc, and the grants are exact.

ENVIRONMENT_POLICY_TENANT_QUAL in run_plane.rs moved with the sweep. If it ever drifts back, the reconciler REVERTS the sweep on every existing run-plane database - a silent re-opening of the settable-claim boundary rather than a visible failure.
close_reason: 114b5a8f replaces both wrong conflict dialects with shared insert-or-verify-identical catalog routines used by the publication builder surface and migrate_catalog. Exact retries preserve byte-identical rows; every source and attachment non-key field is verified, nullable routes use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, and divergence raises frozen PostgreSQL 23505 literals catalog-release-source-content-conflict or catalog-release-attachment-content-conflict. The former builder DO NOTHING was treated as the R55 false-convergence instance and the register-release wamn-0h0g.15.159/cd9462f9 pattern supplied the repair. The temporary wamn-0h0g.11.47 conflict exclusion/defer wording was removed in this same commit and its guard now asserts full parity. Premise correction: fresh-schema-only routines would break already-provisioned catalogs, so an exact to_regprocedure-probed additive slice, all-or-none partial-install refusal, and live reconvergence proof landed too. Fresh PostgreSQL 18 migration and upgrade guards passed; 222 focused package tests plus four exposure tests and strict all-target Clippy passed. Bare DO NOTHING, omitted attachment_kind/source_hash/nullable-route comparisons, tenant-scope loss, and missing-upgrade-probe mutants all turned red and were hash-restored; root independently reproduced the source-hash omission red and clean reconvergence.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): tools/repo-lint aborts at rustfmt and never reaches ANY of its six clippy legs
description:
## Why

*** tools/repo-lint IS A COMPLETE LINT GATE THAT CANNOT REACH A SINGLE ONE OF ITS CLIPPY LEGS. MEASURED 2026-08-19 at 53afb31a. ***

The script is set -euo pipefail and runs its legs SEQUENTIALLY, so the first failing leg aborts everything after it. Execution order (tools/repo-lint:161-175):

  1. connection-http per-invocation client check
  2. root rustfmt      cargo fmt --manifest-path root --all -- --check
  3. components rustfmt
  4. root Clippy       cargo clippy --manifest-path root --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
  5. components native Clippy
  6. connection-http-standard native Clippy   (RUSTFLAGS=-C panic=abort)
  7. flowrunner native Clippy                 (-A dead-code)
  8. components wasm Clippy                   (--target wasm32-wasip2)
  9. flowrunner wasm Clippy                   (--target wasm32-wasip2, -A dead-code)

MEASURED: leg 2 EXITS 1. cargo fmt --check reports 43 FILES with diffs, across crates/control, crates/execution, crates/platform, services/ctl, services/scenario-worker, tests/conformance and more.

*** THEREFORE LEGS 3 THROUGH 9 HAVE NEVER RUN. NOT ONE OF THE SIX CLIPPY LEGS IS REACHABLE. ***

## This corrects a banked fact, and the correction matters

The standing baseline memory recorded that components/ is a separate cargo workspace that HAS NEVER HAD A CLIPPY BASELINE, and attributed it to needing its own invocation. *** THAT CAUSE WAS WRONG. *** The invocation EXISTS -- four dedicated components legs including two wasm32-wasip2 targets -- and it is pinned token-by-token. It simply is never reached. The effect was right; the diagnosis was wrong, and the wrong diagnosis pointed at building something that already exists.

## The purest instance of the invisible-red class yet found on this branch

tests/conformance/tests/repo_lint.rs PASSES. It pins the exact argv of every leg, token by token (repo_lint.rs:185-275), and asserts the tool executes argv directly. *** IT NEVER RUNS THE TOOL. *** So there is a GREEN CONFORMANCE TEST asserting a lint plan that has never executed a single lint. A gate that does not run is indistinguishable from a gate that passes -- here the indistinguishability is certified by a passing test.

## Interaction with wamn-0h0g.12.147 -- do not resolve these independently

None of the six legs carries --keep-going, so every one is ALSO subject to the within-run fail-fast masking .12.147 identifies. There are now FOUR distinct reasons a lint red is invisible here:
  1. cargo aborts scheduling within a run                     -> --keep-going (.12.147)

  3. the lint SCRIPT aborts at leg 2, so six legs never run   -> THIS BEAD

tools/repo-lint argv is PINNED TOKEN-BY-TOKEN by tests/conformance/tests/repo_lint.rs:185-275. Adding --keep-going, reordering legs, or making rustfmt non-fatal REDS THAT CONFORMANCE TEST unless the pin is updated in the same commit. Treat the tool and its pin as one edit.

## Note on sequencing, not a decision

Landing the six root-clippy fixes does NOT unblock this -- rustfmt aborts BEFORE root Clippy. Conversely, formatting the 43 files would let root Clippy run and then fail on the six known errors, and only after BOTH are clean would legs 5-9 execute for the first time and produce a components baseline nobody has ever seen. Expect that first components run to surface new reds; that is success, not regression.

## Scope

description:

exists (41898 bytes). It is a STUB CLOSED BY RULING that refuses at RUNTIME. Anything

30 adjudications. It was split out of wamn-0h0g.15.173 by owner ruling (dkk,

The carrier argument may not hold. Whoever runs this must verify the swap produces an

expect false reds. Do NOT use the live kind cluster -- it is frozen.

architecture/protected-writes.json is MACHINE-GENERATED and must NEVER be hand-edited.
