title: [SR-MVP] fix(runtime): the management admission statement has no production caller and no recovery lookup
description:
FILED 2026-08-19 by the bead-close-reason coverage sweep. wamn-0h0g.15.160's close reason recorded that rider 3's 'recovery-by-producer-key stays primary' names a path that does not exist, and said it was 'filed as follow-up'. NO SUCH BEAD EXISTED. This is that bead.

MEASURED: the management admission statement has no production caller and no recovery lookup. wamn-0h0g.8.5 and .7.4 are open and would build consumers, but neither records this, so neither is a real owner of it.

CONSEQUENCE: the SQL classifier fallback is TODAY THE ONLY REPLAY MECHANISM, and it is load-bearing by default rather than by decision. A fallback that is silently primary is the shape that hides until it fails.

ACCEPTANCE: either the recovery-by-producer-key path exists and is exercised by a named test, or the design is amended to make the classifier path primary DELIBERATELY, with the rider corrected rather than left describing a path that is not there.
notes:
*** WAVE-9 MEASUREMENT LANE, 2026-08-19. THIS BEAD'S CENTRAL CLAIMS ARE REFUTED. NO CODE WAS
WRITTEN. THE LANE STOPPED FOR AN OWNER RULING, WHICH IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME. ***

Measured in an isolated worktree off f27ad353 with a private target dir. A throwaway
postgres:18 was created on port 55432 and removed; the frozen kind cluster was not touched.

=====================================================================
FIVE CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD AS FILED
=====================================================================
C1. IT IS RIDER 2, NOT RIDER 3. wamn-0h0g.15.160's description reads
    "RIDER 2: lane 2's recovery-by-producer-key path stays PRIMARY." There is no rider 3.

C2. *** "NO RECOVERY LOOKUP" IS FALSE. *** A recovery-by-producer-key lookup EXISTS, works,
    and is exercised by a live test that actually ran:
      admission.rs:750-754  keyed_run AS MATERIALIZED (... WHERE r.idempotency_key = k.producer_key)
      admission.rs:804      COALESCE(xr.run_id, kr.run_id) AS existing_run_id
      admission.rs:850-851  emits it
    Presenting the same key with a DIFFERENT run id -- exactly the crashed-and-re-minted
    shape -- answers conflicting-run-identity NAMING THE EXISTING RUN. Proven live at
    admission_live.rs:957-960. What does NOT exist is a standalone read-only lookup, the
    management analogue of lookup_invocation_recovery_sql.
    So producer_key has THREE uses here: persisted as runs.idempotency_key (:834), the
    divergence operand (:785), and the recovery lookup (:750-754 -> :804).

C3. *** "LOAD-BEARING BY DEFAULT RATHER THAN BY DECISION" IS FALSE. *** wamn-0h0g.15.160
    already made the classifier path primary BY DECISION, in code, with rationale and a
    named passing test:
      admission.rs:678-697   a 20-line ARM ORDER -- IDENTITY BEFORE DRIFT block that says
                             "the reverse of admit_sql, and deliberately so
                             (wamn-0h0g.15.160). Do not fix the asymmetry."
      admission.rs:367-377   the matching DRIFT BEFORE IDENTITY block on the callable side
      admission.rs:1389-1418 test an_exact_management_retry_is_answered_before_the_world_is_
                             rechecked, asserting the ordering in BOTH statements. It passes.
    The stated consequence is therefore ALREADY REMEDIATED IN CODE.

C4. "NEITHER 8.5 NOR 7.4 RECORDS THIS" IS HALF WRONG. wamn-0h0g.8.5's acceptance explicitly
    requires "including crash after project commit" -- that IS the recovery requirement,
    recorded. 7.4 records nothing about recovery and is not an owner.

C5. *** THE PREMISE IS STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE FOR THE ONLY PARTLY-BUILT PRODUCER. *** The
    bead's motivating story is "a crashed producer's run id it never recorded". A test-case
    producer CANNOT fail to record its run id, because the id is a PURE FUNCTION OF THE
    COORDINATE: services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs:167-171
    test_case_run_id(tenant, report, ordinal, case) = "test-run-" + sha256(preimage)[7..].
    Belt and braces: reserve_test_report commits the ordinal-to-run_id mapping into the
    CONTROL db (insert_test_case_run_sql, :92-108) BEFORE admission runs. A crash re-drives
    the identical admission and gets duplicate with the SAME run id -- the leg already at
    admission_live.rs:911-926, whose own comment calls it "The crash-recovery leg".

=====================================================================
CONFIRMED: NO PRODUCTION CALLER (the one claim that survives)
=====================================================================
ManagementRun occurs ONLY at admission.rs:8/205/231 (the definition), admission.rs:1484
(a cfg(test) unit test) and admission_live.rs:835 (the ignored live test). The only two
production callers of admission_transaction are both CallableFlow:
components/execution/materializer/src/main.rs:407 and
crates/platform/runtime/src/flow_invocation.rs:665.
Searched beyond Rust per the deletion-collateral rule -- sh, md, sql, yaml, json, toml, wit.
No caller. The deploy/sql hits for draft-run (control-portable-store.sql:293,
catalog-schema.sql:1396) are a CHECK constraint on the control-plane authoring command
ledger: a different draft-run (a command KIND), not the admission producer.
NOTE: the two pin scripts named in 15.160's close reason, admission-execution-pin.sh and
http-ordinary-admission.sh, DO NOT EXIST on this branch. No scraped-name collateral.

=====================================================================
WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT -- SMALLER THAN THE BEAD, AND IT IS A TRUTH DECISION
=====================================================================
TWO FALSE DOC COMMENTS, both in this bead's own file:
  admission.rs:103-110  "... and it is also how a crashed producer's control-side reconciler
                        recovers the run id it never recorded."
  admission.rs:1305-1306 repeats the same claim.
A reconciler does exist (reconcile_test_report, test_orchestration.rs:341) but it NEVER
queries by idempotency_key -- it takes run ids as already-observed arguments (:317-319).
Grep for idempotency_key across all of services/scenario-worker/src/ returns ZERO hits.
This is the FALSE COVERAGE CLASS again, in a doc comment.

*** THE LANE DID NOT FIX THEM, DELIBERATELY AND CORRECTLY: choosing the replacement text
STATES THE DESIGN CONCLUSION, which is an owner call. ***

=====================================================================
A SEPARATE CODE-SHAPED QUESTION, FLAGGED AND NOT ACTED ON
=====================================================================
The SQL recovers the run id and THE RUST BOUNDARY THROWS IT AWAY.
AdmissionResult::ConflictingRunIdentity is a UNIT variant (admission.rs:151); from_parts
drops the id (:173); admission.rs:1378-1381 PINS the discard.
Today that costs nothing (no caller). It becomes load-bearing the moment wamn-0h0g.8.5
mounts a consumer that must distinguish "your coordinate is taken by run X" from "your
coordinate is taken."
*** MAKING IT CARRY THE ID IS A PUBLIC-TYPE AND WIRE CHANGE WITH A SECURITY EDGE: ***
flow_invocation.rs:933 maps this result to HTTP 409, and the CALLABLE statement also returns
a run id on that code (:551, :632) -- so the change would expose an internal run id to an
HTTP caller. That is an owner decision, not a lane decision.

=====================================================================
PROOF THE LIVE SUITE ACTUALLY RAN (not a vacuous green)
=====================================================================
Shape: admission_live.rs:139-141 is #[test] + #[ignore], ONE test fn for the whole file. It
is ignore-gated, NOT self-skipping, so it needs -- --ignored.
  cargo test -p wamn-run-state --test admission_live -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; in 17.81s
Negative control: with the env var unset it PANICS and FAILS in 0.00s at :143 (.expect, not
a skip-and-return), so a vacuous green is structurally impossible.
Durable side effects: the throwaway db afterwards held exactly the management rows the legs
write (draft-run-1 / scenario-draft / full / draft:cmd-1 and case-run-0 / test-case / off /
case:report-a:0) and ZERO rows for draft-run-2 and case-run-9, proving the four
conflicting-run-identity legs ran and refused atomically. Fresh cluster confirmed first:
zero wamn% roles before the run.
Also green: cargo test -p wamn-run-state --lib admission -- 28 passed; 0 failed.

=====================================================================
RULING OWED
=====================================================================
Neither acceptance branch is right as written. (a) would ADD a second uncalled artifact --
the very defect class this bead was filed against -- serving an unbuilt consumer whose
run-id strategy is undecided. (b) is largely ALREADY DONE by 15.160.
What the owner must decide:
  1. Will the draft-run producer derive its run id from command_id the way test_case_run_id
     derives from the coordinate? If yes, recovery-by-producer-key is PERMANENTLY
     unnecessary and the two comments should simply say so.
  2. May ConflictingRunIdentity carry a run id on the callable path, or do the two
     statements need separate result types? (This is the HTTP-409 exposure question.)
The lane has a proposed two-comment, zero-behaviour-change correction ready to apply on a
ruling; the existing named test already covers the replacement claim.
close_reason: CLOSED AS REFUTED by owner ruling 2026-08-19, on a wave-9 read-only measurement that overturned this bead's premise. THREE of its claims are false. (1) 'No recovery lookup' -- a recovery-by-producer-key lookup EXISTS and works: keyed_run at admission.rs:750-754, carried out at :804 and emitted at :850-851, so presenting the same key with a different run id answers conflicting-run-identity NAMING the existing run. Proven by a live test that actually ran (admission_live.rs:957-960). What does not exist is a standalone read-only lookup. (2) 'Load-bearing BY DEFAULT rather than BY DECISION' -- wamn-0h0g.15.160 already made the classifier path primary BY DECISION, with a 20-line ARM ORDER rationale block at admission.rs:678-697, its callable-side counterpart at :367-377, and a named passing test at :1389-1418. (3) The motivating story, a crashed producer's run id it never recorded, is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for the only partly-built producer: test_case_run_id (test_orchestration.rs:167-171) derives the id as a pure function of the coordinate, and reserve_test_report commits the mapping to the control database BEFORE admission runs. Also corrected: it is RIDER 2 of .15.160, not rider 3; and .8.5 DOES record the recovery requirement in its acceptance, so 'neither records this' was half wrong. NEITHER ACCEPTANCE BRANCH WAS RIGHT -- (a) would add a SECOND uncalled artifact, the very defect class this bead was filed against, serving an unbuilt consumer; (b) is largely already done. THE ONE SURVIVING CLAIM: the management admission statement genuinely has NO production caller, confirmed tree-wide including shell, markdown, sql, yaml, json, toml and wit. Residue filed as wamn-0h0g.15.179 (the two false doc comments) and wamn-0h0g.15.180 (the ConflictingRunIdentity discard, which has an HTTP 409 exposure edge); both existed before this reason was written. NO CODE WAS WRITTEN.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(router): re-home or retire ThrottleTable and ConcurrencyGate before wamn-0h0g.26.4 deletes flow-engine
description:
FILED 2026-08-19 by the bead-close-reason coverage sweep the owner ruled. *** THIS IS A BEAD'S OWN STATED FAILURE MODE COMING TRUE. ***

wamn-0h0g.16.6's close reason said: re-home or explicitly retire ThrottleTable/ConcurrencyGate (129 LOC, flow-engine/src/throttle.rs) under .17.1/.19.1 before .26.4 deletes the engine, or that behaviour is lost silently.

MEASURED: NEITHER NAMED OWNER TOOK IT. wamn-0h0g.17.1 closed as per-digest instance pools without touching throttle.rs. wamn-0h0g.19.1 is inline HTTP routing and never mentions it. wamn-0h0g.16.7's close reason later records that the owner was offered the port as an explicit alternative and CHOSE DISSOLUTION, attaching only the in_flight counting shape to .19.2 -- which covers in-flight counting but NOT per-flow concurrency and NOT cross-run throttling.

SO: ConcurrencyGate (per-flow concurrency) and ThrottleTable (cross-run throttle keys) have no owner, and wamn-0h0g.26.4 is OPEN and deletes flow-engine wholesale. When it lands, the behaviour goes silently -- which is precisely what .16.6 warned about.

THE DECISION IS GENUINELY OPEN, not a formality. The ledger already records (section H.2) that these are in-memory HashMaps with no durable deadline, no multi-replica authority and no restart recovery, and that wamn-ynwf owns the durable production wiring. So one legitimate answer is: they were never production-grade, wamn-ynwf owns the real thing, delete them and record it. The other is: per-flow concurrency is load-bearing today and must land somewhere before the deletion. EITHER IS DEFENSIBLE; NEITHER HAS BEEN CHOSEN.

ACCEPTANCE: a recorded ruling, and if retirement, an explicit note on wamn-0h0g.26.4 that the deletion is intentional rather than collateral.
notes:
MEASUREMENT 2026-08-19 (read-only, main loop, before asking the owner to rule).
Two facts that change how this decision is priced. Both were measured, not recalled.

1. CONCURRENCYGATE AND THROTTLETABLE HAVE ZERO CONSUMERS OUTSIDE FLOW-ENGINE.
   A tree-wide grep for the two type names over every .rs file returns only:
     - crates/execution/flow-engine/src/throttle.rs  (the definitions themselves)
     - crates/execution/flow-engine/src/lib.rs:71    (the pub use re-export)
     - crates/execution/flow-engine/src/lib.rs:47    (a doc comment)
     - crates/execution/flow-engine/tests/runner.rs:567,587,597 (flow-engine's OWN tests)
   Nothing else in the tree names either type. So the description's second horn --
   "per-flow concurrency is load-bearing today and must land somewhere before the
   deletion" -- IS FALSE AS STATED. Nothing calls it today. The only thing the
   deletion can lose is the CODE and its three own-tests, not a live behaviour.
   That does not settle the ruling by itself: the owner may still want the concept
   carried forward as a requirement. But the decision is between RETIRE and
   PRESERVE-AS-INTENT, not between RETIRE and BREAK-PRODUCTION.

2. *** A SEPARATE AND MORE SERIOUS CORRECTION, ABOUT .26.4 RATHER THAN THIS BEAD.
   MY BANKED MEMORY SAID "crates/execution/flow-engine is wamn-runner (and nothing
   depends on it)". THAT IS FALSE. *** Measured consumers of the wamn-runner package:
     - crates/execution/run-state/Cargo.toml:25 -- and it is a REAL source dependency,
       not a dev one: src/status.rs:155 and :233 carry From impls over
       wamn_runner::ExecutionStatus and wamn_runner::ExecutionFailureKind.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(provision): reusable A/B generations for scoped workload logins
description: Generalize the proven A/B credential lifecycle across one exhaustive provisioning-only WorkloadRoleFamily set: effect-writer, control-author, dispatch-reader, service-reader, app, and retention. The app member is a per-tenant generated workload login family targeting a stable NOLOGIN ACL role; it does not preserve the rejected shared wamn_app LOGIN. Existing effect-writer and control-author A/B implementations migrate into this single lifecycle rather than remaining bespoke dialects. Run-projection-writer is retired input, not a family, because wamn-0h0g.26.3.1 deletes its sole node_runs authority.
design: Define a closed WorkloadRoleFamily provisioning enum distinct from runtime AuthorityClass. Tenant-scoped families are app, effect-writer, and retention. Project-environment-scoped families are dispatch-reader and service-reader. Control-author is control-scoped. One generic lifecycle owns bounded deterministic names, advisory-locked prepare/harden, state inspection, credential rendering, bounded A/B overlap, selection, retirement, and old-session termination. Existing effect-writer and control-author implementations are absorbed with equivalence probes. Stable ACL roles remain NOLOGIN/passwordless and every generated membership is SET FALSE and ADMIN FALSE. Legacy effect-writer projection membership may be recognized and revoked during migration but is never modeled or minted as a WorkloadRoleFamily. Runtime AuthorityClass remains separate.
acceptance_criteria: One exhaustive WorkloadRoleFamily enum contains exactly effect-writer, control-author, dispatch-reader, service-reader, app, and retention; adding a family is a code change and there is no arbitrary role-name escape hatch. Scopes are exact: app, effect-writer, and retention tenant-scoped; dispatch-reader and service-reader project-environment-scoped; control-author control-scoped. Existing effect-writer and control-author A/B lifecycles are absorbed, with equivalence probes rejecting two dialects. No run-projection-writer family, name, Secret, generation, or grant is created; legacy membership is retirement input only. Names, locking, lifecycle state, overlap, retirement, session termination, password handling, SET FALSE/ADMIN FALSE membership, pool multiplication, and connection-budget tripwires retain the previously ruled contract. Shared wamn_app LOGIN retirement remains wamn-0h0g.12.140.

title: fix(deploy): bootstrap.sh cannot invoke provision-project-env at all — the required credential args are supplied nowhere
description:
PRE-EXISTING BREAKAGE, landed by wamn-0h0g.12.122 at e22233c3 on 2026-08-18. Measured 2026-08-19.

.12.122 made --dispatch-reader-password a REQUIRED clap argument (services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs:137, field type String, no default_value). deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh invokes provision-project-env at :171, :226, :315, :349 and :628 and supplies NEITHER the flag NOR the env var WAMN_DISPATCH_READER_PASSWORD -- neither string appears anywhere in the file, and nothing in deploy/ or tests/ exports it. *** EVERY ONE OF THOSE FIVE INVOCATIONS THEREFORE FAILS AT ARGUMENT PARSING TODAY. ***

*** THIS WAS SUPPOSED TO HAVE BEEN FILED AND WAS NOT. *** .12.122's close reason says: BREAKAGE REPORTED, NOT FIXED (filed separately). No such bead exists -- bd search for bootstrap.sh, mode-scoped, and provision-project-env modes all return nothing. That is the SAME false-coverage class the owner ruled a ledger sweep for on 2026-08-19 (findings.md:569 asserting the wamn_app role was already tracked), except here the false claim lives in a bead close reason rather than the findings ledger. THE SWEEP SHOULD COVER CLOSE REASONS TOO, not just ledger rows.

THE UNDERLYING CLI-CONTRACT DECISION IS STILL OWED AND IS THE OWNER'S, exactly as .12.122 said. Three of the five call sites (:171, :226, :315) are effect-writer GENERATION modes -- --abort-effect-writer-generation, --prepare-effect-writer-generation, --retire-effect-writer-generation. They provision no database and never reach role_sql, so requiring a database credential from them is semantically wrong, not merely inconvenient.
  (a) MODE-SCOPED REQUIREMENT: credentials required only for modes that actually provision. Correct-by-shape, but moves the field off the .12.122 String-no-default pattern to Option<String> plus a manual check.
  (b) SUPPLY THE ARGS EVERYWHERE: matches the letter of the sweep rider, keeps the .12.122 shape, but threads unused credentials through generation-management calls.

NOTE THE COMPOUNDING: the required-arg remedy for wamn-0h0g.12.129 / .12.134 adds a SECOND required credential argument to this same already-broken script.
notes:
NOT CAUSED BY the .12.129/.12.134 remedy -- measured broken BEFORE it. Recording that ordering explicitly so the credential fix is not later blamed for this.
VERIFICATION: grep -n 'DISPATCH_READER|dispatch-reader|APP_PASSWORD|app-password' deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh returns nothing.
SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-19, MEASURED: THIS IS NOT ONLY bootstrap.sh.

docs/archive/build-and-test.md -- the RUNBOOK OF RECORD -- contains EIGHT-PLUS provision-project-env recipes (around :2101, :2111, :2151, :2182, :2230, :2295, :2385, :2386) and grep for dispatch-reader-password / DISPATCH_READER_PASSWORD / app-password / APP_PASSWORD across that entire file returns *** ZERO OCCURRENCES ***. So every one of those recipes has been broken since .12.122 landed on 2026-08-18, alongside all five bootstrap.sh call sites, and nobody noticed for a day because nothing executes the runbook automatically.

INTEGRATOR ACTION TAKEN, deliberately minimal: a prominent warning block was added at the section head of build-and-test.md's provision-project-env section naming both required arguments, both env vars, and this bead. The recipes were NOT rewritten one by one, for two reasons: (1) it is 8+ blocks of churn, and (2) if the mode-scoped answer is chosen, most of those edits would be reverted. The warning is honest today under either ruling; the recipe edits are not.

The .12.134 CDC runbook at build-and-test.md:1265 WAS edited in place, because --replication-password is required in ALL modes of enable-cdc-project-env -- there is no mode-scoping question there, so the correct recipe is knowable now.

*** THE CLASS LESSON, worth carrying into the ledger sweep the owner ruled: making an argument required is a BREAKING CHANGE TO EVERY CALLER, and callers live in shell scripts and markdown runbooks that no compiler and no test suite checks. .12.122 landed one such change; the fix in c3a079ec landed a second one on the same commands. Neither would be caught by cargo test, cargo clippy, or the sweep of record. ***
OWNER RULING 2026-08-19: OPTION (a) MODE-SCOPED, WITH ONE PREMISE CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN OPTION TEXT.

Verbatim option chosen: 'Mode-scoped, enforced at parse time'. Owner's rider: clap required_if_eq / ArgGroup keyed on the mode, so the generation modes need no credential and the provisioning modes still refuse AT PARSE TIME. Stated reason: it keeps the no-default guard tests meaningful -- the refusal stays a parse error, not a runtime one -- and makes the five bootstrap sites correct without inventing dummy secrets.

*** PREMISE CORRECTION, RECORDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION. *** This bead's option (a) says mode-scoping 'moves the field off the .12.122 String-no-default pattern to Option plus a MANUAL CHECK'. That is wrong on the second half and the owner's ruling turns on exactly that point. clap enforces conditional requirement at PARSE time via required_unless_present_any / required_if_eq; no manual runtime check is needed. The expected shape is Option<String> plus required_unless_present_any over the three generation-mode flags, which keeps enforcement in the parser where the .12.129 guard tests can still see it. THE LANE MUST VERIFY THIS AGAINST THE ACTUAL FLAG NAMES AND CLAP VERSION AND CORRECT ME IF IT DOES NOT HOLD.

SCOPE OF THE REMEDY, both required credentials on the same command:
1. services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs -- --dispatch-reader-password and --app-password both become mode-scoped on the same rule.
2. deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh -- the two provisioning call sites (:349, :628) gain explicit args; the three generation-mode sites (:171, :226, :315) gain NOTHING, which is the whole point of the ruling.
3. enable-cdc-project-env is OUT OF SCOPE and stays required-always -- --replication-password is required in ALL its modes, already recorded in this bead's notes and already fixed in the runbook.
4. docs/archive/build-and-test.md recipe rewrites are INTEGRATOR-OWNED and do NOT belong to the lane. The warning block already standing there becomes replaceable with correct per-recipe args once the ruling is implemented.

GUARD OBLIGATION: the new tests must prove BOTH arms -- a provisioning mode without the credential FAILS to parse, and a generation mode without the credential PARSES. One arm alone re-admits the defect from the other side.

WAVE 7 LANE 4. Authorized for implementation by the owner in the same turn as this ruling.
MEASUREMENT PASS 2026-08-19, READ-ONLY. THE RULING IS IMPLEMENTABLE. Three corrections, one of them to the ruling's own mechanism.

MY PREMISE CORRECTION IS VERIFIED, AND BY IN-FILE PRECEDENT RATHER THAN ARGUMENT. This exact struct ALREADY USES the shape, at provision_project_env.rs:244-249, where emit_secret carries required_unless_present_any over revoke_pat_prefix, prepare_effect_writer_generation, retire_effect_writer_generation, abort_effect_writer_generation. The remedy is to copy that list verbatim onto the two credential args. clap 4.6.1 (root Cargo.toml:55, Cargo.lock:503). Enforcement is in the validator at parse time (clap_builder validator.rs:361-367), so the guard tests stay parse-level exactly as the owner required.

CORRECTION 1, TO THE RULING'S NAMED MECHANISM. *** required_if_eq CANNOT EXPRESS THIS RULE. *** It means 'required IF arg X EQUALS value V'; it cannot say 'required unless any of four modes is present' without four inverted rules keyed on values the mode args do not have. required_unless_present_any is the primitive. ArgGroup is also unnecessary: the generation flags already form an exclusive set via pairwise conflicts_with_all at :180-183, :191-194, :205-208. THE RULING'S SUBSTANCE -- mode-scoped, enforced at parse time, no manual runtime check -- IS UNAFFECTED. Only the named attribute changes.

CORRECTION 2, TO MY OWN NOTE. I wrote that the modes are bool flags. THEY ARE NOT. All four are value-taking options: prepare/retire/abort are Option<CredentialGeneration> (:177-210) and revoke is Option<String> (:273-282). The error is in the safe direction -- required_unless_present_any over value args is the simplest case, with none of the SetTrue default-value subtlety I was worried about.

CORRECTION 3, TO THIS BEAD'S OWN SCOPE. *** THERE ARE FOUR CREDENTIAL-FREE MODES, NOT THREE. *** --revoke-pat-prefix returns at :331 before touching anything. And *** bootstrap.sh:349 IS THE REVOKE MODE, NOT A PROVISIONING SITE *** -- this bead's remedy item 2 names it as one, so implementing that item literally would put a database credential on the revoke path, which is precisely the dummy-secret outcome the owner's ruling exists to prevent. Only ONE of the five bootstrap sites (:628) is a provisioning site.

CONSEQUENCE: bootstrap.sh MAY NEED ZERO EDITS. :628 does raw pass-through of bootstrap's own argv (:19) and the wrapper's rejection list at :53-63 does not list either credential flag, so an operator can already pass them through; deploy/mvp/tests/bootstrap.sh:472 relies on exactly that channel. Adding an explicit flag there would require inventing a new wrapper-parsed variable AND would put a secret on a ps-visible argv. THE LANE SHOULD RAISE THIS RATHER THAN MECHANICALLY EXECUTING REMEDY ITEM 2. Correspondingly, this bead's claim that all five invocations fail at parsing today is OVERSTATED for :628: it fails only when neither the env var nor a pass-through flag is supplied.

TWO COMPILE BREAKS THIS BEAD DOES NOT LIST -- a lane scoped to the bead's four items ships RED:
  services/ctl/tests/effect_writer_generation_live.rs:72-99 builds ProvisionProjectEnvArgs as a STRUCT LITERAL with app_password and dispatch_reader_password set to 'unused'. Option<String> breaks it at compile time. It is ignore-gated at runtime but compiles on every cargo build -p wamn-ctl --tests. Under the change those become None, which is the honest value.
  deploy/mvp/tests/bootstrap.sh:469-473, the only automated executor of bootstrap.sh (invoked from build-and-test.md:3726), passes --app-password through but never --dispatch-reader-password, so it is broken today AND STAYS BROKEN after the ruling, because :628 remains a provisioning site.

TEST IMPACT, precise. BREAKS: the_dispatch_reader_password_has_no_default :2543-2548 (assert_eq against a String field; needs as_deref). SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the_app_password_has_no_default :2556-2574. SURVIVES BUT ITS COMMENT BECOMES FALSE: pat_issue_flags_select_independently_and_revoke_conflicts :2232-2236, whose in-tree comment says the requirement is not mode-scoped and cites this bead -- the lane must rewrite it. THE SECOND ARM DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE: no test asserts that a generation mode WITHOUT the credential PARSES. It must be written against a bare TestCli::try_parse_from, NOT via the parse_args helper (:2034-2053), which injects both credentials and would make the arm vacuous. Cover all FOUR exempt modes.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE FOR THE LANE: run must destructure the Option at :415 and :423. That should be an expect() naming the clap invariant, NOT a context()? that re-implements the check -- a runtime bail would create a second, weaker enforcement point and hollow out the parse-time guarantee the owner ruled for.

CITATION DRIFT IN THIS BEAD: the args are at :134-139 and :150-151, not :126/:137. The build-and-test.md recipes are at :2113/:2123/:2163/:2194/:2242/:2307/:2397/:2398 -- all shifted about 11 lines by the integrator warning block this bead's own notes record inserting. Same unverified-citation failure this bead was filed to indict.

TWO NEW FINDINGS FOR THE LEDGER SWEEP:
  (a) *** THE ENV-VAR ESCAPE HATCH. *** Because both args carry env=, an exported WAMN_APP_PASSWORD or WAMN_DISPATCH_READER_PASSWORD counts as PRESENT to clap and SILENTLY DISARMS the is_err() guard tests. build-and-test.md's own warning block at :2096-2106 instructs operators to export exactly those. Same defect class as the documented default that c3a079ec removed: a value nobody sets deliberately satisfying a check nobody re-reads. Edition 2024 makes std::env::remove_var unsafe, so there is no trivial in-test fix. NEEDS ITS OWN BEAD.
  (b) *** A SECOND FALSE CITATION IN wamn-0h0g.12.122's CLOSE REASON. *** It names tools/gate-mutants/effect-writer-primitive.sh:271,273 as a broken caller. THAT FILE DOES NOT EXIST -- tools/gate-mutants/ was deleted in full at 5c47074b. This is the same close reason already indicted for claiming a filing that never happened. Feed it to the close-reason sweep.

title: fix(scenario-worker): test_orchestration_live fails the effect-uncertain guard once the bootstrap defect stops masking it
description:
REVEALED BY FIXING wamn-0h0g.20.6, 2026-08-19, and proven pre-existing by a controlled base comparison on two fresh postgres:18 instances.

THE CONTROL, run by the integrator:
  BASE (733ea4ce): services/scenario-worker/tests/test_orchestration_live.rs panics at :95 with
      role wamn_run_projection_writer does not exist
    -- the .20.6 bootstrap defect.
  WITH .20.6 APPLIED: the bootstrap succeeds, the suite runs FURTHER, and then fails with
      ERROR: authoring-test-case-not-effect-uncertain
    raised from deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql:225.

*** THIS DEFECT IS NOT A REGRESSION. IT WAS MASKED. *** The suite has never been able to reach this
point, so nobody has ever observed it. That is the whole hazard of a gate that is broken at base:
it hides everything downstream of the break, and the count of defects it conceals is unknown until
the break is repaired. Two of .20.6's three fold-in sites now pass live (the claims.rs effect-
authority gate and run_state_live); this is the third.

THE GUARD, deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql:217-226: setting a test case's failure_kind to
effect-uncertain requires an EXISTING wamn_run.runs row for the same tenant_id/run_id whose status
is effect-uncertain. The test drives the case to that failure_kind without the run being in that
status.

WHICH SIDE IS WRONG IS NOT YET DETERMINED and was deliberately not investigated further -- it is
outside .20.6's scope, which is the bootstrap. Three candidates, in the order I would check them:
  (a) the test fixture never transitions the run to effect-uncertain and should;
  (b) the transition happens through a path the disposable-database harness does not exercise;
  (c) the guard is over-strict relative to the orchestration contract.
Note that the sibling guards immediately above it (deadline-exhausted arms at :202-216) are
clock-sensitive, so a mis-sequenced fixture can plausibly land in the wrong arm.
notes:
DO NOT FOLD THIS INTO .20.6. .20.6 is the bootstrap defect and its scope is closed by the three role/rename fixes; this is a distinct failure with an independent green state, per the granularity rule.
REPRODUCTION: fresh postgres:18, then WAMN_TEST_ORCHESTRATION_PG_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:PORT/postgres cargo test --locked -p wamn-scenario-worker --test test_orchestration_live -- --test-threads=1. One fresh container per suite -- PostgreSQL roles are cluster-wide and a reused container fails the next suite with a password error that LOOKS like a mutant kill.
MEASUREMENT PASS 2026-08-19, READ-ONLY. The guard characterisation is EXACT, the failure line is confirmed, and *** THE EVIDENCE POINTS AT A FOURTH OPTION THIS BEAD DID NOT LIST. OWNER RULING NEEDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION. ***

GUARD VERIFIED, deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql:217-226. A BEFORE UPDATE setting failure_kind = effect-uncertain requires a matching wamn_run.runs row on (tenant_id, run_id) with status = effect-uncertain, else RAISE 55000 authoring-test-case-not-effect-uncertain. The neighbouring arms are unreachable on this update: :209 is gated on failure_kind NOT IN (deadline-exhausted, effect-uncertain).

FAILURE LINE: services/scenario-worker/tests/test_orchestration_live.rs:249, the expect on the third reconcile_test_report call, raised from services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs:369-384. The two earlier calls at :224 and :231 pass empty or non-matching id sets, match zero rows, and never fire the trigger.

*** THE TEST NEVER ESTABLISHES THE ROW DELIBERATELY. *** test_orchestration_live.rs:202-207 is a standing comment recording that wamn-0h0g.8.18 made effect uncertainty an ALREADY-OBSERVED project fact arriving as an argument rather than as a join this store cannot perform, and that the proof no longer seeds a run row because there is no run plane in the store under test. git show 4bee577a shows the deleted INSERT INTO runs block plus its node_runs and catalog seed rows, about 40 lines, removed on purpose.

*** THE DECISIVE FINDING: THIS GUARD IS RESIDUE 8.18 FORGOT, AND IT VIOLATES AN INVARIANT THE SAME CRATE TESTS FOR. ***
  8.18 (4bee577a) removed a cross-database join from reconcile_test_report and LEFT THE TRIGGER BEHIND.
  The guard DOES NOT EXIST IN PRODUCTION. The three tables moved to the control database; deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql creates all three (:309, :332, :369) and installs only the generic immutability trigger. crates/control/provision/tests/control_portable_store.rs:95 ASSERTS THE ABSENCE: assert not contains guard_authoring_test_orchestration_write. Commit 99a84c46 says so outright.
  services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs:510-527 is a conformance test named no_statement_reaches_the_project_run_plane which FORBIDS the tokens run.status and run.run_id. authoring-tests.sql:221-222 contains literally both. The crate's guard scans only the Rust module, so the DDL slipped past it.
  Production scenario-worker connects via WAMN_CONTROL_AUTHORING_PG_URL to the control database. THE GUARD IS ENFORCED IN EXACTLY TWO LIVE TESTS AND NOWHERE ELSE, and test_orchestration_live.rs:249 is the ONLY line in the repository that ever fires this arm.

THE CANDIDATES, RANKED. (b) IS REFUTED OUTRIGHT -- there is no such path; the only writer of runs.status = effect-uncertain in the tree is a test fixture at crates/execution/run-state/tests/effect_writer_live.rs:577, and the scenario-worker names runs nowhere in its implementation. (a) merely makes the test pass: mechanically viable since rewrite_schema gives the test a runs table, but it means reverting 8.18's deletion, re-adding the catalog FK seed rows, and re-asserting a cross-plane fact the production topology cannot produce -- leaving the test STRICTER THAN PRODUCTION in exactly the direction 8.18 ruled out. (c) is right but undersells it: the guard does not merely over-constrain a contract, it contradicts a landed ruling.
*** RECOMMENDED, THE MISSING OPTION (d): DELETE THE ARM AT :217-226. *** Correct-by-shape on four independent grounds -- it is 8.18 residue, it is absent from the production store by explicit assertion, no production write path exercises it, and it encodes a join the codebase tests against elsewhere. Deleting it loses ZERO coverage. A fifth option, degrading the guard with to_regclass IS NOT NULL, ranks LAST, below (a): a guard that silently disables itself wherever it matters is worse than no guard.
RANKING: (d) > (c) > (a) > (e) > (b, refuted). Said plainly: THE GUARD IS THE THING THAT IS WRONG.

*** WHY THIS IS AN OWNER RULING AND NOT A LANE DECISION: *** deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql is a governed DDL record registered in architecture/state-owners.json:157-160. Deleting an arm is a SCHEMA-OF-RECORD change, and the run-plane reconciler will plan a RepairHelperFunction against any deployed database. That is correct propagation, not breakage, but it is deploy-visible.

FILE DOMAIN -- THIS BEAD'S LIST IS INCOMPLETE. Beyond authoring-tests.sql, option (d) REQUIRES docs/archive/build-and-test.md:4688 and :4694, where the file's sha256 is pinned TWICE and the gate block's first command is sha256sum --check. Verified reproducing at HEAD. That file is INTEGRATOR-OWNED, so the re-pin is not the lane's to make. Verified NOT needing edits: crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs extracts the guard body from the file at compile time (authoring_test_helper_sql, :822-838) and every Rust assertion matches on NAME only, so the change propagates automatically and breaks no Rust test; tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs:2016 embeds a SYNTHETIC guard string, not a copy.

ENV GATING -- *** THIS IS WHY A P1 DEFECT SURVIVED UNSEEN. *** test_orchestration_live.rs:61-67 self-skips on WAMN_TEST_ORCHESTRATION_PG_URL and is NOT marked ignore. So a plain cargo test -p wamn-scenario-worker RUNS it, prints one line to stderr, and REPORTS PASS. That is the worst combination in the tree. read_authority.rs:161-169 has the same shape on WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL. By contrast run_state_live.rs:44-47 is ignore-gated and panics if run without the var, which is honest, and claims.rs:2732 carries both.

ORDERING VERSUS .20.14: GENUINELY INDEPENDENT, and the plan-of-record ordering was BACKWARDS. .20.14 operates on the role bootstrap at :69-90 and completes before any DDL is applied; this defect fires 180 lines later inside a trigger on a runs-row predicate, and roles are not in that predicate. Fixing .20.14 first buys NOTHING here. *** DO .20.12 FIRST *** -- it is P1 and the actual red; .20.14 is P3 tidying whose own bead says the copies are correct today.
close_reason:
Landed at 80f455af, option (d) per the owner's 2026-08-19 ruling -- the arm at deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql:217-226 is deleted.

THE RESIDUE CASE IS STRONGER THAN THE BEAD OR THE MEASUREMENT PASS STATED. The lane checked rather than assumed: git show 4bee577a -- deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql is EMPTY. wamn-0h0g.8.18 never opened the file. It is a pure leave-behind, not a partial edit.

The other three grounds held: absent from the production control store (control_portable_store.rs:95 asserts it), unreachable by any production write path (WAMN_CONTROL_AUTHORING_PG_URL is the sole authoring connection, no fallback), and it encoded the tokens run.status and run.run_id that the owning crate's own conformance test no_statement_reaches_the_project_run_plane forbids -- the guard scanned only the Rust module, so the DDL walked past the test written to stop exactly this.

THAT GAP IS THE PROBE. The guard now scans the DDL record as well as the Rust module, with wamn_run.runs added to the token list. Proven, not asserted: re-inserting the arm fails it with 'the DDL record reaches the project run plane via run.status'.

GATE OF RECORD: test_orchestration_live PASSES END TO END FOR THE FIRST TIME, against a fresh postgres:18. VERIFIED REAL RATHER THAN TRUSTED -- my first residue check was WRONG, because the test drops both schemas in its own teardown, so an empty database proves nothing either way. The container log is the evidence: three OTHER guards fired as the test's negative assertions require (deadline-not-exhausted, uncontrolled-update, orchestration-immutable) and authoring-test-case-not-effect-uncertain appears ZERO times. wamn-schema-control 147 passed, confirming the HelperSpec extraction carries the new body through.

build-and-test.md:4688 and :4694 re-pinned to 73e08867f0b29d8c6aec39b47a68c33bf1d38f48374bf4cf9320083df161fb9f, with a note recording that a pin moves when the bytes are deliberately changed. The runbook's own sha256sum --check command was run and passes.

FOUND WHILE GATING, FILED SEPARATELY AS wamn-0h0g.20.16 (id given because a filing claim without one is the defect this wave swept for): run_plane_reconcile_live is RED at HEAD, proven pre-existing by a base control on a fresh container, and that suite must run with --test-threads=1 or it reports seven concurrency artifacts as failures.

title: decide(gates): impactproof's disposition once the postgres entity node retires -- retire or re-scope, not default
description:
## Why

tests/integration/src/impactproof.rs proves the NAME-KEYED edge of impact analysis: plan ops -> entities -> flows, where the flow references an entity BY NAME through node config. Its fixture at :83 seeds a flow whose single node is {id: n, type: postgres, config: {entity: orders, op: get}}, and its own comment reads 'one active postgres node reading entity orders BY NAME'.

wamn-0h0g.26.8 deletes PostgresEntity, and measurement during the exe wave-4 phase-2 survey established that *** IT IS THE ONLY SHIPPED NODE TYPE WHOSE CONFIG NAMES AN ENTITY BY NAME. *** PostgresQuery, the other node in the same file (impl at crates/execution/standard-nodes/src/postgres.rs:386), takes sql and params and never entity.

So once .26.8 lands, this gate asserts over a node type the tree no longer ships.

## Why this must be decided and not defaulted

The two obvious quick fixes are both wrong in the way this repo has been bitten before. Repointing the fixture at a type that no longer exists, or at postgres-query which carries no entity config, leaves impactproof GREEN AND INERT -- passing while proving nothing. Deleting the gate silently removes coverage of the name-keyed edge without anyone ruling that the edge itself is retiring.

## The options

(a) RETIRE impactproof with the flow layer, on the ground that the name-keyed entity reference is a flow-language concept and retires with it. Then the name-keyed edge in the impact analysis is dead code and should be filed for deletion too.
(b) RE-SCOPE impactproof onto whatever the successor grammar is -- if a wiring or component surface still references entities by name, prove the edge through that producer instead.
(c) KEEP the name-keyed edge and give it a new production producer, which is only coherent if some post-flow-layer surface really does name entities by name.

The choice determines whether crates/schema/control/src/impact's name-keyed path survives at all.

## Note

The registration-keyed (id-keyed) edge is unaffected -- impact analysis reads RegistrationEdge by entity_id and that path has its own producers.
design: Formally retire impactproof with its name-keyed subject. Commit 90ae43c9 already deleted the production flow-node-config impact edge after the flows relation disappeared; the surviving integration gate is corpse coverage that expects output no live analyzer can emit. No successor is required: generated API resources are derived directly from the catalog, and future wiring impact belongs to declared wiring references rather than resurrecting the deleted PostgresEntity config path.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded owner ruling naming (a), (b) or (c), with the consequence for the name-keyed path in crates/schema/control/src/impact stated explicitly. impactproof must not survive .26.8 in a state where it passes while asserting over a node type the tree does not ship.
notes:
OWNER RULING CONFIRMED 2026-08-21: retirement follows the subject under the .11.46 split ruling. Close cites deletion commit 90ae43c9. .26.8 owns deleting the stale impactproof carrier alongside PostgresEntity retirement; registration-keyed impact remains untouched.
GIT RECEIPT c9fee3a9: empty-tree decision commit records retirement of the name-keyed impactproof subject and cites deletion commit 90ae43c9 without bundling active live-document changes.
close_reason: RATIFIED RETIREMENT: the name-keyed production impact edge was deleted in 90ae43c9 with the retired flow registry path. The surviving impactproof carrier is corpse coverage and transfers to .26.8 for deletion; registration-keyed and catalog-derived impact remain, with no successor bead required.

title: fix(exec): delete catalog_json and the postgres entity node -- the cluster wamn-0h0g.11.46 part A parked
description:
## Why this is separate from wamn-0h0g.11.46

.11.46 part A (f09e2550) deleted the app-schema-catalog-snapshot family from the manifests and greened eleven state-ownership guards. Part B -- the code half of the owner's complete-the-deletion ruling -- was SPLIT OUT because measurement showed it is not a capability removal but a CLUSTER OF RETIREMENTS, and its siblings die in this epic.

The coupling that forces the cluster: PostgresEntity::run calls ctx.catalog_json() at crates/execution/standard-nodes/src/postgres.rs:154, so removing the trait method requires resolving the node, and the node is a REGISTERED SHIPPED NODE TYPE.

## The measured surface

Capability removal: the trait decl at crates/execution/flow-model/src/node_contract.rs:307; the policy wrapper at crates/execution/standard-nodes/src/policy.rs:101-106 with its test double at :142 and assertions at :169 and :190; the guest impl at components/execution/flowrunner/src/lib.rs (see the parked-closed arm landed by .11.46); two test doubles at crates/execution/flow-engine/tests/lifecycle_node_abi_prototype.rs:31 and crates/execution/standard-nodes/tests/nodes.rs:47.

NODE_TYPES goes 9 to 8 and INTERFACES: LazyLock<[NodeInterface; 9]> goes to 8, which rewrites the positional pure_interface(NODE_TYPES[n]) indices. The 'postgres (catalog-derived entity ops)' test section from ~:631 to ~:800 of standard-nodes/tests/nodes.rs goes with it, plus the mock catalog field at :30 and the catalog_json() fixture at :131.

## Follow the established idiom -- do NOT invent one

This repo already retires node types. Removed types go into TWO lists currently reading ['cron', 'time-shift']: removed_node_types_are_unknown_to_dispatch at standard-nodes/tests/nodes.rs:899, and the retained-resolution-surface guard at :963-970. The NODE_TYPES pin at :939 is updated in the same commit. Add 'postgres' to both lists.

## THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MADE THIS ITS OWN BEAD

*** PostgresEntity IS THE ONLY SHIPPED NODE TYPE WHOSE CONFIG NAMES AN ENTITY BY NAME. *** Verified: PostgresQuery, the other node in the same file (impl at postgres.rs:386), takes sql and params and never entity. So deleting PostgresEntity removes the sole production producer of the name-keyed entity reference that impact analysis exists to trace.

tests/integration/src/impactproof.rs:83 seeds exactly such a flow -- its own comment reads 'one active postgres node reading entity orders BY NAME' -- to prove the name-keyed edge (plan ops -> entities -> flows). Repointing that fixture at a node type that no longer exists, or at postgres-query which has no entity config, would leave impactproof GREEN AND INERT. That disposition is decided by the sibling bead, NOT defaulted here.

## Guest rebuild

The engine ships inside flowrunner.wasm (components/Cargo.toml pulls crates/execution/standard-nodes in as wamn-nodes), so the guest must be rebuilt before any live gate or a stale wasm gives a false result.

The production name-keyed analyzer edge was already deleted in 90ae43c9, so no successor proof is filed. Preserve the independent registration-keyed impact path and catalog-derived generated-API resource reporting.

D24 remains shipped and re-anchors to H5-API-PUBLISH while impactproof source/module/CLI/Job/registry carrier retire atomically. Current implementation is intentionally held behind wamn-0h0g.15.24 because architecture/gate-registry.json and its conformance owner are dirty in that active consolidation. There is no honest landable partial fragment: deleting the node while impactproof survives recreates green-but-inert corpse coverage.
IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY CORRECTION 2026-08-21: add postgres to all three retirement proofs (dispatch, descriptor resolution, capability-row absence), not only the two lists named in the original text. Remove only the now-unused wamn-schema-model dependency; preserve PostgresQuery, pg_to_api/shape_rows, wamn-entity-access, wamn-pg-core, and standard-nodes-raw-sql. Impactproof source/module/CLI/Job/gate entry retires atomically; D24 stays shipped with primary recipe H5-API-PUBLISH. No protected-write regeneration and no archive/doc edit belong to this bead.

title: fix(exec): the trusted HTTP effect refuses in the default tier -- attempt_matches is a fifth class-gate site outside the four claim-path points
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.20.2 landed the durability class gate at FOUR claim-path enforcement points (queue/claim.rs:97 and :123, queue/sql.rs:69, park_sql at queue/sql.rs ~:318). Measured 2026-08-19 during the exe wave-4 phase-2 survey: THERE IS A FIFTH SITE, and it is not on the claim path at all, so the .20.2 sweep could not have found it.

crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/connection_http.rs:356-363 -- authorize_snapshot returns EffectError::InvalidContext whenever !snapshot.attempt_matches. That flag is computed at crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/claims.rs:262-271 as attempt.attempt_id IS NOT NULL off a LEFT JOIN effect_attempts on the full eight-tuple (run, root plan, current plan, frame, node, occurrence, source artifact, requirement).

So the trusted HTTP effect REFUSES UNLESS AN effect_attempts ROW ALREADY EXISTS.

## Why that is unsatisfiable today

deploy/sql/run-state.sql:617-618 grants INSERT on effect_attempts ONLY to wamn_effect_writer, the private writer role. And there is no production caller of that writer: crates/execution/run-state/src/effect_writer.rs:60-63 says so in its own module doc ('there is no caller today'), and crates/execution/host/src/effect_writer.rs:74-85 carries a LANDED GREEN GUARD, retained_private_client_has_no_effect_operation_caller, which asserts that .begin_attempt(, .acquire_dispatch( and .record_outcome( appear nowhere in the host. A caller sweep confirms those three appear only in tests/effect_writer_live.rs and production_claim_live.rs.

The effect ledger is being SHELVED behind the premium durable tier (wamn-0h0g.20.3, docs/exe-model.md:255-257), and DurabilityClass::default() is Standard. So on the default tier -- which is every run -- this precondition can never be met and the trusted HTTP effect is permanently dead.

## Consequence beyond the effect itself

This is what makes wamn-0h0g.11.3 (M0 check 3, HTTP connection confinement) GREEN-BUT-INERT rather than merely blocked. Every negative case in that proof -- undeclared requirement, foreign binding or generation, escaped base path, disallowed address -- refuses at attempt_matches long BEFORE reaching the surface actually under test. A mutant that deletes the base-path check, the address policy, or the declared-connection authority would still pass. A proof written against HEAD would assert nothing it claims to assert.

## Options, none taken -- this is an owner decision

(a) delete the attempt_matches conjunct outright;
(b) gate it on DurabilityClass::admits_effect_evidence(), matching the four landed sites and the one SQL spelling at durability.rs:85;
(c) keep it and declare the trusted HTTP effect premium-durable-tier-only, which makes .11.3 a durable-tier proof and shelves it alongside .11.4.

Each yields a materially different wamn-0h0g.11.3.

## Ownership note

The edit lands in connection_http.rs. That file is the effect-span lane's exclusive domain in the current wave, NOT the shelving lane's, so whoever takes this must coordinate with wamn-0h0g.24.3 rather than editing from a shelving worktree.
design: Keep trusted HTTP effects reachable on the default standard tier. Gate attempt_matches through the same DurabilityClass::admits_effect_evidence decision and single SQL spelling as every other premium crash-floor enforcement point. Standard bypasses effect-attempt evidence and must reach the actual connection-confinement checks; durable continues to require exact attempt evidence. The class read is the immutable runs.durability_class carrier from .20.1.
acceptance_criteria: Either the trusted HTTP effect is reachable on the default tier, or it is explicitly declared premium-durable-tier-only and wamn-0h0g.11.3 is re-scoped to match. In the first case the class gate reads through DurabilityClass::admits_effect_evidence() at this site as it does at the other four, using the single SQL spelling. In every case a negative-path proof of connection confinement must fail when the check it targets is mutated away -- no refusal may be reachable only via attempt_matches.

Mutants for unconditional evidence, unconditional bypass, and downstream declared-egress bypass each failed and were restored.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(registries): regenerate protected-writes.json against a converged database
description:
## Why

architecture/protected-writes.json is MACHINE-GENERATED, not hand-maintained: services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs installs the control and project databases into a disposable PostgreSQL, reads real ACLs, constraints, triggers and policies from pg_catalog, and writes the file when WAMN_UPDATE_PROTECTED_RELATIONS is set. Every banked delta for this file -- the nine catalog relations losing wamn_app, event_registrations keeping update(tenant_id), the wamn_run.runs release_version/manifest_digest/durability_class grants, all three runs_admission_pins_immutable trigger-column corrections, the wamn_control_author grants and restrictive policies -- is OUTPUT of that one command, not input to a hand edit.

wamn-0h0g.15.22 deliberately did NOT hand-apply them. Measured during that bead: the committed wamn_run.runs row records 73 operations while the SQL grants 37, so a hand patch that added the four banked operations would have ADDED two grants the database does not hold and LEFT 36 phantom grants on the most privileged relation in the run plane.

## State at hand-off

wamn-0h0g.15.22 landed the state-ownership half: architecture/state-owners.json now declares 86 objects + 3 families = 89, and services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs:201 already reads 89. The four rows whose declarations were deleted (wamn_run.flows, wamn_run.run_flow_resolutions, both wamn_run.authoring_test_sets legs) were removed from protected-writes.json, taking it 87 -> 83.

SIX ROWS ARE STILL MISSING and can only be produced by the generator: registry.retired_project_envs, wamn_authority.author_login_tenants, and the four catalog.wiring* relations. protected_relations.rs:322 asserts the row key set equals the state-owners key set EXACTLY, so protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership stays red until they exist.

## Procedure

  WAMN_UPDATE_PROTECTED_RELATIONS=1 WAMN_CTL_PG_URL=... cargo test --locked --offline -p wamn-ctl --features ops --test protected_relations_live -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
  then re-run WITHOUT the update variable to confirm it is stable
  then cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --test protected_relations --test state_ownership

Semantically diff the result against the banked expectations and treat anything beyond them as a red flag.

## Blocked by

wamn-0h0g.15.172 -- the control database cannot be installed at all today, so the generator panics before emitting a single row.

## Traps

PostgreSQL roles are CLUSTER-WIDE: use a FRESH container per gate family or expect false reds. Do not use the live kind cluster.
acceptance_criteria: After the enumerated decision-complete authority gate closes, architecture/protected-writes.json is regenerated from a fresh converged PostgreSQL database through the protected-relations generator, never hand-edited. The generated relation key set exactly equals the current state-owners key set; no fixed row-count literal substitutes for that equality. The expected semantic diff is reviewed against the named authority dispositions and source changes. A second run without the update variable is a no-op, and the protected-relations plus state-ownership conformance targets pass.
notes:
*** THE DEPENDENCY ON wamn-0h0g.11.28 WAS MEASURED AND REMOVED, 2026-08-19. THE EDGE WAS
SOFT. OWNER-AUTHORIZED EXIT: "edge soft -> re-record it with the finding cited, inversion
gone." ***

Measured by a strictly read-only wave-9 lane (zero writes, zero builds) at f27ad353.

=====================================================================
THE DISTINCTION THAT DECIDES IT -- KEEP THESE TWO APART
=====================================================================
THE BLOCKAGE IS REAL. This bead's Procedure, run verbatim today, PANICS. It does not
produce a wrong protected-writes.json; it produces NO file. Fail-closed.
THE EDGE IS SOFT. What blocks this bead is A SINGLE CALL-SITE SWAP INSIDE THIS BEAD'S OWN
GATE FILE, on a verb whose only caller in the entire repository is that gate. Nothing
wamn-0h0g.11.28 delivers AS A BEAD changes anything about the database, about convergence,
or about protected-writes.json.
*** THE EDGE ENCODED WHO OWNS THE EDIT, NOT WHAT MUST BE TRUE. ***

=====================================================================
WHERE THE EDGE CAME FROM -- it was not silent, and it was not original
=====================================================================
This bead was created 2026-08-19T03:36:58Z and its own "Blocked by" section named ONLY
wamn-0h0g.15.172. The .11.28 edge appeared LATER the same day, around 10:55Z, when clearing
.15.172 exposed the next refusal.
Its rationale is stated in the commit body of 12b8d2b0 -- which is itself a .15.173 commit
editing .15.173's own gate:
  "It still cannot reach the generator: install_project_database drives publish_catalog::run,
   which is CLOSED by ruling and refuses with control-definition-publish-requires-
   wamn-0h0g.15.14. That is a THIRD instance of wamn-0h0g.11.28's class -- recorded there and
   on this bead -- and RE-ANCHORING THE INSTALL ONTO THE LIVE CARRIER IS THAT BEAD'S SCOPE,
   NOT A FIXTURE REPAIR."
That final clause is the entire edge: a scope-hygiene judgement ("these fixture repairs are
mine, that call-site is yours") recorded as a blocking dependency.

=====================================================================
WHY IT IS SOFT, IN THE FORM THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE CARRIER ARGUMENT
=====================================================================
*** BOTH OF .11.28's NAMED VICTIMS WERE ALREADY REMEDIATED BY .11.28's OWN COMMIT a1ecc789. ***
ri_orch_live.rs was deleted outright; orphan_guard_live.rs had its publish half removed and
was re-anchored onto migrate_catalog::run. NEITHER NAMED GATE DRIVES THE CLOSED VERB AT HEAD.
What remains under .11.28 is loud-skip hardening. LOUD-SKIP HARDENING CANNOT BE A
PRECONDITION FOR REGENERATING protected-writes.json. The edge is therefore soft regardless of
how the carrier question below resolves.

=====================================================================

=====================================================================
install_project_database calls publish_catalog::run (protected_relations_live.rs:327), which
at publish_catalog.rs:107-112 validates the schema name then unconditionally bails with
CONTROL_DEFINITION_PUBLISH_REFUSAL before any I/O. The expect at :342 panics, BEFORE the

target and skip_reconcile_replica_identity: true at orphan_guard_live.rs:149-160, :305.

  CREATE TABLE wamn_catalog  -> DELIBERATELY GONE; its family declaration was deleted by

CLINCHER: repo-wide, publish_catalog::run has exactly ONE caller outside its own two unit
tests -- protected_relations_live.rs:327. It is no longer wired to the CLI. a1ecc789's body
says it was retained solely for "an unlisted live caller, services/ctl/tests/
protected_relations_live.rs". Swapping that one call site makes run and PublishCatalogArgs

*** RESIDUAL RISK, STATED HONESTLY AND NOT CLOSED. *** The lane was read-only and did NOT run
the gate against live PostgreSQL, so "migrate_catalog::run produces byte-identical rows to
the deleted publish path" is argued from source diff plus a sibling test that demonstrably

carry_forward_release / ensure_existing_release_manifest impose an extra precondition in this
fixture (orphan_guard_live.rs:305 runs a fresh v1 through the same path successfully, strong
but not identical evidence), and whether install_project_database's preamble, which drops
catalog and wamn_run at :299-303, leaves residue that changes the outcome.

=====================================================================

=====================================================================
"Converged" means: when generate_rows runs for each half, the disposable PostgreSQL
materializes EVERY declared (scope, relation) pair, enforced at

NONE of the three is a thing .11.28 causes to become true. .11.28 touches no SQL and no

=====================================================================
The description says "86 objects + 3 families = 89" and claims protected_relations_live.rs:201
already reads 89. AT HEAD IT IS 86 + 2 = 88 and :201 reads 88. The ACCEPTANCE CRITERION still
