description:
## Why

a1ecc789 (wamn-0h0g.11.28, delete the closed publish-catalog verb) removed the ONLY code that creates the per-tenant catalog snapshot table: the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wamn_catalog block with its ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and the wamn_catalog_tenant policy. Nothing in the tree creates or inserts into it any more -- verified by repo-wide grep for CREATE, INSERT and any schema-qualified reference.

THE CONSUMER SURVIVED. components/execution/flowrunner/src/lib.rs:207 implements the guest-facing catalog_json() capability as: SELECT document::text FROM wamn_catalog LIMIT 1. On any freshly provisioned project schema that query now raises 42P01 undefined_table, which the guest receives as a raw PgCapError::QueryError rather than the designed refusal message, no catalog snapshot published for this project.

## Evidence

architecture/state-owners.json declares the family app-schema-catalog-snapshot (pattern <app_schema>.wamn_catalog, migration owner ctl-publish, writers [ctl-publish], readers [flowrunner]) with schema_source services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs and marker CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wamn_catalog. The manifest is telling the truth; the tree is inconsistent with it.

## Why this blocks wamn-0h0g.15.22

validate_sources runs before validate_canonical_inventory, and it refuses to certify a canonical source that no longer contains the DDL it claims. That single refusal is the sole remaining cause of ELEVEN red guards in tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs. Proven during .15.22: with the state-ownership inventory reconciled, all 32 tests in that file pass under one temporary local change -- repointing this marker -- which was reverted, not committed. Writing a marker that points at absent DDL would green the guard and leave it inert.

## The decision, which is the owners

(a) Restore the installer. Additive and safe; note the publish verb that POPULATED the table is closed by ruling, so the table would be permanently empty and catalog_json() would return its designed refusal instead of a raw 42P01 -- strictly better behaviour than today, but a compatibility shim.
(b) Complete the deletion: remove catalog_json() from the guest and the family from architecture/state-owners.json. This is a WIT/SDK capability removal and needs the four state_ownership.rs references retargeted (the resolver special case at :1334, the positional families[0] probe at :1796 and its id assertion at :1811).

Do NOT resolve it by editing the marker.
acceptance_criteria: Either the installer exists and the marker resolves, or the capability and the family are both removed; repository_state_ownership_manifest_is_complete and the ten sibling guards are green for a true reason.
notes:
=====================================================================
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-19): COMPLETE THE DELETION. Option (b).
RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.
=====================================================================
The product question dissolves once the consumer's own fate is named. catalog_json()
lives in the FLOWRUNNER -- a component the plan of record retires -- and the snapshot it
reads served the OLD guest world: flow expressions introspecting catalog metadata.

Under rev 4 the question "does the platform still promise guests a catalog snapshot?"
has a PER-AUDIENCE answer, and every audience already has its ruled grammar:
  - developer components get the catalog through SQLX AT COMPILE TIME (the
    Developer-surface ruling -- runtime snapshot introspection is precisely what
    compile-checked queries replace);
  - wirers get it through the PALETTE;
  - external consumers through GENERATED ROUTES.
A guest-readable snapshot table is the FOURTH GRAMMAR NOBODY RULED FOR, fed by a verb
closed by ruling, read by a component on the deletion list.

*** Restoring the installer would be a shim (permanently-empty table) FEEDING A CORPSE
(doomed reader) -- two compatibility layers for zero live consumers. ***

THEREFORE: remove catalog_json() and its call sites; delete the wamn_catalog family from
architecture/state-owners.json; retarget the four references. The 42P01 hazard does not
get a nicer refusal -- it becomes UNREACHABLE, which is the only refusal better than a
designed one.

SCOPE NOTE (owner): this is a slice of the flow-layer deletion arriving early, which is
fine -- it is exactly the Tier-B "delete whole, no seams" shape, and it releases 11 reds.

DISCIPLINE NOTED FOR THE RECORD (owner): refusing to edit the marker to whatever text
happens to match is evidence-integrity done right -- a guard greened by redefinition is
worse than a red one.

=====================================================================
PREMISE CORRECTION FROM THE INTEGRATOR -- THE BLAST RADIUS IS WIDER THAN
"DELETE THE GUEST IMPL". Measured 2026-08-19, no code changed.
=====================================================================
catalog_json() is a RUST TRAIT METHOD, not a WIT export, so there is no generated-code
or WIT-world change -- but it is a REQUIRED trait method, so removal is ALL-OR-NOTHING
across every implementor. The surface:

  crates/execution/flow-model/src/node_contract.rs:307   the trait declaration
  crates/execution/standard-nodes/src/policy.rs:101,105  gating wrapper that delegates
    (+ its own tests at :142, :169, :190)
  crates/execution/standard-nodes/src/postgres.rs:155    *** A SECOND REAL CONSUMER ***
  components/execution/flowrunner/src/lib.rs:206         the guest impl doing the SQL read
  test doubles: crates/execution/flow-engine/tests/lifecycle_node_abi_prototype.rs:31,
    crates/execution/standard-nodes/tests/nodes.rs:47

THE SECOND CONSUMER IS THE STANDARD-NODES ENTITY NODE. postgres.rs:155 does
`let raw_catalog = ctx.catalog_json()...` then `Catalog::from_json(...)` to resolve
create/get/update/delete. Deleting catalog_json() therefore deletes that node's catalog
resolution, i.e. its run path -- a functional deletion, not a cleanup.

*** THIS DOES NOT CONTRADICT THE RULING -- IT CONFIRMS IT. *** That node's run() ships
INSIDE flowrunner.wasm: components/Cargo.toml:24 pulls crates/execution/standard-nodes in
as `wamn-nodes`. services/scenario-worker and services/ctl depend on the crate but touch
only describe_interface() (authoring metadata), never run(). So catalog_json()'s only
RUNTIME home is the retiring guest, exactly as the ruling says. The correction is about
SIZE, not direction: the deletion reaches the trait, the entity node's run path, and the
policy wrapper, not just the guest impl.

=====================================================================
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN -- NOT STARTED, AWAITING AN EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION
=====================================================================
A. MANIFEST HALF (this is what releases the 11 reds; it is self-contained)
   1. architecture/state-owners.json: delete the families[] element
      "app-schema-catalog-snapshot" (18 lines), AND delete the canonical_sources[]
      element for services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs (6 lines, the one carrying
      "marker": "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wamn_catalog").
      *** TRAP, HIT ONCE ALREADY: "services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs" appears TWICE in
      this file -- at the principals entry "ctl-publish" and at the canonical source.
      Target the canonical source only. Verify the anchor before deleting. The file mixes
      compact and expanded array styles and does NOT round-trip through a pretty-printer,
      so edit by line and validate by parsing. ***
   2. architecture/protected-writes.json: delete the row
      ("production-project-database", "<app_schema>.wamn_catalog"). This file DOES
      round-trip byte-identically at indent=2.
   3. tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs: delete the resolver special case
      (~:1334) `if basename == "wamn_catalog" { return family(manifest, "app-schema-catalog-snapshot"); }`
      and retarget the positional families[0] probe (~:1796, :1802) and its id assertion
      (~:1811, currently expects "app-schema-catalog-snapshot"), which after the deletion
      resolves to "app-schema-entity-map".
   4. services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs:201: 89 -> 88 (86 objects + 2 families).
   VERIFIED ARITHMETIC: after A the declared total is 88 and protected-writes holds 82 rows.

B. CODE HALF (the flow-layer slice; larger, and it deletes a node's run path)
   Remove the trait method, the policy wrapper and its three tests, the guest impl, the
   entity node's catalog resolution, and the two test doubles. Then decide what
   PostgresNode::run does without a catalog -- most likely the node goes with it.
   Guest rebuild required before any live gate: the engine ships inside flowrunner.wasm.

C. ORDER. A alone greens the eleven and is safe on its own: the manifest describes
   RELATIONS, and the relation genuinely has no installer, so removing it is true
   independently of whether dead code still tries to read it. B should follow so the
   hazard becomes unreachable as the ruling directs; leaving B undone leaves a live
   42P01 path.

INTEGRATOR MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-19 (read-only, before implementing; owner authorised implementation of this bead this session).

PART A IS VERIFIED SAFE AND SELF-CONTAINED. Every banked anchor still lands exactly where the plan said -- state_ownership.rs :1334/:1796/:1802/:1811, protected_relations_live.rs :201, state-owners.json :173/:176 and :1760. No drift this time. Specifics now pinned: the canonical_sources element is lines 172-177 (6 lines, trailing comma included) and the families element is 1759-1776 (18 lines); after deletion families[0] does resolve to app-schema-entity-map exactly as predicted. Arithmetic confirmed by parsing: state-owners currently holds 86 objects + 3 families = 89, matching the :201 assertion, so :201 becomes 88.

TWO NEW SAFETY FACTS, both measured: (1) THE ONLY schema_source ANYWHERE IN state-owners.json NAMING publish_catalog.rs IS families[0] ITSELF, so deleting the family and its canonical source together orphans nothing. Lines 99 (the ctl-publish principal) and 256 (its wamn_run default-schema mapping) are unrelated and MUST STAY -- ctl-publish is still a writer on app-schema-entity-map, and publish_catalog.rs is still live code. (2) *** PART A CANNOT ORPHAN THE FLOWRUNNER READ, because discover_writes (state_ownership.rs:1044) only matches WRITES -- INSERT INTO, UPDATE with SET, DELETE FROM, MERGE, TRUNCATE and DDL. The surviving SELECT document::text FROM wamn_catalog is a READ and is never discovered. The resolver special case at :1334 is therefore ALREADY DEAD CODE: the CREATE TABLE that was its only discovery site went with a1ecc789. *** This is what makes part A safe to land before part B.

CORRECTION TO STEP 2 OF THE RECORDED PLAN -- DO NOT HAND-EDIT protected-writes.json IN PART A. The plan said to delete the row (production-project-database, <app_schema>.wamn_catalog). Measured: protected-writes.json holds 83 rows, the wamn_catalog row is index 33, and declared is 89, so the current 6-row delta IS exactly wamn-0h0g.15.173's known red. That file is MACHINE-GENERATED via WAMN_UPDATE_PROTECTED_RELATIONS and hand-editing it is forbidden here; wamn-0h0g.15.173 owns regenerating it and the generator will drop that row on its own, because a relation with no installer and no declaration cannot exist in a converged database. The cost of deferring is cosmetic only: tests/conformance/tests/protected_relations.rs:143 panics at :200-204 with 'undeclared protected relation' instead of failing the set-equality assert at :321. IT IS RED EITHER WAY AND IS ALREADY ONE OF THE 14. Recommend part A leaves protected-writes.json alone and .15.173 absorbs the row. NOTE FOR .15.173: after part A its delta becomes 88 declared vs 83 actual with one actual-but-undeclared row, so it must handle the removal as well as the six additions.

PART B IS SMALLER THAN THE PLAN FEARED -- ONE STRUCT, NOT THE FILE. crates/execution/standard-nodes/src/postgres.rs is 571 lines and carries TWO nodes: PostgresEntity (impl Node at :140), whose run() calls ctx.catalog_json() at :154 -- the banked :155 is one off, that line is the following Catalog::from_json -- and PostgresQuery (impl Node at :386), which calls ctx.pg_execute(sql, ...) at :425 and ctx.pg_query at :429. *** THAT SECOND NODE IS THE DECLARED DYNAMIC WRITER: state-owners.json scan_policy.dynamic_writers carries { path: crates/execution/standard-nodes/src/postgres.rs, principal: standard-nodes-raw-sql, family: generated-tenant-entities, marker: ctx.pg_execute(sql }. So part B deletes PostgresEntity ONLY; the file survives, PostgresQuery survives, and that manifest entry stays valid and must NOT be touched. *** I had flagged a risk that deleting the file would orphan the dynamic-writer declaration; measured, that risk does not materialise.

WHAT PART B DOES COST, STATED PLAINLY: PostgresEntity::run resolves create/get/update/delete/list against the catalog snapshot, so removing catalog_json() removes that node's entity resolution entirely -- a functional deletion of the standard entity node, not a cleanup. This is consistent with the ruling (its runtime home is flowrunner.wasm, which retires) and the owner was told this before authorising implementation.

CROSS-LANE CLEARANCE, from two independent measurement lanes: crates/execution/router does NOT depend on crates/execution/flow-model (its only deps are serde_json and opentelemetry; the manifest says 'Deliberately NO wamn-flow'), and nothing in the router references catalog_json, node_contract or standard-nodes -- so deleting catalog_json() CANNOT break the router build. The ingress/executor surface touches none of part B's files either. One addition to the surface list, already in the bead: crates/execution/flow-engine/tests/lifecycle_node_abi_prototype.rs:31 is one of the two test doubles that implements catalog_json and must go with it.
PART A LANDED at f09e2550, pushed. state_ownership.rs is 32 passed / 0 failed -- all eleven green for a true reason. The full wamn-proof-conformance package is green except protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership, which was ALREADY one of the 14 and is owned by wamn-0h0g.15.173; it changes failure mode as predicted, from six missing rows to panicking at protected_relations.rs:203 with 'undeclared protected relation <app_schema>.wamn_catalog'. protected-writes.json was deliberately NOT hand-edited -- reasoning in the previous note and in the commit body.

*** PART B IS BLOCKED ON A CONSEQUENCE THE RULING DID NOT PRICE. NOT STARTED. ***

Part B cannot be split: PostgresEntity::run calls ctx.catalog_json() at postgres.rs:154, so removing the trait method REQUIRES resolving the node, and resolving the node is where a product decision lives.

MEASURED SURFACE OF PART B: the trait decl at flow-model/src/node_contract.rs:307; the policy wrapper at standard-nodes/src/policy.rs:101-106 plus its test double :142 and assertions :169 and :190; the guest impl at components/execution/flowrunner/src/lib.rs:206; two test doubles at flow-engine/tests/lifecycle_node_abi_prototype.rs:31 and standard-nodes/tests/nodes.rs:47. THEN the node itself: PostgresEntity is a REGISTERED SHIPPED NODE TYPE -- struct at postgres.rs:138, impl at :140, static POSTGRES at standard-nodes/src/lib.rs:75, a match arm in node(), and an entry in pub const NODE_TYPES: [&str; 9] at lib.rs:57. Deleting it takes NODE_TYPES to 8 and INTERFACES: LazyLock<[NodeInterface; 9]> to 8, and rewrites the positional pure_interface(NODE_TYPES[n]) indices. Roughly nine tests in standard-nodes/tests/nodes.rs (the 'postgres (catalog-derived entity ops)' section from ~:631 to ~:800) go with it, along with the test-double catalog field at :30 and the catalog_json() fixture at :131.

GOOD NEWS -- THE REPO HAS AN ESTABLISHED IDIOM FOR RETIRING A NODE TYPE, so this is not novel: removed types go into two lists currently reading ['cron', 'time-shift'] -- removed_node_types_are_unknown_to_dispatch at nodes.rs:899 and the retained-surface guard at :963-970 -- and the NODE_TYPES pin at :939 is updated. Following it exactly is the low-risk path.

*** THE CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS STOPS FOR A RULING: PostgresEntity IS THE ONLY SHIPPED NODE TYPE WHOSE CONFIG NAMES AN ENTITY BY NAME. *** Verified: PostgresQuery, the other node in the same file (impl at :386), takes sql and params and never entity. And tests/integration/src/impactproof.rs:83 seeds exactly such a flow -- its own comment reads 'one active postgres node reading entity orders BY NAME' -- to prove the NAME-KEYED edge of impact analysis (plan ops -> entities -> flows). Deleting PostgresEntity therefore removes the sole production producer of the name-keyed entity reference that impact analysis exists to trace, and breaks that in-cluster proof's fixture. Repointing the fixture at a node type that no longer exists, or at postgres-query which has no entity config, would leave impactproof GREEN AND INERT -- the exact failure mode this bead's own ruling praised the refusal to commit.

THE OWNER'S OPTIONS, none taken: (a) delete PostgresEntity now and accept that the name-keyed impact edge loses its only producer until the rest of the flow layer goes, retiring or re-scoping impactproof in the same commit; (b) keep PostgresEntity and re-source its catalog from somewhere that is not a guest-readable snapshot, which contradicts the per-audience grammar the ruling rests on; (c) SPLIT part B into its own bead and sequence it with the flow-layer deletion, so the entity node, impactproof and the name-keyed edge retire together rather than one at a time. Recommendation is (c) or (a); the choice is the owner's because it decides what ships and what an in-cluster gate proves.
close_reason: Closed on part A plus the refusal arm, per the owner's ruling of 2026-08-19 (option 1 with the hardening rider). Part A at f09e2550 deleted the app-schema-catalog-snapshot family and its stale publish_catalog.rs canonical source from architecture/state-owners.json, dropped the already-dead resolver special case, retargeted the positional families[0] assertion to app-schema-entity-map, and moved the declared-relation count to 88. state_ownership.rs went 32 passed / 0 failed -- all ELEVEN reds green for a true reason, not by repointing a marker at absent DDL. The refusal arm at f411f272 then made the interim state fail-closed and marked rather than dead-ish: 42P01 undefined_table now answers with the designed 'no catalog snapshot published for this project' refusal, proven non-vacuous by a mutant that fails exactly one of the four new cases, with 42501 pinned as NOT absorbed. flowrunner 30 passed and still checks clean for wasm32-wasip2. Both tombstones name their successor. THE CODE DELETION IS wamn-0h0g.26.8, split out because it is a CLUSTER, not a capability removal: PostgresEntity is the only shipped node type whose config names an entity BY NAME -- postgres-query takes sql and params -- so it is the sole producer of the name-keyed impact edge that impactproof proves, and deleting it piecemeal would leave that gate green while asserting over a node type the tree no longer ships. impactproof's disposition is wamn-0h0g.26.9, decided there and not defaulted. architecture/protected-writes.json deliberately NOT hand-edited: it is machine-generated, the generator drops the wamn_catalog row on its own, and wamn-0h0g.15.173 owns that regeneration -- which now inherits an actual-but-undeclared row alongside its six missing ones.

title: feat(run-plane): the legacy execution-pin cutover needs its own additive durability_class migration
description: Carve-out reported by the EXE wave-3 lane 4 and DELIBERATELY not taken there. wamn-0h0g.20.2 added wamn_run.runs.durability_class to deploy/sql/run-state.sql, which is the FRESH-INSTALL path. The execution-pin cutover migration in crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs (~:3145-3190) is a named one-shot whose preflight demands an empty runs table and which adds only its OWN columns — capture_mode is absent from it too, so this is a pre-existing pattern, not a new gap. Teaching its CREATE OR REPLACE guard to reference a column it does not add would BREAK it. A legacy plane therefore needs a separate additive durability_class migration plus a guard refresh. Same class as the wave-2 lesson: a relation is not landed when the DDL file declares it — the converge path is a separate encoding.
acceptance_criteria: A database provisioned before wamn-0h0g.20.2 gains runs.durability_class and the refreshed admission guard through a named migration, proven against a throwaway PostgreSQL that starts at the legacy shape.
notes:
MEASUREMENT VERDICT (wave-5 read-only pass, 2026-08-19): *** THE HEADLINE PREMISE IS REFUTED. DO NOT IMPLEMENT AS WRITTEN. THE BEAD TYPE IS ALSO WRONG. ***

REFUTED, INTEGRATOR-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: execution_pin_cutover_sql (crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs:3085) NEVER NAMES durability_class ANYWHERE in its body. I grepped the whole function range and confirmed zero occurrences. The generic AddColumn planner already adds the column, so bolting an ADD COLUMN for durability_class onto the cutover -- which is what this bead literally asks for -- would produce a DUPLICATE ADD in the same turn.

THE REAL DEFECT IS DIFFERENT AND LARGER: the cutover CREATE-OR-REPLACEs the guard and recreates the trigger WITHOUT the durability_class arms. RepairHelperFunction is emitted at :3805, BEFORE the cutover at :4318, so the plan repairs the guard to canonical and the cutover immediately clobbers it -- a non-convergent, enforcement-DROPPING cutover. That is a BUG, not the feature this bead is typed as.

*** capture_mode IS STRICTLY WORSE AND IS A HARD MIGRATION ABORT, VERIFIED. *** The cutover's trigger is created BEFORE UPDATE OF catalog_id, catalog_version, environment, execution_bundle_hash, capture_mode, ... (run_plane.rs ~:3189) and the guard body tests NEW.capture_mode IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.capture_mode (~:3162) -- while the cutover never ADDs capture_mode either. PostgreSQL validates the UPDATE OF column list at CREATE TRIGGER time, so a legacy runs table that lacks capture_mode and needs the pin cutover ABORTS THE WHOLE CUTOVER with: column capture_mode of relation runs does not exist. Fixing only durability_class leaves that live abort standing.

FALSIFIABLE CHECK THE OWNER SHOULD ORDER BEFORE ANY EDIT: services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs:786 asserts again.is_noop(). If the analysis is right that assert is RED TODAY. One docker run of execution_pin_cutover_live settles it and decides whether any new live test is needed at all. A lane cannot run it; the integrator can.

RULINGS REQUIRED: (1) re-type P1 feature to P1 bug; (2) does capture_mode ride along in the same fix (same 5-line ADD COLUMN block, same skip set) or split per R12 -- noting that splitting leaves a live abort until the sibling lands; (3) does the cutover add durability_class BARE or WITH its inline CHECK -- bare re-creates the non-convergence.

DROPPED FROM WAVE 5 on this evidence. Do not let one worktree carry this and wamn-0h0g.20.6 together.
*** PROBE RUN AND PREDICTION CONFIRMED (integrator, 2026-08-19, owner-ordered before any re-type). Fresh throwaway postgres:18 (PostgreSQL 18.6), removed after. NOT the live cluster. ***

COMMAND: WAMN_CTL_PG_URL=<throwaway> cargo test --locked -p wamn-ctl --test run_plane_live execution_pin_cutover_live -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
RESULT: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed. The predicted assertion is RED TODAY, exactly as forecast.

FAILING ASSERTION, VERBATIM:
  thread 'execution_pin_cutover_live' panicked at services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs:786:5:
  cutover converged: [ ... ]

AND THE PLAN IT PRINTED IS THE SPEC OF THE DEFECT -- after the cutover has run, the reconciler STILL wants to emit TWO actions, so it never reaches a no-op:
  1. RunPlaneAction { kind: RepairHelperFunction, target: guard_run_admission_pins_immutable }
     whose canonical body DOES test both arms:
        OR NEW.capture_mode IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.capture_mode
        OR NEW.durability_class IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.durability_class
  2. RunPlaneAction { kind: RepairTrigger, target: runs.runs_admission_pins_immutable }
     DROP TRIGGER runs_admission_pins_immutable ON rp_live.runs; CREATE TRIGGER
     runs_admission_pins_immutable BEFORE UPDATE OF catalog_id, catalog_version, environment,
     execution_bundle_hash, capture_mode, durability_class, release_version, manifest_digest
     ON rp_live.runs FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION rp_live.guard_run_admission_pins_immutable();
So the plan repairs the guard to canonical and the cutover clobbers it back, forever. NON-CONVERGENT AND ENFORCEMENT-DROPPING, exactly as the measurement lane reasoned. THIS IS A BUG.

*** SECOND PREDICTION ALSO REPRODUCED, BY DIRECT SQL, WHICH IS WHAT JUSTIFIES BUNDLING THE TWO COLUMNS. *** On a LEGACY runs table lacking BOTH columns, issuing the exact CREATE TRIGGER the cutover emits gives, verbatim:
  ERROR:  column "capture_mode" of relation "runs" does not exist
PostgreSQL validates the BEFORE UPDATE OF column list at CREATE TRIGGER time. It aborts on capture_mode FIRST because that is the earlier missing column in the list -- so FIXING ONLY durability_class LEAVES THE ABORT STANDING AND CHANGES NOTHING FOR A LEGACY DATABASE. The two columns are two instances of ONE defect in ONE code path, which is why R12's granularity rule is satisfied by a single bead rather than bent by it: they have no independent green state.

MEASUREMENT NUANCE WORTH KEEPING: this red does NOT appear in the sweep of record. execution_pin_cutover_live is env-var gated on WAMN_CTL_PG_URL and self-skips when unset, so the 159-target / 3-red baseline never sees it. A green sweep is not a green tree -- the same lesson the clippy base red taught this session.

RE-TYPED feature -> bug on this evidence. The originally filed premise (that the cutover needs its own additive durability_class migration) was REFUTED: execution_pin_cutover_sql never names durability_class at all, and the generic AddColumn planner already adds it. Recorded so the tracker shows why a feature became a bug.

STANDING PLAN, per the owner ruling, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: fix both columns in the same ADD COLUMN block with the same skip set. Closing proof is the SAME predicate that opened it -- again.is_noop() on a re-run against BOTH populations: fresh, and legacy-missing-both-columns. Re-verify the immutability-trigger column list for BOTH columns in the same commit (the .20.1 unnamed-column-arm-never-fires class, now with a second column that could be missed the same way).
LEDGER ROW FILED, 2026-08-19 -- the OPEN FOR THE OWNER question in the close reason above is now ANSWERED.

RULED: option 3, a GENERALIZED row, not an instance-shaped one. It is *** R55 *** in docs/archive/findings.md -- title: a converge path reports success before its enforcement object exists. Board row plus a narrative subsection at the end of section 2.

WHY GENERALIZED. The owner's reasoning, recorded because it settles how this ledger is used: the ledger is NOT an open-risk queue, it is the findings RECORD, and its rows exist to be CITABLE -- R28's clause archaeology and the coverage-claim sweep both worked because closed findings stayed addressable. An instance-shaped row would merely mirror this close reason and would be history-inflation; the marginal value is entirely in the CLASS.

R55 carries: the class in one sentence, the detection signature (apply succeeds AND enforcement absent AND a re-run still emits actions), the proof obligation generalized from this bead's own closing predicate (convergence is witnessed by a re-run producing NO ACTIONS, never by the apply's exit code), and the mechanical question a future review can apply -- does this apply path assert that a second run is a no-op, or does it assert its own exit status.

R55 cites a00c5d1a as first instance and THIS BEAD as the instance record. This note is the other half of that bidirectional cite, per the R28 transfer pattern, so neither record dead-ends.

R55 opens and closes in one act: status closed, class live for citation.
close_reason:
Landed a00c5d1a on deploy-simplification. Both pin carriers now ride one ADD COLUMN block with the same skip set, each WITH its inline named CHECK.

OWNER RULING IMPLEMENTED AS RULED: inline CHECK, not bare -- a bare carrier is non-canonical, so the reconciler sees drift and keeps repairing it, re-creating the very non-convergence this bead exists to fix. The definition is pulled VERBATIM from the schema of record by a new runs_record_column_def(), so the fix creates no second encoding of the column shape. The lane's canonical-shape read supplied what to paste; the ruling supplied that bare loses.

TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS FROM THE LANE, both against MY banked evidence:
 (a) *** RE-EMITTED FOREVER IS WRONG. *** It converges on a third apply: run_execution_pin_contract_complete inspects only columns, types, nullability, FKs and indexes -- never the guard or the trigger -- so the cutover stops re-firing after one run. THE REAL DEFECT IS WORSE IN A DIFFERENT WAY: a single-shot reconcile --apply leaves the pin UNGUARDED AND REPORTS SUCCESS.
 (b) The guard divergence was THREE arms, not one. The cutover's private copy also dropped AND OLD.durability_class = 'durable' from the release-record arm, reverting it to pre-.20.1 semantics in which ANY effect attempt blocks on EVERY class. Fixed by construction: the duplicated guard and trigger copies are collapsed to one shared const each.

title: feat(admission): the durable tier has no writer — .20.1's policy SOURCE is in a different database
description: Found by the EXE wave-3 lane 4 while landing wamn-0h0g.20.2, and it is a hole in the wamn-0h0g.20.1 RULING itself, not in the implementation. .20.1 says the durability class is 'derived from registry.env_policies at admission'. THAT IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN: registry.env_policies lives in deploy/sql/system-schema.sql, whose own header calls it 'a different plane entirely' — the wamn_system database. No run-plane statement can join it; only system-schema.sql and ops-schema.sql reference registry.* at all. So the derivation needs either a control-plane push of the policy into the tenant database or a host-injected claim on the admission path. CONSEQUENCE TODAY: .20.2 landed the carrier with runs.durability_class WITHHELD from wamn_app in both the INSERT and UPDATE sets, so nothing can write 'durable' and every production run takes the fail-open 'standard' default. That is exactly R2's default and is correct for .20.2, but it means THE PREMIUM TIER IS UNREACHABLE IN PRODUCTION and the machinery behind it is unexercised outside gates.
design: Add an explicit durability_class field to the org-scoped registry environment policy with frozen standard/durable literals and standard as the absent-policy default. Provision/reconcile projects that value into one platform-owned project-local admission-policy row keyed by tenant and environment. Admission reads that row inside the same project-database transaction and writes the resolved class into runs.durability_class; callers never supply it. Policy changes converge the projection for future admissions, while existing runs retain the immutable class they admitted under. The claim path reads only the .20.1 carrier column.
acceptance_criteria: An admitted run's durability_class is derived from the env/org policy by a named, tested path, and a run can actually be admitted as 'durable' in production.
notes:
OWNER RULING CONFIRMED 2026-08-21: this is the .20.1 source/carrier composition made executable without a cross-database lookup or forgeable host claim. Projection is converged on policy change; runs freeze their admission-time class.
OWNER TRANSPORT RULING 2026-08-21: reconcile-run-plane is the cross-plane convergence actor and reads registry.env_policies directly; admission never reads the system registry. It projects a platform-owned wamn_run policy row keyed by environment. The reconciler authority writes; wamn_app is SELECT-only. The relation joins declared protected-write ownership and the generated artifact updates once at wave end. Admission reads the local row and freezes runs.durability_class; claims remain lookup-free.
IMPLEMENTATION PREMISE CORRECTION 2026-08-21: the project database may serve multiple tenants; environment-only storage would bleed policy across tenants. The projected relation and trigger lookup remain keyed by (tenant_id, environment), exactly as the design field requires.
FOLLOW-UP FILED 2026-08-21: wamn-0h0g.20.19 owns exact project-env database binding/current_database refusal for the privileged reconciler. This issue keeps the already-ruled policy projection and does not expand into wrong-target operator hardening.
LANDED 2026-08-21 in 1afa593a. Final shape: registry durability carrier converges additively for all three consumers; reconcile-run-plane resolves system policy and projects tenant -> expected_environment + durability_class into the project database; a fail-closed insert trigger refuses missing/mismatched projection and pins the run; exact ENABLE/FORCE/full-policy RLS plus SELECT-only ACL are observed and repaired; claim/admission paths never read the system registry; dry-run is byte-read-only even on a pre-carrier registry. Validation: schema-control 124, ctl lib 51, run-state lib 70, store 9, control-storage live 11, focused PG18 migration/RLS/admission/confinement/run-state gates, strict Clippy/rustfmt/YAML/diff checks. Named mutants killed missing/unforced/widened RLS, missing system column, missing/mismatched local projection, wrong policy source, added writer grant, existing-run rewrite, and dry-run mutation.
OWNER CORRECTION 2026-08-21, authoritative over the earlier preliminary composite-key note: retain the landed one-row-per-tenant PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id). expected_environment is a verified constant of the per-(org, project, env) database, not a selector; absent projection and environment mismatch refuse with typed SQLSTATE 55000 literals. The exact mismatch arm is live-probed in admission_live. A composite key would permit a second foreign-environment row for the same tenant and is rejected.
FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-21: wamn-0h0g.20.21 owns the one stale terminalize-effect-uncertain live fixture that did not seed the required project-local environment policy after 1afa593a. Production carrier semantics remain owned and closed here.

title: feat(host): no production process constructs a WiringCache or starts the wiring doorbell listener
description: Found by the EXE wave-3 lane 3 (wamn-0h0g.16.15). title: fix(router): WiringCache::insert re-installs a pointer read before the flip, defeating invalidation
description: Found by the EXE wave-3 lane 3 (wamn-0h0g.16.15) and deliberately NOT fixed there, because the remedy is an API change outside that bead's scope. WiringCache::insert writes state.active.insert(pointer, version) UNCONDITIONALLY (crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs). The interleaving: thread T misses and reads the store at t0 (sees v1); the activation flip commits at t1; the doorbell calls invalidate at t2; T calls insert(env, wiring, v1) at t3 > t2 and RE-INSTALLS the pointer it read before the flip. The cache then serves the superseded version indefinitely, until the next flip. This predates wamn-0h0g.16.5's landing, applies equally to invalidate and invalidate_all, and defeats the reconnect whole-drop the same way — so wamn-0h0g.16.15's correctness is real but not complete while this stands.
acceptance_criteria: A resolution in flight across an invalidation cannot install its stale pointer, proven by a named test that interleaves a store read with a doorbell invalidation. Likely shape: a generation counter — a get-miss hands out a token and insert refuses a token older than the last invalidation.
notes:
Lane 3 verified the unconditional write by reading resolution.rs; it is not inferred from the doc comment.
MEASUREMENT VERDICT (integrator lane, 2026-08-19, read-only, no code changed): *** IMPLEMENTABLE NOW. THE BUG IS CONFIRMED IN SOURCE. ***

CONFIRMED: crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs:160 writes state.active.insert(pointer, version) unconditionally, inside pub fn insert (:144-181), as the FIRST statement after the lock -- before the residency check (:161) and before eviction (:165-176). Nothing between the get-miss and the insert correlates the two.

THE STATE STRUCTURE, measured: WiringCache (:81-85) holds max_entries, state: Mutex<CacheState> -- a std::sync::Mutex (import :34), NOT an RwLock and NOT tokio::sync -- and lookups: Counter<u64>. CacheState (:57-64) holds active: HashMap<Pointer, u32> (:60), entries: HashMap<EntryKey, Arc<Wiring>> (:62), least_to_most_recent: VecDeque<EntryKey> (:63). EXISTING VERSIONING IS ONLY EntryKey { pointer, version: u32 } (:51-55), which is the WIRING's version keyed to catalog.wirings.version. There is NO cache generation counter, epoch or sequence number of any kind, so the proposed token is genuinely new state.

*** THE API CHANGE IS CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS: THERE ARE ZERO PRODUCTION CALLERS OF get OR insert. *** Exhaustive caller list: production code calls only invalidate_all/invalidate, at crates/platform/runtime/src/wiring_doorbell.rs:103, :125 and :139. Every get/insert call site is a test -- wiring_doorbell.rs's own cfg(test) module (insert at :388,389,416,420,426,438,462,480,510,511,531,605,606,607; get at :398,403,421,450,470,494,519,520,621,625), crates/platform/runtime/tests/wiring_doorbell_live.rs (insert :176,194,213,232; get :186,207,224,235), and crates/execution/router/tests/resolution.rs (18 insert + 14 get sites). The whole resolve-on-miss path is unbuilt, so the token change costs test churn only.

EDIT SET: crates/execution/router/src/resolution.rs (the fix + its module and method doc comments, which state the current contract and would go stale); crates/execution/router/src/lib.rs:57 (pub use resolution::{ActiveWiring, WiringCache} must export the token type -- get and insert are pub and every caller is out-of-crate); crates/execution/router/tests/resolution.rs (the named acceptance test + 18 insert sites); crates/platform/runtime/src/wiring_doorbell.rs (cfg(test) module only, 14 sites); crates/platform/runtime/tests/wiring_doorbell_live.rs (4 sites).

*** HIDDEN CONSTRAINT -- A SOURCE-TEXT PIN. crates/execution/router/tests/resolution.rs:228 does include_str!(../src/resolution.rs) and asserts the file LITERALLY contains the substrings u64_counter("wamn.run.wiring.cache.lookups"), KeyValue::new(, "hit" and "miss". Any restructuring of get must preserve those exact substrings or that test fails for an unrelated reason. ***

*** SEQUENCING COLLISION WITH wamn-0h0g.19.1 -- SEMANTIC, NOT MERELY TEXTUAL. .19.1 (hot HTTP routes inline on the router, no Postgres in path) is PRECISELY the miss-resolve-insert path that today has no production caller. It will write the first production cache.get/cache.insert, most likely in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/flow_http_routing.rs, against the OLD signature, while .16.16 changes that signature. Two parallel worktrees would then produce code that MERGES CLEANLY AND DOES NOT COMPILE. Remedy: land .16.16 first, or hand .19.1 the token-shaped signature up front. ***

SEPARABILITY FROM .16.7: they share no file except crates/execution/router/src/lib.rs, where .16.16 touches :57 and .16.7 would touch :59 -- adjacent lines in one hunk, so git would conflict unless sequenced.

ONE CHEAP OWNER RULING, NOT TAKEN: is the token PER-POINTER (a flip of wiring A does not defeat an in-flight resolution of wiring B) or GLOBAL (any invalidation, including the reconnect invalidate_all, defeats every in-flight resolution)? Global is simpler and strictly safe; per-pointer avoids spurious re-reads in a busy multi-wiring environment. invalidate_all must invalidate every outstanding token either way, which pushes toward global.
close_reason: Landed at c9dbbc10. CacheState gains one generation: u64. WiringCache::get now returns a Lookup -- Hit, or Miss carrying a ResolutionToken stamped with the generation read UNDER THE SAME LOCK HOLD that decided it was a miss, so nothing can slip between deciding to read the store and the generation that read is attributed to. insert takes the token and refuses any generation an invalidation has overtaken, BEFORE the pointer write; on refusal nothing is installed, neither pointer nor graph. invalidate and invalidate_all bump the generation UNCONDITIONALLY including when they drop nothing -- load-bearing, because an in-flight read is exactly the case with no resident pointer to drop. GLOBAL counter per the ruling, not per-pointer: invalidate_all must overtake every outstanding token anyway, and the cost is a re-read, not a wrong answer. *** MUTANT RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE INTEGRATOR: removing only the generation check reproduces the original unconditional write and fails EXACTLY THREE TESTS ACROSS TWO CRATES AND ONLY THOSE THREE -- the invalidation and reconnect cases at tests/resolution.rs:165 and :212, and the doorbell case at wiring_doorbell.rs:486. The 11 pre-existing router tests and 10 pre-existing doorbell tests stay green, so the new cases are the only things that catch it. *** THE LIVE GATE WAS RUN RATHER THAN INSPECTED: wiring_doorbell_live passes against a throwaway postgres:18.6. The lane could not run it and correctly declined to claim it, having edited its four insert and six get sites by inspection only -- that was the single largest gap in its verification and it is now closed. Also green: wamn-router 58 passed across 6 targets, wamn-runtime lib 159 passed, run-state shelving_contract 4 passed (it include_str!s all seven router sources and would red on a new module or a new router dep -- this change adds neither), clippy clean on wamn-router, all five files rustfmt-clean. TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS FROM THE LANE: wiring_doorbell_live has SIX get call sites, not the four briefed -- two are multi-line chains at :197 and :215; and wiring_doorbell.rs's own cfg(test) module carries a SECOND source-text pin, include_str! of itself asserting the LISTEN is established before the pointers are dropped, which any lane touching that file's production half must know. The API change stayed cheap because there is still NO production caller of get/insert -- production calls only invalidate/invalidate_all. This is a contract fix landing AHEAD of its caller: the eventual resolver must take the token BEFORE its store read and treat None from insert as 'resolve again', not 'serve what I read'. Deliberate non-goal, flagged as a cheap follow-up if re-read cost ever shows: a refused insert also declines to cache the immutable graph entry, losing the rollback-is-a-hit property across a refusal.

title: fix(host): revoke_identity is not exact — WamnLogging and RunnerEgressPolicy have no clear
description: Carve-out reported by the wamn-0h0g.17.7 lane and deliberately left, because both surfaces are outside that lanes file domain. ExecutionHost::revoke_identity clears the wamn:postgres claims exactly, but WamnLogging has no clear_claim and RunnerEgressPolicy has no clear_declared, so those two are left OVERWRITTEN-ON-NEXT-BIND rather than REMOVED. This is bounded by live instance count rather than by acquisition count — because the claim scope is per-instance, not per-acquisition — so it is NOT a growth leak, but it is not exact revocation either: an idle pooled instance still carries a resolvable logging claim and egress declaration for the tenant it last served. Should be closed before the router consumes the checkout seam.
acceptance_criteria: revoke_identity removes the logging claim and the egress declaration as well as the postgres claims, proven by a named test asserting an idle instance resolves none of the three.
close_reason: Integrated 2a13a2bc + 6cd04dc9. revoke_identity now clears all three registries: new WamnLogging::clear_claim (wamn_logging.rs) and RunnerEgressPolicy::clear_declared (runner_egress.rs) join the existing wamn:postgres clear. Removal, NOT an empty write — Some(empty) is a stored deny-all narrowing, absent is the never-supplied state, pinned by clearing_a_declaration_removes_it_rather_than_storing_an_empty_one. ExecutionHost gained an egress: Arc<RunnerEgressPolicy> field, cloned off ExecutionCapabilities before the Production arm moves its own handle into RunnerEgress. Proved on BOTH checkout exits (drop-the-lease and finish()) by ending_a_checkout_revokes_every_registry_the_instance_resolved_under and a_finished_lease_revokes_every_registry_too, each reproduced failing at base first. PREMISE REFINEMENT: the bead framed this as a bind/revoke asymmetry; it is broader. The egress registry is not written by bind_identity at all — the guest's trusted wamn:runner/egress channel writes it mid-run — so it was a registry NOTHING on the identity seam owned, which is why ExecutionHost had to grow a field rather than gain a line. wamn-0h0g.19.1/.19.6 will need the same Arc when the router consumes the seam. Design call stated: the egress declaration is cleared at revoke only, not also at bind — it is declared per-run by the trusted runner, a prewarmed instance never declares one, and revoke runs on every checkout exit, so revoke-only is exact and a bind-time clear would be dead code.

title: decision(validation): WIT subtyping is absent from wasmtime — size it before .18.3 binds to WIT-type-compat
description: The wamn-0h0g.16.9 spike proved wasmtime types::Type implements PartialEq and that the comparison is STRUCTURAL ACROSS SEPARATELY COMPILED COMPONENTS: two components with different package names and different type names compare equal on identical shapes, one extra record field makes them unequal, and cross-port assignability correctly returns false. That makes a wiring validator a == b plus a renderer rather than a hand-written engine. WHAT IS MISSING IS SUBTYPING: PartialEq is EQUIVALENCE ONLY, so callee-accepts-a-superset and WIT @since/@unstable version compatibility are hand-written work. ComponentExtern::is_implements does version matching for (implements ..) annotations only, not structural widening. This only matters if wamn-0h0g.16.9 is ruled TYPED; under UNIFORM the validator is JSON-schema compat and this bead dissolves.
acceptance_criteria: Either wamn-0h0g.16.9 is ruled uniform and this bead closes as dissolved, or it is ruled typed and the subtyping gap is sized with a named owner before wamn-0h0g.18.3 claims.
close_reason: DISSOLVED by the wamn-0h0g.16.9 ruling (owner, 2026-08-18): option (a), the uniform seam with types moved to the layer that renders. All three questions arise ONLY under the per-component typed-WIT reading — .16.11 sizes WIT subtyping that wasmtime does not provide, .16.12 handles resource-carrying WIT signatures that cannot be type-cached across instances, and .16.13 adjudicates a JSON-to-WIT value projection that is a host invention because WIT has no canonical JSON projection. Under the uniform seam none of the three has a subject: port schemas are JSON Schema, checked by JSON-Schema compat at wamn-0h0g.18.3, and no arbitrary author-declared WIT type is ever marshalled. If wamn-0h0g.16.9's named reopen trigger fires — a consumer needing WIT-level composition, e.g. WAC fusion — these three reopen with it; the wave-2 spike's findings on each are preserved in .16.9's notes.

title: remediate(auth): wamn_scenario_worker_identity is live with no in-tree definition — give provisioning ownership of it
description: wamn-0h0g.12.67 points at wamn-0h0g.12.119 as the owner of the live-role re-narrowing. That is a MIS-CITATION: .12.119 is fix(ctl) the D24 orphan guard fails open on an unreadable registration set, closed at 9edc7898. notes:

A tree-wide grep for wamn_scenario_worker_identity returns exactly TWO hits and NEITHER is code: docs/archive/build-and-test.md:2591 (English prose) and one bd close reason inside .beads/interactions.jsonl. There is NO CREATE ROLE, no GRANT, no REVOKE, no deploy manifest, no Secret, no test and no SQL literal naming it anywhere in the tree.

*** WHERE I DISAGREE WITH THE LANE: IT CONCLUDED THE ROLE WAS NEVER SHIPPED AND THERE IS NOTHING TO RE-NARROW. THAT CONCLUSION IS TOO STRONG AND RESTS ON A STALE DOCUMENT. *** The lane cited docs/archive/build-and-test.md:2591-2592, which says the identity.sessions and wamn_scenario_worker_identity grant delta have been applied only to throwaway PostgreSQL and the in-cluster sysdb rollout is deferred. If that close reason is accurate, THE ROLE EXISTS IN THE LIVE wamn-sysdb AND WAS CREATED BY AN OUT-OF-TREE OWNER-RUN SCRIPT. That is EXACTLY what this bead's title means by 'the live role has no owner', and it makes the bead well-founded rather than empty.

SO THE TWO RECORDS CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, and build-and-test.md:2591-2592 is the stale half. That staleness is itself worth fixing (integrator-owned file).

THE DECIDING EVIDENCE IS ONE READ-ONLY QUERY, NOT MORE SOURCE READING: does wamn_scenario_worker_identity exist in the live wamn-sysdb, and what does it hold? A SELECT over pg_roles plus information_schema.role_table_grants settles it. *** wamn-sysdb IS PART OF THE FROZEN LIVE CLUSTER. The query is strictly read-only and mutates nothing, but it is NOT authorized by the freeze, so it needs an explicit owner go-ahead before anyone runs it. ***

OWNER DISPOSITION REQUIRED, and it should follow the query, not precede it: (a) if the role exists live, this bead is REAL and becomes an in-tree ownership bead -- give the role a definition in provisioning so something owns its grants -- plus the narrowing; (b) if it does not exist live, close as already-gone and fix the stale doc.

SEPARATE OBJECT THE LANE SURFACED, deliberately NOT folded in here: the unprobed WAMN_SYSTEM_URL credential next door. Per R12 that CONSTRUCTS MACHINERY, so it is FILE, not LAND. It needs its own bead if the owner wants it.
*** LIVE EVIDENCE, owner-authorized read-only query against the FROZEN cluster, 2026-08-19. THE MEASUREMENT LANE'S CONCLUSION IS REFUTED. THE ROLE EXISTS. ***

Queried wamn-sysdb (CNPG primary wamn-sysdb-2, wamn-system namespace). Strictly read-only SELECTs over pg_roles and information_schema.role_table_grants; nothing was created, altered or dropped.

ROLE EXISTS: wamn_scenario_worker_identity is present with rolcanlogin=t, rolreplication=f, rolsuper=f, rolbypassrls=f.

ITS LIVE GRANTS IN DATABASE wamn_system, exactly:
  identity.local_credentials   SELECT
  identity.pats                INSERT, SELECT
  identity.principals          SELECT
  identity.project_roles       SELECT

THIS MATCHES wamn-ctc8.10's CLOSE REASON VERBATIM (SELECT times 3 plus pats SELECT,INSERT, corrected from SELECT-only because /login INSERTs the PAT). So the close reason is ACCURATE and docs/archive/build-and-test.md:2591-2592 is the STALE half -- it says the delta was applied only to throwaway PostgreSQL and the sysdb rollout is deferred. IT WAS NOT DEFERRED; IT SHIPPED.

*** THE DOC IS ALSO WRONG ON THE SHAPE, NOT JUST THE TIMING: it describes the delta as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE. THE LIVE ROLE HOLDS NO UPDATE ANYWHERE. *** And there is no identity.sessions grant, consistent with f967d2cd having deleted that relation.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE BEAD -- THE TITLE IS RIGHT BUT THE VERB MAY BE WRONG. The live grants are already narrow (four relations, read-only except the one INSERT that /login provably needs). There may be little or nothing left to RE-NARROW. The real, confirmed defect is the one the title's second clause names: THE LIVE ROLE HAS NO OWNER. Nothing in the tree creates it, grants it, revokes it or reproduces it -- a fresh provisioning run does not produce this role at all, so the live sysdb and the tree have permanently diverged and no gate can detect it.

OWNER RULING NEEDED, and the evidence now supports re-scoping rather than closing: (a) RE-SCOPE to 'give the role an in-tree definition so provisioning owns its grants', keeping the measured four-relation grant set as the target shape, and drop the re-narrow framing; (b) close as already-narrow and file the ownership gap separately; (c) something else. Also fix the stale and incorrect paragraph at build-and-test.md:2591-2592 (integrator-owned).
*** OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-19): RE-SCOPE TO IN-TREE OWNERSHIP. The bead is CONVERTED, not closed. *** RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED -- implementation remains held pending an explicit instruction. Title updated to match.

THE GENERAL RULE THE OWNER STATED, and it is the reusable part: *** A CORRECT STATE THAT NOTHING IN-TREE PRODUCES IS A DEFECT OF OWNERSHIP, NOT A PROOF OF HEALTH. *** The live evidence refuted the SYMPTOM (the grants are already narrow), which converts this bead rather than closing it. The hazard was never the width of the grant set. It is that the cluster's four-relation reality has NO tree-side definition, so no reconciler converges it, no drift gate can detect its divergence because there is no declared shape to diff against, and the next provisioned environment reproduces it only by archaeology. The owner places this in the same class as .15.135 (authority state arriving without a grant decision) and .12.126 (tree and cluster disagreeing about grants); the R10 writers-empty amendment supplies the vocabulary -- an undeclared-but-live authority is exactly what the inventory exists to make impossible.

THE MEASURED SET BECOMES THE TARGET SHAPE, which is the correct epistemics: reality was adjudicated narrow by whoever built it, and this bead's job is to make the tree the author of record. From the live read of wamn-sysdb:
  identity.local_credentials   SELECT
  identity.pats                INSERT, SELECT
  identity.principals          SELECT
  identity.project_roles       SELECT

WHY NOT THE ALTERNATIVES, in the owner's words: option 2's split fails R12's own test the way .20.9 did -- close the re-narrow and file the ownership produces two beads over one deliverable, where the first closes on evidence the second exists to make REPRODUCIBLE, and a close whose proof cannot be regenerated by the tree is banked on a snapshot. Option 3 pursues narrowing the evidence just refuted, and concedes its own floor: pats INSERT is load-bearing because /login writes the PAT, leaving three SELECTs whose necessity should be adjudicated IN THE DEFINITION rather than whittled speculatively.

RIDERS, ALL BINDING ON THE EVENTUAL IMPLEMENTATION:
1. The definition goes where the sibling roles live -- the provisioning grant blocks the .13.31 family uses -- expressed as the four explicit grants with A ONE-LINE CONSUMER CITE PER GRANT: pats INSERT cites /login; each SELECT cites its reader. That way the next narrowing question is answered by the definition instead of by another probe.

It says the delta was applied only to throwaway PostgreSQL with the sysdb rollout deferred (it shipped), and describes the grants as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (the live role holds NO UPDATE anywhere).

title: [SR-MVP] feat(runtime): request-scoped principal context into the RLS session at effect time
description:
## Why — ruled 2026-08-18 as the request-grain half of wamn-0h0g.23.4

The identity grain is BOTH, LAYERED. Workload identity (wamn.tenant / wamn.runner) is the platform
grain and is landed. END-USER identity is request-scoped by construction, and without it the
generated-CRUD RLS story is theater.

wamn-0h0g.23.1 landed the mechanism: CLAIM_SQL binds app.role ($5) and app.user_id ($6) as
parameters, with SET-override refusal coverage, proven red-then-green against a real Postgres 18.6.
What it does NOT have is a per-request SOURCE — the values come from a per-component registry
populated by host-only setters, so in a deployed pod they bind '' and every per-user policy denies.
wamn-0h0g.23.4 proposed filling that registry from per-WORKLOAD config keys; the grain ruling
SUPERSEDED that approach, because one workload serves many users.

## The ratified shape

Request-scoped principal context is CARRIED STATE ON THE INVOCATION:
  - it already rides `http-entry` per the controller story — the authenticated principal and its
    claims as typed context on the request;
  - it flows HOST-SIDE into the RLS session variables at effect time, i.e. into the same
    begin_with_claims parameter binding wamn-0h0g.23.1 built;
  - it is plumbing through the wamn-0h0g.22.4 seam. NOT a parallel identity system, NOT a second
    claims registry, and NOT a guest-settable value at any point.

## Scope

1. Define where authenticated principal + claims attach to an invocation (the typed context on
   http-entry, and what paths 2/3 carry when there is no HTTP request).
2. Carry it host-side to the effect boundary so begin_with_claims binds THIS request's role and
   user_id rather than a per-component registration.
3. Preserve every invariant wamn-0h0g.23.1 established: bound as PARAMETERS, never interpolated;
   the guest cannot set or override them; the $5/$6 bare-bind (NOT COALESCE-to-current) stays, since
   re-asserting a pooled connection's current value is the cross-connection escalation .23.1
   documented at claims.rs:377-386.
4. Interacts with wamn-0h0g.17.7: a pooled instance's identity is rebound PER CHECKOUT, and
   request-scoped principal context is part of the identity tuple that rebind must cover. Ship these
   consistently or the pool leaks the principal instead of the tenant.

## Blocks

wamn-0h0g.23.2 (the entity component) and wamn-0h0g.23.3 (generate crud) — both assume RLS scopes
rows to the calling END USER. Until this lands, generated CRUD enforces tenant scope only.
acceptance_criteria: An authenticated request's principal and claims reach begin_with_claims as THIS request's app.role and app.user_id, bound as parameters, with a live test proving two different end users on ONE workload each see only their own rows through a generated CRUD route. The guest cannot set or override either value; the $5/$6 bare-bind is preserved; and the values are part of the identity tuple wamn-0h0g.17.7's per-checkout rebind covers.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(wit): wamn:node@0.2.0 violates the MVP version-identity rule — rule the version before .15.22
description:
## Why -- a live conflict between two rules, surfaced by the wamn-0h0g.16.2 integration sweep

`tests/conformance/src/version_identity.rs:514` fails at HEAD:

    WAMN WIT package version drift:
    crates/execution/router/wit/package.wit:1: WAMN package `wamn:node@0.2.0` must use @0.1.0

This is NOT registry drift and NOT wamn-0h0g.15.22 regeneration-class. It is two defensible rules
disagreeing, and the tree cannot satisfy both.

RULE 1 -- the archived package's own compatibility clause.
docs/archive/contracts/wamn-node.wit:11-13: "0.1.x admits only additive or clarifying changes; any
breaking change (a new/removed variant case or a changed signature) waits for 0.2." The .16.2
revision REMOVES types (payload-ref, framing, the streamed payload arm, the payloads/credentials/
control interfaces, two worlds) and CHANGES the run-context record into node-context. That is
breaking by the clause's own definition, so the lane shipped @0.2.0 and explicitly argued that
reviving under @0.1.0 "would have lied about a frozen contract."

RULE 2 -- the MVP version-identity governance rule.
version_identity.rs holds every first-party `wamn:*` WIT package at @0.1.0 for the MVP identity
window, and it is a hard assertion, not a lint.

## Why rule 1's argument is weaker than it looks

The 0.1.0 contract it protects is ARCHIVED and has no live consumer: the package was deleted, its
name was banned by two conformance guards, and nothing in the tree binds it. There is no deployed
0.1.0 wamn:node for a 0.2.0 to be compatible-or-not with. "Don't lie about a frozen contract" is the
right instinct in general, but the contract in question is a museum piece, and the freeze rule it
cites governs evolution of a LIVE package.

Against that: shipping @0.1.0 means a future reader diffing the archived 0.1.0 against the live
0.1.0 finds two different shapes under one version -- which is the specific confusion the compat
clause exists to prevent.

## Options

(a) SHIP AT @0.1.0 and record in the package header that it supersedes the archived 0.1.0 wholesale
    rather than evolving it -- the MVP identity window stays uniform, no governance exception, one
    line changes in the WIT plus the existence assertion in wit_coherence.rs / invocation.rs which
    pins "package wamn:node@0.2.0;". Cheapest, keeps the guard meaningful.
(b) GRANT wamn:node A NAMED EXCEPTION in version_identity.rs, on the grounds that it is the one
    package with an archived predecessor of a different shape. Costs an exception the rule then has
    to carry, and invites the next one.
(c) MOVE THE WHOLE MVP WINDOW off 0.1.0. Out of scope here; recorded only for completeness.

## Scope note

wamn-0h0g.16.2 is CLOSED (integrated at bab899bd/764c2756/5fecc218 + relocation 2e417c13). Its close
reason endorses the @0.2.0 reasoning, which this bead partially reverses -- naming that here rather
than editing the closed record. Whichever option is ruled, the ban markers ["wamn:node/",
"wamn:node@"] keep working unchanged; only the version literal and the positive existence assertion
move.

## Acceptance

version_identity::wamn_wit_packages_stay_at_mvp_version passes at HEAD, either because the package
moved to @0.1.0 with its supersession recorded in the header, or because a named exception was added
with its rationale. The wamn:node existence assertion and the two ingress ban markers must still
bite afterwards -- re-derive the nested-package mutant to prove it.
acceptance_criteria: version_identity::wamn_wit_packages_stay_at_mvp_version passes at HEAD, either by moving wamn:node to @0.1.0 with its supersession of the archived 0.1.0 recorded in the package header, or by a named exception in version_identity.rs carrying its rationale. Afterwards the two ingress ban markers and the positive existence assertion must still bite — re-derive the nested-package mutant to prove it.
notes:
RULING (owner, 2026-08-18): SHIP AT @0.1.0, WITH THE SUPERSESSION RECORDED IN THE PACKAGE HEADER.
Ratified as recommended. Bead stays OPEN until the rename lands.

REASONING: version numbers exist to manage DEPLOYED incompatibility, and there is no deployed 0.1.0
consumer — the archived contract is banned by two conformance guards and bound by nothing in the
tree. Option (b), a named exception in version_identity.rs, would be the first crack in a rule whose
entire value is having NO cracks during the MVP identity window.

EPISTEMICS, RECORDED DELIBERATELY: the integrator's close reason on wamn-0h0g.16.2 endorsed the
@0.2.0 reasoning, and this ruling reverses that half of it. The reversal is recorded here rather
than edited into the closed record — a close reason is evidence of what was believed at close, and
correcting it in place would erase the fact that the guard, not review, caught this.

ON LANDING: the tree goes green on the rename. version_identity::wamn_wit_packages_stay_at_mvp_version
(version_identity.rs:514, "WAMN package `wamn:node@0.2.0` must use @0.1.0") is the ONLY
non-regeneration-class red in the post-integration sweep of 31; every other new red closes in
wamn-0h0g.15.22's single pass.

WHAT MOVES, AND WHAT MUST NOT: only the version literal in
crates/execution/router/wit/package.wit and the POSITIVE EXISTENCE ASSERTION that pins
"package wamn:node@0.2.0;" (in flow-invocation's wit_coherence.rs and tests/conformance/src/
invocation.rs). The two ingress ban markers ["wamn:node/", "wamn:node@"] keep working UNCHANGED.
AFTERWARDS: re-derive the nested-package mutant (inline a `package wamn:node@0.1.0 { ... }` header
into the ingress WIT) to prove the pair still bites — the broadening was load-bearing and must not
be lost to a version edit.
close_reason: [28201e38] Shipped wamn:node at @0.1.0 with the supersession recorded in the package header, per the owner ruling. Acceptance MET: version_identity::wamn_wit_packages_stay_at_mvp_version passes — the branch's ONLY non-regeneration-class red is now green. Only the version literal moved, plus the positive existence assertions in wit_coherence.rs:265-266 and invocation.rs:211; the two ingress ban markers ["wamn:node/","wamn:node@"] are BYTE-IDENTICAL. *** ONE THING THE RULING COULD NOT COVER AS WRITTEN: invocation.rs:215 held a NEGATIVE assertion, assert!(!code.contains("package wamn:node@0.1.0;")), which asserted the live package is NOT 0.1.0 — now exactly what it is. It could not move; it was replaced by a pin on the supersession record, with an in-place note that the version literal no longer separates live from archived and that the 12-marker retired-vocabulary sweep at :261-279 is what does. Integrator verified the sweep survived intact. *** NESTED-PACKAGE MUTANT RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY IN THE MAIN TREE: appended a package wamn:node@0.1.0 { interface types { type json = string; } } block to crates/execution/flow-invocation/wit/package.wit (baseline sha256 5f6d96c996a3be2823cc62c1524b851259713c605cb6122a49fdfd67cea9d834 -> mutant 1e838140592e790393dcae504cfbcba51bd257b14e79a666e0fed0fd85a22129), reproduced the lane's result EXACTLY — negative_ingress_contract_does_not_alias_the_live_node_abi panicked at wit_coherence.rs:243 on marker "wamn:node@" with the identical message; restored byte-identical (sha matches baseline) and all 13 wit_coherence tests green. The broadening survived the version edit. ALSO FIXED: the header's false STAGING LOCATION paragraph claiming the router crate does not exist yet — it was relocated at 2e417c13. STILL STALE, deliberately left and reported rather than swept: the same claim in wit_coherence.rs:215-218 and invocation.rs:138-142.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(runtime): wire the role/user identity source into the wamn:postgres bind hook
description:
## Why -- wamn-0h0g.23.1 IS NOT DELIVERED IN PRODUCTION WITHOUT THIS

Found by the .23.1 lane at implementation and deliberately left undone: it is a DESIGN CHOICE about
the identity source, not a compiler-forced edit, and mod.rs was outside that lane's write domain.

.23.1 binds `app.role` and `app.user_id` into CLAIM_SQL as parameters ($5/$6) and proves, against a
real Postgres 18.6, that a compiled per-user policy permits the injected caller (red-then-green,
commits e4e442a7 then 40d026eb). The plumbing is correct and the SET-override refusal covers both
new GUCs.

BUT: `set_role` / `set_user_id` (claims.rs:709 / :734) are host-only setters that nothing calls in a
deployed pod. `on_workload_item_bind` (mod.rs:159-218) reads a config key for the RUNNER claim
(RUNNER_CONFIG_KEY) but has no equivalent for role/user. So in production both maps stay empty,
`role_for` / `user_id_for` return None, `begin_with_claims` binds `''`, and every per-user policy
STILL DENIES -- the exact symptom .23.1 exists to remove.

In other words .23.1 makes the injection POSSIBLE and proves it WORKS; this bead makes it HAPPEN.

## Scope

Mirror the RUNNER_CONFIG_KEY block exactly (~20 lines): two consts near mod.rs:120-133 and two
`if let Some(...)` blocks in `on_workload_item_bind` reading the workload's role/user config keys and
calling the existing validated setters. `clear_component_claims` (claims.rs:832-839) already reaps
both maps, so unbind needs no change.

## The design question inside it

WHAT IS THE IDENTITY SOURCE? The frozen wamn:postgres WIT says claims are "derived from the executing
WORKLOAD's identity", and the landed model is per-component host injection (wamn.tenant /
wamn.runner). The .23.1 lane therefore mirrored per-component injection rather than inventing a
request-scoped identity -- correctly, since no per-request identity plumbing exists in the runtime.

Confirm that per-workload identity is the intended grain for role/user. If a generated CRUD route is
meant to carry the END USER's identity per request (which "every per-user RLS policy" and the entity
component's RLS-scoped row access both suggest), then per-workload config keys are the wrong grain
and the real answer is request-scoped identity plumbing -- a materially larger change that belongs
with wamn-0h0g.23.2 / .23.3 and interacts with wamn-0h0g.22.4.

Rule the grain before implementing, or implement the per-workload keys as the MVP floor and file the
request-scoped question against .23.2.

## Blocks

Closing wamn-0h0g.23.1 as production-complete. .23.1 may close on its own acceptance (the binding and
its proof) only if this bead is filed and linked, so the residual production gap is not lost.
acceptance_criteria: on_workload_item_bind populates the role and user_id component registries from workload config (or from the ruled identity source), so a deployed pod binds real values for app.role and app.user_id rather than empty strings; a live test proves a per-user policy permits the caller through the deployed bind path, not only through a hand-called setter.
notes:
RULING (owner, 2026-08-18): THE GRAIN IS BOTH, LAYERED — so this bead as filed is two beads, and
its workload-grain half is already landed. Closing on the ruling, NOT on implementation.

WORKLOAD IDENTITY (wamn.tenant / wamn.runner) is the PLATFORM grain: pools, claims, effect
authority, connection generations. Landed, correct, untouched. It needs no role/user config key —
so the per-workload config-key approach this bead proposed (two consts near mod.rs:120-133 plus two
if-let blocks in on_workload_item_bind, mirroring RUNNER_CONFIG_KEY) is SUPERSEDED rather than
implemented. Do not build it.

END-USER IDENTITY IS REQUEST-SCOPED BY CONSTRUCTION. The entity component's RLS story is written
against app.role / app.user_id compiled into EVERY generated policy
(crates/schema/compiler/src/rls/compile.rs:46-57). A CRUD route serving all users under one workload
identity would make those generated policies THEATER — every user would present the same role and
user_id, and per-user row scoping would be decorative.

RATIFIED SHAPE: request-scoped principal context is CARRIED STATE ON THE INVOCATION. It already
rides http-entry per the controller story (authenticated principal / claims as typed context), and
flows HOST-SIDE into the RLS session variables at effect time. That is plumbing through the
wamn-0h0g.22.4 seam — NOT a parallel identity system, and not a second claims registry.

DISPOSITION: the request-grain half is re-filed and joins wamn-0h0g.23.2 / .23.3, sized honestly
rather than as the ~20-line config-key change this bead estimated.

wamn-0h0g.23.1 REMAINS CORRECTLY CLOSED: its CLAIM_SQL binding is the mechanism BOTH grains use to
reach Postgres. What was missing was never the binding — it was the source feeding it, and the
ruling above says that source is per-request, not per-workload.
close_reason: RULED, NOT IMPLEMENTED (owner, 2026-08-18). The grain is BOTH, LAYERED, so this bead as filed was two beads. Workload identity (wamn.tenant/wamn.runner) is the platform grain and is already landed and correct — it needs no role/user config key, so the per-workload config-key approach this bead proposed is SUPERSEDED, not built. End-user identity is request-scoped by construction: a CRUD route serving all users under one workload identity would make the compiled per-user RLS policies theater. The request-grain half is re-filed as wamn-0h0g.23.5 (blocks .23.2 and .23.3), ratified as carried state on the invocation flowing host-side into the RLS session at effect time, through the .22.4 seam rather than as a parallel identity system. wamn-0h0g.23.1 remains correctly closed: its CLAIM_SQL binding is the mechanism BOTH grains use; what was missing was the source feeding it, and that source is per-request. Full ruling in this bead's notes.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(obs): per-wiring and per-registration metrics
description:
## RE-SCOPED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-23 — HOST PROJECTION, option (a)

Emit per-wiring and per-registration THROUGHPUT and ERROR counters from the host router-delivery
bridge. Everything required is already in one Rust scope at
crates/execution/host/src/router_delivery.rs:64-138 -- the registration or attachment id (:77-83),
the manifest-resolved wiring_id and wiring_version (:88-89, :111-116), the release triple
(:110-113) and an exhaustive Ok/Err outcome (:126-138). Cardinality is bounded by construction
because resolve_target refuses an unknown id, so an unknown id can never become a label.

No WIT change. No guest change. No new capability.

## WHAT THE RULING DROPPED, AND WHY -- measured 2026-08-23

- DLQ DEPTH IS NOT IN SCOPE: IT ALREADY SHIPS. wamn.jetstream.dlq.depth is registered at
  crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_jetstream.rs:333 as a u64 observable gauge labelled
  wamn.tenant / wamn.environment / wamn.catalog / wamn.registration (:341-357), fed from the
  dead-letter publish path (:1410-1418). It landed in 2411b02b (.19.4).
- THE PRESCRIBED METHOD WAS IMPOSSIBLE. The bead asked to convert the materializer's in-memory
  Counters to OTel instruments. components/execution/materializer is a wasm32-wasip2 COMMAND
  component whose world imports exactly five interfaces (wit/world.wit:14-20) and none is a
  metrics capability, so a guest-side global meter resolves to a no-op with no host provider.
  Separately its Counters struct is one process-global threaded by mut reference and carries no
  registration dimension, so even a working conversion would emit unlabelled series.
- ERROR-FAMILY METRICS ALREADY EXIST ON PATH 1. wamn.http.route.shed and
  wamn.http.route.in_flight are emitted per attachment at flow_http_routing.rs:135 and :161.
- ACK LAG IS SPLIT OUT (see the follow-up bead). It is a small addition at an already-instrumented
  site, not part of this bead.

## PROOF

Deterministic and in-process. Copy the .24.2 harness shape (2d3578f7) but with
InMemoryMetricExporter, which is already available: crates/execution/host/Cargo.toml:25 declares
opentelemetry_sdk with the testing feature.

*** THE LANE MUST INJECT A METER AT CONSTRUCTION, NOT CALL opentelemetry::global::meter. *** The
global provider is process-global and irreversible (the only in-tree set_meter_provider is
services/dispatcher/src/main.rs:79), so a global-meter design is untestable per-test and would
establish the wrong convention for every later metrics bead. This is the repository's first
deterministic metric proof; the convention it sets will be copied.

## NAME FREEZE

Every new series is a dashboard contract that grep cannot find, because dots become underscores at
the Prometheus exporter. Decide the exact names in the first commit and pin them the way
tests/conformance/tests/effect_spans.rs:471-502 pins the postgres four.

## BOUNDARY

crates/execution/host/src/router_delivery.rs and crates/execution/host/Cargo.toml only. Do NOT
touch crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_jetstream.rs -- keeping out of it is what makes
this lane collision-free.

## VALIDATION HONESTY

The gate of record does not compile at base (wamn-0h0g.11.55). Report the per-package result only;
do not write that the gate of record ran.
acceptance_criteria: Per-wiring and per-registration throughput and error counters are emitted from the router-delivery bridge with bounded label cardinality; a deterministic in-process test asserts the exported data points via an injected Meter and InMemoryMetricExporter; the published series names are pinned; no WIT, guest, or jetstream file is modified.

description: R2 says the crash floor shelves as "landed code behind a class gate, not deleted" — but this branch has already deleted parts of it (BackfillEffectAttempts and its legacy-effect-attempt-incomplete refusal, removed by b2283d54). Owner call; it changes how Y-epic sweeps treat floor-adjacent code.

RULING (2026-08-18; ratified on the merits. BEAD STAYS OPEN -- closing is D's ratifying act.)

OPTION (b): ACCEPT DELETION AT THE EDGES -- CONDITIONAL. The condition executes FIRST.

touching run-state transitions/attempt/status, run_plane.rs, run-state.sql and claims.rs. What it
removed is recovery machinery that would be rebuilt differently anyway. Freeze-in-tree would mean
reverting a landed cleanup and taxing every future Y-epic sweep to preserve code the tier may never
sell.

WHAT R2 ACTUALLY PROMISES OPERATIONALLY is in exe-model "The boundary": the premium durable tier
"slots in at path 3's claim (classifier + ledger re-enabled per class) WITH ZERO CHANGES TO PATHS
1-2." That re-entry point and that invariant are what must be inviolate -- not every line of
machinery.

BLOCKING CONDITION (owner-sharpened). (b) EXECUTES ONLY AFTER .20.3 PRODUCES THIS ARTIFACT. It must
state:
  1. THE RE-ENTRY POINT -- path 3's claim -- and the four enforcement points.
  2. THE PATHS-1-2 NO-CHANGE INVARIANT, ideally AS A TEST that fails if paths 1-2 ever grow a
     durability dependency. A test is worth more here than prose: it is the only form of the
     invariant that survives people forgetting it.
  3. THE EROSION BOUNDARY -- what the shelf rule still binds after edge deletions: THE FOUR
     ENFORCEMENT CORES STAY COMPILING WITH UNIT TESTS GREEN; EDGES ARE DELETABLE.

RATIONALE FOR THE CONDITION: once the code is gone, "we preserved the contract" is unfalsifiable.
The artifact makes the erosion boundary WRITTEN rather than remembered, so a later sweep can tell
an edge from a core without re-litigating R2.

Until that artifact exists, floor-adjacent code is treated as under (a) -- not deletable.

path only.

InstancePolicy, from_component, and WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING appear NOWHERE in wamn's own Rust.

poolSize in workload YAML ("poolSize {n} enables reusable component stores"), mutation-tested at
