title: [SR-MVP] X — Release closure and promotion
description:
exe-model.md §Promotion and the release closure: the release is the deployable closure; promotion is four rules. Schema: release names the catalog version it was gated against; target applied version must be >= it, else migrate-catalog (additive-or-refuse) first. Components: the release lists (component, interface-version) + digests; target library must cover at compatible WIT interfaces, else deploy pulls digests first; late binding holds within an interface version. Integrations: requirements bound in target; generations never travel. Wirings: re-gated at target against target palette + bindings, then pointer-flipped; the promote verb records one provenance fact (wiring hash, source env, both gate report ids, principal, timestamp). Deploy order: migration -> components -> wirings -> flips; each step idempotent; resumable, no saga. Two speeds: seconds-fast flip within the deployed closure; the packaged path only when the closure grows.

GROUNDED FACTS: rule 1's operands exist (catalog_heads.applied_catalog_version; validated_flow_drafts pins) but every landed comparison is exact-equality same-environment — the cross-env >= gate is new. Rule 2 has NO storage (no component-digest relation). Rule 3's three-table shape is landed but keyed on flow artifact_hash. Rule 4's pointer-flip + provenance has an exact template (attachment_activation + events) but re-gating at target has no precedent. The publish gate's EXECUTING surface is unbuilt: only save-flow-draft is mounted, all queries answer 501, the sequential case executor is explicitly deferred, and wamn_scenario_model::evaluate has zero callers — .8.5/.8.6/.7.4 (rescoped) are on this epic's critical path. The frozen ServingManifest schema is flow-shaped (plan_hash, reachable_flows) and must be revised to components+digests+wirings, re-pinning the golden vector once. publish-catalog/publish-release verbs are CLOSED behind CONTROL_DEFINITION_PUBLISH_REFUSAL; publish_release.rs (2001 LOC) survives as a library.

title: [SR-MVP] U — Developer data access: sqlx over wamn:postgres
description: Developer data access uses a runtime-checked custom sqlx Database over wamn:postgres. The host retains credentials, tenant identity, pooling, sockets, and effect policy; components receive only the typed transport. The SQLx 0.9 compatibility spike proved query_as! is built-in-driver-only and Postgres transport aliasing requires private internals, so MVP has no cargo sqlx prepare, offline-cache, or compile-time query-shape guarantee. Shipping remains blocked on the non-settable per-tenant database identity and workload-authority partition.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): --app-password defaults to the known string wamn_app
description:
## Why -- the shipped bootstrap provisions every project-env with a publicly known password

services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs:124 declares

    #[arg(long, env = "WAMN_APP_PASSWORD", default_value = "wamn_app")]
    pub app_password: String,

so an operator who runs `provision-project-env` without `--app-password` gets a `wamn_app`
role whose password is the string `wamn_app`. deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh invokes the verb at
:171, :226 and :315 and passes no `--app-password`, so the shipped bootstrap path takes the
default. deploy/mvp/tests/bootstrap.sh:472 passes ROLE_SQL_PASSWORD_SENTINEL, which is a test
sentinel, not a credential. docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79 documents the default as
intentional ("matching the hand-written schemas").

`wamn_app` is the role guest-authored SQL executes as. A known password on it is a credential
defect, not a convenience.

## Why it is filed rather than fixed in wave 13

wamn-0h0g.12.122 adds a sibling `--dispatch-reader-password`. The owner ruled (2026-08-18) that
the NEW argument is required with no default_value, and that the pre-existing `--app-password`
default is the same defect on the older principal and must be filed rather than folded into
that bead. Fixing it here without filing it would leave the class half-closed.

## Scope

Remove `default_value = "wamn_app"` from `--app-password`, keeping the `WAMN_APP_PASSWORD`
env binding, so the verb refuses rather than minting a known-password role. Update the three
deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh call sites to supply a password, and correct
docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79, which currently documents the default as a feature.

## Boundary

The CLI contract and its callers. Does not change the role builder, the grants, or the
Secret rendering.
acceptance_criteria:
`provision-project-env` refuses when no app password is supplied by flag or environment;
deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh provisions successfully with an explicitly supplied password at all
three call sites; deploy/mvp/tests/bootstrap.sh still passes its sentinel unchanged; the
provisioning doc no longer advertises a default; a mutant restoring the default_value fails a
named test.
notes:
*** LIVE EXPOSURE MEASURED 2026-08-19. THIS BEAD'S PREDICTION IS NOW CONFIRMED FACT, NOT INFERENCE. ***

This bead reasoned that the shipped bootstrap path takes the default. An owner-authorized read-only verifier check has now measured the consequence directly.

METHOD: SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier arithmetic against pg_authid, NOT authentication -- PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(candidate, salt, iters) -> ClientKey -> StoredKey, compared to the stored verifier. No login attempt, no auth-log entry, no write, no DDL; the frozen cluster was not modified. The candidate was extracted programmatically from source and is cited only as THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT AT docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79. Positive control (RFC 7677 test vector) passed BEFORE any live verifier was touched, so a no-match means no-match and not a broken instrument.

RESULT over 11 LOGIN roles carrying verifiers across 3 clusters:
  wamn-pg    wamn_app   *** MATCH ***
  fixture    wamn_app   *** MATCH ***
  wamn-sysdb            (has no such role)
  all 9 other roles     no-match
*** THE RATIO IS NOT 2 OF 3 CLUSTERS. IT IS 2 OF 2 -- EVERY CLUSTER ON WHICH THE ROLE EXISTS CARRIES THE DOCUMENTED DEFAULT. Nothing, anywhere, ever overrode it. That is precisely the consequence this bead predicted from deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh:171/:226/:315 passing no --app-password. ***
SEVERITY CALIBRATION, stated honestly: the measured clusters are a LOCAL KIND DEV CLUSTER, frozen and non-production. The exposure is bounded by that. The weight of the finding is TREE-SIDE -- a default nothing overrides means any real deployment inherits it.

*** SCOPE CORRECTION: THERE IS A THIRD CALL SITE THIS BEAD DOES NOT NAME. ***
  services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs:126   (named here)
  services/ctl/src/provision.rs:49                *** NOT NAMED HERE -- same flag, same env var, same default, flows to ensure_app_role_sql the same way ***
  services/ctl/src/enable_cdc_project_env.rs:82   the CDC sibling, owned by wamn-0h0g.12.134
Both app-password sites reach crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs:28 ensure_app_role_sql, which emits CREATE ROLE ... LOGIN PASSWORD <literal>. The remedy must cover BOTH or the defect survives in the surviving path.

OWNER RULING 2026-08-19 -- REMEDY IS A REQUIRED ARG, NO DEFAULT.
Delete default_value from all three sites; the env var stays so deployment supplies it. The evidence is eleven lines of one struct: provision_project_env.rs:126 has the default (the defect) and :137 declares --dispatch-reader-password with NO default (the cure, the wamn-0h0g.12.122 shape). The tree ALREADY documents the asymmetry deliberately at :133 and :2502. This is not choosing a policy; it is FINISHING one already chosen.
FAILURE-MODE ASYMMETRY: a required arg fails loudly at provision time, in the operator terminal, once. A default fails silently, in every environment nobody overrode, forever. The read above measured what forever looks like.
GENERATE-WHEN-ABSENT REFUSED BY NAME: it converts a loud misconfiguration into a silent credential-custody problem. The platform has exactly one blessed shape for machine-minted credentials -- the wamn-0h0g.13.31 A/B generation family. If auto-generation is ever wanted here it arrives as EXTEND THE GENERATION FAMILY, not as ring SystemRandom at a flag default. The ring import at provision_project_env.rs:66 is temptation, not precedent.
FIXTURE CARVE-OUT REFUSED: the genuinely-needs-a-default set is EMPTY.
RIDERS: all three sites in ONE commit (one pattern, the R12 singular-defect reading); provisioning.md:79 rewrites in the SAME commit from defaults-to-X to required-supplied-via-env-var, because that doc line was the exposure's own citation and must die with it; the missing-arg error names the ENV VAR not just the flag; bootstrap scripts and runbooks gain explicit args in the same sweep.
KNOWN BREAKAGE, precedented: wamn-0h0g.12.122 hit exactly this when it made --dispatch-reader-password required -- deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh:171/:226/:315/:349/:628 and the gate-mutants script needed supplied passwords. The same call sites are implicated here.

ROTATION OF THE ALREADY-EXPOSED VALUE IS A SEPARATE BEAD: wamn-0h0g.12.140.
CREDENTIAL HYGIENE: the default password IS the role name, so it cannot be fully scrubbed from text without making the defect undescribable. Cite it as the documented default at provisioning.md:79 rather than adding copies.
close_reason:
Landed c3a079ec on deploy-simplification, ONE commit for all three call sites per the owner ruling (one pattern, the R12 singular-defect reading).

REMOVED default_value from:
  services/ctl/src/provision.rs:49                --app-password           (.12.129)
  services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs:126   --app-password           (.12.129)
  services/ctl/src/enable_cdc_project_env.rs:82   --replication-password   (.12.134)
Env vars retained so deployment still supplies the values. Field shape matches wamn-0h0g.12.122 exactly: String, no default, refuses at parse time.

RIDERS ALL LANDED IN THE SAME COMMIT:
 - docs/archive/platform/provisioning.md:79 rewritten -- it documented the default as intentional and matching the hand-written schemas, and was the exposure's OWN CITATION, so it died with the exposure. :460 likewise gained the required-no-default statement plus the cluster-wide REPLICATION reason.
 - The missing-argument error now NAMES THE ENV VAR, not just the flag. Verified by running the binary; it prints: the following required arguments were not provided: --app-password <PASSWORD ()>. Clap's default names only the flag, so this needed an explicit value_name.
 - The .12.122 comment asserting Deliberately has no default_value, UNLIKE --app-password above was corrected -- it is no longer true, and a comment that misdescribes the trust model is the class that produced .12.138.
 - Three named guard tests added, mirroring the_dispatch_reader_password_has_no_default: provision::tests::the_app_password_has_no_default, provision_project_env::tests::the_app_password_has_no_default, enable_cdc_project_env::tests::the_replication_password_has_no_default. Each asserts the parse FAILS without the argument. All four now pass; wamn-ctl --lib is 48/48.

*** PRE-EXISTING BREAKAGE FOUND AND FILED, NOT CAUSED BY THIS FIX: wamn-0h0g.12.141. *** deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh ALREADY could not invoke provision-project-env -- .12.122 made --dispatch-reader-password required on 2026-08-18 and NEITHER the flag NOR the env var appears anywhere in that file, so all five call sites fail at argument parsing today. .12.122's close reason says that was filed separately; NO SUCH BEAD EXISTED. That is the same false-coverage class the owner ruled a ledger sweep for, except living in a bead close reason rather than a findings row -- THE SWEEP SHOULD COVER CLOSE REASONS TOO.
The still-owed CLI-contract decision (required-always vs mode-scoped) rides .12.141: three of those five sites are effect-writer GENERATION modes that provision no database and never reach role_sql, so requiring a database credential from them is semantically wrong, not merely inconvenient. An in-tree test comment already noted the awkwardness; it now names .12.141.

VERIFIED: cargo test -p wamn-ctl --lib 48 passed / 0 failed; cargo build -p wamn-proof-integration --tests clean (provisionbench already passed --app-password explicitly). rustfmt run per-file; all three files were rustfmt-clean at base, so the diff carries no drive-by reformatting.
NOT CLAIMED: no live provisioning run. The frozen kind cluster was not touched and no credential was rotated.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): guard wamn_run.runs DELETE to terminal runs only
description:
## Why -- the residual wamn-0h0g.12.40 could NOT revoke, and said so

wamn_app holds table-wide DELETE on wamn_run.runs because `wamn-ctl prune-run-history` CONNECTS AS
THAT ROLE -- documented outright at services/ctl/src/prune_run_history.rs:10-16 and :27-29. That
overturned the brief's assumption that DELETE could simply be revoked.

*** The statement filters status IN (terminal). The GRANT does not. *** So author-reachable SQL can
delete a LIVE dispatched or running run, cascading its wamn_run.run_queue row and its
wamn_run.invocation_admissions idempotency ledger entry -- destroying replay identity, not merely
history.

## Two shapes, and the first is preferred

(a) A BEFORE DELETE row trigger refusing non-terminal deletes. *** AN ORDINARY TRIGGER, NOT A
    SECURITY DEFINER ROUTINE -- ruling R12's rider stands and the definer trio was rejected once
    already (docs/plane-amendment.md:301-303, docs/scope-reduction-mvp.md:398-399, ratified as
    wamn-0h0g.7.5). *** A trigger needs no new principal and no new credential lifecycle.
(b) Move the prune verb to an admin connection and revoke DELETE from wamn_app entirely. Cleaner in
    principle, but it makes retention a privileged operation and interacts with
    wamn-0h0g.12.69's role isolation -- decide them together if this shape is chosen.

## Boundary

The DELETE boundary on runs. Does not reopen the INSERT/UPDATE column sets wamn-0h0g.12.40 ratified.
acceptance_criteria:
A DELETE of a non-terminal run is refused by name whichever shape is chosen; prune-run-history still
prunes terminal runs and its cascade still reaps run_queue and invocation_admissions; a live test
covers both directions; no SECURITY DEFINER routine is introduced without citing the prior rejection.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-21 — THE TERMINAL-ONLY DELETE GUARD REMAINS INDEPENDENT. Do not absorb this invariant into the retention role or its grants. wamn-0h0g.12.69 bounds who may delete; this issue bounds what may be deleted, including under a compromised or accidentally over-granted retention credential. The ordinary non-SECURITY-DEFINER trigger and its own live refusal probe remain load-bearing, and wamn-0h0g.12.69 hard-depends on this issue. Split coordination origin: wamn-0h0g.22.4. OPEN, UNCLAIMED, POST-MERGE; implementation not started.
SEQUENCING SUPERSESSION 2026-08-21 — Earlier POST-MERGE / wait-for-wamn-0h0g.15.25 text is superseded by the owner's active rule: all scope-reduction and authority work lands before the single final RC and merge. This issue no longer waits on .15.25; .15.25 waits on it. Scope, priority, acceptance, and product semantics are unchanged.
close_reason: Completed by d93fa8bc: ordinary non-SECURITY-DEFINER BEFORE DELETE guard permits only completed/failed/infrastructure-failure and refuses all other runs with SQLSTATE 55000 run-delete-nonterminal; schema-control owns exact repair/no-op convergence. Fresh PG18 confinement 3/3, admission/store live, real prune retention, and full run-plane aggregate green; strict affected Clippy/fmt/diff green; four mutants killed/restored; independently approved.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(run-plane): the reconciler spec still re-grants catalog.catalogs full DML
description:
## Why -- found at integration by BISECTING a gate wamn-0h0g.12.20's lane never ran

wamn-0h0g.12.20 (e2b2d90c) confined catalog.catalogs to SELECT in deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql
AND in the publish/migrate converge path ensure_authoring_catalog_privileges. It missed a THIRD
place, and the miss made the confinement ineffective:

*** crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs AUTHORING_PRIVILEGE_SPECS[0] still declared
    catalogs -> app: ["SELECT", "INSERT", "UPDATE", "DELETE"] ***

The run-plane reconciler plans a RepairAuthoringPrivilege action from that spec. Left at full DML
it (a) planned the repair on EVERY pass, so the reconciler NEVER CONVERGED, and (b) each repair
re-granted the exact DML the DDL and the converge path had just revoked -- so the confinement was
undone by the next reconcile.

## How it was found, because the method matters more than the fix

services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs went 5 passed / 2 failed at a46f23ec to 4 passed / 3 failed,
with retired_effect_disposition_cutover_live failing on assert!(plan.is_noop()). Bisecting the
wave's commits put it exactly at e2b2d90c: green at 9b83d968, red at e2b2d90c. Printing the
non-noop plan named the action, the target and the offending GRANT verbatim.

*** wamn-0h0g.12.20's lane never ran run_plane_live -- it ran connection_storage_live,
impact_report_live and admission_live. No gate it did run observes this spec. ***

## The wider point, and why this is its own bead rather than a silent amend

This is the SIXTH independent encoding of the same blanket-grant assumption found in this wave.
wamn-0h0g.12.40 found four (the repair builder, the add-column auto-grant arm, execution_pin_cutover_sql,
and select_run_capture_privileges_sql) and a fifth in a gate assertion. A confinement in this
codebase is not done when the DDL is narrowed; it is done when every observation, repair, cutover
and gate that encodes the old shape has been found. The reconciler spec table is the canonical
place to look FIRST.

Verified: with the spec at ["SELECT"], run_plane_live returns to 5 passed / 2 failed, matching
a46f23ec exactly, with only the two known pre-existing failures.

## Boundary

The one spec entry. The other nine relations wamn-0h0g.12.20-.12.29 confined are NOT in
AUTHORING_PRIVILEGE_SPECS at all -- checked, all nine absent -- so none of them has this defect.
acceptance_criteria: AUTHORING_PRIVILEGE_SPECS declares catalog.catalogs as SELECT only; ctl run_plane_live returns to its a46f23ec baseline of 5 passed / 2 failed; a reconcile against a confined database plans no RepairAuthoringPrivilege for catalog.catalogs; reverting the spec reproduces the non-convergence.
close_reason: [d201d02b] AUTHORING_PRIVILEGE_SPECS[0] still declared catalog.catalogs as SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE for wamn_app after .12.20 confined it to SELECT in the DDL and the converge path. The run-plane reconciler builds RepairAuthoringPrivilege from that spec, so it (a) planned the repair on EVERY pass -- NEVER CONVERGING -- and (b) re-granted the exact DML just revoked. *** THE SIXTH INDEPENDENT ENCODING OF THE BLANKET RULE FOUND IN THIS WAVE. *** Found by BISECTING run_plane_live (5/2 at a46f23ec -> 4/3 at HEAD; green at 9b83d968, red at e2b2d90c) and replacing the bare assert!(plan.is_noop()) with one that PRINTS the plan, which named the action, target and offending GRANT in one run. .12.20's lane never ran run_plane_live and no gate it did run observes this spec. Scoped precisely: all nine other confined relations were checked by name and are ABSENT from the spec list, so none has this defect; of eighteen entries only catalogs and runs grant beyond SELECT, and runs at SELECT,DELETE already matches .12.40. Restored to 5/2 matching baseline exactly.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(provision): apply the dispatch-reader read surface from the run-plane reconciler
description:
## Why -- BLOCKING, and the sibling of wamn-0h0g.12.122

The dispatch reader's SELECT grants target relations in the run-plane schema, which does not
exist at provision-project-env time -- it is created and converged by the run-plane reconciler.
So grant_dispatch_reader_read_surface_sql (crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs, landed by
wamn-0h0g.12.66 at d63f09bf) has to be applied from there, not from provisioning.

Nothing calls it today. Together with wamn-0h0g.12.122 this is what stands between the landed
role and a dispatcher that can actually read its queue.

## Scope

Emit the read-surface grants from services/ctl/src/reconcile_run_plane.rs /
crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs, on the same convergent footing as the rest of the run
plane: the builder already precedes each grant with a blanket REVOKE over the same scope, so an
environment where someone widened the reader narrows back on the next reconcile. Add an
observation arm so drift is detected rather than assumed, matching how the run plane treats every
other privilege it owns.

*** MIND THE CLASS OF BUG wamn-0h0g.12.40 HIT: an observation query that encodes the grant shape
in a form the narrowed grant can never satisfy makes the reconciler plan a repair forever and
never converge. Whatever observation arm is added must be checked against a converged database,
not only against a fresh one. ***

## Boundary

Applying the landed builder. Does not change the ratified read surface.
acceptance_criteria:
The run-plane reconciler grants the dispatch reader USAGE on the run-plane schema and SELECT on
run_queue and effect_attempts; re-running converges to a no-op and does NOT plan a repeating
repair action; a widened reader is narrowed back on the next reconcile; the dispatcher dials and
reads on a freshly provisioned environment with no manual SQL.
close_reason:
Landed cc85e15b on deploy-simplification (lane commit 6b14a039).

The run-plane reconciler now grants the dispatch reader USAGE on the run-plane schema and
SELECT on run_queue and effect_attempts, with a real OBSERVATION arm
(RunPlaneActionKind::RepairDispatchReaderPrivilege) rather than an assumed grant.

PREMISE CORRECTION THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN: the layering the brief assumed is not
available -- wamn-schema-control does not depend on wamn-control-provision, so the pure
planner CANNOT call grant_dispatch_reader_read_surface_sql. Rather than re-encode the
read surface (which would have created a SEVENTH encoding of the exact kind wave 12
spent itself finding), run_plane.rs owns the observation SQL, the fields and the action
kind, and the effect shell appends the action. is_noop() is actions.is_empty(), so the
returned, printed and gated plan stays truthful.

ALSO CORRECTED: there is NO bare assert!(plan.is_noop()) in run_plane_live.rs -- every
is_noop assertion already prints {:#?} actions, so the brief's fallback instruction was
moot. And run_plane_live REQUIRES -- --test-threads=1: its legs share the catalog
schema, the run-plane schema and cluster-wide roles, and the documented
[RUN-PLANE-RECONCILE] recipe omits it, which is what produces a spurious 1 passed / 6
failed.

*** INTEGRATOR RE-VERIFICATION OF THE NON-CONVERGENCE CLASS (wamn-0h0g.12.40), the whole
point of this bead. Independent mutant M5: expected privilege set widened from {SELECT}
to {SELECT, UPDATE} -- an observation a narrowed grant can NEVER satisfy.
cd6d311e272b20bbc8f876247129b122d2c08b0a89826ca5524ee38c4aaf57ed ->
caf26a820f7f1fcf1c69da10dc68b449f9b9d1f96f8e50c93b3451146c6018c8. Killed by BOTH
the unit test a_converged_dispatch_reader_plans_no_repair AND the live gate
dispatch_reader_read_surface_live, the latter with "the reader repair repeats on a
converged database -- the observation arm encodes a state the grant cannot reach".
Restored exactly. ***

REGRESSION CHECK, the wave-12 lesson applied: run_plane_live at BASELINE CODE (measured
in a worktree whose only delta from 78afe665 is an unrelated test file, own target dir,
fresh container, --test-threads=1) = 5 passed / 2 failed. WITH this bead = 6 passed /
2 failed -- one new pass, the SAME two pre-existing failures
(execution_pin_cutover_live plans a RepairHelperFunction for
guard_run_admission_pins_immutable; run_plane_reconcile_live asserts all fourteen
run-plane tables at target and reads 12). Both verified identical at base, both
unrelated to grants, both filed.

Combination check after all five wave commits: cargo check --workspace --all-targets
clean; unit suites for wamn-ctl / wamn-schema-control / wamn-control-provision /
wamn-scenario-worker all green.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(provision): invoke the dispatch-reader role from provision-project-env
description:
## Why -- BLOCKING. wamn-0h0g.12.66 landed the builders; NOTHING CALLS THEM.

wamn-0h0g.12.66 (commit d63f09bf) added, unit-tested and live-proved three builders in
crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs: the advisory-locked create-or-harden role builder, the
additive CONNECT grant, and the convergent in-database read surface. It also re-pointed
deploy/platform/dispatcher-projects.example.yaml at the new principal.

*** SO THE EXAMPLE MANIFEST NOW NAMES A ROLE PRODUCTION PROVISIONING DOES NOT CREATE. *** The
wiring was out of that lane's file domain (services/ctl/src/*.rs belonged to concurrent lanes),
so it was reported rather than smuggled.

## Scope

In services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs:
- ensure_dispatch_reader_role_sql into the role_sql block (around :362-365)
- grant_dispatch_reader_connect_sql(&db_name) into privilege_sql (around :369-373), *** AFTER
  the ALTER DATABASE ... OWNER TO statement ***, because that statement rewrites the outgoing
  owner's ACL entry and carries away any CONNECT that merged into it -- the hazard wave 11
  measured at 47b404cf for wamn_app.

*** THIS IS NOT A MECHANICAL HUNK: it needs a new --dispatch-reader-password CLI argument
mirroring --app-password, which is a design decision for whoever owns that file. Note the
adjacent lesson from wamn-0h0g.12.64's adjudication: --app-password's default_value = "wamn_app"
means the shipped bootstrap provisions every project-env with a known password. Do not reproduce
that; decide the credential story deliberately. ***

## Boundary

Provisioning invocation only. The role's definition, grants and proofs are done.
acceptance_criteria:
provision-project-env creates wamn_dispatch_reader and grants it CONNECT, idempotently, with the
CONNECT grant emitted after the owner statement; re-running is a no-op proven by applying the
batch twice and diffing every aclitem; a fresh environment lets the dispatcher dial with the new
principal without any manual SQL.
close_reason:
Landed e22233c3 on deploy-simplification (lane commit e800baa9).

provision-project-env now invokes the landed wamn-0h0g.12.66 builders:
ensure_dispatch_reader_role_sql in role_sql, grant_dispatch_reader_connect_sql in
privilege_sql AFTER the ALTER DATABASE ... OWNER TO statement.

OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-18): --dispatch-reader-password is REQUIRED with NO
default_value, env WAMN_DISPATCH_READER_PASSWORD. Provisioning refuses rather than
minting a known-password LOGIN principal. Enforced by the named test
the_dispatch_reader_password_has_no_default. The adjacent --app-password default defect
was filed separately as wamn-0h0g.12.129, not folded in.

PREMISE CORRECTION FROM THE LANE, measured on PG 18: the CONNECT-ordering rationale
does NOT transfer to the reader. ALTER DATABASE ... OWNER TO rewrites only the OUTGOING
OWNER'S aclitem, so with both grants issued before the owner statement wamn_app (the
outgoing owner) loses CONNECT while wamn_dispatch_reader keeps it. For the reader the
placement is DEFENSIVE, not load-bearing. The lane implemented the ordering as directed
and turned the asymmetry into owner_statement_asymmetry_leg, because a reordering
regression breaks the RUNTIME while leaving the dispatcher working -- a one-sided break
a reader-only probe misses. It also found the live gate is BLIND to the reordering
mutant (the converged ACL is byte-identical; only the grantor rewrite differs), which is
why privilege_sql is pinned whole.

INTEGRATOR RE-VERIFICATION (independent): baseline sha256 of provision_project_env.rs
reproduced to the lane's value exactly,
051b23ff19e91f55878a72bae1b3b9065748971cf0c7c5d5ad41dc1d038ca2ef. Mutant restoring
default_value = "wamn_dispatch_reader" ->
a4326ed5e68b94b3ac08a9e00d3bf37d5bb4687f7d31ccb9ed4f1a1e580d2b78 killed the NAMED test
the_dispatch_reader_password_has_no_default. Restored exactly.

BREAKAGE REPORTED, NOT FIXED (filed separately): the required argument now applies to
provision-project-env modes that provision no database, so deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh:171,
:226, :315, :349, :628 and tools/gate-mutants/effect-writer-primitive.sh:271,:273 need
either a supplied password or a mode-scoped requirement. That is a CLI-contract decision
and is the owner's, so it was not taken here.

NOT CLAIMED: no in-cluster verification. The acceptance clause "a fresh environment lets
the dispatcher dial with the new principal" is proven against a throwaway postgres:18
(real dial as wamn_dispatch_reader, real reads of run_queue/effect_attempts, 42501 on
runs/node_runs), NOT against the frozen kind cluster.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(publish): the manifest digest is not a pure function of the release version
description:
## Why -- a consequence of wamn-0h0g.15.121's option (a) or (b), surfaced by the .15.14 mint

Every other manifest input is immutable-per-version: flows, artifacts, execution bundles,
attachments and sources are all keyed by (tenant, catalog, version) and never rewritten.
*** catalog.event_registrations is HOT-EDITABLE and carries NO catalog_version column at all. ***

So if registrations travel in the manifest, a re-mint of THE SAME release legitimately yields a
DIFFERENT digest after any registration edit. The digest stops being a function of the release.

## Who is affected

- wamn-0h0g.8.21 (the deployment attestation) records a digest as the thing a release IS, under
  ruling .13.54: a digest is RELEASED iff an attestation references it.
- wamn-0h0g.15.44 garbage-collects superseded release-manifest-<digest> ConfigMaps and must know
  whether two digests for one release is normal or a bug.
- wamn-0h0g.15.97 / .15.98 push and publish those bytes.

## The question

Is a version-stable digest a requirement? If yes, registrations must be version-pinned at mint (a
schema change) or excluded (which is wamn-0h0g.15.121 option (c)). If no, every consumer above must
be told that one release maps to many digests over time, and the attestation becomes the only thing
that says which digest is current.

Resolving wamn-0h0g.15.121 as option (c) DISSOLVES this question entirely; the two should be ruled
together, in that order.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded ruling on whether the manifest digest must be stable per release version, with the
consequence propagated to wamn-0h0g.8.21, .15.44, .15.97 and .15.98.
notes:
EXE-MODEL TRIAGE 2026-08-18: does NOT dissolve — its escape hatch was .15.164 option (c), which the spec forecloses. Hot-editable version-less registrations really do make the digest a non-function of the release version; .15.44 (ConfigMap GC), .8.21 (attestation), .15.97/.15.98 all need the answer. Options: version-pin registrations at mint (digest stays a function of the version) vs accept many digests per release with the deployment attestation as the sole current-digest fact — the latter matches R3's hot-pointer posture but re-educates every downstream consumer. Rule alongside .15.164 and wamn-0h0g.25.1.
RULING (2026-08-18; ratified on the merits. BEAD STAYS OPEN -- closing is D's ratifying act.)

VERSION-PIN REGISTRATIONS AT MINT. The manifest digest stays a pure function of the release version.

GROUNDED AT HEAD e1d95806:
- catalog.event_registrations has NO catalog_version column -- PK is (tenant_id, catalog_id,
  registration_id), catalog-schema.sql:1704-1712 -- and carries INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants. It is
  hot-editable by construction, and it is the ONLY manifest input that is. Flows, artifacts,
  execution bundles, attachments and sources are all keyed by (tenant, catalog, version) and never
  rewritten.
- The decisive evidence is the weld itself. crates/platform/runtime/src/release_manifest.rs:1-12:
  it "derives both halves of the (release version, manifest digest) pair from the verified content
  itself", and it is explicitly "a weld, not a cache -- do not add invalidation, a TTL, a refresh,
  an eviction policy". A hot-editable input makes that pair unstable per version, which is
  incoherent with a structure designed to resolve once and hold for the life of the process.
- .15.61 (closed, commit e38dd2a1) ALREADY SHIPS FOUR DIGEST-STABILITY TESTS. Pinning is consistent
  with the frozen primitive; many-digests-per-release would contradict tests that are already green.
- Many-digests also breaks .13.54 ("a digest is RELEASED iff an attestation references it") and
  leaves .15.44's ConfigMap GC with no fact by which to distinguish superseded from concurrent.
- Pinning is also closest to what already ships: the .15.14 mint takes the registration set as a
  REQUIRED ARGUMENT.

CONSEQUENCE -- ACCEPTED, AND RECORDED VERBATIM PER OWNER:
Hot registration semantics, if ever demanded, ride pointer-flipped activation like wirings; the
manifest stays immutable. Hot things get pointer flips.
The template is catalog.wiring_activation (.18.1) / attachment_activation at
catalog-schema.sql:629-733. NOT digest instability.

STATED PLAINLY: a registration edit after mint does NOT affect the released manifest; it lands on
the next mint. That is a real semantic and belongs in the promote UX.

PROPAGATE THE CONSEQUENCE TO: .8.21 (deployment attestation), .15.44 (ConfigMap GC), .15.97 (OCI
push), .15.98 (GitOps desired state).

SUPERSESSION: this ruling shares the wamn-0h0g.13.53 env-hot-condition supersession recorded in
full on .15.164, including the reversal of .13.53's identity-only consequence frozen in .15.61.
Rule the pair together, .15.164 first.
close_reason: RATIFIED (owner, 2026-08-18, batched ratification). The ruling, its grounding at HEAD e1d95806, and the owner's additions are recorded verbatim in this bead's notes; this close is the ratifying act, not a summary. Version-pin registrations at mint; the manifest digest stays a pure function of the release version. Consistent with the four digest-stability tests .15.61 already ships. Consequence, recorded verbatim per owner: hot registration semantics, if ever demanded, ride pointer-flipped activation like wirings; the manifest stays immutable. Hot things get pointer flips. Propagates to .8.21, .15.44, .15.97, .15.98; shares the .13.53 supersession recorded on .15.164.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): the D24 orphan guard fails open on an unreadable registration set
description:
## Why -- the SAME collapse as wamn-0h0g.12.103, on a DESTRUCTIVE path, and LIVE

services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs:1235 guard_registration_orphans is the D24 refusal that stops a
migration from removing an entity still referenced by an event registration. It probes with
to_regclass and, at :1247-1249, returns Ok(()) -- a CLEAN PASS -- when catalog.event_registrations
is absent.

*** AND ITS OWN DOCSTRING ASSUMES WHAT NOTHING ASSERTS: "the caller connects as a superuser, so RLS
is bypassed". catalog.event_registrations is FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so a caller that does NOT
bypass RLS -- a non-superuser table or schema owner included, because FORCE strips the owner's usual
exemption and PostgreSQL checks BYPASSRLS on the current role only, never through inherited
membership -- reads ZERO ROWS WITH NO ERROR. The guard then finds no orphans and passes. ***

## Why this is MORE severe than wamn-0h0g.12.103, which it mirrors

.12.103 degraded CAPTURE: a wrong REPLICA IDENTITY reset means events lose their old image until
the next repair. THIS guard gates a DESTRUCTIVE APPLY. A silent pass lets migrate-catalog REMOVE an
entity that event registrations still reference -- the exact outcome D24 exists to prevent -- and
the run reports clean.

## It is LIVE, unlike the .12.103 CronJob framing

publish_catalog.rs:194 sits below the wamn-0h0g.8.18 unconditional refusal at :131 and is dead. But
services/ctl/src/migrate_catalog.rs has NO refusal: guard_registration_orphans is called at :118
(dry-run, where a failure is reported as "[dry-run] would REFUSE at apply") and at :148 (the real
apply, before the apply transaction opens). migrate-catalog is a live verb.

## Scope

Apply the wamn-0h0g.12.103 remedy to this call site: refuse by name on absent, and run the
cross-tenant read under `row_security = off` (the pg_dump idiom) so PostgreSQL raises SQLSTATE 42501
instead of silently filtering. Correct the docstring, which currently ASSERTS the superuser property
as a fact rather than establishing it. Reuse the UnreadableRegistrations error shape .12.103 landed
in crates/schema/control/src/replica_identity.rs rather than minting a second taxonomy.

Filed rather than fixed in wave 12 because publish_catalog.rs was held by another lane.

## Boundary

The orphan guard's read. Does not change the D24 refusal semantics, the migrate planner, or any
credential.
acceptance_criteria:
A migrate-catalog dry-run and apply against a database whose catalog.event_registrations is absent,
or readable-but-RLS-filtered, refuse by name instead of passing the orphan guard clean; a live test
proves both, proves a correctly-provisioned environment with genuinely zero registrations still
passes, and proves no entity is removed as a side effect of an unreadable registration set; a mutant
restoring the Ok(()) early return fails a NAMED test while the positive test stays green.
close_reason:
Landed 9edc7898 on deploy-simplification (lane commit bbbb2d10).

guard_registration_orphans now refuses BY NAME on both unreadable states instead of
returning a clean pass: absent (the explicit Ok(()) early return) and
readable-but-RLS-filtered (catalog.event_registrations is FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so a
non-BYPASSRLS session read zero rows with NO error). The cross-tenant read runs under
SET row_security = off, the pg_dump idiom, so PostgreSQL raises 42501 instead of
filtering. Docstring now ESTABLISHES the superuser requirement instead of asserting it.

TAXONOMY DECISION: the .12.103 literals do NOT fit. Their Display renders "refusing to
reconcile REPLICA IDENTITY", which would misdirect an operator running migrate-catalog.
UnreadableRegistrationsKind gained OrphanGuardAbsent/OrphanGuardUnreadable
(orphan-guard-registrations-{absent,unreadable}) and the message verb became
kind-dependent via refused_action(). The two original variants keep BYTE-IDENTICAL
output by construction (refused_action returns "reconcile REPLICA IDENTITY" for them),
so .12.103's unit test and replica_identity_unreadable_live stay green untouched. This
extends read-mostly replica_identity.rs -- the lane flagged it rather than smuggling it.

INTEGRATOR RE-VERIFICATION (independent, in the integration tree, not accepted on the
lane's report):
- mutant restoring the Ok(()) fail-open reproduced BIT-FOR-BIT to the lane's hashes,
  e0a972ef422f84bbdb1eddf2ae0ccae39571bcf036eb0545fe258629631743a4 ->
  959ab6c7a8d37ad77a0f8766d40c57bdd8179dff0f75921fead90f0076162122, proving the mutant
  was the shipped code. It killed the NAMED test
  an_unreadable_registration_set_refuses_the_migration_by_name with "an absent
  registration table must refuse the dry run: ()" WHILE the positive control
  a_provisioned_but_empty_registration_set_still_passes_the_guard STAYED ok -- exactly
  the acceptance criterion. Restored to e0a972ef, tree clean.
- both new live tests green in the integration tree.
- wamn-schema-control unit suite green, including BOTH
  an_unreadable_registration_set_refuses_by_name (.12.103, untouched) and
  an_unreadable_registration_set_refuses_the_orphan_guard_by_its_own_name (new).

PREMISE CORRECTIONS FROM THE LANE: the Ok(()) was at :1295-1297, not :1247-1249. And
wamn_app CANNOT stand in as the non-bypassing role -- read_current_applied ends in FOR
UPDATE, and wamn-0h0g.12.126 (one commit before this wave's base) removed exactly that
grant, so wamn_app dies with "permission denied for table catalogs" BEFORE reaching the
guard and proves nothing. The lane built a purpose-made d24_rls_reader instead.

NOT CLAIMED, deliberately: the (apply x RLS-filtered) cell is not covered end-to-end.
Reaching the apply guard as a non-bypassing caller needs that caller to own the catalog
tables, and catalog-schema.sql:27 hard-codes CREATE SCHEMA catalog AUTHORIZATION
postgres. Both call sites share the one function and apply x absent IS proven, but the
cell is documented in-code rather than claimed.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(provision): issue the ratified wamn_management_admitter role from provisioning
description:
## Why -- a RATIFIED DESIGN THAT PROVISIONING DOES NOT BUILD

wamn-0h0g.7.5 settled the management-admission authority question (docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md:2611,
docs/plane-amendment.md:289-317): a stable host-only ACL role `wamn_management_admitter`,
NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS, with project-env
scoped A/B LOGIN generations, granted column-exact authority and nothing else, with wamn_app,
guests, author SQL, wamn_scenario_author and wamn_effect_writer all explicitly denied.

*** IT EXISTS ONLY INSIDE A TEST FILE. *** It is created at
crates/execution/run-state/tests/admission_live.rs:172-173 and granted at :818-832. The comment at
:812-815 states the position outright: "issuing them from provisioning is deferred, and
deploy/sql/run-state.sql deliberately still names no management role." Repo-wide, every other
occurrence is documentation.

## Why this is worth its own bead rather than riding a confinement

Three separate confinement beads -- wamn-0h0g.12.63, .12.67, .12.69 -- are each asked to instantiate
a partitioned workload authority, and the repository's one worked example of that pattern is a role
provisioning does not create. Landing it gives the next three beads a TEMPLATE TO COPY rather than a
pattern to re-derive three times, and it is the difference between a ratified decision and a
shipped one.

wamn-0h0g.12.40's own plane-amendment note says "do not make the remediation issue implement that
role twice" -- which forbids .12.40 from implementing it, and is precisely why it needs its own home.

## Scope

Issue the role and its A/B LOGIN generations from crates/control/provision, following the shape
already used for wamn_effect_writer (sql.rs:199-239) and wamn_control_author (sql.rs:521-560),
including the advisory-locked create-or-harden idiom of ensure_control_author_acl_role_sql. The
exact grants are already written down at admission_live.rs:818-832 and must be copied, not
re-derived. Retire the test-local CREATE ROLE in the same change or the test stops proving anything
about the shipped role.

## Boundary

Provisioning the role. Does not change any wamn_app grant and does not touch the admission code
path.
design: Implement ManagementAdmitter as the seventh project-environment-scoped WorkloadRoleFamily through the generic lifecycle landed by wamn-0h0g.13.59. No bespoke prepare, retire, Secret, or A/B implementation. The stable NOLOGIN role receives only surviving management-kind statement grants plus the required read-only environment policy access; the pairwise denial matrix gains this role. Record the six-to-seven enum transition with cite wamn-0h0g.13.61.
notes:

CARGO_TARGET_DIR=~/.cache/wamn-w53/lane-12118 cargo check -p wamn-control-provision -p wamn-ctl -p wamn-run-state --all-targets --keep-going
