title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): provision the T1 event-reader registration role
description:
## Why -- the second half of wamn-0h0g.12.67, split out because it is a DISJOINT grant set

wamn-0h0g.12.67 names one Secret, `wamn-system-db`, serving TWO consumers whose required authority
does not overlap at all:

  scenario-worker  -> SELECT on identity.pats, identity.principals, identity.project_roles
                      (crates/identity/platform/src/lib.rs:62-67, :48-49)   <- stays on .12.67
  cdc-reader       -> SELECT on registry.event_readers                       <- THIS BEAD
                      (crates/control/registry/src/sql.rs:196-201, executed
                       services/cdc-reader/src/lib.rs:424-437, off WAMN_SYSTEM_URL at :105-106)

Different schema, different relation, zero intersection. *** One Secret name serving two disjoint
grant sets is exactly how a role gets widened to the union. *** Split so neither lane provisions
one role for both.

## What exists today -- nothing

deploy/sql/system-schema.sql contains ZERO executable GRANT and ZERO REVOKE; all four GRANT matches
are comments (:19, :82, :84-85), and :83 says so: "Left as a documented seam -- RBAC is a separate
subsystem." No manifest, no renderer in crates/control/provision/src/secret.rs, and no path in
deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh creates `wamn-system-db`. The only T1 credentials the repository mints are
`wamn-sysdb-app` (authenticating as wamn_system, the AUTHORIZATION owner of registry/provisioning/
identity per system-schema.sql:77-79) and `wamn-sysdb-superuser` (wamn-sysdb.yaml:52). An operator
following the repository has only those two choices, and both are far wider than a registration read.

## A SECOND GAP, found while measuring: the consumer has no manifest either

deploy/platform/event-reader.example.yaml was DELETED by 2099d754. Only
deploy/platform/event-reader-rbac.yaml survives, and its header at :8-9 still asserts the credential
surface it no longer wires. Either restore the Deployment manifest with the new Secret, or record
the deletion as intentional and say what replaces it -- do not leave an RBAC manifest describing a
workload that is not deployed.

## Boundary

The registry read only. The identity.* reader is wamn-0h0g.12.67.
acceptance_criteria:
A distinct role granted SELECT on registry.event_readers and nothing else, with its own Secret
name (never `wamn-system-db`); the cdc-reader probes role and database at startup and refuses on
mismatch; a negative proof shows it cannot read identity.*; the event-reader Deployment manifest is
restored or its absence is recorded as intentional with its replacement named;
architecture/protected-writes.json updated.
notes:
GRANT DOOR OPENED 2026-08-26 BY OWNER RULING. Phase B ITEM 2 IS OPEN FULLY - this bead is no longer parked. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED; no lane is claimed.

The standing rule was that wamn-0h0g.8.25 was the LAST item-2 first commit and further grant asks wait for the item-2 build proper. RULED: that rule's purpose was preventing piecemeal grants DURING the transitional schema, not deferring the build past its own precondition. Phase A has closed and epic .21 measures 11/12, so the precondition is met.

BOTH NARROWER OPTIONS WERE REJECTED ON THE RECORD. Opening narrowly for wamn-0h0g.22.8 alone (the RC spine) is the one-off-widening shape the rule exists against. Holding until wamn-0h0g.13.7 is dispositioned misreads the order - the developer SDK is item-1 POLISH, not item-2's gate, and .13.7 is a hold:post-mvp placeholder gated on .1.3, re-assess the held backlog at program close.

HOW ITEM 2 LANDS, as ruled: as THE ONE CONSTRUCTION the rule promised - role families, current_user authority, grants, denial probes and regeneration TOGETHER. Built once, proven once. Not as four separate grant widenings that happen to be unblocked on the same day.

THE FOUR NOW OPEN: wamn-0h0g.7.7 (HTTP Publish, carrying the three-things-moving inventory), wamn-0h0g.12.116, wamn-0h0g.12.67, wamn-0h0g.22.8 (also on the RC spine per authority-pre-rc-graph). The ruled fragments - the five-way current_user split and wamn-0h0g.13.59 - are ITS SPEC, not separate work.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): prune-run-history must not default its schema
description:
## Why -- a silent mistarget, found by the wamn-0h0g.12.69 adjudication 2026-08-18

services/ctl/src/prune_run_history.rs:35-36 declares
    #[arg(long, default_value = "wamn_run")] pub schema: String
and the statement it drives is UNQUALIFIED -- crates/execution/run-state/src/sql.rs:141-147 is
`DELETE FROM runs WHERE ...`, resolved through a SESSION-level search_path set at
prune_run_history.rs:113 (set_config(..., false) -- not LOCAL).

*** So a retention CronJob that omits --schema for a project-env whose run plane lives elsewhere
silently prunes the canonical `wamn_run` schema instead of the project's, prints
"pruned N terminal run(s) ... in schema wamn_run", and exits 0. *** The shipped example uses
`--schema poc_f1` (deploy/platform/run-retention.example.yaml:65), so the default is not what any
real deployment wants.

EVERY in-repo caller already passes --schema explicitly -- run-retention.example.yaml:65 and
tests/integration/src/capturebench.rs:506-507. The default therefore serves nobody and only
enables the silent mistarget.

This is the same failure class as wamn-0h0g.12.103: a destructive operation that targets the wrong
thing and presents as a clean, successful, idempotent-looking run.

## Scope

Remove `default_value` from the `schema` argument, making it required, and say in the doc comment
why: the DELETE is unqualified, so a defaulted schema silently prunes a relation the operator did
not name. Pin the absence with a named test in the repository's existing include_str! guard idiom.

## Boundary

The argument default only. The retention role isolation -- the CronJob holds a full `wamn_app`
credential for a workload needing SELECT+DELETE on one relation -- is the construction half of
wamn-0h0g.12.69 and is filed separately. No grant changes; the wamn-0h0g.15.22 freeze is untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
`--schema` is required; a named test pins that no `default_value` remains on it; both existing
callers still work unchanged; a mutant restoring the default fails that named test.
close_reason: [43235c58] --schema is now required. The DELETE it steers is UNQUALIFIED (run-state/src/sql.rs:141-147, DELETE FROM runs) through a SESSION-level search_path (set_config(..., false)), so omitting the flag pruned the canonical wamn_run history instead of the project's, printed "pruned N terminal run(s) ... in schema wamn_run" and exited 0 -- the .12.103 failure class exactly. The default served nobody: the shipped example already passes --schema poc_f1. PREMISE CORRECTION: the bead names two callers as EVERY caller; there is a third at test-support/infrastructure/ctl_process.rs:172,:181 with no --schema. Harmless today because command_preserves_the_ops_cli_boundary only CONSTRUCTS the Command and asserts argv -- the binary is never spawned -- but the enumeration was incomplete, and if that test ever executes it becomes a real caller this would have broken. RECORDED NOT FIXED: terminalize_effect_uncertain.rs:24 carries the identical default on another MUTATING verb; filed. Verified behaviourally as well as by source guard: the built binary now refuses with "the following required arguments were not provided: --schema <SCHEMA>" before any I/O.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(host): drop the DATABASE_URL ambient fallback from both host pools
description:
## Why -- a LIVE selection defect, found by the wamn-0h0g.12.65 adjudication 2026-08-18

The host process builds TWO independent database pools from FOUR DIFFERENT precedence chains,
and `WAMN_PG_URL` vs `DATABASE_URL` is INVERTED between the host and the other workloads:

  wamn:postgres (guest SQL + claim_next_production)
    crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/pool.rs:45-47
    DATABASE_URL -> WAMN_PG_URL          (silent None if neither)
  wamn:flow-invocation (HTTP/flow admission)
    crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_flow_invocation.rs:46-49
    WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL -> DATABASE_URL -> WAMN_PG_URL   (silent None)
  executor  services/executor/src/lib.rs:381-386
    --database-url -> WAMN_PG_URL -> DATABASE_URL          (hard error)
  dispatcher  services/dispatcher/src/lib.rs:473-479
    --projects-file -> --database-url -> WAMN_PG_URL -> DATABASE_URL   (hard error)

The two host plugins are constructed 42 lines apart in one function (services/host/src/host.rs:215
and :257-259). `deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml:124-129` sets ONLY `WAMN_PG_URL`, from
Secret `wamn-host-db`. `DATABASE_URL`, `WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL` and `WAMN_PG_PROJECTS_FILE` are set
NOWHERE under deploy/. *** So the two host backends agree today by the ABSENCE of the variables
they disagree about, not by any enforced invariant, and NOTHING asserts they agree. *** The only
nearby test (crates/platform/runtime/src/flow_invocation.rs:1699-1713) pins pool shape, never
ordering and never cross-plugin agreement.

## The exposure

`DATABASE_URL` is the most generic Postgres environment name in existence -- routinely injected by
base images, operators, sidecars and PaaS wrappers. If it appears in the host Pod's environment,
BOTH host backends silently prefer it over the Secret the manifest wired, with no log line, no
probe and no gate: the manifest then describes a principal the process is not using. Conversely,
setting only `WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL` makes flow-invocation live while every guest SQL call returns
`connection-unavailable` -- one process, two effective principals, or one and a hole.

## Scope -- five lines, and it REMOVES a capability nobody legitimately holds

Delete the `DATABASE_URL` arm from both host plugins. Nothing in deploy/ sets it; the only in-repo
producer is crates/control/provision/src/dump.rs:235, which injects it into a pg_dump SIDECAR
CONTAINER -- a different image and process, untouched by this change. `WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL`
survives as the one deliberate, named, tested override. Also correct the now-stale comment at
services/host/src/host.rs:241.

Lands now under ruling R12 (`defects with proofs` and `revocations of authority nobody legitimately
holds`) and R4 (`THE ONLY THING THAT WAITS IS PAPERWORK; THE ONLY THING THAT DOES NOT IS AUTHORITY`).

## Boundary

Precedence only. Startup identity/database/ACL assertion is the construction half of
wamn-0h0g.12.65 and is filed separately. No grant changes, so no architecture/protected-writes.json
row goes stale and the wamn-0h0g.15.22 freeze is untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
Neither host plugin reads `DATABASE_URL`; a named test pins its absence in both source files via
the repository's include_str! guard idiom; `WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL` still overrides for
flow-invocation; a mutant restoring either fallback fails a NAMED test.
close_reason: [4cffb3b0] Both host pools dropped the DATABASE_URL arm. *** They agreed only because the variable they ordered DIFFERENTLY happened to be unset everywhere -- wamn:postgres read DATABASE_URL BEFORE WAMN_PG_URL, wamn:flow-invocation read it second, both fall silently to None, and nothing under deploy/ sets it. *** An injected DATABASE_URL (base image, operator, sidecar, PaaS) would have flipped both onto a principal the manifest never named, with no log line and no gate. WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL survives as the one deliberate override, and the guard's pre-existing count assertion on it is the other half -- mutation-verified by deleting the WRONG arm. Two of the four mutants hash BIT-FOR-BIT to the pre-fix baselines (db7e6ae0, 11fead7f), so they are provably the shipped code rather than paraphrases; re-derived at integration. PREMISE CORRECTIONS: claims.rs:482-484 carries the SAME false claim one call frame up and is left stale (outside the lane's domain, filed); and flowbench.rs:266-272 / matbench.rs:610-616 DO consume the removed fallback via WamnPostgresConfig::from_env() -- nothing breaks, but their refusal strings now name a variable they no longer honour. dump.rs:235 confirmed a CONTAINER env injection on postgres:18, not a host read. FOR .15.22: nothing newly stale; flow-invocation-listener.sh and flow-invocation-replay.sh were ALREADY stale at a46f23ec (baseline hashes 1b36e485, matching neither pin), and the former is stale twice over -- its NEEDLE occurs zero times at baseline.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): amend the never-ratified writers-empty rule with a retired state
description:
## Why -- OWNER RULING R10, 2026-08-17

tests/conformance/tests/protected_relations.rs:178-184 asserts that a relation with
`writers: []` in architecture/state-owners.json MUST be author-SQL writable
(`author_reachable == AUTHOR_SQL_EXPOSURE`). The owner ruled THAT RULE WAS NEVER
RATIFIED:

  "`writers:[]` was only ever EVIDENCE toward 'authors own it', never a definition.
   The gate hardened evidence into a theorem, and wamn_run.flows is the counterexample
   the theorem was always exposed to -- a platform relation whose writer WE DELETED,
   which the rule now launders into tenant business state."

## The amended predicate

    writers:[]  =>  author-writable  XOR  (retired AND superseded_by present AND zero grants)

A relation whose writer was deleted is RETIRED, not tenant-owned. `retired` carries a
MANDATORY `superseded_by` naming the relation that took over -- "a forwarding address,
not a parking permit" -- and a retired relation must be FULLY revoked: zero grants to
any principal, wamn_app included.

## Scope

1. architecture/state-owners.json: add the `retired` lifecycle state with its mandatory
   `superseded_by` to the schema, and classify wamn_run.flows as retired, superseded_by
   the immutable release path (catalog.release_flows + catalog.flow_artifacts).
2. tests/conformance/tests/protected_relations.rs: amend the writers-empty rule to the
   XOR predicate above, and ASSERT THE RETIRED STATE POSITIVELY -- a retired relation
   must carry zero grants to any principal, not merely "not author-writable".
3. tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs: validate the new field (retired REQUIRES
   superseded_by; superseded_by must name a relation that exists in the manifest), and
   re-anchor a_relation_with_only_author_sql_mutation_may_have_no_static_writer, which
   currently uses wamn_run.flows as its worked example of the rule being amended.

## THE FREEZE EXCEPTION

architecture/*.json is FROZEN until wamn-0h0g.15.22. The owner authorised the
state-owners.json `retired` field as THE ONE EXPLICIT EXCEPTION. Nothing else in
architecture/ may move under this bead -- protected-writes.json in particular stays
frozen, and its wamn_run.flows row is reconciled by .15.22.

## MEASURED, so the "zero grants" half is not a leap

wamn_run.flows has NO wamn_app reader in production. The recorded readers
["flowrunner","dispatcher"] are STALE: crates/execution/run-state/src/queue/sql.rs:440
active_flows_sql has ZERO callers (only its own re-export at queue/mod.rs:76), and the
sole production read -- services/ctl/src/impact_report.rs:157 via
crates/schema/control/src/sql.rs:315 select_active_flows_sql -- runs on
args.admin_database_url, a SUPERUSER connection, behind a table_present guard.

## Boundary

The gate rule and its manifest vocabulary. The SQL revoke itself is wamn-0h0g.12.37;
the deletion is wamn-0h0g.12.102 and carries the decay clause.
design:
DECAY CLAUSE (binding, owner ruling R10): `retired` is a TRANSITIONAL classification
whose population should trend to ZERO. Any relation sitting in `retired` past its named
successor's landing is a FILED BUG, not a status. This clause is what keeps the amendment from
quietly becoming a third ownership category that future deletions park in forever. The
disposition bead for the first and only current inhabitant is wamn-0h0g.12.102.
acceptance_criteria:
The writers-empty rule reads as the amended XOR predicate; `retired` exists in
architecture/state-owners.json with a mandatory `superseded_by` that is validated against the
manifest; wamn_run.flows is classified retired and superseded_by the immutable release path;
a retired relation is asserted POSITIVELY to hold zero grants to any principal including
wamn_app; a mutant that removes superseded_by from a retired relation, and a mutant that gives
a retired relation a grant, each fail a NAMED test.
close_reason: [9b83d968] The writers-empty theorem is replaced by ruling R10's amended predicate -- writers:[] => author-writable XOR (retired AND superseded_by present AND zero grants) -- and architecture/state-owners.json gains the `retired` lifecycle state with a MANDATORY superseded_by, validated same-plane, non-empty, no self-reference, no static writer, zero grants. *** THE FINDING: wamn_run.flows was the rule's ONLY WITNESS, EVER. Across 84 objects and 3 families it is the sole `writers: []` entry, so the branch fired exactly once in the whole repository -- on the counterexample. The rule was never tested against a case it was true of. The author-writable arm of the XOR now has ZERO inhabitants; the test was RENAMED, not split, because a companion test would have had no witness to assert about. *** superseded_by is a LIST because the retired path did two jobs (graph_json body, active marker) and the immutable release path splits them across catalog.flow_artifacts and catalog.release_flows; a scalar would be half a lie. DELIBERATELY LEAVES protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership RED (deliberate-red count 3 -> 4) with a TRUE message naming open P1 .12.37; ruling R4 permits exactly this window, and experiment R0 (pre-applying the revoke + regeneration) turns it green, isolating the red to the unrevoked grant. build-and-test.md gains the third Known-red row plus a standing DO-NOT-EXEMPT instruction. PREMISE CORRECTIONS: only TWO of the three pre-existing reds are the inventory mismatch -- host_owned_production_claim_authority fails on a pinned writer-set assertion, so repairing validate_canonical_inventory alone will not green it; and wamn_run.flows' recorded readers are not stale-by-degree but FALSE IN BOTH ENTRIES (zero `flows` hits in flowrunner and dispatcher; active_flows_sql belongs to run-state). readers left alone on purpose -- it names principals, not roles, and emptying it collides with the unrelated ratified at-least-one-reader rule; .12.102 deletes the rows. 6 mutants killed; the plane conjunct re-derived independently at integration (kills retired_relation_cannot_forward_across_planes, a green test) and restored byte-identical. FOR .15.22: protected-relations.sh:13 expected_static_sha invalidated (41f3a76a -> 97f4fc23, RE-DERIVE); :12 expected_live_sha was ALREADY stale at a46f23ec (pins fcd56d66, file is 44fa713d); :11 still matches.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): provision-project creates superuser-owned databases
description:
## Why

services/ctl/src/provision.rs (the legacy 2.3 provision-project path) calls
create_database_sql, which has NO OWNER clause -- so wamn-db-<project> ends up owned by postgres.

That is the OTHER failure mode owner ruling R9 names. R9 rejected postgres-as-owner explicitly:
it trades escalation-from-below for maximal blast radius from above, and it makes the five
in-tree datdba probes false in the opposite direction. wamn-0h0g.12.108 fixed the project-env CR
path; this path was deliberately left because it has no CR and no project-env, and changing it
touches the provisionbench gate.

## Boundary

The legacy provision-project path only. wamn_db_owner already exists
(wamn-0h0g.12.108); this bead gives that path the same title role and nothing else.
acceptance_criteria: No database created by provision-project is owned by postgres or by any login role; wamn_db_owner holds title; the provisionbench gate passes; the ownership probes assert the positive state on this path too.
close_reason: implemented in def2e498: legacy provision-project now ensures stable NOLOGIN wamn_db_owner, converges fresh/existing database ownership before CONNECT, and proves replay; aggregate/unit/PG18 live/provisionbench/Clippy/fmt and five mutants green

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): narrow the CDC role's table read to the entity map
description:
## Why

grant_replication_access_sql granted the CDC replication role SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN
SCHEMA -- every tenant data table. Its stated justification was 'an initial-snapshot/backfill
needs table reads', and its own next clause contradicted it: 'logical decoding itself reads WAL,
not tables'.

The shipped reader performs no snapshot and no backfill. Its only SELECT against the project-env
database is the entity map (services/cdc-reader/src/lib.rs:317); StreamingMode::Off is the
pgoutput in-progress-transaction option, not a table snapshot.

WHY IT IS A CONFIDENTIALITY OVER-GRANT AND NOT TIDINESS: the replication path is gated by the
REPLICATION attribute, the walsender protocol and slot ownership. GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES gave
THE SAME CREDENTIAL a plain SQL read of all tenant data with none of those gates.

## Scope

Narrow to the entity map, with a RETROACTIVE REVOKE for already-provisioned
environments -- without it the fix reaches only new ones, which is the single most likely way this
lands incompletely. Ordering inside the bundle is already safe: the entity map is created before
the grants.

## Boundary

The table read only. Does NOT touch the REPLICATION attribute -- that is not a
grant, it is a role attribute, and removing it breaks logical decoding outright. The CDC blast
radius question is wamn-0h0g.12.68 and remains unruled.
acceptance_criteria: The CDC role holds SELECT on the entity map and on no tenant table; an already-provisioned environment is converged by re-running the bundle; decoding of a table the role cannot SELECT still yields frames; the pre-existing not-retro-granted assertion still passes.
close_reason: [47b404cf] grant_replication_access_sql granted the CDC role SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA -- every tenant data table -- justified as needing reads for an initial snapshot, while its own next clause said decoding reads WAL not tables. The shipped reader performs no snapshot: its only project-env table query is the entity map (cdc-reader/src/lib.rs:317), and StreamingMode::Off is the pgoutput in-progress-transaction option, not a snapshot. This was a CONFIDENTIALITY over-grant, not tidiness: the replication path is gated by the REPLICATION attribute, the walsender protocol and slot ownership, and this grant gave the SAME CREDENTIAL a plain SQL read of all tenant data with none of those gates. Narrowed to the entity map WITH A RETROACTIVE REVOKE -- without it the fix reaches only new environments, the single most likely way it would have landed incompletely. MUTATION-VERIFIED: dropping the retroactive REVOKE turns the new test red while the OLD one still passes (exactly the gap it was written to catch); swapping REVOKE/GRANT order turns both red; restored. Decoding of a table the role cannot SELECT still yields frames. NOINHERIT added for exactness (the only role in the repo defaulting to INHERIT); inert today since the role holds no memberships, and existing roles keep INHERIT because the IF NOT EXISTS guard is retained. The REPLICATION attribute is untouched -- it is an attribute, not a grant, and removing it breaks logical decoding outright. Blast radius stays wamn-0h0g.12.68, still unruled.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): close the template1 route out of the CONNECT floor
description:
## Why

revoke_public_connect_floor_sql looped WHERE NOT datistemplate, so template1 kept
PostgreSQL's default PUBLIC CONNECT. template1 has datallowconn = true, so wamn_app could log
into it on every cluster -- and from a template1 session ALTER or DROP every database it owns,
needing CONNECT on none of them. This is the route that made the database-ownership authority
trivially reachable.

## Scope

Replace the template filter with a connectability filter (datallowconn), which includes
template1 and correctly still excludes template0.

## Boundary

*** NOT every datistemplate site. non_template_databases_sql must KEEP the template filter: its
caller OPENS A CONNECTION to every name it returns, and an open template1 session breaks
concurrent CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE template1. That asymmetry is documented in place so a
future consistency edit does not cause an outage. ***
acceptance_criteria: PUBLIC holds no CONNECT on template1 after the floor runs; template0 is untouched; non_template_databases_sql still excludes templates and its reason is documented; no workload connects to template1 or postgres as a non-superuser.
close_reason: [47b404cf] The PUBLIC CONNECT floor looped WHERE NOT datistemplate, and template1 is datallowconn=true with PostgreSQL's default PUBLIC CONNECT -- so wamn_app could log into template1 on every cluster and from there ALTER or DROP every database it owned while holding CONNECT on none. That is what made the database-ownership authority trivially reachable. Filter is now datallowconn: includes template1, still excludes template0. *** NOT every datistemplate site moved, deliberately: non_template_databases_sql KEEPS the template filter because its caller OPENS A CONNECTION to every name it returns, and an open template1 session breaks concurrent CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE template1. The asymmetry is documented in place so a future consistency edit does not cause an outage. *** MUTATION-VERIFIED: filter set back to NOT datistemplate turns the template1 probe red; restored. Verified no workload connects to template1 or postgres as a non-superuser, and that CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE template1 needs no CONNECT (proved with a non-superuser CREATEDB role holding none). The m1 gate is unaffected -- the floor never runs there; its only callers are provision_project_env and the effect-writer live test, which passes green with the widened floor.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(deploy): move platform-tier inline credentials into Secrets
description:
## Why

deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml and deploy/platform/run-retention.example.yaml
each carried a literal postgres://wamn_app:wamn_app@... as a plain env value in a workload spec.
That violates the recorded R8b posture (deploy/platform/wamn-sysdb.yaml:8-11): the registry stores
Secret REFERENCES; actual material lives in K8s Secrets.

These are the only two inline production-shaped credentials in the platform tier. The remaining
occurrences are inside a Secret's stringData (which is the correct home) or outside this tier.

## Scope

secretKeyRef in both workload specs, with a companion example Secret per consumer as a
SEPARATE manifest -- the tier's established convention (runner-db, dispatcher-projects,
runner-credentials all carry the same 'DELIBERATELY a separate manifest' rationale), so that
re-applying Helm values never clobbers a customised Secret back to a demo value.

MEASURED CORRECTION worth preserving: the two URLs are NOT interchangeable. runner-db's ends
?sslmode=disable and the host tier's did not; reusing that Secret would have silently changed the
host tier's connection parameters -- a behaviour change smuggled into a credential-hygiene fix.
Retention likewise targets poc-f1 while runner-db is the demo project-env.

## Boundary

Credential CARRIAGE only. No authority, role, or grant changes.
acceptance_criteria: Neither values-host-default.yaml nor run-retention.example.yaml contains an inline credential; both reference a Secret defined in the tier; every referenced Secret name and key exists; all manifests parse; the operator ordering obligation (Secret before workload) is recorded in-file.
close_reason: [fd6723ba] values-host-default.yaml and run-retention.example.yaml carried literal postgres://wamn_app:wamn_app@... in workload specs, against R8b. PREMISE CORRECTION THAT CHANGED THE DESIGN: the two URLs are NOT interchangeable -- runner-db's ends ?sslmode=disable and the host tier's did not, so reusing that Secret would have silently altered the host's connection parameters. Retention targets poc-f1 while runner-db is the demo project-env. Each consumer got its own Secret carrying its URL byte-for-byte. Chart passthrough verified at the pinned fork rev daba602 (toYaml verbatim), not assumed. OPERATOR ORDERING, both hard blocks: Secret before workload; the CronJob sets backoffLimit 0 so a tick that cannot start is LOST, not retried. The two directory-walking conformance tests were checked against their filter predicates (Role/ClusterRole and WorkloadDeployment) -- neither new file is enumerated. All 7 manifests parse; every secretKeyRef has exactly name+key; no value survives beside a valueFrom.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(deploy): scenario-worker manifest cannot start as checked in
description:
## Why

services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs ManagementServeArgs declares two REQUIRED
clap arguments that deploy/platform/scenario-worker.yaml supplies in neither form:

1. control_authoring_database_url, a bare String with no default, reads env
   WAMN_CONTROL_AUTHORING_PG_URL. The manifest set WAMN_AUTHORING_PG_URL -- the PRE-8.18 name,
   which management.rs's own test module puts on a DENYLIST (asserts the implementation does not
   contain it, and that exactly one _PG_URL arg exists). The code can never re-accept it.
2. environment, a bare String with no default, reads WAMN_MANAGEMENT_ENVIRONMENT. Supplied by
   neither flag nor env.

Two required args missing means Cli::parse() exits non-zero before main does any work ->
CrashLoopBackOff. services/scenario-worker/src/main.rs directly tests this: it iterates the
required flags and asserts try_parse_from ERRORS when any one is omitted.

Provenance: a stale artifact of wamn-0h0g.8.18 (4bee577a), whose own commit body says
'ManagementServeArgs had no --environment, so one-instance-one-scope was unenforceable as
configured' -- and which touched control-portable-store.sql but NOT this manifest.

## Boundary

The manifest only. No Rust change; the code is correct and guarded by its own tests.
acceptance_criteria: deploy/platform/scenario-worker.yaml supplies every required ManagementServeArgs argument; the env var name matches what the binary reads; the manifest parses; no denylisted pre-8.18 name remains.
close_reason: [f9505bad] Manifest could not start: ManagementServeArgs declares control_authoring_database_url and environment as bare String with no default, so clap refuses before main runs. The manifest set WAMN_AUTHORING_PG_URL, the pre-8.18 name that management.rs's own test module DENYLISTS, and supplied --environment in neither form. main.rs already tests the failure directly. Stale artifact of 4bee577a, which touched control-portable-store.sql but not this manifest. --environment passed as a flag per the file's convention; value dev corroborated by the wamn.env label, the Secret name, and runner.yaml. Stale header block rewritten from control_author.rs parse_control_authoring_url. VERIFIED: independently re-read management.rs field-by-field (no Option, no default_value on either); manifest parses (2 docs).

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): refuse the replica-identity reconcile when registrations are unreadable
description:
## Why -- a LATENT FAIL-OPEN that exists today, independent of any authority change

services/ctl/src/reconcile_replica_identity.rs:170-184 returns Ok(Vec::new()) when
catalog.event_registrations is merely ABSENT. The planner
(crates/schema/control/src/replica_identity.rs:127-169) cannot distinguish an empty
registration set from 'no entity needs FULL', so it computes desired = DEFAULT for EVERY entity
and emits a flip for every table currently at FULL.

*** The flip is NON-RETROACTIVE (reconcile_replica_identity.rs:19-22). So every row event
captured before the next repair PERMANENTLY lacks its old image -- and the CronJob presents as
a clean, successful, idempotent-looking run. That is the exact correctness class the whole
replica-identity subsystem exists to protect, failing open in a design that is fail-closed
everywhere else (the materializer refuses old-image-absent rather than evaluating condition-false). ***

Trigger: a project-env whose catalog schema was dropped and partially rebuilt.

Found by the wamn-0h0g.12.70 adjudication, 2026-08-17. Deliberately filed SEPARATELY from the
authority question: this is a correctness fix and lands whichever way the superuser posture is
ruled.

## Scope

Replace the empty-set early return with a hard refusal. A project-env that is not yet
registration-provisioned must either provision or refuse explicitly -- never silently reset.

## Boundary

The unreadable-registrations path only. Does not touch the reconciler's credential, the CronJob
manifest, or the ALTER authority -- those are wamn-0h0g.12.70.
acceptance_criteria: A reconcile run against a database whose catalog.event_registrations is absent or unreadable refuses by name instead of planning resets to DEFAULT; a live test proves the refusal and proves that a correctly-provisioned environment still reconciles; no REPLICA IDENTITY FULL table is flipped as a side effect of an unreadable registration set.
close_reason: [e96bb401] The reconciler returned Ok(Vec::new()) when catalog.event_registrations was merely ABSENT; the pure planner cannot distinguish that from "no entity needs FULL", so it planned a reset to DEFAULT for every table at FULL -- a NON-RETROACTIVE flip presenting as a clean idempotent run. Now refuses by name: replica-identity-registrations-absent / -unreadable, in the crate's existing PublicationError shape. *** THE SILENT THIRD STATE WAS THE DANGEROUS ONE and it could NOT be deferred: the table is FORCE RLS, so a non-bypassing session reads zero rows with NO error, and the module's own doc advertised "a superuser (OR THE SCHEMA OWNER)" as supported -- FORCE strips the owner's exemption and PostgreSQL checks BYPASSRLS on the current role only, so the documented-supported credential WAS the silent full reset. The cross-tenant read now runs under row_security = off (the pg_dump idiom) so PostgreSQL raises 42501 instead of filtering; inert for asuperuser. *** PREMISE CORRECTION: never a CronJob-only exposure -- publish_catalog's call site is dead under .8.18's unconditional bail, but migrate_catalog.rs:178 is live and unclosed, and ri_orch_live is consequently red on baseline and no longer covers reconcile_after_apply. New gate replica_identity_unreadable_live proves absent + RLS-hidden refuse on dry-run AND apply with 'f' intact, demonstrates the silence directly, and proves a genuinely-empty provisioned env still reconciles including the legitimate reset direction, idempotently, inside a caller's open transaction with no GUC leak. Precision pair re-derived AT INTEGRATION: restoring the early return turns the refusal test RED (printing ReplicaIdentityFlip orders/sales_orders Full->Default) and leaves the positive test GREEN; restored byte-identical by sha256 and re-verified. THREE SIBLINGS FILED, one MORE severe than this bead: .12.119 (guard_registration_orphans repeats the collapse on a DESTRUCTIVE apply, live via migrate-catalog), .12.120 (impact-report understates blast radius), .11.26 (replica_identity_live cannot pass on its own documented recipe). Nothing left stale for .15.22.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(publish): let the service tier admit a grown release, as the database now does
description:
## Why

Under the grow-only release membership ratified by owner rulings R1/R5 (wamn-0h0g.15.159), a
tested publish APPENDS a member to the applied catalog version. The database now permits that --
proven live on PostgreSQL 18.6 during .15.159: seal a one-member release, append a second member
in a LATER transaction, COMMITS. But the SERVICE tier still refuses it.

*** CORRECTED SCOPE 2026-08-17 (found while implementing .15.159). This bead originally named
publish_catalog.rs:1157's stored_members == members.len() as the defect. That line is NOT the
sharpest edge and fixing it alone would be misleading. ***

THE REAL BLOCKER IS THE PREFLIGHT. publish_catalog.rs:884 (and copy_project_env.rs:784) compare
the requested member set against the stored one with EXACT serde_json::Value equality and raise
catalog-release-content-conflict. Republishing a release that has grown by one member is refused
THERE, before :1157 is ever reached. :1157 only misfires when the request is a strict subset of
what is stored -- which the preflight already rejects first -- so it is a redundant restatement,
not the cause.

Both are the same abolished invariant ('two representations must agree exactly') restated in
Rust after it was removed from the database. wamn-0h0g.15.159 preserved them verbatim on purpose:
ruling R1's rider required the consumers keep their refusal literals, and changing the append
policy is a different decision from dropping the column.

## Scope

Adjudicate and implement the service-tier append policy: what a republish of a grown release
should do. Both preflights (publish_catalog.rs:869-895, copy_project_env.rs:761-802) and the two
count checks (publish_catalog.rs:1147-1158, copy_project_env.rs:978-990) move together.
catalog-release-content-conflict must still fire on a genuinely conflicting member -- a different
flow_version or bundle hash for a flow_id already in the release.

## Boundary

Service-tier append policy only. The database side is settled and landed. Does not touch the
per-member readback assertions, which are the enforcement of record for content conflict per R5.
acceptance_criteria: A republish of a catalog version whose membership grew through a tested publish is admitted rather than refused, at BOTH the preflight and the count check, in publish-catalog and copy-project-env alike; catalog-release-content-conflict still fires on a genuinely conflicting member; a named test pins the grown-release case end to end against a live PostgreSQL.
close_reason: [29bae414] Both preflights now refuse only what an append cannot explain -- a flow id both sides carry at a different flow-version or artifact hash; a member only one side carries is the permitted append, either direction. catalog-release-content-conflict still fires on a genuine conflict. *** THE COUNT CHECK WAS DELETED, NOT WEAKENED, and that is a larger claim than the bead made: under grow-only it is a TAUTOLOGY, because the per-member readback above it already asserts every requested member landed at its exact (flow_id, flow_version, bundle hash) -- the R5 enforcement of record -- so stored >= requested can never fail. The only thing the old equality added was "and nothing else is stored", the abolished invariant. *** PREMISE CORRECTION THAT COSTS THIS BEAD ITS CLAIM TO BE A LIVE FIX: BOTH sites are unreachable today. plan_copy emits CopyStep::CopyDefinition for CopyInclude::Definition ALONE (the sibling arm sends Data|Both to snapshot+restore), and copy_project_env.rs:199 refuses Definition|Both before any I/O -- so the one include mode that produces the step is one of the two that never runs. Nothing was unblocked; what was fixed is the logic .15.14's successor inherits. Second correction: neutering the preflight does NOT let a changed member through -- the database still catches it, but with flow-version-content-conflict, a DIFFERENT literal, so the preflight is what preserves the contracted refusal. 58 passed / 0 failed serially against a fresh database at integration.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(auth): adjudicate all 29 wamn_app confinements now; revokes land immediately, benign deltas ride .15.22
description:
## The ruling (owner, 2026-08-17)

The question raised at the wave-10 close was whether the 29 `remediate(auth)`
beads (wamn-0h0g.12.20-.12.37, .12.63-.12.70, all P1) land BEFORE
wamn-0h0g.15.22 -- one big registry regeneration, consistent with the churn
doctrine that put .15.20 before it -- or AFTER, accepting a second, smaller
regeneration.

*** THE OWNER RULED THAT THIS IS A FALSE CHOICE AND TOOK THE SPLIT. ***

1. ADJUDICATE ALL 29 NOW. They are PURE DECISIONS -- "adjudicate the intended
   lifecycle boundary for this one relation and role" -- unblocked, requiring no
   file writes. They are P1 SECURITY questions about guest-reachable mutation
   authority through the cluster-global wamn_app LOGIN: "the exact class the
   shared-wamn_app arc taught us not to sit on."

2. TRIAGE THE OUTCOMES INTO TWO LANES.

   a. ANY ADJUDICATION FINDING A REAL OVER-GRANT LANDS ITS `REVOKE` IMMEDIATELY,
      as a found-defect fix under the floor rule ratified for L4/L5. *** A
      SECURITY FIX NEVER QUEUES BEHIND A REGISTRY REGENERATION. *** A grant delta
      is a one-line DDL, and its inventory row can note "regeneration pending
      wamn-0h0g.15.22" without lying.

   b. BENIGN DELTAS -- confirmations, boundary notes, no-grant-change
      adjudications -- BANK and ride .15.22's single regeneration, per the
      doctrine.

## The reasoning to preserve

"Before" never meant blocking .15.22 on deliberation, and "after" never had to
mean delaying a revoke. THE ONLY THING THAT WAITS IS PAPERWORK; THE ONLY THING
THAT DOES NOT IS AUTHORITY.

## Consequences for execution

- The adjudications do not touch architecture/protected-writes.json, so they do
  not violate the freeze and do not need to wait for .15.22.
- A REVOKE that lands early makes the frozen inventory temporarily describe a
  wider authority than the database grants. That is ACCEPTABLE and must be noted
  on the row rather than hidden; .15.22 reconciles it.
- Do not batch a revoke behind another revoke. Each is its own found-defect fix.

## Boundary

This decision governs sequencing only. It does not pre-judge any of the 29
adjudications, and it does not authorize widening any grant -- only confining
one.
acceptance_criteria: All 29 remediate(auth) beads are adjudicated. Every adjudication finding a real over-grant has landed its REVOKE as an independent found-defect fix without waiting for a registry regeneration. Benign deltas are banked on wamn-0h0g.15.22. No adjudication was deferred for freeze reasons.
notes:

Same class exactly — an authority delta that arrived as an upgrade side-effect rather than a grant decision — so it takes the same split: adjudicate now as a pure decision, land a revoke immediately if it is a real over-grant, ride .15.22 if benign. SEQUENCING CONFIRMED AND NOW ENFORCED BY A DEPENDENCY EDGE: this bead's 30 adjudications run BEFORE wamn-0h0g.15.22's regeneration pass. Running the regeneration first would mint the second regeneration this ruling exists to forbid.
FACT CORRECTION (integrator, 2026-08-18, EXE wave 2 — recorded immediately per the standing rule that

  .12.20 .12.21 .12.22 .12.23 .12.24 .12.25 .12.26 .12.27 .12.28 .12.29
  .12.30 .12.31 .12.32 .12.33 .12.34 .12.35 .12.36 .12.37   -- ALL EIGHTEEN CLOSED (wave 12)

With wamn-0h0g.15.135 pulled in as #30, the REMAINING adjudication set is EIGHT, not thirty.

THE NINETEEN ARE GENUINELY ADJUDICATED, NOT MERELY CLOSED — spot-checked .12.20 and .12.37, both of
which carry reasoned lifecycle verdicts with live evidence, premise corrections and re-derived
mutants in their close reasons (.12.20: ten catalog relations confined, six with no reader and no

verification sweep confirming each of the nineteen closed ones carries an adjudication rather than

THE DEPENDENCY EDGE TO wamn-0h0g.15.22 IS UNAFFECTED — the regeneration still runs after the

This bead stays OPEN pending owner ratification of those eight.

*** NO REVOKE LANDED, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME UNDER THIS BEAD'S OWN RULING — NOT A LANE
FAILURE. *** Every over-grant found is one where NO GRANT EXISTS TO CONFINE: the remedy is minting a

=====================================================================

*** NOT-ADJUDICATED: NONE. *** Structurally, 17 of 19 share a batch close reason (ten catalog beads

STRENGTHS WORTH PRESERVING: .12.29 (catalog.event_registrations) records the bare-REVOKE-UPDATE
production outage as a REPRODUCED result and narrows to UPDATE(tenant_id); .12.34
(app_system.configurations) is the set's one deliberate BENIGN, kept as an over-revocation tripwire;
.12.66 carries two premise corrections, one of which inverts its own design.

SEPARATE DEFECT FOUND AND RECORDED ON ITS OWN BEAD: .12.37's close reason cites commit [7c2f5b2b],
which is NOT A VALID OBJECT in this repository. The real commit is 78afe665. The other three cited
hashes resolve correctly.

POST-CLOSE CORRECTION (integrator, 2026-08-18, same day). THE CLOSE REASON ABOVE OVERSTATES THE
UNIFORMITY OF THE EIGHT, AND THE RECORD SHOULD NOT CARRY THAT.

CONSTRUCTION, not revocation", and a blanket re-homing note saying so was applied to all eight. That
is TRUE OF FOUR OF THEM. Verified verdict by verdict afterwards, the eight are THREE classes:

  CONSTRUCTION — the close reason is accurate for these four:
    .12.64  REAL OVER-GRANT, but with NO land-now surface
    .12.65  CONSTRUCTION HALF ONLY
    .12.67  REAL OVER-GRANT, AND A LIVE AUTHENTICATION-FORGERY PRIMITIVE — no revoke to land
    .12.69  REAL OVER-GRANT, CONSTRUCTION ONLY — NO REVOKE EXISTS TO LAND

  BENIGN, RIDES .15.22 — no build to do at all; these CLOSE WHEN .15.22 LANDS:
    .12.68  ACCEPT the REPLICATION attribute scoped to T3. BENIGN, no grant change.
    .15.135 BENIGN — option (a), accept upstream's posture.

  *** STILL AN OPEN OWNER RISK DECISION — RATIFYING THIS BEAD DID NOT SETTLE THESE TWO: ***
    .12.63  OWNER RISK DECISION, and the bead is additionally a DUPLICATE of wamn-1nd (deferred),
            so a deferred bead transitively gates an open one — flagged at wave 12, still true.
    .12.70  OWNER RISK DECISION — the AUTHORITY half is open, urgency assessed LOW.

*** THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: ratifying that the adjudication PASS is complete is not the same
as ratifying each bead's DISPOSITION. *** The pass did its job on .12.63 and .12.70 precisely by
determining they cannot be settled by analysis and need an explicit risk call. Reading this bead's
close as having settled them would silently adopt a risk position nobody took. Corrective notes are

NOTE ALSO, on the 26-vs-29 correction in the close: .15.135's own ruling note records it as being
"PULLED INTO THE wamn-0h0g.15.161 ADJUDICATION SET AS #30", which implies the intended base was 29
rather than the 26 the two named ranges actually contain. So "29" was an intent, not purely a typo —
the ranges under-name the set the owner had in mind. The verified, enumerable set is 26 plus .15.135.

SECURITY ITEM WORTH NOT LOSING IN THE PAPERWORK: .12.67's verdict names A LIVE
AUTHENTICATION-FORGERY PRIMITIVE. It is construction-blocked rather than revocable, which is exactly
the situation where a finding can go quiet. It should not.
close_reason:
*** OWNER RATIFICATION (dkk, 2026-08-18): THE ADJUDICATION PASS IS COMPLETE UNDER THIS BEAD'S OWN STANDING RULING. *** This bead's product was DECISIONS, and they exist. Closing it releases wamn-0h0g.15.22, its only remaining open dependency.

COUNT CORRECTION, RECORDED SO THE NUMBER STOPS PROPAGATING: *** THE SET IS 26, NOT 29. *** This bead's own description says 29 and names two ranges — wamn-0h0g.12.20-.12.37 and .12.63-.12.70 — which contain 18 and 8 respectively, plus wamn-0h0g.15.135. The 29 is a text error in this bead, carried forward into the wave-2 and wave-3 reports before it was checked bead-by-bead. THE DELIVERABLE: all 26 carry recorded verdicts. The 18 revocable ones were adjudicated, remediated and closed. The 8 that remain open are open CORRECTLY, and this is the substantive point rather than an exception to it: THEIR VERDICTS CALL FOR CONSTRUCTION, NOT REVOCATION — scoped roles, generation extensions, provisioning that does not yet exist. R4's fast lane existed for REVOKES precisely because a REVOKE is instant and a construction is not. 'Authority moves now, paperwork waits' never meant 'build now.' NO REVOKE LANDED AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME, NOT AN OMISSION: every over-grant found was one where no grant exists to confine yet, so the remedy is to build the narrower thing.

RE-HOMING, PART OF THIS RULING: the 8 stop being 'the auth adjudication' and become ORDINARY CONSTRUCTION BEADS UNDER THEIR EPICS (.12 and .15), each carrying its recorded verdict AS ITS SPEC. They are named build work now, not open questions. A note to that effect is appended to each.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(admission): evaluate the identity arms before the drift arms
description:
## Why -- OWNER RULING 2026-08-17

wamn-0h0g.8.20 shipped the callable statement's arm ordering: drift arms first
(head-not-found :85, head-drift :86, definition-drift :87, missing-root-plan :88),
identity arms last (conflicting-run-identity :89/:101, duplicate :102).

Consequence: management admits a draft run at catalog v7; a publish moves the head
to v8; the producer crashes and retries with its original v7 parameters. It hits
head-drift and NEVER REACHES duplicate -- even though the run exists and the retry
is byte-identical.

*** THE RULING'S REASON IS THE RATIFIED RETRY CONTRACT, NOT THE BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE
LINE. wamn-0h0g.7.1 made durable outcome replay UNCONDITIONAL: same producer
identity -> same run -> same stored outcome, NO expiry carve-out, NO environmental
carve-out. A publish moving the head is precisely an environmental change, and the
current order silently converts an exact retry from "returns the run" into a typed
drift refusal -- a carve-out that was already deleted once. ***

THE SEMANTIC ARGUMENT, worth keeping verbatim: the drift arms exist to stop NEW
work being admitted against a stale view. An exact retry admits nothing new -- by
definition the run already exists. So identity-first is the honest order: FIRST
"is this the same command?" (return it), THEN "is this new work coherent with the
world?" (drift-check it).

The symmetry with the callable statement that the original ordering preserved is
AESTHETIC CONSISTENCY BETWEEN STATEMENTS WITH DIFFERENT JOBS -- the callable path
has no producer-idempotency contract to honor.

## Scope

Reorder the management classifier so the identity arms precede the drift arms.

RIDER 1: the divergence gets a comment AT BOTH SITES naming why the orders differ,
because someone will otherwise "fix" the asymmetry.

RIDER 2: lane 2's recovery-by-producer-key path stays PRIMARY. This change makes
the retry fallback truthful rather than load-bearing; do not re-architect recovery
around it.

## Boundary

Management statement only. The callable statement's ordering is unchanged and must
stay unchanged -- it has no producer-idempotency contract. Filed from the
wamn-0h0g.8.20 close.
acceptance_criteria: An exact management retry returns duplicate with the existing run id even when a catalog publish has moved the head since admission; the callable statement's ordering is unchanged; and both statements carry a comment explaining why their orders differ.
close_reason: [bac4e99b] Management classifier now evaluates identity before drift per owner ruling R2. THE REORDER ALONE DOES NOT SATISFY THE ACCEPTANCE -- it retypes the refusal: the identity divergence arm's xr.execution_bundle_hash IS DISTINCT FROM plan.execution_bundle_hash operand derives plan from the LIVE head, and the four drift arms were what made it reachable only with head found and equal to expected. Moving identity first exposes IS DISTINCT FROM NULL -> TRUE, so a byte-identical retry refuses conflicting-run-identity and never reaches duplicate. The operand is gated on exactly the old reachability condition; byte-identical wherever it previously ran. PREMISE CORRECTIONS to the ruling's cited authority (conclusion survives, citation does not): wamn-0h0g.7.1 is the CALLABLE contract (flow-invocation 0.2, client idempotency key; the deleted expiry carve-out was invocation_admissions.expires_at, a callable-side column) and says nothing about draft:/case: coordinates; and 'the callable path has no producer-idempotency contract' is false -- it has existing_http, idempotency-key-reused, idempotency-scope-changed and the evt: key space. The real asymmetry, which is what the two comments state: an exact callable retry never reaches admit_sql, because flow_invocation.rs runs recover() -> lookup_invocation_recovery_sql() before admission is composed and that lookup carries no head or drift operand. The management statement has no such pre-read, so its classifier IS the replay path. FURTHER FINDING: there is no management recovery lookup and NO PRODUCTION CALLER of the management admission statement anywhere in the tree -- rider 3's 'recovery-by-producer-key stays primary' names a path that does not exist, so today the SQL fallback is the only mechanism. Blast radius of this change is currently the live gate only. Filed as follow-up. Riders honoured: comment at both sites forbidding the symmetry fix; callable order pinned unchanged by callable_admission_is_unchanged_by_management_admission; no identity arm reaches ready, so the order can only turn a refusal into the stored answer. Live coverage rides inside admission_live() because the gate invokes it --exact and the DROP SCHEMA CASCADE fixture lives in that function. VERIFIED: cargo check -p wamn-run-state --all-targets clean; 24 admission unit tests pass. NOT verified: admission_live needs PostgreSQL; no per-commit gates on this branch by owner ruling; rides the .15.25 RC. FOR .15.22: admission-execution-pin.sh:35 and http-ordinary-admission.sh:36 were ALREADY stale at c7cb73b3 (expect 0defa0c2, actual pre-edit e1e9dc29b20bfcbc966568d73fce333532d80cc1357df39a38a796a57bda9446); both NEEDLEs target the untouched callable statement so both survive regeneration. admission.rs must be on the list.

title: [SR-MVP] test(deploy): prove the two-release split and CrossEnvironmentSchedulingDenied on a fresh namespace
description:
## Why

Everything wamn-0h0g.15.15 landed is STATIC TEXT AGREEMENT -- nine conformance
assertions that two values files and two workload manifests name consistent
namespaces, environments and chart versions. None of it proves convergence,
because the live kind cluster is frozen and the bead's own acceptance is
fresh-namespace-only.

## Scope

At the RC, prove on a fresh namespace: the pinned chart's host groups run our
wamn-host images in that namespace; the flow-http and materializer
WorkloadDeployments schedule onto them; HTTP reaches flow-http through the
operator-managed EndpointSlices; and a workload naming a host in another
environment is REFUSED with CrossEnvironmentSchedulingDenied (flip one
`environment:` string to produce it).

Also prove the ordered install: operator release first, host release second.

## Boundary

Rides wamn-0h0g.15.25, the single RC validation. Not runnable before it -- the
live cluster is frozen by owner ruling. Filed by lane 3 of wave 10.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh namespace converges from the two pinned releases, workloads schedule onto the chart's host groups, HTTP reaches flow-http via operator-managed EndpointSlices, and a cross-environment workload is refused with CrossEnvironmentSchedulingDenied.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): distribute the chart CA and host client certs into environment namespaces
description:
## Why -- and this CORRECTS A LANDED OWNER RULING

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.50 says the host tier is ONE HELM RELEASE PER ENVIRONMENT,
and that "MVP's single environment makes it moot today, which is why the
principled shape is taken now while it is free."

*** IT IS NOT FREE. Measured at chart daba602 by lane 3 of wave 10 and
independently verified: a host release in a NAMESPACE OF ITS OWN does not
converge, on either of the two available settings. ***

(1) With the chart defaults (global.tls.enabled: true,
    global.certificates.generate: true), templates/certificates.yaml does
    `lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace .Values.global.certificates.caSecretName`
    -- release-namespace-scoped, with no cross-namespace CA reuse. A second
    release finds no CA and MINTS A FRESH ONE. The host then presents a client
    cert the operator's NATS does not trust, and never registers.

(2) With global.certificates.generate: false instead, nothing renders
    wasmcloud-runtime-tls / wasmcloud-data-tls into that namespace, and
    templates/runtime/deployment.yaml:83-89 mounts both BY NAME
    (`secretName: {{ ... runtimeCertSecretName }}`), which resolves in the POD's
    namespace. The Pod never starts.

Either path needs the CA plus two client-cert Secrets present in every
environment namespace, and nothing distributes them.

## What wave 10 did instead

wamn-0h0g.15.15 took the split SHAPE but set the MVP environment's namespace
equal to the operator's release namespace (wamn-system) -- the one configuration
in which .13.50 genuinely is free, because the operator release already renders
those Secrets there. The host release sets global.certificates.generate: false
(the operator release owns the Secrets; re-rendering collides on Helm ownership)
while keeping global.tls.enabled at its default true, so mTLS on both NATS
connections is retained.

*** SO ENVIRONMENT #2 IS BLOCKED ON THIS BEAD, NOT ON THE VALUES FILES. ***

## Scope

Distribute the chart CA and the two host client-cert Secrets into each
environment namespace, so a host-tier release can live in a namespace of its own.

## Boundary

Does not re-litigate .13.50's shape -- the split is taken. This supplies the
precondition the ruling assumed. Note also the ordered migration an existing
cluster needs: hostgroup-default's Deployment/Service/NetworkPolicy are named
after the host GROUP, not the release, so the operator release must be upgraded
first (its `hostGroups: []` deletes them) before the host release is installed,
or Helm refuses on ownership metadata. A fresh namespace has nothing to collide
with, which is the RC's proof shape.
acceptance_criteria: A host-tier Helm release converges in a namespace other than the operator's, with the CA and both client-cert Secrets present, and the host registers over mTLS against the operator's NATS.
close_reason: LANDED in wave 57 on deploy-simplification; see the commit carrying this bead id. Full lane evidence recorded at integration.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(host): an opted-in guest runs under EgressMode::Count so its allowed_hosts is advisory
description:
## Why

Traced and verified at fork daba602, 2026-08-17.

1. EgressMode::Count is upstream's `#[default]` (sockets/policy.rs:79-80). It
   "evaluate[s] the policy, log[s] and count[s] what it would refuse, allow[s] it
   anyway."
2. SocketPolicy::default() sets `egress_mode: EgressMode::Count` and
   `host_loopback_enabled: false`.
3. wamn installs NO host socket policy at all (zero call sites), so the engine
   takes SocketPolicy::default() -- i.e. wamn's host-wide mode is Count.
4. shape_socket_policy (engine/linked_call.rs:274-286) forces
   `egress_mode: Enforce` ONLY on the no-opt-in branch. With
   `wamn.allow-raw-sockets` it returns the policy UNSHAPED, and the fork's own
   doc says "the host-configured mode, allowlist, and connection quota apply as
   upstream ships them."

*** THEREFORE: for a guest that opts in to raw sockets, its allowed_hosts
allowlist is evaluated, logged and counted -- and violations are ALLOWED. The
allowlist is advisory for exactly the guests that were granted the most reach. ***

## Why it is not a live breach today

Owner ruling wamn-0h0g.13.47 states as a RULE that flow guests never perform raw
wasi:http egress, and wamn-0h0g.15.35 is the reachability guard of record. No
production guest opts in. The defect is that the posture depends entirely on
nothing ever opting in, rather than on the mode being right.

## Scope

Decide the host-wide default deliberately and record it. The likely answer is an
Enforce host default so the opt-in widens the ALLOWLIST without also silently
disabling enforcement, but that is a posture ruling, not a refactor -- upstream
chose Count so upgrading a host does not sever live traffic, and that rationale
has to be answered rather than ignored.

## Boundary

Depends on the sibling bead that makes a host socket policy installable at all.
Does not change shape_socket_policy's opt-out branch, which is correct and is
pinned by wamn-0h0g.15.20's named test. Filed by lane 5 of wave 10.
acceptance_criteria: The host-wide EgressMode is chosen deliberately and recorded, and an opted-in guest's allowed_hosts is either enforced or documented as advisory with the reason. A named test pins whichever is chosen.
notes:
DECISION TO BE MADE BEFORE THIS CAN BE LANED (measured 2026-08-23, wave-55 prep).
*** EgressMode LIVES IN THE wash-runtime FORK, NOT IN THIS TREE. *** The only in-tree occurrences are pinned FORK SOURCE TEXT inside tests/conformance/src/ip_name_lookup.rs at :139 and :151. So the repair locus is ambiguous and the answer changes the cost by an order of magnitude:
(a) IN-TREE: if the host chooses the mode, never opt a guest into Count and the advisory-allowed_hosts hole closes with a local change plus a guard. Cheap, no fork involvement.
(b) FORK: if Count is selected inside wash-runtime for opted-in guests, the fix needs a fork commit - which drags in wamn-9inf, because *** THE FORK REV IS PINNED IN ABOUT 8 PLACES AND CARGO CANNOT RESOLVE AN UNPUSHED REV: bumping before publishing makes the WHOLE WORKSPACE UNRESOLVABLE, not merely red. *** That makes this bead blocked behind a publish decision, not merely large.
MEASURE FIRST, THEN RULE. Read the fork at the pinned rev in the cargo git checkout; do NOT bump it to investigate. This is a SECURITY defect - an opted-in guest whose allowed_hosts is advisory has no egress confinement - so it should not sit unmeasured.
MEASURED 2026-08-23 (wave-55, fork read at the pinned rev). REPAIR LOCUS RESOLVED: OPTION (a), IN-TREE. NOT BLOCKED BEHIND wamn-9inf.

*** THE HOST CHOOSES THE MODE. *** The fork exposes a public builder method taking a host-supplied socket policy, and carries egress_mode through to the guest unmodified - the per-guest derivation copies it, and the shaping function only ever overrides it DOWNWARD on the opt-out branch; with the opt-in it returns the host's policy verbatim. The mode enum is public.
So the Count comes from WAMN, not from wash-runtime: crates/platform/runtime/src/engine.rs constructs SocketPolicy::default at two sites, and that default carries EgressMode::Count. The escape hatch added by .15.141 (a build entry point taking an explicit policy) HAS ZERO NON-TEST CALLERS - both serving deployables go through the sized builder, which hardcodes the default.
IN-TREE OCCURRENCE CLAIM VERIFIED with one addition: EgressMode appears in-tree only as pinned fork source text in the conformance ip-name-lookup guard, as the bead says - but SocketPolicy itself IS used in production code in engine.rs, which the bead's note does not mention.

EXPOSURE, PRECISELY. Both real-egress refusals route through one gate function; under Count it logs at debug and returns Ok. So an opted-in guest can raw TCP or UDP connect to ANY ROUTABLE ADDRESS - the cluster service network, a sibling pod, Postgres directly (bypassing the credential-hiding wamn:postgres interface), cloud metadata endpoints - with both its declared allowed_hosts and the address-range policy reduced to debug log lines. Only the per-guest connection quota still bites.
THREE BOUNDS, recorded as scope rather than comfort: the host-loopback surface is UNAFFECTED (it errors directly, never through the gate); the EXECUTOR PATH NEVER CONSULTS THIS POLICY AT ALL (it links upstream wasi sockets whose default check is a hard deny), so the defect is scoped to the wamn-host/washlet path and the component-plugin tier; and NOTHING OPTS IN TODAY - the raw-sockets flag appears in no deploy manifest, only in a gate fixture and docs. The exposure is LATENT, not live.

PRICE: roughly a 15-line diff in engine.rs plus a named unit test in its existing test module. NO call-site edits, NO fork commit, NO PIN TOUCH. *** Do NOT thread the policy through the sized builder's signature - that variant would edit services/executor/src/lib.rs, which is contended, and buys nothing since the default inside engine.rs already covers both deployables. ***

*** ONE QUESTION RESERVED FOR THE OWNER, NOT DELEGATED TO THE LANE: the address policy ALSO defaults to permissive, so under Enforce the declared allowed_hosts becomes the SOLE confinement. Whether that is the intended posture, or whether the address-range policy should also tighten, is a security-posture ruling. The lane implements Enforce only. ***

DISPATCHED as wave-55 lane w55-engine, paired with wamn-t883 because both write engine.rs.
close_reason:
CLOSED at 76620ceb, pushed to origin/deploy-simplification. Lane w55-engine, second commit. INDEPENDENTLY re-verified in the main tree.

REPAIR LOCUS WAS THE OWNER'S DECISION AND THE ANSWER WAS (a), IN-TREE. The host chooses the mode: the fork exposes a public builder taking a host-supplied socket policy and carries egress_mode through to the guest unmodified, and SocketPolicy::default() carries EgressMode::Count. Under Count, the gate function records a meter, logs at debug, and returns Ok - so an opted-in guest's declared allowed_hosts AND the address-range policy were both reduced to log lines, and it could raw TCP or UDP connect to any routable address. Now the host constructs its policy with Enforce.
*** NO FORK COMMIT, NO PIN TOUCHED. The rev is pinned in 17 sites across 11 files and cargo cannot resolve an unpushed rev; this bead never went near it. It was ALSO NOT blocked behind wamn-9inf, contrary to the original framing. ***

SCOPE, MEASURED AT THE PINNED REV AND NARROWER THAN THE BEAD IMPLIED - all four confirmed by the lane reading the fork:
- *** wasi:http IS UNAFFECTED. Outgoing HTTP is gated by check_allowed_hosts in the fork's http host, NOT by SocketPolicy or EgressMode. Enforce touches ONLY the raw-socket path. ***
- *** THE EXECUTOR WAS NEVER AFFECTED. RouterDriver links upstream wasmtime_wasi p2, whose SocketAddrCheck default is a hard deny. The fork's SocketPolicy never governed that path. The defect was scoped to wamn-host/washlet. ***
- The host-loopback surface is unaffected; it refuses directly rather than through the gate.
- NOTHING OPTS IN: wamn.allow-raw-sockets appears in no deploy/ manifest, only a conformance test, a fixture and archived docs. THE EXPOSURE WAS LATENT, NOT LIVE.

PROOF. Mutant: host_socket_policy returns Count - KILLED by the_host_socket_policy_enforces_egress_rather_than_counting_it. Integrator re-verified all eight file sha256 byte-for-byte, runtime lib 156 / host bins 5 / executor lib 6 green, workspace check ZERO errors.

*** A SURVIVING MUTANT, FILED AS wamn-qk15 (P2) AND NAMED HERE RATHER THAN BURIED: reverting build_engine_sized to SocketPolicy::default() restores Count - this bead's exact defect - and every test still passes. The fork's Engine::socket_policy is pub(crate) with no accessor, so no test can observe which policy an engine carries. The named test pins the CONSTRUCTOR; it cannot pin the two CALL SITES. So this fix is correct today and unguarded against the next edit.
THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS wamn-vr1q, found in the same wave on the ctl lane: a function proven correct, with nothing proving the production path calls it. Two instances in one wave is a pattern worth watching, not a coincidence. ***

PREMISE CORRECTIONS: build_engine_inner never CONSTRUCTED a default, it RECEIVES one - the two construction sites were build_engine and build_engine_sized. And the diff is ~55 lines, not the briefed ~15, of which 24 are the rationale doc-comment this bead's own acceptance criterion requires be recorded.

*** RESERVED FOR THE OWNER AND FILED AS wamn-d0w4 SO IT DOES NOT DIE WITH THIS CLOSE: EgressAddressPolicy::permissive() is still the default, so under Enforce the declared allowed_hosts is now the SOLE confinement for an opted-in guest. Whether the address-range layer should also tighten is a security-posture ruling, not an implementation detail. The lane implemented Enforce only, exactly as instructed. ***

title: [SR-MVP] feat(runtime): build_engine cannot install a host socket policy
description:
## Why

crates/platform/runtime/src/engine.rs's build_engine never calls
EngineBuilder::with_socket_policy, so EngineBuilder::build() takes
`socket_policy: self.socket_policy.unwrap_or_default()` (fork engine/mod.rs:998)
and the engine silently carries SocketPolicy::default().

Measured 2026-08-17: grepping all of crates/ services/ components/ for
with_socket_policy, host_loopback_enabled, SocketPolicy returns ZERO production
call sites.

## Consequence

No gate and no operator can configure host_loopback_enabled, egress_mode,
egress_addrs (EgressAddressPolicy) or the connection quota. The upstream
`--allow-host-loopback` flag is a `wash` CLI flag (fork crates/wash/src/cli/host.rs
:227-228, consumed at :407) and wamn does not use the wash CLI, so that whole
surface is unreachable here rather than merely off.

This is what blocked wamn-0h0g.15.52 from covering the granted-and-enabled case
end to end: the positive half of the loopback grant is only reachable in-process
against SocketPolicy::decide, never through the gate's host.

## Scope

Give build_engine an optional host socket policy and a single place that decides
it. Do NOT let a gate construct a second Engine::builder to work around this --
that duplicates the pooling/epoch configuration and proves nothing about the
production store path.

## Boundary

Does not decide WHAT the policy should be -- that is the sibling posture bead.
Filed by lane 5 of wave 10 at the wamn-0h0g.15.52 close.
acceptance_criteria: build_engine can install a host socket policy through one decision point, and a gate can configure host_loopback_enabled and egress_mode without constructing a second engine.
notes: IMPLEMENTATION BOUNDARY 2026-08-21: preserve build_engine(proposals) and add the minimum additive build_engine_with_socket_policy(proposals, SocketPolicy) seam in engine.rs, with the existing entry delegating to the default policy. Exercise the new seam only from the owning egressbench conformance gate. Policy values/operator posture remain explicitly out of scope for .15.142/.15.143; do not churn unrelated engine callers or construct a second Engine::builder.
close_reason: Completed by fba9921c: additive explicit SocketPolicy engine seam; runtime/conformance suites, strict Clippy, and three mutation kills green; independent review approved.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): a verification artifact must not report success without executing its subject
description:
## Why

Four separate mechanisms, each found by accident, in a different wave, by a
different lane, are all the SAME defect: a verification artifact that reports
success without executing its subject.

1. wamn-0h0g.15.125 -- 39 of 40 gate-mutant campaigns are referenced by nothing.
2. wamn-0h0g.15.129 -- `cargo test NAME -- --exact` against a MISSING test runs
   zero tests and EXITS 0, which a mutation harness reports as SURVIVED.
3. wamn-0h0g.15.131 -- an integration-test guard sat red for a whole wave because
   the recorded sweep bar was `--lib`, which selects no `tests/` binary at all.
   The guard file was then EDITED TWICE while red (b405694e, then 7da5a70d
   adding a new test to the guard file itself) and nobody observed the failure.
4. wamn-0h0g.15.136 -- 109 of 135 gate-mutant baselines are stale, so 31 of 37
   campaigns abort on their hash check before mutating anything.
5. tools/contract-diff leg 3 DOES invoke the .15.131 guard for real, but
   tests/conformance/tests/contract_diff.rs proves that leg's ARGV against a
   FAKE CARGO (FAKE_CARGO, contract_diff.rs:14-29). So a green contract_diff is
   evidence the plan is right and NEVER evidence the guards are green -- and
   nobody ran `tools/contract-diff run` during waves 8 or 9.

## Scope

State the invariant once, then audit against it once:

  *** EVERY GUARD MUST HAVE A NAMED RUNNER THAT IS ACTUALLY INVOKED, AND EVERY
      HARNESS MUST FAIL CLOSED WHEN ITS SUBJECT IS ABSENT. ***

Enumerate every verification artifact in the tree (conformance guards,
gate-mutant campaigns, contract-diff legs, deploy gate Jobs, bench modes) and
for each record: which runner of record invokes it, and what happens when its
subject is missing, renamed, or unbuilt. Anything that can pass vacuously is a
finding.

## Boundary

This is the umbrella. It does NOT re-baseline (wamn-0h0g.15.22) and does not
re-implement the individual fixes (.15.125, .15.129, .15.131, .15.136) -- it
exists so a FIFTH mechanism is not discovered by accident in a later wave. Its
deliverable is the invariant plus the audit, not another guard.

Filed by lane 4 of wave 10 at the wamn-0h0g.15.131 close.
acceptance_criteria: Every verification artifact in the tree is enumerated with its runner of record and its behaviour when its subject is absent. Any artifact that can report success without executing its subject is either fixed or filed. The invariant is written down where a future wave will read it.
notes:
WAVE 54 SLICE LANDED; UMBRELLA STAYS OPEN AS THE INVENTORY. Commits bd4d0d36 and 568875e2.
*** THE FLAGSHIP RESULT IS A NEW MEMBER OF THE FAMILY: .split(marker).next() IS UNCONDITIONALLY
INERT. *** Split::next NEVER returns None, so any .expect() after it is unreachable and the span
silently collapses to end-of-file. Proved by a matched mutant pair on component_export_index: the
SAME mutant is KILLED with split_once and SURVIVES with the old idiom, because the tokens it scans
for occur zero times in the file and both scans still succeeded. Use split_once / rsplit_once.
This is the same disease as wamn-3o3a (29 self-scanning include_str sites in 14 files) seen from
the other end - there the literal self-matches, here the delimiter never fails.
FIXED THIS WAVE: workspace_tiers bare-Cargo count loop (was DOUBLE-vacuous: hardcoded literals
compared against the manifest's own prose, JSON vs JSON, THROUGH contains - so the substring 6
was satisfied inside 16; live instance said 6 against a true 7); component_export_index span
collapse; instance_suffix_ownership pinning a method name rather than an invariant; contract_diff
LEG_COUNT 5 vs 4 after ea71c1c4 deleted WAMN_FLOWRUNNER_WORLD. DELETED OUTRIGHT:
specialization_fixtures_are_classified_once_and_excluded_from_product_tiers - a fifty-line body
over a ZERO-LENGTH array, executing zero times since f6bc01eb deleted the custom component plane,
while still counting as a passing test.
STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY NOT FILED AS SEPARATE BEADS (owner direction: no testing churn) -
1. docker_component_provenance stage() searches for a newline-FROM, so a stage whose body BEGINS
   with another FROM is not bounded and the span runs past the real boundary. Same family.
2. contract-diff lists its dry-run plan and its run legs independently, so the dry-run test
   structurally CANNOT catch a run-leg deletion - a mutant proved it stays green.
3. The enumeration deliverable belongs in findings.md, which is integrator-only.
MEASURED CONFORMANCE STATE at 4eeb2ab1, for the record and NOT as a work queue: 167 passed,
52 failed, 13 RED BINARIES of 27. The earlier seven-of-27 figure UNDERCOUNTED.
=== WAVE 56 INVENTORY (2026-08-24). Inventory lines, NOT a work queue, NOT N new beads. ===

Added here rather than filed separately, per the owner's standing churn rule.

1. *** services/dispatcher/tests/read_authority.rs IS THE EXACT SHAPE THIS BEAD NAMES, AND
   IT IS THE STRONGEST INSTANCE FOUND SO FAR. ***
   Its guard is: let Ok(url) = std::env::var("WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL") else { eprintln!(
   "skipping ..."); return; }. libtest's default capture swallows the eprintln, so a
   passing run prints "test result: ok. 1 passed".
   *** WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL IS SET BY NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY *** - no script, no CI
   config, no deploy/gates job. It appears only as a manual command in an archived doc.
   CONSEQUENCE: this gate had almost certainly NEVER EXECUTED A SINGLE ONE OF ITS FOUR
   PROOFS. When wave 56 set the variable by hand and ran it, it failed at FOUR independent
   layers, three of which no measurement pass had found. A verification artifact reporting
   success without executing its subject is precisely this bead's subject.

2. services/dispatcher/tests/read_authority.rs never seeds wamn_run.environment_policies,
   so the pin_run_durability_class() BEFORE-INSERT trigger raises
   environment-policy-not-converged and the seed phase dies. The sibling gate
   crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs DOES seed it - that is the house
   pattern to copy. This was masked behind the retired-relation seed that wamn-q9wa removed,
   and behind the LOCK TABLE defect now filed as wamn-jnms.

3. THE BROADER POINT FOR THIS BEAD: two of the four layers above were invisible to two
   separate read-only measurement passes and only appeared under execution. A gate nothing
   runs decays silently and its decay is not measurable by reading it. Wiring
   WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL into a gate job - or converting the self-skip to the loud-fail
   shape - is higher leverage than repairing the SQL inside any individual gate.

RELATED, filed as their own beads because they are defects rather than guard hygiene:
  wamn-jnms  deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql bare LOCK TABLE, illegal under psql autocommit
  wamn-kk1s  publish_release.rs wiring-compatibility gate call site is unpinned

INVENTORY FROM WAVE 58, not a new bead per the churn rule. Two self-scan guard sites in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/production_claim.rs were repaired under wamn-3o3a and DO have teeth, but they use bare unwrap() rather than expect(), so when the subject is absent they panic WITHOUT NAMING THE ABSENCE. That is the weaker half of this bead's shape - the artifact does execute its subject, but its failure message does not say what is missing. Left alone as outside surgical scope. Separately: tests/system/src/deadlineproof.rs is a source-scan guard of a DIFFERENT file (it asserts services/host source contains bounded_outgoing_config(config)) and is currently RED at c2d805e0 - it is not wamn-3o3a's self-scan defect, but it is this bead's family and nobody owns it yet.
WAVE 60 INVENTORY, filed here rather than as N new beads. NOT A WORK QUEUE. Measured at the wave 60
tip; nothing below was fixed and nothing below is claimed.

A. THE ROOT AND COMPONENTS rustfmt GATE LEGS ARE RED, AND WERE ALREADY RED AT BASE c2d805e0.
   Eight files, every one of them unformatted at base - re-checked by extracting each file's BASE
   blob to a temp path and running rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on it, because rustfmt --check
   reading from STDIN does not report through its exit code and silently reports clean.
     crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs, src/wiring.rs, tests/identity.rs
     services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs, src/store/test_orchestration.rs
