title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): 109 of 135 gate-mutant baselines are stale, so 31 of 37 campaigns cannot run
description:
## Why

Measured 2026-08-17 at 8e917afc, against the git blobs at HEAD (so lane edits
cannot skew it): of the 135 (TARGET, EXPECTED_SHA) pairs across the 37
tools/gate-mutants/*.sh campaigns, only 26 baselines match their target file.

*** 109 OF 135 BASELINES ARE STALE. 31 OF 37 CAMPAIGNS CANNOT EXECUTE AT ALL. ***

Each script verifies sha256(TARGET) against its inline EXPECTED_SHA and aborts
with "hash mismatch" BEFORE mutating anything. So 31 campaigns abort on their
first check and have been silently not-running. Exactly six campaigns are fully
runnable today: authoring-cli-collection-drift, authoring-cli-unmounted-green,
authoring-smoke-collection-drift, control-portable-store,
node-abi-outcome-validation, protected-relations.

34 distinct target files are pinned at a stale digest; 15 are current.

## Why this is a structural bug, not a chore

A hand-written digest literal of a file under active development ALWAYS rots.
Nothing in the tree asserts that a campaign's baseline still matches its target,
so rot is invisible: the campaign exits non-zero in a way no gate observes, and
the mutation evidence recorded in architecture/gate-registry.json keeps claiming
"proven" for a campaign that has not run since its baseline drifted.

This is the same disease family as wamn-0h0g.15.125 (39 of 40 campaigns
referenced by nothing), wamn-0h0g.15.129 (cargo test NAME -- --exact against a
MISSING test runs zero tests and EXITS 0, which a harness reports as SURVIVED),
and wamn-0h0g.15.131 (an integration-test guard red for a whole wave because the
recorded sweep bar was --lib). In every case the defect is the same: evidence
that nothing runs.

## Scope

Own the STRUCTURAL fix, not the re-baseline. The re-baseline itself belongs to
wamn-0h0g.15.22, which owns the EXPECTED_SHA freeze and now carries this
measurement.

Decide and implement one of:
  (a) a conformance test that asserts, for every campaign, that every
      EXPECTED_SHA equals sha256 of its TARGET at HEAD -- turning silent rot into
      a named red test; and/or
  (b) deriving the baseline instead of pinning it (record the digest at the
      commit the campaign was authored against, resolved via git, so the check
      still detects an unexpected working-tree change without rotting), and/or
  (c) making a mismatched baseline a LOUD failure that the gate of record
      observes, rather than a non-zero exit nobody reads.

Whichever is chosen, a campaign whose baseline has rotted must become visible
without anyone running it.

## Boundary

Does NOT re-baseline anything -- that is wamn-0h0g.15.22, and every EXPECTED_SHA
is frozen until it lands. Note tools/gate-mutants/profile-selectors.sh pins
architecture/workspace-tiers.json, itself a frozen file, so that one campaign
cannot be corrected before .15.22 even in principle.

Also note tools/gate-mutants/m1-composition.sh already indirects its digests
through readonly constants (M1_SHA, CAUSATION_SHA); that is cosmetic, not a fix
-- M1_SHA is current but CAUSATION_SHA is stale.

Found by the integrator during wave 10 dispatch, while verifying the single
stale baseline that wamn-0h0g.15.123 exposed in test-orchestration.sh.
acceptance_criteria: A rotted gate-mutant baseline is detectable without running the campaign: a named test fails, or the baseline can no longer rot by construction. The measurement is reproducible from the repository. No EXPECTED_SHA is re-baselined here.
close_reason:
Deleted, not repaired, at 5c47074b -- tools/gate-mutants/ no longer exists.

Owner ruling 2026-08-18: this branch is simplification and mutation testing is out of scope,
so the honest resolution of the whole gate-mutant cluster is rm, not five repairs. Measured at
78afe665: 37 scripts / 6390 lines, 117 of 146 baseline pins stale, ONLY 4 OF 37 CAMPAIGNS
COULD EXECUTE AT ALL, and two inbound code references.

The dependency edge on wamn-0h0g.15.22 was removed rather than forced through: it existed only
because this bead was expected to be fixed AFTER the re-baseline, and the re-baseline no longer
has a subject.

title: [SR-MVP] docs(fork): record the accepted UdpBind posture and its confinement proof
description:
Accept the upstream UdpBind posture at the pinned runtime revision. With the Wamn socket policy shaped to an empty allowlist under Enforce, off-box sends never populate egress_peers; the receive path therefore drops off-box inbound datagrams. The residual private virtual-network receive surface and bounded scan or wakeup cost are accepted.

Landing work corrects the fork ledger and pins the actual confinement mechanism. It does not add a Wamn-side clamp or a new carried fork commit.
acceptance_criteria: The a9f9c57d fork-ledger row no longer claims service-loopback-only or denial for non-service components. It states the actual Component and Service UdpBind behavior, names raw_socket_opt_out_shapes_an_empty_allowlist_under_enforce as the load-bearing policy guard, and cites evidence that an empty egress_peers set makes off-box inbound datagrams unreachable. The accepted virtual-network receive and bounded scan or denial-of-service residuals are named. A mutant restoring the old ledger claim or weakening empty-allowlist plus Enforce turns a named proof red. No fork clamp is added.
notes:
Found during wamn-0h0g.15.20 while re-pinning the four egressbench socket
drift-guards, which could not be made green without deciding what they should
now assert.

WHAT wamn-0h0g.15.20 DID, so this bead starts from a known state: it re-pinned
the guard to the ACTUAL daba602 text rather than papering over the change. The
guard is renamed from `udp_bind_policy_and_p2_p3_call_sites_are_service_loopback_only`
to `..._are_pinned`, and its doc comment records the before/after and the
wildcard-bind reality in full. So the tree is HONEST at the pin; what is
undecided is the posture, not the record.

STILL ENFORCED at daba602, verified, so this is not a hole in raw egress: the
three raw-egress operations (TcpConnect, UdpConnect, UdpOutgoingDatagram) all
route through `resolve_connect`, which denies every non-loopback destination once
`shape_socket_policy` has emptied the allowlist and forced
`EgressMode::Enforce`. A bound socket with no permitted destination cannot send
off-box. The question is purely about what an unsolicited INBOUND datagram can
reach.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING for whoever takes this: `EgressMode::Count` is upstream's
`#[default]` and merely logs-and-counts what it would refuse while allowing it.
wamn's deny-without-opt-in therefore depends on BOTH halves of
`shape_socket_policy` -- empty allowlist AND Enforce. wamn-0h0g.15.20's new test
`raw_socket_opt_out_shapes_an_empty_allowlist_under_enforce` pins them together
for exactly that reason.
RULING (owner, 2026-08-18): PULLED INTO THE wamn-0h0g.15.161 ADJUDICATION SET AS #30. The UdpBind widening is EXACTLY the confinement class .15.161 adjudicates — an authority delta that arrived as an UPGRADE SIDE-EFFECT rather than a grant decision. At 09b1132f a Component could not bind at all and a Service only on loopback; at daba6029 SocketPolicy::decide_bind gives BOTH Component and Service UdpBind on loopback OR unspecified. Nobody decided that; the pin did. Adjudicate it alongside the 29 wamn_app confinements, under the same rule: a real over-grant lands its revoke immediately with probe arms (fast lane, R4 floor), a benign delta rides the single .15.22 regeneration. LIKELY LANDING, stated so the adjudication has a default to argue against: the wamn-side clamp pattern that wamn-0h0g.17.4 just established — deny at OUR layer, leave the fork pinned and untouched. That pattern was ratified for the pooling kill-switch on the reasoning that 'mechanism kept' names the concept, not the fork's code path; the same reasoning applies to a socket-policy widening we did not ask for.
ADJUDICATION #30 (EXE wave 2 lane 4, 2026-08-18) — under wamn-0h0g.15.161. PENDING OWNER RATIFICATION.

VERDICT: BENIGN — OPTION (a), ACCEPT UPSTREAM'S POSTURE. Banks on wamn-0h0g.15.22.

*** THE STATED DEFAULT (the wamn-side clamp) WAS ARGUED AGAINST AS INSTRUCTED, AND IT DID NOT SURVIVE
— BUT NOT FOR THE REASON EXPECTED. THE CLAMP PATTERN HAS NO IMPLEMENTATION SITE HERE. ***
wamn-0h0g.17.4's clamp worked because wamn owns the pooling CALL SITE. decide_bind is consulted INSIDE
the fork's own SocketAddrCheck closure, built by the fork from a GuestKind wamn NEVER NAMES —
integrator-verified: `grep -rn GuestKind crates/ services/` returns ZERO hits (the only four in the
tree are in tests/conformance/src/egressbench.rs). linked_call.rs:331-335 selects it internally from
is_service. There is no wamn-side seam between a guest's bind call and decide_bind. Re-asserting the
stricter posture therefore means EDITING THE FORK — that is option (b), an eleventh carried commit,
NOT the clamp pattern. The ruling's stated default named a mechanism that does not exist on this
surface.

THE DECISIVE ARGUMENT FOR (a): egress_peers is written at only two send sites (host_udp.rs:609-615,
host_udp_p3.rs:214-221 — grep-verified as the only writers), and BOTH sit DOWNSTREAM of the policy
check (prepare_one, host_udp.rs:719-741). Under wamn's shaping (shape_socket_policy,
linked_call.rs:274-287 -> empty allowlist + Enforce) every non-loopback destination is denied at
resolve_connect, so send_one_net is unreachable for off-box addresses and THE NETWORK HALF'S PEER SET
IS PROVABLY ALWAYS EMPTY. An always-empty peer set makes the wildcard-bound socket drop 100% of
inbound datagrams (p2 host_udp.rs:410-416 -> Ok(None); p3 host_udp_p3.rs:339-343 -> continue).
wamn does NOT depend on upstream's "reply-only" claim being right — it gets a STRICTLY STRONGER
property, admit-nothing, as a corollary of the egress denial it already enforces and already pins.
Off-box inbound reachability: ZERO, for any guest, screened or not.

Upstream's comment IS wrong about the mechanism, as this bead says: TCP rewrites to loopback, UDP
deliberately does not (udp.rs:330-354). The mitigation is nonetheless sound, and wamn's posture does
not rest on it.

THE STRONGEST CASE AGAINST (a), stated fairly: wamn's entire confinement rests on a two-field struct
edit in one function; EgressMode::Count is upstream's #[default] and logs-and-ALLOWS. A bind refusal
FAILS SAFE; an egress-derived filter FAILS OPEN. That asymmetry is real. It does not carry the day
because (i) there is no clamp site, as above, and (ii) the fail-open concern is ALREADY guarded —
wamn-0h0g.15.20's raw_socket_opt_out_shapes_an_empty_allowlist_under_enforce pins BOTH halves
together, which is precisely the regression feared. Option (b) would cost a carried fork commit
forever, buy ZERO additional off-box confinement, and close only R1 below — inside a trust boundary
wamn does not draw.

RESIDUALS, named because the bead does not:
  R1 (the actual surviving delta) — the unspecified bind also creates the virtual half
     (udp.rs:365-372), and the LOOPBACK half carries NO peer filter; resolve_connect step 2
     (policy.rs:249-253) admits every loopback destination as Plane::Virtual with no egress policy.
     So a COMPONENT can, for the first time, be an unsolicited UDP receiver on the workload's private
     virtual network; at 09b1132f it could not bind at all. This crosses no wamn boundary — the
     virtual network is per-WORKLOAD by construction (for_guest(kind, &template.workload_id)) and
     those components already share a process.
  R2 — the wildcard OS bind is a genuinely open UDP port on the pod: scan-visible, and a remote
     flooder costs one wakeup + syscall per packet. Bounded DoS; no confidentiality or integrity reach.

*** PREMISE CORRECTION TO THE RULING ITSELF — MY COST ARGUMENT WAS OVERSTATED. *** The ruling asserted
that crates/platform/component-policy "structurally REFUSES publication of any first-party component

title: [SR-MVP] fix(schema): runs_release_record_check admits a half-recorded release pair
description:
## Why

`runs_release_record_check` (deploy/sql/run-state.sql) does NOT pair the two
claim-time columns, despite the CheckSpec comment at
crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs:214-216 claiming "absent, or COMPLETE and
well formed".

## Measured (proven on throwaway postgres:18, wave 9)

The constraint is
  (release_version IS NULL AND manifest_digest IS NULL)
  OR (release_version > 0 AND manifest_digest ~ '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$')

With exactly one half present and well formed, the second disjunct is
TRUE AND NULL = NULL and the first is FALSE, so the whole expression is NULL --
and a CHECK constraint is SATISFIED when its expression is NULL. Verified by
insertion:
  (7, NULL)                 -> ACCEPTED   (should refuse)
  (NULL, <valid digest>)    -> ACCEPTED   (should refuse)
  (0, <valid digest>)       -> refused    (control, correct)

## Reachability

The claim path cannot reach it: ReleaseIdentity (claims.rs:79-88) carries both
fields, so it binds both-or-neither. But architecture/protected-writes.json marks
wamn_run.runs author-reachable ("author SQL, RLS-bounded"), so a tenant author
can write a half record and WEDGE that run's next claim at
run-release-record-immutable, with no crash-budget spend.

## Scope

Add the two IS NOT NULL conjuncts. Verified fix refuses both half-pairs and
still accepts both legitimate shapes. Four sites carry the predicate and must
move together: deploy/sql/run-state.sql, the run_plane.rs CheckSpec definition,
the run_plane.rs RUN_STATE_SQL needle, and the stand-in DDL in
crates/platform/runtime/tests/production_claim_live.rs.

## Boundary

Found by wamn-0h0g.15.23 (whose two half-pair test legs are red until this
lands, so this sequences BEFORE it). Introduced by wamn-0h0g.15.11 / 618a5800.
design:
The exact pg_get_constraintdef rendering of the fixed constraint, DERIVED on
postgres:18 rather than predicted (a predicted rendering in the originating lane
report was wrong -- it omitted the parens):

CHECK ((((release_version IS NULL) AND (manifest_digest IS NULL)) OR ((release_version IS NOT NULL) AND (manifest_digest IS NOT NULL) AND (release_version > 0) AND (manifest_digest ~ '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$'::text))))

The CheckSpec.definition is compared against pg_get_constraintdef by the
reconciler, so E2 must match what Postgres RETURNS. Confirm the reconciler's
repair path actually REPLACES a drifted CHECK (drop + add) rather than only
reporting it.
close_reason: Pair fixed (080fc89a). Two IS NOT NULL conjuncts. Proven on postgres:18 that (7,NULL) and (NULL,digest) were both ACCEPTED because a half pair leaves the disjunct NULL and a NULL CHECK is satisfied, and that the fix refuses both while still accepting both legitimate shapes. Four sites moved together. The CheckSpec literal is the pg_get_constraintdef(oid,true) PRETTY rendering derived on PG18 — my first derivation used the non-pretty overload and was wrong; the pre-fix literal was confirmed to match the pretty rendering byte-for-byte before the new one was trusted.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(exec): no entry input-schema guard is enforced for HTTP-admitted runs
description:
## Why

Found while taking wamn-0h0g.15.96 (2026-08-17). Closing that bead removed the only enforcement point for HTTP-admitted payloads, and the alternative would have been to refuse every route.

## Measured

The entry input-schema document exists ONLY inside the execution plan's `entry_input_schema_guard`, and plan bytes are pulled only by the flowrunner process -- the wash host mounts no plan source by design ("both of which are already inside the verified manifest, so it fetches nothing"). So the host-side routing provider cannot supply the real schema and returns the no-constraint spelling.

The flowrunner validates the entry guard only on the CALL-FLOW path (components/execution/flowrunner/src/frames.rs); a root `request` entry node is admitted unconditionally. The flow-http adapter's own `validate_schema` was therefore the SOLE enforcement point for HTTP-admitted payloads, and with a no-constraint schema there is now none.

## Scope

Either carry the entry guard in the manifest attachment projection so the routing provider can serve it, or have the flowrunner validate a root `request` entry's payload against its own plan-resident guard.

## Boundary

Not a regression introduced by choice: the routing provider cannot read plan bytes, so the alternatives were this gap or refusing every route. Disclosed rather than papered over.
acceptance_criteria: An HTTP-admitted run whose payload violates the entry input schema is refused, with a named test, and the refusal names the same classification the call-flow path uses.
close_reason: Root entry guard enforced at its authority (8f616ea8). execute_root validates against the root plan's own hash-verified guard through the SAME validator and SAME call-input-invalid classification the call-flow boundary emits — no new code, kind, SQL literal or WIT change. Ordered after the single-shot latch so a refusal still burns the root, and before projection or any dispatch debit. Event roots unaffected by construction (their guard must be exactly true). Branch (a) rejected on merit: the host has no plan bytes on the serving path so it could only compare a manifest copy against nothing, and two enforcement points where the downstream one decides give false confidence or spurious refusals. TWO CORRECTIONS: the gap is LATENT — execute_root has zero production callers and Guest::run still returns the interpreter refusal, so a frame-stack unit proof is the honest ceiling; and the host DOES read hash-verified plan bytes at ADMISSION (decode_target reads exact_bytes, derives one bool, discards), so a third option existed that neither bead nor brief named — refuse pre-admission in begin, no WIT change. Recorded for the routing-WIT revision.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(catalog): the manifest and admission disagree on the definition-hash prefix
description:
## Why

Found while taking wamn-0h0g.15.96 (2026-08-17). Two halves of the flow-http admission path spell the same hash differently, and nothing reconciles them.

## Measured

- `ServingManifest::validate` requires attachment `definition_hash` to be `sha256:<64 hex>` (crates/catalog/model/src/lib.rs, the shared digest validator).
- `resolve_exposure` mints the definition hash as BARE HEX (crates/schema/control/src/exposure.rs), which is what `catalog.release_attachments.definition_hash` stores and what admission compares `expected_definition_hash` against (crates/platform/runtime/src/flow_invocation.rs).

So a mint that copies the database value FAILS manifest validation, and a mint that prefixes it makes EVERY flow-http admission refuse on definition-hash mismatch. There is no spelling that satisfies both today.

## Why it is not visible yet

No production code constructs a `ServingManifest`, so neither half has met the other. This will bite the FIRST end-to-end route, which is exactly when it is most expensive to diagnose.

## Scope

Pick one spelling and converge both halves, or give the manifest projection an explicit conversion at the mint boundary with a test pinning both directions.

## Boundary

Blocked on the mint (wamn-0h0g.15.14) for anything to converge against. Related: `wamn:flow-http-routing` has no canonical WIT home -- flow-invocation's canonical package lives in its own crate with vendored copies, while routing's only copy was inside the flow-http component, so wamn-0h0g.15.96's vendored copy is a copy-of-a-copy. Whoever lands the mint should settle that too.
acceptance_criteria: A single definition-hash spelling satisfies both ServingManifest::validate and admission's comparison, proven by a test in both directions.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-17 — THE SPELLING IS DECIDED: PICK THE PREFIXED FORM.

`sha256:<64 hex>` wins. It is what ServingManifest::validate already enforces and what the ManifestDigest newtype family mints. THE DATABASE'S BARE-HEX MINTING SITE IS THE BUG -- resolve_exposure (crates/schema/control/src/exposure.rs) is what changes, not the manifest's validator.

SEQUENCING, binding: this bead's spelling contradiction resolves FIRST, and only then does wamn-0h0g.15.105 land the four flow-level hash newtypes on top of it. .15.105 is now this bead's successor (dep edge added 2026-08-17) rather than an independent tidiness sweep, because this contradiction is the observed instance of the class those newtypes make unrepresentable.

Note for whoever takes it: fixing definition_hash by hand here while leaving plan_hash, source_artifact and binding_base_artifact bare is patching one instance of a class. That is acceptable ONLY because .105 follows immediately.
close_reason: Converged exposure definition hashes on the catalog's canonical sha256:<64 lowercase hex> spelling. Added a pure release-mint boundary proof that the minted value parses as DefinitionHash, round-trips unchanged through serving-manifest v2 admission, and that the retired bare spelling refuses. Normal schema-control library check, targeted rustfmt, and diff checks pass; the owner integration binary's cold dependency build was hard-capped before reaching project source.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(conformance): reconcile governed first-party version identities with the demolished surface
description:
## Why

tests/conformance/src/version_identity.rs:504 fails with four governed first-party version drifts, all caused by earlier waves deleting or moving the artifacts it watches:

  crates/scenarios/model/src/test_set.rs: No such file or directory (os error 2)
  deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql: expected 1 occurrence of governed identity 'schema_version text NOT NULL CHECK (schema_version = ''0.1''),', found 0
  crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs: expected 1 occurrence of governed identity 'definition: "CHECK (schema_version = ''0.1''::text)",', found 0
  clients/authoring-client/src/generated/authoring.ts: expected 2 occurrences of '"schema-version": "0.1";', found 4

Discovered 2026-08-17 while taking wamn-0h0g.15.12, which is what first made wamn-proof-conformance compile again. The guard has been unrunnable since .15.10, so these have been latent since the waves that deleted the watched surface.

## Scope

Retire the watch entries whose subjects the ruling deleted, and correct the occurrence counts for the ones that legitimately moved. Each retirement must name the bead that deleted its subject, so the reconcile is auditable rather than a silencing.

The TypeScript count (4 vs an expected 2) is a client-surface drift and is subject to the Rust-only-MVP standing direction; if it cannot be resolved without TS work, split it out rather than blocking the Rust legs.

## Boundary

This is guard content, not a registry regeneration, so it is NOT part of wamn-0h0g.15.22. Do not relax a governed identity that still has a live subject.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --lib version_identity passes, and every retired watch entry cites the bead that deleted its subject.
close_reason: Landed at 306b46f9. All four governed drifts grounded to commits BEFORE editing: three retired with the deleting bead and commit cited in place, one count corrected. (1) crates/scenarios/model/src/test_set.rs TEST_SET_SCHEMA_VERSION retired — .15.27 (3a042d96) deleted the self-describing test-set document and the constant; .15.76 (eb1c3a88) separately MOVED the file to crates/execution/flow-model/. The reported 'No such file' symptom is misleading and the retire-vs-correct dichotomy was false here: correcting the path alone would have turned a file-mode failure into found 0. The identity merged rather than vanished — cases ride the flow document, covered by the existing flow-model SCHEMA_VERSION entry. (2) deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql retired — 3a042d96 dropped wamn_run.authoring_test_sets, the only relation carrying a governed schema version; re-grepped, the file retains no 0.1 of any form. (3) crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs retired — the authoring_test_sets_schema_version_check CheckSpec went with its table; the admission-context CheckSpec at :146 is the only governed 0.1 reconciliation identity left and stays. (4) clients/authoring-client/src/generated/authoring.ts count 2 -> 4 — NOT client drift and NO TypeScript work, so the rust-only-mvp direction does not bite: the generated file already sits at four correct occurrences, regenerated by .7.3 (ce919195) when the wire contract gained the query envelope pair, and the stale half was the guard's own expectation written by .10.7 five days earlier. Corroborated in Rust: crates/authoring/model/src/lib.rs has exactly four schema_version fields. Since expected_count is exact equality this is a TIGHTENING — mutant-proven, unpinning one of the four yields 'expected 4 occurrence(s), found 3'. NOTHING REFUSED: every retired subject verified gone at HEAD by independent grep, not inferred from diffs; no governed identity lost coverage; no entry added. Watch list 47 -> 44. VERIFIED: cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --lib version_identity = 5 passed; whole --lib suite 63/63 green; clippy -D warnings clean; rustfmt already clean (no reformat). All three cited commits independently re-verified by subject line. FILED: .15.114 (P3 — governed_literal_violations reports at most ONE violation per entry, so an unreadable file short-circuits and MASKS a missing occurrence; that is exactly what made entry 1's symptom misleading. Guard mechanism, not content, so deliberately out of this bead).

title: [SR-MVP] fix(conformance): governed-dependency guard must admit a self dev-dependency
description:
## Why

tests/conformance/src/manifest_dependencies.rs:123 fails: 'crates/catalog/model/Cargo.toml:37: wamn-catalog must inherit its native workspace identity'. The offending line is the SELF dev-dependency wamn-catalog = { path = ".", features = ["test-util"] } that wamn-0h0g.15.104 (e87133fa) added deliberately, so that wamn-catalog's own tests/ compilation unit can see its parent's test-util feature under a plain cargo test -p wamn-catalog.

The guard reads it as ungoverned dependency drift. It is not: a self dev-dependency by path is the only construction that makes a crate's own integration tests see its own feature, and it cannot 'inherit its native workspace identity' because the workspace entry is what it is a copy of.

Discovered 2026-08-17 while taking wamn-0h0g.15.12, which is what first made wamn-proof-conformance compile again — the guard has been unrunnable since .15.10 and this has been latent since e87133fa.

## Scope

Teach the guard that a dev-dependency whose path is "." and whose name equals the package's own name is a governed construction, not drift. Keep every other identity rule intact.

## Boundary

Guard logic only. Do NOT 'fix' this by removing the self dev-dependency or by promoting test-util to the normal dependency — that deletes the M-TEST-UTIL fence for every crate downstream, which .15.104's ruling forbids.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --lib manifest_dependencies passes with the self dev-dependency in place, and still fails if a genuine ungoverned dependency identity is introduced.
close_reason: Landed at 46801104. The guard now admits a dev-dependency whose name equals the manifest's own package name and whose path is exactly '.', and nothing else. TWO PREMISE ADDITIONS the bead did not anticipate: the guard did NOT distinguish dev-dependencies (one bool collapsed dependencies/dev-dependencies/build-dependencies, so condition (a) of the exemption did not exist) and it had NO access to any manifest's package name (so condition (b) did not exist either) — the amendment could not be a one-line predicate; both inputs had to be plumbed in. The table-kind derivation was rewritten to assign both bools from one derived kind so they cannot desync, and is behaviour-preserving for the target-cfg and workspace header forms. VERIFIED: cargo test -p wamn-proof-conformance --lib manifest_dependencies = 3 passed; the whole --lib suite is 63/63 green; clippy -D warnings clean; rustfmt clean. NEGATIVE PROOF (the acceptance criterion's second half): five near-miss fixtures each differing in exactly one dimension — the same declaration under [dependencies] and under [build-dependencies], path='.' naming a DIFFERENT governed crate, this package by another path, and plain duplication — each refused with the identity message; plus a test that reads the REAL crates/catalog/model/Cargo.toml so the exemption cannot outlive the construction it exists for. Two real-tree mutants dead with sha256 restore: self-dep-promoted (dev->normal table) and self-dep-deleted. FILED: .15.115 (P3 — a dotted [dev-dependencies.crate] header makes the whole table escape the identity rule, because the header's last dotted segment is the crate name, not a keyword; pre-existing and latent, zero occurrences in the tree today) and .15.116 (P2 — this guard has no gate recipe of record anywhere in docs/archive/build-and-test.md, plausibly why it and version_identity went red unnoticed from .15.10 to .15.12). Recipe appended to build-and-test.md; the mutants are recorded there as a table rather than a tools/gate-mutants script, because the guard surface and its registries are frozen until .15.22 and a new script would drift them.

title: [SR-MVP] test(publish): the mint must match the reader-side golden vector
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.104's COUPLING acceptance clause reads 'the digest of a golden manifest equals the mint's recorded digest byte-for-byte, same vector both sides'. Only ONE side exists.

.15.104 pinned the reader side: crates/catalog/model/tests/serving_manifest_digest.rs the_golden_vector_digest_is_pinned asserts minimal().digest() == sha256:9eccdfb279fef3993b75e41b1f5ad622022d896db78ac5f74a954435daf3795e, the derived digest of the preimage that manifest_preimage_bytes_are_pinned already fixes, and asserts it is a plain SHA-256 over those bytes with no domain framing.

There is no producer to compare against: the release-manifest mint is wamn-0h0g.15.14, which is blocked on wamn-0h0g.8.7 (no publish transaction A exists to attach to). ServingManifest still has zero non-test producers.

## Scope

When the mint lands, assert the SAME vector on the producer side: mint the golden manifest through the mint's own path and assert the digest it records equals that literal, byte for byte. Two independent code paths, one literal, so a producer revision cannot move identity on one side only.

## Boundary

Does not re-pin the preimage — manifest_preimage_bytes_are_pinned owns that. Does not touch the reader-side test. If the mint's construction path cannot reproduce the fixture exactly, that is a finding about the mint, not a reason to weaken either assertion.
acceptance_criteria: A real producer-side mint constructs a genuinely mintable execution plan and its serving manifest, then the producer and reader assert the same canonical manifest bytes and derived digest. The vector is generated by the real mint in-test or committed from its output with the exact generating command cited; no artificial plan hash that production validation refuses is accepted. A named producer-coupling test fails when either side changes identity independently.
notes:
OWNER PREMISE-CORRECTION RULING 2026-08-21 — RE-PIN TO A GENUINELY MINTABLE PLAN; KEEP THE SAME-VECTOR WELD. The current reader vector hardcodes an artificial plan hash that the real producer correctly rejects because it does not hash the plan bytes. Relaxing the same-vector requirement would discard the producer-coupled identity invariant, so it is rejected. The replacement vector is minted through the real producer in-test, or committed from producer output with the exact generating command cited, and both reader and producer pin its canonical bytes and digest. The close must name the original artificial vector as the premise defect. IMPLEMENTATION PLAN NOT STARTED.
BOUNDARY CORRECTION FROM THE SAME OWNER RULING: the original description says this issue does not touch the reader-side test. That sentence is superseded. Replacing the artificial vector necessarily re-pins the reader fixture and the producer proof together; the preimage and identity stay one shared real-mint vector.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-21. Premise defect: the old reader golden used an artificial plan hash the real mint correctly could not reproduce. A fresh PostgreSQL 18 run of the real mint generated one shared 1,560-byte canonical vector with digest sha256:973018f34b03bf2724abcfd765a4bfaf30d1143c5f1a7d9ae5056a7dadc7001c. Reader and producer now consume those exact bytes and assert the same digest; the former minimal fixture is explicitly synthetic serializer-shape coverage only. Reader 8/8 and producer live 1/1 passed; strict Clippy/format/diff passed. Independent all-zero producer-digest and reader-digest mutants each failed their new coupling assertion; production sources were restored byte-for-byte.
Landed in a5fb050f.
FOLLOW-UP 2026-08-21: wamn-0h0g.11.52 owns the release-manifest mint live test's pre-existing envless early-return false-green. The producer/reader vector remains closed here; gate visibility is repaired with .11.43.
close_reason: COMPLETE: replaced the artificial reader-only vector with canonical bytes emitted by the real PostgreSQL mint and pinned one shared producer/reader digest. Reader 8/8, live producer 1/1, strict Clippy/format/diff green; independent producer and reader identity mutants failed; production sources restored byte-for-byte.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(runtime): two carriers exist for the release-identity pair
description:
## Why

Found building wamn-0h0g.15.100. The (release version, manifest digest) pair now reaches the host by TWO independent routes, and nothing reconciles them.

  1. PER-WORKLOAD CONFIG KEYS, landed by wamn-0h0g.15.11. crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/mod.rs:143 RELEASE_VERSION_CONFIG_KEY = 'wamn.release-version' and :147 MANIFEST_DIGEST_CONFIG_KEY = 'wamn.manifest-digest', read at on_workload_item_bind (:222-256) into set_release_identity(component_id, ...) (claims.rs:633). This is what the production claim records write-once onto a run. It is PER COMPONENT and OPTIONAL: mod.rs:140-142 states that absent leaves a claim recording nothing so every non-release path stays byte-unchanged. Half a pair is a hard bind-time refusal (:246-255).

  2. THE MOUNTED RELEASE-IDENTITY ConfigMap, read by the weld (wamn-0h0g.15.100). Per pod, and mandatory for the weld: it supplies the digest the manifest is verified against.

.15.11's own doc comment already anticipates this — it says the config keys 'mirror the keys of the mounted release-identity ConfigMap'. Mirror, but nothing enforces the mirroring.

## The hazard

A pod could mount release identity naming digest D1 while a component's workload config names D2. The weld would serve the manifest for D1; the claim would stamp D2 onto the run. Effect authority (wamn-0h0g.15.66) then binds runs to plans through a digest that names a manifest the pod never loaded. That is the exact failure the .2.3/.2.7 successor rule exists to prevent, and it would be silent.

## The decision

Rule which is authoritative and how divergence is handled. Options:
  (a) THE MOUNT WINS AND THE CONFIG KEYS ARE RETIRED. One carrier, one truth. Feeds set_release_identity from the weld instead of from workload config. Changes .15.11's landed workload-config contract and the per-component optionality that keeps non-release paths byte-unchanged.
  (b) BOTH STAND, CROSS-CHECKED. Keep the config-key path for its per-component optionality, and refuse at bind when a component's pair disagrees with the pod's weld. Smallest change to landed behaviour; keeps two carriers but makes divergence impossible.
  (c) THE CONFIG KEYS WIN. The weld takes its expected digest from config rather than the mount, and RELEASE_IDENTITY_MOUNT_PATH stays unread. Then the mount constants should be deleted rather than left as dead scaffolding.

## Boundary

Decision only. The implementation rides whichever of wamn-0h0g.15.101 (weld construction and hand-out) or wamn-0h0g.15.66 (effect authority) the ruling assigns it to. Note .15.66 independently requires an equality check between the run's recorded manifest_digest and the digest of the manifest the serving pod actually loaded — that check is only meaningful once this decision names the authoritative carrier.
design:
OWNER RULING, 2026-08-17: THE MOUNT IS THE SOLE CARRIER; THE CONFIG KEYS DELETE.

Reframed at the ruling: this is not a reconciliation problem. It is a DUAL-REPRESENTATION BUG wearing one, and the fix is the standing single-authority rule, not a comparator. Option (b) from the description — 'both stand, cross-checked' — is rejected, and the reasoning is the load-bearing part:

THE TWO CARRIERS ARE NOT PEERS.
  · The mounted ConfigMap is WELDED: digest-named and byte-verified at load, sha256(bytes) = <name>. The name and the content are ONE FACT, so what the weld holds cannot misdescribe itself.
  · The .15.11 config keys are ASSERTED: env-var strings whose agreement with anything is a template author's promise.

WHY A COMPARATOR IS THE WRONG SHAPE. When a welded carrier and an asserted carrier disagree, the asserted one is wrong BY CONSTRUCTION. So a reconciliation check could only ever confirm the mount — and a check whose outcome is knowable in advance is machinery with no information content.

WHY DELETION AND NOT TENDING. Keeping both keys alive keeps the MISDESCRIPTION CHANNEL open for every future reader that grabs the env var because it is easier than taking the manifest handle. Today's skew hazard becomes a recurring class. Deletion closes the class; reconciliation would tend it forever.

WHAT FOLLOWS.
  1. .15.11's per-workload (release version, manifest digest) keys are REMOVED FROM THE TEMPLATES.
  2. Every consumer that read them — the claim-time recording above all — takes its pair FROM THE LOADED WELD INSTANCE: manifest.digest() and the release version, both from verified content.
  3. .15.66's dependency COLLAPSES. Its 'mount digest equals the run's recorded digest' check stops being a cross-carrier comparison and becomes the tautology it should be: the recorder and the authority are THE SAME OBJECT, so equality is structural and the check DOCUMENTS rather than DEFENDS.
  4. The pod template shrinks to ONE deployment-varying line, the ConfigMap name — itself the skew-surface argument in miniature: one thing to roll, nothing to keep in agreement.

TWO HONEST EDGES, PRICED BY THE RULING.
  · VERSION-IN-PREIMAGE. The release version must live INSIDE the manifest bytes or deleting the env carrier would orphan it. It does — ServingManifest.release.catalog_version, a header field inside the canonical preimage (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:111 under :284). The weld exposes it FROM VERIFIED CONTENT, NEVER FROM THE OBJECT NAME.
  · PRE-LOAD CONSUMERS. Anything needing release identity before the manifest loads — logging banners, readiness annotations — either moves after load (readiness already gates on the loaded weld per the prefetch rule) or does without. Nothing load-bearing reads identity pre-load. A diagnostic that wants it reads the ConfigMap name and SAYS SO, labelled as unverified.

.15.11 GETS A FOLLOW-UP COMMIT STRIKING THE KEYS, NOT A REVERT. That bead's workload-config MECHANISM survives for genuinely per-workload knobs; what deletes is release identity impersonating one.
acceptance_criteria: The authoritative carrier of the release-identity pair is named; divergence between carriers is either impossible by construction or a named fail-closed refusal; any carrier ruled redundant has its constants and read path deleted rather than left dead.
close_reason:
Ruled by the owner 2026-08-17, recorded in DESIGN. THE MOUNT IS THE SOLE CARRIER; THE CONFIG KEYS DELETE. Option (a) of the three, with the reasoning that it is a dual-representation bug rather than a reconciliation problem: a welded carrier (digest-named, byte-verified, name and content one fact) and an asserted carrier (env strings, a template author's promise) are not peers, so a comparator could only ever confirm the mount and a check whose outcome is knowable in advance carries no information. Deletion closes the misdescription channel as a class; reconciliation would tend it forever.

Implementation split into three beads rather than done here (decision bead): wamn-0h0g.15.103 strikes the keys from templates and repoints consumers; wamn-0h0g.15.104 revises the weld to derive both halves from verified content and drop the second mounted carrier; and the collapse of .15.66's check from a cross-carrier comparison to a structural tautology is recorded on .15.66 itself.

CONSEQUENCE THE RULING SURFACES IN ALREADY-COMMITTED CODE: wamn-0h0g.15.100 (commit e5c52aab) reads a SECOND MOUNTED CARRIER — the release-identity ConfigMap — for its expected digest and release version. 'One thing to roll, nothing to keep in agreement' deletes that too: two ConfigMaps that must agree is the same skew surface one level down. That is wamn-0h0g.15.104.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(schema): the control plane has no retirement mechanism at all
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.78 retired `wamn_run.authoring_test_sets` on the RUN plane, through the existing `RETIRED_STORED_SUITE_TABLES` machinery in crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs.

`deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql` ALSO created that table, with the identical FK shape from `authoring_test_run_reservations` and `authoring_test_reports` (verify with `git show 3a042d96 -- deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql`). wamn-0h0g.15.27 deleted it from the artifact.

**THE CONTROL PLANE HAS NO RETIREMENT MECHANISM.** The artifact is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` throughout — there is nothing to hook a retirement into. So every control database provisioned before this wave keeps, forever:
  · the stale `wamn_run.authoring_test_sets` relation,
  · its grants — which, exactly as on the run plane, no reconciler can now see because the relation left the record,
  · and the two `test_set_hash text NOT NULL` FK columns on the two RETAINED tables, which have no default and therefore refuse every reservation and report INSERT.

## Scope

Give the control plane a retirement mechanism, and retire this table through it.

## Boundary

This is NOT a variant of wamn-0h0g.15.78 and could not ride it: .15.78 extends machinery that exists on the run plane. Here the machinery itself is missing, so there is no exact patch to propose — building the mechanism IS the bead.

Related: wamn-0h0g.15.79 found the same class of gap from the other direction — `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` with a changed arity creates an OVERLOAD rather than replacing, so an already-provisioned control DB would keep both signatures with the REVOKE covering only the new one. It fails closed on the shape-drift refusal rather than half-migrating, but there is no DROP FUNCTION and no migration path. Same missing mechanism.

Filed at the wave-4 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.78 report.
close_reason: Commit 1225515c. Retirement mechanism built as a fourth DO block in the artifact's own idiom, CATALOG-DRIVEN so it needs no 'has this run' state (the retired object IS the record a database predates the artifact, so converged replay is a no-op -- the run plane's answer in principle, different vehicle). Five divergences that previously survived replay, two SILENTLY, now converge or refuse by name. The vehicle had to differ for two verified reasons: no Rust step ever visits the control database (the artifact is applied as text), and it applies under a NOSUPERUSER wamn_system with FORCE RLS on all 19 relations, so the applying owner reads ZERO rows and any in-artifact emptiness guard would call a populated table empty. Which arms converge vs refuse is FORCED, not chosen: the retained shape-drift fingerprint hashes a.attnum, and PostgreSQL never renumbers attnum, so no ALTER can reach the pinned constant for those four relations -- hence refuse-by-name with reprovision rather than a permanently-failing replay. PREMISE CORRECTION: 'keeps its grants' is imported from the run plane and false here -- the artifact has ZERO GRANT statements and revokes everything from PUBLIC. Recorded an upgrade path if the owner wants the drop (ADD CONSTRAINT CHECK(false) is an emptiness oracle that survives FORCE RLS), and refused to hand-recompute the retained fingerprint.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(registry): the project-env read path does not return the instance suffix
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.83 stores `registry.project_envs.instance_suffix` and returns it from the upsert, but the READ path cannot see it:

  · `crates/control/registry/src/sql.rs` `select_org_project_envs_sql` selects project, env, secret_name, secret_namespace — not the suffix.
  · `crates/control/registry/src/types.rs:406-410` `ProjectEnv { triple, db_secret }` has no field for it, and the type is `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, so THE JSON EXPORT CONTRACT CHANGES WITH IT.

A consumer that derives the environment namespace must read the column, and today none can.

## Scope

Add the column to the select and the field to `ProjectEnv`, and account for the export-contract change the `deny_unknown_fields` derive makes non-optional.

## Boundary

Blocks wamn-0h0g.15.15 and wamn-0h0g.15.16 — the ruling requires both to take the suffixed name, and neither can until the value is readable.

Filed at the wave-4 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.83 report.
close_reason: Read path returns the suffix (fbee2853). Column added to the listing select, field added to ProjectEnv, REQUIRED with no serde default so a pre-field document fails from_json by design; SCHEMA_VERSION stays 0.1 because that literal is pinned by system-schema.sql AND a frozen conformance literal, so the parse failure IS the signal and is pinned. TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS THAT CHANGED THE SHIP: select_org_project_envs_sql has ZERO callers (its move-org-tier consumer is gone), so the listing column alone would have unblocked nothing — added select_project_env_sql, the single-triple read the three blocked beads actually need. And to_json/from_json have no production callers and no golden fixture anywhere, so the whole export-contract fallout is in-crate; 19-site ledger on the bead. Validation extended to mirror the storage CHECK, since refusing a missing suffix while accepting an explicit empty one would be incoherent. Unblocks .15.15 .15.16 .15.88.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(provision): carry the instance suffix into the cluster-global Postgres names
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.83 put the minted 8-character instance suffix on the derived NAMESPACE, which makes every namespace-scoped resource instance-unique by containment. Two name families are NOT contained and still carry the delete-and-recreate reuse hazard:

  1. `project_env_database_name` — cluster-global inside Postgres, and the CR name lives in the shared `wamn-system` namespace.
  2. `cdc_object_name` (publication / slot / role) — cluster-global in Postgres, and a replication slot OUTLIVES a dropped database.

`docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md:1580` names a database explicitly as the hazard. It is not yet closed.

## Why it could not ride .15.83

`project_env_database_name(org, project, env)` is RE-DERIVED FROM THE TRIPLE at 8 call sites that never read the registry: services/ctl/src/copy_project_env.rs:231-232, restore_project_env.rs:306, enable_cdc_project_env.rs:150, provision_project_env.rs:438 and :632, crates/control/provision/src/database.rs:52, tests/integration/src/provisionbench.rs:366/385/439/495/663, services/ctl/tests/effect_writer_generation_live.rs:236.

A RANDOM suffix is not derivable. Every one of those inverts to a registry lookup, and `Triple` (crates/control/registry/src/types.rs) has to carry the instance.

It also RE-KEYS THE FROZEN CREDENTIAL-SCOPE HASHES, which take the database name as a framed input — `effect_writer_scope_hash` and `artifact_reader_generation_scope_hash` in crates/control/provision/src/name.rs, whose frozen literals are asserted in name.rs and in crates/control/provision/src/artifact_reader.rs.

## Scope

Convert the derive sites to registry lookups, carry the instance on `Triple`, extend the two name families, and re-freeze the credential-scope literals in the same pass.

Filed at the wave-4 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.83 report.
notes:

IT ALSO COLLIDES WITH .15.12 ON THREE MORE FILES and therefore cannot be a concurrent lane with it: crates/control/provision/src/name.rs, services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs (.15.12 has 342 hits there, the largest surface in that bead) and services/ctl/tests/effect_writer_generation_live.rs (which .15.12 must fix at :89-93 for its own out-of-domain break).

title: [SR-MVP] feat(provision): mint an instance suffix so a recreated environment cannot reuse names
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.57. `docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md:1580-1583` requires that physical resource names carry the minted key OR ITS UNIQUE SUFFIX, because "if a database, bucket prefix, backup path, or Kubernetes resource is named from the reusable abbreviation alone, the delete-and-recreate hazard the suffix exists to prevent simply reappears one layer down."

The namespace form wamn-0h0g.15.57 shipped has no suffix. Delete an environment, recreate it, and the new one inherits the old namespace and whatever survived inside it.

## Scope

An **8-character provision-minted instance suffix**, stored as ONE column on `registry.project_envs`, appended to the derived namespace and to the physical resource names. Randomness is the entire uniqueness mechanism — the ruling is explicit that no further machinery is wanted.

The refusal formula in `validate_project_env` updates to include the suffix in the 63-character bound.

## Boundary

The owner REJECTED minting registry abbreviations ("a naming registry with a uniqueness discipline, pure churn for aesthetics") and kept the shipped provision-time composite refusal as authoritative. This bead adds only the suffix.

Consumers of the derived name — wamn-0h0g.15.15 and .15.16 — must take the suffixed form.

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16 (wave-3 decisions).
close_reason: SHIPPED e86e9833. 8-char [a-z0-9] suffix (41.4 bits, rejection-sampled), one NOT NULL CHECKed column on registry.project_envs, appended to the namespace. Hyphen excluded outright since the suffix owns the DNS-1123 label's last byte. Mint lives in services/ctl using the existing SystemRandom; wamn-control-provision stays pure with no new dependency. Upsert is READ-OR-MINT (never refreshed on conflict, RETURNs the stored value) so a re-provision keeps deriving existing names. PREMISE CORRECTION -- MY INSTRUCTION WAS WRONG: I said preserve the namespace-before-database check order. The property .15.72 recorded is that both branches stay REACHABLE, and the order achieving it is looser-bound-first. The suffix makes the namespace stem the TIGHTER bound (44 vs 51), so keeping my order would have made the DATABASE branch dead code -- the same hazard inverted. Order flipped; a test pins the sharpest pair. SCOPE HONESTLY SHORT OF THE RULING: namespace-scoped resources are instance-unique by containment, but the cluster-global per-env database and CDC objects are NOT -- their names are re-derived from the triple at 8 call sites that never read the registry and they frame the frozen credential-scope hashes. Filed .15.88; PLAN.md:1580's database leg is NOT closed. Envelope narrows 51->44 combined bytes; validate_project_env_cdc's branch is now subsumed, kept and documented.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(deploy): re-rule the namespace bound now the abbreviation premise is gone
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.50 said: namespaces DERIVE from registry-minted abbreviations, which are bounded by construction (`wamn-<org<=12>--<proj<=12>--<env>`, well under the 63-byte DNS-1123 cap), so NO TRUNCATION RULE EXISTS and provision simply refuses a breaching environment name.

THAT PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD IN THIS REPOSITORY, verified at the wave-3 close.

- There are no abbreviation columns anywhere. A full sweep of .rs/.sql/.sh/.yaml/.md/.wit found none.
- The components are the RAW registry slugs, each bounded at 40 bytes and nowhere else: orgs_id_charset_check, projects_id_charset_check and env_policies_name_charset_check in deploy/sql/system-schema.sql, mirrored by MAX_ID_LEN in crates/control/registry/src/validate.rs.
- So `wamn-` + org(40) + `--` + proj(40) + `--` + env(40) = 129 bytes against a 63-byte cap.
- The <=12 figure is real but belongs to the TENANT KEY settled in docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md:1527-1574, which has zero schema and zero code. The ruling treated a settled design as a shipped one.
- Even granting the abbreviations, the ruling's own form leaves `<env>` unbounded, and this repo bounds env at 40 — so the form can still reach 73 bytes. An env-only refusal was never sufficient.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT CONTRADICTION. PLAN.md:1580-1583 says physical resource names must carry the minted key OR ITS UNIQUE SUFFIX, because 'if a database, bucket prefix, backup path, or Kubernetes resource is named from the reusable abbreviation alone, the delete-and-recreate hazard the suffix exists to prevent simply reappears one layer down.' The ruled namespace form has no unique suffix. Delete acme/recv/prod, recreate it, and the new environment inherits the old namespace and whatever survived in it.

## What shipped in the meantime

wamn-0h0g.15.57 and .15.72 implemented the ruling's INTENT against what is true: one derivation function, and a real composite refusal at provision using the existing NameTooLong. That is correct and shippable. But it makes the bound a LATE REFUSAL, not a construction guarantee — the ruling's headline claim ('no truncation rule exists BECAUSE the bound holds by construction') is not yet true; what is true is 'no truncation rule exists because we refuse.'

## The decision

1. **Mint abbreviation columns** (registry.orgs.abbrev, registry.projects.abbrev, <=12; env <=30). Cost: registry schema change, migration, a uniqueness discipline (org-global, project-per-org), a slugify-with-override path on the project-request API, and backfill. Makes the ruling literally true. Does NOT address the PLAN:1580 reuse hazard.
2. **Keep the composite bound at provision** (what shipped). Cost: zero schema. But the refusal is late — see below.
3. **Bound the components directly** so the sum cannot breach (e.g. org <=20, project <=20, env <=11). Cheapest to reason about, harshest on users, and a breaking narrowing of a published id discipline.

## A live gap either way

provision-org runs only per-component validation and never checks an assembled length, so the registry accepts an org and project whose triple CAN NEVER BE PROVISIONED into any environment: the provisionable envelope is 51 combined bytes against the 120 the registry admits. The failure surfaces at environment creation, after the org and project are durable rows. Moving that check into crates/control/registry would catch it at creation time, but it narrows an already-published discipline.

## Also open

Whether the ruled namespace form needs the unique suffix PLAN:1580 requires — and if it does, whether that does not resurrect exactly the readability problem abbreviations were meant to solve.

Filed at the wave-3 close (2026-08-16), from the wamn-0h0g.15.57 evidence.
design:
OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16, wave-3 decisions):

KEEP THE SHIPPED COMPOSITE REFUSAL, ADD THE SUFFIX — AND THE ABBREVIATION PREMISE WAS MY ERROR.

.13.50 rested on registry-minted abbreviations that do not exist. I asserted machinery instead of checking the tree. WITHDRAWN, OWNED.

MINTING THEM NOW IS REJECTED: it is a naming registry with a uniqueness discipline, pure churn for aesthetics.

THE SHIPPED PROVISION-TIME COMPOSITE REFUSAL STAYS AUTHORITATIVE. It is "late" only in the sense of provision-time, which is the right time.

THE IMPORTANT HALF: an 8-CHARACTER PROVISION-MINTED INSTANCE SUFFIX, stored as one column on project_envs, appended to the namespace AND to physical resource names. That satisfies PLAN.md:1580's non-reuse requirement across delete-and-recreate with ZERO uniqueness machinery beyond randomness. The refusal formula updates to include the suffix in the 63-character bound.
close_reason: RULED by owner 2026-08-16. KEEP THE SHIPPED COMPOSITE REFUSAL, ADD THE SUFFIX — AND THE ABBREVIATION PREMISE WAS MY ERROR.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(catalog): does release_flow_test_evidence keep its test-set hash
description:
## Why

The spec says the two-artifact lineage becomes one — the draft hash now covers both flow and tests. That argues `catalog.release_flow_test_evidence.test_set_hash` should go.

wamn-0h0g.15.27 LEFT IT IN PLACE, deliberately, on three grounds: it is a `catalog.*` relation rather than one of the `authoring_test_*` relations either bead names; it is part of the explicitly RETAINED publish weld; and wamn-0h0g.15.29 is open and actively owns that table's `tested_resolution_map` columns, so touching it mid-wave risked a collision.

## The decision

Does the column go? And if so, does it go under wamn-0h0g.15.27's successor or under wamn-0h0g.15.29, which is already in that table?

## What it costs if it goes

deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql: the column, the `register_release_flow_test_evidence` signature, the `evidence_columns` drift array, and `evidence_constraints_fingerprint`. Plus crates/control/provision/tests/control_portable_store.rs's constraint counts (16/11/4/1). The fingerprint regeneration already has its own bead, so the marginal cost is small if it rides that pass.

Filed at the wave-3 close (2026-08-16).

title: [SR-MVP] fix(schema): regenerate the control-portable-store retained-shape fingerprint
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.27 changed the retained-relation set and two column lists in deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql, which invalidates the apply-time `retained_fingerprint` constant. APPLYING THE ARTIFACT NOW RAISES `control-portable-retained-shape-drift`.

`evidence_constraints_fingerprint` should still be valid — `catalog.release_flow_test_evidence` was not touched — but it is asserted in three places and is worth reconfirming in the same pass.

## Boundary

Distinct from wamn-0h0g.15.22, which regenerates the architecture registries and the gate-mutant EXPECTED_SHA baselines. This is an in-SQL apply-time constant, and the artifact will not apply until it is right — so it must land before the merge gate wamn-0h0g.15.25, not with the registries.

CORRECTION: the bead's 16/11/4/1 is the PRE-drop shape and was already in the file -- the real post-drop answer is 15/10/4/1, proven with a negative control. Two sites the scope missed would have broken it: the REVOKE's 11-type argument list, and six POSITIONAL p_test_set_hash arguments beyond the two column lists. The old retained value reproduced NOTHING, confirming the staleness came entirely from .15.27. build-and-test's DDL sha refreshed. DEFERRED TO .15.22 (frozen): protected-writes.json row + gate-mutant baselines, one of which is a DEAD ANCHOR tracked on .15.33. RISK RECORDED on .15.91: CREATE OR REPLACE with changed arity creates an OVERLOAD; an already-provisioned control DB would keep both signatures with REVOKE covering only the new one -- it fails closed on shape-drift rather than half-migrating, but no migration path exists.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(schema): retire authoring_test_sets on already-provisioned schemas
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.27 removed `wamn_run.authoring_test_sets` from the run-plane contract but did NOT add it to `RETIRED_STORED_SUITE_TABLES` / `RETIRED_STORED_SUITE_FUNCTIONS` (crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs).

Consequence for any environment provisioned before this wave: the stale table SURVIVES WITH LIVE GRANTS, and `ensure_authoring_run_privileges` no longer REVOKEs on it because the relation left the record. A dropped-from-the-record table that keeps its grants is a privilege the reconciler can no longer see.

## Scope

Retire the table and its `reject_immutable_authoring_test_set_change` helper through the existing retirement mechanism, including the DROP ordering against the FK drops the planner already emits.

## Boundary

Deliberately not folded into wamn-0h0g.15.27: that bead says delete, not retire; the retirement const's doc attributes it to wamn-0h0g.8.10 and appending would conflate two unrelated retirements; and the DROP ordering is not obviously safe without checking the planner's emitted sequence.

Filed at the wave-3 close (2026-08-16).

THE BEAD'S CENTRAL PREMISE WAS FALSE and it changed the work: 'the FK drops the planner already emits' do not exist. authoring_test_sets was the FK PARENT of two RETAINED tables; the FK reconciler walks a fixed record list with no drop-extra arm, and DropExtraConstraint sweeps only contype='c'. A bare DROP TABLE would have FAILED with a dependency error. The surviving test_set_hash columns are also text NOT NULL with no default, so leaving them would refuse every reservation and report INSERT. The cutover now emits both ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN before the parent DROP TABLE. title: [SR-MVP] test(scenarios): the case evaluator has no producer and no caller

## Scope

## Boundary

Pre-existing rather than wave-introduced. Depends on the in-draft cases bead for anything to evaluate.

Filed at the wave-3 close (2026-08-16).

Closed a LIVE defect: Captured had no validator while Expect had one, so a Captured carrying BOTH a response and a failure code satisfied both a responded AND a failed expectation; the new test fails on the pre-change tree. Neither-field-set is deliberately still accepted — five persisted fail kinds have no authorable FlowFailureKind, so that shape is legitimate. title: [SR-MVP] chore(provision): refuse an environment name that breaches the namespace bound
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.50: namespaces DERIVE from the registry-minted abbreviations, which are bounded by construction (`wamn-<org<=12>--<proj<=12>--<env>`, well under the 63-character DNS-1123 cap), and are never derived from raw names. Because the bound holds by construction there is no truncation rule — but only if nothing can mint a name that breaches it.

## Scope

Make provision refuse an environment name that would breach the bound, so the by-construction guarantee is enforced at the only point that can violate it.

## Boundary

This is the guard that makes 'derive, don't truncate' true. Without it the ruling rests on convention. Pairs with the rescoped wamn-0h0g.15.57.

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16.

Mutant-verified: unreachable bound fails that assertion only, restored sha256 d9a804ef. 67 tests pass, rustfmt clean. KNOWN GAP raised for owner: the refusal is LATE - provision-org never checks an assembled length, so the registry admits triples (120 combined bytes) that can never be provisioned (51-byte envelope), surfacing only after org and project rows are durable.

title: [SR-MVP] test(exec): hash-at-transfer verification has no producer and no coverage
description:

title: [SR-MVP] docs: amend the spec for the manifest facts the freeze established
description:
## Why

Freezing the serving manifest (wamn-0h0g.15.61) established four things the ratified spec does not say, two of which contradict what it does say.

## Scope

Amend docs/deployment-simplification-spec.md for:
1. The manifest is (release, environment)-scoped, not release-scoped, because it carries per-environment activation. (Decision filed separately.)
2. The per-flow projection carries `flow-version` in addition to the spec's three named fields — every admission path writes (flow_id, flow_version) onto the run row, so the spec's three-field list is shorthand, not exhaustive.
3. `release-manifest-<digest>` cannot be spelled literally: a Kubernetes object name is a DNS-1123 subdomain and cannot contain a colon, so the name is release-manifest-<64 hex> with the sha256: prefix stripped.
4. Mounted bytes must be EXACTLY canonical — the reader re-canonicalizes before comparing digests, so the ConfigMap value must be byte-exact with no trailing newline. This is a hard constraint on the GitOps writer.

## Boundary

Distinct from wamn-0h0g.15.24 (the charter read-through amendment of docs/scope-reduction-mvp.md). This one amends the deployment-simplification spec itself.

Filed at the wamn-0h0g.15.61 close (2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1).
design:

8. The manifest boundary must be stated as a principle, since it settles two clauses at once: THE MANIFEST CARRIES RELEASE SHAPE; ENVIRONMENT-OPERATIONAL STATE STAYS IN POSTGRES (rulings .13.52, .13.53).
9. The audit rule for what a release is: a digest is RELEASED iff a deployment attestation references it (ruling .13.54).
10. spec:98's Deleted list — 'hand-rolled host Deployment manifests' scopes to wasmCloud host Deployments only; wamn-run-worker is not one and is retained (ruling .13.46).

Two contradictions the amendments exposed were fixed with them: Tier B was ordering deletion of runner.yaml, which ruling .13.46 retains and .15.49 rewrites (delete set now stated empty); and a second 'write-once' occurrence in Tier C item 2.
