title: [SR-MVP] feat(schema): give the binding-base artifact hash a home or prove it needs none
description:
## Why

The deleted `CandidatePlanOverride` carried BOTH `draft_artifact_hash` and `source_artifact_hash` — the draft's own artifact and the binding base against which connection requirements were resolved. The frozen serving manifest (wamn-0h0g.15.61) has ONE `source-artifact` field per flow, so the binding base has no home.

The keystone judged this acceptable because the ruling moves the binding gate from per-flow claim time to pod readiness, making the binding base no longer a manifest concern. That judgement is untested.

## Scope

Either prove readiness genuinely needs only `source-artifact` (in which case record why and close), or add `binding-base-artifact` to ServingFlow before consumers land.

## Boundary

Cheap now, expensive after wamn-0h0g.15.13 and .15.12 consume the schema.

Filed at the wamn-0h0g.15.61 close (2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1).
design:
SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

NOT RULED — THE OWNER SPECIFIED A PROBE (2026-08-16). Spend the ten minutes and bring back a finding, do not rule blind.

THE PROBE: bindings are keyed by ARTIFACT HASH, and a candidate flow's artifact hash DIFFERS from the released one its bindings were bound under. The specific test is therefore whether a candidate manifest's readiness/binding resolution MISSES bindings keyed to the prior artifact.

IF IT DOES, the fix direction is keying bindings by (catalog, requirement, flow identity) rather than by artifact hash — artifact-hash keying may itself be pinning-era residue that this ruling's 'no version pinning' premise has already invalidated.

Report the finding; the keying change is a separate ruling.

PROBE EXECUTED (2026-08-16, wave 3). VERDICT: **YES — the miss is real, and it is structural rather than incidental.**

WHY IT MISSES BY CONSTRUCTION. A candidate flow's own artifact hash can NEVER have a connection_bindings row, on four independent DDL facts:
  1. connection_bindings FK-requires a matching connection_requirements row (catalog-schema.sql:1175-1177).
  2. connection_requirements has a BEFORE INSERT trigger requiring the artifact_hash to exist in catalog.flow_artifacts (catalog-schema.sql:1054-1073).
  3. A draft artifact is never written to flow_artifacts — pinned by an assertion inside the validated-draft insert itself (services/scenario-worker/src/store/drafts.rs:193). It cannot be: flow_artifacts PK is (tenant_id, flow_id, flow_version) and register_flow_artifact raises flow-version-content-conflict for different content at the same coordinate (catalog-schema.sql:108, :159-173).
  4. The binding insert trigger require_binding_release_environment additionally demands the artifact be a RELEASE MEMBER (catalog-schema.sql:1203-1214); a candidate is by definition not one.

THAT THE TWO HASHES DIFFER IS A STORED, TESTED INVARIANT, NOT A HYPOTHESIS. catalog.validated_flow_drafts carries draft_artifact_hash AND binding_base_artifact_hash as separate NOT NULL columns, both inside the exact-pin unique constraint (catalog-schema.sql:492-504). The base is read from the released member (drafts.rs:64-77, whose own doc says that member "supplies its existing connection bindings but never supplies the graph executed by the draft run"), populated at authoring.rs:937, and asserted equal to the release artifact hash by a live test at services/scenario-worker/tests/authoring_loop_live.rs:248 — which pins the candidate at flow_version 2 against a released flow_version 1.

THE BINDING KEY AS BUILT: PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, artifact_hash, requirement_name) at catalog-schema.sql:1158-1180. connection_requirements is keyed (tenant_id, artifact_hash, requirement_name) at :1041.

WHERE IT BREAKS IN SHIPPED CODE: claims.rs:211-216 joins connection_bindings on artifact_hash = $7, and :194-197 joins connection_requirements on the same $7. $7 is guest-supplied source_artifact_hash (connection_http.rs:111) — and it is FORCED to the flow's own artifact, because flowrunner refuses the snapshot with run-resolution-source-mismatch unless plan.header.root_artifact_hash equals it (components/execution/flowrunner/src/lib.rs:122-124), while a draft plan's root_artifact_hash is compiled from the DRAFT's artifact (authoring.rs:879-884). Result: both joins go NULL, and every effectful candidate run refuses at its first HTTP effect with UndeclaredRequirement (connection_http.rs:226-228), Unbound behind it.

*** THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT ***
`source-artifact` IS ALREADY DOUBLE-DUTY, AND THE TWO DUTIES DEMAND DIFFERENT VALUES FOR A CANDIDATE:
  - As PLAN-INTEGRITY ANCHOR it must equal the plan's own root-artifact-hash — enforced live in TWO places, flowrunner/src/lib.rs:122 and crates/events/materializer/src/lib.rs:77-79.
  - As BINDING KEY it must equal the RELEASED base — asserted in the very next sentence of its own doc comment, serving_manifest.rs:137-139.
ONE FIELD CANNOT SATISFY BOTH FOR A CANDIDATE. Set it to the draft artifact and readiness plus effect authority miss; set it to the binding base and flowrunner and the materializer refuse the plan.

PREMISE CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD AND TO THE RULING:
1. "The ruling moves the binding gate to readiness, so the binding base is no longer a manifest concern" is FALSE. The ruling RETAINS the effect-time binding gate verbatim (spec:67-69; docs/flow-execution-amendment.md:284-291 states the chain is unchanged), and the artifact-hash-keyed lookup survives in shipped code at claims.rs:211-216. Readiness is an ADDITIONAL gate, so moving it doubles the sites needing the base rather than removing them.
2. "The binding base has no home" is true only of the MANIFEST. It has a durable home already: validated_flow_drafts.binding_base_artifact_hash (catalog-schema.sql:495), mirrored at control-portable-store.sql:164 and migrated at run_plane.rs:2391-2395. What is missing is only its CARRIAGE into the mounted candidate manifest. That materially narrows the fix.
3. "Artifact-hash keying may be pinning-era residue" is HALF right. It does three jobs beyond pinning: it is the FK that makes a requirement_name identifiable at all (requirements are artifact-owned, :1032-1042); it forces a fresh binding decision when a flow's content changes; and it is what the release-membership trigger proves membership with (:1203-1214). Only the assumption that an executing flow's artifact is always a RELEASED artifact is pinning-era — and candidate execution is exactly what breaks it.
4. THE RULING'S PROPOSED REKEY NEEDS A NARROWER "FLOW IDENTITY" THAN IT SOUNDS. A candidate also carries a different flow_version (2 vs 1). So (catalog, requirement, flow identity) fixes the miss ONLY if flow identity means flow_id ALONE; (flow_id, flow_version) misses exactly as badly as the artifact hash does.

COST OF THE REKEY, IF RULED: DDL — connection_bindings PK + both FKs + the require_binding_release_environment trigger (:1158-1224); connection_requirements PK, which is artifact-keyed and must itself be rekeyed or the FK dropped; drift registries at run_plane.rs:1984, :5332, :5361, :5390, :5416, :6493. Code — connections.rs:163-191, claims.rs:158-231 plus its shape tests, serving_manifest.rs:133-140.
THE EXPENSIVE PART IS NOT SQL: the effect path has NO FLOW IDENTITY TO KEY ON. The WIT invocation-context carries no flow-id (wamn-runner/package.wit:68-78, mirrored in the flowrunner copy), nor does HttpEffectPrincipal (invocation_context.rs:104-112), nor does the effect_attempts table (run-state.sql:440-452). runs.flow_id is the ROOT flow only, so it cannot serve a callee frame. The flowrunner does have it. So the rekey is a FROZEN-WIT wire change plus DDL plus migration, not a SQL edit.
MIGRATION COST IS LOWER THAN IT LOOKS: there is no production writer for connection_bindings or connection_requirements anywhere in the tree — insert_connection_binding_sql is called only from tests. No publish-path writer to change, no populated table to migrate.

THE CHEAPER ALTERNATIVE THE PROBE SURFACED (and this bead's own title anticipated): add a per-flow `binding-base-artifact` to ServingFlow, defaulting to `source-artifact` for released members and carrying the released base only for the candidate overlay. One field in an unconsumed frozen type; the binding key and BOTH plan verifiers stay intact; the value already exists in validated_flow_drafts.binding_base_artifact_hash.
IT IS ALSO SAFE AGAINST A DRIFTED DRAFT: claims.rs:200-205 compares the plan node's source-connection-requirement descriptor against the stored requirement_json, so a draft that CHANGES a requirement fails closed as node-not-permitted rather than authorizing under the base. That check is why base-substitution is not a hole — worth recording whichever way this is ruled.

WHAT COULD NOT BE DETERMINED: what the deleted CandidatePlanOverride assigned to each of its two fields (the type is gone; only a removal assertion survives at production_claim.rs:723-730) — though the schema makes only one assignment coherent. Also, READINESS DOES NOT EXIST YET: no implementation is in the tree, so that half of the verdict rests on the specified contract rather than shipped code. If readiness is built as specified, a candidate manifest's pods NEVER BECOME READY, and the scratch Job of ratification ruling 1 cannot run at all.

AWAITING OWNER RULING. Per the owner's instruction the keying change is a separate ruling; this bead stays open on the finding. The dep edges to .15.12 and .15.13 already prevent consumers landing first.

SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

RULED: ADD THE FIELD.

`binding_base_artifact` on `ServingFlow`, defaulting to `source_artifact` for released members, sourced from the existing `catalog.validated_flow_drafts.binding_base_artifact_hash`.

THE REKEY IS REJECTED ON THIS BEAD'S OWN FINDINGS: keying by `flow_id` alone changes binding semantics platform-wide, and making the effect path carry flow identity is a FROZEN-WIT WIRE CHANGE IN THE MIDDLE OF A DEMOLITION — maximal churn for a problem one manifest field dissolves.

DOCUMENTATION RIDER, so the double-duty never recurs silently: the manifest field docs must NAME BOTH CONSUMERS EXPLICITLY — plan verifiers read `source_artifact` (flowrunner's root-artifact-hash check and the materializer's), binding resolution reads `binding_base_artifact` — and must record that the drift case fails closed on the descriptor comparison at claims.rs:200-205, as this bead's probe verified.

This bead is now ordinary implementation work: the field, its default, the docs, and the digest/field-classification tests that pin every key set by design.
close_reason: SHIPPED 7ac775ef. binding_base_artifact added to ServingFlow as a REQUIRED non-Option field per the owner ruling; rekey rejected. A serde default cannot express the ruled default (defaults cannot read a sibling field) and required is the only shape that forces .15.14's mint to decide released-vs-candidate at construction. No released() constructor on purpose. Documentation rider honoured: both consumers named, fail-closed descriptor comparison documented. Every manifest digest moves, which costs nothing since nothing mints one yet. CORRECTIONS: CanonicalJson does not interact at all (guards definition documents only); lib.rs needed no change; the source column carries only CHECK(<>'') so the mint is a NARROWING point, not a pass-through. Three prose sites carrying the per-flow projection updated (2 in plane-amendment.md here, 1 in the spec).

title: [SR-MVP] test(deploy): quantify the release manifest against the NATS payload budget
description:
## Why

For operator-scheduled Workloads (flow-http, materializer) the release manifest is NOT kubelet-mounted. The operator reads the ConfigMap from the workload namespace and ships the merged config map to the host over NATS in WorkloadStart (runtime-operator workload_controller.go:69,:79,:303 -> utils.go:158-181), against the 1 MiB NATS server default (the chart sets no max_payload). If a real manifest does not fit, those two workloads need manifest-by-OCI-pull instead of configFrom.

## Scope

Measure a representative release manifest against the budget and record the headroom.

## Boundary

Distinct from wamn-0h0g.15.46, which bounds the manifest against the ~1 MiB ConfigMap/etcd object limit. This one is the NATS transport limit on a different delivery path. Needs a real manifest or a running NATS, and the kind cluster is frozen this wave.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
close_reason: Closed with wamn-0h0g.15.63 in commit c240c4a4, paired with .15.46 because the two size bounds only mean something together. QUANTIFIED: ~553 bytes per member flow, ~1,360 per flow carrying one HTTP attachment and one registration, 772 fully-attached flows to fill 1 MiB exactly. A 100-flow release is 135,989 bytes = 13% of budget, ~7.7x headroom -- so flow-http and the materializer do NOT need manifest-by-OCI-pull and configFrom is fine. WHICH BOUND BINDS: NATS. Both caps are the same number (1048576), but the ConfigMap cap covers the manifest bytes ALONE while the NATS cap covers the whole published message including headers, and on the operator-scheduled path the manifest rides inside a WorkloadStart envelope -- so MAX_SERVING_MANIFEST_BYTES is necessary but NOT sufficient there. Deliberately no invented envelope reserve subtracted from the constant: picking one would be exactly the undocumented magic these beads exist to remove. The envelope's own size is the one thing unmeasurable without a live cluster.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(deploy): namespace naming rule and DNS-1123 truncation
description:
## Why

The wamn-0h0g.15.3 verdict maps one environment `(org, project, env)` to one Kubernetes namespace. Namespace names are DNS-1123 labels capped at 63 characters and there is no truncation rule today, so long triples collide or are rejected at apply time. The `--` separator already landed in deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh:92, and crates/events/wire/src/lib.rs:132 already implements a hash-suffix truncation for subject tokens — the same pattern applies.

## Scope

Fix the namespace naming function and its truncation rule, reusing the existing hash-suffix pattern, and pin it with a test.

## Boundary

The naming form itself (double-dash versus single-dash separator) is an owner choice — see the decision filed alongside this bead.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
design:
SCOPED BY OWNER RULING (dkk, 2026-08-16):

RESCOPED BY RULING .13.50 — THERE IS NO TRUNCATION RULE TO WRITE.

Namespaces derive from the REGISTRY-MINTED ABBREVIATIONS, which are bounded by construction: `wamn-<org<=12>--<proj<=12>--<env>` sits well under the 63-character DNS-1123 cap. They are NEVER derived from raw names.

The work is therefore: derive the namespace from the registry abbreviations, and make PROVISION REFUSE an environment name that would breach the bound. Delete the hash-suffix truncation approach from this bead's plan — it was the right answer to the wrong question.
close_reason: Landed at dfd4c034. project_env_namespace derives wamn-<org>--<project>--<env> in crates/control/provision/src/name.rs beside the wamn-db-/wamn-cdc- family, with its own MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN. No truncation, no hash suffix. Zero call sites redirected: nothing in the tree derives a per-environment namespace today (wamn-system is flat and hardcoded); consumers are .15.15 and .15.16. PREMISE FAILURE RECORDED: the ruling's '<=12 registry-minted abbreviations, bounded by construction' does not hold - no abbreviation columns exist, components are 40-byte raw slugs (system-schema.sql orgs/projects/env_policies checks, MAX_ID_LEN in control/registry), assembled name reaches 129 bytes vs a 63 cap. The <=12 figure is the tenant key settled in docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md, which has no schema and no code. Needs owner re-ruling.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(publish): name the minting pod's flowrunner source
description:
## Why

Ruling 1's per-report scratch Job and the wamn-0h0g.8.18 management-to-control authoring move both need exact flowrunner bytes locally present. The deployed scenario-worker refuses validate for lack of them (services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs:691-695) and its image ships none (Dockerfile:223-228). Unowned across the current bead set.

## Scope

Name where the minting pod gets flowrunner bytes from, and wire it.

## Boundary

Surfaced by spike wamn-0h0g.15.4; independent of whether flowrunner ships in-image (which it does, per that verdict).

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.4 report.
close_reason: Minting pod carries the flowrunner bytes (4bee577a). The scenario-worker image COPYs the same locked-builder component at the same path the run-worker loads, so the two agree on the digest by construction rather than via a skew detector; the process refuses to start without them and no transport can choose them. Premise corrected: the cited line is a doc comment, not a runtime check — the deployed worker refused validate because the ROUTE IS UNMOUNTED, so shipping bytes does not make validate work. Mounting it is .7.4's. The docker provenance guard gained the second COPY.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(publish): mint-time size assertion on the release manifest
description:
## Why

catalog.execution_bundles has no byte cap (deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql:180-193) but a ConfigMap is bounded at roughly 1 MiB. Without an assertion at mint, an oversized release manifest passes the control-plane gate and then fails at deploy — the gate would have certified something undeployable.

## Scope

Assert the canonical manifest byte length against the ConfigMap/etcd object limit inside the mint transaction.

## Boundary

Ruling 4 makes the digest-named ConfigMap the serving path, which is what imports the limit.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.2 report.
close_reason: Closed with wamn-0h0g.15.63 in commit c240c4a4. SCOPE CORRECTED: there is NO MINT to assert inside -- no publish/ctl path constructs a ServingManifest, and ::new appears only in weld fixtures (the mint is .15.14, blocked). The bound went ON THE TYPE instead, which is better anyway: MAX_SERVING_MANIFEST_BYTES = 1 MiB next to the mount constants, refused in ServingManifest::new so the unlanded mint inherits it, and at the top of from_canonical_bytes before parsing so the reader side is covered too. New CatalogIdentityError::ManifestTooLarge, safe because that enum has zero consumers outside its crate and the weld already funnels every variant through Display into ManifestRejected. TWO MORE PREMISE CORRECTIONS: catalog.execution_bundles is the wrong relation (it stores execution PLAN bytes; the serving manifest has no table at all) and it does carry a byte_length CHECK, just no cap; and 'roughly 1 MiB' is exactly 1048576 counting len(value) over data+binaryData ONLY -- keys and metadata are NOT counted, so the manifest bytes get the whole allowance, and etcd's 1.5 MiB never binds. Both limits documented with their sources per M-DOCUMENTED-MAGIC. 4 asserts, each killed by a distinct mutation.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(deploy): durable OCI registry posture or re-push reconciler
description:
## Why

The dev registry is emptyDir (deploy/platform/registry.yaml:17-19). A registry pod restart loses every plan blob, and readiness prefetch then fails cluster-wide until republish. The spec accepts an OCI AVAILABILITY trade (line 113); this is availability AND durability.

## Scope

Either give the registry durable storage, or build the re-push reconciler that ruling 2 makes possible — the OCI copy is idempotently re-derivable from the authoritative catalog.execution_bundles.

## Boundary

Ruling 2 keeps catalog.execution_bundles as the authoritative bytes home, which is exactly what makes a reconciler cheap.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.2 report.
close_reason: Commit 82a4bf90. Durable storage chosen over the re-push reconciler: PVC registry-data (RWO, 2Gi, no storageClassName -- matching the repo's only two other PVC consumers; a tree-wide grep for storageClassName returns zero) plus strategy: Recreate, which the RWO swap REQUIRES (the default rolling update deadlocks because the incoming pod cannot mount a claim its predecessor holds). NOT APPLIABLE AS CHECKED IN header added following runner.yaml's convention: a plain apply is REJECTED against the live Deployment (defaulted strategy.rollingUpdate cannot coexist with type: Recreate and a strategic merge will not remove it), so adoption needs a DESTRUCTIVE delete then apply then a re-push of every artifact. Recorded in-file what the PVC does NOT solve: one replica on one RWO volume is still a full plan-pull outage on node drain/loss, and on a node-local default StorageClass losing the node IS losing the volume; the reconciler survives volume loss and remains the better eventual answer, it just needs a service to live in.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(exec): re-home ResolutionPlanCache ahead of the artifact-reader deletion
description:
## Why

control_artifact_reader is scheduled for wholesale deletion by wamn-0h0g.15.12, but it is not self-contained: runner_plan_supply.rs:23-24 imports ResolutionPlanCache and InvalidPlanCacheLimit from it, and runner_plan_supply is one of the five surviving executor plugins. Deleting the file wholesale breaks a survivor.

## Scope

Move ResolutionPlanCache (and InvalidPlanCacheLimit) to a home that survives the deletion, before or within wamn-0h0g.15.12.

## Boundary

Makes the wamn-0h0g.15.12 deletion less cheap than the spec implies. Both wave-1 investigations independently flagged the cache as a keep.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.6 report.
close_reason: Commit e4996633. ResolutionPlanCache and InvalidPlanCacheLimit moved into runner_plan_supply.rs, their single surviving consumer, rather than into a new sibling module: after the .15.12 deletion the cache has exactly one consumer, runner_plan_supply was already the public face of InvalidPlanCacheLimit via a re-export, and the cache's three unit tests already lived in its test module. The public path plugins::runner_plan_supply::InvalidPlanCacheLimit is byte-identical before and after and plugins/mod.rs is untouched, so no external consumer moves. runner_plan_supply no longer names control_artifact_reader anywhere, which is the property .15.12 needs; the dependency is now inverted and evaporates on deletion. Verified structurally (five checks: zero back-references, symbol definitions relocated, import direction inverted, complete repo-wide importer enumeration, mod.rs untouched) and by compiling — cargo check -p wamn-runtime --all-targets reports no error in either changed file. One visibility widening recorded for .15.12 to revert: from_non_zero private -> pub(crate). Five deletion obligations and one cross-lane hazard (runner_plan_supply.rs:14 imports RunResolutionMetadata from wamn_postgres, which .15.10 is rewriting) folded into .15.12's design field as obligations of that bead.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(wit): give wamn:flow-invocation begin/wait an error channel
description:
## Why

The one real no-trap gap found by gate B. wamn:flow-invocation/invocation declares NO error channel: begin returns a variant (admitted|rejected) and wait an option, neither a result. Every host-side failure is therefore converted to a wasm trap via wasmtime::Error::msg — a transient DB failure traps and poisons the flow-http ingress instance instead of returning a rejection.

## Scope

Give begin and wait result-shaped returns with a WIT-shaped error enum, per the repository convention at WIT boundaries.

## Boundary

Pre-existing and NOT pin-caused — the contract never had a result. flow_invocation is not among the five executor plugins gate B covers. A WIT change, so it interacts with Tier C item 4 (the flow-http leg).

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.6 report.
close_reason: Error channel landed (7da5a70d). variant invocation-error with four payload-free arms, each earned by real call sites rather than invented; rejection stays SEPARATE because it is an answer with a durable status and frozen code, while this is the platform declining to decide — collapsing either way would fabricate a decision or strip a code the caller needs, and two tests exist to stop that simplification. ONE wire enum: the runtime's InvocationFailure is a contextual struct whose kind IS that enum, translated exactly once at the plugin with the context logged and stopped there. The bug was worse than filed: Error::msg also LEAKED raw host error text including DB messages to the guest. Both closed. Frozen package amended in place at 0.1.0 with the reason in the WIT header rather than bumped. The pure adapter needed no change — its 503 paths existed and were merely unreachable — which is why the ripple is 11 files not 20. Carve-out to tests/conformance/src/invocation.rs applied.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(egress): outgoing_request_p3 skips the connection-derived narrowing
description:
## Why

RunnerEgress overrides outgoing_request (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:302-341, which applies allowed_hosts AND the connection-derived policy) but NOT outgoing_request_p3, so the p3 egress path skips the wamn-fqg.11 connection-derived narrowing.

## Scope

Apply the same narrowing to the p3 path, or prove the p3 path is unreachable and pin that.

## Boundary

Surfaced by gate A (wamn-0h0g.15.5); independent of the fork pin.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.5 report.
close_reason: SHIPPED ad34415f. Narrowing applied to outgoing_request_p3 AND the unreachability proven -- both, deliberately. CORRECTION: the inherited trait default is NOT 'no policy'; it calls check_allowed_hosts, so the host allowlist was already enforced. Three things were skipped and the bead named one: the connection-derived narrowing, self.inner ENTIRELY (the default calls default_send_request directly, dropping the configured handler -- the fork's own HttpServer does not do this), and the MAX_HOST_CALL_DURATION clamp. NEW SECOND UNREACHABILITY PROOF, stronger than the world-import one: crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs registers only the p2 linkers and never p3::add_to_linker, so a guest importing wasi:http 0.3 fails instantiate_pre LOUDLY. Applied anyway because that is ONE line nothing pins in a compiled way, the fork's engine adds p3 in three places, and the p2 sibling is equally unreachable yet enforced deliberately. DISCLOSED GAP filed as .15.87: no timeout clamp -- p3 defaults None to 600s against p2's 30s and the epoch deadline does not interrupt an awaited host call. *** NOT COMPILED OR TESTED: wamn-execution-host depends on wamn-runtime, which does not build at this baseline (.15.12's 4 known errors). This change is UNVERIFIED BY THE COMPILER and must be re-checked when .15.12 lands. ***

title: [SR-MVP] chore(test-contract): sweep the now-vacuous resolution-map-mismatch failure family
description:
## Why

After wamn-0h0g.15.7 the surviving case-vs-reservation comparison legs (deploy/sql/authoring-tests.sql:362-370), the resolution-map-mismatch failure_kind CHECK (:140), the every_map_matches report aggregate (:392-396, :407, :414), TestCaseFailure::ResolutionMapMismatch and TestCaseFinalization.resolution_map compare maps that can no longer diverge. finalize_test_case has zero in-tree callers.

title: [SR-MVP] test(battery): p0 deltas — reader role removed, write-once columns covered
description:
## Why

Tier D battery deltas, settled by ratification ruling 6: the artifact-reader role leaves the live probes and the two claim-time columns need coverage. The name p0 battery retires with the archived p0-* artifacts — the two live homes below are the deliverable.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(dispatch): wake signal as operator CRD patch
description:
## Why

Host/workload scaling is operator territory (hostReplicas / workload scalers). The dispatcher wake signal becomes a CRD patch, replacing the waker actuator — the named trigger for the waker deletion.

## Scope

Give the dispatcher wake path a CRD-patch actuation (scale the target workload/host replicas from zero via the operator surface) with the same doorbell semantics the waker provides today. Prove wake-from-zero on the operator path. Supersedes held wamn-fqg.40, whose scoping questions (which scale subresource; operator/HPA/KEDA elimination of the native actuator) resolve here.

## Boundary

Waker code deletion is the trigger bead dep-blocked on this one. M2 check clause rewrites ride the deletion bead. Post-merge train — not required for the wave RC.
notes: FALSE-READY MEASUREMENT (2026-08-23 at pushed 82617b9e): the repository exposes no operator CRD whose patch scales host-group replicas. The only runtime.wasmcloud.dev CRs are WorkloadDeployment objects, whose spec.replicas scales component workload instances; host-group replicas remain a Helm value (deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml runtime.hostGroups[].replicas) rendered as a Kubernetes Deployment. The current waker wakes the executor/host Deployment through deployments/scale. Replacing it with a 'CRD patch' therefore needs the exact operator resource and field named (or a ruling that direct Deployment/scale remains the actuation); patching WorkloadDeployment would change the wrong grain. Do not implement a CRD-looking wake against the component replica field. Continue scanning.

title: [SR-MVP] spike(exec): flowrunner as operator Workload vs in-image
description:
## Why

Spec open verification item: whether flowrunner ships as an operator-scheduled Workload (revision changes without host-image rebuilds) or stays in-image for MVP (provider changes force rebuilds regardless). Shapes the Host CRD content in the operator-adoption bead.

## Scope

Weigh Workload scheduling of flowrunner.wasm against in-image shipping for MVP: rebuild cost, revision identity (the pod carries release identity either way), readiness interaction. Written verdict with a recommendation.

## Boundary

Investigation only.
design:
WAVE-1 VERDICT (2026-08-16, branch deploy-simplification, sub-epic wamn-0h0g.15): FLOWRUNNER STAYS IN-IMAGE FOR MVP — no operator Workload/Artifact entry for it.

The Workload option is not a packaging swap but a redesign: a new trigger for a custom export, migrating four executor-only plugins into wamn-host, and relocating the native claim loop — which spec:24-27 forbids ("adoption is substitution, not redesign"). Its advertised benefit is illusory: the plan header binds `flowrunner_component_digest`, so every flowrunner revision forces a re-mint plus revalidate->republish regardless of shipping shape. It would also re-open exactly the artifact/pod skew window ruling 4 abolished, after Tier C deletes the only detector. flowrunner stays at Dockerfile:219 (/components/flowrunner.wasm) with runner.yaml's `--flowrunner /components/flowrunner.wasm` unchanged; only flow-http and materializer remain operator-scheduled workloads.

TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS that wamn-0h0g.15.15 and .15.18 must absorb (tracked as wamn-0h0g.15.48):
1. The operator's `Host` CR is OBSERVED state written by the operator from host heartbeats (host_controller.go:223-270); the Host type carries no image, replicas, or podTemplate (host_types.go:38-56). "Author Host CRDs carrying our custom host images" is not achievable. Images enter via the chart's `runtime.hostGroups[].image`; Host CRs then appear as inventory.
2. `wamn-run-worker` is not a wasmCloud host at all — no ClusterHost, no heartbeat, its own entrypoint and CLI, plus DB/credential/effect-writer/egress volumes and a native claim loop. It cannot become a chart hostGroup this wave.

CONSUMER IMPACT.
- wamn-0h0g.15.15: rescope to pinning the operator chart per environment and setting runtime.hostGroups[].image for the wamn-host host groups.
- wamn-0h0g.15.18: BLOCKED as written. deploy/platform/runner.yaml has no operator Host CRD replacement, so deleting it removes the executor with nothing standing in its place. It must be REWRITTEN (mount the digest-named manifest, add the readiness gate, drop resolution-map/artifact-reader leftovers) — filed as wamn-0h0g.15.49, which now blocks .15.18. scenario-worker.yaml is in the same position. The bead's scope may in fact be EMPTY under the narrow reading of spec:98 — see decision wamn-0h0g.13.46.
- wamn-0h0g.15.13 SIMPLIFIED for leg 1: with flowrunner in-image the executor pod mounts the digest-named ConfigMap on its own filesystem and serves adjacency plus plan bytes to the guest over the EXISTING trusted `wamn:runner/plan-supply` channel (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:473) — no new host interface, no new WIT, no guest world change. Legs 2 (materializer) and 3 (flow-http) are unaffected and stay the hard ones; flow-http IS an operator Workload, so its manifest-derived routes must arrive through the first host-side `wamn:flow-http-routing` implementation configured via hostInterfaces, not a workload volume.

RISKS ACCEPTED: flowrunner revisions are locked to executor image rebakes for MVP (the re-mint plus revalidate->republish->drain cost dominates the rebake, and the rebake is fully BuildKit-cached). Two conformance guards pin the in-image shape (docker_component_provenance.rs:44-64, effect_provider_revision.rs:1377-1450) — protective under this verdict, and any later reversal must delete both in the same commit.

DEFERRALS FILED: wamn-0h0g.15.48 (tracker premise correction), .15.49 (rewrite runner.yaml, blocks .15.18), .15.50 (name the minting pod's flowrunner source — the deployed scenario-worker refuses validate for lack of bytes, management.rs:691-695), .15.51 (OCI-pull flowrunner by digest, demand-gated). OWNER DECISION FILED: wamn-0h0g.13.46 (operator adoption boundary: Deleted-list scope, and whether the executor stays outside operator management for MVP).
close_reason: Verdict recorded in the design field. flowrunner STAYS IN-IMAGE for MVP — the Workload option is a redesign (new trigger for a custom export, four plugins migrated, claim loop relocated), which spec:24-27 forbids, and its benefit is illusory because the plan header binds flowrunner_component_digest so every revision re-mints anyway. Two premise corrections land on .15.15/.15.18: the operator Host CR is OBSERVED heartbeat state with no image/replicas/podTemplate, and wamn-run-worker is not a wasmCloud host at all. Simplifies wamn-0h0g.15.13 leg 1 to the existing plan-supply channel. Deferrals: .15.48 .15.49 (now blocks .15.18) .15.50 .15.51; decision .13.46.

title: [SR-MVP] spike(deploy): namespace-per-environment under operator tenancy
description:
## Why

Spec open verification item: namespace-per-environment mapping under the runtime-operator tenancy assumptions. Wrong-target protection is namespace/context targeting, so the GitOps convergence bead needs this settled.

## Scope

Verify how the operator scopes Host/Workload reconciliation across namespaces at v2.7.0, what a per-environment namespace means for NATS topology and Secret placement, and record the mapping rule. Written verdict.

## Boundary

Investigation only.
design:
WAVE-1 VERDICT (2026-08-16, branch deploy-simplification, sub-epic wamn-0h0g.15): MAPPING RULE: one wamn environment (org, project, env) = ONE KUBERNETES NAMESPACE, named `wamn-<org>--<project>--<env>`. The `--` separator already landed at deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh:92; the DNS-1123 63-character label cap needs the hash-suffix truncation rule that crates/events/wire/src/lib.rs:132 already implements for subject tokens (filed as wamn-0h0g.15.57; naming form is decision wamn-0h0g.13.50).

OPERATOR INSTALL: ONE PER CLUSTER, in wamn-system — NOT one per environment. Three independent facts force this.
(a) OPERATOR_NAMESPACE is mandatory and every Host CR is written there regardless of where the host pod runs (runtime-operator cmd/main.go:161-167, host_controller.go:245), so two operators on one NATS would each build a duplicate host registry and race each other's scheduling.
(b) The operator connects to exactly one -nats-url (cmd/main.go:95) and the wire has no lattice/tenant prefix — subjects are flat `runtime.operator.heartbeat.>` (host_controller.go:205) and `runtime.host.<hostID>.*` (host_client.go:31-37) — so per-environment operators would require per-environment NATS.
(c) The five CRDs live in charts/runtime-operator/crds/, which Helm installs once and never upgrades, and they are cluster-scoped; a second release cannot carry a different CRD version.

TENANCY IS NOT HOST NAMESPACE — IT IS Host.Environment. All five CRDs are scope: Namespaced, but Host CRs are forcibly relocated into the operator namespace, and tenant attribution rides the .environment field, stamped by the chart from the host pod's own namespace via the downward API (runtime/deployment.yaml:135-138,:162 -> host_types.go:49-53). Everything else in the chain — WorkloadDeployment -> WorkloadReplicaSet -> Workload -> Artifact -> ConfigMap/Secret/Service/EndpointSlice — is strictly same-namespace; cross-namespace reference is not even expressible (corev1.LocalObjectReference is name-only).

NATS: CLUSTER SINGLETON in wamn-system, shared by every environment. The control-plane/scheduler bus must be shared because the operator has one bus and all hosts must heartbeat onto it. Isolation is not on the bus — it is the Host.Environment match. Hosts in environment namespaces dial cross-namespace to nats://nats.wamn-system.svc.cluster.local:4222, already the chart's overridable default (_helpers.tpl:172). The data-plane evt-nats also stays a singleton: it is already tenant-scoped by stream name EVT_<org>_<env> (crates/events/wire/src/lib.rs:126-128) and must NOT be duplicated.

SECRETS: same namespace as the consuming Workload, no exceptions. Registry pull credentials and DB credentials both replicate per environment namespace. Bundled TLS Secrets follow host groups automatically when runtime.hostGroups[].namespace is set.

release-manifest-<digest> ConfigMap: the ENVIRONMENT namespace — but via two different mechanics. For wamn's own Deployments the kubelet mounts it from the pod's namespace. For operator-scheduled Workloads (flow-http, materializer) there is NO kubelet mount: the operator reads the ConfigMap from workload.Namespace and ships the merged map to the host over NATS in WorkloadStart (workload_controller.go:69,:79,:303 -> utils.go:158-181), so the bytes must fit the NATS payload limit (chart sets no max_payload, so the 1 MiB default applies) — filed as wamn-0h0g.15.59. Ruling 4's atomicity still holds: the Workload object carries image and configFrom digest name together, so changing either rolls a new WorkloadReplicaSet.

WRONG-TARGET PROTECTION — four locks, ranked by load:
1. `operator.allowSharedHosts: false`. THE LOAD-BEARING LOCK, and it SHIPS TRUE. With false, a Workload can only land on a Host whose .environment equals its own namespace; explicit cross-env targeting is rejected with a CrossEnvironmentSchedulingDenied Warning Event plus HostSelection=False (workload_controller.go:144-166). The chart's own values.yaml calls the default "permissive across tenants" and describes exactly the attack (values.yaml:165-180). LEAVING THE DEFAULT MAKES THE WHOLE MAPPING COSMETIC.
2. Host.Environment from the downward API — not forgeable from the Workload side. Caveat: the operator takes it verbatim from the heartbeat and does not validate it against cluster state (host_controller.go:231-234), so this is a GitOps/RBAC boundary, not a cryptographic one.
3. `operator.watchNamespaces` plus namespaced RBAC. Setting it drops the ClusterRole entirely in favour of per-namespace Roles; a namespace not in the list gets no reconciliation — manifests apply cleanly and sit inert. That stops a mis-targeted apply from taking effect, but SILENTLY.
4. GitOps destination plus namespace-stripped manifests. A manifest with no `namespace:` cannot land in the wrong one by accident, only by an explicitly wrong destination.
Plus a cheap fifth wamn already half-has: label the namespace wamn.org/wamn.project/wamn.env (keys bootstrap.sh:99-101 already verifies) and have readiness assert they equal the pod's WAMN_ORG/WAMN_PROJECT/WAMN_ENVIRONMENT (services/executor/src/lib.rs:68-76) — wrong-target becomes "pod never ready" instead of "converged silently", and it proves in a fresh namespace with zero cluster state (wamn-0h0g.15.60).

CONSUMER IMPACT.
- wamn-0h0g.15.16: the namespace is the convergence unit — one Argo/Flux Application per environment namespace. Strip literal `namespace:` from every per-environment manifest and let the GitOps destination supply it.
- wamn-0h0g.15.15: install ONE operator in wamn-system, never one per environment. Required values settings, none of which exist today: operator.watchNamespaces, operator.allowSharedHosts: false, operator.hostNamespaces, and one runtime.hostGroups[] entry per environment carrying namespace: <env ns>. Host tier shape is decision wamn-0h0g.13.50.
- wamn-0h0g.15.17: the registry itself stays a cluster singleton in wamn-system — it is pulled FROM, needs no per-env copy, and its in-cluster FQDN resolves from any namespace. Pull CREDENTIALS are the opposite: one dockerconfigjson Secret replicated into every environment namespace, with no cluster-wide alternative.

REJECTED FOR MVP (recorded, not deferred): per-environment control-plane NATS (forces an operator per environment, which collides with the CRD singleton); per-environment evt-nats (already tenant-scoped by stream name — duplicating it would be actively harmful); multiple orgs/projects sharing one namespace (expressible via the landed naming, but re-opens the wrong-target hole spec:51-52 closes); cross-namespace host sharing with allowSharedHosts=true (a real v2.7.0 capability and the direction the chart defaults toward, but the exact inverse of this isolation posture).

RISKS: allowSharedHosts defaults permissive (above); Host.Environment is unvalidated heartbeat data, so a host started with a hand-set --environment claims any environment it likes; onboarding an environment is a chart upgrade, not a pure GitOps apply, and an unwatched namespace fails silently; bare-podSelector NetworkPolicies (deploy/platform/runner-netpol.yaml:35-58) restrict egress to same-namespace peers and break against the wamn-system singletons — the runner starts, pulls its image, and fails at connect (wamn-0h0g.15.58); the chart 2.5.2 -> 2.7.0 pin is a hard prerequisite of .15.15, coupling operator adoption to the fork-sync gates.

DEFERRALS FILED: wamn-0h0g.15.57 (naming/truncation), .15.58 (NetworkPolicy namespace split), .15.59 (manifest vs NATS payload budget), .15.60 (namespace-label readiness cross-check). OWNER DECISIONS FILED: wamn-0h0g.13.49 (the CRD singleton contradicts spec:117-120's per-environment operator version pin — the clause needs amending), .13.50 (namespace naming form and host tier shape), .13.51 (what 'fresh namespace' means for the RC validation).
close_reason: Verdict recorded in the design field. One environment (org, project, env) = ONE namespace wamn-<org>--<project>--<env>; ONE operator per cluster in wamn-system, never one per environment (Host CRs are forcibly written to OPERATOR_NAMESPACE, the operator has a single -nats-url with no lattice prefix, and the five CRDs are a Helm install-once cluster-scoped singleton). Tenancy rides Host.Environment stamped from the pod's namespace via the downward API, not Host namespace. NATS stays a shared cluster singleton (control plane by necessity, evt-nats because it is already stream-name tenant-scoped); Secrets and the release-manifest ConfigMap replicate per environment namespace. THE LOAD-BEARING WRONG-TARGET LOCK IS operator.allowSharedHosts, WHICH SHIPS TRUE — leaving the default makes the whole mapping cosmetic. Deferrals: .15.57 .15.58 .15.59 .15.60; decisions .13.49 .13.50 .13.51.

title: [SR-MVP] spike(deploy): Artifact CRD for plans/manifest vs plain OCI pulls
description:
## Why

Spec open verification item: whether the runtime-operator Artifact CRD can carry plans and the release manifest (data, not components) or they remain plain OCI pulls in our host code. Gates the executor OCI-pull rewrite and the publish-side push.

## Scope

Verify against the operator at chart v2.7.0 (fork wamn/2.7.0): what Artifact reconciliation does with non-component media types, pull identity/credentials, digest verification semantics, and cache behavior. Produce a written verdict with the consuming beads named.

## Boundary

Investigation only; no adoption code.
design:
WAVE-1 VERDICT (2026-08-16, branch deploy-simplification, sub-epic wamn-0h0g.15): REJECT THE ARTIFACT CRD; NAMED SPLIT — and half the question was already closed by ruling 4.

At wamn/2.7.0 the Artifact CRD pulls nothing. Its entire reconcile body is `Status.ArtifactURL = Spec.Image` (runtime-operator/internal/controller/runtime/artifact_controller.go:34-45): a string alias plus a readiness condition plus a deletion finalizer over an OCI reference. It never contacts a registry, never verifies a digest, never caches, and never materializes bytes anywhere a pod can read; its own `imagePullSecret` field is dead code (declared artifact_types.go:17, read by no reconciler). Its sole consumer `resolveArtifacts` rewrites `artifact://<name>` back into that same string (workload_deployment_controller.go:312-350). Its own doc comment scopes it to components. Adopting it would buy a name-to-URL map at the cost of a Kubernetes object, a finalizer, and v1alpha1 tracking.

MANIFEST LEG — already closed by ruling 4: the immutable `release-manifest-<digest>` ConfigMap referenced by name in the pod template is the serving path (spec:322-331). Only plan bytes were genuinely open.

PLAN BYTES — plain OCI pull-by-digest in wamn host code, using `oci-client` 0.17 directly (already in Cargo.lock via wash-runtime, so zero new lock entries), behind the EXISTING `ArtifactSource` trait. NOT via `wash_runtime::oci::pull_component`, which hardcodes the wasm layer media types and runs `wit_component::decode_reader` over the payload (fork oci.rs:528-532, :561, :762-766) — exactly wrong for canonical-JSON plan data. `Client::pull` accepts an arbitrary accepted-media-type list, giving digest verification at two levels (manifest digest against a digest-pinned reference; each layer blob against its manifest entry) while our own sha256(exact_bytes) recompute stays the trust anchor.

MOUNT PATH — the chart renders per-hostGroup `.volumes`/`.volumeMounts` (charts/runtime-operator deployment.yaml:96-101, :236-241), which is where the digest-named ConfigMap mounts. That seam is UNDOCUMENTED (absent from the values.yaml hostGroups keys, :336-420) and therefore rename-prone across chart bumps — guarded by wamn-0h0g.15.54. Note a component `Volume` supports only `ephemeral` and `hostPath`, never a ConfigMap volume, so a component can never mount the manifest as a file; the Workload `configFrom` path resolves named ConfigMaps into flat string config instead.

CACHING — do NOT reach for wash-runtime's disk cache for plan bytes: it is keyed by reference and re-fetches the manifest digest from the registry on every cache read, putting a network round-trip back on the hot path. Ruling 3's process-lifetime cache is the in-process one, and host pods run readOnlyRootFilesystem with only emptyDirs writable — a further reason the disk-cache deferral (.13.41) stays held.

CONSUMER IMPACT.
- wamn-0h0g.15.12 UNBLOCKED and materially smaller than written: one new `OciArtifactSource` impl behind the existing trait (control_artifact_reader.rs:256-263), delete `PostgresArtifactSource` (:265-335), and keep verbatim the `ResolutionPlanCache`, the format/length/hash verification block that emits `HashMismatch` (:524-542), and the `wamn:runner/plan-supply` WIT seam — so the guest contract and refusal literals do not move.
- wamn-0h0g.15.14 gains three constraints: the manifest has TWO destinations (ConfigMap = serving, OCI = audit copy — see decision wamn-0h0g.13.45, which may delete the second); the pushed plan layer must be exactly `exact_bytes` so the OCI layer digest equals `execution_bundle_hash`; plan-bytes media types are a shared wire literal between publish and executor with nothing enforcing agreement (oci-client fails the pull with IncompatibleLayerMediaTypeError on drift).
- wamn-0h0g.15.17 RELEASED FROM HOLD and shrinks: deploy/platform/registry.yaml is already anonymous plain-HTTP at a Service DNS name the host pods reach, so the dev acceptance criterion needs zero credentials. What .15.17 actually owns is push credentials for the publish pipeline and, for production, a pull Secret.

DEFERRALS FILED: wamn-0h0g.15.44 (GC superseded release-manifest ConfigMaps), .15.45 (durable registry posture / re-push reconciler — the dev registry is emptyDir, so a restart loses every plan blob and breaks readiness prefetch cluster-wide), .15.46 (mint-time manifest size assertion against the ~1MiB ConfigMap limit), .15.54 (chart volume-seam fork-sync assertion). OWNER DECISION FILED: wamn-0h0g.13.45 (does the manifest OCI push survive ruling 4).
close_reason: Verdict recorded in the design field. REJECT the Artifact CRD (at wamn/2.7.0 it pulls nothing — reconcile is Status.ArtifactURL = Spec.Image; no registry contact, no digest verification, no cache, no byte materialization, imagePullSecret is dead code). Manifest leg already closed by ruling 4 (digest-named ConfigMap = serving path). Plan bytes: plain OCI pull-by-digest in host code via oci-client 0.17 behind the existing ArtifactSource trait, NOT via pull_component (wasm media types + component validation). Releases wamn-0h0g.15.17 from hold and shrinks wamn-0h0g.15.12 to one trait impl. Deferrals: .15.44 .15.45 .15.46 .15.54; decision .13.45.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] decision(ui): test level for behavioural done-checks (DOM env or manual)
description: Step 1 settled the test level as vitest with Solid's SSR entry (solid({ssr:true}) + renderToString, environment node), which proves rendered markup with zero new dependencies. But that level loads Solid's SSR build, in which the reactive graph is inert — verified directly: a createSignal/createMemo pair does not propagate under it. Steps 3, 6 and 7 have behavioural done-checks that cannot be proven there: 'each primitive renders every state' (disclosure toggling), 'navigation entirely mouse-driven works end to end' plus roving focus and anchor scroll-tracking, and 'every navigation and view action reachable via palette alone'. clients/loop-console/src/routing/location.ts already ships untested for exactly this reason. Options: (A) amend clients/dependency-policy.json to allow a DOM environment (jsdom or happy-dom) — a second supply-chain amendment after D2 option B; (B) adopt Vitest browser mode — heavier, needs a browser in CI; (C) record explicitly that steps 3/6/7 done-checks are demonstrated manually and keep the pure/SSR level. The rationale is recorded in clients/loop-console/vitest.config.ts. Owner decision — do not resolve silently.
design: Raised by the step-1 adversarial review (wamn-dggp.2), which proved reactive inertness under the SSR test level rather than asserting it.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded here and in docs/wamn-dev-ui-spec.md; if it amends the dependency policy, that amendment is its own commit and the policy gate plus client:build and client:test are green.
close_reason: Decided by dkk: client only, never SSR. Landed in 28ad5724. Setup is the documented Solid 2 one (https://v2.solidjs.com/guides/testing): vitest environment jsdom, plain solid() plugin, setup file registering @testing-library/jest-dom/vitest, render from @solidjs/testing-library, flush() before reading the DOM. The prior config's resolve.conditions [solid] override was the actual bug - it selected the server build. Allowlist gained jsdom 30.0.1, @solidjs/testing-library 1.0.0-beta.2, @testing-library/jest-dom 6.9.1, each deviating from the guide deliberately and for a recorded reason. Switching to the shipped runtime immediately caught a defect the SSR level hid: toolchain.test.ts wrote to a signal inside an owned scope (Solid 2 refuses this) and had been passing vacuously; it now proves memo propagation. happy-dom was tried first on a packaging argument with no research and is fully reverted. Deferred to wamn-dggp.16: layout/CSS/true focus need Vitest browser mode, blocked by Playwright's postinstall against the denied-lifecycle-script policy. Gates green on Node 24.19.0.

Foundation shared by every primitive: status.ts maps run and node statuses to the five SS1.1 tones and takes a bare string so an unheard-of wire word renders as itself in neutral; tone.css assigns --tone per data-tone so no component names a status colour; copy.ts is the one clipboard call and never throws; app.css declares the single :focus-visible signal ring, which the floor test lints as declared exactly once and erased nowhere.

Primitives: StatusBadge, PassGlyph, VerdictBar, SectionLabel, KeyValue, Disclosure (uncontrolled, or controlled for step 4's expand-all), CopyId (middle-ellipsis first/last 4, full id in the name and on hover, copies the whole id), RefreshControl, JsonView (collapse depth, per-subject accessible names, copy), SourceView (line numbers, no phantom line for a trailing newline, error-line tint only when the engine gave a line, byte-faithful copy), DataTable (caption, per-row tone, row disclosure into its own row, empty slot, truncation footer), FailurePanel, ErrorPanel (three states kept distinct, platform literals verbatim), LoadingBlock/EmptyState.

Every state is driven by a step-2 fixture; ErrorPanel's three states come from the fixture reader's reserved error probes. Verified by the integrator rather than taken on report: all three gates green, and 12 mutants killed by named tests (colour-alone, ellipsized copy, reassembled bytes, phantom line, leading-zero revision, dropped caption, leaked listener, dropped aria-expanded, paraphrased literal, tone-for-word, skipped not-found branch, raw disclosure over nothing).

Integrator decision the review escalated: KeyValue's key no longer wears the .label role. That role is SS1.4's uppercase section divider; SS2.2 and SS2.4 draw pair keys lowercase in an aligned data-face column, which uppercasing would break.

Deferred and filed: wamn-dggp.20 (tree glyph widening), .21 (placeholder h1 collision), .22 (raw disclosure on the detail line); browser-only evidence recorded on .16.

title: [SR-MVP] test(security): prove accepted T3 replication-attribute confinement
description:
Retain PostgreSQL REPLICATION for the per-environment CDC role in the T3 shared-trials pool. PostgreSQL offers no narrower logical-decoding role attribute. The boundary is the deployed combination of a pg_hba rule with no physical-replication entry and the database CONNECT floor that admits the role only to its own project database.

This issue owns landing the production-shape proof and aligning the existing gate with that deployed posture. It does not revisit the accepted attribute or invent a revoke that would disable CDC.
acceptance_criteria: A production-shaped PostgreSQL proof shows: logical replication succeeds against the role’s own database; physical replication and BASE_BACKUP are rejected by pg_hba; logical replication against a sibling database is rejected by the CONNECT floor; unrelated SQL DML remains denied; and the own-database CDC path remains usable. The existing gate uses the production pg_hba posture rather than a stricter per-role fixture. Named mutants removing the pg_hba denial or CONNECT floor fail. No REPLICATION revoke or fictitious narrower attribute is introduced.
notes:
WAVE-11 ADJUDICATION, 2026-08-17 -- recorded 2026-08-18 because it existed only in
session memory and would otherwise have been lost. This is the analysis, NOT an owner ruling;
the risk decision is still OPEN and is the owner's.

*** THE BEAD'S OWN FRAMING CONTAINS A FALSE PREMISE. *** "Narrower capture authority" DOES NOT
EXIST in PostgreSQL. REPLICATION is a ROLE ATTRIBUTE, not a per-database or per-table grant.
There is no way to grant "logical decoding of these tables only". Dropping the attribute does
not narrow the CDC role; it breaks logical decoding outright. So the only available moves are
ACCEPT, or REPLACE THE ARCHITECTURE -- there is no middle setting to dial.

WHAT THE ATTRIBUTE ACTUALLY CONFERS. A REPLICATION role may open a walsender connection to ANY
database in the cluster it can reach, create and drop replication slots, and -- the part that
matters -- run BASE_BACKUP, i.e. read the entire cluster's data directory. That is a
whole-cluster confidentiality reach from a single per-project credential.

REACHABILITY IS BOUNDED, BUT BY NOTHING WE ASSERT. Two things bound it: pg_hba (a replication
connection needs an hba line that admits it) and the CONNECT floor. NEITHER IS ASSERTED
ANYWHERE IN THIS REPOSITORY. Worse, the M1 gate proves confinement under a pg_hba that
production does not have -- so the existing proof does not cover the deployed posture.

EXPOSURE IS CONFINED TO THE T3 SHARED TRIALS POOL under the D6 four-tier topology.

RECOMMENDATION (owner decides): ACCEPT the attribute, scoped to T3, conditional on two proof
beads -- and the PHYSICAL-REPLICATION-DENIAL proof is BLOCKING, because it is the only thing
standing between a leaked CDC password and BASE_BACKUP of the whole cluster.

over-grant on the same role -- grant_replication_access_sql had GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES,
now narrowed to the entity map with a retroactive REVOKE. That was the SQL-grant half and is
done; this bead is the ATTRIBUTE half and is not.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): make host database credential selection exact
description: Create the reusable typed credential-exactness seam consumed by future database authority wiring. The seam accepts only an explicit credential source and proves session_user, current_user, database, tenant binding, memberships, ACL, and independent listener identity. It creates no Secret, role, grant, authority selector, RLS policy, or runtime consumer wiring.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): partition shared wamn_app workload authorities
description:
Split the shared WamnPostgres connection authority by lifecycle. The guest pool serves only guest-visible WIT SQL operations: query, execute, begin, and their one-shot helper. The platform pool serves every host-owned database path: production claim and reap, HTTP effect-authority snapshots, and run-release or plan-supply reads.

This is session-lifecycle isolation, not a grant-enforced database boundary. The broad wamn_app credential remains an accepted interim. Full workload-owned roles, Secrets, grant partitioning, and non-settable tenant identity remain owned by the non-settable identity and RLS redesign.
acceptance_criteria:
Guest-visible WIT SQL and all host-owned database paths use structurally separate pools and cannot reuse one another's checked-out connections, session state, or lifecycle. Deterministic interleaving tests fail if a guest path is routed through the platform pool or any claim, reap, HTTP authorization, or plan-supply path is routed through the guest pool.

Each lifecycle has a separately named chart maximum. The shipping defaults are guest 14 and platform 2: the platform value covers the measured one active operation plus one headroom slot, while the guest receives the remaining bounded share of the former total budget of 16. The implementation must not copy the former mixed-pool maximum onto both pools. Pool telemetry carries a lifecycle attribute, and the chart values carry a one-line starvation rationale.

No distinct database-role, Secret, RLS, or protected-write boundary is claimed or constructed here. The same commit amends the existing findings-ledger row to name broad wamn_app authority as accepted interim, name the non-settable identity and RLS redesign as owner, preserve separate ownership for cluster-global credential isolation, and make any tenant promotion the tripwire.

title: [SR-MVP] audit(ownership): inventory every protected runtime write
description: Generate one canonical protected-relation table from declared ownership and a reconciled scratch PostgreSQL database. Do not infer writes from Rust call sites. Each row records the qualified relation, installer, lifecycle owner, database mechanisms, executing roles, whether author SQL can reach it, and database guards. The audit records current truth and changes no production permissions.
design: Owner ruling 2026-08-12: derive database authority, do not grep for writes. The installer comes from the migration owner in architecture/state-owners.json; the owner is the semantic chokepoint owner in that file; executing roles come from PostgreSQL grants after installing the reconciler SQL into a disposable PostgreSQL 18 database. Read pg_catalog for table and column grants, row-security state and policies, foreign-key cascade rules, triggers, trigger/function owners, and relevant constraints. Calls above an owner API are clients and are out of scope. If wamn_app has mutation authority, record the exposure exactly as author SQL, RLS-bounded; do not search for a code caller. Record cascades as mechanisms and immutability/RLS enforcement as guards. Generate one deterministic table only. Catalog inspection is read-only after scratch setup and the audit changes no production permission.

Installer and owner exactly match architecture/state-owners.json. Any wamn_app mutation grant produces the exact author SQL, RLS-bounded exposure. No Rust call-site, SQL-text-write, carrier, or invoker inventory remains. Named tests reject a missing relation, changed owner/installer, changed role/grant, missing cascade, missing immutability/RLS guard, and incorrect author exposure. title: [SR-MVP] decision: call-flow executes as engine frame machinery; the registry stays the verbatim nine
description:
The amendment calls `call-flow` "an ordinary node — like transform, conditional, or an integration node", while closed wamn-0h0g.5.7 froze the standard-node dispatch registry at the verbatim nine and the charter allowlist still reads "absent from runtime dispatch (it compiles away at validation, cut 4)" — a line the amendment's Read-as clause does not explicitly rewrite, and which is now false.

**Owner ruling (dkk, 2026-08-11):** `call-flow` is a plan instruction the flow-engine interprets as FRAME MACHINERY (call-enter guard → push → execute → pop). It does NOT enter the standard-node registry. Closed 5.7 and every "verbatim nine" count stand.

The allowlist line is read as: `call-flow` is accepted by flow-schema 0.2 and executes as engine frame entry, not a registry node. The allowlist's "reject recursive call cycles" reads "recursion bounded by the runtime depth and dispatch budgets" (amendment Read-as).

Consumers: wamn-0h0g.3.4 (frame-stack execution), wamn-0h0g.5.4 (registry stays nine), wamn-0h0g.12.8 (record-equals-allowlist sweep restates the line).
close_reason: Owner ruled 2026-08-11: call-flow executes as engine frame machinery (guard, push, execute, pop); the standard-node registry stays the verbatim nine; the allowlist line is restated per the amendment Read-as.

title: [SR-MVP] decision: typed claim refusal terminalizes the run
description:
The amendment adds typed claim-time refusals — unresolvable name, hash-invalid bytes, foreign revision, incompatible contract, unbound requirement — that refuse "at claim, typed, before any guest execution", but states no run disposition for a refused claim.

**Owner ruling (dkk, 2026-08-11):** a typed claim refusal TERMINALIZES the run — typed `fail_kind`, queue row removed, the caller receives the stored typed failure. It never enters `effect-uncertain` or operator machinery (no guest ran; no effect intent exists).

Rationale: resolution is release-bound and the run's `catalog_id + catalog_version` is pinned at admission — "activating a later catalog release affects later admissions, never an admitted or queued run" — so a claim retry of the same run can only refuse identically; leaving the queue row claimable would spin forever. A fixed release requires a new invocation.

Consumers: the NB3 typed-failure vocabulary bead (exact literals), the NB4 claim-time resolution bead (transaction behavior), wamn-0h0g.4.1 (fourth classifier outcome), wamn-0h0g.4.6 (refusals must not enter operator machinery).
close_reason: Owner ruled 2026-08-11: a typed claim refusal terminalizes the run — typed fail_kind, queue row removed, caller receives the stored typed failure; never operator machinery. Release-bound resolution makes refusal deterministic for the pinned run.

title: [SR-MVP] decision: call-flow effect ceiling is contract-only — no call-site effect attempt
description:
The amendment (docs/flow-execution-amendment.md) sets `CallableContract.effect_ceiling = effectful`, so every `call-flow` classifies as effectful. Read literally against the ledger rule (effectful ⇒ one immutable write-ahead attempt before external send), every call site would mint a write-ahead effect attempt — and then any crash inside a purely computational callee classifies `effect-uncertain` and requires operator terminalize.

**Owner ruling (dkk, 2026-08-11):** the effectful ceiling drives idempotency-key derivation and recorded contract data ONLY. A `call-flow` site writes NO write-ahead effect attempt. Only genuinely effectful nodes — in whichever frame they execute — write intents. A crash inside a pure callee therefore classifies pre-effect and re-executes fresh under the unchanged reclaim classifier.

Consumers: wamn-0h0g.4.1 (effectful-intent classifier arm carve), wamn-0h0g.4.9 (ledger rule reads the current frame's plan policy), wamn-0h0g.3.4 (frame execution writes no site intent), wamn-0h0g.7.1 (required-key derivation: own plan contains an effectful node OR a call-flow instruction ⇒ key required).
close_reason: Owner ruled 2026-08-11: the effectful ceiling is contract/idempotency-key-derivation data only; a call-flow site writes no write-ahead effect attempt; a crash inside a pure callee classifies pre-effect and re-executes fresh.

title: [PLAN-6A] Define an exact uint64 wire representation for JavaScript clients
description: The public authoring schema exposes revisions and other Rust u64 values as JSON numbers with format uint64. JavaScript JSON parsing cannot preserve integers above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so a schema-valid value can otherwise be silently rounded by generated clients. Select and codify one exact cross-language wire representation: string-encoded uint64, an explicit safe-integer contract/range, or an admitted lossless-number transport/parser strategy. Until resolved, the TypeScript client must reject non-safe integers rather than corrupt identity.
design: Treat revision and identity precision as protocol integrity, not a frontend convenience. Update the Rust model/schema generator, checked-in schema, TypeScript generator/runtime, request collection, and compatibility documentation together. Do not add dual spellings or silently coerce rounded values. Include Rust-to-wire-to-TypeScript round trips at the chosen boundary and a controlled precision-loss mutant.
acceptance_criteria: One owner-approved exact uint64 representation is normative across Rust serde, JSON Schema, generated TypeScript types, runtime parsing/serialization, and examples; boundary values including 2^53-1, 2^53, and u64::MAX have deterministic accepted/refused behavior without rounding; drift and precision-loss mutants fail; compatibility/versioning impact is recorded; temporary TypeScript safe-integer refusal is retired or documented as the final contract.
close_reason: Safe-integer contract codified end to end per the decision recorded in comments, landed at post-integration sha bad0b4f. SafeUint64 bounded newtype (TryFrom-only construction makes out-of-domain values UNREPRESENTABLE on the emit path; custom Deserialize refuses >2^53-1 through the existing ContractDecodeError::Json 400 rejection — NO new frozen wire literal) replaces u64 at all six sites; schema regenerated with exactly six added maximum lines; generated TS regenerated; validate.ts isSafeInteger documented as the FINAL contract; normative '## Integer wire domain' section in authoring-surface.md; PLAN open-decisions row folded in the same commit. LOAD-BEARING SUBTLETY: schemars NumberValidation::maximum is f64 and 9007199254740991.0 parses back as ...990 (one BELOW the bound) — silently caught by the existing collection drift guard; the maximum is published via SchemaObject::extensions as an integer literal and every_uint64_schema_site_publishes_the_safe_integer_maximum asserts as_u64() on committed bytes. Boundary tests: safe_integer_maximum_round_trips_exactly_in_both_directions (2^53-1), two_to_the_fifty_third_is_refused_in_both_directions, u64_max_is_refused_in_both_directions + TS boundary test. Gates on integrated main: model 11+2, scenario-worker 35, TS harness 14/14, generate.mjs --check exit 0, clippy clean on wamn-authoring-model. Mutants (sha256-restored, rerun green): drift (dropped one maximum) killed by the named schema test + committed-schema drift + TS --check; precision-loss (stripped TryFrom bound) killed by both refusal tests. Compatibility: schema narrowing only — no legitimate producer can emit above the bound (storage is bigint i64, fields are server-assigned counters/latencies). Platform-wide extension question (flow-schema + connection-contract uint64 sites) filed as its own bead.

comments.author: dkk
comments.text: DECIDED (dkk 2026-08-07 via decision prompt): SAFE-INTEGER CONTRACT. Normative wire domain for every format:uint64 field is [0, 2^53-1]: schema gains maximum 9007199254740991 on all six sites (revision :223/:231/:748/:768/:841/:1157 of authoring-surface.schema.json; model fields expected_revision/revision/actual_revision/edit_to_run_ms), the Rust boundary refuses values above it in BOTH directions (never emits, never accepts; storage is already bigint i64 and all fields are server-assigned counters/latencies), and the TS client's Number.isSafeInteger fail-closed check (validate.ts:109,:131) is the FINAL contract, retired as temporary. 2^53-1 accepted; 2^53 and u64::MAX deterministically refused without rounding. No dual spellings, no string encoding, no lossless-parser requirement. String-encoded and lossless-transport options were presented and rejected. IMPLEMENTATION IN FLIGHT at compact time: lane/ftfc-21 in worktree /tmp/wamn-wt-ftfc-21 off 4acc8e4, isolated target /tmp/wamn-t-ftfc21, single opus lane implementing model attributes + schema regen + emit guard + boundary tests (2^53-1/2^53/u64::MAX) + drift and precision-loss mutants + authoring-surface.md normative section + the PLAN open-decisions row (exact row text in the lane brief). Lane was told to STOP if a new frozen wire literal seems unavoidable. ON RESUME: if lane/ftfc-21 carries a commit, rebase onto main, run authoring-model tests + schema drift + clippy/fmt on the integrated tree, close citing the post-rebase sha, git push, bd dolt push, remove worktree/branch/target; if the lane stopped with a report, act on it per the delegate rule; if no commit and no report, re-run the implementation from this recorded contract.

title: [PLAN-6A] Align authoring refusal schema fields with serde wire names
description: The generated authoring command schema advertises snake_case properties for structured AuthoringRefusal variants, while Rust serde decoding with rename_all_fields accepts kebab-case. A schema-valid client payload therefore fails AuthoringDocument::from_json. Establish one canonical wire spelling in the model/generator/schema, regenerate the artifact, and do not accept dual aliases or silently coerce drift.
design: Repair the contract at its source rather than weakening client examples. Add table-driven round-trip coverage for every structured refusal variant using exactly the property keys emitted by the generated schema, plus a controlled drift mutant that proves mismatched field spelling is rejected. After landing, regenerate/revalidate the TypeScript client and authoring request collection if their generated artifacts are affected.
acceptance_criteria: Every structured AuthoringRefusal schema object round-trips through AuthoringDocument::from_json using schema-emitted keys; generated schema and serde wire names have one canonical spelling; a deterministic drift guard and controlled negative mutant fail on mismatched naming; no dual aliases or silent coercion are introduced; affected client artifacts are regenerated and verified.
close_reason: SHIPPED 953321a (pushed, rebased). Root cause: schemars_derive 0.8.22 hard-codes a SERDE_KEYWORDS allowlist omitting rename_all_fields, so the schema advertised snake_case fields while serde decoded kebab-case. Canonical spelling fixed as kebab-case at the source: explicit #[schemars(rename_all="kebab-case")] on 8 AuthoringRefusal + 1 PendingReportReason + 2 SuiteExecutionRefusal variants (no serde wire change, no dual aliases, no coercion). Regenerated docs/contracts/authoring-surface.schema.json (exactly 18 field-name lines: actual/expected-revision, node-types, connection-names, report-id, run-ids) and clients/authoring-client generated TS (27/27 line swap + source SHA header). Tests reproduce-first: structured_refusals_round_trip_the_property_names_the_schema_publishes (walks the generated schema, self-updating) and drifted_refusal_field_spelling_is_rejected (deny_unknown_fields mutant) both FAILED on the old code, now green. GATES: cargo test -p wamn-authoring-model 7+2 green (re-run on integrated main tree), clippy -D warnings, fmt, TS generate --check clean, client test suite green in lane.

title: [CLIENT-COLLAB-D1] Decide per-principal drafts and shared visibility
description: Settle the per-principal collaboration axis left open by wamn-ftfc.6. The proposed posture is separate revisioned work-in-progress per principal for one flow; editing another principal's work creates a successor under the editor's own principal with lineage; authorized peers can view; no locks or leases; an optional soft assignee may come later.
acceptance_criteria: The owner approves draft ownership keys, shared-visibility roles, successor and lineage semantics, conflict/refusal behavior, retention interaction, and audit attribution; locks/leases and agent-specific draft machinery are rejected; PLAN records that agents are ordinary service principals and external session-log links are metadata only; implementation scope is unambiguous.
close_reason: DECIDED (dkk 2026-08-07 via decision prompt — UNLIMITED drafts per (flow, principal), diverging from the one-per-flow recommendation) and folded into PLAN.md open-decisions at 4acc8e4: each draft carries an immutable denormalized owner principal (id/kind/subject); draft_id stays freeform so a principal may hold unlimited parallel drafts of one flow; only the owner mutates (uniform authorization-denied otherwise); project-author/project-admin may view all project drafts; editing another's draft is an explicit create-successor command copying content into a NEW draft owned by the editor with predecessor draft-id + revision lineage metadata, source untouched; lineage is metadata, never roots retention (deleted predecessor -> dangling ref rendered unavailable); every mutation audited via the ctc8.8 ledger. Rejected: locks, leases, agent-specific draft machinery. Agents are ordinary service principals; external session-log links are metadata only. wamn-ftfc.18 implements; wamn-jvzx.7 documents.
