title: [CLIENT-AUTH-A1.3] Authenticate management authoring requests and audit principals
description: Install one authentication and authorization middleware on the management authoring HTTP surface. It verifies the PAT presenter, derives trusted principal and project-role context, supplies that context to the canonical authoring commands, and records the resolved principal on every command audit entry. It is the shared management-plane bridge for authoring and project effect-disposition adapters, not the generated data gateway RLS bridge.
design: PROPOSED by orchestrator 2026-08-07, pending dkk ratification (one-line ack or veto on resume). PLACEMENT: extend services/scenario-worker with an HTTP listener — its authoring module docstring deliberately deferred transport until 'item 5 owns retained client identity', which ctc8.6/.7 have now delivered; the backend (InternalAuthoringBackend), its capability token, and the PG role probe already live there, so transport co-locates with the only command implementation and no new deployable is minted. STACK: raw hyper 1.x (already a workspace dependency used in services/builder and test-support) — two routes do not justify the axum supply-chain decision. ROUTES: POST /authoring (single command endpoint, matching the request collection's existing single-POST + Bearer assumption) and POST /login (reserved route implementing ctc8.7's documented wire contract: subject/secret/label in, token/expires_at out). FLOW: Bearer PAT -> wamn-platform-identity::authenticate_pat -> AuthenticatedPrincipal -> project_roles check -> principal passed into canonical authoring commands -> principal recorded on every command audit row. Refusals before command execution for absent/forged/expired/revoked/cross-project/client-injected identity, uniform anti-oracle shape. Bind address via env; deploy/platform manifest update for scenario-worker; respect the 4q3c.12 NetworkPolicy posture. Mutants: authentication-bypass and audit-attribution per acceptance.
acceptance_criteria: A valid human or service PAT reaches one landed authoring endpoint with trusted principal/role context; absent, forged, expired, revoked, cross-project, and client-injected identity attempts refuse before command execution; two principals performing the same command are distinguishable in immutable audit evidence; every canonical authoring mutation records principal attribution; deterministic tests kill an authentication-bypass and an audit-attribution mutant.
close_reason: Landed the authenticated management authoring surface per the three dkk-ratified decisions (see comments): services/scenario-worker/src/management.rs (new, sibling module — internal_adapter_carries_no_client_principal guard intact) holds PAT verification, project-role resolution, non-constructible/non-deserializable AuthorizedAuthor, the audit-ledger writer, audited wrappers for all four backend mutations, and the hyper 1.x server; serve subcommand in main.rs; NEW deploy/platform/scenario-worker.yaml (event-reader.example.yaml pattern, references operator wamn-system-db Secret so no control_storage allowlist edit was needed); NEW append-only catalog.authoring_command_audit modeled on effect_disposition_requests (denormalized principal, effective_role+command_kind CHECKs, persists command_id, immutable trigger, written BEFORE the command so authorized attempts are retained), with schema-control mirrors, publish-catalog additive migration slice, and its state-owners.json row. Routes: POST /authoring mounting save-flow-draft (other five kinds bare 501 — deferral beaded wamn-ftfc.22); POST /login per the frozen ctc8.7 rustdoc contract. Uniform 403 {"kind":"authorization-denied"} (the repo's own frozen literal, no parallel taxonomy) byte-identical for absent/malformed/forged/expired/revoked/cross-project/unroled and all login failures; identity settled from the authorization header before the body is read; client-injected principal rejected by deny_unknown_fields with no ledger row. Landed at post-rebase sha 30d4a95. Gates on integrated main: scenario-worker 35 + schema-control 78/5/19/13 + ctl-tests green, rustfmt clean, control_storage 11/11, management_live 1/1 over real HTTP + postgres:18; state_ownership red only at the pre-existing SR28 scanner stage (wamn-2jdm.36, message identical pre/post). Pre-existing reds verified-at-HEAD and beaded: wamn-j5h0 (ctl lib test), wamn-tsm1/wamn-ppts (clippy). Mutants (baseline sha256 fea8442f…): auth-bypass (fabricated principal on None) and audit-attribution (hardcoded identity) each killed by named test management_surface_authenticates_and_attributes_authoring_commands (200-vs-403 assert; alice-is-attributed assert); byte-restored, sha256sum -c OK, suite re-green. Rollout deferred to wamn-ctc8.10 (carries the .example.yaml naming question).

title: [CLIENT-AUTH-A1.2] Add PAT issuance, verification, revocation, and login
description: Add the CLI/agent presenter over the first-party identity core: opaque personal access tokens minted through the reserved login flow, hashed at rest, prefix-addressable for lookup, expirable and revocable, and resolved into the same authenticated-principal value used by every management adapter. Include the headless wamn login/token workflow needed by S0; do not add cookies or OIDC.
acceptance_criteria: wamn login obtains a PAT through an authenticated reserved route; only a hash and non-secret lookup metadata persist; valid, expired, revoked, malformed, and forged tokens resolve or refuse deterministically; human and service principals are supported without client-supplied identity fields; token material is returned only at issuance and never appears in audit or logs; cookie and OIDC presenters remain absent.

PAT presenter delivered transport-neutral in wamn-platform-identity per the A1.2/A1.3 scope split (no management HTTP surface exists anywhere in-repo — verified; the reserved route, middleware, and audit wiring ride wamn-ctc8.8, and the login wire shape (subject/secret/label in, token/expires_at out) is documented verbatim in a '# Wire contract' rustdoc on login_local for .8 and wamn-jvzx.13 to carry). title: [CLIENT-AUTH-A1.1] Build the first-party sysdb identity core
description: Implement the platform-plane first-party identity core in sysdb: principals with human and service kinds, local human credential verification using Argon2, minimum authoring role assignment and lookup, and one presenter-neutral authenticated-principal seam for later PAT, cookie-session, and OIDC issuers. This is distinct from the per-project app_system identity substrate and from generated-data-API RLS claims. OIDC, browser cookies, and transport middleware are out of scope.
design: Owner-approved identity-core seam 2026-08-07: add crates/identity/platform as package wamn-platform-identity and an identity schema in the T1 system database. Human principals carry Argon2 local credentials; service principals have no local password and authenticate through later presenter work. Project-role assignments use validated opaque role slugs in this bead and carry no implicit permission semantics; authorization mapping lands at the management boundary. AuthenticatedPrincipal is non-deserializable with private construction, produced only after trusted in-crate verification so request fields cannot forge it. OIDC, PAT issuance, cookies, middleware, and per-project app_system authority remain excluded.
acceptance_criteria: Sysdb can create, disable, and resolve human and service principals and their authoring roles; local secrets are Argon2-verifiable and never stored in plaintext; the authenticated-principal value cannot be supplied by an untrusted request; migrations and deterministic positive/negative tests cover duplicate identity, invalid secret, disabled principal, and role lookup; no OIDC/JWT, cookie, or per-project app_system authority is introduced.
close_reason: SHIPPED 89803fb (pushed to origin/main). crates/identity/platform = wamn-platform-identity: human/service principals, atomic human+Argon2id local-credential insert, canonical fail-closed subject/role slugs, disable idempotency, opaque project-role assignment/lookup, and the non-deserializable AuthenticatedPrincipal seam (private construction, compile_fail doctest proves forgery is rejected). identity schema added to deploy/sql/system-schema.sql; architecture manifests + workspace tiers updated (51 root packages). GATES (documented gate of record, docs/build-and-test.md [5 / wamn-ctc8.6]): cargo test -p wamn-platform-identity (4 unit + 2 doctests incl compile_fail), clippy -D warnings, fmt --check, and LIVE identity_live round-trip vs throwaway postgres:18 — all green. Caveat: system mold linker is missing (machine-level regression); gates ran with RUSTFLAGS override falling back to GNU ld — linker choice does not affect test semantics. Unblocks wamn-ctc8.7 (PAT issuance/login).

title: [PLAN-6A] Define the public editor command and projection contract
description: Enumerate and version the frontend-neutral authoring contract sufficient for any editor client without a privileged frontend. The editor is a client role, not a platform component: a reference SPA, an alternative frontend, or a human/agent using checkout files plus CLI/API consumes the same canonical commands and projections. The contract covers validate, draft-run, suite-run, and publish composition; stable draft, report, node, branch, and edge identity; typed results and refusals; and versioning/evolution rules. It decides no shell hosting or rendering.
acceptance_criteria: A checked-in contract identifies every command, request/result/refusal, projection, stable identity, and version needed for a client to complete edit through publish; validate, draft-run, and suite-run map to wamn-ftfc.1 canonical handlers and wamn-ftfc.11 durable draft reports; node/branch/edge identities and coverage states are client-renderable without parsing prose or privileged data; conformance guards reject unversioned or frontend-specific drift; no SPA, shell-hosting, or platform-plane authority is introduced.

title: [PLAN-1] Cut runtime effect authority to immutable attempt facts
description: Switch all production effect-attempt writers and readers from mutable node_runs authority columns to effect_attempts plus dispatch/outcome ledgers and the constrained current pointer. This includes begin/dispatch/completion transitions, cancellation/child liveness checks, and the wamn:postgres HTTP/custom-node authorization snapshots.
design: Activate only after the schema/backfill child through one explicit writer handoff. Drain and quiesce every legacy binary; while quiesced, run the final reconcile/backfill under its handoff lock and prove zero NULL current pointers plus exact equality between each immutable current attempt and every legacy authority projection. Then activate the immutable reader/writer before any writer resumes. Runtime append uses a genuinely distinct host-only database credential and narrow adapter unavailable to guest SQL; app.runner, custom GUCs, SQL blocklists, and the shared wamn_app session are not authentication. EXECUTE and table authority are revoke-by-default, wamn_app remains refused even under stale grants, and the insert guard continues to enforce that boundary. Revoke or guard wamn_app mutation of current_effect_attempt_id and legacy authority fields at activation. Attempt intent appends a server-minted immutable row; authorized replay/idempotent redispatch appends a same-occurrence lineage-linked successor and advances only the pointer. Keep current effect-uncertain terminalization until the separately authenticated host-owned auto-park adapter lands.
acceptance_criteria: The cutover gate proves legacy writers are drained, runs final reconcile/backfill, refuses any NULL pointer or immutable-vs-legacy mismatch, and activates the new writer/reader before allowing execution to resume; an old and new authority writer never coexist. The production adapter authenticates with a host-only credential unavailable to guests, exposes only narrow typed operations, grants no direct ledger or pointer DML to wamn_app, and stale-grant/GUC/blocklist mutants remain refused by trigger enforcement. Existing imported in-flight attempts retain their exact recovery decision and explicit legacy-import marker. New prepared, dispatched, completed, replay, idempotent-with-key, and never-replay attempts use only immutable facts and same-occurrence predecessor lineage; no old node_runs attempt field participates in production authorization. HTTP and custom-node snapshots bind the exact current attempt, generation facts, input ref/key, and dispatch boundary. Cross-occurrence pointers or predecessors, missing ledgers, NULL or mismatched handoff facts, unrecorded dispatch/outcome, cancellation/child liveness, guest pointer mutation, and mutable-field mutants refuse deterministically. Direct flowrunner fixtures and system/integration proofs compile and pass against canonical reconciled DDL.

title: [PLAN-1] Reconcile immutable effect ledgers and legacy attempt backfill
description: Add the immutable effect-attempt, dispatch, outcome, disposition-request, and per-attempt disposition ledgers to the run-plane schema of record. Extend reconcile-run-plane to converge columns, constraints, indexes, helper guards, and triggers; add verified release provenance columns; and transactionally backfill the current immutable attempt pointer and boundary facts from legacy node_runs before any new reader activates.
design: The migration is additive and does not change runner behavior or activate the new pointer as runtime authority. Retain legacy node_runs authority columns; create immutable attempt, dispatch, outcome, request, and disposition ledgers first; add the nullable current pointer; then, under a writer-blocking table lock and full-RLS administrative visibility, import only structurally complete legacy attempts, append dispatch/outcome boundaries, prove the pending set is zero, and finally add the composite pointer FK. Legacy rows carry an explicit legacy_imported marker because the old schema had no predecessor identity; new successors require same-run/node/occurrence lineage. Existing publication provenance stays nullable rather than inventing identity, while both provenance columns and non-empty CHECKs converge idempotently. Immutable fact appends are migration-only in this child: wamn_app receives no INSERT authority and trigger guards defeat stale grants or pg_temp shadowing. Runtime writes remain unavailable until .42.3 performs the drained host-authority handoff.
acceptance_criteria: From-zero apply, partial reapply, and legacy reconcile converge idempotently under SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS; a plain owner is refused before observation or mutation so forced-RLS rows cannot be hidden. A pre-migration started/dispatched node gets exactly one explicit legacy-imported immutable current attempt with matching recovery/generation/input/key/timing facts and its dispatch fact; completed legacy rows additionally get one outcome fact. NULL-incomplete authority, unresolved attested connection identity, join-lost rows, or a nonzero pending set abort with typed errors before the pointer FK activates. Catalog provenance columns and exact non-empty CHECKs converge before backfill. Cross-run/node/occurrence current pointers and predecessors, direct or stale-grant wamn_app fact/disposition inserts, update/delete of all five ledgers, NULL outcome holes, wall-clock latest-order mutation, pg_temp role shadowing, and partial migration replay are deterministically refused/proven. The old runner remains functional because legacy columns stay present and the new pointer is not production authority; .42.3 is explicitly responsible for draining legacy writers, final zero-and-match validation, and the distinct host-only writer/reader activation.

Boundary: this is storage/backfill only, not runtime activation. Project-facing disposition adapters remain gated on real caller AuthN per wamn-4u7p.42.5/wamn-ctc8.5; wamn-4u7p.42.3 owns drained final zero-and-match reconcile plus activation of the distinct host-only immutable reader/writer credential and adapter before writers resume.

title: [PLAN-1] Host-owned automatic effect-uncertain park adapter
description: Ship the trusted system adapter that lets flowrunner park a dispatched never-replay attempt with unknown outcome without exposing disposition append authority to guest SQL or a shared wamn_app session. The adapter must bind tenant, target/authority run identity, node occurrence, and the live queue fence from host-owned invocation context, then atomically append the system disposition, preserve the full checkpoint, set the existing queue condition to indefinite park, and release the lease.
design: app.runner is a freely settable PostgreSQL custom GUC and the runner currently shares the wamn_app database session with guest queries, so neither the GUC, a SECURITY DEFINER grant to wamn_app, nor the guest SQL blocklist is authentication. Use a truly host-owned/non-guest transport or separately authenticated store session whose credential and invocation path are unavailable to the guest. A dedicated role alone is insufficient if the guest shares its session or credentials. Preserve run -> queue -> node lock order and refuse stale/expired fences before append or queue mutation.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatched current never-replay attempt is parked atomically with an immutable system disposition and unchanged run status; the checkpoint is preserved and the existing queue row becomes indefinitely unavailable with its lease released. Missing/forged system identity, guest/direct wamn_app invocation, cross-run authority, stale generation, expired lease, non-current/non-dispatched/non-never-replay attempt, terminal run, and concurrent resolution all refuse before mutation. Deterministic live mutants prove app.runner spoofing, guest SQL access, credential/session sharing, and helper invocation cannot gain append authority. The flowrunner consumes the adapter and never terminalizes effect-uncertain.

title: [PLAN-4] Runner egress address-level enforcement
description: Close the address-level enforcement gap in the host-native HTTP path. Current connection authority validation is hostname-based, deploy/platform has no runner NetworkPolicy, and connection_http.rs names an allow-all policy ExternallyEnforced. Before implementation the owner selects either the runner egress NetworkPolicy that the name promises or an in-process IP-pinning and DNS-rebinding guard. Preserve connection-defined authority, TLS identity, redirect/proxy refusal, credential isolation, and the rule that flows never carry endpoints or flow-level allowed-hosts.
design: Choose one real enforcement owner rather than stacking nominal controls. Kubernetes policy must be effective for the cluster CNI and narrowly admit required infrastructure; an in-process guard must pin the connected address across resolution, redirects, proxies, and TLS verification.
acceptance_criteria: The owner-selected enforcement boundary is recorded before code changes; admitted hostname resolution cannot reach an address outside the environment-owned policy and a DNS-rebinding or redirect mutant is refused before network access; required platform and connection traffic remains functional; no raw guest/flow allowlist bypass exists; deterministic tests plus an exact deployed proof demonstrate allowed egress and blocked address escape.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-07, before code: choose effective Kubernetes NetworkPolicy as the sole runner address-level enforcement owner. Retain the existing in-process per-attempt DNS pin and logical-host/TLS identity preservation, but do not add a second in-process address policy. The enforced runner floor is default-deny with explicit DNS, project PostgreSQL, control NATS, OTLP, signed custom-node transport, and environment-admitted connection targets. External business destinations are supplied by additive environment-owned CIDR/port NetworkPolicies. Required proof: exact connection_http credproof with an admitted target and a blocked address-escape target plus a widening mutation that turns the gate red, followed by the normal deployed F3 runner regression. Current kind v0.32.0 / Kubernetes v1.36.1 kindnetd:v20260528-9350166c is policy-enforcing (NetworkPolicy watch plus live kindnet-network-policies nftables table); wamn-0si.8's older inert-kindnet statement is stale and is not a blocker.
COMPLETION EVIDENCE 2026-08-07: kindnet enforcement verified; focused system tests 6/6, integration check, builder goldens 4/4, manifest client/server dry-runs, rustfmt, diff/script checks passed. Exact wamn-gates image sha256:2de0b2046aacaadfb7e43668e692625a8bb206067a0b5c00c49b996d90162659. Live credproof passed with admitted serve-echo and blocked equally hostname-authorized egress-escape; widening policy baseline deb05f78... -> mutant a0e9e5bf... made the target respond and killed the gate; trap restored byte-exact policy and final green passed. Production runner rolled out 2/2 with PostgreSQL/NATS dependencies admitted. Runner-profile nodebench completed 2,000 cross-pod signed-node calls and all assertions passed. The requested F3 follow-up could not be credited: PARK/DISPATCH/WAKE passed, but pre-existing catalog serving-state mismatch left run v2 unresolved before egress; exact evidence is on wamn-2jkm.71 (R35). This does not weaken the causal address proof or required platform/connection/signed-node traffic proofs, and no unrelated R35 repair was folded into this security issue. Builder all-target Clippy remains red only on pre-existing removed-field test drift/doc warnings; changed integration/system targets were clean.

description: While migrating the callable F4 publication in wamn-4u7p.41, the legacy tests/integration f4proof and pocsuiteproof runnable fixtures exposed an independent mixed-runtime conflict: their HTTP callback must use a portable connection, which makes allowed-hosts forbidden for the whole flow, while their custom-node internal endpoint still relies on allowed-hosts and has no connection-backed runtime specialization. design: Approved 2026-08-05: ERP callback is the sole portable HTTP connection, named erp-callback, with path-and-query /dispositions. Custom-node invocation is a trusted platform-plane capability whose guest-visible type accepts admitted node identity only and contains no endpoint or URL. It carries a one-frame invocation context; verifies the implementation-digest claim against the admitted release; returns typed variant refusals; and denies before network access. Transport reuses signed node-host machinery with signing required. Environment-owned platform configuration maps pinned implementation digest to endpoint. Transport failures are infrastructure faults; node faults are node failures. Flow-level allowed-hosts is absent. Plan sentence to land with the fixture commit: node placement and execution transport are platform-plane — flows reference implementations, never endpoints — and connection-backed HTTP excludes flow-level allowed-hosts.

The owning live integration gate passes with the ERP callback bound through exactly one portable connection named erp-callback at /dispositions and no flow-level allowed-hosts. The guest-visible node-invocation interface carries admitted node identity only; the host verifies one-frame context and implementation digest against the admitted release before any network access, uses environment-owned digest-to-endpoint placement, returns typed refusals, and classifies transport failures as infrastructure faults and node faults as node failures. title: [PLAN-2B] Prove connection-generation activation is atomic and fail-closed
description: Add the focused deterministic v1 generation-activation proof. Exercise compatible activation and later-occurrence resolution, every intrinsic and active-binding floor incompatibility class, an instance with no active bindings, and stale races for the active pointer, binding set, requirement, policy, and credential-kind record. Kill mutants that omit a validation class, swap after any snapshotted input changes, disable or fork a binding, or clear the working active generation on refusal.
acceptance_criteria: Compatible v1 activation performs exactly one audited pointer swap; a valid unbound instance can activate; every floor incompatibility and stale case refuses with no pointer or binding mutation while existing compatible traffic continues; explicit disable and create-instance operations remain separate; every named omission, stale-CAS, auto-disable or fork, and status-quo mutant makes the focused proof fail.

title: [PLAN-2B] Validate a staged generation against every active binding

Return the complete binding, requirement, and generation input identities plus typed per-binding failures; never weaken a claim or disable or fork a binding. Semantic-strengthening evidence is parked separately.
acceptance_criteria: A candidate satisfying all v1 active bindings returns one auditable compatibility result; an instance with zero active bindings succeeds after intrinsic and outer validation; any type, contract, field, authority, credential-kind, or non-default recovery mismatch names the affected requirement and fails the whole evaluation; a concurrent binding-set change makes the result stale, and no binding state or active pointer changes.

Inspect credential kind only, never secret material; return typed failures and the validated input identities.

Vary pool sizing and concurrency; report peak checked-out and idle stores, reserved bytes, and warm-versus-cold throughput, and quantify the cross-wiring amortization that justifies the router over compile-time composition. title: [PLAN-2A] Acquire pooled component instances in router invocation leaves
description: The adopted mechanism is the upstream pooling allocator: pre-initialized modules yielding fresh instances at microsecond cost, with linear-memory reuse off. The landed ExecutionInstancePool in crates/execution/host/src/pool.rs is keyed on (bundle, revision, entitlement), which fragments precisely the sharing the spec requires — rekey it per component digest so every wiring and tenant flow using a component shares one warm pool. Wire acquire and release into the router's per-node invocation leaf, and route success, trap, cancellation, deadline, cleanup failure, and revocation through the pool lifecycle. Expose density counters, take per-host pool sizing from a chart value, and never let two invocations share one store.
acceptance_criteria: Production executor and inline-host paths use exclusive pool leases; every outcome maps to the required reuse or retirement disposition; revision and entitlement invalidation fence checked-out stores; density counters match observed live, idle, checked-out, byte, and reuse totals; cold fallback remains bounded.

title: [PLAN-4] Enforce and record the wamn_entities tenant-floor exception
description:
## Goal

Turn the deliberate no-RLS posture of each project schema's wamn_entities OID map into a narrow, enforced, and auditable exception rather than an unguarded platform table.

## Current evidence

crates/control/provision::ensure_entity_map_sql creates relation_oid/entity_id/table_name with no tenant_id or RLS and states that it holds no tenant data and the CDC role can see the schema's WAL. The table is maintained by publish/migrate paths and read by the CDC reader. PLAN §4 permits a recorded exception, but no executable grant/shape boundary currently proves the rationale stays true.

## Scope

Record the table's owner, writers, readers, project-env placement, allowed columns, and compromise radius in the security/schema ownership sources; grant no access to application or user-SQL roles; grant only schema-control maintenance and the minimum CDC read; make restore/copy/OID refresh preserve ownership. Add drift guards so new sensitive columns, broad grants, cross-environment placement, or runtime writes invalidate the exception. If evidence shows the map is shared across project environments or carries tenant-sensitive state, replace the exception with a canonical tenant floor before closing.

## Exposure gate

Blocks multi-project or multi-client project-data exposure until the exception is mechanically enforced.

## Evidence

Use real provisioned roles and schemas: schema-control can upsert, the intended CDC reader can select, application/user-SQL/dispatcher identities cannot select or mutate, and one project's credentials cannot address another project's map.
acceptance_criteria:
- The authoritative ownership/security inventory records why wamn_entities has no row-level tenant key and the exact project-env boundary that substitutes for it.
- Table shape is limited to relation OID plus non-secret catalog/physical identifiers; schema drift adding sensitive or tenant-varying state fails.
- Application, user-SQL, dispatcher, and unrelated runtime roles have zero SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE authority; only named schema-control writers and minimum CDC read are granted.
- Copy/restore/OID-refresh paths retain the same owner/grants and cannot broaden the exception.
- Live negative role/cross-project tests and mutants for a broad grant, added sensitive column, or shared placement fail by name.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [PLAN-4] Enforce the D8 raw-SQL enablement gate
description:
## Goal

Make it impossible for a real project environment to enable author-written raw SQL before both database-role boundaries are present and proven.

## Current evidence

D8 chose a parameterized raw-SQL node behind a per-project-env flag defaulting off. The POC explicitly accepted enabling it before the dedicated-role precondition. PLAN §4 says that exception does not transfer. wamn-1nd owns the user-SQL role/non-rewritable tenant boundary; R45/wamn-2jkm.85 owns cross-project login isolation.

## Scope

Keep the feature default off in provisioning, copy, promotion, templates, and checked deployments; make enablement validate/select the dedicated user-SQL identity rather than wamn_app; fail closed if role/grants/credential/tenant binding are absent or stale; expose auditable enable/disable state. Do not add a studio/UI surface.

## Exposure gate

Blocks raw SQL in every non-POC pilot, studio, API, starter template, or real client project. The POC remains the only named exception until this gate passes.

## Evidence

Against provisioned throwaway project environments, precondition-absent enablement must fail without changing state; after both role boundaries land, bound-parameter SQL succeeds, dynamic claim/bookkeeping/cross-project attacks fail, and copy/promotion cannot widen the flag.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every new and copied/promoted environment starts with raw SQL disabled unless an explicit authorized enable operation passes all structural checks.
- Enablement refuses wamn_app, missing/stale credentials, excess bookkeeping grants, rewritable tenant authority, or a login usable against another project database.
- Successful enablement uses only the dedicated user-SQL identity; disabling revokes future admission without corrupting existing run evidence.
- A named live gate proves positive parameterized execution and negative dynamic-SQL, bookkeeping, claim-rewrite, and cross-project cases.
- Mutants that bypass a prerequisite, default the flag on, or copy a wider flag fail by name.

title: [PLAN-4] Gate custom-node transport with the H9 adversarial suite
description:
## Goal

Create the named, fail-capable black-box gate of record for the custom-node transport and runtime boundary.

## Current evidence

Existing nodeinvoke/nodebench coverage proves happy-path invocation and selected signing cases, but PLAN §4 requires one adversarial suite that simultaneously discriminates concurrency, slowloris, oversized bodies, fail-closed signing, finite node execution, and recovery of bounded capacity.

## Scope

Drive the real wamn-node-host binary/image over TCP with a real signed node component. The suite owns deterministic concurrency/slowloris/framing/body-limit/signing/runtime-timeout cases, reports each phase by name, fails on skip or partial execution, and leaves no listener/task/process residue. It consumes the production limits rather than copying them into a permissive stand-in.

## Exposure gate

This is the gate of record before custom-node execution is described as shipped or exposed through any client/multi-author surface. PLAN 0.2 owns the independent mutation-proof schedule for this gate.

## Evidence

Run locally against the debug binary and in the exact gates image/in-cluster Job. Pin source/image/component/signing identities and kill at least one load-bearing mutant per accept, parser/limit, auth, and runtime-budget layer.
acceptance_criteria:
- A held incomplete socket cannot delay healthy signed requests beyond the gate's bound, and bounded overload recovers.
- Slow headers/body/trailers time out; oversized fixed/chunked requests and ambiguous/malformed framing are rejected without node invocation.
- Default keyless, unsigned, forged, stale, and revoked-key requests are rejected; current and explicitly-overlapping previous keys succeed.
- A non-returning or memory-growing node is bounded and retired; a later healthy invocation succeeds on a clean instance.
- Every phase is named and mandatory, local plus exact-image/in-cluster modes exercise production code, and deliberate mutants fail the corresponding phase.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)
close_reason: The custom-node transport this suite gates is deleted; no node-host binary or invocation wire remains to drive adversarially.

title: [PLAN-4] Generation-fence capability dispatch at the host boundary
description:
## Goal

Make stale execution authority unable to begin or continue a capability effect after its run/attempt generation is cancelled, seized, expired, or replaced.

## Current evidence

Run-state transitions fence database completion by lease generation and deferred seizure protects a live attempt, but the capability context sent to standard/custom nodes carries no lease/authority generation and the host does not recheck it immediately before an HTTP, Postgres, credential, or custom-node effect. FLOW-SPEC §10.7 says generation-fenced capability dispatch retires deferred seizure.

## Scope

Carry a host-trusted authority generation and effective attempt deadline in InvocationCapabilityContext; define the authoritative invalidation/seizure handshake; check the generation immediately before every effect-capable host dispatch and again where a multi-stage host operation can cross invalidation; refuse stale/expired contexts with a typed non-effect outcome; prevent old tasks or pooled instances from reacquiring a newer context. Cover standard and custom node paths plus P2/P3 mirrors.

## Exposure gate

Blocks less-trusted multi-author execution and custom-node composition (PLAN 2D). Stage in the same runtime wave as H9, but only the invocation-context issue is a hard implementation prerequisite.

## Evidence

Race a paused capability call against cancellation, deadline sweep, lease seizure, and generation replacement. Prove zero effect after invalidation, exactly the authorized effect before it, and no stale-context reuse across instance retirement.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every effect-capable host boundary receives and validates an unforgeable current authority generation and effective deadline.
- Stale, seized, expired, missing, or mismatched context is refused before the external effect; refusal is typed and auditable.
- Cancellation/seizure races have a documented linearization point and do not depend on cooperative guest checks.
- Standard/custom nodes and P2/P3 capability surfaces have equivalent generation-fence coverage.
- Race tests and mutants kill a removed pre-dispatch check, a check moved after the effect, generation substitution, and stale pooled-instance reuse.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [PLAN-4] Make credential and egress authority invocation-scoped
description:
## Goal

Replace component-global mutable credential and egress declarations with immutable authority owned by one invocation.

## Current evidence

NodeRuntime installs a credential grant into an RwLock around a serialized warm instance. WamnCredentials and RunnerEgressPolicy hold mutable component-id keyed maps; the trusted runner replaces them before dispatch and runner egress is not cleared. This is safe only while NodeRuntime's mutex, one active dispatch slot per run, and &mut ExecutionHost driving remain incidental serialization.

## Scope

Define one host-owned InvocationCapabilityContext containing component/run/tenant/project identity, credential grant, egress narrowing, trace context, effective deadline, connection/config generation references, and an unforgeable context generation. Bind host capability calls to the active invocation context rather than shared component-id maps; revoke/drop it on every return, error, cancellation, timeout, and trap. Cover NodeRuntime, ExecutionHost, injected scenario/test hosts, and P2/P3 adapters without granting concurrency itself.

## Exposure gate

Blocks any concurrency inside a component store, P3 service-style concurrency, executor instance pooling that shares capability providers, less-trusted multi-author execution, and custom-node composition.

## Evidence

A deterministic overlapping-invocation harness uses disjoint credentials, allowed hosts, identities, trace values, config, and generations and proves exact non-leakage across success, error, cancellation, timeout, trap, and instance reuse.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every credential read and egress decision resolves exclusively through the immutable context of the invocation performing the host call.
- No component-id keyed mutable grant/allowlist can be overwritten by another invocation or survive completion.
- Context cleanup is guaranteed for success, guest error, host error, cancellation, timeout, trap, and dropped task.
- P2 and P3 host surfaces and production/injected ExecutionHost and NodeRuntime paths have equivalent coverage.
- A named overlap/leakage gate and mutants prove credentials, egress, trace, tenant/project/run identity, connection/config generation, and guest state cannot cross invocation boundaries.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [PLAN-4] H9: bound and retire custom-node runtime instances
description:
## Goal

Give NodeRuntime a finite per-invocation deadline and memory ceiling, with poisoned or interrupted warm instances retired before reuse.

## Current evidence

crates/platform/node-runtime creates one warm store with set_epoch_deadline(u64::MAX / 2), no WamnStoreLimiter, and returns a retryable node-trap while retaining the instance. PLAN's v2.6 upgrade appendix explicitly leaves both the deadline and memory gaps with H9.

## Scope

Derive each call's effective deadline from the trusted host ceiling and request budget; re-arm the epoch deadline per call; attach the standard memory limiter and account the aggregate instance budget; bound outgoing host calls; retire and safely recreate an instance after interruption, trap, policy generation change, or resource-limit breach. Preserve config-cache behavior only where it cannot reuse poisoned guest state.

## Exposure gate

Blocks custom-node execution. Any later instance pool or P3 service concurrency also depends on this close and on invocation-scoped capability context.

## Evidence

Use finite-loop, memory-growth, slow-host-call, trap-then-healthy, and repeated-reuse fixtures through NodeRuntime and the real node-host boundary. Record per-store and aggregate bounds separately.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every node invocation has a finite, re-armed epoch deadline bounded by trusted host policy, regardless of guest-supplied deadline shape.
- Node stores have the standard memory limiter and a documented aggregate workload budget.
- Timeout, trap, and memory-limit breach cannot return the same instance to service; a later healthy call uses a clean instance.
- Outgoing HTTP/credential capability operations cannot outlive the effective invocation budget.
- Named tests kill mutants restoring the infinite deadline, omitting re-arm, retaining a trapped instance, or removing the memory/host-call bound.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [PLAN-4] Refuse unsigned custom-node invocations by default
description:
## Goal

Make the custom-node transport fail closed when invocation-signing material is absent or a request is unsigned.

## Current evidence

RequestAuth accepts every body when no current signing key is resolved unless --require-signing-key is set. The checked serve-node deployment documents this as a legacy network-trust posture. With a key, missing and invalid signatures are already rejected and current/previous rotation is supported.

## Scope

Invert the production default so a keyless node host refuses all invocation traffic; remove the production fail-open path and any checked manifest that selects it. If an explicit unsigned development override remains, name it as unsafe, keep it absent from production renderers, and make startup/telemetry disclose it. Preserve current/previous-key rotation and timestamp freshness.

## Exposure gate

Blocks custom-node execution and any client or multi-author surface able to invoke custom nodes.

## Evidence

Exercise default keyless, keyed-current, keyed-previous, missing, malformed, forged, stale, and rotation-removal cases against the real node-host request path and checked deployment rendering.
acceptance_criteria:
- Default startup with no signing key refuses every invocation with a stable unauthorized reason.
- A configured key requires a valid signature; previous-key overlap works only while explicitly configured, and removal revokes it.
- No checked production manifest or renderer opts into unsigned invocation.
- Any development-only escape hatch is explicit, loudly observable, and rejected by production conformance.
- Named tests kill mutants that restore the keyless allow branch, omit signature verification, or retain previous-key authority after removal.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)
close_reason: The custom-node transport and its keyless fail-open path are deleted; artifact-level verification is carried by wamn-0si.9 at component admission.

title: [PLAN-4] H9: bounded concurrent node-host accept and request handling
description:
## Goal

Remove the unauthenticated head-of-line denial-of-service in services/node-host without making the warm component or mutable capability state concurrently shared.

## Current evidence

NodeHost::serve awaits serve_connection inline. read_request accepts unbounded headers and fixed/chunked bodies with no header, body, idle, or write deadline and does not reject ambiguous framing. One incomplete peer can stall every later connection.

## Scope

Accept connections into bounded tasks with explicit overload behavior; bound header count/bytes and decoded body bytes; reject malformed, duplicate, conflicting, or overflowed framing; enforce header/body/idle/write deadlines; keep each connection's parser buffers private. Invocation may remain serialized at the NodeRuntime boundary until invocation-scoped context and safe instance pooling land.

## Exposure gate

Blocks custom-node execution and every pilot/client surface that can invoke a custom node. It does not block standard-node-only HTTP ingress, which owns a separate ingress gate.

## Evidence

Black-box tests must hold an incomplete connection while valid signed requests complete, exhaust and recover bounded connection capacity, and prove slowloris, oversized fixed/chunked bodies, framing ambiguity, and malformed lengths are rejected without unbounded allocation or starving healthy peers.
acceptance_criteria:
- One slow or incomplete socket cannot prevent an independently accepted valid request from completing.
- Concurrent connection tasks are explicitly bounded and overload fails fast; parser/body buffers and all read/write phases have named limits and deadlines.
- Content-Length plus chunked ambiguity, duplicate/conflicting lengths, invalid or overflowing sizes, oversized headers, fixed bodies, chunks, and trailers are refused.
- No two invocations concurrently mutate or use one warm NodeRuntime instance as a consequence of this issue.
- Unit and black-box tests kill mutants that restore inline awaiting, remove the capacity bound, remove a deadline, or remove each size/framing refusal.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)
close_reason: exe-model.md §The router / §Ingress paths 1: the node-host accept loop is deleted and component invocation is in-process; HTTP-level concurrency is the route's bounded in-flight limit.

title: [PLAN-4] Bring the inline wamn_catalog snapshot onto the tenant floor
description:
## Goal

Bring each project schema's inline wamn_catalog serving snapshot onto the same hardened tenant floor as checked platform DDL.

## Current evidence

services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs creates wamn_catalog inline with tenant_id and ENABLE/FORCE RLS, but its policy compares directly to current_setting('app.tenant', true) and the table lacks CHECK (tenant_id <> ''). The canonical a45 floor uses NULLIF(..., '') plus the non-empty CHECK. Host/plugin tenant validation reduces current exploitability but is not the database boundary PLAN §4 requires.

## Scope

Move or generate the table definition from an authoritative schema owner; migrate existing tables additively to the canonical non-empty tenant column/policy shape; keep runtime access least privilege and snapshot publication atomic with its owning catalog lifecycle. Cover publish, migrate, copy/restore, reconciliation, and schema-drift detection without duplicating DDL strings.

## Exposure gate

Blocks multi-project or multi-client data exposure through the generated API/catalog-serving path.

## Evidence

A throwaway/live-schema gate seeds distinct tenants plus a superuser-created empty-tenant sentinel, then proves correct own-tenant reads and zero foreign/empty-claim reads through the real plugin/gateway query path. Drift and mutation tests pin the floor shape and migration.
acceptance_criteria:
- wamn_catalog has tenant_id NOT NULL CHECK (tenant_id <> ''), ENABLE and FORCE RLS, and USING/WITH CHECK keyed through NULLIF of the host claim.
- Existing project schemas migrate additively and idempotently; publish/migrate/copy/restore/reconcile cannot recreate the weaker inline shape.
- Runtime roles have only the required read surface and no broad write grant.
- A live two-tenant plus empty-claim gate proves zero leakage and correct own-tenant serving.

title: [PLAN-4] Kickoff: sequence the structural closes

design:
## Filed close graph

### Parallel structural tranche

- wamn-4q3c.4 — bounded concurrent node-host accept/request handling.
- wamn-4q3c.5 — unsigned invocation fails closed by default.
- wamn-4q3c.6 — finite NodeRuntime deadline, memory budget, and instance retirement.
- wamn-4q3c.7 — immutable invocation-scoped credential/egress/identity context.
- wamn-1nd — dedicated user-SQL role plus non-rewritable tenant authority.
- wamn-4q3c.3 — canonical tenant floor for inline wamn_catalog.
- wamn-4q3c.11 — enforced recorded exception for wamn_entities.

These are logically parallel. .6 and .7 collide in NodeRuntime/runtime policy files and should use isolated lanes plus serialized integration, not a false hard dependency.

### Direct build-on tranche

- wamn-4q3c.8 depends on .7: capability dispatch validates the invocation context's authority generation at the effect boundary.
- wamn-4q3c.9 depends on .4 + .5 + .6: named black-box H9/signing adversarial gate.
- wamn-4q3c.10 depends on wamn-1nd + R45/wamn-2jkm.85: D8 real-project enablement gate.
- wamn-tsl5 now depends on .10 because it is the known raw-SQL consumer.

No other sequencing is encoded as a dependency: PLAN §4 runs continuously, and exposure conditions belong in each issue.

## Exposure conditions

- Custom-node execution/client exposure: .4, .5, .6, then .9.
- Less-trusted multi-author execution and custom-node composition: .7, then .8.
- Raw SQL outside the named POC exception: wamn-1nd plus R45, then .10.
- Multi-project/multi-client project-data exposure: .3 and .11.
- Mutation-proof credit remains owned by PLAN 0.2; .9 supplies the named custom-node gate it must mutate.
notes:
Kickoff evidence 2026-08-01

- services/node-host/src/main.rs awaits serve_connection inline; its parser has unbounded headers/bodies and no phase deadlines.
- RequestAuth admits keyless unsigned requests unless --require-signing-key; deploy/platform/serve-node.yaml documents the legacy network-trust default.
- crates/platform/node-runtime uses one mutexed warm instance, a mutable credential-grant RwLock, an effectively infinite epoch deadline, no store limiter, and retains the instance after traps.
- runtime WamnCredentials and RunnerEgressPolicy use mutable component-id keyed maps; egress declarations are replaced but not invocation-owned.
- FLOW-SPEC §10.7 and the v2.6 upgrade plan require host-boundary authority fencing, dual P2/P3 coverage, and instance retirement.
- wamn-1nd is the correct existing D8 carrier; R45 is a separate hard prerequisite for cross-project credential isolation.
- Current table classification: inline wamn_catalog has RLS but not the canonical a45 NULLIF/non-empty floor; wamn_entities explicitly has no RLS and claims a project-env metadata exception. .3/.11 require evidence to confirm or correct those identities before code changes.

title: [PLAN-5] Decision: who holds v1 disposition verbs and at what granularity
description: PLAN.md v1 recovery posture makes disposition, not re-execution, the v1 operator surface. Decide which project or platform roles may park, release, and resolve an effect attempt; whether resolve requires a stronger role than park/release; the single-attempt and bulk authorization granularity; and the audit/separation-of-duties rules for bulk filters by connection, generation, flow, and time window. Resolution asserts succeeded or failed with a typed basis and dispositions an immutable attempt; it never rewrites the original or grants compensation, Replay, or silent re-execution. Consumers: PLAN-1 disposition surface, PLAN-5 role model, and PLAN-6A run visibility.
design: Decision only. Do not reopen the parked semantic-strengthening, re-attempt, compensation, declarative failure-policy, or controlled-Replay scope.
acceptance_criteria: The owner approves an explicit role-by-verb matrix, single and bulk granularity, filter scope, separation-of-duties posture, and audit identity/basis requirements; attempts remain immutable; no ordinary flow author receives implicit self-approval; the decision is folded into PLAN.md and unblocks wamn-4u7p.42.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-06: automatic park is system-owned. Project deployer and project admin may manually park/release; only project admin may resolve. Platform admin is audited break-glass and cross-project authority. Bulk park/release is project-scoped. Bulk resolve is admin-only, materializes immutable attempt ids, and requires connection+generation plus a bounded time window; flow may only narrow. Every resolve records principal, role, typed basis, evidence reference, exact attempt set, and correlation id. The author/publisher may not self-resolve except via separately audited platform break-glass. Fold into PLAN before closing and dispatching wamn-4u7p.42.

The item-8 historical-vs-current-definition question is the event-plane instance. Consumers: 1, 8, 6A.

description: PLAN.md item 5. title: [PLAN-2B] Connections
description: PLAN.md section 2B. The env/artifact boundary for anything external - closes the known gap that outbound endpoints live in flow artifacts (http-request takes url in node config, so dev tests v3 while prod runs v4). Three concepts: connection requirement (artifact/template, portable), connection instance (environment-owned), connection binding (env-specific release). Egress derives from connections as the innermost of three layers (connection authority, platform host policy, cluster network policy) through one canonical resolver that redirects/DNS/proxy cannot widen. Per-attempt generation pinning; controlled activation (compatibility validation fail-closed, status quo preserved); semantic attestations are privileged, attributable, expiring - expiry fails explicitly, never silently downgrades. Owns the connection ABI (WIT) - universal for standard and custom nodes; 2C owns the SDK bindings over it. Record-map (adjacent, not reparented): wamn-fqg.13 (5.9 live K8s Secret credential source), wamn-5x0.1 (2.2b live credential provider), wamn-fqg.24 (5.6 egress platform-internal class), wamn-ou1 (per-project egress entries).
acceptance_criteria: The identical flow artifact runs in dev and prod against different connection definitions; a flow referencing an unsatisfied connection fails at publish, not dispatch; a destination outside the connection authority fails at dispatch; a connection that cannot satisfy a declared recovery requirement rejects the artifact rather than silently degrading; an incompatible new generation is refused while the existing compatible generation stays active.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [PLAN-2A] Execution-bundle specialization
description: PLAN.md section 2A. Capability by construction: a flow capability set decided by what it is composed of, not what its runner imports. Decides packaging granularity (exact-node vs capability-class - the load-bearing ambiguity 2A must distinguish, not merely measure), capability worlds, and the economics: composition latency, cache hit rate, cold start, memory, and the platform-upgrade recomposition event. Instance pooling is the density mechanism and it is wamn to build (upstream pool_size does not cover a manually constructed ExecutionHost). Compositions keyed by execution-bundle identity, never node-type names; cache reuse respects entitlement once private components exist. Fallback if economics fail: linked runner - only the structural capability ceiling is lost, everything else survives. Capability-bearing evidence must use the 2B minimum typed-connection WIT. Blocks PLAN-3 and PLAN-6A. Record-map: wamn-2jkm.78/.79/.80 (SR15/SR16/SR17), wamn-4tob.6.28 (VERIFY-NODE-WORKLOAD), wamn-4tob.1.40 (AUDIT-ADOPT-RUNTIME), wamn-fqg.40 (D21-WAKER), wamn-l5i9.49/.51/.71 (E12a run-worker Service, D21-DISPATCH decisions).
acceptance_criteria: The packaging shape is chosen from measured evidence; a capability-bearing node composes; a composed runner imports exactly its bundle capability classes, proven by inspecting the artifact; draft and published execution use the same bundle.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [PLAN-1] Payload durability and the blob boundary
description: PLAN.md section 1. Owns what is durable and where bytes live, including the handle and streaming contract that the 2C blob node consumes. Three storage classes with different scaling models - active checkpoint (bounded by nonterminal working set), replay/audit seed (retention-bounded), capture (independent, optional) - measured separately. Capture must never be load-bearing: today reconstruct() replays captured emissions (ReconstructError::CaptureOff proves it); this item finishes the boundary-checkpoint migration. Claim-check offload above threshold; streaming blob node for bulk; strict platform/client blob split (separate namespaces, credentials, buckets); two GC mechanisms (referenced-object retention by replay reachability, uncommitted-orphan TTL). Blocks the PLAN-3 exit and the bulk capability in items 8-9. Record-map: wamn-sdp (5.10 payload store and limits), wamn-fqg.25 (5.6 streamed payloads), wamn-72i (wamn:node 0.2 / WASI 0.3 - input to the streaming ABI decision), wamn-l5i9.13 (EVT-CLAIMCHECK inherits the store), wamn-l5i9.29 (payload-store backend spike), wamn-h0rf (cold-path offload), wamn-ohsr (per-payload thresholding), wamn-mdgf (lineage-aware retention), wamn-q8my (content-aware scrubbing), wamn-wpaj (streamed-payload cases).
acceptance_criteria: A run recovers correctly with capture off; over-threshold payloads ride as references with bytes in the blob store; a crash between blob write and checkpoint leaves an orphan and a resumable run, never a dangling reference; GC reclaims orphans without reaching client objects; the same F1 scenario measured before and after shows the WAL and storage difference the model predicts.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [PLAN-0.2] Gate integrity
description: PLAN.md section 0.2 (docs/PLAN/PLAN.md) - continuous obligation. Gates backing shipped decisions variously cannot fail, soft-skip, or cover a fraction of what they claim, and the suite is hand-run, so a decorative gate is undetectable. Foundational: until this holds, every Done-when in PLAN.md is unfalsifiable. Failure mode: a decision found resting on a gate that never could have failed. Record-map (existing beads serving this item, not reparented): wamn-2jkm.98 (SR26 gate-of-record receipts), wamn-4tob.6.25 (VERIFY-GATE-RECEIPT), wamn-2jkm.24 (SR13 schema drift guard), wamn-2jkm.25 (SR10 gates submodules), wamn-48o (live gate standard-node), wamn-ec7j (EVT-CAUSATION-E2E gate), wamn-v1pp (pg-init ConfigMap drift guard), wamn-uu0g (testgate hard fixture), wamn-rif5 (cold-miss gate coverage), wamn-0vfn (streambench guard).
acceptance_criteria: Every gate backing a shipped decision has a mutation proof - a deliberate break that makes it red - and the suite runs on a schedule rather than by hand.

title: [AUDIT-VERIFY-NODE-WORKLOAD] Prove component-first custom-node hosting in one wasmCloud workload
description:
## Goal

Discriminate whether the current custom-node HTTP serving responsibility can become a trusted wasmCloud service/component linked to the tenant wamn:node component, instead of creating a permanent native node-host exception.

## Questions

- Can the pinned wash-runtime/operator compose a service or wrapper component that invokes a wamn:node export in the same Workload while preserving the existing invocation contract?
- Can hostInterfaces, credentials, outbound HTTP, memory limits, and allowed-host policy remain least-authority per node workload?
- Can node artifact replacement, restart, scaling, and rollback occur without rebuilding or rolling the general host image?
- If the path fails, which exact runtime, WIT-linking, lifecycle, or capability limitation requires a native exception, and what is its exit condition?

## Evidence Required

- A real componentized node artifact plus wrapper/service workload on the pinned fork/operator, not a synthesized-only WIT fixture.
- The existing wamn:node, wamn-node-invoke, builder grant derivation, nodeinvoke, credential, egress, and resource-limit evidence.
- Immutable artifact identities and observed Workload/host placement for both wrapper and tenant node.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A valid signed invocation reaches the real node through the component workload and produces the same typed result as the current serve-node path.
- Missing or undeclared imports fail at bind/start, and the workload receives only its declared credential and egress capabilities.
- Node update, crash, restart, and rollback are bounded to the node workload and do not roll the general wasmCloud host artifact.
- The proof records exact source/component/deployment identities and distinguishes component-link behavior from an in-process unit test.
- Failure to satisfy the path records a concrete unavailable capability or runtime limitation plus an owner and exit condition; native placement is not accepted merely because it is current.

title: [R54] Development admission lacks a measured fail-closed capacity invariant
description:
## Goal

Enforce an evidence-derived, configuration-specific development admission invariant so new workload state or resources are refused before measured capacity exhaustion can violate correctness.

## Questions

- Which measured resources and compound workload dimensions define the safe admission envelope for the current exploratory deployment?
- Which authority owns the versioned budget and which provisioning, activation, registration, route, runtime, database, broker, and queue boundaries must consult it?
- How are stale or missing measurements, concurrent admissions, capacity release, hysteresis, and operator override handled without over-admission or stranded capacity?
- Which exhaustion cases require refusal, backpressure, quiescence, or explicit degraded operation?

## Evidence Required

- Source evidence that the current T3 path has no tenant/connection admission bound, creates per-project pools and workloads, and omits a default Database connectionLimit.
- wamn-4tob.6.27 baseline-matched DEV-CAP-ADMISSION reproduction identifying the first relevant resource limits, interactions, and safety margins on the exact consumer-hardware configuration.
- Atomic concurrent-admission, stale-telemetry, overload, release/retry, restart, and recovery tests.
- Proof that refusal occurs before acknowledged-write loss, silent corruption, cross-client leakage, unrecoverable event gaps, or nondeterministic recovery.

## Steps to Reproduce

Run the DEV-CAP-ADMISSION ladder from wamn-4tob.6.27 against a baseline-matched exploratory deployment. Increase evidence-selected configured and active workload variables until the first resource safety margin is exhausted. The current platform has no authoritative capacity budget or capacity reservation, so provisioning and activation can continue until a downstream connection, WAL, storage, broker, Kubernetes/etcd, route, runtime, queue, backup, or reconciliation limit fails independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One explicit authority owns a versioned, hardware/configuration-specific admission budget derived from wamn-4tob.6.27 evidence.
- Every resource-allocating or workload-activating boundary covered by that budget admits atomically or refuses visibly before side effects or acknowledgement.
- Concurrent requests cannot over-admit; stale or unavailable capacity evidence fails in the owner-decided safe direction.
- Capacity release, retries, restarts, overrides, and topology changes are idempotent and auditable.
- A targeted overload gate proves zero acknowledged-work loss, silent corruption, cross-client leakage, unrecoverable event gap, and nondeterministic recovery at refusal.
- The development budget is not exposed as a production, customer, or general-hardware scale promise.
notes:
Created from the owner-set fail-closed capacity requirement in wamn-4tob.1.12 and the source-supported absence of a current admission invariant in findings J.1/J.3. Measurement/proof .6.27 is a hard prerequisite. This implementation finding is not authorized for execution now.

## Steps to Reproduce

title: [AUDIT-VERIFY-JS-DR] Destroy all event-broker PVCs after ACK and before materialization
description:

## Decision Constraint

title: [R51] Event-plane disaster recovery is absent after source feedback advances
description:
## Goal

Make total JetStream loss recoverable before Wamn claims lossless broker disaster recovery. Until then, keep the unsupported failure envelope explicit and never represent broker acknowledgement as end-to-end recovery.

## Questions

- Which acknowledged events can exist only in JetStream after source-slot feedback advances?
- Where will stream/account snapshots be stored, verified, retained, and restored if production policy requires them?
- How will source database/capture epoch, WAL position, JetStream stream/consumer state, and PostgreSQL source-derived run identity be reconciled?
- Which production recovery policy will wamn-4tob.1.19 eventually select?

## Evidence Required

- Current stream, consumer, source-slot, LSN, capture-epoch, and PostgreSQL run identities.
- The accepted state-authority decision in wamn-4tob.1.17: JetStream remains durable in-flight transport and no direct-PostgreSQL replacement or separate receipt table is selected.
- A baseline-matched total-broker-loss campaign after source feedback advances but before every event materializes.

## Steps to Reproduce

Publish a committed source event and allow every JetStream server acknowledgement to complete so source feedback advances. Prevent the materializer from committing that event to PostgreSQL, then destroy every JetStream persistent copy. Attempt the documented recovery, if one exists, and compare source LSN/capture epoch, broker state, PostgreSQL runs, queues, and effects with the acknowledged source set.

## Decision Constraint

The owner keeps the current WAL to JetStream to materializer architecture and defers JetStream backup and total-loss recovery until production policy work. This finding remains open; the deferral creates no current lossless-DR claim and does not select a direct-PostgreSQL fallback.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An implemented, integrity-checked snapshot/restore path reconstructs required stream bytes, configuration, consumers, and acknowledgement floors before lossless broker disaster recovery is claimed.
- Restored source or broker history cannot reuse semantic event identity or silently duplicate effects.
- Recovery reports the exact recovered point and any missing interval; an unsupported interval fails visibly.
- Evidence correlates source LSN/capture epoch, broker state, source-derived PostgreSQL run identity, and effects.
- wamn-4tob.6.23 proves the implemented behavior; a design decision alone does not close R51.
notes:
ARC9 found no event stream/account snapshot or restore path. The reader advances PostgreSQL feedback after broker ACK, so total broker-PVC loss can destroy ACKed-but-unmaterialized events after source WAL is recyclable. This is distinct from R48 PostgreSQL PITR, R44 dedupe identity, and E18/E19. Proof wamn-4tob.6.23; .1.17 chooses whether JetStream remains an authority and .6.18 compares direct Postgres.
DEC-STATE OUTCOME 2026-07-23: keep current JetStream architecture; defer backup/total-loss recovery to .1.19; keep R51 open; make no lossless-DR claim. Reconcile source-derived PostgreSQL run identity, not a separate receipt table.
held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [R50] Bound JetStream capacity to physical storage and source-WAL safety
description:

## Acceptance Criteria

- Configured server capacity is below usable persistent storage with an explicit safety margin.
- Every production EVT stream has an explicit byte/time bound and a loss-safe discard or refusal policy.
- Alerts fire before both broker and source-WAL safety thresholds by the owner-set recovery margin.
- One tenant or cell cannot exhaust unrelated recovery domains.
- The documented expansion/recovery path catches up without dropping or silently recreating the source slot.

title: [R49] Untrusted custom-node build shares artifact-signing authority
description:
## Goal

Make tenant-controlled compilation and test execution unable to observe or exercise artifact-signing or registry-publish authority.

## Questions

- What immutable handoff binds source revision, policy result, SBOM, toolchain identity, and exact Wasm digest?
- Is signing keyless or KMS-backed, or performed by a separately scheduled signer principal?

## Evidence Required

- An adversarial root build script that attempts to read signing material, environment, service-account state, and registry credentials.

- Rotation and revocation proof showing old authority cannot produce deployable bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Compilation and tests receive no signing key, KMS capability, registry-write credential, or Kubernetes token.
- The signer and publisher never execute tenant source or its build scripts.
- The signer verifies policy and provenance and signs the exact immutable digest from the approved handoff.

Cargo root build scripts are executable tenant code.
