title: [AUDIT-DEC-STATE] Choose authoritative state and reconciliation model
description:
## Goal

Choose one explicit authority and reconciliation contract for Wamn application state and every native-system boundary it crosses.

## Questions

- Which state is authoritative, derived, cached, or audit evidence at every cross-plane boundary?
- Which stable identity, transaction, acknowledgement, retention, and recovery rules prevent split brain?
- What roles, if any, do JetStream and a durable workflow engine have alongside PostgreSQL?

## Evidence Required

- ARC4 state-transition matrix and R34-R44, E18, R28/R29, and SR13 evidence.
- ARC5 runtime alternatives, ARC6 PostgreSQL topology, ARC7 event topology, ARC9 recovery analysis, and STR6 source-of-truth policy.
- Named crash/replay/restore proofs for unresolved acknowledged cross-store transitions.

## Decision

PostgreSQL is the durable authority for Wamn application and execution state, not a universal infrastructure metadata or control plane.

- T1 PostgreSQL owns only Wamn organization, project, environment, product placement, and other product records genuinely required by Wamn.
- Project/environment PostgreSQL owns tenant data, catalog/schema lifecycle, flows/tests, runs, queue, timers, leases, checkpoints, dead letters, replay lineage, and idempotency state.
- PostgreSQL run/queue/checkpoint state remains the sole flow-orchestration authority. No co-equal durable workflow engine is selected.
- Keep the current PostgreSQL WAL to CDC reader to JetStream to materializer to PostgreSQL run/queue path. JetStream owns durable in-flight transport after source feedback, not business or orchestration state. Total-broker-loss recovery remains explicitly deferred.
- Semantic event identity derives from source database/capture epoch, WAL position or ordinal, and registration identity. JetStream sequence is transport order and diagnostics only. The existing run row is the deduplication marker while retained; no separate receipt table is decided.
- Kubernetes owns deployment specifications, Jobs and retries, rollout, readiness, reconciliation, resource generations/status, scheduling, networking, storage orchestration, and runtime operation. PostgreSQL does not mirror, journal, coordinate, or inherit those capabilities.
- OCI/build owns artifact manifests and immutable digest-addressed bytes; native Secret storage owns credential bytes and metadata; backup tooling/object storage owns backup objects and native metadata. Wamn stores only a narrow reference when an application record genuinely requires it.
- Telemetry systems own telemetry as derived evidence, never application truth.

This decision does not silently rewrite D6, D18, D19, or another canonical decision row.

## Alternatives Considered

- A universal PostgreSQL-centered infrastructure control model with desired/observed Kubernetes state: rejected as overreach and duplication of Kubernetes capability.
- Direct CDC to a PostgreSQL receipt/run/queue transaction: not selected; retained only as comparison evidence.
- A platform-wide log-centered/event-sourced model: rejected as the general authority model.
- A durable workflow engine replacing PostgreSQL orchestration: not selected.
- The current topology with clarified native authorities and corrected event identity/recovery claims: selected.

## Rationale

The selected boundary preserves the strongest existing PostgreSQL transactions without turning PostgreSQL into a second Kubernetes, registry, Secret manager, broker, or backup catalog. It retains JetStream for the WAL handoff the product chose, makes delivery guarantees explicit, and keeps unresolved correctness gaps under their existing finding and proof owners.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every named application or native-system state class has one explicit authority and recovery owner.
- Cross-system handoffs state stable identity, acknowledgement, retention, and failure semantics without inventing a universal PostgreSQL reconciler.
- Exactly-once claims name the identity, effect boundary, and retention horizon; external effects remain explicitly at least once unless the sink is idempotent.
- JetStream is retained as transport, PostgreSQL is the sole orchestration authority, and Kubernetes remains the sole deployment authority.
- Existing unresolved identity, broker-recovery, artifact, Secret, backup, copy, and restore gaps remain open under named Beads and findings.
- ARC11 and STR9 can use the decision without inventing state ownership or treating a target proposal as an implemented fix.
notes:
RESTRUCTURE ROUTING (wamn-4tob.9; docs/findings.md section I): the proposal table list is not a complete authority model. Decide current and target authority, writers/readers, stable identity/version, retention, reconciliation, and migration owner for Postgres plus JetStream, WAL slots/publications, OCI/object artifacts, Kubernetes generations, Secrets, and backups. One semantic authority does not imply one crate or one physical store.
ARC6/ARC7 HANDOFF 2026-07-23: evaluate the state decision against separate T1 plus bounded tenant cells and a queue-first trigger plane. The preferred hypothesis is a source-derived compact receipt plus run/queue transaction before logical-slot feedback; JetStream or a raw inbox is derived/optional only for accepted replay, late fan-out, or measured outage buffering. Assign authority for placement generation, source database/capture epoch, receipt retention, broker/consumer state, and restore timeline identity. Proof .6.18 discriminates direct Postgres, broker, and inbox variants.
ARC9 HANDOFF 2026-07-23: cross-store recovery cannot restore PostgreSQL/WAL slots, JetStream consumer floors, target receipts, OCI bytes, Kubernetes generations, Secrets, and backup bytes independently. Assign capture epoch/timeline and restore reconciliation. R51/wamn-2jkm.91 is the current broker-DR contradiction; proof .6.23 and alternative comparison .6.18 discriminate retained-broker versus direct-Postgres authority.
STR6 HANDOFF 2026-07-23 (docs/findings.md R.2): apply explicit reconciliation policies to WAL/JetStream positions, desired/observed stream and consumer config, publication/slot shape, OCI/deployed bytes, Kubernetes desired/observed generation, Secret reference/version/cache, and backup bytes/checkpoint metadata. Structural comparison is required except exact artifact bytes; Secrets deliberately version separately through immutable references. Existing R/E owners remain authoritative.
ISOLATION DECISION HANDOFF 2026-07-23: wamn-4tob.1.15 sets client isolation as a current correctness invariant at every supported platform API. Evaluate the effective authority reachable through each narrow WIT/WASI interface, including host credentials and shared connections. Detailed trust, infrastructure-security profiles, credential lifecycle, residency/regulation, audit/operator access, and retention/erasure are deferred to .1.25-.30 and must not be invented in this development state-authority decision. Ordinary cross-client data/effect scope remains disqualifying.
AUTHORIZED RESUME PLAN 2026-07-24: On resume execute ONLY wamn-4tob.1.17, then stop. Run bd prime; verify the issue remains open and ready, no other issue is active, dependency cycles are absent, HEAD/local tracking/actual origin agree, and preserve user-owned dirty paths .beads/interactions.jsonl, AGENTS.md, and untracked docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md. Claim .1.17 only. Re-read ARC4/ARC6/ARC7/ARC9/STR6 evidence and docs/findings.md state, topology, event, recovery, and source-of-truth sections, including REVIEW-260723 and RESTRUCTURE-260723 routing already integrated into the bead. Conduct owner Q&A one contextual question at a time: explain the concrete state classes and failure being decided, present correctness-qualified alternatives and a recommendation, then wait for the answer. Start with the proposed PostgreSQL-centered durable core; separately decide JetStream role, workflow-engine role, cross-store acknowledgement/identity/reconciliation, and authority for OCI/object bytes, Kubernetes generations, Secret references, and backup/checkpoint metadata. Respect settled constraints: correctness above all; client isolation is current; trust/security and production SLO/topology details are deferred; do not invent them. After owner acceptance, update docs/findings.md and affected audit-bead handoffs without rewriting canonical decision rows; file every residual unknown as its own granular decision or proof bead; run documentation/dependency validation only unless baseline-matched live proof is specifically applicable. Close .1.17, commit and git push the issue-specific changes, run bd dolt push, report, and stop before .1.12, .1.13, .1.16, ARC11, STR9, or verification work. No subagents are planned for the serial owner Q&A; use at most one read-only evidence lane only if a bounded evidence gap emerges.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q1 DURABLE AUTHORITY: The owner concurs that PostgreSQL should be the source of durable truth. Apply this as a semantic authority rule, not a one-physical-database rule: T1 PostgreSQL owns durable control intent and generations; project/environment PostgreSQL owns durable tenant, catalog, flow/test, run/queue/timer/lease, and idempotency state. A broker, cache, Kubernetes object, or telemetry store must not be the sole surviving record of accepted work. Exact artifact bytes, Secret bytes, JetStream's permitted derived role, workflow-engine disposition, and cross-store receipt/recovery details remain to be decided in the following questions.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q2 JETSTREAM ROLE: Keep the current event architecture: committed PostgreSQL WAL is decoded by the CDC reader, published to JetStream, then materialized into the PostgreSQL run/queue authority. JetStream is therefore a required durable in-flight delivery store after source-slot feedback advances, not merely an optional projection. Defer JetStream backup and total-broker-loss recovery; do not represent that deferred development failure envelope as solved or lossless. Existing R51/wamn-2jkm.91 and proof wamn-4tob.6.23 retain the broker-DR gap, with production outage/recovery policy in wamn-4tob.1.19. Preserve stable source identity and PostgreSQL receipt/idempotency requirements; no implementation change is authorized inside the audit.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q3 WORKFLOW AUTHORITY: Retain PostgreSQL run, queue, timer, lease, node-checkpoint, dead-letter, and replay-lineage state as the sole durable flow-orchestration authority. Do not introduce a co-equal external durable workflow engine. A future workflow-engine adoption would require an explicit replacement/migration decision rather than duplication of retries, timers, or completion authority; it remains deferred and receives no current target role. External effects remain at least once unless the sink honors durable idempotency.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q4 EVENT IDENTITY: Use a canonical source-derived identity for event idempotency and run creation: source database/capture epoch plus WAL event position or ordinal plus registration identity. JetStream stream sequence is transport ordering/diagnostic state only and must not define semantic run identity. This decision does NOT prescribe a separate receipt table. The existing run row is the durable materialization/dedupe marker while retained. R44/wamn-2jkm.82 and proofs wamn-4tob.6.9/.6.17 retain the post-pruning/replay-horizon gap and may choose retention coupling, a compact tombstone, or explicit refusal of replay older than retained identity. Exact schema and performance impact require implementation proof; no fix occurs in this audit.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q5 CONTROL RECONCILIATION: Every control-plane operation that affects PostgreSQL/CNPG, Kubernetes, Secrets, OCI/object storage, or another external system records stable desired identity and generation in T1 PostgreSQL and remains incomplete until the external resource is verified and its observed identity/generation/status is recorded. T1 owns durable desired intent and operation progress; the external system remains authoritative for its actual current condition, and the T1 observation is evidence that must be refreshed rather than blindly trusted. Divergence is visible and fails closed. Documented manual reconciliation is acceptable during development; no immediate continuous-controller implementation is implied by this audit decision.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q6 ARTIFACT AUTHORITY: PostgreSQL owns durable artifact metadata and semantic state: immutable digest, version, publication/approval state, and required deployment generation. OCI or object storage owns the exact immutable bytes addressed by that digest. Publication completes only after byte presence and digest verification; deployments refer to the immutable digest rather than treating mutable tags or annotations as authority. Missing or corrupt bytes fail closed, and a rebuild produces a new digest/generation rather than silently replacing recorded identity. Source, built, signed, published, fetched, packaged, and invoked bytes must compare to the same identity; existing R43/SR17/SR26 and their proof owners remain open.
OWNER SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-07-23: Reconsider the broad Q5/Q6 interpretation that PostgreSQL should store or coordinate metadata for every external system. The owner rejects turning PostgreSQL into a universal infrastructure metadata/control model and states that this is going too far. Q7's proposed PostgreSQL/Kubernetes generation model is NOT accepted. Do not require PostgreSQL to mirror Kubernetes deployment specifications/status or automatically centralize OCI, Secret, JetStream, object-store, or backup metadata. Q5/Q6 remain provisional only to the extent they implied that broad centralization; establish a narrower application-state boundary with the owner before final integration.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q5/Q6/Q7 SCOPE RESET: PostgreSQL authority is limited to Wamn application and execution state: tenant data, catalog/schema lifecycle, flows/tests, runs, queue/timers/leases/checkpoints/idempotency, plus existing T1 product identity and placement records. Wamn is NOT inheriting, mirroring, or reimplementing Kubernetes capabilities. Kubernetes remains authoritative for deployment specifications, scheduling, reconciliation, rollout, readiness, resource generations, networking, storage orchestration, and runtime status. OCI/build systems own artifact manifests and immutable bytes; Secret storage owns credential state; JetStream owns transport state; object/backup systems own backup objects and native metadata. PostgreSQL stores only narrow external references genuinely required by an application record. This supersedes Q5's broad desired/observed-resource model, rejects Q7, and narrows Q6: PostgreSQL does not become a universal artifact or infrastructure metadata catalog.
OWNER CORRECTION 2026-07-23 — KUBERNETES DEPLOYMENT AUTHORITY: Kubernetes owns deployment. Kubernetes Jobs, Deployments, custom resources, operators/controllers, and their native status own deployment execution, retry, reconciliation, readiness, and failure evidence. PostgreSQL is not a Kubernetes desired-state store, deployment coordinator, deployment-status mirror, or deployment operation journal. Do not add T1 saga/progress rows to coordinate Kubernetes deployment. T1 may retain Wamn product identities and placement configuration that the application genuinely needs, but not Kubernetes step state. The prior proposed minimal PostgreSQL journal for multi-system deployment is rejected. Existing provisioning saga rows receive no target-authority justification from this decision; their disposition belongs to later architecture synthesis, with no implementation change inside the audit.
FINAL INTEGRATION 2026-07-23: docs/findings.md F.6 records the controlling owner decision and reconciles the affected ARC4/ARC5/ARC7/ARC9, restructure, deployment-structure, roadmap, and STR6 sections. Handoffs were appended to ARC4, ARC5, ARC6, ARC7, ARC9, STR6, ARC11, and STR9. R44, R51, and proofs .6.11/.6.17/.6.18/.6.23 were clarified without execution or closure: no separate receipt table, direct PostgreSQL and workflow alternatives are comparison-only, JetStream remains the current handoff, and total-loss recovery remains deferred. Existing Beads cover every residual; no duplicate was created. bd lint passed for seven affected issues, bd dep cycles is clean, and git diff --check passed. No Rust/runtime source changed and no live gate was applicable.

Integrated in docs/findings.md F.6 and affected audit handoffs; unresolved findings/proofs remain open. Documentation and Beads validation passed; no runtime change or live gate.

title: [E18] Materializer silently accepts stale durable-consumer configuration
description:
## Goal

Make a materializer bind either prove that the existing JetStream durable consumer matches the requested filter and delivery policy or refuse visibly before consuming.

## Questions

- Which actor owns changes to filter subject, explicit-ack policy, ack wait, and maximum delivery count?
- Should drift be reconciled, refused, or migrated under a new durable identity?
- How is a registration edit prevented from continuing on an old entity filter or delivery policy?

## Evidence Required

- Baseline source evidence from `crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_jetstream.rs:357-388` and the pinned async-nats 0.47 `Stream::get_or_create_consumer` contract/source.
- A baseline-matched JetStream test that pre-creates the same durable name with a conflicting filter, ack wait, or max-deliver value and then binds through the production plugin.

## Steps to Reproduce

title: [R44] Event dedupe expires when run-history retention removes the identity
description:
## Goal

Preserve the deterministic identity of a materialized event for at least every stream-retention, consumer-replay, redelivery, and recovery horizon, independently of prunable run history.

## Questions

- Which durable state owns the event identity after the corresponding terminal run is pruned?
- What retention relation must hold between event dedupe, stream replay, run history, and backup restore?
- How are intentional replay-namespaced executions distinguished from accidental redelivery?

## Evidence Required

- Baseline source evidence from `docs/event-plane-jetstream.md:126-138,191-229`, `crates/wamn-run-store/src/sql.rs:215-239`, and `deploy/sql/run-state.sql:50-74`.
- A baseline-matched crash/replay test that materializes an event, terminalizes and prunes the run, recreates or rewinds the durable consumer, and redelivers the original stream sequence.
- Observed run, queue, node-effect, consumer, and durable-dedupe state before and after redelivery.

## Steps to Reproduce

Materialize an event into deterministic run ID `<flow>:evt:<stream_seq>`, complete the run, prune terminal history past its retention window, recreate or rewind the registration's durable consumer to the retained event, and deliver it again. The `runs` primary key that made `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` absorb the first redelivery no longer exists, so the current transaction can insert and enqueue the same event identity again.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A durable identity or tombstone outlives every accidental redelivery/replay horizon, or configuration structurally prevents redelivery after identity expiry.
- Pruning terminal run history cannot make a previously materialized event eligible for a second enqueue or external effect.
- Intentional replay uses a distinct, auditable namespace and does not weaken accidental-redelivery dedupe.
- A targeted gate covers prune plus consumer recreation/rewind and proves zero second enqueue/effect.
notes:
AUDIT PROOF: wamn-4tob.6.9 blocks AUDIT-X1 and owns the prune-plus-consumer-rewind reproduction.
ARC7 SCOPE 2026-07-23: the durable identity must also survive source republish with a new JetStream stream sequence after Nats-Msg-Id duplicate-window expiry. Use source database epoch plus source row identity plus registration identity, not transport sequence alone. Proof wamn-4tob.6.17 is separate from the existing prune/rewind proof .6.9.
DEC-STATE CLARIFICATION 2026-07-23: use source database/capture epoch plus WAL position or ordinal plus registration identity. The retained run row is the current dedupe marker; no separate receipt table is selected. This finding still owns identity after run pruning and remains open.

description:

- Which dependency failures should make startup fatal versus temporarily unready?

description:

title: [AUDIT-DEC-UPGRADE] Set release compatibility and maintenance contract
description:
## Goal

Set the product compatibility and maintenance contract required to judge schema, runtime, component, service, event-wire, and deployment upgrade alternatives.

## Questions

- What downtime, degraded operation, tenant coordination, and maintenance windows are permitted in each deployment class?
- Which old and new host, guest, WIT, event-wire, SQL-schema, catalog, and service versions must interoperate, and for how long?
- What must happen to acknowledged requests and in-flight, parked, scheduled, and replayed runs during partial rollout, rollback, forward-fix, or failed state migration?

## Evidence Required

- Named product and operations owners for supported release channels and maintenance promises.
- Current schema lifecycle, wire-version, fork-upgrade, rollout, provenance, rollback, and recovery mechanisms.
- Representative mixed-version and failed-rollout scenarios by deployment class.

## Decision

Accepted for development on 2026-07-23: use a quiesced, atomic, reversible single-version release bundle with one commit point. Fence new state-changing admission; preserve acknowledged work; require every retained PostgreSQL or JetStream record to be drained, read compatibly, or migrated; and remain quiesced on an unprovable partial rollout. Kubernetes owns Wamn deployment and repointing. Transactional application migrations roll back; incompatible or destructive state changes require verified backup plus WAL recovery and CNPG new-cluster recovery when reversal is needed. No concurrent mixed-version, zero-downtime, production support-window, or custom-node versioning promise is made.

## Alternatives Considered

Quiesced stop-the-world development cutover is selected. Mixed-version rolling, blue-green, canary, zero-downtime, and production maintenance behavior are deferred to wamn-4tob.1.31. Production external-client compatibility is wamn-4tob.1.32. Custom-node artifact, WIT, and invocation versioning is deferred to wamn-4tob.1.33. Forward-only migration without a proven recovery path is rejected.

## Rationale

Correctness is controlling. An atomic release contract is simpler than unsupported mixed-version operation while still requiring immutable provenance, durable-state compatibility, acknowledged-work preservation, and deterministic reversal or recovery. Kubernetes rollout capability does not by itself prove Wamn compatibility, and database recovery remains a CloudNativePG responsibility rather than application deployment state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Compatibility windows, maintenance/degradation allowances, and tenant-notification obligations are explicit by plane and deployment class.
- In-flight and persisted work semantics are stated for partial rollout, rollback, forward-fix, and failed migration.
- Immutable artifact identity and rollback provenance are required wherever rollback is promised.
- ARC5, ARC9, ARC10, ARC11, and STR5 can eliminate alternatives without inventing an upgrade contract; numeric availability and recovery targets remain owned by wamn-4tob.1.14.
notes:
RESTRUCTURE ROUTING (wamn-4tob.9; docs/findings.md section I): include immutable execution-artifact identity for active runs, versioned invocation and route-binding contracts, old/new wire interoperability, additive and round-trip stored-state migration, quiesce/drain/resume policy, readiness before cutover, preservation of old capacity, and tested rollback or forward-fix behavior.
ARC9 HANDOFF 2026-07-23: safe rollout currently lacks workload readiness, immutable deployed artifact identity, active/parked-run executor identity, preserved old capacity, and proven mixed WIT/HTTP/NATS/SQL behavior. Fork rollback only repoints a source rev and rebuilds; it does not identify live prior bytes or compatible run routing. Decide quiesce/drain/resume, old/new coexistence, rollback/forward-fix, and per-patch negative conformance requirements.
STR5 HANDOFF 2026-07-23 (docs/findings.md section Q): explicitly decide same-release versus mixed-version behavior for wamn:runner, custom-node HTTP invocation, event-wire strict readers, catalog/flow/schema formats, and independently mutable dispatcher/Postgres-plugin/credential JSON. SR22 wamn-2jkm.94, SR23 .95, and SR24 .96 own the concrete protocol/source/config guards after this product-wide contract is set.
STR7 HANDOFF 2026-07-23: release compatibility must include one immutable identity from source revision through native/component/embedded-Wasm digests to deployed imageID and fresh gate receipt; mutable :dev tags and readiness alone are insufficient. Coordinate SR26/wamn-2jkm.98 and proof .6.25.
OWNER AUTHORIZATION 2026-07-23: Proceed with this issue as a one-question-at-a-time Q&A. Correctness remains controlling; current development versus future production promises must be separated. Preserve the accepted state boundary from .1.17: Kubernetes owns deployment mechanics, while this decision owns Wamn compatibility semantics during and after a rollout.
OWNER ANSWER 1 — DEVELOPMENT UPGRADE MODE (2026-07-23): Development supports a quiesced single-version cutover. Kubernetes owns rollout execution, while Wamn makes no current promise that old and new releases may concurrently process the same databases, queues, event contracts, or persisted runs. Zero-downtime and mixed-version rolling compatibility are deferred to a separate production decision rather than inferred from Kubernetes rollout capability.
DEFERRAL OWNER: wamn-4tob.1.31 [PROD-DEC-UPGRADE] owns the future mixed-version, zero-downtime, production maintenance, and rollback promise. It depends on this development decision and is not authorized for execution now.
OWNER ANSWER 2 — ACKNOWLEDGED WORK (2026-07-23): An upgrade may not cancel, discard, or falsely complete acknowledged work. Quiesce new starts and queue claims; allow active work to reach a durable checkpoint when practical or stop it and rely on lease recovery. Preserve queued, parked, scheduled, and replay runs in PostgreSQL and resume them after cutover. Death after an external effect but before checkpoint remains visibly ambiguous and may retry with the same occurrence identity; deployment completion never implies run success.
OWNER ANSWER 3 — PERSISTED-RUN COMPATIBILITY (2026-07-23): A new release may resume a nonterminal run only when named, tested compatibility covers its stored state, pinned flow, WIT, node, and execution contracts, or an explicit transactional migration converts it. Otherwise cutover fails before the previous release is retired. Each run must carry the immutable execution-artifact and contract identity needed for preflight and evidence; that reference is Wamn execution state and does not create a concurrent multi-version promise.
NEW FINDING/PROOF: R53 wamn-2jkm.99 owns missing immutable trusted-executor identity and fail-closed compatibility checks on persisted runs. Targeted proof wamn-4tob.6.26 owns queued/parked/expired-lease resume across an incompatible executor and blocks AUDIT-X1. Neither is authorized for execution inside this decision.
OWNER ANSWER 4 — CNPG-ALIGNED MIGRATION RECOVERY (2026-07-23): PostgreSQL/CNPG upgrades and Wamn application-state migrations are separate. For PostgreSQL minor upgrades, use the CNPG declarative rolling-update path; for PostgreSQL major upgrades, use one of the CNPG-supported dump/restore, logical-replication, or offline pg_upgrade paths with its documented backup and backup-lineage constraints. For a Wamn application-state migration, Kubernetes quiesces, deploys, validates, and repoints Wamn workloads; CNPG manages PostgreSQL backup and recovery. A transactional migration rolls itself back on failure. An incompatible or destructive migration may start only after base-backup plus WAL recoverability is proven and an explicit pre-migration recovery target exists; Wamn writes remain quiesced through migration and validation. If validation fails after commit, CNPG bootstraps a new cluster to the pre-migration target and Kubernetes repoints Wamn. Do not run the old Wamn release against the changed schema, claim an in-place database rewind, or treat Kubernetes rollout undo as database rollback. This development contract specifies correctness without choosing production RTO or zero-downtime behavior. Official evidence: https://cloudnative-pg.io/docs/1.30/rolling_update/ ; https://cloudnative-pg.io/docs/1.30/postgres_upgrades/ ; https://cloudnative-pg.io/docs/1.30/recovery/ .
OWNER ANSWER 5 — ATOMIC REVERSIBLE DEPLOYMENTS (2026-07-23): A Wamn development deployment is an atomic, reversible release bundle. The exact last-known-good native image, embedded component artifacts, configuration and deployment inputs, contract identities, and compatible database-schema range must remain immutably identifiable so Kubernetes can restore that bundle as a unit. If validation fails before incompatible state or work is accepted, Kubernetes redeploys the previous bundle. If the new release has committed incompatible state or accepted work under incompatible contracts, reversal additionally requires proven backward compatibility, an explicit compatible reverse migration, or restoration through the CNPG recovery path in Owner Answer 4; redeploying the old image alone is not a database rollback. Existing structural owner SR26 wamn-2jkm.98 and targeted proof wamn-4tob.6.25 own the immutable source-to-artifact-to-live identity and rollback evidence required by this contract.
OWNER ANSWER 6 — DURABLE RECORD COMPATIBILITY (2026-07-23): Atomic deployment does not permit abandoning data created by the previous release. Before cutover, every durable record that can remain in PostgreSQL or JetStream—including event envelopes, queued or parked runs, catalog and flow snapshots, schemas, and node metadata—must be proven drained, readable by the new release under named and tested compatibility, or transactionally migrated. Otherwise the deployment is refused and the previous bundle remains authoritative. Development does not promise concurrent old/new services or an arbitrary multi-release compatibility window; it promises that acknowledged durable state survives the single-version cutover.
OWNER ANSWER 7 — CUTOVER ADMISSION FENCE (2026-07-23): Quiescence first closes admission for new API work, triggers, queue claims, catalog publication, and other state-changing control-plane operations. Work arriving during the maintenance interval is refused before acknowledgement with an explicit retryable-unavailable result; previously acknowledged work follows Owner Answer 2. Admission reopens only after required migrations, durable-record compatibility, dependency health, immutable artifact identity, and whole-release readiness have been verified. In development, the operator may initiate this maintenance without an advance tenant-notification or numeric availability promise.
OWNER ANSWER 8 — PARTIAL ROLLOUT FAILURE (2026-07-23): Kubernetes may transiently deploy only part of a new release bundle, but Wamn does not treat that state as an operational release and keeps state-changing admission closed. The release has one commit point after every required workload, component, migration, contract check, dependency, and readiness check succeeds. Failure before that point reverses the entire bundle. If neither complete reversal nor a compatible forward fix can be proven, Wamn remains quiesced and visibly unavailable rather than reopening in a mixed, partially upgraded, or compatibility-unknown state.
OWNER ANSWER 9 — DEVELOPMENT CLIENT COMPATIBILITY (2026-07-23): Independent API and CLI clients are outside the atomic Wamn deployment bundle. During development, a client-facing contract may make an explicit breaking change without supporting the old version concurrently, but the contract version and break must be visible, an incompatible client must be refused before any state-changing effect, and in-repository clients, generated SDKs, fixtures, and tests must change with the release. No production support or deprecation window is inferred. DEFERRAL OWNER: wamn-4tob.1.32 [PROD-DEC-CLIENT-COMPAT] owns the future production external-client compatibility, versioning, notice, migration, and deprecation contract; it depends on this decision and is not authorized for execution now.
OWNER ANSWER 10 — CUSTOM-NODE VERSIONING DEFERRED (2026-07-23): The owner is not yet ready to choose how custom-node artifacts, WIT packages, invocation envelopes, manifests, and persisted references are versioned, or whether incompatibility is contained per flow. This decision makes no such choice and ARC11 must not infer a compatibility promise. Owner Answer 3 remains controlling for acknowledged runs: without named and tested compatibility, a nonterminal run cannot resume under a changed executor or node contract. DEFERRAL OWNER: wamn-4tob.1.33 [DEC-CUSTOM-NODE-VERSIONING] owns the future policy and blocks SR22 wamn-2jkm.94; neither issue is authorized for execution now.
INTEGRATION 2026-07-23: docs/findings.md now records the accepted contract in B.2/B.4/B.7 and N.7, applies it to the restructure/topology/roadmap/contract matrices, updates ARC9 current-versus-target verdicts, adds High finding R53 to N.4 and the status board, and routes SR22-SR24/SR26 plus proofs .6.25/.6.26. Production rollout, external-client compatibility, and custom-node versioning are granular unclaimed decisions .1.31-.33. Validation: git diff --check passed; bd lint passed for the ten affected issues; bd dep cycles reported none. No Rust, implementation, or live-system gate ran because this issue changes only the owner contract, findings ledger, and Beads routing.
close_reason: Development upgrade contract accepted and integrated in docs/findings.md N.7: quiesced atomic reversible single-version releases, fenced admission, durable-record compatibility, acknowledged-work preservation, CNPG-aligned recovery, and fail-closed partial rollout; production/client/custom-node policies remain .1.31-.33; R53 and proofs remain open.

title: [AUDIT-DEC-ISOLATION] Set development client-isolation and security deferral contract
description:
## Goal

Set the development client-isolation contract needed by the architecture audit and explicitly classify the wider trust, security, and regulatory contracts as deferred.

## Questions

- What isolation property is required during development?
- What role do narrow platform and WASI interfaces play in that boundary?
- Which threat, infrastructure-isolation, credential-lifecycle, residency, regulatory, audit, retention, erasure, and operator-access properties are current or deferred?

## Evidence Required

- Owner direction on the current development boundary.
- ARC8 evidence for the authority exposed by platform interfaces and their host implementations.
- Granular future decision Beads for every deferred production contract.

## Decision

Clients are isolated as a present correctness invariant. Every supported platform API must preserve its assigned client boundary, and ordinary use must not cross client data or effect scope. The architecture relies on narrowly exposed platform and WASI interfaces, but the effective capability includes all host implementation, credential, and shared-connection authority reachable through each interface.

Detailed trust and threat modeling, infrastructure and credential isolation profiles, credential lifecycle and compromise response, residency and regulation, audit and operator access, and retention and erasure are deferred. Current topology and labels confer no unstated security or compliance guarantee.

## Alternatives Considered

- Define a detailed adversary and operator model during development.
- Infer security profiles from current database, namespace, runtime, or deployment labels.
- Preserve client isolation as a current correctness invariant and defer the wider production security contract.

The owner selected the third alternative.

## Rationale

The product is still in development. The useful current architectural constraint is which explicit capabilities a client workload can exercise; inventing future actors, regulatory promises, physical boundaries, or response times would prematurely constrain the architecture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Client isolation is stated as a current correctness invariant at every platform API.
- The capability boundary includes the host authority reachable behind each WIT or WASI interface.
- Trust, security, profile, credential, residency, regulatory, audit, operator-access, retention, and erasure properties are explicitly labeled deferred and unproven.
- Deferred production decisions are tracked individually by wamn-4tob.1.25 through wamn-4tob.1.30.
- ARC6, ARC8, ARC9, and ARC11 can reject ordinary cross-client leakage without inventing a broader security or compliance requirement.
notes:
ARC5 HANDOFF 2026-07-23: current wasmCloud workload-security documentation says omitted or empty allowedHosts permits every HTTP destination and does not govern other networking. Decide permitted shared host groups, plugins, broker identities, raw sockets, Kubernetes Secrets, namespaces, and clusters per deployment class.
RESTRUCTURE ROUTING (wamn-4tob.9; docs/findings.md section I): decide route-derived tenant/project/environment/flow identity, external caller versus internal invocation trust domains, replay/key-version authority, credential compromise radius, and whether test-double/scenario capabilities require separate artifacts. Per-route HMAC and nonce storage are hypotheses, not defaults; custom-node signing is a separate boundary.
ARC8 HANDOFF 2026-07-23: dedicated placement currently isolates PostgreSQL pods/recovery domains only. CNPG and Barman are cluster-wide Secret super-principals, while runtime/event NATS identities, object-store root, hostgroups, registry, telemetry, namespace, Kubernetes cluster, and human administration remain shared. Decide which of these may be shared for every supported dedicated/regulated profile; if operator or credential containment is promised, ARC11 must mint the corresponding remediation/proof.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q1 threat-model timing and capability basis: It is too early to define a detailed adversary or actor trust model. Fundamentally, the level of threat follows from which platform APIs and capabilities a workload can access. Wamn is relying on the WASI capability model and exposes only narrowly specified interfaces. Detailed threat-model classification is a future production/security decision, not a current development promise. For the current audit, assess isolation structurally at each exposed interface and do not infer protection beyond those capabilities.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Q2 development isolation boundary: Clients are isolated. Client or tenant separation at platform API boundaries is a current correctness invariant even when underlying development infrastructure is shared. Detailed trust assumptions, adversary modeling, credential-compromise containment, and broader security guarantees are deferred. The audit must not treat that deferral as permission for ordinary cross-client data or effect leakage.
OWNER Q&A 2026-07-23 — Scope correction and final direction: Trust and security are deferred in full. Do not ask separate current questions about actor hostility, physical or infrastructure sharing, operator containment, credential compromise, rotation/revocation bounds, or security deployment classes. The only present development contract established here is client isolation as a correctness property, implemented through narrowly exposed platform and WASI interfaces. Future trust, security, regulatory, residency, audit, retention, erasure, and operator-access contracts must be decided later and must not be inferred from current topology or labels.
INTEGRATION 2026-07-23: docs/findings.md M.6 records the owner-set development contract and related ARC/STR references now distinguish current client isolation from deferred production security. Granular unclaimed P3 decisions are .1.25 threat/capability model, .1.26 production isolation profiles, .1.27 credential lifecycle, .1.28 residency/regulatory scope, .1.29 audit/operator access, and .1.30 retention/erasure. Existing wamn-g1p, wamn-5ts, wamn-owu, and wamn-vpd wait on their corresponding decision. No implementation finding is marked fixed and no live gate was run.
close_reason: Owner decision complete: clients are isolated as a development correctness invariant at every platform API; effective capabilities include reachable host authority behind narrow WIT/WASI interfaces. Trust and security are deferred. docs/findings.md M.6 and dependent audit notes are updated; production decisions are granular unclaimed beads wamn-4tob.1.25-.30; no implementation finding is marked fixed.

title: [AUDIT-DEC-RECOVERY] Set availability, durability, and recovery objectives by plane and tier
description:
## Goal
Set the product recovery contract needed to judge failure domains, state placement, backup topology, and operational completeness.

## Questions
- What availability, RPO, and RTO apply to each architectural plane and pooled, standard, dedicated, regulated, edge, and on-prem deployment class?
- Which operations may degrade during control-plane, Postgres, JetStream, runtime, or regional loss, and which must fail closed?
- What manual intervention and data-reconciliation burden is acceptable?

## Evidence Required
- Customer and operator recovery expectations with named owners.
- Current backup cadences, PITR windows, failover behavior, and restore evidence.
- State-by-state acknowledged-write and replay semantics for each canonical journey.

## Decision
For development, correctness is controlling above availability and every other optimization. No numeric availability or RTO applies. Current T3 is development-only; CloudNativePG remains the database choice for an extended production topology. No cross-region or CDC-outage-buffer promise applies. Documented manual recovery by one general platform owner is acceptable. Production properties are explicitly deferred to granular decisions wamn-4tob.1.18 through wamn-4tob.1.24.

## Rationale
The repository proves useful mechanisms but not a production topology, workload, operating organization, or customer recovery promise. Guessed numbers would prematurely optimize infrastructure and misrepresent development manifests as production evidence. A qualitative correctness contract is sufficient to eliminate unsafe architectures now.

## Alternatives Considered
- Adopt proposed launch and regional availability, RTO, outage-buffer, and PITR numbers now: rejected as premature and unevidenced.
- Treat the current single-instance T3 and development object stores as production profiles: rejected.
- Preserve availability through stale promotion, hidden capture gaps, unsafe replay, or inferred external-effect success: rejected by the correctness-first priority.
- Require fully automated recovery, multiple SRE owners, and separation of duties during development: rejected as premature; production decisions remain filed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Development availability, durability, degradation, recovery-time, manual-repair, and ownership expectations are explicit per plane and deployment class, including explicit unsupported and deferred properties.
- No acknowledged-write-loss, silent-corruption, isolation failure, hidden capture gap, or ambiguous-success allowance is introduced.
- Every deferred production property has its own granular decision bead.
- ARC4, ARC6, ARC7, ARC9, and ARC11 can eliminate alternatives against the development contract without inventing production requirements.
notes:
ARC9 HANDOFF 2026-07-23: docs/findings.md section N records every required failure with current detection, containment, recovery owner/procedure, automatic/manual/expert status, and RPO/RTO as unknown where no product target exists. Set explicit values for T1, each tenant placement class, source-WAL outage buffer, broker loss/full, run recovery/effect ambiguity, backup/region loss, migration rollback, and bounded-cell movement. R50-R52 and proofs .6.22-.6.24 consume those targets.
AUTHORIZED RESUME LANE (next issue, 2026-07-23; preparation only until resume): execute ONLY wamn-4tob.1.14, then stop. On resume run bd prime, verify HEAD/local origin/actual origin and preserve the expected user-owned dirty paths (.beads/interactions.jsonl, AGENTS.md, untracked docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md), confirm no active issue and clean dependency graph, then claim this issue. Use at most one read-only evidence subagent with an explicit available substantive model, high reasoning, fork none, no delegation or repository/Beads mutation; main owns synthesis. Re-read findings B/F/J/K/M/N/P/R/S plus platform/deployment/Postgres/event/recovery/backup docs and the relevant Beads/proofs. Build an evidence-cited matrix by architectural plane and deployment class covering availability, acknowledged-write durability, RPO, RTO, permitted degradation, fail-closed behavior, manual/expert repair allowance, recovery owner, and unresolved product input. Distinguish current measured capability from contractual, target, exploratory, deferred, and unsupported requirements; do not infer numbers from implementation or benchmark ceilings. Explicitly cover T1, every tenant placement class, Postgres failover, source-WAL buffer, JetStream loss/full, run recovery and ambiguous external effects, backups/object loss, regional loss, schema/runtime upgrade rollback, control-plane outage, and edge/on-prem profiles. Present concrete recommended options and the minimum owner choices needed; if owner values are absent, pause for the user rather than guessing or closing. Once accepted, record the decision in the existing findings/Beads information system without rewriting canonical D rows, create granular beads for every genuine residual, validate citations/matrix/dependencies, close, commit and push the issue-specific findings change, run bd dolt push, and STOP before wamn-4tob.1.15, .1.17, ARC11, STR9, or any proof execution. No live gate unless an immutable baseline-matched artifact is first proven.
OWNER DECISION PACK 2026-07-23 (evidence only; issue remains open): No product availability, RPO, or RTO value exists in the pinned baseline. Current facts: T1 is request-path-free but async replicated and has no standing PITR; current T3 is one instance/one PVC/no standing PITR; T2/T4 render async failover; source feedback waits for JetStream ACK but WAL is bounded at 1GB; total JetStream PVC loss has no restore path; Postgres run/queue recovery is durable but non-idempotent external effects remain visibly ambiguous; standing backup/object/region recovery and runtime rollback are unproven. Evidence: docs/findings.md B.2-B.4, F.2-F.3, J.1-J.5, K.1-K.5, N.1-N.5, P.1-P.2, R.2, S.2-S.3; docs/system-cluster.md:47-85; docs/postgres-topology.md:247-330; docs/event-plane-jetstream.md:126-138,425-466; docs/run-state.md:87-126; docs/run-queue.md:24-98,239-278; docs/provisioning.md:631-838; deploy/platform/wamn-sysdb.yaml:34-74; deploy/infra/cnpg-cluster.yaml:33-67; deploy/infra/nats-jetstream.yaml:39-45,105-196; deploy/infra/minio.yaml:1-81.

PROPOSED LAUNCH CONTRACT FOR OWNER ACCEPTANCE: RPO 0 for every acknowledged authoritative mutation inside each supported failure envelope; fail closed rather than promote a stale replica or hide a gap. Use a recovery policy independent of placement labels: T1, bounded pooled production cells, standard, and dedicated default to a single-region production profile; dedicated changes isolation, not recovery SLO. Current single-instance T3 and disposable dev/preview are not production-eligible. Regulated maps to an explicitly regional profile only when contracted. Edge/on-prem remains unsupported until its offline authority contract is decided. Launch profile proposal: 99.9 percent monthly for control, tenant data, flow, and executable trigger planes; routine process/primary recovery within 15 minutes, worker reclaim within 5 minutes, total-cell/new-cluster restore within 4 hours; event path tolerates 60 minutes without loss with measured 2x WAL/storage margin, then admission fails closed before a capture gap; externally durable 14-day PITR window; published artifacts and audit/correctness receipts RPO 0, ordinary telemetry RPO at most 5 minutes; high-risk changes fail closed when recovery/audit evidence is unavailable. Regional profile proposal: 99.95 percent, RPO 0 through declared single-region loss, routine recovery within 5 minutes, regional recovery within 1 hour, 4-hour event buffer, externally independent 30-day checkpoint window. Routine pod/node/primary loss is automatic; manual recovery is allowed only for total-cell/region restore and ambiguous external effects, must be runbooked and attributable, and cannot depend on undocumented expert inference. Point-in-time rewind is an explicit authorized recovery choice whose missing/duplicate interval is reported, never silent infrastructure loss.

MINIMUM OWNER CHOICES: (1) accept or edit the proposed numeric launch and regional profiles; (2) confirm current T3/dev/preview are internal or disposable only, versus requiring them to meet production RPO 0; (3) choose single-region-unavailable rather than stale failover at launch, or require zero-loss regional service now; (4) accept the 60-minute launch and 4-hour regional event outage buffers; (5) accept the manual-repair boundary and functional recovery owners: platform SRE for T1/placement/cluster, DB SRE for tenant data/backups, runtime SRE plus tenant sink owner for effect ambiguity, event/DB SRE for capture, release operator for artifacts, and incident commander for regional recovery. No source document was edited and no proof/live gate ran.
OWNER ANSWER 1 — RTO SCOPE (2026-07-23): Numeric recovery-time objectives are unnecessary at the current product stage and must not be used as architecture acceptance criteria in this audit. Continue to assess whether recovery is possible, deterministic, attributable, and free of acknowledged-write loss or silent corruption, but do not assign or optimize for process, primary/node, cell, or regional recovery-time targets. Revisit quantitative RTO only at a later production-readiness milestone; that follow-up must be represented by its own granular bead before this issue closes.
OWNER ANSWER 2 — AVAILABILITY PRIORITY (2026-07-23): Correctness is the controlling objective above availability and every other optimization. Do not set a numeric availability target at this product stage. An architecture must reject, pause, or become unavailable whenever continued service could cause acknowledged-write loss, silent corruption, cross-tenant leakage, nondeterministic execution, or an unreconcilable state gap. After correctness constraints eliminate unsafe options, assess availability qualitatively through failure containment and graceful degradation; uptime does not justify stale promotion, hidden gaps, unsafe replay, or ambiguous success.
OWNER ANSWER 3 — CURRENT T3 AND DATABASE CHOICE (2026-07-23): The checked-in single-instance T3 topology is a development deployment, not a production durability profile. Its single-instance/PVC limitations therefore must not be interpreted as the intended production contract. CloudNativePG is the selected database operator; production is expected to extend the CNPG topology with the replica, backup, failover, and recovery configuration required by the correctness-first contract rather than replace the database technology. The audit must distinguish dev evidence from production readiness and must not represent the future production topology as already proven.
OWNER ANSWER 4 — REGIONAL SCOPE (2026-07-23): No cross-region availability, durability, or recovery promise applies at the current development stage. On total-region loss, correctness wins: remain unavailable rather than promote an unverified or stale authority. Revisit the supported regional failure envelope alongside the other production topology decisions; deferred decision bead wamn-4tob.1.18 owns that future work and is not authorized for execution now.
OWNER ANSWER 5 — EVENT-OUTAGE BUFFER (2026-07-23): Do not specify a time-based CDC/JetStream outage buffer, WAL-capacity threshold, or concrete admission policy until closer to production. The development-stage audit retains only the correctness invariant that an event-capture gap cannot be silent or represented as successful lossless operation. Deferred production decision bead wamn-4tob.1.19 owns the measured retention, backpressure/admission, recovery-owner, and proof contract; it is not authorized for execution now.
OWNER ANSWER 6 — MANUAL RECOVERY (2026-07-23): Documented manual recovery is acceptable during development, including rare destructive restoration and genuinely ambiguous external-effect reconciliation. This allowance does not permit silent loss, corruption, cross-tenant effects, or undocumented ad hoc repair to be represented as correct. Deferred production decision bead wamn-4tob.1.20 owns the later automatic-versus-manual boundary and is not authorized for execution now.
OWNER ANSWER 7 — RECOVERY OWNERSHIP (2026-07-23): Development does not require multiple recovery owners, a formal RACI, or separation of recovery responsibilities. A single general platform owner may detect, repair, and reconcile all planes during development. Multi-owner allocation and separation of duties are deferred with the other production operating-model decisions; accountability and recovery evidence must still be recorded even when one person holds every role.
FINAL INTEGRATION 2026-07-23: Owner answer 7 is routed to wamn-4tob.1.21. docs/findings.md N.6 records the accepted development contract and plane/deployment overlay; B, D, N, and P references now distinguish it from production claims. Deferred production decisions are wamn-4tob.1.18 regional, .1.19 CDC/broker outage, .1.20 manual/automatic boundary, .1.21 ownership/separation of duties, .1.22 RTO, .1.23 availability, and .1.24 durability/RPO. No runtime source changed and no live gate ran under the baseline-provenance restriction.
close_reason: Development recovery contract decided and integrated in docs/findings.md N.6: correctness above availability; no numeric availability/RTO; current T3 is dev-only with CloudNativePG retained for later production topology; no current regional or event-outage promise; documented manual recovery under one general owner is acceptable. Production properties are split into unclaimed decisions wamn-4tob.1.18-.24. Documentation/Beads validation passed; no runtime or live gate was applicable.

title: [AUDIT-DEC-SLO] Set end-to-end latency, throughput, and backlog service objectives
description:
## Goal

Set the current audit boundary for product-level latency, throughput, backlog, catch-up, and degraded-operation objectives without inventing promises before representative evidence exists.

## Questions

- Which latency percentiles and throughput rates are required for generated APIs, synchronous flows, queue dispatch, CDC materialization, custom-node invocation, builds, and administrative operations?
- What backlog, catch-up, backpressure, payload, and error-budget limits define acceptable degraded operation?
- Which current POC measurements are product objectives versus development evidence?

## Evidence Required

- Owner product-stage direction.
- Existing POC gates and measured ceilings with their environment, artifact, workload, topology, and durability conditions retained.
- A future representative post-POC measurement campaign before any product target is selected.

## Decision

Product service objectives are explicitly deferred until after the owner declares the exploratory POC stage complete and representative end-to-end measurement exists. The current audit sets no numeric latency percentile, sustained or burst throughput, backlog depth or age, catch-up time, backpressure, payload, availability-performance, or error-budget target for any canonical journey or deployment profile.

Existing D15 proposals, P0 gate thresholds, microbenchmarks, and consumer-hardware measurements remain configuration-specific development evidence. They are not customer promises, supported envelopes, or target-architecture selection thresholds. Correctness remains controlling: admitted work may not trade acknowledged-write durability, deterministic recovery, isolation, or visible fail-closed exhaustion for latency or throughput.

The future work is granular. wamn-4tob.1.37 measures representative canonical journeys after the POC stage; wamn-4tob.1.38 depends on that evidence and owns the later product SLO decision. Neither is authorized now or required to complete the current architecture synthesis.

## Alternatives Considered

- Promote D15 or current gate thresholds into product objectives: rejected because their workloads, hardware, topology, durability, and percentile windows do not establish a product promise.
- Invent placeholder latency, throughput, backlog, or catch-up numbers: rejected because they would manufacture requirements before representative product evidence.
- Leave this audit decision open until the future measurement campaign: rejected because the owner has explicitly resolved the present requirement by deferral; ARC11 can synthesize a conditional target without pretending performance objectives exist.
- Ignore performance evidence entirely: rejected because measurements still expose bottlenecks and comparative behavior, provided they retain provenance and are not treated as promises.

## Rationale

The platform is still exploratory and its workload, topology, deployment profile, and user expectations are not stable enough to define meaningful service objectives. Choosing numbers now would optimize the architecture against incidental POC shapes. Finishing the POC stage, measuring representative end-to-end journeys, and then selecting objectives preserves evidence-first design while allowing the correctness-first architecture review to proceed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every canonical journey is explicitly recorded as having no current product SLO rather than receiving a guessed target.
- Existing measurements remain labeled configuration-specific development evidence.
- Correctness and visible fail-closed behavior cannot be weakened for performance.
- A granular post-POC measurement task and a dependent future SLO decision exist.
- ARC11 may proceed without using unratified performance figures as target requirements.
- No implementation, benchmark, deployment, or live gate occurs inside this decision.
notes:

title: [AUDIT-DEC-CARDINALITY] Set supported tenant and deployment cardinality envelopes
description:
## Goal

Set the development-stage cardinality criterion so architecture alternatives are not evaluated against invented product scale or incidental benchmark sizes.

## Questions

- What, if any, organization, project, environment, active-workload, regional, edge, on-premises, node, registration, route, and site limits are supported now?
- Which topology and runtime-placement shapes are committed versus exploratory?
- How must the system behave when finite measured capacity is exhausted?
- Which current measurements are evidence versus product or production promises?

## Evidence Required

- Owner product-stage and correctness priorities.
- Existing measured addressability and topology evidence, including the 10,000-project addressability result and current Kubernetes/Postgres object cardinality.
- Explicit hardware, cluster, artifact, configuration, and workload provenance for every exploratory capacity result.
- Granular future decisions for production cardinality, topology, and economics plus a targeted development capacity proof.

## Decision

The current contract is exploratory development only. It sets no numeric organization, project, environment, active-workload, node, registration, route, site, regional, edge, on-premises, or other cardinality envelope. It selects no T2/T3/T4, bounded-cell, per-organization, per-environment, always-resident, pooled, leased, or scale-to-zero target.

Development correctness applies to admitted finite load. Capacity exhaustion must be rejected or surfaced visibly before it can cause acknowledged-write loss, silent corruption, cross-client leakage, or nondeterministic recovery. Thresholds must be measured on the exact recorded consumer hardware and configuration and remain exploratory evidence.

Multi-region scale, edge/on-premises fleet counts, production maximums, target topology, and commercial unit economics are deferred. The future owners are wamn-4tob.1.34 through .1.36; regional recovery remains .1.18. Exploratory capacity and overload proof are wamn-4tob.6.27.

## Alternatives Considered

- Promote 10,000-project addressability or the 34P/35P configured connection formulas into supported limits: rejected because they are narrow evidence and upper-bound arithmetic, not a fleet workload or product requirement.
- Select the current shared T3 shape or the ARC6 bounded-cell, per-org, or per-environment candidates now: rejected because every topology remains exploratory.
- Prefer always-resident per-project services or pooled, leased, or scale-to-zero runtimes now: rejected pending comparative measurement.
- Invent 100/1,000/10,000 tiers or commercial envelopes: rejected as premature.
- Permit capacity exhaustion without admission control: rejected by the correctness-first priority.

## Rationale

The project is running exploratory development on consumer hardware and lacks production workload, topology, hardware, commercial, and fleet evidence. Converting incidental implementation shapes into commitments would manufacture requirements and constrain the architecture prematurely. Measurement is still required because finite resources must fail closed rather than degrade into incorrect behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The development contract states explicitly that no numeric scale, topology, or runtime-placement commitment exists.
- Correctness for admitted finite load and visible fail-closed exhaustion are controlling requirements.
- Every current capacity result remains tied to its exact hardware, configuration, artifact, and workload and is labeled exploratory.
- Production cardinality, topology, economics, regional, edge, and on-premises unknowns have granular decision beads.
- ARC6, ARC9, ARC10, and ARC11 cannot infer a target or scale promise from T1-T4 labels, bounded-cell recommendations, current manifests, 10,000-project addressability, or 34P/35P formulas.
- The required development capacity and overload evidence has a granular verification bead; no implementation fix occurs inside this decision.
notes:
AUTHORIZED RESUME PLAN (2026-07-23): On resume execute only wamn-4tob.1.12 as a one-question-at-a-time owner Q&A. It remains OPEN and unclaimed during compaction. Do not claim wamn-4tob.1.13, ARC11, STR9, or any deferred production decision.

Resume steps:
1. Run bd prime; verify HEAD and origin/main remain at 1c19c50 and preserve the user-owned dirty files .beads/interactions.jsonl, AGENTS.md, and docs/RESTRUCTURE-260723.md.
2. Show wamn-4tob.1.12, then claim only it.
3. Use docs/findings.md B.2, B.3, B.4, B.7, J.3, J.4, and P.3 plus the already-assessed REVIEW-260723 and RESTRUCTURE-260723 evidence. No subagents are needed for serial owner Q&A and no live gates should run. The 10k addressability and 34P/35P connection figures are evidence or upper bounds, not requirements.
4. Separate the present development architecture from future production commitments. Ask one contextual question at a time; do not demand arbitrary 100/1k/10k production numbers. Suggested sequence:
   Q1. Is the present supported contract development-only, with production/customer cardinalities deferred?
   Q2. For development, are numeric supported org/project/environment/active counts required, or should the contract be correctness for admitted finite load with no scale claim?
   Q3. Does current T3 remain a small shared development topology, with T2/T4, cell, per-org, and per-environment production placement deferred?
   Q4. Even without product counts, must topology be bounded by explicit admission derived from measured connections, storage, WAL, backup, reconciliation, etcd, and object counts rather than permitting unbounded per-project resources?
   Q5. Which axes must remain independently scalable: configured projects P, active projects A, custom nodes N, registrations R, routes F, and regions/edge/on-prem sites Q? Do not collapse them into one project count.
   Q6. Should always-resident per-project native pods/services be disfavored as the default absent a concrete need, while per-project durable database identity remains allowed and runtimes may pool, lease, or scale to zero?
   Q7. Are multi-region, edge/on-prem, commercial unit economics, and production maximum counts explicitly deferred, with granular decision beads for accepted deferrals?
5. After each owner answer, append the answer to wamn-4tob.1.12 and create only necessary granular deferral decisions, deduplicating existing wamn-4tob.1.18 through .1.33 and .1.13. Make no implementation changes.
6. When Q&A is complete, integrate only owner-set criteria into docs/findings.md sections B, J, and P and the ARC11 handoff. Update the issue with Decision, Alternatives Considered, and Rationale. Add findings only for concrete gaps, not for missing guessed numbers.
7. Validate git diff --check, targeted bd lint, and bd dep cycles. Close only wamn-4tob.1.12, commit and push any audit-document changes, run bd dolt push, then stop. Do not proceed to wamn-4tob.1.13 or ARC11 without authorization.
EXECUTION RESUMED (2026-07-23): Baseline verified at 1c19c50 for HEAD and origin/main; only the previously identified user-owned dirty files are present. Claimed only this decision for serial owner Q&A. No implementation changes, live gates, subagents, or other audit issues are in scope.
OWNER ANSWER Q1 (2026-07-23): Yes. The current supported contract is development-only. Production and customer cardinality promises are deferred and must not be inferred from current measurements, addressability, topology, or resource formulas.
OWNER ANSWER Q2 (2026-07-23): Yes. Development has no numeric supported count for organizations, projects, environments, or concurrently active project-environments. Its contract is correctness for admitted finite load: overload or exhausted capacity must be rejected or surfaced visibly, never converted into acknowledged-write loss, silent corruption, cross-client leakage, or nondeterministic recovery. Current measurements and formulas are exploratory evidence, not scale promises.
OWNER ANSWER Q3 (2026-07-23): No current topology is committed. T3, T2, T4, cell-based, per-organization, and per-environment shapes are all exploratory development implementations or hypotheses and are deferred pending development evidence. ARC11 must not present the currently checked-in T3 shape, or any rendered alternative, as the accepted target topology.
OWNER ANSWER Q4 (2026-07-23): Yes. Exploratory development must use fail-closed admission when measured resource capacity is exhausted. The applicable ceilings include connections, storage, WAL, backup, reconciliation, Kubernetes/etcd objects, routes, resident processes, and other demonstrated bottlenecks. Threshold values remain exploratory and must be established by measurement; they are not product cardinality commitments.
OWNER ANSWER Q5 (2026-07-24): No cardinality limit or independent scalability commitment is set for any axis at this exploratory stage. Configured projects, active projects, custom nodes, registrations, routes, and deployment sites are candidate experimental variables, not supported envelopes. Measurement must discover the relevant bottlenecks and interactions before the product selects limits.
OWNER ANSWER Q6 (2026-07-24): Yes. No current preference is set between always-resident per-project services and pooled, leased, or scale-to-zero runtimes; all are exploratory. Current work runs on consumer hardware, so the useful present action is to measure and record behavior on that exact configuration. Those results may compare alternatives and reveal bottlenecks but cannot establish a general deployment or product capacity claim.
OWNER ANSWER Q7 (2026-07-24): Yes. Multi-region scale, edge/on-premises fleet counts, commercial unit economics, and all production maximums are explicitly deferred. The current audit may record only hardware- and configuration-specific exploratory measurements plus the development correctness requirement for visible, fail-closed capacity exhaustion.
INTEGRATION COMPLETE (2026-07-24): Owner answers are integrated into docs/findings.md sections B, J, N, and P plus the ARC11 handoff. The audit records no current numeric cardinality, topology, or runtime-placement target; consumer-hardware measurements remain configuration-specific; admitted finite load must fail closed visibly at measured exhaustion. Granular unclaimed owners: production cardinality .1.34, topology .1.35, unit economics .1.36, exploratory capacity proof .6.27, and open High finding R54/wamn-2jkm.100. Proof .6.27 directly blocks AUDIT-X1 and is a hard prerequisite of R54. Validation: git diff --check for docs/findings.md, targeted bd lint (six issues), and bd dep cycles all pass. No code, deployment, or live gate was changed or run.
close_reason: Decided and integrated the exploratory-development cardinality contract: no numeric/topology/runtime-placement promise; correctness for admitted finite load; visible fail-closed measured exhaustion. Filed granular production decisions .1.34-.1.36, proof .6.27, and open High R54/wamn-2jkm.100. Updated findings and ARC11 handoff; documentation/tracker validation passed; no implementation or live gate ran.

title: [EVT-S-CDC-1] pg_walstream diligence spike — soak, failover-slot switchover, TOAST, streamed-txn memory, Message events
description: Phase 0 spike (v3 section 7): pg_walstream (BSD-3, v0.8, single-author) due diligence before the build-vs-buy call. (1) sustained soak with keepalive+feedback over idle hours; (2) CNPG switchover with a failover-enabled slot (PG18) — successor resumes from confirmed LSN, no gap; (3) TOAST unchanged-column marker surfacing; (4) 1M-row streamed-transaction memory profile; (5) protocol Message-event support (pg_logical_emit_message — the causation channel; fallback: next_raw_event). ANY failure -> fallback assessment (Supabase etl) before proceeding. Feeds EVT-BUILD-VS-BUY.
notes:
S-CDC-1 FINAL VERDICTS (2026-07-18) — ALL FIVE CHECKLIST ITEMS PASS; no fallback assessment needed. Feeds wamn-l5i9.6 [BUILD-VS-BUY]. Harness = poc/cdc1 (committed crate, dkk fork choice; pg_walstream pinned =0.8.0); infra = throwaway 2-instance CNPG cluster cdc1 (poc/cdc1/cdc1-cluster.yaml; PG 18.4, sync_replication_slots=on, hot_standby_feedback=on, spec.replicationSlots.highAvailability.synchronizeLogicalDecoding=true, logical_decoding_work_mem=4MB, max_slot_wal_keep_size=1GB) + NodePort 172.28.0.4:30497; TORN DOWN (0 residue; guardrails wamn-pg 1/1 + wamn-sysdb 3/3 + legacy postgres pod untouched). Soak bounded 30 min (dkk fork choice). Run recipe: docs/build-and-test.md [EVT-S-CDC-1].

(a) SOAK: PASS. 1800s idle: 60/60 checks, walsender reply_time advanced EVERY 30s check (keepalive/feedback continuous), slot active throughout, canary write after the full idle window delivered <20s. Observation: the idle slot pinned ~28MB WAL/30min from cluster background activity (restart_lsn holds with nothing to ack) — the sec11 slot-pins-WAL edge in miniature; max_slot_wal_keep_size + lag monitoring are the production controls.

(b) FAILOVER/SWITCHOVER: PASS across THREE drills + a successor-delivery run; the slot crossed 3 ownership changes (pod-delete failover cdc1-1->2, plugin switchover ->1, plugin switchover ->2) with missing=[] every time and lsn_regressions=0. Successor delivery proven: 95 post-promotion commits delivered through the twice-synced slot; 13 redeliveries observed = the at-least-once window, as modeled. kubectl cnpg plugin 1.29.2 installed (~/.local/bin/kubectl-cnpg) for the graceful promote; the pod-delete variant also run. CNPG slot sync verified live: slot synced=t on the standby (initial 'could not synchronize ... catalog xmin' log lines are the documented transient until the primary slot advances).

(c) TOAST: PASS. High-level RowData SKIPS unchanged-TOAST columns (absent from new_data) while a real NULL is present as ColumnValue::Null -> distinguishable via the Relation column list (EventType::Relation carries it); the raw ColumnData layer preserves the explicit 'u' marker (is_unchanged()). REPLICA IDENTITY FULL old image carries the full 22400B TOAST value (l5i9.31 knob mechanics confirmed); new_data still skips the unchanged col. Reader consequence: materializer 'unchanged' detection = absent-key vs Null against the relation column set.

(d) STREAMED TXN: PASS. 1,000,000-row single txn under 4MB work_mem: 34 StreamStart/StreamStop segments + StreamCommit; all 1M Insert events in 13.2s wall (debug build, ~76k ev/s through the NodePort); harness VmRSS 10048->10504 KiB peak = 456 KiB delta -> the library does NOT buffer streamed transactions (constant memory).

(e) MESSAGE EVENTS: PASS. Transactional (flags=1) + non-transactional (flags=0) pg_logical_emit_message surface as EventType::Message{prefix,content} with config.messages=true. Causation channel works; next_raw_event fallback NOT needed.

FINDING F1 (crate bug, workaround shipped, fork-patchable ~3 lines at l5i9.8): slot_options.failover=true emits LEGACY space-separated `CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT ... FAILOVER`; FAILOVER exists only in the PG17+ parenthesized grammar -> 42601 (proven live both ways). Workaround IN THE HARNESS: create the slot via SQL pg_create_logical_replication_slot(..., failover=>true); run the stream failover=false (ensure_replication_slot tolerates 'already exists').

FINDING F2 (operational, not crate): on this kind rig a graceful CNPG switchover leaves a ~2-3 min primary-less window (old primary demotion is slow); the crate's inner retry (RetryConfig::default ~31s) can give up inside such a window -> the production reader needs a harness-level re-open loop (implemented in the spike's switchover consumer; reopens counted) and/or tuned RetryConfig. In all drills the inner retry happened to ride through (reopens=0).

HARNESS LESSON: an ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING no-op insert emits NO row event — count 'committed' only when rows_affected==1 AND use a per-run id base, else re-runs report false gaps (drill 2's 'missing 100001..100434' was exactly this, not data loss).

BUILD-VS-BUY INPUTS (for l5i9.6): protocol correctness solid across all five probes; single-author risk showed up as exactly one real bug (F1, trivial patch) in a surface we exercise; vendor/fork+pin (l5i9.8) is justified and sufficient; keepalive/feedback, streamed-txn memory, TOAST semantics, Message events, and failover-slot continuity all production-shaped.

title: [REVIEW C2-1/C4-3] Runaway/non-terminating run has no termination bound at any layer — wedges the project run-worker
description: HIGH (docs/review-2026-07.md §C2-1, AR3). wamn-flow/validate.rs:191 rejects only self-loops (from==to); longer cycles pass, reachability is a warning. Engine drive/next (wamn-runner/engine.rs:435,272) have no step/wall-clock cap. run-worker disables the host backstop: set_epoch_deadline(u64::MAX/2) (run_worker.rs:315-317 = C4-3). Lease renews per node (run-queue.md:220) so a live infinite run's lease never expires and the janitor (reaps only expired leases) never reclaims it. A tenant loop whose conditional never flips blocks the single-instance run-worker inside one run-next forever, renews the lease so failover/janitor can't reclaim, starves every other project run, issues unbounded node effects (a->http-request->a = unbounded egress). run-queue.md:266-269 drain-termination proof unsound for a run that neither terminates nor parks. FIX: run-level guard in the pure engine (max node-executions or max wall-clock on drive/RunState) -> terminal FailKind so the run dequeues + frees the runner; finite epoch deadline / tokio timeout on call_run_next as defense-in-depth. Natural home for wamn-dq5 [5.12] on the runner path.

title: [REVIEW C3-1] Credential vault enforces project scope but never the contract's per-execution not-granted grant
description: HIGH (docs/review-2026-07.md §C3-1). wamn:node@0.1.0 models per-execution grants (credential-error::not-granted, wamn-node.wit:181-189) but the host vault implements only project scope: credentials.get(handle) resolves ANY handle in the component's project (wamn_credentials.rs:213-239); resolve returns only Unavailable/NotFound, never not-granted (:158-167). Node-scoping lives only in the SDK CapsCtx facade (node-guest/caps.rs:98-110), bypassed by the direct-import custom-node path. project_for fails OPEN to DEFAULT_PROJECT on a missing wamn.project claim (:147-154). Impact: a custom node importing wamn:node/credentials directly can get(<any-name>) and receive every credential in its project's vault incl. sibling secrets it was never granted — defeats 'secret injected only into executing node's context'. Latent today (only compiled-in std lib calls credentials via safe facade), live when custom nodes ship. FIX: runner registers the executing dispatch's declared credential name(s) with the plugin (like set_project); resolve returns not-granted otherwise (non-breaking, variant exists); make project_for fail-closed. BLOCKS wamn-bd5/wamn-1ab.

title: [REVIEW C4-1] Guest can override app.tenant claim in-band via wamn:postgres txn API and defeat RLS
description: HIGH — review headline (docs/review-2026-07.md §C4-1). Plugin docstring wamn_postgres.rs:10-11 claims 'no guest-facing way to override claims' — FALSE at SQL level. HostTransaction::query/execute (:1365-1405) pass arbitrary guest sql with zero statement filtering; tenant injected only as SET LOCAL app.tenant at BEGIN (:656-682); RLS keys on current_setting('app.tenant') (postgres-init.sql:55), a placeholder GUC wamn_app (NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS) may freely SET; a later SET app.tenant='victim' overrides BEGIN's SET LOCAL. Guest: begin()->execute("SET app.tenant='victim'")->query(...) reads/writes another tenant. Untested by S2, unconsidered by 2.6. Not reachable on shipped defaults (std nodes structured, raw-SQL flag-OFF, custom nodes not shipped) => high not critical, but directly exploitable once raw-SQL node (wamn-1nd) enabled or custom nodes (wamn-bd5) ship. A dedicated user-SQL role does NOT close it (any role can SET app.tenant). FIX: (1) S2 gate phase driving SET/set_config('app.tenant',foreign) asserting zero cross-tenant rows; (2) bind tenant to something guest can't rewrite in-band (per-tenant role via SET ROLE + RLS on current_user, or GUC_SUPERUSER_ONLY app.tenant via extension); (3) correct docstring + security-db-path.md. Extends R2 threat surface; gap in the 2.6 egress review. HARD-BLOCKS wamn-1nd + wamn-bd5.
