title: wamn-provision: drift-guard the inlined quote_ident/quote_literal vs canonical wamn_ddl::sql
description:
HIGH / security-path (external review #1). crates/wamn-provision/src/sql.rs:15-23 inlines quote_ident/quote_literal deliberately (to keep the prod dep closure at serde_json) but NOTHING asserts they match the canonical wamn_ddl::sql::{quote_ident,quote_literal} (crates/wamn-ddl/src/sql.rs:6,11, already pub). If the canonical ever adds escaping (e.g. NUL handling) the copy silently drifts -- and this is the exact function backing the "a slug cannot contain a double-quote, so CREATE/DROP DATABASE + role DDL are injection-safe" argument.

Fix (matches the repo drift-guard idiom): add wamn-ddl as a DEV-dependency of wamn-provision (prod closure unchanged) + a #[cfg(test)] test comparing super::quote_ident/quote_literal to wamn_ddl::sql::* over (a) an adversarial set (double-quote, single-quote, doubled quotes, NUL, backslash, tab, unicode, mixed) and (b) an exhaustive single-ASCII-char sweep 0x00..=0x7f wrapped as x<c>y. Mutation-test the guard (break the inline escaping, confirm the test fails, restore). Alt: extract a zero-dep wamn-sql-esc micro-crate both re-export.
close_reason: Closed

title: [PLAN-4] D8 structural close: dedicated user-SQL role and non-rewritable tenant authority
description:
## Goal

Make D8's dedicated author-SQL identity a structural database boundary before raw SQL can be enabled for any real project environment.

## Current evidence

`wamn_app` owns both entity access and platform bookkeeping access. The shipped SQL blocklist rejects direct claim mutations but dynamic SQL can construct them. PLAN §4 therefore requires a dedicated per-project-env user-SQL role and a tenant identity that author SQL cannot rewrite in-band. R45 separately owns cross-project database-login isolation.

## Scope

Provision and rotate the dedicated role/credential; re-key the user-SQL execution path and its RLS identity to non-author-writable authority; grant entity DML and only the minimum trigger/outbox rights required for entity writes; grant no catalog, flow, run, queue, admission, test, identity, or other bookkeeping access. Cover generated and hand-written floor policies and every raw-SQL execution path.

## Exposure gate

Blocks raw SQL in every non-POC pilot, studio, API, template, or other client surface. The raw-SQL feature remains default off until the separate D8 enablement gate passes.

## Evidence

Use the real provisioned role against a throwaway Postgres/project-env schema. Positive controls prove allowed entity CRUD and required row-event behavior. Adversarial dynamic SQL (DO/EXECUTE, SET/RESET/set_config/SET ROLE, search-path and qualified names) must fail to cross tenant or reach bookkeeping. Mutation proofs must kill removal of the role switch, an added bookkeeping grant, and restoration of a rewritable tenant claim.
acceptance_criteria:
- A provisioned project environment has a distinct user-SQL login/role with independently rotatable material and no database/schema ownership.
- Raw SQL executes under non-author-rewritable tenant authority and cannot change tenant/role claims through direct or dynamic SQL.
- The role can perform the documented entity operations and required event-trigger write, but receives permission-denied for every platform bookkeeping family.
- A live negative gate covers all generated/hand-written floors and kills the named role-switch, excess-grant, and claim-rewrite mutants.
- No real-project enablement flag or client exposure is turned on by this issue.
notes:
Kickoff evidence 2026-08-01: services/ctl and deploy SQL still use wamn_app broadly; cjv.2's reject_claim_mutation is explicitly a blocklist, not the structural close. PLAN §4 is authoritative. Keep R45/wamn-2jkm.85 as the separate cross-project credential boundary; the D8 exposure gate depends on both.

FIRST STEP is therefore to audit wamn/2.5.2's content — confirm its base is the upstream 2.5.2 rev and that it carries an epoch commit whose diff matches patches/0001 (pushing/fixing it if not) — before switching anything.

DELETE the apparatus: the [patch] block, scripts/vendor-wasmcloud.sh, patches/ (+README), the /vendor/ .gitignore line, the Dockerfile vendor stage (git dep resolves inside cargo build — network in the build stage is already true for crates.io). wasmtime alignment: currently exactly one wasmtime in the graph (46.0.0 @ git rev 7535c025; root Cargo.lock has a single entry, fork workspace pins the same rev) — re-verify single-wasmtime after the rev bump. Patch 0002 expected dead as a git dep (upstream lints get --cap-lints allow automatically); only re-add as a fork commit if -D warnings actually fires. Validate: cargo update -p wash-runtime (lockfile records fork source+rev) -> clean build (0002 verdict lands here) -> run the upgrade gate subset once to establish the fork baseline -> commit.

STANDING SYNC RUNBOOK (record in docs — patches/README.md's successor): Triggers, priority order: (1) wasmtime SECURITY ADVISORY on our version line — immediate (weekly cargo audit against the lockfile until CI exists); (2) upstream MINOR release — evaluate, batch quarterly unless a needed fix pulls; (3) WASI 0.3 / wasmtime MAJOR — planned work with the wamn:node 0.2 revision. Per sync: pre-read upstream log over crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/; new branch wamn/X.Y.Z from the new rev; cherry-pick the carried commits (conflict = review event, not merge chore — upstream changed that code for a reason; re-check each commit's EXIT CONDITION and DROP if upstream now does it); push; bump rev; re-align wasmtime; run the upgrade gate subset — deliberately not all of P0, just fork-load-bearing behaviors: S1 instantiation p50/p99 + cap-kill + epoch-deadline demo (bench), S2 chaos gate (pgbench), S3 kill/resume (flowbench), the ResourceLimiter differentiation phase once it exists. Record per sync: date, base rev old->new, commits carried/dropped, gate numbers old->new. Rollback: repoint rev at the old wamn/* branch tip — never delete a branch wamn ever pinned (cheap, and the bisect trail). Drift check between syncs (before host-touching feature work): git fetch upstream && git log <BASE>..upstream/main -- crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/. ESCALATION THRESHOLD (standing): the fork carries host-integration commits ONLY (things upstream should arguably own); wamn features never land there. Past ~4-5 commits, or the same commit conflicting on consecutive syncs, it is no longer dependency management — engage upstream or accept runtime-maintainer status as an explicit decision-table entry.

External review R4 (docs/review-findings.md § R4), verified at tip 873c3d8. Sequencing: immediate — everything else from the review lands on top of this switch.

title: [1.3] Per-component memory limits via Store ResourceLimiter (fork commit #2) + differentiation bench gate
description:
S1 finding #2, formalized with a decision record. LocalResources.memory_limit_mb is carried end-to-end upstream but never plumbed into wasmtime — zero ResourceLimiter/Store::limiter call sites (verified: vendor/wasmcloud/crates/wash-runtime — types.rs:76 carries the field; washlet/mod.rs:645,769,800,823 only copy it). Today's 256 MiB cap is the pooling allocator's ENGINE-WIDE max_memory_size (crates/wamn-host/src/engine.rs:9,28-29) — uniform across all components on a host, not per-workload. The plan promises per-component sandbox caps (1.3, 8.2 isolation story, 9.8 "memory vs cap" metric); that promise is currently weaker than written and, unlike the epoch gap, had no decision record.

DESIGN (two-tier): pooling max_memory_size = the PLATFORM CEILING (largest budget any component may hold; pre-sizes pool slots). memory_limit_mb = the PER-COMPONENT BUDGET enforced below the ceiling by a per-Store ResourceLimiter — pure arithmetic (desired > limit -> deny) consulted on initial memory creation + every memory.grow. Denial => grow fails in-guest -> allocator abort -> service trap: the exact failure shape S1 validated at the engine cap, so restart accounting is untouched; initial-memory checking is a freebie (over-budget baseline fails at instantiation with a clear error). Strictness: budget > ceiling = hard workload-start error (never a silent clamp); absent field => budget = ceiling => behaviorally invisible to every existing workload (the regression guard); v0 per-linear-memory with a documented multi-memory note; the same limiter applies a modest fixed table-growth cap (closes the resource-exhaustion sibling free).

IMPLEMENTATION (fork commit #2, beside the epoch commit): new_store_from_templates in crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/linked_call.rs — verified the single production store-creation site (linked_call.rs:259 is the only wasmtime::Store::new; new_ephemeral_store delegates at :373; remaining sites are tests + the pooling capability probe). Budget resolution order: LocalResources.memory_limit_mb if the workload spec is reachable there; else the wamn.memory-limit-mb component-config key (the epoch commit's identical stopgap routing); else WAMN_MEMORY_LIMIT_MB env; else ceiling. Verify sync ResourceLimiter suffices with the async store (ResourceLimiterAsync is the fallback). Commit message carries the ledger fields; exit condition: "upstream plumbs memory_limit_mb into a Store limiter — delete this commit." The most upstreamable commit we carry (implements their own dead field).

OBSERVABILITY: the limiter is also the 9.8 meter — record per-component high-water mark; increment wamn.memory.denied{component} on every refusal (S5 counted-never-silent). Denials become alertable; high-water data right-sizes tier budgets.

GATE (new wamn-host bench phase, S1-style): (1) cap honored: memhog at a 64 MiB budget under a 256 MiB ceiling traps at ~64 MiB, heartbeat healthy, host accepts new work; (2) DIFFERENTIATION (the point): two components at 64 and 192 MiB budgets resident concurrently, each capped at its own number — closes S1 finding #2; (3) denial metric incremented with component id + log line; (4) no-regression: unlimited workloads byte-identical, S1 instantiation p50/p99 unchanged (one predicate per grow — expect noise, confirm).

Doc closure: decision-table row (chosen: ceiling + per-component limiter; rejected: engine-uniform — contradicts 8.2; wait-for-upstream — dead field, no signal). Amend "per-component sandbox limit" claims to LINEAR-MEMORY budget (compiled-code residency, stacks, host-side buffers live under separate engine config — 8.2 must not overclaim). Mark S1 finding #2 resolved in docs/p0-results.md with commit + bench-phase pointers, and update the superseded note on wamn-6oa. External review R3 (docs/review-findings.md § R3), verified at tip 873c3d8. Sequencing: before P1 multi-tenant density work; depends on the fork-consumption switch (this lands as a fork commit).
close_reason: Fork commit 5b158ff (wamn/2.5.2, pushed): WamnStoreLimiter enforces per-component linear-memory budgets below the 256MiB pooling ceiling; budget>ceiling hard-fails at store creation (WAMN_MEMORY_CEILING_MB advertised by wamn-host); denials logged+counted (wamn::memory); no budget = no limiter (byte-identical). Gate: bench phase 5 differentiation PASS (64->56, 192->184 concurrent, unbudgeted 248, over-ceiling never allocates) + phases 1-4 + S2 chaos + S3 resume regression PASS (debug). Doc closure: D16 decision row, 9.8 linear-memory wording, p0-results S1 finding #2 RESOLVED, fork ledger updated.

title: [5.14] Park/wake consumes the redelivery budget: attempts must count crash evidence only (both claim paths)
description:
attempts is meant to bound crash redeliveries; it currently counts every claim. claim_batch_sql (crates/wamn-run-queue/src/sql.rs:61) and claim_partition_head_sql (sql.rs:340) both do `attempts = q.attempts + 1` unconditionally; park_sql (sql.rs:110) releases the lease without touching attempts; a wake is a doorbell hint only (dispatch.rs:537-552), so every park->wake re-claim burns one unit of redelivery budget. Once attempts >= max_attempts (DEFAULT 20, deploy/run-queue.sql) the row classifies Exhausted (claim.rs:45), claims skip it, and the janitor retires the run to infrastructure-failure — a run that parked >19 times is killed having failed zero times. Delay-loop / repeated-backoff / escalation-timer flows hit this; partitioned flows burn fastest (head-first one-in-flight re-claims the parked head on every wake).

FIX (crash-evidence semantics): increment only when the claim reclaims an EXPIRED lease (= the prior owner died without completing, parking, or dequeuing): `attempts = q.attempts + CASE WHEN q.lease_expires_at IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END` in BOTH claim_batch_sql and claim_partition_head_sql (the claim predicate has already established expired-or-NULL, so IS NOT NULL = expired lease = crash evidence). Mirror in the pure layer: claim.rs plan_claim + partition.rs plan_partition_claim post-increment gain the same conditional; claim_state / is_claimable unchanged (Exhausted still attempts >= max_attempts). Semantics after: max_attempts = "how many times may a runner die holding this run" — crash-loops still retire; a run parks unbounded times for free. Rejected: park resets attempts (loses crash history across park boundaries — crash, reclaim, park, wake, crash never exhausts); separate wake_count column (wakes are free by design, no decision needs the count).

GATE EXPECTATIONS: failoverbench asserts attempts == 2 after kill->reclaim (crates/wamn-host/src/failoverbench.rs:579) — becomes 1 under crash-evidence semantics (first claim free, expired-lease reclaim counts); update the assertion WITH the semantics change and state why in the gate comment — the new value is the point, not a regression. New unit cases (tests/queue.rs pure layer): N-park flow with max_attempts=1 stays claimable at every wake; crash-loop (repeated expired-lease reclaims) exhausts at exactly max_attempts; claim -> park -> wake-claim -> crash -> reclaim yields attempts = 1, not 3. queuebench new phase: flow parking 10x with max_attempts=3 completes, repeated through the PARTITION path; janitor sweep after shows no infrastructure-failure rows; existing crash-loop retirement phase unchanged.

Doc closure: docs/run-queue.md lifecycle step 3 states the crash-evidence semantics incl. the first-dispatch case (a first-dispatch crash costs its unit on the RECLAIM). External review R1 (docs/review-findings.md § R1); all claims verified against tip 873c3d8. Severity note: the review's "six delay segments + max_attempts=5 can never complete" narrative assumes a non-default budget; with the DEFAULT 20 the failure needs >19 parks/backoffs in one run — real for delay-loops and long escalation chains, not for S6's single 24h park. Still a correctness bug in the exact mechanism S6 validated, masked in P0 because the bench parked once.
close_reason: Crash-evidence attempts semantics shipped: both claim SQL builders use CASE WHEN lease_expires_at IS NOT NULL (expired-lease reclaim = crash) with pure-layer mirrors; gate expectations updated (failoverbench 1->0/2->1, queuebench reclaim+partition-failover 2->1); new queuebench park mode (10 parks max_attempts=3 completes both paths) + 3 pure unit tests + live-apply first-claim-free/park-free/reclaim-bumps asserts. 5 mutants killed (both SQL sites, both pure mirrors, partition set-to-1). Adversarial review: 1 confirmed coverage gap (partition-mirror additivity) fixed + mutation-verified; 4 refuted. All gates PASS locally (debug): crate 31+live-apply, queuebench --mode all, failoverbench --mode all. Follow-up filed: wamn-fqg.7 (budget-spent NULL-lease wedge). In-cluster image predates the fix (self-consistent old semantics); next host rebuild picks it up.

title: [E13] runtime egress deny: wasi:sockets TcpConnect policy (fork commit) — no-raw-socket boundary enforced
description:
The 2.6 review (wamn-wv3) found the "wamn:postgres plugin is the only DB path" guarantee is enforced ONLY by WIT-world composition at build/publish time. The runtime registers wasi:sockets on every workload linker unconditionally (vendor wash-runtime engine/mod.rs), and the production socket policy allows outbound TCP to any address (linked_call.rs build_ctx_from_template: socket_addr_check TcpConnect => true; allowed_network_uses default tcp:true), consulting allowed_hosts only for wasi:http. So a component whose world imports wasi:sockets could raw-connect to Postgres and bypass the plugin's tenant-claim/RLS injection. Standard/generated workloads are provably safe today (they do not import wasi:sockets — asserted by the 2.6 egressbench gate), so this is defense-in-depth ahead of the production custom-code-node path (5.6).

Add a deploy-time host guard that rejects any workload whose component world imports wasi:sockets (raw TCP/UDP) unless explicitly allowlisted — turning the build-time convention into an enforced host check. Likely a carried wash-runtime patch in the washlet workload_start path (inspect component imports before instantiate), or an admission check in the control plane / operator. Pairs with a K8s NetworkPolicy (deny pod->PG:5432 except the plugin identity) as the network-layer belt (infra/8.x).

Design: docs/security-db-path.md (2.6 review, "Finding" + "Recommended controls"); docs/platform-plan.md 2.6 / 8.2.
acceptance_criteria: A workload whose component world imports wasi:sockets is rejected at workload-start (unless explicitly allowlisted); the standard flow-runner + wamn:postgres path is unaffected; a negative gate proves rejection and a positive control proves wamn:postgres still works.

title: [5.7] Run state persistence (runs/node_runs, replay)
description: runs/node_runs tables; at-least-once semantics with idempotency keys; run history, replay from captured inputs, partial re-run from a failed node. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 5.7
notes:
=== RESUME PLAN (wamn-5xl [5.7] Run state persistence; start after bd prime + bd show wamn-5xl) ===

GOAL: durable run state — `runs` / `node_runs` tables; at-least-once semantics with
idempotency keys; run history; REPLAY from captured inputs; PARTIAL RE-RUN from a
failed node. This is the DURABLE half of what 5.2 (wamn-runner) left as a seam: the
engine has an in-memory RunState + a single `step_seq` checkpoint; 5.7 persists per-node
rows and makes resume BRANCH-AWARE (reconstruct the frontier from node_runs), plus
replay + partial re-run. COMPOSES wamn-runner (5.2, wamn-uyd DONE) + wamn-flow (5.1).

STEP 1 ON RESUME (before writing code — this is design-heavy, mirror the 5.2 approach):
Run an UNDERSTAND PASS (a Workflow of parallel readers, like the 5.2 one) mapping:
  A. plan §5.7 scope vs the siblings it must NOT swallow — quote the plan lines:
     5.14 (durable QUEUE: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + NATS doorbell + dispatcher + run-claim
     leases; "Postgres owns durability — SKIP LOCKED run queue + run state, one domain"),
     9.6 (node-level I/O CAPTURE policy: scrubbing 9.5, truncation, per-flow capture toggle,
     PII; streamed = head-preview+size+hash; hot in node_runs), 5.10 (payload BYTE store for
     streamed payloads, content-addressed). Draw the boundary: 5.7 owns the runs/node_runs
     SCHEMA + at-least-once/idempotency + replay + partial-re-run; NOT the queue (5.14), the
     capture policy (9.6), or the byte store (5.10 — node_runs holds inline + head/size/hash).
  B. the CURRENT S3 storage 5.7 supersedes/augments: deploy/postgres-init.sql s3.flows/
     s3.flow_runs(step_seq/status/state_json)/s3.sink + how components/flowrunner checkpoints
     (step_seq = node index; ON CONFLICT (run_id,step) idempotency). Confirm exact columns.
  C. wamn-runner (5.2) INTERNALS a replay/reconstruct API needs: RunState is opaque (private
     frontier/current/step_seq/result/failure); to rebuild it from persisted node_runs the
     crate likely needs a NEW constructor (e.g. Plan::resume(run_id, completed:&[(node,port,
     payload)]) -> RunState with the frontier re-derived by replaying recorded successes).
     Read crates/wamn-runner/src/{engine,plan}.rs. Dispatch.idempotency_key = "{run_id}:{node}".
  D. the HOUSE tenant-floor/RLS schema pattern (deploy/postgres-init.sql s2/s3 FORCE RLS +
     app.tenant policy; wamn-ddl 3.2 floor; catalog-schema.sql standalone) so the new runs/
     node_runs tables match it (tenant_id + FORCE RLS + policy + grants; idempotency UNIQUE).

SCOPE BOUNDARY (5.7 OWNS): runs + node_runs tables (tenant-scoped, RLS, idempotency-keyed);
at-least-once execution semantics; run history (per-node status/input/output/error/attempt/
timestamps); REPLAY (branch-aware RunState reconstruction from node_runs so a rescheduled
runner resumes EXACTLY, superseding 5.2's step_seq-only linear resume); PARTIAL RE-RUN (re-seed
the frontier from a chosen failed node using its captured input). Does NOT own: durable queue +
SKIP LOCKED + doorbell + leases (5.14); I/O capture POLICY scrub/truncate/toggle/PII (9.6 — 5.7
provides the node_runs columns, 9.6 the policy); streamed-payload BYTE store (5.10 — node_runs
carries inline + head/size/hash preview only); per-node ordering (5.11); cancel op (5.12).

ARCH (CONFIRM via AskUserQuestion on resume, like 5.2's scope+structure Qs):
- STRUCTURE: pure crate (name? wamn-run-store / wamn-runstore) = RunRecord/NodeRunRecord model
  + status enums + REPLAY logic (reconstruct RunState from node_runs) + PARTIAL-RE-RUN logic,
  PURE (no DB — emits the persistence ops / provides a trait the component implements over
  wamn:postgres), unit-tested with no cluster (the wamn-api/wamn-runner split). deps wamn-runner
  + wamn-flow + serde_json. PLUS likely EXTEND wamn-runner with a resume/reconstruct constructor
  (Plan::resume). PLUS DDL for runs/node_runs. PLUS wire components/flowrunner to persist per-node
  rows + replay branch-aware (superseding the step_seq-only checkpoint) — this is the big
  component change + gate impact.
- SCOPE AMBITION (confirm): (A) full — schema + crate(model+replay+partial-rerun) + rewire the
  flowrunner to persist node_runs + branch-aware replay + a partial-re-run entry point, gated by
  the existing flowbench/testhostbench (must stay green) + new crate tests + a live-apply gate;
  or (B) narrower — schema + pure crate (model+replay+partial-rerun, fully unit-tested) + a
  live-apply gate, with the flowrunner rewiring minimal/deferred (keep step_seq for the linear
  fixtures, add node_runs as the durable history + prove replay/partial-rerun at the crate level).
  RECOMMEND deciding after the understand pass shows how invasive the flowrunner rewrite is.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS to confirm on resume:
1. Branch-aware durable replay = reconstruct the frontier from node_runs (supersede step_seq),
   vs keep step_seq for linear + node_runs as history/replay-source only. (5.2 noted branch-aware
   durable resume is explicitly 5.7.)
2. Idempotency key: reuse the engine's "{run_id}:{node}"; loops/re-visits need an occurrence/

3. Schema location: production runs/node_runs in deploy/postgres-init.sql (like s2/s3) vs a

4. node_runs columns for 9.6/5.10 seams: inline input/output jsonb + status + attempt + error +

5. Partial re-run: how the frontier is seeded from a failed node's captured INPUT (replay upstream

GATES: pure crate tests (replay reconstructs the exact RunState/frontier incl. a branch; partial

ASK-FIRST: run the understand pass THEN AskUserQuestion on scope ambition + structure BEFORE

notes/memory via FILES + "$(cat file)", --key not positional. Shared-cluster guardrail: additive

title: [4.1] Per-project API gateway component (REST v1)
description: One gateway instance per project (shared gateway = worst blast radius; Wasm density + scale-to-zero makes per-project nearly free). Reads catalog snapshot; serves /api/rest/{entity} with filter/sort/paginate/expand. REST ships in P1, /api/graphql in P2. v1 fence: CRUD + relation expansion only. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 4.1
notes:
=== 4.1 DECISIONS (user answered Q1/Q2/Q3 on resume 2026-07-11) ===
Q1 SHAPE = C (BOTH in one issue): crate crates/wamn-api (gateway logic) + component
components/api-gateway (exports wasi:http/incoming-handler, imports wamn:postgres) +
host harness crates/wamn-host apibench (drives the component via ProxyPre against a
real PG; in-cluster Job of record).
Q2 CRUD = full CRUD + one-level relation expansion.
Q3 QUERY = all four (filter/sort/paginate/expand), PostgREST-ish (?col=eq.val | ?col=val;
?sort=col,-col2; ?limit=&offset= with MAX cap; ?expand=rel,rel2 one level).

DESIGN (from understand-workflow digests):
- Catalog cross-refs by id (Reference.entity, Relation.from/to/through EntityId; from_field
  FieldId); SQL identifiers by .name (3.2 emits CREATE TABLE "<entity.name>"/"<field.name>").
  Resolve by id, emit by name (quote_ident, reused from wamn_ddl::sql).
- Injection-safe by construction: every VALUE is a $n param (ParamBuilder); every identifier
  is catalog-allowlisted + quote_ident'd; unknown entity/field/relation/operator -> 400.
- Tenant seam: INSERT sets tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant', true) (server expr, no
  param, no 3.2 change) -> satisfies floor WITH CHECK. UPDATE/DELETE rely on RLS USING.
- Projection = id + user fields (tenant_id NEVER exposed). numeric -> exact-decimal STRING in
  params AND response JSON (no float). SqlValue mirrors WIT sql-value 1:1.
- Component: exports wasi:http/proxy (incoming-handler); loads catalog snapshot from DB via
  wamn:postgres (memoized) -> Router::compile -> query/execute -> shape -> HTTP response.
- Harness apibench: ProxyPre + SharedCtx (already WasiHttpView); provision_schema/drop_schema
  (superuser) + wamn_ddl Migration::create floor + seed; asserts CRUD+expand+RLS+injection.
STATUS: implementing crate first.
close_reason: 4.1 REST API gateway: pure crate wamn-api (Catalog->injection-safe parameterized SQL: CRUD + one-level expand + filter/sort/paginate; 30 tests+dt) + component api-gateway (exports wasi:http/incoming-handler, imports wamn:postgres, links the crate; passes 2.6 egress) + host apibench gate (drives it via ProxyPre against real PG: CRUD/expand/RLS/injection all PASS). Adversarially reviewed (5 lenses); only fix = out-of-range offset. clippy/fmt clean; all sibling regressions intact; CLAUDE/AGENTS [4.1] mirrored.

P1; dep wamn-as5 CLOSED; parent epic wamn-5x0 [E2]; BLOCKS/feeds wamn-521 [POC-DM1] (which builds a data model THROUGH the catalog API = define catalog -> migrate live -> get data tables). THE ROLE (survey 2026-07-14): 2.5 is the LIVE EXECUTOR that wraps the ALREADY-SHIPPED machinery. 3.2 wamn-ddl EMITS + CLASSIFIES (Migration::create/migrate -> MigrationPlan{operations:[Operation{summary,sql,safety Additive|Destructive,entity,field,note}]}; Confirmation None|ConfirmedWithBackup gate; sql(confirm)->Result<String,RequiresConfirmation> [destructive refused w/o ConfirmedWithBackup, else prefixes a "-- BACKUP CHECKPOINT REQUIRED" marker 2.5 must honor]; preview_sql/report; k56/nqg/drb name-reuse-safe ordering all in ONE plan). 3.4 wamn-schema owns the PURE IN-MEMORY lifecycle (Environment tracks a Vec<VersionRecord{catalog,state,base}>; State draft->staged->applied->superseded; apply() enforces single-applied [demote prior Applied->Superseded] + the stale-base guard [candidate.base must == current applied_version, else LifecycleError::StaleBase]; promote()/PromotionPlan wraps a MigrationPlan for cross-env). 2.5 = the thing that reads the CURRENT state from a live DB, computes the plan (wamn-ddl migrate current->target), APPLIES it transactionally, advances the lifecycle IN THE DB, records history, and offers dry-run + a rollback plan.

title: [3.1] Metadata model: entity/field/relation catalog
description: Entity/field/relation/index/constraint definitions in catalog tables; system entities flagged read-only-structure but extensible (custom columns on users, etc.). Design: docs/platform-plan.md 3.1
notes:
=== RESUME PLAN (3.1 wamn-it8; start after bd prime + bd show wamn-it8) ===

GOAL: define the METADATA CATALOG MODEL — entity / field / relation / index /
constraint definitions, with system entities flagged read-only-structure but
extensible (custom columns on `users`, etc.). This is the foundation the DDL
compiler (3.2), generated API (4.1), designer UI (3.3), RLS builder (3.5), and
schema-impact analysis (11.8) all READ. Deliverable shape TBD — ASK the user
first (STEP 1); it will most likely mirror 5.1 (contract + shared Rust crate).

SCOPE GUARD: 3.1 is the MODEL (+ the catalog tables that persist it). It is NOT:
- 3.2 DDL compiler (metadata diff -> migration plan -> applied DDL) — wamn-vbd;
- 4.1 generated REST API over the catalog — wamn-759;
- 3.3 visual designer UI (the type PALETTE + rule UX) — wamn-ivi;
- 3.5 RLS policy builder — wamn-idu;
- 3.4 versioning/environments lifecycle (draft->staged->applied) — model only
  here, lifecycle there.
The model must be EXPRESSIVE ENOUGH for the POC data model + 3.3's declared type/
constraint needs, but building DDL emission / API / UI / RLS compilation is
downstream. D14: NEUTRAL PRIMITIVES in core, opinionated domain models in
modules — 3.1 stays domain-neutral (no receipt/hold types baked in).

WHAT THE MODEL MUST EXPRESS (from plan 3.1/3.3/D14 + poc-material-receiving.md):
- ENTITIES: name, is_system flag. System entities (e.g. `users`) =
  structure is read-only (can't drop/retype system columns) but EXTENSIBLE
  (add custom fields, e.g. users.cert_level). Model which mutations each kind
  allows. (POC: users + cert_level = the system-entity-extension hard path;
  traceability 2.4/3.1.)
- FIELDS: name, type, nullable, default?, plus a neutral `sensitive`/mask-ish
  attribute feeding 4.3 field-mask (POC: inspectors can't see supplier pricing).
- FIELD TYPE SYSTEM (the big scope fork — see DECISION below): must cover
  text, int/bigint, bool, uuid, json, timestamptz, date, ENUM(variants), and
  EXACT-DECIMAL numeric(precision,scale) with optional UNIT binding — floats
  DISALLOWED for material quantities/formulations (POC hard req; 3.3). Plus a
  REFERENCE type (FK to another entity) or model FKs via relations (below).
- RELATIONS: 1:N / N:1 (FK), and consider N:M; plus HIERARCHICAL/CLOSURE
  relations (genealogy, asset trees) per D14/3.3. (POC: receipts->lines 1:N,
  lines->materials, holds->lines, dispositions->holds.)
- INDEXES: named, columns, unique?.
- CONSTRAINTS: composite UNIQUENESS (POC: (receipt_no, supplier_id)), not-null
  (or via field.nullable), check? (keep minimal/neutral).

DELIVERABLE DECISION — ASK THE USER (AskUserQuestion) on resume, BEFORE coding:
Q1 shape (mirror the 5.1 fork):
  (A) [likely RECOMMEND] Contract + shared Rust crate `crates/wamn-catalog`:
      canonical types (Entity/Field/FieldType/Relation/Index/Constraint +
      is_system), validation (referential integrity; system-entity extension
      rules; type/constraint well-formedness; numeric-not-float), import/export
      JSON (feeds 3.4 promotion), a structural CATALOG DIFF primitive (feeds 3.2
      migration + 11.8 impact — analogous to wamn-flow's diff), the POC data
      model as a test fixture, a schemars-GENERATED docs/catalog-model.schema.json
      (drift-guarded), docs/catalog-model.md, AND the catalog TABLE DDL (the
      Postgres tables that persist metadata, house-style: own schema, wamn_app
      NOSUPERUSER, FORCE RLS keyed on app.tenant). Does NOT build 3.2/4.1/3.3.
  (B) Contract-first: docs/catalog-model.md + generated JSON Schema + catalog
      table DDL + POC worked example; NO Rust crate (3.2/4.1 build against it).
  (C) = A, PLUS wire the catalog tables into deploy/postgres-init.sql (or a
      migration) so a live project DB carries them — heavier, edges into 3.2/DM1.
Q2 type-system scope: does 3.1 OWN the concrete field-type set (numeric+
  precision/scale+unit, timestamptz, enum, reference, ...) [RECOMMEND yes — 3.2/
  4.1 need types to emit DDL/API; 3.3 is only the palette UI over the model], or
  keep field `type` an open string and defer the type set to 3.3? (Recommend 3.1
  owns it.)
Q3 (fold into Q1 if possible): include the catalog TABLE DDL now (A) or defer
  persistence to 3.2/POC-DM1 (B-ish)? And: provide the catalog DIFF in 3.1
  (mirrors 5.1; 11.8 needs it) or leave all diffing to 3.2? [Recommend: DDL yes,
  diff yes as a primitive 3.2 consumes.]

WHAT EXISTS (probed 2026-07-10): NO catalog/metadata/migration code — greenfield.
deploy/postgres-init.sql = the DDL HOUSE STYLE (schema-per-feature: s2/s3;
CREATE ROLE wamn_app LOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOBYPASSRLS; CREATE SCHEMA x
AUTHORIZATION postgres; FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY + CREATE POLICY keyed on
current_setting('app.tenant', true)). crates/wamn-flow (5.1, commit 1a45998) =
the CRATE PATTERN TO MIRROR EXACTLY: src/{types,validate,diff,lib}.rs; serde
rename_all=kebab-case; schemars 0.8 generating docs/*.schema.json via an
examples/print-schema.rs + a drift test (committed_schema_matches_types); dev-dep
boon (pure-Rust JSON-Schema validator, no reqwest) validating fixtures; fixtures
under tests/fixtures/*.json + tests/*.rs; CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md mirrored gate block;
added as a workspace member in root Cargo.toml. wamn:postgres plugin (2.2) is how
catalog data is read/written at RUNTIME (downstream, not 3.1).

MIRROR THE 5.1 CRATE PATTERN (see memory wamn-5.1-flow-schema-facts): same file
layout, schemars-generated + drift-tested JSON Schema, boon fixture conformance,
POC model as fixture, mirrored CLAUDE/AGENTS block, workspace member. Reuse the
validate() -> Vec<Issue{severity Error|Warning, code, path, message}> shape.

STEPS: 1) ASK user (Q1 shape A/B/C + Q2 type-scope + Q3 DDL/diff). 2) scaffold
crates/wamn-catalog mirroring wamn-flow (add to root Cargo.toml members). 3)
types + validation + import/export (+ catalog diff if chosen) + POC fixture. 4)
catalog table DDL (if chosen) in house style. 5) docs/catalog-model.md + generated
JSON Schema (examples/print-schema.rs). 6) tests (validate negatives + POC-model
round-trip/validate/schema-conformance/drift/diff). 7) clippy+fmt clean; workspace
build. 8) CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md mirrored block (verify identical). 9) bd close
wamn-it8 (--reason --suggest-next) -> unblocks 3.2/4.1/POC-DM1 etc. 10) COMMIT
(standing rule; after close; amend to include .beads/interactions.jsonl like the
5.1 commit). 11) bd remember --key wamn-3.1-catalog-model-facts (via a FILE, no
backticks — the % / backtick shell-substitution lesson).

RISKS/NOTES: (i) bd notes/memory clobber — write notes & memory via FILES + "$(cat
file)"; NEVER inline backticks/% in bd remember; use --key not a positional key
(bd remember takes content as the ONE positional). (ii) serde deny_unknown_fields
is NOT supported on internally-tagged enums (5.1 lesson) — if FieldType /
Relation-kind / Constraint are tagged enums, DROP deny_unknown_fields on them
(keep on plain structs). (iii) exact-decimal numeric NOT float (POC hard req).
(iv) stay domain-NEUTRAL (D14) — no receipt/hold types in core. (v) system-entity
rule: structure read-only, extension (custom fields) allowed — validate this.
(vi) no git remote -> commit only, never push. (vii) let-chains + edition 2024 OK
(used in wamn-flow). (viii) this is a MODEL/CONTRACT issue like 5.1 — proportionate
scope, not the compiler/API/UI.

ENV STATE (2026-07-10, HEAD 1a45998, tree CLEAN): Done S1-S6 + P0-EXIT + 2.1 +
2.2 + 2.6 + 5.1. 3.1 wamn-it8 is a READY root (no blockers); it BLOCKS wamn-vbd
[3.2], wamn-521 [POC-DM1], wamn-ivi [3.3], wamn-i1k [6.6], wamn-759 [4.1],
wamn-idu [3.5]. Open decisions NOT blocking 3.1: D6 (hosting, 2.3) wamn-dxi, D8
(raw SQL, 5.3) wamn-r13. Memories to load: wamn-5.1-flow-schema-facts (mirror
pattern), wamn-2.2-postgres-production-facts + wamn-s2-postgres-plugin-facts (DDL/
RLS/wamn_app house shape), wamn-backlog-conventions-issue-titles-carry-doc-refs.
Standing rules: ONE issue at a time; claim; ALWAYS ask-first before assuming;
commit after bd close; no push; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md mirrored (independent files).
This prep only CLAIMS wamn-it8 + attaches this plan; do NOT start implementing
until the user resumes and Q1/Q2/Q3 are answered.
close_reason: 3.1 metadata catalog model shipped: crates/wamn-catalog (types/validate/diff/lib) + generated JSON Schema (drift-guarded) + POC & genealogy fixtures + catalog table DDL (deploy/catalog-schema.sql) + docs/catalog-model.md. 19 tests, clippy/fmt clean, DDL applies clean on PG18.

=== CRATE crates/wamn-runner (deps: wamn-flow path + serde_json; NO schemars — engine
not a contract, like wamn-ddl/wamn-api). Add to root Cargo.toml members. ===
Modules:
- outcome.rs: NodeOutcome{Success{payload:Value,port:String} | Error(NodeError)};
  NodeError MIRRORS wamn-node.wit variants (like SqlValue mirrors wamn-postgres):
  Retryable(ErrorDetail) | RateLimited{detail,retry_after_ms:Option<u64>,target_host:Option<String>}
  | Terminal(ErrorDetail) | InvalidInput(ErrorDetail) | Cancelled.
  ErrorDetail{message:String, code:Option<String>, data:Option<Value>}. port defaults MAIN_PORT.
- retry.rs: RetryPolicy{max_attempts,base_ms,factor,cap_ms} + from_config(&Value) reads
  reserved node.config["retry"] object else DEFAULT (max=3,base=100,factor=2.0,cap=30_000).
  backoff(attempt)=min(cap, base*factor^attempt) — DETERMINISTIC exponential, NO jitter
  (pure; jitter is a driver concern). Note in doc.
- plan.rs: Plan<'f>{flow, by_id:HashMap<&str,&Node>, out:HashMap<(&str,&str_port),Vec<&Edge>>}.
  Plan::compile(&Flow)->Result<Plan,EngineError> calls flow.validate()? then indexes edges
  by (from,from_port). EngineError::Invalid(Vec<Issue>).
- engine.rs: RunState{run_id,status:RunStatus(Running|Completed|Failed|Cancelled),
  frontier:VecDeque<Token{node,payload}>, pending:Option<Pending{node,payload,attempt,retry_until_ms,throttle:Option<ThrottleKey>}>,
  step_seq:u64, result:Value, fail:Option<(NodeId,ErrorDetail,FailKind)>}.
  API (driver loop):
    plan.start(run_id, input)->RunState  (frontier=[entry token])
    plan.next(&state, now_ms)->Step{ Dispatch(Dispatch) | Wait{node,until_ms,throttle} | Done(RunStatus) }
      selector: pending&until>now->Wait; pending ready->Dispatch(attempt); frontier pop->Dispatch(attempt=0);
      empty&no-pending->status=Completed,Done.
    plan.apply(&mut state, &Dispatch, NodeOutcome, now_ms)  (pure transition; taxonomy logic):
      Success{payload,port}: step_seq+=1; result=payload; enqueue successors from (node,port).
      Retryable: if attempt+1<max -> pending(retry_until=now+backoff) else route_error_or_fail(RetryExhausted).
      RateLimited: pending(retry_until=now+retry_after_ms.unwrap_or(backoff), throttle=Some(key)); bounded by max.
      Terminal: route_error_or_fail(Terminal).
      InvalidInput: NEVER retry -> route_error_or_fail(InvalidInput) [distinct FailKind, no budget burn].
      Cancelled: status=Cancelled.
    route_error_or_fail(node,detail,kind): edges from (node,ERROR_PORT)? enqueue with payload
      {"error":{code,message,data}} : status=Failed,fail=(node,detail,kind).
  Dispatch{node,node_type,config:Value,credential:Option<String>,attempt,idempotency_key,deadline_ms}.
    idempotency_key = "{run_id}:{node_id}" (v1; loops need occurrence disambiguation -> note).
- throttle.rs: ThrottleKey{node_type,credential:Option<String>,host:Option<String>};
  ThrottleTable{gated:HashMap<ThrottleKey,u64 until_ms>} ready(key,now)/gate(key,until);
  Scheduler{per_flow_limit,in_flight:HashMap<flow_id,usize>,throttle} try_admit/finish. Pure.
- lib.rs: re-exports.
Fan-out: multiple edges from one port -> enqueue all (run SEQUENTIALLY in this single-token
engine; true parallelism is 5.11). Merge: multiple edges into a node -> node runs per arrival
(no join barrier in v1 -> note; join=advanced). Cycles allowed by schema -> loop termination
is the node/config concern; engine does not force acyclicity.

TESTS (crates/wamn-runner/tests/runner.rs, pure, no cluster): linear walk; branch (conditional
true/false port selects path); merge (two edges into one node); error-path routing (terminal ->
error port); retry-then-succeed (attempt count + backoff schedule); retry-exhausted -> error port
-> fail; rate-limited honors retry_after_ms + emits throttle key; invalid-input never retries +
distinct FailKind; cancelled -> Cancelled status; unknown node type surfaced (driver rejects;

title: [2.6] Egress/security review: plugin is the only DB path
description: Review that the plugin is the only DB path; components never get wasi:sockets to Postgres directly. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 2.6
notes:
DONE 2026-07-10. Deliverable A (review doc + green static gate + follow-up issue); NetworkPolicy deferred to infra/8.x (recommended in doc).

FINDING: the "plugin is the only DB path" guarantee is enforced ONLY by WIT-world composition at build/publish time, not by the host at deploy. Verified in vendored wash-runtime: (1) wasi:sockets is registered on EVERY workload linker unconditionally (engine/mod.rs:146-190, +add_p3_to_linker :184) and is NOT gated by host_interfaces (that allowlist matches host PLUGINS only, workload.rs:1418 bind_plugins). (2) production socket policy is allow-all for outbound TCP (linked_call.rs:176-191 build_ctx_from_template socket_addr_check TcpConnect=>true; allowed_network_uses default tcp:true, sockets/mod.rs:68,90 coarse on/off) and never consults allowed_hosts. (3) allowed_hosts gates wasi:http only (S6 HostHandler chokepoint). So a component whose world imports wasi:sockets could raw-connect PG:5432 and bypass tenant-claim/RLS. Standard/generated workloads are provably safe (they don't import sockets).

DELIVERED: docs/security-db-path.md (review). New `egressbench` subcommand (crates/wamn-host/src/egressbench.rs) — STATIC gate: compiles each shipped component, walks imports, asserts flow-runner imports wamn:postgres and NOT wasi:sockets, and every swept component has no raw-socket / unexpected-egress import. Pure wasm-byte introspection (no DB/network) => identical in-cluster and locally => NO in-cluster Job of record. FAIL path unit-tested (egressbench::tests: sockets/other-egress/missing-postgres each fail). Local run PASS: flowrunner egress={wamn:postgres, wasi:http}, all shapes raw-socket=[]. CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md mirrored with the run command. clippy/fmt clean.

FOLLOW-UP: wamn-7j0.1 (deploy-time host guard rejecting wasi:sockets-importing workloads) filed under E8; wamn-bd5 [5.6 production custom node] now depends on it. NetworkPolicy left to infra/8.x.

title: [2.3] Managed Postgres provisioning (CNPG/RDS, backups, PITR)
description: Postgres operator per D6; one DB per project; automated backups, PITR. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 2.3
notes:
RESUME AUTHORIZATION (2026-07-13, user: "prepare to compact with plan to take jxm on resume. I want to make sure we discuss before we start"). We DISCUSSED and ALIGNED this turn (AskUserQuestion, 4 forks all resolved — recorded below). Taking THIS bead on resume is approved. Approval scopes to THIS bead only (workflow-rule-approval-scopes-to-the-named-bead): on resume, bd update wamn-jxm --claim, build the MVP below, gate it, then bd close + commit + git push + bd dolt push, then STOP (do NOT chain to 2.4/wamn-as5 — it is the next logical step but needs its OWN approval).

=== AGREED SHAPE (4 decisions, do NOT re-ask) ===
Q1 Backups scope = DEFER archive/PITR. MVP = provisioning + per-project DB/role/Secret + isolation gate. WAL archiving (needs an in-cluster object store / MinIO) + PITR are a FAST-FOLLOW bead (file it on close); the restore DRILL stays 10.3 (wamn-tao).
Q2 CNPG topology = ONE SHARED CNPG Cluster, database-per-project (matches the 2.2 pool-per-project model + today's single-instance shape; lightest; keeps the RDS re-target parallel — one instance, DB-per-project). NOT cluster-per-project.
Q3 Credential read = KEEP wamn-5x0.1 SEPARATE (P2). 2.3 EMITS a real wamn-db-<project> Secret + the gate proves resolution via the StaticCredentialProvider fed from it; the live K8s-client read (K8sSecretProvider) stays 5x0.1. Do NOT pull a K8s read-client dep into this bead.
Q4 Driver = IMPERATIVE CLI subcommand `wamn-host provision-project` (the publish-catalog precedent), run via a Job. NOT a Project CRD + controller (that is the 10.1 control plane, P3).

=== FIXED CONSTRAINTS (already settled, not up for debate) ===
- The 2.2 seam is BUILT: CredentialProvider::resolve(project)->ProjectConfig{database_url, pool_max_size, wait_timeout_ms, statement_timeout_ms, row_limit} (crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_postgres.rs). 2.3 produces what fills it. K8sSecretProvider is a stub that bails (5x0.1).
- NARROW SURFACE is a D6 design requirement: keep provisioning to "a CredentialProvider + per-project DB URL" so an RDS/Cloud SQL re-target stays cheap. Hide CNPG behind that seam.
- The existing deploy/postgres.yaml single pod is LOAD-BEARING + guardrailed (S2-S6 + all crate live-apply gates + all benches run against it). CNPG stands up ALONGSIDE it (additive; legacy pod + gates UNTOUCHED; 2.3's gate targets the new CNPG-provisioned DBs). Migrating the legacy fixtures onto CNPG = a SEPARATE later bead (the D6 handoff says exactly this). NEVER recreate/delete the shared pod (shared-cluster guardrail); project DBs are self-contained + dropped at teardown, like the ephemeral-schema gates.
- 2.3's OUTPUT that 2.4 (wamn-as5) consumes = "a provisioned, credentialed, wamn_app-roled, EMPTY project database." 2.4 installs the system schema into it; 2.5 migrates it.

=== IMPLEMENTATION STEPS ===
1. CNPG operator installed in the kind 'wamn' cluster (Helm chart `cloudnative-pg` or the pinned release manifest) — additive to the runtime-operator chart. Pin a CNPG version. deploy/cnpg-operator.* + deploy/cnpg-cluster.yaml (ONE Cluster, e.g. `wamn-pg` in wamn-system, modest resources, NO cpu limit per the S2 CFS lesson on the DB path). CNPG generates a superuser secret for the Cluster — the provision tool reads it (WAMN_PG_ADMIN_URL-style, the existing superuser-url pattern).
2. PURE provisioning SQL builders (the wamn-ddl / SR3-house-rule-3 pattern — pure text + $n/validated identifiers; NO DB driver in the pure layer). New crate crates/wamn-provision (or a module in wamn-host lib — decide at start; lean: a small pure module reused by the subcommand, or a crate if it grows). Builders: CREATE DATABASE db_<project>; role bootstrap; REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE db_<project> FROM PUBLIC; GRANT CONNECT ... TO wamn_app; plus the wamn_app role ensure (NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOBYPASSRLS LOGIN). Project-id identifier VALIDATION is load-bearing: reuse the valid_ident / wi4-slug precedent AND the wamn-66x reserved wamn_ prefix rule (a project id maps to db/schema/role names — reject wamn_-prefixed + non-slug ids). CompileError-style enum, not Error(String) (SR6 house rule 2).
3. `wamn-host provision-project` subcommand (prod bin, SR1): args --project <id> [--admin-database-url/WAMN_PG_ADMIN_URL superuser to the CNPG cluster] + policy knobs. It: connects as CNPG superuser, runs the pure builders (CREATE DATABASE + role + grants — each its own autocommit stmt where required, e.g. CREATE DATABASE can't be in a txn, the 2.2 multiproject precedent), then EMITS the per-project connection info in the wamn-db-<project> Secret shape.
   SECRET WRITE MECHANISM (resolve at start, lean: K8s-client-FREE): render the Secret YAML / the DB URL and let the provisioning Job `kubectl apply` it — do NOT pull a Rust K8s write-client in (consistent with deferring 5x0.1's read-client). Alternatively the tool prints the projects-file entry the gate/deployment consumes. Secret layout = keys the future K8sSecretProvider reads: at least `url` = postgres://wamn_app:<pw>@<cnpg-rw-svc>:5432/db_<project> (+ optional row_limit etc.). This layout IS the co-designed artifact 5x0.1 depends on — document it.
4. ROLE MODEL (the ONE real implementation detail to nail at start — flag, was a discussion point): PG roles are CLUSTER-GLOBAL, so in one shared cluster there is ONE `wamn_app` role (matches the baked-in DDL grantee — the 3.2 floor + every hand-written schema emit `GRANT ... TO wamn_app`; CONFIRM by grep before deviating). Cross-project isolation = per-project DATABASE + per-DB CONNECT grant (REVOKE FROM PUBLIC) + RLS within (the existing 2.2 model — the multiproject gate already proved DB-level routing/isolation with a shared wamn_app + per-project DBs). Per-project DISTINCT role/password (stronger credential isolation) = a HARDENING follow-up under 8.2, NOT this MVP. Note this explicitly in docs + commit.
5. GATE OF RECORD (in-cluster; new gate subcommand in wamn-gates per SR1, e.g. `provisionbench`, shared measurement via gate-harness): provisions TWO projects (proj-a/proj-b) via the REAL provision-project path against the CNPG cluster, seeds a distinct marker table in each (routing witness, the 2.2 111/222 pattern), asserts: (a) each project's credential resolves via CredentialProvider to the RIGHT DB (marker witness); (b) DB-LEVEL ISOLATION — proj-a's connection cannot reach proj-b's database/tables; (c) wamn_app is NOSUPERUSER/NOCREATEDB (cannot create schemas/DBs); (d) the emitted Secret has the expected layout. deploy/provisionbench-job.yaml (co-located, NO cpu limit). Teardown drops the project DBs (self-contained; never touches the shared pod or, ideally, leaves the CNPG Cluster like the shared postgres pod).
   LOCAL ITERATION is reduced vs the pure-crate beads: the SQL BUILDERS are unit-tested + an OPTIONAL plain-PG live-apply (throwaway postgres:18 container, the wamn-ddl WAMN_*_PG_URL pattern) exercises CREATE DATABASE/role/grant/isolation SQL; the CNPG ORCHESTRATION (operator + Cluster CR + Secret) is proven IN-CLUSTER only (CNPG is a K8s operator). Accept that.
6. MUTATION-TEST the load-bearing asserts (structured-testing rule; apply/test/restore, byte-verified, DEBUG builds): e.g. drop the REVOKE CONNECT / the per-DB GRANT -> the isolation gate (or the plain-PG live-apply isolation assert) FAILS; neuter the project-id validation -> the reserved-prefix/slug unit test FAILS. One mutant per layer (pure builder / gate assert).

=== TESTING / HOUSE RULES ===
- Structured testing NOT review fleets (workflow-rule-structured-testing-not-review-workflows): unit tests on the pure builders + identifier validation, a Secret-layout drift-guard, the in-cluster provisionbench gate, plain-PG live-apply where it exercises real SQL, mutation on load-bearing asserts. Max 3 agents, opus default if any (but likely none needed).
- DEBUG builds only (wamn-feedback-debug-builds-only). The in-cluster gate needs ONE host docker rebuild (new provision-project subcommand + new gate = HOST change): docker build --target host + --target gates + kind load BOTH images (the SR1 two-stage build).
- SR1: prod subcommand in wamn-host; gate in wamn-gates; shared measurement in gate-harness. SR3 rule 3: SQL = pure builders + validated/allowlisted idents. SR6 rule 2: errors are enum variants, never Error(String).
- CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md mirrored BYTE-IDENTICAL: add the [2.3] provisioning gate command block.
- Docs: NEW docs/provisioning.md (CNPG topology, provision-project surface, Secret layout = the 5x0.1 contract, role model + the per-project-password hardening note, isolation gate, deferred items). Update platform-plan.md 2.3 status if warranted (do NOT over-edit).

=== PROCESS ===
- NO fan-out understand phase (surface is small + already read this turn). At implementation START do ONE focused read of the CNPG CRD surface: Cluster bootstrap, whether to create per-project databases via the `Database` CR (CNPG >=1.24) or via bootstrap SQL run by the provision tool as superuser (LEAN: provision tool runs SQL as superuser — matches the imperative-CLI choice + is operator-version-agnostic), and where the Cluster's superuser secret lands. Pin the CNPG version there.
- Confirm the wamn_app-grantee assumption (step 4) with a grep of the emitted floor DDL before building the role model.

=== EXPLICIT NON-GOALS (file follow-up beads on close where noted) ===
- WAL archive / MinIO / PITR config -> NEW fast-follow bead [2.3]. Restore drill stays 10.3 (wamn-tao).
- Live K8sSecretProvider read -> wamn-5x0.1 (P2, exists). 2.3 only EMITS the Secret in the layout it reads.
- Dispatch role (wamn-286) + user-SQL role (wamn-1nd) -> their beads. 2.3 leaves the provision path STRUCTURED so CREATE ROLE hooks slot in (note the seam), does not implement them.
- Migrate the legacy deploy/postgres.yaml fixtures onto CNPG -> NEW later bead (or note if one exists). MVP coexists.
- Per-project distinct role/password hardening -> 8.2 (note it).
- Control-plane automation of provisioning -> 10.1 (P3).
- Dispatcher --projects-file real-entry wiring -> light note / follow-up (MVP proves provisioning + gate; a full dispatcher-consumes-provisioned-entries demo is not required).

=== CLOSE PROTOCOL ===
Run the gates (unit + plain-PG live-apply + in-cluster provisionbench of record), mutation-kill the load-bearing asserts. bd remember a facts memory (wamn-2.3-provisioning-facts) + link [[wamn-2.2-postgres-production-facts]] [[wamn-d6-postgres-hosting-decision-facts]] [[wamn-host-build-facts-s1-for-s2-wash]] [[wamn-sr1-gates-split-facts]]. File the follow-up beads (WAL-archive fast-follow; legacy-fixture-migration if none exists). bd close wamn-jxm --suggest-next (it unblocks wamn-as5 [2.4]). git add + commit (feat(2.3): ...) + git push + bd dolt push. REPORT: 2.3 done, what it unblocks (2.4 -> 2.5/POC-DM1), the filed follow-ups; STOP (2.4 needs its own approval — do NOT claim it).


=== ORIGINAL D6 HANDOFF (preserved from prior notes) ===
D6 DECIDED (wamn-dxi closed 2026-07-12): CNPG (CloudNativePG) in-cluster, chosen-revisitable — see docs/platform-plan.md D6 row for rationale + revisit trigger. Handoff for 2.3: (1) provision one database per project through CNPG CRDs (Cluster + database/role bootstrap); the local kind cluster can run the SAME operator, so the gate of record stays dev/prod-identical (replace the single deploy/postgres.yaml pod only when 2.3 lands its own fixture path — the shared-cluster guardrail applies to the existing pod). (2) Credentials land as K8s Secrets -> pairs with wamn-5x0.1 [2.2b] K8sSecretProvider (currently a defined stub in wamn_postgres.rs that bails; 2.3 + 2.2b were co-designed). (3) Backups/PITR = WAL archiving to object storage (barman plugin); restore DRILL belongs to 10.3, but 2.3 must provision the archive config. (4) Keep the provisioning surface narrow (per-project DB URL + CredentialProvider) so a managed-Postgres (RDS/Cloud SQL) re-target stays cheap — that is the recorded revisit path. (5) The dispatcher --projects-file (deploy/dispatcher-projects.example.yaml) gets real per-project entries from 2.3 provisioning (noted in docs/run-queue.md); the wamn-286 dispatch-role and wamn-1nd user-SQL-role beads want CREATE ROLE hooks in the same provisioning path.

title: [D5] Decide Postgres pooling topology
description: Host-side pools x N host pods x M project DBs explodes connection counts: decide pgBouncer transaction pooling vs strict per-host caps using S2 saturation data. LISTEN/NOTIFY fully removed (D4) so transaction pooling has no listener conflict; interacts with SET LOCAL claim injection. Design: docs/platform-plan.md D5, 2.2
design: DECIDED (P0-EXIT, 2026-07-10): Hybrid. v0/P1 uses strict per-host deadpool caps — exactly what S2 shipped (deadpool per-host pool: 20427 qps, p99 1.98 ms, graceful connection-unavailable under saturation). pgBouncer TRANSACTION-mode pooling is added later, when M×N connection pressure (N host pods × M project DBs) appears against server max_connections. Transaction-mode is safe because D4 removed LISTEN/NOTIFY (no session-scoped listener) and claims inject via SET LOCAL, which resets at COMMIT (session-mode pooling would leak the GUCs). Scale trigger: server-connection pressure. Constraint from the S2 CFS lesson: the DB-serving path must not be CPU-quota-capped. Recorded in docs/platform-plan.md D5 row and docs/p0-results.md cross-cutting exit section. Unblocks [2.2] wamn:postgres host plugin (production).

title: feat(provision): revoke the parked effect_attempts INSERT so parked is true on the server
description:
## Why

OWNER RULING 2026-08-26 on wamn-0h0g.20.28, option (d). This bead is that ruling and nothing else.

The measurement on .20.28 proved parked is currently FALSE ON THE SERVER. deploy/sql/run-state.sql:589-590 grants SELECT, INSERT on wamn_run.effect_attempts to wamn_effect_writer, and crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs grants wamn_effect_writer to a LOGIN generation role with INHERIT TRUE on the ordinary provisioning path. So every provisioned project environment mints a login holding live INSERT on a relation the DDL prose calls parked. That is dormant authority by construction, mass-produced by the provisioner - the p3ze class.

The owner ruled the remaining alternative (c), prose-only, unacceptable precisely because striking the acceptance clause would leave the live grant standing: prose declaring parked over a grantable write path is the exact lie the guard was owed to catch.

## What

Narrow the grant so a fresh environment is BORN PARKED.

1. deploy/sql/run-state.sql: drop INSERT from the effect_attempts grant to wamn_effect_writer. SELECT stays. The REVOKE ALL line above it already names the role, so the narrowing is one clause.
2. crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs, the workload-generation surface for WorkloadRoleFamily::EffectWriter: the same narrowing, so the provisioner is the author of record. THE RIDER IS BINDING - the revoke lands in the provisioner, NOT as a cluster-side patch. Fresh envs are born parked and the tree stays the author of record.
3. crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs carries the generated-SQL drift pins for this grant (EFFECT_WRITER_ROLE arms near the effect_attempts ACL inventory). They move with the change or the build refuses.

## The probe arm - this is the discriminator the acceptance wanted

R12 requires this land with its probe. The probe IS the parked/live discriminator .20.28 asked for:

  parked = DENIAL ASSERTED. Connect as a role holding wamn_effect_writer and assert INSERT on wamn_run.effect_attempts is refused by the server.

Assert the SERVER answer, not the DDL text: has_table_privilege / aclexplode, or carry the real SQLSTATE back into the Rust boundary. Do not pin the static DDL string as the proof - that is the form this repo rates near-tautological. The generated-SQL pins in run_plane.rs are a separate and legitimate arm, because that string is produced by a Rust builder.

Live gates are hermetic: DROP OWNED BY then DROP ROLE, one fresh cluster for the role/grant mutant.

## The re-grant trigger has NO LIVE OWNER - measured, and it is the one clause of the ruling that needs the owner

The ruling said revoke until wamn-0h0g.5.4 wires the durable tier, and that .5.4 re-grant flips the arm. MEASURED: wamn-0h0g.5.4 IS CLOSED, 2026-08-18, and it closed by SHELVING this half - its close reason reads that the effect ledger half shelves as the premium durable tier and needs no unlanded first caller. So .5.4 will never wire it, and the run-state.sql:502-503 comment naming .5.4 as the bead that first wires and activates it is STALE for the same reason.

Epic wamn-0h0g.20 has no other open child that activates the tier: only .20.3, which PARKS the shelf behind the class gate, and .20.28 itself.

So the revoke half is fully specified and can proceed. The RESTORE half names no owner, and repository law forbids committing a sentence that names no owner. Two things are therefore owed from the owner and are NOT assumed here:
  - which bead inherits the activate-the-durable-tier role that .5.4 vacated, so the DDL comment and the probe can name it;
  - whether the stale .5.4 sentence at run-state.sql:502-503 is rewritten in THIS commit or left to the activator.

## Scheduling

FOLDS INTO PHASE B ITEM 2 (owner ruling 2026-08-26). It is grant-posture work on the writer family, which is the construction territory, so it does not open a second door. It must not land as a standalone grant change ahead of the construction; the dependency on wamn-0h0g.22.8 encodes that.
acceptance_criteria: INSERT on wamn_run.effect_attempts is refused by the server to a role holding wamn_effect_writer, proven by a live probe reading the server answer rather than the DDL text. A freshly provisioned environment is born parked, because the narrowing lives in the provisioner and not in a cluster-side patch. The generated-SQL drift pins in run_plane.rs move with the change. SELECT is unaffected. The re-grant trigger is either named with a live bead id or explicitly deferred by the owner; no sentence lands naming wamn-0h0g.5.4 as a future activator. Lands inside the Phase B item 2 construction, not as a standalone grant change.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-26 - THE OPEN CLAUSE IS CLOSED. Both questions this bead carried back are answered.

1. THE RE-GRANT TRIGGER NOW NAMES A LIVE ID: wamn-0h0g.20.31, deferred, event-triggered on the first paying durable-tier client. No closed-out bead resurrects and no phantom gets named - the durable tier's activation is a PRODUCT decision, so it gets a product-shaped owner. .20.31 inherits .5.4's shelved scope and its scope item 2 is to INVERT this bead's probe arm, not delete it. The arm is the contract between the two beads: parked = denial asserted here; .20.31 flips it.

2. REWRITING THE STALE .5.4 SENTENCE IS IN SCOPE FOR THIS COMMIT, not left to the activator. deploy/sql/run-state.sql:502-503 currently reads that wamn-0h0g.4.9 installs the inaccessible writer primitive and wamn-0h0g.5.4 first wires and activates it, until then execution remains hard-refused. .5.4 closed BY REFUSING THAT ROLE. Leaving a DDL comment pointing at it is the FALSE-COVERAGE CLASS AT DDL GRAIN - the same shape as the :569 finding, and this repo has already recorded that a false citation can live in a DDL comment AS AN INSTRUCTION. The same commit that parks the grant fixes the prose that lied about who unparks it: the sentence repoints to .20.31.

So this bead now lands complete in one commit: narrow the grant in the provisioner and in run-state.sql, move the run_plane.rs generated-SQL pins, add the server-side denial probe, and repoint the stale comment to .20.31.

SCHEDULING UNCHANGED: rides inside the Phase B item 2 construction (dep on wamn-0h0g.22.8), not as a standalone grant change.

title: test(conformance): narrow the epoch-cadence scan to a strict identity pin
description:
## Why

Owner spec, 2026-08-26, following wamn-hopk. The epoch-cadence tripwire in
tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs is the other source scan wamn-hopk left standing. It
STAYS TEXT, deliberately, and this bead narrows it to a strict identity pin so it sits squarely
inside R5's one exemption rather than near it.

WHY IT STAYS TEXT. Upstream's EPOCH_TICK is pub(crate) in wash-runtime's src/engine/mod.rs. There is
no linkable surface, so the compiler cannot carry this. And a behavioural timing test is FLAKE
THEATER for what is a constant-equality question - it would measure a scheduler, not a constant.

WHAT IT GUARDS. crates/execution/host/src/router_driver.rs carries MANUAL_STORE_EPOCH_TICK, a hand
mirror of that upstream constant. An unmirrored upstream retune rescales EVERY node deadline
silently.

## The change

Today the tripwire matches two whole SOURCE LINES, so it breaks on upstream reformatting and asserts
a spelling rather than a value. Narrow it to a strict IDENTITY PIN: extract the literal VALUE at the
pinned fork location and assert it equals our MANUAL_STORE_EPOCH_TICK's value. Value equality, not
line equality.

## Required doc line

The test carries a doc comment naming R5's identity-pin exemption and the RE-CONVERGE TRIGGER:
when upstream exposes the constant publicly, link it and DELETE the scan.

## Fork-sync checklist

Add the check to docs/architecture/native-alignment-ledger.md so the next tagged-release sync
verifies it rather than discovering it.
acceptance_criteria: The tripwire asserts VALUE equality between the pinned fork's EPOCH_TICK literal and MANUAL_STORE_EPOCH_TICK, not whole-line text, and survives upstream reformatting while still failing on a retune. Its doc names R5's identity-pin exemption and the re-converge trigger. The fork-sync checklist in the native-alignment ledger carries the check.

Landed at 64ca0aa8. The epoch tripwire now compares VALUES, not source lines.

It stays text on purpose, and the doc says why: upstream's EPOCH_TICK is pub(crate), so there is no
linkable surface for the compiler to carry, and timing a ticker to infer its period would measure the
scheduler rather than the constant. This is wamn-hopk R5's identity-pin exemption, and narrowing it to
value equality is what earns it rather than merely claiming it.

WHAT CHANGED. Before, two whole source lines were matched verbatim - so upstream reformatting or a
visibility change read as a MISSING CONSTANT, and a reformat was indistinguishable from a retune.
Now epoch_millis extracts the millisecond value each side declares and asserts equality. Exactly one
declaration must match, so a second cannot shadow a drifted first, and the failure message names the
rescale factor.

PROVEN, not asserted in prose: the_epoch_pin_survives_upstream_reformatting_but_not_a_retune covers
pub(crate) as spelled today, pub (which is the re-converge trigger, not a failure), a rustfmt line
split, and an underscore-separated literal - and separately that a real retune to 25 is read exactly.

title: decide(run-state): feature-gate the durable-tier shelf, or keep the class as data
description:
## Why

Split out of wamn-hopk under rule 7 on 2026-08-26. That spec's R1 asked that shelved durable-tier API
in wamn-run-state move behind a durable-tier cargo feature, default off, so a reference from a live
path becomes a compile error. R2, R3, R4 and the R5 law landed WITHOUT it, because none of them
depended on it. R1 alone is held, for two measured reasons.

## FINDING 1 - THE WALL ALREADY EXISTS AND IS STRONGER THAN A FEATURE

crates/execution/router/Cargo.toml [dependencies] is exactly serde_json, wamn-event-wire,
opentelemetry. THE ROUTER DOES NOT LINK wamn-run-state AT ALL, so a reference from paths 1-2 to any
run-state item is ALREADY E0433, with or without a feature. A default-off feature would not change
what the router can name. There is also no Postgres client there, so the SQL-shaped vocabulary the
retired scan searched for is inert in router source even as a bare string.

## FINDING 2 - A RATIFIED GUARD FORBIDS EXACTLY WHAT R1 PROPOSES

crates/execution/run-state/tests/shelving_contract.rs, the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag, asserts that
no durability-mentioning line in durability.rs, queue/claim.rs or queue/sql.rs may contain
cfg(feature. Its ground, from wamn-0h0g.20: both tiers ship in ONE image, so a Cargo feature CANNOT
express the class - a feature cannot let two tiers coexist in one binary. Turning the premium tier on
must be a per-run DATA change.

Building R1 therefore requires deleting that guard and retiring wamn-0h0g.20's class-is-data contract.

## THE OPTIONS

(a) DROP R1. The crate boundary enforces rule A for the router more strongly than a feature would, and
    the class-is-data contract stands untouched. Nothing else in wamn-hopk is affected.
(b) BUILD R1 and delete the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag, naming what replaces the class-is-data
    contract.
(c) NARROWER - gate only modules the class does not run through, keep the guard for the class itself.

## TRAP IF EVER BUILT

crates/execution/run-state/src/effect_writer.rs IS NOT SHELVED:
reset_expired_pre_effect_projection has a LIVE production caller on BOTH tiers. Feature-gating it
breaks the default-tier reset path. Any durable-tier feature must exclude it explicitly.

## Coupled cleanup

the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag is itself an R5 source scan and was DELIBERATELY LEFT IN PLACE by
wamn-hopk, flagged in its own comment, because deleting it would pre-decide this question. Whichever
way this rules, that guard's disposition rides this bead.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling picks (a), (b) or (c) with the class-is-data contract explicitly addressed. If a feature is built, effect_writer.rs is excluded and the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag's replacement is named. If R1 is dropped, that guard's R5 disposition is settled in the same ruling.
close_reason: Folded back into wamn-hopk by owner direction 2026-08-26: the spec is completed as a SINGLE issue, not split. R1 is implemented there.

title: chore(tests): retire source-text scanning - reachability by compilation, artifacts by live probes
description:
## Why

Owner spec, 2026-08-26. Two tests read our own source files AS TEXT, strip comments, and grep the
remainder for names. Same disease the mutation-gate deletion diagnosed: a rule enforced by hand-rolled
text processing over our own files, growing parsers to fix its own false positives.

SUPERSEDES the wamn-q3kq comment-stripper ruling and MOOTS wamn-b96x.

## R5 - STANDING LAW: NO TEST READS SOURCE FILES AS TEXT

- Reachability rules -> the compiler: features, visibility, workspace boundaries.
- Artifact contracts (SQL grants, WIT worlds, wire literals) -> live probes and gates, or the
  artifact's own loader. Never regex over text.
- SOLE EXEMPTION: identity pins - a hash or byte-equality check on a named artifact. SEMANTIC scans,
  searching text for meaning, are forbidden.
- New guards violating this refuse at review with this spec cited.

## R2 - delete the shelving scan (crates/execution/run-state/tests/shelving_contract.rs)

Delete the include_str! source array, the Rust comment-stripper, and every grep arm.
KEEP the_router_cannot_reach_the_run_plane_at_all: it reads the router's Cargo.toml, not source, and
it is the manifest check R2 itself sanctions as the survivor. It is already stronger than the
proposed one-line feature check.

## R3 - delete the SQL statement scan (crates/control/provision/tests/control_portable_store.rs)

Delete without_comments and the GRANT-line parser. Enforcement is the startup probe
AUTHORING_ROLE_PROBE_SQL (services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs, queried at :273), which refuses
at startup if the control author holds write privilege outside the two-row allowlist - fail-closed
against the real database. The test-time text scan is a weaker pre-echo of it.

## R1 IS RAISED AS A QUESTION, NOT IMPLEMENTED - see the note on this bead

Measured: it is both unnecessary and contradicted by a ratified guard. Do not build the durable-tier
feature until that is ruled.

## R4 - tracker dispositions

wamn-q3kq closes superseded; wamn-b96x closes mooted.
acceptance_criteria: The shelving source scan and the SQL statement scan are deleted with their strippers. The router manifest check survives. cargo test is green for the affected packages. R1 is not built until its contradiction is ruled. wamn-b96x is closed mooted and wamn-q3kq carries the supersession.
notes:
*** R1 IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. IT IS BOTH UNNECESSARY AND CONTRADICTED BY A RATIFIED GUARD. Measured by
the integrator at bd4450d7, re-derived from the code, not taken from any lane. ***

R1 asks that shelved durable-tier API in run-state move behind a durable-tier cargo feature, default
off, so that a reference from a live path becomes a compile error.

FINDING 1 - THE WALL ALREADY EXISTS, AND IS STRONGER THAN A FEATURE.
crates/execution/router/Cargo.toml [dependencies] is exactly: serde_json, wamn-event-wire,
opentelemetry. THE ROUTER DOES NOT LINK wamn-run-state AT ALL. A reference from the router to any
run-state item is ALREADY E0433 (unresolved crate), with or without a feature. A default-off feature
on run-state would change nothing about what the router can name. There is also no Postgres client in
that dependency set, so the SQL-shaped vocabulary the old scan searched for (effect_attempts,
run_queue, lease_expires_at, 'durable') is inert in router source even as a bare string.

FINDING 2 - A RATIFIED GUARD FORBIDS EXACTLY WHAT R1 PROPOSES.
crates/execution/run-state/tests/shelving_contract.rs, the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag, asserts that
no line mentioning durability in durability.rs, queue/claim.rs or queue/sql.rs may contain
cfg(feature. Its stated ground, from wamn-0h0g.20: both tiers ship in ONE image, so a Cargo feature
CANNOT express the class - a feature cannot let two tiers coexist in one binary. Turning the premium
tier on must be a per-run DATA change, and nothing about the class may be conditionally compiled.

So building R1 would require deleting that guard, which would silently retire wamn-0h0g.20's
class-is-data contract. That is a decision, not a mechanical step, and it is not mine to take.

FINDING 3 - A KNOWN TRAP IF R1 IS EVER BUILT ANYWAY.
crates/execution/run-state/src/effect_writer.rs IS NOT SHELVED:
reset_expired_pre_effect_projection has a LIVE production caller on BOTH tiers. Feature-gating it
breaks the default-tier reset path. Any durable-tier feature must exclude it explicitly.

THE QUESTION FOR THE OWNER:
  (a) Drop R1. The crate boundary already enforces rule A for the router, more strongly than a
      feature would, and the class-is-data contract stands untouched. R2/R3/R5 are unaffected -
      they never depended on R1.
  (b) Build R1 anyway and delete the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag, accepting that the class is no
      longer asserted to be data rather than a build flag. Name what replaces that contract.
  (c) Something narrower - e.g. gate only the modules the class does not run through, with
      effect_writer.rs explicitly excluded, and keep the guard for the class itself.

*** PENDING THIS RULING, the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag IS DELIBERATELY LEFT IN PLACE even though
it is itself an R5 source scan. Deleting it would pre-decide R1 in favour of (b). It is the one
knowing R5 holdout in this change and is recorded here so it is not mistaken for an oversight. ***
close_reason:
DONE as a SINGLE issue at bd4450d7..bdcbcb9f. R1, R2, R3, R4 and R5 all landed here; nothing was
split off. wamn-0h0g.20.29, filed briefly as an R1 split, was closed and folded back.

R5 RESULT: include_str! of a .rs file is now ZERO REPO-WIDE - stronger than the acceptance, which
asked only for tests/. Removed roughly 20 scanning tests across 21 files and, more importantly, three
pieces of SHARED SCANNING INFRASTRUCTURE: services/scenario-worker/src/source_scan.rs (a pub(crate)
module serving nine tests), TWO independent copies of production_half(), and four orphaned
CFG_TEST_MODULE constants plus two implementation-half helpers. Net -2098 lines against +104.

R1 - BUILT, with MEASURED membership rather than assumed. durable-tier feature, default off. Only a
module with zero internal AND zero external references qualifies, so `attempt` is gated and two others
are provably NOT gateable: `durability` threads through live queue/claim.rs and queue/sql.rs, and
effect_writer_credential feeds effect_writer.rs, which is live on BOTH tiers via
reset_expired_pre_effect_projection. Both exclusions are recorded in the feature's own comment.
Verified in both feature states.
THE CONTRADICTION I RAISED DISSOLVED RATHER THAN NEEDING A RULING: the_gate_is_data_not_a_build_flag
forbade exactly this feature, but it was ITSELF an R5 source scan, so R5 deleted it on its own terms.
*** wamn-0h0g.20's class-is-data contract is therefore NO LONGER ASSERTED ANYWHERE. That is a real
consequence of this spec, recorded here rather than left implicit. ***

R2 - the shelving scan, its stripper and every grep arm are gone. The manifest check survives and is
the stronger wall: the router links neither wamn-run-state, wamn-runtime nor any Postgres client, so
the crash-floor vocabulary is unnameable from paths 1-2 and a reference is E0433.

R3 - without_comments, the GRANT-statement parser and the five-file posture scan are gone.
AUTHORING_ROLE_PROBE_SQL (services/scenario-worker/src/authoring.rs:273) enforces the allowlist live,
refusing at startup against the real database.

R4 - wamn-b96x CLOSED MOOTED; wamn-q3kq carries its supersession note. wamn-q3kq's landed fix, the
comment stripper, was deleted along with the guard it narrowed.

TWO SCANNERS DELIBERATELY REMAIN, and they are NOT our source:
tests/conformance/src/wasi_ctx_environment.rs and tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs read the
PINNED WASH-RUNTIME CHECKOUT via fs::read_to_string. R5's rationale does not reach them - we cannot
compile against upstream internals that are pub(crate) there, so there is no native alternative, which

the only guard against a silent upstream epoch retune rescaling every node deadline, and the only
check that the runtime never inherits the host process environment into a guest.

MISTAKES MADE AND FIXED, recorded because they are the method's real cost: removing items by line left
THREE dangling #[cfg(test)] attributes, each of which latched onto the next item and silently
configured out a real re-export (DurabilityClass, PlatformAsyncMessage) or broke a lib. Every grep read
clean throughout; only compiling the workspace found them.
