SET is {connection_http_maps_an_invalid_context_to_a_wit_error_not_a_trap, version_identity} - both
pre-existing standing reds, nothing new. LOCAL CARGO ONLY; the in-cluster gate of record has not run.

title: decide(run-state): what does parked forbid for wamn_run.effect_attempts
description:
## Why

Split out of wamn-0h0g.12.1 under rule 7 on 2026-08-26 as an ACCEPTANCE-BOUNDARY QUESTION the lane
correctly refused to answer. That bead's acceptance required the project record to pin
wamn_run.effect_attempts "as parked premium-durable-tier surface, not as live capability."

Its SHAPE is pinned today - relation, columns, constraints, RLS, immutability triggers and grants all
sit in the project record. What is NOT pinned, and what nobody has defined, is what PARKED FORBIDS.

## The contradiction, measured at cec008d6 and re-verified by the integrator

"Parked" is carried only by PROSE, in deploy/sql/run-state.sql:502-503:
  wamn-0h0g.4.9 installs the inaccessible writer primitive. wamn-0h0g.5.4
  first wires and activates it; until then execution remains hard-refused.

But the obvious reading of parked - NO WRITER MAY REACH IT - is FALSE IN THE TREE TODAY.
deploy/sql/run-state.sql:589-590 reads:

  REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLE wamn_run.effect_attempts
      FROM PUBLIC, wamn_app, wamn_scenario_author, wamn_effect_writer;
  GRANT SELECT ON wamn_run.effect_attempts TO wamn_app;
  GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON wamn_run.effect_attempts TO wamn_effect_writer;

So wamn_effect_writer holds INSERT right now. A guard asserting "parked means no writer" would fail
against the tree as it stands, and a guard asserting the current grants would merely restate them.

## THE QUESTION

What does "parked premium-durable-tier surface, not live capability" FORBID on the server, such that
an assertion can distinguish parked from live?

Candidate readings, each with its consequence:
  (a) Parked is a GRANT posture - the writer role exists and holds INSERT, but nothing GRANTS that
      role to any login. Assert the role-membership edge is absent. Cheap, and true today if no login
      holds wamn_effect_writer - VERIFY THAT BEFORE CHOOSING.
  (b) Parked is a CALLER posture - no production code path reaches the insert. That is a source-scan
      claim, which this repo rates the weakest form and has resolved not to add more of.
  (c) Parked is PROSE ONLY and no assertion is owed. Say so explicitly and strike the acceptance
      clause, so the next reader does not re-open it.
  (d) Parked should become a real posture - revoke the INSERT until wamn-0h0g.5.4 wires it. That is a
      PRODUCTION CHANGE, not a test, and it must not ride a drift-check bead.

## Not urgent

Nothing is broken. This is a definition owed to a guard that does not exist yet. Rule 10 applies: if
the RC does not require it, say so rather than scheduling it.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling states what parked forbids on the server, in terms an assertion can check, or states that no assertion is owed and strikes the clause. If a grant posture is chosen, whether any login currently holds wamn_effect_writer is measured first. Any production grant change is filed separately from the drift-check work.
notes:
MEASUREMENT OWED BY THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, taken 2026-08-26 at 0f752b30 by the integrator.

The criterion said: if a grant posture is chosen, whether any login currently holds wamn_effect_writer is measured first. It is measured, and OPTION (a) IS REFUTED.

A LOGIN DOES HOLD THE ROLE, on the ordinary production provisioning path:

  services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs mints an effect-writer credential
    -> crates/execution/run-state/src/effect_writer_credential.rs
    -> crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs, workload-generation role builder

That builder emits, for WorkloadRoleFamily::EffectWriter:
  CREATE ROLE <generation> NOLOGIN ...            (created inaccessible)
  GRANT wamn_effect_writer TO <generation> WITH ADMIN FALSE, INHERIT TRUE, SET FALSE
  ALTER ROLE <generation> LOGIN PASSWORD ... VALID UNTIL ...
  GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE <db> TO <generation>

INHERIT TRUE plus LOGIN is the whole edge. So the role-membership edge option (a) proposed to assert as ABSENT is PRESENT by construction whenever a project environment is provisioned. Asserting its absence would fail against the tree; asserting its presence merely restates the builder. (a) distinguishes nothing.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OPTION SET - the owner now chooses between two, not four:
  (a) REFUTED by the above.
  (b) BARRED. It is a source-scan claim, and wamn-hopk R5 retired source-text scanning as a technique. Choosing (b) would require re-authorising the technique this branch just removed.
  (c) LIVE. Parked is prose only, no assertion is owed; strike the acceptance clause on wamn-0h0g.12.1 so the next reader does not re-open this.
  (d) LIVE. Parked becomes a real posture - revoke the INSERT until wamn-0h0g.5.4 wires it. A PRODUCTION CHANGE needing its own bead and its own probe arm (R12), not a rider on drift-check work.

NOT IMPLEMENTED. Recorded only. Rule 10 still applies: if the RC does not require this, saying so is a legitimate answer.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-26: OPTION (d) - REVOKE.

The measurement is why it stops being optional. The probe proved parked is currently FALSE ON THE SERVER: every provisioned env mints a LOGIN holding live INSERT on the parked relation - dormant authority by construction, mass-produced by the provisioner, the p3ze class.

  (a) REFUTED by the measurement recorded above.
  (b) BARRED by wamn-hopk R5.
  (c) REJECTED, and the reason is specific: striking the acceptance clause would leave the LIVE GRANT STANDING. Prose declaring parked over a grantable write path is the exact lie the guard was owed to catch.
  (d) RULED. Revoke INSERT on effect_attempts from the writer family until the durable tier is wired. Own bead, own probe arm per R12.

THE PROBE IS THE DISCRIMINATOR THE ACCEPTANCE WANTED: parked = denial asserted; the re-grant flips the arm.

RIDER, BINDING: the revoke lands IN THE PROVISIONER (the sql.rs workload-generation grant narrows), NOT as a cluster-side patch. Fresh envs are born parked and the tree stays the author of record.

SCHEDULING RIDER from the same message: this folds into Phase B item 2's build - it is grant-posture work on the writer family, which is the construction's territory - so the door stays single.

FILED AS wamn-0h0g.20.30, which depends on wamn-0h0g.22.8 to encode that it must not land as a standalone grant change ahead of the construction. NOT STARTED.

ONE CLAUSE OF THE RULING IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT AND IS BACK TO THE OWNER. The ruling names wamn-0h0g.5.4 as the re-grant trigger. .5.4 IS CLOSED, 2026-08-18, and it closed BY SHELVING THIS HALF: its close reason reads that the effect ledger half shelves as the premium durable tier and needs no unlanded first caller. It will never wire the tier. The run-state.sql:502-503 comment naming .5.4 as the bead that first wires and activates it is stale for the same reason, and epic .20 has no other open child that activates - only .20.3, which parks. The revoke half is unaffected and fully specified; the RESTORE half names no owner, and repository law forbids committing a sentence that names no owner. Carried on .20.30 as an owner question.
close_reason: RULED 2026-08-26: option (d), revoke. The acceptance is met - a ruling states what parked forbids on the server in terms an assertion can check: parked = the writer family is DENIED INSERT, asserted as a server-side denial probe, and the re-grant flips the arm. The grant-posture measurement the acceptance required was taken first and REFUTED option (a); it is recorded on this bead. The production change is filed separately as wamn-0h0g.20.30, per the acceptance clause requiring exactly that, and depends on wamn-0h0g.22.8 because the owner folded it into the Phase B item 2 construction so the door stays single. One clause of the ruling - wamn-0h0g.5.4 as the re-grant trigger - is refuted by measurement (.5.4 is closed, and closed by shelving this half); that question is carried on .20.30 and is back to the owner. NOT IMPLEMENTED.

title: feat(contract): carry run and node coordinates from guest to host for effect surfaces
description:
## Why

Split out of wamn-0h0g.24.12 under rule 7 on 2026-08-26, by owner ruling on the refuted
cheap-by-construction premise. This is the contract that unblocks the wamn.postgres effect-span
enrichment; it is filed WITH its consumer named so it is not machinery ahead of demand.

## The measured gap

crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/resources.rs, db_span doc comment around :221,
states in the tree today: run_id/node_id enrichment awaits a guest-to-host run-context contract; the
trusted HTTP effect is the one surface whose WIT carries those coordinates today.

That is the whole blocker. A host plugin serving a guest call has the executing component's
tenant and project (claim maps the guest cannot spoof), but nothing carries the run and node
coordinates of the invocation the guest is executing inside. Only the trusted HTTP effect's WIT
carries them, and only because that WIT was shaped for it.

## Named consumer

wamn-0h0g.24.14 (the wamn.postgres effect-span enrichment) is blocked on this and depends on it.
Do not widen the contract beyond what that consumer needs.

## Scope note

This is an invocation-contract change, which is why it sits under epic F rather than epic W. The
identity vocabulary is already fixed by the router driver's wamn.component.invoke span
(wamn.wiring_id, wamn.wiring_version, wamn.node_id, wamn.component_digest) - reuse it rather than
minting a second spelling.
acceptance_criteria: A host plugin serving a guest call can read the run and node coordinates of the invocation the guest is executing inside, without a trace-parent walk and without the guest being able to spoof them. The vocabulary matches the router driver's existing wamn.component.invoke fields rather than a second spelling. Only the fields wamn-0h0g.24.14 needs are added.

title: decide(security): define ConnectionHttp address-range policy
description: Phase-B WAMN-owned follow-up split from the wasmCloud v2.8 sync. Vanilla SocketPolicy governs wasi:sockets only; the wamn:connection/http plugin resolves and connects through its own reqwest/Tokio path, so its address-range confinement is a separate product boundary. Keep wamn-d0w4 scoped to the raw-socket question and make no upstream filing or contact.
acceptance_criteria: The plugin's policy doc records the binding-scoped confinement model and states in terms that cannot be read as an oversight that RFC1918 and the cluster service network are allowed-because-bound. The SSRF floor - link-local, cloud metadata, and refusal of redirects into denied ranges - is enforced at the reqwest seam after DNS resolution and before connect, without weakening target or authority attestation. Behavioral tests cover allowed and denied destinations including rebinding and multi-address handling, and a redirect into a denied range. Lands before ConnectionHttp egress is broadened.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-26: OPTION (c) - A DIFFERENT POSTURE FROM wamn-d0w4, AND IT IS RECORDED AS
POSTURE, NOT AS AN EXCEPTION.

THE MODEL. wamn:connection/http is the INTENDED, AUTHORITY-MEDIATED egress path. Its confinement is
BINDING-SCOPED, not address-class: admin-bound connections name their targets, and requirement
satisfaction IS the grant. Address-range denial is the wrong instrument for a surface whose whole
design is that an administrator has already named where it may go.

WHY NOT d0w4's DENY-LIST. A blanket RFC1918 and cluster-service-network deny breaks the product's
own shape - in-cluster and private-network endpoints (the ERP case) are THE CUSTOMER, not the threat.
Importing the sockets posture here would deny the surface's primary legitimate use.

THE FLOOR IT DOES ADOPT - the SSRF floor no legitimate binding needs:
  1. link-local
  2. cloud metadata addresses
  3. refuse redirect-to-denied-ranges (a bound target must not be a hop into a denied one)
Enforced AT THE REQWEST SEAM, after DNS resolution and before connect, without weakening target or
authority attestation.

WRITTEN INTO THE PLUGIN'S POLICY DOC, explicitly and as a sentence a later reader cannot mistake for
an oversight: RFC1918 and the cluster service network are ALLOWED-BECAUSE-BOUND. The absence of an
address-class deny for those ranges is a decision, not a gap.

SCOPE FENCE. wamn-d0w4 stays SOCKETS-ONLY as recorded - its ruled tightening (default-deny
link-local, cloud metadata, cluster service network and RFC1918 under EgressMode::Enforce) governs
vanilla SocketPolicy and wasi:sockets, and does NOT reach this plugin, which connects through its own
reqwest/Tokio path. Neither bead's posture is precedent for the other.

IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED. Not in wave 73.

title: feat(architecture): carry reader-only principals in the state-owners manifest
description:
## Why

OWNER RULING 2026-08-26: reader-only principals ARE carried. Today architecture/state-owners.json names a principal only when a file WRITES state; files that only READ are omitted by existing practice and never by any ruling. That is silent under-description - the manifest is the named-authority vocabulary, so a reader with no principal is authority the manifest cannot express, the same class as a comment asserting coverage that nothing checks, at manifest grain.

## Scope

One pass over the manifest adding reader-only principals, so every file that reads a governed relation has a name in the vocabulary and appears in that relation's readers list.

THE SCANNER STAYS WRITE-ONLY. tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs discover_writes recognizes INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE and is not to be widened here - adding reader principals is a manifest edit, so nothing reds. Confirm that by measurement before and after: validate_manifest checks declared-vs-present, and the writer scan is what would otherwise object.

## Boundary

Manifest and its validator only. This does NOT change any grant, does not touch architecture/protected-writes.json (MACHINE-GENERATED, never hand-edited), and does not widen the writer scan. The routine-wrapped-write blind spot in that scan is separate and is inventoried on wamn-0h0g.15.137.

## Measured starting point, 2026-08-26

30 principals, 61 objects. title: feat(publish): reconcile-before-publish is a stated precondition, not a trap
description:
## Why

wamn-xkgp mounts the environment verify-and-refuse arm on publish: the environment carried from the release row is checked against wamn_run.environment_policies.expected_environment, the provisioned identity fact written by reconcile-run-plane from the control-plane registry. Owner ruling 2026-08-26 took option (c) - refuse on a MISSING policy row as well as on a mismatch, because a guard defeated by the row simply not existing is weaker than the bead's own ask.

That refusal introduces a NEW ordering that nothing in the tree enforces or documents today: a project database must have had reconcile-run-plane converge a policy row for the tenant before a release can be published into it. Publishing against a not-yet-reconciled run plane now fails where it previously succeeded.

## Scope

Record reconcile-before-publish as the stated precondition of the publish surface, so the new failure is diagnosable rather than surprising. Name the ordering where an operator will meet it - the publish verb's own help and module doc, and deploy/README.md or the operations runbook, whichever is the live home. Nothing here changes runtime behaviour.

## Boundary

The refusal itself, its typed literal environment-policy-absent, its drift guard and its mutants belong to wamn-xkgp and land there. This issue owns only the stated precondition and its discoverability. It does not add an ordering CHECK to any schema, does not make reconcile idempotently run itself from publish, and does not widen any grant.
notes: OWNER RIDER 2026-08-26, and it is the point of the bead: the refusal message MUST POINT AT THE RECONCILE VERB BY NAME. A fail-closed refusal whose remedy is discoverable in the error text is the difference between a guard and a trap. The typed literal environment-policy-absent is DISTINCT from the mismatch literal - two different operator situations with two different remedies, so they must not collapse into one code.

title: chore(lints): adopt the M-STATIC-VERIFICATION workspace lint set
description:
THE WORKSPACE HAS NO LINT CONFIGURATION AT ALL. Measured 2026-08-25 at ffe54cae: no [workspace.lints] in the root Cargo.toml, no [lints] in any of the 35 crate manifests, no clippy.toml, and no lint flags in .cargo/config.toml rustflags (it sets only the mold linker). Exactly ONE crate-level attribute exists in the whole tree, a single allow(dead_code). So a plain cargo clippy runs pure defaults.

*** MEANWHILE THE POLICY IS ALREADY DENY-EVERYTHING, ENFORCED ONLY BY A GATE THAT HAS NEVER PASSED. *** tools/repo-lint runs clippy with -D warnings on SIX legs: root workspace, components native, connection-http-standard, components wasm, no-std native, and no-std wasm. Per the gate of record, tools/repo-lint run has NEVER been green - the rustfmt legs have been red since before wave 60. Clippy on 1.98 emits 47 warnings today, so the root leg alone fails on all of them.

THERE IS ALSO NO CI. The .github directory does not exist; its only workflow was client.yml, deleted with the JS surface at afc010bf. repo-lint run by hand is the entire enforcement story. *** THE OWNER HAS RULED NO CI - do not add one. ***

WHY THIS IS WORTH DOING: the -D warnings intent is invisible to anyone running cargo clippy directly, and there is no central place to record a deliberate exemption. M-CARGO-WORKSPACE says shared settings belong in [workspace.lints]; M-STATIC-VERIFICATION names the exact compiler and clippy sets to enable; M-LINT-OVERRIDE-EXPECT says overrides use expect with a reason rather than allow, so stale exemptions self-report.

SCOPE: the ROOT workspace. components/ and components/no-std/ are SEPARATE workspaces with their own manifests and are NOT in scope here - note them, do not sweep them in.

MEASURE BEFORE COMMITTING TO A LEVEL. The M-STATIC-VERIFICATION clippy set includes pedantic, which on a 35-crate tree may produce a very large number of warnings. Adopt the set, COUNT what it produces per lint, and choose levels that are honest: deny what is already clean, warn what is not, and record the gap rather than hiding it behind a blanket allow.
acceptance_criteria: Root Cargo.toml carries [workspace.lints] with the M-STATIC-VERIFICATION compiler and clippy sets. Every root-workspace member manifest inherits it with lints workspace = true. The resulting warning count is MEASURED and reported per lint, and the chosen levels are justified against that measurement. cargo check --workspace --all-targets stays clean and the gate-of-record failing NAME SET is unchanged.
close_reason:
Landed at 059e1843. [workspace.lints] adopted per M-CARGO-WORKSPACE with the M-STATIC-VERIFICATION sets; all 35 root-workspace members inherit it.

*** LEVELS WERE SET FROM MEASUREMENT, NOT COPIED FROM THE GUIDELINE, AND THE OWNER'S RULING - CORRECTNESS IS THE GOAL - DROVE THE SHAPE. *** Adopting the full set produced 2316 warnings across 64 lints. Each category was then measured SEPARATELY rather than accepting one number:

DENIED, because they measured ZERO and therefore cost nothing today:
  clippy::correctness and clippy::suspicious - THE TWO CATEGORIES THAT FIND BUGS - plus the five clean compiler lints unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn, ambiguous_negative_literals, redundant_lifetimes, trivial_numeric_casts and unused_lifetimes.
  THE ARGUMENT: a clean lint held at warn only asks to be re-read; held at deny it CANNOT REGRESS. If one fires now it is new code, not old debt. Clippy tool lints are inert under plain cargo build, so denying them does not break an edit loop.
WARN, because they are dirty and the honest level says so: clippy cargo, complexity, pedantic, perf and style, plus missing_debug_implementations and redundant_imports.
ALLOWED - eight lints, removing 1566 of the 2316, each with its count recorded INLINE in the manifest so the exemption stays arguable rather than becoming folklore: must_use_candidate 697, missing_errors_doc 254, doc_markdown 237, cargo_common_metadata 140, too_many_lines 112, missing_panics_doc 72, multiple_crate_versions 46, return_self_not_must_use 8. One argument applied consistently - this is an APPLICATION workspace with nothing published and no external API consumers, and the guidelines scope libs-ux rules to crates that have one.

M-LINT-OVERRIDE-EXPECT is recorded in the manifest so overrides use expect with a reason rather than allow, and stale exemptions self-report.

*** RESIDUE IS 677 WARNINGS ACROSS 56 LINTS AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT HIDDEN. *** Pre-existing debt now visible: 98 unchecked casts across four cast lints, 74 format_push_string, 53 items_after_statements, 23 needless_pass_by_value. A blanket allow would have made the number look good and taught nothing.

*** CONSEQUENCE THE OWNER SHOULD KNOW, AND I INITIALLY GOT THIS WRONG BEFORE CORRECTING IT: the -D warnings gap in tools/repo-lint grows from about 47 to 677. That gate previously ran against clippy DEFAULTS, so pedantic and cargo were never in its scope. This is a disclosure of applicable-but-unenabled lints, not a regression, but it moves repo-lint from nearly-achievable to a project. *** The measured alternative was recorded: dropping pedantic and cargo gives 98 warnings and keeps repo-lint plausibly reachable. The owner chose correctness.

VERIFIED: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets exits 0 with ZERO errors under the deny levels. Full sweep 1451 passed, 14 FAILED, 34 ignored with the failing NAME SET byte-identical to the pre-change baseline - adding a lints section to 35 manifests tripped no manifest-reading guard.
MUTATION-VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED LIVE: an eq_op probe added to crates/platform/component-policy FAILS THE COMPILE under the denied correctness category. Restored byte-identical, sha256 b675d3d9.

OUT OF SCOPE, NOTED NOT SWEPT: components/ and components/no-std/ are SEPARATE workspaces and inherit nothing from here.

title: fix(gates): wasmtime_source_identity demands a dependency execution/host does not use, and self-races on the cargo package lock
description:
TWO DEFECTS IN tests/conformance/tests/wasmtime_source_identity.rs, found while executing wamn-2jr4 and wamn-ufjr. Together they account for BOTH of that binary's standing reds in the gate of record.

DEFECT 1 - A STALE EXPECTATION, NOT A MISSING DEPENDENCY. THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE WRONG ONE.
DIRECT_CONSUMERS at :19-22 declares that crates/execution/host/Cargo.toml must inherit BOTH
wasmtime-wasi and wasmtime-wasi-http. Measured at 1.98.0: crates/execution/host/Cargo.toml:15
declares ONLY wasmtime-wasi, and NO source file under crates/execution/host references
wasmtime_wasi_http at all. Workspace-wide, only crates/platform/runtime/Cargo.toml:55 and
tests/system/Cargo.toml:22 declare it, and only tests/system/src/traceproof.rs actually uses it.

*** SO ADDING THE DEPENDENCY TO SATISFY THE GUARD WOULD DECLARE A DEAD DEP TO SILENCE A FALSE
ASSERTION. THE GUARD IS WHAT IS WRONG. *** This is deletion collateral - the dep was dropped from
execution/host and the guard was never repointed - which is this branch's dominant defect class.

Both reds are the SAME defect seen from two angles:
  direct_wasmtime_consumers_inherit_workspace_source_contract at :250 reads left=None against
  expected Some({workspace=true}).
  resolved_wasmtime_type_universe_is_single_and_canonical at :342 finds the consumer map identical
  to expected EXCEPT for the missing wamn-execution-host wasmtime-wasi-http entry.
FIX: drop wasmtime-wasi-http from the execution/host row in DIRECT_CONSUMERS. Verify the two other
declaring packages still match reality rather than assuming - crates/platform/runtime declares it
with no by-name source use, which may be a second dead declaration and should be MEASURED, not
swept in.

DEFECT 2 - THE BINARY SELF-RACES ON THE CARGO PACKAGE CACHE LOCK AND ITS FAILURES ARE
INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM REAL ONES.
cargo_metadata() at :118-129 shells out to cargo metadata --locked --offline. That takes the cargo
PACKAGE CACHE LOCK. Three tests in this binary each call it, and cargo test runs them in PARALLEL,
so they contend with each other and with any other cargo process. The failure text is Blocking
waiting for file lock on package cache followed by a panic, which reads exactly like an assertion
failure.
MEASURED DIRECTLY: with a concurrent cargo check running,
resolved_async_nats_universe_is_single_and_canonical FAILS; with nothing else running it PASSES.
*** ANY BASELINE COUNT THAT INCLUDED ONE OF THESE THREE TESTS MAY BE WRONG. ***
FIX: resolve the metadata ONCE per binary behind a OnceLock and share it, so three concurrent cargo
invocations become one.

RELATED KNOWLEDGE, NOT A DEFECT: cargo metadata --offline resolves the WHOLE graph including
android and windows targets, so after a cargo update that adds cross-platform packages it fails
with attempting to make an HTTP request, but --offline was specified until cargo fetch runs. That
bit during wamn-ufjr and looks like a broken lockfile.
acceptance_criteria: DIRECT_CONSUMERS matches measured reality with no dead dependency added to any manifest. cargo metadata is invoked once per test binary. Both wasmtime_source_identity reds clear, and the full-workspace failing NAME SET shrinks by exactly those two with no other change.
close_reason:
Landed at 2a1a42c5. BOTH of this binary's standing reds cleared; they were ONE defect seen from two angles.

*** THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS THE WRONG ONE, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS BEAD. *** DIRECT_CONSUMERS demanded that crates/execution/host inherit wasmtime-wasi-http. Measured: that crate declares ONLY wasmtime-wasi (Cargo.toml:15) and NO source file under it references wasmtime_wasi_http. Workspace-wide only crates/platform/runtime and tests/system declare it, and only tests/system/src/traceproof.rs uses it. Adding the dependency to satisfy the guard would have DECLARED A DEAD DEP TO SILENCE A FALSE ASSERTION. The table was never repointed when the dep was dropped - deletion collateral - so the row was what was wrong. Dropped, with the reason recorded inline so nobody re-adds it. expected_direct_dependencies() derives from DIRECT_CONSUMERS, so the one edit cleared both asserts.

DEFECT 2 - THE BINARY SELF-RACED ON THE CARGO PACKAGE CACHE LOCK. cargo_metadata shells out to cargo metadata --locked --offline, which takes that lock; three tests need it and cargo test runs them in PARALLEL. The failure text is Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache followed by a panic, which is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A REAL ASSERTION FAILURE. Measured directly: with a concurrent cargo check running, resolved_async_nats_universe_is_single_and_canonical FAILS; alone it PASSES. Now resolved once per binary behind a OnceLock. *** CONSEQUENCE: ANY EARLIER BASELINE COUNT THAT INCLUDED ONE OF THESE THREE TESTS MAY HAVE BEEN MEASURING THIS RACE RATHER THAN A DEFECT. ***

MUTATION-VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED LIVE: an ADDITIVE mutant (adding an unexpected wasmtime-wasi-http to tests/conformance/Cargo.toml) fails resolved_wasmtime_type_universe_is_single_and_canonical BY NAME on the drift assert. Additive was chosen deliberately - a removal mutant fails to compile and proves nothing, since conformance depends on both execution-host and runtime. Manifest restored byte-identical, sha256 0c97e086.

ACCEPTANCE MET IN FULL: no dead dependency added to any manifest; cargo metadata invoked once per binary; gate 1451 passed, 14 FAILED, 34 ignored, zero compile errors, with the failing NAME SET diffed against the prior sweep showing EXACTLY these two names cleared and ZERO new ones.

FILED-ADJACENT, MEASURED AND DELIBERATELY NOT SWEPT IN: crates/platform/runtime declares wasmtime-wasi-http with no by-name source use either. It causes no red because manifest and table agree, and proving it dead needs a build that could surface a link or feature dependency. Recorded as inventory on wamn-0h0g.15.137.

title: decide(state-owners): no principal covers push_component.rs, so component_library has no nameable writer
description:
Wave 64 lane C REFUTED the writer half of wamn-kf2k by measurement, and the refutation is structural rather than a wrong name.

THE MANIFEST'S OWN STANDARD for a writer is path containment: validate_discovered_writers at tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs:1272-1300 authorizes a discovery only when the file carrying the SQL literal sits under some declared principal path.

MEASURED at 1bffa614, independently re-derived by the integrator:
- The only production INSERT into catalog.component_library is INSERT_COMPONENT_SQL at services/ctl/src/push_component.rs:38.
- NO manifest principal covers that file. Every ctl principal is bound to exactly one file: ctl-copy to copy_project_env.rs, ctl-publish to publish_catalog.rs, ctl-migrate to migrate_catalog.rs, ctl-env-policies, ctl-reconcile-run-plane, ctl-terminalize. None fits the push or promote path.
- promote.rs:60,68,94 and publish_release.rs:62 are FROM clauses - READS, not writes. publish_catalog.rs only does to_regclass probes plus GRANT/REVOKE, and privilege_list_positions explicitly excludes grant lists from counting as writes.

SO wamn-kf2k's premise that ctl is the unnamed writer is only half true: ctl does mint the rows, but naming it requires MINTING A NEW PRINCIPAL, which the lane correctly refused to do unbidden.

ALSO REFUTED: state-owners objects[43] catalog.connection_requirements (project) writers schema-control is TRUE, not a false claim. The INSERT literals are at crates/schema/control/src/connections.rs:225,233, inside the schema-control principal path. push_component.rs:312 merely CALLS insert_component_connection_requirement_sql(). That row is load-bearing - it is what makes those discoveries resolve at all. DO NOT change it.

THE OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER: does services/ctl/src/push_component.rs (and promote.rs) get its own manifest principal, or does component_library's writer attribution change some other way? Nothing in tree settles it.

SECOND, NARROWER QUESTION, same class: ctl-copy drives pg_dump -Fd plus pg_restore --data-only at copy_project_env.rs:353,391 and pg_restore runs -n on the data schema only (crates/control/provision/src/copy.rs:186-197). It touches every relation generically without naming one. Does a generic dump/restore tool count as a writer of relations it never names? That is a policy call, not a measurement.
notes:

title: chore(deploy): the chart CA expires at 365 days and nothing renews it
description: Raised by the wave-57 deploy lane while landing wamn-0h0g.15.152, and deliberately NOT folded into it. The runtime-operator chart mints its CA with a 365-day life and never renews; recovery is delete-and-recreate, which invalidates every certificate issued under it. OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: STAY ADDITIVE for now. cert-manager issues only the per-environment certs while the chart keeps its own CA, so nothing that currently converges gets rewired. THE ALTERNATIVE, recorded and rejected for now: cert-manager owns the entire PKI including the NATS and operator certs, which renews automatically and is genuinely cleaner, but it rewires the one configuration that currently works and could not be tested because the cluster is frozen - it would land unproven until an RC on a fresh cluster. TRIPWIRES, either of which reopens this: the CA approaching one year from its mint date, or any unfreeze that makes a live test possible.
acceptance_criteria: Either the CA renews without manual action, or its expiry date is recorded somewhere an operator will see before it lapses, with the recreate procedure written down.

The arm has no principal. Choosing the replacement is a gate-design call and not a wamn-jnms fix: superuser masks RLS, and wamn_effect_writer is NOLOGIN so it would need SET ROLE, which the file's own doctrine rejects for the reader dial. NOTE THE GATE HAD ALMOST CERTAINLY NEVER RUN - WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL is set by nothing in the repository and the test self-skips silently when unset, so an ordinary sweep reports 1 passed. description: wamn-0h0g.15.183 died twice over: its doc target docs/archive/data-path/security-db-path.md was deleted at ff04842e, and its conformance file was 117 lines of document.contains prose that the owner's delete-doc-reading-tests ruling kills. title: [SR-MVP] test(obs): prove wamn:logging trace correlation once a guest imports wasi:logging
description:
SPLIT OUT OF wamn-0h0g.11.8 by owner ruling 2026-08-24. That bead's acceptance demanded 'one correlated wamn:logging record' alongside the span assertions. The clause is UNSATISFIABLE TODAY and asserting it would be corpse coverage.

THE REFUTER, and the premise correction of record: NO GUEST IN THE TREE IMPORTS wasi:logging. A search for wasi:logging across components/ returns zero hits in any guest WIT. The only importer was components/execution/flowrunner, and FLOWRUNNER IS DELETED FROM GIT - git ls-files on that path is empty, and only untracked empty directories survive on disk. Its retirement is tracked by the still-open wamn-0h0g.26.4.

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT, so this bead is proof and not feature: the plugin at crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_logging.rs implements wasi:logging/logging@0.1.0-draft and DOES correlate. It has parse_w3c_traceparent and calls set_trace_context(trace_id, span_id, flags), pinned by its own unit test traceparent_sets_trace_id_on_record. It reads the traceparent out of the guest-supplied context JSON string.

WHAT IS MISSING is the caller. The plugin's own docstring still says the production flowrunner emits a few structured records per run - describing a caller that no longer exists. Anyone touching that file should fix that sentence; it is the same stale-citation class wamn-a19z cleaned up elsewhere.

THE TRIGGER THAT UNBLOCKS THIS BEAD: a wamn:node guest gains a wasi:logging import AND the router's linker binds it. NodeInstance::instantiate already binds logging as a plugin, so the linker side is half-present. The likely first consumer is the component palette's first logging user. Until then this is not a test gap - it is a test for a path that does not exist, and building the path is a FEATURE decision, not this bead's.

DO NOT re-open this by adding a logging import to a guest purely to satisfy it. That would be building a caller to make a proof pass.
acceptance_criteria: A router-invoked component that imports wasi:logging emits a record, and that record carries the trace id of the incoming traceparent - the same trace id its component-invocation and effect spans carry. Blocked until a guest legitimately imports wasi:logging for its own reasons; adding the import solely to satisfy this bead does not count.

title: feat(obs): copy wiring and node identity into the connection_http effect span
description:

title: test(runtime): prove the release-pull body-digest and body-size refusals against a lying registry stub
description:
Filed 2026-08-23 by the wave-55 integrator, from a coverage hole the w55-e2e lane MEASURED rather than assumed while proving wamn-8yao.

*** TWO REFUSAL ARMS OF pull_verified ARE UNREACHABLE AGAINST A CONFORMING REGISTRY, AND ARE THEREFORE PROVEN BY NOTHING TODAY: release-manifest-artifact-body-digest-mismatch and release-manifest-artifact-body-size-mismatch. ***

WHY THEY CANNOT BE REACHED THE OBVIOUS WAY. The lane tried. It corrupted one byte of the pushed canonical bytes, re-uploaded the blob, and re-pointed the immutable tag at a manifest carrying it. registry:2 VALIDATES BLOB DIGESTS ON UPLOAD and refuses manifests referencing absent blobs, so corrupted bytes cannot be served under a true name. The mutation was still useful - it was killed by the named live test through the EARLIER layout check, release-manifest-artifact-layer-mismatch - but it proves the wrong arm. A real registry structurally cannot lie in the way these two arms exist to catch.

WHAT IT WOULD TAKE: an IN-PROCESS HTTP STUB that serves a manifest whose descriptor disagrees with the body it returns - one response with a mismatched digest, one with a mismatched size. Not a real registry, and not a container.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDINESS: these are the arms that catch a REGISTRY OR PROXY THAT LIES ABOUT WHAT IT SERVED. The whole point of pulling a release by digest is that the transport is untrusted; the two checks that enforce that specific property are the two with no test.

CONTEXT FROM THE SAME LANE, so the next person does not repeat the work:
- The layout check IS proven, by a data-level mutant against a real registry.
- The weld's identity derivation and its canonical-bytes admission are both proven, each killed by two named tests.
- The service call site is proven by the conformance guard one_release_manifest_weld_construction_site_per_host_process (wamn-0h0g.15.101), and that guard is FAIL-CLOSED: the integrator tested an aliased import and the guard trips, because it asserts exactly one occurrence and an alias reads as zero. A separately proposed hardening bead for that alias case was REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT and deliberately not filed.
So this bead is the one remaining named hole in the pull-and-weld proof surface, not a general request for more tests.
acceptance_criteria: An in-process HTTP stub serves a manifest whose descriptor disagrees with the returned body in digest, and separately in size. Each refusal arm fails a named test. No container and no real registry involved.

title: decide(security): EgressAddressPolicy permissive leaves allowed_hosts as the only confinement under Enforce
description:
Filed 2026-08-23. THE OWNER RESERVED THIS QUESTION when ruling wamn-0h0g.15.142; recording it as its own bead so it does not die with that close.

wamn-0h0g.15.142 moved the host engine's socket policy from EgressMode::Count to Enforce, so an opted-in guest's declared allowed_hosts now actually confines it instead of only emitting a debug log line.

*** BUT EgressAddressPolicy::permissive() IS STILL THE DEFAULT. Under Enforce, the declared allowed_hosts is therefore the SOLE confinement for an opted-in guest - the address-range layer permits everything it reaches. ***

THE QUESTION: is allowed_hosts-alone the intended posture, or should the address-range policy also tighten - denying link-local and cloud metadata addresses, the cluster service network, or RFC1918 by default?

Measured context, so the ruling is on evidence:
- Under the fork's SocketPolicy, both refusal paths route through one gate function: an allowed_hosts check and then an address-range check. Enforce activates both; permissive() makes the second one admit everything.
- Nothing opts in today. wamn.allow-raw-sockets appears in no deploy/ manifest - only a conformance test, a fixture, and archived docs. The posture choice is being made AHEAD of the first real opt-in, which is the cheap moment to make it.
- The host-loopback surface is unaffected either way; it refuses directly rather than through the gate.
- wasi:http is unaffected; outgoing HTTP is gated by check_allowed_hosts in the fork's http host, not by EgressMode.
- The executor path is unaffected; RouterDriver links upstream wasi sockets whose default check is a hard deny.
So the whole question is scoped to the wamn-host/washlet raw-socket path for a guest that has deliberately opted in.

*** DO NOT IMPLEMENT BEFORE THE RULING. Tightening the address policy would change refusal behaviour for a capability nobody uses yet, and the ruling is about intended posture, not about a bug. ***
acceptance_criteria: A recorded ruling on whether the address-range policy tightens alongside Enforce, with the chosen default named. If it tightens, a named test pins the denied ranges.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: OPTION (b) TIGHTEN. Under EgressMode::Enforce the address-range policy DEFAULT-DENIES link-local, cloud metadata, the cluster service network, and RFC1918. EgressAddressPolicy::permissive() stops being the default, so allowed_hosts is no longer the SOLE confinement for an opted-in guest. A NAMED TEST MUST PIN THE DENIED RANGES per this bead acceptance. Scope stays the wamn-host/washlet raw-socket path for a deliberately opted-in guest: wasi:http is unaffected (gated by check_allowed_hosts in the fork http host), the executor path is unaffected (RouterDriver links upstream wasi sockets whose default check is a hard deny), and host-loopback refuses directly rather than through the gate. NOTHING OPTS IN TODAY - wamn.allow-raw-sockets appears in no deploy/ manifest - so this lands AHEAD of the first real opt-in, which is the cheap moment. LANED THIS WAVE. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED.
PHASE-ORDER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-24 (memory key phase-order-directive) RE-SEQUENCES THIS BEAD. SCHEDULING QUESTION, OWNER-FACING. The ruled tightening is on a SURVIVING boundary (the wamn-host/washlet raw-socket path), which Phase A admits as a security check. But Phase A also forbids NEW PRIVILEGES AND NEW FIELDS, and a default-deny range set plus its named test is new policy machinery rather than a check of what survives. NOT SCHEDULED PENDING THE OWNER SAYING WHETHER IT RUNS IN PHASE A OR PHASE B.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24, PHASE PLACEMENT: PHASE B, AS A RIDER ON PHASE B ITEM 3 (wiring cases, gate reports, publication, activation). Reasoning recorded so it is not re-litigated: this is NEW POLICY MACHINERY, which Phase A forbids, and NOTHING OPTS IN TODAY - wamn.allow-raw-sockets appears in no deploy/ manifest. Deferral therefore costs nothing, and the cheapest-moment argument SURVIVES because the opt-in surface does not ship until Phase B either. *** IT MUST LAND BEFORE ANY GUEST OPTS IN. *** The option (b) tightening ruled above is unchanged: default-deny link-local, cloud metadata, cluster service network and RFC1918 under Enforce, with a named test pinning the denied ranges. NOT THIS WAVE.

title: fix(runtime): the engine's installed socket policy is unobservable, so a call site can silently revert it
description:
Filed 2026-08-23 by the wave-55 integrator, from a SURVIVING MUTANT the lane reported honestly rather than papering over.

*** THE SURVIVING MUTANT, reproducible on deploy-simplification today: in crates/platform/runtime/src/engine.rs, revert build_engine_sized to pass SocketPolicy::default() instead of host_socket_policy(). The engine is then built with EgressMode::Count again - the exact defect wamn-0h0g.15.142 just fixed - and EVERY TEST STILL PASSES. ***

WHY NO TEST CAN CATCH IT. The fork's Engine::socket_policy is pub(crate) with no accessor, so no test can observe which policy an engine actually carries. The named test the_host_socket_policy_enforces_egress_rather_than_counting_it pins host_socket_policy() ITSELF - it proves the constructor returns Enforce. It cannot prove a call site uses it. THERE ARE TWO SUCH CALL SITES (build_engine and build_engine_sized), so a future edit to either silently restores an unconfined egress path.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS wamn-vr1q, found in the same wave on a different lane: a function is proven correct, and nothing proves the production path calls it. Worth noticing as a pattern rather than two coincidences.

TWO CANDIDATE REMEDIES, both with a real cost - this needs a decision, not just implementation:
 (a) A FORK ACCESSOR for Engine::socket_policy. Clean and observable, but it is a fork commit, which means the drop-or-publish decision on wamn-9inf lands first, and the rev is pinned in 17 sites across 11 files. *** CARGO CANNOT RESOLVE AN UNPUSHED REV - bumping before publishing makes the WHOLE WORKSPACE UNRESOLVABLE, not merely red. ***
 (b) A DELIBERATE SOURCE-SCAN GUARD asserting both call sites pass host_socket_policy(). Cheap and in-tree, but it adds a THIRTIETH self-scanning guard site to the 29 that wamn-3o3a already tracks, and a source scan proves text, not execution.

SECURITY WEIGHT, so the priority is honest rather than inflated: the defect this guards is currently LATENT. wamn.allow-raw-sockets appears in no deploy/ manifest, so nothing opts in; the executor path was never governed by this policy at all (RouterDriver links upstream wasi sockets, whose default is a hard deny); and wasi:http is unaffected, being gated by check_allowed_hosts rather than EgressMode. The exposure is the wamn-host/washlet raw-socket path for a guest that opts in.
acceptance_criteria: Reverting either build_engine or build_engine_sized to SocketPolicy::default() FAILS a named test. If the chosen remedy is a source scan, the bead records why an observable accessor was rejected.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: PHASE A LIVE - CONFIRMED, under the Phase A security posture directive (memory key phase-order-directive). An unobservable socket policy that a call site can silently revert is a SURVIVING-BOUNDARY DEFECT - it is the egress floor itself, the wamn-mrfr class - NOT confinement ceremony. It qualifies under the directive's narrow Phase A allowance for boundaries that definitely survive.
*** SCOPE, RULED AND BINDING: OBSERVABILITY OF THE INSTALLED POLICY ONLY. NO NEW DENIAL MATRIX. ***
Make the engine's installed socket policy observable so a silent revert at a call site is DETECTABLE. Do NOT build denied-range tables, pairwise denial proofs, or a confinement adjudication - all of that is Phase B item 2, and the address-range tightening specifically is wamn-d0w4, ruled a Phase B item 3 rider. NOT YET SCHEDULED INTO A WAVE.
PREMISE RE-MEASURED AND IT STANDS - 2026-08-26, at d455ffa8, the wasmCloud v2.8.0 sync. Recorded so nobody re-checks this next sync.

THE EXPECTATION GOING IN WAS THAT THIS DISSOLVED. It did not. The v2.8.0 sync rewrites engine.rs heavily and retires the raw-socket opt-in, which looked like it might remove the subject. Measured instead:
- Engine::socket_policy is STILL pub(crate) with no public accessor - crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/mod.rs:279 at rev 5c4ec4a3. A grep for a public accessor over the whole vanilla crate returns nothing. The builder method with_socket_policy at :867 sets it; nothing reads it back.
- The surviving mutant therefore STILL REPRODUCES exactly as filed: swap host_socket_policy() for SocketPolicy::default() at either call site and every test still passes.
- THERE ARE STILL TWO CALL SITES, but both were RENAMED by the sync: build_engine and build_engine_with_host_memory (formerly build_engine_sized). Any future mutation work should target those names.
- The named test the_host_socket_policy_enforces_egress_rather_than_counting_it survives and was strengthened to cover all three raw-egress operations, but its limitation is unchanged: it pins the CONSTRUCTOR, not the call sites.

Notably vanilla v2.8.0 DID grow accessors for the neighbouring concern - engine.host_memory() and engine.total_core_instances() are public and the sync uses both in new assertions. Socket policy was simply not given the same treatment, so the asymmetry is upstream, not ours.

title: docs(deploy): record the OCI release rollout and rollback-by-revert runbook
description:
Successor to wamn-0h0g.15.16, which closed REFUTED-AND-SPLIT on 2026-08-23. Markdown only, zero code.

*** THE RUNBOOK IS THE IMPLEMENTATION. With no GitOps controller anywhere in the tree, rollback-by-revert is the deployment model's stated rollback story and this document is the only thing that realises it. ***

REQUIRED FIRST LINE (owner rider): the document opens by naming THE TRIGGER THAT RE-OPENS THE CONTROLLER QUESTION - a second environment, or the first non-human convergence need, i.e. the two-speed model's packaged path arriving for real. GitOps adoption stays a NAMED FUTURE DECISION rather than quietly dead.

CONTENT: mint, push, read the digest off publish-release stdout, hand-edit BOTH carriers, apply. Then git revert plus re-apply is rollback.
HOME: deploy/README.md plus the two pod-template headers.

THE TWO CARRIERS, both holding a 64-zero placeholder today and both different in syntax:
  deploy/platform/executor.yaml            - an env PAIR
  deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml - an extraArgs FLAG pair
The host takes flags DELIBERATELY: clap exits nonzero on an unknown flag, while a misnamed env entry would deploy cleanly and do nothing.

THE FACT THAT MAKES REVERT WORK, and it must be stated in the runbook: NO IMAGE IN deploy/ IS DIGEST-PINNED - every one is a mutable tag. The release digest in those two git-tracked pod templates is therefore THE ONLY THING git revert ACTUALLY ROLLS BACK.

RULING OF RECORD TO CITE: a human reads the digest off publish-release stdout and hand-edits the template. The pod-reads-its-own-digest option is EXPLICITLY REJECTED because it reintroduces the dual carrier that .15.102 and .15.103 deleted. wamn-duyl is the ergonomic improvement on that manual path, not a precondition - if it lands first, the runbook documents the verb instead of the copy-paste.

SECOND OWNER RIDER, SAME PASS: docs/exe-model.md's convergence sentence takes its one-line amendment - converged by operator kubectl per runbook, controller demand-gated - so the design authority catches up to the refutation, per the exe-model-is-sole-live-WIP rule. *** docs/exe-model.md is INTEGRATOR-ONLY and lane-forbidden. ***
acceptance_criteria: deploy/README.md and the two pod-template headers carry the mint-push-read-digest-hand-edit-apply sequence and state that git revert plus re-apply is rollback. The first line names the trigger that re-opens the GitOps controller question. The runbook states that no deploy image is digest-pinned, so the two pod-template digests are the only thing revert rolls back. docs/exe-model.md's convergence sentence is amended in the same pass. Zero code changes.

title: fix(docs): two stale in-tree sentences assert the router has no production driver
description:
Filed 2026-08-23. THIS IS A TWO-LINE DOC FIX THAT HAS MISPRICED AT LEAST FOUR BEADS, which is why it earns a bead of its own rather than going to an umbrella as inventory.

Three independent wave-55 measurement agents converged on the same correction: the router DOES have a production driver. crates/execution/host/src/router_driver.rs landed at 3bc15dd8 (wamn-0h0g.16.24), is constructed by both services/host/src/host.rs and services/executor/src/lib.rs, drives the walk through wiring.next and Step::Invoke, calls WiringCache get and insert from production code, reads wirings from the Postgres store into that cache, and instantiates real wamn:node guests over a generated bindings world. The WIT interface for invoking an operation on a component exists too: wamn:node@0.1.0 at crates/execution/router/wit/package.wit.

What remains true, and is the ONLY true part: the free function wamn_router::route and the NodeInvoker TRAIT have test-only implementors, because invoke is async and the sync trait cannot express it. RouterDriver bypasses the trait entirely and re-implements the walk.

THE TWO STALE SENTENCES:
1. crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/effect_span.rs - states that crates/execution/router has no production NodeInvoker implementor to supply it from. True of the trait, but read as the router having no driver, and that is the sentence behind the program-wide misconception.
2. crates/platform/runtime/wit/world.wit - calls the connection-http-plugin world declaration-only with the adapter owned by wamn-ko5r.8. REFUTED: connection_http.rs serves the adapter - bindgen, add_to_linker, impl HostPlugin, impl http::Host. This stale comment directly produced an incorrect fixture finding on wamn-0h0g.11.3.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: wamn-0h0g.11.3, .12.6, .24.5 and the .19.x cluster were all priced as driver-blocked or fixture-blocked on the strength of these sentences. Both are one-line edits.

Program memory keys wamn-exe-model-reconcile and wamn-sr-mvp-program-standing were corrected on 2026-08-23; the tree was not.
acceptance_criteria: Both sentences state what is actually true at HEAD: the NodeInvoker trait has test-only implementors while RouterDriver is the production driver, and the connection-http-plugin world is served by connection_http.rs. No other code changes.

title: fix(dispatcher): read_authority non-vacuity replays run_queue as wamn_app, an authority 22.7.1 revoked
description:
Split out of wamn-q9wa 2026-08-23 after a wave-55 measurement found the mask is three layers deep from TWO retirements, not one.

Layers 1 and 2 stay on wamn-q9wa: the seed inserts into catalog.execution_bundles (42P01) and into wamn_run.runs.execution_bundle_hash (42703), both retired by 4802daac.

THIS BEAD IS LAYER 3, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF THING. services/dispatcher/tests/read_authority.rs proof 4 is the non-vacuity arm: every denied statement is replayed as wamn_app and MUST SUCCEED. Four of the six cases replay against wamn_run.run_queue - insert, update available_at, delete, and select for update. Commit 7eaeee98 (wamn-0h0g.22.7.1, remove app queue authority) replaced the app grant with REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES ON TABLE wamn_run.run_queue FROM PUBLIC, wamn_app, wamn_effect_writer. wamn_app now holds ZERO privileges there, so all four replays fail 42501.

*** WHY THIS IS SPLIT RATHER THAN FOLDED: it is a retired AUTHORITY, not a retired relation. No grep for retired table names will ever surface it, and the parent bead's acceptance criterion (no reference to catalog.execution_bundles or any other retired relation) does not cover it. ***

DECISION NEEDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION: the four replay arms currently have no principal that can legally execute them. Either the non-vacuity discipline for run_queue moves to a different role, or the arms convert to None the way the insert_ledger case already did in the same file. That is an authority-model call, not an implementer call.

The fifth case (select from runs) still passes - run-state.sql grants SELECT, DELETE on wamn_run.runs to wamn_app. The sixth already has None for its replay by design.
acceptance_criteria: The read_authority non-vacuity arm names a principal that can legally execute every statement it replays, or explicitly records None with the reason. No replay fails 42501. The gate runs to exhaustion with no masked layer behind it.
notes:
WAVE 56 (2026-08-24): wamn-q9wa layers 1+2 LANDED, which UNMASKS this bead. The retired catalog.execution_bundles seed is gone from services/dispatcher/tests/read_authority.rs, so execution now reaches the proofs phase and this bead's 42501 is the live failure.

MEASURED BY EXECUTION, not by reading - the lane ran the gate against a real PostgreSQL 18 with WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL set by hand. THE FILE HAS TWO MORE BLOCKERS BETWEEN THE SEED AND THIS BEAD, neither previously recorded, and both must be cleared before anyone can see this bead's arms run:

  LAYER 0  deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql has a bare LOCK TABLE, illegal under psql
           autocommit, so the DDL apply dies before the seed. Filed as wamn-jnms.
  LAYER 2.5 the gate never seeds wamn_run.environment_policies, so the
           pin_run_durability_class() BEFORE-INSERT trigger raises
           environment-policy-not-converged. Sibling
           crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs seeds it - copy that.
           Inventoried on wamn-0h0g.15.137.

With temporary probes for both in place, proofs 1, 2 and 3 all PASSED, including proof 2's
woken run-a1 and depth 1 - direct positive evidence that the runs rows land correctly with
execution_bundle_hash removed. Then proof 4 failed exactly as this bead predicts:
non-vacuity arm INSERT into run_queue failed as wamn_app, permission denied for table
run_queue.

THE RULING MENU IS NARROWER THAN THIS BEAD IMPLIES. Measured against deploy/sql/run-queue.sql
plus a repo-wide grant sweep, the realistic options are TWO, not a free choice of principal:

  (a) CONVERT THE FOUR ARMS TO None. NOT vacuous, and the file already argues this itself in
      the insert_ledger case's comment: privilege is checked BEFORE column constraints, so a
      42501 can only be the missing grant, and assert_denied still requires SQLSTATE exactly
      42501 AND msg NOT LIKE row-level security - the RLS-versus-grant discrimination, which
      is the arm's stated headline risk, survives intact. A malformed statement does not
      silently pass either: a typo raises 42703 or 42P01, which is not insufficient_privilege,
      so the EXCEPTION arm never catches it and psql exits nonzero. What is genuinely lost is
      only proof that the statement is FK-satisfiable and RLS-legal for someone - near-zero
      marginal evidence for INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE refused before constraint evaluation.
  (b) MINT A THROWAWAY run_queue-writer PROBE ROLE inside the gate (NOBYPASSRLS, CONNECT,
      INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/SELECT), added to the hermetic teardown. About 25 lines, does not
      disturb proof 1, which sweeps only wamn_dispatch_reader and wamn_app. But it fabricates
      an authority that exists nowhere in production, which is arguably WEAKER evidence than
      an honest None.

WHY THERE IS NO THIRD OPTION - each excluded by measurement:
  - wamn_app: re-granting is ACTIVELY REVERTED. crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs carries
    RunPlaneActionKind::RemoveAppRunQueueAuthority, whose planned SQL is REVOKE ALL PRIVILEGES
    ON TABLE run_queue FROM PUBLIC, wamn_app plus a per-column revoke.
  - wamn_db_owner: NOLOGIN. Cannot be dialed.
  - wamn_effect_writer: holds column-level SELECT only.
  - wamn_dispatch_reader: it is the subject under denial.
  - superuser: BYPASSRLS destroys the arm's purpose.
  - THE REAL PRODUCTION run_queue WRITER IS UNPROVISIONED BY DESIGN. run-state.sql's own
    comment says the private management INSERT and executor UPDATE grants are provisioned by
    their owning cutovers, and those cutovers (wamn-0h0g.22.8, wamn-0h0g.12.140) are OPEN. So
    there is no correct principal to name YET, not merely an unmade choice.

ALSO NOTE: grant_connect_on_database_sql grants CONNECT to APP_ROLE only, so option (b) needs
a CONNECT grant too.

RECOMMENDATION FROM MEASUREMENT, for the owner and not acted on: (a), with a one-line reason
mirroring the insert_ledger comment. The diff either way is about 15 lines - THE COST OF THIS
BEAD IS ENTIRELY THE RULING, NOT THE CODE.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24, MIGRATED FROM THE DUPLICATE wamn-dsyn WHICH I FILED IN ERROR AND HAVE CLOSED. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED. REPLACE THE REPLAY WITH AN ERROR-SHAPE ASSERTION: each refused statement must fail SQLSTATE 42501 specifically, insufficient_privilege. A syntax error, a missing relation, or any other class FAILS THE GATE rather than passing as a refusal. NO PROBE ROLE - do not add fixture scaffolding that the generated-grants migration will obsolete. ACCEPT THE NARROWER PROOF and NOTE THE RESIDUAL IN THE FILE COMMENT: an error-shape assertion proves the refusal IS a privilege refusal, but not that the statement would otherwise have succeeded, which is what the replay bought. Rejected minting a dedicated gate-only probe role, for the scaffolding reason above. Rejected deleting the arm: it is the only thing standing between this gate and the vacuous-refusal trap this branch keeps hitting. MEASURED CONTEXT from the wave-57 sql lane, which hit this while fixing wamn-jnms: run-queue.sql grants wamn_app nothing after the .12.20 through .12.29 confinement, so the replay fails with permission denied for table run_queue. Superuser masks RLS and wamn_effect_writer is NOLOGIN so it would need SET ROLE, which the file's own doctrine rejects for the reader dial. ALSO: this gate had almost certainly never run - WAMN_PROVISION_PG_URL is set by nothing in the repository and the test self-skips silently when unset, so an ordinary sweep reports 1 passed. A seed defect behind it was already fixed in wamn-jnms: the run seed predated the environment-policy trigger and raised environment-policy-not-converged from wamn_run.pin_run_durability_class.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED BY PHASE B. Owner ruling 2026-08-24 under the Phase A security posture directive (memory key phase-order-directive). TRANSITIONAL PROBE: read_authority non-vacuity asserts against wamn_app authority that wamn-0h0g.22.7.1 ALREADY REVOKED. Phase B item 2 builds current_user authority once and proves it once. A probe defending a revoked transitional authority is exactly the churn class being retired - no denial proof is owed for an authority that no longer exists.

title: feat(runtime): make the memory cap a real value by advertising the ceiling after arg parsing
description: wamn-0h0g.17.3 shipped --pool-slots as a per-host-group value but DELIBERATELY DID NOT ship --pool-memory-cap-bytes, and the reason is a genuine blocker rather than caution. MEMORY_CAP_BYTES has a SECOND consumer the bead never considered: advertise_memory_ceiling() writes WAMN_MEMORY_CEILING_MB, which the wash-runtime fork's per-store ResourceLimiter reads. That call must run BEFORE the Tokio runtime exists (it uses unsafe set_var), which means inside each binary's main AHEAD OF CLAP PARSING - services/host/src/main.rs:41, services/executor/src/main.rs:23, plus scenario-worker and tests/orchestrator. *** SHIPPING THE FLAG WITHOUT THAT LEG WOULD GIVE AN UPWARD-INERT KNOB: a raised cap is silently re-clamped per store, so the operator sets a value and nothing happens. *** That is precisely the invisible-red class, so the lane shipped the half that works and documented the other half rather than shipping a lie.
acceptance_criteria: A configured memory cap actually moves the pooling ceiling end to end, including the per-store ResourceLimiter. --pool-memory-cap-bytes and runtime.pool.memoryCapBytes both take effect, and a mutant that fails to advertise the configured value fails a named test.
notes: Move advertise_memory_ceiling() to take PoolSizing::memory_cap_bytes and run after Cli::parse() in all four mains. memory_cap_bytes already exists in the PoolSizing struct at its compiled default, documented as awaiting this bead - the shape is ready, only the advertisement leg is missing.
close_reason:
CLOSED at fab307b5 (integrated as the first of two engine-lane commits), pushed to origin/deploy-simplification. Lane w55-engine; INDEPENDENTLY re-verified in the main tree.

THE DEFECT: advertise_memory_ceiling wrote the COMPILED constant into WAMN_MEMORY_CEILING_MB, and in all four binaries it ran from sync main() BEFORE Cli::parse() inside the async main. PoolSizing::memory_cap_bytes already existed and was already honoured by build_engine_inner, but NO FLAG EVER SET IT - both production sites spread ..PoolSizing::default(). An upward-inert knob: even a raised cap was re-clamped per store.

SHIPPED: --pool-memory-cap-bytes on HostArgs and ExecutorArgs mirroring the existing --pool-slots; the parsed value reaches PoolSizing at both build_engine_sized call sites; advertise now takes the configured value and runs AFTER parse in the two SERVING binaries. deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml's comment claiming the cap is deliberately not configurable is gone.

SCOPE FENCE HELD: services/scenario-worker's advertise call is INERT - that process builds no engine and creates no store - and tests/orchestrator has no sizing argument. Neither gained a flag. Both now pass PoolSizing::default().memory_cap_bytes explicitly rather than being silently defaulted.

PROOF. Lane: 154 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored for the runtime lib in its own worktree; 5 host bins; 6 executor lib. Mutants applied, tested, sha256-restored.
INTEGRATOR RE-VERIFIED IN THE MAIN TREE: all eight file sha256 matched byte-for-byte; runtime lib 156 / host bins 5 / executor lib 6, all green; cargo check --workspace --all-targets --keep-going ZERO errors. I re-derived the load-bearing mutant myself - dropping the parsed cap at the host's pool_sizing so the compiled default is restored - and it was KILLED by the_parsed_pooling_flags_reach_the_engine_sizing. Restored byte-identical.
*** COUNT NOTE, so nobody reads a regression into it: the lane saw 154 and the main tree shows 156 because BOTH engine-lane and trace-lane tests compose here. Base was 152, trace added 2, this bead added 2. Only the integrator sees the sum. ***

THE ORDERING MUTANT IS UNCOMPILABLE, WHICH IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN A TEST: main() is restructured so advertise takes a value derived from the parsed Cli, so putting the call back before parse has no value to pass and fails with cannot find value cli in this scope. That avoided adding a thirtieth self-scanning guard to a repository already carrying 29.

*** ONE MUTANT SURVIVES AND THE LANE SAID SO RATHER THAN ROUNDING DOWN: making advertise_memory_ceiling pass the compiled constant to memory_ceiling_mb. Killing it would require reading WAMN_MEMORY_CEILING_MB back, which is forbidden here - set_var on a process global, in a multithreaded test binary, racing every sibling that calls advertise. MITIGATION: the DECISION was split out into memory_ceiling_mb, which IS fully pinned by the_advertised_ceiling_follows_the_configured_cap; what survives is a one-line wrapper with no decision left in it, and it emits an unused-variable warning. The workspace has no lints table and no deny(warnings), so today that is a warning rather than a gate failure - recorded as inventory, not filed. ***

PREMISE CORRECTIONS FROM THE LANE:
- *** cargo test -p wamn-host --lib RUNS ZERO TESTS. wamn-host is bin-only; --bins is required. Any recorded recipe using --lib on it is a FALSE GREEN. ***
- Program memory said build_engine has thirteen call sites; the true count at fa76974c is eleven - and it is irrelevant, since build_engine's signature does not change and this bead touches exactly two build_engine_sized sites.
- TEST-COUNT COMPARISON TRAP: cargo test -p wamn-runtime --lib and a multi-package --lib --bins invocation build DIFFERENT feature-unified test binaries with different counts. Counts are comparable only within one invocation shape.

DEFERRALS: the scenario-worker's inert advertise call (delete it, or give that process a real reason to have it) and whether values-host-default.yaml should state the cap the way it states --pool-slots. Both recorded as inventory rather than filed, per the standing no-churn rule; the flag works end to end either way.

title: feat(ctl): print the two release environment lines for a pod template
description: The (b) half of the owner ruling on the release digest writer: a ctl verb that PRINTS the two environment lines an operator pastes into a pod template. The (a) manual path is what shipped with wamn-cdky - the operator reads the digest off publish-release stdout and hand-edits the template. THE 4TH CANDIDATE IS EXPLICITLY REJECTED AND MUST NOT BE BUILT: a pod reading its own digest from Postgres reintroduces the dual carrier that wamn-0h0g.15.102 and .15.103 deleted, and it rolls a release without a rollout. Lane w54-ctl confirmed it left no seam for it.
acceptance_criteria: A ctl verb prints exactly the environment lines a pod template needs for a given release, and nothing else. It writes no manifest and mutates nothing.
notes:
CANNOT BE WRITTEN YET, and the reason is a real dependency, not caution: deploy/ today carries only WAMN_RELEASE_MANIFEST_ROOT as a ConfigMap mount. The artifact-base and digest environment names are being introduced by wamn-3ceu in lane w54-host. Sequence this AFTER wamn-3ceu lands, then the verb has two concrete names to print.
MEASURED 2026-08-23 (wave-55). GENUINELY UNBLOCKED. IT IS REAL CODE, NOT A DOC CHANGE. ONE PREMISE WRINKLE NEEDS A ONE-SENTENCE RULING.

wamn-3ceu landed both names: the executor takes them as REQUIRED clap args with env fallbacks, and the host takes them as an Option pair with a mutual requires. Both reach OCI, not a file. Deploy side landed too, both carriers holding the 64-zero placeholder and both labelled not-appliable / not-rollable as checked in.

*** THE WRINKLE: THE HOST IS NOT A SECOND ENV-LINE CONSUMER. It takes the pair as extraArgs FLAGS, and the values file says why, in terms that are load-bearing rather than incidental: a flag makes clap exit nonzero on an unknown name, while an env entry with a wrong name would deploy cleanly and do nothing. So "print the two release environment lines for a pod template" is literally correct for EXACTLY ONE of the two release-carrying workloads. RULING NEEDED: does the verb print both forms - the executor env pair AND the host flag pair - or only env lines that a host operator must hand-translate? ***

PRICE: ~125 lines across 3 files - a new services/ctl/src/print_release_env.rs (args mirroring the push verb's database quad, a run function that reads the snapshot and prints, and a test pinning the two exact env names), plus one enum variant and match arm, plus one module line. The seam it needs is ALREADY PUBLIC (read_release_snapshot), and the digest is derivable from the canonical bytes, so NO NEW SQL. About 50 lines of connect-and-transaction boilerplate get duplicated unless a private helper in the push verb is widened.
NO GUARD BLOCKS IT: the ctl verb-surface list is a must-contain, not an exact set.
LANE SHAPE: ride the SAME services/ctl lane as wamn-1xb5 - they overlap on main.rs and lib.rs, and this is a rounding error beside it.
RELEVANCE BEYOND ITSELF: this bead's description carries the ruling of record that a HUMAN hand-edits the digest from publish-release stdout, with the pod-reads-its-own-digest option explicitly rejected. That answers the question that was blocking wamn-0h0g.15.16's residual runbook.
close_reason:
CLOSED at 54da5f16, pushed to origin/deploy-simplification. Lane w55-ctl, second commit.

New ctl verb print-release-env: reads the frozen release snapshot through the already-public read_release_snapshot, derives the digest from the canonical bytes (NO NEW SQL), and prints what the two carriers need. An absent release exits 1 naming the coordinate.

*** THE PREMISE WRINKLE, AND THE INTEGRATOR CALL ON IT - OWNER-REVERSIBLE. The bead says "the two release environment lines for a pod template", but only the EXECUTOR takes them as env entries. title: feat(fork): first-class pooling chart key, triggered by the next fork-chart touch
description: OWNER RULING 2026-08-23. Reason: hostGroups[].env has no schema, no helm lint validation, no type checking, and is silently misspellable - WAMN_POOL_SLOT deploys fine and does nothing, the invisible-red class at config grain. Do not schedule a standalone fork-chart PR for it. *** Two conditions from .17.3 make this a values rewire rather than a code change when the trigger fires: the engine.rs config struct is written KEY-SHAPED at .17.3, and host startup already refuses on an unrecognized pooling config name. Cost noted by lane w53-173 measurement: a chart key likely also needs a new SEAM row in tests/conformance/src/chart_seam_governance.rs, and the fork chart publishes on v-tags so wamn must re-pin both the Cargo rev and the chart --version in two files.
acceptance_criteria: At the next fork-chart touch, runtime.pool.slots and runtime.pool.memoryCapBytes exist as typed chart values with documented defaults and a typed rendering path; deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml moves off the interim mechanism; no wamn code changes because the .17.3 config struct was already key-shaped.
close_reason:
TRIGGER FIRED AND WAS SATISFIED NATIVELY. Closed 2026-08-26 at d455ffa8, the wasmCloud v2.8.0 sync.

This bead named its own trigger: the next planned fork-chart touch, most likely the 2.8 sync, absorbs this free. That touch happened, and the outcome is the ledger principle at its ideal exit - UPSTREAM SHIPPED WHAT WE WERE GOING TO PATCH IN, so WAMN carries no chart patch at all.

WHAT LANDED. Chart 2.8.0 ships first-class, documented, typed sizing keys under runtime.resources: defaultHeapMemory and coreInstances. Verified against the chart source in the pinned checkout, not from the release notes: templates/runtime/deployment.yaml:289 does omit on the resources map for exactly those two keys, and :163-168 renders them as WASH_DEFAULT_HEAP_MEMORY and WASH_CORE_INSTANCES, with limits.memory rendering as WASH_HOST_MAX_GUEST_MEMORY at :159. Each is emitted quoted, so an integer value in the values file is safe.

WAMN moved onto them in the same change: deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml drops --pool-slots=512 from extraArgs and sets defaultHeapMemory 256MiB plus coreInstances 512 as keys, and deploy/platform/executor.yaml carries the matching env.

KEY-NAME DELTA, RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. This bead asked for runtime.pool.slots and runtime.pool.memoryCapBytes. Upstream named them runtime.resources.coreInstances and runtime.resources.defaultHeapMemory, and the semantics shifted with the names - core instances are allocator capacity rather than WAMN pool slots. The REASON this bead existed is nevertheless met: sizing is no longer stringly extraArgs configuration that is silently misspellable. It is a chart-rendered key pair.

THE MISSPELL HAZARD IS COVERED, WHICH WAS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT. This bead was filed because hostGroups env has no schema and WAMN_POOL_SLOT would deploy cleanly and do nothing, and because the flag carrier was chosen precisely so clap would crashloop on a typo. The move to env gives that fail-loud property back to upstream rather than to us - but tests/conformance/tests/chart_seam_governance.rs now pins both spellings hermetically in host_and_executor_use_the_native_v2_8_memory_contract, and additionally asserts the legacy names WAMN_MEMORY_CEILING_MB, WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING, --pool-slots and --pool-memory-cap-bytes are ABSENT. A typo in either file now fails a hermetic gate, which is a stronger guard than the crashloop it replaces.

No successor bead. Nothing is deferred.

title: decide(exec): the execution driver bypasses wash-runtime InstancePool entirely
description: MEASURED 2026-08-23 during wamn-0h0g.17.13. NodeInstance::instantiate builds a WorkloadComponent only to run the plugin linker binds, then creates its OWN Store and calls bindings::Node::instantiate_async. *** IT NEVER ENTERS wash-runtime InstancePool, so the InstancePolicy::Ephemeral it already passes is INERT on this path. *** This matters because the owner ruling that authorized deleting the bespoke pool reasoned that instance reuse, if ever wanted, would come from wash-runtime pool_size and InstancePolicy - the native path. That native path is NOT CONNECTED to the driver today, so the foreclosure is more complete than the ruling assumed. Two further facts: tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs around :390 and :611-616 still fail the build on any nonzero poolSize, so the native warm path is also policy-forbidden by our own guards; and post-deletion instance lifetime is plain Rust scope in invoke_node plus the wasmtime allocator slot accounting. NO DEFECT TODAY - fresh instances are the intended rule and that is exactly what happens. The decision is whether connecting the driver to the native InstancePool is wanted work at all, and if so whether it precedes windowed state with explicit affinity.
design: Option (a) accept: fresh-per-invocation is the shipped semantic, the wasmtime pooling ALLOCATOR already supplies the speed, and instance REUSE waits for windowed state. Close as accepted and record it. Option (b) file the routing work: make the driver acquire through wash-runtime InstancePool so pool_size becomes meaningful, then relax the two runtime_inventory guards behind an explicit affinity contract. Option (b) is materially larger and touches the fork seam.
acceptance_criteria: Owner rules (a) accept the current bypass and record it as the shipped semantic, or (b) authorizes routing the driver through the native InstancePool as its own bead.
notes: OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: OPTION (a) ACCEPT. Fresh-per-invocation is the SHIPPED SEMANTIC. The wasmtime pooling ALLOCATOR already supplies the speed; instance REUSE waits for windowed state with explicit affinity. Do NOT route the driver through wash-runtime InstancePool. The two tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs guards at :390 and :611-616 STAY as-is and nonzero poolSize stays policy-forbidden. *** RIDER: NOTE THE InstancePolicy INERTNESS IN THE VALUES COMMENT *** so the next reader does not assume the Ephemeral already being passed is doing work on this path - it is inert because NodeInstance::instantiate creates its own Store and never enters the pool. RECORD-ONLY THIS WAVE apart from that one comment. IMPLEMENTATION NOT STARTED.

RULED BY THE NATIVE-ALIGNMENT LEDGER. Closed 2026-08-26 at d455ffa8, the wasmCloud v2.8.0 sync. The ledger row IS the disposition, so this decision bead has its answer and needs no further adjudication.

  Deviation: Wasmtime pooling allocator is on, while the router still constructs and drops a fresh store per invocation; wash-runtime warm InstancePool dispatch remains unwired.
  What it buys: Fast allocator-backed fresh instances without guest state surviving a call. Allocator capacity and store reuse are separate controls.
  Disposition: Keep the allocator; keep reuse off. Admission rejects poolSize greater than 0, so every workload stays InstancePolicy::Ephemeral. The .17.x router/native-dispatch wiring remains open only if it preserves that fresh-store rule. Revisit warm reuse with explicit affinity/windowed state; a5e7d5a is already present for that future step.

THIS ANSWERS THE QUESTION AS FILED. The bead asked whether connecting the driver to the native InstancePool is wanted work at all, and if so whether it precedes windowed state. The ruling: not as warm reuse - the fresh-store rule is the product requirement, and the allocator already supplies the speed that warm reuse was the obvious way to get. Any .17.x wiring survives only if it preserves fresh stores, and warm reuse waits for explicit affinity or windowed state.

THE BEAD OBSERVED NO DEFECT AND THAT REMAINS TRUE. Fresh instances were the intended rule and are what happens.

WHAT CHANGED UNDER IT, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. The reasoning has moved off the fork: the bespoke pooling configuration is gone from crates/platform/runtime/src/engine.rs and replaced by vanilla HostMemoryBudgets, and the WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING host env kill switch is retired (ledger former-patch row g2br.16) because admission enforces poolSize 0 and no host switch should duplicate a manifest value WAMN controls. The a5e7d5a instance-pool panic and poison fix, cited when this bead was filed as the argument for adopting the upstream pool, is confirmed present: it is an ancestor of the peeled v2.8.0 tag.

No successor bead. The .17.x wiring question remains open on its own beads with the fresh-store constraint now written down.
