title: fix(obs): two depth gauges freeze instead of alerting when their observer stops
description:
ONE PRINCIPLE, TWO INSTANCES. Filed together deliberately so they do not get two unaware fixes.

INSTANCE 1 - wamn.jetstream.dlq.depth
  crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_jetstream.rs:333, refreshed ONLY inside the dead-letter
  publish path (:1410-1418). A materializer that stops running freezes the series at its last
  value rather than alerting.

INSTANCE 2 - wamn.run_queue.depth
  services/dispatcher/src/lib.rs:437-460, fed by RUN_QUEUE_DEPTH_SQL (:38) executed once per sweep
  (:347). This is what wamn-2jkm.104 already files against the dispatcher: the dispatcher has no
  liveness signal it does not emit itself.

Both are the observer-is-the-subject defect: the metric can only report while the thing it
measures is healthy. Decide one principle (staleness timestamp, separate liveness probe, or an
external scraper) and apply it to both.

Supersedes nothing; coordinate with wamn-2jkm.104 rather than fixing that one alone.
acceptance_criteria: Both depth gauges distinguish healthy-and-zero from observer-stopped, by one shared mechanism, with a deterministic test per instance.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 (wave-55). BOTH INSTANCES CONFIRMED. ONE FACTUAL ERROR IN THE BEAD, AND THE FACT THE RULING TURNS ON.

*** FACTUAL CORRECTION: this bead says the DLQ gauge is refreshed ONLY inside the dead-letter publish path. THERE ARE TWO REFRESH SITES - one after EVERY consumer fetch, and one after a dead-letter publish. The fetch site is far the more frequent, and it changes the freeze analysis materially. ***

THE MECHANISM, precisely. Both are OTel OBSERVABLE gauges over a last-write-wins in-process map, and both callbacks fold every entry UNCONDITIONALLY with no notion of sample age. The exporter invokes the callback on its own clock regardless of whether anything wrote the cache, so it re-observes the last written value forever. A gauge reading zero because the queue is genuinely empty and a gauge reading zero because the observer died an hour ago produce BYTE-IDENTICAL series. This is the observer-is-the-subject defect: the only thing reporting queue health is the thing whose failure you most need to detect. Total process death is a different and slightly better case, since the whole series goes absent and can be alerted on - the freeze case defeats every threshold and rate alert.

REMEDIES, PRICED. NO CHOICE MADE.
A. STALENESS STAMP - add a sampled_at to both sample structs, stamp on write, register a companion age gauge in each callback. ~50 production lines, but ~150 to 200 total: the dispatcher is cheap because its tick already takes an injected instant, while the jetstream plugin HAS NO CLOCK SEAM ANYWHERE (every site calls Instant::now inline), so a deterministic test there needs a new injected clock.
B. SELF-REPORTED LIVENESS COUNTER alerted on a zero rate. ~60 to 80 lines, no clock seam needed, tests trivial via the existing MetricHarness pattern. CHEAPEST. Caveat: still self-reported, so it does NOT satisfy wamn-2jkm.104's acceptance (a signal no dispatcher process produces) - that bead must be amended or B accepted as partial.
C. EXTERNAL SCRAPER - the only remedy that satisfies 2jkm.104. Dispatcher side needs a queue-side age-of-oldest-unclaimed read taken by something that is not the dispatcher. DLQ side is nearly free: the depth is already a NATS stream-subject count, so the external observer is NATS's own stream info via a Prometheus exporter - deploy-only, ZERO Rust. ~200 to 300 lines, almost all YAML.

*** THE FACT THE ONE-PRINCIPLE RULING TURNS ON. At the CODE level the two are near-identical - same map-of-sample shape, same unconditional callback, neither timestamped - so A and B are the same small diff applied twice. AT THE SEMANTIC LEVEL THEY ARE NOT, in four ways:
 1. CADENCE. The dispatcher refreshes on a bounded configured cadence, so a staleness THRESHOLD is derivable from config. The DLQ gauge HAS NO CADENCE AT ALL - it refreshes only when a guest fetches or dead-letters, so a quiet registration legitimately holds an arbitrarily old sample. STALE MEANS BROKEN ON ONE AND QUIET ON THE OTHER.
 2. What "observer stopped" MEANS: a long-lived single-purpose process wedged, versus a component that stopped polling, which is often the correct steady state.
 3. Clock injection is free on the dispatcher and a new seam on the plugin.
 4. Under remedy C the two share NOTHING - a Postgres query versus NATS stream info.
So: one treatment is genuinely available under A or B and is the right call at the code level; under C the single principle is a principle only, with two disjoint implementations. AND UNDER A THE DLQ HALF NEEDS A COMPANION DECISION - either a periodic refresh timer that does not exist today, or an explicit ruling that its age signal is informational rather than alertable. ***

DISPATCH NOTE: instance 1 rewrites the dead-letter depth sample and registry in wamn_jetstream.rs, the same file wamn-0h0g.24.8 writes. Even after the ruling this must sequence AFTER .24.8 or the two merge into one lane.

e88670eaba7b7f1010a8b846fba283076538296978f4f729ac1ab542c55b80f3 (+33/-5).

title: [SR-MVP] fix(conformance): gate_registry pins recipe selectors it never resolves, and one names code that does not exist
description:
## Why

*** A DEAD RECIPE PIN IS PASSING THE GATE THAT EXISTS TO CATCH IT. ***

docs/archive/build-and-test.md:1825 carries:
  recipe-test: H5-CALLABLE-CRON | ... | callable_cron::tests:: | 1 | tests/integration/src/callable_cron.rs
registered at architecture/gate-registry.json:985.

MEASURED 2026-08-19 at 53afb31a: callable_cron DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. There is no tests/integration/src/callable_cron.rs and no callable_cron module.

## The mechanism, which is the more important half

tests/conformance/tests/gate_registry.rs (parse_recipe_selectors at :191, validate_registry around :523) enforces only TWO things: that the id set in build-and-test.md EQUALS the SourceKind::Recipe entry set in architecture/gate-registry.json, and that a selector is non-empty and minimum_tests is not zero.

*** IT NEVER RESOLVES A SELECTOR TO CODE AND NEVER COUNTS TESTS. *** So a recipe can name a module that was deleted, or a test path that has drifted, and the registry stays green. The gate proves the two FILES agree with each other; it does not prove either agrees with the TREE.

This is the invisible-red class applied to the gate registry itself: a pin that does not resolve is indistinguishable from a pin that holds.

## How it was found

Incidentally, during the wave-10 read-only measurement of wamn-0h0g.12.149, while checking whether an edit to rie2ebench could hollow out the H5-RIE2EBENCH pin (:1626, minimum 2 tests, exactly 2 present). That pin is currently honest. H5-CALLABLE-CRON is not.

## Scope

Two separable pieces -- if they are taken separately, split this bead rather than doing half:
  1. Dispose of the H5-CALLABLE-CRON pin: delete it from both files, or restore the code it names if it was deleted in error. Determine which by finding the commit that removed callable_cron.
  2. Decide whether gate_registry should RESOLVE selectors against the tree rather than only cross-checking two documents. This is a real strengthening with real cost and is the part that needs a ruling.

## Note

Do NOT assume piece 1 is a simple delete until the removing commit is found. If callable_cron was deleted as part of a scope cut, its recipe pin is residue; if it was lost, the pin is the only surviving evidence that the coverage was expected.
acceptance_criteria: No recipe pin names code absent from the tree, and the disposition of selector-resolution in gate_registry is ruled and recorded.
notes:
*** OWNER RULING, dkk 2026-08-20: DISPOSE CALLABLE-CRON BY THE ASSERTED ARM, AND RESOLVE EVERY SELECTOR. ***

RULING
- Cron is a refused attachment kind. Determine what callable_cron asserted from its deleted source or history.
- If callable_cron exercised positive cron execution, its removal was correct. Keep it removed and delete the corpse-coverage recipe pin.
- If callable_cron proved cron attachment produces the typed refusal, restore that required refusal test. A ruled refusal without a firing proof is the unwatched-invariant class.
- Ratify selector resolution as a gate obligation: every registered selector must resolve to at least one existing test, and a dangling selector must fail gate_registry.
- The motivating defect is false coverage at registry grain: document-to-registry id equality is insufficient when the selector names no code.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN - NOT STARTED
- Find the commit that removed callable_cron and read the deleted test assertion.
- Dispose of H5-CALLABLE-CRON according to the asserted arm, restoring only a typed-refusal proof if that is what was lost.
- Strengthen gate_registry so every selector resolves to at least one existing test and dangling selectors fail by name.
- Add deterministic positive and dangling-selector tests plus a mutant that proves the new assertion fires.
- Update the governed registry and documentation together in the main loop, then run the conformance gate of record.
*** OWNER CONFIRMATION, dkk 2026-08-20: REMOVE ALL NINE INTENTIONALLY DANGLING SELECTORS; ENFORCEMENT OWNS THE CLASS. ***

MEASURED DISPOSITION
- Recipe inventory moves from 36 to 27.
- H5-CALLABLE-CRON pointed at the deleted positive scheduler proof; removal commit 25129131.
- H5-CALLABLE-F0, F1, F2, F3, F4, CALLABLE-WAVE1 and CALLABLE-WAVE2 pointed at demo/POC surfaces deleted by 3554f140.
- H5-DASHBOARDS pointed at observability extras deleted by d1c9e471.
- Remove all nine directives and registry entries, citing their cutting commits in the surrounding removal record.
- gate_registry must structurally resolve every remaining selector to at least one existing test and fail dangling selectors. The close records: 36 to 27, nine dangling resolved to their cutting commits, enforcement now structural.
- The cron refusal-arm check found no live cron-specific typed-refusal proof. wamn-0h0g.11.50 owns that one-test gap while the deleted positive directive still dies.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN - NOT STARTED
- Remove the nine decision-reconciled pins from both governed files.
- Implement static selector-to-test resolution for all 27 survivors.
- Add a named dangling-selector mutant and verify every survivor resolves.
- Do not restore any intentionally cut execution surface.
*** OWNER RULING, dkk 2026-08-20: TENTH SELECTOR USES DECISION-THEN-LANDING SUCCESSION IN THIS BEAD. ***

PREMISE CORRECTION
- Structural selector resolution found a tenth dangling recipe: PLAN-1-FLOW-SPEC-RECOVERY names absent target flow_spec_recovery_authority.
- Commit 24219bc0 deleted that 197-line proof with the old recovery representation. The proof asserted recovery-authority fields and readers that wamn-0h0g.2.1 deliberately removed, so it must not be restored.
- This selector is D15 primary, so deletion alone would create the exact primary-source false-coverage state this Bead forbids.

title: fix(gate): the tree-wide clippy command masks errors without --keep-going, and the one-error baseline was false
description:
*** THE TREE-WIDE CLIPPY BASELINE COMMAND HAS BEEN LYING, AND IT MADE ME BANK A FALSE FACT. ***
FILED 2026-08-19 by wave-9 lane 2 while working wamn-0h0g.12.146. This is a MEASUREMENT defect,
which is why it gets its own bead: every clippy finding taken with the old command is suspect.

THE DEFECT. The gate command of record has been
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
Cargo ABORTS SCHEDULING NEW UNITS ON THE FIRST ERROR ("build failed, waiting for other jobs to
finish"). So a strict clippy run reports only the FIRST FAILING UNIT'S errors, and every error
in any package scheduled after it is INVISIBLE. This is the invisible-red class applied to the
lint gate itself: a gate that does not finish is indistinguishable from a gate that passes.

HOW IT BIT. wamn-schema-control is an upstream dependency of tests/integration. The single
error at crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs:9907 therefore MASKED everything downstream.
On that basis I recorded, and banked in memory, that the tree had EXACTLY ONE clippy error and
that "everything else is clippy-clean, so any future clippy red is a REGRESSION, not noise".
THAT WAS FALSE.

MEASURED TRUTH at f27ad353, using --keep-going, which defeats the masking:
  SEVEN errors across THREE packages, not one.
    crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs:9907   single_element_loop   (wamn-0h0g.12.146, now fixed)
    tests/conformance/tests/effect_spans.rs:96    type_complexity
    tests/conformance/tests/effect_spans.rs:211   collapsible_if
    tests/conformance/tests/effect_spans.rs:273   collapsible_if
    tests/conformance/tests/effect_spans.rs:284   type_complexity
    tests/integration/src/rie2ebench.rs:151       dead_code (fn flow_json never used)
    tests/integration/src/runnerbench.rs:315      single_element_loop
  SIX remain after .12.146. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY THE INTEGRATOR in the main tree at
  six distinct sites; exit 101.

THE FIX THIS BEAD OWNS: the gate command of record becomes
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-deps --keep-going -- -D warnings
and the correction is written wherever that command is recorded, so the next lane does not
repeat the masking. NOTE the integrator may not edit docs/archive/build-and-test.md from a
parallel worktree; sequence this accordingly.

*** A SECOND SCOPE HOLE, SEPARATE AND STILL OPEN: --workspace IS THE ROOT WORKSPACE ONLY.
components/ IS A SEPARATE CARGO WORKSPACE AND HAS STILL NEVER HAD A CLIPPY BASELINE AT ALL.
--keep-going does not fix that; it needs its own invocation. ***

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATED: wamn-0h0g.11.34 (P3) already owns runnerbench.rs:315 and records the
SYMPTOM ("no lane can run a workspace-wide strict clippy as a gate") WITHOUT identifying the
masking cause. This bead identifies the cause. Both .11.34 and .12.146 carry an acceptance
criterion of "workspace clippy exits 0" that NEITHER CAN REACH ALONE, because each owns one of
seven errors -- that shared unreachable criterion is itself a defect in how those beads were
written, and is called out here rather than silently ignored.

ACCEPTANCE: the recorded gate command carries --keep-going; the false "exactly one error /
otherwise clippy-clean" claim is corrected wherever it was recorded; and the remaining error
inventory is owned by beads rather than by a stale measurement.
notes:
*** A SECOND SCOPE HOLE, MEASURED 2026-08-19 DURING THE WAVE-10 PRE-PARTITION PASS.
IT IS IN THE DOCUMENTED DEVELOPER COMMAND, NOT IN THE GATE COMMAND. THE DISTINCTION IS
THE WHOLE POINT AND I ALMOST RECORDED IT WRONG. ***

MEASURED WITH cargo metadata, not inferred:
    total workspace members: 39
    default-members:         20
    wamn-proof-integration is a MEMBER but NOT a default-member.

THE GATE COMMAND IS FINE ON THIS AXIS. --workspace overrides default-members and selects
all 39. That is confirmed by evidence already in hand, not just by doctrine: the wave-9
and wave-10 baselines were taken with
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-deps --keep-going -- -D warnings
and they DID surface the tests/integration errors. So this bead's --keep-going
correction stands unqualified for the gate command.

*** THE HOLE IS README.md:125, THE DOCUMENTED DEVELOPER COMMAND: ***
    cargo clippy --all-targets
It carries NO --workspace, so it selects DEFAULT-MEMBERS ONLY -- 20 of 39 crates.
NINETEEN CRATES ARE SILENTLY UNLINTED BY THE COMMAND DEVELOPERS ARE TOLD TO RUN,
including wamn-proof-integration, which owns two of the six known baseline errors.
Corroboration: wamn-proof-integration is likewise absent from the 32-package
fast_developer_native tier in architecture/workspace-tiers.json; it appears only in
full_ci (:113) and deployed_system_proof (:151).

CONSEQUENCE: a developer runs the documented command, sees green, and concludes the tree
is clean. The gate later disagrees. That is the invisible-red class -- a check that does
not run is indistinguishable from one that passes -- reproduced at the developer's desk
rather than in CI.

A SECOND-ORDER EFFECT, WORTH KNOWING BEFORE TRUSTING ANY GREEN CLIPPY LINE. The two
tests/integration errors fail DIFFERENT TARGETS and so are invisible in different ways:
  runnerbench.rs:315 single_element_loop is in #[cfg(test)] -- it needs --all-targets on
    -p wamn-proof-integration specifically. Even cargo clippy -p wamn-gates --all-targets
    never builds this crate's lib-test target (build-and-test.md:665, 696, 1305).
  rie2ebench.rs:151 dead_code is on the LIB target -- it surfaces as a plain WARNING when
    wamn-gates is built, and becomes an ERROR only under the -p wamn-proof-integration
    ... -- -D warnings form (build-and-test.md:1432, 4016, 4133).

*** SO THERE ARE THREE DISTINCT REASONS A CLIPPY RED CAN BE INVISIBLE HERE. THIS BEAD AS
WRITTEN ADDRESSES ONLY THE FIRST: ***
  1. FAIL-FAST MASKING within a run        -> fixed by --keep-going (this bead)
  2. DEVELOPER COMMAND SELECTS 20 OF 39    -> NOT fixed by --keep-going (new, above)
  3. components/ IS A SEPARATE WORKSPACE and has still never had a clippy baseline
                                           -> NOT fixed by --keep-going (already noted)

RECOMMENDED, NOT DECIDED: correct README.md:125 to carry --workspace so the documented
developer command matches the gate, or state explicitly which crates it does not cover.
Silently implying full coverage is the defect. Note README.md is NOT integrator-only, so
a lane may take it -- but it is also being edited by wamn-0h0g.12.150 (the deploy/sql
tree listing at README.md:86), so SEQUENCE THE TWO or they collide.
close_reason:
CLOSED: DONE. All three acceptance clauses met, one of them by a route the bead did not
anticipate.

1. THE RECORDED COMMAND CARRIES --keep-going. Added to docs/archive/build-and-test.md in the
   repo-lint section (blocking check 16) with the REASON stated, so the next reader learns
   the mechanism and not just the flag: cargo stops scheduling new units at the first error,
   so a workspace run without it reports only the first failing unit and hides every error in
   any package scheduled after it.

2. THE FALSE CLAIM IS CORRECTED WHEREVER IT WAS RECORDED -- AND IT WAS NOT RECORDED WHERE
   THIS BEAD ASSUMED. Grepping build-and-test.md for the "exactly one error / otherwise
   clippy-clean" claim found NOTHING: it lived only in the standing baseline MEMORY, which is
   now corrected in place. What build-and-test.md carried instead was a subtler problem, and
   it is now fixed: the doc described the blocking lint check as deriving its selection from
   "all 39 root workspace members and all six component workspace members" -- accurate about
   INTENT, and completely misleading about REALITY, because that check never reaches a single
   Clippy leg. A blockquote now says so and cites wamn-0h0g.12.157, so the coverage paragraph
   can no longer be read as evidence the coverage was exercised.

3. THE ERROR INVENTORY IS OWNED BY BEADS, AND IT IS NOW EMPTY FOR THE ROOT WORKSPACE.
   *** MEASURED AT 67b5986a: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-deps --keep-going
   -- -D warnings EXITS 0 WITH ZERO ERRORS. *** All six of the true baseline are closed:
   wamn-0h0g.12.148 (four in effect_spans.rs), .12.149 and .11.34 (two in tests/integration),
   and .12.146/.12.144 earlier. So "any root-workspace Clippy red is a regression" is TRUE
   FOR THE FIRST TIME -- which is the statement this bead existed to make honest.

A SECOND HOLE FOUND AND FIXED UNDER THIS BEAD. README.md:126 documented the developer
command as cargo clippy --all-targets, with NO --workspace. Measured with cargo metadata: 39
workspace members, 20 default-members. So the command developers are told to run SILENTLY
SKIPPED 19 OF 39 CRATES, including wamn-proof-integration, which owned two of the six
baseline errors. A developer would see green and conclude the tree was clean. Now reads
--workspace --all-targets --keep-going, with the reason inline, and cargo fmt --all --check
to match what tools/repo-lint actually invokes.
*** NOTE THE GATE COMMAND WAS NEVER WRONG ON SELECTION: --workspace overrides
default-members and selects all 39. An earlier draft of this correction said otherwise and
was wrong; it was measured before being recorded. ***

SO THERE WERE THREE DISTINCT INVISIBILITY MECHANISMS, NOT ONE:
  1. fail-fast masking within a run       -> fixed here (--keep-going, both places)
  2. dev command selected 20 of 39        -> fixed here (README --workspace)
  3. the lint script aborts at leg 2, so all six Clippy legs never run
                                          -> NOT fixed here; wamn-0h0g.12.157 owns it,
                                             and it is the reason components/ still has no
                                             baseline. That is a 43-file rustfmt problem,
                                             not a clippy problem.

VERIFIED: gate_registry 10 passed and workspace_tiers 11 passed after the build-and-test.md
edit -- the two gates that scan that file, for receipt-family aliases and for the six
workspace-tier command strings respectively. Neither was disturbed.

title: test(run-state): wamn_scenario_author has the same create-only role hazard and no production builder to mirror against
description:
FOUND 2026-08-19 by the wave-8 lane implementing wamn-0h0g.20.15, and deliberately
NOT fixed there because it is outside that bead's ruled scope.

## The gap

crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs bootstraps four roles. Three of
them -- wamn_scenario_author, wamn_effect_writer, wamn_run_projection_writer -- use
IF NOT EXISTS ... CREATE ROLE with NO ELSE ALTER branch. Only wamn_app has the ALTER
fallback.

PostgreSQL roles are CLUSTER-WIDE. So a role left behind by an earlier suite, carrying
attributes that differ from what the bootstrap intends (SUPERUSER, BYPASSRLS, LOGIN),
is SILENTLY KEPT: the create-only guard sees the name exists and skips.

wamn-0h0g.20.15 closed this hole for two of the three by adding a pg_roles assertion
that reds when wamn_effect_writer or wamn_run_projection_writer carry anything other
than NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS.
The mutant proved it fires.

*** wamn_scenario_author IS NOT COVERED, AND CANNOT BE COVERED THE SAME WAY. *** The
.20.15 assertion is a drift contract against a PRODUCTION BUILDER
(ensure_effect_writer_acl_role_sql, crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs:288-301):
it asserts the test's hand-rolled roles still match what production mints. THERE IS NO
ensure_scenario_author_role_sql ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. So there is no production
attribute set to mirror wamn_scenario_author against, and asserting its attributes
would be asserting the test's own literal back to itself -- true by construction and
worth nothing as a drift guard.

## What is actually owed, and it is a real question

Either:
 (a) wamn_scenario_author genuinely has no production builder because nothing in
     production mints it, in which case the interesting question is what DOES mint it
     in a real environment and whether that path has the same attribute set; or
 (b) it should have one, and its absence is itself the finding -- the role that
     guest-authored SQL interacts with is bootstrapped only by hand-rolled test SQL.

crates/control/provision, deploy/sql and the ctl provisioning subcommands. The answer
decides whether this is a test-hygiene bead or an authority-provisioning bead, and

title: fix(schema): catalog-schema.sql names two deleted ctl preflights as live membership coverage and instructs against the DB RAISE
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-19 during the wave-8 read-only measurement pass, while
establishing wamn-0h0g.12.144's disposition. Filed separately under the granularity
rule: it is a defect in the SCHEMA OF RECORD, not a subsection of a dead-code
deletion in services/ctl.

## The false claim

deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql, in the comment block above
catalog.register_release_manifest (around :266-274), states:

  "The membership half of that literal did not vanish, it moved up a tier: the ctl
   preflights (services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs and copy_project_env.rs) now
   derive the member set from catalog.release_flows and raise the SAME literal on a
   mismatch. Do not re-add a membership RAISE below; ..."

BOTH NAMED PREFLIGHTS ARE GONE. Measured at 0a9a9cd8:
 - services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs: the caller
   (publication_is_same_target_retry) was deleted by a1ecc789
   (chore(wamn-0h0g.11.28): delete the closed publish-catalog verb). What survives
   is divergent_release_members plus index_release_members, which NOTHING outside
   cfg(test) calls -- that is the clippy red wamn-0h0g.12.144 owns.
 - services/ctl/src/copy_project_env.rs: grep for release_flows, content-conflict
   and divergent returns ZERO hits. It does not derive a member set at all.

## Why this is worse than an ordinary stale comment

It is not merely a claim, it is an INSTRUCTION: "Do not re-add a membership RAISE
below." A future maintainer who checks whether the database should defend
membership reads that the application tier already does, and the application tier
does not. This is the false-coverage class the wave-7 sweep chased, except that
this instance actively directs the next person AWAY from the enforcement.

## The behaviour itself is NOT lost -- verify before acting

The same comment gives the structural account, and it appears to be the true one:
"under row-per-member truth the primary key refuses a CHANGED member, the
UPDATE/DELETE immutability triggers refuse a REMOVED one, and an ADDED one is
permitted by ruling."

So the correct repair is almost certainly to REPLACE THE JUSTIFICATION, not to add
a RAISE: the reason not to re-add a membership RAISE is that the primary key and
the immutability triggers already enforce it -- NOT that ctl does. CONFIRM THE
STRUCTURAL CLAIM AGAINST THE ACTUAL DDL BEFORE REWRITING THE COMMENT. If the PK
and triggers do NOT in fact cover the changed-member case, this stops being a
comment fix and becomes a real enforcement gap, and it should be re-priced.

## Handling constraint -- READ THIS BEFORE EDITING THE FILE

deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql is read by
tests/integration/src/catalog_live.rs, whose test
ddl_pins_immutable_and_atomic_release_boundaries is IN THE KNOWN-RED SET at HEAD
and belongs to wamn-0h0g.11.47, which is AWAITING AN OWNER RULING and marked DO
NOT TOUCH. The pins observed are .contains() checks against RAISE literals
(for example flow-version-content-conflict at catalog_live.rs:87), so a
comment-only edit should not move them -- but that must be VERIFIED, not assumed,
and this bead must not be used as a reason to touch .11.47's red.

## Acceptance

The comment names an enforcement account that is true at the commit that lands it,
cites what actually enforces each of the three cases, and no longer names a
deleted caller. Any discovered enforcement gap is filed as its own bead rather
than fixed inline.
close_reason: LANDED the justification replacement in deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql; no RAISE was added, per this bead's own ruling. All three structural legs were confirmed against the actual DDL before any edit: CHANGED is refused by the primary key at :327 PLUS the release_flows_immutable UPDATE trigger at :347-349 (the PK alone does not stop an in-place UPDATE, so the bead's own phrasing was imprecise and was not copied); REMOVED is refused by release_flows_delete_immutable at :350-352, with no cascade path and no DELETE anywhere in the tree; ADDED is permitted, both triggers being scoped BEFORE UPDATE and BEFORE DELETE only. *** THE COMMENT WAS WRONG IN A WAY THE BEAD DID NOT KNOW: it named the wrong files. A live application-tier divergence check DOES exist, in a third file the comment never mentioned -- services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs:305-321 locks FOR SHARE and calls verify_release_member (crates/control/provision/src/publish_release.rs:500-522) -- and it refuses as a ReleaseConflict, NOT with the catalog-release-content-conflict literal. So 'raise the SAME literal' was false even for the surviving check. The new text says so. *** Also measured and written into the comment: insert_release_flow_sql carries ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so the DB guarantees a divergent member is never STORED but not that the writer is TOLD; every caller was checked and there is NO silent-drop gap in production. The residual design question -- whether the two tiers should share one vocabulary -- is filed as wamn-0h0g.12.151, which existed before this reason was written. *** MY OWN HAZARD WARNING WAS WRONG AND THE LANE REFUTED IT: gate_registry.rs does NOT scan deploy/sql; its governed_files list at :755-767 does not include it. The test was run anyway and passes 10/10. *** The two wamn-0h0g.11.47 known-reds were re-run and are UNCHANGED, still failing at catalog_live.rs:101 and exposure_live.rs:157 on include_str pins over Rust files that were not touched; catalog_live panics PAST its six CATALOG_SCHEMA.contains pins, which is direct evidence the comment edit moved no pin.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): run_plane_reconcile_live is RED at HEAD -- a fifth invisible-red instance
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-19 during wave 7 integration, with a base control proving it pre-existing.

services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs::run_plane_reconcile_live fails at :947 with:
  seed persisted retired flow ordering keys: relation rp_live.flows does not exist  (SQLSTATE 42P01)

PROVEN PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY WAVE 7. The wave-7 tree gave 7 passed / 1 failed. The eight modified files were then reverted to HEAD, a FRESH postgres:18 container started, and the same target re-run: IDENTICAL RESULT -- same test, same line :947, same SQLSTATE, same 7/1 split. Files restored afterwards and verified byte-identical by sha256 manifest.

*** TWO SEPARATE MEASUREMENT TRAPS FOUND ON THE WAY, BOTH WORTH KEEPING: ***
  1. THIS SUITE MUST RUN WITH --test-threads=1. Run with default parallelism against one database it gives 7 FAILED / 1 passed, and every failure is a concurrency artifact, not a defect: six tests race on ALTER ROLE wamn_scenario_author and die with 'tuple concurrently updated', while two more collide creating schema catalog and relation runs. This is the cluster-wide-roles lesson in its sharpest form -- one fresh container is necessary but NOT sufficient, the suite also has to be serialized. A reader who ran it in parallel would report eight defects that do not exist.
  2. The genuine failure is invisible to every routine gate. run_plane_live self-skips on WAMN_CTL_PG_URL, so the sweep of record never runs it, and the recorded baseline (3 sweep reds) does not contain it.

THIS IS A FIFTH INSTANCE OF THE INVISIBLE-RED CLASS, after the two wave-6 reds, the shell-and-markdown callers of wamn-0h0g.12.141, and clippy-red-on-wamn-ctl at wamn-0h0g.12.144. The generalization now has enough instances to state plainly: *** A GATE THAT DOES NOT RUN IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A GATE THAT PASSES, AND THIS TREE HAS FIVE DIFFERENT MECHANISMS FOR NOT RUNNING ONE. ***

DIAGNOSIS NOT ATTEMPTED. rp_live.flows is the RETIRED wamn_run.flows relation, which is adjacent to wamn-0h0g.15.173 and wamn-0h0g.12.113 territory, so the fix may belong with them rather than standing alone. Deliberately not investigated further -- recording the measurement is the deliverable here.

ACCEPTANCE: run_plane_reconcile_live passes on a fresh postgres:18 with --test-threads=1, and the serialization requirement is recorded in the runbook so the next reader does not re-derive trap 1.
notes:
WAVE-8 MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-19 -- ROOT CAUSE FOUND, AND THE BRIEF IS OVERTURNED. THIS IS NOT A DEAD TEST TO DELETE; IT IS A LIVE TEST THAT LOST ITS FIXTURE.

WHY IT FAILS. partition_plane_authored_ordering_refusal_leg (services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs:934+) calls install_current_run_plane, then at :938 seeds INSERT INTO SCHEMA.flows. install_current_run_plane (:263-273) applies CATALOG_SCHEMA_SQL, RUN_STATE_SQL, AUTHORING_TESTS_SQL and RUN_QUEUE_SQL. NONE of them create a flows table -- deploy/sql/run-state.sql declares exactly seven tables (runs, invocation_admissions, node_runs, effect_attempts, effect_attempt_dispatches, effect_attempt_outcomes, operator_run_actions) and flows is not among them.

WHO DELETED IT. deploy/sql/flows.sql was deleted by wamn-0h0g.12.102 (e45ca35b, chore: delete the retired wamn_run.flows relation). flows is no longer one of RUN_PLANE_FILES, so no fresh install creates it.

*** THE REFUSAL PATH IS STILL LIVE PRODUCTION CODE. *** crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs still observes flows (:2044-2046, flow_graph_observable plus the lock_targets array) and still emits the DO retired_authored_ordering refusal for schemas that PHYSICALLY RETAIN the table. So the leg proves real behaviour and deleting it would lose coverage of a live refusal.

*** THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THE TREE AND THE SAME COMMIT WROTE IT. *** run_plane.rs:6515-6531 has fn add_legacy_flow_registry, whose doc comment says verbatim: the retired flow registry (deploy/sql/flows.sql), deleted by wamn-0h0g.12.102 (e45ca35b) ... an observation derived from the record no longer carries it -- but partition_plane_cutover_sql still locks and preflights it for schemas that physically retain the table, so THE FIXTURE MUST INJECT IT. e45ca35b updated the UNIT-test fixture and did NOT update the LIVE test. Textbook deletion collateral.

THE FIX, PRECISELY. Add a legacy installer to run_plane_live.rs following the house shape already there (install_legacy_partition_plane :275, install_legacy_child_run_state :303): CREATE the retired flows table in SCHEMA with the seven columns add_legacy_flow_registry declares -- tenant_id, flow_id, version, active, graph_json, created_at, updated_at -- and call it in partition_plane_authored_ordering_refusal_leg before the seed at :938. Do NOT re-add deploy/sql/flows.sql and do NOT put flows back in RUN_PLANE_FILES; the relation is retired by ruling and only the legacy fixture needs it.
close_reason:
Landed 976262b7 on deploy-simplification. run_plane_reconcile_live goes 7 passed/1 failed -> 8 passed/0 failed on a fresh postgres:18 with --test-threads=1. The fifth invisible-red instance is closed.

*** THE BEAD'S FRAMING WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE VALUABLE PART. *** The title reads as a missing relation to restore. It is not. deploy/sql/flows.sql was deleted by wamn-0h0g.12.102 (e45ca35b) and flows left RUN_PLANE_FILES, so no fresh install creates it -- but the refusal this leg proves is STILL LIVE PRODUCTION CODE. crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs observes flows via flow_graph_observable and the four-element lock_targets array, and still emits the retired_authored_ordering refusal for schemas that physically retain the table. DELETING THE LEG WOULD HAVE LOST COVERAGE OF A LIVE REFUSAL, which is the obvious reading of a red test naming a deleted relation.

ROOT CAUSE: e45ca35b updated the UNIT-test fixture and not the LIVE one. run_plane.rs:6515-6531 add_legacy_flow_registry exists precisely for this, and its doc comment says outright that the fixture must inject it. Textbook deletion collateral, and the same commit demonstrably knew about the problem in the other half of the tree.

FIX: a legacy installer in services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs following the house shape already there (install_legacy_partition_plane, install_legacy_child_run_state). DDL recovered from e45ca35b^:deploy/sql/flows.sql -- seven columns verbatim with types, nullability and defaults, plus the tenant_id CHECK and the PK. The two secondary indexes, RLS/policy and REVOKE are deliberately omitted, and the lane VERIFIED the omission is safe rather than assuming it: the reconciler never observes relrowsecurity or relforcerowsecurity, grant and owner observation is restricted to fixed relname IN lists that do not contain flows, and index handling is name-keyed rather than a drop-unrecognized sweep. That mattered because the leg ends on converged.is_noop(), where an extra unmanaged object would have failed it.

VERIFIED TWICE. Lane: base control at HEAD 7/1 failing exactly here, then 8/0 with the fix. Integrator, independently in the main tree on its own fresh container: 8/0. Both proved real execution via docker logs rather than a post-hoc query, because the legs drop their own schemas -- the refusal is logged with its STATEMENT and the lock target list is exactly rp_live.run_queue and rp_live.flows.

MUTANT re-derived and restored byte-identical by sha256 (22194fbdac3e84befd0ed4c3f07ca106535853179e21dfe39d251ec4d20717d7): removing only the installer call reproduces the original failure at the same seed with the same error.

NEW FACT WORTH CARRYING, found by the lane and in neither the bead nor the brief: the reason the OTHER SEVEN legs survived flows being deleted is a guard at services/ctl/src/reconcile_run_plane.rs:617-626, which runs count_retired_authored_ordering_rows_sql only when obs.tables for flows carries graph_json. The PRODUCTION path was updated defensively for the table's absence; only the live fixture was left behind. Without that guard the deletion would have broken every leg, not one.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(deploy): --plan-artifact-base defaults to the bare name registry:5000

title: [FINDINGS] decision(cdc): bound one project's slot WAL retention against co-tenant impact on the shared T3 pool
description:
FILED 2026-08-19 by the findings-ledger coverage sweep. The ledger's N.2 slot-WAL-exhaustion row states plainly that shared T3 WAL pressure affects co-tenants, and assigns that consequence to NO OWNER.

The three beads cited nearby each own something else: R29 / wamn-2jkm.47 owns slot and publication SHAPE convergence; R50 / wamn-2jkm.90 owns broker capacity and the outage chain; wamn-2jkm.46 owns credential blast radius. The cross-tenant consequence of one project's retained slot pinning WAL on a pool everyone shares is owned by none of them.

CONTEXT ALREADY RECORDED IN TREE: max_slot_wal_keep_size is 1GB and always-on since wamn-l5i9.32, so there IS a bound -- but the bound protects the CLUSTER by invalidating the slot, which converts a co-tenant capacity problem into a capture gap for the victim project. That is a policy choice nobody has made explicitly.

THE DECISION: who absorbs the cost when one tenant's stalled reader pins WAL on a shared pool. Options include per-project slot bounds, admission rules gating CDC to dedicated placement, or an explicit accepted-risk record. This is adjacent to wamn-2jkm.46's shared-pool CDC posture decision and may want to be ruled alongside it.

ACCEPTANCE: a recorded decision naming who bears the cost and what the enforcement point is.
notes: OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: ACCEPTED-RISK RECORD ONLY. The cross-tenant cost of one project stalled reader pinning WAL on the shared T3 pool is ACCEPTED for now. max_slot_wal_keep_size at 1GB (always-on since wamn-l5i9.32) protects the CLUSTER by invalidating the slot, and the resulting CAPTURE GAP for the victim project is the accepted consequence, now explicitly chosen rather than inherited. PER-PROJECT SLOT BOUNDS ARE DEFERRED TO A NAMED TRIGGER: THE FIRST REAL T3 TENANT. Admission rules gating CDC to dedicated placement are NOT adopted. RECORD-ONLY - no enforcement point is built this wave.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): clippy is RED at HEAD on wamn-ctl -- a fourth invisible-red class instance
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-19 during wave 7 integration, on a file the wave did not touch.

cargo clippy --locked -p wamn-ctl --all-targets -- -D warnings EXITS 101 at HEAD with two errors:
  function divergent_release_members is never used
  function index_release_members is never used
Both in services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs:746 and :760. divergent_release_members is pub(crate) and index_release_members is private; every caller of either is inside the #[cfg(test)] module at :886-896. So under a non-test build both are genuinely dead.

Running the same command with -A dead_code exits 0, which isolates these two as the entire finding.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN JUST FIXED: the disposition is a real question, not a mechanical one. Either the functions have a production consumer that was deleted -- in which case the deletion is the defect and the release-member divergence check silently stopped running -- or they are test-only helpers that belong behind cfg(test). THOSE TWO ANSWERS HAVE OPPOSITE REMEDIES and one of them is a behaviour finding, so it needs a read of what consumed them before .

*** THIS IS A FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE INVISIBLE-RED CLASS, and it widens the standing lesson. *** The recorded baseline says the sweep runs NO clippy and names wamn-runtime as the package to check, because that is where wave 6 found its regression. wamn-ctl was never checked and has been red for an unknown duration. notes:

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): an exported credential env var silently disarms the no-default guard tests
description:
FOUND 2026-08-19 during wamn-0h0g.12.141's measurement pass. Filed as a named target for that bead's close reason.

--app-password and --dispatch-reader-password both carry env = on their clap declaration (services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs), and clap counts an env-supplied value as PRESENT: clap_builder matched_arg.rs:135-138 returns false only for ValueSource::DefaultValue, so EnvVariable satisfies required_unless_present_any exactly like an explicit flag.

CONSEQUENCE: every guard test that asserts a missing credential FAILS TO PARSE stops guarding the moment WAMN_APP_PASSWORD or WAMN_DISPATCH_READER_PASSWORD is exported in the developer's or CI shell. The tests still report PASS -- they simply stop testing anything. Affected: the_app_password_has_no_default, the_dispatch_reader_password_has_no_default, and the new the_credential_free_modes_parse_without_either_password.

WHY THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL: docs/archive/build-and-test.md's own warning block instructs operators to export exactly those two variables.

SAME DEFECT CLASS AS THE ONE .12.129 REMOVED: a value nobody sets deliberately, satisfying a check nobody re-reads.

NOT TRIVIALLY FIXABLE: edition 2024 makes std::env::remove_var unsafe, so a test cannot simply clear the environment. Options to weigh: run the guard arms in a child process with a scrubbed env; assert on a clap Command built without the env source; or accept and document, with a CI assertion that neither variable is exported.

title: docs(ctl): the pre-role-bootstrap allowlist is a permission, not an ordering claim -- document and rename it
description:
FOUND BY WAVE-6 LANE 2 while fixing wamn-0h0g.20.9. Reported, deliberately NOT fixed -- out of that bead's scope.

services/ctl/src/reconcile_run_plane.rs:80-91 defines LEADING_CUTOVER_ACTIONS, which NAMES ExecutionPinCutover, implying the cutover should run first. But it only consumes a PREFIX of the action vector, and RepairHelperFunction / EnsureSchema are pushed EARLIER, so on the legacy path the pin cutover is never actually in that prefix.

*** THAT MISMATCH IS WHAT LET THE .20.9 CLOBBER HAPPEN AT ALL: *** the helper repair at run_plane.rs:3804 precedes the cutover push at :4319 in the vector, so turn 1 repaired the guard to canonical and the cutover then clobbered it back.

.20.9's fix makes the clobber HARMLESS -- the cutover now emits text identical to canonical, so ordering is no longer load-bearing for correctness. But the constant's INTENT and its BEHAVIOUR still disagree, and a future action added to the vector ahead of the cutover would silently reintroduce an ordering bug that the constant's name says is impossible. A name that asserts an ordering the code does not enforce is the doc-comment-as-mechanism class in constant form.
notes:
Not urgent BECAUSE .20.9 removed the consequence, which is exactly why it is easy to lose. File-and-forget risk is the reason this is a bead and not a comment.
MEASUREMENT PASS 2026-08-19, READ-ONLY. *** THIS BEAD'S CORE CLAIM IS FALSE, AND ITS PROPOSED FIX WOULD SILENTLY REGRESS WORKING CODE. DO NOT IMPLEMENT AS WRITTEN. ***

THE CLAIM REFUTED. ExecutionPinCutover is NOT a dead member of LEADING_CUTOVER_ACTIONS. It is reached AT INDEX 0 on the populated-refusal path, which is the only path the leading-prefix mechanism exists to serve. Chain: crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs:3493 computes execution_pin_cutover_needed; :3497-3511, if needed AND obs.run_rows or obs.release_flow_rows is nonzero, pushes ExecutionPinCutover into an EMPTY plan and RETURNS at :3510. So plan.actions == [ExecutionPinCutover], index 0, and reconcile_run_plane.rs:159 finds it with applied == 0. Two planner tests already assert exactly this (run_plane.rs:7630 populated_execution_pin_drift_refuses_before_every_other_action, and :7649 for the partial variant) and the live gate drives it through the real shell loop at run_plane_live.rs:803 and :848.

GIT HISTORY CONFIRMS THIS WAS THE CONST'S ORIGINAL AND ONLY PURPOSE. The loop was born at 4cb1d427 as a literal single-kind check on ExecutionPinCutover; 8d340b0c generalized it to a list and extracted the named const. Every later member was added TO it.

*** WHY FIX (a) IS ACTIVELY DANGEROUS. *** Removing ExecutionPinCutover from the const would make the populated-refusal path run ensure_wamn_app_role -- which CREATE ROLEs wamn_app, ALTERs wamn_scenario_author, and REVOKEs -- ON A DATABASE IT IS ABOUT TO REFUSE TO TOUCH. That breaks the property the mechanism protects: refuse before you mutate. AND NOTHING CURRENTLY TESTED WOULD CATCH IT. run_plane.rs:7630 is a planner test that never runs the shell; the live assertions at run_plane_live.rs:811-822 only check that COLUMNS are absent, which stays true because the refusal still raises. The regression is completely silent under the present suite. This bead's text names (a) as the obvious fix.

WHAT THE BEAD ACTUALLY OBSERVED, correctly but mis-titled: the SECOND push site at run_plane.rs:4319-4325 -- the empty-database path that really performs the migration -- is deliberately mid-plan and can never lead. That is BY DESIGN: :3881-3883 places catalog creates before it because runs now has immediate catalog FKs, and :4512-4528 places the generic AddColumn pass after it.

SECOND CATEGORY ERROR IN THE BEAD. It says this mismatch is what let the .20.9 clobber happen. IT CANNOT HAVE. The clobber was INTRA-VECTOR ordering (RepairHelperFunction at :3805 preceding the cutover at :4319). LEADING_CUTOVER_ACTIONS has NO influence on relative order within the vector -- contains() is order-insensitive, and the const's sole effect is WHERE ensure_wamn_app_role is called. Even if the empty-path cutover were allowlisted it would still sit behind the helper repair. The two facts are individually true and causally unrelated.

CONSEQUENCE: INERT. An operator sees nothing. Since .20.9 (a00c5d1a) collapsed the private guard and trigger copies onto the shared builders, the repair-then-cutover sequence emits byte-identical text twice and the clobber is an identity operation. Converges in one apply; run_plane_live.rs:783-786 proves it. *** PRIORITY SHOULD GO DOWN, NOT UP. ***

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION -- OWNER'S CALL, NOT A LANE'S: option (c), the const and the consumer are BOTH RIGHT and the defect is documentational. LEADING_CUTOVER_ACTIONS has ZERO doc comment and its name reads as an ordering assertion when it is a PERMISSION: these kinds may execute before the wamn_app role bootstrap because they are locked preflights that refuse. Remedy is a doc comment stating what the allowlist gates, that ExecutionPinCutover earns membership via the :3497 early return only, and that the array order is NOT execution order. Optional rename to PRE_ROLE_BOOTSTRAP_ACTIONS. Confined to services/ctl/src/reconcile_run_plane.rs, no spill.
EITHER WAY THIS BEAD'S TITLE AND DESCRIPTION MUST BE REWRITTEN OR IT MUST BE CLOSED AS NOT-A-BUG WITH THIS REASONING RECORDED. Leaving the text standing invites the harmful change.

TWO GENUINE RESIDUES WORTH KEEPING:
  (1) execution_pin_cutover_sql is the ONLY leading-allowlisted builder that references wamn_app -- GRANT INSERT/UPDATE on runs TO wamn_app at run_plane.rs:3184-3186. Every other allowlisted builder was checked and none touches it. So it is the sole place where 'leading' and 'needs the role bootstrap it is permitted to precede' collide. Unreachable in practice; belongs in the doc comment, not in code.
  (2) THE REAL UNGUARDED HAZARD is not what the bead describes. It is (i) a new refusal cutover pushed into the :3526-3660 window WITHOUT being added to the allowlist, so it mutates roles before refusing, or (ii) a non-allowlisted push interleaved into that window, which TRUNCATES the prefix and silently strips the pre-bootstrap property from every allowlisted action after it. Neither is guarded today.

PROBE ARM if any change lands: services/ctl/src/reconcile_run_plane.rs mod tests, a POSITIVE reachability assertion (the module currently has only negative-membership ones at :855 and :863) building a RunPlaneObservation with runs present and run_rows nonzero, asserting the plan is exactly one action, that it is ExecutionPinCutover, and that the allowlist contains it. Kills two mutants: deleting the const member, and deleting the :3497 early return -- the latter pins a cross-crate coupling nothing currently pins.

GAP FOUND IN THE LIVE GATE, worth its own bead: execution_pin_cutover_live asserts the refusal SQLSTATE and that no columns were added, but NOTHING ASSERTS THE ROLES WERE NOT CREATED OR HARDENED FIRST. That absence is precisely why fix (a) would land green.
PREMISE CORRECTION TO MY OWN MEASUREMENT NOTE, from the implementing lane, 2026-08-19. Recording it because I stated it more strongly than the code supports.

I WROTE, in the measurement note above: removing ExecutionPinCutover from the const would make the populated-refusal path run ensure_wamn_app_role on a database it is about to refuse. THAT IS TRUE OF MUTANT 1 (deleting the const member) but I ALSO ATTACHED IT TO MUTANT 2 (deleting the planner early return at run_plane.rs:3510), AND THERE IT IS WRONG. Deleting the early return does NOT let the bootstrap run first: the action is still pushed first and still allowlisted, so the loop still applies it at index 0, it still raises 55000, and reconcile still returns Err before the bootstrap. What the early return actually guarantees is that the refusal is the WHOLE PLAN -- 1 action, not 89 -- which is what dry-run reporting, is_noop and at_target depend on. The mutant does die, on plan.actions.len(), not on a role-mutation ordering violation. The lane wrote the probe doc to the accurate version rather than repeating my stronger claim, which is the correct call.

SECOND CORRECTION, mine to make: I described the members as locked preflights that refuse. That undersells two of them. VerifyEffectWriterRole and VerifyRunProjectionWriterRole are NOT cutovers and take NO lock -- they are pure DO blocks that RAISE 42501 or do nothing. So the old name LEADING_CUTOVER_ACTIONS was wrong twice over: it asserts an order it does not have, AND it calls two of its ten members cutovers when they are not.

THIRD, found by the lane unprompted and worth keeping: EffectWriterCutover has the IDENTICAL two-push shape -- a populated-ledger early return at run_plane.rs:3517-3521 plus a mid-plan push at :3656. Applying this bead's original reasoning to that kind produces the same false report. It is now documented in the const so the next reader does not refile it.

The wamn_app wrinkle I asked the lane to verify HELD, and it verified it by tracing all ten builders rather than trusting me: execution_pin_cutover_sql at run_plane.rs:3184-3186 is the only allowlisted builder whose SQL names wamn_app. It is additionally unreachable, because that builder leads only via the populated early return and its own preflight raises 55000 on exactly the nonempty tables that put it there -- so the GRANT is never reached.
close_reason:
Landed at 30300f70, as a DOCUMENTATION-ONLY change per the owner's 2026-08-19 ruling. The bead's original claim was FALSE and its named fix would have regressed the code; the title and body were rewritten before closing so the record does not keep inviting that change.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG: a const named LEADING_CUTOVER_ACTIONS with zero doc comment reads as an ordering assertion when it is a PERMISSION -- these kinds may execute before ensure_wamn_app_role because they refuse before they mutate, and that call is itself a write (it CREATE ROLEs wamn_app, hardens wamn_scenario_author, and REVOKEs). The property bought is refuse-before-you-mutate.

WHAT WAS NOT WRONG: ExecutionPinCutover is reached at index 0 on the populated-refusal early return, where it is the whole plan. Two planner tests and the live gate had been asserting that all along, and git history shows the loop was BORN at 4cb1d427 as a literal single-kind check on exactly this action.

DELIVERED: the doc comment; a rename to PRE_ROLE_BOOTSTRAP_ACTIONS (confined -- nothing outside the file referenced it, verified by grep across the workspace) plus the two test names for coherence; and the module's first POSITIVE reachability probe, which pins that the plan is exactly one action, that it is the pin cutover, that the allowlist contains it, and that the shell appends nothing behind it.

MUTANT RE-DERIVED AT INTEGRATION by doing precisely what this bead's text told a maintainer to do, including the tidy-up of the exactness test a maintainer would also make: 49 passed, 1 failed, and THE NEW PROBE IS THE ONLY TEST IN THE CRATE THAT CATCHES IT. Restore verified byte-identical by sha256. That number is the whole justification for the bead: before this commit, the change the bead recommended would have landed green.

VALIDATION: wamn-ctl 75 passed, 0 failed. clippy unchanged at its two pre-existing dead_code findings in publish_catalog.rs, tracked as wamn-0h0g.12.144.

TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS the lane made to the integrator's own measurement note are recorded in the notes above rather than buried here: the early-return mutant does not have the role-ordering consequence I attributed to it, and two of the ten members are not cutovers at all.

DEFERRED, NOT FILED, AND SAYING SO EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN CLAIMING A FILING: the two planner-side hazards the doc names -- a new refusing cutover pushed into the plan without being added to the allowlist, and a non-allowlisted push interleaved ahead of allowlisted ones, which truncates the prefix -- are NOT guarded. Guarding either means a test inside plan_run_plane in crates/schema/control, which was outside a documentation-only ruling and outside this lane's file domain. The natural shape is a planner-side test asserting every action emitted in the run_plane.rs:3526-3660 window is allowlisted, which needs the const exported across the crate boundary. THAT IS AN OWNER DECISION about crate boundaries, not a mechanical follow-up, which is why it is surfaced here rather than filed unilaterally.

title: fix(test): the production-claim fixture's runs guard is weaker than production DDL, and the divergence was load-bearing
description:
## Why

Found by the wamn-0h0g.20.4 lane while splitting the production-claim live suites, and confirmed at source by the integrator.

deploy/sql/run-state.sql:181-184 carries AND OLD.durability_class = 'durable' on the effect-attempt EXISTS leg of guard_run_admission_pins_immutable. The live fixture's stand-in guard, installed by install_schema in crates/platform/runtime/tests/common/mod.rs, DOES NOT carry that conjunct.

## Why it matters -- this was not cosmetic

The pre-split test's 'an attributed effect pins the release record' leg ran on run release-record, which is durability_class standard. *** UNDER PRODUCTION DDL THAT ERASURE WOULD HAVE SUCCEEDED AND THE expect_err WOULD HAVE FAILED. *** The assertion passed only because the fixture guard is weaker than the guard it stands in for. A proof that passes because its fixture is more permissive than production is asserting something production does not do.

wamn-0h0g.20.4 made that leg faithful by moving it to the durable suite on a durable run, so the assertion is now true for the right reason. IT DID NOT FIX THE UNDERLYING DIVERGENCE: the fixture guard still omits the class conjunct, so any future leg written against it can repeat the same mistake.

## Scope

Add the class conjunct to the fixture stand-in so it matches deploy/sql/run-state.sql:181-184. This is a behavioural fixture change and both live suites must be re-run against it -- they need a throwaway PostgreSQL 18, one container per suite, because the fixture creates a LOGIN role and PostgreSQL roles are cluster-wide.

## Related

wamn-0h0g.20.8 already records that this stand-in escapes the schema-drift guard entirely (it calls neither assert_run_state_stand_in nor assert_stand_in). The .20.4 lane established that bringing it under that guard is NOT cheap: the guard requires the spec to classify every schema-of-record table Required or AbsentByDesign, requires the stand-in to be spelled wamn_run.* where this one is wamn_claim_live.* (so install_schema must become a schema-parameterised DDL builder), and when runs is Required it demands every RunStatus literal appear, where this stand-in has no status CHECK and carries only dispatched and running. THIS BEAD IS THE CHEAP TARGETED FIX; .20.8 IS THE STRUCTURAL ONE. Landing .20.8 would subsume this.
acceptance_criteria: The fixture stand-in's admission-pin guard carries the same durability-class conjunct as deploy/sql/run-state.sql:181-184, and both production_claim_live and production_claim_durable_live still pass live against a throwaway PostgreSQL 18 with one container per suite.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-21 — TAKE THE TARGETED ONE-CONJUNCT REPAIR. This issue corrects the RC fixture now; it does not wait for the larger structural stand-in rewrite. wamn-0h0g.20.8 is the post-merge successor and the implementation commit for this issue must cite it so the targeted repair is not represented as the end state. IMPLEMENTATION PLAN NOT STARTED.
IMPLEMENTATION CHECKPOINT 2026-08-21: the exact one-conjunct fixture correction is applied in isolated lane w14-2011; both fresh-PG18 live suites and focused strict Clippy pass. Premise correction: M2011_REMOVE_DURABLE_CONJUNCT survives every existing assertion because the durable suite seeds only durable rows and the standard-ledger leg never exercises release clearing. A narrow proof can set then clear the existing standard-ledger release pair after its effect row exists: real guard succeeds, removed-conjunct mutant refuses. Owner authorization is required before adding that assertion; otherwise the patch is correct but unguarded. .20.8 remains the structural successor.
OWNER RULING CONFIRMED 2026-08-21: add the narrow standard-tier effect-plus-release-erasure assertion. It is the direct L4 mutant-killing proof for the repaired conjunct, not the broader .20.8 fixture rewrite. M2011_REMOVE_DURABLE_CONJUNCT must refuse the clear and fail the named leg; .20.8 remains the structural successor.
IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE 2026-08-21: fixture guard now includes OLD.durability_class = 'durable'; the existing standard-ledger live arm proves an attributed effect does not freeze a Standard run's release pair. Separate fresh PostgreSQL 18 standard and durable suites passed; strict focused Clippy passed. M2011_REMOVE_DURABLE_CONJUNCT failed at the exact standard release-pair clear with run-release-record-immutable and restored green. wamn-0h0g.20.8 remains the structural successor.
close_reason: CLOSED 4e0ae576: the stand-in release-pin guard now carries the production durability-class conjunct, and a live Standard-tier attributed-effect arm proves release-pair clearing remains legal. Separate fresh PG18 Standard/Durable gates and strict Clippy passed; M2011_REMOVE_DURABLE_CONJUNCT failed with run-release-record-immutable. wamn-0h0g.20.8 remains the structural successor.

title: [SR-MVP] test(integration): catalog_live and exposure_live assert a production-writer surface that no longer exists
description:
## Why

Two guards in the wamn-proof-integration LIB target assert that services/ctl/src/publish_catalog.rs and services/ctl/src/copy_project_env.rs contain named publication-boundary strings. Every one of those strings is now absent from BOTH files, so both tests fail in every ordinary workspace sweep. They are plain #[test] over include_str!, with no database and no ignore attribute.

  catalog_live::tests::ddl_pins_immutable_and_atomic_release_boundaries (tests/integration/src/catalog_live.rs:101) -- stages after-artifacts, after-members, after-journal, before-head.
  exposure_live::tests::ddl_and_both_production_writers_share_the_exposure_boundary (tests/integration/src/exposure_live.rs:157) -- register_release_exposure_manifest_sql, insert_release_source_sql, insert_release_attachment_sql, apply_release_exposure_sql, after-members.

## Measured, not inferred

The four stage strings occur NOWHERE in the tree outside catalog_live.rs itself. a1ecc789 deleted 1397 lines from publish_catalog.rs and 5bb69f0d deleted 889 from copy_project_env.rs; neither commit touched these guards.

Re-pointing them is not available as a simple repair. services/ctl/src/migrate_catalog.rs carries only two of the five exposure boundaries (register_release_exposure_manifest_sql at :573 and :756, apply_release_exposure_sql at :607) and carries no after-members; it copies sources and attachments with raw INSERT..SELECT rather than the builders.

## The separable finding, which is the more important half

insert_release_source_sql and insert_release_attachment_sql (crates/schema/control/src/sql.rs) and publication_boundary_sql now have ZERO production callers tree-wide -- their only remaining references are these tests and their own unit tests. The guard was proving that TWO production writers crossed the SAME exposure boundary. There is now one writer and two orphaned builders, so the invariant is not merely unpinned, it is no longer true in the shape it asserted.

## Scope

Rule whether the exposure boundary is still a contract worth proving and, if so, against which writer; then either re-anchor both guards or retire them explicitly. If retired, delete the orphaned PUBLISHER and COPIER consts at exposure_live.rs:8-9, which become dead. Separately rule whether the three zero-caller SQL builders are retained-for-future or deletable.

Deliberately NOT folded into wamn-0h0g.15.22: that bead regenerates and reconciles manifests, and the only mechanical repair here retires a guard, which is a decision. Sibling instance of the same class as wamn-0h0g.11.28, which names two DIFFERENT gates (orphan_guard_live, ri_orch_live).
acceptance_criteria: Neither guard asserts against a deleted surface; whatever exposure-boundary invariant survives is proven against a writer that actually exists, or its retirement is recorded with a reason.
notes:
*** OWNER RULING, dkk 2026-08-19: RULE THE DIVERGENCE FIRST. ***
Option chosen verbatim: "Rule the divergence first."

THE RULING. Before this bead's guards are retired, re-anchored, or repaired, ONE prior
question must be decided: is it INTENDED that services/ctl/src/migrate_catalog.rs
copies release sources and attachments with raw INSERT..SELECT instead of going through
the shared publication-boundary builders? Both other dispositions PRESUPPOSE an answer
to that question, which is why neither could be chosen first.

WHY THE QUESTION IS PRIOR, AND WHY IT IS NOT A FORMALITY. This bead's own measurement
records that migrate_catalog carries only two of the five exposure boundaries
(register_release_exposure_manifest_sql at :573 and :756, apply_release_exposure_sql at
:607), carries no after-members stage, and copies sources and attachments with raw
INSERT..SELECT rather than the builders. The retired guard asserted that TWO production
writers crossed the SAME exposure boundary.

*** SO THE GUARD MAY NOT BE OBSOLETE. IT MAY BE CORRECTLY RED. *** If the surviving
writer bypassing the shared builders is UNINTENDED, then the boundary has silently
diverged -- one path through the builders, one path around them -- and that divergence
is exactly what the guard existed to catch. Retiring it in that case would RATIFY the
defect and record the ratification as a cleanup. That is the false-coverage shape this
program chases, in its most expensive form: a red turned green by deleting the
instrument.

If instead the raw INSERT..SELECT is the deliberate shape of migrate_catalog, then the
two-writer invariant is genuinely no longer true as asserted, retirement is correct,

IMPLEMENTATION AUTHORIZED

title: decision(router): WiringEdge.to_port is authored but the router has nowhere to put it
description: Found by the EXE wave-3 lane 2 (wamn-0h0g.18.5) while mapping the authoring document onto the router graph. The catalog's WiringEdge carries to_port: Option<String> ('Target input port. Absent means the component's single declared input'), but the router's own WiringEdge has NO to_port field — it routes by the EMITTING node's port alone. So a document that names a target input port is silently ignored by the walk. Either to_port is load-bearing and the router needs somewhere to put it, or it is vestigial and should leave the document before wirings become tenant data people rely on. The same lane found WiringNode.interface_version is likewise dropped, but that one is defensible: the router's NodeCall has no interface-version field because late binding holds it elsewhere.
design: Retain and honor WiringEdge.to_port. An explicit target port is carried through lowering and the router walk and is validated against the target component interface. Omission is accepted only when the target declares exactly one input; ambiguous omission is a typed validation refusal. Inference is therefore shorthand only where ambiguity is structurally impossible, never a guess.
acceptance_criteria: An explicit ruling: to_port is either honoured by the walk or removed from the authoring document, with the deciding reason recorded.
notes:
OWNER RULING CONFIRMED 2026-08-21: typed wiring requires explicit routing whenever ambiguity is possible. The banked catalog-to-router compiler and router graph must carry this field; silently dropping it is forbidden.
GIT RECEIPT 73535346: empty-tree decision commit records the ratified to_port contract without bundling active live-document changes.
close_reason: RATIFIED: retain and enforce to_port. Explicit target selection is required whenever multiple inputs exist; omission is legal only for a structurally single-input target, and ambiguous omission refuses during validation.

title: fix(router): route() panics on a node-data ApplyError instead of failing the walk
description: Pre-existing, predates EXE wave 2, surfaced by the wamn-0h0g.16.3 lane. crates/execution/router/src/lib.rs:99 uses .expect(..) on the apply result, which turns ApplyErrorKind::InvalidContext — a node returning a non-object context replacement, i.e. GUEST DATA, not a host bug — into a router panic. A guest that returns the wrong shape should fail its walk, not take down the router. The .16.3 lane widened the expect message rather than the behaviour and deliberately routed its new emit failure around the panicking surface (MissingDedupId takes the ordinary error edge instead). Fix: fold a data-shaped ApplyError into a walk failure and keep the panic only for genuine host-invariant violations.

PREMISE CORRECTION — THE BEAD UNDERSTATES ITS OWN BLAST RADIUS BY 3x. It names only InvalidContext. THREE of the six ApplyErrorKind variants are reachable from route() and are node data, not host bugs, and all three panic the router at base: InvalidContext (a node returning a non-object context replacement), RespondWithoutCaller (a respond wiring meeting an ingress path-2 stream delivery with caller_attached: false) and SecondVerdict (a fan-out into two terminals). Fixing only InvalidContext would have satisfied the bead's first sentence and violated its own second acceptance clause, so all three are fixed. Each was reproduced FIRST at base f7e96856 with a #[should_panic] test printing the real panic at lib.rs:116:22. Three new typed FailureKind variants; ApplyError::node_data_failure() matches ApplyErrorKind EXHAUSTIVELY so a seventh variant cannot compile without a decision. 5 named tests in the new crates/execution/router/tests/route.rs. Wiring::apply's atomic refusal is unchanged and invalid_replacement_is_atomic still passes untouched. Integrator independently re-derived the mutant: InvalidContext arm -> None repanics at lib.rs:129:26 with the original message across 3 tests; restore byte-identical (e4ed99f3). title: decision(contracts): the JSON-to-WIT value projection is an invented contract that must be frozen once
description: Proved by the wamn-0h0g.16.9 spike. WIT has NO canonical JSON projection, so the variant, result, flags, char and f64 encodings the spike used are HOST INVENTIONS. Under a TYPED per-component seam the SDK, the router and the studio must all agree on one projection the platform mints and freezes. Known lossy points measured: JSON has no char (a one-code-point string is the only encoding); NaN and infinities are legal f64 and illegal JSON, so they become null and the type is destroyed; option<option<T>> is inexpressible under null-means-none; u64 above 2^53 does not survive a non-Rust JSON producer. Also worth carrying into either ruling: the spike caught all five injected type errors with a path such as at spec.window tuple arity 1 != 2, which shows dynamic dispatch does NOT remove runtime shape-checking at the edges, it RELOCATES it. Dissolves if wamn-0h0g.16.9 is ruled UNIFORM, where config json is already the declared carrier.
acceptance_criteria: Either wamn-0h0g.16.9 is ruled uniform and this closes as dissolved, or a single JSON-to-WIT projection is specified, frozen, and shared by SDK, router and studio.
close_reason: DISSOLVED by the wamn-0h0g.16.9 ruling (owner, 2026-08-18): option (a), the uniform seam with types moved to the layer that renders. All three questions arise ONLY under the per-component typed-WIT reading — .16.11 sizes WIT subtyping that wasmtime does not provide, .16.12 handles resource-carrying WIT signatures that cannot be type-cached across instances, and .16.13 adjudicates a JSON-to-WIT value projection that is a host invention because WIT has no canonical JSON projection. Under the uniform seam none of the three has a subject: port schemas are JSON Schema, checked by JSON-Schema compat at wamn-0h0g.18.3, and no arbitrary author-declared WIT type is ever marshalled. If wamn-0h0g.16.9's named reopen trigger fires — a consumer needing WIT-level composition, e.g. WAC fusion — these three reopen with it; the wave-2 spike's findings on each are preserved in .16.9's notes.

title: fix(cache): a per-digest component cache must key on ComponentExportIndex, never on export name
description: Proved by the wamn-0h0g.16.9 spike and worth recording regardless of how that decision is ruled. ComponentExportIndex::lookup compares component.inner.id == self.id, so a cached export descriptor used against the WRONG component digest returns None — index-based lookup is SELF-FENCING. Name-based lookup is NOT: it will happily resolve a different component's identically-named export. Any per-digest cache the router or host keeps over component exports must therefore key on the index rather than the name, or a digest mix-up degrades from a clean miss into a silent wrong-component call.
acceptance_criteria: Any per-digest export cache in the tree keys on ComponentExportIndex, with a named test proving a descriptor from one digest does not resolve against another.

Fixture WAT parsing, targeted rustfmt, and cached diff checks pass; the isolated focused Cargo build was capped in third-party dependencies before project source.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(connections): bring postgres stores under the connection-generation model
description: The wamn:postgres connection is OUTSIDE the credential-generation authority model today: per-project database_url from env/K8s Secret keyed by a flat wamn.project config key (pool.rs:23-40, mod.rs:159-218); connection_generations covers requirement_type='http' only (connection_generation.rs:16-19). Add a postgres requirement_type and a wamn:connection/postgres contract descriptor so a DB store is an instance with staged, validated, activatable generations like HTTP; the plugin resolves its project pool through the binding->active_generation snapshot instead of an env URL. Delivers "requirements bound in target, generations never travel" for the store the developer surface actually uses.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(components): the standard nodes return as ordinary palette components
description: The nine language builtins retire; their useful subset returns as ordinary, separately-published palette components with typed WIT ops (http-request over wamn:connection/http, transform, conditional-shaped routing expressed as ports, respond/emit as router terminals rather than nodes). Scope the initial set to what wirings demonstrably need; each is an ordinary library citizen (digest-pinned, import-audited, gate-tested) with no language privileges. The entity component is separate (epic V).
design: Publish the minimal initial ordinary component palette: http-request and transform only. Conditional behavior remains wiring composition, not component code. Respond and emit remain router terminal dispositions under the .16.25 ruling. Do not add entity, conditional, response, emission, standard-node compatibility, or palette abstractions beyond these two admitted components.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly http-request and transform are admitted, published, digest-addressed ordinary components through the production validator/publisher path. Their typed schemas, imports, operation identity, and digest facts pass the same tenant admission contract as any future component. Conditional behavior is represented only by wiring, and respond/emit only by router terminals. No other legacy standard-node executor or compatibility carrier is introduced.
close_reason: Implemented by 88ef99b8: exactly transform and http-request now build as ordinary no_std components, use exact governed WIT capabilities, carry typed admission declarations, and publish through wamn-ctl push-component.

title: [SR-MVP] V — Generated APIs: entity component and generate crud
description:
exe-model.md §Developer surface — one pattern, three grammars: authoring automation emits ordinary gated artifacts; nothing generated is gate-exempt or reflection-served. generate crud walks the applied catalog and emits, per relation, five wirings (http-entry -> entity.<op> -> respond), their route attachments, and auto-written cases — arriving gate-green by construction. The entity component (standard library, platform-authored) is the wirer's generic data node: relation and filter spec as declared parameters, RLS enforcing row/tenant scope. One generic component = one warm pool across every CRUD route. Regeneration is emit-if-absent. Per-relation typed codegen is the demand-gated alternative.

GROUNDED FACTS: the audited kernel exists and is complete — crates/data/entity-access (1,261 LOC: List/Get/Create/Update/Delete, Compare/Like/In filters, sort, pagination caps, one-level expansion, $n-bound, catalog-allowlisted identifiers) — but as a host-side library reached through a retiring standard node. LIVE CORRECTNESS HOLE (independent of the spec): compiled RLS policies key on app.role/app.user_id (crates/schema/compiler/src/rls/compile.rs:46-57) but production CLAIM_SQL injects only app.tenant/statement_timeout/search_path/app.runner (wamn_postgres/claims.rs:359-363), so every per-user/per-role policy silently DENIES in production — the P0 child fixes this regardless of the rest. Route naming reuses impact/mod.rs:249-262 api_resources_for so generator and impact report cannot disagree.

title: [SR-MVP] test-support: the PUBLIC-CONNECT posture is hand-duplicated across live preambles

to lack it. The same shape also governs
crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs:5162,5189, which refuses
effect-writer-role-out-of-bounds / run-projection-writer-role-out-of-bounds on the same

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): run_plane_live::from_zero_leg drops cluster-wide roles its siblings need
description:
## Why -- a SECOND instance of the wamn-0h0g.11.28 class, previously unknown

services/ctl/tests/run_plane_live.rs:2868-2906 (from_zero_leg) runs
DROP OWNED BY wamn_app; DROP ROLE wamn_app; DROP OWNED BY wamn_scenario_author;
DROP ROLE wamn_scenario_author; and then asserts CLUSTER-WIDE that neither role exists.

THREE distinct exposures:
 1. DROP ROLE fails on cross-database dependencies -- DROP OWNED BY is PER-DATABASE, so a
    role owning objects in another database cannot be dropped. Measured on the sibling
    instance: "role wamn_app cannot be dropped because some objects depend on it / DETAIL:
    1 object in database otherdb".
 2. the assertions read a CLUSTER-WIDE fact that any concurrent sibling binary can flip.
 3. it DELETES roles every sibling gate depends on -- so it is a CONTAMINATOR as well as a
    victim, and it interacts with the shared-WAMN_CTL_PG_URL contention filed separately.

## Scope

Draw this leg's hermeticity at cluster scope: scope the teardown to objects it created, or
give the binary its own cluster. Same class as wamn-0h0g.11.28 (grant_confinement_live).

## Boundary

This leg's role teardown and its assertions.
acceptance_criteria:
from_zero_leg passes on a cluster where wamn_app owns objects in another database; a
concurrently running sibling gate is not broken by it; the whole run_plane_live binary is
green with -- --test-threads=1 on a shared cluster.
close_reason: Completed in fa4d0d95: from_zero_leg preserves the shared wamn_app and wamn_scenario_author roles, runs against an empty current-database schema, and pins cross-database ownership sentinels for both roles before/after reconcile. Exact rustfmt and diff checks pass.
