title: [SR-MVP] fix(schema): catalog.release_flows has no immutability trigger
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.29 welds tested_resolution_map evidence derived from the release manifest's
member plan hashes, and its retry-stability argument depends on those members not moving:
an exact retry must recompute identical bytes or it refuses itself as EvidenceConflict.

Member append-only-ness is a property of the PUBLISH CODE PATH, not of the schema.
deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql:89-104 defines catalog.release_flows with NO
immutability trigger; the guarantee rests on insert_release_flow_sql being
`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and on a source audit forbidding UPDATE in that module.

A direct UPDATE from outside step A could therefore move a plan hash under an existing
evidence row, silently invalidating evidence that is supposed to be immutable.

Raised by the wamn-0h0g.15.29 lane as a caveat on its own correctness argument -- unchanged
by that bead, and explicitly flagged as wanting an owner's eye.

## Scope

Decide whether release_flows earns a row-immutability trigger of the kind
runs_admission_pins_immutable provides, or whether the code-path guarantee is accepted and
recorded.

## Boundary

The immutability guarantee for release_flows members. Does not change the publish path.
acceptance_criteria:
Either a trigger refuses an UPDATE to a released member's plan hash, proven by a named
test and a mutant, or a recorded decision that the code-path guarantee suffices with the
reasoning stated in the DDL.
close_reason: INVALID PREMISE (evidence-only): release_flows UPDATE/DELETE immutability predated this filing—56f9e1a6/deadbc863 in catalog-schema and be601c16 in control-portable-store; current exact trigger fingerprints remain generated in architecture/protected-writes.json. No implementation change.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): give the dispatch reader a per-project-env identity
description:
## Why -- the residual blast radius wamn-0h0g.12.66 deliberately did not close

wamn-0h0g.12.66 minted wamn_dispatch_reader on the same CLUSTER-GLOBAL shape as wamn_app, because
mirroring the existing pattern was the smaller change and the confinement it delivers (35 writes ->
0) is the large win. But a leaked reader credential still reads run_queue and effect_attempts in
EVERY project database on the cluster, not one.

A per-project-env reader would cut that to a single database. It is expressible today: the projects
file already carries one URL per project, so the credential is already per-project at the manifest
layer -- only the role is shared.

This is the same axis as wamn-0h0g.12.64 (scope cluster-global wamn_app credentials) and should
probably be decided together with it rather than separately; .12.64 is blocked on wamn-0h0g.15.88's
scope-hash re-key, and a per-project reader would likely want the same generation machinery.

## Also unresolved on this role, and worth deciding in the same breath

The reader has NO A/B generation pair; its password is create-time only, the same gap wamn_app has.
wamn-0h0g.12.66 did not solve it because the dispatcher's credential is mounted config rather than a
saga-managed slot. If a per-project-env identity lands, rotation should land with it.

## Boundary

The reader's identity scope and rotation. Its ratified read surface is settled and is not reopened.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded ruling on whether the dispatch reader is per-project-env or cluster-global, and if
per-project-env, its provisioning, its generation pair, and a proof that a credential for one
project database cannot authenticate to another.
notes:
SPLIT EXCLUSION 2026-08-21 — DISPATCH ALREADY HAS ITS OWN PRINCIPAL FAMILY. This issue remains the sole owner of dispatch-reader project-environment identity and rotation; the ratified read surface is not reopened. Reuse wamn-0h0g.13.59 generation machinery and the cross-project authentication floor rather than copying lifecycle SQL. It is not absorbed by wamn-0h0g.22.4 and is not one of the run-queue mutation operation owners because the dispatcher principal is read-only. The final wamn_app retirement uses it only as a regression control. OPEN, UNCLAIMED, POST-MERGE; implementation not started.
SEQUENCING SUPERSESSION 2026-08-21 — Earlier POST-MERGE / wait-for-wamn-0h0g.15.25 text is superseded by the owner's active rule: all scope-reduction and authority work lands before the single final RC and merge. This issue no longer waits on .15.25; .15.25 waits on it. Scope, priority, acceptance, and product semantics are unchanged.

description:

title: [SR-MVP] test(ctl): the publish_catalog live tests are not safe under the default parallel harness
description:
## Why -- measured at wamn-0h0g.15.163's integration

The publish_catalog `#[test]`s that take WAMN_MIGRATE_PG_URL all share ONE database and interfere
under the default parallel test harness. Three consecutive runs of the identical tree, differing only
in database freshness and --test-threads, produced FOUR failures, then ONE, then ZERO.

  cargo test -p wamn-ctl --all-features --lib                       -> 54 passed, 4 failed
  (re-run, dirty db)                                                -> 57 passed, 1 failed
  fresh db, -- --test-threads=1                                     -> 58 passed, 0 failed

None was a code defect. But a suite that fails nondeterministically under its own default invocation
will bite the wamn-0h0g.15.25 release candidate, and worse, it trains the reader to re-run until
green -- which is how a real failure gets dismissed.

## Scope

Give each live test its own database or schema, or mark the shared-database set to run serially, so
the default invocation is deterministic. Whichever is chosen, the suite must be green on a FRESH
database at default parallelism, not only at --test-threads=1.

## Boundary

Test isolation only. No production code.
acceptance_criteria:
cargo test -p wamn-ctl --all-features --lib against a fresh database at DEFAULT parallelism is green
and repeatable across three consecutive runs; re-running against the same database is also green.
close_reason:
Landed bedd5d56 on deploy-simplification (lane commit 91499213).

The publish_catalog live tests are deterministic at DEFAULT parallelism. TWO independent
causes, not one -- the second was not in the bead and serialization alone would NOT have
met the acceptance criterion:
1. the tests all rebuild the fixed `catalog` schema and cargo runs a binary's tests in
   parallel threads, so they interfered. Now serialized on a LIVE_DB mutex.
2. every_failed_publication_boundary_... used a FIXED tenant (release-retry-{index}) and
   COMMITS, so it was non-idempotent: green on a fresh database, red on the re-run. That
   is why the original report saw 4 failures, then 1, then 0 -- freshness was doing work
   that --test-threads was getting credit for.

INTEGRATOR RE-VERIFICATION (independent): cargo test -p wamn-ctl --all-features --lib at
DEFAULT parallelism, three consecutive runs on three FRESH databases:
  ok. 59 passed; 0 failed   (x3)
plus a re-run against a DIRTY database: ok. 59 passed; 0 failed. Both halves of the
acceptance criterion met in the integration tree.

The lane also reproduced the original red first (55 passed; 4 failed) before fixing, so
the fix is pinned to an observed failure rather than to a theory.

title: [SR-MVP] test(ctl): five live-gate sites skip silently instead of failing loudly
description:
## Why -- found during wamn-0h0g.12.20's integration; PRE-EXISTING at a46f23ec

services/ctl's `orphan_guard_live` (:227) and `ri_orch_live` (:219) both drive publish_catalog::run,
which wamn-0h0g.8.18 CLOSED: it bails at :131 with CONTROL_DEFINITION_PUBLISH_REFUSAL before any I/O
and its whole body carries #[expect(unreachable_code)]. Both gates therefore fail with
control-definition-publish-requires-wamn-0h0g.15.14.

*** THE REASON THIS WENT UNNOTICED IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: both gates SKIP SILENTLY when
WAMN_CTL_PG_URL is unset, so they report success in any run that does not provide a database. They
are not red in CI; they are absent from it, while presenting as passing. ***

That is the same failure class as wamn-0h0g.12.103 one level up: a verification artifact reporting
success without executing its subject. wamn-0h0g.15.137 already owns that class as a general rule;
this is a concrete instance with two named victims.

## Scope

Re-anchor both gates onto whatever replaces the closed verb (wamn-0h0g.15.14 landed
mint_release_manifest in publish_release.rs), or mark them ignored with a named blocker so their
absence is visible. Then make the skip loud: a live gate that cannot reach its database should say so
in a way a CI reader notices, not exit 0.

## Boundary

The two gates and their skip behaviour.
acceptance_criteria:
Neither gate drives the closed publish_catalog::run; a run without WAMN_CTL_PG_URL makes their
non-execution visible rather than reporting success; a run with it exercises the live path and passes.
notes:
THIRD INSTANCE, FOUND 2026-08-19 WHILE UNBLOCKING wamn-0h0g.15.173.

services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs is a THIRD gate driving the closed
publish_catalog::run. install_project_database calls it to materialize the
application-family witnesses and receives
control-definition-publish-requires-wamn-0h0g.15.14.

*** THIS ONE IS NOT MERELY SILENT -- IT BLOCKS WORK. *** That gate is the ONLY
generator for architecture/protected-writes.json (WAMN_UPDATE_PROTECTED_RELATIONS),
so wamn-0h0g.15.173 cannot regenerate the manifest, and
protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership stays red until this bead
re-anchors the install onto the live carrier.

Measured on throwaway postgres:18.6 at 12b8d2b0: with wamn-0h0g.15.172's fingerprint
fix and this bead's two fixture repairs, install_control_database now succeeds
COMPLETELY. The refusal is the next step, install_project_database, and it is the
only thing between the branch and a regenerated protected-writes.json.

So the scope line "re-anchor both gates onto whatever replaces the closed verb"
now covers THREE gates, and the third has a dependent.

*** THE EDGE FROM wamn-0h0g.15.173 TO THIS BEAD WAS MEASURED AND REMOVED, 2026-08-19.
THIS BEAD IS NO LONGER THE ROOT BLOCKER OF THE RELEASE CANDIDATE. ***

Owner-authorized sequence: measure the edge first, because "when a chain looks inverted, the
suspect is the chain". The edge was SOFT. It encoded WHO OWNS THE EDIT (a scope-hygiene
judgement recorded in 12b8d2b0's commit body: "re-anchoring the install onto the live carrier
is that bead's scope, not a fixture repair"), NOT what must be true. Full mechanism and
citations are on wamn-0h0g.15.173.

*** THE RE-PRICING FALLBACK IS THEREFORE NOT TRIGGERED. This bead was NOT re-priced, and
priority was NOT inherited through a dependency edge -- the standing wave-8 principle stands
untouched: PRIORITY PRICES RISK; IT DOES NOT INHERIT THROUGH DEPENDENCY EDGES. ***

=====================================================================
BUT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND THE P2 LABEL IS STALE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.
RAISED FOR THE OWNER, NOT ACTED ON.
=====================================================================
1. *** BOTH NAMED VICTIMS ARE ALREADY REMEDIATED -- BY THIS BEAD'S OWN COMMIT. *** a1ecc789
   (chore(wamn-0h0g.11.28): delete the closed publish-catalog verb, 2026-08-18) deleted
   ri_orch_live.rs outright and removed the publish half of orphan_guard_live.rs, re-anchoring
   it onto migrate_catalog::run. NEITHER GATE NAMED IN THIS BEAD'S TITLE DRIVES THE CLOSED
   VERB AT HEAD. So the title now over-describes what is left.
2. WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS under this label is (a) loud-skip hardening -- orphan_guard_live.rs
   :179-180, :286-287, :436-437 and protected_relations_live.rs:894-895 still eprintln and
   return -- and (b) a THIRD gate's call-site swap, which arrived BY NOTE, not by this bead's
   title or acceptance criteria.
3. *** MY OWN SKETCHED PRICING RATIONALE WAS WRONG AND THE LANE REFUTED IT. *** I had framed
   the dependent red as invisible-red class. IT IS NOT.
   protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership is a PURE STATIC COMPARISON OF TWO JSON
   FILES, needs no database, and fails in ordinary CI at protected_relations.rs:204 on the
   undeclared app-schema wamn_catalog row. It is VISIBLE, not silent, and is not a member of
   this bead's class at all.
4. DURATION OF SILENCE, measured: ABOUT 20 HOURS, not a long-standing invisible red. The
   refusal landed 2026-08-17 15:21 (4bee577a, which introduced
   CONTROL_DEFINITION_PUBLISH_REFUSAL); this bead was filed 2026-08-18 11:32 during .12.20's
   integration.

SO THE LABEL PRICES A SUBJECT THAT IS LARGELY FIXED, while the note it carried was the RC's
apparent root blocker. The staleness was a CONSEQUENCE of the edge, not an independent
finding -- which is why removing the edge, not re-pricing, was the right first move.

OPEN AND UNRESOLVED, for the owner: whether this bead should be re-titled and re-scoped to
what actually remains (loud-skip hardening plus deleting the now-fully-dead
publish_catalog::run and PublishCatalogArgs once .15.173 swaps the last call site), or split.
NOT ACTED ON.

ONE FURTHER FACT THE OWNER MAY WANT: once .15.173 swaps its call site, publish_catalog::run
and PublishCatalogArgs have ZERO callers outside their own two unit tests and become fully
deletable. a1ecc789's body says they were retained solely for "an unlisted live caller,
services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs".

*** RE-SCOPED AND RE-TITLED BY OWNER RULING, 2026-08-19. THE OLD TITLE DESCRIBED WORK THAT WAS
ALREADY DONE. ***

Old title: "two live gates drive the closed publish_catalog::run and fail silently in CI".
BOTH NAMED GATES WERE ALREADY REMEDIATED BY THIS BEAD'S OWN COMMIT a1ecc789 (2026-08-18):
ri_orch_live.rs was deleted outright -- CONFIRMED, the file does not exist -- and
orphan_guard_live.rs had its publish half removed and was re-anchored onto migrate_catalog::run.
A title that describes completed work is the false-coverage shape at bead grain, which is why
the owner ruled re-scope rather than leave-as-is.

=====================================================================
WHAT THIS BEAD NOW OWNS: FIVE SILENT-SKIP SITES. VERIFIED BY THE INTEGRATOR, NOT INHERITED.
=====================================================================
  services/ctl/tests/orphan_guard_live.rs:180  WAMN_CTL_PG_URL unset -- skipping the D24
                                               orphan-guard gate
  services/ctl/tests/orphan_guard_live.rs:287  WAMN_CTL_PG_URL unset -- skipping the
                                               wamn-0h0g.12.119 refusal gate
  services/ctl/tests/orphan_guard_live.rs:390  WAMN_CTL_PG_URL is not a TCP url -- skipping the
                                               RLS-filtered arm
  services/ctl/tests/orphan_guard_live.rs:437  WAMN_CTL_PG_URL unset -- skipping the
                                               wamn-0h0g.12.119 precision control
  services/ctl/tests/protected_relations_live.rs:895  WAMN_CTL_PG_URL unset -- skipping
                                               protected-relation PostgreSQL gate

*** COUNT CORRECTION: FIVE, NOT FOUR. *** The wave-9 measurement lane named four sites
(orphan_guard 179-180, 286-287, 436-437 plus protected_relations 894-895) and MISSED
orphan_guard_live.rs:390, which skips on a DIFFERENT CONDITION -- the url is present but is not
a TCP url. That one matters more than the others precisely because it can fire on a machine
where the env var IS set, so an operator who believes they configured the gate still gets a
silent pass. Verified directly by the integrator against the working tree at 53afb31a.

Each site prints one stderr line and returns, so it REPORTS PASS. That line is invisible
without --nocapture. This is mechanism 2 of the standing invisible-red class: a gate that does
not run is indistinguishable from a gate that passes.

=====================================================================
WHAT THIS BEAD NO LONGER OWNS
=====================================================================
THE CALL-SITE SWAP IS NOT THIS BEAD'S WORK. protected_relations_live.rs:327 is the last
remaining caller of the closed publish_catalog::run tree-wide -- confirmed, it is the only hit
in services/ctl/tests. That file is wamn-0h0g.15.173's own gate, and the wave-9 edge measurement
established that re-anchoring it is .15.173's work, not a precondition owed by this bead. The
dependency from .15.173 to this bead HAS BEEN REMOVED on that basis.

THE FOLLOW-ON DELETION IS FILED SEPARATELY. Once .15.173 swaps that call site,
publish_catalog::run and PublishCatalogArgs have zero callers outside their own two unit tests
and become fully deletable. That is separate work with its own green state and is filed as its
own bead rather than kept here as a subsection.

=====================================================================
PRICING NOTE, FOR THE RECORD
=====================================================================
This bead was NOT re-priced. The wave-9 measurement found the P2 label had been stale in both
directions, but the fix was to correct the EDGE and the TITLE, not the number -- and the
standing principle stands untouched: PRIORITY PRICES RISK; IT DOES NOT INHERIT THROUGH
DEPENDENCY EDGES. For the record, the silence here was measured at ABOUT 20 HOURS (the refusal
landed 2026-08-17 15:21 in 4bee577a; this bead was filed 2026-08-18 11:32), not a long-standing
invisible red. And the red that appeared to depend on it,
protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership, is a PURE STATIC COMPARISON OF TWO JSON
FILES that fails visibly in ordinary CI -- it is not a member of this bead's class at all.

ACCEPTANCE, RESTATED: each of the five sites either fails loudly, or is converted to an
explicit ignore-gate whose absence of an env var is a hard error rather than a pass. The
distinction matters -- run_state_live already demonstrates the loud shape (ignore-gated plus
expect, so it fails at 101 rather than passing) and is the model to copy.

OWNER RECONCILIATION 2026-08-21: this issue is the sole implementation owner for all five ctl live-gate silent-skip sites. It absorbs the exact orphan_guard_refuses_then_proceeds skip clause from duplicate wamn-0h0g.15.169; that issue is superseded before either lane is claimed. The green state is explicit ignored gates in ordinary sweeps plus fail-loud behavior when an ignored gate is invoked without a valid PostgreSQL configuration.
IMPLEMENTATION CLAIM 2026-08-21: isolated lane w15-1128 owns only services/ctl/tests/orphan_guard_live.rs and protected_relations_live.rs. It will not run the generated registry update or edit architecture/docs/archive.
LANDED 2026-08-21 in 37dfffd5. title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): the release-manifest mint gate false-reds on any cluster carrying wamn_scenario_author
description:
## Why -- measured during wamn-0h0g.15.14's integration, on the integrator's own machine

services/ctl/tests/release_manifest_mint_live.rs bootstraps hermetically PER DATABASE: it drops and
recreates every schema and creates wamn_system and wamn_control_author. *** BUT POSTGRESQL ROLES ARE
CLUSTER-WIDE, NOT PER-DATABASE, AND THE CONTROL STORE'S AUTHOR-BOUNDARY GUARD READS A CLUSTER-WIDE
FACT. ***

deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql:1188-1191 fires
control-author-authority-boundary-violated when

    EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles
             WHERE rolname = 'wamn_scenario_author'
               AND pg_catalog.has_database_privilege(oid, current_database(), 'CONNECT'))

In a stock PostgreSQL database PUBLIC holds CONNECT, so the moment `wamn_scenario_author` exists
ANYWHERE in the cluster this arm is true for every database in it and the bootstrap refuses.

REPRODUCED EXACTLY: running the wamn-0h0g.12.103 gate first (whose preamble creates
wamn_scenario_author) and the mint gate second, in one postgres:18 container on separate databases,
turns the mint gate RED with control-author-authority-boundary-violated. A fresh container makes it
green. The gate is correct; its hermeticity boundary is drawn at the wrong scope.

## Why this matters beyond one machine

Any real deployment HAS wamn_scenario_author -- deploy/sql/postgres-init.sql:27 creates it. So this
gate can only pass on a cluster that does not resemble production, and it fails in a way that reads
like a code defect rather than an environment one. That is the worst kind of false red: it will be
"fixed" by someone changing the guard.

## Scope

Make the preamble hermetic at CLUSTER scope for the facts the guard reads -- either revoke PUBLIC
CONNECT on the test database (which is also the production posture,
crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs revoke_public_connect_floor_sql) or drop/neutralise
wamn_scenario_author's CONNECT for the duration. Audit the other live gates for the same class:
any gate whose bootstrap asserts a cluster-wide role fact is per-database-hermetic only.
close_reason:
Landed 78352f22 on deploy-simplification (lane commit 23595aff).

release_manifest_mint_live now establishes the PRODUCTION posture at CLUSTER scope
before bootstrapping: establish_control_connect_posture() constructs the contaminated
cluster deliberately (creates wamn_scenario_author exactly as postgres-init.sql does,
restores PUBLIC's stock CONNECT), asserts the guard's fact is TRUE, revokes PUBLIC
CONNECT on current_database(), asserts it is FALSE. The guard is untouched -- which was
the point, since the bead warns this false red "will be fixed by someone changing the
guard".

TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS, both correct: (1) scoped to current_database(), NOT
revoke_public_connect_floor_sql(), because that builder loops EVERY database in the
cluster and would have made this gate reach across its siblings -- the same bug in
reverse. (2) ONE statement, because effect_writer_generation_live.rs:456 asserts
public_connect_databases_sql() is empty CLUSTER-WIDE; a grant-then-revoke in two
statements would commit an observable window. Measured, not reasoned: a concurrently
sampling session read 0 throughout (before/during/during/after), and 1 with the block
absent.

INTEGRATOR RE-VERIFICATION (independent, and on a GENUINELY contaminated cluster rather
than a constructed one -- my integration container had accumulated wamn_scenario_author
from earlier gate runs, with has_database_privilege(...,'CONNECT') = true on a fresh
database): the mint gate PASSES. Baseline sha256 reproduced to the lane's value exactly,
702fd9bb170d926f01cde33d3746ec7e231dcf9f84db0eb089eaa1f35e38850f. Mutant removing the
posture call -> 246a24dd1074d4cb8b0df828a6869760d08d3383be219bc5c044a49bdb1ed1de
reproduced the ORIGINAL false red verbatim: SqlState(E42501)
control-author-authority-boundary-violated. Restored exactly; gate green again.

MUTANT M3 (role-scoped REVOKE FROM wamn_scenario_author) SURVIVED and was therefore NOT
shipped -- nothing in the repo grants that role database CONNECT directly, so no probe
could kill it. The bead's "or drop/neutralise the role's CONNECT" alternative is
measurably dead code here.

AUDIT DELIVERED (the acceptance asked for a list, not fixes). VULNERABLE and MEASURED:
control_portable_store.rs's control_portable_store_applies_twice_...; management_live;
and *** control_author_two_tenant_authority_holds_on_postgres, which is ALREADY RED ON
EVERY STOCK POSTGRESQL TODAY -- line 1087 asserts NOT has_database_privilege(author,
current_database(), 'CONNECT'), which PUBLIC's stock grant makes unconditionally false.
Same root cause, opposite polarity, same one-line remedy; proven by revoking PUBLIC
CONNECT and watching the binary go 5 passed. *** VULNERABLE BY CODE, UNRUN and not
claimed: authoring_loop_live. DIFFERENT FACT, MEASURED: grant_confinement_live's
cross-database DROP ROLE, plus a SECOND instance the bead did not know about,
run_plane_live::from_zero_leg. NOT VULNERABLE, verified: protected_relations_live,
terminalize_effect_uncertain_live, run_plane_live's main preamble (all three already
revoke PUBLIC CONNECT), and effect_writer_generation_live -- where the lane's own
hypothesis was DISPROVED by measurement (CREATE DATABASE leaves datacl NULL, so
acldefault() re-grants PUBLIC CONNECT regardless of template1).

ALSO CORRECTED: the #[ignore] gotcha does not apply to the two gates in the acceptance
(they gate on an env var and skip with eprintln!). It DOES apply elsewhere and it bit the
lane -- #[ignore = "reason"] does not match a bare #[ignore] grep.

All audit items filed as beads.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): impact-report silently understates blast radius when registrations are unreadable
description:
## Why -- the third instance of the wamn-0h0g.12.103 collapse

services/ctl/src/impact_report.rs:134 guards the registration read with table_present and contributes
NO registration edges when catalog.event_registrations is absent. The same read is subject to the
FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY silence: a non-bypassing identity reads zero rows with no error.

The consequence is milder than its two siblings -- the report is ADVISORY output, not an effect --
but it is the wrong kind of mild: an impact report that understates blast radius WITHOUT SAYING SO is
worse than one that refuses, because an operator uses it to decide whether a destructive migrate is
safe. A silently-empty registration edge set reads as "no flows are affected".

Note impact_report connects on args.admin_database_url, a superuser connection (module docstring at
:5), so the RLS arm is not reachable through the shipped verb today. The ABSENT arm is.

## Scope

Either refuse by name, or -- better for an advisory verb -- report the unreadable registration set
explicitly in the output so the operator sees that the edge class was not evaluated. Decide which and
say why; do not leave the silence.

## Boundary

The registration edge only. Sibling of wamn-0h0g.12.103 and the D24 orphan-guard bead; all three
share one mechanism and should share one remedy shape.
acceptance_criteria:
An impact report against a database whose registration set is absent or unreadable either refuses by
name or states in its output that registration edges were not evaluated; a named test pins the chosen
behaviour; the report never silently reports zero registration edges for an unreadable set.

title: [SR-MVP] test(conformance): no workload manifest may put a database URL in a component environment
description:
## Why -- an invariant that is TRUE TODAY and asserted NOWHERE

wamn-0h0g.12.65's acceptance requires that "no guest receives a connection secret". Nothing checks it.

services/host/src/host.rs:229-233 builds DynamicConfig with copy_environment(true), which merges a
component's DECLARED LocalResources.environment into its wasi:config/store view (wash-runtime
crates/wash-runtime/src/plugin/wasi_config/mod.rs:144-155 iterates
component_handle.local_resources().environment).

*** PRECISION THAT MATTERS AND THAT A FIRST MEASUREMENT GOT WRONG: this copies the COMPONENT's
declared environment, NOT the host process environment. It does not leak WAMN_PG_URL today. The
hazard is a MANIFEST-AUTHORING one -- a future manifest that puts a database URL in a component's
localResources.environment hands it to the guest, silently and by construction. ***

Today no manifest does: deploy/platform/materializer.example.yaml:84-93 carries only WAMN_MAT_*,
and flow-http-workload.example.yaml carries none. So the invariant holds and the test would be
green on landing -- which is the cheapest moment to write it.

## Boundary

A static manifest guard. Does not change host behaviour or any grant. Route it AWAY from
tests/conformance/tests/dispatcher_boundary.rs while wamn-0h0g.12.66 holds that file.
acceptance_criteria:
A conformance test walks deploy/platform/*.yaml and, for every localResources.environment block,
refuses any key matching the database-URL name set (*_PG_URL, DATABASE_URL, or any key whose value
parses as a postgres URL); a mutant adding such a key to a manifest fails that NAMED test.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION CLAIM 2026-08-21: isolated lane w15-12117 owns only tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs and the component-localResources environment guard. No manifest or authority change.
LANDED 2026-08-21 in c16c4dac. The existing WorkloadDeployment/localResources walk now refuses component environment DATABASE_URL and *_PG_URL keys, including empty placeholders, plus neutral keys whose scalar parses as postgres/postgresql. Host process env and arbitrary Secret fields remain outside the boundary; errors never echo URL credentials. title: [SR-MVP] fix(test): the system-cluster guard trips on prose, not on request paths
description:

no_data_plane_manifest_references_the_system_cluster does a RAW substring check for
wamn-sysdb / wamn_system across every deploy manifest. Its own docstring scopes the invariant to

title: [SR-MVP] chore(deploy): suspend the superuser-credentialed reconcile CronJob by default
description:
## Why

deploy/platform/replica-identity-reconcile.example.yaml runs every five minutes mounting the
postgres-fixture-superuser Secret. The AUTHORITY question -- least authority vs risk acceptance vs
deleting the recurring job -- is wamn-0h0g.12.70 and remains unruled.

What is landable independently of that ruling is making application a DELIBERATE ACT rather than a
side effect of applying the platform tier. A CronJob is a self-renewing grant with a mutable spec:
an attacker who can patch cronjobs (a far weaker permission than get secrets) obtains superuser
execution inside the database on a timer, with no interactive session and no Secret read.

On-demand runs are unaffected -- kubectl create job --from=cronjob/... bypasses suspend -- so the
documented manual path still works.

## Boundary

suspend: true plus a comment naming wamn-0h0g.12.70. Does NOT touch
deploy/platform/postgres.yaml's Secret, which is shared with run-plane-reconcile and the f1-provision
Job and whose fixture pod is frozen. Does not resolve the authority question.
acceptance_criteria: Applying the platform tier no longer starts a five-minute superuser cadence; the suspend carries a comment naming its owning bead; on-demand invocation still works; the shared fixture Secret is untouched.
close_reason: [7fdd7235] suspend: true plus a comment naming wamn-0h0g.12.70, which still owns the unruled authority question. The exposure that matters is NOT cadence but STANDING-NESS: resting exposure is identical to the one-shot Job, which mounts the same Secret with byte-identical wiring, and patching cronjobs is a far weaker permission than reading secrets while yielding superuser DB execution on a timer. On-demand runs unaffected (kubectl create job --from=cronjob bypasses suspend). postgres.yaml's Secret deliberately untouched -- shared with run-plane-reconcile and the f1-provision Job, fixture pod frozen. NOTED, not fixed: this file also carries a dangling reference to deploy/poc/f1-provision-job.yaml (deleted by wamn-0h0g.12.2 / 3554f140) and mounts a ConfigMap f1-fixtures that is not defined anywhere under deploy/ -- if so the job could not have run successfully even before the suspend, which makes suspending strictly safer.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(run-plane): delete wamn_run.flows, the retired mutable registration path
description:
## Why -- OWNER RULING R10, 2026-08-17

wamn_run.flows has NO writer anywhere in the tree; architecture/state-owners.json records
writers: []. Its writer was DELETED, not delegated -- the immutable release path

The owner ruled that tests/conformance/tests/protected_relations.rs:178-184 ('no static writer
=> must be author-SQL writable') WAS NEVER RATIFIED -- writers: [] was only ever EVIDENCE
toward 'authors own it', never a definition, and this relation is the counterexample the
theorem was always exposed to. The revoke lands under the amended predicate; THIS bead is the
disposition.

## Scope

Delete deploy/sql/flows.sql; remove FLOWS_SQL from RUN_PLANE_FILES (run_plane.rs:71, :1820),
the flows CheckSpec (:478), the retired-authored-ordering DO guard (:2096-2120),
select_active_flows_sql (crates/schema/control/src/sql.rs:284) and its one caller

(crates/execution/run-state/src/queue/sql.rs:440, zero callers) and its re-export at

being the permanent answer

`retired` is a TRANSITIONAL classification and a FORWARDING ADDRESS, not a parking permit. Its
population should trend to ZERO. Any relation sitting in `retired` past its named successor's

title: [SR-MVP] rename(catalog): release_manifests names a thing that carries no manifest
description:
## Why -- OWNER RULING R6, 2026-08-17

wamn-0h0g.15.159 drops members_json, leaving catalog.release_manifests with
(tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, verified_publisher_principal). The owner ruled the
table KEEPS ITS PLACE but its NAME IS NOW A LIE -- the exact flow-tests.sql situation that
earned a rename bead last time, and un-filed name-lies are how the next seven-collision
cluster starts.

THE ANSWER IS PRE-LOADED. This bead is a RENAME-AND-DOCUMENT, not a redesign. Do not
re-derive whether the table should exist; the owner already did, and the derivation is:

The retained row is THE RELEASE IDENTITY ROW, with three jobs.
1. IDENTITY / IDEMPOTENCY ANCHOR. Publish step A is idempotent on (draft, report); it needs
   one row whose insert IS the 'release exists' event, so ON CONFLICT verify-identical makes
   retry-never-remints STRUCTURAL rather than checked. A release whose existence is only the
   presence of member rows has no single row to conflict on, and idempotency degrades to
   counting.
2. PUBLICATION PROVENANCE. verified_publisher_principal is minted inside the publish
   transaction, attested by the verb that verified the PAT. No member row can carry it -- it
   is a fact about the PUBLICATION EVENT, not about any flow. Evidence rows record test
   lineage, not publisher identity.
3. MEMBERSHIP FK ROOT. catalog.release_flows FKs to it, which is what makes 'member of a
   release that does not exist' unrepresentable -- the same role execution_bundles plays for
   plan references. wamn_run.runs also FKs to it, so the run plane's release pin is enforced
   against this table.

## Scope

Rename to catalog.releases under the greenfield rule -- call it what it is. Its doc comment
states the three jobs above, so no future lane reads 'manifests' and goes hunting for bytes
that live in ServingManifest.

Touch surface measured 2026-08-17: deploy/sql/catalog-schema.sql, deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql
(both the DDL and the 17-relation retained-shape list), deploy/sql/run-state.sql (the runs FK),
crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs (~20 mentions incl. RUNS_RELEASE_FK_DEF and
RELEASE_PUBLISHER_CHECK_NAME/DEF), architecture/state-owners.json, architecture/protected-writes.json,
the portable-store inventory arrays, and every fixture.

## Boundary

Rename and document only. No column changes, no semantics changes, no FK topology changes.
The retained-shape fingerprint moves and must be recomputed against a live PostgreSQL.
acceptance_criteria: catalog.release_manifests is renamed to catalog.releases across DDL, Rust, registries and fixtures with no semantic change; its doc comment names the three jobs (identity/idempotency anchor, publication provenance, membership FK root); the retained-shape fingerprint is recomputed; versions remain 0.1/0.1.0.
notes:
PARALLEL COLLISION (2026-08-23, main f282fe83): this rename necessarily touches architecture/protected-writes.json (live-PG regenerated shape fingerprint) and crates/execution/run-state/tests/admission_live.rs (release seed SQL), both owned by the frozen .12.118 implementation lane. Deferring either would fail .15.162's all-surfaces/repin acceptance, so do not split it around that lane. This is a temporary file collision, not a semantic dependency; no Beads dependency added. Reclaim after .12.118 integrates.
PARTIAL AT WAVE 57. The rename landed across 27 files as commit 3a8b338c on deploy-simplification, with three digests recomputed against a live throwaway PostgreSQL rather than guessed: deployment-attestation constraints and the retained-shape fingerprint both moved, and the release-evidence fingerprint was UNCHANGED, which is the control proving the throwaway install reproduced the canonical shape. The sorted catalog inventory also moved because under C collation releases sorts after release_sources. OWED, AND ONLY THIS: architecture/protected-writes.json is not regenerated. The tool refuses before writing, blocked on catalog.execution_bundles being declared live in state-owners.json while no DDL creates it - see the note added to wamn-0h0g.15.173, and the execution-bundle retirement wamn-0h0g.26.6. Until then tests/conformance/tests/protected_relations.rs protected_relation_table_matches_declared_ownership fails with undeclared protected relation catalog.release_manifests. That is the one new failure this work introduces and it is exactly the repin the bead names. DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED, flagged as possible follow-up: catalog.register_release_manifest the routine, release_manifest_exists_sql, push_release_manifest.rs, release_manifest_mint_live.rs - routine and gate identifiers, not the relation. ALSO CONFIRM: this is a GREENFIELD rename with no in-place migration. A database provisioned before it will not upgrade; ensure_catalog_storage refuses loudly with catalog release storage is partially installed rather than corrupting anything.
OWNER CONFIRMED 2026-08-24: GREENFIELD IS CORRECT. No ALTER TABLE RENAME TO. Pre-RC every database is disposable and the loud refusal from ensure_catalog_storage is the right failure mode. The rename stays a pure rename. Do not add a migration.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): serve the in-cluster registry over TLS so host groups can use runtime.ociCaPaths
description:

values.yaml:258-273 at daba602 says --allow-insecure-registries "does not relax

runtime.ociCaPaths, retiring --allow-insecure-registries.

Live kind cluster is frozen; this is a manifest + values change proven at the RC.
Filed by lane 3 of wave 10.

MEASURED CORRECTION: chart_seam_governance is the ONLY test in the repository that reads either YAML, and validate_workload_policy's poolSize guard never sees them - it runs only over the two example WorkloadDeployment manifests in the inventory, not all of deploy/platform. title: [SR-MVP] chore(egress): decide the RunnerEgress client-pool scope under the pooled allocator
description: Measured at daba602 and independently verified: RunnerEgress is installed on the STORE's Ctx (crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs, both arms of one match on a single Ctx::builder), and the fork's Ctx path consults a HostHandler ONLY through CtxHttpHooks::send_request / CtxHttpHooksP3::send_request (engine/ctx.rs:509, :572). The workload lifecycle hooks fire only for a handler registered as the ENGINE's HTTP handler (host/http.rs:1231, :1259), so RunnerEgress's hooks are UNREACHABLE as wired, and the 60s-idle-lingering premise does not hold — `inner` owns its WorkloadClients outright and is dropped with the Store, so drop is the invalidation. Decide whether the pool is per-store (today's shape: isolation-first, drop-invalidated, hooks decorative) or engine-scope shared (both hooks load-bearing). docs/exe-model.md adds the input that sharpens this: the pooled allocator is adopted platform-wide with instance REUSE off, so every delivery on the hot route path takes a fresh store at microsecond cost and a per-store connection pool amortizes across nothing — while a shared pool must answer the credential-generation and per-attempt-authority isolation the authority model rests on. Owner ruling wamn-0h0g.13.48 (DefaultOutgoingHandler::default(), private per-instance quota registry, isolation-first) is the INPUT to this decision, not overturned by it.
acceptance_criteria: The pool's scope is decided and recorded, the .13.48 isolation ruling is either reaffirmed or explicitly revised, and RunnerEgress's lifecycle hooks are either load-bearing or documented as contract hygiene.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(fork): expose ResolvedWorkload::call_concurrency and add a HostHandler bind hook
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.37 forwarded OutgoingHandler::on_workload_unbind but could NOT
forward on_workload_bind, because the figure it needs is unreachable. Two
independent walls, both verified at daba602:

(a) ResolvedWorkload::call_concurrency is `pub(crate)` (engine/workload.rs:1563),
    and its chain is closed too -- WorkloadComponent.instances is pub(crate) on a
    pub(crate) InstancePool.
(b) The apparent public workaround does NOT typecheck: WorkloadMetadata::component()
    (workload.rs:478) returns `&wasmtime::component::Component`, while
    InstancePolicy::from_component (instance_pool.rs:55/:184) takes
    `&crate::types::Component` -- the wire type carrying pool_size /
    max_invocations / max_concurrency. The engine consumes that wire type at
    engine/mod.rs:554 and drops it.

Also: HostHandler declares no bind hook at all. Its registration hook is
on_workload_resolved(&ResolvedWorkload, &str), which carries no concurrency figure.

## Scope

In the fork: promote ResolvedWorkload::call_concurrency to pub, and add a
defaulted `async fn on_workload_bind(&self, resolved: &ResolvedWorkload,
component_id: &str) -> anyhow::Result<()>` to HostHandler, called from
HttpServer::on_workload_resolved alongside the existing
outgoing_handler.on_workload_bind (host/http.rs:1231). Then wamn forwards
faithfully with no duplicated derivation.

## Boundary

Only worth doing if the bind half becomes load-bearing -- see the sibling
engine-scope decision. Rejected alternatives, recorded so they are not retried:
re-deriving in wamn (impossible via public API), and forwarding a documented `1`
(buys nothing, since 1 is DefaultOutgoingHandler's effective behaviour anyway,
while planting a number that reads as authoritative). Filed by lane 6 of wave 10.
acceptance_criteria: The fork exposes the concurrency figure and a HostHandler bind hook, and wamn's RunnerEgress forwards on_workload_bind faithfully with the fork fields cited.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(host): decide whether wamn exposes a host-loopback enable at all
description:
## Why

LocalResources.allowed_host_loopback_ports (fork types.rs:134,
Arc<[AllowedLoopbackPort]>) is dead surface in wamn: a workload grant is inert
without the host's own enable, and wamn has no way to set that enable (sibling
bead). So the gate's negative assertion currently passes by ACCIDENT of
configuration rather than by policy.

Note the door is genuinely narrow: resolve_connect checks
internal_names::is_host_sentinel FIRST (policy.rs step 1), so only
127.255.255.254 (HOST_SENTINEL) or its v4-mapped form reaches it. Plain
127.0.0.1 falls to step 2 and returns Plane::Virtual with no egress policy
applied.

## Scope

Either wire an operator-visible enable with --allow-host-loopback semantics, or
record the decision to keep the door permanently shut -- so the refusal is
policy, not accident.

## Boundary

Coverage of the grant surface already landed with wamn-0h0g.15.52. Filed by
lane 5 of wave 10.
acceptance_criteria: wamn either exposes a host-loopback enable, or records the decision to keep it shut, and the gate's refusal cites that decision rather than the absence of configuration.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): audit bare-substring guard needles that are ordinary English or collide with an upstream path
description:

`use wash_runtime::host::allowed_hosts::AllowedHost;`, so any future legitimate
use of that upstream module in the wash host trips a guard about deleted INLINE
execution. The obvious intermediate narrowing to `allowed_hosts:` does NOT fix
it, because `allowed_hosts::AllowedHost` contains `allowed_hosts:` -- the first
colon of the `::`. Only the `pub `-prefixed field form separates them, which is

ordinary word, or that is a prefix of an upstream module path. Start with the

Narrow each to a code shape, or justify keeping it bare, and record the reason
at the needle so a later wave does not re-broaden it.

## Boundary

This is the repo-wide sweep of the same class. Filed by lane 4 of wave 10.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): contract-diff proves its argv against a fake cargo and is never run for real

`cargo test --manifest-path <root> --locked --offline -p wamn-runtime --test

guards are green. And `tools/contract-diff run` was not invoked during wave 8

execution, so the two together read as coverage.

Does not change the seven legs' contents. Umbrella is wamn-0h0g.15.136's
sibling theme bead. Filed by lane 4 of wave 10.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(deploy): keep instance reuse off on component hosts, per capability
description: Carried fork commit fc4d2b22 (wamn-g2br.16) adds WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING, which clamps every component to InstancePolicy::Ephemeral at the single wire-decode point, because upstream v2.7.0 (03d621c0, 630f84d3) serves concurrent and linked calls on WARM pooled instances — so a store and its linear memory can survive across calls for any workload whose link closure sets pool_size > 0. Verified at the pin: the string appears NOWHERE in this repository — no manifest, no values file, no Dockerfile, no docs — so the per-delivery isolation guarantee is unenforced in deployment. docs/exe-model.md keeps exactly this mechanism and sharpens it: the pooled ALLOCATOR is adopted platform-wide (pre-initialized modules, fresh instances at microsecond cost, per-component-digest pools shared across wirings), while instance REUSE stays off until windowed state ships with explicit affinity, and the kill-switch narrows from per-host to per-capability. Set it and record it where the host BoM is recorded — deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml runtime.hostGroups[].env (which already carries WAMN_PG_URL and WAMN_EVT_NATS_URL) and/or deploy/platform/runner.yaml — scoped to the hosts that instantiate palette components rather than to the retiring flowrunner. Semantics before choosing a value: env-only by design so a manifest cannot override it, and a set-but-unparseable value FAILS CLOSED. Live kind cluster is frozen: landing the manifest and the record is in scope, rolling it is not.
design:
Found while writing the carried-commit ledger row for `fc4d2b22` during
wamn-0h0g.15.20. The commit message says "Set this on wamn flowrunner hosts",
which is a deploy obligation with no home in the repo -- exactly the class that
must become a bead rather than a note (workflow-rule-file-all-deferrals-as-beads).

The fork-side switch is at crates/wash-runtime/src/engine/instance_pool.rs in the
daba602 checkout (+68 lines, one wire-decode clamp plus a warn so an ignored
pool_size is visible). Clamp, not reject, was deliberate: a hardening flag must
not turn deploys into outages, and an ephemeral store per call is always a
correct way to serve them.
acceptance_criteria: Every host manifest that instantiates flowrunner sets WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING, and the host BoM records it.
notes:
Deferred out of wamn-0h0g.15.20, whose scope is the pin itself. The pin does
carry the ledger row that documents the switch; this bead carries the deployment.
close_reason:
CLOSED AS REFUTED 2026-08-23 by the wave-53 measurement pass. Instance reuse is ALREADY OFF three independent ways, so the bead's premise does not hold:
1. wash-runtime decodes pool_size <= 0 to InstancePolicy::Ephemeral (fork daba602, instance_pool.rs:227-231) and NO manifest in this repo sets poolSize.
2. tests/conformance/src/runtime_inventory.rs:611-616 validate_workload_policy fails the build on any nonzero poolSize in deploy/platform/*.yaml, with a negative mutation test at :794-799.
3. wamn's own pool pins INVOCATIONS_PER_INSTANCE = 1 (crates/execution/host/src/pool.rs:60).

Three further premises are individually false:
- The named target deploy/platform/runner.yaml DOES NOT EXIST; deleted by ea71c1c4 (.26.7.2).
- The claim that WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING appears nowhere in the repository is false; it is in docs/archive/platform/wash-runtime-fork.md. Only the deploy half of that claim holds.
- The suggested landing site deploy/infra/values-wamn.yaml runtime.hostGroups[].env does not exist; that file sets hostGroups: [] deliberately per ruling .13.50.
- The claim that per-delivery isolation is unenforced in deployment is refuted by item 2 above.

RESIDUAL CARRIED, NOT DROPPED: the single belt-and-braces env entry WAMN_DISABLE_INSTANCE_POOLING on deploy/platform/values-host-default.yaml hostGroups[0].env is folded into wamn-0h0g.17.3, which already opens that exact YAML block. Per capability had no referent: the fork flag is documented env-only with no per-workload config (instance_pool.rs:123-127), and exe-model.md contains no per-capability kill-switch language.

The structural successor is wamn-0h0g.17.13, which deletes the bespoke pool outright in favour of wash-runtime InstancePolicy.

title: [SR-MVP] test(runtime): equality-export retained executor-plugin WIT type identities
description: Three retained executor-plugin no-trap guests fail Wasmtime component validation because named WIT types are reconstructed structurally inside imported instance types instead of being equality-exported and referenced through the imported type identity. The three repaired tests are no longer ignored, validate under the pinned Wasmtime component model, enter the real host call, and observe their mapped typed error rather than a trap. Logging equality-exports level. title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): --exact makes every gate-mutant campaign silently vacuous when its gate test is renamed
description:
## Why — this is the mechanism, not another instance

Found independently by two lanes in wave 9 (wamn-0h0g.15.121 and .15.124).

Every gate-mutant script runs its gate as
`cargo test ... <TEST_NAME> -- --exact`. When TEST_NAME does not exist, cargo
runs ZERO tests and EXITS 0. The harness reads exit 0 as "the mutant was not
killed" and reports SURVIVED. So a renamed or deleted gate test converts a real
guard into misleading evidence — it reads as coverage and proves nothing.

This is strictly worse than a dead anchor: a stale EXPECTED_SHA exits 2 and
refuses to start, LOUDLY. A missing gate test is silent.

## Measured

wamn-0h0g.15.121 found two campaigns in this state (capture-mode.sh's
default-draft-capture-off, unconditional-publish-gate.sh). wamn-0h0g.15.124
found the same class again. Both were repaired by writing the missing tests, but
the MECHANISM is untouched and will recur.

## Scope

One-line hardening per script in `run_gate`: assert the gate actually ran at
least one test — e.g. parse cargo's `running N tests` line and refuse on N == 0,
or add a `--list` existence probe to the `check` verb. Converts the whole failure
class from misleading-green to hard error.

## Boundary

Touches all ~37 gate-mutant scripts, so it must not ride a wave that has lanes
editing individual scripts. Related to wamn-0h0g.15.125 (39 of 40 campaigns are
referenced by nothing) — that bead is about campaigns nobody RUNS; this one is
about campaigns that run and lie. Fix .15.125 first and this one starts
mattering immediately.

Deleted, not repaired, at 5c47074b. Owner ruling 2026-08-18: this branch is
simplification and mutation testing is out of scope, so the honest resolution of the whole
gate-mutant cluster is rm, not five repairs.

Measured at 78afe665 before any repair work: 37 scripts / 6390 lines; 146 baseline pin sites
over 48 target files; 117 of 146 pins STALE; ONLY 4 OF 37 CAMPAIGNS COULD EXECUTE AT ALL
(authoring-cli-collection-drift, authoring-cli-unmounted-green, authoring-smoke-collection-drift,

title: [SR-MVP] fix(exec): a corrupted plan transfer is classified retryable, so the run requeues forever
description:
## Why

crates/platform/runtime/src/plan_artifact.rs maps EVERY pull_blob error to
PlanFetchErrorKind::Unavailable -- including oci-client's
OciDistributionError::DigestError, which is exactly the corrupted-transfer case.

runner_plan_supply.rs:368 then maps Unavailable -> PlanSupplyFailureKind::
Unavailable, whose documented disposition is "release and requeue".

## Consequence

A registry serving a blob that does not hash to the descriptor it arrived under
makes the run REQUEUE FOREVER against the same corrupt blob. Re-fetching only
ever yields the same bytes. The integrity disposition wamn-0h0g.15.12's
acceptance table assigns to a hash mismatch NEVER FIRES.

It also contradicts Unavailable's own doc comment ("could not be reached in
time, or holds no artifact under this name").

## Measured

PlanFetchErrorKind::Mismatched ALREADY EXISTS and its doc says "Not retryable
and not a transport fault" -- the correct destination. oci-client 0.17.0 digests
every blob it streams against the descriptor (client.rs:1290-1297,
digest.rs:93-99), verified by reading the dependency source, so a body that
disagrees surfaces as DigestError.

## Scope

One transport_kind() classifier mapping DigestError -> Mismatched and everything
else -> Unavailable, plus its two call sites (manifest pull and blob pull) and
one import.

## Boundary

Found by wamn-0h0g.15.67, whose corrupted-transfer live proof is red until this
lands, so this sequences BEFORE it. A conformant registry cannot serve a corrupt
blob (it digests on upload), which is why that proof stands up a deliberately
hostile registry on a loopback socket rather than using registry:2.
close_reason: Classification fixed (57946ca7). DigestError now maps to Mismatched; everything else stays Unavailable. Mismatched already existed and its own doc already said not-retryable, so this is a classification fix not a new disposition. Verified by reading oci-client's source that it digests every streamed blob against its descriptor, which is why a corrupt body surfaces here at all. Unblocked .15.67's corrupted-transfer proof.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ingress): authenticate trusts a policy string the guest echoes back
description:
## Why

Found while taking wamn-0h0g.15.96 (2026-08-17).

## Measured

`wamn:flow-http-routing`'s `authenticate(policy, headers)` receives the policy string the HOST handed the guest in a `route-definition` and the GUEST hands back. Nothing re-derives it from the attachment, so a guest could present a weaker policy than its route carries.

INERT TODAY on two grounds: the only policy the host honours grants access unauthenticated, so there is nothing to downgrade TO; and there is no auth-policy vocabulary anywhere in the tree (the exposure resolver validates an auth source as nothing more than is_object(), and four fixtures invent four incompatible shapes).

## Scope

Re-derive the policy from the attachment id inside `authenticate` rather than trusting the echoed string, and settle the auth-policy vocabulary while doing it.

## Boundary

Changes the `routing` interface signature, which is a frozen WIT contract -- so this rides a deliberate revision of that package, not a patch. Do not weaken the typed refusal that currently rejects every unrecognized policy.
acceptance_criteria: authenticate derives the policy from the attachment rather than the argument, and a guest presenting a policy its route does not carry is refused by a named test.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(provision): a superseded instance leaves its resources with no handle
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.83's whole purpose is that a recreated environment CANNOT reuse the old instance's names. The consequence is that after a delete-and-recreate, NOTHING RECORDS WHAT THE PREVIOUS SUFFIX WAS — the row was replaced (or cascaded away and re-inserted).

That is correct for the hazard. It also means the orphaned namespace and whatever survived inside it have no handle: no query returns the dead instance's derived names, so cleanup cannot be automated and an operator cannot even enumerate what to delete.

## Scope

Give a superseded instance a handle — retention of prior suffixes, a GC pass, or an explicit operator-facing enumeration. Which of those is the right shape is the decision this bead has to settle first.

## Boundary

Deliberately NOT folded into .15.83: the owner ruled that randomness is the entire uniqueness mechanism and that no further machinery was wanted. Reclaiming the orphan is a separate concern from preventing the collision, and adding it to that bead would have been exactly the machinery the ruling rejected.

Filed at the wave-4 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.83 report.
close_reason: Landed WHOLE per owner ruling (a1039a91): DDL + BEFORE DELETE trigger, live cascade proof, and the enumeration builder in one commit. SHAPE SETTLED FIRST as the bead required: retention of prior suffixes in a non-FK'd relation. THE WRITE PATH MUST BE A TRIGGER and that is the finding — nothing in the tree ever deletes a registry.project_envs row from application code; every removal is a CASCADE from an org/project DELETE, which runs no application code at all. GC rejected on merit: without retention its delete list could only come from enumerating cluster state minus the one live row, and the scenario is precisely the one where that row is GONE, so a glob-driven GC would target every instance of the stem including a live one from a concurrent re-provision — a destructive actor taking a guess as input. GC is a CONSUMER of retention. Operator enumeration has the identical dependency and is the right surface once retention exists. Not FK'd, per the provisioning.sagas.target precedent: an FK would erase the record at the moment it becomes the only copy. Stays on the reclaim side of the .13.57 ruling — nothing here is consulted when a suffix is minted. Proof is the cascade: deleting org acme leaves all three handles with prod's suffix verbatim; drop the trigger and it reads 0. Also closed a pre-existing gap in the SR2 drift guard, which covered only the upsert and neither read.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(egress): the p3 egress path has no host-call duration clamp
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.36 added the connection-derived narrowing to `RunnerEgress::outgoing_request_p3` and DELIBERATELY LEFT ONE LEG OUT, disclosing it rather than widening that bead's scope.

`outgoing_request` (p2) runs `bounded_outgoing_config`, which clamps to `MAX_HOST_CALL_DURATION` = 30s (crates/platform/runtime/src/engine.rs:25). The p3 override passes `options` straight through.

p3's `RequestOptions` fields are `Option<Duration>`, and `default_send_request` substitutes **600 seconds** for each `None` (wasmtime-wasi-http-47.0.1/src/p3/request.rs:305-322). So p3 is unbounded relative to p2 by a factor of twenty — and the store's epoch deadline DOES NOT interrupt a host call parked in `await`, so nothing else catches it.

## Scope

Clamp the p3 path to `MAX_HOST_CALL_DURATION` the way p2 does.

## Boundary

This is a SECOND POLICY, not part of the narrowing — which is why .15.36 did not fold it in. It carries a real semantic decision that must be made explicitly: `None` must become `Some(MAX_HOST_CALL_DURATION)`, NOT stay `None`. Passing `None` through is exactly the bug.

LATENT, NOT LIVE: the p3 path is unreachable from production guests today on two independent grounds — the flowrunner world imports no `wasi:http` at all, and crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs:469-488 registers only the p2 linkers, never `wasmtime_wasi_http::p3::add_to_linker`. A guest that imported wasi:http 0.3 would fail `instantiate_pre` loudly rather than bypass silently.

Filed at the wave-4 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.36 report.
close_reason: Commit 5c729c72. bounded_request_options clamps all three p3 RequestOptions timeouts to MAX_HOST_CALL_DURATION, and the semantic point is honoured: None becomes Some(30s) rather than staying None, because default_send_request substitutes 600s for each None (three sites in wasmtime-wasi-http-47.0.1) and passing None through IS the bug. Destructured field-by-field so a new upstream timeout is a compile error. All three fields are duration governors; there is no non-governor field. PREMISE CORRECTIONS: the fix is NOT in plugins/runner_egress.rs (which holds only RunnerEgressPolicy and no timeout code) but in crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs; the p2-only linker cite drifted from :469-488 to :606-623; the 600s block is :305-328 not :305-322. Both latency grounds re-verified real, so it stays latent. 2 named tests; verified the deadlineproof source-text gate and the in-file p3 ordering gate both still pass. Behaviour change named: any future p3 guest's effective default drops 600s -> 30s, which is p2 parity but a real narrowing.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(exec): a starved or refused claim has no run-level signal
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.69 fixed the mechanism — a refused claim now advances its crash-evidence counter so the janitor can eventually reap the run. It did NOT fix the observability, which the bead named in its Why but not its Scope.

A refused claim still surfaces as exactly ONE `tracing::warn` per drain turn from services/executor/src/lib.rs:239-247 ('run-worker: drain failed (retrying after backoff)'). `observe_drive` is never reached, `report.claimed` stays 0, and there is no run-level metric at all. An operator watching dashboards sees a flat line, not a refusing run.

## Scope

Give a refused or repeatedly-failing claim a run-level signal an operator can alert on.

## Boundary

The mechanism is already fixed; this is the signal. Filed separately because it is distinct work and wamn-0h0g.15.69's scope was explicitly the counter.

Filed at the wave-3 close (2026-08-16).
close_reason: Commit e2d39852. New instrument wamn.run.drain.failures (counter, wamn.tenant + wamn.project, no error text, no run id) on the non-fatal drain-error arm, before the existing warn. Deliberately its OWN instrument rather than another `outcome` bucket: folding it in would corrupt the documented completed/(completed+failed) success ratio and break metricbench's per-label delta assertions. PREMISE CORRECTION: starvation is NOT a drain failure -- an empty queue returns Ok with claimed == 0 and is already derivable from a non-zero queue depth against flat executions; what had no signal is the FAILING turn, so the bead's title is wider than the real gap. Also corrected: metrics.md attributed wamn.run.executions to crates/execution/host/src/lib.rs; it is emitted by the run-worker's RunMetrics::record_drive. Absorbed the duplicated attribute-pair construction into one shared identity(). Verified there is no drift guard pinning the metric set and no collector allowlist, so no carve-out was needed for the family to reach Prometheus.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(catalog): two RFC 8785 canonicalizers exist in one workspace
description:
## Why

crates/execution/flow-model/src/canonical.rs implements RFC 8785 canonical JSON and is exposed as wamn_flow::canonical_json_bytes / canonical_json_sha256. crates/catalog/model/src/lib.rs:1351-1411 carries a SECOND private implementation (canonical_json / write_json / ecma_number, ryu-js based) in the same workspace.

Two canonicalizers means two number-formatting edge-case behaviours can drift apart while both claim to be RFC 8785. Everything content-addressed in this program depends on canonical bytes being one thing.

## Scope

Collapse to one, or prove byte-equivalence with a shared test vector and record why both exist.

## Boundary

PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by this program — found while freezing the serving manifest (wamn-0h0g.15.61), which deliberately used the wamn-flow one and touched neither.

Filed at the wamn-0h0g.15.61 close (2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1).
notes:
ESCALATED BY OWNER RULING wamn-0h0g.15.104 (2026-08-17) — this duplication is now a named silent-fork channel, not hygiene.

The ruling makes release identity PRODUCER-COUPLED: the weld derives a pod's manifest digest by re-serializing the mounted bytes through the SAME RFC 8785 producer that minted them, so 'a producer revision cannot silently fork weld-side identity'. That property is only as strong as there being ONE producer.

There are two:
  1. SHARED, and the one both sides must use: wamn_flow::canonical_json_bytes (crates/execution/flow-model/src/lib.rs:76) and canonical_json_sha256 (:62), implementation in crates/execution/flow-model/src/canonical.rs. ServingManifest::canonical_bytes (crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs:316) and ::digest (:321) already route through it, and ::read (:340) re-canonicalizes through it and refuses on mismatch. The wamn-0h0g.15.14 mint is independently required to use it.
  2. PRIVATE, ryu-js based: canonical_json / canonical_serialized / write_json at crates/catalog/model/src/lib.rs:1376-1386, used for identity-frame hashing. Same crate as ServingManifest, so it is the nearest thing to hand for anyone adding a hashing path there.

THE HAZARD, CONCRETELY. If a future change routes any part of manifest identity through (2), or if (1) and (2) drift in their number formatting, escaping, or key ordering, then mint-side and weld-side digests fork for the same content. The failure is silent and total: every run records one digest while the serving pod derived another, and wamn-0h0g.15.66's effect authority binds against the wrong one. Nothing in the tree currently prevents an implementer picking the wrong function — they are both in scope in the same file.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD NOW DELIVER, beyond deduplication: whichever way the two are collapsed, leave a structural guard that manifest identity cannot be computed by anything except the shared producer. The golden-vector test wamn-0h0g.15.104's acceptance now requires (digest of a golden manifest equals the mint's recorded digest, byte-for-byte, same vector both sides) proves the two AGREE at a point in time; it does not prevent a third path appearing. A repo-lint tripwire or a visibility narrowing is what closes the class.

Priority is worth re-rating against that: filed P2 as a tidiness item, but it is now the single point of failure behind the audit chain the platform sells (bytes-that-served bound to facts-that-resulted).

MEASURED AT THE wamn-0h0g.15.104 CLOSE (2026-08-17) — the duplication is currently INERT, and that is exactly what makes it dangerous.

A mutant named digest-uses-the-other-canonicalizer swapped ServingManifest::digest from wamn_flow::canonical_json_sha256 onto this crate's private ryu-js path (crate::digest(&crate::canonical_serialized(self))). ALL 47 wamn-catalog tests stayed GREEN, including the newly pinned golden vector. It is the only mutant in that campaign that survived, and it survived because the two implementations agree BYTE FOR BYTE on manifest-shaped documents: every field in the projection is a string, an integer, or a BTreeMap of them, and the shape admits no value the two format differently. The divergence risk is entirely in the NUMBER and STRING-ESCAPE paths, which this document shape never reaches.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRODUCER-COUPLING RIDER. The rider ('the weld MUST import the mint's serializer, never reimplement 8785') cannot be enforced by pinning the digest — no digest assertion can tell which producer ran. .15.104 therefore added the alarm instead: serving_manifest.rs tests the_two_canonicalizers_cannot_diverge_on_this_projection asserts wamn_flow::canonical_json_bytes == crate::canonical_json for two manifest fixtures. Proven load-bearing by a canonicalizer-divergence mutant (appending one byte to crate::canonical_json), which fails that named test. So a future ryu-js bump or escape-path change trips an alarm BEFORE a forked identity can ship.

WHAT THIS BEAD STILL OWES, and why the second option in its scope is only half taken: the byte-equivalence proof now exists for the SERVING MANIFEST projection only. It does not exist for the shapes that actually differ — floats, non-ASCII strings, escape sequences — and those are what the identity-frame hashing path feeds through crate::canonical_json. Either collapse to one implementation, or extend the equivalence vector to the number and string-escape edge cases the two could realistically diverge on.

PRIORITY: still recorded P2 and still unruled. The measurement argues both ways — no live fork today (softer), but a silent-fork channel that the program's whole content-addressing rests on and that no digest test can detect (harder). Owner's call.
close_reason: Commits c240c4a4 + c740379b (lockfile). COLLAPSED TO ONE PRODUCER, the preferred outcome: 56 lines of the private ryu-js implementation deleted, canonical_serialized rerouted through wamn_flow, the dependency removed from the crate AND the workspace (which is what actually shuts the door -- the source guard only bites on source). encode_utf16, RFC 8785's key-ordering fingerprint, now appears EXACTLY ONCE in the tree. THE BEAD'S CENTRAL MEASURED CLAIM IS FALSE: ServingAttachment::definition and ::auth_policy are serde_json::Value validated only by is_object(), so arbitrary user JSON -- floats, non-ASCII, escapes -- DOES travel in the manifest projection. .15.104's mutant survived because the FIXTURE had no float, not because the SHAPE forbids one; the silent-fork channel was live in manifest identity. AND THE DIGIT SOURCES HAD ALREADY SPLIT: ryu-js 1.0.3 is byte-identical to ryu, while serde_json 1.0.150 replaced ryu with zmij -- two unrelated float formatters, arrived at by a patch bump. Measured before collapsing: strings, object keys and key ordering were IDENTICAL SOURCE in both (so the 'string-escape divergence risk' never existed); numbers were the only independent code and agree on every finite f64 branch by branch, so the collapse is byte-neutral. Structural guard replaces the point-in-time alarm: a source-scan tripwire over the two routes a second producer actually arrives by, concat!-split so it cannot match itself. Also added flow-model's float_roundtrip feature -- it was enabled by exactly one crate while wamn-flow parses documents itself and is now the sole canonicalizer, and per-build feature unification meant `cargo test -p wamn-flow` and `--workspace` could hash the same document differently. RATED P1 not P2 for the record: both halves of the 'softer' argument were wrong.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(deploy): namespace-label cross-check as a readiness gate
description:
## Why

Cheap wrong-target protection that wamn already half-has. Environment namespaces can be labelled wamn.org / wamn.project / wamn.env — keys deploy/mvp/bootstrap.sh:99-101 already verifies — and readiness can assert they equal the pod's WAMN_ORG / WAMN_PROJECT / WAMN_ENVIRONMENT (services/executor/src/lib.rs:68-76). A mis-targeted apply then becomes 'pod never ready' instead of 'converged silently'.

## Scope

Label the namespaces and add the readiness assertion.

## Boundary

Proves in a fresh namespace with zero cluster state, so it satisfies the wave's cluster-freeze constraint. Complements, does not replace, operator.allowSharedHosts=false, which remains the load-bearing lock.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16).
close_reason: Commit 88248125. Closed on the corrected finding, with the residual hole shut. THE PREMISE IS TWICE FALSE: (1) there is no readiness mechanism -- the run-worker exposes NO listener at all, so the only available mechanism is a fail-closed startup refusal (CrashLoopBackOff), which still delivers 'pod never ready' rather than 'converged silently'; (2) the cross-check ALREADY EXISTS in a stronger form -- the mounted effect-writer credential carries its OWN (org, project, environment, database), is refused unless it equals the pod's WAMN_*, and is then confirmed against the live current_user/current_database(); that is true target identity, not the manifest self-consistency the bead's design would have achieved. The genuine residual was that all three arguments absent opts out entirely, right for a bench and wrong for a welded replica -- now refused at startup, with serving-ness read from the argument. (3) The bootstrap.sh citation is wrong twice and bootstrap.sh NEVER CREATES OR LABELS A NAMESPACE; nothing in the repo does. Recorded what this does NOT catch (a consistently-but-wrongly edited triple, a wrong --tenant/--schema, a mis-targeted bootstrap --namespace) so it does not overclaim. The namespace-label design itself is NOT built and needs an owner ruling: no pod can read its own namespace's labels without new RBAC, so it means a namespace-adoption protocol in bootstrap.sh -- an ownership question, not a P2 detail.

The chart is NOT in the repo — pulled from OCI at install — so no in-repo test can assert it renders the keys; rather than ship a skip-when-absent test this follows the three existing fork-governance guards' mechanism and is HONEST that it guards the forcing function, not the fact. The version misalignment is worse than one release — the values file claimed the chart matched pinned rev 8b53285, TWO fork retargets stale; replaced with an accurate record. Added the missing chart axis to the fork sync runbook.

title: [SR-MVP] test(runtime): runtime proof of the no-trap discipline for the executor plugins
description: Drive the complete retained executor-plugin inventory through real guest-to-host error paths and prove mapped errors return without trapping. The retained set is exactly runner-egress, logging, PostgreSQL, and connection_http. Runner-plan-supply is excluded because wamn-0h0g.26.6 owns deletion of that plugin and its proof.
design: Use the existing hermetic WAT guest, real store, linker, and call instrumentation. Runner-egress remains the passing control. wamn-0h0g.15.133 repairs equality-bound named type identities for logging, PostgreSQL, and connection_http. Each proof must enter the real host call and discriminate the mapped typed error from a component trap. The inventory is closed at the four retained subjects; runner-plan-supply deletion remains owned by wamn-0h0g.26.6.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly four retained production subjects are driven: runner-egress, logging, PostgreSQL, and connection_http. Each guest validates and invokes the real host path, and each host error returns through the expected mapped error rather than trapping. Entry and resume markers, plugin counters, and typed refusal discriminants prove the host call was not bypassed. Named mutants remove one required type identity, bypass one host call, replace a mapped error with a trap, or resurrect runner-plan-supply as retained coverage and fail the owning gate. Runner-plan-supply remains explicitly sequenced to deletion under wamn-0h0g.26.6.
notes:
CORPSE-COVERAGE WARNING, migrated from the wave-23 memory key on prune 2026-08-23 (it existed only in memory; bd is now its only home).

*** DO NOT IMPLEMENT THIS BEAD'S CURRENT INVENTORY AS CORPSE COVERAGE. *** The design authority is
explicit: retired surfaces keep no corpse coverage, and the gate registry is exhaustive only for
LIVING gates. Before writing any runtime no-trap proof, re-derive which executor plugins still
exist and are reachable; prove only those. Siblings .15.177 and .15.133 carried the same warning
and were both closed rather than implemented against a dead inventory.

comments.text: DECISION CONSUMER NOTE 2026-08-23: wamn-0h0g.15.188 retires runner-egress from the production inventory.
