title: [SR-MVP] test(socketguard): cover the new allowed_host_loopback_ports grant surface
description:
## Why

Upstream added a loopback-port grant surface (LocalResources.allowed_host_loopback_ports, fork crates/wash-runtime/src/types.rs:134). Gate B's compile fix restores compilation with the fail-closed empty value, but nothing asserts that an ungranted loopback port is actually refused.

## Scope

Extend the sockprobe/socketguard gate to exercise granted and ungranted loopback ports.

## Boundary

Rides the fork pin wamn-0h0g.15.20; the empty default is fail-closed, so this is coverage, not a live hole.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.6 report.
close_reason: [f8d61b80] Six tests plus a third sockprobe run covering the loopback grant surface. THE DECIDING FACT, in no earlier bead: resolve_connect checks is_host_sentinel FIRST, so the surface is reachable only via 127.255.255.254 -- a 127.0.0.1 test would have proven nothing silently. EgressMode is IRRELEVANT here (resolve_host_loopback returns Err directly, never through gate()), which reverses the usual Count warning; asserted with a same-policy control. The host half is UNREACHABLE in wamn, not merely off: --allow-host-loopback is a wash CLI flag and wamn has zero SocketPolicy call sites, so the granted-and-enabled case is covered in-process only. socketguard.rs was the wrong file (publish-time import guard) and is untouched. HONEST SCOPE: upstream already tests these cases; ours are a drift guard at our pin. Filed .15.141/.15.142/.15.143/.15.150/.15.151.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(deploy): GC superseded release-manifest-<digest> ConfigMaps
description:
## Why

Ruling 4 creates one immutable ConfigMap per release digest, referenced by name in the pod template. Nothing reaps superseded ones, so a namespace accumulates one object per release forever and etcd pressure becomes a slow leak nobody owns.

## Scope

Define and implement the reaping rule (retain the active release plus N predecessors, or GitOps-pruned).

## Boundary

Not owned by wamn-0h0g.15.14 (publish) or wamn-0h0g.15.16 (GitOps) as currently scoped.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.2 report.
close_reason: CLOSED AS REFUTED by wave-57 measurement. No code written. THE PREMISE HAS NO PRODUCER: the bead assumes Ruling 4's release-manifest-<digest> ConfigMap accumulates, but nothing in the tree creates that object, so its stated choice between retain-N-predecessors and GitOps-pruned is moot. Evidence: both release-carrying workloads pull over OCI BY DIGEST, not a mount, and services/host/src/host.rs around 226 records the reason as ratified design - a projected ConfigMap carries no usable binding between the bytes and the name the template asked for, while a registry is a third party (wamn-0h0g.15.98). ReleaseManifestWeld::load, the mount reader, has ZERO callers in production or test. release_manifest_configmap_name has exactly one caller, its own unit test at crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs around 563, and RELEASE_MANIFEST_CONFIGMAP_PREFIX has no non-definition caller. No release-manifest ConfigMap exists in deploy/, and there is NO Kubernetes client crate anywhere in services/ or crates/, so nothing in-tree can create a ConfigMap at runtime; none of wamn-ctl's 15 verbs renders one. The repository actively forbids adding one: runtime_inventory one_release_manifest_weld_construction_site_per_host_process pins exactly one weld construction site per host process and passes today, so a second ConfigMap carrier fails it. THE CONCERN MIGRATED AND IS FILED AS wamn-dqw6 - published OCI artifacts in wamn/releases are never pruned. That is a different object and a different mechanism, so it was filed rather than silently retargeted onto this bead. Dead code mentioned and deliberately not deleted per the surgical-changes rule: RELEASE_MANIFEST_CONFIGMAP_PREFIX, release_manifest_configmap_name, ReleaseManifestWeld::load.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(credentials): credential material is a process-lifetime snapshot
description:
## Why

WamnCredentials::from_file is read once at executor startup (services/executor/src/lib.rs:302) into a HashMap (wamn_credentials.rs:86-97). Rotating the underlying Secret material under an UNCHANGED handle therefore does not take effect until the pod restarts.

## Scope

Decide and record whether rotation-under-unchanged-handle is supported; if it is, reload or re-read the material.

## Boundary

Consistent with ruling 3's process-lifetime immutability posture, but that ruling is about plan bytes, not credential material — the coupling is worth making explicit.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.5 report.
close_reason: Commit 5064a4da. Recorded as NOT SUPPORTED, and THE EXPECTED VERDICT WAS INVERTED: rotation-under-unchanged-handle IS the documented rotation shape -- the handle lives in the connection definition, rotation mints a new CREDENTIAL generation without changing the portable artifact, and catalog.connection_generations' UNIQUE over definition_hash makes a same-handle new CONNECTION generation inexpressible. So 'a rotation mints a new handle' is false. The snapshot is still correct for a better reason: an attempt's durable facts pin the credential_generation that authorized it, recovery must reuse that material or refuse, and the v1 {project:{handle:secret}} mount carries no generation -- so a blind re-read could not tell rotated from pinned material and would silently substitute credentials under a recovering attempt. A reload would be WRONG, not merely absent; supporting rotation properly needs the generation first-class in the source. Pinned by one named test so a future helpful reload is a test failure.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(egress): forward workload lifecycle callbacks to the pooled handler
description:
## Why

OutgoingHandler::on_workload_bind / on_workload_unbind are new at the wamn/2.7.0 pin (fork host/http.rs:489, :499) and drive pool sizing and eager pool invalidation. wamn's HostHandler::on_workload_unbind returns Ok(()) without touching the inner handler, so a per-workload pool would linger to its 60s idle window instead of being invalidated at workload stop.

## Scope

Forward both callbacks to the inner handler.

## Boundary

Harmless today — the pooled path is unreachable from production guests and the handler is per-instance. Becomes load-bearing if either changes.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.5 report.
close_reason: [0addc315] Forwarded HostHandler::on_workload_unbind to the inner OutgoingHandler. THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG: the pool cannot 'linger to its 60s idle window' -- RunnerEgress sits on the store's Ctx, whose only HostHandler calls are outgoing_request/outgoing_request_p3, so the lifecycle hooks were unreachable dead code and `inner` is dropped with the Store. DROP IS THE INVALIDATION; this is contract hygiene, and the doc comment says so. BIND HALF NOT DONE, deliberately: HostHandler declares no bind hook, and call_concurrency is unreachable behind pub(crate) AND a type mismatch (wasmtime::component::Component vs crate::types::Component). Passing a documented 1 was rejected. Filed .15.144 (fork change), .15.145 (engine-scope decision), .15.146 (real invalidation test). All five text-pinning guards checked; none break.

title: [SR-MVP] docs: strike release-bound resolution-map text from build-and-test

close_reason: SHIPPED 124109ef. Both named sites struck. .15.10 CONFIRMED LANDED structurally, not assumed: resolution.rs gone, run-state.sql has zero references, run_flow_resolutions survives only in two registries (.15.22 regenerates), one gate-mutant needle, and comments describing the deletion. title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): repair gate-mutant anchors already stale at b863a735
description:
## Why

Two gate-mutant baselines were ALREADY broken at b863a735, before the demolition branch touched anything, so Tier D regeneration will not necessarily repair them:

- tools/gate-mutants/control-portable-store.sh:98 anchors the retained-drift-acceptance mutation on fb752b79..., but deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql has carried 91f3ffe8... since before this branch (verified against git show HEAD:). run-all mode was already broken.
- tools/gate-mutants/test-orchestration.sh:32 EXPECTED_SHA is 2dc1ee0e0c50..., while the file at b863a735 hashes to e39d3c7f12fa... The baseline was stale at HEAD.

## Scope

title: [SR-MVP] chore(schema): drop the superseded 9-argument register_deployment_attestation overload
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.8 shortened catalog.register_deployment_attestation's parameter list. CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION with a shortened list creates a NEW 8-arg function beside the old 9-arg one on any database that already applied the previous DDL; deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql contains no DROP FUNCTION, and the drift block validates table inventory and column/constraint shape only, with no function inventory. The stale overload therefore survives replay silently with nothing re-revoking PUBLIC EXECUTE on it.

## Scope

Decide whether the DDL carries an explicit DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS for the 9-arg signature, or whether the M1 cutover-apply path handles it. Same concern applies to CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS keeping the dropped column on a pre-existing database, which fires the shape-drift assert at :761-763.

## Boundary

Non-issue for fresh installs and for the provision proof (which DROP SCHEMA CASCADEs first). Adding a DROP was declined in wamn-0h0g.15.8 because Tier B is pure deletion and a DROP is new machinery.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.8 report.
close_reason: Closed with wamn-0h0g.15.91 in commit 1225515c -- it is the same mechanism seen from the function side and is not separable from it. The answer to 'decide whether the DDL carries an explicit DROP FUNCTION' is YES, through .15.91's retirement block: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS for the 9-arg register_deployment_attestation overload, plus the dropped-column sibling the bead names (deployment_attestations.deployed_resolution_map). .15.8's objection that 'Tier B is pure deletion and a DROP is new machinery' is spent, because .15.91 authorizes exactly that machinery. PREMISE CORRECTIONS: the stale overload's PUBLIC EXECUTE is real but UNREACHABLE (schema USAGE on catalog is revoked from PUBLIC and never re-granted), so it is a latent zombie rather than a live privilege leak; and the cited shape-drift assert line is the release-evidence one, not the attestation one. Absorbed the un-filed twin from .15.79: register_release_flow_test_evidence's 11-arg overload and release_flow_test_evidence.test_set_hash, the identical class created by 3d2bfc46 in this same wave.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] feat(ui): dim the structure anchor on a draft that does not parse
description: §2.0 says the draft's 'structure' anchor is shown dimmed with a tooltip when the draft does not parse. wamn-dggp.7 added ScreenAnchor.unavailable and the panel honours it end to end — dims the row, says the screen's own reason, and refuses to act on it — but NO SCREEN SETS IT, so the dimmed anchor never appears in the real app. Landing it is three coordinated edits across two lanes' files, which is why it was not forced in the wave: draft-screen.tsx contributes { id: 'draft-structure', label: 'structure', unavailable: <the parse refusal> }; palette/commands.ts filters anchors with an unavailable reason, or the palette would offer a dead 'go to structure' row; and draft-screen.test.tsx:464 ('offers the palette no way into a structure that is not there') updates, since it currently asserts the anchor list is exactly the source anchor. That test was deliberately not weakened.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] test(ui): prove the section-in-view mark against a real scroll
description: wamn-dggp.7 shipped §2.0's scroll-tracking as a pure sectionInView plus an IntersectionObserver wired behind a capability check. The pure half is exhaustively tested; the wiring is inert in jsdom (no IntersectionObserver there at all) so nothing asserts that a real scroll actually moves the mark. Browser mode was adopted in wamn-dggp.16 precisely for this, and is now available: a *.browser.test.tsx runs in real chromium. See src/styles/painted.browser.test.tsx for the shape. NOTE from the step-6 wave: a browser test cannot live under src/ui/ until wamn-dggp.7's sibling fix landed — the floor test now reads files only, so this is no longer a constraint, but keep browser proofs beside the thing they prove.
acceptance_criteria: A browser test scrolls a run screen and asserts the panel's marked section follows, failing if the observer is unwired.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] test(ui): cover the start screen's jump rules
description: The start screen (§2.1) shipped without its own test file, against the repository convention that every component has one, because the owner asked for prototype velocity over coverage. The load-bearing behaviour is all in two pure exported functions, jumpRoute and inferredKind, so it is cheap to cover: id@revision addresses a draft and outranks the selected kind; a bare id under the draft kind addresses nothing and says which rule it broke; the kind is inferred from the most recent run-or-report visit and the author's own choice then stands; focus lands on the field on load.
acceptance_criteria: start-screen.test.tsx exists and covers jumpRoute, inferredKind, the refusal wording, and focus on load.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] fix(ui): lint that no aria-* attribute renders as the empty string
description: Found by the step-6 spike. @solidjs/web does not drop a boolean aria value — it renders it as an EMPTY STRING: <div aria-selected={true}> emits aria-selected="", which is not one of the enumerated values 'true'/'false' and reports nothing to a screen reader. (Numbers are kept correctly: aria-level={2} emits "2".) The existing rule of thumb in the codebase was 'booleans are dropped', which understates it — a dropped attribute is absent and obvious, an empty one is present and silently meaningless. Step 6's tree is the first place aria-selected and aria-expanded are set from real state on many rows at once, so this is where the trap bites. accessibility-floor.test.tsx has no rule against it today.
acceptance_criteria: A rendered aria-* attribute whose value is the empty string fails the accessibility floor, and the rule is mutation-checked by a component that sets one from a boolean.
close_reason: Fixed at aadb619a. Floor rule added at both levels (primitive and assembled screen): no rendered aria-* attribute may be the empty string. Measured the real behaviour rather than trusting the earlier note that booleans are 'dropped' — a static literal AND a dynamic accessor both emit aria-selected="" when true; false is absent; numbers are fine. Sharpened the finding: it is a FIRST-PAINT fault only. A later change goes through setAttribute, which stringifies, so a control that starts closed and is then opened reports "true" correctly forever. Proven by the first mutant surviving: making disclosure's aria-expanded a boolean did NOT trip the rule because disclosures start closed. Making LoadingBlock's aria-busy a boolean did, naming element and attribute.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] fix(ui): give the palette's groups real list semantics
description:
Found by the step-7 review. The palette's three ranked groups are a visual fact only: the group name is a

, not a heading; the rows are not a list; and nothing associates a row with the group it belongs to. A screen-reader user hears a flat run of buttons with no sense of go-to versus this-screen versus console, which is the whole ranking the spec's step 7 describes.
acceptance_criteria: Each group announces itself and its rows are associated with it, without turning the rows into anything other than the real buttons the floor requires.
close_reason: Fixed at bed813d1. Each palette group is now a named role=group holding an <h2> it is labelled by and a role=list of its own rows; rows stay the real buttons the accessibility floor requires. Chose a grouped list of buttons over a listbox/option pair deliberately — an option is not a tab stop and every row here is a button a keyboard reader reaches and presses, so half a listbox would be a worse claim than the plain one; the reasoning is in a comment beside the markup, consistent with the existing 'deliberately not a combobox' note on the input. Group heading ids derive from the group name, not a counter, so they are stable across the rebuilds the list does while the palette is open. Verified in a real browser: all three groups report role=group with aria-labelledby resolving to their own heading id, and role=list on each row list.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] feat(ui): visited store — ids and cached display text
description: Split out of wamn-dggp.7 (step 6), because the store is not the side panel: spec section 6 says the entity screens (steps 4-5) WRITE it and the panel and palette (steps 6-7) READ it, so it cannot land inside the panel's bead without blocking two other steps on the panel. Ids and cached display text only - kind, id, revision, label, verdict glyph state, visitedAt - never a Run/Report/Draft, so the tree can never render an entity from a stale copy of itself. Namespaced by target (project and environment join the key when step 9 brings real proxy config), capped ~20 per kind, most-recent-first, re-visit replaces rather than appends, localStorage-backed and degrading to session-lived when storage refuses. Spec: docs/wamn-dev-ui-spec.md section 2.0, section 6 step 6.
design: Value is an authoritative module array; the signal beside it only announces change. Solid 2 stages a write until flush, so deriving the next state from a signal read would drop a visit whenever two screens recorded in one tick.
acceptance_criteria: The store records, replaces on re-visit, caps per kind, survives a reload, clears, and decodes a hand-edited or foreign stored value without losing the whole history.
close_reason: Shipped in 48273c1a. The visited store (ids + cached display text, capped per kind, re-visit replaces, localStorage-backed, degrading to session-lived when storage refuses) plus the screen-action seam. Both hold their value in a plain module variable with a signal beside it that only announces change: Solid 2 stages a write until flush, so a store deriving next state from a signal read drops a visit when two screens record in one tick, and createSignal(fn) builds a writable memo that calls fn, so a getter cannot live in a signal at all. Writes licensed with ownedWrite. Run screen records its visit and contributes its anchors. Killed: cap removal and the terminalized-run verdict, each by a named test.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] docs: record the run-status wire-vs-durable deviation in the findings ledger
description:
The owner decided (dkk, 2026-08-15) to keep the WIRE run vocabulary in the console's reader and add an explicit durable-to-wire mapping the screens use; wamn-dggp.14 carries the code half. This bead is the ledger half, split out because it CANNOT be done from the loop-console worktree: CLAUDE.md forbids editing docs/archive/findings.md from a parallel worktree, and this branch is one. Do it from the main tree.

Record: the wire RunStatus (queued|dispatched|running|succeeded|failed|effect-uncertain) against the durable one (dispatched|running|completed|failed|infrastructure-failure|effect-uncertain) - the wire invents queued, renames completed to succeeded, and drops infrastructure-failure entirely even though assertions still assert on it; and the same split on RunFailureKind, where the durable FailKind has 12 values, the wire keeps 4, adds deadline-exhausted (not durable on a run at all, only on a test case), and gives the seven budget/resolution kinds no wire form. Today the deviation lives only in a doc comment on RunStatus in clients/loop-console/src/reader/types.ts.
acceptance_criteria: The deviation and the owner's decision are recorded in docs/archive/findings.md, from the main tree.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] fix(ui): drop the placeholder h1 when a real screen mounts a verdict bar
description: VerdictBar renders the verdict as the screen's h1 — SS1.3 makes it the answer the eye reaches first, so it is the heading, and SectionLabel below it is h2. The step-1 placeholder in clients/loop-console/src/app/views.tsx still renders its own <h1 class=screen-name> per route. The moment step 4 or step 5 mounts a real screen inside that placeholder, the page has two h1s and the heading outline stops describing the screen. Whichever lane replaces a placeholder view drops or demotes its h1.
design: Found by the step-3 review across lane boundaries: neither the atoms lane (which owns VerdictBar) nor the routing lane (which owns views.tsx) could see it alone.
acceptance_criteria: No screen renders two h1 elements; the verdict is the only h1 on an entity screen.
close_reason:
Step 4 shipped: #/run/:id over the reader, mounted at the run route. 142 new tests (139 -> 281 package-wide), all three gates green, and the integrator killed 15/15 of their own mutants against named tests.

Structure: RunScreen owns the read; RunVerdict, ExecutionTable, FactInspector and the new UncertainPanel render it. Solid 2 has no createResource — an async read is a memo returning a promise through Loading/Errored boundaries, verified empirically before the wave. All three read outcomes are real, the refresh control survives a refusal, and the screen drives §1.4's read status while refusing to let a stale or abandoned read move it.

Truthfulness, which is most of the work: the run-level plan hash is claimed only when the returned facts agree on one; a truncated read says its context fold and hash agreement cover the returned window alone; null attempt and duration render as not recorded, never zero; an outstanding effect never reads as errored; and §6 step 4's effect-attempt drill-down is stated as absent rather than inferred from the authored node type, because the read carries no effect attempts and nothing marks a node effectful (STEP-9).

Also landed here because assembling the screen exposed them: DataTable's row disclosure gained Disclosure's controlled contract for trace mode, with a row group per row so an expand-all sweep does not drop the focus of the toggle the reader is standing on; and aria-controls is dropped while a disclosure is closed, in all three files carrying the pattern (the review found it and correctly refused to fix one file in isolation).

wamn-dggp.21 closed with it: the run route no longer renders a placeholder h1 over the verdict bar's.

Review found and remediated 3 blockers (focus loss on expand-all, a controlled row with no onToggle being a dead button, a red suite from a section-label selector reaching into UncertainPanel) and 7 majors. Done-check met: all six run fixtures render, §2.2's wireframe is reproduced line by line in run-acceptance.test.tsx, and the whole-run trace opens and collapses.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] feat(ui): widen the verdict glyph to the tree's four states
description: Step 3 shipped PassGlyph as props { passed: boolean } — correct for SS2.3's case list, which is pass/fail and nothing else. SS2.0's tree needs four verdict glyphs, each 'always with an accessible label': OK (ok), x (fail), o (effect-uncertain, the one purple state) and . (a draft, which has no verdict at all). A boolean cannot carry those. Decide in the step-6 lane whether PassGlyph widens to a tone-plus-word API or whether the tree gets its own TreeGlyph beside it, and keep the accessible label on every state either way.

acceptance_criteria: PassGlyph's boolean API is unchanged, so section 2.3's case list is untouched. A four-state verdict glyph exists beside it, rendering ok / fail / effect-uncertain / none, each with an accessible label and none of them told by colour alone. The tree renders them: that clause belongs to wamn-dggp.7, which owns the tree.
close_reason: Shipped in c46280df. PassGlyph's boolean API is untouched, as this bead's acceptance required; the tree gets VerdictGlyph beside it, over ok/fail/uncertain/none, each with an accessible label and none told by colour alone. Words are entity-verdict words, not PassGlyph's case words. title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] decide whether focus behaviour needs Vitest browser mode

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] decide whether focus and layout behaviour needs Vitest browser mode
description: The test level (wamn-dggp.12) is jsdom, which the Solid 2 testing guide calls the right default but explicitly does not consider sufficient for layout, real CSS, or true focus behaviour — it sends those to Vitest browser mode with Playwright. This console is focus-heavy by design: spec §2.6 specifies roving focus with role=tree semantics and arrow-key navigation (step 6), focus restore on palette close (step 7), and visible focus-visible rings as an accessibility floor (§3). jsdom models activeElement and .focus() but has no layout and no real :focus-visible, so some of that is asserted only structurally. Cost of browser mode: @vitest/browser-playwright plus playwright, and Playwright downloads browser binaries through a postinstall lifecycle script — which this repository denies by default (pnpm-workspace.yaml onlyBuiltDependencies is empty, strictDepBuilds true). That is the real blocker, not the packages. Revisit when step 6 or 7 hits something jsdom cannot express; if it never does, close as not needed and say so.
acceptance_criteria: Either browser mode is adopted with its lifecycle-script implications resolved, or the decision records which specific behaviours stay structurally asserted and why that is acceptable.
notes:
Step 3 (wamn-dggp.4) accumulated the concrete evidence this decision needs — every item below is a real assertion the jsdom level cannot make, found while building the primitives:

• §1.3's 3px verdict rule is a ::before pseudo-element; jsdom parses no stylesheet, so nothing proves it renders at all.
• §1.4's section hairline is a flex-fill span between the heading and the trailing slot; its fill is unverified.
• KeyValue's 8ch key column and the label widths that align stacked pairs are computed values jsdom does not compute.
• The single :focus-visible signal ring in app.css is asserted today as a SOURCE LINT (accessibility-floor.test.tsx: exactly one declaration, and no src/ui file erases it) — that it is actually visible on a focused control is unproven.
• SourceView's no-wrap horizontal scroll (§2.4) and the disclosure's 120ms ease-out height (§1.4) are both CSS-only; the floor test lints that every transition reaches for --motion-fast, which is as far as the source can go.
• CopyId's hover-reveal is asserted through the title attribute, not through hover.
The floor test says so in its own comments where each lint stands in for a browser check.

STEP-6 SPIKE, 2026-08-16 — the trigger this bead named ('revisit when step 6 or 7 hits something jsdom cannot express') has now fired, and it is the first BEHAVIOUR rather than styling to do so. Measured in this jsdom (30.0.1), not assumed:
• IntersectionObserver is UNDEFINED. §2.0's 'the section in view is marked as you scroll' has no idiomatic implementation that runs in the test environment at all.
• getBoundingClientRect returns all zeros, offsetTop/offsetHeight are 0, Element.scrollTo is undefined. Every element reports the same geometry, so a scroll-listener implementation is equally unassertable — the fallback is not a fallback.
• ResizeObserver and window.matchMedia are also undefined (matchMedia bears on step 8's reduced-motion sweep, wamn-dggp.9).
• What DOES work, and needs no browser: scroll events dispatch and are heard; element.scrollTop is settable and reads back; roving focus is fully assertable (tabindex moves reactively, focus() on tabindex=-1 lands, document.activeElement updates); keydown on a descendant reaches a container handler, so the whole role=tree arrow-key pattern is testable.
So the split is now sharp: step 6's tree semantics, roving focus, keyboard, active-entity marking, collapse and persistence are all provable at this level; only WHICH SECTION IS IN VIEW is not. The recommended shape — keep the tracking decision a pure function over 'which sections are intersecting' and test that directly, wiring an IntersectionObserver around it behind a capability check — leaves exactly the observer wiring unasserted, which is the same class as the CSS lints above rather than a new one.
The blocker on adopting browser mode is unchanged and confirmed against pnpm-workspace.yaml: onlyBuiltDependencies is empty and strictDepBuilds is true, so Playwright's postinstall browser download is denied by policy; minimumReleaseAge 1440 with minimumReleaseAgeStrict also applies to any new dependency.
close_reason: Decided and implemented at 91f4e9de: browser mode ADOPTED. The bead's own trigger fired — step 6 hit something jsdom cannot express, and it is the first behaviour rather than styling to do so. Measured, not assumed: IntersectionObserver, ResizeObserver, matchMedia and Element.scrollTo are all undefined in jsdom 30.0.1, and getBoundingClientRect answers every element with zeros, so §2.0's 'the section in view is marked as you scroll' has neither an implementation nor a fallback there. The lifecycle-script blocker this bead named turned out NOT TO EXIST: playwright 1.62.1 declares no postinstall (browser fetching is an explicit command), so the install is clean with onlyBuiltDependencies still [] and strictDepBuilds still true. No supply-chain rule was relaxed; the policy gate passes unchanged; the CI canonical run steps are untouched. Two vitest projects, one run: 'unit' keeps all 450 tests in jsdom, 'browser' takes only assertions needing real layout/CSS/focus (*.browser.test.tsx). First two proofs shipped and mutation-checked: §3's single focus ring actually reaches a focused control, and §1.3's 3px ::before verdict rule is really painted. Two seams: the browser setup loads tokens.css+app.css (main.tsx is otherwise their only importer) so a browser test cannot be written against an unstyled page; and vitest.config.ts is type-checked in its own program (tsconfig.vitest.json) because @vitest/browser and @testing-library/jest-dom each declare TestingLibraryMatchers and augment vitest's Assertion with it, which fails on every matcher in a program holding both. Also added the missing 'dev' script — there was none, so the console could not be opened at all.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] fix(ui): reconcile the draft revision type across the router and reader seams
description: The two step-1/step-2 lanes landed a type seam mismatch on the draft revision. The router (clients/loop-console/src/routing/route.ts) treats the #/draft/:id/:revision revision segment as an OPAQUE bounded string — that is what the step-1 bead's opaque-id rules ask for, and it is what keeps a malformed URL from throwing. The reader contract (clients/loop-console/src/reader/contract.ts) declares drafts.get(draftId: string, revision: number), grounded in the contract's DraftRevisionRef, and Draft.revision is a number throughout. Step 5 (the draft screen, wamn-dggp.6) is the first consumer that has to bridge them. Decide where the conversion lives and what a non-numeric revision in the URL renders — most likely: keep the route opaque, convert at the screen boundary, and treat a non-numeric revision as not-found rather than as a failed read.
design: Not a defect of either bead: each lane implemented its own contract correctly. It surfaces only where the two meet, which is step 5.
acceptance_criteria: One named boundary converts the route's opaque revision to the reader's numeric revision; a non-numeric revision in the URL has a defined, tested rendering.
close_reason:
The seam is closed at one named boundary: parseRevision in clients/loop-console/src/routing/revision.ts converts the route's opaque revision segment to the reader's number, or returns null. It matches a canonical non-negative decimal integer rather than coercing — Number accepts '+1', ' 17 ', '1e3', '0x11' and every leading-zero form, each of which would make two URLs address one revision — and gates the result on Number.isSafeInteger. Eleven rejected spellings are eleven named tests.

Per the bead's recorded decision the route stays opaque and a non-numeric revision renders not-found rather than a failed read: it never becomes a read at all. views.tsx converts at the screen boundary and checks identity, not truthiness, so revision 0 is a revision. Mutants killed: relaxing the regex fails the '017' test; bypassing the null check fails the shell rendering test.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] decide the run-status wire-vs-durable vocabulary deviation
description:
Owner decision (dkk, 2026-08-15): KEEP the wire run vocabulary in the reader and add an explicit durable-to-wire mapping the screens use. This bead is the code half; the findings-ledger half is wamn-dggp.23, split out because CLAUDE.md forbids editing docs/archive/findings.md from a parallel worktree.

The reader encodes the WIRE vocabulary (queued|dispatched|running|succeeded|failed|effect-uncertain) because that is what the console will receive. The durable schema says dispatched|running|completed|failed|infrastructure-failure|effect-uncertain, and assertions assert on the DURABLE words: SS2.3 renders 'expected run-terminal-outcome: completed' and its 'run ->' handoff opens a run whose status word is 'succeeded'. Same split on the failure kinds. Build the named mapping so the report screen can show that an assertion's 'completed' and a run's 'succeeded' are one state, and so 'infrastructure-failure' - assertable, with no wire form at all - has somewhere truthful to land.
acceptance_criteria: One named mapping converts durable run vocabulary to the wire words the reader carries and back where it can; the durable words with no wire form are explicit rather than silently absent; SS2.2 and SS2.3 agree on the status word an author sees on both screens.
close_reason:
Owner decision (dkk, 2026-08-15) implemented in clients/loop-console/src/reader/run-vocabulary.ts: the reader keeps the WIRE run vocabulary, and screens translate through a named mapping.

Four total, exhaustive functions — wireRunStatus, durableRunStatus, wireFailureKind, assertableFailureKind — each over a union checked with satisfies, so a vocabulary that gains or loses a word fails to compile rather than falling through to a wrong one. Where a word has no counterpart the answer is NAMED, never the nearest neighbour: infrastructure-failure and the three budget kinds answer no-wire-form (answering failed would tell an author their infrastructure failure was an ordinary one), deadline-exhausted answers not-assertable since it is a test-case failure and not a durable run one, and the pre-terminal wire words answer not-terminal.

Verified against the platform source, not just the doc comment: crates/execution/run-state/src/status.rs FailKind::ALL is 12 and the wire keeps 4, so EIGHT durable kinds have no wire form — three budget plus five resolution — where the comment had said seven. Corrected in types.ts, with the STEP-9 RISK notes left intact.

Mutant killed: making infrastructure-failure answer the wire's failed fails 'answers the absence for infrastructure-failure rather than calling it failed'.

Split out and still open: wamn-dggp.23, recording the deviation in docs/archive/findings.md, which must be done from the main tree. Step 5 still owns the call of whether the report screen prints the durable word, the wire word, or both.

title: [CLIENT-AUTH-A2] Add cookie sessions and CSRF-safe reserved auth routes
description: Add the browser presenter over the same first-party identity core and authenticated-principal seam: reserved login/logout routes, HttpOnly and SameSite session cookies, expiry/revocation, and CSRF protection in the W16 shape. This enables the Loop Console without creating a second identity authority. OIDC remains a later issuer.
acceptance_criteria: Browser login establishes a revocable HttpOnly/SameSite session and logout invalidates it; authenticated management requests resolve the same principal/role shape as PATs; state-changing requests without the required CSRF proof fail before command execution; session fixation, stale/revoked session, cross-project, and forged-cookie probes fail; no JWT/OIDC dependency or alternate role store is introduced.
notes: INTEGRATION FOLLOW-UP a73a486: the tean conformance re-gate caught identity.sessions missing from architecture/state-owners.json (the lane's gate set did not include wamn-proof-conformance). Registered platform-identity-owned, mirroring identity.pats; repository_state_ownership_manifest_is_complete green again. Lesson: any lane adding a persisted table must run the state-ownership conformance suite.
close_reason: Shipped at 195c7ef on main (+1576/-43 across 6 files). Four dkk rulings recorded here because W16 exists only in the out-of-repo Studio spec: CSRF = synchronizer token bound to the session row (digest at rest, returned in the POST /session body, echoed in X-Wamn-Csrf, verified with the cookie BEFORE the body is read); routes = POST /session + DELETE /session beside the untouched byte-frozen PAT /login; cookie = HttpOnly SameSite=Strict Secure; TTL = absolute expiry only (pats analogue, one-way revoked_at). identity.sessions mirrors identity.pats column-for-column; both presenters resolve through one new role_for seam pinned by both_presenters_resolve_through_one_role_seam (which also asserts no jwt/oidc/openid anywhere) — no second authority, no alternate role store. Frozen guard identity_is_settled_before_the_request_body_is_read strengthened, intent preserved: authorize/refuse before body, presenter reads exactly the credential-bearing headers, authorize_session must precede the body read and carry csrf; new guards pin logout verify-before-revoke and login-reads-no-cookie (fixation). Acceptance proven in management_live over real HTTP + throwaway PG: login/logout, same principal/role shape as PATs, CSRF refusal pre-execution, fixation/stale-revoked/cross-project/forged-cookie probes all refuse. Gates on the integrated ROOT tree (result of record, re-run after the lane's mutation-harness incident): unit suites 13+1+1+4+52+3+1+1+1 green; management_live green vs postgres:18 (race-guarded); clippy wamn-platform-identity -D warnings clean; scenario-worker clippy stays red with the 6 pre-existing findings (wamn-tsm1, verified unchanged). Mutants 3/3 killed by name (CSRF check removed, expiry predicate neutered, cookie-principal join pinned), restores sha256-verified. LOCAL GATES ONLY — the in-cluster rollout is deferred: staged owner-run script scratchpad/ctc89-sysdb-sessions.sh (additive identity.sessions + column-scoped grant delta SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE(revoked_at)); rollout bead filed at close.

title: [FORK-2.6.0-E] Investigate whether a replacement policy can retire the socket patches
description:
## Goal

Investigate whether a replacement policy built on `allowIpNameLookup` could retire the
carried socket patches `8b76869` and `eef76cd` — and record the answer either way.

This is the investigation the `8b76869` ledger entry has implied since the fourth carried
commit. Upstream has now built the `ip_name_lookup` hook that entry named as the missing
primitive.

## Normative anchors

docs/PLAN/WASMCLOUD-UPGRADE-2.6.0.md section 2, which states the five conditions a
replacement must satisfy before either patch retires.

Planning alias: FU-SOCKET-RETIRE. Type: spike.

## Owned collision domain

Analysis only, across both repositories. No policy change lands under this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Positive:** The investigation answers all five conditions with evidence: that an approved
  lookup cannot be bypassed by a literal socket address; that a resolved address cannot be
  substituted; that DNS change does not silently widen authority; that TCP connect and UDP
  send/bind obey one declared policy; and that P2 and P3 socket surfaces reach the same
  decision.
- **Negative:** Anything short of all five leaves both patches in place, and the exit
  conditions unamended. "Upstream has a hook now" is not an answer to any of the five.
- **Fault:** A proposed replacement that passes a happy-path test while failing any bypass
  condition must be recorded as a refutation, not a partial success.

## Validation

Written finding on this issue, with the retirement decision and its evidence. If retirement
is justified, the follow-up work is filed as its own beads — this issue does not remove code.

## Explicit exclusions

No code removal. No ledger amendment without the full five-condition answer.

## Hard dependencies

- E1
notes:
COMPACT HANDOFF 2026-07-31

NEXT AUTHORIZED TARGET: wamn-8zht.19 only. This issue is prepared but not started: leave it OPEN and unclaimed until resume.

Repository baseline:
- wamn main and origin/main: 4c4227cfbd30a6f57f8e962129286993ce73ba42
- wasmCloud wamn/2.6.0 and origin/wamn/2.6.0: 0928c3ecdc56d1674cab90b66125b06d58145e22
- Preserve .beads/interactions.jsonl and never stage it.
- Current carried socket commits under review are 89d24ebc and 11bef6ee, re-ports of the 2.5.2 commits 8b76869 and eef76cd.

Preliminary evidence-backed verdict to verify on resume: RETIREMENT REFUTED. allowIpNameLookup is resolver authorization, not an end-to-end socket authorization policy. Keep both carried socket commits and leave their ledger exit conditions unchanged unless current refs have materially changed.

Five-condition matrix:
1. Literal-address bypass: FAIL. AllowedIpName is consulted only by P2/P3 resolve_addresses. TCP/UDP APIs accept guest-provided IpSocketAddress, SocketAddrCheckFn sees only SocketAddr plus use, and unpatched v2.6.0 permits TcpConnect, UdpConnect, and UdpOutgoingDatagram.
2. Resolved-address substitution: FAIL. P2 returns a bare IpAddress stream and P3 returns Vec<IpAddress>; subsequent socket operations accept arbitrary plain socket addresses. No provenance token or binding connects lookup approval to connect/send.
3. DNS drift: FAIL. P2 ToSocketAddrs and P3 tokio lookup_host resolve afresh. Policy matches the requested name, with no TTL/cache, approved-address pin, or connect-time revalidation.
4. One declared TCP/UDP send/bind policy: FAIL. allowIpNameLookup governs resolution only. The fork separately uses wamn.allow-raw-sockets and socket_addr_permitted for TCP/UDP egress, while bind is separately constrained. The carried patches provide the unified socket decision; the lookup hook does not replace it.
5. Same P2/P3 decision: FAIL as a replacement. Both generations share lookup matching and the address callback, but neither integrates lookup-derived authority into socket operations. Current P2/P3 socket parity is supplied by the carried patches.

COMPLETION/FINDING 2026-07-31

Exact evaluated refs:

- wasmCloud wamn/2.6.0/origin/wamn/2.6.0: 0928c3ecdc56d1674cab90b66125b06d58145e22

DECISION: RETIREMENT REFUTED. allowIpNameLookup authorizes name resolution only; it is not an end-to-end socket authorization policy. Keep both carried socket patches. Leave both ledger exit conditions unchanged.

Five-condition result:
1. Literal-address bypass — FAIL. P2/P3 TCP and UDP accept guest-supplied IpSocketAddress values directly. AllowedIpName is consulted only by resolve_addresses. SocketAddrCheckFn receives only SocketAddr plus SocketAddrUse, with no requested-name identity. At unpatched v2.6.0, linked_call.rs returned true for TcpConnect, UdpConnect, and UdpOutgoingDatagram; removing the carried patches restores that bypass.
2. Resolved-address substitution — FAIL. P2 resolution yields a stream of bare IpAddress values and P3 yields Vec<IpAddress>; later connect/send calls accept arbitrary plain socket addresses. No capability token, name provenance, or approved-resolution binding survives into the socket operation.
3. DNS drift — FAIL. P2 performs a fresh ToSocketAddrs lookup and P3 performs a fresh tokio::net::lookup_host. Policy matches the requested name, not a pinned approved address set. There is no TTL/cache authority boundary or connect-time revalidation, so changed DNS answers silently alter reachable addresses.
4. One declared TCP/UDP send/bind policy — FAIL. allowIpNameLookup controls only resolution. The fork separately resolves wamn.allow-raw-sockets and applies socket_addr_permitted to TCP connect, UDP connect/send, and service-loopback-only bind. Lookup policy cannot express operation, port, or local-bind authority and therefore cannot replace the shared socket policy.
5. Same P2/P3 decision — FAIL as a replacement. Both generations use the same lookup matcher and address callback, but neither derives socket authority from an approved lookup. Current P2/P3 parity for TCP connect, UDP connect/send, and bind is supplied by 89d24ebc and 11bef6ee.

title: [AUDIT-ADOPT-RUNTIME] Apply the accepted wasmCloud-first D17/D21/D23 decision to canonical design docs
description:
## Goal

After the audit synthesis is accepted, update the canonical platform decision records and architecture descriptions to express the owner-confirmed WASI/Wasm/wasmCloud-first target without carrying the superseded native-first ARC11 language.

## Questions

- Which D17, D21, and D23 text must change while preserving their history and non-runtime decisions?
- Which platform-plan, pivot, README, runtime, deployment, and build documents currently describe native transition packaging as the target?
- How are concrete native exceptions and their exit conditions cross-linked to their implementation/proof Beads?

## Evidence Required

- Closed decision wamn-4tob.1.39, corrected ARC11 section U, completed STR9 section V, and final AUDIT-X1 owner acceptance.
- A search inventory of canonical and operational docs for component-first, native-service, hybrid, Posture B, and fork-governance claims.
- Link validation from each retained native exception to its protocol/toolchain/capability evidence and exit owner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Canonical D17, D21, and D23 retain history but clearly state wasmCloud as the platform runtime and components as the default for eligible trusted and untrusted workloads.
- Native exceptions are limited to named runtime-host, protocol, toolchain, operator-tool, or Kubernetes-capability needs with owners and exit conditions.
- PostgreSQL remains sole durable flow authority, Kubernetes remains deployment authority, and the retained WAL to JetStream event architecture is unchanged.

title: [POST-POC-DEC-SLO] Set product service objectives from representative measurements
description:
## Goal

After the post-POC measurement campaign, set product-level latency, throughput, backlog, catch-up, and degraded-operation objectives for each canonical journey.

## Questions

- Which measured workload classes become supported product classes?
- What percentile latency, sustained and burst throughput, backlog age/depth, catch-up time, backpressure, and error-budget objectives apply to each class?
- Which deployment profiles receive different objectives, and which journeys remain explicitly unsupported or best-effort?
- What safety margin separates product objectives from measured saturation and correctness limits?

## Evidence Required

- Completed representative measurements from wamn-4tob.1.37 with immutable provenance and correctness results.
- Product journey priority, user expectations, and any customer-facing promise proposed at that time.
- Cost, topology, durability, workload, payload, and deployment-class context needed to interpret the measurements.

## Decision

Pending. No product objective may be selected until wamn-4tob.1.37 is complete and the owner explicitly approves the supported workload classes and targets. The current controlling decision is the deferral in wamn-4tob.1.13.

## Alternatives Considered

- Promote current D15 or POC gate thresholds: excluded by wamn-4tob.1.13 because they are configuration-specific development evidence.
- Set targets before representative measurement: excluded because it would manufacture requirements.
- Keep a journey permanently best-effort or unsupported: remains a valid per-journey outcome, but it must be explicit when this decision is taken.

## Rationale

Separating measurement from the product decision prevents observed ceilings from becoming accidental promises and lets the owner choose objectives with explicit workload, cost, topology, durability, and correctness context.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every canonical journey receives a measurable objective or explicit supported-state deferral.
- Each objective states percentile, offered/completed load, duration, concurrency, payload/dataset, backlog/catch-up behavior, durability, and deployment class.
- Objectives preserve margin from measured saturation and never weaken correctness or fail-closed behavior.
- Existing POC gates and historical ceilings remain evidence rather than being silently promoted into promises.
- Accepted objectives are integrated into the canonical product and operational documents only after owner approval.

title: [PROD-DEC-TOPOLOGY] Select tenant database and deployment placement topology
description:
## Goal

Select the supported tenant database and deployment placement topology only after exploratory development supplies the product, correctness, scale, failure-domain, and operability evidence.

## Questions

- Should supported deployments use shared pools, bounded cells, per-organization clusters, per-environment clusters, dedicated profiles, or a deliberate combination?
- Which authority, credential, runtime, database, broker, Kubernetes, backup, upgrade, and failure boundaries may each placement class share?
- How are tenants admitted, moved, copied, restored, upgraded, and rebalanced without dual authority or acknowledged-write loss?
- Which current T1/T2/T3/T4 concepts should be retained, amended, replaced, or retired?

## Evidence Required

- Exploratory development evidence for each current and proposed topology.
- Production durability, isolation, cardinality, availability, recovery, and cost decisions when they are made.
- Baseline-matched measurements of connection, storage, WAL, backup, reconciliation, Kubernetes-object, route, and resident-process behavior.
- A reversible migration proof between any topology that ships and its successor.

## Decision

Deferred by the owner during wamn-4tob.1.12. No current T3, T2, T4, cell-based, per-organization, or per-environment shape is committed; all remain exploratory development implementations or hypotheses.

## Alternatives Considered

The existing four-tier D6 model, one unbounded shared pool, bounded shared cells, per-organization clusters, per-environment clusters, dedicated profiles, and hybrid placement selected by explicit policy. None is selected yet.

## Rationale

Current manifests and renderers prove that shapes can be expressed, not that one is the right product topology. Adopting a target before exploratory evidence and production requirements would turn implementation accidents into architecture commitments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every supported placement class has explicit authority, sharing, admission, scaling, failure, recovery, backup, upgrade, and movement boundaries.
- The choice is supported by measured exploratory evidence and the relevant owner-set production requirements.
- Current D6/T1-T4 material receives an explicit keep, amend, replace, or retire verdict rather than silently remaining canonical.
- Transition from any exploratory or previously shipped topology is atomic, reversible, and does not create dual authority.
- Unsupported topology and scale combinations are explicit.

Related future requirement decisions include durability .1.24, isolation profiles .1.26, and cardinality .1.34; references do not authorize or serialize their execution. title: [PROD-DEC-CARDINALITY] Set production tenant and deployment cardinality envelopes
description:
## Goal

Set supported production tenant, project, environment, activity, and deployment cardinality envelopes before making customer scale or topology promises.

## Questions

- How many organizations, projects per organization, environments per project, configured project-environments, and concurrently active project-environments must each production deployment class support?
- Which pooled, cell, per-organization, per-environment, dedicated, regional, edge, and on-premises deployment classes are supported?
- Which limits are contractual, planning targets, exploratory, or explicitly unsupported?
- What admission and degradation behavior applies when an envelope is reached?

## Evidence Required

- Product and commercial deployment assumptions from accountable owners.
- Baseline-matched measurements for connections, storage, WAL, backup, reconciliation, Kubernetes objects, routes, resident processes, and independent workload axes.
- Cost and operability evidence at representative supported loads, without treating current addressability or formulas as requirements.

## Decision

Deferred by the owner during wamn-4tob.1.12. The current supported contract is development-only and makes no production or customer cardinality promise.

## Alternatives Considered

Treat the 10,000-project addressability result as a commitment; derive limits from current 34P/35P connection formulas; invent arbitrary 100/1,000/10,000 tiers; or defer production envelopes until product and production topology decisions exist. The owner selected deferral.

## Rationale

Current measurements and resource formulas describe implementation behavior, not product demand or a supported production operating envelope. Turning them into promises now would manufacture requirements and prematurely constrain topology.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every supported production deployment class has explicit configured and active cardinality envelopes.
- Independent scale axes and admission behavior are stated rather than collapsed into one project count.
- Each limit is labeled contractual, target, exploratory, or unsupported.
- Architecture, cost, operability, and failure-domain evidence supports every promised envelope.
- No current development measurement is presented as a production commitment without an explicit owner decision.

title: [DEC-CUSTOM-NODE-VERSIONING] Set custom-node artifact and invocation compatibility model
description:
## Goal

Choose the custom-node artifact, WIT, and invocation versioning model needed for safe platform upgrades and durable-run resume.

## Questions

- Which identity versions the node artifact, imported WIT capabilities, invocation envelope, node manifest, and persisted run reference?
- Which changes are backward or forward compatible, and how are incompatible combinations refused before effects?
- Does one incompatible node block the platform release or only its dependent flows and runs?
- How are rebuild, migration, deprecation, rollback, and parked-run resume handled?

## Evidence Required

- Current custom-node build, manifest, signing, publish, routing, invocation, capability, and persisted-run contracts.
- Representative old-node/new-platform and new-node/old-platform fixtures, including a parked run.
- Owner requirements for extension stability, upgrade coordination, and failure containment.

## Decision

Deferred by the owner during wamn-4tob.1.16. No versioning or containment model is selected by the development upgrade audit.

## Alternatives Considered

Exact platform-release pinning, independently versioned semantic contracts, rebuild-on-platform-upgrade, and compatibility isolated per node or flow.

## Rationale

Custom nodes are independently built durable artifacts and cannot safely inherit either the atomic platform bundle contract or the external-client contract without an explicit owner decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Canonical identities and owners are explicit for artifact, WIT, invocation, manifest, and persisted references.
- Compatibility, refusal, migration, rollback, and resume behavior is stated.
- Platform-wide versus per-flow failure containment is decided.
- Required conformance fixtures and implementation owners are named without conflating trust or supply-chain policy.

title: [PROD-DEC-CLIENT-COMPAT] Set external client compatibility and deprecation contract
description:
## Goal

Set the production compatibility, versioning, and deprecation contract for independently deployed API and CLI clients.

## Questions

- Which HTTP, generated SDK, GraphQL, OpenAPI, CLI, and other client-facing contracts are supported production interfaces?
- Which changes are backward compatible, how are breaking versions identified, and how long must prior versions remain usable?
- What deprecation notice, tenant coordination, client migration, and pre-effect refusal behavior is required?

## Evidence Required

- Current and planned public contract owners, consumers, generators, version fields, and compatibility tests.
- Representative old-client/new-platform and new-client/old-platform scenarios.
- Owner decisions for production release channels, support windows, and deprecation obligations.

## Decision

Pending production owner decision. The development contract permits explicit breaking changes without an old-version support window and fails incompatible clients before effects.

## Alternatives Considered

Single current version, bounded N-version compatibility, explicit versioned endpoints, and additive-only evolution with scheduled removals.

## Rationale

Independent clients are outside the atomic Wamn deployment bundle, so production compatibility and deprecation cannot be inferred from the development single-version cutover.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every supported client-facing contract has an explicit version and compatibility policy.
- Breaking-change, deprecation, notice, migration, and refusal behavior is stated.
- Required compatibility fixtures and release gates are named.
- The decision does not broaden internal mixed-version or availability promises owned elsewhere.

title: [PROD-DEC-UPGRADE] Set production mixed-version and maintenance contract
description:
## Goal

Set the production upgrade contract before Wamn claims rolling, mixed-version, zero-downtime, rollback, or tenant maintenance guarantees.

## Questions

- Must production remain available while old and new Wamn releases coexist?
- Which host, guest, WIT, event-wire, SQL-schema, catalog, service, and persisted-run versions must interoperate, and for how long?
- Which maintenance windows, tenant notifications, drain limits, rollback windows, and forward-fix rules apply by deployment class?
- How are active, queued, parked, scheduled, and replayed runs routed to compatible immutable artifacts during rollout and recovery?

## Evidence Required

- The development contract selected in wamn-4tob.1.16.
- Measured rollout, drain, persisted-run resume, schema migration, artifact provenance, and rollback evidence.
- Production deployment classes and availability/recovery contracts once selected.

## Decision

Deferred. Development uses a quiesced single-version cutover and makes no mixed-version or zero-downtime promise. This issue must be decided before production claims those properties.

## Alternatives Considered

- Quiesced production maintenance windows with one active release.
- Bounded current-plus-previous mixed-version rolling upgrades.
- Blue-green or canary cutover with preserved old capacity.
- Forward-only migration with explicit recovery windows and no rollback promise.

## Rationale

Kubernetes can execute a rollout but cannot establish compatibility among Wamn contracts or persisted work. Production requirements and deployment classes are not yet selected, so choosing a compatibility window now would invent obligations. A separate decision keeps the development contract correct and prevents rollout mechanics from being mistaken for a product guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Production maintenance and availability behavior is explicit by deployment class.
- Every independently changing contract has a supported old/new compatibility window or a required quiesce boundary.
- Active and persisted work semantics are explicit for partial rollout, rollback, forward-fix, and failed migration.
- Immutable artifact identity, readiness, preserved old capacity, and recovery evidence are required wherever rollback or mixed-version operation is promised.
- The decision does not move Kubernetes deployment mechanics into PostgreSQL or another Wamn state store.

title: [PROD-DEC-DURABILITY] Set production acknowledged-write failure envelope and RPO
description:
## Goal
Define which production failures every acknowledged authoritative mutation must survive and the explicit RPO for each state class.

## Questions
- Which process, node, disk, primary, zone, cluster, object-store, broker, and regional losses are inside each production placement class failure envelope?
- Which state is authoritative, reconstructible, disposable, or permitted to lag, and what acknowledgement boundary applies?
- What CloudNativePG replication, backup, restore, event, artifact, secret, and audit topology proves the selected envelope?

## Evidence Required
- The accepted production placement and state-authority design.
- CloudNativePG failover and backup configuration plus baseline-matched loss/restore drills.
- End-to-end evidence for tenant data, T1, run/queue state, event capture, artifacts, Secrets, audit evidence, and object storage.

## Decision
The checked-in single-instance T3 topology is development-only and carries no production durability claim. CloudNativePG remains the selected database operator; production will extend its topology after the supported failure envelope is chosen. No operation may silently claim durability it cannot provide.

## Rationale
Database technology is selected, but replica, synchronization, backup, and failure-envelope policy require production requirements and executable proof. Development topology must not be mistaken for the target.

## Alternatives Considered
- Treat the current one-instance T3 manifest as production-ready: rejected.
- Replace CloudNativePG solely because the development topology is minimal: rejected by the owner technology decision.
- Advertise zero-loss behavior without declaring the failures it covers: rejected as non-falsifiable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each production state class has a declared authority, acknowledgement boundary, supported failure envelope, and RPO or explicit disposable/unsupported status.
- The selected CloudNativePG and adjacent-store topology has targeted failure and restore proof.
- A failure outside the supported envelope is reported explicitly and cannot become silent corruption, stale promotion, or false success.

Deferred from wamn-4tob.1.14 by owner decision on 2026-07-23: current T3 is development-only; CloudNativePG is the database choice and production topology/durability are decided later. Do not execute without explicit authorization.

title: [PROD-DEC-AVAILABILITY] Set production availability and degradation objectives
description:
## Goal
Set production availability, error-budget, maintenance, and degraded-operation objectives after correctness constraints are fixed.

## Questions
- Which user journeys and control/data/event/runtime planes receive an availability promise?
- Which dependency failures may degrade a journey, and which require fail-closed unavailability?
- How are maintenance, customer-requested destructive operations, and unsupported failure envelopes counted?

## Evidence Required
- Production customer promises and journey priorities.
- Accepted topology, dependency, and failure-domain design.
- Baseline-matched availability and recovery drills using functional rather than pod-health signals.

## Decision
No numeric availability target applies during development. Correctness is controlling; the system must pause or refuse service when continued operation could corrupt, leak, lose, or ambiguously execute accepted work.

## Rationale
An early uptime percentage would encourage availability machinery before the supported product and failure envelope are known. Qualitative containment is sufficient for the current audit.

## Alternatives Considered
- Adopt 99.9, 99.95, or 99.99 percent now: rejected as premature.
- Preserve availability through stale promotion or hidden gaps: rejected by the correctness-first priority.
- Ignore availability permanently: rejected because production journeys eventually need an explicit promise or unsupported verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every offered production journey has a measured availability/degradation contract or explicit unsupported status.
- Accounting rules cover maintenance, dependency loss, destructive recovery, and placement class.
- No availability objective permits acknowledged-write loss, silent corruption, cross-tenant access, unsafe replay, or ambiguous success.
notes:
Deferred from wamn-4tob.1.14 by owner decision on 2026-07-23: no numeric availability objective during development; correctness is above availability. Do not execute without explicit authorization.

title: [PROD-DEC-RTO] Set quantitative recovery-time objectives before production
description:
## Goal
Set evidence-based production recovery-time objectives by plane, failure class, and placement class.

## Questions
- Which failures need separate process, node, primary, cell, restore, and regional recovery clocks?
- When does each clock start and what state marks functionally correct recovery rather than mere pod readiness?
- Which objectives permit automatic versus documented manual recovery?

## Evidence Required
- Production business tolerances and deployment topology.
- Baseline-matched failure drills measuring functional recovery and reconciliation.
- Capacity, staffing, backup, and dependency evidence for each proposed objective.

## Decision
No numeric RTO is required during development and recovery speed is not an architecture acceptance criterion at this stage. Quantitative objectives are deferred until production planning.

## Rationale
Guessed RTO values would force premature infrastructure choices without customer, topology, or drill evidence. Recoverability and correctness remain review requirements now.

## Alternatives Considered
- Adopt proposed 5-minute, 15-minute, one-hour, or four-hour values now: rejected as unevidenced.
- Treat process restart as full recovery: rejected because functional state and cross-store reconciliation may still be incomplete.
- Never define recovery timing: rejected because production operations eventually need measurable objectives.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every supported production failure has a measurable functional-recovery clock or an explicit unsupported verdict.
- Objectives identify load, placement class, dependency state, manual intervention, and verification point.
- No RTO target weakens acknowledged-write durability, isolation, or deterministic recovery.
notes:
Deferred from wamn-4tob.1.14 by owner decision on 2026-07-23: quantitative RTO is unnecessary during development. Do not execute without explicit authorization.

title: [PROD-DEC-RECOVERY-OWNERSHIP] Set recovery ownership and separation of duties before production
description:
## Goal
Define production recovery ownership, escalation, privileged access, and separation-of-duties boundaries.

## Questions
- Which functional owner detects, contains, authorizes, executes, and verifies recovery for each architectural plane?
- Which recovery privileges must be separated to prevent one credential or operator from crossing tenant or plane boundaries?
- What on-call, escalation, incident-command, and customer/sink-owner participation is required?

## Evidence Required
- The production organization and operating model.
- Accepted trust, regulatory, and privileged-access requirements.
- Recovery drills and runbooks showing ownership at every handoff and ambiguous-effect decision.

## Decision
A single general platform owner may perform recovery across all planes during development. Multiple owners, formal RACI, and separation of recovery duties are deferred until production planning.

## Rationale
Development does not yet justify inventing an SRE organization, but production accountability and privilege separation depend on the eventual operating and trust model.

## Alternatives Considered
- Require distinct SRE roles during development: rejected as premature.
- Leave production failures without named accountability: rejected because manual recovery would become unsafe and unowned.
- Treat one unrestricted credential as the permanent operating model: rejected because production isolation requirements are undecided.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every supported production failure has named detection, authorization, execution, verification, and escalation ownership.
- Privileged recovery access and separation of duties match the accepted isolation and regulatory contract.
- Ambiguous external effects name the platform and external-system decision owners without silently assigning success.
notes:
Deferred from wamn-4tob.1.14 by owner decision on 2026-07-23: one general owner is acceptable during development; decide multi-owner recovery responsibility and separation of duties with production operations. Do not execute without explicit authorization.

title: [PROD-DEC-MANUAL-RECOVERY] Set automated versus manual recovery boundary before production
description:
## Goal
Define which production failure classes must recover automatically and which may require documented operator intervention.

## Questions
- Which routine process, node, database, broker, and flow failures must self-recover?
- Which destructive restores or ambiguous external effects legitimately require human authorization or reconciliation?
- What runbook, tooling, audit evidence, access control, and staffing make permitted manual recovery safe?

## Evidence Required
- The accepted production topology and operating model.
- Failure drills covering routine restart, failover, restore, event-gap handling, and ambiguous external effects.
- Evidence that each manual procedure is deterministic, attributable, access-controlled, and does not depend on undocumented expert knowledge.

## Decision
Development may use documented manual recovery for rare, destructive, or genuinely ambiguous failures. The stricter production automation boundary is deferred until production planning.

## Rationale
Automating every rare recovery path is premature during development, while undocumented repair or silent correctness loss is unacceptable at any stage.

## Alternatives Considered
- Require full recovery automation during development: rejected as premature.
- Permit undocumented database surgery or individual expert memory: rejected as unsafe and unreviewable.
- Forbid human judgment for inherently ambiguous external effects: rejected because automation cannot infer an unobserved external outcome safely.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every production failure class has an explicit automatic, documented-manual, or unsupported verdict.
- Manual procedures name authorization, owner, evidence, reconciliation, and rollback requirements.
- No permitted manual path hides acknowledged-write loss, corruption, cross-tenant effects, or unresolved execution ambiguity.
notes:
Deferred from wamn-4tob.1.14 by owner decision on 2026-07-23: documented manual recovery is acceptable during development; set the production automation boundary later. Do not execute without explicit authorization.

title: [PROD-DEC-EVENT-OUTAGE] Set lossless CDC outage and admission policy before production
description:
## Goal
Set the production CDC and broker-outage retention/admission contract without imposing an arbitrary duration or byte threshold during development.

## Questions
- How much logical-decoding backlog must production retain during JetStream or reader outages?
- What measured safety margin and admission behavior prevent replication-slot invalidation or an unrecoverable event gap?
- Which writes or trigger paths pause, reject, or degrade when lossless capture can no longer be guaranteed?

## Evidence Required
- Production write-rate and WAL-generation measurements by placement class.
- Final Postgres storage, max_slot_wal_keep_size, JetStream retention, and monitoring topology.
- Targeted failure proof covering reader outage, broker outage or full storage, restart, replay, slot invalidation, and recovery ownership.

## Decision
No outage-duration, WAL-capacity, or admission threshold is selected during development. Make the production decision from measured workload and topology evidence; silent capture gaps remain forbidden.

## Rationale
The owner deferred an outage-duration and retention threshold until production planning. The values require measured production topology and workload evidence, while the correctness constraint against silent capture gaps applies now.

## Alternatives Considered
- Set a 60-minute or other guessed development threshold: rejected as premature and unevidenced.
- Permit silent capture loss after capacity exhaustion: rejected by the correctness-first priority.
- Treat a fixed 1 GB slot bound as a product contract: rejected because it is an implementation setting rather than a workload-derived guarantee.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The supported outage envelope and capacity margin are explicit and evidence-derived for each production placement class.
- Admission, backpressure, and recovery behavior prevents or explicitly refuses any transition to an undetected capture gap.
- Monitoring, operator ownership, and executable failure proof are named before production use.

title: [PROD-DEC-REGION] Set cross-region durability and recovery contract before production
description:
## Goal
Set the cross-region authority, durability, and recovery contract when the production topology is designed; no cross-region promise applies during development.

## Questions
- Which production placement classes, if any, include total-region loss in their supported failure envelope?
- Which state is synchronously or asynchronously replicated, independently backed up, or reconstructed, and which copy is authoritative after regional loss?
- Is regional continuity required, or is correct fail-closed recovery sufficient, and what operational ownership applies?

## Evidence Required
- The accepted production topology and placement-class decisions.
- CloudNativePG, object-store, JetStream, registry/artifact, secret, control-plane, and Kubernetes-state regional recovery designs.
- A targeted proof that the chosen design cannot promote stale authority, lose acknowledged writes inside its declared envelope, or silently omit or duplicate recovered work.

## Rationale
The owner explicitly deferred any cross-region promise during development. The decision belongs with production topology work because its value and implementation depend on the production placement classes and authoritative-state design.

## Alternatives Considered
- Require regional continuity during development: rejected as premature.
- Silently assume regional recovery is unnecessary forever: rejected because production requirements may change.
- Promote an unverified or stale regional copy to preserve availability: rejected by the correctness-first priority.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The supported regional failure envelope and explicitly unsupported cases are stated per authoritative state store.
- Correctness remains controlling; no availability goal permits acknowledged-write loss, silent corruption, or unsafe promotion.
- Recovery ownership, reconciliation behavior, and required proof are explicit before any production cross-region promise is made.
notes:
Deferred from wamn-4tob.1.14 by owner decision on 2026-07-23: no cross-region promise at the development stage; revisit alongside the other production topology decisions. Do not execute without explicit authorization.
held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [SR22] Custom-node invocation wire lacks a version and mixed-version contract
description:
## Goal

Give the independently deployed flowrunner and serve-node a canonical, explicitly versioned custom-node invocation protocol with safe rolling-upgrade behavior.

## Questions

- Where is the wire version represented and which crate owns it?
- Which request, context, response, and node-error changes are backward or forward compatible under strict readers?
- What rollout, drain, key-rotation, rollback, and refusal policy coordinates old and new flowrunner/serve-node pairs?
- How is this internal authentication domain kept separate from public ingress and other workload identities?

## Evidence Required

- Source evidence from crates/wamn-node-invoke/src/lib.rs, including deny_unknown_fields and the unversioned request envelope.
- An old-server/new-client and new-server/old-client fixture matrix covering an additive optional request field, a response/error change, key rotation, and rollback.
- Production-path evidence that an incompatible version refuses before executing the node or acknowledging success.
- Alignment with the owner-set compatibility contract in wamn-4tob.1.16.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One canonical owner and explicit version identity exist for the invocation protocol.
- A documented producer/consumer compatibility matrix defines accepted and refused combinations.
- Mixed-version fixtures prove both rolling directions and deterministic pre-effect refusal for incompatible pairs.
- Internal HMAC/key rotation and replay behavior remain distinct from external caller authentication.
- Drain, rollback, and parked-run resume behavior preserve the exact compatible executor and node artifact identity.
