title: [SR21] Stored-suite drivability duplicates an incomplete production dispatch contract
description:
## Goal

Give production dispatch and stored-suite drivability one exhaustive, guest-safe source of supported node types.

## Questions

- Should runner-intrinsic built-ins live in an existing contract crate, be generated into both consumers, or be exposed through a non-runnable descriptor API?
- Are built-in and standard-node descriptors one compatibility surface or two composed surfaces?
- What versioning rule applies when a supported node type is added, removed, or renamed?

## Evidence Required

- A regression showing an added production built-in passes the current private-source guard yet is refused by stored-suite drivability.
- Cargo metadata proving the chosen canonical owner remains guest-safe.
- Compatibility evidence for existing flowrunner dispatch, stored suites, testkitbench, and suite gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Delete the duplicated built-in list or generate it from the canonical owner.
- Delete private-source text scanning as the completeness mechanism.
- Dispatch and drivability consume one exhaustive descriptor set.
- Addition, removal, or rename fails a completeness test until execution and scenario support are intentionally classified.
- Unknown node types remain fail-closed.
- Existing flowrunner, testkit, suite, and stored-case evidence remains equivalent.
- Production code does not depend on wamn-gates or another test-only composition root.
notes:
STR4 source proof: crates/wamn-gates/src/testkitbench.rs duplicates built-in names in BUILTIN_NODE_TYPES and is_drivable. Its pinning test only checks that each existing string occurs somewhere in components/flowrunner/src/lib.rs; unlike the standard-node guard, it cannot detect an additional production dispatch arm. A new built-in can therefore pass the guard but be rejected as undrivable. STR5 owns canonical contract placement; STR9 owns packaging.
STR5 VERDICT 2026-07-23 (docs/findings.md Q.2): one exhaustive guest-safe composed descriptor classifies every flow node type and scenario-support level. Standard descriptors may remain in wamn-nodes; execution-contract ownership covers intrinsic/custom/legacy classes. Flowrunner and stored-suite drivability consume the same composition. title: [SR18] Control-plane image cannot execute advertised dump, restore, and copy paths
description:
## Goal

Give every direct dump-project-env, restore-project-env, and copy-project-env path one explicit immutable operational artifact containing its required PostgreSQL client tools.

## Questions

- Should version-matched pg_dump and pg_restore ship in the ctl image or a separate recovery image?
- Which direct dump, restore, copy data, copy both, and cutover paths spawn each tool?
- Which Job, CronJob, or runbook owns credentials, object storage, rollback, and artifact provenance?

## Evidence Required

- The 15-command ctl surface and every checked-in invocation environment.
- Exact tool-spawning paths in dump_project_env.rs, restore_project_env.rs, and copy_project_env.rs plus Dockerfile ctl contents.
- Exact-image dump, scratch restore, and copy round trips against every supported PostgreSQL major version.

## Steps to Reproduce

Build the Docker ctl target and invoke dump-project-env --run-now, restore-project-env, or a copy-project-env data, both, or cutover path that shells pg_dump or pg_restore. The final image contains wamn-ctl but explicitly installs neither client, so execution fails unless an undocumented alternate environment supplies it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each advertised operational path names and ships in a versioned artifact with all required tools.
- PostgreSQL client/server and dump-format compatibility is explicit and tested.
- Production Jobs, CronJobs, and runbooks reference the exact immutable artifact and least-privilege credentials.
- Unsupported command/image combinations fail at configuration or startup, never mid-recovery or cutover.
- Exact-image dump-to-scratch-restore and source-to-destination copy round trips pass.

title: [R38] Materializer acknowledges refusals without durable refusal evidence
description:
## Goal

Make every ACK or TERM of a refused or malformed event leave durable, queryable, alertable evidence before the consumer advances.

## Questions

- Which store owns refused-event evidence and its retention?
- Which conditions are retryable, refused, or poison-message terminal?
- How can an operator replay or explicitly dispose of a refusal?

## Evidence Required

- Baseline source evidence in components/materializer/src/main.rs:427-550.
- Restart-after-ACK/TERM tests proving refusal evidence survives process and host loss.
- Alert and runbook evidence tied to stream, sequence, registration, tenant, and reason.

## Steps to Reproduce

Deliver an event that deterministically refuses or a malformed message, leave the optional report path unset, and restart the materializer after its ACK or TERM. Query durable product state and the consumer position; the message has advanced while refusal evidence existed only in process output/counters.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ACK/TERM occurs only after durable refusal evidence is committed or an equivalently durable external sink confirms it.
- Evidence has stable event identity, bounded payload handling, reason taxonomy, retention, and tenant scope.
- Operators can distinguish retry backlog from permanently refused messages and take an authorized recovery action.
- A targeted refusal gate proves the behavior across materializer restart.

title: [EVT-RI-ORCH] registration-change RI reconcile hop — API-path writes leave an old-image gap until the next publish/migrate
description: Deferred from wamn-l5i9.61 (93ed048): publish/migrate-catalog now auto-reconcile REPLICA IDENTITY, but registration create/update/delete on the API path runs under wamn_app which cannot ALTER — a registration that adds/removes an old-image or delete subscription on an already-applied catalog opens an old-image gap until the next publish/migrate-catalog run or a manual wamn-ctl reconcile-replica-identity. Correctness is protected (the materializer treats old-absent as an alertable cannot-evaluate refusal, never condition-false), so this is an operational-latency gap, not a data hole. Full solution needs a control-plane hop (queued reconcile drained by a control-plane actor/verb) — l5i9.61 deliberately did not build a new long-lived service. The pure detect surface exists: ReplicaIdentityPlan::pending_old_image_gap in wamn-migrate. Parent epic wamn-l5i9.
notes: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-20 (AskUserQuestion at the l5i9.19 boundary): mechanism = PERIODIC CRONJOB — a K8s CronJob runs the EXISTING wamn-ctl reconcile-replica-identity verb per project-env on a ~5min cadence (no new long-lived service, no queue; reuses the shipped verb + the provisioning-Job superuser-creds pattern; the gap closes within one cadence, and l5i9.66's response warning covers the window). REJECTED: dispatcher-drained queue (the dispatcher runs as wamn_app — no ALTER; draining would add a superuser credential to an always-on service against the R8b scoping posture) and detect+runbook-only (leaves the gap open indefinitely). title: [5.6-AUTHN] runner<->node authn — mTLS or signed invocation envelope (v0 trusts the network layer)
description: wamn-bd5 v0 trusts in-cluster callers at the network layer: any pod that can reach the serve-node Service can POST an invocation envelope. Host-side containment already holds (grant installed get-only; project pinned to the serve-node's own --project, never the request; E17 import screen at load) so a forged envelope cannot self-grant or cross projects — but it CAN invoke the node with attacker-chosen input and read the response, including any credential the envelope declares within the project. AR1 trust-assumption theme (docs/review-2026-07.md): this is load-bearing once untrusted tenant nodes ship.

title: [EVT-RI-ORCH] reconcile-replica-identity has no operational caller — wire into publish/migrate-catalog and/or registration change
description: l5i9.31 shipped reconcile-replica-identity as a standalone wamn-ctl superuser verb; nothing calls it automatically. A registration created (or a catalog published) without the operator running the verb leaves the entity on REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT, so its old-value/delete conditions refuse old-image-absent until someone reconciles — and the NON-RETROACTIVE flip means that window is a permanent old-image gap. Decide and wire the operational caller: run reconcile inside publish-catalog/migrate-catalog (they already touch the catalog under a privileged role — but adding a cross-tenant ALTER pass widens their blast radius, which is why l5i9.31 did not do it), and/or a registration-create/update/delete hook on the API path (wamn_app cannot ALTER — needs a control-plane hop or queued reconcile). Until closed, the runbook step is manual (docs/provisioning.md reconcile-replica-identity).
close_reason: Shipped in 93ed048 (integrated from the wave5 lane): publish-catalog/migrate-catalog auto-reconcile REPLICA IDENTITY after apply — auto-ALTER decision over refuse-posture because both verbs already connect as the superuser the ALTER requires (WAMN_PG_ADMIN_URL, same as the standalone verb) and the pass is idempotent + scoped strictly to the verb's --schema (the cross-tenant union only selects which registrations demand FULL); reuses the tested l5i9.31 reconcile() path; --skip-reconcile-replica-identity escape hatch on both verbs; new pure detect surface ReplicaIdentityPlan::pending_old_image_gap. Manual runbook step retired for the publish/migrate path (docs/provisioning.md); [EVT-RI-ORCH] recipe in build-and-test.md. title: [5.14/D20] terminal business-failure of a blocking partition head — wedge semantics undefined
description: Deferral from wamn-fqg.9 (091e35a): a terminally-failed (business-failure, retries exhausted -> error route/RetryExhausted) HEAD of a blocking-policy partition currently dequeues like the unpartitioned path, so the partition UNBLOCKS past a failed head. D20 wedging covers crash-exhaustion (janitor-exempt) and head-unavailability (claim SQL) but has no precedent for a terminally-failed head; leaving the row would redrive-loop, dequeuing silently violates strict ordering past a failure. Decide the contract (wedge partition + alert? dead-letter the head + continue? policy knob?) and gate it. Not exercised by the fqg.9 gates (seeded flow always completes). Relates D20 (ordering decision), wamn-jkrz (failoverbench retry-phase gap).
notes: OWNER DECISION 2026-07-20 (AskUserQuestion at the cleanup-wave boundary): wedge semantics = DEAD-LETTER + CONTINUE (owner: 'leaning towards dead letter queue'). A terminally-failed (business-failure/RetryExhausted→error-route) HEAD of a blocking partition DEQUEUES and the key CONTINUES in order — but never silently: the dequeue must land an alertable dead-letter record (a wamn_run dead-letter ledger row in the SAME txn as the dequeue: tenant, run_id, partition_key, flow, reason, failed_at) so an operator sees that strict ordering proceeded past a failed head. The run's own history stays on runs (5.7); the DL row is the ordering-was-breached marker, not a second run-state. REJECTED: wedge+alert (the D20 crash-exhaustion posture — owner chose availability; leapfrog remains the pre-existing opt-out axis) and a new per-flow wedge-on-terminal knob (surface for a case leapfrog mostly covers). title: [R32] Retryable/RateLimited node errors abort the invocation ('unexpected retry wait'), hold the lease, and never advance the retry budget — production dispatch path
description: docs/findings.md s2 R32 (Wave-1 review, High). Both drivers advance the engine with clock 0 (flowrunner lib.rs:682,731,987,1032). Un-exhausted Retryable -> schedule_retry(0+backoff_ms) (engine.rs:399-405, default base 100ms) -> next() returns Step::Wait -> BOTH drivers Err('unexpected retry wait') (lib.rs:703,1005). Standard nodes really emit these (http.rs:187,194; postgres.rs:37-45). In run_next the Err propagates before park/dequeue: lease held to expiry, reclaimed, attempt resets to 0 on reconstruction (engine.rs:308) -> budget never advances, error edge never fires, run reaped as infra-failure. Contradicts the inline design note lib.rs:699-702 (cross-invocation retry belongs to the queue layer via park_sql) which is unimplemented. FIX: translate Step::Wait into a park (ClaimOutcome outcome=1, park_ms=until-now) so run_next parks + releases; for execute() park equivalently or drive a real clock. VERIFY: flow with a Retryable-on-attempt-0 node parks and eventually error-routes or fails RetryExhausted.
close_reason: R32 shipped a59619d (worktree commit 48504b9, clean cherry-pick). Step::Wait now carries the pending attempt; both drivers (execute AND execute_claimed — the production run_next path) translate it into a park (ClaimOutcome outcome=1, park_ms=until_ms) reusing the delay-node park path, so the lease releases instead of aborting with 'unexpected retry wait'. Attempt persists across reclaim via (node,attempt) in runs.state_json + Plan::restore_retry after reconstruct (front-check guards stale state), so the budget advances to RetryExhausted or error-route instead of resetting to 0 and being reaped as infra-failure. Gates: worktree 39/39 wamn-runner tests incl. 6 new R32 tests + 2 mutants killed by named tests (attempt-persistence drop; Wait attempt:0) with sha256-verified restore + clippy clean; MAIN-tree re-gate 39/39 + flowrunner wasm32-wasip2 check clean + poc-webhook-f1 still compiles. title: [R24] Plan::resume unrecoverable for merge/loop flows: N visits collapse to one node_runs row (occurrence=0) -> spurious Mismatch/Overrun
description: docs/findings.md s2 R24 (Wave-1 review, Med). The walk dispatches a node once PER edge (engine.rs:438-446; merges run once per arriving token, engine.rs:20-22) and cycles are permitted (RunawayBudget), but record_node_run writes occurrence=0 (flowrunner lib.rs:234-237) into node_runs PK (tenant,run,node,occurrence) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (run-state.sql:131; run-store sql.rs:102-107) -> N dispatches persist 1 row. Plan::resume (engine.rs:529-557) demands exactly one Recorded per dispatch matched by node id -> resumed merge/loop runs die with spurious Mismatch/Overrun; a loop that crashes after 2 visits is permanently unrecoverable. FIX: compute occurrence from prior visits end-to-end (schema anticipates it) + visit-aware match in resume; OR enforce acyclic-single-visit at compile if resume must hold. VERIFY: diamond flow (A->B,A->C,B->D,C->D) killed mid-D reconstructs without Mismatch. Latent today (shipped fixtures acyclic); escalates to High when a merge/loop flow needs resume.
close_reason: R24: resume is visit-aware via per-visit history — seq-ordered replay folds one Recorded per visit, so merge/loop runs reconstruct exactly (schema anticipated it; only driver/store hardcoded 0). VERIFY held: diamond A->{B,C}->D killed mid-D reconstructs without Mismatch and re-dispatches only D@1 (resume_diamond_killed_mid_merge_reconstructs_and_completes); loop killed after 2 laps resumes at x@2 (resume_mid_loop_continues_at_the_right_visit); store-level per-visit reconstruction + full-history idempotence; a LEGACY collapsed history now fails LOUD (reconstruct_detects_legacy_collapsed_merge_history: Mismatch e-vs-d) instead of silently re-running effects. Live: runnerbench merge-resume reconstructs a partially-recorded merge through the production claim path (parks between visits).

title: [SR11] Sql{text,arity} composition type; convert the three composing call sites
description: docs/findings.md section-4 SR11 (High). run-queue/src/sql.rs:214 hardcodes $7/$8 on the assumption that wamn_run_store::sql::insert_node_run_success_sql — A DIFFERENT CRATE — uses exactly $1..$6. The type system cannot see it; no test in wamn-run-queue can (the coupling is to a string produced elsewhere); the only guard is a comment. This is the bill for pure-crates-emit-SQL-strings: the strings compose, their CONTRACTS do not. FIX: struct Sql{text,arity} with append(tail,tail_arity) renumbering the tail against the head arity (safer), or expose base.arity so callers write the offset (one afternoon). Home: wamn-ddl or a new wamn-sql leaf; convert the three composing call sites first; leaves may keep returning String. VERIFY: assert arity per composed statement against a pinned constant. Before the next composed statement.

title: [R14] held outbox rows head-of-line-block the poll window
description: docs/findings.md section-2 R14 (Med, liveness — LIVE per R10: the outbox is the only working capture path until the l5i9.19 teardown). outbox_poll_sql is WHERE dispatched_at IS NULL ORDER BY seq LIMIT n; plan_ack correctly refuses to ack HELD rows (an active-but-unparseable flow), so they stay NULL forever and, being oldest, permanently occupy the lowest seq slots. Once --batch (64) held rows accumulate, row-event dispatch STOPS PROJECT-WIDE for every flow because of one broken flow. FIX: (A, no schema change) pass the held (table,event) set into the poll and exclude it — the dispatcher already reads the registry inside the transaction, so reorder rather than add a round trip; (B, preferred) a held_since timestamptz the poll filters on, which also gives the backlog an AGE to alert on. Either way bound the backlog and escalate past it. VERIFY: pure-layer poll-window model; dispatchbench with an invalid flow generating batch+1 events plus one healthy event.
close_reason: R14 shipped (main cebd722, from wave2/queue b3174fe): outbox.held_since timestamptz; poll excludes held rows (AND held_since IS NULL, outbox_pending partial index updated); outbox_hold_sql stamps once (age-preserving); pure plan_hold = exact complement of plan_ack; dispatcher stamps held rows in the ack txn + warns with count — held rows no longer head-of-line-block, backlog has an age to alert on. LOCAL gates: pure poll-window model (held batch + healthy → healthy reached), drift guards, live-PG on real SQL, 1 mutant killed, re-gated in main tree. In-cluster dispatchbench invalid-flow batch+1 scenario rides wamn-2jkm.41.

NOT an argument against the split — an argument for: (1) qualify the crate headers now (this bead); (3) make the claim_batch_sql-style annotation (what the pure test does not cover) the convention for every composed or plan-sensitive statement. The live-test extension is SR12b.

title: [E4] run_id lexical vs numeric stream_seq: carry stream_seq BIGINT ahead of run_id in the queue ordering key

FIX: carry stream_seq as a BIGINT column ahead of run_id in the ordering key (numeric semantics, indexable, no width ceiling); zero-pad run_id to fixed width as the belt. Inert today (all rows 0); materializer passes real values. LOCAL gates: re-pinned ORDER BY/DDL drift guards, live-PG numeric-head assertion (8→9 not 10→11), 1 mutant killed, re-gated in main tree. title: [E1] publish pipelining: settle acks at the Commit frame, bounded in-flight set, retry from first unacked
description: docs/findings.md section-3 E1 (High). drain() awaits each row ack before reading the next — the entire capture path capped at one round trip per row. Sequential-ack buys NO ordering: NATS is ordered per connection and assigns stream_seq on arrival, so pipelined publishes land in publish order; ordering is broken by parallel connections, not pipelining. FIX: publish without awaiting, hold the ack futures, settle them at the Commit frame before advancing the LSN (the v3 section-4 invariant is preserved exactly — it was always per-transaction); bound the in-flight set (~256) and drain mid-transaction when hit (safe, the LSN still holds); on failure retry the transaction publishes from the first unacked row — the dedupe window absorbs the landed prefix, ON CONFLICT absorbs what it misses. If insufficient (C-CDC decides): shard M connections HASHED ON PARTITION KEY. NEVER unordered publish with consumer-side reordering. REPLICA IDENTITY FULL is NON-RETROACTIVE — it enriches only WAL written after the flip, so every event captured before a table flips permanently lacks old-images and cannot be backfilled; the migration cost is that irrecoverable gap (growing with capture time), not the cheap metadata ALTER. This knob must therefore ship and apply at/before registration BEFORE the materializer (wamn-l5i9.17) exposes old-value/changed-to conditions — full contract in l5i9.17's DESIGN field. Do NOT flip the global default (per-table WAL amplification; poc/cdc1 toast test ships the full 22.4KB old value under FULL).

title: [EVT-MAT] materializer as a Service workload v1 — condition eval, causation enforcement, ON CONFLICT enqueue, doorbell takeover
description: v3 section 5: durable consumer per subscribing flow; condition evaluates HERE (hot-editable; filtered-out events remain in the stream so condition edits are replayable); causation max-depth + cycle check — refusals are a distinct, alertable outcome; deterministic run_id = <flow>:evt:<stream_seq> + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING = the exactly-once guarantee (dedupe window is fast path only). Delivery order = stream order = commit order per DB. partitioned(key) extracts the key from the payload — hard-depends on the R6 blocking sign-off (EVT-P0-DECISIONS) and wamn-fqg.20. Takes over the wake doorbell after the enqueue commit (else async latency degrades to the reconciliation sweep). v1 NATIVE in the dispatcher; component target = EVT-COMPONENT.
design: De-facto replica-identity contract (Q2/wamn-l5i9.56, 2026-07-19, as of tip 92f96ae): every captured table runs REPLICA IDENTITY DEFAULT over the surrogate 'id uuid' PK (emit.rs:149; nothing in provisioning or the DDL compiler sets it). pgoutput therefore emits: INSERT -> full new, no old; UPDATE -> full new with unchanged out-of-line TOAST columns ABSENT from the map (a real NULL is present as null - distinguishable) and NO old image at all (old-key emits only when a PK column changes, which app writes never do); DELETE -> old carrying the key column id ONLY (not even tenant_id) and no new. Verified live: event_reader_live.rs:619-645, poc/cdc1 TOAST test. Design against exactly this: the exactly-once enqueue (run_id=<flow>:evt:<stream_seq> + ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) is stream-derived and image-independent -> DEFAULT is SUFFICIENT for it and for new-value conditions; any changed-to/changed-from/old-vs-new condition and any delete-payload condition beyond the key is UNEVALUATABLE under DEFAULT - that is what the per-entity FULL knob (wamn-l5i9.31) fills. Do NOT flip the global default to FULL (per-table WAL amplification; the toast test ships the full 22.4KB old value). ALTER ... REPLICA IDENTITY FULL is NON-RETROACTIVE: the pre-FULL window is a permanent old-image gap that grows with capture time, so (a) l5i9.31 must ship and apply at/before registration BEFORE the materializer exposes old-value conditions, and (b) treat old-absent as cannot-evaluate, never as condition-false. Note also: a DELETE event alone cannot be tenant-scoped under DEFAULT (tenant_id is not in the PK; the subject carries org/project/env, not intra-DB tenant_id).

== SCOPE (bd desc + v3 §4) ==
When a connection belongs to a run, the wamn:postgres plugin emits ONE pg_logical_emit_message('wamn.causation', {run, root, depth}) per transaction; the reader stamps it onto that txn's envelopes. Transactional (rides the txn commit — a rolled-back txn emits nothing), guest-unforgeable, zero schema footprint (event plane). Depth/CYCLE ENFORCEMENT is NOT this bead — it lives in the materializer (EVT-MAT, l5i9.17, does not exist yet); the reader only CAPTURES {run,root,depth}. Message-event surfacing was verified by S-CDC-1 (fallback: next_raw_event). The wire side is ALREADY DONE: wamn_event_wire::Causation{run,root,depth} (serde, deny_unknown_fields, depth u32) + Envelope.causation:Option<Causation> exist; the reader's drain() sets causation:None with the comment "stitching = wamn-l5i9.12". This bead fills that None.

== FORKS -> AskUserQuestion at execution (two calls: F0+FA+FB, then FC+FD+FE) ==
 F0 SCOPE / SPLIT (raise FIRST): the bead bundles TWO deliverables — (A) the wamn:postgres plugin EMIT (host injects the transactional message into run-owned txns) and (B) the reader STITCH (enable messages, decode the Message frame within a txn, stamp {run,root,depth} onto that txn's envelopes). They are SEPARABLE and INDEPENDENTLY GATABLE: (B) is gated with test-SQL-emitted messages (no plugin needed) — local live gate + reader in-cluster; (A) is gated by asserting the emitted message reaches the WAL and (end-to-end) that a flow run's row events carry causation — which needs the FLOWRUNNER PATH + an IMAGE REBAKE gate of record (heavier; the flow engine ships inside flowrunner.wasm). issues-are-granular says: decide BEFORE starting whether to SPLIT into .12a [reader stitch] + .12b [plugin emit] (recommended — different gates, the stitch is the light half and unblocks nothing else, the emit carries the WIT/architecture risk in FA) or keep as one. If split: file the two children with deps/parent, claim ONLY the one being executed, leave the other in bd ready.
 FA RUN-CONTEXT SOURCE (the crux of the EMIT half): how does the plugin learn {run, root, depth} to emit? TWO hard constraints — (1) the wamn:postgres WIT is FROZEN 0.1.0 (2026-07-10, S2-passed) — a NEW guest-facing method to declare run context UN-FREEZES it (avoid, or it becomes an interface-evolution decision); (2) the run id is GUEST-CLAIMED mid-drain (the flowrunner's run-next claims one run from the queue INSIDE the guest call; run_worker.call_run_next returns run_id only AFTER the guest returns — so the run id is NOT host-known before the transactions that need stamping). set_tenant/set_runner are host-side, keyed on component_id, STABLE per replica — the run id is NOT stable per component (one component drains many runs). Candidates: (1) host-native set_run_context called from a run-aware seam — but WHERE does the host learn the run id mid-drain without a WIT round-trip? (would need the run-queue claim to move host-native, or a host callback the guest triggers); (2) a NEW WIT method (unfreezes 0.1.0 — an explicit interface decision, flag it to the owner); (3) derive from run-state: the plugin observes the run-owned connection's writes / app.runner — fragile. root comes from runs.root_run_id (EXISTS); run = the current run_id; depth is FB. GROUND in run_worker drain + how flowrunner claims BEFORE presenting — if the run id genuinely can't reach the plugin without a WIT change or an architecture move, SURFACE that as the decision (this may be why the emit half deserves to be its own bead).
 FB DEPTH SOURCE: runs.root_run_id EXISTS (so root is free); depth is NOT stored in runs. Options: (a) a root/webhook/cron run (trigger_source != event) is depth 0, root = its own run_id — the MVP can stamp exactly this; (b) an EVENT-triggered run's depth = triggering event's depth + 1 — but that threads from the MATERIALIZER (l5i9.17, sets run_id=<flow>:evt:<seq> and would carry the parent causation), which DOES NOT EXIST — so event-run depth is NOT computable this bead; (c) add a depth column to runs (run-state is OURS, not the event plane — "zero schema footprint" is about the EVENT plane, so this is legal if wanted). LEAN: MVP stamps depth from what's knowable now (root runs = depth 0); note HONESTLY that the depth-increment for event-triggered chains lands with .17 (the reader passes through whatever depth it's given — it does not compute the chain). Do NOT fake a depth the system can't yet derive.
 FC EMIT MECHANICS: transactional pg_logical_emit_message(true, 'wamn.causation', <content>) — `true` = transactional so it rides the commit (a rolled-back txn emits nothing = the unforgeable property). Content = the Causation JSON (pin the exact bytes with a string test — the reader parses it). Injected ONCE per plugin-managed transaction: at BEGIN alongside the SET LOCAL claims (begin_with_claims, simplest) vs lazily before COMMIT. Guest-forgeability: the guest must NOT be able to emit its own 'wamn.causation' message (it would forge causation) — extend the statement_mutates_session-style guard to reject pg_logical_emit_message / pg_logical_emit_message_bytea with the wamn.* prefix on the raw query/execute surface (defense-in-depth, mirrors the SET-guard; note it is a blocklist not a structural close — the AR1 theme). The plugin's OWN emit is the only legitimate wamn.causation writer.
 FD READER STITCHING: enable protocol Messages on the stream — ReplicationStreamConfig has with_messages(bool); the .10 reader does NOT enable it (verify the current config — StreamingMode::Off path). In drain(), EventType::Message{flags,message_lsn,prefix,content} currently `=> continue`: decode when prefix=="wamn.causation" and flags&1 (transactional), parse the Causation JSON, and STAMP it onto that txn's envelopes. FRAME ORDER IS THE OPEN QUESTION (instrument, do NOT assume): a transactional message is delivered in the stream at its LSN position within the Begin..Commit — it may arrive BEFORE or AFTER the row events of the same txn. If it can arrive AFTER a row event, the streaming-publish drain (publish each row as it arrives) CANNOT stamp retroactively — the reader must BUFFER the txn's row events and publish at Commit with the causation attached. That is a MATERIAL change to drain()'s shape (today: publish-as-you-go; then: buffer-per-txn). Instrument the real frame order in the live gate FIRST, then choose. title: [3.2] Outbox write-amplification: registration-driven per-entity trigger emission
description:
Split from wamn-d8v per the issues-are-granular rule (d8v narrows to the GC half). AMPLIFICATION half, verified at 873c3d8 and still true at 1e1bc99: outbox_triggers_plan (crates/wamn-ddl/src/outbox.rs:134-158) emits an AFTER ... FOR EACH ROW trigger for EVERY catalog entity unconditionally when the opt-in plan is applied — no per-entity filter tied to actual row-event flow registration (the loop is 'for e in &catalog.entities'; drop_outbox_triggers_plan loops identically). A 100k-row bulk import pays 100k outbox inserts inside the user's transaction (write amplification, txn bloat, WAL) and then up to 100k firings per registered flow. The dispatcher acks unregistered rows cheaply, but the WRITE cost is paid regardless of registration.

FIX DIRECTION: per-entity emission driven by actual row-event registration (or an explicit designer flag per entity), reconciled when registrations change — CREATE OR REPLACE + constant-named triggers already make re-apply idempotent, so narrowing coverage is mechanical. Separately: a coalescing/rate policy story for registered high-churn tables (statement-level triggers with transition tables are the escape hatch if per-row ever dominates — payload-shape change, so a deliberate decision, not a default).

GATE THIS BEFORE bulk-import tooling lands (3.6-adjacent; no bulk-import bead exists yet — this issue is its prerequisite). VERIFY: bulk-write bench case — 10k-row single-statement UPDATE on a registered table: outbox insert cost measured, firing count correct. External review R8c (docs/review-findings.md § R8). The wamn-z7b.2 C2 bench (outbox trigger overhead) quantifies this cost — related, not blocking.

A record stream feeds many records through ONE flow while amortizing per-invocation overhead (component instantiation, plan compile) with per-key order preserved — this REPLACES any batch API (decision D9). Design source: docs/platform-plan.md 5.11.

Needs a design pass first: the record-stream API shape (how a stream is declared on a flow; how records map to runs and partition keys; how invocation overhead is amortized — warm-instance reuse vs pooled dispatch — while keeping the 5.7 per-record checkpoint / exactly-once guarantees). The D20 partition head-unavailability policy (wamn-1d4) is the ordering substrate a record stream's per-record dispatch preserves order over; wamn-fqg.9 (guest self-claim of partitioned work) materializes a flow's declared ordering/policy onto the queue row at enqueue and is the likely integration point.
notes: DESIGN DECIDED (dkk 2026-07-17, AskUserQuestion): (1) API shape = RECORDS ARE RUNS — no new contract surface; a record stream is many runs of one flow; per-record 5.7 audit/exactly-once falls out. (2) Ordering declaration + dispatcher key stamping SPLIT OUT to wamn-fqg.20 (granularity rule); fqg.9 (guest partitioned claim, now P2) depends on it. (3) fqg.18 scope = AMORTIZATION ONLY, mechanisms chosen: MEASURE FIRST (runnerbench stream mode baseline: N records through one flow, per-record cost), then (a) guest plan+owner cache — memoize parsed Flow keyed by (flow_id, active version) with a cheap version probe so hot-reload-on-version-bump is preserved (a hot-reload gate assertion is REQUIRED); cache the runner owner once per instance; (b) SQL trip combining — one CTE statement for claim+mark-running+dispatch-read (can also return the active flow version, making the cache probe free), one for complete+dequeue (also makes completion+dequeue ATOMIC, strictly better than today's split), renew_lease folded into record_node_run (2 trips/node -> 1), keeping per-node checkpoint commits. Batched claim (run-next-many) NOT chosen. Baseline today ~7 fixed trips + 2/node + full graph fetch/parse/compile per record; component instantiation is ALREADY amortized (run-worker one-instance — the bead description's instantiation claim is stale). Combined builders live in wamn-run-queue::sql (precedent: write_ahead_run_sql already writes runs; keep the fqg.4 AS MATERIALIZED claim fence — shape-pin it). Gates: runnerbench stream mode before/after + correctness (all complete, per-record node_runs, exactly-once, hot-reload mid-stream) + crate shape/live-apply for new builders + mutation; in-cluster gate of record (guest changes -> full rebuild).
close_reason: Record-stream dispatch amortization shipped (D9: records map 1:1 to runs, no batch API). Combined one-statement claim+mark-running+dispatch-read+version-probe / per-node checkpoint+lease-renew / atomic complete+dequeue builders in wamn-run-queue (claim scan shared by fragment with claim_batch_sql), guest plan cache keyed by active version (hot-reload invalidation gated) + instance-cached owner. 66.1 -> 32-37 ms/record local (statements ~18 -> ~8/record, no per-record parse/compile). Gates: runnerbench stream+stream-reload phases, failoverbench 6/6, flowbench, testhostbench, queuebench x5, 37 crate tests + extended live-apply (real combined builders via PREPARE/EXECUTE incl flows.sql), 5/5 mutants killed, in-cluster gate of record = full rebuild both images + deployed runner + ladderproof rungs 3/2/1 all PASS. Ordering declaration split to wamn-fqg.20; guest partitioned claim = wamn-fqg.9 (P2).

title: [EVT-C1] retained-events-table prototype + measured knee (the section-13 alternative)
description: Build the minimal Postgres alternative: events table (append), per-flow cursor rows, cursor-claim loop. Matrix: append rate 250->500->1k->2k->5k->knee events/sec x consumers 1/5/20 x payload 1/16/64 KiB, co-resident with app CRUD at fixed rate on the same instance. Measure: app-path p99 delta, bloat growth, WAL share, cursor-claim throughput per consumer, end-to-end latency. Replaces v1's FABRICATED '1-2k events/sec/org' with a measured knee — the honest crossover criterion for D19. Deliberately sequenced BEFORE C4/any new infra (v2.1 re-sequencing): cheapest experiment, decision-relevant; the standing NATS cluster is the design's main cost and should not be stood up to discover it wasn't needed. The prototype's outbox/subject/materializer semantics are shared with the JetStream branch — not throwaway. Design: docs/event-plane-jetstream.md sections 10 (C1) + 13.
notes:
RESUME PLAN (banked 2026-07-18, dkk directed 'take z7b.3 on resume'; prior bead wamn-z7b.2 closed 64b0d83, tree clean+pushed, wamn-gates:dev image at that tip). A MEASUREMENT+PROTOTYPE bead (§10 C1 + §13): build the minimal retained-events-table alternative and measure its knee — THE decision input for the D19 checkpoint (z7b.4, which this UNBLOCKS on close; z7b.4 is a DECISION bead, do NOT auto-claim it). Output = ceilings.md C1 section + docs/ceilings-data/c1-* CSVs; only sanity asserts gate (every event delivered to every consumer exactly once, in per-consumer seq order). Replaces the §11 ledger's 'fabricated 1-2k events/sec/org — retracted' row with measured.

CARRY-OVER FACTS: (1) env provenance MUST note the fixture pod's fsync=off/synchronous_commit=off (ceilings.md C7 env correction 2026-07-18; the flip is deferred = wamn-dzhw P2 — do NOT touch the pod); WAL-share byte counts unaffected, latencies exclude per-commit fsync. (2) WAL measure = pg_current_wal_insert_lsn() deltas (NEVER pg_current_wal_lsn — reads ~0 under async commit; the C2 instrument lesson). (3) $n binds: always $1::text::<type> double casts (uuid/pg_lsn/jsonb/numeric). (4) Reuse: wamn_gate_harness::ceiling::Ramp (coarse-double→bisect knee controller, LevelStats/saturated) + emit_csv (harness) + catch-up-pacing producers + prepared-once statements + the outboxbench provisioning pattern (superuser ephemeral schema, connect_app w/ search_path+tenant claim). (5) Knee searches ARE stall-poisonable on this rig (C7: one-sided noise, up to 3× downward) — unlike C2 this HAS a knee search, so the noise strategy is a real fork.

FORKS for AskUserQuestion on resume: (a) NOISE STRATEGY — recommend implementing wamn-z7b.7's retry-a-saturated-level-once INSIDE the harness Ramp first (small pure change + units + mutants; serves this campaign AND closes z7b.7 which blocks z7b.6 — but z7b.7 is a SEPARATE bead, needs explicit approval to claim alongside) vs two-runs-per-cell (C7 practice, expensive × matrix) vs single-run+caveat. (b) MATRIX SCOPE — the full §10 matrix is 3 consumers × 3 payloads = 9 knee ramps (very long); recommend a TRIMMED first pass: consumers {1,5,20} at 1 KiB payload (3 ramps) + payload {1,16,64 KiB} at consumers=5 (2 more ramps), co-resident app-CRUD p99-delta probe at ONE operating point (80% of the 5-consumer knee), defer the full cross-product to phase 2 (file a bead). (c) PROTOTYPE CURSOR SHAPE — recommend per-consumer cursor ROW claimed via UPDATE cursors SET last_seq=<new> WHERE consumer=$ AND last_seq=<old> (optimistic CAS; batch = SELECT ... WHERE seq > last_seq ORDER BY seq LIMIT b) vs FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on the cursor row (locked-section poll) — the CAS shape mirrors how competing replicas of ONE logical consumer would share a cursor; single-writer-per-cursor v1, note the replica seam. Also fork-lite: co-resident CRUD shape (recommend the C2 items-table single-row INSERT/UPDATE mix at a fixed modest rate, its p50/p99 sampled per level).

IMPLEMENT after forks: NEW wamn-gates subcommand eventsbench (own ephemeral schema wamn_events_bench, modes ramp/matrix/all per the fork outcome + deploy/eventsbench-job.yaml, no NATS): events table (tenant_id, seq bigint IDENTITY, payload jsonb or bytea per payload-size axis — decide: jsonb for 1KiB realism, note TOAST kicks in ≥ ~2KB so 16/64KiB cells measure TOAST-path costs, WORTH CALLING OUT in the reading) + cursors table + appenders (open-loop catch-up pacing at the ramp's offered rate) + N consumer tasks (claim loop per the fork shape); per-level measure: achieved append rate, per-consumer delivery throughput + end-to-end latency (append-commit→consumer-read, enq_at map pattern), max consumer lag, app-CRUD p99 delta, WAL share (insert-lsn deltas apportioned), bloat probe (rel_size + n_dead_tup on events); saturation via the harness predicate (p99 doubling / delivery diverging from achieved append / drain timeout) — knee published as SUSTAINED delivered rate. Retention/pruning of the events table: v1 = none within a ramp (append-only window), reset between levels; a growth/retention sub-measure is NOT in C1's §10 scope (don't build). Sanity asserts: exactly-once + per-consumer order + completeness at drain. Gates: harness units (+ mutants if the Ramp gains the retry arm), bench sanity asserts, clippy/fmt; local smoke on a throwaway pg:18 (:5443 pattern) with tiny knobs; in-cluster = gates-only rebuild (~25min, detached+monitor) + kind load + deploy/eventsbench-job.yaml (noise strategy per fork (a)). Teardown: job + throwaways; guardrails (postgres pod / wamn-pg / wamn-sysdb ×3) untouched.

CLOSE: ceilings.md C1 section (§11 shape: date/env+fsync-caveat/rev/knobs/raw pointers/curves-over-numbers; the reading must state the CROSSOVER VERDICT INPUT plainly — C1 knee vs target scale is what z7b.4 decides on); §11 ledger row (fabricated→measured); build-and-test.md [EVT-C1] block; core-pivot-plan.md event-plane section (C1 done → 'D19 checkpoint (z7b.4) is READY — the user's decision'); commit-per-issue, push git+dolt. Do NOT auto-claim z7b.4 or z7b.7 (approval-scopes-to-the-named-bead; z7b.7 only if fork (a) approves folding it in).

The in-flight eventsbench prototype (~1070 lines: events table, per-consumer CAS cursors, knee-ramp matrix, co-resident CRUD probe) is PRESERVED on branch park/c1-eventsbench (single commit atop 87e9be7) — start there if C-EVTBL is ever needed. The z7b.7 noise-defense half of this work WAS finished and shipped (commit 87e9be7). Successor epic: wamn-l5i9.

title: [EVT-C2] outbox trigger overhead bench — the cost the customer pays (quantifies R8c)
description: Measure: single-row write latency with/without the outbox trigger; bulk single-statement UPDATE of 1k/10k/100k rows on a registered table (write amplification curve, txn duration, WAL); outbox table growth vs GC cadence under sustained load. Replaces R8c's adjectives with numbers. DEP wamn-d8v: the growth-vs-GC sub-measure needs a GC to exist (verified missing — ack only sets dispatched_at); the trigger-overhead half can run first if d8v lags. Output: curves to docs/ceilings.md. Design: docs/event-plane-jetstream.md section 10 (C2). Safe to interleave with the ladder: measurement only.
notes:
RESUME PLAN (banked 2026-07-18, dkk directed 'take z7b.2 on resume'; prior bead wamn-z7b.1 closed b24092a, tree clean, wamn-gates:dev image at that tip). A MEASUREMENT bead (§10: curves not verdicts) — output = a C2 section in docs/ceilings.md + docs/ceilings-data/ c2-* CSVs; only sanity asserts gate (trigger fires exactly once per written row; GC never prunes pending). Carry the z7b.1 lessons: run the in-cluster record job TWICE (roaming shared-disk noise, one-sided — report max/best; see wamn-z7b1-ceiling-facts), publish sustained/measured numbers not schedules, per-conn PREPARED statements.

SURVEY FINDINGS (verified at b24092a): (1) Trigger emitter = wamn_ddl Migration::outbox_triggers(catalog, &OutboxOptions{schema}) -> MigrationPlan (lib.rs:158; drop counterpart :171; one shared plpgsql fn wamn_outbox_event + per-table constant-named triggers, to_jsonb(NEW/OLD) payload — wp4). Functional live-apply gate exists in wamn-ddl tests; NO perf bench anywhere. (2) GC = outbox_prune_sql(limit) ($1 retention ms, batch-bounded ctid DELETE) + the d8v dispatcher maintenance step (tick_project step 5, 10-min cadence, saturated-batch = keep draining). (3) outbox DDL = deploy/run-queue.sql wamn_run.outbox (tenant_id, seq IDENTITY, table_name, event CHECK, payload jsonb, dispatched_at, partial pending index, FORCE RLS). (4) WAL per-txn measure: pg_current_wal_lsn()/pg_wal_lsn_diff() deltas bracketing the statement (verify wamn_app may call them; fallback = admin conn). (5) Reuse from z7b.1: the bloat-sampler pattern + producer catch-up pacing + CSV-marker extraction; emit_csv is private in queuebench.rs — C2 is its SECOND consumer, so pull it into wamn-gate-harness per the SR1 'until a second consumer pulls it here' note (no user fork needed). (6) Entity table: build a small catalog + Migration::create floor + the real outbox_triggers plan (apibench/dm1 pattern); one modest row shape v1, row-WIDTH as a possible phase-2 axis (note, don't build).

FORKS for AskUserQuestion on resume: (a) BENCH HOME — recommend a NEW wamn-gates subcommand outboxbench (own superuser ephemeral schema wamn_outbox_bench, modes trigger/bulk/growth/all + own deploy/outboxbench-job.yaml, no NATS) vs a dispatchbench mode (has outbox fixtures but is the stepped-time engine gate). (b) WITH/WITHOUT SHAPE — recommend PAIRED same-table (apply trigger plan -> measure -> apply the drop plan -> measure; no twin-table asymmetry); ops = single-row INSERT + UPDATE (+DELETE cheap) p50/p99 + WAL/row, then bulk single-statement UPDATE at 1k/10k/100k (txn duration, WAL bytes, outbox rows, amplification factor). (c) GROWTH-vs-GC SHAPE — recommend a direct prune-loop sweep (sustained row-event INSERT load at a fixed rate; sweep cadence {off, 60s, 600s-production} sampling outbox rel_size/n_dead_tup/pending via the z7b.1 bloat-sampler; the production SEAM is already d8v-gate-proven, so the real Dispatcher::tick_project variant is the heavier alternative).

title: [EVT-C7] queuebench ceiling mode — run-queue transitions/sec knee (retires D3 folklore)
description: Extend wamn-gates queuebench (crates/wamn-gates/src/queuebench.rs) + wamn-gate-harness with a ceiling mode: ramp profiles (step 1min/level; find-knee binary search on p99-doubling or divergence), sustained soak 30min at 80% of knee, burst 10x/60s. Measure on reference hardware: transitions/sec at knee vs fillfactor / batch-claim size / autovacuum settings; bloat curve over a 1M-run soak. Output: curves + knee published to docs/ceilings.md with date/env/raw-data pointer. This measures the '~1-5k transitions/sec' D3 ESTIMATE that every downstream capacity statement inherits — valuable regardless of D19's outcome. Design: docs/event-plane-jetstream.md section 10 (C7). Safe to interleave with the ladder: measurement only, no mechanics change.
notes:
RESUME PLAN (2026-07-18, dkk directed 'take z7b.1 on resume'; prior bead wamn-d8v closed 817937d, tree clean, both images at tip). A MEASUREMENT bead — curves + knee, NOT a pass/fail gate (event-plane doc §10 philosophy: 'the owner attaches decision rules after the numbers exist'); no production-mechanics change, safe to interleave with the ladder; mutation testing does not apply the usual way (no new load-bearing correctness logic — the harness's own exactly-once sanity asserts ride along). Sources of truth: docs/event-plane-jetstream.md §10 C7 row + 'Environment & methodology' block + §11 provenance ledger (every figure carries date/env/git-rev/config-knobs/raw-data pointer; curves over single numbers).

SURVEY FINDINGS (verified at 817937d): (1) queuebench modes today = dispatch/throughput/reclaim/janitor/park/doorbell/partition/all; throughput_phase is claim-ONLY drain at fixed concurrency (12) with a one-shot rate>=500/s assert — NOT a knee: ceiling is a NEW Mode::Ceiling, not a throughput tweak. (2) wamn-gate-harness is tiny (lib.rs: percentile/check/as_array/has_name) — per the doc the ceiling LOAD-GEN helpers (ramp scheduler: 1min/level steps; find-knee binary search on p99-doubling-or-divergence; soak; burst 10x/60s; per-level stats + CSV emit) land THERE so C1/C2 reuse them later. (3) queuebench provisions an ephemeral schema via superuser + reset() — the fillfactor/autovacuum matrix is feasible by re-provisioning run_queue WITH (fillfactor=X, autovacuum_...) per matrix point. (4) Bloat curve WITHOUT pgstattuple: pg_relation_size + pg_stat_all_tables.n_dead_tup (no extension needed on the shared pod). (5) docs/ceilings.md does NOT exist — this bead creates it. (6) deploy/queuebench-job.yaml passes --mode all; a ceiling campaign needs its OWN job manifest (long activeDeadline, --mode ceiling + knobs) — 30min soak + 1M-run bloat soak make it a LONG job.

FORKS for AskUserQuestion on resume: (a) TRANSITION DEFINITION — what 'transitions/sec' measures: recommend full-lifecycle cycles/sec (producer tasks write_ahead+enqueue at target rate, claimer tasks claim_batch/claim_dispatch + complete_dequeue; steady-state completed-runs/sec = the number capacity statements inherit) vs claim-only (today's throughput shape) vs per-statement mix; also whether to measure the fqg.18 combined-statement path (claim_dispatch_sql/complete_dequeue_sql — the production guest path) or the split builders, or BOTH as a comparison curve. (b) CAMPAIGN SCOPE v1 — full program per the bead (ramp+knee, 30min soak at 80%, burst 10x/60s, matrix fillfactor x batch-claim x autovacuum, 1M-run bloat soak = MANY HOURS wall-clock, run detached/overnight) vs a trimmed first pass (find-knee + short soak + batch-claim dimension now; fillfactor/autovacuum + 1M soak as a follow-on run) — present wall-clock estimates honestly. (c) NUMBERS-OF-RECORD ENV — in-cluster kind job (the p0-reference class + queuebench-job co-located/no-cpu-limit topology; document kind-on-dev-host caveats in ceilings.md) vs local-only; recommend in-cluster for the numbers of record. (d) RAW DATA HOME — commit aggregated per-level CSVs (curves) to the repo (docs/ceilings-data/ or similar) with scratchpad for raw samples + a pointer, vs pointer-only; §11 requires a raw-data pointer either way.

IMPLEMENT after forks: harness ceiling module (ramp/knee/soak/burst + stats + CSV) in wamn-gate-harness; queuebench Mode::Ceiling + ceiling_phase (producer+claimer JoinSets at scheduled offered load per level, per-level p50/p99/p999 + achieved rate; knee = p99 doubling vs baseline or achieved-rate divergence from offered; matrix loop re-provisions the schema per point; bloat probe sampled during the soak); NEW deploy manifest for the campaign job; docs/ceilings.md with the §11 provenance shape (git rev, env description incl the kind caveat, knobs, date, raw pointer) + the D3 row/docs updated to cite the MEASURED number (platform-plan D3 mentions ~1-5k transitions/sec estimate — after measuring, note the measured knee with a ceilings.md pointer; run-queue.md gates section += ceiling mode). Gates: the bench itself + its sanity asserts (exactly-once under load at every level), clippy/fmt; commit-per-issue; close unblocks NOTHING immediately (z7b.3/z7b.4 need C1/C2 too — z7b.4 blocked on .1/.2/.3; do NOT auto-claim z7b.2 — approval-scopes-to-the-named-bead). Update core-pivot-plan.md event-plane section on close (C7 done).

title: [3.2/8.2] Least-privileged DDL/migrate role: apply Check/RolePredicate DDL with no app_system/wamn_run grants
description: cjv.5 fix part 2 (structural close). Catalog Check + RLS RolePredicate expressions are spliced verbatim into batch-executed DDL; cjv.5 shipped the lexical chaining guard (wamn_catalog::unsafe_expression_reason, rejects top-level ';'/unbalanced parens/comment-open at validate time). That is defense-in-depth: raw dynamic SQL (DO/EXECUTE) inside an expression could still build a chaining payload at runtime that a lexical scan cannot see. The structural close applies migrations under a least-privileged DDL/migrate role WITHOUT grants on app_system/wamn_run (and the registry), so a chained statement cannot reach those tables regardless of what slips past the guard. Build-time mirror of wamn-1nd's runtime user-SQL role. Touches provisioning (create the role) + BOTH exec paths: crates/wamn-host/src/migrate_catalog.rs (batch_execute) and crates/wamn-host/src/copy_project_env.rs (definition-pass RLS re-apply). AR1 prerequisite for the multi-author-authorship future (multi-author flows / self-serve schema editor supplying Check/RolePredicate expressions). See docs/security-db-path.md 'Build-time DDL expression splicing (wamn-cjv.5)'.
notes:
Deferred from cjv.5 per its Q3 (all-deferrals-as-beads rule). Overlaps wamn-1nd's role machinery (runtime user-SQL role) and wamn-286 (dispatch role); coordinate so the platform doesn't grow N near-identical least-priv roles. cjv.5 (the guard + trust-boundary docs) is DONE.

title: [REVIEW C7-3] RLS read-leak probe salt range (0..99999) vs seeded keys (1..1000) — ~99% of attempts cannot leak
description: MEDIUM test-honesty (docs/review-2026-07.md §C7-3). Fixture seeds 1000 rows/tenant secret-<t>-1..1000 (postgres-init.sql:68-71); the cross-tenant read probe builds LIKE secret-{foreign}-{salt}% with salt=rng.below(100000) (pgbench.rs:517-525). A LIKE matches a seeded row only when salt is a decimal prefix of 1..1000 (~1%); the other ~99% query a non-existent key and return 0 rows even with RLS fully disabled. So the read half of the S2 RLS gate has effective coverage of ~hundreds, not the '10,000 randomized cross-tenant attempts' p0-results.md:184 advertises (~100x overstated). NOT vacuous — the ~1% that match + the salt-independent cross-tenant WRITE-denial assert (pgbench.rs:539-544) still catch the RLS-off mutant — but a subtle partial-leak mutant could evade the thin read coverage. FIX: draw salt from rng.below(1000)+1 so every read probes an existing foreign key; or assert a minimum count of real-key reads. Verifies-prior: R5b.
close_reason: Shipped cb644ba: rls_phase salt drawn from the seeded key range (rng.below(SEEDED_SECRETS_PER_TENANT)+1, const=1000 citing deploy/sql/postgres-init.sql generate_series(1,1000)) so EVERY cross-tenant read probe addresses >=1 real foreign row (was ~1%); addressability counter asserts 10000/10000 in the pass condition; positive control every 100th iteration (own-tenant read of the same salted pattern, >=1 row required, 100/100) catches seed-range drift; write-denial cadence preserved (salt%10, 1033/1033 denied). Lane mutant: salt reverted to below(100000) -> --mode rls FAILS on the addressability self-check BY NAME. Main-tree live re-verify vs throwaway postgres:18 + postgres-init.sql + pgprobe.wasm: PASS, 0 leaks. The S2 read gate's advertised 10,000 attempts are now genuinely 10,000 addressable attempts. Unblocks-note: C7-3 was a hard precondition rider on wamn-1nd (raw-SQL flag enablement) — the read-coverage half is now honest; C4-1 remains the open precondition there. In-cluster pgbench-job re-run rides the wave sweep.

title: [REVIEW C5-2] Gateway static OnceLock<Catalog> forecloses the 4.4 hot-reload its own comment promises

title: [REVIEW C5-5] API expansion ignores Relation.cardinality/through — many-to-many mis-served; forks the catalog model
description: MEDIUM (docs/review-2026-07.md §C5-5). router.rs:670-728 derives relation direction from from/to position + from_field presence and never reads rel.cardinality/through (grep-confirmed), though the catalog has Cardinality::{OneToMany,ManyToMany,Hierarchical} + Relation.through (catalog/types.rs:305,318,329-333). A ManyToMany (from_field=None) is rejected as UnknownRelation (misleading); a ManyToMany with a stray from_field is silently treated as a direct FK against the wrong table ignoring through -> wrong rows, no error; Hierarchical always takes the to-one branch. Latent (POC only OneToMany) but exactly the seam GraphQL (wamn-tsn) will walk by cardinality — the crate's relation model has already forked from the catalog's. FIX: switch resolve_expands on rel.cardinality; handle/clearly reject ManyToMany/Hierarchical with a distinct error; stop inferring from from_field presence. Reconcile BEFORE wamn-tsn.
close_reason: Fixed at 72b9f3b (lane 4a8ca9d): resolve_expands switches on rel.cardinality first — ManyToMany/Hierarchical rejected up front with new distinct ApiError::UnsupportedExpansion (code unsupported-expansion, 400); OneToMany keeps to-one/to-many serving with from_field required, matched-but-missing now ApiError::UnservableRelation (code unservable-relation) instead of misleading UnknownRelation; from_field-presence inference removed, un-forking the router from the catalog model ahead of wamn-tsn. Pinned by many_to_many_expansion_is_unsupported_not_unknown / hierarchical_expansion_is_unsupported_not_to_one / one_to_many_missing_from_field_is_unservable_not_unknown / truly_unknown_relation_is_still_unknown over an in-code odd_catalog (no shared fixture touched). title: [REVIEW C2-2] occurrence=0 is 'exact for acyclic' but a merge/diamond revisits its node — history silently dropped
description: MEDIUM (docs/review-2026-07.md §C2-2). occurrence is a compile-time literal 0 (run-store/sql.rs:99,:106,:123; model.rs:137) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; run-state.md:112 claims 'exact for acyclic'. title: [REVIEW C1-2] Catalog validates index/constraint names per-entity; Postgres relation namespace is schema-wide
description: MEDIUM (docs/review-2026-07.md §C1-2). catalog/validate.rs:240,:273 declare index_names/constraint_names HashSets INSIDE the per-entity loop; emit.rs:288/:246 use bare user names sharing the schema-wide pg_class namespace (+ synthesized _pkey/_fkey/wamn_mig_drop_*). title: [REVIEW C6-1] Tier-move plan has no quiesce step — an automated saga loses all writes in the dump->flip window
description: HIGH (docs/review-2026-07.md §C6-1). plan_tier_move (tier_move.rs:98-140) emits ProvisionClusters -> per-env{Dump,ProvisionEnv,Restore} -> FlipRegistry with no quiesce/verify step. resolve() routes OLD until the final FlipRegistry, and databaseReclaimPolicy:retain keeps the old DB live+writable throughout (move_org_tier.rs:264-275). Every write between an env's Dump snapshot and the flip lands only in the old DB, absent from the restored new DB. postgres-topology.md:375 calls it a 'downtime window' but nothing enforces it — and wamn-2ib, whose job is to drive the plan automatically, will drop a paying customer's in-flight writes at cutover. No post-cutover deprovision of the retained old DBs, no row-count verify before flip. FIX: explicit Quiesce{triple} primitive (revoke writes / default_transaction_read_only / logical-replication cutover) + VerifyRestored/DeprovisionOld; saga refuses cutover until quiesce+verification recorded. Prerequisite for wamn-2ib tier-move automation (see saga-readiness §).
notes: Approach superseded by wamn-8df.5 (generic env-symmetric copy API with a quiesce step). The quiesce requirement is satisfied by the unified copy operation; do NOT build a tier-move-only quiesce fix in isolation — coordinate with 8df.5.
close_reason: Fixed by wamn-8df.5 (commit 3cc017a): the unified copy subsumes tier-move (tier_move.rs retired) and ships the full C6-1 fix list — Quiesce primitive (default_transaction_read_only + backend termination, proven by a fresh-session 25006 probe), Verify (exact per-table counts before flip), saga-gated Cutover (executor re-reads the saga and REFUSES unless quiesce+verify are durably recorded; mutant-proven), and --confirm-gated DeprovisionOld. title: [5.14/2.6] Egress governance for queue/cron-dispatched flows (in-proc run-worker path)
description: The deployed run-worker (fqg.8) instantiates the flowrunner IN-PROCESS with a WasiCtx and drives claimed runs. Its outbound wasi:http (the http-request node's egress) is governed by NEITHER a wash WorkloadDeployment allowedHosts NOR any current mechanism: allowedHosts is a wash-workload property (2.6/wamn-wv3), and the run-worker is not a workload. So cron/queue-dispatched flows currently have NO egress allowlist - a flow node can call any host (or, if the run-worker's default WasiCtx socket policy denies, none). POC-F3's allowedHosts=[notify.example] clause cannot be honored on this path. Need: a per-project/per-flow egress allowlist resolved by the run-worker at dispatch and enforced on the executing node's outbound wasi:http. Cross-ref 2.6 egress review (wamn-wv3), the deploy-time no-raw-socket DB guard (wamn-7j0.1 - sockets, not http), and 8.2 tenant isolation.
acceptance_criteria: A queue/cron-dispatched flow's outbound HTTP is allowed only to an allowlisted host set (resolved per project/flow); a call to a non-allowlisted host is denied; a gate proves both allow and deny on the deployed run-worker.
notes:
SCOPE UPDATE (2026-07-16, wamn-17o): the HOST-LEVEL half landed with the credential vault — the run-worker store previously had NO outgoing wasi:http handler at all (an outbound call trapped 'http client not available' and poisoned the instance); wamn-17o wired RunnerEgress (check_allowed_hosts over DefaultOutgoingHandler, 9.2 trace inject included) gated by --allowed-hosts / WAMN_ALLOWED_HOSTS, EMPTY = DENY-ALL fail-closed. REMAINING fqg.11 scope: per-FLOW allowedHosts (the flow-level allowlist POC-F3's notify wants, e.g. allowedHosts=[notify.example] carried in/next to the flow and intersected with the host list) + provisioning-driven per-project entries + parity for any future multi-project runner.
IMPLEMENTED (2026-07-17, local gates green; in-cluster gate pending image rebuild): per-flow allowedHosts via the cjv.3 trusted-channel shape. DECIDED (dkk): deny-all default — a flow declaring no allowed-hosts gets NO egress; declared hosts are intersected with the host-level list (both must allow). LANDED: wamn-flow Flow.allowed_hosts (kebab-case 'allowed-hosts') + validation (invalid-allowed-host/duplicate-allowed-host) + regenerated flow-schema.schema.json; wamn:runner/egress set-allowed-hosts WIT (both vendored copies synced); flowrunner declare_run_egress on every walk (both call sites, incl. resume); host RunnerEgressPolicy plugin (plugins/runner_egress.rs, unparseable entries dropped fail-closed) enforced in RunnerEgress::outgoing_request as a second check_allowed_hosts pass; three gate harnesses (testhostbench/flowbench/failoverbench) link+register the channel; fixtures migrated (f3/f4 inert node-config allowed-hosts moved to the real top-level field; deploy/cred/notify.flow.json declares both echo authorities). GATE: credproof extended — allow half = cred-notify completing under deny-all default; deny half = new deploy/cred/deny.flow.json (egress-deny: same echo target the host list admits, declares nothing) asserted failed + egress-denied, discriminating the flow layer from the host layer. REMAINING before close: (1) run the in-cluster gate of record (FULL rebuild both stages — host + guest + gates images; register BOTH cred fixtures per build-and-test.md); (2) provisioning-driven per-project host-level entries have NO surface today (nothing renders runner deploys — deploy/runner.yaml is hand-maintained); decide whether that half moves to E1/10.1 or stays here.

title: wamn-catalog: newtype EntityId/FieldId (schema-transparent) instead of String aliases
description:
External review #2. crates/wamn-catalog/src/types.rs:30,35 are `pub type EntityId = String; pub type FieldId = String;` -- zero compile-time safety. The confusion is load-bearing: router.rs mixes rel.from/rel.to (entity ids) with rel.from_field (a field id).

Make them newtypes via a macro with: Deref<Target=str> + inherent as_str/into_string + From<&str>/From<String>/From<&String> + PartialEq<str/&str/String> + Display + Borrow<str> + AsRef<str>, #[serde(transparent)], derive(Clone,PartialEq,Eq,Hash,PartialOrd,Ord).

TWO invariants MUST be preserved:
(1) Debug MUST delegate to the inner String (validate.rs prints ids with {:?} in error messages -- deriving Debug would change them to EntityId("x") and break message text / assertions).
(2) SCHEMA-TRANSPARENT: a MANUAL JsonSchema impl delegating to String with is_referenceable()==false, so the published contract docs/catalog-model.schema.json is byte-unchanged and the committed-schema-matches-types drift guard still passes.

Churn map: diff.rs construction sites need .into() (entities_added/removed, EntityChange.id, FieldChange.id, fields_added/removed); comparisons in wamn-ddl/wamn-rls/wamn-seed/wamn-schema/wamn-migrate are compiler-guided; validate.rs + wamn-api router.rs need ~no change (covered by Deref/as_str/PartialEq/From). Test helpers already use .into() so most tests are unaffected.

RelationId intentionally EXCLUDED: Relation.id has no confusion partner (never cross-referenced into another collection), so a newtype there is pure churn for zero safety gain -- Relation.id stays String.

Verify: cargo test -p wamn-catalog (ESPECIALLY the schema drift guard) + full workspace build/test/clippy.

title: [5.14] claim_partition_head_sql: FROM-join the SKIP-LOCKED subquery (same over-lock as fqg.4 claim_batch_sql)
description: claim_partition_head_sql (fqg.1 per-partition claim) uses the same 'WHERE (tenant_id,run_id) IN (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE OF c SKIP LOCKED LIMIT n)' shape that fqg.4 proved over-leases when run through the wamn:postgres plugin's cached extended-protocol path (the IN-subquery is re-executed per outer row; SKIP LOCKED advances, leasing the whole batch on a bounded claim). Today only host-side raw callers (queuebench/dispatchbench) use it, so it is not triggered; wamn-fqg.9 (guest-side partitioned claim) will run it through the plugin and hit the identical bug. Fix: rewrite to the canonical 'UPDATE ... FROM (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE OF c SKIP LOCKED LIMIT n) sub WHERE q.pk=sub.pk' form (mirrors the claim_batch_sql fix), keep the JOIN partition_owner + NOT EXISTS head predicate inside the subquery, update the partition shape drift-guard, regress via queuebench partition mode + wamn-run-queue partition unit/live-apply tests.
close_reason: Subsumed by wamn-fqg.4 (commit 96ffd6e): the over-claim fix — fencing the locking SELECT in a WITH ... AS MATERIALIZED CTE — was applied to claim_partition_head_sql there. Its original premise (a plain FROM-join fixes the over-lock) was disproven; a derived table is not an evaluation fence, only MATERIALIZED is. Nothing left to build; drift-guard pins the fence on the partition builder.

title: [5.14] Guest-side partitioned claim — run-next claims partitioned(key) runs in order
description: fqg.4's run-next claims only UNPARTITIONED runs (claim_batch_sql, partition_key IS NULL). Partitioned(key) runs stay on the per-partition ownership path (fqg.1: acquire_partitions + claim_partition_head). Extend run-next (or add run-next-partitioned) so the guest leases a partition, claims its head in order, renews the partition lease, and steps down when drained — the guest-side counterpart of the host-side partition claim. Needs in-order-per-key + partition-failover gate assertions.

Guest run-next now serves partitioned(key) runs: global claim empty -> acquire_partitions_sql(1) -> claim earliest HEAD across owned partitions in stream order (claim_partition_head_sql(1), one in flight per key, D20 policy on the row) -> mark running -> select_run_dispatch_sql -> SHARED execute_claimed path (partition lease renewed per node via new partition:Option<&str> param) -> release_partition_sql step-down when a just-acquired partition has no head. WIT UNCHANGED; RunWorker.drain loops unchanged. Feature-gate finding: partition builders were already outside the dispatcher gate — default-features=false exposed them, nothing moved, no croner/chrono in wasm. Ordering semantics taken verbatim from the existing pure model (blocking/one-in-flight/leapfrog) — no new semantics. GATES (worktree + main tree): pure guest_partition_loop_drives_each_key_in_stream_order; LIVE partition-order vs throwaway PG (stream_seq tiebreak kseq + enqueued_at tiebreak kenq per-key in order, NULL-key 5/5 via old path, 11/11 exactly once); LIVE partition-failover (A drove head then lease force-expired, B reacquired + resumed in order, 3/3 exactly once); 3 mutants KILLED one per layer (pure stream_key / SQL blocking-arm stream_seq / guest short-circuit; M2 first read was a cargo stale-fingerprint flake, confirmed killed under forced rebuild, script hardened). title: [2.3/D6] Research: Postgres topology — shared Cluster (DB-per-project) vs cluster-per-project vs tiered
description:
Re-opens a refinement of D6 surfaced after 2.3 (wamn-jxm) shipped. CNPG's idiomatic/recommended pattern is ONE application database per Cluster (the 'microservice database' model — bootstrap makes one app DB + owner; backup/PITR, monitoring, failover, pooling are all Cluster-scoped; multi-DB is supported, incl. the newer declarative Database CRD + managed.roles, but against the grain). 2.3 shipped the OPPOSITE: one shared Cluster, database-per-project (pooled multi-tenancy) — economical for many small/idle tenants, which is wamn's likely shape (CNPG's advice targets a few well-resourced services, not many-tenant SaaS).

DECISION DRIVER: is per-project point-in-time recovery + per-project resource/failure isolation a firm near-term product requirement? On a shared Cluster, PITR is CLUSTER-WIDE — restoring one project to a past point = restore the whole Cluster to a scratch instance + pg_dump the one DB out; and one Cluster down = all projects down. Cluster-per-project makes per-project backups/isolation/upgrades native but costs a full Postgres instance (pod+PVC) per project — doesn't scale cheaply to many small projects.

OPTIONS TO EVALUATE: (a) KEEP shared Cluster, database-per-project (as shipped); (b) CLUSTER-PER-PROJECT (CNPG-idiomatic; provision-project reworks to render a Cluster CR + wait, instead of CREATE DATABASE); (c) TIERED/HYBRID: shared Cluster default + opt-in dedicated Cluster for heavy/regulated projects; (d) CNPG-NATIVE shared: stay shared-Cluster but manage per-project DBs/roles via the Database CRD + managed.roles instead of the imperative CREATE DATABASE/GRANT SQL.

NOT A ONE-WAY DOOR: the 2.2 CredentialProvider seam (project -> per-project URL) is substrate-agnostic — a project URL can point at a DB in a shared Cluster OR at its own dedicated Cluster's -rw service with NO change to the runtime, the wamn:postgres plugin, or the provisionbench gate/credential contract. Only provision-project's internals change. So pooled-now + promote-heavy-projects-later is viable.

RESEARCH TASKS: quantify the per-project restore cost/runbook on a shared Cluster; assess CNPG Database CRD + managed.roles maturity (would replace the imperative SQL for option a/d); estimate resource cost of cluster-per-project at N=10/100/1000 projects; confirm the tiered promotion path (move a project from shared to dedicated Cluster) is operationally feasible; decide the default + the escape hatch. Output: a D6-topology decision recorded in docs/platform-plan.md + docs/provisioning.md, and the shape wamn-e1g (WAL/PITR) builds on.

GATES wamn-e1g (backup granularity depends on the topology). Context: docs/provisioning.md, [[wamn-2.3-provisioning-facts]], D6 row (wamn-dxi).

title: [8.2/5.14] Dedicated per-project wamn_dispatch DB role: wamn_run-schema grants only, zero user-entity access
description:
The projects Secret centralizes every project's DB credentials in one always-on control-plane deployment — inherent to the dispatcher's job (it must reach all projects; same blast-radius logic as the D2 per-project-gateway argument). But deploy/run-queue.sql grants the wamn_run tables to wamn_app (:67 run_queue, :94 partition_owner, :137 outbox) — the same role that holds user-entity grants — and deploy/dispatcher-projects.example.yaml's example entries connect as wamn_app. A compromised dispatcher pod (it continuously parses tenant-authored graph_json and outbox payloads) therefore reads USER DATA it never needs: its entire job is run_queue / runs / outbox / trigger registry / partition_owner, and row-event payloads arrive in outbox rows, not entity tables. Scope note from verification: wamn_app is NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS so RLS still scopes the dispatcher per-tenant — this is a least-privilege role-separation gap, not an RLS bypass.

FIX: dedicated per-project wamn_dispatch role — GRANT on the wamn_run schema tables only, ZERO user-schema grants, same FORCE RLS tenant floor; deploy/run-queue.sql mints + grants it; the projects Secret carries wamn_dispatch credentials; hosting/2.3 provisioning mints it per real project. Compromise then yields trigger forgery/replay (bounded, auditable — deterministic run ids make replays visible) instead of tenant-data read.

LAND TOGETHER with wamn-ngb (publish-only NATS verify_and_map identity for the doorbell): same blast-radius argument, same dispatcher/deploy touch, one commit.

VERIFY: dispatchbench (or S2-style) negative gate — the wamn_dispatch connection attempts a user-entity SELECT, asserts permission-denied. External review R8b (docs/review-findings.md § R8), verified at tip 873c3d8.

title: [5.14] Cron anchor table upserted in the fire txn: decouple cron dedupe from run-history retention
description:
The dispatcher's cron state IS the runs table: cron_last_run_sql (crates/wamn-run-queue/src/sql.rs:232-237) recovers the last-fired tick from max(run_id) over the flow's trigger_source='cron' runs; the write-ahead dedupe is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, run_id) DO NOTHING (sql.rs:170-172); runs_cron_anchor (deploy/run-state.sql:80-81) is only a partial INDEX over those same rows. Elegant — nothing dispatcher-local to desync — but BOTH the anchor and the dedupe evidence live in prunable run history. When 9.6 retention ships with retention < cron period (e.g. 7-day retention, monthly job), the anchor is pruned between fires; due_tick computes anchorless and re-fires an already-fired tick — and ON CONFLICT cannot absorb it because the conflicting row is the one that was pruned. Duplicate fire of a by-construction infrequent, likely-important job. Latent today (nothing prunes yet); MUST land before 9.6 retention ships (hard-blocks wamn-srb).

FIX (review option b, recommended): tiny wamn_run.cron_anchor(tenant_id, flow_id, last_tick) upserted INSIDE the existing fire transaction — the anchor becomes definitionally correct rather than correct-by-retention-policy; one more row-write per fire; cron_last_run_sql demotes to bootstrap fallback for pre-anchor flows. Rejected: (a) retention carve-out (pruner always keeps each flow's latest cron run) — couples the pruner to dispatch correctness; see also the standing tension the verification surfaced: deploy/run-queue.sql:116-117 punts OUTBOX retention to "an operational concern", and a generic operational pruner pointed at runs would today break cron dedupe — the anchor table removes that trap; (c) validation rule (retention >= 2x longest cron period) — couples two policies tuned by different people at different times; fails silently when either moves.

VERIFY: dispatchbench gains a retention mode — fire a tick, delete the run row (simulated prune), advance stepped time past the next tick, assert exactly the NEXT tick fires (no re-fire of the pruned one). Doc closure: docs/run-queue.md § Trigger dispatcher cron-state paragraph. External review R8a (docs/review-findings.md § R8), verified at tip 873c3d8.
close_reason: [5.14] Cron anchor SHIPPED + PROVEN (commit 93e84b5; job fix e959204 n/a). wamn_run.cron_anchor upserted unconditionally INSIDE the fire txn (GREATEST-monotonic — a losing replica/replay never rewinds; heals pruned-anchor+surviving-run); recovery = cache → cron_anchor → cron_last_run fallback (pre-anchor flows) → first_seen. reconcile-run-plane auto-creates the table (run_plane pin tests updated = the rollout proof); applied LIVE 2026-07-22 to poc_f1 + wamn_runner_demo (dry-run showed exactly CreateTable: cron_anchor), dispatcher rolled after. docs/run-queue.md rewritten. Gates: dispatchbench Retention mode (pruned run does NOT re-fire via surviving anchor; pre-anchor fallback honestly DOES; upsert co-transacted via INSERT trap) — local --mode all PASS + IN-CLUSTER dispatchbench overall PASS. 3 mutants killed by named tests (GREATEST→LEAST; recovery-skips-anchor; upsert-outside-txn). Unblocks wamn-srb — NOT claimed.

title: [2.2] wamn:postgres begin_with_claims: replace validated SET LOCAL interpolation with bound set_config()
description:
begin_with_claims (crates/wamn-host/src/plugins/wamn_postgres.rs:598-611) builds "BEGIN; SET LOCAL app.tenant = '{tenant}'; SET LOCAL statement_timeout = {ms};" (+ optional SET LOCAL search_path = {schema}) via format!, executed with batch_execute (simple query protocol). Safe today — inputs are host-derived and charset-validated (valid_tenant :300-306, valid_schema :321-333) — but it contradicts the WIT's own contract ("Parameterized ONLY -- there is no string interpolation path", docs/wamn-postgres.wit:92-93), and the format! template is the foot-gun: 4.2's app.user_id/app.role claims could be appended by someone who forgets the validator; nothing structural stops them. House principle: injection unrepresentable, not validated.

FIX: SET LOCAL cannot take binds, but its exact equivalent can: set_config(name, value, is_local := true). After BEGIN, ONE prepared fully-bound statement: SELECT set_config('app.tenant', $1, true), set_config('statement_timeout', $2, true), set_config('search_path', COALESCE($3, current_setting('search_path')), true). statement_timeout binds as text (GUC values are strings); $3 = NULL preserves the absent-schema server-default behavior (fallback: two prepared variants if the self-referential current_setting read is awkward — still zero interpolation). KEEP valid_tenant/valid_schema as identity-format checks (they define legal ids; the no-hyphen schema rule still matters for DDL quoting) — no longer the security boundary. Delete the format! claim template; signature and all callers (one-shots, explicit transaction, cursors) unchanged. Grep-gate: no format! containing SET LOCAL left in the plugin. (Verified: the only other format!-built SQL is host-minted cursor names + a u32 FETCH count — wamn_postgres.rs:1286, :1391 — no data-value interpolation anywhere.)

COST (honest trade-off): claims currently ride the same batch_execute round trip as BEGIN — the fix adds one round trip on txn open; tokio-postgres pipelining (join the futures) collapses most of it. S2 measured p50 710us / p99 1.98ms with 5-10x gate headroom; ~100-200us added RTT is well inside it but must be MEASURED: re-run the full S2 gate set (throughput, p99, chaos x100, RLS x10k, injection x10k), thresholds unchanged, and record new p50/p99 next to the old in docs/p0-results.md as an addendum. New injection cases target the claim path itself: tenant/schema containing ' ; -- unicode now legal to ATTEMPT (bind as data, name a nonexistent tenant/schema) — assert no statement-level effect either way.

Doc closure: docs/security-db-path.md + the WIT header — the "no interpolation path" claim becomes unconditionally true; note the validators' demoted role. HARD-BLOCKS wamn-0xd [4.2]: user/role claims must be born as bind parameters in this statement, never joining a format! template.
