title: [3.2] migrate_plan orders CREATE TABLE before the RENAME/DROP that frees a reused table name
description: Confirmed by the wp4 adversarial review (pre-existing, not outbox-related): emit.rs migrate_plan emits added entities' CREATE TABLE at step 1 and defers table renames + DROP TABLEs to step 4. A valid evolution that reuses a name — v1{entity B, table 'receipts'} -> v2{B renamed 'receipts_old', NEW entity D named 'receipts'} — compiles to CREATE TABLE "receipts" while B still holds the name: 42P07 'relation already exists', the whole migration rolls back under the 2.5 transactional apply, the catalog version is unappliable. Same transient collision for remove-and-re-add in one version bump. Fix: order name-freeing renames/drops of reused names before the adds (or a two-pass name-collision analysis). Design: docs/ddl-compiler.md; crates/wamn-ddl/src/emit.rs migrate_plan steps 1/4.
notes:
=== RESUME PLAN (wamn-k56 [3.2] migrate_plan name-reuse ordering — NOT STARTED; start after bd prime + bd show wamn-k56) ===

STANDING RULES (always apply): DEBUG BUILDS ONLY (never cargo build --release; gates run ./target/debug/wamn-host — but k56 is PURE-CRATE, no host binary involved). ONE issue at a time (k56 is sole in-progress). AskUserQuestion on genuine design forks BEFORE implementing. After bd close: stage .beads/interactions.jsonl IN the issue commit, commit direct on main, git push (STOP+report on rejection). Shared-cluster guardrail applies only if an in-cluster step is chosen (none anticipated).

STATE (2026-07-12, HEAD b687d45, tree CLEAN): wp4 DONE — Migration::outbox_triggers/drop_outbox_triggers + emit-outbox example shipped, committed+pushed; memory wamn-wp4-outbox-triggers-facts stored. Local containers wamn-rq-pg :5459 / wamn-rq-nats :4232 / wamn-vrf3-pg :5471 / wamn-vrf3-nats :4245 up (k56's live gate uses its own throwaway wamn-ddl-pg :5451 per CLAUDE.md [3.2]). Kind cluster image predates wp4 but wp4 was pure-crate — NO rebuild owed. In-cluster residue: wamn_dispatch_demo has wp4_receipts + the COLLATE-fixed trigger fn, all flows inactive (reusable, not needed for k56). Siblings NOT to take: wamn-fqg.4, wamn-1d4, wamn-ngb, wamn-oj7.

THE BUG (confirmed by wp4 adversarial review, verifier-checked line refs): crates/wamn-ddl/src/emit.rs migrate_plan emits added entities' CREATE TABLE at step 1 (~lines 313-318) but defers table RENAMEs (emit_destructive_changes ~541-554) and removed entities' DROP TABLE (~343-353) to step 4. wamn-catalog diff keys identity on entity ID and validate() only requires name uniqueness WITHIN a version, so v1{B:'receipts'} -> v2{B renamed 'receipts_old', NEW D named 'receipts'} is valid yet compiles CREATE TABLE "receipts" while B still holds the name -> 42P07, whole migration rolls back under the 2.5 transactional apply; catalog version unappliable. Same for remove-and-re-add of a name in one bump. NOTE ALSO the pathological SWAP case: v2 renames A->B AND B->A in one version — NO ordering fixes it without a synthesized temp name; any fix must handle or explicitly reject it.

PRE-SCOUTED FIX OPTIONS (Q1 fork, ask user): (a RECOMMENDED) TARGETED HOIST — compute the set of names claimed by step-1 CREATEs and step-3/4 rename-TO names; hoist ONLY the name-freeing ops (RENAME of a table whose OLD name is reclaimed, DROP TABLE whose name is reclaimed) ahead of step 1, keeping everything else in the current additive-first/destructive-last order (that order is a deliberate review property, and DROP TABLE ordering vs dependent-FK/constraint drops matters — a blanket 'destructive first' reorder can break DROP TABLE on FK-referenced tables and reads worse in report()). Hoisted renames/drops KEEP their Destructive classification (plan still gates). (b) global reorder destructive-before-additive — simpler but breaks the FK-unwind ordering + review shape. (c) reject-with-CompileError on name reuse — safest/simplest but blocks a legitimate low-code evolution ('archive old table, start fresh'). For the A<->B SWAP cycle under (a): either synthesize an intermediate temp rename (e.g. ALTER ... RENAME TO __wamn_mig_tmp_<n> then final renames; temp ops classified Destructive with a note) or reject that cycle with a new CompileError variant (RECOMMEND: reject in v1 — swaps are rare and a temp-name protocol deserves its own review; document in ddl-compiler.md). Q2 fork (minor, could fold into Q1): does the hoist also need to consider column-level renames? NO — column renames are table-scoped, no cross-entity name pool; scope is TABLE names only. Q3 proof depth: (a RECOMMENDED) unit tests (reuse-via-rename, reuse-via-remove+add, swap-rejected, no-collision plans byte-unchanged = regression that hoisting only fires on collision) + extend the EXISTING live-apply test emitted_sql_applies_on_postgres (or a new gated test) with the rename-reuse evolution actually APPLIED on throwaway :5451 (proves 42P07 gone); no in-cluster step (pure crate, identical semantics).

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES: the fix lives in migrate_plan (emit.rs) — collect planned ops as today, then a POST-PASS partitions out name-freeing ops and splices them ahead of the CREATEs (or compute collision set FIRST and emit in adjusted order; post-pass is less invasive). Name-collision set: for entities_added -> new names; old names come from old catalog by id. Careful: a rename whose old name is reused AND whose new name collides with ANOTHER old table's current name forms a chain (A->B where B is also being renamed B->C): hoisting must order the chain (C-freeing before B->C before A->B) — topological order on 'name freed by' edges; a CYCLE in that graph = the swap case = reject (per Q1 rec). Plan-shape tests that pin CURRENT op order exist (dropped_column_is_gated_destructive etc.) — they must stay green (no collision => order unchanged). wamn-schema promote() wraps migrate() (regression: cargo test -p wamn-schema); wamn-rls/wamn-seed use create only. Ordering property to KEEP: within hoisted block, constraint/index drops needed before a hoisted DROP TABLE? A dropped table's own constraints die with it; INBOUND FKs from OTHER old tables reference it — current step-4 drops constraints per-changed-entity only; a hoisted DROP TABLE referenced by a REMAINING table's FK fails regardless (pre-existing limitation, out of scope — note it, don't fix silently).

EXECUTION ORDER: understand pass INLINE (read emit.rs migrate_plan + emit_destructive_changes + wamn-catalog diff() identity rules + tests/ddl.rs plan-shape tests — small, self-authored, recent) -> AskUserQuestion (Q1 fix strategy + swap handling, Q3 proof depth) -> implement + unit tests -> local gates: cargo test -p wamn-ddl (+ WAMN_DDL_PG_URL live gate on throwaway wamn-ddl-pg :5451, docker run per CLAUDE.md [3.2]; NOTE the two live tests run in PARALLEL — new live scenarios need either the existing test extended or a DISTINCT ephemeral schema name, and the wamn_app role-provision block must keep catching duplicate_object OR unique_violation) -> regressions cargo test -p wamn-schema -p wamn-rls -p wamn-seed -p wamn-catalog + clippy/fmt -> adversarial review Workflow (lenses: ordering correctness incl chains/cycles, plan-shape regression, gate blind spots) + kill mutants (e.g. hoist-disabled, chain-order-scrambled) -> docs: docs/ddl-compiler.md (migration-plan ordering paragraph + swap-rejection rule) + CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md [3.2] block ONLY if gate commands change (unlikely — text mention of ordering fix optional; MIRROR BYTE-IDENTICAL via python block-compare up to CLAUDE.md's '## Conventions & Patterns' trailer) -> bd close -> commit+push -> bd remember wamn-k56-migrate-ordering-facts. Memories to load: wamn-3.2-ddl-compiler-facts (crate architecture), wamn-wp4-outbox-triggers-facts (review findings incl this bug's full verifier reasoning + live-test parallel-schema lesson).
close_reason: Fixed: migrate_plan name-freeing preamble (aside-renamed reclaimed dropped tables + their indexes with namespace-wide collision checks, pre-rename hoisted constraint/index drops incl implicit-drop force-hoist, dependency-ordered table renames with pkey-follow, per-entity column-namespace freeing with column-rename ordering); swap cycles rejected (TableRenameCycle/ColumnRenameCycle). 31 tests incl live-apply on PG18; 13 mutants killed; adversarially reviewed (all confirmed findings fixed or filed: wamn-drb, wamn-nqg).

title: [5.14] Checkpoint/resume on replica loss (first-class failover)
description: Deferred from the 5.14 walking skeleton (wamn-m2z). The pieces exist — lease-expiry reclaim (5.14) hands a run to a new replica, and 5.7 branch-aware reconstruction resumes it from node_runs — but wire them into a first-class failover primitive: a runner that dies mid-run has its lease reclaimed and the new claimant resumes via reconstruction (exactly-once effect), with a queuebench failover gate that kills a claimant mid-run and asserts single-side-effect completion on another replica. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 5.14 (checkpoint/resume on replica loss); composes 5.7 (wamn-5xl, done) reconstruction + 5.14 reclaim.
notes:
=== RESUME PLAN (wamn-fqg.2 [5.14] Checkpoint/resume on replica loss — first-class
failover; start after bd prime + bd show wamn-fqg.2) ===

GOAL: wire the two EXISTING pieces into a FIRST-CLASS FAILOVER PRIMITIVE — a runner
that dies mid-run has its run-lease RECLAIMED (5.14 queue) and the NEW claimant RESUMES
the run via BRANCH-AWARE RECONSTRUCTION (5.7 node_runs), completing with EXACTLY-ONCE
side effects. Deliver a failover gate that KILLS a claimant mid-run and asserts
single-side-effect completion on ANOTHER replica. Composes 5.7 (wamn-5xl, DONE:
reconstruct + Plan::resume) + 5.14 reclaim (wamn-m2z, DONE: claim_batch_sql re-claims an
expired lease, bumping attempts). Depends only on wamn-m2z (DONE) -> READY.

THE CORE SEAM TENSION (probed 2026-07-12): NO single bench today has BOTH halves.
- queuebench (crates/wamn-host/src/queuebench.rs): has run_queue + claim/RECLAIM
  (reclaim_phase = A claims short-ttl, B blocked while live, sleep>ttl, B reclaims
  attempts==2) + the ephemeral-schema-via-superuser pattern — but NO wasm guest (pure
  tokio_postgres; SKIP LOCKED is pure PG).
- flowbench (flowbench.rs) + testhostbench (testhostbench.rs): DRIVE the flowrunner
  GUEST (which reconstructs from node_runs + resumes in execute()) — but NO run_queue.
- flowbench ALREADY has the RESUME machinery: `run-until-kill` (epoch-kill a runner
  AFTER its pg-write side-effect commits but BEFORE its checkpoint; a FRESH instance
  reconstructs -> exactly 1 sink row via ON CONFLICT idempotency). That is the closest
  existing "kill-mid-effect -> reconstruct -> exactly-once" proof.
So fqg.2 must UNION run_queue (queuebench) + the guest reconstruction (flowbench). The
NOVELTY over the existing flowbench resume gate: the resume is TRIGGERED BY QUEUE
LEASE-RECLAIM across a REPLICA boundary (replica A dies, its lease expires, replica B
CLAIMS the reclaimed run from run_queue and resumes) — not just a same-process re-run.

STEP 1 ON RESUME (before code): RE-LOAD memories (bd memories <kw> or they're in bd
prime): wamn-fqg.1-partition-ownership-facts + wamn-5.14-run-queue-facts (queue/reclaim
+ ephemeral-schema + the mTLS NATS lesson + queuebench Harness), wamn-5.7-run-state-facts
(reconstruct(plan,run,node_runs) + Plan::resume + the runs/node_runs schema + capture-off
+ the s3.runs/s3.node_runs additions to postgres-init.sql + testhostbench template),
wamn-5.2-flowrunner-facts (the GUEST execute() = open_run -> load_completed -> reconstruct
-> loop next/dispatch/record/apply; pg-write idempotent by (run_id,step) ON CONFLICT),
wamn-s3-flowrunner-facts (flowbench run-until-kill resume gate; std_node dispatch),
wamn-s6-testhost-facts (testhostbench two-host + ephemeral schema provision via SUPERUSER
+ WAMN_PG_ADMIN_URL), wamn-host-build-facts-s1-for-s2-wash (host build + kind + epoch
kill = Trap::Interrupt via KILL_TICKS). Then UNDERSTAND PASS (inline or 2-3 reader
Workflow): map (A) queuebench claim/RECLAIM + its ephemeral queue_ddl (runs + run_queue);
(B) flowbench run-until-kill + how the guest reconstructs on a fresh execute(); (C) the
flowrunner guest execute() reconstruction path (components/flowrunner) + wamn-run-store
reconstruct/Plan::resume + the s3.* fixtures (deploy/postgres-init.sql) that the guest
uses; (D) platform-plan 5.14 "checkpoint/resume on replica loss" + docs/run-queue.md +
docs/run-state.md VERBATIM. Confirm: does the guest need a run_queue row to run, or does
it just take a run_id? (per 5.14 the queue is HOST-side, guest unchanged -> the host
harness owns the claim/reclaim and hands a run_id to whichever guest instance.)

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS — confirm via AskUserQuestion (scoping IS the game):
1. HARNESS location/shape (the core fork): where does the failover gate live?
   (A) NEW dedicated `failoverbench` (crates/wamn-host/src/failoverbench.rs): provisions
       an ephemeral schema UNIONING runs + node_runs + run_queue (+ the flow/sink s3.*
       fixture the guest needs), drives the flowrunner guest, orchestrates replica-A-
       claims(queue) -> guest-A run-until-kill(mid-effect) -> A-lease-expiry -> replica-B-
       reclaims(queue) -> guest-B reconstruct+resume -> assert exactly-once sink +
       run=completed. Cleanest composition; own Job of record. RECOMMEND leaning here.
   (B) EXTEND flowbench with a `failover` mode: reuses its run-until-kill + guest resume,
       ADD run_queue + a lease claim/reclaim wrapper. Less new scaffolding but bolts
       run_queue onto the S3 gate.
   (C) EXTEND testhostbench (two-host + ephemeral schema already) with a failover mode.
   Decide after the understand pass by which already has the most reusable machinery.
2. GUEST INTEGRATION: does fqg.2 need the GUEST to CLAIM from the queue (= mini
   wamn-fqg.4), OR does the HOST harness orchestrate claim/reclaim ON BEHALF of the guest
   (guest UNCHANGED, the 5.14 host-side-queue model)? RECOMMEND host-orchestrates (guest
   unchanged) so fqg.4 stays DEFERRED and fqg.2 = gate + thin wiring, NOT a guest rewire.
   Confirm the user doesn't want the guest-self-claim rewire folded in.
3. CODE SURFACE: pure GATE composing existing primitives (claim_batch_sql reclaim +
   wamn_run_store::reconstruct/Plan::resume), OR also a small DOCUMENTED "failover"
   primitive/helper (e.g. a wamn-run-queue reclaim-then-resume seam)? RECOMMEND
   gate-first; add a helper only if the wiring reveals a reusable primitive. Likely NO
   new crate.
4. (Confirm) KILL MECHANISM: reuse flowbench's epoch run-until-kill (kill AFTER the
   side-effect commits, BEFORE the checkpoint) so reclaim+resume REPLAYS the effect and
   the ON CONFLICT idempotency proves exactly-once — the real crash-safety proof. And
   assert the reclaimed+completed run ends `completed`, NOT `infrastructure-failure`
   (the janitor must not reap a run a replica successfully reclaimed).

DELIVERABLES: (1) the failover gate (per Q1) — the kill-mid-run -> queue-reclaim ->
reconstruct-resume -> EXACTLY-ONCE side-effect + run=completed assertion, across a
replica boundary. (2) if Q3=helper: a small documented primitive. (3) docs/run-queue.md
+ docs/run-state.md gain a "checkpoint/resume on replica loss" / failover section
(the deferred run in run-queue.md's Scope table becomes real). (4) CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md
gate command (BYTE-IDENTICAL mirror). (5) if new bench: deploy/failoverbench-job.yaml
(co-located w/ postgres, NO cpu limit = S2 CFS lesson, WAMN_PG_URL + WAMN_PG_ADMIN_URL
superuser for the ephemeral schema; initContainer nc-wait).

GATES: cargo test (+ clippy/fmt) if a crate changes; the failover gate LOCAL (throwaway
postgres:18 -p 5459 + postgres-init.sql for the s3.* flow/sink fixture the guest needs;

title: [5.14] Per-partition ownership for partitioned(key) dispatch
description: Deferred from the 5.14 walking skeleton (wamn-m2z). Add per-partition run-claim ownership so partitioned(key) flows (5.11 ordering semantics) dispatch in-order per key across replicas: a replica claims a partition, not just individual runs. The run_queue.partition_key column + run_queue_partition index are already reserved by deploy/run-queue.sql; the pure claim logic (crates/wamn-run-queue) needs a partition-ownership arbitration fn + a partition-scoped claim SQL. queuebench gains a partition-ordering gate. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 5.14 (per-partition ownership) + docs/run-queue.md (deferred table); pairs with 5.11 (wamn-1d4).
notes:
=== RESUME PLAN (wamn-fqg.1 [5.14] Per-partition ownership for partitioned(key) dispatch;
start after bd prime + bd show wamn-fqg.1) ===

GOAL: extend the 5.14 walking-skeleton queue so `partitioned(key)` flows dispatch IN-ORDER
PER KEY across replicas — a replica OWNS a partition (all runs sharing a partition_key), not
just individual runs, so ordering within a key is preserved under horizontal scaling. The seam
is already reserved: deploy/run-queue.sql has `partition_key text` (nullable) + the
`run_queue_partition` index (tenant_id, partition_key WHERE partition_key IS NOT NULL). This
PAIRS with 5.11 (wamn-1d4, OPEN, NOT a hard dep): this issue owns the per-partition CLAIM/
OWNERSHIP MECHANISM; 5.11 owns the ordering SEMANTICS (strict/partitioned/unordered) + the
runner's in-order execution. Draw that line carefully.

STEP 1 ON RESUME (before code): RE-LOAD the memory `wamn-5.14-run-queue-facts` (THE crate this
extends — the claim/lease/janitor/reconcile builders, the queuebench ephemeral-schema +
percentile + JoinSet pattern, the CRITICAL mTLS NATS lesson, the ClaimState/Exhausted budget-
guard). Then map (a focused understand-pass Workflow of 2-3 readers, OR inline since the code
is recent and I authored it — decide by how much context survived compaction):
  A. crates/wamn-run-queue/src/{sql,claim,lease,model,janitor}.rs + lib.rs — where a partition-
     scoped claim + partition-ownership arbitration slot in (claim_batch_sql is the anchor; the
     new claim must restrict to owned/claimable partitions and preserve per-partition order).
  B. deploy/run-queue.sql — the reserved partition_key column + run_queue_partition index; decide
     if an ADDITIVE partition-owner table (or column reuse) is needed.
  C. crates/wamn-host/src/queuebench.rs — the modes/Harness/reset()/provision pattern to add a
     `partition` mode; and how the ephemeral queue_ddl clone would gain any partition DDL.
  D. platform-plan.md 5.14 ("per-partition ownership for partitioned(key)") + 5.11 (per-node
     strict/partitioned(key)/unordered dispatch, D9 no-batch-API) VERBATIM + the scope line vs 5.11.

KEY DESIGN DECISIONS — confirm via AskUserQuestion (scoping IS the game, like 5.2/5.7/5.14):
1. OWNERSHIP MODEL (the core fork):
   (A) DEDICATED partition-lease table wamn_run.partition_owner (tenant_id, partition_key) ->
       lease_owner + lease_expires_at; a replica LEASES a partition, then the claim SQL restricts
       to runs whose partition is owned-by-me (or unowned+leasable). Explicit multi-run-per-
       partition ownership + batching; failover = partition-lease expiry reclaim (mirrors the
       5.14 run-lease design). ADDITIVE table to run-queue.sql + live-apply coverage.
   (B) CLAIM-BY-PARTITION-HEAD (no new table): the claim SQL atomically claims the SINGLE earliest
       ready run per partition (SELECT DISTINCT ON (partition_key) ... ORDER BY partition_key,
       available_at FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), and a partition is IMPLICITLY owned while its head
       run's lease is live — a partition's 2nd run is not claimable until the head completes
       (dequeues). Lightest; in-order-per-key falls out of "at most one in-flight run per
       partition"; reuses the existing run_queue, NO new table. RECOMMEND leaning (B) for the
       skeleton unless partitioned(key) must mean "a replica owns a key's whole backlog + batches"
       (then A). Decide after the understand pass.
   (C) pg advisory locks per partition (pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtext(partition_key))) — fast, no
       durable ownership, but lease/failover is session-bound (a crash releases the lock at conn
       close, not via a durable timeout) — weaker crash-safety than A/B; likely NOT the pick.
2. COORDINATION WITH 5.11 (wamn-1d4): proceed INDEPENDENTLY (this issue = the mechanism, kept
   consumable by 5.11) vs co-design/fold-in. wamn-1d4 is OPEN, NOT a dep. RECOMMEND independent +
   note the seam. Confirm the user doesn't want 5.11 folded in.
3. STRUCTURE (confirm): extend the PURE crate wamn-run-queue (partition-scoped claim SQL builder +
   partition-ownership/arbitration decision fns as pure fns of (rows/owner-rows, now); model +
   ADDITIVE DDL if (A)) + a queuebench `partition` mode + docs/run-queue.md (deferred section ->
   real) + CLAUDE/AGENTS [5.14] block note. The obvious mirror of the whole codebase.

DELIVERABLES: (1) pure wamn-run-queue additions — partition_scoped_claim_sql (+ partition-owner
model + lease/renew/expiry SQL if A) + pure decision fns (owns_partition / partition_claim
planning), unit-tested off-cluster + a claim-SQL string test. (2) queuebench `partition` mode:
seed runs across P partitions each with an in-partition sequence, N concurrent claimers, ASSERT
(i) at most ONE in-flight run per partition at any instant (per-key serialization), (ii) IN-ORDER
dispatch within a partition (seq monotonic per key), (iii) partition FAILOVER (a claimant dies /
head lease expires -> another replica takes the partition, still in order, exactly-once). (3)
docs/run-queue.md deferred-per-partition section becomes real. (4) CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md [5.14] block

title: [4.2] Bind authenticated callers to generated-API RLS claims
description: Bridge the canonical authenticated-principal context into the per-project generated data API and Postgres RLS session variables. Resolve project scope and effective application role from trusted identity/authorization context, then bind app.user_id and app.role with parameterized set_config calls; never accept caller identity or role from request payloads. This is separate from management authoring middleware and from the first-party identity authority.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated human/service callers reach the generated REST/GraphQL data surface with correctly bound user/project/role claims; absent, forged, cross-project, disabled, and stale credentials refuse before SQL; a randomized two-user one-project RLS gate performs at least 10,000 cross-user attempts with zero leaks; claim values are bound parameters; management authoring S0 does not depend on this bridge.
notes:
External review R5b (docs/review-findings.md § R5): S2 proved TENANT-level RLS only — and docs/p0-results.md already scopes that claim correctly (component-identity -> app.tenant; the gate was 10k randomized cross-TENANT attempts), so no doc fix is needed. What lands HERE: 4.2 acceptance criteria gain an S2-style randomized gate at the USER level — two users, one tenant, row-ownership policies, x10k cross-user attempts, zero leaks (field-mask read/write assertions ride 4.3 wamn-sbh). And the new app.user_id/app.role claims must be born as BIND PARAMETERS in the set_config claim statement (the wamn-5x0.2 dependency) — never joining a format! template. wamn-rls already reads them defensively (NULLIF(...)::uuid / COALESCE).

title: [5.9] Credential vault (K8s Secrets per project)
description: Per-project credential vault: flows reference a credential BY NAME (the wamn-flow CredentialRef, 5.1 - never inlined secret material); the runner resolves the named credential at dispatch and injects it ONLY into the executing node's context; the http-request node (and any credential-consuming node) reads it there. Backed by a per-project credential source (config/env v1; K8s Secrets later). Design: docs/platform-plan.md 5.9.
design: Surfaces ALREADY shipped: (a) wamn-flow CredentialRef{name,kind?,description?} + node.credential (5.1, by-ref only, no secret in flow data); (b) the wamn:node credentials WIT import FROZEN at 5.4 but UNWIRED (no host impl). Real work: (1) host-side resolution - read the named credential from a per-project source; (2) wire the frozen wamn:node credentials import (or an inject-into-config seam) so a node fetches a named credential; (3) http-request node consumes it (credential -> header). SECURITY INVARIANTS: referenced-never-inlined; injected only into the EXECUTING node's context (never into flow data, run/node_run records, or sibling nodes). OPEN DESIGN FORKS (resolve when scoping): [i] WIT-import-the-node-calls vs host-templates-value-into-config-before-dispatch; [ii] credential SOURCE - static config/env map (v1, the 2.2 StaticCredentialProvider pattern) vs live K8s Secret (shares the namespaced Secret client wamn-5x0.1 builds for DB creds). RELATIONSHIP (not a hard dep): wamn-5x0.1 [2.2b] reads wamn-db-* Secrets for the PLUGIN's DB pool; 5.9 reads per-project credential Secrets for FLOW NODES - both want the same namespaced K8s Secret client, so the live-Secret fork should share that infra.
notes: Pivot target 2026-07-16 (from POC-F3 wamn-24i, which this blocks). ACCEPTANCE: a flow references a credential by name; the runner resolves it at dispatch from a per-project source and injects it only into the executing node's context; the http-request node sends it to a target; a gate proves the credential reached the target AND did NOT leak into run/node_run records or other nodes. Scope the two design forks (import-vs-config, static-vs-K8s) before building - likely an AskUserQuestion.
close_reason: Credential vault shipped: frozen wamn:node/credentials WIT seam host-implemented (wamn_credentials plugin — project-scoped, audit-logged, WAMN_CREDENTIALS_FILE mounted-Secret source), per-dispatch guest scoping (CapsCtx carries only the declared name), http-request consumption (authorization header); fail-closed run-worker egress (--allowed-hosts, empty=deny-all) wired alongside since the store had NO outgoing handler (outbound calls trapped). Gate: credproof — delivery via serve-echo's one-way fnv1a digest + TOTAL containment scan; local e2e + in-cluster gate of record both PASS 23/23; 4 mutants killed; all regressions green (flowbench/failoverbench/testhostbench/runnerbench/egressbench).

title: [5.11] Ordering & concurrency policies
description: Per-node strict / partitioned(key) / unordered dispatch in the runner; record streams amortize invocation overhead with order preserved — replaces any batch API (D9). Design: docs/platform-plan.md 5.11
notes:
External review R6 + R8d (docs/review-findings.md, verified at tip 873c3d8): 5.11 must DECIDE ordering-under-unavailability for partitioned(key) BEFORE any partitioned flow ships — today the mechanism decides it silently. claim_partition_head_sql's blocker predicate (crates/wamn-run-queue/src/sql.rs:351-362) orders only CURRENTLY-READY siblings: a transiently backed-off (future available_at) or parked head YIELDS the key and a later run overtakes it, so partitioned(key) currently means ordered-except-under-retry-or-park — weaker than the plan's Kafka model (a Kafka consumer blocks its partition on retry, never leapfrogs) and corrupting for genealogy consume-before-produce / state-machine streams on nothing more than a transient network blip. The danger is flows shipping and silently depending on whichever behavior exists, after which the default is a breaking change.

PROPOSED (review): per-flow (or per-node) policy on partitioned(key) — `blocking` DEFAULT (a backed-off/parked run still blocks its key; mechanically: drop the available_at <= now() arm from the blocker check so the head is the earliest LIVE run, ready or not; choosing partitioned IS opting into ordering), `leapfrog` OPT-IN (today's (available_at, run_id) behavior — for keys where ordering is a throughput heuristic). The already-deferred TERMINAL wedge-vs-release question folds into the same knob: blocking + budget exhausted => wedge (operator unblocks; janitor verdict releases the key only under leapfrog) — the strict-traceability behavior D14 genealogy wants. Implementation preference: materialize the policy onto the queue row at enqueue (claim SQL stays self-contained); wamn-flow ordering config gains the field; partition.rs pure layer models both; the park path needs no change. VERIFY: queuebench partition phase gains both-policy cases (blocking: kill/backoff the head, assert run 2 does NOT dispatch until head completes; leapfrog: assert today's behavior) + a wedge case (exhaust head budget under blocking, key stalls, janitor verdict does not release).

ALSO riding 5.11-adjacent (R8d): per-flow cron MISFIRE policy — `collapse` default (current, documented) | `catch-up` with a bounded backfill window (Quartz-precedented; deterministic tick-named run ids make it mechanically trivial — fire each missed tick's id, ON CONFLICT dedupes). Linkage: row-event flows on genealogy tables will want partition_key = row pk so outbox seq order survives dispatch — one more consumer of the blocking default.

Doc closure with the decision: run-queue.md:129-133 policy paragraph -> pointer to the decided policy; decision-table row (chosen: per-key policy, blocking default; rejected: inherit (available_at, run_id) order silently — semantics by accident). Interim honest-behavior doc line is in wamn-m5g.
EVENT-PLANE LINKAGE (2026-07-17, wamn-z7b): the R6 blocking decision is now load-bearing for a SECOND subsystem — the event-plane materializer hard-depends on it for partitioned(key) materialization (docs/event-plane-jetstream.md v2.1 section 6; wamn-z7b.5 depends on this bead). Decide once, serve both: the ladder's 5.11 needs the same decision. Note the doc's ordering key is the OUTBOX seq (source-derived), so 'partition_key = row pk preserves outbox order' composes cleanly with blocking.
RESUME PLAN (2026-07-17, dkk-approved sequencing — take the R6 SLICE of 5.11 first, not the whole feature):
SCOPE: decide + implement + gate the R6 ordering policy only. Record-stream amortization and the R8d cron-misfire knob stay in this bead for later slices. Guest-side partitioned claiming is fqg.9's scope, NOT this slice — today partition claims are exercised by queuebench host-side, so R6 lands entirely in SQL + pure layer + bench.
DECISION (proposed by review, endorse unless evidence emerges): per-key policy on partitioned(key) — 'blocking' DEFAULT (backed-off/parked head still blocks its key; head = earliest LIVE run ready or not), 'leapfrog' OPT-IN (today's (available_at, run_id) order). Terminal fold-in: blocking + budget exhausted => key wedges (operator release; janitor infrastructure-failure verdict releases the key only under leapfrog).
STEPS: (1) wamn-flow ordering config gains the policy field (default blocking) + schema regen via print-schema (drift-guarded — same flow as fqg.11's allowed-hosts). (2) Materialize the policy onto the queue row at enqueue (preferred per review: claim SQL stays self-contained) — enqueue writers + run-queue DDL column + fail_kind-style CHECK? keep additive. (3) claim_partition_head_sql (crates/wamn-run-queue/src/sql.rs:351-362) branches the blocker predicate on the row's policy: blocking = drop the available_at <= now() arm from the blocker check. (4) partition.rs pure layer models both. Park path unchanged (parking already releases the run lease). (5) queuebench partition phase gains both-policy cases (blocking: kill/backoff the head, assert run 2 does NOT dispatch until head completes; leapfrog: assert today's behavior) + wedge case (exhaust head budget under blocking => key stalls, janitor verdict does not release). (6) Doc closure: run-queue.md:129-133 policy paragraph -> decided policy; NEW decision-table row in platform-plan.md (D20; chosen: per-key policy blocking default / rejected: inherit (available_at, run_id) silently); 5.11 note in the bead.
GATES: cargo test -p wamn-run-queue (+ wamn-flow schema drift guard); local queuebench vs throwaway postgres (build-and-test.md 5.14 section); in-cluster queuebench-job.yaml = gate of record (gates image rebuild + kind load — one stage, guest unchanged for this slice UNLESS the flow schema field is read by the guest; it is not, until fqg.9).
WORKFLOW: commit after the slice completes (rule fqg11-workflow-commit-per-issue); say explicitly whether the in-cluster gate ran. Cluster: healthy as of 2026-07-17 after the inotify fix (bd memory kind-cluster-inotify-reboot) — runner + serve-echo deployed, images at tip c4b6e64.
R6 SLICE DONE (2026-07-17, D20 chosen): per-key head-unavailability policy on partitioned(key). SHIPPED — (1) wamn-flow Flow::partition_policy {blocking default / leapfrog} + schema regen (docs/flow-schema.schema.json); (2) run_queue.partition_policy column (DEFAULT 'blocking' CHECK) materialized at enqueue (enqueue_with_policy_sql) + QueueEntry.partition_policy/enqueued_at; (3) claim_partition_head_sql branches the blocker predicate on the row policy — blocking ranks by the STREAM order (enqueued_at, run_id) so a backed-off/parked/exhausted earlier run blocks (Kafka model); leapfrog keeps the pre-D20 (available_at, run_id) currently-ready ranking; (4) janitor_sweep_sql EXEMPTS a blocking-policy row (wedge — operator release) + JanitorVerdict::Wedged in the pure janitor; (5) partition.rs pure layer models both via blocks(b,c,now); (6) gates: 3 new pure tests (policy overtake, wedge-vs-release, janitor wedge verdict) + shape/DDL drift guards + live-apply Phase A/B (real builders) + queuebench partition_policy_cases. VERIFIED local: crate 36 pure + live-apply through throwaway PG18 :5468 (all D20 asserts) + queuebench --mode partition PASS (blocking holds/wedges, leapfrog overtakes/releases) + failoverbench regression + 4 mutants KILLED (mutate_1d4.py: pure blocks / pure janitor / SQL janitor exemption / SQL head-claim swap). In-cluster queuebench-job = gate of record (gates-image rebuild only, guest UNCHANGED — the guest does not read the flow field until fqg.9). Doc closure: platform-plan.md D20 row, run-queue.md Head-unavailability policy section, flow-schema.md partition-policy field row, build-and-test.md [5.14] D20 note. STILL OPEN in this bead (later slices): record-stream amortization (D9 batch-API replacement) + R8d per-flow cron MISFIRE policy (collapse default / bounded catch-up). fqg.9 wires the guest to read partition_policy at enqueue (materialize the flow's declaration onto the queue row on the guest-claim path). wamn-z7b.5 (event-plane materializer) hard-depends on this blocking decision.
SPLIT + CLOSED (2026-07-17, dkk directive: issues must be granular — no in-bead 'slices'/subsections; a distinct piece is a separate issue). The R6 ordering-POLICY decision (D20: per-key blocking-default / leapfrog head-unavailability policy) shipped in commit 84233fa (in-cluster queuebench gate of record PASS). The two remaining distinct pieces are NOW SEPARATE BEADS: wamn-fqg.18 [5.11] record-stream dispatch / amortize per-invocation overhead (D9 batch-API replacement) and wamn-fqg.19 [5.14] per-flow cron misfire policy (R8d collapse|catch-up). The runner-side wiring that reads a flow's ordering mode + policy and materializes it onto the queue row at enqueue is wamn-fqg.9 (guest self-claim). Closing this bead satisfies the R6-decision dependency for wamn-z7b.5 (event-plane materializer).
close_reason: R6 ordering-policy decision (D20) shipped (commit 84233fa, in-cluster gate PASS); remaining scope split into separate granular beads wamn-fqg.18 (record-stream/D9) + wamn-fqg.19 (cron-misfire/R8d)

notes:
External review R7a (docs/review-findings.md § R7): any alert that fires on the infrastructure-failure TRANSITION will false-alarm on every slow resume — by design (fqg.2 reverse-race), the janitor may reap a slow-but-alive resume to infrastructure-failure and the runner's deliberately unconditional completion write then overrides it back to completed; the work happened exactly once and the FINAL status says so. title: [3.4] Schema versioning & environments (draft->staged->applied)
description: Draft -> staged -> applied lifecycle; JSON export/import for promotion between dev/prod projects. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 3.4
notes:
=== RESUME PLAN (3.4 wamn-d6d; start after bd prime + bd show wamn-d6d) ===

GOAL: Schema versioning & environments. A catalog version has a lifecycle
draft -> staged -> applied; JSON export/import promotes a model between dev/prod
projects. 3.4 COMPOSES the two E3 crates already shipped: wamn-catalog (versioned
Catalog + from_json/to_json + diff) and wamn-ddl (Migration::create/migrate +
additive/destructive Confirmation gate). It formalizes: (a) the LIFECYCLE state
machine over catalog versions with legal transitions + guards; (b) PROMOTION =
import a source (e.g. dev-applied) catalog into a target env, diff vs the
target's current applied catalog, compile a MigrationPlan (wamn-ddl) carrying the
safety gate; (c) STORAGE: a lifecycle `state` on catalog.catalogs + the
single-applied-per-catalog invariant (the existing `active` pointer generalized).
Deliverable shape TBD -- ASK the user first (STEP 1); it will most likely mirror
the crate pattern (new crate wamn-schema depending on wamn-catalog + wamn-ddl).

SCOPE GUARD: 3.4 is the LIFECYCLE + PROMOTION model. It is NOT:
- 3.2 DDL compiler (DONE -- 3.4 REUSES Migration::migrate to compile the
  promotion diff + the Confirmation/backup gate; do NOT re-emit DDL);
- 3.3 visual designer UI (the draft-editing UX / staging screen) -- wamn-ivi;
- 2.5 migration ENGINE (versioned forward-only history + rollback + live
  transactional APPLY) -- 3.4 produces the plan; 2.5/hosting apply it;
- 2.3/10.3 the real backup/PITR mechanism (3.4 keeps the gate POLICY only);
- 4.x API generation.
CRITICAL: export/import JSON is ALREADY wamn_catalog::Catalog::to_json/from_json
(the promotion FORMAT, documented in 3.1). 3.4 WRAPS it into a promotion
WORKFLOW; it does NOT reinvent serialization. Stay PROPORTIONATE -- 3.4 is P2 and
blocks nothing; keep it to lifecycle + promotion + storage, reuse wamn-ddl.

WHAT THE MODEL MUST EXPRESS:
- LIFECYCLE STATE per catalog version: Draft (editable, not applied) ->
  Staged (frozen candidate, impact-analyzed by 11.8, awaiting apply) ->
  Applied (the live schema; EXACTLY ONE per (environment, catalog_id)) ->
  Superseded (a previously-applied version). Legal transitions with guards:
  Draft->Staged (freeze); Staged->Applied (apply; demotes the prior Applied to
  Superseded); Staged->Draft (unstage); Draft discard. Guards: only Draft is
  editable; can't apply a Staged whose base version is no longer the current
  Applied (stale-base / rebase guard = concurrent-change safety).
- ENVIRONMENTS: dev/prod. In the per-project-DB model (2.2/2.3) environment ~=
  project, so each env's catalog.catalogs holds THAT env's versions + its own
  applied pointer. Promotion moves a version's CONTENT from source env to target
  env as a new Draft/Staged there, then diffs vs the target's Applied.
- PROMOTION: promote(source: &Catalog, target_applied: Option<&Catalog>)
  -> PromotionPlan { imported catalog, MigrationPlan (Migration::migrate(
  target_applied, source) OR Migration::create if target has none), safety
  classification, warnings }. Reuses the wamn-ddl Confirmation gate verbatim.
- STORAGE (additive to deploy/catalog-schema.sql, the STANDALONE artifact --
  NOT deploy/postgres-init.sql): add `state text` (draft|staged|applied|
  superseded, CHECK) to catalog.catalogs (generalizing the bare `active` bool);
  enforce single-applied via a PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX (tenant_id, catalog_id)
  WHERE state='applied'. Keep house style (FORCE RLS on app.tenant already
  there). Environment is implicit (per-project DB) OR a light `environment`
  label column -- decide in Q3.

DELIVERABLE DECISION -- ASK THE USER (AskUserQuestion) on resume, BEFORE coding:
Q1 shape:
  (A) [likely REC] NEW crate crates/wamn-schema (depends on wamn-catalog +
      wamn-ddl): lifecycle State enum + legal-transition fn/guards; promote()
      -> PromotionPlan reusing Migration + Confirmation; catalog storage
      additions (state column + single-applied partial-unique); docs. Composes
      the two E3 crates; mirrors the 3.1/3.2/5.1 crate pattern.
  (B) module inside wamn-catalog (no new crate).
  (C) protocol/docs-only: define states + transitions + promotion protocol +
      worked example; NO new Rust (3.3/control-plane implement against it).
Q2 lifecycle scope: does 3.4 own the FULL state machine (draft/staged/applied/
  superseded + transitions + guards incl the stale-base rebase guard) [REC], or
  just export/import + the promotion diff, leaving draft/staged as UI-only states
  owned by 3.3?
Q3 environments: model environments as a first-class dimension (a per-env applied
  pointer + promote(source_env -> target_env) diffing vs target's applied,
  environment column in storage) [REC], OR keep it project-to-project JSON
  export/import only (promotion = import + diff vs whatever Catalog you pass; no
  env registry -- env ~= project via per-project DB)? (Per-project-DB makes a
  full env registry possibly overkill; a light label may suffice.)
(Fold storage into Q1: add the lifecycle-state DDL now [REC] or defer.)

WHAT EXISTS (probed 2026-07-11, HEAD 76779f6):
- wamn_catalog::Catalog{schema_version, catalog_id, version:u32, ...} +
  from_json/to_json (THE promotion format) + diff()->CatalogDiff + validate().
- wamn_ddl::Migration::create(&Catalog)/migrate(&old,&new)->MigrationPlan;
  MigrationPlan.sql(Confirmation::{None,ConfirmedWithBackup}) safety gate;
  Operation{safety Additive|Destructive, entity, field, ...}. REUSE THIS.
- deploy/catalog-schema.sql catalog.catalogs(tenant_id, catalog_id, version,
  schema_version, name, active bool) -- the version rows + active/applied
  pointer already exist (active flips like s3.flows.active). 3.4 generalizes
  `active` -> a `state` lifecycle. STANDALONE artifact (not in postgres-init.sql).
- No existing versioning/lifecycle/promotion code -- greenfield beyond the above.

MIRROR THE CRATE PATTERN (see memories wamn-3.1 / wamn-3.2 / wamn-5.1): if A,
crates/wamn-schema added to root Cargo.toml members; reuse the Issue/Result +
Debug/Clone/PartialEq shape; serde (rename_all=kebab-case) only if a new
serialized type is introduced (State transitions may not need schemars -- no JSON
Schema unless a new persisted contract appears); tests over the POC fixture
(promote a v1->v2, assert PromotionPlan + gate; transition legality; stale-base
guard); storage additions additive + house style; CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md mirrored
[3.4] block; docs/schema-lifecycle.md (or extend docs/catalog-model.md).

STEPS: 1) ASK Q1/Q2/Q3 (+storage). 2) scaffold crate (if A; members +=). 3)
lifecycle State + legal transitions + guards. 4) promote() reusing wamn-ddl
Migration + Confirmation. 5) storage additions (state column + partial-unique
single-applied) additive to deploy/catalog-schema.sql. 6) tests (transition
legality, promote additive/destructive, stale-base guard; export/import
round-trip already covered in wamn-catalog). 7) clippy+fmt clean; workspace
build; regressions (wamn-catalog 19 / wamn-flow 13 / wamn-ddl 8+doctest). 8)
docs. 9) CLAUDE.md+AGENTS.md mirrored block (verify byte-identical). 10) bd close
wamn-d6d (--reason --suggest-next). 11) COMMIT (standing rule; after close; amend
.beads/interactions.jsonl like prior commits). 12) bd remember --key
wamn-3.4-schema-versioning-facts (via a FILE, no backticks -- the %/backtick
shell-substitution lesson).

RISKS/NOTES: (i) bd notes/memory via FILES + "$(cat file)"; NEVER inline
backticks/% in bd remember; --key not a positional (bd remember takes content as
the ONE positional). (ii) serde deny_unknown_fields NOT supported on
internally-tagged enums -- if State/PromotionPlan are tagged enums, DROP it (keep
on plain structs). (iii) PROPORTIONATE: 3.4 is P2 and blocks nothing -- do NOT
build 2.5's migration engine/rollback or 3.3's UI; reuse wamn-ddl, don't re-emit
DDL. (iv) export/import ALREADY = Catalog::to_json/from_json -- wrap, don't
reinvent. (v) single-applied invariant = partial unique index WHERE
state='applied'. (vi) environment ~= project (per-project DB) -- a full env
registry may be overkill; a light label likely enough (Q3). (vii) no git remote
-> commit only, never push. (viii) catalog storage additions are ADDITIVE to the
STANDALONE deploy/catalog-schema.sql (never postgres-init.sql; S2-S6 fixtures
untouched); if the state column changes an existing catalog.catalogs column,
prefer ADD + keep `active` OR replace cleanly since the file is standalone/not
yet deployed anywhere -- validate the whole file re-applies clean on a throwaway
PG18 (like 3.1/3.2 did). (ix) let-chains + edition 2024 OK.

ENV STATE (2026-07-11, HEAD 76779f6, tree CLEAN): Done S1-S6 + P0-EXIT + 2.1 +
2.2 + 2.6 + 5.1 + 3.1 + 3.2. 3.4 wamn-d6d = OPEN P2, depends only on wamn-vbd
[3.2] (DONE), BLOCKS NOTHING (leaf). No in-progress issues. Sibling-ready E3/E4
work also unblocked: wamn-759 [4.1 API gateway] (ready since 3.1), wamn-ivi [3.3],
wamn-idu [3.5], wamn-i1k [6.6]. Memories to load: wamn-3.1-catalog-model-facts
(model + from_json/to_json + catalog.catalogs storage), wamn-3.2-ddl-compiler-
facts (Migration::create/migrate + Confirmation gate to REUSE), wamn-5.1-flow-
schema-facts (crate pattern), wamn-backlog-conventions-issue-titles-carry-doc-
refs. Standing rules: ONE issue at a time; claim; ALWAYS ask-first before
assuming; commit after bd close; no push; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md mirrored
(independent files). This prep only CLAIMS wamn-d6d + attaches this plan; do NOT
start implementing until the user resumes and Q1/Q2/Q3 are answered.

WHAT 9.2 IS: run-context carries W3C traceparent; SDK helpers propagate it; and the host plugins (wasi:http outgoing, wamn:postgres) STAMP trace context onto any outbound call that LACKS it — propagation is HOST-ENFORCED, not authorship-dependent, so a broken trace from an SDK-bypassing custom node is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE. 9.2 is the follow-on 9.1 explicitly deferred (docs/tracing.md sec Boundaries): 9.1 threads WITHIN a process (tracing parent/child -> OTel) but breaks ACROSS pods because outbound HTTP does not inject traceparent.

The flowrunner guest fabricates traceparent: None (components/flowrunner/src/lib.rs:538-539) = UNWIRED. So the FIELDS exist; 9.2 WIRES them.
- Outbound HTTP does NOT inject traceparent today: wash-runtime host/http.rs only EXTRACTS incoming traceparent (line 949 opentelemetry::global::get_text_map_propagator().extract). NO inject anywhere (grep 9.1 confirmed). The inbound side ALREADY continues a caller's trace (extract + the #[instrument] handle_http_request span); the missing half is OUTBOUND inject.

- THE CRUX / injection site (host.rs survey): host.rs:171 builder.with_http_handler(Arc::new(server)) sets the INBOUND HttpServer (DynamicRouter), NOT the outbound handler. The OUTBOUND handler in production is wash-runtime's DEFAULT (DefaultOutgoingHandler + allowed_hosts gating in vendored engine/linked_call.rs / ctx.rs build_ctx_from_template). The S6 egress-spy used CtxBuilder::with_http_handler(Arc<dyn HostHandler>) but that is a PER-STORE GATE path (testhostbench builds its own store) — it likely does NOT reach the production washlet ClusterHostBuilder stores. So injecting the outbound traceparent WAMN-SIDE has NO obvious production hook -> 9.2 LIKELY NEEDS A CARRIED FORK COMMIT on wash-runtime's outbound send path (host/http.rs, at/near outbound_client_span http.rs:876-910/1137 where wash already creates the outbound client span = the natural inject point: inject the CURRENT span's W3C context into the request headers before send). The 9.1 wamn.postgres DB span ALREADY nests under the current span (trace context is captured). title: finding(auth): control-author RLS uses the mapping-table shape the guest ruling bans
description:
FINDING, DATED AND ACCEPTED FOR MVP - not a waiver, and not an inconsistency for the next reader to trip over.

## The finding

deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql creates wamn_authority.author_login_tenants, a MAPPING TABLE, and wamn_authority.session_author_tenant() reads it. Control-author RLS policies then read tenant_id = wamn_authority.session_author_tenant().

The owner ruling of 2026-08-26 on wamn-0h0g.22.6 rejected exactly that shape for the guest path, on the principle that the ban targets MUTABLE SETTABLE STATE BETWEEN IDENTITY AND AUTHORITY. That argument is about the shape, so on its face it applies here too. The guest path instead derives authority through wamn.tenant_key, a pure immutable function with no writer and no state.

## Why it is DEFERRABLE, which is not the same as fine

  - THREAT MODEL DIFFERS IN DEGREE, not in kind. Control-plane authors are a BOUNDED, PLATFORM-ADMINISTERED principal set - dozens, provisioned by us. Tenant guest code is UNBOUNDED and adversarial by assumption. The severity that forced immutability on the guest side does not transfer at the same weight.
  - THE FIX IS REAL WORK, NOT A RENAME. A table-reading function cannot become IMMUTABLE. The actual remedy is PER-AUTHOR LOGIN GENERATIONS CARRYING THE TENANT IN THE ROLE IDENTITY - the guest-side pattern applied to authors - which is item-2-class construction, not a patch.

## Accepted for MVP on the bounded-principal argument.

## TRIGGERS - either one reopens this

  1. ANY WIDENING OF WHO CAN HOLD AUTHOR LOGINS. The acceptance rests entirely on the principal set being bounded and platform-administered; widening it removes the argument.
  2. THE FIRST CONTROL-PLANE MULTI-TENANCY EXPANSION.

## Owner

The owner named THE IDENTITY-MODULARIZATION EPIC. NO SUCH EPIC EXISTS IN THE TRACKER - measured 2026-08-26 across every open epic. Filed under wamn-0h0g.9 (Management auth, ctl, additive schema) as the nearest existing owner, because the remedy is authoring-identity work. REPOINT THIS BEAD if that epic is created; it is homed here so it has a real owner rather than a phantom one.

Cross-cited from session_author_tenant()s doc comment in control-portable-store.sql, so the next reader meets a DATED DECISION rather than an apparent inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: Either a trigger fires and this is reopened as construction - per-author login generations carrying the tenant in the role identity, the guest-side pattern applied to authors - or the MVP ships with the acceptance recorded, dated, and cross-cited in the DDL so no reader mistakes it for an oversight.

title: chore(hygiene): audit and retire 17 stale lane branches
description:
## Why

Measured 2026-08-26 at e256db2e while planning wave 74. The repository carries 27 local branches.
A cleanup on 2026-08-23 took it from 96 to 9; it has re-accumulated to 27, so the cleanup was a
one-off rather than a habit, and lane branches are not being removed at integration as the wave
machinery requires.

## The 17 lane-shaped strays

  worktree-agent-* x12
  wave59/lane1-components, wave59/lane2-trace
  wave60/lane3-registries, wave60/lane4-creds
  w57-lane-e

These are NOT wamn-59ho's subjects. That bead is scoped to exactly three preserved branches
(agent/cf-flow-34, agent/cf-attempts-54, codex/wamn-8zht-13) and its disposition is already ruled.

## THE TRAP THAT MAKES THIS REAL WORK RATHER THAN A ONE-LINE DELETE

git merge-base --is-ancestor reports MERGED for only 3 of the 17. *** THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE THE OTHER
14 HOLD UNMERGED WORK. A CHERRY-PICKED LANE BRANCH IS NEVER AN ANCESTOR OF HEAD *** - and this
repository integrates lanes by cherry-pick, so not-ancestor is the EXPECTED reading for a lane whose
content landed in full.

Deleting on the ancestor test alone would be safe-looking and wrong in both directions: it would
refuse to delete branches whose work is fully landed, and it offers no protection for one whose work
is not.

## The audit that is actually required

The same one the 96-to-9 cleanup used, per branch:
  git cherry against deploy-simplification for patch-id equivalence, OR
  an exact subject match for every unique commit in the landed history of deploy-simplification,
  main or mvp.
Only a branch that passes gets deleted. Anything that does not is held and reported, the way
wamn-59ho held its three.

## Also in scope

sync/wasmcloud-2.8.0 is a true ANCESTOR of deploy-simplification (fast-forwarded at d455ffa8) and is
safe to delete without audit. Confirm no other worktree has it checked out first.

## Prevention, which is the actual point

The wave machinery already says to remove the worktree, branch and target dir at integration. Wave 73
did that for all three of its lanes. The 17 strays predate it. Name in the close reason whether any
mechanism now enforces it, or say plainly that it remains a discipline rather than a check.
acceptance_criteria: Every one of the 17 lane-shaped branches is either deleted after passing a patch-id or exact-subject audit against landed history, or held with the measured reason recorded. No branch is deleted on the ancestor test alone. sync/wasmcloud-2.8.0 is deleted. The close reason states whether anything now enforces lane cleanup or whether it stays a discipline.

title: decide(test-support): source-scanning guards have no shared comment-stripper home
description:
## Why

Filed 2026-08-26 from wave 73's wamn-q3kq lane, which measured a REFUTED PREMISE in that bead's
2026-08-24 ruling.

The ruling said: narrow the shelving guard's needle to executable positions with a SHARED
comment-stripper, following the technique wamn-0h0g.15.140 and wamn-0h0g.15.149 already established
for WIT and SQL guards. *** BOTH OF THOSE STRIPPERS ARE GONE FROM THE TREE, DELETED WITH THEIR
FILES. *** Verified at cec008d6:

  wamn-0h0g.15.140  f0c027e5  without_wit_comments
    crates/platform/runtime/tests/flow_invocation_wit_coherence.rs   FILE DELETED
  wamn-0h0g.15.149  4ce0e1ff  sql_without_comments
    services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs         FILE DELETED

So there was nothing to share WITH. The lane ported the technique into
crates/execution/run-state/tests/shelving_contract.rs, the one file inside its fence, and documented
the lineage in the function doc.

## The actual state now

TWO live implementations of one idea, in crates that cannot see each other:
  crates/execution/run-state/tests/shelving_contract.rs   without_rust_comments + literal_width
  tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs:1062         strip_sql_comments  (SQL, line-based)
  tests/conformance/tests/state_ownership.rs:947          rust_string_literals (extracts literals
                                                          rather than returning stripped source)

The conformance pair lives in a tests/ integration binary of wamn-proof-conformance.
wamn-run-state cannot depend on it without a layering inversion.

## What this bead decides and does

Whether source-scanning guards get a real shared home - a small test-support crate - or whether
per-crate copies are accepted as the cheaper honest answer. THIS IS A DECISION FIRST. Do not build
the crate before it is ruled: rule 10 demotes machinery that the RC does not require, and a third
copy of a stripper is cheaper than a crate nobody else imports.

If ruled to build it, the home is test-support/, the consumers are named up front, and the existing
copies converge onto it in the same change rather than being left as drift.

## Not urgent

Nothing is broken. wamn-q3kq's guard is correct and mutation-proven in both directions. This is
about the NEXT guard that needs the technique finding it.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling is recorded on whether source-scanning guards get a shared test-support home or accept per-crate copies. Not superseded by a successor bead - the SUBJECT is retired, so there is no successor to name.

title: feat(obs): measure and copy wiring and node identity into the JetStream effect span
description:
## Why

Split out of wamn-0h0g.24.12 under rule 7 on 2026-08-26, by owner ruling. The parent bead argued
that widening effect_span.rs's shared identity block enriches all four effect surfaces at once. It
does not: each call site must be able to SOURCE the new fields.

## MEASURE FIRST - this site is PARTIAL AT BEST

Measured 2026-08-26 at b45bfb54: crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_jetstream.rs holds
wiring_id only in the router-tap preview path (router_tap_subject / preview.wiring_id). That is a
tap SUBJECT, not an effect-span identity, and it carries no node_id.

THE FIRST TASK IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN EDIT: determine whether the publish path can reach an
invocation binding at all. If it cannot, this bead needs the same guest-to-host run-context contract
as wamn-0h0g.24.14 (filed as wamn-0h0g.7.9) - in which case say so, add the dependency, and stop
rather than inventing a second identity route.

## Precedent to follow

wamn-0h0g.24.12's connection_http site reads its identity back from the ConnectionInvocation the
router driver binds per invocation. Check whether an equivalent binding is reachable here before
concluding anything.
acceptance_criteria: Either the JetStream effect span carries wiring and node identity sourced from a real invocation binding with a mutant-checked named test, or the bead records the measured reason it cannot and takes a dependency on wamn-0h0g.7.9. A tap subject is not an acceptable identity source.
notes:
PATTERN ESTABLISHED BY wamn-0h0g.24.12 (landed 2026-08-26). FOLLOW IT; DO NOT RE-DERIVE.

The enrichment is NOT a widening of EffectIdentity. Every call site builds EffectIdentity with a
STRUCT LITERAL, so adding fields to it breaks every surface at once - including the ones that cannot
source the new values. That is the same coupling whose absence the refuted cheap-by-construction
premise assumed.

What landed instead, in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/effect_span.rs:
  - the macro DECLARES the wiring keys as tracing Empty fields
  - a separate pub(crate) struct EffectWiring and pub(crate) fn record_wiring(span, Option<..>) FILL
    them, called from the surface's own file-local span constructor
  - passing None records all four keys EMPTY, not absent, per the module's
    empty-string-means-no-claim convention

So declaring a field is one edit here; filling it is one edit per surface, and only a surface that
can SOURCE the claim fills it. Your surface adds a call to record_wiring in its own span constructor.

KNOWN ASYMMETRY, deliberate and documented at both sites: record_run is invoked BY the macro, while
record_wiring is invoked by the CALL SITE. Making record_wiring a macro argument would force
placeholder arguments onto surfaces that cannot compute them. Do not "fix" this asymmetry as drive-by
tidying; if it genuinely blocks your surface, say so rather than changing the macro's arity.

SPELLING IS FIXED: wamn.wiring_id, wamn.wiring_version, wamn.node_id, wamn.component_digest, exactly
as the wamn.component.invoke parent span spells them. Never a second vocabulary for the same
coordinates - a mutant renaming one key was measured to vanish silently, because tracing drops an
undeclared key without erroring.

title: chore(components): drop the unconsumed wamn-run-state workspace dep and its false in-tree assertion
description:
Two related findings about the same dead dependency, surfaced by lane w59-components while doing
wamn-0h0g.11.56 and deliberately not folded into that merge (owner ruling 2026-08-24: folding
buries findings in an unrelated commit).

FINDING 1 - A DECLARED WORKSPACE DEPENDENCY NO MEMBER CONSUMES.
components/Cargo.toml:27 declares wamn-run-state in [workspace.dependencies]. No component member
consumes it. Confirmed by its absence from components/Cargo.lock at base c2d805e0 AND at the lane
HEAD, so this is not something the workspace split introduced.

FINDING 2 - A COMMENT THAT ASSERTS THE OPPOSITE, AND IS ALSO LINE-STALE.
crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs:65 states that wamn-run-state ships INSIDE the
guest components and cites components/Cargo.toml:25. Both halves are wrong: nothing ships it into
a guest, and the declaration is at line 27, not 25.

WHY THIS IS THE FALSE-COVERAGE SHAPE, NOT MERE UNTIDINESS: the dangerous citation is the ADJACENT
one. A reader checking whether the guests carry run-state finds a confident in-tree assertion that
they do, with a line number, and stops looking. The line number being stale is what makes it
legible as drift rather than as fact.

SCOPE: drop the unused declaration, and correct or delete the assertion at run_state_live.rs:65.
Verify no member gains it before dropping. Prefer deleting the sentence over repairing its line
number if nothing depends on the claim.
acceptance_criteria: components/Cargo.toml no longer declares wamn-run-state, components/Cargo.lock is unchanged by the removal (it never carried it), and run_state_live.rs no longer asserts that guests ship it. Component builds unaffected.
notes: Found by lane w59-components during wamn-0h0g.11.56 and kept out of that commit on owner ruling. Pre-existing at c2d805e0 - not introduced by the workspace split.

title: chore(deps): refresh the remaining 133 semver-compatible dependency versions
description:
Refresh the semver-compatible dependency set. Cargo.lock only, no manifest change.

SECURITY - THIS IS WHY IT IS NOT ROUTINE HYGIENE.
RUSTSEC-2026-0258, h2 unbounded empty DATA frames, published 2026-08-17. The lockfile carries
h2 0.4.15; the fix is >= 0.4.16 and a plain cargo update takes it to 0.4.19. It is purely
transitive - no manifest edit - and reaches us through
  hyper -> hyper-rustls -> reqwest -> oci-client -> oci-wasm -> wash-runtime
i.e. the OCI pull and push path used by host, executor and ctl. cargo audit at c2d805e0 reports
exactly this one vulnerability across 538 crate dependencies.

SCOPE, MEASURED 2026-08-24 at c2d805e0 with cargo update --dry-run: 134 packages move within
semver. Notables: tokio 1.52.3 to 1.53.1, hyper 1.10.1 to 1.11.0, rustls 0.23.41 to 0.23.43,
serde 1.0.228 to 1.0.229, thiserror 2.0.18 to 2.0.20, uuid 1.23.4 to 1.25.0, and the wasmtime
family 47.0.3 to 47.0.4, which is a PATCH inside the pinned major and therefore in scope.

*** OUT OF SCOPE AND NOT NEGOTIABLE: ANYTHING GOVERNED BY WASMCLOUD UPSTREAM. ***
Verified 2026-08-24 against upstream wasmCloud/wasmCloud main, not merely against the fork:
upstream ITSELF specifies async-nats 0.49.1 and the whole wasmtime family at 47.0.3, and the fork
at daba602 does not diverge from upstream on any dependency version - the only workspace-manifest
difference is three entries added to the cargo-machete ignored list. async-nats 0.50.0 and
wasmtime-wasi / wasmtime-wasi-http 48.0.1 do exist, but taking either would diverge from upstream
on the exact dependency whose shared type universe
tests/conformance/tests/wasmtime_source_identity.rs exists to guarantee - that guard pins
WASMTIME_VERSION 47.0.3 and ASYNC_NATS_VERSION 0.49.1 as literals. These move at upstream pace,
never ours.

ALSO OUT OF SCOPE, recorded here so they are not lost rather than to schedule them: the remaining
semver-incompatible direct deps are schemars 0.8 to 1.2.2; opentelemetry, opentelemetry-otlp and
opentelemetry_sdk 0.31 to 0.32 with tracing-opentelemetry 0.32 to 0.33 as one set; jmespath 0.3 to
0.5; wasm-encoder 0.251 to 0.258; and syn 2 to 3 transitively. Each is its own decision and earns
its own bead if and when it is wanted.

The broader hygiene umbrella already exists and is deferred pre-MVP: wamn-4tob.3.1, AUDIT-CQ1
workspace quality gates and dependency hygiene.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo.lock is the only file changed. cargo audit reports zero vulnerabilities. Full workspace sweep re-measured at the tip and compared against the attributed 31-red baseline in exe-branch-baseline-red, with no new failures. No manifest edited. Nothing upstream-governed moved - async-nats stays 0.49.1 and the wasmtime family stays on the 47 line.
notes:
Land separately from the toolchain bump, with a sweep between, or a breakage cannot be attributed to one or the other. The h2 fix alone is cargo update -p h2 and can land first as its own commit if the advisory should close ahead of the bulk refresh.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: NOT HIGH PRIORITY. Scope-reduction work on this branch comes first. Repriced from the as-filed priority to P3 and held. Neither of these is on the usable-loop path and neither is required by the RC, so they sit behind the scope-reduction and exe-model set. Do not pull either into a wave ahead of that work. The h2 advisory in wamn-ufjr is a one-command lockfile move if it ever needs to jump the queue on its own.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: SPLIT EXECUTED. The h2 advisory is now wamn-lh3c at P1 - fix(deps): close RUSTSEC-2026-0258 by moving h2 off 0.4.15 - on the two-token security fix rule: one cargo update -p h2 closing a live RUSTSEC beats parking it inside 134 packages. THIS BEAD RETAINS THE OTHER 133 SEMVER-COMPATIBLE MOVES AND STAYS AT P3 behind the scope-reduction set. Its acceptance no longer includes closing the advisory; cargo audit should already be clean by the time this runs, and if it is not, that is a NEW advisory and not this one.
close_reason:
Landed at d569d461 with wamn-2jr4, one commit at owner direction. Cargo.lock ONLY - Cargo.toml is NOT touched, as the bead required.

*** THE SECURITY PREMISE WAS ALREADY SATISFIED BEFORE THIS RAN, AND THAT IS A PREMISE CORRECTION. *** This bead exists for RUSTSEC-2026-0258 (h2 unbounded empty DATA frames) and cites the lockfile carrying h2 0.4.15. Measured at claim: the lockfile ALREADY carried h2 0.4.19 - wamn-lh3c took that advisory in wave 66. So this was routine hygiene, not an advisory fix, and nothing here closed a live vulnerability.

UPSTREAM-GOVERNED VERSIONS HELD, VERIFIED AFTER THE UPDATE RATHER THAN TRUSTED: async-nats stayed at 0.49.1, and cargo correctly declined wasmtime-wasi and wasmtime-wasi-http 48.0.1 as semver-incompatible while taking the in-scope 47.0.3 to 47.0.4 PATCH inside the pinned major. The out-of-scope list on this bead is intact.

*** THE PATCH EXPOSED A REAL GUARD DEFECT, FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT BECAUSE THIS CHANGE CAUSED IT. *** tests/conformance/tests/wasmtime_source_identity.rs used ONE constant, WASMTIME_VERSION, for TWO different facts: the version the lockfile RESOLVES to, and the caret requirement string the workspace manifest DECLARES. Those were equal until 47.0.4 and a patch release pulls them apart. Split into WASMTIME_RESOLVED (47.0.4) and WASMTIME_REQUIREMENT (47.0.3), so the manifest requirement stays where upstream owns it while the resolved check tracks the lock.

OPERATIONAL NOTE FOR THE NEXT REFRESH: cargo metadata --offline resolves the WHOLE graph including android and windows targets, so once this refresh added the windows-sys 0.60.2 family the conformance guard died with attempting to make an HTTP request, but --offline was specified. NOT a lockfile defect - the fix is one cargo fetch.

GATE: 1449 passed, 16 FAILED, 34 ignored, zero compile errors; failing NAME SET byte-identical to the pre-refresh baseline.

title: chore(toolchain): bump the pinned Rust line from 1.97.0 to current stable 1.98.0
description:
Move the pinned Rust line from 1.97.0 to current stable 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae, 2026-08-18).

TWO PINS, ONE COMMIT. They are coupled and the coupling is easy to miss.
  rust-toolchain.toml:3   channel = "1.97.0"
  Dockerfile:16           FROM rust:1.97-trixie AS chef
Dockerfile:88 records that rust-toolchain.toml is DELIBERATELY not copied into the image, because
the base image already ships the pinned line and copying it would force a rustup download. The
image Rust line therefore comes ONLY from the FROM tag. Bump one without the other and local
builds and the in-cluster gate of record silently run different compilers.

MEASURED 2026-08-24 at c2d805e0.
- 1.98.0 is already installed locally as the stable toolchain, so no download is needed.
- The workspace declares NO rust-version anywhere. The only floor is upstream wasmCloud
  rust-version 1.94.0, which 1.98 clears comfortably.
- WE ARE ALREADY AHEAD OF UPSTREAM, NOT BEHIND. Upstream wasmCloud/wasmCloud main pins channel
  1.96.0, and the fork at daba602 is byte-identical to upstream on that file. This bump widens an
  existing deliberate gap rather than catching up, so the justification has to be ours.

CLIPPY IS THE ACTUAL WORK, NOT THE VERSION EDIT. Upstream states the rule in its own pin comment:
pin an explicit stable so clippy is deterministic, because a floating stable turns CI red whenever
a new toolchain ships new lints, and bump it in a dedicated change alongside the lint fixes the new
toolchain requires. Clippy is NOT part of the workspace sweep here and requires --keep-going.

COST. A toolchain change invalidates the entire target dir - 538 crate dependencies - and
.cargo/config.toml currently sets jobs = 4, so the rebuild is long and serialized. Budget for it.
acceptance_criteria: Both pins move in ONE commit. cargo check --workspace --all-targets is clean. clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going is triaged and any fixes land in the same commit. Gate-of-record counts re-measured at the tip and compared against the attributed baseline in exe-branch-baseline-red, with no new failures and no unrelated red driven green.
notes:
Land separately from the semver dependency refresh, with a sweep between, or a breakage cannot be attributed to one or the other. Nothing here touches any upstream-governed version.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: NOT HIGH PRIORITY. Scope-reduction work on this branch comes first. Repriced from the as-filed priority to P3 and held. Neither of these is on the usable-loop path and neither is required by the RC, so they sit behind the scope-reduction and exe-model set. Do not pull either into a wave ahead of that work. The h2 advisory in wamn-ufjr is a one-command lockfile move if it ever needs to jump the queue on its own.
close_reason:
Landed at d569d461, together with wamn-ufjr in ONE commit at owner direction (both beads' land-separately note was overridden; the trade is attribution, the saving is a second cold rebuild of 538 crates at jobs=4).

BOTH PINS MOVED IN LOCKSTEP as the bead required: rust-toolchain.toml:3 channel 1.97.0 to 1.98.0, and Dockerfile:16 FROM rust:1.97-trixie to rust:1.98-trixie. Dockerfile:88 documents that rust-toolchain.toml is deliberately NOT copied into the image, so the image Rust line comes ONLY from the FROM tag - bumping one without the other silently runs different compilers locally and in-cluster. 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae) was already installed as stable, as the bead measured.

*** CLIPPY WAS THE REAL WORK AND IT CAME TO ONE LINE - ESTABLISHED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ASSUMPTION. *** Rather than guess which of the 47 warnings the new toolchain introduced, clippy --workspace --all-targets --keep-going was run on BOTH toolchains with the dependency set HELD CONSTANT and the warning sets diffed: 1.97 gives 28 lint warnings, 1.98 gives 29. THE SINGLE ADDITION is an unused clap Parser import in a cfg(test) module at services/scenario-worker/src/main.rs:51. Removed and verified compiling. The other 28 are pre-existing on 1.97 and deliberately untouched - a toolchain bump must not drive unrelated warnings green.

ACCEPTANCE MET: cargo check --workspace --all-targets is CLEAN on 1.98 (exit 0, zero errors). Gate of record re-measured at the tip: 1449 passed, 16 FAILED, 34 ignored, zero compile errors, and the failing NAME SET is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-bump baseline. Zero regressions, nothing unrelated driven green.

title: chore(registry): nothing prunes published release-manifest and component artifacts
description: Successor to the wamn-0h0g.15.44 refutation of 2026-08-24. The original bead assumed an accumulating release-manifest-<digest> ConfigMap; measurement showed nothing creates that object, so the concern migrated to the carrier that IS written. Every wamn-ctl push-release-manifest writes an immutable digest-addressed artifact into wamn/releases and nothing prunes it. Bounded, not urgent: the registry PVC is 2Gi and MAX_SERVING_MANIFEST_BYTES is 1 MiB, so manifests alone need roughly 2000 releases to matter and component artifacts dominate. Note registry GC is not automatic - it needs REGISTRY_STORAGE_DELETE_ENABLED plus explicit manifest deletion before registry garbage-collect reclaims anything.
acceptance_criteria: A stated retention rule for published artifacts and a mechanism that enforces it, or an explicit ruling that unbounded growth is accepted at MVP scale with the tripwire named.

title: test(runtime): prove the ack path actually exports the JetStream ack-lag series
description:
Filed at wamn-0h0g.24.8's close (wave 56, 2026-08-24) as the honest residue of its proof.

WHAT .24.8 PROVED: the lag arithmetic, the clock-skew clamp, the label vector on both the registration-bound and the plain-bind paths, and - by a source assertion over the sliced ack body - that the recording call is written at the production call site. Five mutants, five kills, including the call-site deletion.

WHAT IT COULD NOT PROVE: that the call FIRES and the series reaches an exporter. There is no in-process fake for async_nats jetstream Message. HostJsMessage ack needs a real delivered message in the resource table, and both ack-exercising tests in wamn_jetstream.rs are WAMN_EVT_NATS_URL-gated and silently return when it is unset. So the strongest available in-crate guard is a source scan, and it is honestly labelled as one in its own doc comment.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY PEDANTIC: a source assertion cannot notice a call that is present but unreachable, guarded, or recording into a histogram whose provider was never installed. It also cannot notice the reverse - the metric silently ceasing to arrive.

CONTEXT THAT RAISES THE PRICE, measured 2026-08-24: metricbench HAS BEEN DELETED. It survives only as stale comments in deploy/infra/otel-collector.yaml, deploy/infra/otelcol-local.yaml and tests/integration/src/dashproof.rs. THE REPOSITORY CURRENTLY HAS NO METRIC-EXPORT PROOF AT ALL - wamn.run_queue.depth is equally unproven in-tree. So this bead is really asking for the first one back, and whoever takes it should decide whether to rebuild a shared metric-export harness rather than a one-off.

NATURAL HOMES: the existing WAMN_EVT_NATS_URL-gated ack tests in wamn_jetstream.rs, or a rebuilt metric-export gate under tests/integration. deploy/infra/otelcol-local.yaml and prometheus-local.yaml are documented docker configs, so this does NOT need the frozen kind cluster.

*** IF IT LANDS AS AN ENV-GATED TEST, IT MUST BE THE LOUD-FAIL SHAPE, NOT SELF-SKIP. *** Wave 56 measured a gate (services/dispatcher/tests/read_authority.rs) that self-skips silently on a missing URL, reports 1 passed, and had almost certainly never executed. wamn-0h0g.15.137 owns that principle.
acceptance_criteria: A run against a real NATS JetStream shows wamn.jetstream.ack_lag_ms arriving at a collector with the expected label set, for both the registration-bound and plain-bind paths. If the test is env-gated, an explicitly missing or malformed URL FAILS LOUDLY rather than skipping, so an ordinary sweep can never report it green without executing it.
notes:
REOPENED 2026-08-26 BY OWNER RULING - the rule-7 carve-out. This was merged into wamn-0h0g.24.12 on 2026-08-24 to keep the observability residue as one bead; that merge is undone because the two halves are different animals.

wamn-0h0g.24.12 is a pure in-tree enrichment: one edit to the shared macro_rules field block in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/effect_span.rs, provable by a mutant against a named test. THIS bead needs a live NATS server, has no in-process fake (HostJsMessage ack needs a real delivered message in the resource table), and both ack-exercising tests in wamn_jetstream.rs are WAMN_EVT_NATS_URL-gated. Carrying them as one bead would have made a cheap lane wait on infrastructure.

SEQUENCED BEHIND .24.12 by a dependency edge, not merely by preference.

STANDING CONSTRAINT, carried back from the merged text: IF THIS LANDS ENV-GATED IT MUST BE LOUD-FAIL, NOT SELF-SKIP. A self-skipping gate reports PASS and proves nothing. Note also that metricbench is DELETED, so the repository currently has NO metric-export proof at all; wamn.run_queue.depth is equally unproven.
GRAPH DEFECT INTRODUCED BY THE 2026-08-26 RULE-7 SPLIT - MARKED, NOT SILENTLY REWIRED.

This bead depends on wamn-0h0g.24.12. That edge was created on 2026-08-24 when the ack-lag proof was
carved back OUT of .24.12, so it encoded WHO OWNED THE EDIT, not what must be true first.

.24.12 has since been narrowed by owner ruling to the connection_http site ONLY. It no longer touches
wamn_jetstream.rs at all. The JetStream enrichment is now wamn-0h0g.24.15.

So the edge as it stands blocks a JetStream metric-export proof behind an unrelated connection_http
span change. Two candidate corrections, NOT taken here because this is the owner's call:
  (a) repoint the edge to wamn-0h0g.24.15 - both touch wamn_jetstream.rs, so there is a real
      edit-ordering reason, though it is FILE COLLISION rather than a hard blocker
  (b) drop the edge entirely - this bead proves a metric reaches an exporter, which does not depend
      on span identity in any direction; bd deps are documented to encode HARD blockers only, with
      soft sequencing riding phase labels and priority

Nothing about this bead's own scope changes either way.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-26: OPTION (b) - EDGE DROPPED, not repointed. Applied.

This bead proves a metric reaches an exporter; that does not depend on span identity in any
direction, so there was no hard blocker to encode. bd deps carry HARD blockers only - the
wamn_jetstream.rs file overlap with wamn-0h0g.24.15 is soft sequencing and rides phase label and
priority, not an edge.

This bead is now unblocked and independently schedulable. Its scope is unchanged, and the
loud-fail-not-self-skip requirement above still governs if it lands env-gated.

title: decide(hygiene): three preserved branches hold commits that exist nowhere else
description: Branch cleanup on 2026-08-23 took the repo from 96 local branches to 9. Eighty-seven were verified safe and deleted: each was either patch-id equivalent to landed work (git cherry against deploy-simplification) or every one of its unique commits had an exact subject match in the landed history of deploy-simplification, main or mvp. THREE WERE HELD BACK because their work is NOT present anywhere: agent/cf-attempts-54 carries 608289ad fix(runner) distinguish unsent attempts (wamn-5wd1.54); agent/cf-flow-34 carries 66559cfd feat replace triggers with typed entry nodes (wamn-5wd1.34); codex/wamn-8zht-13 carries 2d35522c test(execution) guard deadline rearming (wamn-8zht.13). All three from 2026-07-27 to 07-29. ALL THREE BEADS AND BOTH PARENT EPICS ARE CLOSED, so the program considered the work done - but the content is absent from the tree today: no rearm or re-arm anywhere in crates/execution/host/src, no unsent anywhere in crates or deploy, and docs/flow-schema.schema.json is gone with the flow language. So either the work never landed and the beads closed anyway, or it landed and the scope reduction later deleted it. I could not establish which, and these branches are the ONLY COPY, so deleting them would be irreversible.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling: keep the three branches as an archive, or confirm the work is superseded and delete them. If kept, say what would make them droppable.
