title: chore(components): components/Cargo.toml cannot control feature selection for root-workspace path deps
description: A structural blind spot found while testing an alloc-only serde_json fix for wamn-1yj4. Four crates that enter the components wasm32-wasip2 graph - wamn-event-reg, wamn-event-wire, wamn-materializer, wamn-schema-model - each declare serde_json = workspace true. Because they are PATH DEPENDENCIES BELONGING TO THE ROOT WORKSPACE, that resolves against /Cargo.toml:75, serde_json = 1 with default features, and NOT against components/Cargo.toml:15. So any feature policy expressed in the components workspace silently fails to apply to them. Combined with the fact that Cargo feature unification is ADDITIVE-ONLY, this means the components workspace cannot narrow a feature that any root-workspace crate widens. This is not itself a bug today - it is the reason a plausible one-line fix for wamn-1yj4 failed, and it will be the reason the next such attempt fails too. Worth recording so it is not rediscovered a third time.
acceptance_criteria: Either a comment at components/Cargo.toml naming the limitation, or a documented rule that components-side feature policy applies only to crates declared inside that workspace.
notes: Discovered 2026-08-23 during wave-54 integration while testing option 3 of wamn-1yj4. Note the three EXTERNAL crates in the same graph - boon 0.6.1, jmespath 0.3.0, schemars 0.8.22 - expose no feature knob at all, so they are fatal to any narrowing attempt regardless of which workspace declares what.

title: [SR-MVP] test(conformance): reject closed Beads used as live documentation owners
description: wamn-0h0g.12.160 began from a manual inventory of thirteen citations to the split-closed wamn-0h0g.15.22. Five were repaired by an earlier overlapping bead; one survivor was already a valid historical no-subject record. A structural repository scan then found an additional stale SQL-comment owner citation outside the original documentation inventory. No check distinguishes an active ownership assertion from a valid dated historical citation, so every umbrella split can silently orphan documentation. Design an explicit governed live-owner citation form and a CI-stable status source. Do not treat every Bead-like token as live: closed findings, precedents, and archaeology must remain legal and mechanically distinguishable. The check must not depend on network access or an ambient Dolt server.
design:
Governed documentation uses two explicit machine-readable forms: live-owner:<bead-id> for a claim that an issue currently owns unfinished work, and historical-cite:<bead-id> for provenance, precedent, or dated archaeology. Bare Bead-like tokens do not satisfy a live-ownership assertion.

Offline authority is a small checked-in generated status and successor manifest under architecture/. It contains only schema version plus the referenced issue id, status, and explicit successor relation needed by the guard. It contains no descriptions, comments, interaction history, timestamps, or full issue export. A deterministic generator reads Beads when maintainers refresh the artifact; the conformance test reads only the checked-in manifest and never invokes bd, Dolt, or the network.

A closed live-owner is valid only when its manifest successor chain terminates at an existing non-closed owner. Historical citations remain valid regardless of later closure because they assert provenance, not current ownership.
acceptance_criteria:
The active plan, build-and-test recipes, plane amendment, and explicitly enumerated executable-artifact comments use live-owner:<bead-id> for current ownership and historical-cite:<bead-id> for provenance. Unknown live owners fail. Closed live owners fail unless the generated manifest carries an explicit successor chain ending at a non-closed owner. Historical citations to closed issues remain legal and are never interpreted as live claims.

A small deterministic checked-in status and successor manifest is generated from Beads and is the sole offline CI authority. It is not a full issue export or second task database. The conformance gate runs without bd, Dolt, an ambient server, or network access. Named mutants for a closed live owner, unknown live owner, broken successor chain, and stale manifest entry fail; dated historical citations pass. The repository finishes with zero false live-owner claims.
notes:
OWNER RULING RECORDED 2026-08-20 — EXPLICIT CITATION CLASSES PLUS GENERATED OFFLINE MANIFEST; IMPLEMENTATION PLAN NOT STARTED.

Historical citations remain permanently valid as provenance. Only live ownership claims are status-sensitive. The implementation uses explicit live-owner and historical-cite syntax and a small generated status/successor manifest; a full tracked Beads export is rejected because it would be a second database that drifts.

No conformance source, documentation, SQL comment, architecture manifest, generator, or test edit begins in this decision-recording turn.

title: [SR-MVP] docs(gates): rie2ebench documents a subcommand that does not exist, and its gate body is unreachable
description:
## Why

tests/integration/src/rie2ebench.rs line 1 module doc says: The rie2ebench subcommand ...

*** THAT IS FALSE. *** MEASURED 2026-08-19 at 53afb31a: there is NO Rie2ebench subcommand in tests/orchestrator/src/main.rs. rie2ebench::run is reachable from NOTHING. Roughly 470 lines of live gate body cannot be invoked, and the two unit tests in its #[cfg(test)] module are the ENTIRE enforceable proof of gate EVT-RI-E2E.

Compare runnerbench in the same crate, which IS wired: tests/orchestrator/src/main.rs:14, :38, :77.

## The nuance that decides how to fix it

*** THE ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE AND DOCUMENTED, SO THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A MISSING WIRING. ***
docs/archive/build-and-test.md:1624 records: Integration-proof boundary: rie2ebench fixtures are owned by the integration library rather than the command router.

So the boundary is intentional. What is NOT intentional is a module doc asserting a subcommand exists, and a large live-infra body retained with no way to run it. The defect is the MISMATCH, not the boundary.

## Scope, and the question inside it

Correct the module doc to describe what this module actually is. Then rule the larger question, which is the real content: if the gate body is unreachable by design, is retaining ~470 lines of live-infra code correct, or should the body be retired and the two unit tests kept as the proof of record? EVT-RI-E2E currently rests entirely on those two unit tests either way -- that fact should be stated wherever the gate is registered, rather than left implied by an unreachable function.

## Related

wamn-0h0g.12.149 (flow_json on the lib target of this same file), wamn-0h0g.12.154 (this file prints that it seeded a flow it no longer seeds), wamn-0h0g.12.155 (the H5-RIE2EBENCH pin at build-and-test.md:1626 requires minimum 2 tests and exactly 2 exist -- so the pin is honest today, but it is pinning unit tests while its descriptor reads as though it pins a gate run).
acceptance_criteria: The module doc describes what the module is; the retention-or-retirement of the unreachable gate body is ruled and recorded; and what actually proves EVT-RI-E2E is stated where the gate is registered.
notes:

- The close reason must cite the gate-mutants deletion as precedent.

title: fix(run-state): two admission.rs doc comments describe a reconciler recovery path that does not exist
description:
FILED 2026-08-19 as the surviving residue of wamn-0h0g.15.174, whose central premise was
REFUTED by measurement. This bead is small and precise on purpose.

TWO DOC COMMENTS IN crates/execution/run-state/src/admission.rs ASSERT A PATH THAT DOES NOT
EXIST AND IS NOT NEEDED:
  admission.rs:103-110   "... and it is also how a crashed producer's control-side reconciler
                         recovers the run id it never recorded."
  admission.rs:1305-1306 repeats the same claim.

WHY IT IS FALSE, MEASURED:
- A reconciler does exist -- reconcile_test_report at
  services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs:341 -- but it NEVER queries by
  idempotency_key. It takes run ids as ALREADY-OBSERVED ARGUMENTS (:317-319: "project run
  identities the caller has ALREADY observed ... they were reserved under test_case_run_id").
- Grep for idempotency_key across ALL of services/scenario-worker/src/ returns ZERO hits.
- And no such recovery is needed: test_case_run_id
  (services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs:167-171) derives the run id as a
  PURE FUNCTION OF THE COORDINATE, sha256 over tenant, report, ordinal and case. A producer
  cannot "fail to record" an id it recomputes. Belt and braces, reserve_test_report commits the
  ordinal-to-run_id mapping into the CONTROL database via insert_test_case_run_sql (:92-108)
  BEFORE admission runs.

THIS IS THE FALSE-COVERAGE CLASS IN A DOC COMMENT: it plainly covers the topic while describing
a mechanism that is not there, which is the same shape as wamn-0h0g.12.145 (a DDL comment that
was an instruction) and R55 in the ledger.

*** WHY THE WAVE-9 LANE DID NOT JUST FIX IT, AND WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: CHOOSING THE
REPLACEMENT TEXT STATES A DESIGN CONCLUSION. *** The truthful replacement has to say what DOES
happen, and that commits to a position on the draft-run producer, which is unbuilt.

THE PROPOSED CORRECTION, zero behaviour change, no SQL change:
Replace the trailing clause at :103-110 (and the repeat at :1305-1306) with a statement that
the coordinate is recovered BY RE-DRIVING THIS STATEMENT, whose classifier answers duplicate
with the run id (identity-before-drift arm order, ruled in wamn-0h0g.15.160), and that no
separate lookup exists because the producer derives its run id from the coordinate.
The existing named test already covers the replacement claim:
  admission.rs:1389-1418 an_exact_management_retry_is_answered_before_the_world_is_rechecked.

*** THE ONE OPEN QUESTION THIS BEAD MUST NOT SILENTLY DECIDE: will the draft-run producer
derive its run id from command_id the way test_case_run_id derives from the coordinate? If YES,
recovery-by-producer-key is permanently unnecessary and the comment should say so flatly. If
NOT DECIDED, the comment must be written so it does not pre-empt the choice. Ask before writing
the final wording. ***

ACCEPTANCE: both comments state something true; the replacement does not assert a design
decision that has not been made; no SQL and no behaviour changes.

title: decision(catalog): release-membership divergence is refused in two vocabularies -- reunify the literal or keep them distinct
description:
FILED 2026-08-19 by wave-9 lane 1 while repairing wamn-0h0g.12.145. The lane deliberately did
NOT decide this; it wrote the measured facts into the DDL comment and raised the choice here.

THE MEASURED SITUATION. Release-membership divergence is refused at two tiers, and THE TWO
TIERS DO NOT SPEAK THE SAME WORD.
  DB tier   catalog.release_flows guarantees a divergent member is never STORED: the primary
            key (catalog-schema.sql:327) covers the member coordinate and leaves flow_version
            and execution_bundle_hash outside it, and the release_flows_immutable UPDATE
            trigger (:347-349) closes the mutate-in-place route.
            *** BUT THE REFUSAL IS SILENT. *** The sole production append,
            insert_release_flow_sql (crates/schema/control/src/sql.rs:176-182), carries
            ON CONFLICT (tenant_id, catalog_id, catalog_version, flow_id) DO NOTHING. Under
            that statement the PK does not raise -- it discards the divergent member and
            returns zero rows.
  APP tier   services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs:305-321 locks the existing member FOR SHARE
            via lock_release_member_sql (crates/control/provision/src/publish_release.rs:359-365)
            and calls verify_release_member (:500-522), repeating it on the concurrent-append
            arm at :337-365. It refuses with PublishReleaseErrorKind::ReleaseConflict --
            NOT with the catalog-release-content-conflict literal.

SO THE DIAGNOSABLE REFUSAL AND THE STRUCTURAL REFUSAL USE DIFFERENT VOCABULARY. A caller
handling one does not thereby handle the other.

WHY THIS IS NOT wamn-0h0g.12.145. That bead was a false comment claiming two DELETED ctl
preflights raised the SAME literal. The comment is now accurate: it names the real enforcement
and says plainly that ctl refuses as a release conflict rather than reusing the literal. The
remaining question is whether that divergence SHOULD persist, which is a design decision, not
a documentation defect.

*** NO SILENT-DROP GAP EXISTS IN PRODUCTION TODAY -- verified, so this is not urgent. *** The
lane checked every caller of insert_release_flow_sql: publish_release.rs:329 verifies before
and after; migrate_catalog.rs:742 is cfg(test) setup; catalog_live.rs:184 is a test. The
production copy-forward at migrate_catalog.rs:548-554 is a same-content SELECT-into-INSERT at
a fresh target version, so DO NOTHING there absorbs only an identical retry.

THE DECISION: leave the two vocabularies distinct (they describe genuinely different events --
"never stored" versus "you were refused"), or reunify them so one literal covers both tiers.
Leaving them distinct is defensible and is the status quo; the risk of reunifying is that the
DB tier cannot in fact raise under DO NOTHING, so "reunify" may really mean "change the append
to raise", which is a behaviour change with retry-convergence consequences.
NOT ACTED ON.
notes: OWNER RULING 2026-08-24: RIDES wamn-0h0g.11.49. NO SEPARATE WORK. The two vocabularies REUNIFY ON ReleaseConflict inside .11.49, which already owns insert-or-verify-identical typed-refusal convergence for BOTH the builder and raw-migration paths. Do NOT open a parallel reunification and do NOT lane this. RECORD-ONLY. This bead closes into .11.49 rather than being scheduled.

title: [SR-MVP] req(execution): per-flow concurrency has no owner after ThrottleTable and ConcurrencyGate retire
description:
FILED 2026-08-19 as the carried half of the wamn-0h0g.26.10 ruling. THIS BEAD EXISTS SO THAT
A DELETION IS NOT ALSO AN ERASURE OF INTENT.

wamn-0h0g.26.10 was ruled RETIRE-AND-CARRY: ConcurrencyGate and ThrottleTable are deleted
with wamn-0h0g.26.4, and the REQUIREMENT they represented is carried here rather than lost.

WHAT IS BEING RETIRED (measured 2026-08-19, zero consumers outside flow-engine):
  crates/execution/flow-engine/src/throttle.rs, 129 LOC.
  - ThrottleTable  : cross-run throttle keys. When a node returns rate-limited, all runs
                     sharing the throttle key back off together.
  - ConcurrencyGate: the per-flow in-flight cap plus claim-side backpressure.
Neither type is referenced anywhere outside throttle.rs, its pub use re-export at
flow-engine/src/lib.rs:71, a doc comment at lib.rs:47, and flow-engine's own tests
(tests/runner.rs:567, :587, :597). Nothing calls them, so the deletion breaks no live path.

*** WHY A SEPARATE BEAD AND NOT JUST wamn-ynwf. *** wamn-ynwf is titled "wire the cross-run
ThrottleTable (shared per-host throttle gate)" and is DEFERRED at P3. It covers the
CROSS-RUN THROTTLE HALF ONLY. PER-FLOW CONCURRENCY -- ConcurrencyGate's actual job -- has
no owner at all once the code is gone. wamn-0h0g.19.2 (bounded in-flight per route with 429
shedding) is adjacent but not the same thing: it bounds in-flight PER ROUTE at ingress, not
PER FLOW at claim time, and wamn-0h0g.16.7's close reason records that only the in_flight
counting shape was attached to .19.2, explicitly not per-flow concurrency.

THE REQUIREMENT, STATED SO A FUTURE IMPLEMENTER CAN PRICE IT:
  A flow must be able to declare a maximum number of concurrently executing runs, and the
  claim path must refuse to start run N+1 while N are in flight, applying backpressure at
  claim rather than failing the run.
The retired implementation was NOT production-grade and should not be treated as a design:
per the ledger (section H.2) it was an in-memory HashMap with no durable deadline, no
multi-replica authority and no restart recovery. In a multi-replica deployment the real
version needs durable authority, which is precisely why retiring the in-memory one costs
nothing.

*** THIS BEAD IS DELIBERATELY UNOWNED AND UNSCHEDULED. It is a requirement of record, not a
commitment. It exists so that the next person asking "did we ever have per-flow concurrency
control, and where did it go" gets an answer instead of an archaeology problem -- which is
exactly the failure mode wamn-0h0g.16.6 warned about and that .26.10 was filed to catch. ***

ORIGIN: wamn-0h0g.26.10 (the ruling). Deletion lands under wamn-0h0g.26.4.
Cross-run half: wamn-ynwf (deferred P3). Adjacent-but-distinct: wamn-0h0g.19.2.
notes: ORIGIN CITE (bidirectional, R28 pattern): this bead was filed by the wamn-0h0g.26.10 ruling of 2026-08-19. That bead carries the full ruling text and the measurement that made it decidable; wamn-0h0g.26.4 carries the note that the throttle.rs deletion is intentional. If this requirement is ever satisfied, superseded, or judged unnecessary, say so on .26.10 as well so the retirement record stays complete.

     |
9907 |         for (ddl, table) in [(RUN_STATE_SQL, "runs")] {
     = note: -D clippy::single-element-loop implied by -D warnings

So the tree is clippy-clean apart from this one site. That is a useful baseline to
hold, and it means any future clippy red is a regression rather than noise.

CAVEAT ON SCOPE: --workspace covers the ROOT workspace only. components/ is a
SEPARATE cargo workspace and is NOT covered by this baseline. A components-workspace
clippy baseline has still never been taken.

## Why this is not merely a lint

*** A SINGLE-ELEMENT LOOP IS A FINGERPRINT OF DELETION, AND THIS ONE IS. ***
Traced through history:

  e80ff0fd introduced it as:  for (ddl, table) in [(RUN_STATE_SQL, "runs"), (FLOWS_SQL, "flows")]
  e45ca35b removed the second element (chore(wamn-0h0g.12.102): delete the retired
           wamn_run.flows relation)

FLOWS_SQL now has ZERO references anywhere in the tree. So the loop is the residue of
a two-element sweep reduced to one.

*** THIS IS THE THIRD TRACE OF THE SAME DELETION. *** e45ca35b left:
 1. the LIVE test fixture broken -- run_plane_reconcile_live red at HEAD, which was
    wamn-0h0g.20.16, fixed in wave 8;
 2. the UNIT test fixture, which that commit DID update (add_legacy_flow_registry in
    run_plane.rs, with a doc comment explaining why the fixture must inject the table);
 3. this loop, reduced to one element and visible ONLY to clippy -- which nothing runs.
Three traces, one deletion, and only the middle one was handled at the time.

## The disposition question, and it is real

Do NOT reflexively collapse the loop to a straight-line assertion. Decide first:

 (a) COLLAPSE IT. If wamn_run.flows is retired for good and no second (ddl, table)
     pair will ever return, the loop is dead scaffolding and should become a plain
     assertion over RUN_STATE_SQL. Simplest and probably right.
 (b) REPOPULATE IT. If other run-plane DDL records deserve the same rewrite_schema
     assertion and were simply never added, the loop is under-populated rather than
     over-built, and the fix is to add them. Check what RUN_PLANE_FILES contains now
     versus what this test covers -- the test asserts rewrite_schema rewrites the
     schema header, and there is no obvious reason that should be proven for only one
     record.

(b) is the possibility worth actually checking, because it would mean this test QUIETLY
LOST COVERAGE in e45ca35b rather than merely gaining a lint. Establish which before
writing code.

## Acceptance

The loop is either collapsed or repopulated, with the choice justified against what the
run-plane DDL set actually contains; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-deps
-- -D warnings exits 0; and the wave sweep is unchanged at 3 known reds.

Decisive evidence: the loop's membership criterion was never 'run-plane record files' but 'record files production rewrites WHOLE-FILE through rewrite_schema', and exactly ONE such call site remains tree-wide (publish_catalog.rs:693). e45ca35b deleted ensure_flow_registry and its loop element together. run-state.sql is also the ONLY record file that HAS a schema header, so adding AUTHORING_TESTS_SQL or RUN_QUEUE_SQL would make assertion 3 vacuous and assertion 2 tautological. Lane enumerated all 16 DDL constants in the module; none other belongs. Behaviour is byte-identical for the runs case. Four mutants, each killed by the named test schema_rewrite_is_dot_anchored on three distinct assertion lines; the integrator independently re-derived one of them, which fired at run_plane.rs:9913, proving the second collapsed assertion executes. *** THIS BEAD'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERION -- workspace clippy exits 0 -- WAS WRITTEN ON A FALSE PREMISE AND IS NOT REACHABLE WITHIN THIS BEAD. The one-error baseline was an artifact of cargo fail-fast masking; the true baseline was SEVEN errors across THREE packages. Six remain, independently re-verified by the integrator at six distinct sites. The cause is filed as wamn-0h0g.12.147, the remaining errors as wamn-0h0g.12.148 and wamn-0h0g.12.149, and the stale flows.sql doc references as wamn-0h0g.12.150; all four existed before this reason was written. FLOWS_SQL is NOT dead code -- the constant does not exist at all, e45ca35b deleted the declaration with all six references, so no bead was warranted.

title: decision(tests): live-role bootstraps -- tripwire, self-healing, or both
description:
RAISED 2026-08-19 by the wave-8 lane implementing wamn-0h0g.20.15. Reported rather
than done, because it changes behaviour rather than asserting it, and the lane was
explicitly instructed to report such calls.

## The choice

crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs bootstraps wamn_scenario_author,
wamn_effect_writer and wamn_run_projection_writer with IF NOT EXISTS ... CREATE ROLE
and NO ELSE ALTER branch. wamn_app, in the same block, DOES have an ELSE ALTER arm.

Because PostgreSQL roles are cluster-wide, a leftover role from an earlier suite keeps
whatever attributes it already had. wamn-0h0g.20.15 added a pg_roles assertion that
TURNS THAT INTO A LOUD FAILURE for two of the three roles.

The open question is whether the failure is the right response:

 (a) KEEP THE TRIPWIRE (status quo after .20.15). A dirty cluster reds the suite by
     name and the operator learns the cluster is dirty. Cost: a shared or reused
     cluster reds until someone drops the role by hand.

 (b) ADD THE ELSE ALTER ARM, making the bootstrap self-healing like wamn_app's. The
     suite then converges on any cluster. Cost: it SILENTLY REPAIRS the very condition
     the assertion exists to reveal, so a cluster that keeps acquiring bad roles never
     tells anyone. It also makes the assertion nearly unfalsifiable -- it would only
     catch a bug in the ALTER itself.

 (c) BOTH, ordered: ALTER to the intended attributes AND keep the assertion, so the
     suite converges but the assertion still guards the builder-drift contract that
     .20.15 actually cares about. This is probably what wamn_app should have too, but
     it is a real design call, not an obvious merge of (a) and (b).

## Why this is not obvious

.20.15's assertion is a DRIFT CONTRACT against the production builder
(ensure_effect_writer_acl_role_sql), not a cleanliness check. Under (b) and (c) the
contract still holds, because the ALTER would be written from the same attribute list.
Under (b) alone the DIRTY-CLUSTER signal is lost. Under (a) the drift contract and the
cleanliness check are welded together, and a dirty cluster is indistinguishable from a
genuine production-drift regression -- which is its own diagnostic cost, and is the
strongest argument for (c).

## Acceptance

A ruling names which of (a)/(b)/(c) applies, and whether wamn_app's existing ELSE ALTER
arm is consistent with it or is itself the odd one out. Any code change lands with the
ruling cited.

RELATED: the sibling bead on wamn_scenario_author being uncovered by the .20.15
assertion. Distinct question -- that one is about WHAT to assert, this one is about
what to DO when the assertion would fail. Do not merge them.
notes:
*** OWNER RULING 2026-08-19: OPTION (a), KEEP THE TRIPWIRE. ***

Chosen over (b) self-healing and (c) both. The owner's reasoning of record:
  "A live gate should FAIL on a dirty cluster rather than quietly repair it -- self-healing is
   exactly the mechanism that let a leftover healthy object satisfy an IF NOT EXISTS guard and
   mask a mutated builder (the M2 lesson already in force here)."

This ratifies the status quo established by wamn-0h0g.20.15 (dc7d35d6). NO CODE CHANGE IS
REQUIRED OR AUTHORIZED BY THIS RULING: run_state_live.rs already bootstraps
wamn_scenario_author, wamn_effect_writer and wamn_run_projection_writer with
IF NOT EXISTS CREATE ROLE and no ELSE ALTER branch, and .20.15's pg_roles assertion already
turns a leftover role into a loud, named failure.
The accepted cost is explicit and stands: a shared or reused cluster reds until someone drops
the role by hand. That is the intended behaviour, not a defect. The standing operating rule
already matches it -- POSTGRES ROLES ARE CLUSTER-WIDE, SO USE ONE FRESH CONTAINER PER SUITE.

*** ONE INCONSISTENCY THE RULING CREATES, RAISED AND NOT ACTED ON. *** wamn_app, in the SAME
bootstrap block, DOES carry an ELSE ALTER arm -- it is self-healing. Under a tripwire-only
ruling wamn_app is now the odd one out: three roles trip on a dirty cluster and the fourth
silently repairs itself. Option (c)'s own text anticipated this ("this is probably what
wamn_app should have too"), but the owner did not rule on wamn_app, and removing a self-healing
arm is a behaviour change that could red suites that currently pass.
SO IT IS RECORDED, NOT CHANGED. If the owner wants the block made uniform, that is a separate
authorization and should be its own bead.
close_reason: RULED 2026-08-19 by the owner: option (a), KEEP THE TRIPWIRE. A live gate should FAIL on a dirty cluster rather than quietly repair it; self-healing is the mechanism that lets a leftover healthy object satisfy an IF NOT EXISTS guard and mask a mutated builder. This ratifies the status quo from wamn-0h0g.20.15 (dc7d35d6), so NO CODE CHANGE was required or made. The accepted cost is explicit: a shared or reused cluster reds until the role is dropped by hand, which is intended behaviour and matches the standing rule that PostgreSQL roles are cluster-wide and each suite needs one fresh container. RAISED AND NOT ACTED ON: the ruling leaves wamn_app the odd one out, since it alone in that block carries a self-healing ELSE ALTER arm; making the block uniform would be a behaviour change and needs its own authorization.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(tests): run_state_live cannot take the production role builder -- run-state ships inside guest components
description:
SPLIT OUT OF wamn-0h0g.20.14 on 2026-08-19, at integration, because the leg is blocked by a structural constraint rather than by effort.

WHAT WAS ATTEMPTED: point crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs at wamn_control_provision::sql::ensure_effect_writer_acl_role_sql(), as the other two sites now do, by adding wamn-control-provision as a dev-dependency.

WHY IT CANNOT LAND AS WRITTEN:
  crates/execution/run-state ships INSIDE guest components -- components/Cargo.toml:25 declares it -- and components is a SEPARATE CARGO WORKSPACE.
  wamn-control-provision is not a member of that workspace and nothing there depends on it.
  tests/conformance/tests/workspace_tiers.rs computes each tier's PATH-DEPENDENCY CLOSURE at path_dependency_closure (around :386-414) and DOES NOT FILTER BY DEPENDENCY KIND -- it walks every dependency carrying a path, so a DEV-dependency counts exactly like a normal one.
  Result: workspace_tier_membership_matches_live_classification panics at :402 with 'selected package wamn-control-provision missing from cargo metadata'.
Isolated at integration by reverting this leg alone and re-running: 11 passed, 0 failed. With the leg, 10 passed, 1 failed.

THE OTHER TWO LEGS ARE UNAFFECTED AND LANDED at 0a9a9cd8. crates/platform/runtime and services/scenario-worker are not components-workspace dependencies, so their dev-dependency on wamn-control-provision creates no cross-workspace closure demand.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, and it is genuinely open:
  (a) Accept the divergence. run_state_live keeps its hand-rolled bootstrap and gains a comment saying WHY it cannot use the builder. Cheapest, honest, and leaves exactly one dialect behind rather than three.
  (b) Teach workspace_tiers to exclude dev-dependencies from the tier closure. Defensible -- a dev-dependency is not shipped -- but it WEAKENS A CONFORMANCE GUARD, and the guard may include dev-deps deliberately, since cargo test in a tier really does need them. Do not do this without deciding that question.
  (c) Move the two role-name constants somewhere both workspaces can see, so the builder is not needed for this leg at all. The names already come from wamn-run-state itself (EFFECT_WRITER_ROLE, RUN_PROJECTION_WRITER_ROLE), so what run_state_live actually lacks is the ATTRIBUTE SET, not the names.

NOTE ALSO: even setting the workspace problem aside, this leg introduces a DEV-DEPENDENCY CYCLE -- wamn-run-state (dev) depends on wamn-control-provision, which depends on wamn-run-state with the effect-writer-credential feature. Cargo permits it and it was measured building cleanly, but it is a graph change that deserves the same sign-off as the rest.
notes:
=====================================================================
OWNER RULING, 2026-08-19 (dkk). RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED.
=====================================================================

OPTION (a) RULED: ACCEPT THE DIVERGENCE, COMMENT IT, CLOSE AT P3.

Owner's reasoning on why the alternatives fell -- recorded because both were
defensible and the reasons are the durable part:

 (b) teach workspace_tiers to exclude dev-dependencies:
     "weakens a conformance guard to make one test prettier -- and the guard's
     dev-dep inclusion is plausibly load-bearing (a tier that runs cargo test
     genuinely needs its dev-deps), so the 'fix' is a semantics change to shared
     enforcement smuggled in as test hygiene -- plus it introduces a dev-
     dependency cycle REGARDLESS, meaning it pays the guard-weakening price and
     still doesn't arrive clean."

 (c) move the attribute set to a shared home:
     "the correct shape for a problem this size doesn't have: a new cross-
     workspace home crate for one attribute set consumed by one live test is
     infrastructure minted for a single reader -- the reimplementation-audit
     reflex in miniature ('could share' is not 'must share')."

With the other two legs landed at 0a9a9cd8, the residue is ONE DIALECT IN ONE
TEST, and "one hand-rolled bootstrap with an honest comment is cheaper than any
machinery that unifies it."

=====================================================================
RIDERS -- "acceptance without teeth is how divergence rots" (owner)
=====================================================================
NOT STARTED. All three are the implementing work, listed here so it is scoped.

R1. THE COMMENT MUST BE LOAD-BEARING, NOT APOLOGETIC. It must:
    - name the structural cause: run-state ships inside the guest workspace;
      workspace_tiers computes path closures KIND-BLIND, so the builder crate is
      unreachable from here without breaking the tier guard;
    - cite wamn-0h0g.20.15 and this ruling;
    - state the DRIFT CONTRACT: the bootstrap mirrors EFFECT_WRITER_ROLE and
      RUN_PROJECTION_WRITER_ROLE attribute-for-attribute, and ANY CHANGE TO THE
      PRODUCTION ATTRIBUTE SET UPDATES THIS BLOCK IN THE SAME COMMIT.
    Owner: "that sentence is what turns an accepted divergence into a maintained
    mirror."

R2. IF CHEAP, VERIFY THE MIRROR AT RUNTIME. If the live suite can cheaply assert
    equivalence -- query pg_roles for the built roles' attributes and compare to
    the hand-rolled set -- add that ONE assertion. Owner: "then the mirror is
    VERIFIED each run and the acceptance costs nothing forever."
    Judgment call left to the implementer on "cheaply"; if it is not cheap, say
    so rather than building machinery for it.

R3. REOPEN TRIGGER, RECORDED HERE ON PURPOSE: a SECOND CONSUMER needing the
    attribute set is the moment option (c)'s home crate earns existence. Until
    then: one dialect, documented, guarded.

=====================================================================
Priority stays P3. This bead closes when R1 lands (and R2 if it proves cheap).
=====================================================================

WAVE-8 MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-19 -- TWO FACTS THAT CHANGE THE RIDERS.

FACT 1: THE MIRROR IS EXACT TODAY. Verified attribute-for-attribute. crates/execution/run-state/tests/run_state_live.rs creates wamn_effect_writer (:73-75) and wamn_run_projection_writer (:77-80) with NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS. crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs:288-301 ensure_effect_writer_acl_role_sql emits CREATE ROLE %I NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS. IDENTICAL. The drift contract R1 asks for is therefore TRUE at the moment it is written, which is what makes it worth writing.

FACT 2: RIDER R2 IS NOT TAUTOLOGICAL AND IT HAS REAL TEETH -- BUT NOT FOR THE REASON THE RIDER GIVES. It cannot compare built-vs-hand-rolled, because the builder crate is exactly what this test cannot reach. What it CAN do is assert the roles carry the expected attributes in pg_roles, and that catches a live hazard: all three NOLOGIN roles use IF NOT EXISTS ... CREATE with NO ELSE ALTER branch, unlike wamn_app at :64-68 which DOES have one. PostgreSQL roles are CLUSTER-WIDE, so a leftover wamn_effect_writer from an earlier suite carrying SUPERUSER or BYPASSRLS is SILENTLY KEPT and the proof runs against a role that bypasses the very policies it is proving. That is precisely the hazard this file's own comment at :57-59 names against wamn-0h0g.15.23, defended for wamn_app and NOT for the other three.

RECOMMENDED SHAPE for R2, cheap and with teeth: after the bootstrap, assert rolsuper, rolbypassrls, rolcanlogin, rolinherit, rolcreatedb, rolcreaterole and rolreplication are all false for wamn_effect_writer and wamn_run_projection_writer. Alternatively give the three roles the same ELSE ALTER treatment wamn_app already gets -- but that CHANGES BEHAVIOUR rather than asserting it, so it is a separate call and should be raised, not assumed.
close_reason:
Landed dc7d35d6 on deploy-simplification. Owner ruling implemented as ruled: option (a), accept the divergence, comment it, close at P3.

PART 1, the drift contract: a load-bearing comment naming the structural cause (run-state ships inside the guest components workspace at components/Cargo.toml:25; workspace_tiers computes path closures KIND-BLIND on dependency.path alone, so a dev-dependency counts like a real one), citing this bead and the ruling, stating the mirror explicitly, and recording the reopen trigger. The sentence the owner asked for is in the code verbatim in substance: ANY CHANGE TO THAT PRODUCTION ATTRIBUTE SET UPDATES THIS BLOCK IN THE SAME COMMIT.

PART 2 proved CHEAP and it landed: a pg_roles assertion that both writer roles carry exactly NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOINHERIT NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS. Written as a conforming-role ROLL-UP rather than seven separate asserts, deliberately -- a MISSING role drops the count, so it cannot pass vacuously.

*** THREE PREMISE CORRECTIONS FROM THE LANE, AND THE FIRST ONE IS AGAINST MY OWN STATED REASONING. ***
 (a) I claimed a leftover BYPASSRLS role would mean the proof runs against a role that bypasses the policies it proves. THAT IS FALSE FOR THIS FILE. run_state_live only ever SET LOCAL ROLE wamn_app, at exactly two sites; the three NOLOGIN roles exist solely so the DDL GRANT/REVOKE targets resolve, and no assertion here executes as them. The assertion is still worth having, for two DIFFERENT reasons now written into the code: it is the drift contract's own tripwire, and it catches a dirty cluster before that role is handed to the NEXT suite -- crates/platform/runtime claims.rs and effect_writer_live.rs DO exercise those roles' ACLs. My conclusion survived; my reasoning did not.
 (b) The mirror is NARROWER than the brief assumed. EFFECT_WRITER_ROLE and RUN_PROJECTION_WRITER_ROLE are defined in run-state itself (src/effect_writer_credential.rs) and crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs:14 imports them FROM here -- the dependency arrow runs run-state <- provision. So the role NAMES never had a drift surface; only the ATTRIBUTE SET does. Folded into the comment, and it sharpens the reopen trigger: a shared home crate would only ever need to host the attribute set.
 (c) My mid-flight warning about self-skipping live tests DOES NOT APPLY to this target. run_state_live is #[ignore]-gated and reads its env var with .expect(), so without WAMN_RUN_STORE_PG_URL it FAILS LOUDLY rather than reporting a silent ok in 0.00s, and it needs -- --ignored to run at all. The lane tested this rather than taking my word for it.

VERIFIED TWICE. Lane: run_state_live 1 passed; wamn-run-state --all-targets 103 passed/0 failed/4 ignored; wamn-proof-conformance 248 passed/1 failed where the 1 is the known .15.173 red and WORKSPACE_TIERS IS GREEN AT 11 PASSED -- exactly the count wave 7 measured with the offending leg reverted, so the guard wave 7 broke is intact. Integrator, independently on its own fresh container: 1 passed, proven to have EXECUTED by server-side ground truth (zero wamn% roles before, four roles and 13 wamn_run.runs rows after).

MUTANT re-derived by the integrator, not merely accepted from the lane: ALTER ROLE wamn_effect_writer BYPASSRLS, which the create-only bootstrap does not repair. The assertion fired by name in 0.22s and its diagnostic named the SURVIVING role, identifying the drifted one by omission. Restored, suite green, source sha256 unchanged at 89ce32cfeb64dada8b0ed21ea9124acb1391a6c8d9a4a9931bd4d4f0dbe6339e.

DEFERRALS FILED, BOTH EXIST AND WERE CREATED BEFORE THIS CLOSE REASON WAS WRITTEN: wamn-0h0g.20.17 (wamn_scenario_author carries the identical create-only hazard and CANNOT be covered the same way, because no ensure_scenario_author_role_sql exists to mirror against -- so the real question is whether that absence is itself the finding) and wamn-0h0g.20.18 (whether these bootstraps should be tripwires, self-healing via ELSE ALTER, or both -- noting wamn_app already has the ALTER arm and may be the odd one out).

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): database_owner.rs mutates cluster-wide database ACLs from a test
description:
## Why

crates/control/provision/tests/database_owner.rs:138-152 deliberately re-seeds template1 and
runs the CLUSTER-WIDE revoke_public_connect_floor_sql(), mutating PUBLIC CONNECT on EVERY
database in the cluster -- the reverse-direction reach of the wamn-0h0g.11.27 class.

The auditing lane found no in-tree gate it currently breaks, because every LOGIN role in every
sibling gate gets an explicit GRANT CONNECT. So this is fragile-by-construction rather than
presently broken.

Related measurement worth keeping, because it disproved the lane's own hypothesis: a revoked
template1 ACL does NOT propagate to new databases. CREATE DATABASE leaves datacl NULL, so
acldefault() re-grants PUBLIC CONNECT regardless of template1.

## Scope

Scope the test's floor run to its own database, or isolate the binary, so a test cannot
change a cluster-wide security posture out from under its siblings.

## Boundary

The test's reach. The production floor builder is correct and unchanged.
acceptance_criteria:
database_owner.rs no longer alters PUBLIC CONNECT on databases it did not create; its
own assertions still hold; sibling gates are unaffected by running it first.
close_reason: Committed 4718ca99: database_owner live gate now exercises only project-database ACL builders; sibling canary proves no cluster-global revoke, and the sibling provisioning gate passes afterward.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(ctl): PublishReleaseErrorKind cannot distinguish a manifest-projection refusal
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.15.29 added a refusal for the case where the minted release manifest resolves no
plan for the flow being published, so the publish would record an empty tested resolution
map. It reports under an existing PublishReleaseErrorKind rather than its own.

The coarsening is pre-existing and was noted in the code rather than smuggled into that
bead's scope. It matters because the refusal it hides is the exact defect wamn-0h0g.15.29
exists to prevent: a caller cannot tell an empty-projection refusal from the other members of
its kind.

## Boundary

The error taxonomy at this boundary. No behaviour change.
acceptance_criteria:
An empty manifest projection refuses under a kind that names it; existing callers and
gates keying on the current literals still pass.
close_reason: The dedicated kind the bead asks for already exists and is in use (crates/control/provision/src/publish_release.rs:164-166; services/ctl/src/publish_release.rs:617), and the refusal's subject — the flow→plan tested resolution map — retires under exe-model.md §What retires: plans + compiler.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(schema): UnreadableRegistrations serves two subsystems from a replica-identity module
description:
## Why

wamn-0h0g.12.119 correctly reused the wamn-0h0g.12.103 error shape rather than minting a
second taxonomy, and extended UnreadableRegistrationsKind with
OrphanGuardAbsent/OrphanGuardUnreadable. The type now serves BOTH the REPLICA IDENTITY
reconcile and the D24 registration-orphan guard, but lives in
crates/schema/control/src/replica_identity.rs.

Two consequences, both deliberate at the time and both worth revisiting:
 - the module name no longer describes its contents;
 - the two ORIGINAL literals (replica-identity-registrations-{absent,unreadable}) carry no
   subsystem prefix, while the two new ones do. They were frozen deliberately because live
   gates key on them verbatim, so the asymmetry is intentional, not an oversight.

## Scope

Decide whether the shape moves to a neutral module (and whether the older literals are worth
a coordinated rename across the gates that assert them), or whether the current home is
accepted and documented as such.

## Boundary

Placement and naming. No behaviour change; the four literals are a stable refusal contract
and any rename is a coordinated edit with the gates that key on them.
acceptance_criteria:
Either the type has a home whose name covers both consumers, or a recorded decision
that it stays put; the literal asymmetry is either resolved or documented as frozen; every
gate keying on the four literals still passes.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): workspace clippy fails on runnerbench for-loop-over-single-element
description:
## Why

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on
tests/integration/src/runnerbench.rs:315, "for loop over a single element". Last changed by
618a5800; untouched by wave 13.

It means no lane can run a workspace-wide strict clippy as a gate -- each must scope to its
own crates, which is how a lint regression elsewhere would go unnoticed.

## Boundary

The single lint site. Not a behaviour change.
acceptance_criteria: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0.
notes:
*** THE CAUSE OF THE SYMPTOM THIS BEAD RECORDS HAS BEEN FOUND, 2026-08-19 (wave-9 lane 2).
FILED AS wamn-0h0g.12.147. ***

This bead records the symptom -- "no lane can run a workspace-wide strict clippy as a gate" --
without identifying why. The cause: cargo ABORTS SCHEDULING NEW UNITS ON THE FIRST ERROR, so
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
reports only the first failing unit's errors and hides every error in any package scheduled
after it. The fix is --keep-going.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD SPECIFICALLY: its acceptance criterion, "workspace clippy exits 0",
IS NOT REACHABLE WITHIN THIS BEAD'S BOUNDARY. The true baseline at f27ad353 was SEVEN errors
across THREE packages, of which this bead owns exactly one (tests/integration/src/
runnerbench.rs:315, single_element_loop). wamn-0h0g.12.146 owned another and has now landed.
The remaining five are owned by wamn-0h0g.12.148 (four in effect_spans.rs) and wamn-0h0g.12.149
(rie2ebench.rs:151 dead_code).

*** RAISED, NOT ACTED ON: this bead's acceptance criterion should be narrowed to its own site,
since a shared unreachable criterion across several beads is itself the false-coverage shape --
each bead appears to promise a tree-wide green that none of them can deliver alone. I did not
edit the acceptance; that is an owner call. ***

WORTH NOTING FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: runnerbench.rs:315 is a single_element_loop, the SAME lint
and the same shape as .12.146, which turned out to be DELETION RESIDUE -- the third surviving
trace of one deletion. Check whether this loop also lost elements to a deletion before
flattening it. In .12.146's case the collapse was correct, proven by showing the loop's
membership criterion had legitimately shrunk to one; do the equivalent check here rather than
assuming either answer.

*** PRE-PARTITION MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-19 at 53afb31a. READ-ONLY, NOTHING EDITED.
COLLAPSING THIS LOOP WOULD BE WRONG. THE CORRECT FIX IS TO RESTORE A MISSING MEMBER. ***

Line and lint CONFIRMED EXACTLY as briefed: tests/integration/src/runnerbench.rs:315:9,
clippy::single_element_loop, on the (lib test) target of wamn-proof-integration.
(Package name VERIFIED from tests/integration/Cargo.toml -- it is wamn-proof-integration,
not a path-derived name. A wrong -p ERRORS and greps as a false green.)

=====================================================================
THE LOOP, AND ITS MEMBERSHIP CRITERION
=====================================================================
    for required in ["CREATE TABLE wamn_run.effect_attempts"] {
        assert!(ddl.contains(required), "runnerbench DDL lacks {required}");
    }
Enclosing test: runnerbench_stand_in_carries_production_claim_surfaces.
CRITERION: SQL object headers the runnerbench stand-in DDL (runner_ddl(), :47) must
carry BECAUSE THE PRODUCTION CLAIM TRANSACTION NAMES THEM.

=====================================================================
THE SHRINK WAS LEGITIMATE -- BUT IT IS NOT wamn-0h0g.12.146's DELETION
=====================================================================
*** A BRIEF CORRECTION THAT MATTERS: this is NOT another trace of e45ca35b. *** The list
was born with THREE members in da58814f (wamn-0h0g.4.1, install global FIFO claim):
    CREATE TABLE wamn_run.effect_attempts
    CREATE TABLE wamn_run.run_flow_resolutions
    CREATE FUNCTION wamn_run.materialize_run_flow_resolutions
It was cut to one by fcf0dd99 (wamn-0h0g.15.10, delete release-bound resolution,
2026-08-16), whose message says "The claim's five steps were lock, classify, resolve,
materialize, lease. Steps three and four are gone verbatim." The two dropped members
were exactly the objects of steps 3 and 4. A DIFFERENT deletion, two days earlier.

PROOF THE TWO DROPPED MEMBERS LOST THEIR SUBJECT, NOT THEIR COVERAGE:
  materialize_run_flow_resolutions -- ZERO occurrences tree-wide outside .git.
  run_flow_resolutions -- zero live code/SQL references. Only docs prose, four
    explanatory comments in crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/claims.rs,
    and one NEGATIVE guard at services/scenario-worker/src/store/test_orchestration.rs:601
    asserting its permanent ABSENCE.
  Neither is in deploy/sql/run-state.sql, whose CREATE TABLE wamn_run.* set is now
    runs, invocation_admissions, node_runs, effect_attempts, effect_attempt_dispatches,
    effect_attempt_outcomes, operator_run_actions.

=====================================================================
*** BUT THE CRITERION HAS NOT SHRUNK TO ONE. THIS IS WHERE IT DIVERGES FROM .12.146. ***
=====================================================================
For .12.146 the collapse was proven correct by showing membership had legitimately
shrunk to exactly one. THAT PROOF CANNOT BE PRODUCED HERE. Enumerating what the current
production claim path actually names (crates/execution/run-state/src/queue/sql.rs,
composed by production_claim.rs, driven by runnerbench::run via claim_next_production):

  run_queue        select_production_claim_sql        PINNED by the sibling test
  runs             select_production_claim_sql        PINNED (8 claim columns)
  effect_attempts  select_production_claim_sql +
                   select_claim_effect_attempt_sql    PINNED by this one-element loop
  node_runs        select_pre_effect_projection_sql
                   (production_claim.rs:411)          *** NOTHING PINS IT ***

runner_ddl deliberately CREATEs node_runs with an RLS policy and a GRANT SELECT -- it IS
on the surface -- yet no assertion pins it, and it was NEVER in the list, not even at
da58814f. So this is a PRE-EXISTING gap, not one the deletion created.

*** THEREFORE THE HONEST FIX IS TO RESTORE TRUE MEMBERSHIP: add
"CREATE TABLE wamn_run.node_runs". That silences the lint TRUTHFULLY and closes the gap.
Collapsing would silence it by ratifying an incomplete list -- turning a lint that is
accidentally reporting a real coverage hole into a green line. ***

CAVEAT ON THE TEMPTING ALTERNATIVE: do NOT swap this for
wamn_run_state::schema_drift::assert_run_state_stand_in. Need::Required demands full
column parity and the stand-in is deliberately narrow -- effect_attempts is 2 columns vs
~24 shipped, node_runs 5 vs ~22. That is exactly why a presence-only contains check was
used.
RELATED WEAKNESS, RECORDED NOT FIXED: ddl is the return of runner_ddl(), a local format!
literal, so this loop is a SELF-CHECK. It detects stand-in EROSION, never production
drift.

HAZARD: NONE for runnerbench. No recipe-test directive, no deploy/gates job yaml, no
shell script, no workspace_tiers entry names it. Its only pins are the orchestrator
subcommand wiring (tests/orchestrator/src/main.rs:14,38,77) and a prose mention at
crates/execution/run-state/src/schema_drift.rs:7. Editing the loop body breaks nothing
registered. (runnerbench::run IS reachable, via wamn-gates runnerbench, superuser PG
required, so in-cluster only.)
close_reason:
CLOSED: DONE, but NOT the way this bead was written -- and the difference is the finding.

*** THE LOOP WAS NOT COLLAPSED. A MISSING MEMBER WAS RESTORED. ***
This bead was filed as a lint to silence (for loop over a single element). Measurement
showed that collapsing would have silenced a lint that was ACCIDENTALLY REPORTING A REAL
COVERAGE GAP.

THE MEMBERSHIP CRITERION of the list is: SQL object headers the runnerbench stand-in DDL
must carry BECAUSE THE PRODUCTION CLAIM TRANSACTION NAMES THEM. Enumerating what the claim
path actually names (queue/sql.rs composed by production_claim.rs, driven by
runnerbench::run via claim_next_production):

  runs             select_production_claim_sql                     PINNED (8 claim columns)
  effect_attempts  select_production_claim_sql +
                   select_claim_effect_attempt_sql                 PINNED (this loop)
  node_runs        select_pre_effect_projection_sql
                   (queue/sql.rs:114 FROM node_runs, called at

SO THE FIX IS: add "CREATE TABLE wamn_run.node_runs". The lint goes green TRUTHFULLY and a

*** THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF wamn-0h0g.12.146, AND THE CONTRAST IS THE LESSON. ***
There, the collapse WAS correct, proven by showing membership had legitimately shrunk to

THE SHRINK ITSELF WAS LEGITIMATE, AND IT IS NOT e45ca35b's DELETION. The list was born with
three members at da58814f (wamn-0h0g.4.1) and cut to one by fcf0dd99 (wamn-0h0g.15.10,
2026-08-16), whose message reads "The claim's five steps were lock, classify, resolve,

*** A BRIEF CORRECTION: this is a DIFFERENT deletion from the one behind .12.146 and

title: [SR-MVP] docs: the [RUN-PLANE-RECONCILE] recipe omits --test-threads=1 and reports false failures
description:
## Why

run_plane_live's legs share the `catalog` schema, the run-plane schema and CLUSTER-WIDE
roles, so they stomp each other under the default parallel harness. The documented
[RUN-PLANE-RECONCILE] recipe in docs/archive/build-and-test.md does not pass
-- --test-threads=1.

MEASURED: the same tree and the same container gives 1 passed / 6 failed under the
documented invocation and 6 passed / 2 failed with -- --test-threads=1. A reader following
the recipe sees five failures that are not real, which is the exact failure mode
wamn-0h0g.11.29 documents for the publish_catalog suite: it trains the reader to re-run
until green.

## Scope

Correct the recipe. Consider whether the serialization belongs in the test binary instead of
the recipe (wamn-0h0g.11.29 took the in-binary route with a mutex, which cannot be forgotten
by a caller).

## Boundary

Recipe correctness. docs/archive/build-and-test.md is integrator-owned; this is filed rather
than edited in-wave because wamn-0h0g.15.22 also rewrites that file and a concurrent edit
would collide.
acceptance_criteria:
The recipe reproduces 6 passed / 2 failed (or better) as written, with no
undocumented flag needed; if serialization moves into the binary, the recipe no longer needs
the flag and a named test proves the legs cannot run concurrently.

title: [SR-MVP] docs: two runtime doc comments still advertise DATABASE_URL as a supported source
description:
## Why -- left stale by wamn-0h0g.12.114, which could not reach them

wamn-0h0g.12.114 removed the DATABASE_URL fallback from both host pools and corrected the comment at
services/host/src/host.rs:241. Two more places still claim it:

1. crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/wamn_postgres/claims.rs:482-484 documents
   WamnPostgres::from_env() as taking "the default project from `DATABASE_URL`/`WAMN_PG_URL`" -- the
   same false claim as the host.rs comment, one call frame up. *** This is the one that matters: it
   is the doc a reader hits when asking what from_env() reads. *** Replacement text:
       /// Build from the environment: the default project from `WAMN_PG_URL`, plus
       /// any explicit projects listed in the JSON at `WAMN_PG_PROJECTS_FILE`
       /// (mounted like a Secret/ConfigMap).
2. tests/integration/src/flowbench.rs:266-272 and matbench.rs:610-616 build a
   WamnPostgresConfig::from_env() and fall back to it when --database-url is absent; their refusal
   strings say "set DATABASE_URL / WAMN_PG_URL" and now name a variable they no longer honour.
   Nothing breaks -- every documented recipe passes --database-url, and the Job manifests those
   recipes cite no longer exist -- but the text misleads.

Both were outside .12.114's lane domain and were reported rather than edited.

## Boundary

Comments and refusal strings. No behaviour change.
acceptance_criteria:
No doc comment or refusal string in the runtime or the integration harnesses advertises DATABASE_URL
as a source the host pools honour.
close_reason: Fixed by d5bdbb35: production comments/refusals now name only WAMN_PG_URL; new conformance guard preserves the separate test-only DATABASE_URL fallback. Exact guard green, strict Clippy/rustfmt/diff green; five independent drift mutants red and restored.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(ctl): terminalize-effect-uncertain carries the same defaulted schema on a mutating verb
description:
## Why -- the sibling wamn-0h0g.12.115 found and deliberately did not widen into

services/ctl/src/terminalize_effect_uncertain.rs:24 carries
`#[arg(long, default_value = "wamn_run")] schema` -- byte-identical in shape to the default
wamn-0h0g.12.115 just removed from prune-run-history, and on another MUTATING verb.

.12.115's argument was that a default is only safe on a destructive verb when the default is what
the operator would have chosen, and that an operator whose run plane lives in a project schema gets
a successful-looking run against the WRONG schema. Whether that argument transfers here depends on
whether this verb's statements are schema-qualified or resolved through search_path -- CHECK THAT
FIRST rather than assuming the analogy holds. If they are qualified, the default is harmless and
this bead closes with that evidence recorded; if they are not, it is the same defect.

.12.115's guard was deliberately NOT widened to cover this file, because it is a different bead's
surface and widening a guard across a boundary nobody adjudicated is how a fix acquires scope it
was never reviewed for.

## Boundary

This verb's schema argument only.
acceptance_criteria:
Either the default is removed and a named test pins its absence, or the statements are shown to be
schema-qualified and the default is recorded as safe with that evidence cited to source.
notes: SHELVED 2026-08-18: terminalize-effect-uncertain is operator terminalize — crash-floor machinery parked behind the durable-tier class gate (exe-model.md R2; wamn-0h0g.20). The --schema default defect is real but travels with the verb; nothing this verb touches survives the default tier.

title: [SR-MVP] remediate(auth): consider a definer lock bridge to retire UPDATE (tenant_id) on event_registrations
description:
## Why -- filed under ruling R12's rider, and the honest case is WEAK

wamn-0h0g.12.29 confined catalog.event_registrations to SELECT plus UPDATE (tenant_id). The column
grant exists solely because PostgreSQL requires UPDATE on at least one column for the FOR KEY SHARE
that callable admission takes as wamn_app (admission.rs:379-384). A SECURITY DEFINER lock bridge
mirroring wamn_run.lock_catalog_head (run_plane.rs:737) would let the grant be dropped entirely.

*** R12's RIDER: SECURITY DEFINER routines have a RULING HISTORY. The definer trio was killed once
already. Any proposal must CITE THE PRIOR REJECTION and make the new case. The prior rejection is
docs/plane-amendment.md:301-303 -- "This is not a separate admission RPC or a SECURITY DEFINER path"
-- and docs/scope-reduction-mvp.md:398-399, ratified as wamn-0h0g.7.5 and recorded at
docs/archive/PLAN/PLAN.md:2611. What was chosen INSTEAD is the grant-enforced role pattern
(wamn_management_admitter), not a definer. ***

## The case against, stated first because it is the stronger one

The grant this would retire is PROVEN SEMANTICALLY INERT. catalog.event_registrations is FORCE ROW
LEVEL SECURITY and its policy's WITH CHECK admits only the value already in the row, so the sole write
UPDATE (tenant_id) permits is the identity write -- verified live: SET tenant_id = tenant_id commits
and changes nothing, SET tenant_id = 't2' is refused by the policy, SET flow_id is refused by
privilege. Retiring an inert grant by adding a definer routine trades a proven no-op for new
privileged machinery of exactly the kind the prior ruling rejected.

## The case for

architecture/protected-writes.json records column grants as update(<column>), so
catalog.event_registrations KEEPS a wamn_app entry and REMAINS author-reachable in the inventory --
the only one of the ten that does not flip to "no". If inventory cleanliness is judged to matter more
than avoiding new definer machinery, this is the change that achieves it.

## Recommendation

Do not build it unless the owner rules that the residual inventory entry is unacceptable. File-and-
park is the expected outcome.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded ruling. If built: a definer lock bridge mirroring wamn_run.lock_catalog_head, the
UPDATE (tenant_id) grant dropped, admission_live still green, and the prior rejection addressed
explicitly in the commit body.

title: [SR-MVP] refactor(publish): give the mint's projection and document refusals their own step-A variants
description:
## Why -- a deliberate coarsening wamn-0h0g.15.14 flagged rather than smuggled

wamn-0h0g.15.14 introduced MintManifestErrorKind::{Projection, Document}. Neither has a counterpart
in PublishReleaseErrorKind, so step A's boundary translation coarsens both onto ReleaseCoordinate,
preserving the exact predicate in detail() and on the retained source. The test
every_mint_refusal_translates_once_at_step_a pins that behaviour, so the coarsening is visible rather
than silent.

The clean fix is two new variants in crates/control/provision/src/publish_release.rs. That file was
outside .15.14's lane domain and was deliberately not touched.

This is a wire-boundary taxonomy change: the repository convention is that at public, persisted and
WIT/wire boundaries the repository-defined error enums and frozen serialized literals are the
controlling contract, so adding variants needs the owning boundary's agreement, not a drive-by edit.

## Boundary

The two variants and the translation. Does not change the mint or its refusal predicates.
acceptance_criteria:
PublishReleaseErrorKind carries variants that distinguish a projection failure from a document
failure; step A's translation maps MintManifestErrorKind onto them one-to-one; the coarsening
assertion in every_mint_refusal_translates_once_at_step_a is updated to assert the exact mapping
rather than the coarsening.
close_reason: No longer applicable: commit 4802daac (.26.6.2) deleted crates/control/provision/src/publish_release.rs and its PublishReleaseErrorKind/step-A translation; HEAD f282fe83 has no PublishReleaseErrorKind or every_mint_refusal_translates_once_at_step_a symbol. The surviving services/ctl manifest mint owns its own typed MintManifestErrorKind boundary and has no coarsening seam to repair.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(catalog): ServingManifest::new's doc contradicts itself and the mint cannot use it
description:
## Why -- found by wamn-0h0g.15.14, which had to route around it

crates/catalog/model/src/serving_manifest.rs's `new()` is `#[cfg(feature = "test-util")]`. Its own
doc says "the release mint is the only legitimate producer, and it builds through this path with the
feature on", and three lines later says "NEVER move this onto a normal dependency. That silently
deletes the fence for the whole dependency graph."

*** BOTH CANNOT HOLD. The mint is production code in wamn-ctl, which cannot take a test-util
dependency without deleting the fence the same comment forbids deleting. ***

wamn-0h0g.15.14 used neither: all ServingManifest fields are pub, so the mint builds a struct
literal, calls the ungated canonical_bytes(), and then ADMITS ITS OWN OUTPUT through
from_canonical_bytes. That satisfies the fence's intent more strictly than new() would -- the value
handed on is derived from bytes that were actually produced and re-admitted -- and needed no
serving_manifest.rs or Cargo.toml edit.

RELATED STALENESS, same file: wamn-0h0g.15.14's bead and brief both name a reader
`ServingManifest::read`. There is no such function; it is `from_canonical_bytes`. Every line number
quoted for that file in .15.14's text (:316, :321, :332, :340, :395) is stale.

## Scope

Correct the doc to describe what is actually true and what the production producer actually does.
Docs only unless the fence itself is found to be wrong.
acceptance_criteria:
ServingManifest::new's documentation no longer claims the release mint builds through it; the
production construction path (struct literal, canonical_bytes, re-admission through
from_canonical_bytes) is documented where a reader will find it; no stale `::read` reference
survives in the module.
close_reason: Already satisfied by wamn-0h0g.25.1 commit 71f9bf99. At df4d12b9, ServingManifest::new is explicitly documented as test-only, the production path is documented as projected facts serialized then re-admitted through Self::from_canonical_bytes, and the module contains no stale ::read reference. Source check: git blame attributes both corrective lines to 71f9bf99; no additional repository edit is warranted.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(test): replica_identity_live cannot pass on its own documented recipe

premise in a P1 security adjudication (wamn-0h0g.12.66 'the dispatcher performs queue AND catalog
reads'). A stale comment that mis-scopes a security bead is worth a commit of its own. ***

## Boundary

Comment only.
acceptance_criteria: The dispatcher projects contract describes the dispatcher's actual read surface; no manifest comment claims a catalog read; the claim is narrow enough to survive the cron_attachments view's existence.

Committed on its own because this sentence was the ORIGIN of a false premise in P1 bead wamn-0h0g.12.66. Scoped narrowly: catalog.cron_attachments IS defined as a view and granted, and one integration test names it -- but that test only asserts the CREATE VIEW string exists in the schema FILE and issues no query, so the replacement states the dispatcher-specific claim rather than a broad one.

title: [SR-MVP] test(egressbench): pin the HostOwnedPort refusal on the sentinel path
description:
## Why

fork sockets/policy.rs resolve_host_loopback refuses HostOwnedPort AFTER the
grant check, with the deliberate comment that this ordering exists "so an operator
cannot grant it by listing the port" -- a guest reaching a host-owned port would
be reaching the host's own ingress or control plane, or another tenant's published
service.

Nothing in wamn asserts that ordering, so a future fork sync could move the check
before the allowlist (making a listed host-owned port grantable) without any test
noticing.

## Scope

Pin the HostOwnedPort refusal and, specifically, that it is evaluated after the
loopback allowlist rather than before it.

## Boundary

Unreachable in wamn today: no PortTable is installed, so self.host_owned_ports is
None and the arm never fires. This is drift protection on a fork invariant, not
coverage of live behaviour -- say so in the test. Filed by lane 5 of wave 10.
acceptance_criteria: A named test pins that a host-owned port is refused on the sentinel path even when listed in the loopback grant, and that the check follows the allowlist.

Correct the record on wamn-0h0g.15.68 so a later reader does not trust the

title: [SR-MVP] fix(gates): every_vendored_contract_refuses_deleted_vocabulary strips only /// comments
description:

crates/platform/runtime/tests/flow_invocation_wit_coherence.rs's
`every_vendored_contract_refuses_deleted_vocabulary` filters comment lines by

## Scope

generally (and any block form WIT admits) rather than `///` alone.

Latent, not red. In .15.131's owned file but outside its scope, so deliberately
not touched there. Filed by lane 4 of wave 10.

notes:

=====================================================================
OWNER RULING 2026-08-17 -- THE PRECEDENT LIMIT ON THIS CLOSURE
=====================================================================

running apply/test/restore, because the harness is frozen until wamn-0h0g.15.22.
The owner confirmed the closure and gave the reason it does not weaken the rule:

  The apply/test/restore rule exists because REASONING ABOUT KILLS IS HOW

EXECUTION DEBT. Do not cite this closure shorn of those two conditions. If you
are about to accept a reasoned kill and there is no freeze forbidding execution,
or no named bead carrying the debt, then the rule applies unchanged: apply, test,
restore, and watch it fail a NAMED test. ***
