title: [SR-MVP] test(runtime): flow-http-routing has no WIT-coherence test
description:
## Why

Found while taking wamn-0h0g.15.96 (2026-08-17). Every other wamn runtime plugin has a `crates/platform/runtime/tests/*_wit_coherence.rs` guard -- flow_invocation, jetstream, postgres, connection, http_effect -- and tests/conformance/tests/contract_diff.rs registers the flow-invocation one BY NAME. The new flow-http-routing plugin has none, so nothing pins its generated bindings against the WIT it binds.

This matters more than the usual parity argument because the package is vendored twice (the component's copy and the runtime crate's), so the two can drift apart with nothing observing it.

## Scope

Add `crates/platform/runtime/tests/flow_http_routing_wit_coherence.rs` following the sibling guards' shape, and register it in contract_diff.rs alongside the flow-invocation entry.

## Boundary

Test parity only; do not change the plugin or the WIT. Coverage of the wire spellings partially exists inside the plugin's own mapping-shape test helper, which is not a substitute for the coherence guard.
acceptance_criteria: flow-http-routing has a WIT-coherence guard registered in contract_diff.rs, and it fails when the vendored package and the component's copy diverge.
close_reason: Coherence guard landed and registered (5fc09941). Seventh contract-diff leg; both tool and the test pinning its exact argv, label order and leg count widened together. Uses BYTE-EQUALITY because the two copies ARE byte-identical — correcting my own brief, which generalised a measured fact about a different package (the runtime's flow-invocation copy is doc-stripped) into a wrong claim. There is also no normalization helper anywhere in the family; three siblings use three unrelated shapes and flow_invocation_wit_coherence compares no copies at all. Layered so it fails on one-sided drift, on a change made identically to BOTH copies (frozen whole-block literals), and on an unregistered THIRD copy (tree walk). Bead's parity premise was false — four plugins have no guard, filed as backlog. Its recipe-test directive is WITHHELD: it would take the frozen count 37 to 38. Banked on .15.22.

title: [SR-MVP] fix(conformance): a dotted dependency table escapes the identity rule
description:
## Why

Found while taking wamn-0h0g.15.109 (2026-08-17). A pre-existing blind spot in
tests/conformance/src/manifest_dependencies.rs, unchanged by that bead.

## Measured

The guard tracks whether it is inside a dependency table by taking the LAST
dot-separated segment of the table header. That is correct for
[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] and [workspace.dependencies], but wrong for the
single-dependency form:

  [dev-dependencies.wamn-catalog]
  path = "."

Here the last segment is the CRATE NAME, not a dependency-table keyword, so the
table flag goes false and every line in that table escapes the identity rule
entirely — including the very construction wamn-0h0g.15.109 wrote a narrow
exemption for.

LATENT TODAY, which is why it is P3: grep for a dotted dependency-table header
over every manifest in the tree returns ZERO hits. Nothing exploits it now.

## Scope

Recognize the single-dependency table form: a header whose FIRST segment is a
dependency-table keyword is a dependency table for the crate its remaining
segments name. Keep the existing target-cfg and workspace forms working.

## Boundary

A different rule from wamn-0h0g.15.109's exemption, and it changes verdicts for
table shapes that bead was told not to touch — which is why it was not folded in.
Fixing it must not widen the self dev-dependency exemption: the three conjuncts
(dev table, own name, path ".") stay exactly as narrow.
acceptance_criteria:
A dotted single-dependency table is scanned by the identity rule, proven by a
fixture in both the admitted and the refused direction; the existing exemption and
every other verdict are unchanged.
close_reason: Commit 93896fa6. TWO PREMISE CORRECTIONS, and the first changes the shape of the fix: flipping the table flag is NOT SUFFICIENT, because inside a dotted table the per-line split_once('=') reads `path` and `features` as the dependency NAME, so every line still escapes. The dotted table has to be judged as a UNIT -- header names the crate, following lines are its keys -- which is why this is a restructure into dependency_declarations (parse) + duplicates_governed_identity (judge), leaving one copy of the rule, the exemption and the message. Second: the bead's stated rule ('a header whose FIRST segment is a keyword') would NOT catch [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies.wamn-x], whose first segment is `target` -- same escape, same latency; the rule implemented instead is 'the first segment that names a dependency keyword decides, the rest names the crate', closing both spellings with one predicate. Exemption boundary held exactly: the three conjuncts unchanged. Verdicts bit-identical on all 44 manifests (old and new logic run side by side), which is structurally guaranteed. Absorbed at no extra code: the dotted target-cfg spelling is now fixtured, and plain [target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies] gets its FIRST fixture. Deliberately not changed and flagged: workspace_dependency_names still matches only the plain header, so a dotted [workspace.dependencies.serde] would de-govern that name (zero occurrences, different rule).

title: [SR-MVP] fix(conformance): a missing file must not mask a missing occurrence
description:
## Why

Found while taking wamn-0h0g.15.110 (2026-08-17). The version-identity guard
reports at most ONE violation per watch entry, and file-absence short-circuits the
occurrence check.

## Measured

In tests/conformance/src/version_identity.rs, governed_literal_violations turns an
Err from read_to_string straight into a single '{path}: {error}' violation and
never reaches the count check. So when a watched file is BOTH moved and emptied of
its governed literal, the guard reports only the missing file.

This is not hypothetical — it is what made wamn-0h0g.15.110's first entry
misleading. crates/scenarios/model/src/test_set.rs failed as 'No such file or
directory', which reads as a path that needs correcting. In fact the file MOVED
(wamn-0h0g.15.76, eb1c3a88) and the governed constant TEST_SET_SCHEMA_VERSION had
separately been DELETED (wamn-0h0g.15.27, 3a042d96). Correcting the path alone
would have turned a file-mode failure into a found-0 failure rather than a pass.

## Scope

Report file-absence and count-mismatch independently, so one entry can surface both
faults in one run. Any future path correction in this guard must otherwise re-check
the count by hand.

## Boundary

Guard MECHANISM. wamn-0h0g.15.110 reconciled guard CONTENT and deliberately did not
touch this — the two are separate concerns and the content fix stands on its own.
Not part of wamn-0h0g.15.22, which is registry regeneration.
acceptance_criteria:
A watch entry whose file is missing AND whose occurrence count is wrong reports both
faults in one run; the existing content reconcile still passes.
close_reason: Commit 1a636d78. A read failure now pushes its violation AND substitutes an empty source so the count check still runs, so one entry surfaces both faults and names the governed literal nobody can account for. PREMISE CORRECTION: the guard walks 50 watch entries, not the 44 assumed -- GOVERNED_LITERALS (44) plus GOVERNED_JSON_SCHEMAS (6). The JSON half deliberately still short-circuits: a missing JSON file has no second independent expectation, so an empty string would only add a redundant EOF parse error per entry. Acceptance's second clause verified by re-measuring all 44 literal entries out of band (paths plus exact counts, including .15.110's tightened authoring.ts count of 4): zero faults, so the new path is never entered on the real tree.

title: [SR-MVP] test(ctl): writer-ACL inventory accepts an unexpected object kind unchallenged
description:
## Why

Measured by a mutation run during wamn-0h0g.15.107 (2026-08-17). Widening the accepted object-kind set in verify_effect_writer_acl_role_inventory (services/ctl/src/provision_project_env.rs) from `"schema" | "relation" | "column"` to also admit `"database"` leaves stable_acl_inventory_accepts_only_the_complete_writer_schema_set GREEN. The mutant SURVIVED.

The guard's first ensure! — that a stable writer role carries no non-writer ACL kind — is therefore unverified: no fixture in that test presents an out-of-set object kind, so nothing observes the rejection.

## PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED BY THE DELETION

This is a surviving function that wamn-0h0g.15.107 only edited AROUND (it deleted the artifact-reader sibling in the same match). The gap predates that commit and predates this branch: the test asserts the COMPLETE writer schema set from schema/relation/column fixtures and never exercises the kind filter.

## Scope

Add one fixture with an out-of-set object kind (e.g. a `database` CONNECT ACL on the stable role) and assert the named refusal, so the kind filter has coverage.

## Boundary

Coverage only. Do not change the accepted kind set or the guard's behaviour. The reader-side sibling verify_artifact_reader_acl_role_inventory is deleted and does not come back.
acceptance_criteria: A named test fails when verify_effect_writer_acl_role_inventory's accepted object-kind set is widened by one kind; the mutation that survived at wamn-0h0g.15.107 is dead.
close_reason: Commit 0d5001fe. One fixture with a database/CONNECT ACL on the stable role, asserting the NAMED refusal. PREMISE CORRECTION, more precise than the bead and it is what makes the test load-bearing: the surviving mutant does not leave the test green by omission -- under it the fixture STILL errors, just later, on the exact-grant-set comparison. So an is_err()-only test could NOT have killed it; the assertion has to pin the refusal message, and the test comment says so to stop anyone weakening it back. Accepted kind set and guard behaviour untouched; the deleted reader-side sibling does not come back. Mutation evidence recorded in build-and-test.md alongside the two sibling guard-mechanism fixes.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(catalog): give the release manifest's artifact and definition hashes validating newtypes
description: Successor to wamn-0h0g.15.117, which resolves the definition-hash spelling contradiction first (prefixed form wins; the bare-hex minting site in crates/schema/control/src/exposure.rs:248 is the bug). Retrofit the manifest's remaining bare-String hash fields into the crate's hash-newtype family (DefinitionHash, ArtifactHash, DraftContentHash, ManifestDigest) with a VALIDATING Deserialize, so the observed prefix contradiction becomes unrepresentable instead of patched at one site. Scope is now three fields — ServingFlow.source_artifact (:179), ServingFlow.binding_base_artifact (:208), ServingAttachment.definition_hash (:258): ServingFlow.plan_hash (:165) drops out because execution plans and their hashes retire with the deterministic compiler. The stated cost is smaller than filed: the family is #[serde(transparent)], so Serialize-side byte equivalence is structural, and one manifest golden vector serialized and compared is the whole proof. wamn-3560 stays out — different document, same class.
acceptance_criteria: A ruling exists on whether the serving manifest's four flow-level hash fields join the newtype family; if they do, the retrofit lands as one sweep with a byte-for-byte proof that canonical encoding and existing manifest digests are unchanged; if they do not, the reason is recorded where a future reader will look.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-17 — RE-POINTED AS wamn-0h0g.15.117'S SUCCESSOR. No longer refused; the motive changed and so did the cost.

THE COST COLLAPSED. The bead's stated price -- "proving byte-for-byte that the canonical encoding and therefore every existing manifest digest is unchanged" -- is much cheaper than written, because the newtype family uses #[serde(transparent)]. A transparent newtype over String serializes IDENTICALLY to the String, so Serialize-side byte-equivalence is STRUCTURAL, not empirical. The only real work is the validating Deserialize each newtype needs.

THE MOTIVE CHANGED FROM TIDINESS TO AN OBSERVED BUG CLASS. wamn-0h0g.15.117 found a LIVE prefix contradiction on ServingAttachment.definition_hash: the manifest requires sha256:<64hex> while resolve_exposure mints bare hex, which is what the database stores and what admission compares -- so no spelling currently satisfies both. A validating newtype is exactly what makes that unrepresentable.

SEQUENCE, binding: (1) .15.117 resolves the spelling contradiction FIRST, taking the PREFIXED form (the bare-hex minting site is the bug). (2) Then the four newtypes land together -- ServingFlow.plan_hash, .source_artifact, .binding_base_artifact and ServingAttachment.definition_hash -- with a byte-equivalence golden test: one manifest vector, serialize and compare.

wamn-3560 (Relation.id is a plain String while sibling fields are id-newtypes) is RULED OUT of this bead and into the deferral sweep's backlog. Same class, different subject, DIFFERENT DOCUMENT -- bundling unrelated schemas is how a targeted fix becomes a migration.
CURRENT FORMAT-2 PREMISE CORRECTION (2026-08-23, grounded at c239e3f0): .25.4 removed ServingFlow and its cited fields. The issue's three-field count projects exactly onto the complete surviving bare-String digest set in ServingManifest: ServingComponent.digest is ArtifactHash; ServingWiring.graph_hash is DefinitionHash (WiringDocument::wiring_hash already mints that type); ServingAttachment.definition_hash is DefinitionHash. The transparent-serialization/golden-vector acceptance remains unchanged. This is a subject rename under the ratified v2 format, not a new policy choice.
close_reason: Landed validating ArtifactHash/DefinitionHash manifest fields with canonical-byte identity proof and dependent production sweep in fc0367d4

title: [SR-MVP] docs: CLAUDE.md names two services that do not exist
description:
## Why

CLAUDE.md:109 is the agent-facing repository-structure contract and it is stale. It reads:

  services/{host,node-host,ctl,dispatcher,executor,scenario-worker,builder,cdc-reader,waker}

services/ actually contains exactly: cdc-reader, ctl, dispatcher, executor, host, scenario-worker, waker. Both services/node-host and services/builder are ABSENT — no directory, no workspace member in root Cargo.toml, nothing. Only docs/archive/platform/builder.md survives, and it is archived.

This is not cosmetic. The stale line caused a wave-5 mapping pass to be dispatched on the premise that 'services/builder pushes signed artifacts to a registry', which is the natural place to look for reusable OCI push code. There is none — the absence is what makes wamn-0h0g.15.97 greenfield, and the stale contract actively hides that.

## Scope

Correct the services list at CLAUDE.md:109. While there, confirm the rest of the repository-structure section against the tree (the crates/, components/, tests/, test-support/, poc/ and deploy/ lines) rather than fixing only the two known-bad entries, and state whether builder/node-host were removed by the MVP scope reduction or never landed on this branch — the answer decides whether the line should be deleted or re-added later.

## Boundary

Documentation only. Do not reinstate either service.
acceptance_criteria: CLAUDE.md's repository-structure section matches the tree; every named directory exists; the disposition of builder and node-host is stated.
close_reason: Commit 89b70fe4. Audited all nine bullets rather than the two named and found FIVE false claims: services/{node-host,builder}, crates/node, components/nodes all absent, and poc/ DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL (bullet deleted, not corrected), plus deploy/'s poc/ tier absent while an undocumented deploy/mvp/ exists. DISPOSITION as required: REMOVED, not never-landed -- builder/node-host/crates/node deleted together in f6bc01eb (wamn-0h0g.6.3), components/nodes+poc/+deploy/poc in 3554f140 (.12.2), established with git log --diff-filter=D. The operational consequence is recorded with it: no in-tree OCI push path to reuse, which is what makes .15.97 greenfield and what the stale line hid (it had already mis-dispatched a wave-5 mapping pass). deploy/README.md's 'four tiers, nothing at the top level' also does not account for deploy/mvp -- described accurately, not blessed.

title: [SR-MVP] test(ingress): the flow-http adapter does not cover attachment-disabled
description:
## Why

`components/ingress/flow-http/tests/adversarial.rs:367-377` enumerates the typed rejections the adapter passes through. `attachment-disabled` is ABSENT from that list.

The adapter is pass-through, so this is a coverage gap rather than a live hole — but `attachment-disabled` is the refusal that carries emergency-off (wamn-0h0g.15.71), and it is the one status a caller actually observes when an operator switches an attachment off.

## Scope

    old:         (404, "attachment-not-found"),
    new:         (404, "attachment-not-found"),
                 (404, "attachment-disabled"),

## Boundary

Coverage, not enforcement. Enforcement is pinned host-side by wamn-0h0g.15.71.

SEPARATE OBSERVATION, unexamined and NOT this bead's: the same file maps `admission-retry` to 503 where crates/platform/runtime/src/flow_invocation.rs emits 409. That is an ingress remap nobody has adjudicated.

Filed at the wave-4 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.71 report.
close_reason: attachment-disabled covered (7da5a70d). Verified 404 against BOTH the adapter and the host rather than transcribed. PREMISE CORRECTED: the adapter performs NO mapping — rejection_response is verbatim pass-through — so the bead's 'the file maps admission-retry to 503' describes a TEST FIXTURE that pairs a status the platform never produces (the host emits 409 at four sites), not a live ingress remap. Left untouched and filed as a misleading fixture rather than a remap.

title: [SR-MVP] spike(deploy): executor-as-operator-host, if it ever gains a host identity
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.46 ratified that MVP operator management covers the wamn-host host groups and the flow-http/materializer workloads, and that **wamn-run-worker remains a plain Deployment** — it is not a wasmCloud host (no ClusterHost, no heartbeat) and pretending otherwise would be adoption theater.

## Scope

Post-MVP, and only on a named trigger: if wamn-run-worker ever gains a genuine host identity — a ClusterHost registration and a heartbeat — revisit whether it should become a chart host group under operator management.

## Boundary

NOT MVP work and not to be picked up speculatively. The trigger is the executor acquiring host identity, not a calendar date.

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16.
notes: OWNER RULING 2026-08-17: DEFERRED, NOT CLOSED. This is a well-formed trigger bead whose VALUE IS THE TRIGGER -- wamn-run-worker acquiring a genuine host identity (a ClusterHost registration and a heartbeat). Closing would destroy the tripwire; sitting in bd ready is noise. Deferred is the correct third state. Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.46 stands: the run-worker remains a plain Deployment and pretending otherwise would be adoption theater. Revisit ONLY on the named trigger, never on a date.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(catalog): catalog_version has four different widths
description:
## Why

The same value is `u32` in ReleaseId, `i32` in InvocationTarget (crates/execution/run-state/src/invocation.rs), `u64` in RouteDefinition (components/ingress/flow-http/src/lib.rs:61), and `int` in SQL. The serving manifest chose u32, following the in-crate ReleaseId precedent, so consumers will need conversions at three boundaries.

## Scope

Pick one width and converge, or record why each boundary differs.

## Boundary

Pre-existing; surfaced by wamn-0h0g.15.61. Low priority, but every conversion is a place a release version can silently truncate.

Filed at the wamn-0h0g.15.61 close (2026-08-16, commit e38dd2a1).
close_reason: Commit 93a2a97a. Closed on the bead's second option -- recorded why each boundary differs -- plus the one real defect it warned about. PREMISE CORRECTION: there are THREE Rust widths, not four. SQL `int` IS the i32 in InvocationTarget (tokio-postgres has no other int4 decode), so the set is u32 canonical, i32 row projection, u64 frozen WIT wire. Two of the three are externally fixed, so converging to one Rust width would move the conversion, not remove it. THE REAL DEFECT: crates/schema/control/src/engine.rs was the only place in the tree narrowing this value with `as`, at three sites -- a version past i32::MAX wraps NEGATIVE and the promoted and history rows then name a DIFFERENT release. Every other crossing already uses checked TryFrom. Fixed with a named storable_version helper that stops the program rather than wrapping (a panic not an error variant, per M-PANIC-ON-BUG: versions increment by one per migration, and build_apply_plan is infallible by construction). The fourth `as i32` in that function is an operation COUNT and is left alone. Also unreported by the bead: InvocationTarget::flow_version is i32 while InvocationOutcome::flow_version is u32 in the same file. The full u32 convergence would need concurrent edits to another lane's flow_invocation.rs; the four exact edits are recorded on the bead for whoever wants it.

title: [SR-MVP] spike(exec): OCI-pull flowrunner by digest, demand-gated
description:

The middle option rejected by spike wamn-0h0g.15.4. It preserves the exact-bytes derivation guard (tests/conformance/.../effect_provider_revision.rs:1377-1450) and would decouple flowrunner from executor image rebakes, but adds a second pull channel.

## Scope

Revisit only if MVP needs per-tenant flowrunner variants or hot revision rolls without a pod restart.

## Boundary

Demand-gated. Reversing the in-image verdict also requires deleting the two conformance guards that pin the in-image shape, in the same commit.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.4 report.
close_reason: OWNER RULING 2026-08-17: CLOSED AS DEMAND-NOT-ARISEN, zero code. The bead's own trigger is answerable today and the answer is STRUCTURAL rather than circumstantial: the release model is pod-identity-based, so a release change IS a pod roll by construction. 'Hot revision roll without a pod restart' is therefore not an unarrived demand but a contradiction of the ratified model. wamn-0h0g.15.38's rotation-equals-roll posture is the same ruling wearing credentials. Spike wamn-0h0g.15.4's in-image verdict stands. THE REVERSAL PRICE TAG, kept deliberately for whoever reopens this: reversing the in-image verdict also requires DELETING THE TWO CONFORMANCE GUARDS that pin the in-image shape, in the same commit (the exact-bytes derivation guard at tests/conformance/tests/effect_provider_revision.rs and its sibling). Reopen only on a real need for per-tenant flowrunner variants.

title: [SR-MVP] perf(egress): per-request TCP/TLS handshake per credentialed effect call
description:
## Why

Every credentialed effect call opens and closes its own connection (connection_http.rs:363-389) — exactly the TIME_WAIT / ephemeral-port pressure the fork's new pooled http_client.rs was written to fix, and the fork's motivation applies to wamn verbatim under load.

## Scope

If pooling is ever wanted on the credentialed path, it must be keyed such that a connection cannot cross a credential generation. Design it against gate A's finding before implementing.

## Boundary

The per-request client IS the safety property that makes gate A pass. Do NOT add pooling as a performance fix without carrying the generation-partitioned key.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.5 report.
notes:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-25 via wamn-p94i option (a): the runner egress and causation plugin seams ARE DELETED - zero registrations, zero production callers, measured at c935b88f. THIS BEAD THEREFORE CLOSES AS DEAD-SUBJECT COVERAGE when that deletion lands, per deletion rule 9 (one commit takes the whole tail). Do not implement it. NOT STARTED.
WAVE 63 REFUTATION - THIS BEAD DOES NOT CLOSE WITH wamn-p94i, AND ITS DEPENDENCY ON IT IS REMOVED. Verified by the integrator directly against the tree.
Its subject is NOT the runner egress seam. This bead is about EVERY CREDENTIALED EFFECT CALL OPENING AND CLOSING ITS OWN CONNECTION, and that code is ALIVE: crates/platform/runtime/src/plugins/connection_http.rs execute() still calls reqwest::Client::builder() and .build() PER CALL (around :621-632; the bead's own :363-389 anchor has drifted, anchor on content). The wamn-p94i deletion did not touch it.
wamn-0h0g.15.145 and wamn-0h0g.15.146 DID close with that deletion - their subjects are gone. This one stands on its own.
UNRELATED TO THIS BEAD - IGNORE. (placeholder guard against mis-noting; no change.)

title: [SR-MVP] chore(schema): construct collation stability for the attestation constraint fingerprint
description:
## Why

The attestation constraint fingerprint's ORDER BY (deploy/sql/control-portable-store.sql:783-789) lacks the COLLATE "C" that the sibling evidence fingerprint carries at :772-773, and the evidence one is additionally guarded by a dedicated collation-stability-bypass mutant (tools/gate-mutants/control-portable-store.sh:93-95). The attestation constant is collation-independent today (verified byte-identical under C, C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8) — so the protection is accidental rather than constructed.

## Scope

Add COLLATE "C" to the attestation fingerprint ORDER BY and a matching collation-stability mutant, or record why the asymmetry is intended.

## Boundary

Nothing is broken today. Pre-existing asymmetry, surfaced by wamn-0h0g.15.8, not caused by it.

Filed at the wave-1 close (2026-08-16) from the wamn-0h0g.15.8 report.
close_reason: Commit 8e013010. COLLATE "C" added to the attestation fingerprint's ORDER BY, byte-mirroring the evidence block, and pinned as a string in control_portable_store.rs. THE REQUESTED MUTANT CANNOT EXIST, which is the finding: the nine deployment_attestations constraint definitions sort identically under C and en_US.UTF-8 (the only same-prefix pair, catalog_id/catalog_version, resolves at i<v in both), so REMOVING the collation leaves the fingerprint byte-identical, the gate passes, run_mutant reports SURVIVED, returns 1, and set -e aborts the whole run-all campaign -- the harness has no expected-survivor concept. Substituted attestation-order-stability-bypass, which appends DESC to the very ORDER BY the collation hardens and dies against the attestation-constraint-drift refusal, with an in-script comment so nobody re-adds the unkillable one. All three of the bead's cited line ranges were stale. No sha baseline touched; the DDL sha moved and is banked for .15.22.

title: [LOOP-CONSOLE] feat(ui): add the panel toggle to the palette's console group

title: [D21-DISPATCH-SERVICE] Replace the native dispatcher with a wasmCloud Service workload
description:
## Goal

Move the dispatcher effect shell to a wasmCloud Service component after its placement and credential scope are decided, while preserving PostgreSQL as sole timer and run-queue authority.

## Questions

- Which existing dispatcher loop/config/metrics behavior belongs in the thin Service shell versus wamn-run-queue or other retained pure owners?
- Which host interfaces provide project PostgreSQL, clock, logging/metrics, and optional doorbell publication with the selected scope?
- What quiesce, parity, rollback, and native-shell removal sequence avoids dual scheduling authority?

## Evidence Required

- Closed placement decision wamn-l5i9.51 and the pinned wasmCloud Service/runtime capabilities.
- Differential scheduling, cron, parked-wake, janitor, duplicate-instance, lost-doorbell, connection-bound, and fail-closed tests against the native dispatcher.
- Immutable component/deployment identities, readiness, metrics, rollback, and exact gate receipts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A thin dispatcher Service component consumes existing flow/queue/registry decisions and only the selected scoped host capabilities.
- PostgreSQL remains sole timer/run-queue/lease authority; NATS remains an optional lossy hint and Kubernetes mutation remains absent.
- Duplicate Service instances preserve deterministic IDs, claim safety, backpressure, and visible refusal at admitted bounds.
- Cutover quiesces one path, validates the exact component, and commits traffic once; rollback restores the exact prior native bundle without dual scheduling.
- Native dispatcher code, image, manifests, config, and proof reachability are removed only after component parity, and no scheduler crate or second state store is introduced.
notes: held for [SR-MVP] scope reduction (program wamn-0h0g); re-assess at program close (wamn-0h0g.1.3)

title: [D21-WAKER] Retarget the narrow wake actuator to the wasmCloud workload scale boundary
description:
## Goal

Preserve scale-to-zero wake after execution moves from a native runner Deployment to a wasmCloud WorkloadDeployment, while keeping Kubernetes as deployment authority and the waker as a narrowly justified native capability exception.

## Questions

- Which WorkloadDeployment scale subresource and identity replace the current deployments/scale target?
- What is the minimum Role/ServiceAccount permission for get/patch on only the admitted execution workloads?
- Can a future operator, HPA, KEDA, or equally narrow host capability eliminate the native actuator without granting Kubernetes credentials to general wasmCloud hosts?

## Evidence Required

- The completed run-worker Service-workload shape from wamn-l5i9.49.
- Current waker pure decision, NATS re-hint recovery, Kubernetes client, RBAC, and wakeproof evidence.
- A scale 0 to 1 proof against the actual WorkloadDeployment scale subresource plus missed-hint recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Waker maps admitted project identity to the intended WorkloadDeployment and scales only its standard Kubernetes scale subresource.
- RBAC cannot mutate unrelated Deployments, WorkloadDeployments, or other resource classes.
- Lost doorbells still recover from the PostgreSQL-authoritative dispatcher re-hint path, and wakeproof restores prior scale deterministically.
- The native exception records Kubernetes scale API access as the unavailable WASI capability and an exit condition tied to an equally narrow operator/autoscaling path.
- General wasmCloud host pods receive no Kubernetes mutation credential as a consequence of this change.

title: [PROD-DEC-UNIT-ECONOMICS] Set production deployment and tenant cost envelope
description:
## Goal

Set evidence-based production unit economics before selecting commercial plans, quotas, topology defaults, or supported scale commitments.

## Questions

- What infrastructure and operational cost applies per deployment, organization, configured project-environment, active workload, custom node, event volume, storage unit, and edge/on-premises site?
- Which costs are fixed, shared, burst-sensitive, tenant-attributable, or dominated by availability, recovery, isolation, and support obligations?
- What utilization, headroom, support, margin, and hardware or provider assumptions define viable commercial envelopes?
- How do pricing, quota, admission, and placement decisions respond when measured cost exceeds the selected envelope?

## Evidence Required

- Measured resource use from representative production-candidate hardware and provider configurations, not extrapolation from the current consumer development machine.
- Accepted production topology, cardinality, durability, isolation, availability, recovery, observability, support, and edge/on-premises requirements.
- Cost allocation and sensitivity analysis across configured versus active workloads and steady-state versus burst behavior.
- Accountable product and commercial owner decisions for plans, margins, and unsupported cases.

## Decision

Deferred by the owner during wamn-4tob.1.12. Current consumer-hardware measurements and exploratory topology shapes establish no commercial unit-economics promise.

## Alternatives Considered

Infer pricing from current development hardware; inherit cost from the existing T1-T4 topology; choose arbitrary project-count tiers; or defer until measured production candidates and product requirements exist. The owner selected deferral.

## Rationale

Cost depends on topology, activity, recovery, isolation, support, and provider assumptions that are intentionally uncommitted. Premature unit economics would turn experimental resource shapes into product constraints.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Cost drivers are measured independently for configured, active, storage, event, custom-node, regional, and edge/on-premises dimensions where relevant.
- Every commercial envelope states hardware/provider, topology, availability/recovery, isolation, utilization, headroom, operations, and support assumptions.
- Plans, quotas, admission, and placement policies trace to the accepted cost evidence.
- Consumer-development measurements are clearly separated from production-candidate evidence.
- Unsupported or uneconomic combinations are explicit.
notes:
Created from owner answer Q7 on wamn-4tob.1.12. Existing wamn-ax7 and wamn-7r2 own plans/quotas/billing implementation and should consume, not invent, this future decision. This issue is not authorized for execution now.

title: [PROD-DEC-DATA-LIFECYCLE] Define production retention and erasure contract
description:
## Goal

Define retention, legal-hold, deletion, and verifiable erasure behavior for every production data class.

## Questions

- What retention and deletion rules apply to tenant data, catalogs, runs, captures, replays, events, WAL, backups, artifacts, logs, metrics, traces, and audit records?
- How do legal holds, copies, restores, caches, replicas, and derived data affect deletion?
- What completion evidence proves erasure without silently destroying required recovery or audit material?

## Evidence Required

- Product, customer, legal, recovery, and audit requirements.
- Complete state-authority and duplication inventory.
- Retention-expiry, deletion, restore-after-delete, legal-hold, and erasure-verification tests.

## Decision

Deferred. Development makes no contractual retention or erasure claim beyond behavior explicitly implemented and tested for individual stores.

## Alternatives Considered

Uniform retention; per-data-class retention; customer-configurable policy; or no contractual lifecycle until production requirements are selected.

## Rationale

Retention and erasure cross authoritative stores, replicas, backups, event logs, observability, and replay fixtures and cannot be derived from one database policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every production data class has an explicit retention, hold, deletion, and erasure policy.
- Copies, backups, caches, derived data, and restores cannot silently resurrect erased data.
- Recovery, audit, and erasure obligations have a resolved precedence policy.
- Named executable evidence proves each lifecycle claim.

title: [PROD-DEC-AUDIT-ACCESS] Define production audit evidence and operator-access contract
description:
## Goal

Define the production contract for privileged operator access, separation of duties, break-glass actions, and customer-visible audit evidence.

## Questions

- Which human and service operators may access each client, plane, secret, database, broker, artifact, backup, and telemetry store?
- Which actions require approval, separation of duties, break-glass procedure, or customer notification?
- Which audit records must be immutable, retained, exportable, attributable, and reviewable?

## Evidence Required

- The accepted production operating model and isolation profiles.
- Privilege and administration inventory across Kubernetes, Postgres, brokers, builders, registries, object storage, and observability.
- Access, denial, break-glass, tamper, export, and review drills.

## Decision

Deferred. Development assumes general operator access and makes no production operator-containment or audit-evidence promise.

## Alternatives Considered

Single trusted operator; role-separated platform operations; customer-controlled administration; or dedicated regulated operations.

## Rationale

Operator containment and audit obligations depend on future production and regulatory profiles and must not be inferred from current RBAC or log presence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every privileged action has an authorized principal, approval path, and attributable evidence.
- Required separation of duties and break-glass behavior are explicit.
- Audit tamper resistance, retention, export, and customer visibility are stated.
- Every promised denial and audit property has executable proof.

title: [PROD-DEC-RESIDENCY] Define production data-residency and regulatory scope
description:
## Goal

Define which data-residency regions, regulatory regimes, certifications, and regulated deployment profiles the product will support.

## Questions

- Which customer data and metadata classes may be stored, processed, backed up, observed, or administered in each geography?
- Which regulatory or certification claims are contractual, target-state, or unsupported?
- Which operators, infrastructure providers, replication paths, and recovery locations may cross a residency boundary?

## Evidence Required

- Product-market and customer requirements.
- Legal and regulatory interpretation from accountable owners.
- Complete data-flow, backup, telemetry, support-access, and subprocessors inventory.

## Decision

Deferred. Development makes no residency, regulatory, or certification claim, and current dedicated or regulated labels provide no such guarantee.

## Alternatives Considered

No regulated profiles; selected regional profiles; customer-dedicated regulated profiles; or broad claims based on infrastructure location alone.

## Rationale

A topology cannot establish a regulatory contract without declared data classes, jurisdictions, operator access, and evidence obligations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Supported and unsupported geographies and regulatory profiles are explicit.
- Every stored, processed, replicated, backed-up, and observed data class has a permitted location.
- Cross-boundary operator and provider access is defined.
- Each contractual claim has named evidence and an accountable owner.

title: [PROD-DEC-CREDENTIAL-LIFECYCLE] Define production credential lifecycle and compromise response
description:
## Goal

Set the production contract for credential issuance, scope, rotation, revocation, cache convergence, break-glass use, and compromise response.

## Questions

- Which credentials are workload-, project-, organization-, environment-, cluster-, operator-, or platform-scoped?
- How are current and previous versions distributed, cached, retired, and audited?
- What bounded rotation, revocation, stale-cache, and compromise-response behavior applies to each credential class?

## Evidence Required

- The accepted production identity and isolation profiles.
- Credential inventory, distribution paths, cache behavior, and authority graph.
- Rotation, revocation, stale-reader, rollback, and compromised-key drills.

## Decision

Deferred. Development has no quantitative credential lifecycle or compromise-containment promise.

## Alternatives Considered

Static development credentials; manual production rotation; automated versioned rotation; or external identity and secret-management systems selected closer to production.

## Rationale

Selecting bounds or machinery before production identity and isolation profiles would manufacture requirements and could entrench the wrong authority model.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every production credential has one owner, scope, issuance path, rotation and revocation procedure, and maximum compromise radius.
- Stale caches and dual-key windows have explicit bounded behavior.
- Break-glass access is attributable and reversible.
- Named executable drills prove each lifecycle claim.

title: [PROD-DEC-ISOLATION-PROFILES] Define production client and infrastructure isolation profiles
description:
## Goal

Define the production isolation profiles and the infrastructure boundaries each profile may share.

## Questions

- Which runtime processes, host groups, plugins, Postgres roles or clusters, replication credentials, broker accounts, namespaces or clusters, telemetry stores, builders, registries, object stores, and encryption keys may be shared?
- Which profiles are pooled, organization-isolated, environment-isolated, dedicated, regulated, edge, on-premises, or explicitly unsupported?
- What maximum cross-client failure or compromise radius is permitted for each profile?

## Evidence Required

- Accepted customer and production deployment classes.
- Cost, scale, operational, failure-domain, and security evidence for each proposed shared boundary.
- Baseline-matched cross-client denial and failure-containment tests.

## Decision

Deferred. Current development requires client isolation at platform API boundaries but does not promise physical or credential isolation, and current topology labels confer no production security guarantee.

## Alternatives Considered

One shared production profile; progressively isolated profiles; fully dedicated profiles; or no production isolation promise until requirements are known.

## Rationale

Current database placement, namespaces, and service names do not define an end-to-end isolation domain. The target must follow later product and security requirements rather than current implementation shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every supported profile names all permitted shared authorities and maximum blast radius.
- Client isolation is proven across every platform API and shared substrate.
- Dedicated or regulated labels are used only when their complete boundary is specified and tested.
- Unsupported profiles are explicit.

title: [PROD-DEC-THREAT] Define production capability and adversary model
description:
## Goal

Define the production trust and adversary model from the platform APIs and capabilities each actor or workload can access.

## Questions

- Which callers, tenants, authors, workloads, maintainers, operators, and infrastructure providers are mutually untrusted or trusted?
- Which WIT, WASI, HTTP, SQL, broker, filesystem, socket, secret, build, signing, and deployment capabilities can each principal access?
- What compromise radius and protection claims apply when a guest, host, plugin, credential, operator, or infrastructure provider is compromised?

## Evidence Required

- The accepted production deployment profiles and identity model.
- A complete platform-interface and capability inventory tied to runtime enforcement.
- Targeted abuse and cross-boundary tests for every claimed denial.

## Decision

Deferred. Development currently requires client isolation as a correctness property at narrowly exposed platform and WASI interfaces, but makes no broader trust or adversary-model promise.

## Alternatives Considered

Define a detailed development threat model now; infer trust from current topology; or defer the production model while preserving the current capability-boundary evidence. The owner selected the final option.

## Rationale

The owner considers detailed trust modeling premature. The useful present architectural fact is which explicit capabilities are exposed, not an invented classification of future actors.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every supported production actor and workload has an explicit trust classification.
- Every accessible platform capability and authority escalation path is mapped.
- Every claimed isolation boundary has a stated compromise radius and executable evidence.
- No production security property is inferred solely from a WASI boundary, resource name, namespace, or deployment label.

title: [SR25] CDC reader public API leaks pg_walstream cancellation type
description:
## Goal

Keep the pg_walstream fork cancellation primitive inside the CDC adapter while preserving deterministic service shutdown for binaries, tests, and gates.

## Questions

- Should the local boundary be an opaque shutdown handle, owned receiver, or cancellation future?
- Which side owns cancellation, completion, and repeated-shutdown semantics?
- Can every consumer stop the production reader without depending directly on the fork?

## Evidence Required

- Source inventory of wamn_cdc_reader::run_with_token and every consumer of pg_walstream::CancellationToken.
- Dependency evidence showing gates import pg_walstream solely for the leaked cancellation type.
- Shutdown tests for cancellation before start, during open/read/publish, repeated cancellation, and normal completion.
- A dependency check proving consumers no longer require the fork for shutdown.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No public wamn-cdc-reader API exposes a pg_walstream control type.
- The reader adapter alone translates the local shutdown contract to the fork primitive.

title: [SR24] Mounted runtime configuration contracts are unversioned and inconsistent
description:
## Goal

Give independently mutable dispatcher, Postgres-plugin, and credential mounted JSON formats explicit ownership and safe image/config compatibility behavior.

## Questions

- Does each format require a version discriminator, or must image and configuration change atomically?
- Which unknown, missing, wrong-type, and invalid optional values are accepted, defaulted, or refused?
- How are rotation, rollback, cache refresh, and secret data distinguished from structural configuration?

## Evidence Required

- Source inventory for dispatcher projects.json, the Postgres project map, and the credential vault map, including all writers and consumers.
- Old-image/new-config and new-image/old-config fixtures for each format.
- Negative cases for unknown, missing, wrong-type, and invalid optional fields.
- Deployment evidence for how ConfigMap/Secret updates reach and refresh running processes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each mounted format has one canonical owner, version or atomic-rollout rule, and declared forward/backward compatibility policy.
- Invalid values cannot silently become permissive defaults or retain stale security-relevant state.
- Old/new fixture matrices prove every declared accepted and refused combination.
- Rotation and rollback preserve tenant isolation and produce actionable refusal evidence.
notes:
DEC-UPGRADE HANDOFF 2026-07-23: N.7 selects atomic image/config rollout for development. Each mounted config must be immutably attributable to the release bundle and have explicit missing/unknown/wrong-type refusal behavior; a concurrent old/new config compatibility window is not required.

title: [SR23] wamn:runner WIT has no canonical source or coherence guard
description:
## Goal

Make the trusted host-to-flowrunner control ABI a single owned contract whose vendored copies cannot drift silently.

## Questions

- Which execution-contract package owns wamn:runner@0.1.0?
- Should consumers be generated from one source or byte-compared against a checked canonical file?
- Is host/flowrunner compatibility intentionally same-release only, or must mixed versions be supported?

## Evidence Required

- Exhaustive inventory of every wamn:runner package copy and consumer.
- Current equality evidence for crates/wamn-host/wit/deps/wamn-runner/package.wit and components/flowrunner/wit/deps/wamn-runner/package.wit.
- A discovery-based negative mutation proving a one-sided declaration change fails the named guard.
- Release-policy evidence aligned with wamn-4tob.1.16.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One canonical source and owner are explicit.
- Every repository copy is discovered automatically and generated or byte-compared against that source.
- Add, remove, or change mutations on either side fail a named test.
- The same-release or mixed-version compatibility policy is documented and enforced at rollout.
notes:
DEC-UPGRADE HANDOFF 2026-07-23: N.7 selects a same-release-only atomic host/runner bundle for development; no mixed-version wamn:runner ABI is promised. Implement one canonical WIT source, exhaustive copy discovery, and a one-sided-edit guard. Persisted trusted-executor identity remains the distinct High finding R53/wamn-2jkm.99.

This bead remains valid as the tuning lever (the ~160ms floor IS paced by fetch_ms and the per-registration consumer topology) but it is NOT the cliff the local shape suggested — priority stays P3, scope tilts toward the fetch_ms/batch sweep before any parallel-fetch redesign.

title: [EVT-TOAST-COND] a condition over an unchanged out-of-line TOAST column reads JMESPath null on the NEW image — guard or document
description: pgoutput omits unchanged out-of-line TOAST columns from the NEW image map (a real NULL is present as null — distinguishable, l5i9.17 DESIGN). The l5i9.31 old-absent guard keys on whole-old-image absence only, so a condition referencing new.<toasted-col> (or comparing new vs old on a column that was TOASTed and unchanged) silently evaluates that reference as JMESPath null instead of the actual stored value — condition-false where the truth may be condition-true. Options: detect referenced-but-absent NEW columns the same per-event way (cannot-evaluate refusal), or document the authoring constraint (conditions must not reference large/TOAST-able columns). Evidence: poc/cdc1 TOAST test; the FULL old image is complete (FULL logs the whole old row), so the gap is NEW-side only.
notes:
C-CDC RI axis quantified the TOAST-old-image cost this bead tracks (wamn-l5i9.14, 2026-07-20, docs/ceilings.md § C-CDC (c)): under REPLICA IDENTITY FULL a NON-TOAST-column update on a 6KiB-TOAST row writes the flattened UNCHANGED old image into WAL — 320B -> 6560B per op, a 20x multiplier (the decoded envelope still omits the unchanged column; the WAL pays anyway). Wide delete +93 percent, wide TOAST-rewrite update +46 percent, narrow ops +50-80B. Raw: ccdc-ri.csv (per-op medians, FPI-excluded).

title: [R26] resume folds error-routed records through the Success arm — step_seq/result diverge from live execution

Resumed runs count error-routed nodes in step_seq (documented as 'the checkpoint key ... compared on resume', engine.rs:123-126) and momentarily assign the error payload to result; observable-result divergence gated by flow-version skew. FIX: detect port==ERROR_PORT during replay and route without touching result/step_seq, or drop the compared-on-resume claim. VERIFY: resumed error-routed run's step_seq+result equal the live run's.
close_reason: R26: resume replays an ERROR_PORT record via the shared route_error helper (clear current + visits bump + enqueue error successors) instead of apply(Success) — step_seq and result untouched, exactly live error_or_fail parity; the helper is shared by live and replay so they cannot drift. Named tests: resumed_error_routed_run_matches_live_step_seq_and_result (live==resumed step_seq+result), resume_partial_after_error_route_leaves_step_seq_zero_and_null_result, resume_error_route_still_advances_the_occurrence (b@1 key r1:b:1 — occurrence semantics preserved through the new path). title: [R25] idempotency_key is run_id:node — identical across merge/loop visits; external dedupe silently drops a legitimate second execution
description: docs/findings.md s2 R25 (Wave-1 review, Low). build_dispatch (engine.rs:355-369) sets idempotency_key=format!("{run_id}:{node}") — stable across retries (documented) but ALSO across distinct visits of a fan-in/loop node. On resume, a merge node whose first arrival committed is re-dispatched for its second arrival with the SAME key; an external system honoring idempotency headers dedupes the distinct execution away. FIX: include visit occurrence (run:node:occurrence) so distinct arrivals differ while retries of one arrival keep theirs. Shares the occurrence plumbing with R24 (wamn-2jkm R24 bead).
close_reason: R25: idempotency_key is now run:node:occurrence (build_dispatch reuses the R24 visit counter). Retries of one visit keep their key (trailing :0 pinned in retryable_retries_then_succeeds_with_stable_idempotency_key); distinct merge arrivals differ (r1:m:0 vs r1:m:1); a RESUMED outstanding visit gets the same key it would have live (r1:d:1 — replay rebuilds visits, so no collision with the recorded first execution). Mutant killed: key reverted to run:node -> merge_visits_carry_distinct_occurrences + resume_diamond_killed_mid_merge + retryable_retries all FAIL by name. Guest rebuilt (key rides the custom-node envelope + SDK RunContext).

title: [R15] parked_due_sql lacks the partition guard — wake scan pins cadence at min behind a wedged partition

Behind a D20 blocking wedge this is PERMANENT (the janitor is exempt from reaping a blocking head by design): one wedged key holds the whole project dispatcher at the 250 ms floor and defeats zero-continuous-polling. FIX: add the guard, or exclude partitioned wakes from found_work() — cadence must reflect ACTIONABLE work.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-07-20, commit 522cc6e (Lane B 44b4bca cherry-picked; cleanup wave). parked_due_sql gains the partition_key IS NULL guard, mirroring global_claim_cte verbatim (Option A, not a found_work exclusion). Design-care resolved first: partitioned runs are claimed ONLY via acquire_partitions_sql + claim_partition_head_sql, driven by the run-worker's own poll-with-backoff reconcile independent of doorbell hints — so excluding partitioned rows from the dispatcher wake scan creates no never-woken parks; a due partitioned park wakes on the run-worker cadence (the same backstop as any lost hint). A follower behind a wedged D20 blocking head can no longer pin found_work/next_interval at the 250ms floor. Gates: SQL pin asserts the guard; live suite extended with the wedge-cadence scenario (wedged follower NOT woken / unpartitioned due park wakes / partitioned park still claimable via its path) — re-run PASS in the MAIN tree (38 live tests) vs throwaway PG. title: [D21-DISPATCH] Select dispatcher Service-workload placement and credential scope
description:
## Goal

Select the dispatcher Service-workload placement and credential scope from measured development topology rather than assuming a per-org, per-project, or shared unit.

## Questions

- Which shared, per-org, per-environment, or bounded-cell placement keeps credential, connection, and failure scope acceptable for measured admitted load?
- Which PostgreSQL and doorbell identities are required at that placement, and can they remain client-scoped without multiplying unbounded connections?
- Which measurement would require revisiting the selected placement?

## Evidence Required

- Current dispatcher project/config/credential topology, connection counts, two-replica failure behavior, and measured admitted project cardinality.
- Candidate Service-workload placement and host-interface scopes on the pinned operator.
- Cross-client negative evidence and a failure/blast-radius comparison for each surviving candidate.

## Rationale

STR9 selects a wasmCloud Service as the target dispatcher packaging, but packaging does not determine workload cardinality or credential scope. Choosing shared, per-org, or per-environment placement before development measurements would invent a production topology and could unnecessarily broaden credentials or multiply PostgreSQL connections. This decision therefore remains open until measured evidence can select the narrowest viable development placement.

## Alternatives Considered

- Shared Service workload with bounded client-scoped credentials.
- Per-organization Service workloads.
- Per-environment Service workloads.
- Bounded cells that admit a measured maximum set of clients.
- Retaining the native dispatcher permanently; rejected as the target because no concrete capability gap currently requires a native exception.

## Acceptance Criteria

- One development placement and credential-scope rule is selected with measured cardinality, connection, failure, and isolation evidence.
- PostgreSQL remains sole timer/run-queue authority and NATS remains an optional lossy wake hint.
- Unsupported cardinality or credential combinations fail closed visibly rather than falling back to a broader identity.
- The decision records revisit triggers and makes no production, regional, or fixed per-org/per-project topology promise.
- Implementation is owned separately by wamn-l5i9.71.
notes:
STR9 TARGET 2026-07-24: component Service packaging is selected by wamn-4tob.1.39/STR9. This issue now decides measured placement and performs the eventual migration; the old per-org wording was a hypothesis, not a target. R45 isolation and the immutable release/readiness owners remain correctness constraints and are not solved by changing packaging.
CORRECTION 2026-07-24: this decision selects placement and credential scope only. The component-Service migration is implemented by wamn-l5i9.71.

title: [POC-F3] Scale-to-zero / parked-project wake proof for the deployed runner
description: POC-F3 names 'parked-project wake (project idles overnight - scale-to-zero proof)'. The dispatcher (a52) fires cron on schedule regardless of runner replica count, enqueuing to run_queue. A runner scaled to zero must wake / scale up to drain the queued run. Today the runner Deployment (fqg.8) runs a fixed replica count; there is NO gated proof that a runner scaled to zero comes up (or is woken) and drains a cron-enqueued run. This is deployment topology (HPA/KEDA-on-queue-depth or a doorbell-driven wake), not a flow-engine capability. Need: a proof that a parked (0-replica) runner drains a cron-fired run within a bounded window. Cross-ref a52 (dispatcher idle->fire), fqg.8 (runner Deployment), the NATS doorbell (5.14).
acceptance_criteria: With the runner at 0 replicas, a dispatcher cron fire enqueues a run; the runner scales up / is woken and drives it to completion within a bounded window; a gate asserts it.
notes: Raised by POC-F3 (wamn-24i) scoping 2026-07-16. P3: honest deployment-topology nicety, not a core capability - F3 can document this as a v1 caveat (a52 already shows idle->fire); this bead is the real proof that removes the caveat.
close_reason: [POC-F3] Scale-to-zero wake proof SHIPPED + PROVEN IN-CLUSTER (commit 004d720, pushed). Topology: new crates/wamn-waker minimal actuator Deployment (doorbell wamn.doorbell.<tenant> -> k8s scale 0->1 via merge-patch on deployments/scale; reqwest/rustls already in-tree via oci-client, cluster-CA-only trust; NATS required, no polling — the dispatcher parked_due re-hint is the retry; never scales down). deploy/platform/waker.yaml (SA+Role get/patch deployments+scale — the ONE k8s-privileged component; dispatcher/runner no-k8s posture preserved; KEDA rejected as third-party infra = owner decision). Gate of record wakeproof (wamn-gates subcommand + deploy/gates/wakeproof-job.yaml): park runner 0 -> seed every-second cron flow -> DISTINCT dispatcher-fires phase (~40s, isolates projects-config failure from wake failure) -> completion + observed-replicas>0 within 120s -> zero-residue teardown + scale restore (floored at 1). IN-CLUSTER PASS 2026-07-21 all 6 phases; waker log pins actuation 'scaled parked runner up from=0 to=1' ~12s after deploy. LIVE WIRING FIX (per-env Secret, not manifest-managed): wamn-dispatch-projects gained runner-demo entry (demo-tenant/wamn_runner_demo) alongside f1 — the deployed dispatcher swept ONLY f1 before, so no cron could ever reach the runner's project; dispatcher rolled, projects=2, existing demo flows all manual-trigger (verified side-effect-free). Tests: 6 waker decision tests + wakeproof cron-flow drift guard; mutant (decide() ==0 -> !=0) killed by NAMED test decide_skips_an_already_awake_deployment, sha256-verified restore. Main-tree re-verify green (52+6+12). Deferrals filed: wamn-fqg.35 (idle->0 park automation), .36 (projects-file config shape), .37 (subscribe-only NATS identity), .38 (probes + scale-conflict backoff). title: Optimize Docker builds: cache cargo registry+git so gates/host rebuilds don't re-fetch wasmtime
description: The Dockerfile builder stage runs a plain 'cargo build --release -p wamn-host -p wamn-gates' with NO BuildKit cargo cache mount (Dockerfile:22). Any crates/ change busts the COPY+build layer, so the fresh RUN re-fetches ALL git deps from scratch inside the isolated build container (it can't see the host ~/.cargo) — including the large bytecodealliance/wasmtime git repo. This makes every gates/host rebuild slow and prone to transient git-fetch stalls (observed 2026-07-16 during wamn-ojm.3: the wasmtime fetch hung with 0 disk writes / idle cargo, requiring a kill+retry). Fix: add --mount=type=cache for /usr/local/cargo/registry and /usr/local/cargo/git (and optionally a target cache) to the builder RUN, so deps are fetched once and reused across builds. Verify a crates/-only change rebuilds without re-fetching wasmtime. Infra/tooling change; deferred out of ojm.3 scope per user (2026-07-16).
close_reason: Shipped 2026-07-20, commit f07f95b (Lane C c203251 cherry-picked; cleanup wave). Builder RUN (single stage shared by all six image targets) gains --mount=type=cache for /usr/local/cargo/registry + /usr/local/cargo/git (CARGO_HOME confirmed empirically in rust:1.97-trixie); no target/ cache by design (later stages COPY binaries out of target/release). Two-build verification (--target ctl): build A cold 1211s populating the cache (8 fetch lines incl. wasmtime + 4 wasm submodules); build B after a crates/ change 1171s with ZERO fetch/update lines — the wasmtime re-fetch (the historical ~20min stall class) is eliminated; wall delta modest because the busted layer still recompiles (no target cache) and the host was under concurrent lane build load. Probe images removed, buildkit cache retained. The lane-B engine rebake rides this Dockerfile.

title: [2.1] wamn:postgres WIT drift guard: assert the 6 vendored copies match docs/wamn-postgres.wit (mirror wit_coherence.rs)
description: GAP (from the 2026-07-15 external architecture review, the one confirmed net-new finding). The frozen wamn:postgres 0.1.0 contract is vendored into SIX copies with NO automated coherence test: components/api-gateway, components/fixtures/pgprobe, components/flowrunner, components/poc-webhook-f1, crates/wamn-host/wit/deps/wamn-postgres, crates/wamn-node-guest/wit-caps/deps/wamn-postgres — each a package.wit — plus the source of truth docs/wamn-postgres.wit. The existing drift guard crates/wamn-node-sdk/tests/wit_coherence.rs covers the wamn:NODE contract ONLY; nothing guards the postgres copies (the repo structure-review SR7 overstates this: it claims wit_coherence drift-guards all vendored WIT — it does not). RISK: a silent edit to one copy (a clarifying comment, a future 0.1.x additive change applied unevenly) drifts a guest, which then fails at INSTANTIATION with a cryptic linker error (component imports instance wamn:postgres/client@0.1.0, but a matching implementation was not found in the linker) — the exact class the Rust type system cannot catch. LOW PRIORITY: the contract is frozen and rarely changes, so drift is unlikely near-term — this is cheap hygiene (SR7 was tagged Optional, do opportunistically).

title: wamn-host: declare its own tokio features (macros, rt-multi-thread, signal)
description: External review (Rust best practices / tokio feature fragility). crates/wamn-host/Cargo.toml:20 declares tokio features=[time,fs,net,io-util,rt,sync], but main.rs uses #[tokio::main] (needs macros + rt-multi-thread) and dispatch.rs uses tokio::signal::unix (needs signal). It compiles today only because the workspace tokio declaration (root Cargo.toml:24 = [rt-multi-thread, macros, signal]) contributes those features and cargo unifies them -- a workspace-level trim would silently break wamn-host. Add macros, rt-multi-thread, signal to wamn-host's OWN feature list so the crate declares what it uses. Latent fragility, not a current bug.
close_reason: wamn-host now declares the tokio features it directly uses: added macros + rt-multi-thread (#[tokio::main]) and signal (tokio::signal::unix/ctrl_c in main.rs/dispatch.rs/host.rs). A/B proof (simulated workspace-root tokio trim): with the fix wamn-host builds self-sufficiently (A); the features are also transitively provided by wash-runtime, so it was not a current bug (matches the bead) — declare-what-you-use hygiene against a workspace/dep trim. Cargo.lock unchanged.

title: wamn-api: ApiError::message -> Cow<'static,str> (thiserror evaluated + declined)
description:
External review #6/#7 (Low). Change ApiError::message() from `-> String` to `-> Cow<'static, str>` so the static-message variants (PayloadRequired / MethodNotAllowed / NotFound) do not allocate; the format!/clone variants stay Cow::Owned. to_json's json!({"message": ...}) works via serde_json's From<Cow<str>>. KEEP the hand-rolled Display/Error. Check no external caller expects an owned String from message() (Display + to_json are the internal callers).

THISERROR DECLINED (recorded here, deliberately NOT done): ApiError variants carry Strings, not inner errors, so #[from]/source() gain nothing; deriving thiserror::Error would replace the composite Display "{status} [{code}] {message}" with per-variant messages (a behavior change) for zero benefit; and SR6 keeps error enums hand-rolled (mirroring WIT variants). If a future variant wraps a real error, revisit. ProvisionError is likewise data-carrying (no chaining) -- no thiserror there either.
close_reason: ApiError::message() now returns Cow<'static,str>: static-message variants (PayloadRequired/MethodNotAllowed/NotFound) borrow (no allocation), format!/clone variants own. Display/to_json (via serde_json From<Cow>) and the one external caller (classify_api -> .into_owned()) updated. Hand-rolled Display/Error kept; thiserror declined per the recorded rationale. Unit test pins borrow-vs-own; 2 mutants killed.

- classify_api (wamn-nodes) already has a `_ =>` arm on ApiError (safe).
Method/ExpandDir external uses are constructions (from_http) or same-crate matches -> not affected. Same-crate matches inside wamn-api (router compile) are unaffected by non_exhaustive.

title: [9.2] Thread a per-run traceparent to host-invoked guests (flowrunner)
description: 9.2 ships host-enforced outbound traceparent injection + the SDK http-request-node forward. The flowrunner guest is host-invoked via an exported run() (no inbound HTTP request), so it has no header to source RunContext.traceparent from — it stays None (its outbound calls are still traced by the host inject). To surface a per-run traceparent to a host-invoked guest, the queue/dispatch path must carry one (e.g. the write-ahead run row / dispatch persists the active trace context; ties into fqg.4 guest-self-claim). Then flowrunner sets RunContext.traceparent and its SDK nodes forward it. Parent: E9 wamn-7ok.

title: [2.5] migration engine: residue janitor + apply journal for non-txn steps (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY)
description: wamn-d8u v1 applies the whole plan in ONE transaction, so the wamn-ddl name-freeing preamble leaves zero wamn_mig_drop_* residue (R9c). When the engine grows a non-transactional step (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a txn block), it must add (a) a residue janitor that sweeps wamn_mig_drop_* older than a grace with no in-flight migration, and (b) an apply journal to resume/repair a partially-applied plan. v1 emits no such step. Design: docs/migration-engine.md (One-transaction invariant).

title: [SR5] CronError(String) -> structured variants (ride the next dispatcher touch)
description: docs/structure-review.md SR5. CronError(pub String) in wamn-run-queue cron.rs is the one stringly-typed error in the workspace (every other error is a structured enum folded mechanically). FACTS (gathered pre-compact):
- CronError(pub String) @ cron.rs:31; Display 'cron: {0}' @ :33; impl Error @ :39; re-exported lib.rs:63 (stays pub).
- FOUR construction sites, ALL in cron.rs, ALL parse/eval (cron.rs is PURE, no I/O): (1) parse() :42 Cron::from_str err = INVALID-EXPRESSION; (2) to_dt() :47 from_timestamp_millis None = OUT-OF-RANGE-INSTANT; (3) next_fire() :56 find_next_occurrence err = NO-OCCURRENCE; (4) due_tick() :83 find_previous_occurrence err = NO-OCCURRENCE.
- CONSUMERS use Display or .is_err() ONLY, NO string-match anywhere: dispatch.rs:445-450 quarantines ANY err via 'error = %e' (Display) into p.bad_schedules; dispatch.rs:470 next_fire(..).ok(); dispatchbench '.is_err()' hits are EPOCH TRAPS not CronError; tests/queue.rs .is_err() @ 567/609/613/614. => Display MUST be preserved (log shape) but there is NO variant match to migrate.

IMPLEMENTATION: enum CronError derive(Debug,Clone,PartialEq,Eq): InvalidExpression{schedule:String,detail:String} (parse); OutOfRangeInstant{ms:Millis} (to_dt); NoOccurrence{schedule:String,detail:String} (next_fire + due_tick). Display preserves current strings: InvalidExpression->'cron: bad schedule {schedule:?}: {detail}', OutOfRangeInstant->'cron: out-of-range instant {ms}', NoOccurrence->'cron: no occurrence for {schedule:?}: {detail}' (next_fire's 'no next fire' wording collapses into NoOccurrence — fine). detail = e.to_string().

title: [5.8/4.4] Reject webhook path collisions at flow registration
description: Two ACTIVE flows can declare sync-webhook triggers on the SAME path; the webhook-entry ingress route pick is deterministic (ORDER BY flow_id, added in wamn-067) but arbitrary. Enforce single-active-flow-per-webhook-path at registration: publish-catalog register_flow (crates/wamn-host/src/publish_catalog.rs) should scan the tenant's other active flows' graph_json webhook paths and bail on collision; optionally add an expression partial-unique index on (tenant_id, graph_json->'trigger'->>'path') WHERE active AND trigger type webhook in deploy/flows.sql. Found during wamn-067 review; the editor (5.8) and gateway routing (4.4) own the long-term policy.
notes:
RESUME SCOUTING (2026-07-12, pre-compaction, verified against tip 8804bc2 — all facts from code I wrote this session):

WHAT EXISTS: (1) publish_catalog::register_flow (crates/wamn-host/src/publish_catalog.rs, ~:370-420): parses+validates the graph, then TWO client.execute calls NOT in a transaction — UPDATE flows SET active=false WHERE tenant_id=$1 AND flow_id=$2 (prior versions of the SAME flow only), then INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (tenant,flow_id,version) DO UPDATE SET graph_json, active=true. Superuser conn => explicit tenant predicates. (2) The ingress (components/webhook-entry/src/lib.rs load_active_flows) reads 'SELECT graph_json::text FROM flows WHERE active ORDER BY flow_id' and .find()s the first Trigger::Webhook{sync:true, path:Some(p)} == request path — deterministic but ARBITRARY on collision (the ORDER BY was the wamn-067 stopgap). (3) deploy/flows.sql: wamn_run.flows (tenant_id, flow_id, version, active, graph_json, created_at, updated_at; PK (tenant,flow_id,version); partial index flows_active ON (tenant,flow_id) WHERE active; FORCE RLS). Trigger JSON shape: {"type":"webhook","sync":true,"path":"/receipts"} under graph_json->'trigger'. (4) f1bench provision() already calls register_flow TWICE (same flow — deactivate/reactivate arms covered) + asserts one active row.

PLAN (the review verifier's 'do both' recommendation, already in the description): (a) DB constraint in deploy/flows.sql — CREATE UNIQUE INDEX flows_active_webhook_path ON wamn_run.flows (tenant_id, (graph_json->'trigger'->>'path')) WHERE active AND graph_json->'trigger'->>'type' = 'webhook' AND graph_json->'trigger'->>'path' IS NOT NULL — race-proof, rewritten per-schema by the existing publish-catalog --runstate include_str path automatically. (b) register_flow friendly pre-check: if the new graph's trigger is Webhook with Some(path), SELECT other ACTIVE flows for the tenant, parse graphs (skip unparseable), bail with a named error on path collision BEFORE any write. title: [5.14] Budget-spent row with NULL lease is invisible to claim, wake scan, AND janitor (wedged run)
description:
Pre-existing corner, surfaced while verifying wamn-fqg.5 (crash-evidence attempts): a run_queue row with attempts >= max_attempts and lease_expires_at IS NULL is unreachable by every mechanism. claim_batch_sql / claim_partition_head_sql skip it (attempts < max_attempts guard -> ClaimState::Exhausted); parked_due_sql filters attempts < max_attempts so the dispatcher never hints it; janitor_sweep_sql requires lease_expires_at IS NOT NULL (expired past grace) so it is never retired to infrastructure-failure. The run wedges silently: runs.status stays 'running'/'dispatched' forever, the queue row never drains, and (if partitioned) it permanently blocks its partition head.

How the state arises: the run takes its FINAL budgeted expired-lease reclaim (attempts becomes max_attempts), the resuming runner is alive and PARKS (a delay node / backoff) — park_sql releases the lease. At wake the row is Exhausted-with-NULL-lease. Under the pre-fqg.5 count-every-claim semantics this same wedge was the actual failure mode of the park-loop bug (R1's 'janitor retires it' was imprecise — with a NULL lease the janitor never fires either); post-fqg.5 it needs max_attempts real crashes followed by a park, so it is rare but still a liveness hole.

Candidate fixes (design open): (a) janitor gains a second disjunct for lease-NULL budget-spent rows older than some horizon (needs a due-ness/staleness signal — enqueued_at or available_at + grace); (b) the claim predicate allows a lease-NULL row regardless of attempts (parking proved the last owner was alive, so the budget argument does not apply — but this makes max_attempts never terminal for park-loop crash cycles); (c) 5.11/5.12 policy seam: an operator-visible 'wedged' state + cancel. Whichever lands must keep the fqg.5 invariant (parks are free) and the janitor completion-race guard intact.

Relates to wamn-fqg.5 (crash-evidence attempts), wamn-1d4 [5.11] (ordering/wedge policy), wamn-dq5 [5.12] (cancel).

title: [3.1] Reserve the wamn_ identifier prefix at catalog validation
description:
wamn-ddl's TempNameCollision (lib.rs:59-62, raised at emit.rs:444-447) conservatively rejects a plan whose synthesized aside name (wamn_mig_drop_<table>) collides with any relation across both catalog versions — correct, but it means a user who names an entity wamn_mig_drop_orders learns the rule at MIGRATION-COMPILE time, and only when a colliding evolution happens to occur. Verified: wamn-catalog validation (validate.rs) checks only empty-name / uniqueness / field-resolution — no reserved-prefix rule exists; the only reserved names anywhere are wamn-ddl's id/tenant_id column reservations (lib.rs:78). A user CAN name an entity/field/index/constraint wamn_anything today.

One validation rule + one test; document the reserved prefix in the schema-designer naming rules (docs/catalog-model.md). Rides the next 3.1 catalog-validation touch. title: [3.2] Empty-string tenant GUC matches only by accident: NULLIF the floor tenant read + CHECK (tenant_id <> '')
description:
Postgres resets a custom GUC to the EMPTY STRING (not NULL) once SET LOCAL scope ends, so an idle pooled connection carries app.tenant = ''. Every tenant floor policy compares tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant', true) WITHOUT NULLIF — verified in the 3.2 emitted floor (crates/wamn-ddl/src/emit.rs:137-140) AND all four hand-written schemas (deploy/run-state.sql:85-86,136-137; deploy/run-queue.sql:65-66,92-93,135-136; deploy/catalog-schema.sql all 8 policies; deploy/postgres-init.sql all 9). '' matches nothing ONLY while no row ever has tenant_id = '' — an invariant NOTHING enforces (no CHECK anywhere; emit.rs:114 emits tenant_id text NOT NULL only). Today it holds by construction (the plugin's valid_tenant rejects empty; WITH CHECK forces claim equality for wamn_app writes), but a superuser/BYPASSRLS write path (provisioning, migrations, dispatcher admin URLs, catalog snapshot publishing) could land a ''-tenant row that an idle claimless connection would then SEE. docs/p0-results.md:194-198 ("empty-claim reset is safe") documents the invariant-dependent version — accidentally-match-nothing, not structurally-match-nothing.

FIX (defense-in-depth, structural): (1) emit tenant_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant', true), '') in the 3.2 floor template (USING + WITH CHECK) and mirror in the four deploy/*.sql schemas — NULL comparison matches no row, ever, including a hypothetical ''-tenant row; (2) belt-and-braces CHECK (tenant_id <> '') on tenant-scoped tables (floor emission + hand-written schemas); (3) wamn-seed compile(dataset, catalog, tenant) rejects empty/whitespace tenant (crates/wamn-seed/src/emit.rs:49 currently passes any &str straight into quote_literal/row_id).

CORRECTION vs the review: R5a aimed the fix at wamn-rls/src/compile.rs — MISATTRIBUTED. That crate emits only role/user policies and already guards its claim reads (NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::uuid at :53-56; COALESCE(current_setting('app.role', true), '') at :46-49); it has no tenant read at all. And wamn-catalog has no tenant concept, so "catalog validation rejects empty tenant_id" has no home there — the seed-compile check (3) is the real belt-and-braces spot.

VERIFY: extend the S2 RLS gate with an empty-claim pass — superuser-seed a ''-tenant row, query on a connection with claims deliberately unset, assert zero rows BOTH before and after the template change (documenting the invariant->structural conversion). Rides the next wamn-ddl/schema touch. External review R5a (docs/review-findings.md § R5), corrected + verified at tip 873c3d8.
