title: [3.2] Reference->Uuid retype never drops the emitted FK constraint (later DROP of the target table fails 2BP01)
description: Confirmed live (PG 18) by the wamn-k56 adversarial review; PRE-EXISTING (not from the k56 ordering fix). v1{x:'audit'; y:'log' with field aref=Reference{x}} -> v2{x removed; y.aref retyped to Uuid, same field id}: the plan emits only ALTER TABLE "log" ALTER COLUMN "aref" TYPE uuid USING "aref"::uuid, then DROP TABLE "audit" — but the FK constraint log_aref_fkey (synthesized by fk_op from the reference field, never modeled as a catalog constraint) survives the retype, so the drop fails: 2BP01 'constraint log_aref_fkey on table log depends on table audit' and the one-txn apply rolls back. Fix: emit_column_alters (crates/wamn-ddl/src/emit.rs) should emit ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT <t>_<f>_fkey when type_changed leaves Reference (and conversely ADD the FK when a retype ENTERS Reference). Same unwind-completeness family as wamn-k56. Design: docs/ddl-compiler.md.
close_reason: Fixed: emit_column_alters now maintains the reference-field FK lifecycle across a retype. A reference field's FK (<table>_<field>_fkey) is synthesized by fk_op and never modeled as a catalog constraint, so ALTER COLUMN TYPE did not carry it: a Reference->Uuid retype left log_aref_fkey behind, and a later DROP TABLE of the (removed) target failed 2BP01. Fix uses type_changed's Option<(old,new)> — when the type LEAVES Reference, emit ALTER TABLE ... DROP CONSTRAINT before the retype (drops by the pre-rename field name if the same bump renames it); when it ENTERS Reference, emit fk_op ADD CONSTRAINT after the retype; a Reference re-pointed at a new target does both. Added a shared fk_constraint_name() helper (fk_op refactored onto it) + drop_reference_fk_op(). Tests: 3 units (Reference->Uuid drop-before-DROP-TABLE, Uuid->Reference add-after-retype, Reference->Reference re-point drop+add) + a dedicated live-apply gate (own schema wamn_ddl_retype_fk_test, 2 scenarios: retype-away-drops-target succeeds [was 2BP01] with the referencing row surviving; retype-into-Reference adds a REAL enforcing FK proven by a rejected bogus insert). TWO mutants killed (neuter drop -> 3 drop-tests fail incl live 2BP01; neuter add -> 3 add-tests fail incl live foreign_key_violation-expected), each killed by exactly its half. cargo test/clippy/fmt -p wamn-ddl green (39 tests); consumer regressions (schema/rls/seed/catalog) green. docs/ddl-compiler.md documents the retype FK lifecycle + Verification section updated (5 live gates). Pure-crate, no docker/in-cluster. Residual (broader, out of scope): a table renamed in a PRIOR bump leaves the synthesized FK name reflecting the older table prefix — the same synthesized-name-drift family, unsolvable from (old,new) alone.

title: [3.2/4.1] Exclude NaN/infinity special values from exact-decimal and timestamp columns

title: [4.1] PUT full-replace semantics (v1 treats PUT as partial)
description: The REST gateway v1 (wamn-api) treats PUT identically to PATCH (partial update of only the provided fields). Implement true PUT semantics: a full replace where every writable non-defaulted field must be present and omitted nullable fields are reset to NULL/their default, distinct from PATCH's partial merge. Small refinement in crates/wamn-api compile_update path + tests. Design: docs/api-gateway.md.
acceptance_criteria: PUT /api/rest/{entity}/{id} requires all writable required fields and nulls omitted nullable fields (full replace); PATCH remains a partial merge; both covered by wamn-api tests.
notes:
=== RESUME PLAN (wamn-61q.2 [4.1] PUT full-replace; start after bd prime + bd show wamn-61q.2) ===

GOAL: Give PUT true full-replace semantics, distinct from PATCH's partial merge.
Today the router treats PUT identically to PATCH (partial update of only the
provided fields). SMALL, PURE-CRATE change: crates/wamn-api only + its unit tests.
No component/host/cluster/DB needed — acceptance is "covered by wamn-api tests".

CURRENT STATE (probed 2026-07-11, HEAD 5ebc627):
- crates/wamn-api/src/router.rs:194 dispatch: `(Method::Put | Method::Patch, Some(id))
  => self.compile_update(entity, id, body)` — PUT and PATCH share one path.
- compile_update (router.rs:438-477): PARTIAL — iterates entity.fields, and for each
  field PRESENT in the body emits `SET "col" = $n(value)`; omitted fields are left
  untouched. Guards: reject_unknown_keys (rejects managed id/tenant_id + unknown),
  `obj.is_empty() -> 400 "no fields to update"`. RETURNING projection, status 200,
  WHERE "id" = $n (RLS USING scopes tenant). value_for_field validates per type.
- Method enum has Put/Patch (router.rs:33-34, from_http 40-45).
- compile_create already computes field requirement as `required = !nullable &&
  default.is_none()` (the create path — reuse/mirror this exact rule).

THE CHANGE (crates/wamn-api/src/router.rs):
1. Thread a `replace: bool` into compile_update (replace = matches!(method, Put)), or
   split into compile_replace + compile_update sharing a helper. Simplest: pass a bool.
   Dispatch becomes: Put -> replace=true, Patch -> replace=false.
2. PATCH branch: UNCHANGED (partial — only SET present fields; keep the
   `obj.is_empty() -> 400 "no fields to update"` guard).
3. PUT (replace=true) branch: iterate ALL writable entity.fields:
     - field PRESENT in body -> `SET "col" = $n(value_for_field(f, v))` (as today).
     - field ABSENT ->
         * if required (!nullable && default.is_none()) -> return
           Err(ApiError::InvalidRequest("missing required field <name>")) [400].
           (Consider ApiError::PayloadRequired if a dedicated code reads better.)
         * else -> `SET "col" = DEFAULT` (NO param). This is the clean full-replace
           reset: a nullable-no-default col -> NULL; a col WITH a default -> its
           default. Postgres `UPDATE ... SET col = DEFAULT` does exactly this.
   reject_unknown_keys still runs first (managed/unknown body keys -> 400). Managed
   id/tenant_id are never in entity.fields, so they are never SET. RETURNING/status/
   WHERE id unchanged.

DECISION TO CONFIRM ON RESUME (minor — recommend, then proceed unless told otherwise):
- Omitted field that HAS a default on PUT: reset to its DB default via `SET col =
  DEFAULT` (my recommendation — true full-replace: the body IS the new resource).
  The only alternative (leave it untouched) would blur PUT back toward PATCH. Confirm
  the SET DEFAULT choice; if the user prefers "omitted defaulted -> NULL", change the
  else-branch to bind SqlValue::Null instead of the DEFAULT keyword.

TESTS (crates/wamn-api/tests/api.rs — run `cargo test -p wamn-api`):
- PUT missing a required field -> 400 (InvalidRequest).
- PUT full replace: an omitted NULLABLE field emits `"col" = DEFAULT` (assert the
  compiled SQL contains it) and provided fields become $n params.
- PUT with all writable fields present -> normal UPDATE, 200-shaped plan.
- PATCH partial unchanged (regression): only provided fields SET, others untouched;
  `obj.is_empty()` PATCH still 400.
- Reuse the poc-receiving fixture (suppliers has a nullable numeric standard_cost +
  a required text name -> ideal: PUT without name = 400; PUT without standard_cost =
  `standard_cost = DEFAULT`).

SCOPE / NON-GOALS:
- PURE crate: crates/wamn-api/src/router.rs + tests/api.rs. Injection-safety invariants
  unchanged (values are still $n params; DEFAULT is a keyword, not user input).
- docs/api-gateway.md: one line on PUT vs PATCH (optional).
- The api-gateway COMPONENT links wamn-api, so shipping the behavior to the DEPLOYED
  gateway would need a component rebuild + wash re-push + workload restart — but the
  issue's acceptance is crate-test coverage, so that deploy refresh is OPTIONAL/out of
  scope for this P3 (note it; the apibench/apiproof gates don't currently exercise PUT).
- No CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md change: the [4.1] gate command is already `cargo test -p
  wamn-api` (no new command). Only touch the docs if adding a PUT example.

STANDING RULES: ONE issue at a time (this prep CLAIMS wamn-61q.2; nothing else in
progress — wamn-61q.1 is closed). ALWAYS ask-first on the SET-DEFAULT decision above
before finalizing if unsure. Commit after bd close (git commit direct on main; no
remote -> no push). bd remember via FILES + "$(cat file)"; --key not positional.

ENV STATE (2026-07-11, HEAD 5ebc627, tree CLEAN): 4.1 (wamn-759) + 4.1b (wamn-61q.1)
both DONE + committed. This prep only CLAIMS wamn-61q.2 + attaches this plan; do NOT
implement until the user resumes. Sibling still open: wamn-61q.3 [add api-gateway to
2.6 egressbench] P3. Memories to load: wamn-4.1-api-gateway-facts (router.rs
compile_create/compile_update + value_for_field + ParamBuilder + injection-safety),
wamn-4.1b-api-gateway-serving-facts (the deploy path, if a component refresh is wanted).

title: [11.8] Schema-change impact analysis
description: Catalog dependency graph (flow <-> entity <-> generated API) identifies affected flows when a migration is staged (3.2) and auto-runs their suites before DDL applies; failing assertions reported in the schema designer. Design: docs/platform-plan.md 11.8
notes:
External review R9b (docs/review-findings.md § R9, verified at tip 873c3d8) — NAMED TEST CASE for 11.8: table rename x row-event registration = silent trigger loss. The outbox triggers are rename-safe at the physical level (constant-named, CREATE OR REPLACE — a renamed table keeps its trigger) and emit TG_TABLE_NAME = the NEW physical name (crates/wamn-ddl/src/outbox.rs:104,108), while row-event flows register the OLD declared table string (wamn-flow types.rs:119-123; matching is plain name-equality in crates/wamn-run-queue/src/outbox.rs:75-77) — and unmatched outbox rows are ACKED, never HELD (outbox.rs:106-111; HELD covers only parse-skew and flow-id mismatch). So renaming a watched table makes every registered row-event flow silently stop firing: no error, no failed run, no held rows — exactly the silent-breakage class 11.8 exists to catch. REQUIREMENT: staging a migration that renames a table flags every row-event flow registered on it. REMEDIATION DECISION (take when implementing): auto-migrate the registration to the new name in the same catalog bump (matches the trigger's rename-follows behavior; review-recommended) vs require explicit re-registration (safer against accidental renames, worse UX). NOTE: wamn-ddl structurally CANNOT emit this notice — its only workspace dep is wamn-catalog, no flow-registration input — so the check necessarily lives at this layer (catalog dependency graph / dispatcher registry), not the DDL compiler; the review's "migration path emits a notice" sub-suggestion is redirected here. Interim doc warning: wamn-m5g. VERIFY: register a row-event flow, stage a rename, assert the flag (and the chosen policy's outcome) rather than silence.

L5I9.19 UPDATE (2026-07-20): the R9b rename-x-row-event case above is STRUCTURALLY RETIRED with the outbox path — the referenced code (wamn-ddl outbox.rs, run-queue outbox.rs match_outbox) is deleted, and the CDC path is rename-proof by construction: the reader keys on relation OID -> stable entity id (EVT-OIDMAP, l5i9.11) and event registrations declare the ENTITY ID, not the table name, so a rename changes nothing a registration matches on (proven by the l5i9.11 live rename drill). 11.8 impact analysis remains for its broader scope (flow<->entity<->API dependency graph, suite auto-run); the rename-silent-loss test case is no longer reproducible.

Suite execution stays wamn-0lfu — its input contract (the report's tenant/flow_id/version/suite_id tuples) noted on 0lfu. title: feat(run-state): activate the premium durable tier
description:
## Why this bead exists

OWNER RULING 2026-08-26. The durable tier is a PRODUCT DECISION - premium, demand-gated - so its activation gets an honest owner rather than a resurrected bead or a phantom id.

wamn-0h0g.5.4 used to be named as the activator, in deploy/sql/run-state.sql and on wamn-0h0g.20.28. IT IS CLOSED, and it closed BY REFUSING THAT ROLE: its close reason records the effect ledger half shelving as the premium durable tier, needing no unlanded first caller. A closed-out bead does not resurrect. This bead inherits the scope .5.4 shelved.

## Trigger

FIRST PAYING DURABLE-TIER CLIENT. Event-triggered, not dated. Deferred until then.

## Scope inherited from the .5.4 shelving

1. Re-grant INSERT on wamn_run.effect_attempts to the writer family - the grant wamn-0h0g.20.30 revokes. It narrows in the PROVISIONER (crates/control/provision/src/sql.rs, WorkloadRoleFamily::EffectWriter) and in deploy/sql/run-state.sql, so it widens in the same two places, with the generated-SQL drift pins in crates/schema/control/src/run_plane.rs moving alongside.
2. FLIP wamn-0h0g.20.30 PROBE ARM. That probe is the parked/live discriminator: parked = server-side denial asserted. Activation inverts the assertion. The arm is the contract between the two beads - do not delete it, invert it.
3. Wire the ledger path per the wamn-0h0g.20.3 shelving contract.
4. FEATURE ON per the wamn-hopk cfg-gate: the durable-tier cargo feature on crates/execution/run-state, default off, currently carrying only the attempt module. Membership was MEASURED, not assumed - durability and effect_writer_credential deliberately do NOT belong to the shelf because both thread through live default-tier code.

## What this bead is NOT

Not machinery ahead of demand. Nothing is built here until the trigger fires. It exists so that the DDL comment and the .20.30 probe arm can name a LIVE id instead of a bead that closed by refusing the role.
acceptance_criteria: Deferred until the first paying durable-tier client. On activation: the writer family holds INSERT on wamn_run.effect_attempts again, granted from the provisioner so fresh environments are born live rather than patched; the wamn-0h0g.20.30 denial probe is INVERTED rather than deleted, and passes; the ledger path is wired per the wamn-0h0g.20.3 shelving contract; the durable-tier feature is on, with its membership re-measured rather than assumed.
notes: Event-triggered, not dated: the trigger is the first paying durable-tier client. The durable tier is a product decision, demand-gated, so nothing is built here until demand exists. The bead exists so wamn-0h0g.20.30's probe arm and the run-state.sql DDL comment can name a live id from birth.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(management): expose inert attachment status only to authorized callers on demand
description: The anonymous callable boundary deliberately makes a cron-attached path indistinguishable from an absent path: both return 404 attachment-not-found. A cron-specific public refusal would disclose configuration existence. If an authenticated management consumer later requires the reason an attachment is inert, expose it as status on an authorized get-attachment surface instead of changing the anonymous wire literal. This work is demand-gated; do not build it without a named consumer.
acceptance_criteria: A named authenticated management consumer justifies the surface. Authorized get-attachment callers can read an inert attachment status without exposing the attachment through the callable path. Unauthorized and anonymous callers still receive the same 404 attachment-not-found bytes for cron-attached and absent paths. Authorization, non-enumeration, wire compatibility, and named mutants are proven.

title: [SR-MVP] chore(fmt): normalize the bounded Rust formatting debt in a quiet wave boundary

The root Clippy baseline is already green, so this is bounded cosmetic drift rather than a prerequisite for lint reachability. It must not ride beside active Rust lanes because broad whitespace churn manufactures collisions without semantic value. Run it only in a quiet window after one wave is fully integrated and before the next issues are claimed.

Mix in no hand edits or semantic changes. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo fmt --manifest-path components/Cargo.toml --all -- --check`, root workspace strict Clippy with `--keep-going`, every component Clippy leg in `tools/repo-lint`, and the workspace test gate match their recorded baselines. The formatting diff is reviewable as pure mechanical churn.

QUIET-WINDOW EXECUTION STARTED, 2026-08-20 at 114b5a8f: Wave 12 implementation commits are pushed; all w12 worktrees, lane branches, isolated targets, and disposable containers are removed. No next-wave issue has been claimed. The change will be formatter output only across the root and components Cargo workspaces.

title: [SR-MVP] defer(router): per-item routing / fan-out construct for wirings
description: Closing the bounded-for-each deferral (.13.18) with the node language leaves a real gap the spec does not cover: exe-model defines NO iteration or fan-out construct at the router — its only array shape is stream batch input (one router run carrying the ordered array), which pushes per-item work inside a component. That serves map-shaped work but gives a wirer no way to route N items through downstream nodes per item. If a wiring ever needs per-item routing, design it against the ROUTER (frontier semantics, hop-limit interaction, live-view tap shape) — never resurrect the flow-language node. Demand-gated: promotion needs a named wiring that cannot express its shape inside a component.

title: [SR-MVP] feat(audit): per-segment release attribution on the claim/lease event stream
description:
## Why

Ruling wamn-0h0g.13.55 redefined the run's release record as "the release of the claim currently executing this run", which deliberately gives up the ability to say from the run row alone what release nodes 1..k executed under.

The owner's framing: that is a PER-SEGMENT AUDIT QUESTION, and its honest home is per-claim, not per-run.

## Scope

If it is ever needed: release identity joins the claim/lease event stream, so each claim segment carries its own release and the per-segment history is reconstructible without denormalizing it onto the run.

## Boundary

EXPLICITLY DEMAND-GATED, and NOTHING IS TO BE BUILT FOR IT NOW. The trigger is named: park ships to production AND audit names the need. Do not pick this up speculatively.

Named by an owner ruling of 2026-08-16 (wave-3 decisions).
notes: OWNER RULING 2026-08-17: DEFERRED as part of the named-trigger sweep -- demand-gated with a stated trigger, so it belongs on ice rather than in the ready frontier. P4. Revisit on its own trigger.

title: [SR-MVP] decision(hosting): customer run-plane trust and signed release closures
description:
## Decision
If customer-hosted project databases are promoted after MVP, choose whether the executor/router remains with the platform and verifies a control-signed release-closure envelope, or whether customer-controlled bindings, run-state and activation facts remain explicitly attestational.

## Rationale
Component digests and the content-addressed release manifest are independently verifiable, but a customer superuser controls binding generations, wiring activation pointers, run rows and effect-authority inputs. The platform-hosted plane does not need the mechanism, so choosing now would add unused signing and key-lifecycle work.

## Hold
Post-MVP; must not block the platform-hosted plane cutover. Promotion needs a concrete customer-hosting demand and an owner ruling naming router residency, signed-envelope requirement or explicit attestational guarantees, key ownership and rotation, replay/freshness semantics, and required proofs.
design:
When promoted, compare threat model, tenancy, key custody, offline operation, rotation, manifest replay, incident recovery, and which audit claims remain independently enforceable. Do not infer this choice from digest verification alone.

DEPLOYMENT-SIMPLIFICATION AMENDMENT (2026-08-16, rulings wamn-0h0g.13.43/.13.44; freeze wamn-0h0g.15.1): Rationale: 'deployed release' drops from customer-superuser-controlled inputs; desired state lives in Git + etcd and the release manifest is content-addressed, digest-verifiable (ruling 4). Bindings/generations/run-state remain customer-DB-controlled; the decision itself stays held.
acceptance_criteria: The issue remains held through wamn-0h0g.1.3. Promotion requires a concrete customer-hosting demand and an owner ruling that names executor residency, signed-envelope requirement or explicit attestational guarantees, key ownership and rotation, replay/freshness semantics, failure behavior, and required proofs. No customer-hosted signing surface ships in MVP.

title: [SR-MVP] defer(exec): demand-gated verified disk plan cache
description:
## Why
MVP uses a bounded process-memory cache and readiness prefetch. A disk cache adds persistence, atomic insertion, eviction, corruption, and credential-boundary work without a current demand signal.

## Scope
After MVP close, evaluate a verified disk-backed cache only if measurements show repeated cold fetches or store availability materially harm the approved service floor.

## Boundary
No disk bytes, fallback path, cache daemon, shared volume, or relaxed readiness belongs in MVP.
acceptance_criteria: This issue remains held through wamn-0h0g.1.3. Promotion requires measured cold-fetch pressure, one owner-approved storage and eviction model, atomic hash-verified insertion, corruption and partial-write recovery, tenant isolation, bounded resource use, and named failure/mutation gates. Until then the bounded process-memory cache is the sole executor cache.
close_reason: Execution plans and the deterministic compiler retire, so there are no plan bytes to cache on disk; the plan supply path retires with them (exe-model.md §What retires). A host-side component-module cache is different machinery, new work.

title: [SR-MVP] defer(plan-store): evaluate OCI execution-plan artifacts
description:
## Why
The amendment deliberately keeps execution-plan bytes in the control execution_bundles table for MVP and marks plans-as-OCI demand-gated.

## Scope
After MVP close, evaluate whether measured scale, distribution, or retention needs justify a content-addressed OCI carrier while preserving the frozen plan-byte digest, tenant authorization, publish verification, reader isolation, and cache semantics.

## Boundary
No OCI registry dependency, dual artifact carrier, mirroring, migration, or runtime fallback belongs in MVP.
acceptance_criteria: This issue remains held through wamn-0h0g.1.3. Promotion requires measured pressure that the control table plus bounded cache cannot satisfy, an owner decision on the sole bytes home, exact migration and rollback semantics, authorization and tenant-isolation design, and named structured gates. Until then execution_bundles remains the only artifact store.

DDL smoke on throwaway PG: ladder_ddl provisions cleanly, both fallthrough statements execute as a clean 0-row no-op. run_dead_letters stays AbsentByDesign — ladderproof rungs always reach completed, the terminal-settle dead-letter path is never driven. Emergent: Need::RequiredExcept removed from schema_drift.rs (ladderproof was its sole constructor; surviving Required/AbsentByDesign asserts byte-unchanged, all six stand-in tests green in the MAIN tree). description: Residual from wamn-l5i9.32 (2b8728c): single-instance rendered clusters (and live wamn-pg, 256Mi) keep the PG default logical_decoding_work_mem=64MB; the multi-instance render pins 16MB. Evidence first: measure before changing.
notes:
C-CDC EVIDENCE RECORDED (wamn-l5i9.14, 2026-07-20, docs/ceilings.md § C-CDC — the evidence gate this bead is parked on): VERDICT = no always-on logical_decoding_work_mem raise is justified. (1) Narrow-row workloads cannot plausibly spill the default 64MB: the reorder buffer holds ~190 B/change (tuple + TOAST pointers), so a single txn needs ~330k row changes to cross it. (2) The controlled spill-cost pair (single-txn 50k narrow at a forced 64kB vs default) prices spilling at -18 percent drain rate (49.4k vs 60.1k rows/s) under a pathological 1000x starve — bounded, not cliff-shaped. (3) The one real default-64MB spill observed — a 12000 x 6KiB single-txn wide import (82.8MB buffered, TOAST content IS buffered) — still drained at 92.6 MB/s. If a tenant workload lives in the giant-single-txn-import regime, the knob is a per-cluster tuning lever per this bead's own gate ('measure before changing' — measured). Raw: ccdc-drain.csv spill columns.

No component copy of the logic exists — materializer + gates bind wamn_event_wire::subject_token directly, publish/consume stay coherent by sharing one impl. E3/l5i9.52 confirmed orthogonal (cross-schema same-name collision is the envelope-qualifier concern; premise note already on that bead). Gates: wamn-event-wire 10/10 (+1) lane AND main tree; clippy clean; consumers compile-checked in main tree (wamn-cdc-reader, wamn-gates native; materializer wasm32-wasip2). Mutant: suffix no-op'd -> subject_token_distinguishes_dot_from_underscore FAILED by name; restored sha256-verified. title: [R20] bound author-supplied retry cap-ms
description: docs/findings.md section-2 R20 (Low). Author-supplied retry cap-ms is unbounded. With runner work.
close_reason: R20 fixed (main commit = cherry-pick of lane-a3 eeb7d41): author-supplied retry cap-ms clamped at parse time to RetryPolicy::CAP_MS_CEILING = 3_600_000 (1h), a one-liner .map(min) in from_config mirroring the max-attempts shape; the 30s default untouched. Ceiling derived from code: 1h is the janitor reap grace (janitor_sweep_sql $1 at every call site — failoverbench/queuebench/dispatchbench/queue.rs all pass 3_600_000), the longest run-lifecycle timescale before a stuck run is reaped as infrastructure-failure; a retry is error RECOVERY (unlike a delay node which parks unboundedly by design) so a single backoff must not out-park that horizon. Not vacuous vs base-ms/factor: the cap applies AFTER scaling (backoff_ms clamps scaled>=cap), so a giant base or factor is already capped; max-attempts is a separate count axis (u32, .max(1)) — verified, only cap-ms implemented per the bead. Gates: wamn-runner 40/40 + clippy clean, lane AND main tree; flowrunner wasm32 release build green in BOTH (the engine ships in the guest — the deployed-runner rebake rides the wave-end sweep). Named tests: author_cap_ms_over_ceiling_is_clamped / in-range passes through / default unchanged. Mutant: clamp removed -> author_cap_ms_over_ceiling_is_clamped FAILED by name; restored sha256-verified.

title: [R19] row_to_map lossy on non-UTF-8 (from_utf8_lossy)
description: docs/findings.md section-2 R19 (Low). row_to_map uses from_utf8_lossy and silently corrupts non-UTF-8 bytes. With reader work.
close_reason: R19 fixed (main commit = cherry-pick of lane-a1 23e7ce4): row_to_map is now fallible — a non-UTF-8 pgoutput value returns ReplicationError::Config, classified SessionFate::Fatal (reader exits loudly, non-retryable, slot holds WAL) instead of the silent from_utf8_lossy U+FFFD corruption. Rationale: the frozen v3 wire carries values as JSON strings (UTF-8 by definition), so non-UTF-8 = non-UTF-8 SOURCE DATABASE encoding — systemic misconfiguration, not per-row anomaly; a UTF-8 Postgres validates text on input so the path is unreachable there. Both drain call-sites sever via DrainOutcome::Severed. Envelope untouched (FROZEN 0.1.0 held). Gates: wamn-cdc-reader --lib 19/19 (was 17, +2 named tests: clean-UTF-8-unchanged incl. multibyte, non-UTF-8-refuses) in the lane AND independently re-run in the MAIN tree post-cherry-pick; clippy clean. Mutant: lossy reverted -> row_to_map_refuses_non_utf8_rather_than_corrupting FAILED by name; restored sha256-verified. event_reader_live env-gated live test skipped in-lane by design; the reader image rebake rides the wave-end sweep.
